9.09%。这两个百分比描述了具有不同分母的相同排列。第一项措施增加了相对于预付款的信贷。第二个衡量全额购买的有条件折扣。如果不进行转换，则无法在两个碱基之间转移百分比。百分比图表通过假设充分使用和相同的结帐价格来隔离此计算。它没有声称所选的部分用例获得了 9.09% 的回报。它也不包含在工具中其他地方输入的竞争现金价格。将这个简单的分母问题分开可以更容易地了解标题奖金的实际衡量标准。未使用的积分仍然可见，而不是被视为损失。选定的使用计划将在期限内兑换已加载 110 加元的 80%，即 88 加元。22 加元的限制积分仍然存在。瀑布可以核对已支付的信用、奖金和扣除的购买金额，而不会假装奖金是作为另一笔银行存款到达的。对于完全相同的购买，假设替代结账价格低 5%。因此，在其他地方购买这些产品将花费 83.60 加元。该卡需要预付 100 加元现金，比迄今为止匹配购买所需的现金多出 16.40 加元。该差异并非 16.40 加元的实际损失。在该模式下，持卡人仍拥有 22 加元未使用的限制信用。剩余部分不适用到期、注销、现金退款或最终现金估值。现金比较回答了有关已支付款项的狭义问题，必须与剩余余额一起阅读。更便宜的现金价格替代方案可以吸收部分奖金优势 现在考虑充分使用默认的 110 加元，同样降低 5% 的竞争结帐价格。在其他地方，整个篮子的售价为 104.50 加元。支付 100 加元购买该卡可以在相同的购买中节省 4.50 加元的现金，而不是 10 加元。相对于 104.50 加元的替代方案，节省了约 4.31%。差异来自于比较实际假设的篮子价格，而不是使用卡的面额作为唯一的基准。尚未收集商家价格或可用交易； 5% 的差异是作者输入的。比较需要可比的总结帐金额。如果某一价格省略了税费、运费、费用或所需的额外购买，则在输入计算之前需要进行调整。该模型还假设这些商品已经成为家庭计划的一部分。购买额外物品只是为了消耗信用改变购物篮，并不能证明奖金改善了预算。跟踪现金离开的时间，而不是将信用视为银行准备金 现金图表在零月份支付全部卡金额。匹配的替代方案仅在选定的购买发生时付费，统一在每个假定的月底进行。两条路径在该期限内获得相同的篮子数量，但在不同的日期投入银行现金。这些线显示累计支付的现金，而不是银行余额或净财富。承诺给商家的钱不会仅仅因为它仍然显示为卡上的信用而被认为可用于另一张账单。未用余额也不能同时分配给两个未来的购物计划。该插图不包括卡外保留的现金的任何利息或其他用途。它同样假设在选定的时间内固定价格、免费且无到期日。这些是建模条件，而不是实际促销信用没有限制的声明。即使全额赎回会产生有利的名义现金比较，时间和条款也很重要。使用网格来测试计划，而不预测未来的赎回 该矩阵会改变信用使用比例和竞争价格差异。单元格为正值意味着此时已向该卡支付的现金多于其他地方匹配购​​买所需的现金。负细胞意味着更少。在保持拥有状态时，剩余信用不包括在该支出衡量标准中，因此颜色不是最终损益估计。在默认奖金和 5% 竞争价差的情况下，必须使用约 95.69% 的充值额度，匹配替代方案的累计现金支出才能达到原来的 100 加元卡付款。这是现金承诺的门槛，而不是对未使用余额的经济盈亏平衡估值或更多购物的建议。足够便宜的替代方案甚至可以消除充分利用现金的优势。例如，如果相同的 110 加元篮子在其他地方的价格低 15%，则其现金价格为 93.50 加元，即使在每次使用积分后也低于该卡的 100 加元成本。一起评估百分比、预期篮子和时机，并始终保持剩余的受限余额可见。

6f0827e0da22cf5bd26e0d492eca018d02012cc6.src: A performance average needs a defined membership rule as well as returns. Removing a record changes the reported denominator; it does not remove the investor’s original outcome. Define the original group before reading its average An end-of-year fund directory can look like a convenient starting point for comparing past performance. But a list of funds still present at the end of a period need not represent the whole group that existed at its beginning. This article constructs a small original example with eight invented funds, labelled A through H. Each begins the same one-year period with CAD 10,000. Their assumed complete-period total returns, with all income retained and before fees and taxes, are +20%, +12%, +8%, +4%, 0%, −5%, −15% and −40%. Every return remains known throughout the exercise. This is a fully specified teaching cohort, rather than a random sample, a market database or a forecast. The calculator does not infer missing returns or estimate a closure process. The equal opening allocations total CAD 80,000. With no deposits, withdrawals or other adjustments, the simple return of that original basket equals the arithmetic mean of its eight individual one-year returns. This is a cross-sectional average over one common period, rather than an average of successive annual returns. Change the directory without erasing the known outcomes At the default setting, the end-of-year directory omits funds F, G and H. Their complete-year outcomes remain in the first chart, marked as omitted. The other five records are still listed. This is an assumed reporting status at the end of the observation window. It does not assert that a poor return caused a closure, that a missing listing means liquidation, or that a discontinued fund necessarily lost all its value. Carhart, Carpenter, Lynch and Musto’s working-paper abstract on mutual fund survivorship explains why the survival rule and the observation period matter when studying performance. The numerical cohort here is separate from that research and imports none of its empirical estimates. The omission-count control removes H first, then G, then F from the reported directory. It leaves all eight original records available for the complete-cohort calculation. That distinction makes the selection visible instead of silently changing the historical population. Calculate both means with their own denominators The five listed returns add to 44 percentage points. Dividing by five gives a listed-group mean of 8.8% . The three omitted returns add to negative 60 percentage points, giving that group a mean of −20% . All eight returns add to negative 16 percentage points. Dividing by eight gives a complete-cohort mean of −2% . The listed mean therefore exceeds the complete-cohort mean by 10.8 percentage points in this invented case. The count chart explains why the denominator changes from eight to five. It is not a probability chart and does not estimate the chance that a fund will survive. There are exactly eight known members in the stated example. Also keep percentage points separate from a relative percentage change. The difference between 8.8% and −2% is 10.8 percentage points. Describing it as a percentage increase over a negative baseline would obscure the comparison. Weight the subgroup means by their original-cohort shares The complete-cohort mean can be reconstructed from the two disjoint groups. The five listed funds represent five-eighths of the original cohort; the three omitted funds represent three-eighths. The calculation is (5 ÷ 8) × 8.8% + (3 ÷ 8) × (−20%) = −2% . The waterfall displays a positive 5.5 percentage-point contribution from listed records and a negative 7.5 percentage-point contribution from omitted records. Adding 8.8% directly to −20% would give the two groups equal weight despite their different membership counts. Their arithmetic sum is not the mean return of all eight funds. This weighting works because the example uses equal opening amounts and one common complete year. An asset-weighted study would require its specified asset weights. A multi-period strategy with changing membership would need a return and rebalancing method for each period rather than this one-year identity. An omitted record does not disappear from the investor’s original result The listed positions finish with CAD 54,400: CAD 50,000 of opening allocations plus CAD 4,400 of gains. The omitted positions finish with CAD 24,000: CAD 30,000 initially, less CAD 6,000 of losses. Together they finish with CAD 78,400, a CAD 1,600 decline on the original CAD 80,000. The 8.8% listed average does not turn that original basket into a gain. It summarizes a smaller group with only CAD 50,000 of opening capital. Do not compare the two groups’ ending dollar totals as if both began with the same investment. Their capital and member counts differ. The metrics retain the original whole-basket ending value so the reporting filter cannot erase its losses. An actual liquidation, merger or distribution would require its real cash and successor records. This example assigns an end-year directory status after a complete known year; it does not fabricate an unobserved post-closure return or assume that missing history is worth zero. The sign of the gap depends on the outcomes omitted The sensitivity control adds an assumed percentage-point adjustment only to the records currently omitted. It holds the listed records and directory membership fixed. This changes the invented underlying outcomes rather than estimating a statistical correction. With three omissions and a +60 percentage-point adjustment, their returns become +55%, +45% and +20%. The complete-cohort mean becomes 20.5%, while the listed mean remains 8.8%. The listed-minus-complete gap is now negative 11.7 percentage points. The sign has reversed because the omitted group is now stronger. A label such as missing, closed or discontinued does not by itself establish the omitted performance. The data and selection mechanism need examination. With no omissions, all eight records are still listed and both means equal one another. The adjustment has no recipients, so it changes nothing. No omitted-group mean is defined when that group has zero members; its contribution to the full-cohort mean is simply zero. Ask how the history was assembled before using it in a plan Investor.gov’s performance-claims bulletin discusses calculation methods, excluded costs and selective presentation. These are useful questions alongside the membership rule: what period, which records, what return definition and which expenses? For a real database, check how it handles new entries, name changes, mergers, liquidations, incomplete periods and records removed after the fact. Retaining a list of discontinued names is not enough if their relevant return histories are absent or incompatible. This article supplies no evidence of manager skill, market-wide bias or a future expected return. Its eight funds are invented, and the directory is observed after the modeled year. Selecting only those records retrospectively is not an investment rule a reader could necessarily have followed at the beginning. A financial plan still needs defensible return assumptions, uncertainty, fees, taxes and a workable cash calendar. Use this example to inspect the history behind an average before allowing that number to drive a savings target or retirement projection.
6f0827e0da22cf5bd26e0d492eca018d02012cc6.zh: 绩效平均值需要明确的会员资格规则和回报。删除记录会更改报告的分母；它不会消除投资者的原始结果。在读取其平均值之前定义原始组年终基金目录看起来像是比较过去表现的一个方便的起点。但在一段时期结束时仍然存在的基金清单不一定代表其开始时存在的整个群体。本文构建了一个小型原始示例，其中包含八个发明基金，标记为 A 到 H。每个基金都以 10,000 加元开始相同的一年期。他们假设的完整期间总回报率（保留所有收入且未计费用和税金）为 +20%、+12%、+8%、+4%、0%、-5%、-15% 和 -40%。在整个练习过程中，每次返回都是已知的。这是一个完全指定的教学群体，而不是随机样本、市场数据库或预测。该计算器不会推断缺失的回报或估计关闭过程。等额开放拨款总额为 80,000 加元。在没有存款、取款或其他调整的情况下，原始篮子的简单回报等于其八个单独的一年回报的算术平均值。这是一个共同时期的横截面平均值，而不是连续年度回报率的平均值。更改目录而不删除已知结果 在默认设置下，年终目录忽略基金 F、G 和 H。它们的全年结果保留在第一个图表中，标记为省略。其他五项记录仍然列出。这是观察窗口结束时的假定报告状态。它并不断言回报不佳会导致关闭，未上市意味着清算，或者终止的基金必然会失去其所有价值。卡哈特、卡彭特、林奇和穆斯托关于共同基金生存的工作论文摘要解释了为什么生存规则和观察期在研究业绩时很重要。这里的数字队列与该研究是分开的，并且没有导入任何经验估计。遗漏计数控制首先从报告的目录中删除 H，然后是 G，最后是 F。它留下所有八个原始记录可用于完整队列计算。这种区别使选择变得可见，而不是默默地改变历史人口。用各自的分母计算这两个平均值 列出的五个回报率加起来为 44 个百分点。除以 5 得出列出组的平均值为 8.8%。三个省略的回报增加了负 60 个百分点，使该组的平均值为 -20% 。所有 8 项回报率合计为负 16 个百分点。除以 8 得出的完整队列平均值为 -2% 。因此，在本发明的案例中，列出的平均值超出了整个队列的平均值 10.8 个百分点。计数图解释了为什么分母从 8 变为 5。它不是概率图，也不会估计基金生存的机会。在所述示例中恰好有八个已知成员。还要将百分点与相对百分比变化分开。 8.8%和-2%之间相差10.8个百分点。将其描述为相对于负基线的百分比增长会模糊比较。通过原始队列份额对子组均值进行加权 完整队列均值可以从两个不相交的组中重建。这五只上市基金占原来基金数量的八分之五；被遗漏的三个基金占八分之三。计算结果为 (5 ÷ 8) × 8.8% + (3 ÷ 8) × (−20%) = −2% 。瀑布显示列出的记录带来了 5.5 个百分点的正贡献，而遗漏的记录带来了 7.5 个百分点的负贡献。直接将 8.8% 添加到 -20% 将使这两个组的权重相等，尽管它们的成员数量不同。它们的算术总和并不是所有八只基金的平均回报。这种加权之所以有效，是因为该示例使用相同的期初金额和一个共同的完整年份。资产加权研究需要指定的资产权重。成员不断变化的多时期战略需要每个时期的回报和重新平衡方法，而不是一年的身份。遗漏的记录不会从投资者的原始结果中消失列出的头寸最终为 54,400 加元：50,000 加元的开仓分配加上 4,400 加元的收益。省略的头寸最终为 24,000 加元：最初为 30,000 加元，减去 6,000 加元的损失。他们最终的成交价为 78,400 加元，比最初的 80,000 加元减少了 1,600 加元。 8.8% 的平均收益率并没有将最初的篮子转化为收益。它总结了一个规模较小的集团，其开业资金只有 50,000 加元。不要将两组的最终美元总额进行比较，就好像两者都以相同的投资开始一样。他们的资本和成员数量不同。这些指标保留原始的整篮最终值，因此报告过滤器无法消除其损失。实际的清算、合并或分配将需要其真实的现金和继任者记录。此示例在完整的已知年份后分配年终目录状态；它不会制造未观察到的关闭后回报，也不会假设缺失的历史价值为零。差距的符号取决于省略的结果。敏感性控制仅对当前省略的记录添加假定的百分点调整。它保存列出的记录和固定的目录成员资格。这改变了发明的基本结果，而不是估计统计修正。剔除三项并进行+60个百分点的调整后，他们的回报率分别变为+55%、+45%和+20%。完整队列平均值变为 20.5%，而列出的平均值仍为 8.8%。上市减去完成的差距现在为负 11.7 个百分点。符号已经逆转，因为被忽略的群体现在更强了。缺失、关闭或停产等标签本身并不构成遗漏的性能。数据和选择机制需要审查。没有任何遗漏，所有八项记录仍然列出，并且两者的含义相同。该调整没有接收者，因此不会改变任何内容。当该组有零个成员时，不会定义省略组均值；它对全队列平均值的贡献简直为零。在将其用于计划之前，先询问历史记录是如何组合的 Investor.gov 的业绩声明公告讨论了计算方法、排除成本和选择性表述。这些都是与会员资格规则一起有用的问题：什么时期、哪些记录、什么回报定义以及哪些费用？对于真实的数据库，检查它如何处理新条目、名称更改、合并、清算、不完整期间和事后删除的记录。如果相关的退货历史不存在或不兼容，则仅保留已停产名称的列表是不够的。本文没有提供经理技能、市场范围偏见或未来预期回报的证据。其八只基金均已发明，目录按照模型年份进行观察。仅回顾性地选择这些记录并不是读者一开始就一定要遵循的投资规则。财务计划仍然需要合理的回报假设、不确定性、费用、税收和可行的现金日历。使用此示例检查平均值背后的历史记录，然后再允许该数字推动储蓄目标或退休预测。

1cd1dc1dfeaafb43d4accbe5ba22c66ee7137b03.src: A lower price reduces the contribution on every unit already being sold. Compare the additional units at the new contribution per unit before carrying a revenue increase into the household income plan. A household supported by a small business needs more than a revenue target A successful-looking promotion can sell more units and collect more revenue while leaving less to support the owner. The missing link is the contribution left after the variable cost of each sale. The U.S. Small Business Administration’s break-even guide separates unit selling price, variable costs and fixed costs in a one-product calculation. BDC’s break-even explanation also distinguishes the sales level needed to cover costs from a wider analysis of price and volume. These sources support the framework; every business amount and sales case here is invented. The tool compares two monthly operating plans for one product or standard service unit. It assumes every selected sale is collected and its variable cost is paid in the same month. It does not predict how customers respond to a price or certify that the selected volume can be achieved. Calculate what each original unit contributes before fixed costs The original price is CAD 100 per unit. The variable-cost input is 60% of that original price, producing a cash cost of CAD 60 per unit . This cost is then held fixed during the discount comparison. It is not recalculated as 60% of the discounted selling price. Each original sale contributes CAD 100 − CAD 60 = CAD 40 toward monthly fixed costs and surplus. At 100 units, revenue is CAD 10,000, variable costs are CAD 6,000 and contribution is CAD 4,000. Subtracting the unchanged CAD 2,500 of fixed operating costs leaves CAD 1,500 of monthly operating surplus . That is before owner transfers and income tax, with financing, equipment spending and working-capital timing outside this simplified model. The distinction matters because a dollar of revenue is not a dollar available to spend at home. Variable costs need to be funded first, and fixed costs still need to be covered. A 20% price cut halves this example’s contribution per unit The entered 20% cut lowers the selling price from CAD 100 to CAD 80 . Since the same unit still costs CAD 60, its contribution falls from CAD 40 to CAD 20 . A 20% reduction in the selling price has produced a 50% reduction in contribution per unit. The selected comparison sells 150 units, 50% more than before. Revenue becomes CAD 12,000 , a 20% increase. Variable costs become CAD 9,000 , a 50% increase, because they follow the unit count at the unchanged CAD 60 cost. Only CAD 3,000 of contribution remains. After the same CAD 2,500 fixed costs, operating surplus is CAD 500 , down CAD 1,000 or about 66.67% from the original CAD 1,500. The first chart puts revenue and both cost categories beside each other so that the stronger revenue headline does not hide the weaker surplus. The two unit counts are independent scenario inputs. Their comparison does not estimate that a 20% price cut will cause a 50% volume increase. Preserving revenue, breaking even and preserving surplus are three different targets At CAD 80 per unit, preserving the original CAD 10,000 revenue requires 125 units. Those sales produce 125 × CAD 20 = CAD 2,500 of contribution, exactly equal to the fixed operating costs. The operating surplus is zero. Thus 125 units is also this discounted case’s operating break-even point . It covers the modeled costs but does not preserve the owner’s original CAD 1,500 surplus. To keep that original surplus with unchanged fixed costs, contribution must remain CAD 4,000. The required volume is CAD 4,000 ÷ CAD 20 = 200 units . The business must double its original unit sales, rather than merely increase volume by 20% or match the old revenue. More generally, with positive contribution per discounted unit, the comparison target is original units × original contribution per unit ÷ new contribution per unit. The headline rounds that result upward to a whole unit. A fractional calculated equality may be useful on the curve, but a whole-unit sales plan must meet or exceed it. Check the volume target against capacity before treating it as household income The separately entered capacity is 180 units per month. The 200-unit target exceeds it. At 180 units and the discounted CAD 20 contribution, the operating surplus would be 180 × CAD 20 − CAD 2,500 = CAD 1,100 , still CAD 400 below the original plan. The selected 150-unit comparison fits within that capacity, but fitting within capacity does not prove demand exists. Conversely, a case above the entered limit is flagged as arithmetic that is not feasible under that capacity assumption. Expanding capacity could require more staff, space, equipment or other spending. Those changes would invalidate the assumption of unchanged fixed and per-unit costs. The model does not add them automatically or assume that capacity can be raised without cost. The volume curve and matrix therefore remain conditional comparisons. Points or cells beyond the entered capacity are not sales forecasts. Their role is to expose the scale of the required change. Reconcile the change in surplus without counting the interaction twice The waterfall starts with the original CAD 1,500 surplus. First, applying the CAD 20 price reduction to the original 100 units removes CAD 2,000 . Then the additional 50 units contribute 50 × CAD 20 = CAD 1,000 at the new margin. The endpoint is CAD 500. Using the old CAD 40 contribution for those extra units would overstate their benefit. They are sold at the reduced price too. The bridge’s order keeps that price-volume interaction inside the new contribution used for the volume change. A different decomposition order could assign the interaction to a different step while reaching the same final surplus. The chart is an exact accounting explanation of two entered cases, not evidence that one action caused a particular customer response. More units cannot repair a non-positive contribution per unit With the original CAD 100 price and CAD 60 variable cost, a 40% price cut leaves a CAD 60 selling price and zero contribution. No number of those sales produces the original CAD 4,000 contribution. Fixed costs still leave an operating loss of CAD 2,500. A larger cut puts the selling price below the unchanged variable cost. Each additional sale then reduces the modeled surplus. When original contribution is positive and discounted contribution is zero or negative, the tool reports no finite volume that preserves the original surplus instead of displaying an artificial huge target. With zero original sales, there is no original contribution to preserve; zero comparison units meet that baseline. Also, preserving an original negative surplus does not make a business profitable. These boundary cases are reasons to keep the target definition visible. Carry a supported cash amount into the household plan Before relying on a promotion to support personal spending, check the actual price, unit costs, fixed costs, realistic demand and operational capacity over the same period. Separate costs that change with volume from costs that remain fixed only within a relevant range. This tool excludes sales tax, income tax, debt payments, new equipment, extra staffing, inventory timing and unpaid customer invoices. Even its positive operating surplus is not automatically after-tax household income or cash available for an owner withdrawal. The related business-cash guide follows stock, receivables and withdrawals; the contractor guide looks at billable capacity. Together, those questions help prevent a sales target from becoming a personal income assumption before the necessary costs, cash dates and constraints have been checked.
1cd1dc1dfeaafb43d4accbe5ba22c66ee7137b03.zh: 较低的价格会减少对已售出的每件商品的贡献。在将收入增加纳入家庭收入计划之前，比较每单位新缴款的额外单位。由小企业支持的家庭需要的不仅仅是收入目标 看似成功的促销活动可以销售更多单位并获得更多收入，同时留下更少的钱来支持业主。缺失的环节是每笔销售的可变成本后留下的贡献。美国小企业管理局的盈亏平衡指南将单位售价、可变成本和固定成本分开计算在一种产品中。 BDC 的盈亏平衡解释还将覆盖成本所需的销售水平与更广泛的价格和销量分析区分开来。这些来源支持该框架；这里的每一项业务金额和销售案例都是发明的。该工具可以比较一种产品或标准服务单元的两个月度运营计划。它假设每个选定的销售都已收集，并且其可变成本在同一个月支付。它不会预测客户对价格的反应或证明可以达到选定的数量。计算每个原始单位在固定成本之前的贡献 原始价格为每单位 100 加元。可变成本投入为原价的 60%，产生每单位 60 加元的现金成本。然后，该成本在折扣比较期间保持固定。不重新计算为折扣售价的 60%。每笔原始销售为每月固定成本和盈余贡献 100 加元 - 60 加元 = 40 加元。如果数量为 100 个，收入为 10,000 加元，可变成本为 6,000 加元，贡献为 4,000 加元。减去不变的 2,500 加元的固定运营成本，剩下 1,500 加元的每月运营盈余。这是在所有者转让和所得税之前，融资、设备支出和营运资金时间安排超出了这个简化模型。这种区别很重要，因为一美元的收入并不是可以在家花的一美元。首先需要为可变成本提供资金，并且仍然需要支付固定成本。降价 20% 使该示例的每单位贡献减半 输入的 20% 降价将售价从 CAD 100 降低到 CAD 80 。由于同一装置的成本仍为 60 加元，因此其贡献从 40 加元降至 20 加元。销售价格下降 20%，单位贡献减少 50%。选定的对比销量为 150 件，比之前增加了 50%。收入变为 12,000 加元，增加 20%。可变成本变为 9,000 加元，增加了 50%，因为它们遵循单位计数，成本不变为 60 加元。捐款只剩下 3,000 加元。同样2,500加元的固定成本后，营业盈余为500加元，比原来的1,500加元减少了1,000加元，降幅约为66.67%。第一个图表将收入和两个成本类别放在一起，以便较强的收入标题不会掩盖较弱的盈余。这两个单位计数是独立的场景输入。他们的比较并未估计降价 20% 会导致销量增加 50%。保持收入、盈亏平衡和保持盈余是三个不同的目标。以每单位 80 加元计算，保持原来的 10,000 加元收入需要 125 个单位。这些销售额产生 125 × 20 加元 = 2,500 加元的贡献，正好等于固定运营成本。营业盈余为零。因此125台也是该折扣案例的运营盈亏平衡点。它涵盖了模型成本，但不保留所有者原来的 1,500 加元盈余。为了在固定成本不变的情况下保持原始盈余，捐款必须保持为 4,000 加元。所需数量为 4,000 加元 ÷ 20 加元 = 200 单位。企业必须将原来的单位销售额增加一倍，而不是仅仅将销量增加 20% 或与原来的收入持平。更一般地，对于每折扣单位的正贡献，比较目标是原始单位 × 原始每单位贡献 ÷ 新每单位贡献。标题向上舍入为整个单位。分数计算的等式可能在曲线上有用，但整体销售计划必须满足或超过它。在将其视为家庭收入之前，请根据容量检查数量目标。单独输入的容量为每月 180 台。 200 台的目标超出了它。按 180 个单位和 20 加元折现缴款计算，运营盈余将为 180 × 20 加元 – 2,500 加元 = 1,100 加元，仍比原计划低 400 加元。选定的 150 台比较符合该容量，但符合容量并不能证明需求存在。相反，高于输入限制的情况被标记为在该容量假设下不可行的算术。扩大产能可能需要更多的人员、空间、设备或其他支出。这些变化将使固定成本和单位成本不变的假设失效。该模型不会自动添加它们，也不会假设可以在没有成本的情况下提高容量。因此，体积曲线和矩阵仍然是有条件的比较。超出输入容量的点或单元格不是销售预测。他们的作用是揭露所需变革的规模。协调盈余变化，无需对交互进行两次计算 瀑布从最初的 1,500 加元盈余开始。首先，对原来的 100 件产品降价 20 加元，可减少 2,000 加元。然后，额外的 50 个单位按照新的保证金贡献 50 × 20 加元 = 1,000 加元。终点是 500 加元。对这些额外单位使用旧的 40 加元贡献会夸大其收益。它们也以折扣价出售。桥的顺序将价格与数量的相互作用保留在用于交易量变化的新贡献内。不同的分解顺序可以将交互分配到不同的步骤，同时达到相同的最终剩余。该图表是对两个输入案例的精确会计解释，而不是一项操作引起特定客户响应的证据。更多单位无法修复每单位的非正贡献 在原始 100 加元价格和 60 加元可变成本的情况下，降价 40% 后，售价为 60 加元，贡献为零。这些销售中没有任何一笔能够产生 4,000 加元的原始捐款。固定成本仍造成 2,500 加元的运营亏损。大幅降价使售价低于不变的可变成本。每次额外的销售都会减少模拟的盈余。当原始贡献为正且贴现贡献为零或负时，该工具报告没有保留原始盈余的有限数量，而不是显示人为的巨大目标。由于原始销售额为零，因此无需保留原始贡献；零比较单位符合该基线。此外，保留原来的负盈余并不能使企业盈利。这些边界情况是保持目标定义可见的原因。将支持的现金金额纳入家庭计划 在依靠促销来支持个人支出之前，请检查同期的实际价格、单位成本、固定成本、实际需求和运营能力。将随数量变化的成本与仅在相关范围内保持固定的成本分开。该工具不包括销售税、所得税、债务支付、新设备、额外人员配备、库存时间和未付客户发票。即使其正营业盈余也不会自动成为税后家庭收入或可供所有者提取的现金。相关业务现金指南遵循库存、应收账款和提款；承包商指南着眼于计费容量。总之，这些问题有助于防止在检查必要的成本、现金日期和限制之前，销售目标成为个人收入假设。

d6a12a83e53e5862a1fa71e2d21991370e1a6cfb.src: Match the service period before comparing costs. An annual equivalent can standardize a repeated-cycle calculation, while purchase dates still require their own cash. Define the service being compared before annualizing the price A less expensive durable item may need replacement sooner, while a higher-priced alternative may provide more service years. Comparing only their initial prices leaves the service period unresolved. This example gives both options the same required function continuously. Option A costs CAD 1,200 at each cycle's start, lasts four complete service years and has CAD 80 of running cost at every year-end. Option B costs CAD 2,000, lasts eight years and has CAD 50 of annual running cost. The lives are deterministic scenario assumptions, not warranties, observed averages or probabilities of survival. Quality, capacity, convenience and reliability are assumed equivalent solely to isolate the cost arithmetic. ACCA's equivalent-annual-cost explanation provides the general valuation method. The calculator uses its own amounts and complete transaction schedule, without reproducing the source's machine examples or prescribing a household discount rate. Value each complete service cycle with its own dates The purchase price is paid immediately. Running cost is paid after each full year of use, including the final service year. It represents the year just completed, rather than an optional overhaul performed after the item is discarded. At the independently entered 4% effective annual discount assumption, the four-year annuity factor is the sum of the discount factors for year-ends one through four. Option A's one-cycle present cost is its CAD 1,200 price plus the present value of four CAD 80 running-cost payments, approximately CAD 1,490.39. Option B uses its own eight-year factor. Its CAD 2,000 price plus eight discounted CAD 50 payments gives approximately CAD 2,336.64. Those two present costs cover different lengths of service and cannot answer the equal-service comparison by themselves. Both cycles end with zero salvage value in this illustration. There is no resale receipt, tax depreciation, grant or borrowing fee. A real item with a different residual value or cost pattern would need the corresponding dated cash flow. Convert present cost into a level year-end annual equivalent An annuity factor converts a constant year-end annual amount into present value. Dividing one cycle's present cost by its own factor reverses that calculation and produces an equivalent annual cost. The default annual equivalents are approximately CAD 410.59 for A and CAD 347.06 for B. They compare the cost of one year of the defined equal service under the selected valuation and repetition assumptions. The difference does not mean a seller accepts an annual payment of CAD 347.06 for B. The actual CAD 2,000 purchase is still due immediately. The annual equivalent is a valuation transformation, not a financing installment, accounting depreciation charge or required contribution to a replacement fund. At zero discount, the formula simplifies to purchase price divided by service years plus annual running cost. With a positive discount assumption, simply dividing the present cost by the number of years would not preserve the present value of a year-end payment stream. Recheck the result over a common complete service horizon The default common horizon is eight years. A completes two four-year cycles, while B completes one eight-year cycle. A is purchased at time zero and again at year four. B is purchased once at time zero. Both pay running cost for every completed service year through year eight. At year four, A's running cost for the completed year and its replacement purchase share the same transaction date. At year eight, running costs still apply, but neither option buys a replacement for service beyond the comparison window. The present cost over those same eight years is approximately CAD 2,764.38 for A and CAD 2,336.64 for B. Each equals its annual-equivalent cost multiplied by the eight-year annuity factor. This independent repeated-calendar calculation checks that the annualized comparison covers equal service. When the two selected lives do not divide each other, the tool uses their least common multiple. For example, seven- and eight-year lives create a fifty-six-year comparison. That is a conditional arithmetic device, not a forecast that identical items and unchanged prices will actually be available for fifty-six years. Keep the lumpy cash schedule beside the annual equivalent The cumulative cash chart preserves the purchase and year-end payment dates. It is undiscounted. At the default eight-year endpoint, A has paid CAD 3,040 and B CAD 2,400, while their time-zero present costs are lower because later outflows are discounted. B still needs CAD 800 more at the initial purchase date. A lower annual-equivalent cost or lower long-horizon present cost does not supply that extra opening cash or establish that the purchase is affordable. The chart includes no income, bank balance or financing. A separate funding calendar would need the household's resources, payment obligations and any actual credit terms. It would also need to confirm when future replacement money becomes accessible. A shorter intended ownership period can change the comparison. If the service ends before the item finishes its life, the remaining value, disposal proceeds and whether replacement is needed must be specified. The repeated complete-cycle result should not silently substitute for that limited-horizon question. Test the price and life assumptions that drive the apparent saving The matrix varies B's price and service life while retaining B's annual running cost, the discount assumption and all of A's selected terms. Every cell reports B's annual equivalent minus A's. A negative value is a lower modeled annual cost for B; it does not guarantee service quality or available cash. Shortening B's assumed life can reverse a comparison that initially favored it. So can changing its price or running cost. A lifespan claim deserves evidence rather than being chosen to justify an already preferred purchase. The model repeats identical cycles at constant nominal prices and running costs. It has no inflation, technological change, downtime or uncertain failure. Costs and the discount assumption share that stated nominal basis; the calculator does not mix inflation-linked bills with a real rate. Use the annual equivalent to understand the conditional cost comparison, then restore the details that matter to the actual decision: required service, supported life range, all cash costs, residual value, intended horizon and funding dates. The four charts keep equal-service valuation and the real shape of payments visible together.
d6a12a83e53e5862a1fa71e2d21991370e1a6cfb.zh: 在比较成本之前先匹配服务期限。年度当量可以标准化重复周期计算，而购买日期仍然需要自己的现金。在按年计算价格之前定义要比较的服务 较便宜的耐用物品可能需要更快更换，而价格较高的替代品可能会提供更长的服务年限。仅比较它们的初始价格就无法确定服务期限。此示例连续为两个选项提供了相同的所需功能。选项 A 在每个周期开始时的成本为 1,200 加元，持续四个完整服务年，每年年底的运行成本为 80 加元。选项 B 的成本为 2,000 加元，持续八年，每年运行成本为 50 加元。寿命是确定性的情景假设，而不是保证、观察到的平均值或生存概率。质量、容量、便利性和可靠性被假定为等同，只是为了隔离成本算术。 ACCA的等值年成本解释提供了一般评估方法。该计算器使用自己的金额和完整的交易时间表，无需复制来源的机器示例或规定家庭折扣率。重视每个完整的服务周期及其自己的日期 购买价格立即支付。运行成本在每个完整使用年（包括最后服务年）后支付。它代表刚刚完成的年份，而不是在该项目被丢弃后执行的可选检修。在独立输入的 4% 有效年度折扣假设下，四年年金系数是第一年末到第四年末的折扣系数之和。选项 A 的一个周期当前成本是其 1,200 加元的价格加上四笔 80 加元运行成本付款的现值，大约为 1,490.39 加元。选项 B 使用自己的八年因子。其 2,000 加元的价格加上八次 50 加元的折扣付款，价格约为 2,336.64 加元。这两项现有成本涵盖了不同的服务年限，它们本身无法回答同等服务比较的问题。在此图中，两个周期均以零残值结束。没有转售收据、税收折旧、赠款或借款费用。具有不同残值或成本模式的实际项目将需要相应的日期现金流量。将当前成本转换为年末年等值水平 年金因子将年末不变的年金额转换为现值。将一个周期的当前成本除以它自己的系数可以颠倒该计算并产生等效的年度成本。 A 的默认年度等值约为 410.59 加元，B 的默认年度等值约为 347.06 加元。他们比较了在选定的评估和重复假设下定义的同等服务一年的成本。差异并不意味着卖方接受每年为 B 支付 347.06 加元。实际购买的 2,000 加元仍需立即支付。年度等价物是估值转换，而不是融资分期付款、会计折旧费用或所需的重置基金捐款。在零折扣下，公式简化为购买价格除以服务年限加上年度运行成本。在正折扣假设下，简单地将当前成本除以年数并不能保留年终付款流的现值。在公共完整服务期限内重新检查结果 默认公共期限为八年。 A完成两个四年周期，而B完成一个八年周期。 A 在零时购买，并在第四年再次购买。 B 在零时间购买一次。两者都为从第八年完成的每项服务支付运行费用。在第四年，A 全年的运行成本与其替换购买共享相同的交易日期。在第八年，运行成本仍然适用，但两种选择都不会在比较窗口之外购买服务的替代品。在这八年中，A 的当前成本约为 2,764.38 加元，B 的成本约为 2,336.64 加元。每项都等于其年度等效成本乘以八年年金系数。这种独立的重复日历计算检查年度比较是否涵盖同等服务。当两个选定的生命不互相分割时，该工具将使用它们的最小公倍数。例如，七年和八年的生命形成了五十六年的比较。这是一个条件算术装置，而不是预测相同的商品和不变的价格实际上将在五十六年内可用。将块状现金表保留在年度等值额旁边。累积现金表保留购买日期和年末付款日期。这是不打折的。在默认的八年终点，A 支付了 3,040 加元，B 支付了 2,400 加元，而他们的零时当前成本较低，因为后来的流出已打折。 B 在最初购买日还需要 800 加元。较低的年度等效成本或较低的长期当前成本并不能提供额外的期初现金或证明购买是可以承受的。该图表不包括收入、银行余额或融资。单独的融资日历需要家庭的资源、付款义务和任何实际的信贷条件。它还需要确认未来何时可以获得替代资金。较短的预期所有权期限可能会改变比较。如果服务在物品寿命结束之前结束，则必须指定剩余价值、处置收益以及是否需要更换。重复的完整周期结果不应默默地取代有限视野问题。测试推动明显节省的价格和寿命假设 该矩阵改变 B 的价格和使用寿命，同时保留 B 的年度运行成本、折扣假设和 A 的所有选定条款。每个单元报告 B 的年度当量减去 A 的年度当量。负值表示 B 的年建模成本较低；它不保证服务质量或可用现金。缩短 B 的假定寿命可以扭转最初对它有利的比较。改变其价格或运行成本也是如此。寿命声明应该有证据，而不是被选择来证明已经首选的购买的合理性。该模型以恒定的名义价格和运行成本重复相同的周期。它没有通货膨胀、技术变革、停机或不确定的故障。成本和折扣假设份额表明名义基础；该计算器不会将与通货膨胀相关的账单与实际利率混合在一起。使用年度当量来了解条件成本比较，然后恢复对实际决策重要的细节：所需的服务、支持的寿命范围、所有现金成本、残值、预期期限和融资日期。这四个图表将同等服务估值和支付的真实形式放在一起。
