1a7c2c3b960fbf84cdf3e671312bff5f2394ad2a.src: Read the period and seasonal-adjustment label first. A repeated monthly rate is a scenario; the total of a year’s changing bills also needs their dates. Put the comparison window beside every percentage Statistics Canada’s September 2026 CPI release , published on 19 October, reports a 3.1% year-over-year increase, a 0.1% unadjusted month-over-month increase and a 0.4% seasonally adjusted monthly increase. The year-over-year figure compares September 2026 with September 2025. The monthly figures compare September with August 2026, using two different time-series treatments. These are three descriptions with labels, not three inflation components that can be added. The first two charts keep those definitions visible. The second chart uses the published one-decimal percentages directly. Its common percentage unit does not make the three comparison periods interchangeable. Read the index level separately from a dollar bill The retained Bank of Canada table of Statistics Canada CPI series shows an unadjusted all-items index of 164.9 in September 2025, 169.8 in August 2026 and 170.0 in September 2026. The reference base is 2002=100. An index value of 170.0 is not a CAD 170 bill. It is a relative price-level measure. A household spending amount requires an independently defined basket, quantities and starting cost; the last two charts use a deliberately separate authored example. The history chart places the unadjusted and seasonally adjusted series on a common index scale and explicitly focuses the vertical axis on 160 to 172. This makes their modest differences easier to inspect, while the labelled range prevents a small movement from being mistaken for a change from zero. The accessible table retains each actual reference month. The source dates formatted as the first day of a month identify monthly periods, rather than a claim that all prices were observed on that day. Preserve seasonal adjustment and the source vintage Statistics Canada’s CPI FAQ explains that seasonal adjustment removes recurring seasonal and calendar influences to support interpretation of underlying movements. It also states that seasonally adjusted data are revised monthly. The retained snapshot flags the August 2026 adjusted index of 169.4 as revised. The first chart’s table preserves that R label. A connected historical curve should not erase it or combine an earlier release’s adjusted rate with a newly revised index. Precision matters as well. Dividing the displayed September unadjusted level of 170.0 by August’s 169.8, then subtracting one, gives approximately 0.1178%. The published monthly headline is 0.1%. The former is a calculation from rounded displayed indices; it is not a recovered unrounded official estimate. Similarly, 170.0 divided by the adjusted August level of 169.4 implies about 0.3542% from those displayed levels. Treat its extra decimal places as arithmetic precision, not additional precision supplied by the publisher. Annualizing a monthly rate requires a repeated-rate assumption The independent example assumes a price change of 0.4% in every future month. Repeating that factor twelve times produces (1.004) 12 minus one, or approximately 4.91% over twelve months. That conditional 4.91% is not the observed 3.1% year-over-year CPI change. One describes a hypothetical future path with twelve identical monthly factors; the other describes a published comparison between two past reference months. It is also not simply twelve times 0.4%. Multiplying by twelve gives a 4.8% linear shortcut, while compounding includes changes on prior price changes. The distinction grows when the selected monthly change is larger. Changing the hypothetical input to zero holds future basket costs flat; selecting a negative rate produces a declining path. None of those edits changes the official historical indices or published percentages. The tool supplies no likelihood that a chosen path will occur. A changing monthly price needs twelve separate bill amounts The original cash example starts with a CAD 3,000 reference-month basket cost and holds its quantities fixed. Month zero is that reference cost. The first assumed 0.4% price change occurs before the first future bill, making month one CAD 3,012. At the same assumed monthly rate, month twelve costs approximately CAD 3,147.21. The sum of all twelve future monthly bills is approximately CAD 36,949.87. The final waterfall reconciles CAD 36,000 of unchanged reference-cost bills plus CAD 949.87 from the intervening price path. The CAD 949.87 increment is about 2.64% of the CAD 36,000 reference-year total, while month twelve’s price is about 4.91% above the reference price. Those percentages use different denominators and timing. The spending increase builds gradually across the twelve bills; the final-price comparison measures only the endpoint. A single annual bill would need its own payment date. A price change before that bill could affect the whole payment, while a change after payment would not retroactively increase it. This illustration assumes monthly bills throughout and should be rebuilt if the actual contract has a different calendar. Multiplying the final month’s CAD 3,147.21 by twelve would charge that higher price for every month. It does not reproduce the total of the twelve gradually changing bills. Adding month zero as another payment would introduce a thirteenth bill. These are spending requirements for an invented basket, not a forecast of a particular household’s cost of living. Income, saving returns, changing quantities, taxes and other bills are outside the illustration. Statistics Canada also distinguishes the CPI’s price-index concept from a full cost-of-living measure. For a budget review, identify the bill’s present cost, its possible change dates and the quantities that can actually vary. Use the official rates as dated economic context, then keep those independently supported household assumptions beside the payment calendar.
1a7c2c3b960fbf84cdf3e671312bff5f2394ad2a.zh: 首先阅读期间和季节性调整标签。重复的月费率是一种情况；一年中变化的账单总数也需要它们的日期。将比较窗口放在每个百分比旁边 加拿大统计局 10 月 19 日发布的 2026 年 9 月 CPI 报告显示，同比增长 3.1%，未经调整的环比增长 0.1%，经季节性调整后的月度增长 0.4%。同比数据比较了 2026 年 9 月和 2025 年 9 月。月度数据比较了 9 月和 2026 年 8 月，使用两种不同的时间序列处理。这是带有标签的三个描述，而不是可以添加的三个充气组件。前两个图表使这些定义可见。第二个图表直接使用已发布的一位小数百分比。其共同的百分比单位并不使得三个比较期可以互换。将指数水平与美元钞票分开阅读加拿大央行保留的加拿大统计局CPI系列表显示，2025年9月未经调整的所有项目指数为164.9，2026年8月为169.8，2026年9月为170.0。参考基数为2002年=100。指数值 170.0 不是 170 加元的钞票。它是一个相对价格水平的衡量标准。家庭支出金额需要独立定义的篮子、数量和起始成本；最后两个图表使用了一个故意单独编写的示例。历史图表将未经调整和季节性调整的序列放在共同的指数刻度上，并明确地将垂直轴集中在 160 到 172 上。这使得它们的适度差异更容易检查，而标记的范围可以防止小幅变动被误认为是从零开始的变化。可访问的表格保留每个实际参考月份。格式为每月第一天的源日期标识每月周期，而不是声称所有价格均在当天观察到。保留季节性调整和来源年份加拿大统计局的消费者物价指数常见问题解答解释说，季节性调整消除了反复出现的季节性和日历影响，以支持对潜在变动的解释。它还指出，季节性调整后的数据每月都会进行修订。保留的快照标记了 2026 年 8 月调整后的指数 169.4。第一个图表的表格保留了 R 标签。连接的历史曲线不应将其删除或将早期版本的调整后的汇率与新修订的指数相结合。精度也很重要。将显示的 9 月份未调整水平 170.0 除以 8 月份的 169.8，然后减去 1，得出大约 0.1178%。公布的月度标题为0.1%。前者是根据四舍五入显示的指数计算得出的；这不是恢复后的未经四舍五入的官方估计。同样，170.0 除以调整后的 8 月水平 169.4 意味着与所显示的水平相比约为 0.3542%。将其额外的小数位视为算术精度，而不是发布者提供的额外精度。将月度利率年化需要重复利率假设。独立示例假设未来每个月的价格变化为 0.4%。重复该因子 12 次，得到 (1.004) 12 减 1，或者在 12 个月内大约为 4.91%。这个有条件的 4.91% 并不是观察到的 3.1% 的 CPI 同比变化。其中一个描述了一条假设的未来路径，其中包含十二个相同的每月因素；另一个描述了过去两个参考月份之间已发布的比较。它也不仅仅是 0.4% 的 12 倍。乘以 12 得到 4.8% 的线性捷径，而复利则包括之前价格变化的变化。当所选的每月变化较大时，差异就会增大。将假设投入更改为零可以使未来的篮子成本保持不变；选择负利率会产生下降路径。这些编辑都不会改变官方历史指数或公布的百分比。该工具不提供所选路径发生的可能性。变化的每月价格需要 12 个单独的账单金额 原始现金示例以 3,000 加元的参考月篮子成本开始，并保持其数量固定。零月份是参考成本。第一个假定的 0.4% 价格变化发生在第一个未来账单之前，即第一个月为 3,012 加元。按照相同的假设月费率，第 12 个月的费用约为 3,147.21 加元。未来所有十二个月度账单的总和约为 36,949.87 加元。最终瀑布调节 36,000 加元不变的参考成本账单加上干预价格路径中的 949.87 加元。 949.87加元的增量约为参考年总额36,000加元的2.64%，而第12个月的价格比参考价格高出约4.91%。这些百分比使用不同的分母和时间。十二项法案的支出逐渐增加；最终价格比较仅衡量终点。单一年度账单需要有自己的付款日期。该账单之前的价格变化可能会影响整个付款，而付款之后的价格变化不会追溯增加它。此图假设自始至终都是每月账单，如果实际合同有不同的日历，则应重新构建。将最后一个月的 3,147.21 加元乘以 12，每个月都会收取更高的价格。它没有再现十二个逐渐变化的法案的总数。添加零月份作为另一笔付款将引入第十三项法案。这些是发明的篮子的支出要求，而不是对特定家庭生活成本的预测。收入、储蓄回报、变化数量、税收和其他账单不在插图中。加拿大统计局还将 CPI 的价格指数概念与全面的生活成本衡量标准区分开来。对于预算审查，请确定账单的当前成本、可能的更改日期以及实际可能变化的数量。使用官方利率作为过时的经济背景，然后将那些独立支持的家庭假设保留在付款日历旁边。

eac69d96cc370cc8aa9ef7caf0223033c6d13997.src: A household-size adjustment changes the unit used for an income comparison. The household’s cash budget still needs its actual receipts, costs and number of people. Identify the statistical unit and the adjustment being made An income figure can describe an individual, a family or everyone sharing a private household. It can also be adjusted for household size. Those distinctions change what a comparison means before any personal budget is built. Statistics Canada’s private-household standard defines adjusted after-tax income as household after-tax income divided by the square root of household size. The method recognises that people living together can share resources and that additional members need not increase costs in direct proportion to their number. This article illustrates that documented method. The word “adjusted” can mean something else in another series, including an adjustment for prices or for public services received in kind. Read the definition attached to the particular table rather than transferring one meaning to every income statistic. Calculate the three amounts without turning them into separate income streams The default household has four people and CAD 72,000 of annual after-tax income for the statistical illustration. Its unadjusted income remains CAD 72,000. The square root of four is two. Dividing CAD 72,000 by two gives an adjusted comparison amount of CAD 36,000. Dividing the same income by all four people instead gives CAD 18,000 per person. These are three descriptions of one entered income amount. The household has not received CAD 72,000 plus CAD 36,000 plus CAD 18,000. The adjustment also does not mean its bank deposits fall to CAD 36,000 or that every person receives CAD 18,000. Understand what the square-root scale does and leaves out For a one-person household, both denominators equal one. At four people, the square-root adjustment divides by two while a per-person calculation divides by four. The curve shows this difference while keeping annual income fixed. A comparison scale can represent shared resources without pricing the actual rooms, meals, transport or care a household needs. It does not record individual access to money or establish that every member benefits equally. Households of the same size can have different costs because of ages, disability needs, location, housing and other circumstances. An identical adjusted-income amount therefore does not establish identical cash needs or a particular standard of living for two specific households. Build a separate budget from independently entered monthly cash The cash example starts with CAD 6,000 a month assumed available after deductions. This is entered separately from the annual statistical income. The tool does not automatically treat the annual amount divided by twelve as a bank-deposit forecast. The illustrative monthly costs are CAD 2,200 shared across the household plus CAD 600 for each of four people. The per-person costs total CAD 2,400, so the remaining cash is CAD 6,000 less CAD 2,200 less CAD 2,400: CAD 1,400. This fixed-plus-per-person cost rule is an independent teaching assumption. It is not derived from the square-root scale or presented as an observed spending estimate. The remaining amount is after only the listed costs; other expenses and saving commitments still need their own entries. Change one kind of input and observe which charts should move Increasing the annual statistical-income input changes the comparison bars and income curves. It does not create new monthly cash in the independent budget. Changing the cash-cost inputs moves the budget figures without changing the statistical adjustment. Changing household size affects both exercises for different reasons. It changes the denominator of the income measures, while also changing the number of per-person cost amounts in the cash scenario. The tool keeps those calculations distinct. The matrix varies household size and the additional cost per person while retaining monthly cash and shared costs. It reveals possible monthly gaps under those assumptions. It does not estimate poverty status, classify the household into an income group or measure the probability of meeting its needs. Bring the comparison back to the household’s actual decisions When reading an income headline, record its population, year, household or family unit, price basis and size adjustment. A relevant benchmark can provide context without becoming a target salary or a forecast of cash receipts. For planning, record the money actually available, the bills due, who shares each cost and the resources accessible to each person. A fair cost-sharing rule and a workable payment calendar require more information than an equivalized income figure supplies. The first pair of charts explains a statistical measure. The second pair shows how a deliberately simple cash model answers a different household question. Use both with their stated units and assumptions.
eac69d96cc370cc8aa9ef7caf0223033c6d13997.zh: 家庭规模调整会改变用于收入比较的单位。家庭的现金预算仍然需要其实际收入、成本和人数。确定统计单位和正在进行的调整 收入数字可以描述个人、家庭或共享私人家庭的每个人。它还可以根据家庭规模进行调整。这些区别改变了在制定任何个人预算之前进行比较的含义。加拿大统计局的私人家庭标准将调整后的税后收入定义为家庭税后收入除以家庭规模的平方根。该方法认识到生活在一起的人们可以共享资源，并且额外的成员不需要与其人数成正比地增加成本。本文说明了该记录方法。 “调整”一词在另一个系列中可能有其他含义，包括对价格或实物公共服务的调整。阅读特定表格所附的定义，而不是将一种含义转移到每一项收入统计数据上。计算这三项金额，而不将其转化为单独的收入流 默认家庭有四口人，年税后收入为 72,000 加元，用于统计说明。其未经调整的收入仍为 72,000 加元。四的平方根是二。将 72,000 加元除以二即可得到调整后的比较金额 36,000 加元。将相同的收入分摊给所有四个人，每人可得到 18,000 加元。这是对一项输入的收入金额的三种描述。该家庭尚未收到 72,000 加元加 36,000 加元加 18,000 加元。此次调整也不意味着其银行存款降至36,000加元或每人收到18,000加元。了解平方根标度的作用和遗漏 对于一个单人家庭，两个分母都等于 1。如果是四人，则平方根调整除以二，而每人计算则除以四。该曲线显示了在保持年收入固定的情况下的这种差异。比较量表可以代表共享资源，而无需对家庭实际需要的房间、膳食、交通或护理进行定价。它不记录个人获得资金的情况，也不规定每个成员平等受益。由于年龄、残疾需求、地点、住房和其他情况，相同规模的家庭可能有不同的费用。因此，相同的调整收入金额并不能为两个特定家庭确定相同的现金需求或特定的生活水平。根据独立输入的每月现金制定单独的预算 现金示例以每月 6,000 加元开始，假设扣除后可用。这是与年度统计收入分开输入的。该工具不会自动将年度金额除以十二作为银行存款预测。示例性的每月费用为家庭分担 2,200 加元，加上四人每人 600 加元。每人总共花费2,400加元，所以剩下的现金是6,000加元减去2,200加元减去2,400加元：1,400加元。这种固定加每人成本的规则是一个独立的教学假设。它不是从平方根尺度得出的，也不是以观察到的支出估算的形式呈现的。剩余金额仅扣除列出的费用；其他费用和储蓄承诺仍然需要单独的条目。改变一种输入并观察哪些图表应该移动 增加年度统计收入输入会改变比较条和收入曲线。它不会在独立预算中创造新的每月现金。改变现金成本投入会改变预算数字，但不会改变统计调整。家庭规模的变化会出于不同的原因影响这两项活动。它改变了收入衡量标准的分母，同时也改变了现金情景中人均成本金额的数量。该工具使这些计算保持清晰。该矩阵会改变家庭规模和每人的额外成本，同时保留每月现金和分摊成本。它揭示了这些假设下可能存在的月度差距。它不估计贫困状况、将家庭划分为收入组或衡量满足其需求的可能性。将比较带回家庭的实际决策 在阅读收入标题时，记录其人口、年份、家庭或家庭单位、价格基础和规模调整。相关基准可以提供背景信息，而不会成为目标工资或现金收入预测。为了进行规划，记录实际可用的资金、应付的账单、谁分担每项成本以及每个人可以使用的资源。公平的成本分摊规则和可行的付款日历需要比等值收入数字提供的更多信息。第一对图表解释了统计测量。第二对展示了故意简单的现金模型如何回答不同的家庭问题。将两者与其规定的单位和假设一起使用。

c65c2bd1e949928346c6c2ebd78c4bd5721ec831.src: Read what the percentage multiplies. A deductible based on declared insured value can be much larger than the same percentage of a repair bill, and it can change when that declared base changes. The percentage alone does not identify the cash amount A percentage deductible is incomplete without its base. Two descriptions can both contain “2%” and still assign very different amounts of an accepted loss to the household. The U.S. National Association of Insurance Commissioners’ hurricane-deductible explainer describes percentage deductibles that use a home’s insured value. It also explains that the applicable triggers depend on the contract and jurisdiction. That source supplies a concrete reason to inspect the base; it does not establish a Canadian rule or determine which deductible applies to a particular loss. This article uses an original teaching contract stated in CAD. Its declared insured-value basis is CAD 600,000 and its deductible is 2% of that basis. A single CAD 40,000 damage amount has already been accepted as covered. The charts assume the rule applies and focus on the arithmetic after that assumption. The tool does not decide coverage, value a building or reproduce a real storm policy. All permitted damage inputs are no greater than the minimum declared basis, so a separate policy-limit shortfall does not enter this particular calculation. Calculate the threshold before comparing it with the damage The deductible threshold in the teaching contract is CAD 600,000 × 2% = CAD 12,000 . It is not CAD 40,000 × 2%. Under the stated single-loss formula, the household bears the smaller of the accepted damage and that threshold. For the selected CAD 40,000 damage, the household share is therefore CAD 12,000 and the insurer share is CAD 28,000 . The two amounts add to the same CAD 40,000 accepted loss. Although the contract label contains 2%, the household’s share is 12,000 ÷ 40,000, or 30% of this selected loss . The 2% and 30% describe different relationships: the threshold as a share of insured value, and the household portion as a share of damage. Neither percentage can replace the other. The insured-value basis is an entered contract amount. The tool does not equate it with a property’s sale price, mortgage balance, original purchase price or a recommended reconstruction estimate. Use alternative formulas to expose the difference in bases The first chart compares three separate teaching rules for the same CAD 40,000 damage. The entered insured-value rule assigns CAD 12,000 to the household. A different rule charging 2% of the damage would assign CAD 800 . A separate CAD 2,000 flat-dollar threshold would assign CAD 2,000 . The corresponding insurer portions are CAD 28,000, CAD 39,200 and CAD 38,000. Each stacked bar totals the same accepted damage. What changes is the division of that loss, not the amount of damage. These countercases are not three options a claimant can select after an event. Nor are they quotes with identical premiums, coverage and eligibility. Their purpose is to show why the written basis must be understood before using the percentage in a cash plan. Actual contracts may have minimum amounts, different triggers, per-occurrence rules, annual aggregates or other adjustments. None is inferred from the three rows, and no premium comparison or policy recommendation follows from them. A threshold is not an extra bill when the loss is smaller Change the accepted damage to CAD 5,000 while leaving the CAD 12,000 threshold unchanged. In this formula, the household bears CAD 5,000 and the insurer portion is zero. The calculation does not make the household pay CAD 12,000 on top of that repair. The loss curve therefore rises with damage until it reaches CAD 12,000, then levels off at that threshold within the simplified covered-loss range. At zero damage both portions are zero. With a zero deductible percentage, the household share is zero throughout this assumed covered-loss formula. The curve also includes the loss-based countercase, whose household share grows at 2% of damage instead. That line answers a different contract question. The contrast makes the difference in bases visible over a range of losses, not only at one example amount. The plateau does not promise that a real policy caps every household cost at the deductible. Exclusions, sublimits, uninsured amounts, depreciation and other claim adjustments can change the result. This tool deliberately models none of them. Fund the household portion, and keep reimbursement timing as a separate question The default assigned cash reserve is CAD 8,000. Against the selected CAD 12,000 household portion, the additional funding requirement is CAD 4,000 . The reserve bridge shows CAD 12,000 less CAD 8,000, rather than subtracting the reserve from the entire CAD 40,000 loss and calling that a deductible gap. If assigned cash exceeds the household portion, the model uses only the amount needed and leaves the rest available. Its additional funding gap is floored at zero. With CAD 5,000 of damage and the original CAD 8,000 reserve, there is no extra final-share funding gap and CAD 3,000 of assigned cash remains unused. This is a final loss-sharing calculation, not a settlement calendar. A contractor’s invoice may come before an insurer’s payment. Funding that temporary timing difference needs a separate cash bridge, even when the eventual household portion is fully covered by an existing reserve. The related reimbursement guide examines that timing issue. The related fixed-deductible guide considers premium and reserve trade-offs, while the rebuilding guide addresses coverage limits. Those are distinct from identifying the base of this percentage. An unchanged percentage can still produce a different dollar threshold Increase the declared basis from CAD 600,000 to CAD 800,000, holding the 2% rate and CAD 40,000 accepted damage fixed. The threshold rises from CAD 12,000 to CAD 16,000 . With the same CAD 8,000 assigned reserve, the additional funding requirement rises from CAD 4,000 to CAD 8,000 . The matrix varies the percentage and declared basis while retaining the selected damage and reserve. Larger thresholds increase the household portion only until that portion reaches the accepted damage amount. At that point, an even larger threshold does not create more damage under the stated formula. The grid contains alternative arithmetic cases without probability weights. It does not suggest lowering a building’s insurance amount to reduce a deductible. Choosing an appropriate insured value and checking the full coverage terms requires a different assessment. Record the complete rule beside the amount reserved A useful planning record includes the applicable event, the base the percentage multiplies, the percentage itself, any dollar minimum or other adjustment, and whether the rule applies per event or on another basis. Then translate the supported rule into a dollar amount before comparing it with available cash. The NAIC page reviewed for this article was last updated on 2 June 2025. Its U.S. context is used only to explain why insured-value percentage deductibles need careful reading. The article applies no state trigger, statutory threshold or Canadian policy condition. The chart inputs are transparent assumptions. For an actual household, the policy wording and confirmed claim treatment control the calculation. The practical lesson is to preserve the denominator and the settlement assumptions, rather than placing an unexplained percentage in the budget.
c65c2bd1e949928346c6c2ebd78c4bd5721ec831.zh: 读出百分比的乘数。基于申报保险价值的免赔额可能远大于维修费用的相同百分比，并且当申报的基础发生变化时，免赔额可能会发生变化。百分比本身并不能确定现金金额 如果没有其基础，免赔额百分比是不完整的。两种描述都可以包含“2%”，但仍然为家庭分配非常不同的可接受损失金额。美国全国保险专员协会的飓风免赔额解释器描述了使用房屋保险价值的百分比免赔额。它还解释了适用的触发因素取决于合同和司法管辖区。该消息来源提供了检查该基地的具体理由；它没有制定加拿大规则或确定哪种免赔额适用于特定损失。本文使用以 CAD 表述的原始教学合同。其申报的保险价值基础为 600,000 加元，免赔额为该基础的 2%。单个 40,000 加元的损坏金额已被接受为承保范围。这些图表假设规则适用，并重点关注该假设后的算术。该工具不会决定覆盖范围、评估建筑物或重现真实的风暴政策。所有允许的损失输入均不大于声明的最低基础，因此单独的保单限额缺口不会进入此特定计算。计算阈值，然后与损害进行比较 教学合同中的免赔额阈值为 600,000 加元 × 2% = 12,000 加元。不是 40,000 加元 × 2%。根据规定的单一损失公式，家庭承担可接受的损失和阈值中的较小者。对于选定的 40,000 加元损失，家庭分担额为 12,000 加元，保险公司分担额为 28,000 加元。这两笔金额加起来同样是 40,000 加元的可接受损失。虽然合同标明包含2%，但家庭的份额是12,000 ÷ 40,000，即这个选定损失的30%。 2% 和 30% 描述了不同的关系：阈值作为保险价值的份额，家庭部分作为损失的份额。任何一个百分比都不能取代另一个百分比。保险价值的基础是签订的合同金额。该工具并不将其等同于房产的销售价格、抵押贷款余额、原始购买价格或建议的重建估算。使用替代公式揭示基础差异 第一个图表比较了相同 40,000 CAD 伤害的三个单独的教学规则。输入的保险价值规则将 12,000 加元分配给该家庭。另一种按损害赔偿 2% 的规则将分配 800 加元。单独的 2,000 加元固定美元阈值将分配 2,000 加元。相应的保险公司部分为 28,000 加元、39,200 加元和 38,000 加元。每个堆叠的条的总伤害相同。改变的是损失的分配，而不是损害的数额。这些反案例不是索赔人在事件发生后可以选择的三个选项。它们的报价也不具有相同的保费、承保范围和资格。它们的目的是说明为什么在现金计划中使用百分比之前必须理解书面基础。实际合同可能有最低金额、不同的触发器、每次发生的规则、年度总计或其他调整。从这三行中没有推断出任何内容，也没有从中得出保费比较或政策建议。当损失较小时，阈值不是额外费用 将可接受的损坏更改为 5,000 加元，同时保持 12,000 加元阈值不变。在此公式中，家庭承担 5,000 加元，保险公司部分为零。根据计算，该家庭除修理费用外，并未支付 12,000 加元。因此，损失曲线随着损坏而上升，直到达到 12,000 加元，然后在简化的承保损失范围内的该阈值处趋于平稳。在零损坏时，两个部分都为零。由于免赔额百分比为零，因此在整个假设的承保损失公式中，家庭份额为零。该曲线还包括基于损失的反案例，其家庭份额反而以损失的 2% 增长。该行回答了另一个合同问题。这种对比使得碱基的差异在一系列损失中可见，而不仅仅是在一个示例量上。稳定状态并不能保证真正的政策能够将每个家庭的费用限制在免赔额上。除外责任、次级限额、未投保金额、折旧和其他索赔调整可能会改变结果。该工具故意不对其中任何一个进行建模。为家庭部分提供资金，并将报销时间作为单独的问题。默认分配的现金储备为 8,000 加元。对于选定的 12,000 加元家庭部分，额外资金要求为 4,000 加元。准备金桥梁显示 12,000 加元减去 8,000 加元，而不是从整个 40,000 加元损失中减去准备金，并将其称为可扣除缺口。如果分配的现金超过家庭部分，该模型将仅使用所需的金额，其余部分可用。其额外资金缺口为零。由于损失为 5,000 加元，原始储备金为 8,000 加元，因此不存在额外的最终份额资金缺口，分配的现金 3,000 加元仍未使用。这是最终的损失分摊计算，而不是结算日历。承包商的发票可能先于保险公司付款。即使最终的家庭部分完全由现有储备金覆盖，为临时时间差异提供资金也需要单独的现金桥梁。相关的报销指南研究了这个时间问题。相关的固定免赔额指南考虑了保费和准备金的权衡，而重建指南则解决了承保范围限制。这些与确定该百分比的基础不同。百分比不变仍会产生不同的美元门槛 将申报基础从 600,000 加元增加到 800,000 加元，保持 2% 的税率和 40,000 加元的可接受损害固定。门槛从 12,000 加元提高到 16,000 加元。在分配储备金相同的 8,000 加元的情况下，额外资金需求从 4,000 加元增加到 8,000 加元。该矩阵改变了百分比和声明的基础，同时保留了选定的损害和储备。较大的阈值只会增加家庭部分，直到该部分达到可接受的损害金额。此时，根据规定的公式，更大的阈值不会造成更多的损害。网格包含没有概率权重的替代算术情况。它并不建议降低建筑物的保险金额以减少免赔额。选择适当的保险价值并检查全额承保条款需要不同的评估。在保留金额旁边记录完整的规则有用的计划记录包括适用的事件、百分比乘法的基础、百分比本身、任何最低美元或其他调整，以及该规则是否适用于每个事件或其他基础。然后将支持的规则转换为美元金额，然后与可用现金进行比较。本文审查的 NAIC 页面的最新更新日期为 2025 年 6 月 2 日。其美国背景仅用于解释为什么需要仔细阅读保险价值百分比免赔额。该文章不适用任何州触发因素、法定门槛或加拿大政策条件。图表输入是透明的假设。对于实际家庭，保单措辞和确认的索赔处理控制着计算。实际的教训是保留分母和结算假设，而不是在预算中放置一个无法解释的百分比。

cafc2a040af04b23e572e2bd1fdd805901469ce8.src: For a fixed unit holding without distributions, market-price change equals the NAV growth factor multiplied by the exit-premium factor and divided by the entry-premium factor, minus one. An ETF has a trading price as well as a NAV per unit Suppose a hypothetical ETF has a NAV of CAD 100 per unit. Its market purchase price is CAD 102, a 2% premium to that matched NAV. Later, NAV has risen to CAD 105, but the selected market sale price is CAD 103.95, a 1% discount to the later NAV. NAV per unit rose 5%. The price paid and the price received rose by a different percentage: CAD 103.95 ÷ CAD 102 − 1 = approximately 1.9118% . The SEC’s ETF investor bulletin explains that retail transactions occur at market prices, which can differ from NAV. This page uses original prices to examine that distinction. No market data or actual fund quote is implied. Compare each price with the NAV for the same comparison point A premium or discount here is market price ÷ matched NAV − 1 . CAD 102 against CAD 100 gives +2%; CAD 103.95 against CAD 105 gives −1%. A positive sign means premium and a negative sign means discount. The NAV at purchase and the NAV at sale are separate observations. Applying a later NAV to an earlier trade, or comparing a current quote with an older NAV without understanding the timing, can answer a different question from the one intended. The chart assumes perfectly synchronized hypothetical comparisons. Real data require a check of valuation time, market-price convention and currency. The SEC notes that NAV is calculated each business day while shares trade during the day. This calculator does not reconstruct an intraday fair value or decide whether a displayed gap is an executable opportunity. Use three factors rather than subtracting percentage labels Let g be the change in NAV per unit, p-in the entry premium and p-out the exit premium, written as fractions. With no distribution and fixed units, the market-price growth factor is (1+g) × (1+p-out) ÷ (1+p-in) . The example gives 1.05 × 0.99 ÷ 1.02 − 1 = 1.9118% . The exact difference from the 5% NAV change is about −3.0882 percentage points . Simply calculating 5% − 2% − 1% gives 2%. That additive shortcut misses the purchase-price denominator and the interaction of the factors. The discrepancy is small in this example but the correct identity remains useful across the selected sensitivities. A premium is not automatically an annual fee If both purchase and sale occur at the same 2% premium, the two premium factors cancel. With the same 5% NAV change, market-price change is exactly 5% in this simplified no-distribution model. If the purchase premium is 2% and the exit is at NAV, the return falls to approximately 2.9412%. If entry is at a 2% discount, exit is at NAV and NAV itself is unchanged, the return is approximately 2.0408%: the gain is measured relative to a CAD 98 purchase price, not a CAD 100 denominator. These are conditional arithmetic outcomes. They do not establish that a discount will close, that the underlying investments are cheap or that the future sale price will be available. The exit-sensitivity curve keeps the entry assumption fixed while showing this dependence explicitly. Follow the units before reconciling the dollars Spending CAD 10,000 at CAD 102 per unit obtains approximately 98.039216 units . The illustration retains fractional units mathematically; it does not promise that a broker can execute that quantity. Those units initially represent about CAD 9,803.92 of NAV value. Their NAV value rises by about CAD 490.20 to CAD 10,294.12. Selling at the assumed 1% discount gives proceeds of approximately CAD 10,191.18 . The waterfall reconciles the same result: CAD 10,000 purchase cash, minus the CAD 196.08 entry adjustment to NAV exposure, plus CAD 490.20 NAV growth, minus the CAD 102.94 exit adjustment. The entry adjustment is not a second charge to the account. It expresses the difference between the cash paid and the NAV exposure obtained. Keep premium, bid–ask spread and fund expenses in their own places A premium compares a market price with NAV. A bid–ask spread compares two market quotes. They describe different relationships. This example enters one execution price at each end and adds no separate spread charge. The illustration also adds no commission, tax or separate fund-expense deduction. An analysis using an actual NAV change needs to understand expenses already reflected in that NAV before deducting them again. Trading costs and cash distributions require their own consistent records. There is no distribution in this model, so NAV change and market-price change are price measures. They are not labelled fund total return when income has been paid out. The comparison interval has no specified length, and neither result is annualized. Use the entry/exit grid to test the price assumption behind the goal The matrix replaces entry and exit premia while retaining the selected NAV change. Equal-premium cells reproduce that NAV change. Other cells show how the two market-price factors can improve or reduce the trading result. Changing the original NAV level changes the number of mathematical units for the same purchase cash, while leaving the percentage identity unchanged. Changing the cash amount scales dollars. Neither control supplies a probability of earning the selected NAV change or a likely future premium. For a financial goal, the relevant cash is what can be sold and received under actual terms, after the applicable costs and taxes and on the required date. A fund’s NAV increase is one part of that assessment, alongside the prices at which the household enters and exits. Use NAV and market prices with consistent dates, times and currency. Record the actual unit quantity and purchase cash. Separate NAV price change from the entry and exit premium factors. Include distributions and other costs consistently when calculating total return. Check the sale and cash-receipt dates against the spending goal.
cafc2a040af04b23e572e2bd1fdd805901469ce8.zh: 对于没有分配的固定单位持有，市场价格变化等于资产净值增长因子乘以退出溢价因子再除以进入溢价因子减一。 ETF 有交易价格和每单位资产净值 假设一只假设的 ETF 的资产净值是每单位 100 加元。其市场购买价为 102 加元，较相应资产净值溢价 2%。后来NAV已经涨到105加元，但选定的市场售价是103.95加元，比后来的NAV有1%的折扣。每单位资产净值上升 5%。支付的价格和收到的价格上涨了不同的百分比：103.95 CAD ÷ 102 CAD - 1 = 约 1.9118% 。美国证券交易委员会的 ETF 投资者公告解释说，零售交易按市场价格进行，这可能与资产净值不同。本页使用原始价格来检验这种区别。不暗示市场数据或实际基金报价。将每个价格与相同比较点的资产净值进行比较 这里的溢价或折扣是市场价格 ÷ 匹配的资产净值 − 1 。 102 加元兑 100 加元可得到 +2%； 103.95 加元兑 105 加元为 -1%。正号表示溢价，负号表示折扣。购买时的资产净值和出售时的资产净值是单独的观察值。将较晚的资产净值应用于较早的交易，或者在不了解时机的情况下将当前报价与较早的资产净值进行比较，可能会回答与预期不同的问题。该图表假设了完全同步的假设比较。真实数据需要检查估值时间、市场价格惯例和货币。美国证券交易委员会指出，资产净值是在股票交易期间的每个工作日计算的。该计算器不会重建日内公允价值或决定显示的缺口是否是可执行的机会。使用三个因素而不是减去百分比标签 令 g 为每单位资产净值的变化，p 为进入溢价，p 为退出溢价，写为分数。在没有分配和固定单位的情况下，市场价格增长系数为 (1+g) × (1+p-out) ÷ (1+p-in) 。该示例给出 1.05 × 0.99 ÷ 1.02 − 1 = 1.9118% 。与 5% NAV 变化的确切差异约为 -3.0882 个百分点。简单地计算 5% − 2% − 1% 就得出 2%。这种加法捷径忽略了购买价格分母和因素的相互作用。本例中的差异很小，但正确的身份在选定的敏感度范围内仍然有用。溢价并不自动成为年费如果购买和销售均以相同的 2% 溢价发生，则两个溢价因素相互抵消。在同样的 5% 资产净值变化的情况下，在这个简化的无分配模型中，市场价格变化恰好是 5%。如果购买溢价为 2%，且以资产净值退出，则回报率降至约 2.9412%。如果入场价格为 2% 折扣，退出价格为资产净值，并且资产净值本身保持不变，则回报率约为 2.0408%：收益是相对于 98 加元的购买价格而不是 100 加元的分母来衡量的。这些是条件算术结果。他们没有确定折扣将会结束、基础投资很便宜或者未来的销售价格将会可用。退出敏感性曲线保持进入假设固定，同时明确显示这种依赖性。在调节美元之前先关注单位。以每单位 102 加元的价格花费 10,000 加元，可获得大约 98.039216 个单位。该插图在数学上保留了分数单位；它不承诺经纪人可以执行该数量。这些单位最初代表资产净值约 9,803.92 加元。他们的资产净值增加了约 490.20 加元，达到 10,294.12 加元。按假设 1% 的折扣出售，所得收益约为 10,191.18 加元。瀑布调整了相同的结果：10,000 加元的购买现金，减去 196.08 加元的资产净值敞口入场调整，加上 490.20 加元的资产净值增长，减去 102.94 加元的退出调整。分录调整不是对账户进行二次收费。它表示支付的现金与获得的资产净值风险之间的差异。将溢价、买卖价差和基金费用保留在各自的位置 溢价将市场价格与资产净值进行比较。买卖价差比较两个市场报价。他们描述了不同的关系。此示例在每一端输入一个执行价格，并且不添加单独的点差费用。该插图还没有增加佣金、税收或单独的基金费用扣除。使用实际资产净值变化进行的分析需要了解资产净值中已经反映的费用，然后再扣除它们。交易成本和现金分配需要有自己一致的记录。该模型中没有分布，因此资产净值变化和市场价格变化都是价格指标。当收入已支付时，它们不会被标记为基金总回报。比较区间没有指定的长度，并且两个结果都不是年度化的。使用进入/退出网格来测试目标背后的价格假设 该矩阵替换进入和退出溢价，同时保留选定的资产净值变化。等额保费单元重现了资产净值的变化。其他单元格显示了两个市场价格因素如何改善或减少交易结果。更改原始资产净值水平会改变相同购买现金的数学单位数量，同时保持百分比不变。改变现金数额会影响美元的规模。两种控制都没有提供赚取所选资产净值变化的概率或可能的未来溢价。对于财务目标，相关现金是指在扣除适用的成本和税费后，在规定的日期，根据实际条款可以出售和收到的现金。基金资产净值的增长以及家庭进入和退出的价格都是评估的一部分。使用具有一致日期、时间和货币的资产净值和市场价格。记录实际单位数量和采购现金。将资产净值价格变化与进入和退出溢价因素分开。在计算总回报时，一致地包括分配和其他成本。根据支出目标检查销售和现金收据日期。

6b23e890340f23c12a07b77ab2dedc831d0ef25a.src: Read who is included in each debt statistic. A graduation median and a later median among people still owing describe different groups, so their difference is not a typical person’s repayment. Begin by reading the condition attached to each amount The selected all-level estimates show CAD 18,800 median debt at graduation among graduates who owed money, and CAD 15,000 median debt at interview among those who still owed. Both are useful statistics. Subtracting them does not calculate a typical graduate’s repayment. The first amount describes graduation debtors. The later amount excludes people who no longer owed by the interview. Those are different denominators, and the middle borrower in one distribution need not be the middle borrower in the other. The charts use Statistics Canada Table 37-10-0255-01 , selecting debt to any government or non-government source, Canada by province of study, all fields and Total – Gender. They do not treat a group estimate as an individual account balance. 2020 is the graduating class, while the interview came three years later The 2023 National Graduates Survey concerns people who graduated from public postsecondary institutions in 2020. The source table used here was released on 2 May 2025. Downloading it on 25 October 2026 does not change the reference class or turn its figures into 2026 loan balances. The table covers graduates living in Canada at interview and excludes those who pursued further education between graduation and interview. Respondents without a declared level or field are also excluded. Its national province-of-study estimates include the three territories. Those exclusions matter when comparing a personal study path. A graduate who immediately entered another program is not represented by this table’s included population in the same way as someone who did not continue studying. The charts cannot describe every graduate’s debt experience. The share who owed and the amount owed answer different questions For all included study levels together, 47% owed education debt at graduation . This describes incidence among the included graduates, including those who owed nothing. The debt mean and median instead summarize people who had debt. The five level-specific incidence estimates range from 32% for doctorate to 80% for professional programs. Their borrower medians range from CAD 13,500 for college to CAD 65,000 for professional programs, with the quality codes shown beside each estimate. The scatter plot puts debt incidence on the horizontal axis and the debtor median on the vertical axis. These dimensions are related to different questions: how common a positive balance was, and how large the middle positive balance was. The overlapping All levels point is an aggregate, not an extra sixth disjoint population that can be added to the five levels. A mean and a median summarize the borrower distribution differently The all-level mean debt at graduation is CAD 25,200 , above the CAD 18,800 median. The mean averages balances among the specified debtors; the median marks their distribution’s midpoint. A difference between the two does not supply the full distribution, identify a particular borrower or set an appropriate personal borrowing limit. The grouped chart retains both measures for each level so one summary is not silently substituted for the other. The level labels also follow the source classification. Its bachelor category includes specified below-bachelor university certificates and diplomas, while professional programs are a separate category. These are published groupings rather than a custom ranking of degree quality or future earning power. The people who fully repaid leave the later debt-amount subgroup The all-level source estimates report that 33% of graduation debtors had paid off their debt by interview . The later debt-amount estimates concern those who still owed: a mean of CAD 21,600 and a median of CAD 15,000. The selected-level chart puts graduation amounts beside still-owing interview amounts, while its captions retain the subgroup condition. It does not label their difference as the amount repaid or the return on paying down a loan. A proper median individual repayment would require an appropriate paired measure for the same individuals, together with a definition of what counts as repayment. Subtracting two published group medians cannot reconstruct that measure. Their difference can also be affected by who remains in the later subgroup. Every borrower can repay while the still-owing median rises The final chart is a fully invented three-person demonstration. Starting balances are CAD 10,000, CAD 20,000 and CAD 30,000. Later balances are CAD 0, CAD 19,000 and CAD 29,000. Every person reduced debt. The starting median is CAD 20,000. Among the two people still owing, the later median is the midpoint of CAD 19,000 and CAD 29,000: CAD 24,000 . That conditional median rose even though no one’s balance increased. Include the paid-off zero and the later all-three median is CAD 19,000. Look instead at individual reductions—CAD 10,000, CAD 1,000 and CAD 1,000—and the median repayment is CAD 1,000. Changing the question changes the correct denominator and calculation. These original invented records are not survey respondents, a fitted model or a reconstruction of private borrower information. Keep the source’s precision warning beside the value The 36 selected observations retain 25 A codes, nine B codes and two C codes. In the source’s classification, A means excellent quality with a coefficient of variation at most 5%; B means very good, above 5% through 15%; C means good, above 15% through 25%. Both professional-program medians in this slice carry C. Their point estimates remain visible with that qualification. The charts do not replace the codes with made-up error bars or treat a descriptive ordering as proof of a statistically significant difference. All source estimates are rounded. The article performs no inflation conversion, adds no household records and estimates no current loan rate. A large difference in plotted amounts can justify a closer look at the evidence, while remaining separate from a causal claim about a program. Use an actual balance and repayment schedule for the personal plan Survey statistics provide context for education funding and debt discussions. A personal repayment plan still needs the actual loan balances, payment obligations, interest terms, support arrangements and cash available after essential expenses. For example, dividing an independently chosen CAD 24,000 balance into 60 equal principal payments gives CAD 400 per payment before any interest, fee or program-specific adjustment. That arithmetic is a stated personal scenario; it cannot be inferred from the survey’s CAD 18,800 median. Check the class year, interview date and excluded population. Separate incidence among graduates from amounts among debtors. Retain each estimate’s quality code and subgroup condition. Use a paired individual measure when the question is individual repayment. Build the household cash schedule from actual balances and contract terms. The source-level control changes the selected historical view and highlighted point. It never edits the official estimates or predicts how quickly a reader will repay.
6b23e890340f23c12a07b77ab2dedc831d0ef25a.zh: 了解每项债务统计数据中都包含哪些人。仍然欠债的人的毕业中位数和后来的中位数描述了不同的群体，因此他们的差异不是典型人的还款额。首先阅读每笔金额附带的条件 选定的各级估计显示，在毕业时欠钱的毕业生中，债务中位数为 18,800 加元，而在面谈时，仍欠钱的毕业生中债务中位数为 15,000 加元。两者都是有用的统计数据。减去它们并不能计算出典型毕业生的还款额。第一个金额描述了毕业债务人。后面的金额不包括因面谈而不再欠款的人。这些是不同的分母，一种分配中的中间借款人不一定是另一种分配中的中间借款人。这些图表使用加拿大统计局表 37-10-0255-01，选择对任何政府或非政府来源的债务、加拿大按研究省份、所有领域和总计 – 性别。他们不会将团体估算视为个人账户余额。 2020年是毕业班，而采访是在三年后进行的。2023年全国毕业生调查涉及2020年从公立高等教育机构毕业的人。这里使用的源表于2025年5月2日发布。2026年10月25日下载它不会改变参考班级或将其数字转换为2026年贷款余额。该表涵盖面试时居住在加拿大的毕业生，不包括毕业至面试期间继续深造的毕业生。没有声明级别或领域的受访者也被排除在外。其全国研究省份估计包括这三个地区。在比较个人学习路径时，这些排除很重要。立即进入另一个项目的毕业生并不像没有继续学习的人那样被该表所包含的人口所代表。这些图表无法描述每个毕业生的债务经历。欠款比例和欠款金额回答了不同的问题 对于所有包括的学习级别而言，47% 的人在毕业时欠有教育债务。这描述了所包括的毕业生中的发生率，包括那些不欠任何人的毕业生。相反，债务平均值和中位数总结了有债务的人。五个级别特定的发生率估计范围从博士项目的 32% 到专业项目的 80%。他们的借款人中位数范围从大学的 13,500 加元到专业课程的 65,000 加元不等，每个估算旁边都显示了质量代码。散点图将债务发生率放在横轴上，将债务人中位数放在纵轴上。这些维度与不同的问题相关：正余额有多常见，以及中间正余额有多大。重叠的所有级别点是一个聚合，而不是可以添加到五个级别的额外的第六个不相交总体。均值和中位数以不同的方式概括了借款人分布。毕业时所有级别的平均债务为 25,200 加元，高于中位数 18,800 加元。平均值是指定债务人之间的平均余额；中位数标志着其分布的中点。两者之间的差异并不提供全部分配、识别特定借款人或设定适当的个人借款限额。分组图表保留每个级别的两种度量，因此一个摘要不会默默地替换另一个摘要。级别标签也遵循源分类。其学士学位类别包括特定的学士以下大学证书和文凭，而专业课程是一个单独的类别。这些是已发布的分组，而不是学位质量或未来收入能力的自定义排名。完全还清的人离开后期债务金额分组 各级消息人士估计，33%的毕业债务人通过面谈还清了债务。后来的债务金额估计涉及那些仍然欠债的人：平均为 21,600 加元，中位数为 15,000 加元。所选级别的图表将毕业金额与尚欠面试金额放在一起，而其标题保留了子组条件。它没有将它们的差异标记为偿还金额或偿还贷款的回报。适当的个人还款中位数需要对同一个人采取适当的配对措施，并定义什么算作还款。减去两个已发布的组中位数无法重建该度量。他们的差异也可能受到留在后面小组中的人的影响。每个借款人都可以在仍欠中位数上升的情况下还款。最终图表是一个完全发明的三人演示。起始余额为 10,000 加元、20,000 加元和 30,000 加元。随后的余额为 0 加元、19,000 加元和 29,000 加元。每个人都减少了债务。起始中位数为 20,000 加元。尚欠的两人中，后来的中位数是19,000加元和29,000加元的中点：24,000加元。尽管没有人的余额增加，但条件中位数还是上升了。包括已赔付的零和后来的全部三个中位数为 19,000 加元。相反，看看个人减免额 - 10,000 加元、1,000 加元和 1,000 加元 - 还款额中位数为 1,000 加元。改变问题会改变正确的分母和计算。这些原始发明记录不是调查受访者、拟合模型或私人借款人信息的重建。将来源的精度警告保留在值旁边。36 个选定的观测值保留 25 个 A 代码、9 个 B 代码和 2 个 C 代码。来源分类中，A表示品质优良，变异系数不超过5%； B表示非常好，高于5%到15%； C 表示良好，高于 15% 至 25%。该部分中的两个专业项目中位数都为 C。他们的点估计在该资格下仍然可见。这些图表不会用虚构的误差线替换代码，也不会将描述性排序视为统计上显着差异的证据。所有来源估计值均经过四舍五入。该文章没有进行通货膨胀转换，没有添加家庭记录，也没有估计当前的贷款利率。绘制的金额的巨大差异可以证明需要仔细研究证据，同时与程序的因果关系保持分离。使用个人计划的实际余额和还款计划 调查统计数据为教育经费和债务讨论提供了背景。个人还款计划仍需要实际贷款余额、还款义务、利息条款、支持安排以及扣除必要费用后的可用现金。例如，将独立选择的 24,000 加元余额分成 60 笔等额本金付款，在任何利息、费用或特定于计划的调整之前，每笔付款为 400 加元。该算术是一个明确的个人场景；不能从调查的中位数 18,800 加元推断出来。检查班级年份、面试日期和排除人群。将毕业生的发生率与债务人的金额分开。保留每个估计的质量代码和子组条件。当问题是个人还款时，使用配对个人措施。根据实际余额和合同条款制定家庭现金计划。源代码级控件更改选定的历史视图和突出显示的点。它从不编辑官方估计或预测读者偿还的速度。

48f77747a75783524d8e3e4c0c6e4f89e25ee861.src: A group’s average trip cannot price your route. Attendance changes some commuting costs; a committed pass and continuing car ownership costs need their own treatment. Start with the people represented by the statistic A commuting headline can prompt a useful budget review, but its population is not a household travel diary. The statistical panels retain a Statistics Canada May 2025 snapshot , released on 26 August 2025. Here, commuters are employed people usually working most hours outside the home. The supplement covers ages 15–69 in the provinces, excluding people on reserves, full-time Canadian Armed Forces members and people in institutions. The first chart selects three main-mode shares: car, truck or van at 80.9%, public transit at 11.9%, and walking or cycling at 6.2%. Other methods are omitted. These figures are not percentages of all adults or a reader’s chances of travelling by a particular method. Keep the reference month visible. A review date in 2026 does not turn May 2025 observations into a current personal schedule. The controls below leave the six published values unchanged. Read the duration bars as group means, rather than a route experiment The second panel gives mean trip-to-work times of 24.7 minutes for car commuters, 44.1 for public transit and 15.0 for active transport. The May 2025 questionnaire asks about the trip to work, rather than the complete return journey. These are different groups, rather than the same travellers randomly assigned to transport methods. They do not establish how much time one person would save by changing modes. No confidence intervals or causal effects are calculated here. For a personal comparison, measure the actual alternatives from the same starting point to the same destination. Include walking to a stop, waiting, transfers, finding parking and getting from the vehicle to the workplace. A quoted station-to-station journey may omit substantial parts of the trip. Also record whether the return journey differs. The calculator uses one entered time for each direction to keep the arithmetic inspectable. If the outward trip takes thirty minutes and the return takes fifty, an average of forty per direction reproduces eighty daily minutes, but it does not describe either trip’s reliability. Specify the attendance calendar before multiplying a daily cost The default scenario assumes twelve on-site days in each of twelve identical months. That gives 144 complete return commutes. It is an original planning assumption, rather than an attendance estimate from the survey. The number of included months matters. A seasonal job, a course or a temporary assignment may require only part of a year. Change that control to describe the intended window, then consider whether each included month really has the same attendance. Holidays, vacation, illness, work travel and changes in a hybrid agreement can alter the actual count. For implementation, replace a repeated monthly assumption with the known calendar. Do not automatically multiply five days by fifty-two weeks if the person does not make that many trips. The model compares three separate ways of paying for the stated commuting need. It does not combine their costs as though the same person simultaneously made all three complete journeys. Nor does it assume that each alternative is available or suitable for the actual route. Compare the pass with the complete return fare at the same attendance The invented monthly pass costs CAD 160 and is purchased in every included month. Across twelve months, its cash cost is CAD 1,920. The assumed complete return fare is CAD 8, so 144 pay-per-use commutes cost CAD 1,152. At these inputs, the per-use scenario requires CAD 768 less cash over the window. That difference follows from the stated prices and attendance. It is not a statement about a real transit system or the best choice for every traveller. The monthly crossing is CAD 160 ÷ CAD 8 = twenty complete return commutes. At twenty on-site days, both alternatives cost CAD 160 per month. Below that count the per-use line is lower; above it the pass line is lower within the stated model. The pass line remains positive at zero on-site days because the scenario still buys it. If the pass can be skipped, cancelled or refunded for an unused month, use a different purchase calendar. A line describing an already committed payment cannot silently assume that refund. Check the terms that a simple crossing leaves out Actual fares may depend on zones, concessions, transfers, payment method, daily caps or monthly caps. A return journey might not cost twice a single fare, and automatic capping can change the shape of a per-use line. The entered fare should represent the cash actually charged for one complete commuting day under the assumed terms. This calculator has no tariff engine. A zero per-use fare is permitted, but then dividing the pass price by that fare does not produce a finite crossing. A pass may also cover useful non-work journeys. Those trips are excluded here so the attendance comparison remains specific. If the decision includes evenings and weekends, add that actual travel need and its alternative cash cost before deciding what the pass would replace. Employer reimbursements, payroll deductions and tax effects also need separate evidence. The displayed amounts are assumed cash prices without those adjustments. A workplace benefit cannot be inferred from the national transport statistics. Separate the cash avoided on a commuting day from continuing ownership costs The invented car input is CAD 18 of avoidable cash for each complete return commute. At 144 commuting days, the displayed amount is CAD 2,592. This might represent genuinely avoidable fuel, parking or toll payments in a separately documented scenario. A prepaid parking contract does not become a daily saving merely because the car stays home. Similarly, financing payments or retained insurance can continue while a person takes transit. Include a cost in the avoidable daily input only when the assumed change actually removes that cash payment. The car line excludes those continuing costs. It therefore cannot answer whether to buy, sell or retain a vehicle, or rank the total economic cost of car ownership against transit. Depreciation, maintenance, insurance and disposal would require their own model and evidence. This distinction prevents a common budget error: describing every allocated ownership expense as immediately spendable cash saved by one fewer drive. Allocation is useful for understanding costs, but the bank balance changes only when an actual payment changes. Keep travel hours visible without booking them as income The independent time input defaults to forty minutes in each direction. With 144 commuting days, that is 2 × 40 × 144 ÷ 60 = 192 travel hours across the included months. The matrix varies attendance and one-way duration while retaining the number of included months. It shows why a modest daily difference can accumulate, and why the number of journeys matters alongside the duration of each journey. Hours saved can matter for care, rest, study or other commitments. They do not automatically become paid work or an amount available to cover a bill. This article therefore keeps hours in their own unit and does not multiply them by a salary. Before changing a travel plan, check the actual route, schedule, access needs, fare terms and payments that can be avoided. Use the published charts as context and the independently entered calendar as an explicit scenario. Revisit both when work arrangements or transport terms change.

日发布。在这里，通勤者是指通常大部分时间在户外工作的就业人员。该补助涵盖各省 15 至 69 岁的人群，不包括预备役人员、全职加拿大武装部队成员和机构人员。第一张图表选择了三种主要方式的份额：汽车、卡车或货车占 80.9%，公共交通占 11.9%，步行或骑自行车占 6.2%。其他方法不再赘述。这些数字不是所有成年人或读者通过特定方式旅行的机会的百分比。保持参考月份可见。 2026 年的审核日期不会将 2025 年 5 月的观察结果转变为当前的个人日程安排。以下控件使六个已发布的值保持不变。将持续时间条视为群体平均值，而不是路线实验第二个面板给出的平均上班时间为汽车通勤者 24.7 分钟，公共交通为 44.1 分钟，主动交通为 15.0 分钟。 2025 年 5 月的调查问卷询问的是上班行程，而不是完整的回程行程。这些是不同的群体，而不是随机分配到交通方式的相同旅行者。他们没有确定一个人通过改变模式可以节省多少时间。这里不计算置信区间或因果效应。为了个人比较，衡量从相同起点到相同目的地的实际替代方案。包括步行到车站、等待、换乘、寻找停车位以及下车前往工作场所。报价的车站到车站旅程可能会省略行程的大部分内容。还要记录回程是否不同。计算器对每个方向使用一个输入的时间，以保持算术的可检查性。如果去程需要 30 分钟，回程需要 50 分钟，则每个方向平均 40 分钟可重现每天 80 分钟，但这并不能描述任一行程的可靠性。在乘以每日成本之前指定出勤日历 默认方案假设 12 个相同月份中的每个月份有 12 个现场日。这提供了 144 次完整的往返通勤。这是最初的计划假设，而不是调查中的出席人数估计。包含的月份数很重要。季节性工作、课程或临时任务可能只需要一年的一部分时间。更改该控件以描述预期的窗口，然后考虑每个包含的月份是否确实具有相同的出勤率。假期、假期、疾病、工作旅行和混合协议的变化可能会改变实际计数。为了实现，用已知的日历替换重复的每月假设。如果此人没有进行那么多次旅行，请不要自动将五天乘以五十二周。该模型比较了满足所述通勤需求的三种不同的支付方式。它并没有将他们的成本结合起来，就好像同一个人同时完成了所有三个完整的旅程一样。它也不假设每个替代方案都是可用的或适合实际路线。将通票与相同出席人数的完整往返票价进行比较 本发明的月票价格为 160 加元，并且在每个包含的月份购买。 12 个月内，其现金成本为 1,920 加元。假定完整往返票价为 8 加元，因此 144 趟按次付费通勤费用为 1,152 加元。在这些投入下，每次使用场景需要减少 768 加元的现金。这种差异是由规定的价格和出席人数造成的。它并不是关于真正的交通系统或每个旅行者的最佳选择的声明。每月过境费为 160 加元 ÷ 8 加元 = 20 次完整的返程通勤。在现场工作 20 天时，两种替代方案的费用均为每月 160 加元。低于该计数，每次使用线较低；在其上方，合格线在所述模型中较低。现场天数为零时，通过线仍然为正，因为场景仍然支持它。如果通票在未使用的月份内可以跳过、取消或退款，请使用不同的购买日历。描述已承诺付款的行不能默默地假定退款。检查简单穿越时遗漏的条款 实际票价可能取决于区域、优惠、转乘、付款方式、每日上限或每月上限。回程的费用可能不会是单程票价的两倍，而且自动上限可以改变每次使用的线路的形状。输入的票价应代表假设条款下一个完整通勤日实际收取的现金。该计算器没有关税引擎。允许每次使用票价为零，但将通票价格除以该票价不会产生有限交叉。通行证还可以涵盖有用的非工作旅程。这些行程此处不包括在内，因此出勤率比较仍然具体。如果决定包括晚上和周末，请在决定通行证将取代什么之前添加实际旅行需求及其替代现金成本。雇主报销、工资扣除和税收影响也需要单独的证据。显示的金额假定为未经这些调整的现金价格。工作场所福利不能从国家交通统计数据中推断出来。将通勤日避免的现金与持续拥有成本分开本发明的汽车投入是每次完整的返程通勤可避免的现金 18 加元。在 144 个通勤日中，显示的金额为 2,592 加元。这可能代表在单独记录的场景中真正可以避免的燃油、停车或通行费。预付费停车合同并不会仅仅因为汽车停在家里而成为日常节省。同样，当一个人过境时，融资付款或保留保险可以继续。仅当假设的变化实际上消除了现金支付时，才将成本纳入可避免的日常输入中。汽车系列不包括这些持续成本。因此，它无法回答是否购买、出售或保留车辆，或对拥有汽车与交通的总经济成本进行排名。折旧、维护、保险和处置需要各自的模型和证据。这种区别可以防止常见的预算错误：将每笔分配的所有权费用描述为通过减少一个驱动器节省的可立即使用的现金。分配对于了解成本很有用，但银行余额仅在实际付款发生变化时才会发生变化。保持旅行时间可见，而不将其预订为收入独立时间输入默认为每个方向四十分钟。通勤天数为 144 个，即所含月份内的出行时间为 2 × 40 × 144 ÷ 60 = 192 小时。该矩阵会改变出勤率和单程持续时间，同时保留所包含的月份数。它说明了为什么每天的微小差异会累积，以及为什么行程次数与每次行程的持续时间都很重要。节省的时间对于护理、休息、学习或其他承诺很重要。它们不会自动成为有偿工作或可用于支付账单的金额。因此，本文将工作时间保留在自己的单位，并且不将其乘以工资。在更改旅行计划之前，请检查实际路线、时间表、交通需求、票价条款以及可以避免的付款。使用已发布的图表作为上下文，使用独立输入的日历作为显式场景。当工作安排或交通条款发生变化时，请重新访问。

d9d69d23e2b8297298d0eaf23c0c50c20f287170.src: A purchase counts once but can carry many dollars. Before reading a payment-method percentage as a spending pattern, identify whether its denominator is transactions, dollars or people. Count the purchases and then count their dollars Suppose a purchase list contains six small cash purchases, three debit purchases and one larger credit purchase. A count-based chart gives every purchase one unit. A dollar-based chart instead weights each purchase by its amount. The same list can therefore have very different method shares without any arithmetic error. For a defined tally, purchase-count share is a method’s count divided by the total number of purchases. Purchase-dollar share is its spending divided by total spending. Neither denominator is income, the number of people holding a card or the amount of money currently available in a bank account. The first two charts use fixed official 2025 observations. The last three use an independently invented tally that the controls can change. The example explains the denominator arithmetic; it does not estimate how an individual should pay or reconstruct the survey from three personal categories. Read the nine published 2025 reporting categories together The Bank of Canada’s Methods-of-Payment Survey dashboard describes consumer purchases, using a questionnaire and a three-day payment diary. Its 2025 data are accompanied by report metadata dated August 2026 . This article reviewed the dashboard and data on 25 October 2026. The paired chart retains all nine current reporting bins. In particular, the standalone labels Credit and Debit sit alongside separately reported contactless categories. Reading Credit’s 14.2% count share as all credit-card use would omit the other credit bins. Published count shares sum to 100.0%; dollar shares sum to 100.1% at the source precision. The table preserves those values instead of changing Other or normalizing every row. These are purchase measures, not a census of every transfer and payment in the economy. The data extract supplies no confidence intervals, so none are invented here. Keep the 2025 classification break visible The dashboard notes a reporting change in 2025. Contactless card payments now distinguish physical cards from cards linked to mobile devices, and the Mobile app category excludes those mobile contactless card purchases. The Bank states that the 2025 categories cannot be fully harmonized with previous survey years. These charts therefore compare categories within 2025. A smooth Mobile app line across the classification change could mix a measurement change with behaviour. Historical blanks in newly introduced categories should also not be replaced with fabricated zeros. The second chart makes a disclosed one-year combination: Credit, Contactless credit and Contactless credit, mobile form the three-credit-bin group; the corresponding debit bins form another. Cash, Mobile app and Other stay separate. This grouping is explicit and does not silently redefine the labels in the original nine-row chart. A difference in percentage points is a denominator comparison In the three combined credit bins, the 2025 count share is 48.2% and the dollar share is 58.5%. Subtracting count share from dollar share gives positive 10.3 percentage points. Cash goes the other way: 9.6% of dollars minus 17.9% of count gives negative 8.3 points. The signed bars display that subtraction. A positive value means the group has a larger share of dollars than purchases; negative means a smaller share. These are neither annual investment returns nor changes from a previous year. A gap of 10.3 percentage points is also different from saying a quantity grew by 10.3%. Different purchase sizes can produce such a pattern, as the invented tally demonstrates. The public shares alone do not identify why payment methods and amounts are associated. They do not establish that choosing a card causes higher spending or that a reader will face an equivalent distribution. The five gaps sum to 0.1 point because source dollar shares total 100.1% and count shares total 100.0%. That small residual is retained as a rounding consequence. It is not treated as missing income or a new payment category. Reconcile the invented ten-purchase example The default tally has six cash purchases at a mean CAD 5, three debit purchases at a mean CAD 40 and one credit purchase at CAD 350. The means are assumed final purchase amounts including applicable taxes. Each purchase belongs to exactly one of the three teaching categories, with no split tender, refund or currency conversion. Method dollars are CAD 30, CAD 120 and CAD 350. Total count is ten and total dollars are CAD 500. The count ring therefore shows 60%, 30% and 10%, while the dollar ring shows 6%, 24% and 70%. One purchase can be only one tenth of the count while carrying seven tenths of the cost. The waterfall reconciles those method dollars to CAD 500. Dividing by ten gives a mean purchase amount of CAD 50. That mean does not identify the median purchase or the distribution within each payment category; the tool knows only counts and assumed category means. The toy’s three broad labels are separate from the Bank’s nine reporting bins. Its 60% cash count share is an invented result, not a competing estimate of the official 2025 cash share. Source figures remain fixed when a toy count or price changes. Change the amount without changing the number of purchases Keep the default counts and raise only the credit mean ticket from CAD 350 to CAD 700. There are still ten purchases, including exactly one credit purchase. The credit count share remains 10%, but total spending rises to CAD 850. The credit dollar share becomes CAD 700 ÷ CAD 850, or about 82.35%. Overall mean purchase amount rises from CAD 50 to CAD 85. The unchanged count ring, changed dollar ring and larger waterfall endpoint show why the same transaction frequency can coexist with very different spending. This comparison changes a price assumption, rather than measuring the effect of switching payment methods. Relabeling the same completed purchases while preserving all final prices leaves total spending unchanged. A real discount, surcharge, interest cost or reward would need its own cash treatment; none is automatically inserted into this tally. The entered average ticket for a method with zero purchases has no effect on its contribution to dollars. It is an unused assumption, not an observed purchase mean. This distinction becomes useful when comparing a rarely used method with a frequently used one. Keep zero purchases distinct from zero purchase dollars If all three counts are zero, total purchases and dollars are zero. Both share distributions are undefined because their denominators are zero. The rings are empty and label their shares unavailable. Three 0% shares would not form a meaningful distribution of purchases. A different case has positive counts but zero prices. Count shares remain defined, while dollar shares are undefined because total dollars are zero. Overall mean purchase amount is zero in that case, because zero dollars are divided by a positive count. With no purchases at all, the overall mean is unavailable. The controls require whole nonnegative counts and nonnegative assumed prices. Cash amounts are rounded to cents before multiplication. A negative purchase amount would represent a refund or another transaction type, which is outside this small model rather than silently mixed into a positive-purchase distribution. The distinction is mathematical, not an assessment of whether a zero-price transaction belongs in the actual survey. The official dataset follows its own transaction definitions; the teaching tally simply makes its assumptions explicit. Bring the purchase tally into a separate funding calendar Purchase dollars measure what the invented list costs. They do not show the income that funds it, when cash leaves a bank account or whether a credit-card balance is paid in full. A method share cannot establish affordability, card interest, unused credit or an emergency reserve. For a budget that recognizes spending when a purchase occurs, a later card payment settles that obligation rather than creating the same consumption expense again. The purchase-and-repayment ledger guide develops that distinction. A separate cash calendar still needs the settlement date and actual amount. Keep those two views consistent instead of adding the purchase and its settlement as two copies of the same spending. This article calculates no rewards, repayment schedule, merchant acceptance, fraud probability or outage risk. Those questions require their own definitions and evidence. The narrow result here is inspectable: counts reconcile to total purchases, method dollars reconcile to spending, and each share states the denominator it uses.

笔较大额信用采购。基于计数的图表为每次购买提供一个单位。相反，基于美元的图表按每次购买的金额进行加权。因此，同一个列表可以具有非常不同的方法共享，而不会出现任何算术错误。对于定义的计数，购买计数份额是方法的计数除以购买总数。购买美元份额是其支出除以总支出。分母都不是收入、持卡人数或银行账户中当前可用的金额。前两张图表使用固定的官方 2025 年观测结果。最后三个使用独立发明的计数，控件可以更改该计数。该示例解释了分母算术；它不会估计个人应如何支付或从三个个人类别中重建调查。一起阅读已发布的 2025 年九个报告类别加拿大银行的支付方式调查仪表板使用调查问卷和三天支付日记描述了消费者的购买情况。其 2025 年数据附有日期为 2026 年 8 月的报告元数据。本文回顾了 2026 年 10 月 25 年的类别无法与之前的调查年份完全一致。因此，这些图表比较了 2025 年内的类别。跨越分类变化的平滑移动应用程序线可以将测量变化与行为混合在一起。新引入的类别中的历史空白也不应该被捏造的零取代。第二张图给出了公开的一年期组合：信用、非接触式信用和非接触式信用、移动形成三信用仓组；相应的借记箱形成另一个借记箱。现金、移动应用程序和其他保持独立。这种分组是明确的，不会默默地重新定义原始九行图表中的标签。百分点差异是分母比较 在三个组合信用仓中，2025 年计数份额为 48.2%，美元份额为 58.5%。从美元份额中减去数量份额可以得到 10.3 个百分点的正值。现金则相反：美元的 9.6% 减去数量的 17.9% 得出负 8.3 个点。带符号的条显示该减法。正值意味着该群体拥有的美元份额大于购买量；负数表示所占份额较小。这些既不是年度投资回报，也不是与上一年相比的变化。 10.3个百分点的差距也不同于数量增长10.3%。正如本发明的计数所表明的，不同的购买量可以产生这样的模式。仅公开份额并不能确定支付方式和金额为何相关。他们并没有证明选择一张卡会导致更高的支出，或者读者将面临同等的分配。这五个差距总计为 0.1 点，因为源美元份额总计为 100.1%，计数份额总计为 100.0%。这个小的残差被保留作为舍入结果。它不被视为缺失收入或新的付款类别。核对所发明的十次购买示例 默认计数有六次现金购买，平均金额为 5 加元，三笔借方购买，平均金额为 40 加元，一笔贷款机构购买，金额为 350 加元。这些平均值假定为包括适用税费的最终购买金额。每次购买都属于三个教学类别之一，没有分割投标、退款或货币兑换。方法美元为 30 加元、120 加元和 350 加元。总计数为 10，总美元为 500 加元。因此计数环显示 60%、30% 和 10%，而美元环显示 6%、24% 和 70%。一次购买只能是数量的十分之一，而成本却是十分之七。瀑布将这些方法美元调整为 500 加元。除以 10 得出平均购买金额为 50 加元。该平均值并不能确定每个支付类别内的中位数购买或分布；该工具只知道计数和假定的类别平均值。该玩具的三大标签与银行的九个报告箱是分开的。其 60% 的现金数量份额是一个虚构的结果，而不是对 2025 年官方现金份额的竞争估计。当玩具数量或价格发生变化时，来源数据保持不变。更改金额而不更改购买数量 保留默认计数，仅将信用平均票数从 350 加元提高到 700 加元。仍然有 10 次购买，其中正好包含 1 次信用购买。信用计数份额仍为 10%，但总支出上升至 850 加元。信用金额份额变为 700 加元 ÷ 850 加元，即约 82.35%。总体平均购买金额从 50 加元上升到 85 加元。不变的计数环、改变的美元环和更大的瀑布端点表明为什么相同的交易频率可以与截然不同的支出共存。这种比较改变了价格假设，而不是衡量转换支付方式的效果。在保留所有最终价格的同时重新标记相同的已完成购买将使总支出保持不变。真正的折扣、附加费、利息成本或奖励需要单独的现金处理；没有一个会自动插入到此计数中。零购买方法中输入的平均门票对其对美元的贡献没有影响。这是一个未使用的假设，而不是观察到的购买平均值。当比较很少使用的方法和经常使用的方法时，这种区别变得很有用。保持零购买量与零购买金额不同如果所有三个计数都为零，则总购买量和金额都为零。两种份额分布均未定义，因为它们的分母为零。这些环是空的，并标记其共享不可用。三个 0% 的股份不会构成有意义的购买分配。另一种情况是计数为正但价格为零。计数份额保持定义，而美元份额未定义，因为总美元为零。在这种情况下，总体平均购买金额为零，因为零美元除以正数。如果根本没有购买，则无法获得总体平均值。控制需要完整的非负计数和非负假设价格。现金金额在乘法之前四舍五入为美分。负购买金额代表退款或其他交易类型，这不属于这个小模型，而不是默默地混合到正购买分布中。这种区别是数学上的，而不是对零价格交易是否属于实际调查的评估。官方数据集遵循自己的交易定义；教学统计只是明确了其假设。将购买计数放入单独的资金日历中 购买美元衡量发明清单的成本。当现金离开银行账户或信用卡余额是否全额支付时，它们不会显示为其提供资金的收入。方法共享不能建立负担能力、卡利息、未使用的信用或紧急储备金。对于在购买时确认支出的预算，稍后的卡付款可以解决该义务，而不是再次产生相同的消费费用。购买和还款分类账指南发展了这种区别。单独的现金日历仍然需要结算日期和实际金额。保持这两个视图一致，而不是将购买及其结算添加为同一支出的两个副本。本文不计算奖励、还款时间表、商家接受度、欺诈概率或中断风险。这些问题需要它们自己的定义和证据。这里的狭义结果是可以检查的：计数与总购买量一致，方法美元与支出一致，并且每个份额都说明它使用的分母。

1dcc9244b0cef28bb7e9531ab73929b3851fc076.src: A discount from face value becomes lower cumulative cash outlay only after enough otherwise-planned purchases are paid by the card. Unused retailer credit is a separate balance, not cash refunded. Start with the cash commitment and the restricted purchasing balance Paying CAD 450 for a retailer card with CAD 500 of face value creates a CAD 50 potential discount on purchases. It also removes CAD 450 from the household’s cash immediately. Those two facts belong together in the plan. FCAC’s gift-card guidance explains that purchases reduce the card balance and that gift cards are generally tied to a retailer or group of retailers. It says gift cards usually cannot be exchanged for cash and advises reading their terms. The source supplies general mechanics; it does not offer the hypothetical discounted card in this article. This example buys one CAD 500 retailer balance at a 10% discount, paying CAD 450 at month zero. Both payment cases make identical eligible purchases of CAD 50 at each month-end for six months, then stop those purchases. The reporting window lasts twelve months. No fee, expiry, refund, resale or reload is assumed. Hold the shopping plan constant before comparing payment methods The pay-as-you-go case pays CAD 50 in cash for each of six monthly purchases, totalling CAD 300 . The card case pays CAD 450 at the beginning and uses CAD 50 of card credit for each of the same purchases. It pays no further cash during those six months. At the reporting date, card-case cash outlay remains CAD 450 , versus CAD 300 for pay-as-you-go. The card case has therefore paid CAD 150 more cash so far . It also has CAD 200 of unused retailer purchasing credit . These statements do not mean the remaining card balance has vanished. They distinguish where the resources are held. The pay-as-you-go household has retained more bank cash, while the other has prepaid purchasing capacity at the retailer. This model records the latter at nominal face value without claiming an equivalent cash refund, resale price or fair value. The final shopping month is a preference assumption. It does not cause the card to expire. Changing the reporting window alone does not create new purchases after the planned shopping has stopped. Follow the cash timeline instead of netting everything at the start The cumulative-cash chart begins at month zero with CAD 450 paid in the card case and zero paid in the other. At month six, the pay-as-you-go line reaches CAD 300. Since there are no more planned purchases in the default case, both lines then stay flat through month twelve. The difference narrows only when the card replaces a purchase that would otherwise require cash. It does not narrow simply because another month passes. Receiving a nominal CAD 500 balance is therefore different from receiving CAD 500 of spendable bank cash. For a household with bills due before those future purchases, the initial commitment can matter even if the card will eventually be fully used. The comparison does not calculate an emergency-fund requirement or assume borrowing will automatically cover the payment. Financing charges would need to be added separately if the purchase were funded with debt. Reconcile the difference without counting a redemption twice The cash comparison has a compact identity: Extra card-case cash = price paid for the card − card credit actually redeemed. With CAD 450 paid and CAD 300 redeemed, extra cash is CAD 150. A redemption is not both a cash inflow and a reduction in the shopping expense. It simply pays for part of the same purchase in place of cash. If purchases eventually exceed the card balance, uncovered amounts require cash top-ups. Those top-ups are included in the card-case cash series. They cancel against the corresponding part of pay-as-you-go spending when taking the difference, leaving the identity above. The waterfall shows the upfront payment and actual purchases replaced, ending at the signed cash difference. Subtracting the unused CAD 200 as well would incorrectly treat restricted credit as if it had been returned to the bank account. A 10% face-value discount still requires 90% redemption to catch up in cash Equal cumulative cash outlay occurs when actual card use reaches its CAD 450 purchase price. That is 90% of the CAD 500 face value . At the assumed CAD 50 monthly use, equality would first occur at the end of month nine if the shopping plan continued that long. The default plan stops after six months, so it does not reach that point within the twelve-month window. Extend planned shopping to twelve months and the result changes: CAD 600 of matched purchases take place, the first CAD 500 is paid by the card, and the last CAD 100 requires cash top-ups. The full-use card case then pays CAD 450 + CAD 100 = CAD 550 , compared with CAD 600 for pay-as-you-go. Its cash reduction is CAD 50 , the original face-value discount. Redeeming more than the face value is not possible in this single-card model. The final chart varies actual redemption from zero to 100% of face value. The curve has no expiry date or usage probabilities. Its zero crossing is an accounting threshold, not a recommendation to spend more in order to make the card appear successful. Keep unwanted extra spending outside the claimed saving The comparison assumes that every redeemed dollar replaces something already planned at the same price. If a household adds purchases only to use the card, the two cases no longer obtain the same goods. The extra spending and its usefulness need a separate decision. Likewise, an alternative shop may have different prices, availability or travel costs. A retailer balance can constrain where the purchases happen, so a face-value discount alone cannot establish the cheapest complete basket. This tool does not estimate those differences. There is also no interest credit on retained cash, no fee or fraud model, and no probability of retailer failure or card loss. A card that remains usable is not declared worthless at the reporting date. The result is a transparent payment-method comparison for one stated plan, with remaining credit shown separately. Use the cash chart alongside the actual terms and purchase plan Before assigning a promotion’s headline discount to a budget, record the cash purchase price, usable face amount, eligible purchases and expected use dates. Check what happens to unused balances under the actual terms and applicable rules. The scenario’s no-fee and no-expiry assumptions do not determine legal rights for any real card. FCAC’s page, dated 23 October 2026 and reviewed for this article on 25 October 2026, distinguishes gift cards from payment-network prepaid cards and notes that rules and exceptions can depend on location. This tool models a retailer purchasing balance and does not apply a provincial fee, expiry or refund rule. Keep three figures visible in the household record: cash paid, credit used against purchases and remaining credit. Together they explain why a discounted purchase can have a favourable eventual cash result while still leaving less flexible cash available today.
1dcc9244b0cef28bb7e9531ab73929b3851fc076.zh: 只有在用卡支付了足够的其他计划购买后，面值的折扣才会变得较低的累积现金支出。未使用的零售商积分是单独的余额，不以现金形式退还。从现金承诺和限制购买余额开始 支付 450 加元购买面值 500 加元的零售商卡可产生 50 加元的潜在购买折扣。它还立即从该家庭的现金中扣除 450 加元。这两个事实属于该计划的一部分。 FCAC 的礼品卡指南解释说，购买会减少卡余额，并且礼品卡通常与零售商或零售商集团绑定。它说礼品卡通常不能兑换现金，并建议阅读其条款。来源提供一般机制；它不提供本文中假设的折扣卡。此示例以 10% 的折扣购买一笔 500 加元的零售商余额，并在零月份支付 450 加元。两种付款方式在六个月内每个月末都会进行相同的符合条件的 50 加元购买，然后停止这些购买。报告窗口持续十二个月。不承担任何费用、到期、退款、转售或重新充值。在比较付款方式之前保持购物计划不变。现收现付情况下，每六个月购买一次，每次支付 50 加元现金，总计 300 加元。卡盒一开始支付 450 加元，每次相同的购买使用卡信用额 50 加元。在这六个月内，它不再支付任何现金。截至报告日期，卡盒现金支出仍为 450 加元，而现收现付为 300 加元。到目前为止，卡盒已多支付了150加元的现金。它还拥有 200 加元未使用的零售商购买信用。这些陈述并不意味着卡内余额已经消失。他们区分资源的持有位置。现收现付家庭保留了更多的银行现金，而其他家庭则拥有在零售商处预付的购买能力。该模型以名义面值记录后者，而不要求等值的现金退款、转售价或公允价值。最后购物月份是一个偏好假设。它不会导致卡过期。在计划购物停止后，单独更改报告窗口不会创建新的购买。遵循现金时间表，而不是一开始就将所有内容都净额累积现金图表从零月份开始，卡盒中支付了 450 加元，另一个卡盒中支付了零。在第 6 个月，现收现付线达到 300 加元。由于默认情况下不再有计划购买，因此两条线在第 12 个月保持不变。只有当该卡取代了原本需要现金的购物时，差异才会缩小。它不会仅仅因为又过去一个月而缩小。因此，收到 500 加元的名义余额与收到 500 加元的可消费银行现金是不同的。对于在未来购买之前有账单到期的家庭来说，即使该卡最终会被完全使用，最初的承诺也很重要。该比较不会计算紧急资金需求，也不会假设借款将自动支付费用。如果购买是通过债务融资的，则需要单独添加融资费用。核对差额，无需计算两次兑换 现金比较有一个紧凑的恒等式：额外的卡盒现金 = 为卡支付的价格 - 实际兑换的卡积分。支付450加元，兑换300加元，额外现金为150加元。兑换并不既是现金流入，又是购物费用的减少。它只是代替现金支付同一购买的部分费用。如果购买最终超过卡余额，未覆盖的金额需要现金充值。这些充值包含在卡盒现金系列中。他们在取差额时将相应部分的即用即付支出取消，留下上面的标识。瀑布显示了预付款和实际购买所替换的内容，以签署的现金差额结束。减去未使用的 200 加元也会错误地将限制信贷视为已退回银行帐户。 10% 的面值折扣仍需要 90% 的兑换才能赶上现金。当实际使用卡达到 450 加元的购买价格时，就会发生等额累积现金支出。即 500 加元面值的 90%。假设每月使用 50 加元，如果购物计划持续这么长时间，平等将首先在第九个月月底实现。默认计划在六个月后停止，因此在十二个月的窗口内不会达到该点。将计划购物延长至12个月，结果发生变化：进行600加元的匹配购买，首笔500加元通过卡支付，最后100加元需要现金充值。全用卡盒则需支付 450 加元 + 100 加元 = 550 加元，而按需付费则需支付 600 加元。其现金减免50加元，原面值折扣。在这种单卡模式中，不可能兑换超过面值的金额。最终图表将实际赎回从面值的 0% 调整到 100%。该曲线没有有效期或使用概率。它的零交叉是一个会计门槛，而不是建议花费更多以使该卡看起来很成功。将不需要的额外支出保留在声称的节省之外 该比较假设每一兑换的美元都以相同的价格替换已经计划的东西。如果一个家庭只是为了使用该卡而增加购买，则这两种情况不再获得相同的商品。额外的支出及其用途需要单独决定。同样，替代商店可能有不同的价格、可用性或旅行费用。零售商余额可能会限制购买地点，因此仅凭面值折扣无法建立最便宜的完整购物篮。该工具不会估计这些差异。保留现金也没有利息信用，没有费用或欺诈模式，也不存在零售商倒闭或卡丢失的可能性。仍然可用的卡在报告日期不会被宣布毫无价值。结果是对一项既定计划进行透明的付款方式比较，并单独显示剩余信用额。使用现金图表以及实际条款和购买计划 在将促销的标题折扣分配给预算之前，记录现金购买价格、可用面额、符合条件的购买和预期使用日期。检查实际条款和适用规则下未使用余额的情况。该场景的免费和无过期假设并不能确定任何真实卡的合法权利。 FCAC 的页面日期为 2026 年 10 月 23 日，并于 2026 年 10 月 25 日审查了本文，该页面将礼品卡与支付网络预付卡区分开来，并指出规则和例外情况可能取决于地点。该工具模拟零售商采购余额，不适用省级费用、到期或退款规则。在家庭记录中保留三个数字：支付的现金、用于购买的信用额和剩余信用额。他们共同解释了为什么折扣购买可以带来有利的最终现金结果，同时仍然留下不太灵活的可用现金。

0986111d38db154e0a19c07ddc1761f8033d8d55.src: Read the quotation basis before adding or subtracting amounts. Surrender cash and a conditional death payout serve different events, and a loan already deducted from a quote must not be deducted twice. Identify the amount, recipient and event on each quotation A policy statement can contain a large death-benefit figure and a smaller cash-value figure. Their labels matter before either amount enters a balance sheet or a spending plan. They describe different rights and circumstances. The Financial Consumer Agency of Canada’s life-insurance guide distinguishes a death benefit from the cash value associated with cancelling a permanent policy. It also notes that unpaid borrowing may affect the amount received on cancellation or by beneficiaries. The charts start with three invented amounts at one date: a complete conditional death quotation of CAD 400,000, a surrender quotation of CAD 50,000 and an existing insurer policy loan of CAD 20,000 including accrued interest. No actual policy is valued. The death quote means the entire quoted conditional amount, rather than base face to which a separate cash account is automatically added. Read whether the surrender quotation is before or after the loan debit The authored CAD 50,000 surrender quote is already after contract surrender charges, but before the existing loan and any tax. Deducting CAD 20,000 gives CAD 30,000 of surrender cash before tax. The waterfall shows that one reconciliation. The loan includes interest already accrued at the quote date. Adding another interest charge without a different dated calculation would repeat part of the debit. The original loan advance is also not another cash receipt today: it is existing borrowing, rather than a newly initiated transaction. For an actual statement, confirm which deductions the quoted amount already includes. If a CAD 30,000 figure is already after the loan, subtracting CAD 20,000 again would incorrectly reduce it to CAD 10,000. A similar check applies to charges already included in a quotation. This tool supplies no tax calculation or estimate of when a surrender payment would arrive. Apply the stated debit to the total conditional claim amount separately Using the same snapshot, the conditional death calculation is CAD 400,000 less CAD 20,000, or CAD 380,000 before any unmodeled adjustments. That is a different branch from full surrender. The model assumes a covered payable claim and no prior cancellation; it does not forecast a future date or policy value. Canada Life’s explanation of accessing cash value states that an unpaid insurer policy-loan balance, including interest, is deducted from the amount paid on surrender or death in its described arrangement. Its corporate ownership and tax discussion is not imported into this household teaching example. The total death quotation is not combined with the surrender quotation to create CAD 450,000 of available resources. Nor are the two after-loan amounts combined into CAD 410,000. Full surrender ends this example’s coverage; the conditional death amount belongs to the alternative claim event and a different recipient. Use the loan curve as a sensitivity, not a forecast of coverage The line chart changes only the assumed existing loan balance while holding the two gross quotation bases fixed. Each CAD 1 of additional debit reduces both separately calculated amounts by CAD 1. The horizontal axis represents alternative debt amounts, not passing years. For example, a CAD 10,000 balance leaves CAD 40,000 of surrender cash and CAD 390,000 of conditional death proceeds. A CAD 30,000 balance leaves CAD 20,000 and CAD 370,000 respectively. Those are independent snapshots; the chart neither creates a new loan nor simulates how interest accumulates. This teaching case requires the loan not to exceed the surrender quote, and the surrender quote not to exceed the total death quote. The controls reject inconsistent combinations and retain the last valid result. These arithmetic limits do not establish an insurer’s borrowing maximum, continuing coverage or treatment if a policy becomes underfunded. Keep guarantees, access methods and future values outside the quotation arithmetic The matrix varies hypothetical surrender quotes and existing-loan shares. A cell is the after-charge quotation less its assumed loan debit. N/A identifies a quotation outside the declared comparison, rather than a denied claim or a quote of zero. A policy loan, a withdrawal and a third-party loan secured by a policy are different arrangements. This page models only an existing insurer policy loan and two alternative settlement amounts. It does not assess access permissions, partial withdrawals, outside lenders, future premiums or interest charges after the quotation date. Canada Life’s participating-life explanation also distinguishes potential dividends from guarantees. No dividend scale or cash-value growth is assumed here. Premium totals alone do not supply the missing quotation, and no return on premiums is calculated from these three entered amounts. Use confirmed net amounts and payment conditions in a separate plan For a real review, obtain a dated quotation that identifies the policyowner, beneficiary, policy status, total payable benefit, surrender amount and loan including accrued interest. Establish whether the displayed figures are before or after the relevant debits. Different quote dates should not silently become one snapshot. Then separate an amount that could be received through surrender from a conditional payment following a covered death. The related family-protection guide examines the need for coverage, and the estate-liquidity guide examines payment timing. Neither question is answered solely by the larger number on a statement. For the fictional household, record CAD 30,000 as a potential receipt requiring surrender in a living cash worksheet. Record CAD 380,000 in a separate covered-death scenario. Keep each worksheet’s event assumption visible when adding other assets or obligations, so one policy is counted only once within each scenario. Finally, treat the displayed residuals as before-tax arithmetic. No policy tax basis, taxable gain, deduction or refund is estimated. No cancellation, withdrawal, loan or replacement is initiated. The point is to reconcile the amounts and avoid counting the same contractual resource twice before deciding how an actual quotation belongs in a household plan.
