These are equal at w = 4.425 ÷ 7.775, or about 56.91% city distance . Between those two shares, B uses fewer litres but A still has lower fuel cash. The signed line chart focuses on this cash comparison and its zero crossing. The equality describes the entered prices and consumption patterns; it does not set a universal city-driving threshold for any kind of vehicle. If both cost patterns are identical, every mix ties. Other inputs may have no equality anywhere between entirely highway and entirely city driving. The model states those cases explicitly. At zero annual distance, both fuel budgets are zero regardless of the mix. Change the driving mix and fuel price separately Raise city distance from 55% to 80%, holding total kilometres and both prices fixed. A’s weighted use becomes 9.2 L/100 km and B’s 7.1. Their annual fuel costs become CAD 3,128 and CAD 2,769 , so B now costs CAD 359 less in fuel. Alternatively, keep the default 55% city split but change B’s hypothetical fuel price to CAD 1.70. B’s fuel budget becomes CAD 2,456.50, CAD 331.50 below A. That test isolates price; the prior test isolated use. Neither establishes that a different fuel grade is suitable for a real vehicle. The matrix varies both city-distance share and B’s fuel price. Its fixed cases are a comparison aid rather than a forecast of local prices. Doubling annual kilometres doubles all modeled fuel cash and differences, but it does not move a unique city-share crossover when prices and consumption remain fixed. Replace the illustration with evidence from the actual vehicle and route Natural Resources Canada explains that standardized test ratings do not capture every road condition. Driving behaviour, weather, traffic, vehicle condition and powered accessories can affect actual consumption. The tool does not estimate those effects or add a universal adjustment percentage. For a household plan, record supported fuel requirements, relevant ratings or measured consumption, expected distance and a dated price assumption. A route change may alter both total kilometres and the city/highway mix. Test those effects explicitly instead of changing only a single combined rating. This page compares fuel spending. Purchase prices, loan interest, depreciation, maintenance, insurance, parking and eventual resale belong in a broader vehicle budget. A favourable fuel result alone does not establish a lower total ownership cost or justify a purchase premium. The related ownership and repair guides address those different cash decisions.
b9601c5d3a5f5a2b97ec71978f9aa4bebf6f4085.zh: 使用相同的行驶距离、支持的消耗估算以及每辆车所需的燃油价格来比较燃油现金。较低的每 100 公里升数只能回答该问题的一部分。在将标签复制到预算之前先阅读单位车辆的油耗等级描述了一段距离内使用的燃料。家庭燃料预算还需要行驶公里数和燃料价格。将一项评级与其他输入进行比较可能会得出错误的现金结论。加拿大自然资源部的 EnerGuide 解释称，综合消费评级反映了 55% 的城市驾驶和 45% 的高速公路驾驶。其年度燃油成本说明使用综合评级、20,000 公里和规定的燃油价格。这些约定可以帮助读者比较标签；它们并不是对任何特定家庭驾驶情况的衡量标准。这里的可编辑示例使用发明的车辆和燃料价格。车辆 A 在城市条件下分配为 10 升/100 公里，在高速公路上分配为 6 升/100 公里，每升 1.70 加元。 B在城市分配7，在高速公路分配7.5，每升1.95加元。这些既不是真实的制造商评级，也不是当前的泵价格。选择对比图案以使算术可见。按公里数而不是驾驶时间来衡量消耗量 默认的年行驶里程为 20,000 公里，其中城市条件下为 55%。这意味着 11,000 城市公里和 9,000 高速公路公里。相关重量是距离，因为消耗单位是每 100 公里升。将 55% 的驾驶时间花在交通上本身并不会产生相同的距离划分。对于A，选择的加权消耗量为10 × 0.55 + 6 × 0.45 = 8.2 L/100 km 。 B 为 7 × 0.55 + 7.5 × 0.45 = 7.225 L/100 km 。第一个图表将城市、高速公路和选定的混合比较分开。其标签将消费四舍五入到小数点后一位，而现金计算则保持完全精确。不要使用城市和高速公路数据的简单平均值，除非距离实际上是 50/50。同样，该说明性加权平均值并不试图根据四舍五入的已发布输入重建官方综合评级。使用支持的评级和适当的使用假设进行实际比较。将加权费率转换为年升，然后每年现金 转换为年升 = 年公里 ÷ 100 × 加权 L/100 公里 。单位很重要：直接将比率乘以 20,000 而不除以 100 会将燃料使用量夸大一百倍。因此，A 使用 20,000 ÷ 100 × 8.2 = 1,640 升。 B 使用 20,000 ÷ 100 × 7.225 = 1,445 升。在相同的假设距离内，B 的油耗减少了 195 升，比 A 少约 11.89%。应用每个输入的价格后，A 的年度燃油预算为 2,788 加元，B 为 2,817.75 加元。尽管 B 使用的燃油较少，但其燃油现金却高出 29.75 加元。差异在于每升 B 使用需支付 1.95 加元，而不是 1.70 加元。第二张图表将每个总计分为城市和高速公路公里的燃料。这些部分是同一年不同部分的成本，因此可以添加它们。升和美元不堆叠在一起。标题差异为 A 减去 B：正结果意味着 B 成本较低，而默认的负数 29.75 加元意味着 A 仅燃料成本较低。消费交叉和现金交叉不必同时发生。合成车辆在这两种情况下具有不同的优势。 A 在高速公路上每公里使用的燃料较少，而 B 在城市中使用的燃料较少。他们的距离加权消费率在城市份额为三分之一时相等：6 + 4w = 7.5 − 0.5w，其中 w 是城市距离分数。燃料现金使用不同的等式，因为每个费率都乘以自己的价格。 A 每百公里 10.20 加元 + 6.80w 加元； B 费用为每 100 公里 CAD 14.625 - CAD 0.975w。它们在 w = 4.425 ÷ 7.775 时相等，即大约 56.91% 的城市距离。在这两种份额之间，B 使用的升数较少，但 A 的燃油现金仍然较低。签名折线图重点关注现金比较及其零交叉。等式描述了输入的价格和消费模式；它没有为任何类型的车辆设定通用的城市驾驶门槛。如果两种成本模式相同，则每种组合都相关。其他输入可能在完全高速公路和完全城市驾驶之间没有任何平等。该模型明确说明了这些情况。在年距离为零的情况下，无论混合如何，两种燃料预算都为零。分别改变驾驶组合和燃油价格将城市距离从 55% 提高到 80%，保持总公里数和两个价格固定。 A 的加权使用量变为 9.2 L/100 km，B 的加权使用量为 7.1。他们每年的燃油成本分别为 3,128 加元和 2,769 加元，因此 B 现在的燃油成本减少了 359 加元。或者，保留默认的 55% 城市分割，但将 B 的假设燃油价格更改为 1.70 加元。 B 的燃油预算变为 2,456.50 加元，比 A 低 331.50 加元。该测试隔离了价格；事先测试隔离使用。两者都没有证明不同的燃油等级适合真实的车辆。该矩阵会改变城市距离份额和 B 的燃油价格。其固定案例是一种比较辅助工具，而不是对当地价格的预测。年公里数加倍会使所有建模的燃油现金和差异加倍，但当价格和消费保持固定时，它不会改变独特的城市份额交叉。将插图替换为实际车辆和路线的证据 加拿大自然资源部解释说，标准化测试评级并不能涵盖所有道路状况。驾驶行为、天气、交通、车辆状况和动力配件都会影响实际消耗。该工具不会估计这些影响或添加通用调整百分比。对于家庭计划，记录支持的燃料需求、相关评级或测量消耗、预期距离和日期的价格假设。路线变更可能会改变总公里数和城市/高速公路组合。明确测试这些效果，而不是仅更改单个组合评级。本页比较燃料支出。购买价格、贷款利息、折旧、维护、保险、停车和最终转售属于更广泛的车辆预算。仅凭良好的燃油结果并不能降低总拥有成本或证明购买溢价合理。相关的所有权和维修指南解决了这些不同的现金决策。

85dc6aac2477ba45cd1bb62e88794726eca52bdf.src: A CAD capital-property calculation needs dated CAD proceeds, cost and expenses. A USD profit translated at one rate can omit the currency change on the original cost. Give the cost and proceeds separate conversion dates A USD statement can show a clear profit while leaving a Canadian-dollar record incomplete. The amount paid, the sale proceeds and the relevant expenses need compatible units before they can be reconciled. CRA’s capital-gains guidance says to convert foreign-currency proceeds using the rate at sale, the adjusted cost base using the rate at acquisition, and disposition expenses using the rate when incurred. This article isolates one purchase followed by a full disposition, with no later adjusted-cost changes. The acquisition input includes any eligible costs incurred on that same purchase date. Disposition expenses are entered separately after conversion to CAD. The example does not rebuild a pooled cost base from several purchases or later adjustments. All rates here are invented. The Bank of Canada’s rate page expresses its foreign quotes as one unit of foreign currency converted into CAD and describes them as indicative averages. The tool uses that clearly stated quote direction without importing a current quote or assuming a bank would execute at an indicative rate. Reconcile a single-purchase example in CAD The authored example starts with USD 10,000 of acquisition cost and an acquisition-date rate of CAD 1.25 for USD 1. That produces a historical CAD cost of 10,000 × 1.25, or CAD 12,500. The full disposition has USD 12,000 of gross proceeds. Its separately entered sale-date rate is CAD 1.35 for USD 1, producing CAD 16,200 of translated proceeds. Eligible disposition expenses have already been converted and are entered as CAD 50. The first waterfall therefore computes CAD 16,200 minus CAD 12,500 minus CAD 50, giving a CAD 3,650 arithmetic gain before any inclusion rate or personal tax calculation. Each number has its own role. The acquisition amount is a historical cost record, the translated proceeds describe the disposition value, and the expense reduces the result once. The three headline metrics should not be added together as household assets. Explain the currency effect on the original cost The USD change in this example is 12,000 minus 10,000, or USD 2,000. Translating only that difference at the sale rate gives CAD 2,700 before the CAD expense. It leaves another part of the dated CAD reconciliation unexplained. The original USD 10,000 cost is affected by the change between the two rates. Multiplying it by 1.35 minus 1.25 gives CAD 1,000. The second waterfall adds CAD 2,700 and CAD 1,000, then subtracts the CAD 50 expense, reaching the same CAD 3,650 result. That is one exact algebraic decomposition. The USD-change term is translated at the full sale rate, so it already incorporates the interaction between the USD change and the currency movement. Adding another interaction amount would count part of the result twice. The decomposition explains the record. It does not identify two separate deposits, attribute a trading skill or calculate the payoff from an actual currency hedge. Zero USD difference does not require zero CAD difference Set USD gross proceeds equal to the original USD 10,000 acquisition cost, while keeping the default acquisition rate, sale rate and CAD expense. The USD difference becomes zero. The translated CAD proceeds are now CAD 13,500. Historical CAD cost remains CAD 12,500. After the CAD 50 expense, the arithmetic CAD gain is CAD 950. No USD price profit is needed for that result. The signed bars keep the equal-USD condition and vary the sale rate. At a rate of CAD 1.00 per USD, the arithmetic result is negative CAD 2,550. At the acquisition rate of 1.25, only the CAD 50 expense remains as a negative result. At a sale rate of 1.50, the arithmetic gain is CAD 2,450. These are separate stress cases. A negative value is not automatically an eligible capital loss, and the chart does not test restrictions, other transactions or special property rules. It also assigns no probability to any currency path. Keep a tax record and a bank-cash plan on their own bases The matrix changes gross USD proceeds and the sale-date rate together. Its column labels are USD amounts, its row labels are CAD-per-USD rates, and its cell values are CAD arithmetic results. The original purchase-date cost remains fixed. A CAD translation used to prepare a record is not proof that the sale proceeds were exchanged into CAD. If settlement produces USD cash that is retained, a later exchange or disposition of that cash creates another record question outside this model. Conversion spreads, actual bank receipts and spending dates require their own ledger. The calculator also stops before tax. It uses no inclusion rate, tax bracket, loss deduction, foreign tax credit or refund estimate. A registered-account transaction, income-account treatment, several acquisition dates, reinvestment or later ACB adjustments would require a different scope. Retain the purchase evidence, its CAD conversion, any subsequent cost adjustments, the sale evidence and separately converted expenses. A single current exchange rate cannot reconstruct that history from a USD statement’s net profit alone. The CRA page reviewed on 25 October 2026 contains 2025-return material. Its conversion framework supports this limited educational example; the tool does not prepare a return or determine the treatment of a proposed transaction.
85dc6aac2477ba45cd1bb62e88794726eca52bdf.zh: 加元资本财产计算需要注明日期的加元收益、成本和费用。按一种汇率换算的美元利润可以忽略原始成本的货币变化。将成本和收益分开转换日期美元报表可以显示明确的利润，同时留下不完整的加元记录。支付的金额、销售收入和相关费用需要兼容的单位才能对账。 CRA的资本利得指引称，外币收益使用出售时的汇率进行兑换，调整后的成本基础使用购买时的汇率进行兑换，处置费用则使用发生时的汇率进行兑换。本文隔离了一次购买和随后的完整处置，之后没有调整成本变化。收购输入包括在同一购买日期发生的任何合格成本。处置费用在转换为 CAD 后单独输入。该示例不会通过多次采购或以后的调整来重建汇总成本基础。这里的所有费率都是发明的。加拿大央行的汇率页面将其外国报价表示为转换为加元的一外币单位，并将其描述为指示性平均值。该工具使用明确规定的报价方向，无需导入当前报价或假设银行将按指示性利率执行。协调 CAD 中的单次采购示例 编写的示例以 10,000 美元的采购成本和 1 美元的 1.25 CAD 的采购日期汇率开始。这将产生 10,000 × 1.25 的历史 CAD 成本，或 12,500 CAD。全部处置的收益总额为 12,000 美元。其单独输入的销售日期汇率为 1.35 加元兑 1 美元，折算后收益为 16,200 加元。符合条件的处置费用已转换并输入为 50 加元。因此，第一个瀑布计算为 16,200 加元减去 12,500 加元再减去 50 加元，在任何包含率或个人税计算之前获得 3,650 加元算术收益。每个数字都有自己的作用。购置金额是历史成本记录，折算收益描述处置价值，费用减少一次结果。这三个主要指标不应作为家庭资产加在一起。解释货币对原始成本的影响 本例中的美元变动是 12,000 减去 10,000，即 2,000 美元。仅按销售价格折算该差额，扣除加元费用即可得到 2,700 加元。它留下了过时的加元调节的另一部分未解释的内容。原来的 10,000 美元成本受到两个汇率之间变化的影响。乘以 1.35 减去 1.25 得到 1,000 加元。第二个瀑布将 2,700 加元和 1,000 加元相加，然后减去 50 加元费用，得到相同的 3,650 加元结果。这是一种精确的代数分解。美元变动术语按全部销售汇率换算，因此它已经包含了美元变动和货币变动之间的相互作用。添加另一个交互量会将部分结果计算两次。分解解释了记录。它不识别两个单独的存款、归因交易技能或计算实际货币对冲的收益。零美元差额并不要求零加元差额 将美元总收益设置为等于原始 10,000 美元购置成本，同时保留默认购置率、销售率和加元费用。美元差额为零。换算后的加元收益现为 13,500 加元。历史加元成本仍为 12,500 加元。扣除 50 加元费用后，算术加元收益为 950 加元。该结果不需要美元价格利润。签名金条保持等值美元条件并改变售价。按照 1 美元兑 1 加元的汇率计算，算术结果为负 2,550 加元。当收购率为 1.25 时，只有 50 加元的费用仍为负结果。如果售价为 1.50，算术收益为 2,450 加元。这些是单独的压力案例。负值并不自动构成合格的资本损失，并且该图表不测试限制、其他交易或特殊财产规则。它还没有为任何货币路径分配概率。根据自己的基础保留税务记录和银行现金计划 该矩阵会同时更改美元总收益和销售日期利率。其列标签是美元金额，行标签是加元兑美元汇率，单元格值是加元算术结果。原始购买日期成本保持不变。用于准备记录的 CAD 翻译并不能证明销售收入已兑换成 CAD。如果结算产生保留的美元现金，则该现金的后续交换或处置会在该模型之外产生另一个创纪录的问题。兑换利差、实际银行收据和支出日期需要有自己的分类账。计算器也会在税前停止。它不使用包含率、税级、损失扣除、外国税收抵免或退款估算。注册账户交易、收入账户处理、多个收购日期、再投资或后来的 ACB 调整将需要不同的范围。保留购买证据、其 CAD 转换、任何后续成本调整、销售证据和单独转换的费用​​。单一的当前汇率无法仅根据美元报表的净利润来重建历史。 2026 年 10 月 25 日审核的 CRA 页面包含 2025 年申报材料。它的转换框架支持这个有限的教育示例；该工具不准备回报或确定拟议交易的处理方式。

381a32e23c2fa473dfb36ea7eeda40f1c595951e.src: An interest rate is multiplied by the debt outstanding when it applies. A simple average discards that pairing, so rate timing can change both total interest and the household payment calendar. Keep each rate beside the amount of debt to which it applies A four-year average interest rate can hide the order in which rates occur. If principal falls during the loan, a high rate in an early year applies to more money than the same high rate near the end. Counting how often each rate appears is therefore insufficient to identify the total dollar interest. The Financial Consumer Agency of Canada’s personal-loan guide explains that borrowing involves principal, interest, payment terms and potentially fees. This illustration keeps those components distinct while using its own simplified repayment rule. It is not a reproduction of a lender’s loan quotation. The model borrows CAD 24,000 and repays CAD 6,000 of principal at the end of each of four whole years. Each year’s interest is paid separately at the same checkpoint. The amount of principal repaid is fixed, while the total annual payment changes with that year’s interest. Reverse the rate blocks without changing their arithmetic average Block A has a hypothetical annual rate of 10% and block B has a hypothetical rate of 6%. The A-first sequence uses 10%, 10%, 6% and 6%. The B-first sequence uses 6%, 6%, 10% and 10%. Each sequence contains two years at each rate, so both have a simple average of 8%. Neither rate is an offer or a forecast. Swapping their order leaves the same four input rates, but changes which rate meets the larger early loan balances. The principal chart is shared by both sequences. Opening balances for the four interest periods are CAD 24,000, CAD 18,000, CAD 12,000 and CAD 6,000. After the final CAD 6,000 principal repayment, the loan is zero. No unpaid interest is added to the balance, and neither sequence receives a larger repayment simply because its interest bill is lower. Because principal repayments occur annually, the opening debt remains outstanding throughout each full year. Dividing an annual payment by twelve could suggest a monthly saving allocation, but it would not convert this into a monthly repayment loan. Actual monthly principal reductions would change the interest calculation and need their own schedule. Calculate interest on each year’s opening balance In the A-first case, the first two interest bills are CAD 2,400 and CAD 1,800. The later 6% rate applies to CAD 12,000 and CAD 6,000, producing CAD 720 and CAD 360. Total interest is CAD 5,280. In the B-first case, 6% on the larger early balances produces CAD 1,440 and CAD 1,080. The later 10% rate produces CAD 1,200 and CAD 600. Total interest is CAD 4,320. The difference is CAD 960 despite the matching 8% simple average. The waterfall subtracts the B-first interest from the A-first interest one year at a time. It adds CAD 960 and CAD 720 in the first two years, then subtracts CAD 480 and CAD 240 in the last two. The early additions exceed the later reductions because more principal was outstanding when the early rate difference applied. Add principal back when assessing the household cash calendar Interest is the borrowing-cost component here, but it is not the full amount leaving the household account. Every annual payment also returns CAD 6,000 of principal. The payment bars include both parts so they can be read as cash requirements. The A-first annual payments are CAD 8,400, CAD 7,800, CAD 6,720 and CAD 6,360. Their total is CAD 29,280: the original CAD 24,000 principal plus CAD 5,280 interest. The B-first total is CAD 28,320, including the same principal and CAD 4,320 interest. The shared principal component cancels when comparing total costs, but it still needs funding on every due date. A household cannot reserve only the interest amounts and assume the loan will disappear. This example also does not assume that money saved on an earlier payment is invested, spent, or used for an additional principal repayment. Such choices would change the modeled cash flows. An average rate applied to average-looking debt is another assumption Using a constant 8% rate on the actual four opening balances would produce CAD 4,800 of interest. That is a third, different rate path. It sits between the two default totals, but it is not equal to either of them. Replacing the original order with an average has changed the calculation. The four opening balances sum to CAD 60,000 across the four one-year exposures. This does not mean the household borrowed CAD 60,000: the same declining loan is observed repeatedly. Dividing each interest total by that balance sum gives 8.8% and 7.2% respectively, making the different balance weights visible. Those last percentages are arithmetic summaries for this invented schedule, not regulated APRs, quoted annual borrowing costs or a substitute for valuing the dated payments. For this assumed balance-based interest rule, applying 8% to the full original CAD 24,000 for all four years would ignore the principal repayments entirely. A contract that explicitly uses a flat original-principal basis is a different calculation. Use the rate-pair matrix without turning the scenarios into a forecast The matrix replaces the two rate blocks while retaining the initial principal and four equal repayments. A positive cell means A-first interest exceeds B-first interest. A negative cell means the reverse. Matching rates produce zero difference, as does a zero initial loan. The direction follows the pairing. Putting the larger rate first applies it to more principal under this repayment schedule. That is a conditional calculation, rather than a claim about which direction market rates will move. The tool does not let the household choose a future rate path or lock in rates shown only as assumptions. An actual loan may instead keep total payments level, change payments after a reset, calculate interest daily, charge fees or capitalize unpaid interest. Those terms can change the principal path and require another model. Record the rate basis, outstanding debt and repayment rule together before using a rate average in a budget. The five views isolate that relationship while keeping total interest, principal repayment and affordability as separate planning questions.
381a32e23c2fa473dfb36ea7eeda40f1c595951e.zh: 适用时，利率乘以未偿债务。简单平均法会放弃这种配对，因此利率时机可能会改变总利息和家庭付款日历。将每个利率放在其适用的债务金额旁边。四年平均利率可以隐藏利率发生的顺序。如果本金在贷款期间下降，那么早年的高利率比临近年底的相同高利率适用的资金更多。因此，计算每种利率出现的频率不足以确定美元利息总额。加拿大金融消费者机构的个人贷款指南解释说，借款涉及本金、利息、付款条件和潜在费用。该图在使用其自己的简化还款规则的同时使这些组件保持独特。它不是贷款机构贷款报价的复制。该模型借款 24,000 加元，并在四年结束时偿还本金 6,000 加元。每年的利息在同一检查点单独支付。偿还的本金金额是固定的，而每年的还款总额则随着当年的利息而变化。反转利率块而不改变其算术平均数 A 块的假设年利率为 10%，B 块的假设年利率为 6%。 A-first 序列使用 10%、10%、6% 和 6%。 B优先序列使用6%、6%、10%和10%。每个序列在每个比率下都包含两年，因此两者的简单平均值均为 8%。这两种利率都不是报价或预测。交换顺序会留下相同的四个输入利率，但会改变满足较大早期贷款余额的利率。主要图表由两个序列共享。四个计息期的期初余额分别为 24,000 加元、18,000 加元、12,000 加元和 6,000 加元。最终偿还 6,000 加元本金后，贷款为零。余额中不会添加未付利息，并且这两个序列都不会仅仅因为其利息费用较低而获得更大的还款额。由于本金偿还每年进行一次，因此每年全年期初债务均未偿还。将每年还款额除以十二可能会建议每月进行储蓄分配，但不会将其转换为每月还款贷款。实际每月本金减少会改变利息计算，需要自己的时间表。计算每年期初余额的利息 在 A-first 情况下，前两笔利息分别为 2,400 加元和 1,800 加元。后面的 6% 利率适用于 12,000 加元和 6,000 加元，分别为 720 加元和 360 加元。总利息为 5,280 加元。在 B-first 情况下，较大的早期余额的 6% 产生 1,440 加元和 1,080 加元。后面的 10% 利率产生 1,200 加元和 600 加元。总利息为 4,320 加元。尽管匹配 8% 的简单平均值，但差异为 960 加元。瀑布每年从 A 优先利息中减去 B 优先利息。前两年加960加元和720加元，后两年减480加元和240加元。早期增加的金额超过了后来减少的金额，因为当应用早期利率差异时，更多的本金未偿还。在评估家庭现金日历时加回本金 利息是此处的借贷成本组成部分，但不是离开家庭帐户的全部金额。每每年还款还可以返还 6,000 加元的本金。付款条包括这两个部分，因此可以将其解读为现金需求。 A 级年付款分别为 8,400 加元、7,800 加元、6,720 加元和 6,360 加元。他们的总额为 29,280 加元：原始本金 24,000 加元加上利息 5,280 加元。 B-first 总额为 28,320 加元，包括相同的本金和 4,320 加元的利息。比较总成本时，共享主成分取消，但在每个到期日仍然需要资金。家庭不能只保留利息金额并假设贷款将会消失。此示例也不假设早期付款中节省的资金被投资、花费或用于额外的本金偿还。这些选择将改变建模的现金流量。另一种假设是对看似平均的债务应用平均利率，对实际四项期初余额使用 8% 的固定利率将产生 4,800 加元的利息。这是第三种不同的利率路径。它位于两个默认总计之间，但不等于其中任何一个。用平均值替换原始订单改变了计算方式。四项一年期风险敞口的四项期初余额总计为 60,000 加元。这并不意味着该家庭借了 60,000 加元：同样的贷款下降现象屡见不鲜。将每笔利息总额除以余额总和分别得出 8.8% 和 7.2%，从而使不同的余额权重可见。最后的百分比是本发明时间表的算术摘要，不是受监管的年利率、引用的年度借款成本或对到期付款进行评估的替代品。对于这个假设的基于余额的利息规则，在所有四年内对原始 24,000 加元全额应用 8% 将完全忽略本金偿还。明确使用固定原始本金基础的合同是一种不同的计算。使用利率对矩阵，而不将场景转化为预测 该矩阵替换了两个利率块，同时保留初始本金和四笔等额还款。正细胞意味着 A-优先兴趣超过 B-优先兴趣。负细胞意味着相反。匹配利率产生零差异，就像零初始贷款一样。方向遵循配对。在此还款计划下，首先将较高的利率应用于更多的本金。这是一种有条件的计算，而不是关于市场利率将朝哪个方向移动的断言。该工具不允许家庭选择未来的利率路径或锁定仅作为假设显示的利率。实际贷款可能会保持总付款水平、重置后更改付款、每日计算利息、收取费用或将未付利息资本化。这些术语可能会改变主要路径并需要另一种模型。在预算中使用平均利率之前，将利率基础、未偿债务和还款规则记录在一起。这五种观点将这种关系隔离开来，同时将总利息、本金偿还和负担能力作为单独的规划问题。

f0f54fb296741728573151011e1a6faae3c02745.src: A cheaper price applies only to the energy moved into that period. Use consumption weights and keep unchanged charges separate before estimating the whole-bill saving. Identify which part of the bill a timing change can affect A lower off-peak energy price can be useful, but it does not apply automatically to every kilowatt-hour or every charge on the monthly bill. The planning calculation begins with the amount of energy that can move and the charges that remain unchanged. The Ontario Energy Board’s bill explanation distinguishes electricity charges that depend on time of use from other bill components. It also explains that some delivery charges are fixed while others vary. That supports reading the parts of the bill separately, rather than treating the entire invoice as one energy price. This tool uses a simplified, original three-period bill: hypothetical energy prices of 20 cents/kWh on-peak, 12 cents mid-peak and 8 cents off-peak, plus CAD 20 assumed unchanged each month. These are not current Ontario prices or a utility quote. Other variable delivery charges, losses, demand charges, taxes, tiers and rebates are outside the calculation. Weight the energy prices by actual use instead of averaging the rate labels The starting allocation is 280 kWh on-peak, 210 kWh mid-peak and 210 kWh off-peak, totalling 700 kWh. The energy costs are CAD 56, CAD 25.20 and CAD 16.80, respectively. Adding them gives a variable energy charge of CAD 98 . The consumption-weighted energy price is CAD 98 ÷ 700 kWh, or 14 cents/kWh . That differs from the unweighted average of the three rate labels: (20 + 12 + 8) ÷ 3, or about 13.33 cents. The household has not used equal quantities in each period, so equal weighting answers a different question. Adding the unchanged CAD 20 produces the simplified baseline bill of CAD 118 . The fixed amount has a separate role; it is not another energy rate applied to the 700 kWh. Likewise, this energy-only weighted rate is not a complete all-in rate for a real utility bill. A quarter of on-peak use is not a quarter of total use The default shift is 25% of the original on-peak 280 kWh. That moves 70 kWh to off-peak. Since the entire month contains 700 kWh, the shifted amount is only 10% of total consumption . After the shift, on-peak and mid-peak use are both 210 kWh, while off-peak use rises to 280 kWh. Total energy remains 700 kWh. The first chart makes that conservation visible: the amount removed from one period appears in the other rather than disappearing from the bill. This is a timing example, not an energy-efficiency improvement. It assumes that moving the selected use does not increase other consumption, change the service provided or require equipment spending. The tool cannot establish whether a particular household can actually move that fraction of its use. Subtract the new charge from the charge avoided The shifted 70 kWh would cost 70 × CAD 0.20 = CAD 14 on-peak. In the off-peak period it costs 70 × CAD 0.08 = CAD 5.60. The saving is therefore CAD 8.40 per modeled month , which is also 70 kWh × the CAD 0.12 price difference. The waterfall keeps both sides of that change visible. Avoiding the original charge is only the first step; the energy still needs to be paid for in the new period. The unchanged charges and all energy that did not move cancel when comparing the two allocations. The after-shift energy charge is CAD 89.60. With the unchanged CAD 20, the simplified bill becomes CAD 109.60 . No payment or rebate of CAD 8.40 is assumed; that amount is cash spending avoided relative to the original allocation. Keep the denominator beside each percentage The off-peak unit price is 60% below the on-peak price in this authored example: (20 − 8) ÷ 20. That comparison applies to the price of the 70 kWh moved, not to all 700 kWh or the complete bill. The variable energy charge falls by CAD 8.40 ÷ CAD 98, or about 8.57% . The simplified whole bill falls by CAD 8.40 ÷ CAD 118, or about 7.12% . The consumption-weighted energy price changes from 14.0 to 12.8 cents/kWh, while total use stays fixed. All three percentages can be correct at once because their denominators differ. Describing the 60% unit-price reduction as a 60% bill saving would apply a limited change to a much larger base. Increase the unchanged monthly amount from CAD 20 to CAD 60 and the dollar saving remains CAD 8.40. The baseline bill becomes CAD 158, so its percentage reduction is about 5.32%. An unchanged charge affects the share of the bill saved even though it does not alter the energy-cost difference. Test the achievable shift and price spread separately The final chart varies the fraction of original on-peak use moved from zero to 100%, keeping the entered quantities, rates and unchanged charge otherwise fixed. The original bill remains a reference line. At zero shift the two bills coincide; with no on-peak use, every shift setting has the same result. The period names alone do not enforce a lower price in the arithmetic. If the entered off-peak rate exceeds the on-peak rate, moving energy raises the modeled bill and the saving metric becomes negative. If the two rates match, timing alone produces no energy saving. Changing only the selected shift updates the headline result and allocation bars while leaving the full-range comparison curve in place. The curve does not assign a likelihood to any amount of shifted use or establish what a household’s appliances can achieve. Use the actual bill before putting a saving into the household plan Record the relevant energy quantities and price periods from the bill. Identify a feasible amount of use to move rather than assuming every kWh can shift. Separate unchanged charges from all other charges that vary. Compare the complete applicable tariff and any switching or equipment costs. Review different seasons before projecting an annual saving. Twelve identical example months would produce CAD 100.80 of timing savings. That is a repeated-case calculation, not an annual forecast: usage, rates, period definitions and the amount that can move may differ through the year. The illustration does not compare actual electricity plans or determine eligibility for them. It explains how a selected timing change passes through an intentionally simple bill. The related utility-payment and upgrade guides address different questions about payment schedules and changes in energy use.
f0f54fb296741728573151011e1a6faae3c02745.zh: 更便宜的价格仅适用于进入该时期的能源。在估计整个账单节省之前，使用消耗权重并保持不变的费用分开。确定时间变化会影响账单的哪一部分 较低的非高峰能源价格可能很有用，但它不会自动适用于每月账单上的每千瓦时或每笔费用。规划计算从可移动的能量和保持不变的电荷量开始。安大略能源委员会的账单解释将取决于使用时间的电费与其他账单组成部分区分开来。它还解释说，有些运费是固定的，而另一些则不同。这支持单独阅读账单的各个部分，而不是将整个发票视为一份能源价格。该工具使用简化的原始三期账单：假设能源价格为高峰 20 美分/千瓦时、中峰 12 美分、非高峰 8 美分，加上假设每月 20 加元不变。这些不是安大略省的当前价格或公用事业报价。其他可变运费、损失、需求费用、税费、等级和回扣均不在计算范围内。按实际使用情况衡量能源价格，而不是对费率标签进行平均 起始分配为高峰 280 千瓦时、中峰 210 千瓦时和非高峰 210 千瓦时，总计 700 千瓦时。能源成本分别为 56 加元、25.20 加元和 16.80 加元。添加它们会产生 98 加元的可变能量费用。消耗加权能源价格为 98 加元 ÷ 700 千瓦时，即 14 美分/千瓦时。这与三个费率标签的未加权平均值不同：(20 + 12 + 8) ÷ 3，即约 13.33 美分。该家庭在每个时期都没有使用相同的数量，因此相同的权重回答了不同的问题。添加未改变的CAD 20产生CAD 118的简化基线账单。固定金额有单独的作用；这不是另一个适用于 700 kWh 的能源费率。同样，这种仅能源加权费率并不是实际公用事业账单的完整总费率。高峰用电量的四分之一并非总用电量的四分之一 默认转换为原始高峰用电量 280 kWh 的 25%。这会将 70 千瓦时的电量移至非高峰时段。由于整个月有700度电，转移量仅占总用电量的10%。转变后，高峰和中峰用电量均为210千瓦时，非高峰用电量升至280千瓦时。总能量仍为 700 kWh。第一个图表使这种保护可见：从一个时期删除的金额出现在另一个时期，而不是从账单中消失。这是一个时间示例，而不是能源效率的改进。它假设移动选定的用途不会增加其他消耗、改变所提供的服务或需要设备支出。该工具无法确定特定家庭是否真的可以转移其部分使用量。从避免的电量中减去新电量 转移的 70 kWh 的费用为 70 × 0.20 加元 = 高峰时段 14 加元。非高峰期费用为 70 × 0.08 加元 = 5.60 加元。因此，每个模型月可节省 8.40 加元，即 70 千瓦时 × 0.12 加元的价差。瀑布使变化的双方都可见。避免原始电荷只是第一步；新时期能源仍需付出。比较两种分配时，未变化的费用和所有未移动的能源被取消。下班后能源费为 89.60 加元。在 20 CAD 不变的情况下，简化账单变为 109.60 CAD 。假定不支付或回扣 8.40 加元；该金额是相对于原始分配避免的现金支出。将分母保留在每个百分比旁边 在本示例中，非高峰单价比高峰单价低 60%：(20 − 8) ÷ 20。该比较适用于移动的 70 kWh 的价格，而不是所有 700 kWh 或完整的账单。可变能源费用下降 8.40 加元 ÷ 98 加元，即约 8.57%。简化后的整体账单下跌 8.40 加元 ÷ 118 加元，即约 7.12%。消耗加权能源价格从 14.0 美分/千瓦时变化至 12.8 美分/千瓦时，而总使用量保持不变。所有三个百分比都可以同时正确，因为它们的分母不同。将 60% 的单价降低描述为 60% 的账单节省，将对更大的基数进行有限的改变。将不变的每月金额从 20 加元增加到 60 加元，节省的金额仍为 8.40 加元。基准账单变为158加元，因此其减少百分比约为5.32%。费用不变会影响节省的账单份额，即使它不会改变能源成本差异。分别测试可实现的转变和价差 最终图表将原始高峰使用比例从 0 更改为 100%，同时保持输入的数量、费率和不变费用不变。原始法案仍然是参考线。在零位移时，两个钞票重合；由于没有高峰使用，每个班次设置都有相同的结果。期间名称本身并不强制算术中的较低价格。如果输入的非高峰费率超过高峰费率，则移动能源会提高建模费用，并且节省指标变为负数。如果两个速率匹配，仅靠计时并不能节省能源。仅更改选定的班次会更新标题结果和分配栏，同时保留全范围比较曲线。该曲线并未指定任何数量的转移使用的可能性，也没有确定家用电器可以实现的目标。在将储蓄纳入家庭计划之前使用实际账单 从账单中记录相关能源数量和价格周期。确定可行的移动用量，而不是假设每千瓦时都可以移动。将不变的费用与所有其他变化的费用分开。比较完整的适用关税和任何转换或设备成本。在预测年度节省之前回顾不同的季节。 12 个相同的示例月份将节省 100.80 加元的时间。这是重复案例的计算，而不是年度预测：使用量、费率、期间定义和可移动的金额在一年中可能会有所不同。该插图并不比较实际的电力计划或确定其资格。它解释了选定的时间变化如何通过故意简单的法案。相关的公用事业支付和升级指南解决了有关支付时间表和能源使用变化的不同问题。

6708ffcda7501c0f7f8da40938278dc69f410ebe.src: Time released from a task can improve quality, learning or life outside work. Additional household cash requires a separate compensation arrangement and actual receipts after relevant costs. Read the work-time observation before turning it into money The Bank of Canada's 2026 Q3 Canadian Survey of Consumer Expectations included questions about AI use at work, time required for tasks and uses of the time respondents felt they had released. Those answers provide context about workers' reported experiences. The report was released on 19 October 2026. Online responses were collected from 5 to 27 August, and follow-up interviews ran from 24 August to 4 September. The reference quarter, collection period and release date are different pieces of information. The two survey charts are categorical summaries from that release. They are not a daily series, a record of each respondent's working hours or an experiment assigning people randomly to use AI. The article does not infer an effect on wages, paid working time or household income from those summaries. The separate calculator begins with independently chosen weekly time and compensation assumptions. It does not turn an aggregate survey median into a personal prediction or transfer a reported time-use percentage into a revenue conversion rate. The two hour measures have different definitions The first source panel reports 2.8 hours per week for active AI use and 4.7 hours for additional time respondents estimated they would need to complete their tasks without AI. Both retain the source's interpolated-median label. Active weekly time is estimated from each respondent's reported duration category and frequency of use. The source uses category midpoints and assigns 7.5 hours to the open-ended daily category above six hours. The aggregate therefore depends on an explicit estimation method rather than a time-clock record. The other measure asks about additional work time in a hypothetical week without access to AI. It is a respondent counterfactual estimate. It does not become a directly observed causal productivity gain merely because it is summarized numerically. Subtracting the active-use median from the additional-time median would not establish an individual's net saving. The questions describe different roles, and the difference of aggregate medians is not automatically the median of individual differences. Likewise, multiplying 4.7 by an assumed wage would introduce compensation assumptions absent from the survey. Time-use shares overlap and do not allocate a single pie The second source panel asks respondents to select every applicable use of the time they felt AI had helped release. The listed options concern task quality, additional tasks, work-life balance, learning or training, and creative work. Because more than one answer is allowed, these percentages are not mutually exclusive groups. The five displayed shares sum to 209.20%, which is compatible with a multiple-response question. Renormalizing them to 100% would answer a different question and hide that design. The percentages retain the denominator of respondents to this saved-time question in the AI-work module. They are not percentages of all Canadians, shares of the working week or the probability that a particular worker will receive additional pay. The aggregate extract does not identify response overlaps or how many hours were assigned to each use. Reporting additional tasks also does not establish additional compensation. A fixed-pay employee can complete more work while receiving the same salary. Enter a separate route from usable time to actual receipts The default scenario independently assumes three usable hours released per week across forty-six weeks. That creates 138 hours of potential capacity. It is deliberately separate from the survey's 4.7-hour estimate. The reader then assumes 50% of that capacity becomes additional paid work, producing sixty-nine paid hours. At CAD 50 of additional gross cash received per converted hour, those hours generate CAD 3,450 of extra receipts during the modeled year. The annual out-of-pocket tool cost is independently set to CAD 240. The waterfall deducts that cost once, leaving CAD 3,210 of cash change before personal tax and other work costs. It is not after-tax take-home pay, business profit or an automatic tax deduction. Every link is a separate assumption: capacity must be usable, additional work must exist, someone must agree to pay for it and cash must actually arrive within the horizon. An unpaid invoice is not counted as a receipt. The example makes no claim about a market hourly rate, demand or the probability of achieving the selected conversion. A fixed salary can leave cash unchanged while time has value The comparison path assumes the same out-of-pocket tool cost but no overtime, bonus or salary increase. Additional receipts are therefore zero, and the narrow cash change is negative CAD 240 at the defaults. This does not mean released time has no value. It may improve quality, reduce pressure, support training or leave more time outside work. Those benefits are simply not priced as additional income in this cash calculation. If an employer pays the tool cost, enter zero personal out-of-pocket cost for the relevant comparison. If compensation changes through an actual agreement, use the confirmed receipt amount and timing. Do not assume that an employee automatically receives an hourly payment for every hour a task takes less time. The paid-work and fixed-pay bars compare defined arrangements. A negative result means the entered cost exceeds additional receipts in that narrow scenario, rather than that the person's total household earnings are negative. Existing salary, ordinary expenses and taxes are outside the chart. Test conversion and cost before adding the result to a budget The matrix varies paid conversion and annual out-of-pocket cost while retaining the independently chosen weekly time, weeks and gross receipts per converted hour. A zero-conversion row makes the cost visible even when no extra paid work materializes. The official survey panels remain fixed when those controls change. An editable scenario is not a revision to the published evidence, and a favorable scenario cell does not establish that the worker can achieve it. Before including extra cash in a personal plan, confirm the work arrangement, actual compensation, collection timing and associated expenses. Determine the relevant personal-tax and benefit effects separately. A pre-tax cash comparison alone does not tell the household how much can safely be spent or saved. The five charts connect the questions without collapsing them: reported hours, overlapping uses of time, a paid-receipt bridge, two compensation arrangements and a conversion/cost matrix. Keep evidence about tasks separate from the contractual and cash conditions that turn a change in work into a change in household resources.
6708ffcda7501c0f7f8da40938278dc69f410ebe.zh: 从任务中释放出来的时间可以提高工作质量、学习或生活。额外的家庭现金需要单独的补偿安排以及相关费用后的实际收入。在将工作时间转化为金钱之前，先阅读工作时间观察结果 加拿大央行 2026 年第三季度加拿大消费者期望调查包括有关人工智能在工作中使用、任务所需时间以及受访者认为自己已腾出时间的使用等问题。这些答案提供了有关工人报告的经历的背景信息。该报告于2026年10月19日发布。8月5日至27日收集在线反馈，8月24日至9月4日进行后续采访。参考季度、收集期和发布日期是不同的信息。这两个调查图表是该版本的分类摘要。它们不是每日系列，不是每个受访者工作时间的记录，也不是随机分配人员使用人工智能的实验。本文并未从这些摘要中推断出对工资、带薪工作时间或家庭收入的影响。单独的计算器从独立选择的每周时间和薪酬假设开始。它不会将总体调查中位数转化为个人预测，也不会将报告的时间使用百分比转化为收入转化率。两小时的衡量标准有不同的定义 第一个来源小组报告称，每周主动使用 AI 的时间为 2.8 小时，受访者估计在没有 AI 的情况下需要完成任务的额外时间为 4.7 小时。两者都保留源的插值中值标签。每周活跃时间是根据每个受访者报告的持续时间类别和使用频率来估算的。来源使用类别中点，并将 7.5 小时分配给 6 小时以上的开放式每日类别。因此，总量取决于明确的估计方法而不是时钟记录。另一项措施要求在没有人工智能的情况下假设一周内增加工作时间。这是受访者的反事实估计。它不会仅仅因为以数字形式总结而成为直接观察到的因果生产力增益。从额外时间中位数减去主动使用中位数并不能得出个人的净储蓄。这些问题描述了不同的角色，并且总体中位数的差异并不自动成为个体差异的中位数。同样，将 4.7 乘以假设工资将引入调查中未包含的薪酬假设。时间使用份额重叠，并且不分配单一饼图第二个来源小组要求受访者选择他们认为人工智能帮助释放的时间的每一个适用用途。列出的选项涉及任务质量、额外任务、工作与生活平衡、学习或培训以及创造性工作。由于允许有多个答案，因此这些百分比并不是相互排斥的组。显示的 5 个股的总和为 209.20%，这与多选题相符。将它们重新标准化为 100% 将回答不同的问题并隐藏该设计。这些百分比保留了人工智能工作模块中这个节省时间问题的受访者的分母。它们不是所有加拿大人的百分比、工作周的份额或特定工人获得额外工资的概率。聚合提取不会识别响应重叠或分配给每次使用的小时数。报告额外任务也不构成额外补偿。固定工资员工在获得相同工资的情况下可以完成更多的工作。输入从可用时间到实际收货的单独路线 默认方案独立假设在四十六周内每周释放三个可用小时。这创造了 138 小时的潜在容量。它故意与调查估计的 4.7 小时分开。然后，读者假设该能力的 50% 变成了额外的带薪工作，产生了 69 个带薪小时。按换算后的每小时额外收到 50 加元的现金总额计算，这些时间在建模年度内会产生 3,450 加元的额外收入。每年的自付费用工具成本独立设置为 240 加元。瀑布式扣除该成本一次，在个人税和其他工作成本之前留下 3,210 加元的现金零钱。它不是税后实得工资、营业利润或自动税收减免。每个环节都是一个单独的假设：容量必须可用，必须存在额外的工作，必须有人同意为其付费，并且现金必须实际到达。未付款的发票不计为收据。该示例未声明市场小时费率、需求或实现所选转换的概率。固定工资可以保持现金不变，而时间有价值。比较路径假设自付费用工具成本相同，但没有加班、奖金或加薪。因此，额外收入为零，默认情况下现金变动为负 240 加元。这并不意味着释放的时间没有价值。它可以提高质量、减轻压力、支持培训或留出更多工作之外的时间。在现金计算中，这些福利根本没有被定价为额外收入。如果雇主支付工具成本，则输入零个人自付费用以进行相关比较。如果补偿根据实际协议发生变化，请使用确认的收款金额和时间。不要假设任务花费的时间每减少一小时，员工就会自动收到按小时支付的工资。有偿工作和固定工资条比较了既定的安排。负结果意味着在这种狭窄的情况下输入的成本超过了额外收入，而不是该人的家庭总收入为负。现有工资、日常开支和税金不在图表内。在将结果添加到预算之前测试转换和成本 该矩阵会改变付费转换和年度自付费用，同时保留独立选择的每周时间、周数和每个转换小时的总收入。即使没有实现额外的付费工作，零转化行也可以使成本可见。当这些控制措施发生变化时，官方调查小组保持不变。可编辑的场景并不是对已发布证据的修订，并且有利的场景单元并不表明工作人员可以实现它。在将额外现金纳入个人计划之前，请确认工作安排、实际薪酬、领取时间和相关费用。分别确定相关的个人税收和福利影响。仅靠税前现金比较并不能告诉家庭可以安全地支出或储蓄多少钱。这五个图表将问题联系起来，但又不破坏它们：报告的时间、时间的重叠使用、付费收据桥梁、两种补偿安排和转换/成本矩阵。将有关任务的证据与将工作变化转化为家庭资源变化的合同和现金条件分开。

fac0634c351a9d59f8b6bc4e9de115247e673ec5.src: The rate table needs an allocation rule. A high rate on the final balance slice does not reprice the dollars that remain in earlier slices. Ask which dollars receive each rate A savings-rate table can list several percentages without showing how much interest a particular balance will earn. The missing detail is the allocation rule: does a higher rate apply to the entire balance after a threshold is met, or only to dollars within a specified slice? The FCAC savings-account guide distinguishes those possibilities and recommends checking the agreement. Its discussion also explains that actual accounts can differ in calculation and payment timing. The interactive example uses progressive balance slices for a constant deposit held for one full year. It does not model an all-balance repricing rule or reproduce any bank’s offer. Allocate the deposit before multiplying by a rate The invented schedule pays 1% on the first CAD 5,000, 3% on the next CAD 5,000 and the entered top rate on any balance above CAD 10,000. The default deposit is CAD 15,000 and the top rate is 5%. The first CAD 5,000 generates CAD 50 of annual interest. The next CAD 5,000 generates CAD 150. The final CAD 5,000 generates CAD 250. Adding those amounts gives CAD 450, before the excluded taxes and fees. Every dollar of principal is assigned once. Crossing CAD 10,000 changes the rate applying to the next dollar; it does not change the rate already assigned to the first CAD 10,000. Divide total interest by the whole balance to find the blended rate The default blended rate is CAD 450 ÷ CAD 15,000 = 3%. It is below the 5% rate paid on the highest slice because two-thirds of the deposit earns lower rates. This is a balance-weighted rate. Averaging 1%, 3% and 5% happens to produce 3% in the default example because the three slices contain equal amounts. With a different deposit, a simple average of the listed rates will generally give the wrong result. For example, CAD 10,000 earns CAD 200, a 2% blended rate. CAD 25,000 earns CAD 950 at the default top rate, a 3.8% blended rate. The schedule has not changed; the weight of each occupied slice has. Reconcile the tempting all-at-top-rate calculation Applying 5% to the entire default CAD 15,000 produces CAD 750. The tiered rule pays CAD 450. The waterfall explains the CAD 300 difference without treating it as a fee. The first CAD 5,000 earns four percentage points less than the top rate: CAD 200 less interest. The next CAD 5,000 earns two percentage points less: CAD 100 less. Subtracting both adjustments from CAD 750 produces the correct CAD 450. A balance below CAD 10,000 has no money in the top slice at all. The label on the highest tier does not, on its own, describe the average rate earned by that smaller deposit. Compare annual interest at the same balance and holding period The default alternative applies 3.5% to all CAD 15,000 for the same full year. It generates CAD 525. The tiered schedule generates CAD 75 less in this particular comparison, even though its top rate is higher. The matrix repeats the comparison across balances and flat rates. Within each cell, both rules use exactly the same principal and year. Differences in access, account fees, taxes, promotional duration or qualification terms are excluded rather than assumed equal in a real account decision. The curve shows why the balance matters. Each additional dollar above CAD 10,000 earns 5% at the default input, but the blended rate approaches that top rate gradually because the earlier slices remain in the account. There is no sudden repricing of the existing deposit. Use the actual agreement and cash calendar for the final budget The model holds the balance constant and pays simple interest once at year-end. Actual accounts may calculate interest on daily balances, credit it monthly, compound it or require other conditions. A quoted rate needs those details before it becomes an annual cash estimate. For a household plan, first identify the amount that can remain deposited and when it may be needed. Then calculate interest using the applicable balance rule and payment calendar. Account access and a bill’s due date still matter even when two options have similar annual interest totals. Use the calculated dollars and any applicable costs or taxes to update the budget. The highest percentage in a rate table is a starting point for reading the terms, not a complete forecast of spendable interest.
fac0634c351a9d59f8b6bc4e9de115247e673ec5.zh: 费率表需要分配规则。最终余额切片的高利率不会对早期切片中剩余的美元重新定价。询问哪些美元可以获得每种利率 储蓄利率表可以列出几个百分比，但不会显示特定余额将赚取多少利息。缺少的细节是分配规则：在达到阈值后，更高的利率适用于整个余额，还是仅适用于指定切片内的美元？ FCAC 储蓄账户指南区分了这些可能性并建议检查协议。其讨论还解释了实际账户的计算和付款时间可能有所不同。交互式示例使用累进余额切片来保存一整年的恒定存款。它不会模拟所有余额重新定价规则或复制任何银行的报价。在乘以利率之前分配存款 本发明的时间表对前 5,000 加元支付 1%，对下一个 5,000 加元支付 3%，并对任何高于 10,000 加元的余额输入最高利率。默认押金为 15,000 加元，最高利率为 5%。首笔 5,000 加元可产生 50 加元的年利息。接下来的 5,000 加元生成 150 加元。最后的 5,000 加元生成 250 加元。将这些金额相加得到 450 加元（不含税费）。每一美元本金都分配一次。超过 10,000 加元会改变下一美元的汇率；它不会改变已分配给前 10,000 加元的费率。将总利息除以总余额即可得出混合利率 默认混合利率为 450 加元 ÷ 15,000 加元 = 3%。它低于最高切片支付的 5% 利率，因为三分之二的存款赚取的利率较低。这是平衡加权利率。在默认示例中，对 1%、3% 和 5% 进行平均会产生 3%，因为这三个切片包含相同的数量。对于不同的存款，所列利率的简单平均通常会给出错误的结果。例如，10,000 加元可赚取 200 加元，混合利率为 2%。按照默认最高汇率（3.8% 的混合汇率），25,000 加元可赚取 950 加元。时间表没有改变；每个占用切片的权重。协调诱人的全顶级费率计算对整个默认 15,000 加元应用 5% 会产生 750 加元。分层规则支付 450 加元。瀑布解释了 300 加元的差异，而不将其视为费用。首笔 5,000 加元的收入比最高利率低 4 个百分点：利息少 200 加元。接下来的 5,000 加元收入将减少两个百分点：减少 100 加元。从 750 加元中减去这两项调整，得到正确的 450 加元。余额低于 10,000 加元时，顶层根本没有钱。最高层的标签本身并不描述该较小存款所赚取的平均利率。比较相同余额和持有期限的年利息 默认替代方案对同一全年的所有 15,000 加元适用 3.5%。它生成 525 加元。在此特定比较中，分层计划生成的费用少 75 加元，尽管其最高费率更高。该矩阵重复了余额和统一费率之间的比较。在每个单元格中，两条规则都使用完全相同的主体和年份。在真实账户决策中，访问权限、账户费用、税收、促销期限或资格条款的差异被排除在外，而不是假定相同。该曲线显示了平衡为何重要。在默认输入下，每增加 10,000 加元以上的美元，即可赚取 5%，但混合利率会逐渐接近最高利率，因为早期的部分仍保留在帐户中。现有存款不会突然重新定价。使用实际协议和现金日历作为最终预算 该模型保持余额不变，并在年底支付一次单利。实际账户可能会计算每日余额的利息、每月记入贷款机构、复利或要求其他条件。报价利率在成为年度现金估算之前需要这些详细信息。对于家庭计划，首先确定可以保留的存款金额以及何时需要。然后使用适用的余额规则和付款日历计算利息。即使两个选项的年利息总额相似，帐户访问权限和账单到期日仍然很重要。使用计算出的美元和任何适用的成本或税费来更新预算。利率表中的最高百分比是阅读条款的起点，而不是可支出利息的完整预测。

8feb5fd806a12be951d8707dfb918fbfb6542ca1.src: Time averages describe a defined population and day. A household plan needs its own exclusive time blocks and actual cash costs; a paid-help quote does not establish how many personal hours it frees. Ask who is included in the daily time average The 2022 Time Use Survey table reports 2.1 hours a day of unpaid household work across the full selected population, compared with 3.0 hours among people who performed that activity on their reference day. Both figures can be correct because their denominators differ. The all-person mean includes people who recorded zero time in that activity that day. The participant mean conditions on doing it. A participant in adult care is not automatically a participant in child care, shopping or household work, so the participant population changes between rows. For child care of people under 18 in the household or family, the published figures are 0.5 hours across the selected population and 3.4 hours among that day’s participants. These do not say every adult performs 3.4 hours of child care daily. The first chart keeps the two measures paired and explicitly labels their different bases. Keep daily participation separate from care provided over a year The companion measure is the share of persons performing the activity on the reference day. For the four plotted groups, the published percentages are household work 71.4%, child care 16.2%, adult care 3.9% and shopping 25.9%. A person can appear in more than one group, so these are not exclusive slices that must sum to 100%. The reference-day denominator differs from reporting unpaid care at any time over twelve months. The existing caregiving cash-plan guide uses that separate participation context. Mixing the two survey concepts would turn a difference in measurement into an unsupported comparison of how common care is. An invented arithmetic example makes the means easier to read. If three of ten people record four hours each and seven record zero, total time is twelve hours. The population mean is 1.2 hours, the participant mean is four hours and participation is 30%. With consistent unrounded quantities, 30% × four equals 1.2. Published figures are independently rounded, so the displayed rates and means need not reproduce that identity exactly. Do not replace a published value with a product of two other rounded values. None of the three measures identifies a personal care need or a recommended daily workload. Preserve the survey year, coverage and published precision The table was released on 5 June 2024 and currently contains reference year 2022. Collection ran from 16 July 2022 through 15 July 2023. This article reviewed the current source on 25 October 2026. The figures describe the 2022 survey cycle, not a measured 2026 household week. The selection is Canada, total persons aged 15 and over, and total all persons in the gender dimension. The survey metadata covers non-institutionalized people living off First Nations reserves in the ten provinces; the territories are outside the coverage. One selected person responded for the diary, rather than a proxy reporting every member’s schedule. The source supplies 95% confidence intervals. The participation chart plots its published bounds, while this table retains the hour estimates and their bounds. A displayed interval of 0.1 to 0.1 reflects one-decimal rounding, rather than certainty about everyone’s time. The selected rows have blank status and symbol fields; no A/B/C grade has been invented. The table’s “Unpaid work activities” aggregate includes household work, household/family child and adult care, and shopping. It reports population/participant means of 3.2/4.0 hours and daily participation of 79.1%. The separately listed outside-household help, community work and volunteering category is not part of that aggregate. Do not add a parent to its components or relabel every unpaid activity as dependent care. A main-activity diary cannot describe every simultaneous responsibility The official diary instructions describe a designated twenty-four-hour period from 4 a.m. to 4 a.m. the following morning. Assigned reference days help represent different days of the week. A reported day is not necessarily the respondent’s usual or preferred routine. The official methods discussion distinguishes main activities, simultaneous activities and time spent with other people. It explains that exact simultaneous-activity duration was not collected and that primary child-care time can miss supervision and interaction. These published means therefore cannot reconstruct all time spent responsible for someone else. The hypothetical weekly schedule below deliberately uses exclusive blocks so each clock hour is assigned once. That is a limited bookkeeping exercise, rather than a claim that real care duties never overlap work, travel or personal activities. An apparently unassigned hour can still involve a responsibility the small ledger does not capture. Build the 168-hour plan from independently entered blocks One person has 168 clock hours in seven days. The invented ledger assigns a fixed 71 hours to sleep, personal activities and other commitments, then adds requested work/travel and own domestic/care blocks. The fixed amount is a teaching assumption, not a health, sleep or care standard. At the defaults, work plus travel takes 45 hours. Own domestic/care time is separately entered as 30 hours before an assumed arrangement and 26 hours after. Assigned time is 146 hours before and 142 after, leaving 22 and 26 hours unassigned. The signed bars compare the two remainders, and the waterfall reconciles the after scenario to 168. The four-hour difference comes entirely from the chosen own-time assumptions. The calculator does not derive it from a provider’s invoice, service duration or a survey mean. The after figure can exceed the before figure if an arrangement adds coordination or other personal time. Each input needs its own evidence when a real plan is reviewed. “Unassigned” means absent from the entered blocks. It does not prove that those hours are usable leisure, available paid work or adequate recovery time. A full plan may need further blocks, a different fixed amount or a dated schedule that this small example does not provide. Retain a negative remainder instead of drawing an impossible schedule If work and travel rise to 80 hours while the after domestic/care block stays at 26, the requested total becomes 71 + 80 + 26 = 177 hours. The remaining amount is negative nine hours. The calculator keeps that sign visible as an overscheduled request. It does not squeeze 177 exclusive hours into a 168-hour donut, cap one category without saying so, or assume sleep or care can safely be cut. The negative number identifies a conflict in the entered exclusive plan. Resolving it requires actual facts about obligations and overlap, rather than a mathematical normalization. Likewise, a four-hour increase in unassigned time is a difference between scenarios, not four extra hours added to the week. Total clock time remains 168. This time constraint is distinct from the cash constraint: a plan can have enough cash while its exclusive time requests still conflict. Price the paid service separately from the time assumption The cash controls use an independent total service quote of CAD 120 per week and CAD 200 per week available after other budget commitments. Over exactly four weeks, available cash is CAD 800 and quoted invoices total CAD 480, leaving CAD 320. Each week’s CAD 200 is a distinct budget amount; the same opening cash balance must not be counted four times. Four weeks is a selected twenty-eight-day window. It is not an average calendar month, and the calculator does not silently use four weeks for every month of a year. It also does not determine whether each receipt arrives before the corresponding invoice. A dated cash calendar may reveal an additional timing need. Changing the quote to CAD 250 per week raises four invoices to CAD 1,000, leaving an unfunded CAD 200 against the same CAD 800. Every time result stays unchanged. Conversely, changing own hours after the arrangement changes the time plan while leaving the quoted cost unchanged. No unpaid-hour-times-wage calculation appears. The service quote supplies a cash amount, not a value for every hour of unpaid work, an income replacement, additional earnings or a guaranteed number of personal hours freed. Money independently available is entered directly; it is not inferred from work/travel hours or assumed to increase when unassigned time rises. Review time and cash as separate constraints For the official charts, retain the reference-day definition, population/participant denominator, age coverage, units and uncertainty. For a household plan, review the actual exclusive time blocks, simultaneous responsibilities, quoted service scope and dated payments. The public survey does not decide whether a particular arrangement meets care needs. The tool does not model taxes, benefits, extra wages, borrowing, investment returns or an assessment of care suitability. A negative cash remainder represents missing funding rather than access to credit. A negative time remainder represents incompatible exclusive requests rather than a medical or safety diagnosis. A useful planning statement keeps both quantities visible: “This assumed arrangement leaves 26 unassigned hours in the small weekly ledger and CAD 320 after four invoices, while the actual time change and service suitability still require verification.” That separates a transparent calculation from claims its inputs cannot establish.
8feb5fd806a12be951d8707dfb918fbfb6542ca1.zh: 时间平均值描述了定义的人口和日期。家庭计划需要有自己专属的时间段和实际的现金成本；付费帮助报价并不能确定它可以释放多少个人时间。询问谁包含在每日平均时间中 2022 年时间使用调查表报告了所有选定人群每天从事 2.1 小时无偿家务劳动，而在参考日进行该活动的人每天从事 3.0 小时无偿家务劳动。这两个数字都可能是正确的，因为它们的分母不同。所有人平均值包括当天在该活动中记录为零的人。参与者意味着这样做的条件。成人护理的参与者并不自动成为儿童护理、购物或家务劳动的参与者，因此参与者人数在各行之间发生变化。对于家庭中 18 岁以下人员的托儿服务，公布的数字是所选人群的托儿时间为 0.5 小时，当天参与者的托儿时间为 3.4 小时。这些并不是说每个成年人每天要照顾 3.4 小时的儿童。第一个图表使两个度量保持配对并明确标记它们的不同基础。将日常参与与一年内提供的护理分开。伴随指标是在参考日进行活动的人数比例。对于四个绘图组，公布的百分比是家务劳动 71.4%、儿童保育 16.2%、成人保育 3.9% 和购物 25.9%。一个人可以出现在多个组中，因此这些并不是总和必须为 100% 的排他性切片。参考日分母与十二个月内任何时间报告的无薪护理不同。现有的护理现金计划指南使用这种单独的参与背景。混合这两个调查概念会将测量的差异变成对普通护理程度的无支持的比较。发明的算术示例使方法更易于阅读。如果十人中的三人每人记录四小时，七人记录零，则总时间为十二小时。总体平均值为 1.2 小时，参与者平均值为 4 小时，参与率为 30%。在未四舍五入的数量一致的情况下，30% × 4 等于 1.2。公布的数字是独立四舍五入的，因此显示的比率和平均值不需要准确地再现该等式。请勿用其他两个舍入值的乘积替换已发布的值。这三项措施均未确定个人护理需求或建议的日常工作量。保留调查年份、覆盖范围和发布精度 该表于 2024 年 6 月 5 日发布，目前包含参考年 2022 年。收集时间为 2022 年 7 月 16 日至 2023 年 7 月 15 日。本文回顾了 2026 年 10 月 25 日的当前来源。这些数字描述的是 2022 年的调查周期，而不是测量的 2026 年家庭周。选择的是加拿大，15 岁及以上的总人数，以及性别维度上的所有人数。调查元数据涵盖十个省份生活在原住民保护区的非收容人口；这些领土不在覆盖范围之内。一名选定的人对日记做出回应，而不是由代理人报告每个成员的日程安排。来源提供 95% 的置信区间。参与图表绘制了其已发布的界限，而该表保留了小时估计值及其界限。显示的 0.1 到 0.1 的间隔反映了一位小数四舍五入，而不是每个人的时间的确定性。所选行的状态和符号字段为空白；尚未发明 A/B/C 级。该表的“无酬工作活动”总计包括家务劳动、家庭/家庭儿童和成人护理以及购物。据报告，人口/参与者的平均时间为 3.2/4.0 小时，每日参与率为 79.1%。单独列出的家庭外帮助、社区工作和志愿服务类别不属于该总数的一部分。不要将父母添加到其组成部分或将每项无偿活动重新标记为家属护理。主要活动日记无法描述每一项同时承担的责任 官方日记说明描述了从凌晨 4 点到次日凌晨 4 点的指定二十四小时时段。指定的参考日有助于代表一周中的不同日子。报告的日期不一定是受访者通常或首选的惯例。官方方法讨论区分主要活动、同时活动和与其他人一起度过的时间。它解释说，没有收集确切的同时活动持续时间，并且初级儿童保育时间可能会错过监督和互动。因此，这些公开的手段无法重建为他人负责的所有时间。下面假设的每周时间表故意使用独占块，因此每个时钟小时都分配一次。这是一种有限的簿记工作，而不是声称真正的护理职责永远不会与工作、旅行或个人活动重叠。明显未分配的时间仍然可能涉及小账本未记录的责任。从独立进入的区块构建 168 小时计划 一个人在 7 天内有 168 个时钟小时。发明的账本分配固定的 71 小时用于睡眠、个人活动和其他承诺，然后添加所要求的工作/旅行和自己的家庭/护理时间。固定金额是一种教学假设，而不是健康、睡眠或护理标准。默认情况下，工作加差旅需要 45 小时。自己的家庭/护理时间分别输入为假定安排之前 30 小时和之后 26 小时。分配的时间为前 146 小时和后 142 小时，其余 22 小时和 26 小时未分配。带符号的条形比较两个余数，瀑布将后续场景调整为 168。四个小时的差异完全来自所选的自身时间假设。该计算器不是从提供商的发票、服务期限或调查平均值中得出的。如果安排增加协调或其他个人时间，之后的数字可以超过之前的数字。当审查实际计划时，每个输入都需要自己的证据。 “未分配”意味着不存在于输入的块中。它并不能证明这些时间是可用的休闲时间、可用的带薪工作或足够的恢复时间。完整的计划可能需要更多的块、不同的固定金额或有日期的时间表，而这个小例子没有提供。保留负余数，而不是制定不可能的时间表 如果工作和旅行时间增加到 80 小时，而术后家庭/护理时间保持在 26 小时，则要求的总时间将变为 71 + 80 + 26 = 177 小时。剩余时间为负九小时。计算器会将该标志显示为超额请求。它不会将 177 小时的独享时间压缩到 168 小时的甜甜圈中，也不会在没有明确说明的情况下限制某一类别，也不会假设可以安全地削减睡眠或护理时间。负数表示输入的独占计划中存在冲突。解决这个问题需要有关义务和重叠的实际事实，而不是数学标准化。同样，未分配时间增加四个小时是场景之间的差异，而不是每周增加四个小时。总时钟时间仍为 168。此时间约束与现金约束不同：计划可以拥有足够的现金，但其独占时间请求仍然存在冲突。将付费服务与时间假设分开定价 现金控制使用每周 120 加元的独立总服务报价，以及其他预算承诺后的每周 200 加元。在整整四个星期内，可用现金为 800 加元，报价发票总计 480 加元，还剩 320 加元。每周 200 加元是一个单独的预算金额；同一期初现金余额不得计算四次。四个星期是选定的二十八天窗口。这不是一个平均日历月，计算器也不会默默地用四个星期来表示一年中的每个月。它还无法确定每张收据是否先于相应的发票到达。带有日期的现金日历可能会揭示额外的时间需求。将报价更改为每周 250 加元会将四张发票提高到 1,000 加元，而 800 加元则剩下 200 加元没有资金。每次结果都保持不变。相反，在安排后更改自己的工作时间会改变时间计划，同时保持报价成本不变。没有出现未付工时工资计算。服务报价提供的是现金金额，而不是每小时无酬工作、收入替代、额外收入或保证释放的个人时间的价值。独立可用的资金直接输入；它不是从工作/旅行时间推断出来的，也不是假设当未分配时间增加时会增加。将时间和现金作为单独的约束进行审查 对于官方图表，保留参考日定义、人口/参与者分母、年龄覆盖范围、单位和不确定性。对于家庭计划，请检查实际的专属时间段、同时承担的责任、报价的服务范围和付款日期。公众调查并不能决定特定安排是否满足护理需求。该工具不会对税收、福利、额外工资、借款、投资回报或护理适宜性评估进行建模。现金余额为负表示缺少资金而不是获得信贷。负时间剩余代表不兼容的排他请求，而不是医疗或安全诊断。有用的计划声明可以使这两个数量保持可见：“这种假设的安排在小型每周分类账中留下了 26 个未分配的小时，在四张发票后留下了 320 加元，而实际时间变化和服务适用性仍然需要验证。”这将透明的计算与其输入无法建立的主张区分开来。

afcbf0f457f70a1609dcf5aee684636262205495.src: An entry rate and an exit rate cannot be directly subtracted to find the change in people. Reconcile the starting populations and flows, then use actual household dollars for a reserve plan. A percentage needs the population that could make the transition Between 2022 and 2023, the selected Canadian statistics show a 4.1% low-income entry rate and a 34.9% exit rate . Those percentages start with different groups. Entry concerns tax filers who were initially outside low income; exit concerns tax filers who were initially in low income. Subtracting 4.1 from 34.9 produces a 30.8-percentage-point difference between two conditional rates. It does not measure the percentage-point change in the overall low-income share, the number of people leaving minus entering or a household’s chance of recovering income. The charts use Statistics Canada Table 11-10-0024-01 , selecting Canada, Both sexes and the Variable low income measure. They retain the first and second years of each transition pair rather than treating the observation as a single-year level. Identify the tax-filer population and the low-income definition This table’s Canada selection covers tax filers aged at least 18 in the ten provinces who filed in both years. It is not a count of every Canadian resident, child or household. The measure uses census-family after-tax income adjusted by the square root of family size, with a threshold based on half the median adjusted income. The variable threshold is re-estimated each year. It differs from the table’s separate measure fixed in 2002 and subsequently price-adjusted. The charts use only the variable measure, so those two definitions are never spliced together. Statistics Canada’s Dimensions of Poverty Hub distinguishes these Low Income Measure transitions from Canada’s official poverty measure based on the Market Basket Measure. A move across the selected statistical threshold is not, by itself, a full account of a person’s living costs or financial security. Use the person counts to reconstruct the two denominators The 2022/2023 matched population contains 28,303,440 tax filers . Of these, 4,439,745 were initially in low income. The initial non-low-income group is the difference: 23,863,695 . There were 980,895 entrants. Dividing that count by 23,863,695 gives about 4.1104%, which rounds to the published 4.1%. There were 1,549,805 exits. Dividing by 4,439,745 gives about 34.9075%, which rounds to 34.9%. The larger exit percentage therefore does not mean applying 34.9% to the much larger non-low-income group. The grouped chart places each actual transition count beside its own eligible starting group. All bars in that figure measure people. Keep the four possible start-to-end states visible The count matrix records two statuses in the first year and two in the second. For 2022/2023, 2,889,940 tax filers remained in low income, 1,549,805 exited, 980,895 entered and 22,882,800 were outside low income in both years. Adding the two cells in the first row reconstructs the initial low-income count. Adding the two cells in the first column reconstructs the later low-income count. Adding all four cells reconstructs the entire matched population. Cell counts and conditional rates are different views of the same selected pair. Normalising each row would produce row-based transition percentages; dividing by the entire population would instead produce population shares. The chart displays counts, with that denominator choice left explicit. Reconcile the change with entrants and exits measured in people The within-pair waterfall follows a count identity: 4,439,745 initially low income + 980,895 entrants − 1,549,805 exits = 3,870,835 low income in the second year . The decrease in the low-income count within this matched pair is therefore 568,910. If a change in the matched-population share is wanted, divide that person-count change by the same 28,303,440 denominator. Directly subtracting the published entry and exit rates cannot perform that calculation. The bridge reports a descriptive reconciliation. It does not establish why a person’s status changed, attribute a movement to a policy or estimate how long a later income interruption might last. Those questions need additional evidence. Adjacent transition pairs do not create one fixed panel The historical line shows five pairs, from 2018/2019 through 2022/2023. Every pair requires qualifying tax returns in both of its years. The participating population can change between pairs. For that reason, the second-year low-income count in the 2021/2022 pair need not equal the first-year count in the 2022/2023 pair, even though both labels refer to 2022. Joining them without checking coverage would erase the difference between two matched populations. The article’s source check preserves each pair’s original values. It verifies all four transition cells, both low-income counts, the total matched count and the four rates. It does not force adjacent pairs into an artificial single cohort or claim that the same people contribute to every plotted point. Build the household reserve from its own cash gap The final chart asks a separate planning question. Suppose essential expenses are CAD 2,500 a month, cash available for them is CAD 2,100 and starting reserve is CAD 2,400. The selected shortfall is CAD 400 per month . Using that reserve for a constant month-end gap leaves CAD 2,000 after one month, CAD 1,200 after three and zero after six. At month seven, the cumulative amount not funded by the initial reserve reaches CAD 400. At month twelve it reaches CAD 2,400. No national entry or exit percentage is multiplied into these cash figures. Changing the historical year changes the source snapshot; it leaves the household scenario intact. Changing expenses, receipts or reserve changes the cash chart without rewriting the official observations. Keep the statistical question beside the financial-planning question The statistics describe movement across a particular income threshold among a particular tax-filer population. The cash example describes a selected household shortfall. They can inform different parts of a planning discussion while retaining their separate units and evidence. A real reserve review also needs payment dates, other expenses, support eligibility, insurance, access to savings and the capacity to rebuild money after use. Income changes can be irregular, and an annual threshold transition does not supply a monthly receipt calendar. Read the population, income measure and two-year reference pair. Match every conditional percentage to its starting group. Use person counts for a flow reconciliation. Check whether a comparison follows the same matched population. Use actual household costs and cash dates to build a reserve scenario. The latest pair in this downloaded table is 2022/2023. Its retrieval date is 25 October 2026; that retrieval does not turn the historical observations into current household conditions or a forecast.

减去 4.1，两个条件利率之间存在 30.8 个百分点的差异。它不衡量总体低收入比例的百分比变化、离开人数减去进入人数或家庭恢复收入的机会。这些图表使用加拿大统计局表 11-10-0024-01，选择加拿大、男女和可变低收入衡量标准。他们保留每个过渡对的第一年和第二年，而不是将观察结果视为单年水平。确定报税者人群和低收入定义 此表的加拿大选择涵盖了这两年报税的 10 个省份中年满 18 岁的报税者。这并不是对每个加拿大居民、儿童或家庭的统计。该衡量标准使用按家庭规模平方根调整的人口普查家庭税后收入，阈值基于调整后收入中位数的一半。每年都会重新估计可变阈值。它与表中 2002 年确定并随后进行价格调整的单独衡量标准不同。图表仅使用变量度量，因此这两个定义永远不会拼接在一起。加拿大统计局的贫困维度中心将这些低收入衡量标准的转变与加拿大基于市场篮子衡量标准的官方贫困衡量标准区分开来。跨越选定的统计阈值本身并不能全面反映一个人的生活成本或财务安全。使用人数来重建两个分母 2022/2023 匹配人口包含 28,303,440 名纳税人。其中，4,439,745 人最初处于低收入状态。初始非低收入组差额为：23,863,695。共有 980,895 名参赛者。将该计数除以 23,863,695 所得结果约为 4.1104%，四舍五入为公布的 4.1%。有 1,549,805 次退出。除以 4,439,745 所得结果约为 34.9075%，四舍五入为 34.9%。因此，较大的退出百分比并不意味着将 34.9% 应用于更大的非低收入群体。分组图表将每个实际转换计数放在其自己的合格起始组旁边。该图中的所有条形都衡量人。保持四种可能的开始到结束状态可见。计数矩阵记录第一年的两种状态和第二年的两种状态。 2022/2023 年，2,889,940 名纳税人仍处于低收入状态，1,549,805 人退出，980,895 人进入，22,882,800 人在这两年中处于低收入之外。将第一行中的两个单元格相加即可重建初始低收入计数。将第一列中的两个单元格相加即可重建后来的低收入计数。添加所有四个细胞即可重建整个匹配的群体。细胞计数和条件率是同一选定对的不同视图。规范化每一行将产生基于行的转换百分比；除以总人口会产生人口份额。该图表显示计数，并明确选择分母。协调变化与以人口为单位衡量的进入者和退出者对内瀑布遵循计数恒等式： 4,439,745 最初低收入 + 980,895 进入者 − 1,549,805 退出 = 第二年 3,870,835 低收入者 。因此，该配对中的低收入人数减少了 568,910 人。如果需要改变匹配人口份额，请将人数变化除以同样的 28,303,440 分母。直接减去公布的进入率和退出率无法执行该计算。桥梁报告了描述性的协调。它没有确定一个人的状况发生变化的原因、将变化归因于一项政策或估计以后的收入中断可能会持续多长时间。这些问题需要额外的证据。相邻过渡对不会创建一个固定面板历史线显示从 2018/2019 年到 2022/2023 年的五对。每对都需要在其两年内提供合格的纳税申报表。参与人群在配对之间可能会发生变化。因此，即使两个标签都指的是 2022 年，2021/2022 年对中的第二年低收入人数不必等于 2022/2023 年对中的第一年计数。在不检查覆盖范围的情况下加入它们将消除两个匹配人口之​​间的差异。文章的源代码检查保留了每对的原始值。它验证所有四个转换单元，包括低收入计数、总匹配计数和四个比率。它不会强迫相邻的对进入一个人为的单一队列，也不会声称相同的人对每个标绘点都有贡献。从自己的现金缺口中建立家庭储备 最终图表提出了一个单独的规划问题。假设基本开支为每月 2,500 加元，可用现金为 2,100 加元，起始准备金为 2,400 加元。选定的缺口是每月400加元。使用该储备金来保持固定的月末差距，一个月后剩余 2,000 加元，三个月后剩余 1,200 加元，六个月后剩余零。第 7 个月，初始储备金未提供的累计金额达到 400 加元。第 12 个月达到 2,400 加元。这些现金数字没有乘以国家进入或退出百分比。更改历史年份会更改源快照；它使家庭场景完好无损。更改支出、收入或准备金会更改现金图表，而无需重写官方观察结果。将统计问题放在财务规划问题旁边统计数据描述了特定纳税人群体中特定收入门槛的变化。现金示例描述了选定的家庭短缺情况。他们可以为规划讨论的不同部分提供信息，同时保留各自的单位和证据。真正的准备金审查还需要支付日期、其他费用、支持资格、保险、储蓄的获得以及使用后重建资金的能力。收入变化可能不规律，年度门槛转变不提供每月收入日历。阅读人口、收入衡量标准和两年参考对。将每个条件百分比与其起始组相匹配。使用人数进行流量调节。检查比较是否遵循相同的匹配群体。使用实际家庭成本和现金日期来构建储备情景。此下载表中最新的一对是 2022/2023。检索日期为2026年10月25日；检索不会将历史观察结果转化为当前的家庭状况或预测。

6cccf8bce9ef892ac67d2d8d4113a84f0627cdf9.src: Track the eligible loss once, identify which gains can absorb it and keep any refund estimate and receipt date in a separate cash plan. Identify the loss type and its measurement basis first A statement showing an investment loss does not by itself identify an amount available for a tax deduction. This article uses an explicitly historical 2025 example of eligible ordinary capital losses, with all amounts already converted to the appropriate allowable-loss and taxable-gain basis. CRA’s capital-loss guidance describes same-year netting before a net capital loss is carried to another eligible year. It also distinguishes loss categories and circumstances that require different treatment. The tool assumes eligibility has been verified separately. It does not establish whether a loss is denied, superficial or subject to special rules. A loss that cannot be claimed must not be inserted simply because a holding declined in value. Because the inputs are already allowable or taxable amounts, applying another inclusion percentage would reduce them a second time. Historical inclusion-rate adjustments and multiple loss vintages need a fuller record than this one-vintage illustration. Use the same-year loss once before allocating it elsewhere The original example enters CAD 12,000 of 2025 allowable capital losses and CAD 3,000 of 2025 taxable capital gains before that loss use. Same-year use is the smaller amount, CAD 3,000. The remaining net capital-loss record is CAD 9,000. The first waterfall shows that bridge. Allocating the full CAD 12,000 again to another year would reuse the CAD 3,000 already absorbed in 2025. The carryback calculation therefore starts with CAD 9,000. If instead the entered 2025 taxable gain exceeds the allowable loss, the loss is fully used in that year and no negative carryover record appears. For example, CAD 2,000 of allowable loss against CAD 3,000 of taxable gain leaves CAD 1,000 of gain and zero loss to allocate elsewhere. These are loss-record identities. They do not subtract investment sale losses from the household bank account or calculate a change in tax payable. Any cash from an actual investment sale belongs in its own transaction ledger. Give each eligible destination year its own gain capacity For a 2025 net capital loss, CRA identifies 2022, 2023 and 2024 as the three previous eligible years and allows the taxpayer to choose destination years. The example assumes independently verified available taxable capital gains of CAD 2,000, CAD 4,000 and CAD 1,000 respectively. The default requested carryback allocation is CAD 7,000. For transparency, this tool visits the destination years in chronological order: first 2022, then 2023, then 2024. It uses CAD 2,000, CAD 4,000 and CAD 1,000, stopping at each year’s entered capacity. This ordering is an authored convention. It is not a rule requiring the earliest destination year or evidence that the allocation gives the largest tax saving. Actual year choices require their own assessment of the complete records and consequences. Do not confuse destination-year choice with the order of loss vintages. CRA’s other-years guidance separately addresses using older loss vintages before newer ones, record keeping and inclusion-rate adjustments. This model contains only the 2025 vintage. A remaining record and an unfilled request have different meanings After the default CAD 7,000 allocation, CAD 2,000 of the CAD 9,000 net capital-loss record remains unapplied. The second waterfall preserves that remainder as a carryforward record. It is not CAD 2,000 available to pay a household bill today. Reduce the requested carryback amount to CAD 3,000. Under the declared order, CAD 2,000 is allocated to 2022 and CAD 1,000 to 2023. The remaining record becomes CAD 6,000. Increasing the request again can use more of that record only while eligible gain capacity remains. Requesting CAD 20,000 at the default gain capacities still allocates only CAD 7,000. A larger request cannot create another eligible gain or another loss. Likewise, entering zero prior-year gain capacity leaves the net loss unapplied even when the requested allocation is large. The matrix changes the 2025 allowable loss and taxable gain while retaining those other conditions. A larger residual can reflect a larger loss, less same-year use or a limit on carryback capacity. It is a record to reconcile, rather than a standalone measure of financial improvement. Build any tax and cash estimate separately from the deduction ledger A complete tax calculation is needed to translate an allowed deduction into its effect on tax payable. Assessments, prior payments and the treatment of the full return also affect whether money is refunded. The four charts therefore do not label a loss deduction as a refund. CRA’s guidance distinguishes taxable-income effects from net-income effects when applying net capital losses across years. The tool does not calculate income-tested benefits, credits or their changes from those different income measures. The statutory context is Income Tax Act section 111 . The official consolidation reviewed here is current to 30 September 2026; the CRA pages address the 2025 return. This dated example is not a determination for a new transaction or a later tax year. For a practical review, keep the verified loss vintage, matching inclusion basis, gain capacity, chosen applications and remaining record together. Then put any separately supported refund amount and receipt date into the household cash calendar. Until that cash is supported, an unapplied loss balance should not be counted again as money assigned to spending.
6cccf8bce9ef892ac67d2d8d4113a84f0627cdf9.zh: 跟踪合格损失一次，确定哪些收益可以吸收该损失，并将任何退款估算和接收日期保留在单独的现金计划中。首先确定损失类型及其计量基础 显示投资损失的报表本身并不确定可用于税收减免的金额。本文使用了 2025 年合格普通资本损失的明确历史示例，所有金额均已转换为适当的允许损失和应税收益基础。 CRA 的资本损失指南描述了净资本损失转入另一个符合条件的年度之前的同年净额。它还区分了需要不同处理的损失类别和情况。该工具假定资格已单独验证。它没有确定损失是否被否认、表面损失或受特殊规则的约束。不得仅仅因为持有的资产价值下降而插入无法申报的损失。由于投入已经是允许或应税的金额，应用另一个包含百分比将再次减少它们。历史包含率调整和多个损失年份需要比这个单一年份插图更完整的记录。在将其分配到其他地方之前使用一次同年损失原始示例在该损失使用之前输入 2025 年允许资本损失 12,000 加元和 2025 年应税资本收益 3,000 加元。同年使用量较小，为 3,000 加元。剩余的净资本损失记录为 9,000 加元。第一个瀑布就是那座桥。将全部 12,000 加元再次分配到下一年，将重复使用 2025 年已吸收的 3,000 加元。因此，结转计算从 9,000 加元开始。如果输入的2025年应纳税所得额超过允许亏损，则该亏损在当年全部使用，不会出现负结转记录。例如，2,000 加元的允许损失与 3,000 加元的应税收益相比，剩下 1,000 加元的收益和零损失可以分配到其他地方。这些都是丢失记录的身份。他们不会从家庭银行账户中扣除投资销售损失或计算应缴税款的变化。实际投资销售产生的任何现金都属于其自己的交易分类账。为每个符合条件的目标年份赋予自己的收益能力 对于 2025 年净资本损失，CRA 将 2022 年、2023 年和 2024 年确定为前三个符合条件的年份，并允许纳税人选择目标年份。该示例假设经独立验证的可用应税资本利得分别为 2,000 加元、4,000 加元和 1,000 加元。默认请求的回转分配为 7,000 加元。为了提高透明度，该工具按时间顺序访问目的地年份：首先是 2022 年，然后是 2023 年，然后是 2024 年。它使用 2,000 加元、4,000 加元和 1,000 加元，并在每年输入的容量处停止。此顺序是一种约定。这并不是一条规则，要求最早的目标年份或证明分配可以带来最大的税收节省。实际年份的选择需要他们自己对完整的记录和后果进行评估。不要将目的地年份的选择与损失年份的顺序混淆。 CRA 的其他年份指南分别解决了在新损失年份之前使用旧损失年份、记录保存和包含率调整的问题。该型号仅包含 2025 年年份。剩余记录和未满足的请求具有不同的含义默认分配 7,000 加元后，9,000 加元净资本损失记录中的 2,000 加元仍未应用。第二个瀑布保留剩余部分作为结转记录。如今，2000 加元不足以支付家庭账单。将请求的回转金额减少至 3,000 加元。根据宣布的命令，2022 年分配 2,000 加元，2023 年分配 1,000 加元。剩余记录变为 6,000 加元。仅当保留合格的增益容量时，再次增加请求才能使用更多该记录。在默认增益容量下请求 20,000 加元仍然只分配 7,000 加元。更大的请求不能创造另一个合格的收益或另一个损失。同样，即使请求的分配很大，输入上一年增益容量为零也会导致净损失不适用。该矩阵改变了 2025 年的允许损失和应税收益，同时保留了其他条件。较大的残差可以反映较大的损失、较少的同年使用量或回转容量的限制。这是一个需要协调的记录，而不是衡量财务改善的独立指标。与扣除分类账分开建立任何税收和现金估算需要完整的税收计算，以将允许的扣除额转化为其对应付税款的影响。评估、预先付款和全额退货的处理也会影响是否退款。因此，这四个图表并未将损失扣除标记为退款。 CRA 的指南区分了跨年应用净资本损失时的应税收入影响和净收入影响。该工具不会计算经过收入测试的福利、信贷或这些不同收入衡量标准的变化。法定范围是《所得税法》第 111 条。此处审查的官方合并截至 2026 年 9 月 30 日； CRA 页面涉及 2025 年纳税申报表。这个过时的示例并不是对新交易或后续纳税年度的确定。为了进行实际审查，请将经过验证的损失年份、匹配包含基础、增益容量、所选应用和剩余记录放在一起。然后将任何单独支持的退款金额和收款日期放入家庭现金日历中。在该现金得到支持之前，未使用的损失余额不应再次计入分配给支出的资金。

a2d1a13da88d820e01a8786986eb81128ae97657.src: A weighted average condenses dates into one number. Funding a particular bill requires enough cash by its actual deadline, even when a later receipt makes the final balance look adequate. Ask which dates disappeared inside the average An average maturity can be a useful summary of a set of future principal payments. It does not identify every date when money arrives. Two schedules can share the same average while providing different amounts at a particular spending deadline. This article constructs that difference directly. Each calendar contains CAD 20,000 of promised future principal. One receives CAD 10,000 in year four and CAD 10,000 in year eight. The other receives the full CAD 20,000 in year six. Weighting by face amounts gives the first calendar a mean maturity of 0.5 × 4 + 0.5 × 8 = six years . The single-receipt calendar also has a six-year mean. Neither that equality nor the equal face total establishes that the investments would have identical purchase prices. The calendars are assumed already held at time zero. No purchase is funded inside this illustration. The model therefore compares receipt timing and payment needs, without ranking investment returns or acquisition costs. State what is included before using principal as a resource Investor.gov’s bond overview describes principal promised at maturity and also discusses the risk of missed payments. This example assumes every stated principal amount is paid in full on its chosen date. It does not assess an actual issuer. The schedule contains principal receipts only, with no coupons or other income. This is a deliberately narrow calendar rather than a complete model of any coupon-bearing portfolio. Face amount is the future payment quantity, not necessarily the cash originally invested. Earlier receipts remain in cash without interest. Later claims are not sold early, pledged for a loan or treated as available cash before their dates. Reinvestment returns, tax, call provisions and settlement delays are excluded. The receipt bars make the distinction visible. In year six, the first calendar has received only half its face total. Its remaining CAD 10,000 is still scheduled for year eight, even though its average maturity is year six. Place the bill after the cash that is actually available The separate opening cash reserve is CAD 2,000. A single CAD 20,000 payment is due in year six. Within a year, any scheduled principal receipt is assumed to arrive immediately before that bill. The two-tranche calendar has received CAD 10,000 by the deadline. Combined with the opening CAD 2,000, it has CAD 12,000 available. After allowing for the CAD 20,000 bill, its position is −CAD 8,000 . The single-receipt calendar receives CAD 20,000 in year six before the bill. Its cash becomes CAD 22,000 and then falls to CAD 2,000 after payment. It needs no additional opening cash under that order of events. The two means remain six years throughout this comparison. The difference comes from how much of each schedule has matured by the deadline. An average date cannot release the second tranche two years early. An equal final balance does not remove a past funding problem The cash chart extends to year twelve so every permitted principal receipt and bill lies inside its window. After the year-eight principal arrives, the two-tranche ledger returns from negative CAD 8,000 to positive CAD 2,000. Both schedules finish with the same arithmetic endpoint: opening CAD 2,000 plus CAD 20,000 principal less the CAD 20,000 bill equals CAD 2,000. That equality is a useful conservation check. It does not mean the first bill was actually financed. A negative segment records the cash that was missing when payment was due. The model does not supply a loan, arrange an overdraft, delay the bill or ignore the temporary gap. Providing an additional CAD 8,000 at the start would make the two-tranche calendar fund this specific payment under the selected assumptions. That extra resource needs its own source and cannot also be allocated to another goal without reconciliation. Vary the spread around the mean rather than changing the mean itself The spacing control moves the two equal tranches symmetrically around the selected mean year. At mean six and spacing one, the principal dates are years five and seven. At spacing three, they are years three and nine. In both cases, the face-weighted mean stays six. With the default bill in year six, half the principal has arrived by the deadline and half has not. Their cash-funding result is therefore the same in this limited example, despite different distances from the deadline. The single-receipt calendar does not always need less cash. Move the bill to year five: the two-tranche calendar needs an extra CAD 8,000, while the year-six-only receipt needs CAD 18,000 because none of its principal has arrived. The deadline determines the comparison. Zero spacing places both halves in year six. They combine into the same payment date as the single-receipt calendar, and the two ledgers coincide. The data table merges equal years instead of presenting the two halves as separate extra money. The matrix changes the bill year and spacing while keeping the common mean selected. A bill after both tranches arrive may need no additional cash. A bill before either receipt can need substantially more. No cell is a probability, investment loss or measure of portfolio duration. Keep the weighting rule separate from interest-rate sensitivity The mean in this example weights dates by the face principal promised at each date.
