These price rows are independent stress cases for the same proposed unit count. They do not describe a trading strategy, predict which price will occur or compare selling first with contributing later. Such a comparison would require its own dates, transactions and applicable rules. A tax consequence also needs a cash plan. Here no sale proceeds arrive to pay a future bill. The calculator stops before tax liability because inclusion rules, offsets, other income and payment timing have not been supplied. Test the market value against reconciled room at the contribution date The default independently entered available room is CAD 15,000. Subtracting the CAD 12,000 proposal leaves CAD 3,000. Using the CAD 8,000 cost instead would incorrectly suggest CAD 7,000 remains, overstating this subtotal by CAD 4,000. At CAD 40 per unit, the same proposed 400 units require CAD 16,000 of room. Against the unchanged CAD 15,000 input, the displayed remainder becomes negative CAD 1,000. The model keeps this failed proposal visible; it neither authorizes an excess contribution nor silently reduces the unit count. The line chart fixes the room input while varying only the contribution-date unit price. In the default example, the two lines cross at CAD 37.50 per unit because 400 × 37.50 equals 15,000. That crossing is arithmetic, not a suggested order price or a guarantee that all records are complete. CRA recommends tracking room from the holder’s own records ; it applies across all of that person’s TFSAs and does not update immediately in the CRA account. Reconcile relevant transactions before relying on the entered capacity. The tool assumes that reconciliation is already complete and does not add an annual limit or calculate excess tax. Retain the contribution-date valuation, unit quantity and allocated cost beside the updated room record. Those separate records make it easier to explain why the contribution, reported gain and remaining capacity have different amounts.
0d74b47f7410400f54d205b6b2882d4c0b010440.zh: 实物捐助可以利用空间并创造可报告收益，而无需产生销售现金。分别核对出资日市场价值、分配成本和验证房间。首先确定正在转移的内容 实物捐赠将投资转移到 TFSA，而无需先将其出售以换取现金。它仍然是一种贡献，投资的账户位置只是其待遇的一部分。 CRA 目前的 TFSA 指南将来自非注册投资组合的合格实物捐助视为公平市场价值的处置。同样的值就是贡献金额。必须报告收益；由此产生的资本损失不能索赔。该插图假设符合条件的加拿大居民和允许的资本财产，没有交易费用。其他注册账户转让、特殊财产规则和资格审查需要单独分析。通过两个账户位置跟踪相同的资产 最初的示例建议以每单位 30 加元的价格捐赠 400 个单位，同时保留同一资产的另外 200 个单位未注册。选定的 600 个单位在变动前的总市值为 18,000 加元。完成提议的捐款后，仍有 200 个单位不在 TFSA 范围内，价值为 6,000 加元。 400 个捐赠单位内含价值 12,000 加元。两部分价格仍为 18,000 加元，价格不变。堆叠的条形使这种保护可见。 12,000 加元的捐款是现有财富的流动。不是在原来的18000加元上再加12000加元。在此示例中，转账本身或报表的缴款条目均不会创建现金收入。这是某一时刻的总市值比较。它不会扣除因视为处置而可能产生的任何税款、为未来避税分配价值或假设后续投资增长。现有 TFSA 资产同样从两个条中排除。将分配的成本记录保留在贡献值旁边。输入的建议 400 个单位的调整成本为每单位 20 加元，或 8,000 加元。按照选定的 30 加元市场价格计算，其价值超出成本 4,000 加元。这是在计算任何包含率或个人税之前显示的正资本收益。 CAD 8,000 描述了分配的成本记录。 12,000 加元描述了贡献日期的市场价值。 4,000 加元描述了差异。它们回答不同的问题，并不是三项独立的资产。 CRA 的资本收益计算指南区分了收益、调整后的成本基础和处置费用。零费用假设让这个例子使用了上面的简单差异。输入经过验证的分配 ACB，而不是假设显示的平均购买报价包括所有相关调整。该工具接受单位成本作为外部事实。它不会重建汇总成本基础、追踪再投资分配、处理公司行动或选择收购批次。改变保留在室外的单位数量不能改变分配给该有限模型中提议的贡献的成本。较小的市场价值可以使用较少的空间，而不会造成可用损失 将出资日期价格更改为 15 加元，同时保留 400 个拟议单位和 20 加元的分配单位成本。捐款额降至 6,000 加元，算术损失为 2,000 加元。收益/损失图表显示 2,000 加元作为拒绝损失幅度。它没有显示负税单、退款或可用来抵消其他收益的损失。在 20 加元的价格下，收益和损失均为零。相反，在 30 加元时，图表显示 4,000 加元的正收益。这些价格行是相同建议单位数量的独立压力情况。他们没有描述交易策略，预测将会出现的价格，也没有比较先卖出和后贡献。这种比较需要有自己的日期、交易和适用的规则。税收后果还需要现金计划。这里没有销售收入来支付未来的账单。计算器在纳税义务之前停止，因为尚未提供包含规则、抵消、其他收入和付款时间。根据出资日期的调节房间测试市场价值 独立输入的默认可用房间为 15,000 加元。减去提案中的 12,000 加元，剩下 3,000 加元。如果使用 8,000 加元成本，则会错误地建议剩余 7,000 加元，从而将该小计多报了 4,000 加元。按每个单元 40 加元计算，同样提议的 400 个单元需要 16,000 加元的房间。对于未更改的 CAD 15,000 输入，显示的余数变为负 CAD 1,000。该模型使这个失败的提案保持可见；它既不授权超额贡献，也不默默减少单位数量。折线图固定了房间输入，同时仅改变贡献日期单价。在默认示例中，两条线以每单位 CAD 37.50 交叉，因为 400 × 37.50 等于 15,000。该交叉是算术运算，而不是建议的订单价格或所有记录完整的保证。 CRA建议从持有人自己的记录中追踪房间；它适用于该人的所有 TFSA，并且不会立即在 CRA 账户中更新。在依赖输入的容量之前核对相关交易。该工具假设对账已经完成，并且不会添加年度限额或计算超额税款。在更新的房间记录旁边保留贡献日期估价、单位数量和分配成本。这些单独的记录可以更轻松地解释为什么贡献、报告的收益和剩余容量具有不同的金额。

a2406eaf9a6b0c19b19bc3412c343bb319b9e6c3.src: A rate table needs a calculation rule. Establish which assets each rate applies to, where the minimum enters and which other charges remain before comparing annual dollars. Start with the formula behind the rate table A schedule that lists 0.8%, 0.5% and 0.3% does not give a complete invoice. It must also explain which assets receive each rate. Two schedules can display the same percentages while assigning them to different amounts. This guide compares two deliberately specified formulas. Progressive pricing charges the first CAD 100,000 at the first rate, the next CAD 400,000 at the middle rate and any excess over CAD 500,000 at the top rate. Whole-balance pricing chooses a band from the total asset base and applies that band's single rate to every dollar. The distinction is arithmetic. It does not establish which formula a particular provider uses or which service is preferable. The word “tiered” by itself is insufficient to resolve the calculation. Investor.gov emphasizes the role of the advisory agreement in identifying services and charges. Its fee-disclosure explanation also distinguishes the advisory charge from other expenses that can apply. Those sources support asking for a complete formula; the numbers and schedules below are independently authored illustrations. Cap each progressive slice before multiplying At the default CAD 250,000 fee base, the first slice contains CAD 100,000 and the second contains CAD 150,000. There is no third-slice amount. The annual asset charge is CAD 100,000 × 0.8% plus CAD 150,000 × 0.5%, or CAD 1,550. The middle rate applies only to the amount in its slice. Multiplying the entire CAD 250,000 by 0.5% gives a different formula. Likewise, charging the full CAD 400,000 middle slice when the client has only CAD 150,000 in it would bill assets that are absent from the stated base. The waterfall exposes each component before the total. Empty slices remain zero, so the reader can see that crossing the first threshold does not erase the first slice or create an immediate full-sized second slice. For nonnegative rates, this progressive asset charge is continuous at both thresholds. Its slope can change when the rate on the next dollar changes. That distinction between a change in slope and a jump in the bill matters when checking a quote near a boundary. A whole-balance band reprices all of the stated base The alternative formula places CAD 250,000 in the middle band and charges 0.5% on all CAD 250,000. Its asset charge is CAD 1,250. This is a valid description of the invented whole-balance formula, rather than the progressive calculation made incorrectly. The boundaries are explicit: a balance of exactly CAD 100,000 remains in the first band; a balance above that amount and up to CAD 500,000 inclusive uses the middle band. Only an amount above CAD 500,000 uses the top band. With descending rates, crossing a boundary can lower the total annual asset charge because the new rate applies to the entire base. The threshold chart compares exactly CAD 100,000 with CAD 100,100 and exactly CAD 500,000 with CAD 500,100. It does not connect widely spaced quotes with a smooth line that conceals repricing. At the first default boundary, the progressive annual charge rises by CAD 0.50, while the whole-balance charge falls by CAD 299.50. At the second, the progressive charge rises by CAD 0.30 and the whole-balance charge falls by CAD 999.70. These are conditional differences in the selected formulas, not promised savings from adding assets to a real account. Place the minimum and the fixed fee in the stated order The example applies a CAD 300 minimum to the annual asset charge first. It then adds a separate CAD 120 annual account fee. The resulting formula is max(calculated asset charge, minimum asset charge) + fixed account fee . At the default base, both calculated asset charges already exceed the minimum. The total quotes are therefore CAD 1,670 for progressive slices and CAD 1,370 for the whole-balance band. The CAD 300 difference comes from allocating the first slice to a different rate; the same CAD 120 fixed fee appears on both sides. At a small enough balance, the minimum can set both quotes to the same amount. A minimum is a floor, not an extra CAD 300 added to every calculated charge. The waterfall's uplift row is only the positive amount required to reach that floor. Other contracts may define a minimum on the final invoice, waive a fixed fee, combine accounts or suspend billing at zero assets. Those are different terms. This illustration keeps a hypothetical account open, with no zero-balance waiver, so a minimum and fixed fee can still produce a positive quote at a zero base. Keep the total charge ratio separate from the next-dollar rate The effective charge ratio divides the complete annual quote by the same stated fee base. For the default progressive example, CAD 1,670 ÷ CAD 250,000 is 0.668%, displayed as 0.67%. It includes the fixed fee and any minimum adjustment. This ratio is not the rate charged on an additional dollar. In the middle progressive slice, a small additional amount receives the entered middle rate while earlier slice charges remain in place. An active minimum can temporarily prevent the invoice from increasing at all. A zero fee base creates an undefined ratio even if the contract produces a positive charge. The headline therefore shows N/A at zero rather than displaying 0% or treating the ratio as an infinite investment loss. The matrix uses positive balances to show how fixed and minimum charges affect the denominator. It is a fee-to-base comparison, not a fund expense ratio, an annual investment return or a judgment about service quality. Changing rates can also reverse the default ranking; neither formula is assumed always cheaper. Reconcile an actual quote with its own billing terms Before applying a real schedule, identify the assets included in the chargeable base. Ask whether the value is measured at a specific date or averaged over a period, how linked accounts are treated and whether cash or particular holdings receive different treatment. Then establish the slice or band formula, exact threshold boundaries, the location of any minimum and the fixed charges included or excluded. Billing frequency, partial-year treatment and applicable taxes need their own terms. Dividing this annual illustration into four parts does not establish a provider's quarterly invoice. The charts hold the base constant and treat the quoted fee as payable from outside it. They calculate no fee deduction from an account, return drag or future portfolio value. A model of ongoing deductions would need to specify when fees leave the account and how subsequent asset values affect later bills. NASAA's fee-disclosure discussion highlights a formula clients can use to verify charges and agreement terms that match billing. The practical check is an itemized dollar calculation for the relevant base and period, followed by a separate comparison of the services received. A lower rate or invoice alone does not show that two engagements meet the same needs.
a2406eaf9a6b0c19b19bc3412c343bb319b9e6c3.zh: 费率表需要计算规则。在比较年度金额之前，确定每个费率适用于哪些资产、最低限额以及剩余的其他费用。从费率表背后的公式开始 列出 0.8%、0.5% 和 0.3% 的明细表并不能提供完整的发票。它还必须解释哪些资产接受每种利率。两个计划可以显示相同的百分比，但将它们分配给不同的金额。本指南比较了两个特意指定的公式。累进定价按第一费率收取前 100,000 加元的费用，接下来的 400,000 加元按中间费率收费，超过 500,000 加元的部分按最高费率收取。整体平衡定价从总资产基础中选择一个区间，并将该区间的单一利率应用于每一美元。区别在于算术。它没有确定特定提供商使用哪种公式或哪种服务更可取。 “分层”一词本身不足以解决计算问题。 Investor.gov 强调咨询协议在确定服务和收费方面的作用。其费用披露解释还将咨询费用与其他可能适用的费用区分开来。这些来源支持要求一个完整的公式；下面的数字和时间表是独立创作的插图。乘法前对每个累进切片设置上限 按照默认 250,000 加元的费用基数，第一个切片包含 100,000 加元，第二个切片包含 150,000 加元。没有第三片数量。每年资产费用为 100,000 加元 × 0.8% 加 150,000 加元 × 0.5%，即 1,550 加元。中间费率仅适用于其切片中的金额。将整个 250,000 加元乘以 0.5% 会得出不同的公式。同样，当客户只有 150,000 加元时，向整个中间部分收取 400,000 加元，则会对规定基础中不存在的资产进行计费。瀑布先暴露每个组件，然后再暴露总数。空切片保持为零，因此读者可以看到，跨越第一个阈值不会擦除第一个切片或立即创建全尺寸的第二个切片。对于非负利率，这种累进资产费用在两个阈值上都是连续的。当下一美元的汇率发生变化时，其斜率也会发生变化。在检查边界附近的报价时，斜率变化和账单跳跃之间的区别很重要。整体平衡区间对所有规定的基数重新定价。替代公式将 250,000 加元置于中间区间，并对所有 250,000 加元收取 0.5% 的费用。其资产费用为 1,250 加元。这是对所发明的整体平衡公式的有效描述，而不是错误地进行的渐进计算。界限很明确：第一段余额正好为 100,000 加元；高于该金额且不超过 500,000 加元的余额使用中间区间。只有 500,000 加元以上的金额才使用顶带。随着费率下降，跨越边界可以降低年度总资产费用，因为新费率适用于整个基础。阈值图表将 100,000 加元与 100,100 加元精确比较，以及 500,000 加元与 500,100 加元精确比较。它不会用隐藏重新定价的平滑线连接宽间隔的报价。在第一个默认边界，累进年度费用增加 0.50 加元，而整体余额费用减少 299.50 加元。第二次，累进费用增加 0.30 加元，总余额费用减少 999.70 加元。这些是所选公式中的条件差异，而不是承诺通过将资产添加到真实账户而节省的费用。按规定顺序放置最低费用和固定费用 该示例首先将 300 加元的最低费用应用于年度资产费用。然后，它会单独添加 120 加元的账户年费。得出的公式为 max(计算的资产费用, 最低资产费用) + 固定账户费用 。在默认基础上，计算出的两项资产费用均已超过最低限额。因此，渐进切片的总报价为 1,670 加元，全平衡带的总报价为 1,370 加元。 300 加元的差异来自于将第一个切片分配给不同的费率；双方均显示相同的 120 加元固定费用。在足够小的余额下，最小值可以将两个报价设置为相同的金额。最低为楼层，而不是在每次计算的费用中额外添加 300 加元。瀑布的上升行只是到达该层所需的正值。其他合同可能会在最终发票上定义最低费用、免除固定费用、合并账户或暂停零资产计费。这些是不同的术语。此图保持假设账户处于开放状态，没有零余额豁免，因此最低固定费用仍然可以在零基数下产生正报价。将总收费率与下一美元费率分开有效收费率将完整的年度报价除以相同的规定费用基数。对于默认累进示例，1,670 加元 ÷ 250,000 加元为 0.668%，显示为 0.67%。它包括固定费用和任何最低调整。该比率不是额外收取一美元的比率。在中间累进切片中，少量额外金额接收输入的中间费率，同时早期切片费用保持不变。有效的最低限额可以暂时阻止发票增加。即使合同产生正费用，零费用基础也会产生不确定的比率。因此，标题显示 N/A 为零，而不是显示 0% 或将该比率视为无限投资损失。该矩阵使用正余额来显示固定费用和最小费用如何影响分母。这是费用与基础的比较，而不是基金费用比率、年度投资回报或对服务质量的判断。改变费率也可以扭转默认排名；这两种公式并不总是更便宜。使实际报价与其自己的计费条款一致 在应用实际计划之前，请确定计费基础中包含的资产。询问该价值是在特定日期测量还是在一段时间内平均，如何处理关联帐户以及现金或特定资产是否受到不同的处理。然后建立切片或频带公式、精确的阈值边界、任何最小值的位置以及包含或排除的固定费用。计费频率、部分年度处理和适用税费需要有自己的条款。将该年度说明分为四个部分并不能建立提供商的季度发票。图表保持基数不变，并将报价费用视为从外部支付。他们不计算账户费用扣除、回报拖累或未来投资组合价值。持续扣除的模型需要指定费用何时离开账户以及后续资产价值如何影响以后的账单。 NASAA 的费用披露讨论强调了客户可以用来验证费用和与账单相符的协议条款的公式。实际检查是对相关基础和期间进行逐项美元计算，然后对所获得的服务进行单独比较。仅较低的费率或发票并不表明两个业务满足相同的需求。

189cbd33605bd588ecab737e05c270fbd54ca37b.src: A clean quote excludes accrued coupon. Include it and separate charges in settlement cash, then reconcile the next coupon with what was already paid before calling the receipt investment profit. A quoted clean price is one component of the cash requirement A coupon bond can be quoted at a price that excludes interest accrued since its preceding coupon date. A purchase cash requirement can therefore exceed the amount obtained by simply multiplying that quote by the face holding. ICE’s clean-price definition distinguishes the price without accrued interest from the dirty price. Its accrued-interest reference connects the accumulated amount to the part of the coupon period already elapsed. The definitions describe the components; the numerical illustration here is independently authored. The example assumes CAD 10,000 face amount and an executed clean quote of 98.5 per CAD 100 face. Clean purchase value is therefore CAD 9,850. That is different from the CAD 10,000 contractual face amount and from the total cash needed to complete this purchase. The bond remains outstanding after the next coupon. The example sells it then; it does not redeem at maturity or receive face value as an additional payment. State the coupon and day-count assumptions explicitly The annual coupon rate is 4% of face, paid in two equal instalments. Each coupon is CAD 10,000 × 4% ÷ 2 = CAD 200 . One chosen coupon period contains 180 model days. Settlement occurs after ninety completed days, halfway through that period. Straight-line accrued coupon is CAD 200 × 90 ÷ 180, or CAD 100 . Dirty purchase value is clean value plus that amount: CAD 9,850 + CAD 100 = CAD 9,950. A separate CAD 10 purchase charge makes the total cash requirement CAD 9,960 . The fee is not accrued interest, and the accrued interest is not a second fee. The 180-day denominator is a teaching assumption. It does not implement an actual bond’s calendar, coupon entitlement, settlement rule or day-count convention. The entered elapsed day refers to the settlement observation. Actual transactions require the instrument’s confirmed dates, conventions and entitled coupon. Receiving the full coupon does not mean earning it all after purchase The buyer is assumed entitled to the full CAD 200 coupon paid on day 180. However, CAD 100 of accrued coupon was already included in the purchase price ninety model days earlier. Subtracting that purchased accrued amount leaves a CAD 100 holding-period coupon component before fees or changes in the clean price. Calling the entire CAD 200 receipt new profit would omit part of the initial outlay. Investor.gov’s accrued-interest glossary describes interest accumulated before payment. Cash payment and the period associated with that amount are therefore separate records. This article’s subtraction is a cash-result reconciliation, not an assessment of taxable interest or any available deduction. Nearness to the coupon date does not make the full coupon a windfall under this model. At day 179, approximately CAD 198.89 of the CAD 200 coupon is already in purchased accrual. Only about CAD 1.11 remains in the holding-period coupon component before fees and price changes. Watch the coupon move from bond value to cash With the default unchanged clean quote, bond value immediately before the coupon is CAD 9,850 plus the full CAD 200 accrued coupon, or CAD 10,050. Immediately after payment, accrued coupon resets to zero in the illustration and bond value is CAD 9,850. The buyer now holds CAD 200 of coupon cash alongside that CAD 9,850 bond value. Combined resources remain CAD 10,050 across the payment event. Adding the coupon to the pre-payment CAD 10,050 bond value would count the distributed amount twice. The change chart subtracts opening dirty value, CAD 9,950, from the bond-value observations. Before payment, the bond change is +CAD 100. After payment, it is −CAD 100, accompanied by CAD 200 cash. The combined change stays +CAD 100 across those two observations. Showing changes makes this transfer visible beside a larger face holding. The chart ends before the sale and excludes both fees. Between the chosen purchase and sale quotes, the clean-value path is assumed linear; it is not a bond-pricing model or a forecast. Reconcile actual assumed receipts against the complete purchase outlay Immediately after the next coupon, the default assumed clean sale quote is still 98.5. Gross sale value is CAD 9,850. Subtracting a separate CAD 10 sale charge leaves CAD 9,840 of sale cash. Sale cash plus the CAD 200 coupon is CAD 10,040. Subtract the original CAD 9,960 purchase cash and the net result is CAD 80 , before tax and with every assumed payment completed. The result waterfall reaches the same answer through components: CAD 200 coupon minus CAD 100 purchased accrued coupon, plus zero clean-price change, minus CAD 10 purchase fee and CAD 10 sale fee. This second route helps identify omissions. Face principal is already represented by selling the bond and cannot be added again as a redemption. Neither fee is deducted a second time. The coupon percentage alone does not identify the holding-period gain or yield to maturity. Vary the exit quote without treating a coupon as price protection Change the clean sale quote to 96 while retaining the default purchase and ninety-day settlement. Clean value falls from CAD 9,850 to CAD 9,600, a CAD 250 decrease. The CAD 100 holding-period coupon component less CAD 20 of fees cannot offset that change: the net result is −CAD 170 . Investor.gov’s selling-before-maturity explanation discusses changing sale values and dealing costs. This calculator selects the exit quote directly; it does not derive a price from interest rates, credit changes or a market yield curve. The signed matrix changes both the settlement day and the later clean quote. A later settlement has a different holding period, so its dollar result cannot be read as an annualized performance ranking against an earlier settlement. Prices, accrual and charges can all affect the cash result. The matrix assigns no probabilities and does not establish that any displayed trade can be executed. Use the confirmed settlement record for an implemented plan For a real purchase, identify the face quantity, the quotation convention, settlement date, coupon schedule, day-count basis, accrued amount and separately charged costs. Check whether a quoted execution price already incorporates a dealer markup or markdown before adding a charge again. The model assumes the promised coupon arrives in full and the buyer can sell immediately afterward at the chosen quote. It does not test creditworthiness, liquidity, settlement delays or ex-coupon arrangements. It also excludes tax, currency conversion and reinvestment. A dated goal needs the cash amount and the date it becomes usable. A future coupon is different from current settlement cash, and a market value is different from net sale proceeds. The four figures make those records visible: price components for the purchase, a coupon transfer in the valuation, a complete cash-result bridge and conditional price-and-timing comparisons. Keep them together when reviewing the transaction rather than allowing the next cash receipt to stand in for the whole investment outcome.
189cbd33605bd588ecab737e05c270fbd54ca37b.zh: 干净的报价不包括累积的优惠券。将其和单独的费用包含在结算现金中，然后将下一张息票与已支付的金额进行核对，然后再调用收据投资利润。干净报价是现金需求的一个组成部分 息票债券的报价价格不包括自前一个息票日期以来应计利息。因此，购买现金需求可能超过简单地将报价乘以面值所获得的金额。 ICE 的清洁价格定义将没有应计利息的价格与肮脏价格区分开来。其应计利息参考将累计金额与已过的息票期部分联系起来。定义描述了组件；这里的数值插图是独立创作的。该示例假设面金额为 10,000 加元，执行的干净报价为每 100 加元 98.5。因此，净购买价值为 9,850 加元。这不同于 10,000 加元的合同金额以及完成此次购买所需的现金总额。该债券在下一次息票后仍保持未偿状态。那么这个例子就卖掉了；它不会在到期时赎回或收到面值作为额外付款。明确说明票面利率和天数假设 年票面利率为面值的 4%，分两期等额支付。每张优惠券为 10,000 加元 × 4% ÷ 2 = 200 加元。选定的优惠券期限包含 180 个模型日。结算发生在九十个完整天后，即该期间的一半。直线累积优惠券为 CAD 200 × 90 ÷ 180 或 CAD 100 。脏购买价值是清洁价值加上该金额：9,850 加元 + 100 加元 = 9,950 加元。单独支付 10 加元的购买费用后，现金需求总额为 9,960 加元。该费用不是应计利息，应计利息也不是第二笔费用。 180 天的分母是一个教学假设。它不实施实际债券的日历、息票权利、结算规则或日计数惯例。输入的经过天数是指沉降观测值。实际交易需要该工具的确认日期、惯例和优惠券。收到全额优惠券并不意味着购买后即可获得全部优惠券 假定买方有权获得第 180 天支付的 200 加元全额优惠券。但是，累积的 100 加元优惠券已在 90 个模型天前包含在购买价格中。减去购买的应计金额，在费用或净价格变化之前留下 100 加元的持有期优惠券部分。将整个 200 加元收入称为新利润将省略部分初始支出。 Investor.gov 的应计利息术语表描述了付款前累积的利息。因此，现金支付以及与该金额相关的期间是单独的记录。本文的减法是现金结果调节，而不是对应税利息或任何可用扣除额的评估。在这种模式下，临近优惠券日期并不会使全额优惠券成为意外之财。在第 179 天，200 加元优惠券中大约 198.89 加元已计入购买应计金额中。在费用和价格变化之前，持有期息票部分中只剩下约 1.11 加元。观察优惠券从债券价值转变为现金 在默认不变的干净报价下，优惠券之前的债券价值为 9,850 加元加上 200 加元应计优惠券，即 10,050 加元。付款后，图中累积的息票立即重置为零，债券价值为 9,850 加元。买家现在持有 200 加元的息票现金以及价值 9,850 加元的债券。在整个支付活动中，合并资源仍为 10,050 加元。将息票添加到预付款 10,050 加元债券价值中，会将分配金额计算两次。变化图表从债券价值观测值中减去期初脏值 9,950 加元。付款前，保证金找零为+100加元。付款后，为-100加元，并附有200加元现金。这两个观察值的综合变化保持+100 加元。显示更改使此转移在更大的面部持有旁边可见。该图表在销售之前结束，不包括这两项费用。在选定的购买和销售报价之间，清洁价值路径假设为线性；它不是债券定价模型或预测。将实际假设收据与完整购买支出进行核对 在下一张优惠券之后，默认假设干净销售报价仍为 98.5。总售价为 9,850 加元。减去 10 加元的单独销售费用，剩下 9,840 加元的销售现金。销售现金加上 200 加元优惠券即为 10,040 加元。减去原来的 9,960 加元购买现金，最终结果为 80 加元（税前）并且每笔假设付款均已完成。结果瀑布通过组件达到相同的答案：200 加元的优惠券减去 100 加元购买的累积优惠券，再加上零净价格变化，减去 10 加元的购买费用和 10 加元的销售费用。第二条路线有助于识别遗漏。面本金已通过出售债券代表，不能再次添加作为赎回。两次费用均不会被扣除。票面利率本身并不能确定持有期收益或到期收益率。改变退出报价，而不将优惠券视为价格保护 将干净销售报价更改为 96，同时保留默认购买和 90 天结算。清洁价值从 9,850 加元降至 9,600 加元，减少了 250 加元。 100 加元的持有期优惠券成分减去 20 加元的费用无法抵消该变化：最终结果为 -170 加元。 Investor.gov 的到期前出售解释讨论了销售价值和交易成本的变化。本计算器直接选择退出报价；它并不从利率、信贷变化或市场收益率曲线中得出价格。签署的矩阵会改变结算日和后来的干净报价。较晚的结算有不同的持有期，因此其美元结果不能被解读为相对于较早的结算的年化业绩排名。价格、应计费用和费用都会影响现金结果。该矩阵没有分配任何概率，也没有确定任何显示的交易都可以执行。将确认的结算记录用于实施的计划 对于实际购买，确定面数、报价约定、结算日期、优惠券时间表、计日基础、应计金额和单独收取的费用。在再次添加费用之前，检查报价的执行价格是否已包含交易商加价或降价。该模型假设承诺的优惠券已全额到达，并且买方可以在之后立即按所选报价出售。它不测试信用度、流动性、结算延迟或息票前安排。它还不包括税收、货币兑换和再投资。一个有日期的目标需要现金金额和可用日期。未来息票不同于当前结算现金，市场价值也不同于净销售收入。这四个数字使这些记录变得可见：购买的价格组成部分、估值中的优惠券转移、完整的现金结果桥梁以及有条件的价格和时间比较。在审查交易时将它们放在一起，而不是让下一个现金收据代替整个投资结果。

a5746b4573dbd940bf708be7232fe6b4c0e28080.src: Compare the additional balance needed for a waiver with the alternative use of that same money. Count waived fees as additional resources only when the freed budget is actually retained. Confirm the waiver condition before comparing the dollars A monthly account fee is visible on a statement. The alternative use of money kept in the account is less visible, but it still belongs in a financial plan. The Financial Consumer Agency of Canada’s chequing-account guidance explains that some accounts waive a monthly fee when a minimum balance is maintained. It also warns that a balance dipping below the requirement for even one day can result in the fee being charged. Check the actual agreement’s measurement rule, qualifying dates and included services. A monthly average is not a substitute for a required daily minimum. This tool accepts a qualifying-month pattern supplied separately; it does not determine whether the entered extra balance satisfies a particular bank’s terms. Use the additional money needed solely for the waiver. Operating cash that would remain in the account under either approach belongs to both plans and is excluded equally. Counting its interest cost in only one alternative would distort the comparison. Give both alternatives the same starting money and outside budget The example assigns CAD 5,000 of additional funds and CAD 16 of outside budget each month to either strategy. It uses a five-year horizon and an independently assumed 3% net effective annual alternative yield. These are authored inputs, not a current account offer. Strategy A retains the CAD 5,000 in non-interest chequing. When a month qualifies for the waiver, its unused CAD 16 budget is deposited at month-end into a separate account earning the assumed yield. When a month does not qualify, that budget pays the fee. Strategy B puts the same initial CAD 5,000 in the alternative account. Its CAD 16 outside budget pays the monthly fee every month. The model does not also remove that fee from B’s invested balance, because doing both would charge the same expense twice. At the defaults, both strategies receive the same CAD 960 of outside budget over sixty months. A retains all of it as saving; B spends it on fees. If the household spends A’s freed budget instead, the resulting wealth path will differ from the saving behavior shown here. Reconcile the ending resources instead of treating the waived fee as a yield With all twelve months qualifying each year, A ends with approximately CAD 6,033.30: the unchanged CAD 5,000 plus saved fees and their growth. B ends with approximately CAD 5,796.37 from the same initial balance earning the assumed yield. A therefore has about CAD 236.93 more ending resources under these conditions. The waterfall reconciles that difference. It adds CAD 960 of avoided fees actually saved, adds about CAD 73.30 of growth on those savings, then subtracts about CAD 796.37 of growth forgone on the additional balance. The common CAD 5,000 cancels from the comparison. No fee principal or interest is counted twice. Neither endpoint includes the household’s other assets or any value assigned to account features. FCAC’s account-maintenance fee review discusses both minimum-balance waivers and the opportunity cost of the funds retained. Its broader account-service comparison is a reason to check features separately, rather than conclude that a positive modeled difference identifies the best banking arrangement. Use a break-even balance with a stated timing convention The net effective annual yield is converted to an equivalent monthly rate: one plus the annual rate, raised to one-twelfth, minus one. Saved fees arrive at month-end and earn nothing before that month’s deposit. With every month qualifying and a positive yield, the break-even additional balance equals the monthly fee divided by that monthly rate. At the default 3% net effective annual yield and CAD 16 monthly fee, it is approximately CAD 6,487.53. This is an equal-ending-resources threshold under the selected saving behavior. It is not a required bank balance. Dividing an annual fee by an effective annual yield uses a different timing shortcut, so it need not give exactly the same result. At a zero alternative yield, the model does not divide by zero. If any fee budget is saved, A has more resources for every finite extra balance in this limited comparison. If no fee saving exists either, all balances tie. Access, other charges and alternative uses outside this model still require their own assessment. Stress eligibility and opportunity cost before changing accounts The signed bars vary how many months qualify each year. The first listed months of each year qualify, and later months do not. This declared ordering matters because an earlier saved deposit has longer to earn the assumed yield. The matrix changes the additional balance and net yield while retaining that same calendar and outside budget. Positive cells mean A ends with more modeled resources; negative cells mean B does. The cells carry no probability or promise that an account will waive its fee. Before applying the comparison, review recent daily closing balances, upcoming bills and the actual waiver wording. Identify the extra cash that can remain assigned without being counted again as money for another goal. Then compare transaction limits, service access, other fees, interest conditions and the reliability of the assumed alternative use. The extra balance remains the household’s money; the waiver condition does not make it legally inaccessible. Drawing on it may simply change eligibility. Keep that practical choice beside the numerical comparison.
a5746b4573dbd940bf708be7232fe6b4c0e28080.zh: 将豁免所需的额外余额与相同资金的替代用途进行比较。仅当实际保留释放的预算时，才将免除的费用计为额外资源。在比较美元之前确认豁免条件 每月的账户费用在对账单上可见。账户中资金的替代用途不太明显，但它仍然属于财务计划。加拿大金融消费者管理局的支票账户指南解释说，某些账户在维持最低余额时可以免除月费。它还警告说，即使有一天余额低于要求，也可能会导致收取费用。检查实际协议的衡量规则、资格日期和包含的服务。月平均值不能替代每日最低要求。该工具接受单独提供的合格月份模式；它不能确定输入的额外余额是否满足特定银行的条款。仅使用豁免所需的额外资金。根据任何一种方法保留在账户中的运营现金都属于这两种计划，并且同样被排除在外。仅计算一种替代方案的利息成本会扭曲比较。为两种备选方案提供相同的起始资金和外部预算 该示例每月为任一策略分配 5,000 加元的额外资金和 16 加元的外部预算。它使用五年期限和独立假设的 3% 净有效年替代收益率。这些是创作的输入，而不是经常账户报价。策略 A 保留 5,000 加元的无息支票。当某个月符合豁免条件时，其未使用的 16 加元预算将在月底存入一个单独的账户，赚取假定的收益率。当一个月不符合条件时，该预算将支付费用。策略 B 将同样的初始 5,000 加元存入替代账户。其每月 16 加元的外部预算支付月费。该模型也不会从 B 的投资余额中删除该费用，因为同时执行这两项操作会收取两次相同的费用。默认情况下，两种策略在 60 个月内收到相同的 960 加元外部预算。 A 将其全部保留为保存； B 将其用于费用。如果家庭花 A 的自由预算，则最终的财富路径将与此处所示的储蓄行为不同。协调最终资源，而不是将免除的费用视为收益 每年所有 12 个月都符合条件，A 最终约为 6,033.30 加元：未改变的 5,000 加元加上节省的费用及其增长。 B 最终从相同的初始余额中获得了大约 5,796.37 加元，赚取了假定的收益率。因此，在这些条件下，A 拥有大约 236.93 加元的期末资源。瀑布弥补了这种差异。它增加了实际节省的 960 加元的避免费用，增加了这些节省的约 73.30 加元的增长，然后减去了额外余额中放弃的约 796.37 加元的增长。普通的5000加元在比较中就被取消了。没有费用本金或利息被计算两次。这两个端点都不包含家庭的其他资产或分配给帐户功能的任何值。 FCAC 的账户维护费审查讨论了最低余额豁免和保留资金的机会成本。其更广泛的账户服务比较是单独检查功能的原因，而不是得出结论：正模型差异可以确定最佳银行安排。使用盈亏平衡和规定的时间约定 将净有效年收益率转换为等值的月利率：一加年利率，提高到十二分之一，减一。节省的费用在月底到达，并且在该月的存款之前没有任何收入。如果每个月都符合资格且收益率为正，那么盈亏平衡的额外余额等于月费除以月费率。按默认 3% 净有效年收益率和 16 加元月费计算，约为 6,487.53 加元。这是所选保存行为下的均等结束资源阈值。这不是必需的银行余额。年费除以有效年收益率使用了不同的时间捷径，因此不需要给出完全相同的结果。在替代收益率为零的情况下，模型不会除以零。如果节省了任何费用预算，则在这个有限的比较中，A 对于每个有限的额外余额都有更多的资源。如果也不存在节省费用，则所有余额平局。该模式之外的访问、其他费用和替代用途仍然需要自己的评估。在更改帐户之前强调资格和机会成本 签署的条形图每年有多少个月符合资格。每年列出的前几个月符合条件，后面的月份则不符合条件。这种声明的顺序很重要，因为较早保存的存款有更长的时间来赚取假定的收益率。该矩阵改变了额外余额和净收益，同时保留相同的日历和外部预算。正细胞意味着 A 结束时有更多的建模资源；阴性细胞意味着 B 确实如此。这些单元不具有账户免除费用的可能性或承诺。在进行比较之前，请查看最近的每日期末余额、即将到期的账单和实际的豁免措辞。确定可以保留分配的额外现金，而不会再次计入另一个目标的资金。然后比较交易限制、服务访问、其他费用、利息条件以及假设的替代用途的可靠性。额外的余额仍然是家庭的钱；豁免条件并不使其在法律上无法获得。利用它可能只会改变资格。除了数值比较之外，还要保留实际的选择。

e5dcc794ab914c052c9578b15e97116028cbdd32.src: The relevant comparison starts with the extra cash needed above your normal working balance. Keeping that cash remains a household asset, while its forgone earnings affect the cost comparison. Read the balance condition before multiplying the monthly fee by twelve The Financial Consumer Agency of Canada’s chequing-account guidance explains that some accounts waive their monthly fee if a minimum balance is maintained. It also warns that falling below the requirement for only one day can trigger a full monthly charge. The applicable account agreement determines the actual condition. A monthly average is therefore not enough to establish eligibility under a daily minimum rule. A pay deposit later in the month does not change an earlier closing balance. Review payment dates, debit timing and the amount available before each transaction. This tool assumes the extra-balance choice successfully meets all requirements for twelve months. It does not simulate a particular account’s transactions or certify that a real household will qualify. Calculate the additional balance rather than charging the whole minimum to the decision Suppose the invented account requires CAD 4,000 and costs CAD 15 each non-qualifying month. The household already plans to keep a minimum working balance of CAD 1,500 after ordinary transactions. The additional cash needed is CAD 2,500. The CAD 1,500 working floor stays in chequing under both choices. This comparison therefore considers only the extra CAD 2,500. If the household’s actual planned minimum were zero, the full CAD 4,000 would instead be additional. An average balance of CAD 1,500 would not establish the same result as a minimum floor of CAD 1,500. When the entered working floor already equals or exceeds the requirement, both modeled choices qualify without adding cash. The incremental fees avoided, interest forgone and resource difference all become zero. There is no extra-balance decision to fund. Give both choices the same cash and monthly budget At the default inputs, both choices begin with CAD 2,500 available in addition to their common working cash. Both also receive CAD 15 each month from the household budget for banking costs. The extra-balance choice keeps CAD 2,500 in non-interest-bearing chequing. Its fee is waived, so the monthly CAD 15 is retained separately at zero return. After twelve months, the resources shown are CAD 2,500 of principal plus CAD 180 of unspent fee budget: CAD 2,680. The no-addition choice keeps CAD 2,500 in an alternative cash account at an assumed 3% effective annual return after its tax and costs. Monthly fees use its CAD 15 monthly budget. The original cash is not drawn down to pay those fees. At year-end, principal and interest total CAD 2,575. Both start with the same resources and receive the same additional household cash. This prevents fee savings from appearing as free money supplied to only one side. Treat the retained principal as an asset and the forgone interest as a cost The fee waiver avoids CAD 180 over the year. The extra CAD 2,500 could have earned CAD 75 at the assumed 3% return. The modeled resource advantage is CAD 105: CAD 180 less CAD 75. The CAD 2,500 principal is not spent as a fee. It remains owned by the household. Its location determines which cash uses remain compatible with the waiver and which earnings are forgone. FCAC’s review of account maintenance fees identifies the same broad trade-off between fee savings, balance requirements and alternative uses of cash. The figures here are independently constructed, with no bank or product recommendation. Use a cash-return hurdle that matches the comparison’s tax and timing assumptions With a positive additional balance, divide annual fees avoided by that balance to find the break-even effective annual return. The default calculation is CAD 180 ÷ CAD 2,500 = 7.2%. At that return, the alternative earns CAD 180, matching the fee budget retained by the extra-balance choice. That percentage is a comparison threshold, not interest earned in chequing. The alternative input is already after its assumed tax and costs, so it should not be filled with a headline promotional rate without adjusting for its actual duration and conditions. The line varies that alternative return. The matrix varies the fee and the extra balance required. A higher fee can make a waiver more valuable while still leaving a different account with a better overall service-and-cost combination. This same-account comparison cannot rank all available accounts. Check the cash calendar and service needs before implementing the result Cash kept for a waiver may also be available in an emergency, but spending it can cause a later account charge. Record both uses without treating the same dollars as separate reserves. A planned payment must have a funding route compatible with the actual account conditions. The FCAC savings-account guide notes that transfer timing can vary. The tool assumes the alternative balance can stay invested for a whole year; it does not establish that transfers will arrive before a real bill or minimum-balance test. For an actual review, compare the services used, all relevant fees, qualification terms and access needs. A lower-cost account may meet those needs without requiring extra cash. A waiver can be valuable, but its arithmetic is only one part of the account choice.
e5dcc794ab914c052c9578b15e97116028cbdd32.zh: 相关比较从超出正常工作余额所需的额外现金开始。保留这些现金仍然是家庭资产，而其放弃的收入会影响成本比较。在将月费乘以 12 之前先阅读余额条件加拿大金融消费者管理局的支票账户指南解释说，如果维持最低余额，某些账户将免除月费。它还警告说，仅一天低于要求可能会触发每月全额收费。适用的账户协议决定实际情况。因此，每月平均值不足以确定每日最低规则下的资格。当月晚些时候支付押金不会改变之前的期末余额。在每次交易前查看付款日期、借记时间和可用金额。该工具假设额外余额选择成功满足十二个月的所有要求。它不会模拟特定账户的交易或证明真实家庭符合资格。计算额外余额，而不是根据决策收取全部最低金额 假设发明的帐户需要 4,000 加元，并且每个不合格的月份花费 15 加元。该家庭已计划在正常交易后保留 1,500 加元的最低工作余额。所需额外现金为 2,500 加元。在这两种选择下，1,500 加元的工作楼层都处于检查状态。因此，本次比较仅考虑额外的 2,500 加元。如果家庭实际计划的最低限额为零，则需要额外支付 4,000 加元。平均余额 1,500 加元不会产生与最低下限 1,500 加元相同的结果。当输入的工作楼层已经等于或超过要求时，两个模型选择都符合资格，无需添加现金。避免的增量费用、放弃的利息和资源差异都为零。没有额外余额决定提供资金。为两种选择提供相同的现金和每月预算 在默认输入下，两种选择除了共同的流动现金外，还可以使用 2,500 加元。两人还每月从家庭预算中获得 15 加元的银行费用。额外余额选择可在无息支票中保留 2,500 加元。它的费用被免除，所以每月15加元单独保留，零回报。十二个月后，显示的资源为本金 2,500 加元加上未用费用预算 180 加元：2,680 加元。不增加的选择将 2,500 加元保留在替代现金账户中，假设扣除税费和成本后的有效年回报率为 3%。每月费用使用其每月 15 加元的预算。原始现金不会被提取来支付这些费用。截至年底，本金和利息总计 2,575 加元。两者都以相同的资源开始，并获得相同的额外家庭现金。这可以防止节省的费用表现为仅提供给一侧的免费资金。将保留的本金视为资产，将放弃的利息视为成本 全年免收费用 180 加元。按假设 3% 的回报率，额外的 2,500 加元本来可以赚取 75 加元。建模的资源优势为 105 加元：180 加元减去 75 加元。2,500 加元本金不作为费用使用。它仍然归该家庭所有。它的地点决定了哪些现金用途仍符合豁免规定以及哪些收入被放弃。 FCAC 对账户维护费用的审查确定了费用节省、余额要求和现金替代用途之间同样广泛的权衡。这里的数字是独立构建的，没有银行或产品推荐。使用与比较的税收和时间假设相匹配的现金回报门槛 在额外余额为正的情况下，将避免的年费除以该余额即可找到盈亏平衡的有效年度回报。默认计算为 180 加元 ÷ 2,500 加元 = 7.2%。在该回报中，替代方案可赚取 180 加元，与额外余额选择保留的费用预算相匹配。该百分比是一个比较阈值，而不是支票赚取的利息。替代投入已经扣除了假定的税收和成本，因此不应在未根据实际持续时间和条件进行调整的情况下填写标题促销率。该线路会改变替代返回值。该矩阵会改变费用和所需的额外余额。较高的费用可以使豁免更有价值，同时仍然为不同的帐户留下更好的整体服务和成本组合。此相同帐户比较无法对所有可用帐户进行排名。在实施结果之前检查现金日历和服务需求 为豁免而保留的现金也可能在紧急情况下可用，但花费它可能会导致以后产生帐户费用。记录两种用途，而不将相同的美元视为单独的储备。计划付款必须有符合实际账户情况的资金路径。 FCAC 储蓄账户指南指出，转账时间可能会有所不同。该工具假设替代余额可以保持投资一整年；它没有规定转账将在实际账单或最低余额测试之前到达。为了进行实际审查，请比较所使用的服务、所有相关费用、资格条款和访问需求。成本较低的帐户可以满足这些需求，而不需要额外的现金。豁免可能很有价值，但其算术只是账户选择的一部分。

19980eed23ab6729f4db4431d98b9afca81e5ada.src: Read who answered, which horizon was asked and which statistic is shown. Then choose and test household price assumptions explicitly, without silently turning a survey median into a promised inflation path. Identify the survey observation before using its number An inflation-expectations headline can sound like a ready-made assumption for every household budget. Before using it, check who supplied the answer, the horizon of the question and the statistic used to summarize the responses. The first three charts reproduce or derive from the Bank of Canada’s Canadian Survey of Consumer Expectations. The quarterly report was released on 19 October 2026. Its online responses were collected from 5 to 27 August, followed by phone interviews from 24 August to 4 September. The source data use quarter-start dates as index keys. For example, 1 July 2026 identifies 2026 Q3; it is not a claim that the survey was conducted that day. Collection dates, reference quarters, publication dates and this article’s retrieval date serve different purposes. The Bank’s survey page explains that these results summarize respondents’ opinions and do not necessarily reflect the Bank’s views or policies. Publishing a survey does not turn each response or its summary statistic into the institution’s own forecast. Keep the perceived past and the expected future separate The latest snapshot contains a perception measure about the preceding twelve months and three expectation horizons. The source labels the statistic an interpolated median. This guide retains that label rather than replacing it with an arithmetic mean or an individual household prediction. The perception row summarizes what respondents thought inflation had been. It is not a direct observation of the Consumer Price Index. The future rows retain the source’s one-, two- and five-year-ahead labels; they are answers to different horizon questions. The bars are percentage levels, not percentages of the population belonging to mutually exclusive groups. Adding them would not produce a total, and a pie chart would give the wrong denominator. Likewise, averaging horizons would create a new statistic without establishing that it has a useful forecasting interpretation. A five-year-ahead label also does not provide a complete sequence of five annual inflation outcomes. Do not take the first-year median, append another horizon’s median as the following year and treat the result as an observed or guaranteed cumulative price path. Compare matching horizons across quarters The history chart keeps eight quarters from 2024 Q4 through 2026 Q3. Each series retains the same expectation horizon and uses the same source vintage. The connected points are quarterly published summaries rather than monthly measurements or the beliefs of one person tracked continuously. The change chart asks a narrower question: how much did each published median move between 2026 Q2 and Q3? It subtracts percentage levels and reports the result in percentage points. A difference of 0.52 percentage points, for example, is not a 0.52% relative change and does not describe a 0.52% rise in the price level. Those calculations need other denominators and definitions. Keeping the unit explicit prevents a small movement in a summary rate from being relabeled as a household bill increase. The extract contains no respondent-level records or uncertainty intervals for the displayed comparisons. The charts therefore make no significance, individual-transition or causal claim. A movement in a median alone does not tell us why respondents answered differently or how broadly a change was shared. Retain the source’s units, dates and missing-data boundaries The source extract preserves the four series identifiers, their labels, the interpolated-median definition, percent units, release and collection dates and hashes of the original public report and linked data. Its checks require eight unique consecutive quarter keys and all thirty-two selected values. The published numbers are percentages. They are converted to fractions once for chart formatting, rather than being multiplied into larger percentages or mistaken for probabilities. Historical values are retained as supplied by the selected report’s data group; the article does not claim they are unchanged from every original quarterly release. The chart table gives full quarter labels even though the narrow axis uses short labels. No missing quarter is filled with zero, and no daily series is invented between quarterly points. The official survey panels remain fixed when the household scenario controls change. This bounded extract is enough for the descriptive comparison shown. It is not a replacement for the full questionnaire, methodology or microdata needed for a different statistical question. If a later source revision changes the schema or selected dates, the extraction check should fail visibly rather than quietly drawing a different dataset. Build the household price example from independent assumptions The last two charts use a separate hypothetical starting annual cost of CAD 12,000 and an independently entered 3% annual price-growth assumption. They do not copy a survey median into the calculator or assign a probability to that rate. The selected ten-year endpoint is CAD 12,000 × 1.03 10 , approximately CAD 16,127.00 for one year’s cost at that future date. This is not the sum of ten years’ bills, a present value or the amount that must already be in savings. The matrix varies price growth and the horizon while retaining the starting annual amount. Its cells are alternative endpoint annual costs, with no confidence level or likelihood attached. A household can use a supported range to see sensitivity without presenting one convenient assumption as certain. The simple model holds the quantity and quality of the planned consumption constant. Actual household costs can also change with location, family circumstances, services required and the prices of specific items. Those changes need their own assumptions rather than being hidden inside the general growth rate. Connect evidence to the plan through a stated assumption Survey expectations can provide context about what people think and how those views vary over time. A household spending model needs an explicit definition of the expense, its date, its price basis and the assumptions that convert today’s amount to a later one. Keep the evidence and the scenario visible side by side. Record the survey’s reference quarter when citing it, and separately record why a chosen household assumption is appropriate for the expense and horizon being tested. A round number in a calculator is not evidence about future prices. If the question is about actual purchasing power lost so far, use the relevant observed price index and matching dates. If it concerns a specific future bill, obtain a current quote and applicable terms where possible. Neither task is completed merely by reading an inflation-expectations median. The five charts make those roles inspectable: survey snapshot, consistent quarterly history, percentage-point differences, an independent annual-cost path and a range of endpoint scenarios. Each has its own units and data table, so the reader can follow the calculation without treating opinion, measurement and a planning assumption as the same thing.
19980eed23ab6729f4db4431d98b9afca81e5ada.zh: 了解谁回答了、询问了哪个范围以及显示了哪些统计数据。然后明确选择和测试家庭价格假设，而不是默默地将调查中位数转变为承诺的通胀路径。在使用数据之前确定调查观察结果 通胀预期标题听起来像是针对每个家庭预算的现成假设。在使用它之前，请检查谁提供了答案、问题的范围以及用于总结答案的统计数据。前三张图表复制或源自加拿大央行的加拿大消费者期望调查。该季度报告于2026年10月19日发布。8月5日至27日收集了网上反馈，8月24日至9月4日进行了电话采访。源数据使用季度开始日期作为索引键。例如，2026 年 7 月 1 日标识 2026 年第三季度；这并不是说调查是在当天进行的。收集日期、参考季度、出版日期和本文的检索日期有不同的用途。世行的调查页面解释说，这些结果总结了受访者的意见，并不一定反映世行的观点或政策。发布调查并不会将每个回复或其汇总统计数据转化为该机构自己的预测。将感知的过去和预期的未来分开最新的快照包含对过去十二个月和三个预期范围的感知测量。来源将统计量标记为插值中位数。本指南保留了该标签，而不是用算术平均值或个人家庭预测取代它。看法行总结了受访者对通货膨胀的看法。它不是对消费者价格指数的直接观察。未来的行保留来源的提前一年、两年和五年的标签；它们是不同地平线问题的答案。条形图是百分比水平，而不是属于相互排斥群体的人口百分比。将它们相加不会产生总数，而且饼图会给出错误的分母。同样，平均范围会创建一个新的统计数据，而无需确定它具有有用的预测解释。提前五年的标签也没有提供五个年度通胀结果的完整序列。不要采用第一年的中位数，附加另一个范围的中位数作为下一年，并将结果视为观察到的或保证的累积价格路径。比较各个季度的匹配范围历史图表保留了从 2024 年第四季度到 2026 年第三季度的八个季度。每个系列都保留相同的期望范围并使用相同的来源年份。连接点是每季度发布的摘要，而不是每月的测量值或连续跟踪的一个人的信念。变化图表提出了一个更狭窄的问题：2026 年第二季度和第三季度之间每个公布的中位数变动了多少？它减去百分比水平并以百分点报告结果。例如，0.52 个百分点的差异并不是 0.52% 的相对变化，也不代表价格水平上涨了 0.52%。这些计算需要其他分母和定义。保持单位明确可以防止汇总费率的小幅变动被重新标记为家庭账单增加。摘录不包含受访者级别记录或所显示比较的不确定区间。因此，这些图表没有任何意义、个体转变或因果关系。仅中位数的变化并不能告诉我们为什么受访者的回答不同，或者改变的范围有多大。保留源的单位、日期和缺失数据边界源摘录保留了四个系列标识符、它们的标签、插值中位数定义、百分比单位、发布和收集日期以及原始公开报告和链接数据的哈希值。它的检查需要八个唯一的连续四分之一键和所有三十二个选定值。公布的数字为百分比。它们会被转换为分数一次以进行图表格式化，而不是乘以更大的百分比或被误认为概率。保留所选报告数据组提供的历史值；该文章并未声称它们与每个原始季度发布的版本相比没有变化。即使窄轴使用短标签，图表也会提供完整的季度标签。缺少的季度不会用零填充，并且在季度点之间不会发明每日系列。当家庭情况发生变化时，官方调查小组保持不变。这个有限的提取足以用于所示的描述性比较。它不能替代不同统计问题所需的完整调查问卷、方法或微观数据。如果稍后的源版本更改了架构或选定的日期，则提取检查应该明显失败，而不是悄悄地绘制不同的数据集。根据独立假设构建家庭价格示例 最后两张图表使用单独的假设起始年度成本 12,000 加元和独立输入的 3% 年度价格增长假设。他们不会将调查中位数复制到计算器中或为该比率分配概率。选定的十年期终点为 CAD 12,000 × 1.03 10 ，大约为未来日期一年的成本 16,127.00 CAD。这不是十年账单的总和、现值或必须已经存入储蓄的金额。该矩阵改变价格增长和范围，同时保留起始年度金额。其单元格是替代终点年度成本，没有附加置信水平或可能性。家庭可以使用受支持的范围来查看敏感性，而无需提出一个方便的假设作为确定。简单模型保持计划消费的数量和质量恒定。实际家庭成本也会随着地点、家庭情况、所需服务和特定物品的价格而变化。这些变化需要它们自己的假设，而不是隐藏在总体增长率中。通过既定假设将证据与计划联系起来 调查预期可以提供人们的想法以及这些观点如何随时间变化的背景。家庭支出模型需要对支出、日期、价格基础以及将今天的金额转换为以后的金额的假设进行明确的定义。让证据和场景并排可见。在引用调查时记录调查的参考季度，并单独记录为什么所选家庭假设适合测试的费用和范围。计算器中的整数并不是未来价格的证据。如果问题是关于迄今为止实际购买力的损失，请使用相关的观察到的价格指数和匹配日期。如果涉及特定的未来账单，请尽可能获取当前报价和适用条款。仅仅通过读取通胀预期中值是无法完成这两项任务的。这五个图表使这些角色变得可检查：调查快照、一致的季度历史记录、百分点差异、独立的年度成本路径和一系列端点场景。每个都有自己的单位和数据表，因此读者可以遵循计算，而无需将意见、测量和计划假设视为同一事物。

21faafdbfa527f149e8823c3be0a7d5591ddcb6b.src: A repayment promise does not fund a bill before the cash arrives. Track unpaid principal separately and test your own payment calendar under a delay. Record the cash leaving before counting any future receipt Lending money to a family member changes the lender’s immediate access to cash. A record of the amount still owed can help track the arrangement, but it cannot be used to pay another bill before the borrower actually repays it. The example starts with CAD 60,000 of accessible cash. An interest-free advance of CAD 20,000 leaves at month zero, reducing that cash to CAD 40,000. The unpaid original principal record starts at CAD 20,000. The calculator keeps those two quantities separate and does not value the receivable as a liquid asset. All amounts and dates are original assumptions. The tool assumes a repayable principal advance for its arithmetic; it does not decide whether a real transfer is legally a loan or a gift, assess collection rights or determine what the borrower can afford. Put the lender’s separate commitments on the same calendar The lender has an assumed CAD 500 monthly cash surplus after ordinary spending and a separate CAD 50,000 bill in month twelve. The surplus is not interest from the loan. It is other household cash left after routine costs and is the same in every comparison. The original repayment schedule begins in month six, with CAD 1,000 of principal returned each month until the original advance is repaid. The model credits each month’s ordinary surplus and any principal receipt before paying the one-time bill at that month-end. A bill arriving earlier within the month could need another timing buffer. The keep-cash control makes no family advance. It provides a useful reference for the lender’s cash, but it does not provide the same assistance to the family member. It should not be described as an equally supportive alternative merely because its cash line is higher. Count only the repayments that arrive before the bill Under the scheduled case, receipts occur in months six through twelve before the lender’s bill. That is seven payments, or CAD 7,000. By the end of month twelve, cash is CAD 40,000 after the advance, plus CAD 6,000 of ordinary surplus, plus CAD 7,000 received, less the CAD 50,000 bill: CAD 3,000 . Without the advance, the same cash calculation ends month twelve at CAD 16,000. The difference is not the full original CAD 20,000 because CAD 7,000 has already returned. The on-schedule loan still has CAD 13,000 of original principal unpaid at that point. A principal repayment moves an amount from the unpaid-principal record into cash. It is not an additional investment gain on top of that principal. This illustration charges no interest and makes no tax calculation. A delayed schedule can leave an earlier bill unfunded The default stress shifts every repayment twelve months later, so the first receipt arrives in month eighteen. There are no principal receipts before the month-twelve bill. The lender’s ledger then becomes CAD 40,000 + CAD 6,000 − CAD 50,000 = minus CAD 4,000 . The negative number identifies an unfunded amount. It does not mean a bank has supplied an overdraft or that the bill has somehow been paid. To make every ledger date non-negative under this exact scenario, the lender would need CAD 4,000 of additional cash available at the start, or another explicitly modeled response. Later receipts can improve the later balance but cannot retroactively fund the earlier payment date. A positive result at the end of a reporting window is therefore not enough to establish that the plan could be carried out throughout it. Keep the ending principal record separate from collectability At the end of the selected 24 months, the on-schedule case has received nineteen CAD 1,000 payments. It shows CAD 21,000 in the cash ledger and CAD 1,000 of unpaid principal. The delayed case has received seven payments and shows CAD 9,000 in its raw cash ledger with CAD 13,000 unpaid. Those are cash-and-principal records under the stated receipt schedules. They do not establish the economic value of either remaining claim. An unpaid amount can be due later, disputed, partly recoverable or not recoverable; the model has no evidence from which to value those possibilities. The delayed case’s CAD 9,000 ending ledger also does not erase the earlier CAD 4,000 funding gap. If CAD 4,000 were actually added at the beginning, it would change every cash point and the ending amount. The displayed ledger remains the unfinanced scenario, with the separate funding-need metric making that missing resource visible. Test the lender’s deadline and the receipt delay together The matrix changes the lender’s bill month and the delay applied to the original repayment schedule. Each cell calculates the extra starting cash needed over the whole selected window. It is not simply the cash balance on the bill date or the amount expected from the borrower at the end. This distinction matters if the ordinary monthly surplus is negative or the advance itself exceeds starting cash. The lender can then need additional funds before the separate bill arrives. The bar comparison includes the keep-cash control so an underlying budget deficit is not silently attributed entirely to helping the family member. A repayment amount of zero produces no receipts in the model, without treating the unpaid principal as forgiven. Likewise, a first receipt or bill after the reporting window remains outside the displayed dates; it is not cancelled. Review the window before concluding that an obligation has disappeared. Use the calendar to make the arrangement specific The Consumer Financial Protection Bureau’s family-lending guidance asks people to clarify whether support is a gift or a loan, consider their own finances, and discuss repayment dates and changed circumstances. That U.S. educational source supports a conversation about expectations; it does not supply Canadian tax or legal treatment for this illustration. Separate money already committed to your own bills from cash available to advance. State the amount, first receipt date and repayment frequency clearly. Check your own payment calendar under an agreed delay stress. Keep actual receipts and unpaid principal in separate records. Revisit the plan when either household’s circumstances change. No default probability, enforcement, collateral, interest, fee, tax, borrowing facility or promise of repayment is included. The purpose is to expose the lender’s cash dependence on future receipts, rather than to label a relative’s reliability or replace an actual agreement.
21faafdbfa527f149e8823c3be0a7d5591ddcb6b.zh: 在现金到达之前，还款承诺不会为账单提供资金。单独跟踪未付本金并在延迟情况下测试您自己的付款日历。在计算未来的收据之前记录留下的现金 借钱给家庭成员会改变贷款机构立即获取现金的方式。仍欠金额的记录可以帮助跟踪安排，但在借款人实际偿还之前不能用于支付其他账单。该示例以 60,000 加元的可用现金开始。零月时可免息预付 20,000 加元，现金减少至 40,000 加元。未付原始本金记录起价为 20,000 加元。计算器将这两个数量分开，并且不会将应收账款作为流动资产进行评估。所有金额和日期均为原始假设。该工具假设其算术需要偿还本金预付款；它不决定实际转让在法律上是贷款还是赠与，不评估收款权或确定借款人的负担能力。将贷款机构的单独承诺放在同一日历上 假设贷款机构在正常支出后每月有 500 加元的现金盈余，并在第 12 个月有单独的 50,000 加元的账单。盈余不是贷款利息。这是扣除日常开支后剩下的其他家庭现金，并且在每次比较中都是相同的。最初的还款计划从第六个月开始，每月返还 1,000 加元的本金，直到偿还最初的预付款。该模型在月底支付一次性账单之前，将每月的普通盈余和任何本金收入记入贷款机构。本月早些时候到达的法案可能需要另一个时间缓冲。保留现金控制不会给家庭带来任何预支。它为贷款机构的现金提供了有用的参考，但它并没有为家庭成员提供相同的帮助。不应仅仅因为其现金额度较高而将其描述为具有同等支持性的替代方案。仅计算在账单之前到达的还款 在预定情况下，收款发生在贷款机构账单之前的第 6 个月到第 12 个月。即七笔付款，即 7,000 加元。到十二月底，预付款后现金为 40,000 加元，加上普通盈余 6,000 加元，加上收到的 7,000 加元，减去 50,000 加元的票据：3,000 加元。如果没有预付款，同样的现金计算在第 12 个月结束时为 16,000 加元。差额不是原来的 20,000 加元，因为 7,000 加元已经退回。此时，按期贷款仍有 13,000 加元的原始本金未付。本金偿还将未付本金记录中的金额转为现金。这不是本金之上的额外投资收益。此图不收取利息，也不进行税收计算。延迟的时间表可能会使较早的账单无法获得资金。默认压力会在十二个月后转移每笔还款，因此第一张收据会在第十八个月到达。第十二个月的账单之前没有主要收据。然后，贷款机构的账本变为 40,000 加元 + 6,000 加元 - 50,000 加元 = 减去 4,000 加元。负数表示未提供资金的金额。这并不意味着银行已提供透支或账单已以某种方式支付。在这种情况下，为了使每个账本日期都为非负数，贷款机构需要在开始时提供 4,000 加元的额外可用现金，或其他明确建模的响应。较晚的收据可以改善后来的余额，但不能追溯为较早的付款日期提供资金。因此，报告窗口结束时的积极结果不足以证明该计划可以在整个报告窗口中得到执行。将期末本金记录与可收回性分开 在选定的 24 个月结束时，按计划进行的案件已收到 19 笔 1,000 加元的付款。它显示现金分类账中有 21,000 加元，还有 1,000 加元未付本金。该延迟案件已收到七笔付款，其原始现金分类账显示 9,000 加元，还有 13,000 加元未付款。这些是规定收据表下的现金和本金记录。他们没有确定剩余索赔的经济价值。未付金额可能会稍后到期、有争议、部分可收回或不可收回；该模型没有证据来评估这些可能性。延迟案件的 9,000 加元期末账簿也没有消除之前 4,000 加元的资金缺口。如果开始时实际添加 4,000 加元，则每个现金点和最终金额都会发生变化。显示的账本仍然是未融资的场景，单独的资金需求指标使缺失的资源可见。一起测试贷款机构的截止日期和收款延迟 该矩阵更改了贷款机构的账单月份和应用于原始还款计划的延迟。每个单元格计算整个选定窗口内所需的额外起始现金。它不仅仅是账单日的现金余额或最终借款人预期的金额。如果普通每月盈余为负或预付款本身超过起始现金，则这种区别很重要。然后，在单独的账单到达之前，贷款机构可能需要额外的资金。酒吧比较包括保留现金控制，因此潜在的预算赤字不会默默地完全归因于帮助家庭成员。还款额为零时，模型中不会产生任何收据，也不会将未付本金视为已免除。同样，报告窗口之后的第一个收据或账单仍然在显示的日期之外；它没有被取消。在得出义务已消失的结论之前检查窗口。使用日历进行具体安排消费者金融保护局的家庭贷款指南要求人们澄清支持是礼物还是贷款，考虑自己的财务状况，并讨论还款日期和变化的情况。美国的教育资源支持关于期望的对话；它不为此插图提供加拿大税收或法律待遇。将已用于您自己账单的资金与可预支的现金分开。清楚注明金额、首次收款日期和还款频率。在商定的延迟压力下检查您自己的付款日历。将实际收入和未付本金分别保存在记录中。当任何一个家庭的情况发生变化时，重新审视该计划。不包括违约概率、执行、抵押品、利息、费用、税收、借款便利或还款承诺。目的是暴露贷款机构对未来收入的现金依赖，而不是贴上亲戚的可靠性标签或取代实际协议。

c0f40d1bdc420a88609b90d7d78aa9f766fbe44a.src: A population estimate describes reported household experiences. A cash plan identifies when entered resources fall short. Neither turns a food-spending amount into a diagnosis or a guaranteed safe budget. Start with the person denominator and the household classification The Statistics Canada table used here reports that 24.0% of persons in Canada lived in food-insecure households in reference year 2024. The estimate includes marginal, moderate and severe food insecurity. It is a percentage of persons classified by the situation of their household, rather than a percentage of Canadian households. The corresponding published estimate is 9,755,600 persons. That is a weighted population estimate, not the number of survey respondents. Counting people and counting households give different weights to households of different sizes. Do not rename the figure “24% of families” or use it as a probability assigned to a particular reader. Statistics Canada’s indicator definition connects food insecurity with reported food-related constraints arising from limited financial resources over the preceding twelve months. A current bank balance or one month’s grocery receipt cannot reproduce that survey measurement. The two survey charts provide context; the three cash charts answer a separate bookkeeping question. Separate the reference year, collection period and publication date The 2024 Canadian Income Survey release was published on 29 April 2026. Food-security responses for that reference year were collected from January through June 2025 and concerned the previous twelve months. A point marked 2024 is therefore not a real-time reading of conditions on the article’s October 2026 review date. The release revised the 2018–2023 estimates using the 2021 Census population base and revised national estimates to include the territories. The line chart uses the current revised table for every displayed year. Mixing an older 2023 figure with a newer 2024 figure would combine different vintages and could change the comparison. In this revised series, the total moves from 25.7% in 2023 to 24.0% in 2024, a decrease of 1.7 percentage points. Moderate-or-severe moves from 19.4% to 18.4%, a decrease of 1.0 percentage point. These are arithmetic differences between published point estimates. This article does not perform a significance test, identify a cause or infer that the same individuals moved between categories. Use separate categories without adding their subtotal twice The 2024 category bars share an all-persons denominator: marginal 5.6%, moderate 11.9% and severe 6.5%. Their sum is 24.0% at the displayed precision. Moderate-or-severe, 18.4%, is the sum of the latter two; it is not a fourth distinct category to add. The inclusive total and its subsets must also not be added together. The categories describe a range of financially constrained experiences. The marginal category includes concern about food running out or constrained selection. Moderate involves reduced quality or quantity, while severe includes reduced intake and missed meals. Those are short paraphrases of the official classification, rather than a questionnaire or a method for assigning a reader’s status. Independent source rounding can make sums differ by a tenth of a percentage point in some years. Keep the source values instead of silently changing a component to force exact agreement. The population total also does not determine a household’s food-spending target, because it contains no suitable household-specific cost or dietary requirement. Retain source quality and survey coverage limits The selected dimensions are Canada, All persons and Percentage of persons in Table 13-10-0835-01. The Canadian Income Survey metadata for 2024 describes exclusions, including people living on reserves and other Indigenous settlements in the provinces, the institutionalized population, and households in extremely remote areas with very low population density. “Canada” in this survey does not imply every living arrangement is covered. Published A, B and C quality codes are retained below: A is excellent, B very good and C good under the source’s quality system. Codes incorporate precision and observation-count criteria. They are not household risk scores. Numerical confidence intervals are not supplied in this small extract, and the chart does not draw invented uncertainty bands. These are estimates from the Canadian Income Survey. The food-security indicator can also be measured in other surveys, whose target populations, reference periods and collection methods can differ. This chart does not splice Canadian Community Health Survey observations into the CIS line. Build a separate essential-cost ledger without choosing a survey category The cash scenario is invented. It starts with CAD 600, receives CAD 3,600 in an ordinary month, and schedules CAD 2,600 of other essential cash commitments plus CAD 800 of intended food spending. Ordinary monthly cash change is therefore positive CAD 200. The input for other commitments excludes food so the same spending is not deducted twice. Receipts are then reduced by CAD 600 in each of Months 3, 4 and 5. Each affected month receives CAD 3,000 against CAD 3,400 of scheduled spending, producing a CAD 400 cash shortfall before using opening cash. The waterfall shows that single-month reconciliation. The reduction does not also appear as an extra expense. The entered food amount is a cash assumption chosen for the example. It is not a nutrition benchmark, a recommended grocery allowance, a benefit standard or a recommendation to cut food. The calculator retains the full amount when income falls. Changing it creates a different spending assumption and does not establish whether that amount is adequate for anyone’s needs. The other-commitment input can include the intended rent, utilities, transport and required debt cash payments. It must be complete for the plan being tested. Nothing in the tool supplies a benefit payment, informal support, affordable credit or another source of money merely because the plan falls short. Check the lowest point even when the ending amount looks acceptable At the defaults, scheduled cash after Months 1–6 is CAD 800, 1,000, 600, 200, negative 200 and zero. Month 6 ends at zero after normal receipts resume, but Month 5 has an earlier CAD 200 gap. A plan that inspects only the endpoint misses that unfunded point. The model keeps negative scheduled cash visible as an accounting shortfall. It does not treat it as a permitted overdraft, silently skip a bill or reduce a food purchase. Without an additional resource or a change in commitments, all the scheduled outflows cannot be funded at that point. For this exact six-month schedule, CAD 800 of opening cash would keep every modeled month-end nonnegative. Compared with the entered CAD 600, the additional opening funding is CAD 200. This amount comes from the most negative cumulative net cash flow, rather than from multiplying the final monthly deficit by six. Ordinary months before the reduction build some cash that is available later. Monthly netting is a limitation. Rent paid before salary arrives could create a larger within-month need than this chart shows. Use a dated pay-and-bill ledger for that question. The additional-funding metric here refers only to the selected monthly schedule and is not a general emergency-fund recommendation. Read the cash-gap grid as alternative plans, not predicted outcomes The matrix changes two assumptions: opening cash in the rows and the receipts reduction during Months 3–5 in the columns. Normal receipts, other commitments and intended food spending remain fixed. Each cell is an independent plan. Neither the row nor column is a percentile, a probability or a Statistics Canada estimate. With default spending and receipts, the CAD 600 reduction requires CAD 800 of total opening cash for the modeled month-ends. Starting with zero leaves an additional need of CAD 800; starting with CAD 600 leaves CAD 200; starting with CAD 1,200 leaves no additional gap on that schedule. A zero cell still does not classify a household as food secure. The purpose is to locate the resource mismatch and its timing. A budget can expose insufficient resources, but arithmetic cannot create income or decide which essential need a household can safely go without. Keep the unmet amount explicit while assessing actual available resources and obligations. Review the evidence and the cash plan with different records For the population chart, check the source table, reference period, denominator, revision vintage and quality codes together. For the cash plan, check actual net receipt amounts and dates, essential commitments, money already available and costs omitted from the small example. The two reviews require different evidence. The calculator includes no interest, inflation adjustment, borrowing, missed-payment costs, benefits calculation, investment returns or within-month receipt ordering. It does not measure the household’s previous twelve months of experiences. A positive modeled cash path cannot rule out reported food-related hardship, while a negative path cannot by itself reproduce the survey classification. Keep the official estimate and the household ledger connected by the planning question—whether essential needs can be funded—while preserving what each can establish. The result is a clearer statement of the observed social context and the specific cash amount a hypothetical schedule cannot currently fund.
c0f40d1bdc420a88609b90d7d78aa9f766fbe44a.zh: 人口估计描述了报告的家庭经历。现金计划可以识别投入的资源何时不足。两者都不能将食品支出金额转化为诊断或有保证的安全预算。从人口分母和家庭分类开始 此处使用的加拿大统计局表格报告称，在 2024 年参考年，加拿大有 24.0% 的人口生活在粮食不安全的家庭中。估计值包括边缘、中度和严重的粮食不安全。这是按家庭情况分类的人员百分比，而不是加拿大家庭的百分比。相应公布的估计人数为 9,755,600 人。这是加权人口估计，而不是调查受访者的数量。统计人口和统计户数时，对不同规模的家庭赋予不同的权重。不要将这个数字重命名为“24% 的家庭”或将其用作分配给特定读者的概率。加拿大统计局的指标定义将粮食不安全与过去十二个月因财政资源有限而报告的粮食相关限制联系起来。当前的银行余额或一个月的杂货收据无法重现该调查测量结果。这两个调查图表提供了背景信息；三个现金图表回答了一个单独的簿记问题。将参考年、收集期和发布日期分开 2024 年加拿大收入调查于 2026 年 4 月 29 日发布。该参考年的粮食安全答复是从 2025 年 1 月到 2025 年 6 月收集的，涉及前 12 个月。因此，标记为 2024 年的点并不是对文章 2026 年 10 月审稿日期条件的实时解读。该版本使用 2021 年人口普查人口基数修订了 2018-2023 年估计数，并修订了国家估计数以将各地区包括在内。折线图对每个显示的年份使用当前修订的表格。将较旧的 2023 年数据与较新的 2024 年数据混合在一起会合并不同的年份，并可能改变比较结果。在本次修订后的系列中，总数从 2023 年的 25.7% 降至 2024 年的 24.0%，下降了 1.7 个百分点。中重度从19.4%下降到18.4%，下降了1.0个百分点。这些是已发布的点估计值之间的算术差异。本文不进行显着性检验、确定原因或推断同一个人在类别之间移动。使用单独的类别，而不将其小计相加两次 2024 年类别栏共享所有人的分母：边缘 5.6%、中等 11.9% 和严重 6.5%。在显示精度下，它们的总和为 24.0%。中度或重度，18.4%，是后两者的总和；它不是要添加的第四个不同类别。包含的总数及其子集也不得相加。这些类别描述了一系列经济拮据的经历。边缘类别包括对食物耗尽或选择受限的担忧。中度涉及质量或数量下降，而严重包括摄入量减少和错过进餐。这些是官方分类的简短释义，而不是调查问卷或分配读者状态的方法。在某些年份，独立来源舍入可能会使总和相差十分之一个百分点。保留源值，而不是默默地更改组件以强制完全一致。人口总数也不能决定家庭的食品支出目标，因为它不包含合适的家庭特定成本或饮食要求。保留来源质量和调查覆盖范围限制 选择的维度是表 13-10-0835-01 中的“加拿大”、“所有人”和“人员百分比”。 2024 年加拿大收入调查元数据描述了排除的情况，包括生活在保留地和各省其他原住民定居点的人们、收容机构的人口以及人口密度极低的极其偏远地区的家庭。本次调查中的“加拿大”并不意味着涵盖所有居住安排。已发布的 A、B 和 C 质量代码保留如下：在来源的质量体系下，A 为优秀、B 为非常好、C 为良好。代码包含精度和观察计数标准。它们不是家庭风险评分。此小摘录中未提供数值置信区间，并且该图表未绘制发明的不确定性带。这些是加拿大收入调查的估计。粮食安全指标也可以通过其他调查来衡量，但其目标人群、参考期和收集方法可能有所不同。该图表并未将加拿大社区健康调查的观察结果拼接到 CIS 线中。在不选择调查类别的情况下建立一个单独的基本成本分类账现金场景被发明了。起价为 600 加元，通常每月收到 3,600 加元，并安排 2,600 加元的其他基本现金承诺以及 800 加元的预期食品支出。因此，普通每月现金变化为正 200 加元。其他承诺的投入不包括食品，因此相同的支出不会被扣除两次。然后，第 3、4 和 5 个月的收据将减少 600 加元。每个受影响的月份，计划支出为 3,400 加元，收到的金额为 3,000 加元，在使用期初现金之前会出现 400 加元的现金缺口。瀑布显示单月调节。减少的费用也不会显示为额外费用。输入的食物量是为本示例选择的现金假设。它不是营养基准、建议的杂货津贴、福利标准或减少食物的建议。当收入下降时，计算器会保留全额金额。改变它会产生不同的支出假设，并且无法确定该金额是否足以满足任何人的需求。其他承诺输入可以包括预期的租金、公用事业、交通和所需的债务现金支付。对于正在测试的计划来说，它必须是完整的。该工具中的任何内容都不会仅仅因为计划的不足而提供福利金、非正式支持、负担得起的信贷或其他资金来源。即使最终金额看起来可以接受，也要检查最低点 在默认情况下，第 1 至第 6 个月后的预定现金为 800 加元、1,000 加元、600 加元、200 加元、负 200 加元和零。正常收款恢复后，第 6 个月结束时为零，但第 5 个月出现了 200 加元的较早缺口。仅检查端点的计划会错过那个没有资金支持的点。该模型将负计划现金视为会计缺口。它不会将其视为允许的透支、默默地跳过账单或减少食品购买。如果没有额外资源或承诺发生变化，届时所有计划的资金流出都无法得到资助。对于这个确切的六个月计划，800 加元的期初现金将使每个建模的月末保持非负数。与输入的 600 加元相比，额外的开业资金为 200 加元。该金额来自最负的累计净现金流量，而不是最终每月赤字乘以 6。削减之前的通常几个月都会积累一些现金，供以后使用。每月净额结算是一个限制。在工资到达之前支付的租金可能会产生比该图表显示的更大的月内需求。使用注明日期的付款和账单分类账来解决该问题。这里的额外资金指标仅指选定的每月计划，而不是一般的紧急资金建议。将现金缺口网格视为替代计划，而不是预测结果 该矩阵改变了两个假设：行中的期初现金和列中的第 3-5 个月期间的收入减少。正常收入、其他承诺和预期食品支出保持不变。每个单元都是一个独立的计划。行和列都不是百分位数、概率或加拿大统计局的估计值。如果采用默认支出和收据，则减少 600 加元需要模型月末期初现金总额为 800 加元。从零开始还需要 800 加元； 600 加元起，剩下 200 加元；从 1,200 加元开始，该时间表上没有额外的差距。零细胞仍然不能将家庭归类为粮食安全家庭。目的是定位资源不匹配及其时间。预算可能会暴露资源不足的情况，但算术无法创造收入或决定家庭可以安全地满足哪些基本需求。在评估实际可用资源和义务时，明确未满足的金额。使用不同的记录审查证据和现金计划 对于人口图表，请一起检查源表、参考期、分母、修订年份和质量代码。对于现金计划，检查实际净收款金额和日期、基本承诺、已可用资金以及小示例中省略的成本。这两项审查需要不同的证据。该计算器不包括利息、通货膨胀调整、借贷、逾期付款成本、福利计算、投资回报或月内收据订购。它不衡量家庭过去十二个月的经历。正向建模的现金路径不能排除报告的与粮食相关的困难，而负向路径本身不能重现调查分类。将官方估算和家庭分类账通过规划问题（是否可以满足基本需求）联系起来，同时保留各自可以建立的内容。结果是对观察到的社会背景以及假设的时间表目前无法资助的具体现金金额进行了更清晰的陈述。

f0fc251e6e2fab5df9330f63d8ed9b7baa857edd.src: Adjusted household disposable income includes an allocated value of in-kind goods and services. It supports a broader resource comparison, while household payments still require a separately defined cash ledger. Identify the adjustment before interpreting the larger figure Statistics Canada’s annual DHEA table includes both household disposable income and adjusted household disposable income. The adjustment adds social transfers in kind: an allocated value of goods and services financed by governments and non-profit institutions serving households. The official concepts reference gives health and education services among the examples and describes how these resources are mapped to households. The addition records a service or goods benefit, rather than another general-purpose money transfer. The word “adjusted” here refers to that broader resource concept. All dollar values in this article are nominal current CAD. They have not been adjusted for price inflation. The ordinary disposable-income series is itself a national-accounts measure, with a broader construction than one person’s take-home-pay deposit. Keep the reference year, grouping rule and measurement unit together The extract covers 2021 through 2025 from the 13 April 2026 release vintage. It selects Canada, the statistic “Value per household,” five income quintiles and three measures. Together these choices produce 75 observations. The source’s default table heading can display million-dollar totals under a different selection; those are not the units used here. The table’s metadata assigns income quintiles using equivalized household disposable income, accounting for household size and composition with the OECD-modified scale. The plotted amounts are then the published means per household, rather than amounts per consumption unit. That distinction matters when reading the group labels. A mean for the highest quintile is not the salary threshold for entering it. The explorer displays the selected source group and does not assign the reader or their household to a quintile. Reconcile the middle group’s 2025 adjustment The default selection is the third income quintile in 2025. Its published household disposable-income mean is CAD 87,705 . Its social transfers in kind mean is CAD 31,905 . Adding them gives the adjusted household disposable-income mean of CAD 119,610 . The grouped bars compare the two income concepts across all five groups. The separate bar chart shows the published in-kind component itself. The waterfall then reproduces the selected group’s accounting addition without treating the two income concepts as separate amounts to be added together. CAD 119,610 already includes the CAD 31,905 component. Adding it again would overstate the adjusted measure. Equally, entering the full adjusted mean as household cash income would assume that the value of those services arrived as spendable money. A similar dollar addition can represent a very different resource share For the lowest income quintile in 2025, disposable income is CAD 32,802 and the in-kind component CAD 30,607, producing adjusted income of CAD 63,409. For the highest quintile, the corresponding figures are CAD 219,061, CAD 27,654 and CAD 246,715. The in-kind component is about 48.27% of the lowest group’s adjusted mean and 11.21% of the highest group’s adjusted mean. Those ratios use published group means. They are not the mean of every household’s individual benefit percentage or a percentage of wages paid by an employer. The scatter plot places ordinary disposable income on the horizontal axis and the in-kind share of adjusted income on the vertical axis. Each point is one income quintile in the selected year. The larger filled marker identifies the selected group; the other markers retain the same year’s context. The five aggregate points do not establish an individual causal relationship or predict a household’s use of services. The ratio also contains a changing denominator. Read it as a defined resource-composition calculation, rather than a test of why one family receives a particular benefit. Allocated service value does not settle the next household bill Publicly financed education or health services can contribute to living standards without an equivalent payment passing through a household’s chequing account. That is why the broader measure is useful for comparing resources, including across systems that finance services differently. The allocated amount is not a voucher that a family can freely redirect to rent, debt repayment or a saving goal. Nor does a group mean establish the exact value of services used by each member. Statistics Canada’s mapping includes distribution variables and proxies, such as demographic information for health-related allocations. A personal cash budget therefore starts separately with usable receipts and actual payment obligations. It can account for the services and benefits the household expects to receive under the applicable arrangements, but it should not insert a national-accounts allocation as an extra bank deposit. The same in-kind resource appears on both sides of the accounts The methodology adds social transfers in kind to disposable income to obtain adjusted disposable income. It also adds the same resource value to household final consumption expenditure to obtain household actual final consumption. The adjustment therefore does not by itself increase household net saving. Adding the resource to income while leaving consumption on its old definition would create an artificial saving increase. The official treatment keeps the two concepts aligned. The downloadable table contains same-named in-kind entries in its income and consumption positions. They were checked for equality in all 25 group-and-year combinations. This article selects the selected series once. Summing every row with the same display label would count the resource twice. Preserve rounding and changing group composition in a historical comparison The source publishes these means in whole dollars. In 21 of the 25 group-and-year identities, disposable income plus the published in-kind mean equals the published adjusted mean exactly. Four differ by CAD 1, consistent with independently rounded component means. The waterfall includes a labelled rounding residual when needed. It preserves the published endpoint and does not invent another benefit to eliminate the difference. All 75 selected values were present, unflagged and checked in the original CSV snapshot. The history chart follows the selected group’s two published means across all five years. Connected group averages do not follow an unchanged set of families: income-group membership and household composition can change. Nominal increases also do not establish an equivalent gain in purchasing power. Choose the measure for the question being answered Use the adjusted concept when the question requires the broader resources that include in-kind services. Use an explicitly defined cash ledger when the question is whether money is available to make a dated payment. A difference between these measures does not make either one erroneous; it identifies different accounting scopes. Record the source year and release vintage. Check whether the statistic is a total, a per-household mean or a per-consumption-unit amount. Identify whether the adjustment adds in-kind resources or changes prices. Keep the related income and consumption definitions aligned. Build the household payment calendar from independently verified cash receipts and obligations. The five charts make the statistical adjustment visible while keeping its interpretation tied to the source definition. They supply economic context, rather than a personal saving target or a determination of public-benefit eligibility.
f0fc251e6e2fab5df9330f63d8ed9b7baa857edd.zh: 调整后的家庭可支配收入包括实物商品和服务的分配价值。它支持更广泛的资源比较，而家庭付款仍然需要单独定义的现金分类账。在解释更大的数字之前先确定调整内容 加拿大统计局的年度 DHEA 表包括家庭可支配收入和调整后的家庭可支配收入。此次调整增加了实物社会转移：由政府和为家庭服务的非营利机构资助的商品和服务的分配价值。官方概念参考提供了健康和教育服务的示例，并描述了如何将这些资源映射到家庭。添加记录的是服务或商品利益，而不是其他通用资金转移。这里的“调整”一词指的是更广泛的资源概念。本文中的所有美元价值均为名义当前加元。它们没有根据价格通胀进行调整。普通可支配收入系列本身就是一种国民账户指标，其结构比一个人的实得工资存款更广泛。将参考年份、分组规则和测量单位保留在一起。摘录涵盖 2026 年 4 月 13 日发布年份的 2021 年至 2025 年。它选择了加拿大的统计数据“每户价值”、五个收入五分位数和三个衡量标准。这些选择总共产生了 75 个观察结果。源的默认表格标题可以显示不同选择下的百万美元总额；这些不是这里使用的单位。该表的元数据使用等值家庭可支配收入来分配收入五分位，并按照经合组织修改后的规模考虑家庭规模和构成。绘制的金额是每个家庭公布的平均值，而不是每个消费单位的金额。在阅读组标签时，这种区别很重要。最高五分之一的平均值并不是进入该五分之一的工资门槛。浏览器显示所选的来源组，并且不会将读者或其家庭分配到五分位。调节中间群体2025年调整默认选择2025年第三收入五分位。其公布的家庭可支配收入平均值为 CAD 87,705 。其社会实物转移平均金额为 31,905 加元。将它们相加后，调整后的家庭可支配收入平均值为 119,610 加元。分组条比较所有五个组的两个收入概念。单独的条形图显示了已发布的实物组件本身。然后，瀑布会重现所选组的会计添加，而不将两个收入概念视为要加在一起的单独金额。 119,610 加元已包含 31,905 加元部分。再次添加它会夸大调整后的指标。同样，将完全调整后的平均值输入为家庭现金收入将假设这些服务的价值以可支配货币的形式出现。类似的美元增加可能代表截然不同的资源份额。对于 2025 年收入最低的五分之一，可支配收入为 32,802 加元，实物部分为 30,607 加元，调整后收入为 63,409 加元。对于最高的五分位数，相应的数字为 219,061 加元、27,654 加元和 246,715 加元。实物成分约为最低组调整平均值的 48.27%，约为最高组调整平均值的 11.21%。这些比率使用已发布的团体平均值。它们并不是每个家庭的个人福利百分比或雇主支付的工资百分比的平均值。散点图将普通可支配收入放在横轴上，将调整后收入的实物份额放在纵轴上。每个点都是所选年份中的一个收入五分之一。较大的填充标记标识所选组；其他标记保留了同一年的背景。这五个聚合点并不能建立个体因果关系或预测家庭对服务的使用情况。该比率还包含变化的分母。将其视为一种定义的资源构成计算，而不是对为什么一个家庭获得特定福利的测试。分配的服务价值并不能解决下一个家庭的账单 公共资助的教育或医疗服务可以提高生活水平，而无需通过家庭支票账户支付同等费用。这就是为什么更广泛的衡量标准对于比较资源非常有用，包括不同的服务融资系统之间的资源比较。分配的金额并不是家庭可以自由用于租金、债务偿还或储蓄目标的凭证。团体也不意味着确定每个成员使用的服务的确切价值。加拿大统计局的地图包括分布变量和代理，例如与健康相关的分配的人口统计信息。因此，个人现金预算分别从可用收据和实际付款义务开始。它可以说明家庭期望在适用的安排下获得的服务和福利，但不应将国民账户分配作为额外的银行存款插入。账户双方都出现相同的实物资源。该方法将实物社会转移添加到可支配收入中，以获得调整后的可支配收入。它还将相同的资源价值添加到家庭最终消费支出中，以获得家庭实际最终消费。因此，调整本身并不会增加家庭净储蓄。将资源添加到收入中，同时保留消费的旧定义，会人为地增加储蓄。官方的处理使这两个概念保持一致。可下载的表格包含其收入和消费状况的同名实物条目。他们在所有 25 个组别和年份组合中进行了平等检查。本文选取精选系列一次。对具有相同显示标签的每一行求和将会对资源进行两次计数。在历史比较中保留舍入和更改组构成 来源以整数美元发布这些方法。在 25 个组和年份恒等式中，有 21 个恒等式中，可支配收入加上公布的实物均值恰好等于公布的调整后均值。四者相差 CAD 1，与独立舍入分量的平均值一致。瀑布包括需要时标记的舍入残差。它保留了已发布的端点，并且没有发明其他好处来消除差异。所有 75 个选定值均在原始 CSV 快照中存在、未标记并已检查。历史图表遵循所选组在所有五年内的两个已发布平均值。关联群体的平均数并不遵循不变的家庭组：收入群体成员和家庭构成可能会发生变化。名义增长也并不能带来购买力的同等增益。选择要回答的问题的衡量标准 当问题需要更广泛的资源（包括实物服务）时，请使用调整后的概念。当问题是是否有钱可以进行指定日期的付款时，请使用明确定义的现金分类帐。这些措施之间的差异并不意味着其中任何一个都是错误的。它确定了不同的会计范围。记录来源年份和发布年份。检查统计数据是总计、每个家庭的平均值还是每个消费单位的金额。确定调整是否增加了实物资源或改变了价格。保持相关收入和消费定义一致。根据独立核实的现金收入和债务建立家庭付款日历。这五个图表使统计调整可见，同时保持其解释与源定义相关联。它们提供经济背景，而不是个人储蓄目标或公共福利资格的确定。

53d515e0ad64943fea1e9a215cd006d250baf461.src: The fee percentage is only one term. The eligible gain, loss carryforward, measurement dates and treatment of cash flows determine what is actually charged. Ask which gain the fee percentage applies to A statement that a manager charges a percentage of performance is incomplete without a definition of performance. A positive gain during one accounting period can occur while an investor is still recovering a loss from an earlier period. The SEC’s investor-education page on hedge funds notes that performance fees can be subject to measures such as high-water marks and hurdle rates.
