EPS时间表改变了周期分母；价值矩阵改变了交易快照时假设的回购价格和发行价格。带符号的条形图比较了每个度量值自身起始基线的百分比变化。它们是单独的数量，具有不同的定义，而不是添加到股东回报中的组成部分。既不是历史观察，也不是以规定价格购买的建议。这些控制措施施加了数字界限，因此公司在发行前绝不会回购所有未发行的股票，并且模拟的股权价值仍然为正。这些是计算限制，而不是建议的支付比率。控制背后没有融资、现金利息、税收、估值反应或价格影响模型。在这些条件下，按每股初始假设价值进行的无发行回购对于该假设价值而言是中性的。增加零现金份额可以抵消这种好处，而改变价值输入可以改变结论。这种依赖性就是为什么单靠每股收益增长无法解决实际回购是否能持续改善股东经济的问题。保持回报模型内部一致如果预测每股收益已经包括假设的股票下跌，那么最终每股收益乘以退出市盈率就已经反映了每股收益。添加单独的回购收益率作为额外的股东回报可以将相同的机制计算两次。或者，从总收益开始，对分配给回购的现金进行建模，估计每年支付的价格，并计算最终的股票路径。将此与股息、再投资和债务变化相协调。一美元不能同时为股息、收购和回购提供资金。授权也不同于执行。将公布的产能、实际支出、平均价格、期末份额和稀释加权平均份额记录为单独的字段。仅大量剩余授权就不足以证明未来减持股份。奖励回购之前需要回答的问题 回购总额中有多少可以抵消员工发行或其他稀释？哪些收益和现金流假设为该计划提供资金？支付的价格与合理的估计价值范围相比如何？债务、流动性和财务灵活性有何变化？ EPS 预测是否已经考虑了股份数量效应？跟踪多个报告周期的答案。严格的计划可以在估值要求较高时减少购买，并在现金真正过剩且价格有吸引力时增加购买。有用的证据是已实现的分配记录及其对持续所有者的影响，并与企业的投资需求一起进行评估。

4ba9a82692c3a7a4e56e2d5efb06e3f185ad2a6f.src: Divide total purchase cash by total units acquired. A lower average cost than the simple mean of quoted prices is an accounting result, and does not guarantee a profit or prove one investment schedule is better. Start with the cash bought and the units received Buying the same dollar amount at regular intervals does not buy the same number of units. The price at each purchase date determines how many units that cash can acquire. An average of price observations therefore answers a different question from the average cost of the units actually owned. Investor.gov defines dollar-cost averaging through equal portions invested at regular intervals. Its description explains the basic quantity effect: the same money buys more units at a lower price and fewer at a higher price. This guide uses that relationship for an accounting illustration, rather than predicting a benefit for a real investment. The original example makes four purchases of CAD 1,000 each. Its entered prices are CAD 20, CAD 10, CAD 25 and CAD 20 per unit. All units belong to one hypothetical unit class, and fractional purchases are allowed. No fee, spread, tax, distribution or currency conversion changes the cash invested. Each CAD 1,000 becomes available at its purchase date. The model does not begin with CAD 4,000 of cash held from day one or compare investing an existing lump sum immediately with holding it for later. Those are different funding assumptions addressed in the related timing guide. Add unit quantities before calculating cost per unit For each purchase, units acquired equal cash invested divided by price. The four purchases acquire 50, 100, 40 and 50 units. Together they cost CAD 4,000 and acquire 240 units. Average purchase cost is therefore CAD 4,000 ÷ 240 = approximately CAD 16.67 per unit . Calculations retain full precision even though the displayed currency is rounded. The first bar chart shows the different quantities directly. The CAD 10 purchase accounts for 100 units, twice the quantity bought by CAD 1,000 at CAD 20. The CAD 25 purchase accounts for only 40 units. These unequal quantities are the weights missing from a simple average of prices. The mechanics assume every order executes fully at its entered price and can buy arbitrary fractions. Actual products may have order sizes, dealing times, spreads, commissions or fractional-unit restrictions. Those conditions can change both the cash used and the quantity received. Cash shares and unit shares have different denominators Every purchase supplies 25% of the total cash because all four cash amounts are equal. The unit shares are approximately 20.83%, 41.67%, 16.67% and 20.83%. Each list separately adds to 100% before rounding. The grouped chart keeps those denominators apart. A purchase can supply one-quarter of the money and more than two-fifths of the units. A percentage is interpretable only after its denominator is named. The simple mean of the four prices is (20 + 10 + 25 + 20) ÷ 4 = CAD 18.75 . It gives each date’s price one equal weight. It does not give each acquired unit one equal weight, so it is not the average cost of the 240 units. The unit-weighted price calculation does reconcile with the cash ledger: (20 × 50 + 10 × 100 + 25 × 40 + 20 × 50) ÷ 240 is CAD 4,000 divided by 240. Adding price observations without those unit weights describes the observations, not the purchase cost. The harmonic mean is an identity under these limited assumptions When the same cash amount B is invested at four positive prices, acquired units sum to B × (1/p 1 + 1/p 2 + 1/p 3 + 1/p 4 ) . Dividing the total 4B cost by that quantity cancels B. The resulting cost per unit is 4 ÷ (1/p 1 + 1/p 2 + 1/p 3 + 1/p 4 ) , the harmonic mean of the prices. With positive prices it cannot exceed their arithmetic mean, and it equals that mean when all four prices are identical. This mathematical comparison does not establish that an investor earned an excess return or chose a better trading plan. The two means are statistics calculated from the same executed purchases. An alternative strategy comparison would need consistent available resources, dated orders, waiting cash and the same endpoint. Changing the cash purchase amount scales quantities and dollar results without changing this frictionless cost-per-unit statistic. It still changes the household money committed. Equal averages do not make two differently sized positions equally important to a financial plan. Mark all accumulated units at the final price At the fourth price of CAD 20, the 240 units have a market value of CAD 4,800. Compared with CAD 4,000 of contributed cash, the final dollar difference is positive CAD 800. The line chart shows the cumulative cash and the marked position after each purchase. After the second purchase, 150 units at CAD 10 are worth CAD 1,500, below the CAD 2,000 already contributed. Buying additional units does not remove the loss on earlier units when the current price is lower. Change the fourth price to CAD 5 and the result becomes a loss. The four purchases then acquire 390 units, with a final market value of CAD 1,950 against CAD 4,000 of contributions. Having more units and a lower average cost does not ensure that the final price is above that cost. The dollar gap is not an annualized, time-weighted or money-weighted return. Cash arrived on four dates, and the tool does not assign calendar spacing for a rate calculation. It also does not calculate cash available after a sale, tax payable or a tax adjusted cost base. Use the accounting before choosing an investment schedule For a real record, reconcile each trade’s cash, execution price and units with its confirmation. Keep fees, distributions, currency conversions and corporate actions in the appropriate ledger. Do not combine incompatible unit classes or unadjusted prices across an event that changes unit counts. FINRA’s discussion distinguishes investing money as it becomes available from intentionally delaying investment of cash already held. It also notes that repeated transaction costs and waiting cash can affect a schedule. These implementation issues remain outside the frictionless four-purchase identity. Neither the chosen price path nor the fact that its harmonic mean is lower than its arithmetic mean supplies evidence about future market direction. A plan must still consider the investment’s suitability, diversification, time horizon, cash needs and the ability to keep funding purchases. The useful accounting sequence is concrete: record the cash invested, calculate and add the units, divide cost by units, then mark the entire position at the valuation price. The four charts preserve those steps so that a price average, unit quantity and dollar gain are each given the meaning their calculation supports.
4ba9a82692c3a7a4e56e2d5efb06e3f185ad2a6f.zh: 将购买现金总额除以购买的总单位数。平均成本低于报价的简单平均值是一种会计结果，并不能保证利润或证明某个投资计划更好。从购买的现金和收到的单位开始定期购买相同的美元金额并不能购买相同数量的单位。每个购买日期的价格决定了现金可以购买的单位数量。因此，价格观察的平均值回答了与实际拥有的单位的平均成本不同的问题。 Investor.gov 通过定期进行等额投资来定义美元成本平均法。它的描述解释了基本的数量效应：同样的钱以较低的价格购买更多的单位，而以较高的价格购买更少的单位。本指南使用这种关系进行会计说明，而不是预测实际投资的收益。原始示例进行四次购买，每次购买 1,000 加元。输入的价格为每件 20 加元、10 加元、25 加元和 20 加元。所有单位都属于一个假设的单位类别，并且允许分批购买。任何费用、利差、税收、分配或货币兑换都不会改变投资的现金。每 1,000 加元于购买之日起即可使用。该模型并没有从第一天起就持有 4,000 加元的现金开始，也没有将立即投资现有的一次性资金与稍后持有进行比较。这些是相关时间指南中讨论的不同资金假设。在计算单位成本之前添加单位数量 对于每次购买，获得的单位等于投入的现金除以价格。这四次采购分别获得 50、100、40 和 50 单位。它们总共花费 4,000 加元，购买了 240 台。因此，平均购买成本为每件 4,000 加元 ÷ 240 = 大约 16.67 加元。即使显示的货币是四舍五入的，计算仍保持完全精度。第一个条形图直接显示了不同的数量。 10 加元购买量为 100 个单位，是 1,000 加元以 20 加元购买数量的两倍。25 加元购买量仅为 40 个单位。这些不相等的数量是简单平均价格中缺失的权重。机制假设每个订单都以其输入的价格完全执行，并且可以购买任意部分。实际产品可能有订单大小、交易时间、点差、佣金或分数单位限制。这些条件可能会改变所使用的现金和收到的数量。现金股和单位股的分母不同。每次购买提供现金总额的 25%，因为所有四种现金金额相等。单位股份约为20.83%、41.67%、16.67%及20.83%。每个列表在四舍五入之前分别相加至 100%。分组图表将这些分母分开。一次购买可以提供四分之一的资金和五分之二以上的单位。百分比只有在分母被命名后才能解释。四个价格的简单平均值为 (20 + 10 + 25 + 20) ÷ 4 = 18.75 加元。它赋予每个日期的价格同等的权重。它没有给每个购买的单位同等的权重，因此它不是 240 个单位的平均成本。单位加权价格计算确实与现金分类帐相符：(20 × 50 + 10 × 100 + 25 × 40 + 20 × 50) ÷ 240 等于 4,000 加元除以 240。添加不带这些单位权重的价格观测值描述的是观测值，而不是购买成本。调和平均值是这些有限假设下的恒等式。当以四个正价格投资相同的现金金额 B 时，获得的单位总和为 B × (1/p 1 + 1/p 2 + 1/p 3 + 1/p 4 ) 。将 4B 总成本除以该数量即可取消 B。得到的每单位成本为 4 ÷ (1/p 1 + 1/p 2 + 1/p 3 + 1/p 4 ) ，即价格的调和平均值。对于正价格，它不能超过算术平均值，并且当所有四个价格相同时，它等于算术平均值。这种数学比较并不能证明投资者获得了超额回报或选择了更好的交易计划。这两个平均值是根据相同执行的购买计算得出的统计数据。另一种策略比较需要一致的可用资源、日期订单、等待现金和相同的端点。更改现金购买金额可以调整数量和美元结果，而无需更改这种无摩擦的单位成本统计数据。它仍然改变了家庭投入的资金。平均数相等并不意味着两个不同规模的头寸对于财务计划同样重要。将所有累计单位标记为最终价格。第四个价格为 20 加元，这 240 个单位的市场价值为 4,800 加元。与贡献的 4,000 加元现金相比，最终的美元差额为正 800 加元。折线图显示了每次购买后的累计现金和标记位置。第二次购买后，10 加元的 150 个单位价值 1,500 加元，低于已经贡献的 2,000 加元。当当前价格较低时，购买额外的单位并不能消除早期单位的损失。将第四个价格改为5加元，结果变成亏损。随后，这四次购买获得了 390 个单位，最终市场价值为 1,950 加元，出资额为 4,000 加元。拥有更多的单位和较低的平均成本并不能确保最终价格高于该成本。美元缺口不是年化、时间加权或货币加权的回报。现金在四个日期到达，并且该工具不会为费率计算分配日历间隔。它也不计算销售后可用的现金、应付税款或税收调整后的成本基础。在选择投资计划之前使用会计为了获得真实记录，请将每笔交易的现金、执行价格和单位与其确认进行核对。将费用、分配、货币兑换和公司行为保存在适当的分类账中。请勿在改变单位数量的活动中合并不兼容的单位类别或未调整的价格。 FINRA 的讨论将可用资金投资与故意延迟对已持有现金的投资进行了区分。它还指出，重复的交易成本和等待现金可能会影响时间表。这些实施问题仍然超出了无摩擦的四次购买身份。所选的价格路径及其调和平均值低于算术平均值的事实都无法提供有关未来市场方向的证据。计划还必须考虑投资的适宜性、多元化、时间范围、现金需求以及保持资金购买的能力。有用的会计顺序是具体的：记录投入的现金，计算并添加单位，将成本除以单位，然后以估值价格标记整个头寸。这四个图表保留了这些步骤，以便平均价格、单位数量和美元收益都得到其计算支持的含义。

ae06cd0ac9c6f65fa641dec97fc26d1d124b637f.src: A group’s average wealth and its share of national wealth answer different questions. Neither reveals a family’s usable cash or the distribution hidden inside that group. Read the reference quarter and the ranking variable first A statement about the wealthiest 20% describes households ranked by net worth. It does not identify the highest-income 20%, the oldest 20% or the households with the largest bank deposits. The sorting variable belongs beside the percentage before any planning interpretation is attempted. This guide uses Statistics Canada’s release table 3 published on 13 April 2026. It contains average net worth per household for the fourth quarters of 2024 and 2025. The selector changes between those two dated snapshots; it does not estimate a current account balance or create a later observation. The source groups the least wealthy 40% together and shows the next three wealth quintiles separately. A quintile represents one-fifth of the household distribution, while that combined first group represents two-fifths. The four rows therefore have different household weights even though they occupy equal space in a chart. A group average is neither its entry threshold nor its median For Q4 2025, the published mean is CAD 81,650 within the bottom 40%, CAD 526,185 within the third quintile, CAD 1,160,145 within the fourth quintile and CAD 3,543,579 within the top quintile. The published all-household mean is CAD 1,078,642. The top-group mean does not tell you the minimum net worth required to enter that group. It also does not tell you the net worth of its middle household. A few very large values can affect an average substantially, and these grouped means do not reveal the observations needed to reconstruct a median, a percentile threshold or an individual distribution. Net worth is a balance-sheet amount: assets less liabilities. It can contain property and other assets whose value cannot be spent immediately without a transaction. A wealth-group mean therefore cannot be copied into a household cash plan as if it were an available bank balance. Use household weights when moving from group means to approximate shares To derive a group’s contribution to the overall mean, multiply its published mean by its household weight. For the top group in Q4 2025, the contribution is 20% × CAD 3,543,579 = CAD 708,715.80. For the combined bottom group, it is 40% × CAD 81,650 = CAD 32,660. Adding the four weighted contributions gives CAD 1,078,641.80. That is 20 cents below the separately published all-household mean, reflecting rounding in the displayed inputs. The website divides each contribution by this weighted sum so that the four approximate derived wealth shares add to 100%. The results are about 65.70% for the top 20% and 3.03% for the bottom 40%. The accompanying release describes those shares at rounded headline precision as 65.7% and 3.0%. The website’s extra decimal place is arithmetic from rounded means, not evidence of a more precise official estimate. The grouped chart places household shares beside wealth shares. A bar at 20% in the first series and about 65.70% in the second uses two different denominators: households and net worth. It does not mean that 65.70% of households are in the top quintile. Trace only the cumulative boundaries the extract actually provides The cumulative chart begins at zero, then adds the wealth shares at 40%, 60%, 80% and 100% of households, ordered from least to most wealthy. The equality reference is a diagonal: under equal net worth per household, a given household share would hold the same share of wealth. The displayed curve is a grouped-boundary picture. Straight connecting segments help locate the known endpoints but do not recover what happens inside each group. In particular, this extract has no separate 20% boundary. Filling it in with half the bottom-40% share would silently assume away within-group inequality. The release explains that the lowest two quintiles are combined because the lowest quintile’s average liabilities exceeded its assets. A positive average for the combined bottom 40% therefore does not establish that its least wealthy households have positive net worth. The missing detail matters. This chart does not calculate an individual-level Lorenz curve or a Gini coefficient. Computing such a statistic from the few straight segments and presenting it as the country’s actual inequality measure would give the unobserved within-group distribution an unwarranted role. A rise in a group mean is not an investment return for its members The final chart retains the source’s rounded changes in group mean net worth from Q4 2024 to Q4 2025: 2.1% for the bottom 40%, 3.2% for the third quintile, 4.4% for the fourth and 6.0% for the top quintile. It compares the same quarter of two years and stays fixed when the snapshot selector changes. Those figures do not show what happened to every household that started in a particular group. Households can move between groups, and a group’s net worth can change through asset values, saving, borrowing and changes in its composition. The chart is a comparison of group averages at two dates, rather than an account statement following the same investors. The values are nominal. They have not been adjusted for inflation. They should also not be read as a return that a family could earn by adopting the financial habits or assets associated with a higher-wealth group. Keep estimation limits visible beside the concentration story The release’s notes describe a distributional economic-account system using different data inputs, models and assumptions, with some components relying on information from earlier periods. These are estimates that can be revised. The release table provides no confidence bounds for the selected means, so none are drawn or inferred here. The grouping is useful for describing concentration at the supported level of detail. It does not establish why an individual household has a particular amount of wealth, forecast where that household will rank later or show its ability to meet next month’s expenses. For a personal plan, prepare a separate list of assets, debts, access conditions and dated cash needs. Distinguish property value from net sale proceeds, a restricted asset from cash available now, and a debt balance from the payment calendar. A national wealth share provides context for that work; it does not replace it. Record the reference date and the variable used to rank households. Keep a group mean separate from a threshold, median or share. Use the correct group weights and disclose rounding in derived shares. Leave unsupported within-group detail unknown. Build the household’s own liquidity plan from its own evidence.
ae06cd0ac9c6f65fa641dec97fc26d1d124b637f.zh: 一个群体的平均财富及其占国民财富的份额回答了不同的问题。两者都没有透露一个家庭的可用现金或隐藏在该群体内部的分配情况。首先阅读参考季度和排名变量 关于最富有的 20% 的陈述描述了按净资产排名的家庭。它没有确定收入最高的 20%、年龄最大的 20% 或银行存款最多的家庭。在尝试任何计划解释之前，排序变量属于百分比旁边。本指南使用加拿大统计局于 2026 年 4 月 13 日发布的发布表 3。它包含 2024 年第四季度和 2025 年每个家庭的平均净资产。选择器在这两个日期快照之间变化；它不会估计经常账户余额或创建稍后的观察结果。来源将最不富有的 40% 分组在一起，并分别显示接下来的三个财富五分位。五分位数代表家庭分布的五分之一，而第一组的总和则代表五分之二。因此，即使四行在图表中占据相同的空间，它们也具有不同的家庭权重。群体平均数既不是其进入门槛，也不是其中位数。对于 2025 年第四季度，公布的平均数为后 40% 内的 81,650 加元，第三五分之一内的 526,185 加元，第四五分之一内的 1,160,145 加元，顶部五分之一内的 3,543,579 加元。公布的全家庭平均收入为 1,078,642 加元。顶级组平均值并不能告诉您进入该组所需的最低净资产。它也没有告诉你中间家庭的净资产。一些非常大的值可能会极大地影响平均值，并且这些分组平均值不会揭示重建中位数、百分位阈值或个体分布所需的观察结果。净值是资产负债表中的金额：资产减去负债。它可以包含财产和其他资产，其价值在没有交易的情况下无法立即花费。因此，财富组均值不能像可用银行余额一样复制到家庭现金计划中。从群体平均值转向近似份额时使用家庭权重 要得出群体对总体平均值的贡献，请将其公布的平均值乘以其家庭权重。对于 2025 年第四季度的顶级群体，贡献为 20% × 3,543,579 加元 = 708,715.80 加元。对于合并后的底部组，其为 40% × 81,650 加元 = 32,660 加元。将四项加权捐款相加得出 1,078,641.80 加元。这比单独公布的全家庭平均值低 20 美分，反映了显示输入的四舍五入。该网站将每项贡献除以该加权总和，使四项近似的衍生财富份额加起来为 100%。前 20% 的人的结果约为 65.70%，后 40% 的人约为 3.03%。随附的新闻稿将这些股票的四舍五入标题精度描述为 65.7% 和 3.0%。该网站的小数点后位数是四舍五入后的算术结果，并不是更精确的官方估计的证据。分组图表将家庭份额与财富份额放在一起。第一个系列中 20% 的条形和第二个系列中约 65.70% 的条形使用两个不同的分母：家庭和净资产。这并不意味着 65.70% 的家庭属于前五分之一。仅追踪提取物实际提供的累积边界。累积图表从零开始，然后添加 40%、60%、80% 和 100% 家庭的财富份额，按从最富有到最富有的顺序排列。平等参考是一条对角线：在每个家庭净资产相等的情况下，给定的家庭份额将拥有相同份额的财富。显示的曲线是分组边界图。直连接段有助于定位已知端点，但无法恢复每个组内发生的情况。特别是，此提取物没有单独的 20% 边界。用底部 40% 的一半份额来填充它会默默地假设消除群体内的不平等。该新闻稿解释说，将最低的两个五分之一合并起来是因为最低五分之一的平均负债超过了其资产。因此，底部 40% 人口总和的平均值为正并不能证明其最不富裕的家庭拥有正的净资产。缺失的细节很重要。该图表不计算个人层面的洛伦兹曲线或基尼系数。从几个直线段计算这样的统计数据并将其作为该国实际的不平等衡量标准，将使未观察到的群体内分布发挥不必要的作用。群体均值的上升并不是其成员的投资回报最终图表保留了来源从 2024 年第四季度到 2025 年第四季度群体平均净资产的四舍五入变化：底部 40% 的群体为 2.1%，第三个五分之一为 3.2%，第四个五分之一为 4.4%，顶部五分之一为 6.0%。它比较两年的同一季度，并在快照选择器更改时保持固定。这些数字并没有显示从特定群体开始的每个家庭所发生的情况。家庭可以在群体之间流动，群体的净资产可以通过资产价值、储蓄、借贷及其构成的变化而变化。该图表是两个日期的群体平均值的比较，而不是跟踪相同投资者的账户报表。这些值是标称值。它们没有根据通货膨胀进行调整。它们也不应该被理解为一个家庭可以通过采用与高财富群体相关的财务习惯或资产来获得的回报。在集中故事旁边保持估计限制可见该新闻稿的说明描述了使用不同数据输入、模型和假设的分布式经济账户系统，其中一些组件依赖于早期信息。这些是可以修改的估计值。发布表没有为所选平均值提供置信界限，因此此处未绘制或推断任何内容。分组对于描述支持的详细程度的集中度很有用。它没有确定为什么单个家庭拥有特定数量的财富，也没有预测该家庭的排名或显示其满足下个月开支的能力。对于个人计划，请准备一份单独的资产、债务、访问条件和注明日期的现金需求清单。将财产价值与净销售收入、受限制资产与现有可用现金以及债务余额与付款日历区分开来。国家财富份额为这项工作提供了背景；它不会取代它。记录参考日期和用于对家庭进行排名的变量。将组均值与阈值、中位数或份额分开。使用正确的组权重并披露派生股份的四舍五入。让不受支持的组内详细信息未知。根据自己的证据制定家庭自己的流动性计划。

3313a136b57c5dfd3ca65375fb3a3b5bae96739d.src: A payment recorded outside a RRIF is not necessarily a deposit of spendable cash. Confirm its form and keep unsold securities separate from the money assigned to the next bill. Ask what actually arrives when the RRIF makes a payment A retirement statement can show a payment without the same number of dollars reaching the bank. The distinction matters when a household has assigned that payment to rent, groceries or an income-tax bill. Paragraph 5 of the CRA’s IC78-18R7 Registered Retirement Income Funds explains that the minimum amount may be paid in a form other than cash. The carrier and the account arrangement still need to confirm what can be delivered and how the actual payment will be valued and recorded. An in-kind payment moves property, such as securities, outside the RRIF without automatically selling it for cash. The illustration assumes an approved ordinary minimum-payment arrangement and a separate non-registered destination. It does not calculate the minimum or decide whether a particular account supports that form. This is distinct from transferring assets directly between registered arrangements. The example follows a payment to the annuitant. CRA’s RRIF overview states that amounts paid out are taxable on receipt; a payment’s non-cash form does not make this illustration a tax-free withdrawal. Split the gross amount before putting it in the cash budget The worked example begins with a RRIF value of CAD 400,000 immediately before the illustrated payment. The independently entered carrier-confirmed gross payment is CAD 25,000. The model does not derive that amount from the current balance or an age factor. At a 60% securities share, CAD 15,000 arrives as securities and CAD 10,000 arrives as bank cash. The RRIF value falls by CAD 25,000 to CAD 375,000, holding prices unchanged. The two payment components total the same CAD 25,000; they are not two withdrawals of that size. The household also has CAD 12,000 of opening bank cash. After the cash component arrives, its bank balance is CAD 22,000 before the tax and spending assignments are paid. The CAD 15,000 of securities remains a separate asset. With no fees, withholding, market movement or completed household payments in this example, the resources reconcile. Opening RRIF value plus bank cash is CAD 412,000. The later RRIF value of CAD 375,000, securities of CAD 15,000 and bank cash of CAD 22,000 add to the same total. Movement between locations has not created wealth. An earmark changes availability before it changes the bank balance The selected tax cash reserve is CAD 6,000, and planned household bills total CAD 18,000. Together they assign CAD 24,000 of cash. Against the CAD 22,000 bank balance, the illustration has an additional cash requirement of CAD 2,000. The waterfall is a budget-capacity bridge. Its negative endpoint does not mean the actual bank account is already overdrawn. Neither assignment is treated as a completed payment. It shows that the same bank balance cannot fund both promises in full. The tax amount is entered independently after a separate assessment. It is not a percentage calculated by this tool or a statement of final tax owing. The illustration assumes no tax is withheld from the payment; if actual source deductions or fees apply, replace this simplified cash plan with the carrier’s real net receipts and the remaining tax requirement. Unsold securities are excluded from bank cash. Selling them could change the plan, but would require a separate decision, price, transaction cost, tax review and receipt date. The calculator supplies no automatic sale or borrowing facility to fill the shortage. Test the form while keeping the total payment unchanged The line varies the securities share while keeping the gross payment and both cash assignments fixed. At an all-cash mix, the CAD 25,000 payment adds to CAD 12,000 opening cash. After assigning CAD 24,000, the budget has CAD 13,000 left. At an all-securities mix, no new bank cash arrives. Opening cash alone leaves CAD 12,000 of the two assignments unfunded. Both mixes represent the same CAD 25,000 payment in this illustration, but they create very different cash capacity. The selected defaults reach a zero budget remainder at a 52% securities share: the remaining 48% supplies CAD 12,000 of cash. That crossing is conditional arithmetic. It does not recommend a payment mix or establish which securities should remain invested. The matrix also changes opening bank cash. More accessible cash can fund a larger securities share without an immediate shortage. A zero cell answers only whether these two entered assignments can be funded now; it does not prove that future expenses, taxes or retirement needs are covered. Confirm the payment record and the usable cash separately For an actual arrangement, confirm the remaining payment requirement, the available form, the valuation used, the destination account and the expected delivery dates with the carrier. Then prepare a separate budget using the cash actually expected to reach the bank and the tax amount still to be funded. The model caps the represented payment at the available RRIF value and identifies any unrepresented selected amount. That is a limit of the cash illustration, not a ruling that a statutory minimum has been breached. Changes in account value and special circumstances belong with the carrier’s actual calculation. Keep the withdrawal record, the securities position and the bank statement in distinct roles. One documents the payment, one shows property still held, and one supplies money available for cash obligations. Reconciling all three prevents a gross retirement payment from being spent twice in the plan.
3313a136b57c5dfd3ca65375fb3a3b5bae96739d.zh: 在 RRIF 之外记录的付款不一定是可使用现金的存款。确认其形式并将未售出的证券与分配给下一张账单的资金分开。 Ask what actually arrives when the RRIF makes a payment A retirement statement can show a payment without the same number of dollars reaching the bank.当一个家庭将这笔款项用于租金、食品杂货或所得税账单时，这种区别就很重要。 CRA IC78-18R7 注册退休收入基金第 5 段解释说，最低金额可以以现金以外的形式支付。承运人和账户安排仍然需要确认可以交付什么以及如何评估和记录实际付款。实物支付将证券等财产转移到 RRIF 之外，但不会自动将其出售为现金。该图假设有经批准的普通最低付款安排和单独的非注册目的地。它不会计算最小值或决定特定帐户是否支持该形式。这与在注册安排之间直接转移资产不同。该示例遵循向年金受益人付款的情况。 CRA 的 RRIF 概述规定，支付的金额在收到时应纳税；付款的非现金形式并不意味着此示例为免税提款。 Split the gross amount before putting it in the cash budget The worked example begins with a RRIF value of CAD 400,000 immediately before the illustrated payment.独立输入并经承运人确认的总付款额为 25,000 加元。该模型不会根据当前余额或年龄因素得出该金额。如果证券份额为 60%，则 15,000 加元作为证券到达，10,000 加元作为银行现金到达。 RRIF 价值下降 25,000 加元，至 375,000 加元，价格保持不变。两笔付款总计为 25,000 加元；它们不是两次如此规模的提款。该家庭还拥有 12,000 加元的开户银行现金。现金部分到达后，在支付税收和支出任务之前，其银行余额为 22,000 加元。 15,000 加元的证券仍然是单独的资产。在本例中，由于没有任何费用、预扣税、市场变动或完成的家庭付款，因此资源可以协调。注册 RRIF 价值加上银行现金为 412,000 加元。后来的 RRIF 价值为 375,000 加元，证券为 15,000 加元，银行现金为 22,000 加元，合计金额相同。地点之间的流动并没有创造财富。 An earmark changes availability before it changes the bank balance The selected tax cash reserve is CAD 6,000, and planned household bills total CAD 18,000.他们总共分配了 24,000 加元现金。相对于 22,000 加元的银行余额，该插图还需要 2,000 加元的额外现金。瀑布是一座预算容量的桥梁。其负端点并不意味着实际的银行账户已经透支。这两项任务均不被视为已完成的付款。这表明相同的银行余额无法全额资助这两项承诺。税额是在单独评估后独立输入的。它不是通过此工具计算的百分比或最终欠税表。该插图假设未从付款中预扣税款；如果实际来源扣除或费用适用，请用承运人的实际净收入和剩余的税收要求替换此简化的现金计划。未售出的证券不计入银行现金。出售它们可能会改变计划，但需要单独做出决定、价格、交易成本、税务审查和收货日期。该计算器不提供自动出售或借用功能来填补短缺。 Test the form while keeping the total payment unchanged The line varies the securities share while keeping the gross payment and both cash assignments fixed.在全现金组合中，25,000 加元的付款加上 12,000 加元的开仓现金。分配 24,000 加元后，预算还剩 13,000 加元。在全证券组合中，不会有新的银行现金到来。仅开期现金就使两项任务中的 12,000 加元没有资金支持。在此图中，两种组合代表相同的 25,000 加元付款，但它们产生的现金容量却截然不同。选定的违约者在 52% 的证券份额中达到零预算剩余：剩余的 48% 提供 12,000 加元的现金。该交叉是条件算术。它不建议支付组合或确定应继续投资哪些证券。该矩阵还改变了期初银行现金。更容易获得的现金可以为更大的证券份额提供资金，而不会立即出现短缺。零单元格仅回答这两项输入的作业现在是否可以获得资助；它并不能证明未来的费用、税收或退休需求得到了保障。 Confirm the payment record and the usable cash separately For an actual arrangement, confirm the remaining payment requirement, the available form, the valuation used, the destination account and the expected delivery dates with the carrier.然后使用实际预计到达银行的现金和仍待资助的税额准备单独的预算。该模型将所代表的付款上限限制为可用的 RRIF 值，并识别任何未代表的选定金额。这是现金说明的限制，而不是对违反法定最低限额的裁决。账户价值变动及特殊情况以承运人实际计算为准。分别保存取款记录、证券头寸和银行对账单。一份记录付款，一份显示仍持有的财产，一份提供可用于支付现金义务的资金。协调这三者可以防止总退休金在计划中被重复支出。

2095ef0782667c1bf802808efc094279a11fce65.src: Divide the relevant cash amount by the units actually acquired. A lower purchase-price average than the arithmetic average does not establish a profit or a superior investing schedule. Give the cash and the units their own records Suppose you invest the same cash amount every month while the unit price changes. Averaging the quoted prices gives each month equal weight. Dividing your purchase spending by your acquired units gives a different average because a lower price allows the same cash to buy more units. The distinction is arithmetic, not evidence that a particular schedule is profitable. A useful record identifies execution prices, cash available, charges, units bought and the price later used to value those units. Investor.gov’s dollar-cost-averaging explanation describes equal purchases at regular intervals and the resulting change in units when prices move. This article uses that mechanism in six original monthly transactions. It does not compare investing an existing lump sum with investing future earnings. The default assigns CAD 200 to each purchase, including a CAD 2 transaction fee. Net security-purchase cash is therefore CAD 198 per order. The six execution prices are CAD 20, 16, 12, 18, 24 and 20 per unit. These are authored numbers, not observations from a fund. Follow each execution before calculating an average At CAD 20, net cash of CAD 198 buys 9.9 units. At CAD 16 it buys 12.375 units; at CAD 12, 16.5 units. The fourth, fifth and sixth purchases add 11, 8.25 and 9.9 units respectively. Total units are 67.925 . Security-purchase spending is six times CAD 198, or CAD 1,188 . Fees total CAD 12, bringing total household cash spent to CAD 1,200 . The unit bars make the changing quantities visible. They should not be interpreted as changes in the amount the household saved: each monthly cash assignment is still CAD 200. The fee is paid from that assignment before the units are acquired. The example allows any fractional unit amount and retains calculation precision. Actual brokers, plans or securities may impose whole-unit orders, rounding rules or minimums. Those restrictions would require a separate cash-residue ledger and could change the units obtained. Identify the numerator before reporting a unit cost The simple arithmetic average of the six execution prices is their sum divided by six: CAD 110 ÷ 6, or approximately CAD 18.33 per unit . It describes this list of prices, with equal weight assigned to every purchase date. The actual purchase-price amount per acquired unit is CAD 1,188 ÷ 67.925, or approximately CAD 17.49 . This is a unit-weighted average: multiplying each execution price by its purchased units reconstructs the CAD 1,188 security spending. Total household cash per unit includes the fees. CAD 1,200 ÷ 67.925 is approximately CAD 17.67 . It exceeds the purchase-price average because the same acquired units must account for an additional CAD 12 of cash spent. The three headline figures are all CAD per unit. None is an account balance or a percentage investment return. The line chart traces their cumulative versions after each purchase so a reader can see how the records develop, rather than replacing the underlying transactions with one unexplained average. Use the harmonic mean only when its equal-cash condition holds Write the six positive prices as P₁ through P₆ and equal net purchase cash as C. Total units are C ÷ P₁ + C ÷ P₂ + … + C ÷ P₆. Total security spending is 6C. Dividing spending by units cancels C and gives 6 ÷ (1/P₁ + 1/P₂ + … + 1/P₆) . This is the harmonic mean of the six positive prices, matching the definition in NIST’s harmonic-mean reference . The identity applies here because equal household cash and an identical fixed fee leave equal net cash at every execution. If the amounts or fees vary between purchases, calculate total actual spending divided by total actual units directly. An unweighted harmonic mean would then generally answer a different question. For positive prices, the harmonic mean is no greater than the arithmetic mean, with equality when all the prices are identical. That mathematical comparison is between two averages of the same price list. It does not compare this schedule’s realized return with another strategy, and it does not remove the effect of charges. Reconcile the separate valuation without treating costs as profit The valuation input is independent of the six execution prices. At the default CAD 20 per unit, the 67.925 units have market value of CAD 1,358.50 . Compared with CAD 1,200 of household cash spent, the unrealized cash gain is CAD 158.50. The waterfall starts with that CAD 1,200, subtracts the CAD 12 paid in fees and adds CAD 170.50 of price change across the purchased units. The resulting CAD 1,358.50 is the market value, with the fee deducted once. Change only the valuation price to CAD 15. Market value becomes CAD 1,018.875 before display rounding, and the unrealized cash result becomes a loss of CAD 181.125. The six-price arithmetic average and purchase-price harmonic mean have not changed. A purchase average below an arithmetic average can therefore coexist with an investment loss. The separate valuation is not an executed sale. Selling costs, tax and access to cash remain outside the illustration. The all-in cash figure is not a determination of the asset’s tax adjusted cost base. Test identical prices and fee drag before drawing a conclusion The variation control scales the authored deviations from the first-price base. At 100%, the default six-price shape is 1, 0.8, 0.6, 0.9, 1.2 and 1 times the base. Zero variation makes all execution prices equal. Changing it does not select a historical market episode or assign probabilities to a decline. With zero variation, a CAD 20 price and the unchanged CAD 2 fee, every purchase buys 9.9 units. Both the arithmetic price and the purchase-price average are CAD 20, while household cash per unit is approximately CAD 20.20. Valuing the units at CAD 20 leaves a CAD 12 loss, exactly equal to the six fees. The signed matrix changes the valuation price and fee while preserving the selected execution prices and monthly cash. Its rows are explicit comparison prices, not confidence bounds. A larger fee reduces the units bought from the fixed budget; a higher valuation price raises their market value. FINRA’s discussion of regular investing identifies transaction costs and the distinction between existing cash and money invested as it is earned. Those practical considerations require their own records. This calculation supplies neither a guarantee of profit nor an allocation or timing recommendation.

FINRA’s discussion of regular investing identifies transaction costs and the distinction between existing cash and money invested as it is earned. Those practical considerations require their own records. This calculation supplies neither a guarantee of profit nor an allocation or timing recommendation.

1fb10cc90e04cdd0411709d6bd50f7fa47d50a94.src: Read the grant’s terms before assigning dollars to a goal. Vested units, owned shares, intrinsic spread and spendable sale proceeds are different quantities. A right to buy shares is different from owning shares or receiving cash A compensation statement may display a large option count without showing money that can pay next month’s rent. The count needs a contract, a time condition and an exercise price before it can become a useful planning input. Investor.gov distinguishes employee stock options from an employee stock ownership retirement plan. An option gives a right to buy company shares at a specified price after the relevant conditions. The grant itself does not mean the employee already owns all the underlying shares. This article uses a fictional grant in Canadian dollars. It is a cash-arithmetic illustration rather than a description of a particular Canadian or U.S. award. Each authored unit buys one share. Keep the granted count, vested count, strike payment, share-sale proceeds and actual cash received on separate lines of the plan. The cliff controls when service first produces vested units The default grant contains 1,200 units. The authored schedule lasts 48 months, with nothing vested through month eleven. At month twelve, it catches up the completed service and vests 300 units. Another 25 units vest per completed month under this particular grant size. At the selected month eighteen, 450 units have vested and 750 remain unvested. The milestone bars are snapshots of that same untouched grant. Adding the bars together would count the grant repeatedly; they are not new awards received each month. For grant sizes that do not divide evenly, cumulative grant multiplied by completed months divided by 48 is rounded down to whole units. At month 48, every remaining unit vests. The control selects completed service, not a forecast of future employment. This fixed convention is invented for the chart. A real grant agreement may use a different cliff, schedule, performance condition or treatment when employment ends. Multiply vested units by the positive price–strike difference The default share-price assumption is CAD 60 and the strike is CAD 50. The price difference is CAD 10 per unit, giving 450 × CAD 10 = CAD 4,500 of vested intrinsic spread. Multiplying all 1,200 granted units by CAD 60 would instead describe a hypothetical underlying share amount, not cash owned through the vested options. Fidelity’s stock-option explanation describes the distinction between the grant’s purchase right and the shares acquired through exercise. Its examples also distinguish vesting from exercise. The chart keeps those steps separate. The price curve is a sensitivity, not a projected stock path. It floors intrinsic spread at zero when the share price does not exceed strike. That does not value every feature of an unexpired option. The opportunity to exercise later, uncertain future prices and contractual restrictions are outside this calculation. Intrinsic spread is therefore neither full option fair value nor a bank deposit. Deduct the strike from a permitted sale before treating proceeds as a resource Suppose the 450 vested units can be exercised and the acquired shares sold immediately at CAD 60 each. Gross sale proceeds would be CAD 27,000. Buying those shares at the CAD 50 strike requires CAD 22,500, leaving CAD 4,500 before taxes and transaction costs. The waterfall reconciles those amounts without adding the spread to the sale proceeds again. The spread is already the difference between the two components. Their chart order is not an instruction about execution or settlement, and the assumed sale is not money already available. Fidelity’s global stock-plan glossary distinguishes exercise and sell from exercise and hold. A permitted sale-funded arrangement can use proceeds to meet exercise costs and other deductions. This model assumes the first arrangement exists for its waterfall only. At or below strike it shows no transaction, which is a plotting convention rather than an exercise recommendation. Positive intrinsic spread does not supply the cash needed to retain shares Exercise and hold is a separate comparison. The employee pays the strike and keeps the acquired shares, so this alternative has no share-sale receipt. The default strike payment is still CAD 22,500, even though the calculated intrinsic spread is only CAD 4,500. With CAD 5,000 of entered uncommitted cash, the strike-only funding gap is CAD 17,500. Comparing the CAD 4,500 spread with the cash balance would miss the larger purchase payment. The cash bars show both amounts and the remaining shortfall without adding them into a fictitious total. For a separate funded example, suppose those 450 shares are retained after paying the strike, then fall to CAD 40 each. Their value becomes CAD 18,000, below the CAD 22,500 purchase payment. This extra arithmetic is outside the chart’s unchanged-price comparison. Exercising changes an option into a shareholding; a previously positive intrinsic spread does not fix the later sale result. The input should represent cash free of other commitments. Money reserved for annual bills, an emergency or another goal cannot simultaneously fund the exercise. A zero gap covers only the modeled strike payment; it does not estimate taxes, withholding or fees. The illustration neither borrows the difference nor executes an exercise, and it does not compare the merits of retaining or selling the shares. Use actual award terms and receipt dates before attaching options to a goal A practical record should identify the award, vested units, strike, exercise window and permitted transaction methods. Keep an expiry date separate from a vesting date. The charts assume the window is open at the selected checkpoint; they do not calculate a deadline or a post-employment exercise period. Review the real agreement and administrator’s current instructions for restrictions and timing. The cited sources explain general concepts and administration methods, rather than establishing any reader’s contract. Their U.S. tax discussions are not imported into this CAD illustration. No personal tax liability or withholding rate is calculated. Finally, place only confirmed cash receipts in a dated spending plan. An option grant, a hypothetical quote and an assumed sale are earlier stages. The related employer-share guide examines the additional risk of salary and investment exposure depending on the same company. This page addresses the prior question: what is owned, what must be paid, and what event would actually produce spendable cash?
1fb10cc90e04cdd0411709d6bd50f7fa47d50a94.zh: 在将资金分配给某个目标之前，请先阅读赠款的条款。既得单位、自有股份、内在价差和可支出销售收益的数量不同。 A right to buy shares is different from owning shares or receiving cash A compensation statement may display a large option count without showing money that can pay next month’s rent.计数需要合同、时间条件和执行价格才能成为有用的计划输入。 Investor.gov 将员工股票期权与员工持股退休计划区分开来。期权赋予在满足相关条件后以指定价格购买公司股票的权利。授予本身并不意味着员工已经拥有所有相关股票。本文使用虚构的加元补助金。这是一个现金算术说明，而不是对特定加拿大或美国奖项的描述。每个授权单位购买一股。将授予数量、既得数量、执行付款、股票出售收益和实际收到的现金保留在计划的不同行中。悬崖控制服务首次产生既得单位的时间 默认授予包含 1,200 个单位。制定的时间表持续 48 个月，到第十一个月为止没有任何归属。在第 12 个月，它赶上了已完成的服务并授予了 300 个单位。在此特定赠款规模下，每个完成月还授予 25 个单位。在选定的第 18 个月，450 个单位已归属，750 个单位尚未归属。里程碑条是同一未触及拨款的快照。将条形图加在一起会重复计算补助金；它们并不是每个月收到的新奖项。对于未均等分配的赠款数额，累积赠款乘以已完成月数除以 48 将向下舍入为整数单位。第 48 个月，所有剩余单位均归属。该控制选择已完成的服务，而不是对未来就业的预测。这种固定约定是为图表发明的。真正的赠款协议可能会在雇佣关系结束时使用不同的悬崖、时间表、绩效条件或待遇。 Multiply vested units by the positive price–strike difference The default share-price assumption is CAD 60 and the strike is CAD 50. The price difference is CAD 10 per unit, giving 450 × CAD 10 = CAD 4,500 of vested intrinsic spread.将所有 1,200 个授予单位乘以 60 加元将描述假设的基础股份金额，而不是通过既定期权拥有的现金。富达的股票期权解释描述了授予的购买权和通过行使获得的股票之间的区别。它的例子也区分了归属和行权。该图表将这些步骤分开。价格曲线是一种敏感性，而不是预计的股票路径。当股价不超过行使价时，它将内在利差降至零。这并不重视未到期期权的所有功能。稍后行权的机会、不确定的未来价格和合同限制不在此计算范围内。因此，内在利差既不是完整的期权公允价值，也不是银行存款。 Deduct the strike from a permitted sale before treating proceeds as a resource Suppose the 450 vested units can be exercised and the acquired shares sold immediately at CAD 60 each.销售总收入为 27,000 加元。以 50 加元的价格购买这些股票需要 22,500 加元，扣除税费和交易费用后还剩 4,500 加元。瀑布会核对这些金额，而不会再次将价差添加到销售收益中。价差已经是两个组件之间的差异。他们的图表订单不是关于执行或结算的指令，并且假设的销售也不是已经可用的资金。富达的全球股票计划术语表将行权和出售与行权和持有区分开来。允许的销售资助安排可以使用收益来支付行权成本和其他扣除。该模型假设第一种排列仅适用于其瀑布。等于或低于行使价时，它显示没有交易，这是一种绘图惯例，而不是演习建议。正的内在利差并不能提供保留股票所需的现金 行使和持有是一个单独的比较。员工支付罢工费用并保留所获得的股份，因此这种替代方案没有股份出售收据。尽管计算出的内在利差仅为 4,500 加元，但默认履约付款仍为 22,500 加元。由于输入了 5,000 加元的未承诺现金，因此仅罢工的资金缺口为 17,500 加元。将 4,500 加元的价差与现金余额进行比较会漏掉较大的购买付款。现金条显示金额和剩余缺口，而不将它们添加到虚构的总额中。对于一个单独的资助示例，假设在支付罢工后保留这 450 股，然后跌至每股 40 加元。它们的价值变为 18,000 加元，低于 22,500 加元的购买付款。这个额外的算术不属于图表中不变价格比较的范围。行使将期权转变为股权；之前的正内在价差并不能修复后来的销售结果。输入应代表不含其他承诺的现金。为年度账单、紧急情况或其他目标预留的资金不能同时为这项工作提供资金。零缺口仅涵盖模拟的罢工付款；它不估算税费、预扣税或费用。该插图既没有借用差额，也没有执行行使，也没有比较保留或出售股票的优点。 Use actual award terms and receipt dates before attaching options to a goal A practical record should identify the award, vested units, strike, exercise window and permitted transaction methods.将到期日与行权日分开。图表假设窗口在选定的检查点打开；他们不计算最后期限或离职后行使期。查看真实协议和管理员当前的限制和时间说明。引用的来源解释了一般概念和管理方法，而不是建立任何读者的合同。他们的美国税务讨论未导入此 CAD 插图中。不计算个人纳税义务或预扣税率。最后，仅将已确认的现金收入放入注明日期的支出计划中。授予期权、假设报价和假设出售均处于早期阶段。相关的雇主份额指南检查了同一家公司的工资和投资风险的额外风险。本页解决了前面的问题：拥有什么，必须支付什么，以及什么事件实际上会产生可支出的现金？

b3d52dd62d67c79d64cf91c52b53e719b50af257.src: A hold can consume borrowing headroom without being a posted expense. Its release, a card payment and a cash refund belong to different records. Distinguish an authorization from a posted purchase A card can have enough unused limit when a trip begins and much less available credit after several merchants request temporary holds. A hold can reserve borrowing capacity while a transaction or security requirement is unresolved. It does not necessarily become a posted purchase for the same amount. Capital One’s explanation of authorization holds describes this temporary reduction in available credit and distinguishes it from a posted charge. It is a US issuer’s general explanation, rather than a rulebook for every Canadian card. The FCAC credit-card guide separately explains credit limits and recognizes temporary merchant holds. The model therefore tests capacity on specific days. It does not predict an issuer’s approval decision or infer that a charge was made simply because a merchant requested a hold. Every amount and date is an independent hypothetical assumption, with no standard hold period implied. Put two incidental authorizations beside the existing balance The default limit is CAD 3,000 and the opening posted balance is CAD 900. Before temporary authorizations, that leaves CAD 2,100 of borrowing headroom. The first requested incidental hold is CAD 1,200 from day one; the second is CAD 900 from day three. On days three through five, both holds overlap and the opening balance remains unchanged. Their combined capacity demand is CAD 900 plus CAD 1,200 plus CAD 900, exactly CAD 3,000. None of that calculation requires the two holds to be recorded as new posted expenses. The example isolates security or incidental authorizations. It assumes that each is eventually released in full without a charge. Any underlying accommodation, rental or other booking cost must be budgeted separately. If part of a hold becomes a real posted purchase, that actual amount belongs in the balance ledger while the unused authorization is removed under the actual processing timeline. Test the next purchase without pretending that it has already been approved A separate CAD 600 purchase is planned for day four. The card has zero headroom under the default overlap, so CAD 600 of additional capacity would be needed for the complete set of demands. The waterfall subtracts each component to show that shortfall. The tool does not add the purchase to posted debt after identifying the shortfall. It is testing a proposed transaction, rather than simulating a merchant successfully charging beyond the limit. Scenarios in which existing requested holds already exceed the limit are also shown as infeasible capacity demands, not accepted transactions. That boundary matters when reading the line chart. The purchase amount stays as a horizontal requirement. The headroom line changes with the existing balance, payment credit and hold releases. Crossing the requirement means the proposed amount fits the arithmetic at that checkpoint; it does not confirm that the issuer will authorize it or that the household can afford to repay it. A credited payment and a released hold restore headroom in different ways The default CAD 600 payment becomes usable credit on day six. Existing posted debt falls from CAD 900 to CAD 300, creating CAD 600 of headroom while both holds remain active. Day six is therefore the first modeled date, searching from day four, when the separate CAD 600 purchase fits. That payment requires household cash even though the model’s capacity line rises. Reducing a card debt is not new income. The calculation applies at most the opening posted balance and does not simulate an overpayment or a credit balance. It also does not assume that a payment sent on one day becomes usable credit immediately; the usable-credit day is entered separately. On day eight, the first hold disappears and headroom increases by CAD 1,200 without a card payment. That is a release of previously reserved borrowing capacity. It is not a CAD 1,200 cash refund into a bank account. The second hold is absent from day twelve onward under the selected illustration. Change the overlap before drawing conclusions from the headline limit The matrix varies the two hold amounts and reports the extra capacity needed on day four. Limit, posted debt, planned purchase and selected processing dates remain fixed. Larger overlapping authorizations generally leave less room for the separate purchase, without necessarily increasing posted spending by those same amounts. If the first hold’s selected release day is day four, it is already absent when that day’s capacity is tested. Changing its matrix row then has no effect on the day-four result. This is intentional: an amount does not consume capacity after the modeled authorization has ended. All day labels describe complete modeled checkpoints. The payment and hold releases occur before that day’s capacity test. A same-day real transaction could have a different order. An issuer’s live available-credit display, merchant confirmation and actual posting sequence are needed when the timing matters; the illustration supplies no service deadline or guaranteed release date. Keep the card-capacity calendar beside the repayment budget The line may show that a purchase fits before the household receives its next pay cheque. That says something about borrowing capacity, not about income or bank cash. Interest, fees and the repayment due date still need their own budget review; none is calculated by this fourteen-day capacity tool. A released hold can remove a temporary restriction without reversing a previously recorded expense. Conversely, an actual purchase refund can reduce posted debt under its own processing date. Recording every hold as spending and every release as income would distort both the expense record and any saving-rate calculation. For planning, record four separate facts: posted balance, active authorizations, payments that have actually restored usable credit, and upcoming real purchases. Keep the corresponding bank payments and contractual bills in the cash ledger. This makes it possible to see a temporary capacity squeeze without mistaking it for a new expense, a cash windfall or a reliable emergency reserve.
b3d52dd62d67c79d64cf91c52b53e719b50af257.zh: 保留可以消耗借贷净空，而不是记入费用。它的发布、刷卡支付和现金退款属于不同的记录。区分授权与已发布的购买 当旅行开始时，一张卡可能有足够的未使用限额，而在多个商家请求临时保留后，可用信用额度就会少得多。在交易或担保要求未解决时，持有可以保留借款能力。它不一定会成为相同金额的过账购买。 Capital One 对授权保留的解释描述了可用信贷的暂时减少，并将其与已公布的费用区分开来。这是美国发卡机构的一般性解释，而不是每张加拿大卡的规则手册。 FCAC 信用卡指南单独解释了信用限额并承认商家临时持有。因此，该模型会测试特定日期的容量。它不会预测发行人的批准决定，也不会仅仅因为商家请求暂缓而推断出收费。每个金额和日期都是独立的假设，没有暗示标准持有期限。在现有余额旁边添加两项附带授权。默认限额为 3,000 加元，期初过账余额为 900 加元。在临时授权之前，还剩下 2,100 加元的借贷空间。从第一天起，首次请求的杂费保留金额为 1,200 加元；第二个是从第三天开始的 900 加元。在第三天到第五天，两者持有重叠，期初余额保持不变。他们的总容量需求为 900 加元加 1,200 加元加 900 加元，正好 3,000 加元。这些计算都不需要将这两次保留记录为新的过帐费用。该示例隔离了安全或偶然授权。它假设每个最终都会免费完整发布。任何基础住宿、租金或其他预订费用必须单独编制预算。如果保留的一部分成为实际过账购买，则该实际金额属于余额分类账，而未使用的授权将在实际处理时间表下删除。测试下一次采购，不要假装已获得批准。计划在第四天单独采购 600 加元。该卡在默认重叠下的净空为零，因此需要 600 加元的额外容量来满足整套需求。瀑布减去每个组件以显示不足。在识别短缺后，该工具不会将购买添加到已过帐债务中。它正在测试拟议的交易，而不是模拟商家成功地超出限制收费。现有请求保留已超过限制的情况也显示为不可行的容量需求，而不是接受的交易。阅读折线图时，该边界很重要。采购金额保持横向要求。净空线随现有余额、付款信用和冻结释放而变化。越过要求意味着提议的金额符合该检查点的算术；它不确认发行人是否会授权或该家庭有能力偿还。记入付款和释放保留以不同方式恢复空间。默认的 600 加元付款在第六天变为可用积分。现有已公布债务从 900 加元降至 300 加元，创造了 600 加元的净空，同时两项持有仍保持活跃。因此，第六天是第一个建模日期，从第四天开始搜索，此时适合单独购买 600 CAD。即使该模型的容量线增加，这笔付款也需要家庭现金。减少信用卡债务并不是新的收入。该计算最多适用期初过帐余额，不会模拟超额付款或贷款机构余额。它也不假设某一天发送的付款立即成为可用信用；可用信用日单独输入。第八天，第一笔保留消失，净空增加 1,200 加元，无需使用银行卡付款。这是之前预留的借贷能力的释放。这不是将 1,200 加元现金退还至银行账户。在选定的插图下，从第十二天开始，第二次保留就消失了。在从标题限制得出结论之前更改重叠 该矩阵改变两个保留量并报告第四天所需的额外容量。限制、过账债务、计划购买和选定的处理日期保持不变。较大的重叠授权通常会为单独购买留下较小的空间，而不一定会增加相同金额的过账支出。如果第一个保留选择的释放日是第四天，则在测试该天的容量时它已经不存在。更改其矩阵行对第四天的结果没有影响。这是有意为之的：建模授权结束后，金额不会消耗容量。全天标签描述了完整的建模检查点。付款和保留释放发生在当天的容量测试之前。当日真实交易可能有不同的顺序。当时间安排很重要时，需要发行人的实时可用信用显示、商家确认和实际过账顺序；该插图没有提供服务截止日期或保证的发布日期。将卡容量日历放在还款预算旁边。该行可能会显示在家庭收到下一张工资支票之前购买适合。这说明了借贷能力，而不是收入或银行现金。利息、费用和还款到期日仍需自行预算审查；没有一个是通过这个十四天容量工具计算出来的。解除保留可以取消临时限制，而无需冲销之前记录的费用。相反，实际购买退款可以减少其处理日期下的过账债务。将每次持有记录为支出，将每次释放记录为收入，会扭曲支出记录和任何储蓄率计算。为了进行规划，记录四个单独的事实：过账余额、有效授权、实际恢复可用信用的付款以及即将进行的实际购买。将相应的银行付款和合同票据保留在现金分类账中。这使得我们可以看到暂时的产能紧张，而不会将其误认为是新的支出、意外的现金或可靠的紧急储备。

c6a3757861bcb8209f50a30ce92dd5a5f5bc7fbf.src: Refundability describes what happens to excess credit value. Your tax-return settlement also includes tax already paid, so a non-refundable credit and a refund can appear together. Separate the tax charge, available credit and prior payments The word “non-refundable” can sound as though a tax return containing that credit can never produce a refund. The missing distinction is between the credit’s unused amount and tax that has already been paid. CRA’s educational material separates the calculation of tax and non-refundable credits from the final refund-or-balance-owing step. A non-refundable credit can reduce the applicable tax charge to zero, while prior tax payments can still exceed the reduced charge. The original example begins with CAD 3,000 of tax before one selected credit, CAD 5,000 of available credit value and CAD 1,200 of tax payments already credited to the settlement. Those are three different inputs. A payment already made is not another tax credit being claimed or another reduction in the underlying charge. This is a deliberately limited calculation for one compatible tax bucket. It does not allow a federal credit to be applied indiscriminately to a provincial charge, determine what credit anyone qualifies for, or reproduce all the additions and adjustments in a tax return. Enter the calculated tax-offset value, not an unconverted claim base A tax form may display an eligible amount, expense or credit base that must be converted using the applicable rules before it becomes a tax offset. Entering that larger base as though it were already a dollar-for-dollar reduction can overstate the result. The credit input here is the value after any required percentage, threshold or other calculation. If an invented eligible base of CAD 10,000 were multiplied by an invented 12% credit factor, the amount entered in this tool would be CAD 1,200. Neither invented number is a current Canadian rate or a claim that a specific expense qualifies. A deduction belongs at another stage: it generally affects an income measure used in the tax calculation, rather than being inserted as a tax-offset dollar in this tool. The model starts after that work has been done and accepts the resulting tax charge independently. Use the actual credit’s instructions when replacing the example. The model cannot infer eligibility, calculate combined federal and provincial value, apply a transfer, or decide which income-tested benefits change when an underlying income figure changes. Cap current non-refundable use at the applicable tax charge The non-refundable teaching case uses the smaller of the tax charge and available credit value. With CAD 3,000 of tax and CAD 5,000 of credit value, the model uses CAD 3,000 and leaves CAD 2,000 unapplied in the current period. The first stacked chart preserves that distinction. Its two pieces still add to the original CAD 5,000 credit value. The unapplied piece has no current-period cash benefit in this illustration. The separate refundable teaching case uses the same entered value under a different hypothetical rule. CAD 3,000 offsets the tax charge and CAD 2,000 is refundable excess. That comparison isolates refundability; it does not mean an actual credit can be elected as refundable or that both cases can be claimed together. Calling value unapplied here is not a claim that it expires forever. Carryforward, transfer and use in another year depend on the actual credit. None is modeled. Similarly, two credits with the same headline eligible amount can have different calculations and conditions, so the comparison must begin with supported tax-offset values. Reconcile the reduced charge with tax already paid After using CAD 3,000 of the non-refundable credit, the modeled remaining tax charge is zero. The household has already paid CAD 1,200. Subtracting that payment gives a settlement balance of negative CAD 1,200, shown as a modeled refund. The waterfall is CAD 3,000 tax − CAD 3,000 usable credit − CAD 1,200 prior payments = negative CAD 1,200 . The refund is not the CAD 2,000 unapplied credit value. It reflects payments exceeding the reduced tax charge. Without the selected credit, the same tax and prior payments would leave CAD 1,800 owing. Moving from CAD 1,800 owing to a CAD 1,200 refund improves the settlement by CAD 3,000, exactly the credit used. Reading only the final refund would miss the avoided balance owing. In the separate refundable case, the settlement is CAD 3,000 − CAD 5,000 − CAD 1,200, or negative CAD 3,200. That combines CAD 2,000 of refundable excess with CAD 1,200 of prior payments above a zero remaining tax charge. It remains a simplified arithmetic result before other adjustments. Keep credit value and prior payments on different axes The credit-value chart holds the tax charge fixed. The non-refundable benefit rises only until it reaches that charge, then plateaus. The hypothetical refundable benefit continues with the available credit value because its excess is refundable under the assumed rule. The final chart instead holds tax and credit fixed while changing prior payments. More tax paid earlier shifts the settlement toward a larger refund or smaller amount owing. It does not increase the credit’s usable amount or change its tax benefit. This distinction also explains why a large refund is not automatically a large tax saving. Part of a refund can simply return the household’s own earlier payments. Judging two years or two people by refund size alone mixes differences in tax liability, credits and payment timing. The curves compare hypothetical prior-payment totals; they are not an instruction to change withholding. Payroll rules, instalment obligations and other circumstances need their own review. A later refund also does not supply cash before it is received. Use the actual return and assessment before budgeting a receipt The illustration omits other taxes, contributions, refundable benefits, instalment adjustments, interest, penalties and other credits. It also omits reassessments and government offsets. CRA’s refund guidance explains that a refund can be applied against certain amounts owed, so the modeled settlement should not automatically become a promised bank deposit. When applying the idea, verify the applicable tax charge, the actual credit’s calculation, how much can be used and which payments have already been credited. Keep any carryforward or transfer on a separate supported schedule. Confirm which year and tax authority each amount belongs to before combining them. Use the filed return and assessment to establish the result, then add the receipt date to the household cash plan. A credit’s effect on tax, the final settlement and cash available today remain separate facts. The four charts are useful because their parts reconcile. They show how a non-refundable credit can reduce tax without paying out its unused portion, while a refund can still arise from payments already made. That explanation applies to the arithmetic of the model; an actual entitlement or filing position requires the relevant current rules.
c6a3757861bcb8209f50a30ce92dd5a5f5bc7fbf.zh: 可退款性描述了超额信用价值会发生什么情况。您的纳税申报表结算还包括已缴纳的税款，因此不可退还的抵免额和退款可以同时出现。将税费、可用抵免额和预先付款分开“不可退还”一词听起来好像包含该抵免额的纳税申报表永远不会产生退款。缺少的区别是信贷的未使用金额和已缴纳的税款之间的区别。 CRA 的教育材料将税收和不可退还抵免额的计算与最终的退款或余额欠款步骤分开。不可退还的抵免可以将适用的税费减少至零，而之前的税款仍然可以超过减少的费用。最初的示例首先是在选定的信用额之前缴纳 3,000 加元的税款、5,000 加元的可用信用额以及已贷记到结算中的 1,200 加元的税款。这是三个不同的输入。已支付的款项不属于要求的另一项税收抵免或基础费用的另一项减少。这是针对一个兼容税桶的故意限制计算。它不允许将联邦抵免不加区别地应用于省级收费，确定任何人有资格获得哪些抵免，或在纳税申报表中复制所有添加和调整。输入计算出的税收抵免值，而不是未转换的索赔基础 纳税表可能会显示符合条件的金额、费用或信用基础，必须使用适用的规则对其进行转换，然后才能成为税收抵免。输入更大的基数，就好像它已经是一美元对一美元的减少一样，可能会夸大结果。这里的信用输入是经过任何所需的百分比、阈值或其他计算后的值。如果发明的合格基础 10,000 加元乘以发明的 12% 信用系数，则在此工具中输入的金额将为 1,200 加元。这两个发明的数字都不是加拿大现行的费率，也不是特定费用符合条件的声明。扣除额属于另一个阶段：它通常会影响税收计算中使用的收入衡量标准，而不是作为税收抵免美元插入此工具中。该模型在该工作完成后启动，并独立接受由此产生的税费。替换示例时请使用实际的信用说明。该模型无法推断资格、计算联邦和省的综合价值、应用转移或决定当基本收入数字发生变化时哪些收入测试福利会发生变化。当前不可退还使用的上限为适用税费 不可退还的教学案例使用税费和可用信用值中的较小者。由于税费为 3,000 加元，信贷价值为 5,000 加元，该模型在本期使用 3,000 加元，并留下 2,000 加元未应用。第一个堆叠图表保留了这种区别。其两件仍增加了原始 5,000 加元的信用价值。在此图中，未应用的部分没有当期现金收益。单独的可退款教学案例在不同的假设规则下使用相同的输入值。 3,000 加元可抵消税费，2,000 加元可退还超额部分。这种比较隔离了可退款性；这并不意味着实际信用可以被选择为可退还，或者两种情况可以一起索赔。此处调用值未应用并不意味着它永远过期。结转、转让、下年度使用，按实际贷记情况确定。没有一个被建模。同样，具有相同标题合格金额的两个学分可以具有不同的计算和条件，因此必须从支持的税收抵免值开始进行比较。将减少的费用与已缴纳的税款进行核对 使用 3,000 加元的不可退还信用后，模型中的剩余税费为零。该家庭已经支付了 1,200 加元。减去该付款得出的结算余额为负 1,200 加元，显示为模型退款。瀑布是 3,000 加元税费 - 3,000 加元可用信用 - 1,200 加元预付款 = 负 1,200 加元。退款并非未使用的 2,000 加元积分金额。它反映了超过减税额的付款。如果没有选定的抵免额，相同的税款和之前的付款将导致欠款 1,800 加元。由于退款 1,200 加元，结算金额从 1,800 加元改为 3,000 加元，正好是所使用的积分。只阅读最终退款将会错过避免的欠款余额。在单独退款的情况下，结算金额为 3,000 加元 – 5,000 加元 – 1,200 加元，或负 3,200 加元。这包括 2,000 加元的可退还超额费用和 1,200 加元的预付款（剩余税费为零）。在进行其他调整之前，它仍然是一个简化的算术结果。将信用值和预先付款保持在不同的轴上 信用值图表将税费保持固定。不可退还的福利只会增加，直到达到该费用，然后趋于稳定。假设的可退还福利继续具有可用信用值，因为根据假定的规则，其超出部分是可退还的。最终的图表在改变先前付款的同时保持税收和信贷固定。较早缴纳的税款越多，结算就会转向更大的退款或更少的欠款。它不会增加信贷的可用金额或改变其税收优惠。这种区别也解释了为什么大额退税不会自动带来大额节税。部分退款可以简单地退还家庭自己的早期付款。仅根据退税金额来判断两年或两年的人会混合纳税义务、抵免和付款时间的差异。这些曲线比较了假设的预先付款总额；它们不是更改预扣税的指示。工资规则、分期付款义务和其他情况需要自行审查。稍后退款在收到之前也不提供现金。在制定收据预算之前使用实际申报表和评估 该插图省略了其他税款、缴款、可退还福利、分期付款调整、利息、罚款和其他抵免。它还省略了重新评估和政府抵消。 CRA 的退款指南解释说，可以对某些欠款进行退款，因此模型结算不应自动成为承诺的银行存款。应用该想法时，请核实适用的税费、实际抵免额的计算、可以使用的金额以及哪些付款已记入抵免额。将任何结转或转移保留在单独的支持计划中。在合并之前确认每笔金额属于哪个年份和税务机关。使用提交的申报表和评估来确定结果，然后将收据日期添加到家庭现金计划中。抵免对税收、最终结算和当今可用现金的影响仍然是单独的事实。这四个图表很有用，因为它们的各个部分是一致的。他们展示了不可退还的信用如何在不支付未使用部分的情况下减少税收，同时仍可以从已付款中获得退款。该解释适用于模型的算术；实际的权利或申请职位需要相关的现行规则。

5e312a5484221d889ed058a8da090ea6ab4a5ccb.src: The number of units, the vested fraction, the price used for valuation and the date cash becomes usable are separate parts of an equity-compensation plan. Identify what was granted before valuing the number on screen A compensation statement may show an attractive total for a share-linked award. The figure alone does not establish how much has vested, what will be delivered or when proceeds can fund a household payment. FINRA’s questions about stock awards distinguishes employee options, restricted stock units and other equity arrangements, and explains why time and performance conditions matter. An option’s exercise right and an RSU-style unit are different instruments. This calculator uses a simplified share-linked unit, without an exercise price. The example is independent of any employer plan. It compares two explicitly invented service schedules applied to one award. The amounts are expressed in CAD solely as the example’s valuation currency; the schedules are not a statement of Canadian or U.S. minimum vesting rules. Write the two service rules before plotting them The original award contains 600 units. Each is valued using an independent CAD 50 share-price assumption, giving a whole-award gross notional value of CAD 30,000 . The selected comparison date is after two completed service years. Under the default cliff rule, no units vest until three whole service years have been completed, at which point all 600 vest. Under the default gradual rule, one-fifth of the original award vests after each completed year, reaching full vesting after five years. The step chart makes both rules visible. It does not spread a cliff award evenly across the preceding years or assume partial-year service qualifies. An actual agreement may count dates, hours or performance milestones differently; replace the simplified exercise with the confirmed schedule before evaluating a real award. The same CAD 30,000 total can contain very different rights At year two, the three-year cliff has not been reached, so the cliff example has zero vested units. All 600 remain unvested, with CAD 30,000 of gross notional value at the entered price. The gradual example has vested two-fifths of 600, or 240 units . At CAD 50 each, their gross notional value is CAD 12,000 . The remaining 360 units have CAD 18,000 of gross notional value and remain unvested. The stacked bars have the same CAD 30,000 total because the award size and valuation price match. Reading only the total would conceal the different composition. Adding CAD 30,000 and CAD 12,000 as separate household assets would count the vested portion twice. A gradual schedule is not ahead at every service date Change completed service to three years. The default cliff rule now vests all 600 units, with CAD 30,000 of gross value at the entered price. The five-year gradual rule vests only three-fifths, or 360 units, with CAD 18,000 of gross value. The ordering has reversed from the year-two comparison. At five completed years, both schedules have vested all units and their classified values coincide. The earlier advantage of a gradual schedule does not make it superior at every date. This comparison isolates vesting mechanics while holding the grant and price fixed. It does not compare salaries, future awards, job satisfaction, employment risk or the value of another offer. A single upcoming milestone is one input to a job-change plan, rather than a complete reason to stay or leave. A vesting percentage and a share price change different quantities Keep the default two-year service date and reduce the valuation price from CAD 50 to CAD 30. The gradual schedule still vests 40% of the award and still corresponds to 240 vested units. Their gross notional value falls from CAD 12,000 to CAD 7,200. The whole award’s value falls from CAD 30,000 to CAD 18,000. Its unvested portion falls from CAD 18,000 to CAD 10,800. All dollar values scale with the chosen price, while the number of units and vested fractions remain unchanged. The price input is a stress assumption, not a forecast of what the employer’s stock will trade at on a future date. The matrix uses the same fixed price across its dates to isolate schedule differences. It does not imply that the stock price will remain constant over time. Reconcile gross vested value without inventing a cash transaction For the gradual schedule at year two, the waterfall begins with the whole-award CAD 30,000 gross value and subtracts CAD 18,000 associated with unvested units. The endpoint is CAD 12,000 associated with vested units. This is a classification bridge. It does not mean CAD 30,000 entered a bank account and CAD 18,000 was then charged as a penalty. No sale, delivery or cash receipt occurs in the model. A potential forfeiture must be evaluated from the actual award’s termination and other provisions. The computation retains fractional units where a chosen award size does not divide evenly into the chosen annual portions. That preserves the stated percentage calculation. Actual rounding, whole-share delivery or cash-in-lieu treatment can differ and must come from the award terms. Vesting, delivery and usable cash need separate dates The U.S. Office of Government Ethics’ RSU definition distinguishes the grant from the later stock or cash distribution and notes that distribution may be deferred under some plans. It is cited here for that instrument distinction, rather than for anyone’s disclosure obligations. Even when an actual award vests, the household still needs to confirm what is delivered, its settlement date, any withholding and whether a sale is permitted. The gross notional value of vested units is therefore not automatically the amount that can be spent. This calculator includes no tax calculation, payroll withholding, sale costs, trading restriction or currency conversion. It also adds no new grants, dividends or dividend equivalents. Entering a higher price cannot resolve those separate questions or supply cash before it is actually usable. Use the matrix to expose a milestone assumption The matrix changes completed service years and the number of years over which equal annual portions fully vest. Each cell values the remaining unvested units using the same award size and entered price. The cliff milestone does not enter this gradual-only comparison. A zero cell means all units have vested under that mathematical schedule. It does not establish that shares were delivered, that a sale can settle in time or that the proceeds will cover a goal. A positive cell is the gross value still attached to unvested units, rather than a probability-weighted loss. Confirm the award type and original unit count. Read each vesting milestone and the service or performance conditions. Check what happens under the relevant departure circumstances. Record delivery, withholding and permitted-sale timing separately. Count only independently verified usable cash against an immediate payment. Employer-linked compensation can also concentrate job income and investment exposure in the same company. The separate employer-concentration article tests that joint risk using existing vested, saleable holdings. Keep contingent awards distinct when connecting the two exercises.
5e312a5484221d889ed058a8da090ea6ab4a5ccb.zh: 单位数量、既得比例、用于估值的价格以及现金可用日期是股权补偿计划的独立部分。在评估屏幕上的数字之前先确定所授予的内容 薪酬声明可能会显示与股票挂钩的奖励的有吸引力的总额。仅凭这个数字并不能确定已归属的金额、将交付的金额或收益何时可以为家庭付款提供资金。 FINRA 关于股票奖励的问题区分了员工期权、限制性股票单位和其他股权安排，并解释了为什么时间和绩效条件很重要。期权的行权权和 RSU 式单位是不同的工具。该计算器使用简化的股票挂钩单位，没有行使价。该示例独立于任何雇主计划。它比较了应用于一项奖项的两个明确发明的服务时间表。金额仅以加元表示，作为示例的计价货币；该时间表并非加拿大或美国最低兑现规则的声明。在绘制两条服务规则之前先写下它们 原始奖励包含 600 个单位。每份奖励均采用独立的 50 加元股价假设进行估值，整个奖励的名义总价值为 30,000 加元。选定的比较日期是在两个完整服务年之后。根据默认的悬崖规则，在三个完整的服务年完成之前，不会授予单位，此时所有 600 个单位都归属。根据默认的渐进规则，每完成一年后，原始奖励的五分之一将归属，五年后将达到全额归属。步骤图使这两条规则可见。它不会在前几年平均分配悬崖奖励，也不会假设部分年份的服务符合资格。实际协议可能会以不同的方式计算日期、时间或绩效里程碑；在评估真正的奖励之前，用已确认的时间表替换简化的练习。同样的 30,000 加元总额可能包含截然不同的权利。第二年，尚未达到三年悬崖，因此悬崖示例的既得单位为零。所有 600 份股票仍未归属，按输入价格计算，名义总价值为 30,000 加元。渐进的例子已经授予了 600 个单位的五分之二，即 240 个单位。每张 50 加元，名义总价值为 12,000 加元。其余 360 个单位的名义总价值为 18,000 加元，尚未归属。由于奖励金额和估值价格匹配，堆叠条的总金额相同为 30,000 加元。只读总数会掩盖不同的成分。将 30,000 加元和 12,000 加元添加为单独的家庭资产，会将既得部分计算两次。渐进的时间表并不是在每个服务日期都提前 将已完成的服务更改为三年。默认悬崖规则现在授予所有 600 个单位，按输入价格计算的总价值为 30,000 加元。五年渐进规则仅授予五分之三，即 360 个单位，总价值为 18,000 加元。与第二年的比较相比，顺序发生了逆转。五年结束后，两个附表均已归属所有单位且其分类值一致。渐进式时间表的早期优势并不意味着它在每个日期都优越。这种比较在保持赠款和价格固定的同时隔离了行权机制。它不会比较工资、未来奖励、工作满意度、就业风险或其他工作机会的价值。即将到来的一个里程碑只是换工作计划的一个输入，而不是留下或离开的完整理由。归属百分比和股价改变不同数量保留默认的两年服务日期，并将估值价格从 50 加元降低至 30 加元。渐进时间表仍归属 40% 的奖励，仍对应 240 个归属单位。它们的总名义价值从 12,000 加元降至 7,200 加元。整个奖项的价值从 30,000 加元降至 18,000 加元。其未归属部分从 18,000 加元降至 10,800 加元。所有美元价值均随所选价格变化，而单位数量和既得分数保持不变。价格输入是压力假设，而不是对雇主股票在未来日期的交易价格的预测。该矩阵在各个日期使用相同的固定价格来隔离时间表差异。这并不意味着股价将随着时间的推移保持不变。在不发明现金交易的情况下调节既得总价值 对于第二年的逐步计划，瀑布从总价值 30,000 加元的整体奖励开始，并减去与未归属单位相关的 18,000 加元。终点是与既得单位相关的 12,000 加元。这是一个分类桥。这并不意味着 30,000 加元存入银行账户，然后收取 18,000 加元作为罚款。模型中没有发生销售、交付或现金收据。潜在的没收必须根据实际裁决的终止和其他规定来评估。计算保留小数单位，其中所选奖励大小未均匀划分为所选年度部分。这保留了规定的百分比计算。实际的舍入、全股交付或现金替代处理可能有所不同，并且必须来自奖励条款。归属、交付和可用现金需要单独的日期 美国政府道德办公室的 RSU 定义将赠款与后来的股票或现金分配区分开来，并指出根据某些计划，分配可能会推迟。这里引用它是为了该文书的区别，而不是为了任何人的披露义务。即使实际奖励归属，家庭仍需要确认交付的内容、结算日期、任何预扣以及是否允许出售。因此，既得单位的总名义价值并不自动成为可支出的金额。该计算器不包括税收计算、工资预扣、销售成本、交易限制或货币兑换。它还没有增加新的赠款、股息或股息等价物。输入更高的价格无法解决这些单独的问题或在实际可用之前提供现金。使用矩阵揭示里程碑假设 该矩阵会更改已完成的服务年限以及等额年度部分完全归属的年数。每个单元格使用相同的奖励金额和输入的价格来评估剩余的未归属单位。悬崖里程碑不属于这种渐进式的比较。零单元意味着所有单位都已归属于该数学时间表。它并没有确定股票是否已交付、出售是否可以及时结算或收益是否可以实现目标。正单元格是仍附加于未归属单位的总价值，而不是概率加权损失。确认奖励类型和原始单位数量。阅读每个归属里程碑以及服务或绩效条件。检查相关出发情况下会发生什么情况。分别记录交付、扣留和允许销售的时间。仅根据立即付款计算经独立验证的可用现金。与雇主挂钩的薪酬还可以将工作收入和投资风险集中在同一家公司。另一篇关于雇主集中的文章使用现有既得、可出售的股份来测试联合风险。在连接这两个练习时，保持或有奖励的不同。

14709e48e053319d608646e61332a06ad9df8a5c.src: A population unemployment rate describes a group, not your personal chance of losing income. Build the cash plan from the household’s available money, expenses and verified continuing receipts. Keep the year and survey population beside the headline The first two graphics use Statistics Canada’s 2025 annual Labour Force Survey estimates for Canada, excluding the territories, age 15 years and over, Total - Gender. They are a dated annual snapshot rather than the latest monthly release. The selected population estimate is 34,569.4 thousand. It comprises 21,028.7 thousand employed people, 1,538.9 thousand unemployed people and 12,001.8 thousand outside the labour force. The source reports counts in thousands to one decimal; these are survey estimates, not exact counts of unique people holding one status throughout the year. The donut’s percentages use the entire illustrated population estimate. The headline unemployment rate uses a different denominator, which is why the unemployment slice and the published unemployment-rate bar do not show the same percentage. Read the denominator before comparing the percentages The Bank of Canada’s labour-market definitions describes the unemployment rate as unemployed people divided by the labour force, and participation as the labour force divided by the population age 15 and over. The labour force combines employed and unemployed people. In the selected snapshot, the labour force is 22,567.6 thousand and the published unemployment rate is 6.8%. Dividing unemployed people by the whole survey population instead gives about 4.5%. That latter percentage is the population share represented in the donut, not the official unemployment rate. The rate chart also shows the published 65.3% participation rate and 60.8% employment rate. Employment uses the population age 15 and over as its denominator. These three rates are different ratios, so adding them would not produce a meaningful population total. A group estimate does not supply an individual job-loss probability Statistics Canada’s LFS overview explains that the survey measures the labour market monthly using a sample. It includes people who work and people who do not, helping describe participation as well as employment. The annual group figures shown here do not follow a currently employed individual through a future transition or estimate how long that person would be without income. Turning the 6.8% annual rate into an individual job-loss probability would require a separate model and information not supplied by these charts. The cash scenario therefore does not multiply the household’s expenses by 6.8% or give that percentage to any path. The observed statistics remain fixed when the household inputs change. The two parts of the article serve different planning purposes. Start the personal scenario with net cash and actual commitments The default hypothetical household has CAD 12,000 set aside, CAD 3,000 of monthly cash expenses and CAD 1,000 of continuing or independently verified replacement net receipts. The monthly net cash balance is negative CAD 2,000. The funding position is starting reserve + months × (continuing net receipts − expenses) . At six months it reaches zero. After twelve months, the arithmetic position is negative CAD 12,000, identifying an unmet funding amount if those assumptions continue. The negative line is not an actual overdraft balance or permission to keep paying bills without money. It displays the amount missing from the selected resources. The model also assumes receipts arrive every month without a waiting period; it makes no Employment Insurance calculation or promise of replacement income. Stress the expense gap separately from the national statistic The line comparison holds opening cash and expenses fixed while changing the continuing net receipt assumption. The matrix replaces monthly expenses and receipts, then asks how much extra initial cash would be needed to cover twelve modeled monthly endpoints beyond the entered reserve. Its formula is the greater of zero and twelve times the expense gap minus the reserve . With CAD 3,000 of expenses, CAD 1,000 of continuing receipts and CAD 12,000 already available, the additional amount is CAD 12,000. A lower expense or higher supported receipt reduces that amount. A zero cell means the specified resources fund this particular monthly scenario. It does not measure the chance of unemployment, establish a benefit entitlement or certify that a reserve is sufficient for every other household risk. Turn the scenario into a dated plan when decisions depend on it Use supported net amounts for any continuing pay, other household income or replacement arrangement. Check when each receipt starts, what conditions apply and when it ends. A twelve-month constant amount is a teaching assumption that may need a more detailed calendar. Likewise, include the expenses that continue during the interruption and distinguish them from costs that actually stop. Monthly totals alone cannot prove that an early bill will be covered by a later payday. The job-loss guide adds settlement and receipt timing to that problem. The labour-market data can provide context for a planning conversation. The household’s own cash amounts and dates are what make its contingency plan concrete.
14709e48e053319d608646e61332a06ad9df8a5c.zh: 人口失业率描述的是一个群体，而不是你个人失去收入的可能性。根据家庭的可用资金、支出和经核实的持续收入制定现金计划。将年份和调查人口放在标题旁边 前两张图表使用加拿大统计局对加拿大 2025 年年度劳动力调查的估计，不包括地区、年龄 15 岁及以上、总计 - 性别。它们是带有日期的年度快照，而不是最新的月度版本。选定的人口估计为34,569.4 千。其中就业人员2102.87万人，失业人员153.89万人，非劳动力人口1200.18万人。源报告的计数单位是千到小数点后一位；这些是调查估计值，而不是全年拥有某种身份的独特人数的准确计数。甜甜圈的百分比使用了整个图示的人口估计值。总体失业率使用不同的分母，这就是为什么失业率切片和公布的失业率条形图显示的百分比不同的原因。比较百分比之前先读一下分母加拿大央行的劳动力市场定义将失业率描述为失业人数除以劳动力，将参与率描述为劳动力除以 15 岁及以上人口。劳动力包括就业人口和失业人口。在选定的快照中，劳动力为 22,567,600 人，公布的失业率为 6.8%。相反，用失业人数除以整个调查人口得出的结果约为 4.5%。后一个百分比是甜甜圈中代表的人口比例，而不是官方失业率。比率图还显示已公布的 65.3% 的参与率和 60.8% 的就业率。就业以 15 岁及以上人口作为分母。这三个比率是不同的比率，因此将它们相加不会产生有意义的人口总数。团体估计并不能提供个人失业概率加拿大统计局的 LFS 概述解释说，该调查使用样本每月衡量劳动力市场。它包括工作的人和不工作的人，有助于描述参与和就业。此处显示的年度团体数据并未跟踪当前受雇个人的未来过渡情况，也不会估计该人没有收入的时间。将 6.8% 的年增长率转化为个人失业概率需要一个单独的模型和这些图表未提供的信息。因此，现金方案不会将家庭支出乘以 6.8%，也不会将该百分比赋予任何路径。当家庭投入发生变化时，观察到的统计数据保持不变。本文的两部分服务于不同的规划目的。以净现金和实际承诺开始个人方案 默认假设家庭已预留 12,000 加元、每月现金支出 3,000 加元以及持续或独立验证的替代净收入 1,000 加元。每月净现金余额为负 2,000 加元。资金头寸为起始准备金+月数×（持续净收入-支出）。六个月时它达到零。十二个月后，算术头寸为负 12,000 加元，如果这些假设继续下去，则确定未满足的资金金额。负线不是实际的透支余额或允许在没有钱的情况下继续支付账单。它显示所选资源中缺失的数量。该模型还假设收据每月都会到达，无需等待期；它不进行就业保险计算或替代收入承诺。与国家统计数据分开强调费用缺口。直线比较保持期初现金和费用固定，同时改变持续净收入假设。该矩阵替换了每月的支出和收入，然后询问需要多少额外的初始现金来覆盖超出输入准备金的十二个建模每月端点。其公式是费用缺口减去准备金的零和十二倍中的较大者。加上 3,000 加元的费用、1,000 加元的持续收据和 12,000 加元的可用金额，额外金额为 12,000 加元。较低的费用或较高的支持收据会减少该金额。零单元格意味着指定的资源为该特定的每月方案提供资金。它不衡量失业的可能性，建立福利权利或证明储备金足以应对所有其他家庭风险。当决策依赖于该情景时，将其转变为过时的计划 使用支持的净额来支付任何持续工资、其他家庭收入或替代安排。检查每张收据的开始时间、适用条件以及结束时间。十二个月的恒定金额是一个教学假设，可能需要更详细的日历。同样，包括在中断期间继续发生的费用，并将其与实际停止的成本区分开来。仅每月总计并不能证明提前的账单可以由较晚的发薪日支付。失业指南为这个问题增加了结算和接收时间。劳动力市场数据可以为规划对话提供背景。该家庭自己的现金数额和日期是其应急计划的具体内容。

b36a585b45b46d9e7667f9f549f07a6522a5a5d6.src: A sensitivity ranking depends on the input ranges you test. Changing one assumption at a time does not describe every joint outcome or assign probabilities to the results. Choose the planning question before ranking the inputs A projection can display a future balance to the nearest cent while its price, saving and return assumptions remain uncertain. Extra decimal places do not make those assumptions more reliable. A useful next step is to ask how the result changes when a specific assumption moves over a stated range. This illustration asks about a signed funding gap : the project bill at the payment date less the savings available then. A positive gap means the modeled bill is not fully funded; a negative gap means savings exceed it. That output combines the cost of the goal with the assets intended to fund it, rather than focusing on the investment balance alone. The default project costs CAD 50,000 today and grows at an assumed 4% annually for five years. Starting savings are CAD 10,000, with CAD 500 deposited at each month-end and a constant assumed 3% effective annual return. The future bill is about CAD 60,832.65, savings about CAD 43,883.22, and the gap about CAD 16,949.42. Read the tornado chart as a set of one-input experiments Each row changes one assumption while holding every other baseline input fixed. The tested quote is 20% lower or higher by default. Monthly deposits are 25% lower or higher. Savings return and project-price growth move two percentage points either side, subject to their stated bounds. The deadline moves one year earlier or later, within one to fifteen years. The first chart expresses every result in the same output unit: CAD change from the baseline gap. Its pale bar connects the two tested changes. A filled marker identifies the lower input, and an open marker the higher input.
