Test the bill dates and rates, then plan the debt repayment The matrix replaces the borrowing rate and the bill spacing while holding project size, cash yield and draw fee selected. Later bills leave more borrowed money idle under the immediate schedule. A larger borrowing-rate margin over the cash rate increases that carrying-cost difference, while extra draw fees can offset it. The cells are alternative calculations, not forecasts of rates or approval. An entered cash rate above the borrowing rate can even produce negative net carrying cost for the immediate schedule. That is a mathematical consequence of the assumptions, rather than evidence that such an arrangement is available, permitted or attractive after tax and other costs. The final planning task remains principal repayment. The calculation stops after twelve months with the project paid and its debt outstanding. It does not assume a home sale, refinancing, future income increase or another loan will clear that balance. Keep the draw calendar, monthly carrying budget and eventual repayment source together. A lower first-year financing cost can improve the cash plan while leaving the same long-term debt obligation.
e1ede24fede12b8aa760a33a5876448da1153d15.zh: 借来的现金伴随着相应的债务。将提款与账单保持一致可以改变持有成本，但未提款限额是一种不同的资源，最终的项目债务仍然需要偿还。将批准的限额、借款交易和项目账单分开 在所有账单到期之前，就可以清楚地了解项目预算。全额借款会立即在账户中产生现金，但也会立即产生债务。仅在账单到期时才提取，可以减少较早的未偿债务，前提是根据实际安排，后来的提取仍然可用。加拿大金融消费者机构的信用额度解释将信用限额与借入的资金区分开来，并解释说利息适用于提取的金额。它还确定了可能的费用以及在不减少本金的情况下支付利息的后果。这些一般机制为本图提供了背景。该模型比较假设设施的两个时间表，而不是两个实际的贷款报价。每个项目都为同一个项目提供 60,000 加元的资金。现在一张可以提取6万加元；另一个则为三张钞票每张提取 20,000 加元。每张账单的批准、持续访问和支付都是假设，需要在实际计划中提供单独的证据。将三份账单放在一年内的明确时间点。默认账单在第三、第六和第九个月的月初到达。因此，前两个月的周期在第一个账单之前就已经过去了。更改间距会将所有三个日期移到一起，同时保持它们的数量相等。最终帐单以四个间隔在十二月初提交。即时开奖时间表全年欠款 60,000 加元。第一张账单时，其借入的项目现金降至 40,000 加元，第二张账单为 20,000 加元，第三张账单为零。向承包商付款使用的是现金；它不偿还贷款人。分阶段时间表在前两个月不欠任何款项，第三个月至第五个月为 20,000 加元，第六至第八个月为 40,000 加元，第九至十二个月为 60,000 加元。每次抽奖都会直接进入相关账单。因此，两个时间表的项目支出相同，所欠本金相同。对实际未偿债务收取利息 默认年度借款投入为 8%，十二分之一适用于每个月。即时计划每月支付 400 加元的利息，十二个月内支付 4,800 加元的利息。分阶段时间表为其较小的早期余额支付利息，并在同一期限内支付 2,800 加元。这是一次刻意统一的每月例会。 FCAC 描述了从提款到还款的利息；实际协议可能会每天计算并应用可变利率。该插图保持其固定的费率，并且没有声称每个实际日历月具有相同的天数。所有借款利息均由单独的家庭现金支付。它不会添加到本金中，也不会通过另一笔提款来提供资金，也不会从指定用于票据的现金中扣除。这使得整个项目都能在两个时间表中得到资助，但这也意味着家庭需要另一个预算额度来支付每月的付款。如果将项目贷款计算为足以支付账单和单独的利息支付，则会夸大所提供的资金。计入未使用的借入现金的利息，无需计算两次。即时计划在项目需要借入资金之前保留借入资金。按照假设的年度现金利息投入 2%，其未使用的项目现金在模型年可赚取 500 加元。利息将单独支付给家庭现金，不会复利或用于改变项目的账单金额。现金池包含两个月期 60,000 加元、三个月期 40,000 加元、三个月期 20,000 加元。将这些余额乘以期间和每月现金利率即可得到 500 加元。分阶段的时间表没有闲置的项目现金，因为每次抽签都会立即支付账单。收入抵消了部分即时计划的借贷成本，但并没有将借来的本金转化为新的家庭财富。首次提取时，60,000 加元的现金和 60,000 加元的债务同时产生。该模型也没有假设项目支出创造了物有所值的资产。任何市场价值、转售收益或税收待遇都需要自己的证据。在描述净节省额之前核对费用 假设每笔正数提取费用为 50 加元，并用家庭现金支付。即时时间表的一项费用为 50 加元。分阶段时间表的三项费用总计为 150 加元。这些是输入的假设，而不是对常见贷款机构定价的主张。因此，当前时间表的净账面成本为 4,800 加元的借款利息加上 50 加元的费用，减去 500 加元的现金利息，即 4,350 加元。分阶段安排的费用为 2,800 加元加 150 加元，即 2,950 加元。在默认输入下，分阶段成本减去直接成本为负 1,400 加元。瀑布调和了符号差异。它添加阶段性利息和费用，减去即时计划的利息和费用，然后加回已从即时成本中扣除的收入。最后一个迹象很重要：忽略收入会夸大分阶段时间表的优势。比较中没有额外的本金扣除，因为两种选择中都存在相同的 60,000 加元债务。测试账单日期和利率，然后计划债务偿还。矩阵替换借款利率和账单间隔，同时保持选定的项目规模、现金收益率和提款费用。稍后的账单使更多借来的资金在当前时间表下闲置。与现金利率相比较大的借款利率差额会增加持有成本差异，而额外的提取费用可以抵消它。这些单元格是替代计算，而不是利率或批准的预测。输入的现金利率高于借款利率甚至可能会在当前进度中产生负的净账面成本。这是假设的数学结果，而不是证明这种安排在税后和其他成本后可用、允许或有吸引力的证据。最终的规划任务仍然是本金偿还。十二个月后，项目已付清且债务未清，计算停止。它并不假设房屋销售、再融资、未来收入增加或其他贷款将清除该余额。将抽奖日历、每月持有预算和最终还款来源放在一起。较低的第一年融资成本可以改善现金计划，同时保留相同的长期债务义务。

a8812c28ca1094b8a2b2ef6b0c3f7ee725b3fe35.zh: 与通胀挂钩的债券现金流

1d5aad82e047fdc6e5cfa127fdf67532dd99b7de.src: A reported loss ranking can identify serious patterns. It cannot supply your personal chance of being defrauded, the typical loss of a household, or a guarantee that money will be recovered. Start with the reporting system and the reference year A financial-safety plan benefits from evidence about fraud, but a headline must be matched to the question it can answer. A reported dollar loss describes a financial amount. A report count describes entries received by a reporting system. Neither is automatically a probability for one person receiving a suspicious message. The Canadian Anti-Fraud Centre’s 2025 top-ten page reports more than CAD 704 million of losses and over 112,000 reports across its system. Its category tables are the controlling source for the charts here. The page was issued and modified on 25 February 2026; the observations concern calendar 2025. The display control selects between three and ten categories from the published dollar-loss ranking. It does not change any observation or construct a household scenario. Five categories appear in the original view. The count chart keeps their dollar-loss order so that the reader can compare the same rows, while the derived-ratio chart deliberately uses its own ordering. These are administrative reported observations, not a representative sample of every Canadian household or every encounter with a scam. The charts provide neither a population exposure count nor the total number of unreported incidents. A denominator needed for a personal victimization probability is absent. Keep the loss amount, report count and victim count separate The first chart ranks selected categories by reported dollar amount. The grouped chart places the source’s report and victim columns beside each other. Different quantities can move differently: a category with fewer listed reports can still have substantial financial losses. Do not add report counts and victim counts together. They describe different units. Nor does a category table establish that every listed victim is a distinct person across all categories, that every report concerns one household, or that the counts represent the number of people who encountered an attempt. The control preserves a common set of categories across all three charts. Expanding to ten reveals more of the source’s loss ranking; it does not turn the selection into the entire reporting system. The selection is by dollar loss, so it should not be presented as the ten most frequent categories or as a ranking of how likely one household is to encounter each type. The first two bar charts begin their magnitude axes at zero. Their different units remain explicit. A long dollar-loss bar and a short count bar cannot be divided visually to obtain a precise rate; the derived calculation needs the actual values and a stated denominator. A loss-per-count ratio is an average of reported aggregates The third chart divides each rounded category loss by its listed victim count. It then rounds the result to the nearest CAD 100. That additional rounding avoids showing cents of precision unsupported by a source that publishes losses in rounded millions. The calculation changes the question from total reported financial scale to reported loss per listed victim count. It can therefore change the category order. That is an arithmetic consequence of choosing another denominator, rather than a contradiction between charts. The result is not a median, a typical household outcome or the cost a particular person should expect. A small number of very large losses can influence an aggregate ratio, and the table does not supply the individual loss distribution needed to inspect that effect. It also supplies no uncertainty interval for the displayed comparison. Reported aggregates should not be treated as independent, identically exposed household observations. Reporting behaviour, category definitions and the underlying incidents can differ. The ratio is useful as a clearly named descriptive calculation, with those limitations retained, rather than as an actuarial price for an individual’s risk. Preserve unavailable amounts and lower-bound headlines The source also publishes a separate frequency table containing N/A dollar-loss entries. An unavailable amount is not the number zero. It should not become a zero-height loss bar, a claim that no harm occurred, or a zero average obtained by dividing it by a count. This article therefore uses the source’s dollar-loss ranking for the selected loss comparisons and preserves the unavailable entries in its source extract. It does not merge the two top-ten selections into a single invented population. The all-category loss headline says more than a stated amount. It is not an exact total with which to calculate exact category shares. Rounded category amounts add another precision limit. The article avoids a pie chart or an exact percentage of all national losses. The Competition Bureau’s March 2026 release describes substantial underreporting. That makes the reporting-system boundary material. It does not justify multiplying every category by one assumed reporting factor or converting the published totals into a new national-loss estimate. Such a calculation would require defensible assumptions about which incidents are missing and how their losses differ. Use the evidence to review a payment process A household can use the patterns as a reason to examine how unusual requests reach its money. The practical record might identify who can approve a large transfer, how an unexpected caller is verified, and which independently obtained contact details are used to check a request. CAFC’s fraud-investigator guidance explains that criminals may impersonate trusted investigators or financial institutions. Verify an unexpected request through a channel you obtain independently, rather than treating a caller’s claimed role or displayed number as proof. The relevant question is whether the request has been authenticated before money or account access is supplied. CAFC’s investment-fraud guidance also supports checking a proposed investment and the people offering it. A polished page, a persuasive introduction or an apparent account balance does not itself verify an opportunity. Use the current official guidance linked below when a specific proposal needs checking; these charts do not assess an actual person or product. The controls and reserves in a financial plan have separate roles. Access to an emergency account can help meet legitimate bills after a disruption, but it does not validate a request to move money. Keeping another account balance on a chart is not evidence that a suspicious transfer can safely be made. Keep reporting, recovery and future planning distinct Reporting an incident helps establish a record; it does not promise recovery or determine reimbursement rights. The official CAFC page links to the reporting service and advises contacting local police when fraud or cybercrime is suspected. Use those official channels and retain relevant transaction records when an actual incident occurs. When planning after a loss, distinguish confirmed available money, disputed transactions and possible recoveries. An amount under investigation should not automatically be treated as cash for next month’s bills. Any reimbursement assumption needs its own support and payment date. Return to the dated source when updating the article. A later release, a partial-year update and an annual table can cover different windows or classifications. Do not splice them into a trend without first checking those definitions. A change in reported totals can reflect reporting as well as the underlying harm. The useful output of these charts is a better set of questions: which unit is being counted, which incidents are represented, how much rounding is present, and what action is supported by the evidence. Keeping those questions visible makes the statistics relevant to a household safety process without pretending they predict one person’s outcome.
1d5aad82e047fdc6e5cfa127fdf67532dd99b7de.zh: 报告的损失排名可以识别严重的模式。它不能提供您个人被诈骗的机会、家庭的典型损失，也不能保证钱会被追回。从报告系统和参考年开始财务安全计划受益于有关欺诈的证据，但标题必须与其可以回答的问题相匹配。报告的美元损失描述的是财务金额。报告计数描述了报告系统接收到的条目。一个人收到可疑消息的概率也不是自动的。加拿大反欺诈中心 2025 年排名前十的页面报告了超过 7.04 亿加元的损失，整个系统收到了超过 112,000 份报告。它的类别表是此处图表的控制源。该页面于2026年2月25日发布并修改；观察结果涉及 2025 年日历。显示控件从已发布的美元损失排名中选择三到十个类别。它不会改变任何观察或构建家庭场景。原始视图中出现五个类别。计数图保留其美元损失顺序，以便读者可以比较相同的行，而派生比率图则故意使用自己的排序。这些是行政报告的观察结果，并不是每个加拿大家庭或每次遭遇骗局的代表性样本。这些图表既没有提供人口暴露计数，也没有提供未报告事件的总数。不存在个人受害概率所需的分母。将损失金额、报告计数和受害者计数分开 第一个图表按报告的美元金额对选定的类别进行排名。分组图表将来源的报告和受害者的列放在一起。不同的数量可能会有不同的变化：列出报告较少的类别仍然可能会造成巨大的财务损失。请勿将报告计数和受害者计数相加。它们描述了不同的单位。类别表也没有规定每一个列出的受害者都是所有类别中的一个独特的人，每份报告都涉及一个家庭，或者计数代表遭遇企图的人数。该控件在所有三个图表中保留一组通用的类别。扩展到 10 个可以揭示更多来源的损失排名；它不会将选择转化为整个报告系统。该选择是根据美元损失进行的，因此不应将其呈现为十个最常见的类别，也不应呈现为一个家庭遇到每种类型的可能性的排名。前两个条形图的幅值轴从零开始。它们的不同单位仍然很明确。长的美元损失柱和空的计数柱无法直观地分开以获得精确的汇率；导出的计算需要实际值和规定的分母。每计数损失比率是报告总数的平均值。第三个图表将每个四舍五入的类别损失除以其列出的受害者数量。然后，它将结果四舍五入到最接近的 100 加元。这种额外的四舍五入避免了显示不受发布单位数百万损失的来源支持的精确度。该计算将问题从报告的总财务规模转变为按列出的受害者人数报告的损失。因此，它可以更改类别顺序。这是选择另一个分母的算术结果，而不是图表之间的矛盾。结果不是中位数、典型的家庭结果或特定人应该预期的成本。少量非常大的损失可能会影响总比率，并且该表不提供检查该影响所需的个体损失分布。它还没有为显示的比较提供不确定性区间。报告的总量不应被视为独立的、相同暴露的家庭观察结果。报告行为、类别定义和潜在事件可能有所不同。该比率可用作明确命名的描述性计算，并保留这些限制，而不是作为个人风险的精算价格。保留不可用的金额和下限标题该消息来源还发布了一个单独的频率表，其中包含不适用的美元损失条目。不可用的金额不是数字零。它不应该成为零高度损失条，声称没有发生伤害，或者除以计数得到的零平均值。因此，本文使用源的美元损失排名来进行选定的损失比较，并在源摘录中保留不可用的条目。它不会将两个前十名的选择合并为一个发明群体。所有类别的损失标题所说明的不仅仅是规定的金额。它不是用于计算准确类别份额的准确总数。四舍五入的类别金额增加了另一个精度限制。这篇文章避免了饼图或所有国家损失的确切百分比。竞争局 2026 年 3 月发布的报告描述了严重的漏报情况。这使得报告系统成为边界材料。它并不能证明将每个类别乘以一个假定的报告系数或将公布的总数转换为新的国家损失估计是合理的。这样的计算需要对哪些事件被遗漏以及它们的损失有何不同做出合理的假设。使用证据审查付款流程 家庭可以使用这些模式作为理由来检查异常请求如何到达其资金。实际记录可能会确定谁可以批准大额转账、如何验证意外呼叫者以及使用哪些独立获得的联系方式来检查请求。 CAFC 的欺诈调查员指南解释说，犯罪分子可能冒充值得信赖的调查员或金融机构。通过您独立获取的渠道验证意外请求，而不是将呼叫者声称的角色或显示的号码视为证据。相关问题是在提供资金或帐户访问权限之前请求是否已经过身份验证。 CAFC 的投资欺诈指南还支持检查拟议的投资及其提供者。精美的页面、有说服力的介绍或明显的账户余额本身并不能证明机会。当需要检查特定提案时，请使用下面链接的当前官方指南；这些图表不评估真实的人或产品。财务计划中的控制和准备金具有不同的作用。使用紧急账户可以帮助在中断后满足合法账单，但它不能验证转移资金的请求。在图表上保留另一个账户余额并不能证明可以安全地进行可疑转账。保持报告、恢复和未来计划的明确性 报告事件有助于建立记录；它不承诺恢复或确定报销权利。 CAFC 官方页面链接到报告服务，并建议在怀疑存在欺诈或网络犯罪时联系当地警方。当实际事件发生时，请使用这些官方渠道并保留相关交易记录。在制定损失后计划时，区分已确认的可用资金、有争议的交易和可能的追偿。接受调查的金额不应自动视为下个月账单的现金。任何报销假设都需要其自己的支持和付款日期。更新文章时请返回注明日期的来源。后续版本、部分年度更新和年度表格可以涵盖不同的窗口或分类。在没有首先检查这些定义之前，不要将它们拼接成趋势。报告总数的变化可以反映报告情况以及潜在的危害。这些图表的有用输出是一组更好的问题：正在计算哪个单位、代表哪些事件、存在多少舍入以及证据支持哪些行动。保持这些问题的可见性使得统计数据与家庭安全过程相关，而不是假装它们预测了一个人的结果。

c22d1a93c2c79b0c5fd84fed5065357376f8531e.src: A negative income-group average describes an aggregate accounting result. It cannot tell you how many households are in deficit or prescribe a saving amount for one family. Start with the annual measure and its release vintage Statistics Canada’s average household net-saving chart , released on 13 April 2026, reports five annual observations for each of five income quintiles. The source is Table 36-10-0587-01 within the Distributions of Household Economic Accounts. The article preserves that release vintage rather than mixing revisions from different downloads. The chart’s unit is current Canadian dollars per household per year. It is not a percentage, thousands of dollars, total saving for an entire group or a quarterly amount. The default controls display 2025, compare it with 2021 and trace the middle income group through all five years. These are national-accounts estimates distributed across household groups. They are not the answers to a survey question asking how much each respondent transferred into a savings account. The separate aggregate-saving-rate article explains the accounting distinction and its pension-entitlement adjustment. Read the sign before comparing the sizes For 2025, the source reports average annual net saving of −CAD 38,907 for the lowest income quintile, −CAD 19,944 for the second and −CAD 10,092 for the middle group. The fourth group is positive CAD 18,912 and the highest is positive CAD 75,469. The signed bars retain both sides of zero. A negative mean is net dissaving on the source’s definition. It is not a negative bank-account balance, a household’s end-of-year net worth or a statement that every member of the group had the same result. The highest-minus-lowest difference is CAD 75,469 − (−CAD 38,907) = CAD 114,376 . That subtracts two group means. It is not the income cutoff separating those quintiles, an amount owed between groups or a recommended annual saving target. An improving figure can remain below zero The difference chart subtracts the reference-year mean from the selected-year mean for each group. With 2021 as the reference and 2025 selected, the lowest group moves from −CAD 24,400 to −CAD 38,907, a difference of −CAD 14,507. The highest moves from CAD 59,395 to CAD 75,469, a positive difference of CAD 16,074. Try changing the reference year to 2024. The middle group then moves from −CAD 10,387 to −CAD 10,092, an improvement of CAD 295. Its level is still negative. Calling every negative mean a worsening result would miss this distinction. The controls allow either year to serve as the reference. Comparing a selected earlier year with a later reference reverses the subtraction. Selecting the same year twice produces zero in the change chart, while the level chart continues to show the actual group means for that year. Use a history and a matrix for different reading tasks The line follows the selected group’s five annual means from 2021 through 2025, with an explicit zero comparison. It helps distinguish the direction of a change from the sign of the level. Exact calendar years and values remain in the data table. The matrix displays three fixed snapshots—2021, 2023 and 2025—for all five groups. Its signed labels remain visible alongside the colour encoding. It supplies context when the controls focus on a different year or a single group. Neither visual follows the same individual families over time. A household can move between income groups, and the composition of each group can change. A line connecting group averages therefore cannot establish how the finances of one unchanged set of households evolved. Three negative group means do not establish that 60% of households are in deficit A mean summarizes the sum divided by the number of observations. It does not preserve the count on either side of zero. Knowing that three income-group means are negative is insufficient to determine how many individual households have negative net saving. Consider two original mathematical examples, separate from the official data. Set A contains five annual amounts: −500, −500, −500, −500 and +1,500. Their sum is −500 and their mean is −100. Four of the five values are negative. Set B contains −4,000, +875, +875, +875 and +875. Its sum is also −500 and its mean is also −100. Only one value is negative. The identical mean coexists with negative shares of 80% and 20% in these invented sets. The official chart does not supply the within-group observations needed to recover such shares. It also does not supply medians or the spread of individual outcomes. Do not turn a group mean into a claim about a typical family or a precise prevalence of financial difficulty. Keep the income grouping separate from wealth and liquidity An income group and a wealth group classify different quantities. The associated DHEA release discusses both, but the net-saving chart here uses income quintiles. Its labels cannot be silently replaced with “poorest” and “richest” by net worth. A household with substantial existing assets can have a low-income year. Another with strong current income may also have large debt payments or near-term obligations. The group chart does not identify those individual circumstances or reveal the money available for the next bill. The explorer supplies no income thresholds and does not assign the reader to a quintile. Choosing group three means “display the source’s third group,” rather than a determination that a particular salary, household size or bank balance belongs there. Use the estimates without treating them as a causal experiment Statistics Canada describes DHEA as combining macroeconomic accounts with distributional information. Some components use timely microdata or models; others rely on assumptions or information from earlier reference periods. The release also notes revisions to prior estimates. The annual values shown here are nominal. A change between 2021 and 2025 has not been adjusted for price inflation. The charts contain no confidence intervals or significance tests, and the subtraction does not establish which policy, price, job event or spending decision caused the difference. Lower-income pressure and wider differences between group means are useful economic context. Assessing their causes requires more evidence than these 25 observations. Assessing one family’s funding capacity requires its actual receipts, obligations and payment dates. Use the group context to ask better household questions The source does not imply that every household can solve a negative cash plan by choosing a different saving percentage. It also does not establish that a positive group average makes a particular household’s goals adequately funded. For a personal plan, start with cash actually received, list required costs, separate debt principal from interest, reserve for predictable irregular bills and write each goal in dollars with a date. Then check whether the proposed contribution fits the remaining cash. Those steps use a separately defined household ledger, rather than importing a group mean as a payment instruction. Keep the statistical release date and the annual reference year beside any number reused elsewhere. The four charts show how outcomes differ across groups and time while preserving what the evidence cannot identify about an individual household.
c22d1a93c2c79b0c5fd84fed5065357376f8531e.zh: 负收入组平均数描述了总体会计结果。它无法告诉您有多少家庭处于赤字状态，也无法规定一个家庭的储蓄金额。从年度指标及其发布开始 加拿大统计局于 2026 年 4 月 13 日发布的平均家庭净储蓄图表报告了五个收入五分之一的五个年度观察结果。来源为家庭经济账户分布中的表 36-10-0587-01。本文保留了发布版本，而不是混合来自不同下载的版本。该图表的单位是每户每年的加元。它不是一个百分比、数千美元、整个团体的总储蓄或季度金额。默认控件显示 2025 年，将其与 2021 年进行比较，并跟踪所有五年的中等收入群体。这些是分布在各个家庭群体中的国民账户估计值。它们并不是询问每个受访者向储蓄账户转入多少钱的调查问题的答案。单独的总储蓄率文章解释了会计区别及其养老金权利调整。在比较规模之前先阅读标志。消息来源报告称，到 2025 年，收入最低的五分之一群体的平均年净节省为 -38,907 加元，第二个收入群体为 -19,944 加元，中间收入群体为 -10,092 加元。第四组为阳性18,912加元，最高为阳性75,469加元。带符号的条保留两侧为零。负均值是对源定义的净贬值。它不是银行账户负余额、家庭年终净资产，也不是群体中每个成员都有相同结果的声明。最高减最低差额为 CAD 75,469 − (−CAD 38,907) = CAD 114,376 。减去两组均值。它不是区分这五分位数的收入界限、各组之间的欠款额或建议的年度储蓄目标。改善的数字可以保持在零以下。差异图从每组的选定年份平均值中减去参考年平均值。以2021年为参考，选择2025年，最低组从-24,400加元移动到-38,907加元，相差-14,507加元。最高价格从 59,395 加元升至 75,469 加元，正差 16,074 加元。尝试将参考年更改为 2024 年。中间组则从 -10,387 加元变为 -10,092 加元，提高了 295 加元。其水平仍然为负。如果将每一个负面结果都称为恶化的结果，就会忽略这一区别。这些控件允许任一年份作为参考。将选定的较早年份与较晚参考年份进行比较会反转减法。选择同一年两次会在变化图表中产生零，而级别图继续显示该年的实际组均值。使用历史记录和矩阵来执行不同的阅读任务 该线遵循所选组从 2021 年到 2025 年的五个年度平均值，并进行明确的零比较。它有助于区分变化的方向和水平的符号。准确的日历年和值保留在数据表中。该矩阵显示了所有五个组的三个固定快照：2021 年、2023 年和 2025 年。其签名标签与颜色编码一起保持可见。当控件集中于不同年份或单个组时，它提供上下文。随着时间的推移，这两种视觉效果都遵循相同的个体家庭。一个家庭可以在收入群体之间流动，每个收入群体的构成也可以发生变化。因此，连接群体平均数的线无法确定一组不变的家庭的财务状况如何演变。三个负组均值并不能证明 60% 的家庭处于赤字状态。均值总结了总和除以观测值数量。它不保留零两侧的计数。知道三个收入组平均值为负不足以确定有多少个家庭的净储蓄为负。考虑两个原始的数学例子，与官方数据分开。 A 组包含五个年度金额：−500、−500、−500、−500 和 +1,500。它们的总和是 -500，平均值是 -100。五个值中有四个为负。集合B包含-4,000、+875、+875、+875和+875。它的总和也是 -500，平均值也是 -100。只有一个值为负数。在这些发明的集合中，相同的均值与 80% 和 20% 的负份额共存。官方图表并未提供恢复此类股票所需的集团内观察结果。它也不提供个体结果的中位数或分布。不要将群体均值转化为对典型家庭或经济困难的精确普遍程度的断言。将收入分组与财富和流动性分开 收入分组和财富分组对不同的数量进行分类。相关的 DHEA 版本讨论了两者，但此处的净储蓄图表使用收入五分位数。它的标签不能默默地被净资产取代为“最穷”和“最富有”。拥有大量现有资产的家庭可能会经历低收入年份。另一个当前收入强劲的人也可能有大量债务偿还或近期义务。集团图表没有识别这些个人情况，也没有透露下一张账单的可用资金。探索者不提供收入门槛，也不将读者分配到五分之一。选择第三组意味着“显示来源的第三组”，而不是确定特定的工资、家庭规模或银行余额属于该组。使用估计值，而不是将其视为因果实验 加拿大统计局将 DHEA 描述为将宏观经济账户与分配信息相结合。有些组件使用及时的微观数据或模型；另一些则依赖于早期参考期的假设或信息。该新闻稿还指出了对先前估计的修订。此处显示的年值是名义值。 2021 年至 2025 年之间的变化尚未根据价格通胀进行调整。这些图表不包含置信区间或显着性检验，并且减法不能确定是哪个政策、价格、工作事件或支出决策导致了差异。较低的收入压力和群体间更大的差异是有用的经济背景。评估其原因需要比这 25 项观察结果更多的证据。评估一个家庭的资金能力需要了解其实际收入、义务和付款日期。利用群体背景提出更好的家庭问题 该消息来源并不意味着每个家庭都可以通过选择不同的储蓄百分比来解决负现金计划。它还没有证明积极的群体平均数可以为特定家庭的目标提供充足的资金。对于个人计划，从实际收到的现金开始，列出所需的成本，将债务本金与利息分开，为可预测的不规则账单预留资金，并以美元写下每个目标并注明日期。然后检查提议的捐款是否适合剩余现金。这些步骤使用单独定义的家庭分类帐，而不是导入团体均值作为付款指令。将统计发布日期和年度参考年份保留在其他地方重复使用的任何数字旁边。这四个图表显示了结果在不同群体和时间之间的差异，同时保留了证据无法识别的关于单个家庭的信息。

eb11674788e2a4eba7a830b8989f0525faca409a.src: A survey’s population, definition and reference year belong beside the percentage. Use disability prevalence as context, then build an income-interruption cash plan from separate evidence. Ask what the percentage actually measures A statement that 27.0% of a covered population had a disability in 2022 does not mean that a currently employed person has a 27.0% chance of losing all income next year. Those statements have different outcomes, populations and time periods. Substituting one for the other can make a precise-looking financial projection answer the wrong question. Statistics Canada’s Table 1.1.A reports a 2022 disability prevalence estimate of 27.0% for its total aged-15+ population, compared with 22.3% in 2017. This guide uses selected all-gender age-group rows from that dated table. It is not a release of new 2026 observations, an insurance-claims dataset or a measure of the probability of a future earnings interruption. The first chart retains both survey years and the source’s published uncertainty. The later interactive example asks a separate arithmetic question about population composition. Its controls do not change the historical estimates. Keep the survey definition and coverage beside the numbers The 2022 Concepts and Methods Guide describes activity limitations connected with a long-term condition or health-related problem. Its framework considers the interaction between functional limitations and environmental barriers. That is a broader subject than a particular insurance contract’s definition of a payable claim. The methods guide describes coverage of people in private dwellings and exclusions including institutional and other collective dwellings, as well as First Nation reserves. Its sample frame was linked to the 2021 Census, with the stated age eligibility based on that census date. A headline label such as “Canadians” should not erase those coverage details. For a planning decision, the event needs its own definition: reduced hours, no earnings, additional support costs or a particular benefit becoming payable. A prevalence measure alone does not specify which of those events occurs, its start date, its duration or the money received during it. An age-group comparison is not an individual lifetime path The selected 2022 estimates are 20.1% for ages 15–24, 24.1% for ages 25–64 and 40.4% for ages 65+. The denominators differ by age group. These rows cannot be added together, and an unweighted average would assign each group equal population weight whether or not that matches the population being discussed. A comparison between people aged 25–64 and those aged 65+ also does not follow the same people into retirement. It does not reveal how many people newly developed a limitation during a year, how long it lasted or whether it interrupted paid work. Those transition questions require information beyond the displayed prevalence estimates. The 2024 analytical profile examines demographics, employment and income as distinct dimensions. Its scope is a reminder to keep the measured condition separate from a financial consequence that a household may need to model. Read the interval as uncertainty about the survey estimate The table gives the 2022 ages-25–64 estimate as 24.1%, with a published 95% confidence interval from 23.7% to 24.5%. For ages 65+, it gives 40.4%, with bounds of 39.6% and 41.3%. The whiskers preserve those asymmetric limits rather than replacing them with visually convenient equal margins. The survey’s data-quality chapter describes a complex sample design and bootstrap-based estimation of sampling error. This website copies the published intervals. It does not recalculate them as if every plotted percentage came from a simple unweighted sample with a known denominator. These intervals concern survey estimation uncertainty. They are not a range of outcomes for one person’s future health or income. They also do not make coverage exclusions or other non-sampling errors disappear. Testing a difference requires the appropriate comparison evidence; it cannot be replaced with a visual judgment about whether two separate intervals overlap. A percentage-point change and a percentage increase use different arithmetic For ages 15–24, the published levels rise from 13.1% to 20.1%. Subtracting them gives an increase of 7.0 percentage points . Dividing that 7.0-point difference by the starting 13.1% gives a relative increase of about 53.44% . Both describe the same two published levels, with different scales and denominators. Neither result is a yearly probability of developing a disability. The five-year gap between survey dates is not permission to divide a prevalence change by five and label it an annual incidence rate. The displayed age-group populations can change between surveys, and prevalence combines more than the arrival of new cases. The change chart therefore uses an explicit percentage-point unit. Statistics Canada flags the three selected age-group year comparisons as significantly different at p < 0.05 in this table. No confidence interval for each difference is supplied here, and none is manufactured by subtracting the separate estimate bounds. Change the population mix while holding subgroup estimates fixed The interactive illustration contains only two groups: ages 25–64 and ages 65+. It is an invented ages-25+ population, excluding youth. The subgroup estimates remain fixed at the published 2022 values of 24.1% and 40.4%. Only the population weights change. Population A assigns an invented 20% weight to ages 65+ and 80% to ages 25–64. Its weighted aggregate is 80% × 24.1% + 20% × 40.4% = 27.36% . Population B uses a 40% older share and a 60% working-age share, giving 30.62% . The 3.26-point difference arises entirely from the chosen weights while both subgroup estimates remain unchanged. These are not observed Canadian age shares, a reconstruction of the national aged-15+ result or an official age-standardization calculation. Nor do they decompose the actual change from 2017 to 2022. The contribution bars explain a weighted mean; the sensitivity line shows every invented older share from zero to 100%. No aggregate confidence interval is inferred by averaging subgroup bounds. Translate a defined income interruption into cash separately A household cash stress needs amounts and dates. For example, assume essential spending of CAD 4,000 a month, other continuing net receipts of CAD 1,500, and three months before any additional receipt is available. The conditional funding need is CAD 2,500 a month, or CAD 7,500 over that assumed window, before considering the starting reserve. That calculation describes the cash consequence if the assumed interruption occurs. The survey prevalence percentages do not supply its event probability, establish benefit eligibility or identify the payment date. A complete plan needs the household’s actual budget, accessible funds and applicable benefit or contract details. Record the statistic’s population, definition and reference date. Keep prevalence, new-event incidence and a future transition probability distinct. Inspect subgroup weights and published uncertainty before interpreting an aggregate. Define the household event and its cash consequences using separate evidence. The related waiting-period and joint-income tools provide separate hypothetical cash scenarios. They do not convert this survey extract into a personal probability estimate.
eb11674788e2a4eba7a830b8989f0525faca409a.zh: 调查的人口、定义和参考年份不属于百分比范围。以残疾患病率作为背景，然后根据单独的证据制定收入中断现金计划。询问百分比的实际衡量标准 2022 年 27.0% 的覆盖人口患有残疾的说法并不意味着当前就业人员明年有 27.0% 的机会失去所有收入。这些陈述有不同的结果、人群和时间段。用其中一种替代另一种可能会使看似精确的财务预测回答了错误的问题。加拿大统计局的表 1.1.A 报告称，2022 年 15 岁以上总人口的残疾患病率估计为 27.0%，而 2017 年为 22.3%。本指南使用了该日期表中选定的所有性别年龄组行。它不是发布 2026 年新的观察结果、保险索赔数据集或衡量未来收入中断概率的指标。第一张图表保留了调查年份和来源公布的不确定性。后面的交互式示例提出了一个有关人口构成的单独算术问题。其控制措施不会改变历史估计。将调查定义和覆盖范围放在数字旁边。2022 年概念和方法指南描述了与长期状况或健康相关问题相关的活动限制。其框架考虑了功能限制和环境障碍之间的相互作用。这是一个比特定保险合同的应付索赔定义更广泛的主题。该方法指南描述了私人住宅中人员的覆盖范围和排除情况，包括机构和其他集体住宅以及原住民保护区。其样本框架与 2021 年人口普查相关，规定的年龄资格基于该人口普查日期。 “加拿大人”等标题标签不应删除这些报道细节。对于规划决策，活动需要有自己的定义：减少时间、没有收入、额外的支持成本或应付的特定福利。单独的流行度衡量标准并不能具体说明哪些事件发生、其开始日期、持续时间或期间收到的资金。年龄组比较并不是个人的一生路径 选定的 2022 年估计值是 15-24 岁年龄组为 20.1%，25-64 岁年龄组为 24.1%，65 岁以上年龄组为 40.4%。分母因年龄组而异。这些行无法加在一起，并且未加权平均值将为每个组分配相同的总体权重，无论其是否与正在讨论的总体相匹配。 25-64 岁的人和 65 岁以上的人之间的比较也不能说明同一个人的退休情况。它没有透露一年中有多少人新出现了这种限制，这种限制持续了多长时间，或者是否中断了有偿工作。这些转变问题需要超出显示的患病率估计值的信息。 2024 年分析概况将人口统计、就业和收入作为不同的维度进行研究。其范围提醒人们将测量的状况与家庭可能需要建模的财务后果分开。将区间解读为调查估计的不确定性 该表给出的 2022 年 25-64 岁估计值为 24.1%，已发布的 95% 置信区间为 23.7% 至 24.5%。对于 65 岁以上的年龄，给出的结果是 40.4%，界限为 39.6% 和 41.3%。胡须保留了这些不对称的限制，而不是用视觉上方便的等边距代替它们。该调查的数据质量章节描述了复杂的样本设计和基于引导的抽样误差估计。本网站复制已发布的间隔。它不会重新计算它们，就好像每个绘制的百分比都来自具有已知分母的简单未加权样本。这些区间涉及调查估计的不确定性。它们不是一个人未来健康或收入的一系列结果。它们也不会使覆盖范围排除或其他非抽样错误消失。测试差异需要适当的比较证据；它不能用视觉判断两个单独的区间是否重叠来代替。 A percentage-point change and a percentage increase use different arithmetic For ages 15–24, the published levels rise from 13.1% to 20.1%.减去它们就增加了 7.0 个百分点。 Dividing that 7.0-point difference by the starting 13.1% gives a relative increase of about 53.44% .两者都描述了相同的两个已发布的级别，但具有不同的比例和分母。这两个结果都不是每年发生残疾的概率。调查日期之间的五年差距不允许将患病率变化除以五并将其标记为年发病率。显示的年龄组人口可能会在调查之间发生变化，而且患病率的组合比新病例的到来还要多。因此，变化图表使用明确的百分比单位。加拿大统计局在此表中将三个选定的年龄组年份比较标记为显着差异，p < 0.05。这里没有提供每个差异的置信区间，也没有通过减去单独的估计界限来产生置信区间。更改人口结构，同时保持子组估计值固定 交互式插图仅包含两个组：25-64 岁和 65 岁以上。这是一个虚构的 25 岁以上人口，不包括年轻人。分组估计值仍固定在已公布的 2022 年值 24.1% 和 40.4%。只有人口权重发生变化。 A 群体将 20% 的权重分配给 65 岁以上的年龄，将 80% 的权重分配给 25-64 岁的年龄。其加权合计为 80% × 24.1% + 20% × 40.4% = 27.36% 。人口 B 使用 40% 的老年人份额和 60% 的工作年龄份额，即 30.62% 。 3.26 点的差异完全是由所选择的权重引起的，而两个分组的估计值保持不变。这些不是观察到的加拿大年龄份额、全国 15 岁以上结果的重建或官方年龄标准化计算。它们也没有分解 2017 年到 2022 年的实际变化。贡献条形图解释了加权平均值；敏感度线显示了从 0 到 100% 的每个发明的旧份额。通过平均子组界限不会推断出聚合置信区间。 Translate a defined income interruption into cash separately A household cash stress needs amounts and dates.例如，假设每月基本支出为 4,000 加元，其他持续净收入为 1,500 加元，并且三个月后才能获得任何额外收入。有条件的资金需求为每月 2,500 加元，或者在考虑起始准备金之前，在假定窗口内需要 7,500 加元。 That calculation describes the cash consequence if the assumed interruption occurs.调查发生率百分比不提供其事件概率、确定福利资格或确定付款日期。完整的计划需要家庭的实际预算、可用资金和适用的福利或合同细节。记录统计数据的总体、定义和参考日期。保持患病率、新事件发生率和未来转变概率不同。在解释汇总之前检查子组权重和已发布的不确定性。使用单独的证据定义家庭事件及其现金后果。相关的等待期和联合收入工具提供了单独的假设现金情景。他们不会将此调查摘录转换为个人概率估计。

436d2f23cec846f6550d630467d02fa26924a359.src: The date tax leaves an investment can affect later compounding. Compare both cases after their remaining gain tax, and distinguish a larger tax bill from a smaller after-tax outcome. Begin with the same capital and an explicitly limited return assumption A tax-timing comparison can be distorted if one investment is shown before tax while another has already paid it. Start with the same resources, use consistent return assumptions and identify any tax still embedded in the ending market value before comparing the two outcomes. This example places CAD 100,000 in each of two non-registered capital-appreciation scenarios. Opening adjusted cost base is also CAD 100,000. There are no new contributions, distributions, withdrawals for spending, fees or losses. Both holdings receive the same constant 5% annual price appreciation. The independently selected tax assumption is 25% of each full dollar of realized gain. It is not a capital-gains inclusion rate or a personal marginal tax rate. The calculator neither combines those two concepts nor estimates a household’s actual tax. The assumption remains identical in both cases throughout the illustration. Follow tax paid from each annual sale before reinvesting The first case sells all its holdings at every year-end. It calculates that year’s gain relative to its current cost base, pays the assumed tax immediately from sale proceeds and reinvests the remainder. That reinvested amount becomes the new cost base for the following year. In year one, CAD 100,000 grows to CAD 105,000. The CAD 5,000 gain produces CAD 1,250 of modeled tax, leaving CAD 103,750 invested. No extra household money pays that tax outside the scenario. Year two therefore earns 5% on CAD 103,750, rather than on CAD 105,000. Its gain is CAD 5,187.50 and modeled tax is CAD 1,296.875 before rounding. The process continues for the selected horizon, with calculations retaining full precision. At the default ten years, the annual-sale case ends with approximately CAD 144,504.39 after all its modeled gain taxes. The tax-payment dates are an arithmetic convention, rather than actual withholding or filing deadlines. Deduct the accumulated gain tax from the final-sale case The other case makes no intervening sale and receives no distribution or other taxable event under the stated assumptions. Its cost base remains CAD 100,000. Market value compounds at the full selected price-appreciation rate until the final sale. After ten years, that market value is CAD 100,000 × 1.05 to the tenth power, or approximately CAD 162,889.46. Its remaining gain is CAD 62,889.46. Applying the same 25% assumption produces CAD 15,722.37 of modeled tax at liquidation. The after-tax endpoint is approximately CAD 147,167.10, rather than the entire CAD 162,889.46 market value. It exceeds the annual-sale endpoint by about CAD 2,662.70 under these specific assumptions. The waterfall taxes the gain, not the original capital. It adds gross appreciation to the initial cost and subtracts the modeled final tax once. The original principal is not subjected to that gain-tax fraction a second time. Explain why the larger tax payment does not reverse this comparison The annual-sale case earns approximately CAD 59,339.19 of cumulative gross appreciation on its changing invested balance. It pays approximately CAD 14,834.80 of modeled tax and retains CAD 44,504.39 of net growth. The final-sale case earns more gross appreciation because its earlier gains remain invested without the intervening tax outflows. Its CAD 62,889.46 gross increase produces the larger CAD 15,722.37 tax payment, while still leaving the larger after-tax endpoint. The grouped bars keep each case’s own gross growth, tax and net increase together. Within a row, net increase equals gross appreciation less modeled tax. Those three bars should not be added as separate sources of wealth. Comparing only cumulative tax dollars would miss the additional growth. Comparing only gross market values would miss the remaining liability. Tax also occurs at different dates, so a simple total of payments is not a present-value measure of their cost. Read intermediate liquidation values as valuations rather than repeated sales The line chart shows the annual-sale balance, the final-sale case’s gross market balance and that same final-sale case’s hypothetical after-tax liquidation value at each completed year. The last line asks what would remain if that position were sold at the indicated year. It does not pay all those intermediate hypothetical tax amounts and then pay them again at the selected finish. There is only one final sale in that scenario. The matrix changes the holding horizon and the tax fraction for both cases together, while keeping initial capital and appreciation selected. One year produces no timing difference because both cases sell at the same date. A zero tax assumption or zero appreciation also removes the modeled advantage. The cells do not assign probabilities to returns or identify a future tax rate. A longer horizon magnifies the effect of constant compounding in the illustration, while real returns, laws, cash needs and portfolio choices can change during that time. Keep actual taxable events and investment decisions outside the shortcut The CRA’s Capital Gains guide explains that a gain or loss usually arises when capital property is sold or considered sold. This article does not model deemed dispositions, reserves, exemptions or other special treatment. It uses the general gain concept with original hypothetical tax inputs. Holding a fund without selling its units does not establish that every return can remain untaxed until a final sale. The CRA’s mutual-fund guidance discusses distributions while a holding is owned, including reinvested amounts. Those events and their cost-base adjustments are deliberately absent here. Reconcile actual income categories, transactions, cost records and payment dates before estimating a real after-tax goal amount. Investment suitability, diversification, fees and the need to sell can matter independently of this timing effect. The comparison isolates one mechanism; it does not determine whether postponing a particular sale is appropriate.
436d2f23cec846f6550d630467d02fa26924a359.zh: 税收离开投资的日期可能会影响以后的复利。比较这两种情况在扣除剩余利得税后的情况，并区分较大的税单和较小的税后结果。从相同的资本和明确限制的回报假设开始 如果一项投资在税前显示，而另一项投资已经支付，则纳税时间比较可能会被扭曲。从相同的资源开始，使用一致的回报假设，并在比较两个结果之前确定仍包含在最终市场价值中的任何税收。此示例在两个非注册资本增值场景中各投入 100,000 加元。期初调整成本基数也是 100,000 加元。没有新的捐款、分配、支出提款、费用或损失。两种持股均获得相同的每年 5% 的恒定价格升值。独立选择的税收假设是每一美元已实现收益的 25%。它不是资本利得包含率或个人边际税率。该计算器既没有结合这两个概念，也没有估计家庭的实际税​​收。在整个插图中，这两种情况下的假设保持相同。再投资前跟踪每次年度出售所缴纳的税款 第一个案例在每年年底出售其所有持股。它计算当年相对于当前成本基础的收益，立即从销售收益中支付假定税款，并将剩余部分进行再投资。再投资金额成为下一年的新成本基础。第一年，100,000 加元增长到 105,000 加元。 5,000 加元的收益产生 1,250 加元的模型税，留下 103,750 加元的投资。在这种情况之外，没有额外的家庭资金可以缴纳该税款。因此，第二年的收入为 103,750 加元，而不是 105,000 加元，赚取 5%。其收益为 5,187.50 加元，四舍五入前的模型税额为 1,296.875 加元。该过程在选定的范围内继续进行，计算保持完全精确。在违约十年中，扣除所有建模利得税后，年度销售案例最终约为 144,504.39 加元。纳税日期是算术惯例，而不是实际的预扣或申报截止日期。从最终销售案例中扣除累计利得税 另一种情况在所述假设下没有进行中间销售，也没有收到分配或其他应税事件。其成本基础仍为 100,000 加元。市场价值以完全选定的价格升值率复合，直至最终出售。十年后，该市场价值为 100,000 加元 × 1.05 的十次方，即大约 162,889.46 加元。其剩余收益为 62,889.46 加元。应用同样的 25% 假设，清算时的模型税额为 15,722.37 加元。税后终点约为 147,167.10 加元，而不是整个 162,889.46 加元的市场价值。在这些特定假设下，它比年度销售终点高出约 2,662.70 加元。瀑布对收益征税，而不是原始资本。它将总增值添加到初始成本中，并减去建模的最终税金一次。原始本金不再需要再次缴纳该利得税。解释为什么较高的纳税额不会扭转这种比较。年度销售案例因其投资余额的变化而获得约 59,339.19 加元的累计总增值。它支付大约 14,834.80 加元的模型税，并保留 44,504.39 加元的净增长。最终销售案例获得了更多的总升值，因为其早期收益仍可用于投资，而无需干预税收流出。其总增长 62,889.46 加元产生较大的 15,722.37 加元税款，同时仍留下较大的税后端点。分组的条形图将每个案例的总增长、税收和净增长放在一起。在一行中，净增长等于总增值减去模型税。这三个栏不应作为单独的财富来源添加。仅比较累计税收将忽略额外的增长。仅比较总市场价值会忽略剩余负债。税收也会在不同的日期发生，因此简单的付款总额并不是其成本的现值衡量标准。将中间清算价值视为估值而不是重复销售。折线图显示了年度销售余额、最终销售案例的总市场余额以及同一最终销售案例在每个完成年份的假设税后清算价值。最后一行询问如果该头寸在指定年份出售，将会剩下什么。它不会支付所有这些中间假设税额，然后在选定的结束时再次支付。在这种情况下，只有一次最终销售。该矩阵同时改变了两种情况的持有期限和税收比例，同时保持选定的初始资本和增值。一年不会产生时间差异，因为两种情况均在同一日期出售。零税收假设或零升值也会消除模型优势。这些单元格不会分配回报概率或确定未来的税率。较长的时间范围放大了图中持续复利的影响，而实际回报、法律、现金需求和投资组合选择在此期间可能会发生变化。将实际应税事件和投资决策排除在捷径之外 CRA 的资本利得指南解释说，当资本财产被出售或被视为出售时，通常会产生收益或损失。本文并未对视为处置、储备、豁免或其他特殊待遇进行建模。它使用一般收益概念和原始假设税收投入。持有基金而不出售其单位并不意味着每笔回报在最终出售之前都可以免税。 CRA 的共同基金指南讨论了拥有控股权时的分配，包括再投资金额。这些事件及其成本基础调整在这里故意缺席。在估计实际税后目标金额之前，核对实际收入类别、交易、成本记录和付款日期。投资适宜性、多元化、费用和出售需求可能与这种时机效应无关。比较分离出一种机制；它不能确定推迟特定销售是否合适。

61fe18fd8dd3494d49f0ea76b43f3c6b92a1e2dd.src: An eventual payment total, its present value and the amount available today answer different questions. Keep all three beside the actual receipt dates. Write down the receipts before choosing a valuation method Suppose a household can receive CAD 50,000 immediately or CAD 12,000 once a year for five years, with the first payment one year from now. The second option totals CAD 60,000. That larger numeral alone does not tell us whether it is more valuable today or whether it can meet a bill due next month. The alternatives have different dates as well as different totals. An immediate receipt can be assigned to a current need. A future receipt is assumed to arrive only on its stated date. This guide keeps a cash calendar beside a present-value comparison so the valuation does not erase that distinction. The tool assumes that the alternatives are mutually exclusive and every scheduled payment is made in full. Enter amounts on the same spendable basis. It does not estimate taxes, establish a right to choose a different payment form, or value a life-contingent pension. A real contract must first identify what is payable, when it is payable and under what conditions. Convert each payment to the same date exactly once The OpenStax discussion of annuities explains how a stream of fixed payments can be valued by discounting each receipt. Its cash-flow timing chapter also shows why a dated timeline matters when amounts occur in different periods. This guide applies that method to an independently authored example. A payment due in year t has a time-zero value of payment ÷ (1 + effective annual discount rate) t . The immediate amount is already at time zero, so it is not discounted for another year. A payment received now likewise has an exponent of zero. The selected discount rate is a valuation assumption. It does not guarantee that the household can earn that rate, and it does not automatically incorporate tax, default risk or inflation. Choosing a rate appropriate to an actual decision needs a separate assessment of its cash flows and alternatives; this illustration does not supply a market quote. Keep the analytical discount rate separate from a price-year conversion. Expressing a future receipt in constant purchasing power requires a specified inflation path. Comparing its value with an alternative use of money requires a consistent valuation assumption. If amounts have already been converted to constant-price dollars, applying a rate on a different price basis can combine inconsistent units. This tool uses payment-year dollars, a discount rate on that basis and no second inflation conversion. Explain the default result through individual discounted receipts At a hypothetical 5% effective annual discount rate, the first CAD 12,000 payment has a present value of approximately CAD 11,428.57. The fifth payment has a present value of approximately CAD 9,402.31 because its receipt is five years away. Adding all five discounted payments produces about CAD 51,953.72. Subtracting the immediate CAD 50,000 alternative leaves a positive valuation difference of about CAD 1,953.72. The waterfall shows each discounted payment and the final subtraction, so the result can be traced without treating the entire CAD 60,000 as money received today. This is an arithmetic comparison under the stated assumptions. It does not create CAD 51,953.72 of accessible cash, nor does it establish that borrowing against future receipts would be available or inexpensive. Discounting a payment to time zero and then deducting an additional generic “waiting cost” would also count the same selected time-value assumption twice unless that cost represents a separate identified cash flow. Keep the cumulative receipt line separate from an investment account The cumulative chart begins with CAD 50,000 received under the upfront alternative and zero received under the default delayed alternative. The latter rises by CAD 12,000 at each annual receipt. It reaches CAD 60,000 after the fifth payment. No return is earned in that chart. The upfront line stays at CAD 50,000 because it records total receipts, rather than a growing investment. Spending is also absent, so neither line is a forecast of the bank balance remaining after bills. A household that spends an immediate receipt will not still own all of it simply because its cumulative-receipts line stays level. A larger eventual receipt total can coexist with a lower present value. At an 8% discount rate, the same five payments are worth about CAD 47,912.52 today, below the CAD 50,000 alternative. The receipt dates and total have not changed; the analytical rate used to compare them has. The matrix makes that sensitivity visible. Shift the whole payment calendar instead of adding an unexplained adjustment The first-payment control can move the equal stream while retaining its size and count. With five payments starting in year zero, the dates are zero through four. Starting in year one gives dates one through five. Starting in year three gives dates three through seven. At 5%, moving the default stream two years later reduces its present value from CAD 51,953.72 to about CAD 47,123.56. This equals the original present value divided by 1.05 squared. The undiscounted total remains CAD 60,000 because no payment has been removed or reduced. At a zero discount rate, the model values every dated dollar equally, so the timing rows show the same difference for a given total. That does not eliminate a household’s need for cash before a payment arrives. It shows the consequence of using zero as the analytical rate. The schedule still identifies those earlier periods without receipts. Check the current spending need and payment conditions separately A household may prefer a regular receipt pattern for budgeting, or need more money immediately for a known obligation. Those practical needs should be specified directly. They are not automatically settled by the sign of a present-value difference. For example, a CAD 15,000 bill due now cannot be paid from the first default installment one year later. Funding that bill from existing savings changes how much of those savings remains for other needs. Borrowing instead introduces its own proceeds, interest and repayment dates. Neither action is assumed in this receipt-only comparison. Before applying the method to an actual offer, check payment certainty, gross versus net amounts, fees, any indexing, transfer restrictions and the consequences of a recipient’s death. A finite stream assumed fully payable differs from a payment that depends on continued survival or another condition. Record those terms alongside the timeline, then value the resulting cash flows on a consistent date. The charts explain the method while leaving those contract-specific facts to the actual evidence.
61fe18fd8dd3494d49f0ea76b43f3c6b92a1e2dd.zh: 最终付款总额、其现值和当前可用金额回答了不同的问题。将所有三个日期保留在实际收货日期旁边。在选择估价方法之前写下收据 假设一个家庭可以立即收到 50,000 加元，或者每年一次收到 12,000 加元，为期五年，从现在起一年后第一次付款。第二个选项总计 60,000 加元。仅凭这个较大的数字并不能告诉我们它今天是否更有价值，或者是否可以满足下个月到期的账单。替代方案有不同的日期和不同的总数。可以将立即收据分配给当前需求。假定未来收据仅在规定日期送达。本指南在现值比较旁边保留了现金日历，因此估值不会消除这种区别。该工具假设替代方案是相互排斥的，并且每笔预定付款均已全额支付。根据相同的可支出基础输入金额。它不估算税收，不确立选择不同付款方式的权利，也不评估终身养老金。真正的合同必须首先确定应付款的内容、何时付款以及在什么条件下付款。将每笔付款转换为同一日期一次 OpenStax 对年金的讨论解释了如何通过对每张收据进行贴现来对固定付款流进行估值。其现金流时序章节还说明了为什么当金额发生在不同时期时，注明日期的时间表很重要。本指南将该方法应用于独立创作的示例。 t 年到期的付款具有零时付款价值 ÷ (1 + 有效年度贴现率) t 。即时金额在时间点已经为零，因此在接下来的一年内不会打折。现在收到的付款同样具有零指数。所选贴现率是一种估值假设。它并不保证家庭能够赚取该利率，也不会自动纳入税收、违约风险或通货膨胀。选择适合实际决策的利率需要对其现金流量和替代方案进行单独评估；该插图不提供市场报价。将分析折扣率与价格年份转换分开。以不变的购买力来表示未来的收入需要指定的通货膨胀路径。将其价值与货币的替代用途进行比较需要一致的估值假设。如果金额已转换为不变价格美元，则在不同价格基础上应用汇率可能会合并不一致的单位。该工具使用支付年美元、在此基础上的贴现率，并且没有第二次通货膨胀转换。通过单独的折扣收据解释默认结果 在假设的 5% 有效年度折扣率下，第一笔 12,000 加元付款的现值约为 11,428.57 加元。第五笔付款的现值约为 9,402.31 加元，因为其收款时间为五年后。将所有五笔折扣付款相加，所得金额约为 51,953.72 加元。减去直接的 50,000 加元替代方案，留下约 1,953.72 加元的正估值差异。瀑布显示了每笔折扣付款和最终减去的金额，因此可以追踪结果，而无需将整个 60,000 加元视为今天收到的款项。这是在规定的假设下的算术比较。它并没有创造出 51,953.72 加元的可用现金，也没有确定未来收入的借款是可用的或廉价的。将付款贴现到零时间，然后扣除额外的通用“等待成本”也会将相同的选定时间价值假设计算两次，除非该成本代表单独的已确定现金流量。将累积收款行与投资账户分开。累积图表从在预付选项下收到的 50,000 加元开始，在默认延迟选项下收到的零。后者每收到一份年度收入就会增加 12,000 加元。第五次付款后，已达到 60,000 加元。该图表中没有获得任何回报。预付款保持在 50,000 加元，因为它记录的是总收入，而不是不断增长的投资。也没有支出，因此这两条线都没有预测账单后剩余的银行余额。一个立即支出收入的家庭不会仅仅因为其累积收入线保持水平而仍然拥有全部收入。较大的最终收款总额可以与较低的现值共存。按 8% 的折扣率计算，同样的五笔付款如今价值约为 47,912.52 加元，低于 50,000 加元的替代方案。收货日期和总额没有改变；用于比较它们的分析率。矩阵使这种敏感性变得可见。移动整个付款日历，而不是添加无法解释的调整 首次付款控件可以移动相等的流，同时保留其大小和计数。从零年开始有五笔付款，日期从零到四年。从第一年开始给出日期一到五。从第三年开始，日期为三到七。按照 5% 的比例，两年后移动默认流会将其现值从 51,953.72 加元减少到约 47,123.56 加元。这等于原始现值除以 1.05 的平方。未折扣总额仍为 60,000 加元，因为没有任何付款被删除或减少。在零贴现率下，模型对每一美元的价值均等，因此时间行显示给定总额的相同差异。这并不能消除家庭在付款到达之前对现金的需求。它显示了使用零作为分析速率的结果。该时间表仍然标识了那些没有收据的早期时期。单独检查当前的支出需求和付款条件 家庭可能更喜欢定期收据模式进行预算，或者立即需要更多资金来履行已知义务。应直接指定这些实际需求。它们不会通过现值差异的符号自动解决。例如，现在到期的 15,000 加元账单无法在一年后从第一期默认分期付款中支付。从现有储蓄中为该账单提供资金会改变这些储蓄中用于其他需求的比例。相反，借款会带来自己的收益、利息和还款日期。在此仅收据比较中，这两种操作均未假定。在将该方法应用于实际报价之前，请检查付款确定性、总金额与净金额、费用、任何索引、转账限制以及接收者死亡的后果。假设完全可支付的有限流与取决于持续生存或其他条件的支付不同。将这些条款与时间表一起记录下来，然后在一致的日期对由此产生的现金流进行估值。图表解释了该方法，同时将那些特定于合同的事实留给实际证据。

1324a1fc3a9f712d21e46b5360cdb6444ca78e3e.src: A sufficient eventual sale receipt can arrive too late for an earlier bill. Check the bank-receipt date as well as the trade and settlement dates. Start with the account that must pay the bill A portfolio can contain enough value to cover a purchase while the spending bank account lacks the cash on the bill’s due date. Before relying on a sale, separate an order submitted, a trade executed, settlement completed, withdrawal eligibility and usable cash received at the bank. The model begins with an assumed executed sale . It does not place an order, assume that a submitted limit order fills, or price the security. The proceeds input is a separately determined net receipt. Costs, tax earmarks and registered-account consequences require their own review; the linked sale-proceeds guide addresses a different part of that work. The financial-planning question here is narrower: does the money reach the account that must pay this one bill in time? A balance available to buy another security need not be available to withdraw to an external bank at the same moment. T+1 describes settlement, rather than external-bank arrival The Canadian Securities Administrators announced Canada’s shorter settlement cycle effective 27 May 2024 . The Canadian Capital Markets Association’s implementation release describes the one-business-day cycle and includes ordinary exchange-traded securities such as ETFs. This is context for an ordinary secondary-market Canadian-listed stock or ETF sale subject to the applicable regular T+1 terms. It does not establish the timetable for every mutual fund redemption, cross-border trade, new issue, special settlement arrangement or foreign-currency transaction. T is the executed trade date. In a one-business-day example, settlement counts the next open business day after it, rather than simply adding 24 hours. Friday can therefore settle on Monday when the intervening weekend is closed. Real securities and banking calendars may differ and can contain holidays, cutoffs or other restrictions. The control’s default settlement count is one. Increasing that count is an assumed operational stress for this calendar, not a choice of an alternative regular settlement rule for the same actual trade. Confirm the executed trade’s settlement date from the actual transaction record. Keep the post-settlement wait as a separate assumption Wealthsimple’s sale guidance distinguishes cash balance, available-to-trade funds and available-to-withdraw funds. Its withdrawal guidance describes separate processing considerations and reasons balances can differ. Those are first-party explanations for that broker, not a service promise for every account. The second delay is therefore labeled assumed post-settlement wait until bank receipt . It can represent separately checked availability restrictions, broker processing and transfer transit. The tool does not infer withdrawal eligibility from settlement or quote an actual transfer service. A zero wait means the illustration assumes usable bank cash on the settlement day. It does not mean any provider promises such a service. For a real payment, verify the actual account’s holds, available balance, request cutoff, transfer method and receiving-bank usability. Read a fictional calendar before counting its days Day 1 is a fictional Monday. Days 6 and 7 are the first weekend; Days 13 and 14 are the second. The first-week trade choices are Monday through Friday, so the assumed execution is always on an open model day. The closure control can add zero to three fictional closed weekdays beginning on Day 8, the second Monday. One extra closure closes only Day 8; two close Days 8 and 9. These are invented operational sensitivities, not actual 2026 holidays. A single shared calendar is used for settlement and bank processing to make the arithmetic inspectable. A positive wait excludes its starting day, then counts only subsequent open model days. A zero post-settlement wait returns the settlement day. The separate calendar matrix marks open days as 1 and closed days as 0, so a weekend is not silently counted as a processing day. The bill occurs on its entered calendar day even if that day is closed. Within a day, assumed bank receipts arrive before the bill. Those are explicit teaching conventions; actual bill debit rules and posting order must be checked rather than inferred from a day-end balance. The same endpoint can hide a CAD 3,000 earlier gap The default bank balance is CAD 1,000. The assumed net sale proceeds are CAD 5,000, and a CAD 4,000 bill is due on Day 10. The executed sale is Friday, Day 5. With one settlement business day and two further business days until bank receipt, settlement is Monday, Day 8 and receipt is Wednesday, Day 10. Under receipt-before-bill posting, bank cash first becomes CAD 6,000 on Day 10, then falls to CAD 2,000 after the bill. No additional opening cash is needed for this one obligation. Add one fictional Day-8 closure. Settlement moves to Tuesday, Day 9 and bank receipt to Thursday, Day 11. Only CAD 1,000 is available for the CAD 4,000 bill on Day 10, leaving an unfunded CAD 3,000 position. Receipt on Day 11 restores the scheduled ledger to CAD 2,000, but it cannot fund the prior day retroactively. Both cases end with the same arithmetic: 1,000 + 5,000 − 4,000 = 2,000. The earlier funding requirement differs. A negative line segment records that missing resource; it is not an approved overdraft, an instruction to pay an unfunded bill or a prediction that a bank will allow the transaction. Do not count the same sale proceeds in three places After execution and before settlement, the illustration classifies the proceeds as an unsettled receivable. After settlement and before bank receipt, it places them in one off-bank processing category. At bank receipt, that same amount becomes the received bank component. The stage chart shows successive snapshots of this one receipt before allocating it to household spending. Its rows must not be added into a larger household balance. The middle category can include transfer transit; it does not claim the money remains withdrawable brokerage cash after a transfer debit. If settlement and bank receipt are on the same modeled day, the settled snapshot already shows bank receipt and the off-bank interval disappears. No additional receipt is created. The bank ledger, separately, deducts the bill once. Selling an investment changes the form of existing assets. Transferring the proceeds between accounts changes their location. Neither operation creates the sale amount as new earned income. This tool tracks a receipt’s timing without reconstructing the unsold security’s value or the household’s total net worth. Keep an arrival beyond Day 14 outside the ledger The charts display fourteen calendar days, but the calendar continues counting when processing lasts longer. With the default Friday trade, one Day-8 closure and six post-settlement business days, receipt is Day 17. It is not moved backward to Day 14 to make the diagram balance. In that case, Day-14 scheduled bank cash remains negative CAD 3,000 and the entered CAD 5,000 receipt is still off bank. An eventual endpoint after receipt would answer a different horizon. Read the arrival-day metric and pending-receipt note with the bank ledger. The sensitivity matrix changes the trade weekday and post-settlement wait while keeping the bill, opening cash, proceeds and selected calendar assumptions fixed. Each cell is an independent scenario, with no probability assigned. The weekday comparison separately contrasts weekends only with exactly one fictional Day-8 closure. Turn a confirmed bank receipt into the spending plan Confirm that the sale executed and read its actual settlement terms. Check withdrawable cash and any account-specific eligibility, holds or restrictions. Verify the request cutoff, transfer route and receiving-bank availability. Determine net spendable proceeds and any tax reserve separately. Match the confirmed usable-cash date with the bill’s debit date and posting order. This is a partial one-bill cash exercise. Other payments, income, emergencies, tax, exchange rates and changes in investment value are omitted. For a real household calendar, add the confirmed receipts and obligations rather than treating this illustration as a complete liquidity assessment.
1324a1fc3a9f712d21e46b5360cdb6444ca78e3e.zh: 对于较早的账单来说，足够的最终销售收据可能来得太晚。检查银行收据日期以及交易和结算日期。从必须支付账单的账户开始投资组合可以包含足够的价值来支付购买费用，而支出银行账户在账单到期日缺乏现金。在进行销售之前，将提交的订单、执行的交易、完成的结算、提款资格和在银行收到的可用现金分开。该模型从假设的已执行销售开始。它不下订单，不假设提交的限价订单已成交，也不对证券定价。收益输入是单独确定的净收入。成本、税收专项和注册账户后果需要自行审查；链接的销售收入指南涉及该工作的不同部分。这里的财务规划问题比较狭隘：钱是否及时到达必须支付这一账单的账户？可用于购买另一种证券的余额无需同时提取到外部银行。 T+1 描述的是结算，而不是外部银行到账 加拿大证券管理局宣布加拿大较短的结算周期于 2024 年 5 月 27 日生效。加拿大资本市场协会的实施版本描述了一个工作日周期，并包括 ETF 等普通交易所交易证券。这是在普通二级市场加拿大上市股票或 ETF 销售的背景，须遵守适用的常规 T+1 条款。它没有为每项共同基金赎回、跨境贸易、新发行、特别结算安排或外币交易制定时间表。 T 是执行交易日期。在一个工作日的示例中，结算计算其后的下一个开放工作日，而不是简单地添加 24 小时。因此，周五可以在周一休市时结算。实际的证券和银行日历可能有所不同，并且可能包含假期、截止日期或其他限制。该控件默认结算计数为1。增加该计数是该日历的假定操作压力，而不是针对同一实际交易选择替代的常规结算规则。根据实际交易记录确认已执行交易的结算日期。将结算后等待作为一个单独的假设 Wealthsimple 的销售指南区分了现金余额、可交易资金和可提取资金。其提款指南描述了单独的处理注意事项以及余额可能不同的原因。这些是该经纪人的第一方解释，而不是针对每个账户的服务承诺。因此，第二次延迟被标记为假定结算后等待直至银行收据。它可以代表单独检查的可用性限制、代理处理和传输中转。该工具不会从结算中推断出提款资格，也不会引用实际的转账服务。零等待意味着该插图假设结算日有可用的银行现金。这并不意味着任何提供商承诺提供此类服务。对于真实付款，请验证实际帐户的持有量、可用余额、请求截止、转账方式和接收银行的可用性。在计算日子之前先阅读虚构的日历 第一天是虚构的星期一。第 6 天和第 7 天是第一个周末；第 13 天和第 14 天是第二天。第一周的交易选择是周一到周五，因此假设的执行始终在开放模型日。关闭控制可以从第 8 天（第二个星期一）开始添加零到三个虚构的关闭工作日。另一项关闭仅在第 8 天关闭；第 8 日和第 9 天是两个休赛日。这些是出于操作敏感性而虚构的，而不是实际的 2026 年假期。结算和银行处理使用单一共享日历，使算术可检查。正等待不包括其开始日，然后仅计算后续开放模型日。结算后零等待返回结算日。单独的日历矩阵将开放日标记为 1，关闭日标记为 0，因此周末不会默默地计为处理日。即使该日休息，账单也会在输入的日历日发生。一天之内，假设银行收据先于账单到达。这些都是明确的教学惯例；必须检查实际的账单借记规则和过帐顺序，而不是从日终余额推断。同一端点可以隐藏 3,000 加元之前的缺口 默认银行余额为 1,000 加元。假定净销售收入为 5,000 加元，第 10 天应有 4,000 加元的账单。执行的销售为第 5 天星期五。银行收款前有一个结算工作日和另外两个工作日，结算为第 8 天星期一，收款为第 10 天星期三。在账单过帐前收款的情况下，银行现金在第 10 天首先变为 6,000 加元，然后在第 10 天后降至 2,000 加元。账单。这项义务不需要额外的期初现金。添加一个虚构的第 8 天结束。结算移至第 9 天，星期二，银行收据移至第 11 天，星期四。第 10 天，4,000 加元的账单只能使用 1,000 加元，留下 3,000 加元的头寸。第 11 天的收据将预定账本恢复至 2,000 加元，但无法追溯前一天的资金。两种情况都以相同的算术结束：1,000 + 5,000 − 4,000 = 2,000。早期的资金要求有所不同。负线段记录了缺失的资源；它不是经批准的透支、支付无资金账单的指令或银行将允许交易的预测。请勿在三个地方计算相同的销售收益 执行后、结算前，插图将收益分类为未结算的应收账款。结算后、银行收款前，将其置于一种非银行处理类别中。在银行收据时，相同的金额成为收到的银行部分。阶段图显示了这张收据在分配给家庭支出之前的连续快照。不得将其行添加到更大的家庭余额中。中间类别可以包括转机过境；它并不声称这笔钱在转账借方后仍然是可提取的经纪现金。如果结算和银行收据在同一天，则结算快照已显示银行收据，离岸间隔消失。不会创建额外的收据。银行账本单独扣除一次账单。出售投资会改变现有资产的形式。在帐户之间转移收益会改变其位置。这两种操作都不会将销售金额创建为新的收入。该工具可以跟踪收据的时间，而无需重建未售出证券的价值或家庭的总净资产。将第 14 天之后的到达情况保留在分类帐之外 图表显示 14 个日历日，但当处理持续时间更长时，日历会继续计数。在默认的周五交易、第 8 天关闭和六个结算后工作日的情况下，收据为第 17 天。它不会向后移动到第 14 天以使图表平衡。在这种情况下，第 14 天预定的银行现金仍为负 3,000 加元，并且输入的 5,000 加元收据仍处于银行外状态。收到后的最终端点将回答不同的地平线。使用银行分类账阅读到货日指标和待收据票据。敏感性矩阵改变交易工作日和结算后等待，同时保持账单、期初现金、收益和选定的日历假设固定。每个单元格都是一个独立的场景，没有分配概率。工作日比较仅将周末与虚构的第 8 天关闭进行单独对比。将确认的银行收据转入支出计划确认销售已执行并阅读其实际结算条款。检查可提取现金以及任何特定于账户的资格、保留或限制。验证请求截止、转账路线和接收银行的可用性。单独确定可支出净收益和任何税收储备。将确认的可用现金日期与帐单的借方日期和过帐订单相匹配。这是一项部分单票现金活动。其他付款、收入、紧急情况、税收、汇率和投资价值的变化均被省略。对于真实的家庭日历，请添加已确认的收据和义务，而不是将此图视为完整的流动性评估。

0f07cc3748b8a894f13e3e3bd4926aee5266532e.src: A quoted hourly rate becomes annual cash only through hours you can sell and collect. Budget unpaid work and fixed costs before treating the quote as a household income rate. Separate the work relationship from the pricing arithmetic An hourly quote is a unit price, not a promise of forty paid hours every week. Before building a household budget around it, establish how many hours can produce collected fees and what those fees must fund. Worker status is a separate question. The CRA’s Employee or Self-employed guide says the facts of the working relationship as a whole decide employment status. A chosen contract label or a favourable calculator result does not settle it. The guide also explains the option of requesting a CPP/EI ruling when status is uncertain. This tool assumes an independently established sole-operator business arrangement. It performs annual capacity and cash-allocation arithmetic. It does not determine employment status, statutory contributions, labour-law rights, tax deductions or the value of an actual employee benefit. Build the time budget before multiplying by the hourly rate The example uses a simple fifty-two-week template, with forty hours assigned to each available workweek. Five weeks are reserved for leave and four other weeks for downtime. These categories are assumed not to overlap, leaving forty-three working weeks. That produces 1,720 working hours. A quarter of them, or 430 hours, is assigned to work that cannot be billed: for example, administration, business development or maintaining systems. The remaining 1,290 hours are the billable capacity used by the model. The time chart also shows 360 hours of no-work capacity. That is nine unavailable weeks multiplied by the forty-hour template; those hours are not actually worked. Billable hours, unpaid working hours and no-work capacity together reconcile to the template’s 2,080 hours. All 1,290 billable hours are assumed to find buyers and be collected in the same year. This is a strong assumption. Time available to sell a service does not establish demand, and an invoice does not establish collection. Use the separate invoice-cash guide to test when money reaches the bank. Follow collected fees through the costs they must cover At CAD 100 per billable hour, the selected capacity generates CAD 129,000 of collected fees, excluding sales tax. Variable business cash costs take 8%, or CAD 10,320. Annual fixed business cash costs take another CAD 12,000, leaving CAD 106,680 before a separate personal allocation. The example then assigns CAD 12,000 to a personal provision. This might represent a separately budgeted amount for protection or saving, but the tool gives it no automatic tax treatment and assumes no equivalence with employer benefits. Counting it as a cash allocation keeps it from being spent again elsewhere. After that provision, CAD 94,680 remains before personal income tax, CPP/QPP, EI and other personal liabilities. It is not take-home pay. It includes the cash available to reward the owner’s work and bear business risk; no separate owner wage has been deducted. BDC’s pricing overview explains the need to account for costs and overhead when examining a break-even point. The waterfall here uses a deliberately simple cash structure, rather than reproducing a formal cost-of-sales statement or claiming that every entered expense is deductible. Solve for a rate only after stating the annual target The target input asks for annual cash remaining after the entered business costs and personal provision, but before personal tax. Its default is CAD 80,000. This target is separate from the CAD 12,000 provision, so the model does not quietly count that allocation twice. To solve for the rate, add the target, fixed business costs and provision. Divide their CAD 104,000 total by the billable hours multiplied by the 92% left after variable costs. The required rate is approximately CAD 87.63 per billable hour under these assumptions. The line chart varies the quote and shows where annual remaining cash meets the target. A crossing above the displayed range can still produce a numeric required rate. That calculation does not make the price commercially attainable or prove that the assumed number of hours will sell. When there are no billable hours, the tool reports that no billable hours are available rather than dividing by zero. Fixed cash costs and the chosen provision remain in the budget. They do not disappear merely because all working time becomes unpaid or every week is unavailable. Use the sensitivity grid to choose what needs better evidence The matrix changes the quote and the unpaid share together. A larger unpaid share leaves fewer hours producing fees while fixed costs continue. A higher quote raises modeled revenue only because the grid holds sold hours unchanged. It does not model customers buying fewer hours at a higher price. Before relying on a cell, check recent time records, confirmed bookings, cancellation terms, collection experience and the costs that continue during downtime. Keep leave and other unavailable weeks distinct so the same week is not removed twice. For household planning, add a separate assessment of personal tax, statutory contributions, protection needs and the timing of withdrawals. A full year’s positive result may still coexist with an early cash shortage. The useful output is a documented capacity budget and a set of assumptions to verify, not a salary comparison or an instruction to charge a particular rate.
0f07cc3748b8a894f13e3e3bd4926aee5266532e.zh: 仅在您可以出售和收取的时间内，报价的小时费率才成为年度现金。在将报价视为家庭收入之前，先对无薪工作和固定成本进行预算。将工作关系与定价算法分开 每小时报价是一个单价，而不是每周四十个小时带薪的承诺。在围绕它制定家庭预算之前，确定可以产生多少小时的费用以及这些费用必须资助哪些内容。工人身份是一个单独的问题。 CRA 的雇员或自营职业者指南称，工作关系的事实作为一个整体决定了就业状况。选择的合同标签或有利的计算器结果并不能解决问题。该指南还解释了在状态不确定时请求 CPP/EI 裁决的选项。该工具假定独立建立的独资运营商业务安排。它执行年度容量和现金分配算术。它不决定就业状况、法定缴款、劳动法权利、税收减免或实际员工福利的价值。在乘以小时费率之前建立时间预算 该示例使用简单的五十二周模板，每个可用工作周分配了 40 个小时。预留五周的休假时间，另外四个星期的停机时间。假定这些类别不重叠，剩下四十三个工作周。这产生了 1,720 个工作小时。其中四分之一（即 430 小时）被分配到无法计费的工作：例如，管理、业务开发或维护系统。剩余的 1,290 小时是该模型使用的计费容量。时间表还显示了 360 小时的无工作能力。这是九周不可用的时间乘以四十小时的模板；这些时间实际上并没有工作。计费工时、无薪工时和无工作能力合计与模板的 2,080 小时相符。假设所有 1,290 个计费小时均在同一年找到买家并收取。这是一个强有力的假设。可用于销售服务的时间并不构成需求，发票也不构成收款。使用单独的发票现金指南来测试资金何时到达银行。跟踪收取的费用及其必须涵盖的成本 按每计费小时 100 加元计算，所选容量会产生 129,000 加元的收取费用（不包括销售税）。可变业务现金成本占 8%，即 10,320 加元。每年固定业务现金成本还需要 12,000 加元，在单独的个人分配之前还剩下 106,680 加元。然后，该示例将 12,000 加元分配给个人供应。这可能代表用于保护或储蓄的单独预算金额，但该工具不会自动进行税收处理，并且假设与雇主福利不相等。将其算作现金分配可以防止其再次花在其他地方。扣除该条款后，未缴纳个人所得税、CPP/QPP、EI 和其他个人负债的金额为 94,680 加元。这不是实得工资。它包括可用于奖励所有者工作和承担经营风险的现金；没有扣除单独的业主工资。 BDC 的定价概述解释了在检查盈亏平衡点时需要考虑成本和管理费用。这里的瀑布故意使用简单的现金结构，而不是复制正式的销售成本报表或声称每项输入的费用都是可扣除的。仅在陈述年度目标后才能求解比率 目标输入要求在输入的业务成本和个人准备金之后、但在个人税之前剩余的年度现金。默认值为 80,000 加元。该目标与 12,000 加元的拨款是分开的，因此该模型不会悄悄地将分配计算两次。要解决费率问题，请添加目标、固定业务成本和准备金。将总费用 104,000 加元除以计费小时数乘以扣除可变成本后剩余的 92%。在这些假设下，所需费率约为每计费小时 87.63 加元。折线图会改变报价并显示年度剩余现金达到目标的情况。超出显示范围仍然可以产生数字所需的速率。该计算并不能使价格在商业上可行，也不能证明假设的小时数可以销售。当没有计费工时时，该工具会报告没有可用的计费工时，而不是除以零。固定现金成本和选定的拨款仍保留在预算中。它们不会仅仅因为所有工作时间变得无薪或每周都无法工作而消失。使用敏感度网格来选择需要更好证据的内容。矩阵将报价和未付份额一起更改。未付份额越大，产生费用的时间就越少，而固定成本仍然存在。更高的报价只会提高模型收入，因为电网保持销售小时数不变。它并没有模拟客户以更高的价格购买更少的时间。在依赖手机之前，请检查最近的时间记录、已确认的预订、取消条款、收集经验以及停机期间持续的费用。将请假周与其他不可用周区分开来，这样同一周就不会被删除两次。对于家庭规划，添加对个人税、法定缴款、保护需求和提款时间的单独评估。全年的积极业绩可能仍与早期的现金短缺并存。有用的输出是记录的容量预算和一组需要验证的假设，而不是工资比较或收取特定费率的指令。

2a4a8b31059a1445085e3adac976ff8b096fcc54.src: A probability-weighted average helps compare modeled cost. It does not tell you whether one household can pay the actual repair bill, or whether a real contract will cover it. Define the comparison period and the repair before assigning a probability An extended warranty or repair service contract can exchange a known upfront payment for help with certain future repair costs. Whether a quoted contract addresses a household’s risk depends on its actual terms, existing coverage and the cost of paying directly. The Office of Consumer Affairs recommends checking the period, parts, service, repair arrangements and additional costs, and considering repair costs and possible overlapping coverage. Those questions establish the contract being compared. They do not supply a failure rate for a particular appliance or vehicle. This guide uses one fixed comparison period with only two possible outcomes: no eligible repair, or one eligible repair costing CAD 800. The original assumed probability of that repair is 20% over the entire period. It is not an annual probability, a measured product statistic or an estimate based on an actual claims file. The hypothetical contract costs CAD 180 upfront and leaves CAD 100 of the modeled repair for the household to pay. It accepts the claim and directly pays the remaining CAD 700. These generous simplifying conditions must be visible before interpreting any saving. Additional repairs, rejected claims, shipping, service delays, benefit limits and provider failure sit outside the model. Read the actual outcome costs before reading their average Without the contract, the modeled no-repair state costs zero and the repair state costs CAD 800. With the contract, the no-repair state costs CAD 180 because the fee has already been paid. The repair state costs CAD 280: the same CAD 180 fee plus CAD 100 out of pocket. The first grouped chart keeps both states visible. The provider’s assumed CAD 700 payment reduces the repair-state burden, while the fee adds a cost to the no-repair state. Buying the contract changes the shape of the possible household outlays, rather than simply removing every repair cost. The out-of-pocket input is capped at the repair amount. If the repair costs less than the stated deductible, the model makes the household pay the repair cost and assumes no covered amount. It never credits the household with a payment larger than the repair or treats unused deductible capacity as cash. All amounts are nominal and undiscounted. The original purchase price of the product is common to both choices and excluded. No borrowing, fee financing, cancellation refund or investment return is inserted. Actual differences in service quality, repair timing or replacement value require separate evidence. Calculate the probability-weighted cost without turning it into a guaranteed bill For this two-state example, expected direct-repair cost is probability × repair cost . At 20%, that is 0.20 × CAD 800 = CAD 160. Expected contract cost is upfront fee + probability × out-of-pocket repair amount , or CAD 180 + 0.20 × CAD 100 = CAD 200. The contract therefore has CAD 40 more expected cost under the original assumptions. That calculation does not mean every buyer loses CAD 40 or receives a CAD 200 invoice. One household pays either zero or CAD 800 directly; under the assumed contract it pays either CAD 180 or CAD 280. The line chart recalculates the expectation across alternative probabilities for the same period. It is an arithmetic sensitivity analysis, not a forecast curve. The selected probability determines the current metric, while the full line shows what different assumptions would imply. An average cost cannot resolve a household’s ability or willingness to absorb a large payment. Expected cost, available reserves, the practical value of a service and exposure to unmodeled contract problems answer different questions. The St. Louis Fed’s consumer-education discussion similarly separates risk preferences, potential repair savings and the costs or limitations of service contracts; its older survey figures are not used here. Use the equality threshold to identify the assumption doing the work When the contract covers a positive part of the repair, equal expected costs occur at fee ÷ (repair cost − out-of-pocket amount) . In the original example, CAD 180 ÷ CAD 700 is approximately 25.71%. At that probability, both expected costs are approximately CAD 205.71. Below it, paying directly has the lower modeled expectation; above it, the contract does. Equality at one point is not evidence that the actual probability is near that point or that either option is suitable. A fee larger than the maximum modeled covered repair amount produces no equality within 0–100%. If the contract pays none of the repair, it cannot reduce expected repair costs in this model; a positive fee only adds expense. With no fee and no covered amount, the two choices are equal for every probability. The matrix varies the repair cost as well as its assumed chance. It holds the selected fee and deductible constant. A repair amount below the deductible leaves no covered portion, while a more expensive eligible repair can change the comparison sharply. The matrix therefore helps locate which severity and probability assumptions support a result, without assigning confidence to any cell. Test the full repair-state cash requirement against the same reserve The original household has CAD 500 available before any contract fee is paid. With no repair, paying directly leaves CAD 500 and the contract leaves CAD 320. If the modeled repair occurs, direct payment requires CAD 800 and leaves a CAD 300 funding gap. The contract’s total CAD 280 outlay leaves CAD 220. The final signed chart displays the reserve less each state’s complete outlay. A negative amount is money still needed, not an assumed overdraft or an available loan. If the upfront fee alone exceeds the reserve, even the no-repair contract state has an initial funding problem. Changing the probability changes expected cost but not the cash required in a specified repair state. Likewise, increasing the reserve improves payment capacity without changing the contract’s expected cost difference. Keeping those controls independent prevents a larger cash balance from being mistaken for better coverage or a lower failure rate. The contract assumes direct settlement of the covered amount. If an actual provider reimburses later, the household may need the full repair bill first. This model also contains no later deposits, so it does not assess how a reserve could be rebuilt over a multi-year coverage period. Replace the two-state example with the facts of the actual decision Before using the comparison, verify what already protects the product, the dates of that protection and whether extra coverage overlaps it. Read the covered parts, excluded causes, required maintenance, approval steps, service locations, claim limits and the amount payable per visit or repair. The Office of Consumer Affairs advises checking whether shipping and service costs are included and whether card-provided protection already applies. These are questions for the actual terms; this article does not determine anyone’s legal entitlement or cancelation rights. Use an independently supported repair estimate and a probability definition matched to the same product, condition, use and period. If there is no reliable probability evidence, retain several clearly labeled scenarios instead of presenting one assumption as a measured rate. More than one potential failure, varying repair severity or a coverage cap requires a richer outcome model. The four charts help separate cost, uncertainty and liquidity. They do not value peace of mind, guarantee claim acceptance or identify the best provider. A useful decision record states the coverage being compared, the modeled outcomes, the assumption driving the cost threshold and the cash available if the less convenient outcome occurs.
2a4a8b31059a1445085e3adac976ff8b096fcc54.zh: 概率加权平均值有助于比较建模成本。它不会告诉你一个家庭是否可以支付实际的维修费用，或者真正的合同是否会涵盖它。在分配概率之前定义比较期和维修 延长保修或维修服务合同可以用已知的预付款来换取某些未来维修成本的帮助。报价合同是否能解决家庭的风险取决于其实际条款、现有承保范围以及直接支付的成本。消费者事务办公室建议检查期限、零件、服务、维修安排和额外费用，并考虑维修费用和可能的重叠承保范围。这些问题确定了正在比较的合同。它们不提供特定设备或车辆的故障率。本指南使用一个固定的比较期，只有两种可能的结果：没有符合条件的维修，或者一次合格的维修费用为 800 加元。最初假设整个期间维修的概率为 20%。它不是年度概率、测量的产品统计数据或基于实际索赔文件的估计。假设的合同费用为 180 加元，家庭需要支付 100 加元的模型维修费用。它接受索赔并直接支付剩余的 700 加元。在解释任何节省之前，必须先看到这些慷慨的简化条件。额外的维修、被拒绝的索赔、运输、服务延迟、福利限制和提供商失败均不在模型之内。在读取平均值之前先阅读实际结果成本。如果没有合同，则建模的免维修状态成本为零，而维修状态成本为 800 加元。如果有合同，则免维修状态成本为 180 加元，因为费用已支付。维修费用为 280 加元：同样的 180 加元费用加上 100 加元的自付费用。第一个分组图表使两种状态都可见。提供商假定的 700 加元付款减少了维修状态的负担，而该费用增加了无维修状态的成本。购买合同改变了可能的家庭支出形式，而不是简单地消除所有维修费用。自付费用以维修金额为上限。如果维修费用低于规定的免赔额，该模型会让家庭支付维修费用，并且不承担承保金额。它绝不会向家庭贷记大于修理费用的付款，也不会将未使用的免赔额视为现金。所有金额均为名义金额且未打折。产品的原始购买价格对于两种选择都是相同的，并且被排除在外。不插入借款、费用融资、取消退款或投资回报。服务质量、维修时间或更换价值的实际差异需要单独的证据。计算概率加权成本，而不将其转化为保证账单 对于这个两种状态的示例，预期直接维修成本为 概率 × 维修成本 。按 20% 计算，即 0.20 × 800 加元 = 160 加元。预期合同成本为预付费用 + 概率 × 自付费用维修金额，即 180 加元 + 0.20 × 100 加元 = 200 加元。因此，在原始假设下，合同的预期成本多出 40 加元。这一计算并不意味着每个买家都会损失 40 加元或收到 200 加元的发票。一户直接支付零或800加元；根据假定的合同，它支付 180 加元或 280 加元。折线图重新计算同一时期内不同概率的预期。这是算术敏感性分析，而不是预测曲线。所选概率决定当前指标，而实线则显示不同假设的含义。平均成本并不能决定一个家庭吸收大额付款的能力或意愿。预期成本、可用储备、服务的实际价值以及未建模合同问题的风险回答了不同的问题。圣路易斯联储的消费者教育讨论同样将风险偏好、潜在的维修节省以及服务合同的成本或限制分开；这里不使用其较旧的调查数据。使用相等阈值来确定进行工作的假设 当合同涵盖维修的正部分时，相等的预期成本按费用 ÷ (维修成本 − 自付费用) 发生。在原始示例中，180 加元 ÷ 700 加元约为 25.71%。按照这种概率，两种预期成本约为 205.71 加元。在它之下，直接支付的模型预期较低；在它上面，合同是这样的。某个点上的相等并不能证明实际概率接近该点或任一选项都是合适的。大于最大模拟承保维修金额的费用不会产生 0-100% 范围内的相等。如果合同不支付任何维修费用，则无法减少该模型中的预期维修成本；正的费用只会增加开支。由于不收取任何费用，也没有承保金额，因此这两种选择在每种概率下都是相同的。该矩阵会改变修复成本及其假设的机会。它保持选定的费用和免赔额不变。低于免赔额的维修金额不会留下承保部分，而更昂贵的合格维修可能会急剧改变比较结果。因此，该矩阵有助于确定哪些严重性和概率假设支持结果，而无需为任何单元格分配置信度。根据相同的储备金测试全部修复状态的现金需求 在支付任何合同费用之前，原家庭有 500 加元可用。如果不进行维修，直接付款需要 500 加元，合同还需要 320 加元。如果进行模型维修，直接付款需要 800 加元，并留下 300 加元的资金缺口。合同总支出为 280 加元，还剩 220 加元。最终签署的图表显示储备金减去每个州的全部支出。负金额是指仍然需要的资金，而不是假定的透支或可用贷款。如果仅预付费用就超过了准备金，即使是无维修合同状态也存在初始资金问题。更改概率会更改预期成本，但不会更改指定维修状态下所需的现金。同样，增加准备金可以提高支付能力，而不会改变合同的预期成本差异。保持这些控制的独立性可以防止更大的现金余额被误认为更好的覆盖范围或更低的故障率。合同假定直接结算所涵盖的金额。如果实际提供者稍后报销，则该家庭可能首先需要全额维修费用。该模型也不包含后期存款，因此它不评估如何在多年覆盖期内重建储备。将两种状态的示例替换为实际决策的事实
