在进行比较之前，请验证已经保护产品的内容、该保护的日期以及额外的承保范围是否与其重叠。请阅读涵盖的部件、排除的原因、所需的维护、批准步骤、服务地点、索赔限额以及每次访问或维修的应付金额。消费者事务办公室建议检查是否包含运输和服务费用以及卡提供的保护是否已适用。这些是针对实际条款的问题；本文并不确定任何人的合法权利或取消权。使用独立支持的维修估算和与相同产品、条件、用途和周期相匹配的概率定义。如果没有可靠的概率证据，请保留几种明确标记的场景，而不是将一种假设呈现为测量率。不止一个潜在故障、不同的维修严重程度或覆盖范围上限需要更丰富的结果模型。这四个图表有助于区分成本、不确定性和流动性。他们不重视安心、保证索赔接受或确定最佳提供商。有用的决策记录说明了比较的覆盖范围、建模结果、驱动成本阈值的假设以及发生不太方便的结果时可用的现金。

cc4958c1c4a28bc94010a69d1cbbb8bf2aa162ca.src: A larger later payment is not directly comparable with cash today. Put both alternatives on one date, show the implied annual rate, and separately check payment reliability and access. Write two alternatives, rather than one combined balance The example offers one of two receipts: CAD 20,000 today or a single CAD 24,000 payment in three years. Receiving one means giving up the other. Adding them into CAD 44,000 of household resources would count an alternative that was never available alongside the first. The nominal difference is CAD 4,000, or 20% of the immediate amount. That 20% covers the entire three-year wait. It is not a 20% annual return. The dates are part of the comparison, just as surely as the amounts. The CFA Institute’s public time-value overview connects current values, future cash flows and implied returns. Here, the calculator applies those principles to a simple original example with one payment under each alternative. Convert the later receipt into a value measured today Let L be the later payment, r the effective annual comparison rate as a fraction, and n the number of years. The present value is PV = L ÷ (1+r) n . This discounts the later amount over the actual waiting period. At the default 5% comparison rate, CAD 24,000 divided by 1.05³ equals approximately CAD 20,732.10 . Compared with CAD 20,000 today, the present-value difference is about CAD 732.10 in favour of the later receipt under the stated assumptions. That value is not a deposit already held in an account. It is today’s equivalent on the selected valuation basis. A household cannot send CAD 20,732.10 to pay an earlier bill merely because the calculator displays that present value. A discount-rate curve shows which assumption changes the answer The first chart recalculates the later receipt’s present value at rates from 0% to 20%. The immediate CAD 20,000 remains a horizontal comparison. At a zero rate, the later receipt has a present value equal to its CAD 24,000 nominal amount. As the rate rises, its present value falls. The crossing is useful because it identifies the rate at which the two valuations are equal. Below that rate, the later receipt has the greater present value. Above it, the immediate cash has the greater present value. Those statements hold for these fixed amounts and dates with full payment assumed. The selected rate needs a reason. It might represent an independently assessed opportunity cost on a consistent cash basis, but the calculator does not identify an available deposit, achievable investment return or appropriate risk premium. An uncertain investment forecast cannot be turned into a guaranteed alternative simply by entering its average return here. Moving both alternatives forward gives the same ordering The common-date bars perform the comparison at the end of year three instead of today. Compounding CAD 20,000 at 5% for three years gives CAD 23,152.50 . The alternative later receipt is CAD 24,000, leaving a future-date difference of CAD 847.50 . The present-date difference was CAD 732.10, not CAD 847.50. The two figures use different dates. Multiplying the unrounded present-value difference by 1.05³ converts it into the future-date difference. It does not create an extra source of profit. The bars assume the immediate receipt remains invested at the entered constant rate with no withdrawals. If the cash is used for living costs, the resulting future balance will differ. Actual spending may meet a real need, but it cannot simultaneously remain available to compound toward the later comparison. Solve for the annual rate instead of dividing 20% by three The break-even annual rate solves cash now × (1+r*) n = later cash . Rearranging gives r* = (later cash ÷ cash now) 1/n − 1 . For CAD 20,000 and CAD 24,000 three years later, the result is approximately 6.26586% effective annually . Compounding at that rate for three years produces the full 20% cumulative increase. Dividing 20% by three gives a simple average of about 6.67%, which does not preserve the compounding equation. The rate is implied by the two offered amounts and their timing. It is not a separately earned coupon or an assurance that anyone will pay it. The California Board of Equalization’s time-value summary explains compounding and discounting as opposite movements between dates. This example uses annual effective compounding consistently in both directions. Keep the future amount fixed when testing a longer delay The matrix changes the waiting time and the comparison rate while retaining the same two receipt amounts. Every cell reports the later receipt’s present value minus the cash-now alternative. A longer wait does not automatically earn a larger payment in this exercise. At a positive rate, postponing the same future amount reduces its present value. At a zero rate, changing the wait leaves the present-value amount unchanged, although the actual availability date still moves. This separates the valuation calculation from the practical need to use money before it arrives. The matrix has no probabilities attached to its cells. It does not forecast which date or rate will occur. It helps reveal whether a conclusion depends strongly on a short delay or a particular valuation rate. A break-even rate can sit outside the plotted range If the two nominal amounts are identical, their implied break-even rate is zero. If the later amount is smaller than the immediate amount, the implied rate is negative. A nonnegative comparison rate will then favour the immediate amount on this narrow valuation basis. A very large later amount over a short period can imply a break-even rate above the graph’s 20% ceiling. The metric still reports the calculated rate, while the chart shows only its stated 0% to 20% range. No crossing inside the visible graph should be invented. These mathematical controls help interpret the output without treating an unusual implied rate as evidence that a high-return product exists. The legal terms, payment source and reliability of an actual offer require their own evidence. Bring the valuation back to the household’s required dates A bill due in six months cannot be paid directly by a receipt arriving in three years. A positive present-value difference does not supply a bridge loan, change the bill’s due date or make the later promise transferable. The calculator includes none of those arrangements. Compare the actual net receipts on the same tax and cost basis. The model does not calculate tax, fees, inflation or default losses. It also does not convert nominal future cash into inflation-adjusted purchasing power; adding such a comparison would require a consistent real-cash and real-rate calculation. Confirm which receipts are mutually exclusive and when each is usable. Put their amounts on a consistent net-cash basis. Document the reason for the comparison rate. Check both present-date and common future-date values. Review payment reliability and earlier cash obligations separately. The result is a transparent valuation comparison. The choice still has to support the actual payment calendar and the terms of the available alternatives.
cc4958c1c4a28bc94010a69d1cbbb8bf2aa162ca.zh: 较大的后期付款与今天的现金无法直接比较。将两种选择放在一个日期，显示隐含的年利率，并分别检查付款可靠性和访问权限。写出两种选择，而不是一种合并余额 该示例提供了两张收据之一：今天的 20,000 加元或三年后的单笔 24,000 加元付款。接受一个就意味着放弃另一个。将它们添加到 44,000 加元的家庭资源中将算作一种替代方案，而这种替代方案是无法与第一种方案并列的。名义差额为 4,000 加元，即即时金额的 20%。这 20% 涵盖了整个三年的等待时间。这不是20%的年回报率。日期是比较的一部分，就像金额一样。 CFA 协会的公开时间价值概述将当前价值、未来现金流和隐含回报联系起来。在这里，计算器将这些原则应用到一个简单的原始示例中，每个选项下都需要一笔付款。将后来的收入转换为今天测量的值 令 L 为后来的付款，r 为分数形式的有效年度比较率，n 为年数。现值为PV = L ÷ (1+r) n 。这会在实际等待期内对后来的金额进行折扣。按照默认的 5% 比较率，24,000 加元除以 1.05³ 大约等于 20,732.10 加元。与今天的 20,000 加元相比，现值差异约为 732.10 加元，有利于根据所述假设稍后收到。该价值不是账户中已持有的存款。根据选定的估值基础，这相当于今天的价格。家庭不能仅仅因为计算器显示现值而发送 20,732.10 加元来支付较早的账单。贴现率曲线显示哪种假设会改变答案 第一个图表以 0% 到 20% 的利率重新计算后来收据的现值。眼前的20,000加元仍然是横向比较。在零利率下，后来的收据的现值等于其面值 24,000 加元。随着利率上升，其现值下降。交叉很有用，因为它确定了两个估值相等的比率。低于该比率，较晚的收据具有更大的现值。高于它，即时现金具有更大的现值。这些报表适用于这些固定金额和日期，并假定全额付款。选择的利率需要一个理由。它可能代表在一致现金基础上独立评估的机会成本，但计算器无法识别可用存款、可实现的投资回报或适当的风险溢价。仅通过在此输入其平均回报率，无法将不确定的投资预测转变为有保证的替代方案。将两种替代方案向前移动会产生相同的顺序。共同日期栏在第三年年底而不是今天进行比较。将 20,000 加元按 5% 的利率计算三年后，得到 23,152.50 加元。另一种较晚收据为 24,000 加元，未来日期差额为 847.50 加元。目前的差异是 732.10 加元，而不是 847.50 加元。这两个数字使用不同的日期。将未四舍五入的现值差值乘以 1.05³ 可将其转换为未来日期差值。它不会创造额外的利润来源。这些条假设立即收据仍按输入的固定利率进行投资，没有提款。如果现金用于生活费用，则未来的余额将会有所不同。实际支出可能满足实际需求，但不能同时保持可用于以后比较的复合效果。求解年利率，而不是用 20% 除以 3 盈亏平衡年利率求解现在现金 × (1+r*) n = 以后现金 。重新排列后得到 r* = (后来的现金 ÷ 现在的现金) 1/n − 1 。对于三年后的 20,000 加元和 24,000 加元，结果约为每年有效 6.26586%。以该速度复利三年可产生 20% 的累计增长。将 20% 除以 3 得到的简单平均值约为 6.67%，这不能保留复合方程。该利率由两个提供的金额及其时间暗示。它不是单独赚取的优惠券，也不是任何人都会支付的保证。加州均衡委员会的时间价值摘要将复利和贴现解释为日期之间的相反运动。此示例在两个方向上一致地使用年度有效复利。测试较长延迟时，保持未来金额固定。矩阵会更改等待时间和比较率，同时保留相同的两个收据金额。每个单元格都会报告后来收据的现值减去立即现金的替代方案。在此练习中，较长的等待时间不会自动获得较大的付款。从正的角度来看，推迟相同的未来金额会降低其现值。在零比率下，更改等待时间会使现值金额保持不变，但实际可用日期仍然会变化。这将估值计算与资金到达之前使用资金的实际需要分开。该矩阵的单元格没有附加概率。它不会预测发生的日期或比率。它有助于揭示结论是否强烈依赖于短暂的延迟或特定的估值率。盈亏平衡率可能超出绘制范围 如果两个名义金额相同，则它们的隐含盈亏平衡率为零。如果后来的金额小于立即的金额，则隐含利率为负。然后，非负比较率将有利于在这个狭窄的估值基础上的即时金额。短期内较大的后期金额可能意味着盈亏平衡率高于图表 20% 的上限。该指标仍然报告计算出的比率，而图表仅显示其规定的 0% 到 20% 范围。可见图表内不应发明交叉点。这些数学控制有助于解释输出，而不会将异常的隐含利率视为存在高回报产品的证据。实际报价的法律条款、付款来源和可靠性需要自己的证据。将估价恢复到家庭规定的日期 六个月内到期的账单不能直接用三年后收到的收据来支付。正的现值差异不会提供过桥贷款、改变账单的到期日或使后来的承诺可转让。计算器不包括这些安排。在相同的税收和成本基础上比较实际净收入。该模型不计算税收、费用、通货膨胀或违约损失。它也不会将名义未来现金转换为通货膨胀调整后的购买力；添加这样的比较需要一致的实际现金和实际利率计算。确认哪些收据是互斥的以及每张收据​​何时可用。将其金额按一致的净现金基础计算。记录比较率的原因。检查当前日期和常见的未来日期值。分别审查付款可靠性和早期现金义务。结果是透明的估值比较。该选择仍然必须支持实际的付款日历和可用替代方案的条款。

0df8d6a189dbe503c7bd672180743fe015d18324.src: A loss inside a TFSA is not a withdrawal. A later ordinary withdrawal adds back the amount actually withdrawn next year, rather than automatically restoring the original contribution. Keep value, cash movements and contribution room in separate records A TFSA can have one account value and a different amount of unused contribution room. An investment loss changes the value of what is held. A withdrawal moves money out. The room record follows the applicable contribution and withdrawal rules, rather than simply mirroring the account balance. CRA’s contribution guidance states that investment-value changes do not affect TFSA contribution room and that an investment loss does not count as a withdrawal. The loss itself is not added back as room. The tool begins just after one assumed lawful contribution. Its unused-room input is already reconciled across the holder’s TFSAs after that contribution. It does not establish eligibility or reconstruct anyone’s full contribution history. Follow the investment change before making any withdrawal The default opening contribution is CAD 10,000, assumed permitted using previously available room. A 20% investment decline reduces the account value by CAD 2,000 to CAD 8,000. No money has been withdrawn at this stage. The room amount entered after the opening contribution remains unchanged. With the default of zero unused room, the loss does not create a new CAD 2,000 deposit allowance. Replacing the lost value with new money would require room available for that contribution through the applicable record. The waterfall shows only the value arithmetic: CAD 10,000 minus CAD 2,000 equals CAD 8,000. It does not record the loss as a cash payment to the holder or a transaction that restores contribution capacity. Use the amount actually withdrawn for the next-year addback The default then withdraws 100% of the remaining CAD 8,000 as an ordinary withdrawal. Account value falls to zero and CAD 8,000 becomes cash held outside the TFSA. Under the reviewed ordinary-withdrawal framework, that CAD 8,000 is the amount added back as room on the next 1 January. CRA’s withdrawal guidance explains that an ordinary withdrawal does not create new room immediately. Re-contributing during the same calendar year requires sufficient unused room already available. The related calendar guide examines that timing constraint in more detail. The withdrawal-based addback in this example is CAD 2,000 below the original CAD 10,000 contribution. That comparison concerns this selected withdrawal only. It is not a complete next-year contribution limit, a required deposit or an estimate of how much the investment could later recover. Room returning does not restore money lost The stacked bars track financial resources separately from the room bars. Before the withdrawal, CAD 8,000 is inside the account. Afterward, CAD 8,000 is outside as retained cash. The total is unchanged by the withdrawal because the model assumes no fees or spending. On the next 1 January, the ordinary withdrawal affects the room record, but there is still only CAD 8,000 of financial resources in this illustration. Adding the room amount to the cash amount as though both were assets would count permission to contribute as money. Rebuilding wealth requires investment changes or additional saving. The model does not project a recovery or recommend keeping, selling or replacing an investment. Its purpose is to keep the value and room calculations from being confused. Test partial withdrawals and gains without changing the rule Change the withdrawal share to 50% while keeping the default 20% decline. The ordinary withdrawal is then CAD 4,000, with CAD 4,000 still in the TFSA. The withdrawal-based next-year addback is CAD 4,000, not the whole remaining account value and not the original contribution. Now try a 20% investment gain and a full ordinary withdrawal. The account reaches CAD 12,000, and the assumed withdrawal is CAD 12,000. The gain alone did not change room while it remained invested; the amount actually withdrawn is what enters this ordinary-withdrawal addback illustration. The matrix combines several value changes and withdrawal shares. Every cell holds the original contribution fixed and calculates the assumed withdrawal after the selected move. It contains neither a future annual dollar limit nor probabilities for market outcomes. Complete the room calculation with the actual record before contributing The room chart deliberately excludes the new calendar year’s annual dollar limit. It also excludes other contributions, withdrawals, transfers and adjustments. Its final bar is only a subtotal of carried unused room plus this one ordinary withdrawal. For example, entering CAD 3,000 of unused room after the original contribution would leave that amount unchanged by the market decline and the same-year withdrawal. Adding the default CAD 8,000 ordinary withdrawal next year produces a CAD 11,000 subtotal before the omitted annual limit and any other adjustments. CRA recommends reconciling contribution room using the holder’s own records. The model assumes Canadian residency and eligibility throughout, and it excludes specified distributions, transfer treatment, excess histories and other special situations. Use the applicable full record rather than an account value or this partial illustration before making a real contribution.
0df8d6a189dbe503c7bd672180743fe015d18324.zh: TFSA 内的损失不是提款。以后的普通提款会加回明年实际提款的金额，而不是自动恢复原来的捐款额。将价值、现金变动和供款空间保存在单独的记录中 TFSA 可以有一个账户价值和不同数量的未使用供款空间。投资损失会改变所持有资产的价值。提款将资金移出。房间记录遵循适用的供款和提款规则，而不是简单地反映账户余额。 CRA 的供款指南规定，投资价值变化不会影响 TFSA 供款空间，并且投资损失不算作提款。损失本身不会作为空间加回。该工具在一项假定的合法贡献后立即启动。在该贡献之后，其未使用房间的投入已经在持有人的 TFSA 之间进行了调节。它不会建立资格或重建任何人的完整贡献历史。在进行任何提款之前，请遵循投资变更的规定 默认开仓资金为 10,000 加元，假设允许使用先前的可用空间。投资下降 20% 会使账户价值减少 2,000 加元至 8,000 加元。现阶段尚未提取任何资金。开仓贡献后输入的房间金额保持不变。由于默认未使用房间为零，因此损失不会产生新的 2,000 加元押金津贴。用新资金弥补损失的价值需要通过适用的记录为该贡献提供空间。瀑布仅显示价值算术：10,000 加元减去 2,000 加元等于 8,000 加元。它不会将损失记录为向持有人支付的现金或恢复贡献能力的交易。使用实际提取的金额用于下一年的加回默认然后提取剩余 8,000 加元的 100% 作为普通提取。账户价值降至零，8,000 加元成为 TFSA 之外持有的现金。根据审查后的普通提款框架，8,000 加元是在下一个 1 月 1 日作为空间加回的金额。 CRA 的提款指南解释说，普通提款不会立即创建新房间。在同一日历年内重新捐款需要已有足够的未使用空间。相关的日历指南更详细地检查了时间限制。本例中基于提款的加回金额比原始 10,000 加元的贡献低 2,000 加元。该比较仅涉及此选定的提款。它不是完整的明年供款限额、所需存款或对以后可以收回投资金额的估计。返还房间并不能挽回损失的金钱 堆积的条形图与房间条形图分开跟踪财务资源。提款前，账户内有8000加元。随后，8,000 加元作为保留现金存入外部。提款后的总额不会改变，因为该模型假设没有费用或支出。次年1月1日，普通提款影响房间记录，但本图中的财力仍然只有8000加元。将房间金额加到现金金额上，就好像两者都是资产一样，将允许捐款视为金钱。重建财富需要改变投资或增加储蓄。该模型不预测复苏或建议保留、出售或更换投资。其目的是防止价值和房间计算混淆。在不改变规则的情况下测试部分提款和收益将提款份额更改为 50%，同时保持默认的 20% 跌幅。普通提款为 4,000 加元，其中 4,000 加元仍在 TFSA 中。基于提款的明年加回金额为 4,000 加元，不是全部剩余账户价值，也不是原始捐款。现在尝试 20% 的投资收益和全额普通提款。账户达到12,000加元，假设提款为12,000加元。仅收益并没有改变空间，同时仍保持投资；实际提取的金额就是这个普通提取加回说明中的内容。该矩阵结合了几个价值变化和撤回份额。每个单元格都保持固定的原始贡献，并计算所选移动后的假设撤资。它既不包含未来的年度美元限额，也不包含市场结果的概率。在贡献之前用实际记录完成房间计算房间图表故意排除了新日历年的年度美元限额。它还不包括其他供款、提款、转移和调整。它的最后一栏只是持有未使用房间的小计加上这一普通提款。例如，在原始捐款后输入 3,000 加元的未使用房间，该金额将因市场下跌和同年撤资而保持不变。加上明年默认的 8,000 加元普通提款，在省略年度限额和任何其他调整之前，小计为 11,000 加元。 CRA 建议使用持有人自己的记录来调节供款空间。该模型自始至终假设加拿大居民和资格，并且不包括特定的分配、转移待遇、超额历史和其他特殊情况。在做出真正的贡献之前，请使用适用的完整记录，而不是账户价值或部分说明。

b84a7870b8db43e8c4511506be13dd337bf55dc9.src: A maturity date gives a choice about principal. If that principal is reinvested, the same dollars are unavailable for spending, and the new interest income still depends on the renewal rate. Distinguish a guaranteed term from an unknown renewal rate A fixed rate for one deposit term does not specify the rate available when that term ends. A plan that intends to reinvest principal needs a separate assumption for the next contract. The Ontario Securities Commission’s investor-education guide describes reinvestment risk as the possibility of reinvesting principal or income at a lower rate. This article isolates principal renewal while interest is paid out for spending. It makes no prediction about future market rates. A ladder spreads initial maturity dates across several years. That changes when different parts of principal encounter the renewal assumption. It does not lock every later term at today’s selected rate or turn an entered future rate into a guarantee. Write the five-rung schedule before counting the receipts The example divides CAD 50,000 equally into five CAD 10,000 rungs. Their initial terms mature at the ends of years one, two, three, four and five. All five initially pay 4% in annual cash interest, even though the terms differ. That equal-rate starting point is a teaching assumption, not a set of available quotes. At each maturity, the whole CAD 10,000 principal is immediately renewed for five years at the selected 2%. One rung therefore matures each year, including years six through ten. Later renewals use the same 2% assumption, with no new rate scenario introduced. OSC’s GIC explanation describes staggered maturities and choices at maturity, including reinvestment or taking cash. Here renewal is an explicit instruction in the model. The charts do not infer an actual bank’s automatic-renewal terms. Keep the old rate through the final year of its original term Year one receives five interest payments of CAD 400, for CAD 2,000 in total. The first rung matures only after paying that year’s interest. Its renewed rate therefore begins contributing to the cash schedule in year two. Year two has four original payments of CAD 400 and one renewed payment of CAD 200, totaling CAD 1,800. Year three has three original and two renewed payments, totaling CAD 1,600. The later totals are CAD 1,400 in year four and CAD 1,200 in year five. In year six all five rungs pay CAD 200, so annual interest is CAD 1,000. With every later renewal held at 2%, income stays at that level through year ten. The composition chart explains the transition rather than implying that all the original 4% income disappears at the first maturity. Do not spend the same matured principal that the model renews Each year CAD 10,000 comes due and is immediately committed to another five-year term. It is a return and reinvestment of principal, not new interest earned. Counting it as spending money while also retaining the renewed rung would create resources twice. Across ten years the schedule rolls CAD 100,000 of gross maturity principal. That does not mean the household began with CAD 100,000 or earned that much. The original CAD 50,000 is being reused as different rungs reach maturity again. Nominal principal remains CAD 50,000 throughout this illustration, while total interest paid outside it is CAD 13,000. That interest is a distinct stream. The tool does not compound it back into the ladder, assume access to locked principal, or replace a spending shortfall with a redemption. Put the interest income beside the spending assigned to it The selected annual cash need is CAD 2,000, received interest arrives before that year’s spending, and the outside reserve starts at CAD 1,000. Year one uses its CAD 2,000 interest without drawing the reserve. Later income falls while the assigned need stays fixed. The first gaps are CAD 200, CAD 400 and CAD 600 in years two, three and four. Outside cash is therefore CAD 800, CAD 400 and negative CAD 200 after those years. An unchanged principal does not remove that spending shortage. By the end of year ten, cumulative gaps total CAD 7,000: CAD 20,000 of assigned spending less CAD 13,000 of interest. The required outside opening reserve is CAD 7,000, while the entered CAD 1,000 leaves CAD 6,000 still to fund. The matrix varies renewal rates and annual needs to show how that requirement changes. Holding the initial 4% and CAD 2,000 annual need unchanged, a 1% renewal assumption requires CAD 10,500 outside the ladder. A 3% assumption requires CAD 3,500. Both cases preserve the same CAD 50,000 of nominal principal. The difference comes from thirty-five renewed rung-years across the ten-year window: one extra percentage point on each CAD 10,000 rung supplies CAD 3,500 more interest in total. That is a sensitivity of the selected calendar, rather than a claim that a higher rate will be available. These annual points also simplify payment timing. An interest deposit at year-end cannot pay a bill due months earlier. A real implementation needs exact interest dates, a within-year cash calendar and a separate review of whether preserving every rung’s principal remains appropriate. Review the actual maturity instructions and the wider plan FCAC’s GIC rights guide identifies information about the term, principal repayment, interest payments and renewal conditions that applicable federally regulated institutions must disclose. Read the new rate and instructions before treating a maturity as a continuation of the same income. The tool excludes tax, inflation, fees, issuer failure, insurance eligibility and any market value before maturity. The nominal principal line is therefore not proof of maintained purchasing power, complete protection or personal suitability. The interest figures are before tax, and annual spending does not rise with prices. Record the intended job of each maturity: renewal, spending or another goal. Then use the corresponding cash treatment consistently. Stress the rate that would fund the next term, and keep reserves already assigned to other bills separate. A ladder is a schedule to manage, rather than a promise that its first year’s income continues indefinitely.
b84a7870b8db43e8c4511506be13dd337bf55dc9.zh: 到期日可以选择本金。如果该本金被再投资，则同样的美元将无法用于支出，并且新的利息收入仍然取决于续订率。区分保证期限和未知续订利率 一个存款期限的固定利率并不指定该期限结束时可用的利率。打算对本金进行再投资的计划需要对下一份合同进行单独的假设。安大略省证券委员会的投资者教育指南将再投资风险描述为以较低利率再投资本金或收入的可能性。本文将本金更新与支出利息分开。它不对未来市场利率做出预测。阶梯将初始到期日期分散在几年内。当委托人的不同部分遇到更新假设时，情况就会发生变化。它不会将每个后续期限锁定为今天选择的利率，也不会将输入的未来利率转变为保证。在清点收据之前写下五级明细表 该示例将 50,000 加元平均分为 5 个 10,000 加元的梯级。他们的初始任期在第一年、第二年、第三年、第四年和第五年结束时到期。尽管条款不同，这五家公司最初都支付 4% 的年现金利息。等利率起点是一个教学假设，而不是一组可用的报价。每次到期时，全部 10,000 加元本金会立即按选定的 2% 续期五年。因此，每年都有一个梯级成熟，包括第六年到第十年。后来的续约使用相同的 2% 假设，没有引入新的费率方案。 OSC 的 GIC 解释描述了交错到期日和到期时的选择，包括再投资或提取现金。这里的更新是模型中的明确指令。这些图表并不推断实际银行的自动续订条款。在原期限的最后一年保持旧利率不变，第一年将收到五笔利息，金额为 400 加元，总计 2,000 加元。第一级仅在支付当年利息后到期。因此，更新后的利率开始对第二年的现金计划做出贡献。第二年有四笔 400 加元的原始付款和一笔 200 加元的续付款，总计 1,800 加元。第三年有三笔原始付款和两笔更新付款，总计 1,600 加元。随后的第四年总计为 1,400 加元，第五年总计为 1,200 加元。第六年，所有五个梯级均需支付 200 加元，因此年利息为 1,000 加元。后来每次续约都保持在 2% 的水平，收入在第十年都保持在这个水平。构成图解释了这种转变，而不是暗示所有原始 4% 收入在第一个到期日消失。不要花费与模型更新相同的到期本金 每年 10,000 加元到期，并立即承诺另一个五年期限。这是本金的回报和再投资，而不是新赚取的利息。将其算作支出，同时保留更新的梯级将创造两倍的资源。该计划在十年内滚动到期本金总额 100,000 加元。这并不意味着该家庭一开始的收入为 10 万加元，或者收入达到了这么多。随着不同级别再次成熟，最初的 50,000 加元将被重新使用。在整个图中，名义本金仍为 50,000 加元，而在其之外支付的总利息为 13,000 加元。这种兴趣是一个独特的流。该工具不会将其重新组合到阶梯中，不会获取锁定的本金，也不会通过赎回来弥补支出缺口。将利息收入放在分配给它的支出旁边选定的年度现金需求为 2,000 加元，收到的利息在当年支出之前到达，外部储备金从 1,000 加元开始。第一年使用 2,000 加元利息，无需提取准备金。后来的收入下降，而分配的需求保持不变。第一个差距是第二年、第三年和第四年的 200 加元、400 加元和 600 加元。因此，这些年之后，外部现金为 800 加元、400 加元和负 200 加元。本金不变并不能消除支出短缺。到第十年年底，累计缺口总计 7,000 加元：指定支出 20,000 加元减去利息 13,000 加元。所需的外部开仓准备金为 7,000 加元，而输入的 1,000 加元还剩下 6,000 加元。该矩阵会改变续订率和年度需求，以显示该要求如何变化。保持最初的 4% 和每年 2,000 加元的需求不变，1% 的更新假设需要阶梯外 10,500 加元。 3% 的假设需要 3,500 加元。两种情况均保留相同的 50,000 加元名义本金。差异来自于十年窗口内 35 个更新的梯级年数：每 10,000 加元梯级增加一个百分点，总共会增加 3,500 加元的利息。这是所选日历的敏感性，而不是声称将提供更高的费率。这些年度积分还简化了付款时间。年底的利息存款无法支付几个月前到期的账单。真正的实施需要准确的利息日期、年内现金日历以及单独审查保留每个级别的本金是否仍然合适。查看实际到期说明和更广泛的计划 FCAC 的 GIC 权利指南确定了适用的联邦监管机构必须披露的有关期限、本金偿还、利息支付和续订条件的信息。在将到期视为相同收入的延续之前，请阅读新的利率和说明。该工具不包括税收、通货膨胀、费用、发行人失败、保险资格以及到期前的任何市场价值。因此，名义主线并不能证明维持购买力、完整的保护或个人适合性。利息数据为税前数据，年度支出不会随物价上涨而增加。记录每个到期日的预期工作：更新、支出或其他目标。然后一致使用相应的现金处理。强调为下一期提供资金的利率，并将已分配给其他法案的准备金分开。阶梯是一个管理时间表，而不是第一年收入无限期持续的承诺。

1b45588d59bf8fc1a5305d2965760f53da934293.src: Expected repair cost, a payable benefit and the cash needed in an actual failure are three different amounts. A contract price buys only the protection its terms actually add. Start with the protection window and the protection you already have A checkout offer can make an extended warranty sound like a simple comparison between a small price now and a large repair later. The useful comparison is more specific: which repair, during which period, under which conditions, and how much of that repair would this extra contract actually fund? The Government of Canada’s warranty guide distinguishes included manufacturer protection from extra-cost extended coverage and asks consumers to review terms, repair costs and possible credit-card overlap. A purchased contract should therefore be evaluated for its additional protection rather than credited with every repair benefit associated with owning the product. This tool uses one common comparison window and a deliberately simplified event structure. There is either no modeled repair, one eligible repair, or one excluded repair. A repair has the same entered cost in the two repair states. The product purchase price is common to both alternatives and excluded. Existing legal, manufacturer and card protection are outside the calculation; the example does not decide anyone’s rights or whether a claim meets a real contract. Separate the chance of a repair from the chance that a repair is eligible The default repair-event probability is an assumed 40% over the entire comparison window. The assumed eligible share is 70% of those repair events. Multiplying them gives a 28% eligible-event probability. The excluded-event probability is 40% × 30%, or 12%, and the no-repair probability is 60%. These are original teaching inputs, not a product failure study, a claim-approval statistic or an annual risk estimate. A different window, product age or definition of an eligible event would need its own evidence and assumptions. The model does not automatically convert a multi-year event probability into an annual rate. The first chart keeps the denominator visible. “70% eligible” refers to the repair branch, not to every product bought. Treating it as a 70% chance of receiving a payment would confuse a conditional share with the overall probability. Even an eligible event can produce a zero payment if the deductible absorbs the entire repair cost. Apply the deductible and payment cap before valuing the contract The example repair costs CAD 800. The owner deductible is CAD 50, leaving CAD 750 before the cap. The provider-payment cap is CAD 500, so the modeled payment is CAD 500, not CAD 750 and not the full CAD 800. The owner retains CAD 300 of repair cost even in the eligible state. The precise convention matters. This illustration defines the cap as a maximum provider payment after subtracting the deductible: payment = min(cap, max(0, repair cost − deductible)) . It does not model a policy that first caps eligible repair charges and then subtracts a deductible. Read an actual contract before using either interpretation. Raising the entered cap beyond CAD 750 cannot increase the default eligible payment because there is no more modeled eligible cost left to fund. Likewise, if the deductible reaches or exceeds the repair cost, the modeled payment becomes zero. A large number printed as a limit is not automatically a large economic benefit. Keep the upfront price in every outcome The contract costs CAD 180 at the start, with no refund in this illustration. If no repair occurs, the owner pays zero repair cost without the extra contract and CAD 180 with it. In the eligible repair state, the comparison is CAD 800 without the contract versus CAD 480 with it: CAD 180 plus the CAD 300 repair remainder. In the excluded repair state, the owner pays CAD 800 without the contract and CAD 980 with it. The extra contract has not removed that repair exposure, and its initial price has already been spent. These bars show total nominal owner cost over the comparison window, not an estimate of an average bill. They also do not show peak cash needed. A provider that reimburses later can leave the owner paying a larger invoice first. Repair timing, claims processing, downtime and shipping are excluded from the arithmetic. Those operational terms need a separate cash-access review even when a final payment is expected. Reconcile the expected cost without turning it into a reserve target Without the contract, expected repair cost is 40% × CAD 800, or CAD 320. The expected provider payment is 40% × 70% × CAD 500, or CAD 140. Expected owner cost with the contract is therefore CAD 180 + CAD 320 − CAD 140 = CAD 360, which is CAD 40 higher than the no-contract expected cost. The waterfall makes the certain price and the contingent payment separate steps. A CAD 140 expected provider payment does not mean the provider pays CAD 140 when a repair occurs. In this restricted model, it pays either zero or CAD 500. Likewise, setting aside CAD 320 does not fully fund the possible CAD 800 repair. Expected cost is one comparison, not a complete decision rule. A household may value reducing a particular cash exposure, convenience or service support, but those features need evidence in the actual offer. The tool places no dollar value on them and does not identify a contract that should be purchased. Read the crossover as an assumption threshold, not a reliability estimate Let W be the upfront contract price, p the whole-window repair probability, q the eligible share and P the provider payment in an eligible event. Expected extra owner cost is W − p × q × P . If qP is positive, cost equality occurs at p = W ÷ (qP) . At the defaults, CAD 180 ÷ (70% × CAD 500) gives about 51.43%. That threshold is above the selected 40% assumption. It does not show that the product’s actual repair probability is 51.43%, and it is not evidence for moving the probability input to make an offer look attractive. A threshold above 100% cannot be reached within this single-event model. If no provider payment is available, a positive contract price cannot be recovered through modeled payments at any event probability. A zero-price, zero-payment contract ties the repair-cost baseline at every probability. These boundary cases are stated explicitly beside the charts. Use the charts to ask better questions about the offer Define the comparison period and remove benefits already provided by other protection. Read the deductible, payment limit, eligible repairs and claim process in the actual terms. Keep the failure probability and conditional eligibility assumption separate. Compare the actual failure-state cash with the probability-weighted average. Test a lower eligible share and a smaller payment cap before interpreting the crossover. The matrix changes eligibility and the payment cap while holding the selected repair probability fixed. Its signed cells report extra expected owner cost, so a negative value means lower modeled cost with the contract. It is not a product rating or a probability forecast. Multiple repairs, replacement instead of repair, depreciation, financing and the opportunity cost of the upfront price require a fuller model.
1b45588d59bf8fc1a5305d2965760f53da934293.zh: 预期维修成本、应付福利和实际故障所需的现金是三个不同的金额。合同价格仅购买其条款实际增加的保护。从保护窗口和您已有的保护开始结账优惠可以使延长保修听起来像是现在的小价格和以后的大修理之间的简单比较。有用的比较是更具体的：哪次维修、在什么时期、在什么条件下，以及这份额外合同实际资助的维修金额是多少？加拿大政府的保修指南将制造商保护与额外费用的扩展保修区分开来，并要求消费者审查条款、维修成本和可能的信用卡重叠。因此，应评估购买的合同是否具有额外的保护，而不是计入与拥有产品相关的所有维修权益。该工具使用一个通用比较窗口和一种特意简化的事件结构。要么没有建模维修，要么有一项符合条件的维修，要么有一项被排除的维修。维修在两种维修状态下具有相同的输入成本。产品购买价格对于两种替代品来说都是相同的，并且被排除在外。现有的法律、制造商和卡保护不在计算范围内；该示例并不决定任何人的权利或索赔是否符合真正的合同。将修复的可能性与修复合格的可能性分开 默认修复事件概率在整个比较窗口中假设为 40%。假定合格份额为这些维修事件的 70%。将它们相乘得出合格事件概率为 28%。排除事件概率为 40% × 30%，即 12%，不修复概率为 60%。这些是原始的教学投入，而不是产品故障研究、索赔批准统计数据或年度风险评估。不同的窗口、产品年龄或合格事件的定义需要有自己的证据和假设。该模型不会自动将多年事件概率转换为年率。第一个图表使分母可见。 “70%合格”是指维修部门，而不是购买的所有产品。如果将其视为收到付款的概率为 70%，则会将条件份额与总体概率混淆。如果免赔额吸收了全部维修费用，即使符合条件的事件也可以产生零付款。在评估合同之前应用免赔额和付款上限。示例维修费用为 800 加元。业主免赔额为 50 加元，在上限之前保留 750 加元。提供商付款上限为 500 加元，因此模拟付款为 500 加元，而不是 750 加元，也不是全额 800 加元。即使在符合条件的州，业主也保留 300 加元的维修费用。精确的约定很重要。此图将上限定义为减去免赔额后的最高提供商付款： payment = min(cap, max(0, Repair cost − deductible)) 。它并没有建立一个首先限制合格维修费用然后减去免赔额的保单。在使用任何一种解释之前，请先阅读实际的合同。将输入的上限提高到 750 加元以上并不能增加默认的合格付款，因为没有更多的建模合格成本可供资助。同样，如果免赔额达到或超过维修成本，则模型付款将变为零。大量打印作为限制并不会自动带来巨大的经济效益。在每个结果中保留预付费用 合同一开始的费用为 180 加元，在此插图中不予退款。如果没有维修，业主支付零维修费用，无需额外合同和 180 加元。在符合条件的维修状态下，比较结果为无合同的 800 加元与有合同的 480 加元：180 加元加上 300 加元的维修剩余费用。在排除维修状态下，业主在无合同的情况下支付 800 加元，在有合同的情况下支付 980 加元。额外的合同并没有消除维修风险，而且其最初的价格已经花掉了。这些条形显示比较窗口内的总名义所有者成本，而不是平均账单的估计值。他们也没有显示所需现金的峰值。稍后报销的提供商可以让业主先支付较大的发票。维修时间、索赔处理、停机时间和运输不包含在计算中。即使预计最终付款，这些运营条款也需要单独的现金获取审查。调节预期成本，但不将其变成储备目标 如果没有合同，预计维修成本为 40% × 800 加元，或 320 加元。预期提供商付款为 40% × 70% × 500 加元，或 140 加元。因此，签订合同后的预期所有者成本为 CAD 180 + CAD 320 − CAD 140 = CAD 360，比实际情况高出 40 加元无合同预期成本。瀑布使确定价格和或有付款成为分开的步骤。提供商预计支付 140 加元并不意味着提供商在维修时支付 140 加元。在这个受限模型中，它要么支付零，要么支付 500 加元。同样，拨出 320 加元并不能完全为可能的 800 加元维修提供资金。预期成本只是一种比较，而不是完整的决策规则。家庭可能会重视减少特定的现金敞口、便利或服务支持，但这些功能需要在实际报价中提供证据。该工具没有对它们赋予任何美元价值，也没有识别应该购买的合同。将交叉视为假设阈值，而不是可靠性估计 令 W 为前期合同价格，p 为整个窗口修复概率，q 为合格份额，P 为合格事件中的提供商付款。预期额外所有者成本为 W − p × q × P 。如果 qP 为正，则成本相等的情况为 p = W ÷ (qP) 。默认情况下，CAD 180 ÷ (70% × CAD 500) 得出的结果约为 51.43%。该阈值高于选定的 40% 假设。它没有显示产品的实际修复概率为 51.43%，也不是移动概率输入以使报价看起来有吸引力的证据。在此单事件模型中无法达到高于 100% 的阈值。如果没有可用的提供商付款，则在任何事件概率下都无法通过建模付款来恢复正合同价格。零价格、零付款的合同尽可能地与维修成本基线挂钩。这些边界情况在图表旁边明确说明。使用图表提出有关该优惠的更好问题 定义比较期并删除其他保护已提供的福利。请阅读实际条款中的免赔额、付款限额、合格维修和索赔流程。将失败概率和条件资格假设分开。将实际故障状态现金与概率加权平均值进行比较。在解释交叉之前，测试较低的合格份额和较小的支付上限。该矩阵会更改资格和付款上限，同时保持选定的维修概率固定。其签署的单元报告了额外的预期所有者成本，因此负值意味着合同的建模成本较低。它不是产品评级或概率预测。多次维修、以更换代替维修、折旧、融资和预付款的机会成本需要更完整的模型。

787c1f0bb83e987fdc679ee9b06d5d3e276f54e3.src: A refund promise changes a cancellation outcome, while the higher price still has to be funded immediately. Check the contract and the cash calendar before interpreting an average cost. Define whose cancellation and which refund the comparison assumes A booking can have several different cancellation situations. This exercise considers a traveler choosing to cancel before using a booking, with the seller accepting an eligible cash refund under the assumed contract. It does not calculate rights when a supplier cancels or changes the service. The Canadian Transportation Agency’s traveler tips recommend reading ticket rules and the tariff, including restrictions and penalties. A broad label such as “flexible” does not supply the exact percentage, fee, deadline or payment form needed by a cash calculation. If the contract returns only a travel credit, that amount cannot simply be inserted as a cash refund. Check what it can purchase, any expiry or transfer restrictions, and whether using it requires another payment. A credit reserved for a future trip also cannot pay an unrelated household bill while the family waits. Every price and refund in these charts is hypothetical. Before using an actual quote, identify the amount refundable, conditions for cancellation, any deduction and whether repayment means cash or a restricted credit. The model accepts cash refunds only and makes no finding about a real booking’s legal terms. Keep the used-booking and cancellation branches separate The default lower-priced booking costs CAD 1,800 and has no modeled refund for an eligible voluntary cancellation. The alternative costs CAD 2,100: a CAD 300 premium. It refunds 100% of its price less CAD 100 retained from that refund. If the booking is used, the cash costs are CAD 1,800 and CAD 2,100. If the traveler cancels under the assumed eligible conditions, they remain CAD 1,800 for the lower-priced contract and become CAD 100 for the alternative. The alternative’s net refund is 2,100 − 100 = CAD 2,000 . The first chart shows those two branches rather than adding them. It also avoids counting the retained amount twice: the CAD 100 has already reduced the refund. The formula floors a refund at zero, so a large retained fee cannot generate another bill in this illustration. A real contract that charges an additional amount needs a different cash model. Treat the cancellation chance as an uncertain assumption The probability control starts at 20%. It is chosen for the example, not estimated from travelers, destinations, health information or a booking provider. Moving the control tests a different assumption; it does not make the chosen probability more reliable. Probability-weighted cost equals the used-booking cost times the chance of using it, plus the cancellation cost times the assumed chance of cancelling. The same calculation can be written price − probability × net refund . At 20%, the default lower-priced booking remains CAD 1,800. The alternative becomes 2,100 − 0.20 × 2,000 = CAD 1,700 . One actual booking does not produce an automatic CAD 1,700 invoice: under these assumptions, the alternative costs either CAD 2,100 if used or CAD 100 if cancelled with the refund received. Read a crossing as arithmetic, rather than a decision rule In the default comparison, the alternative costs CAD 300 more initially and returns CAD 2,000 more if an eligible cancellation occurs. Equal probability-weighted costs occur at 300 ÷ 2,000 = 15% . Below that assumed chance, its weighted cost is higher; above it, lower. The matrix changes the premium and the cancellation assumption. A different premium also changes the alternative’s price and therefore the base used by its refund percentage. Holding that refund fixed while changing the full-refundable price would compare inconsistent contracts. Other inputs can remove a crossing from the 0–100% range. Two contracts can also have equal weighted costs at every assumption. The tool reports those cases directly rather than displaying an impossible probability as a personal forecast. Money is only one part of a booking choice. The comparison assigns no value to the trip, schedule certainty, convenience, provider reliability or flexibility beyond the stated cash refund. An average-cost equality cannot determine how much a particular household values avoiding a large cancellation loss. Fund the premium before relying on the later refund Both bookings are paid in full at time zero. With CAD 2,500 assigned to the purchase, the lower-priced choice leaves CAD 700 and the alternative CAD 400 immediately. The conditional cash chart assumes cancellation in month two and refund two months later. The alternative’s cash stays at CAD 400 until month four, then rises by CAD 2,000 to CAD 2,400. The lower-priced path stays at CAD 700 because its modeled refund is zero. These lines condition on the cancellation branch; they are not the probability-weighted averages from the previous chart. A longer refund wait delays the recovery without changing these undiscounted endpoint costs. Reducing initial cash to CAD 2,000 produces a CAD 100 upfront shortage under the alternative, even though a large refund might arrive later. The calculator labels that shortage without assuming a credit-card advance, asset sale or help from another goal. Keep a refund clause separate from insurance and the rest of the trip Travel.gc.ca distinguishes trip cancellation coverage from trip interruption and medical coverage and emphasizes reviewing policy terms, conditions, exclusions and requirements. A booking’s refund clause and a separate insurance policy need their own review. No insurance premium or claim is included here. Nor are vouchers, exchange rates, rebooking costs, partially used travel, meals, accommodation or other prepaid commitments. A refund for one item cannot be assumed to repair the entire trip budget. For a real plan, list each payment and its cancellation conditions, record the required notice date, and keep confirmation of the promised repayment form. Put any expected cash receipt on its own date. Use a range of cancellation assumptions to understand the price trade-off, then check that the chosen upfront bill fits resources still available after other household commitments.
787c1f0bb83e987fdc679ee9b06d5d3e276f54e3.zh: 退款承诺会改变取消结果，但仍需立即支付更高的价格。在解释平均成本之前检查合同和现金日历。定义比较假设的谁取消以及哪种退款 预订可以有多种不同的取消情况。此练习考虑旅行者在使用预订之前选择取消，而卖方则根据假定的合同接受符合条件的现金退款。当供应商取消或更改服务时，它不计算权利。加拿大运输局的旅客提示建议阅读机票规则和关税，包括限制和处罚。诸如“灵活”之类的宽泛标签并不提供现金计算所需的确切百分比、费用、截止日期或付款方式。如果合同仅返回旅行积分，则该金额不能简单地作为现金退款插入。检查它可以购买什么、是否有过期或转让限制，以及使用它是否需要再次付款。当家人等待时，为未来旅行预留的积分也无法支付不相关的家庭账单。这些图表中的每个价格和退款都是假设的。在使用实际报价之前，请确定可退款金额、取消条件、任何扣除以及还款方式是现金还是受限信用。该模型仅接受现金退款，并且没有发现真实预订的法律条款。将旧预订和取消预订分开 默认较低价格的预订费用为 1,800 加元，并且对于符合条件的自愿取消不提供退款。另一种选择的费用为 2,100 加元：保费为 300 加元。它退还其价格的 100%，减去从退款中保留的 100 加元。如果使用预订，现金费用为1,800加元和2,100加元。如果旅客在假定的合格条件下取消预订，则价格较低的合同的费用仍为 1,800 加元，替代合同的费用为 100 加元。另一种方案的净退款为 2,100 − 100 = 2,000 加元。第一个图表显示了这两个分支，而不是添加它们。它还避免了两次计算保留金额：100加元已经减少了退款。该公式将退款定为零，因此在此图中，大额保留费用不会产生另一笔账单。收取额外费用的真实合同需要不同的现金模式。将取消机会视为不确定的假设 概率控制从 20% 开始。它是为示例选择的，而不是根据旅行者、目的地、健康信息或预订提供商估计的。移动控件测试不同的假设；它不会使选择的概率更加可靠。概率加权成本等于已使用的预订成本乘以使用它的机会，加上取消成本乘以假设的取消机会。同样的计算可以写成价格−概率×净退款。折扣为 20% 时，默认较低价格预订仍为 1,800 加元。替代方案变为 2,100 − 0.20 × 2,000 = 1,700 加元。一次实际预订不会自动生成 1,700 加元的发票：在这些假设下，替代方案的费用要么是 2,100 加元（如果使用），要么是 100 加元（如果取消并收到退款）。将交叉视为算术，而不是决策规则 在默认比较中，替代方案最初会多花费 300 加元，如果发生符合条件的取消，则多返回 2,000 加元。相等的概率加权成本为 300 ÷ 2,000 = 15% 。低于假设的机会，其加权成本较高；高于它，低于它。该矩阵改变了保费和取消假设。不同的溢价也会改变替代品的价格，从而改变其退款百分比所使用的基础。保持退款固定，同时更改全额退款价格会比较不一致的合同。其他输入可以消除 0–100% 范围内的交叉。两个合约在每个假设下也可以具有相等的加权成本。该工具直接报告这些情况，而不是将不可能的概率显示为个人预测。金钱只是预订选择的一部分。除了规定的现金退款之外，这种比较不会对旅行、行程确定性、便利性、提供商可靠性或灵活性赋予任何价值。平均成本等式无法确定特定家庭对避免巨额取消损失的重视程度。在依靠稍后的退款之前先支付保费 两次预订均在时间零时全额支付。由于购买金额为 2,500 加元，价格较低的选择立即剩下 700 加元，而替代品则立即剩下 400 加元。有条件现金图表假设第二个月取消并在两个月后退款。替代方案的现金在第四个月之前保持在 400 加元，然后上涨 2,000 加元，达到 2,400 加元。价格较低的路径保持在 700 加元，因为其模型退款为零。这些行以取消分支为条件；它们不是上一张图表中的概率加权平均值。较长的退款等待时间会延迟恢复，而不会改变这些未折扣的端点成本。如果将初始现金减少至 2,000 加元，则在替代方案下会产生 100 加元的预付款短缺，即使稍后可能会收到大笔退款。该计算器在不假设信用卡预付款、资产出售或来自其他目标的帮助的情况下标记了这种短缺。将退款条款与保险和旅行的其余部分分开 Travel.gc.ca 将旅行取消保险与旅行中断和医疗保险区分开来，并强调审查保单条款、条件、例外情况和要求。预订的退款条款和单独的保险单需要单独审查。这里不包括保险费或索赔。代金券、汇率、重新预订费用、部分使用的旅行、餐饮、住宿或其他预付费承诺也不包括在内。不能假设一件商品的退款可以修复整个旅行预算。对于真正的计划，列出每笔付款及其取消条件，记录所需的通知日期，并保留承诺还款表的确认。将任何预期的现金收据放在其自己的日期上。使用一系列取消假设来了解价格权衡，然后检查所选的预付账单是否适合其他家庭承诺后仍然可用的资源。

b79f2dda8af3e50eff03ed16f0fac6ea2f161bb7.src: A lump sum and a stream of monthly receipts meet different cash calendars. Confirm the claim conditions first, then compare spendable amounts and dates with the costs they must fund. Begin with the payment trigger, before the amount The Financial Consumer Agency of Canada’s health-insurance overview describes critical illness insurance as usually providing a one-time payment following a covered diagnosis. Definitions and covered conditions vary by insurer. A policy document and a claim decision determine whether a particular event qualifies. FCAC’s disability-insurance overview describes protection when a person cannot work and earn income. Definitions, payment limits, duration and receipt delays require checking. A diagnosis and an inability to work are different questions; neither by itself establishes that both contracts will pay. The calculator begins after those questions have been resolved for each alternative. Scenario A receives one independently entered net amount. Scenario B receives a net monthly amount for an independently entered number of months. It does not add the alternatives together. Any tax and offset adjustments must already be reflected in the supplied receipts. Put the household costs on the same monthly calendar The example runs for eighteen whole months. Recurring spending is CAD 4,500 a month, while other spendable income contributes CAD 1,500. A separate CAD 6,000 cost occurs in month one. The household begins with CAD 10,000 of accessible cash. Scenario A receives CAD 50,000 in month two. Scenario B receives CAD 4,500 a month beginning in month four, with twelve payments ending in month fifteen. Their benefit totals are therefore CAD 50,000 and CAD 54,000 within the displayed window. These numbers are authored examples, not advertised benefits or estimates of an actual claim. The event chart highlights months around the first payment, the one-time receipt and the monthly stream’s end. It shows benefit receipts only. The complete month-end cash paths then add other income and subtract both recurring and initial costs. Keeping those two views distinct helps explain why a large benefit bar need not mean a large remaining balance. Every month receives its inflows before its costs are paid. That is a simplifying order. If rent leaves before a benefit arrives in the same month, the practical bank balance may need an additional buffer. Use actual dates for an implemented household plan. Find the deepest shortfall rather than reading only the final balance Before any benefit receipt, month one uses CAD 9,000 more than other income supplies. Under the one-time scenario, the month-two payment replenishes cash, but continuing spending draws it down again. The path ends month eighteen with CAD 0 at the selected CAD 10,000 opening balance. The monthly scenario must first fund three months before its first benefit receipt. Those months create a cumulative CAD 15,000 deficit. During months four through fifteen, benefit payments and other income exceed recurring spending by CAD 1,500 a month. The final three months have no modeled benefit and consume CAD 3,000 each. The ending balance is CAD 4,000, but an earlier point still falls below zero. Scenario A requires CAD 10,000 at the start to fund its entire calendar. Scenario B requires CAD 15,000, making its additional requirement CAD 5,000 above the selected cash. The higher ending balance in B does not make the early payments affordable on their due dates. Required opening cash is the largest cumulative shortfall across the horizon, with a floor of zero. Additional opening cash subtracts the accessible reserve already entered. A negative plotted position remains an unfunded need; the tool creates no overdraft, borrowing facility or interest charge to fill it. Test what changes when a payment arrives later The matrix changes only scenario A’s net amount and receipt month. Spending, other income, the initial cost and accessible cash stay fixed. Each cell reports additional opening cash, rather than total benefits or a probability. A larger payment can improve the final balance without funding the months before it arrives. Moving the same CAD 50,000 receipt from month two to month twelve leaves eleven earlier months to finance. Their cumulative deficit is CAD 39,000, so the extra opening requirement becomes CAD 29,000 above the selected CAD 10,000. The columns are stress assumptions. They do not represent promised insurer processing times or contractual choices. If a selected receipt falls after the displayed horizon, it contributes nothing within that window. The tool does not credit a future payment against an earlier deficit or assume the household can borrow against it. Likewise, the monthly stream’s maximum payment count is an entered calendar limit. It does not calculate an expiry age, a change in the definition of disability or an extension of coverage. Changing the horizon can expose months after the entered stream has ended. Take the calendar back to the actual contracts and budget Confirm the covered event, required evidence, applicable conditions, benefit amount and timing separately for each contract. FCAC identifies tax treatment and benefit offsets as points to check for disability cover. Do not enter a gross quoted amount as spendable cash unless the deductions have been assessed. Next, replace the example’s costs with a household budget. Separate recurring commitments from one-time changes, identify income that would continue, and count only accessible resources assigned to this purpose. Property value or an inaccessible retirement balance cannot automatically pay this month’s bill. Finally, compare premiums, exclusions and protection periods outside this cash exercise. A smaller reserve need under one assumed claim does not establish that a product offers broader cover or better value. These graphics explain payment shape and funding timing; they cannot select insurance or resolve a claim.
b79f2dda8af3e50eff03ed16f0fac6ea2f161bb7.zh: 一次性付款和一系列每月收入符合不同的现金日历。首先确认索赔条件，然后将可支出金额和日期与他们必须资助的费用进行比较。从付款触发开始，在金额之前加拿大金融消费者机构的健康保险概述将重大疾病保险描述为通常在承保诊断后提供一次性付款。定义和承保条件因保险公司而异。保单文件和索赔决定决定特定事件是否符合资格。 FCAC 的残疾保险概述描述了当一个人无法工作和赚取收入时的保护。定义、付款限额、期限和收货延迟需要检查。诊断和无法工作是不同的问题；两者本身都不能确定两个合同都会付款。在解决了每个选项的这些问题后，计算器开始。场景 A 收到一笔独立输入的净额。场景 B 收到独立输入的月份数的每月净额。它不会将替代方案添加在一起。任何税收和抵销调整必须已反映在提供的收据中。将家庭成本放在同一个月历上 该示例运行了整整十八个月。经常性支出为每月 4,500 加元，其他可支出收入为 1,500 加元。第一个月会产生 6,000 加元的单独费用。该家庭拥有 10,000 加元的可用现金。场景 A 在第二个月收到 50,000 加元。方案 B 从第四个月开始每月收到 4,500 加元，并在第 15 个月结束时支付十二笔款项。因此，在显示的窗口中，他们的福利总额为 50,000 加元和 54,000 加元。这些数字是编写的示例，而不是广告中的好处或实际索赔的估计。事件图表突出显示了首次付款、一次性收款和每月流结束前后的月份。它仅显示福利收据。然后，完整的月末现金路径会添加其他收入并减去经常性成本和初始成本。保持这两种观点的不同有助于解释为什么大的福利条不一定意味着大的剩余余额。每个月在支付成本之前都会收到资金流入。这是一个简化的命令。如果租金在同月福利到达之前离开，则实际银行余额可能需要额外的缓冲。使用实际日期来实施家庭计划。找出最严重的缺口，而不是只看最终余额 在收到任何福利金之前，第一个月比其他收入供应多使用 9,000 加元。在一次性情况下，两个月的付款可以补充现金，但持续支出会再次减少现金。该路径在第 18 个月结束时，选定的期初余额为 10,000 加元，金额为 0 加元。每月方案必须在首次领取福利之前三个月首先提供资金。这几个月累计出现了 15,000 加元的赤字。在第四个月到十五个月期间，福利金和其他收入每月超出经常性支出 1,500 加元。最后三个月没有建模效益，每个月消耗 3,000 加元。期末余额为 4,000 加元，但之前的点仍低于零。方案 A 在开始时需要 10,000 加元来为其整个日历提供资金。场景 B 需要 15,000 加元，因此其额外要求比所选现金高出 5,000 加元。 B 中较高的期末余额并不能使到期日提前付款。所需的期初现金是整个范围内最大的累计缺口，下限为零。额外的期初现金减去已输入的可用准备金。负绘制头寸仍然是一个没有资金支持的需求；该工具不会产生透支、借贷便利或利息费用来填补它。测试付款稍后到达时会发生什么变化 该矩阵仅更改场景 A 的净金额和收款月份。支出、其他收入、初始成本和可用现金保持不变。每个单元报告额外的期初现金，而不是总收益或概率。较大的付款可以改善最终余额，而无需在付款前几个月提供资金。将同一张 50,000 加元收据从第二个月转移到第十二个月，剩下十一个月需要融资。他们的累计赤字为 39,000 加元，因此额外开仓要求在选定的 10,000 加元之上变为 29,000 加元。这些列是应力假设。它们并不代表保险公司承诺的处理时间或合同选择。如果选定的收据落在显示的水平线之后，则它在该窗口内没有任何贡献。该工具不会将未来的付款计入先前的赤字，也不会假设家庭可以以此为抵押进行借贷。同样，每月流的最大付款计数是输入的日历限制。它不计算到期年龄、残疾定义的变化或承保范围的延长。改变地平线可能会在输入流结束后几个月暴露出来。将日历带回实际合同和预算 分别确认每份合同的承保事件、所需证据、适用条件、福利金额和时间安排。 FCAC 将税收待遇和福利抵消确定为检查残疾保险的要点。除非已评估扣除额，否则请勿输入总报价金额作为可支出现金。接下来，用家庭预算代替示例中的成本。将经常性承诺与一次性变更分开，确定将持续的收入，并仅计算分配给此目的的可用资源。财产价值或无法使用的退休余额无法自动支付本月的账单。最后，比较本次现金活动之外的保费、除外责任和保护期。一项假设的索赔中较小的储备需求并不表明该产品提供更广泛的覆盖范围或更好的价值。这些图表解释了付款方式和融资时间；他们无法选择保险或解决索赔。

98fa28a067f77800b655da58bef005b7fe485716.src: A popular advice source is not a price quote. Compare the written service scope, translate the full fee into dollars and place its due dates beside cash that can actually pay it. Read advice-source use without turning it into a quality ranking FCAC’s 2024 survey summary supplies the first chart’s eight advice-source percentages. They add to 142%, reflecting overlapping source use. Treat them as mentions, rather than eight slices of one 100% total. The chart measures neither prices nor provider quality. A source someone consults is different from the work a household needs completed. A budgeting conversation, a retirement projection and implementation of an investment account can involve different tasks, responsibilities and charges. Write the question to be answered before comparing the amount on an invoice. The fee controls below start a separate exercise. They do not estimate what survey respondents paid or attach a financial outcome to any of the survey’s categories. Editing a fee leaves the historical bars unchanged. Specify the work before comparing payment labels The age-group and project-review guide examines different survey cuts and the present cost of periodic reviews. Here the focus is a monthly retainer, a fixed asset-based bill and the outside cash that funds those invoices. A one-time project and an ongoing engagement need not provide the same service. A project may end after a defined report or meeting. An ongoing arrangement may include scheduled updates, access between reviews or implementation work. Those details need written confirmation rather than an assumption based on the billing label. FCAC’s advisor-selection guide recommends understanding the services, their cost and how payment works. It also suggests asking about qualifications, compensation and the working relationship. Use the actual engagement terms to establish what is included and which questions need another specialist. In this calculator, the project has no automatic renewal; the retainer continues for every selected month; and the asset-linked charge continues over the same period. These are three hypothetical schedules. The tool does not assert equivalent deliverables, value the advice, or identify which arrangement is suitable. Turn the percentage into dollars using its actual base The default project costs CAD 2,500 immediately. The alternative retainer costs CAD 200 each month. The third schedule applies an annual 0.8% to an unchanged CAD 400,000 calculation base, divided into twelve monthly bills. That last calculation is 400,000 × 0.008 = CAD 3,200 a year , or about CAD 266.67 per modeled month. Over the selected twenty-four months, the totals are CAD 2,500, CAD 4,800 and CAD 6,400. The lines reconcile those amounts without assuming an investment return. The asset figure only calculates a bill. It is not an extra reserve that the cash chart can spend. Every fee in this illustration is paid from outside cash, so the model does not deduct the same charge from the portfolio again. Product expenses, commissions, account charges and taxes are also excluded rather than silently bundled into the selected percentage. Check the first invoice as well as the two-year total The default outside reserve is CAD 2,000. Another CAD 150 becomes available each month before any recurring bill. The full project fee, however, is due at time zero, before those future additions arrive. The project’s initial funding gap is CAD 500. Its outside cash later recovers to CAD 3,100 after twenty-four monthly additions. That positive endpoint does not supply the missing cash on the original invoice date. Under the stated order, the project needs CAD 2,500 available at the start. The retainer uses CAD 50 more than the monthly addition, so its opening-cash requirement over twenty-four months is CAD 1,200. The asset-linked bill uses about CAD 116.67 more each month, requiring CAD 2,800 initially. The entered CAD 2,000 therefore leaves that path CAD 800 short by the end. These requirements cover only the displayed advice bills. Cash already promised to rent, taxes or another goal cannot also pay these invoices. Negative values identify an unresolved funding need; the calculator does not sell assets, open a credit line or postpone a contractual bill. Use a cost-equivalent asset base as a question, not a verdict The matrix translates three annual percentages and three unchanging asset bases into annual dollar charges. It helps expose the denominator: the same percentage can produce very different invoices when the amount subject to the fee changes. At the default 0.8%, CAD 300,000 would produce CAD 2,400 a year, equal in dollars to a CAD 200 monthly retainer. This is a cost-equivalent base for the selected numbers. It does not establish equivalent service or make either structure preferable above or below that amount. At only three months, the selected retainer totals CAD 600 and the asset-linked schedule CAD 800, while the project still costs CAD 2,500. The thirteenth retainer bill brings cumulative charges to CAD 2,600, passing the project amount. A crossing of selected cash totals does not turn a one-time engagement into thirteen months of support. The horizon and the work promised both matter. Actual terms can use average balances, quarter-end values, tiered rates, minimum fees or a different billing frequency. Assets can also change through markets, deposits and withdrawals. The model holds the base fixed to isolate the arithmetic. Before using a real percentage, confirm which assets enter the base and whether additional charges apply. Bring a complete fee calendar into the household plan Record the initial amount, recurring amount, billing dates and expected length of the engagement. Identify any separately quoted follow-up, implementation or product costs. Ask how a change in scope or an end to the relationship affects future invoices and work already paid for. Keep a separate list of deliverables and responsibilities: what information will be reviewed, what written output is expected, who implements changes, and when the plan is revisited. A cheaper bill cannot answer those questions, and a more expensive bill cannot establish better results. The calculator deliberately assigns no extra return, tax saving or avoided loss to an advisor. A claim about financial benefits needs evidence of its own and cannot be reverse-engineered from the fee. Start with a clear task and a complete quote, then reconcile the chosen payment schedule with the rest of the household’s commitments.
98fa28a067f77800b655da58bef005b7fe485716.zh: 流行的建议来源不是报价。比较书面服务范围，将全部费用换算成美元，并将到期日放在实际可以支付的现金旁边。阅读建议来源的使用情况，而不将其转化为质量排名 FCAC 的 2024 年调查摘要提供了第一个图表的八个建议来源百分比。它们加起来达到 142%，反映出重叠的源使用。将它们视为提及，而不是 100% 总数中的八个部分。该图表既不衡量价格，也不衡量提供商的质量。人们咨询的来源与家庭需要完成的工作不同。预算对话、退休预测和投资账户的实施可能涉及不同的任务、责任和费用。在比较发票上的金额之前写下要回答的问题。下面的费用控制开始单独的练习。他们不会估计调查受访者支付的费用或将财务结果附加到任何调查类别。编辑费用会使历史柱保持不变。在比较付款标签之前指定工作年龄组和项目审查指南检查了不同的调查削减和定期审查的当前成本。这里的重点是每月预付金、基于固定资产的账单以及为这些发票提供资金的外部现金。一次性项目和持续参与不需要提供相同的服务。项目可能会在定义的报告或会议之后结束。正在进行的安排可能包括预定的更新、审查或实施工作之间的访问。这些细节需要书面确认，而不是基于账单标签的假设。 FCAC 的顾问选择指南建议您了解服务、其成本以及付款方式。它还建议询问资格、报酬和工作关系。使用实际的参与条款来确定其中包含的内容以及哪些问题需要另一位专家。在这个计算器中，项目没有自动更新；保留期持续到每个选定的月份；与资产挂钩的费用在同一时期继续进行。这是三个假设的时间表。该工具不主张等效的可交付成果、不重视建议或确定哪种安排合适。使用实际基数将百分比转换为美元 默认项目立即花费 2,500 加元。替代固定器的费用为每月 200 加元。第三个附表适用于 400,000 加元不变的计算基数，按年利率 0.8%，分为 12 个每月账单。最后计算结果为 400,000 × 0.008 = 每年 3,200 加元，或每个模型月约 266.67 加元。在选定的 24 个月内，总计为 2,500 加元、4,800 加元和 6,400 加元。这些行在不假设投资回报的情况下对这些金额进行核对。资产数字只计算账单。这不是现金图表可以花费的额外储备。该图中的每项费用都是从外部现金支付的，因此该模型不会再次从投资组合中扣除相同的费用。产品费用、佣金、账户费用和税费也被排除在外，而不是默默地捆绑到选定的百分比中。检查第一张发票以及两年总额 默认外部储备金为 2,000 加元。每月在任何经常性账单之前还可以使用 150 加元。然而，全额项目费用应在零时间支付，即在未来增加的费用到达之前。该项目的初始资金缺口为 500 加元。经过 24 个月的补充后，其外部现金随后恢复至 3,100 加元。该正端点不提供原始发票日期缺失的现金。根据规定，该项目在启动时需要 2,500 加元。预付金比每月增加的金额多使用 50 加元，因此 24 个月内的期初现金要求为 1,200 加元。资产挂钩账单每月多使用约 116.67 加元，最初需要 2,800 加元。因此，输入的 2,000 加元最终使该路径缩短了 800 加元。这些要求仅涵盖显示的建议账单。已经承诺用于租金、税收或其他目标的现金也无法支付这些发票。负值表明资金需求尚未解决；该计算器不会出售资产、开设信用额度或推迟合同账单。使用成本等价资产基础作为问题，而不是结论 该矩阵将三个年度百分比和三个不变的资产基础转换为年度美元费用。它有助于揭示分母：当费用金额发生变化时，相同的百分比可能会产生截然不同的发票。按照默认 0.8% 的利率，300,000 加元每年将产生 2,400 加元，相当于每月 200 加元的保留金。这是所选号码的成本等价基础。它并没有建立同等的服务，也没有使任何一种结构比该数量更可取。仅三个月时间，选定的预付款总额为 600 加元，资产挂钩计划费用为 800 加元，而该项目的成本仍为 2,500 加元。第十三项保留费账单使累计费用达到 2,600 加元，超过了项目金额。选定现金总额的交叉不会将一次性约定变成十三个月的支持。视野和承诺的工作都很重要。实际条款可以使用平均余额、季末价值、分级费率、最低费用或不同的计费频率。资产也可以通过市场、存款和取款而改变。该模型固定底座以隔离算术。在使用实际百分比之前，请确认哪些资产进入基础以及是否收取额外费用。将完整的费用日历纳入家庭计划记录初始金额、经常性金额、账单日期和预期的参与时间。确定任何单独报价的后续、实施或产品成本。询问范围的变化或关系的结束如何影响未来的发票和已支付的工作。保留一份可交付成果和责任的单独列表：将审查哪些信息、预期的书面输出、谁实施变更以及何时重新审查计划。更便宜的账单无法回答这些问题，更昂贵的账单也无法带来更好的结果。计算器故意不向顾问分配额外回报、节税或避免损失。有关经济利益的主张需要有自己的证据，并且不能从费用中进行逆向工程。从明确的任务和完整的报价开始，然后将所选的付款时间表与家庭的其他承诺进行核对。

08dc3a53bbaebc9efbe57ea0698dca9bb7a677ed.src: Record a purchase once as consumption, track the card liability until repayment, and treat transfers between your own accounts as account movements. The bank balance alone is only one part of the household picture. Ask three questions about each transaction A budgeting app can show a grocery purchase on a card, a later payment from chequing to the card, and a transfer to savings. All three change an account, but they do not all measure new consumption. Treating every debit as another household expense can make a balanced plan look as if money disappeared twice. For each entry, ask what was consumed, which account moved and whether a liability changed. A consumed card purchase creates a liability without immediately reducing the bank account. Its repayment later reduces both cash and that liability. A transfer to your own savings account moves an asset between two locations. FCAC’s budgeting guidance supports reviewing income, savings and expenses against actual statements. This guide adds an original consolidated ledger to explain how those statements fit together. It is a teaching model rather than a prescribed accounting standard or a tax calculation. Define the twelve-month window and the nested spending shares The original example receives CAD 5,000 of take-home income at the start of each model month. It spends 60% directly from chequing, or CAD 3,000. The card-purchase input then applies to the CAD 2,000 that remains. A 40% card share therefore means CAD 800 of card purchases, not another 40% of the original CAD 5,000. Total monthly consumption is CAD 3,800, leaving CAD 1,200 after both purchase categories. The saving-transfer input moves 50% of that surplus, or CAD 600, from chequing to a separate savings account. The other CAD 600 remains in chequing after the ordinary monthly flows have settled. These nested shares make consumption no larger than current income within this limited example. They do not establish an appropriate spending target or prove that a real household can meet all its obligations. The tool omits additional loans, taxes beyond the entered take-home amount, emergencies and other accounts. Opening chequing is CAD 10,000, separate savings are CAD 5,000, and the card starts with no purchase liability. Neither bank account earns interest. Every modeled purchase is consumed, with no continuing vehicle, inventory or other asset value. Buying a retained asset would need a different ledger. Separate the purchase month from the repayment month The card’s new purchases are paid in the next model month. Month one therefore consumes CAD 3,800 while only CAD 3,000 leaves the bank for merchants or the card issuer. The difference is CAD 800 owed for purchases already consumed. That amount is not an extra saving created by choosing the card. Each of months two through twelve pays the prior CAD 800 card bill and makes another CAD 800 of card purchases. Consumption and purchase-related bank outflow are both CAD 3,800 in each of those ordinary months, even though the particular purchases being paid are different. The first chart groups those three distinct cases: the first month, each recurring month and a final settlement-only event. Its middle row is a per-month amount, not the eleven-month total. The cumulative chart then shows the complete twelve-month amounts and the remaining timing gap. The model assumes no card interest or fees. FCAC explains the conditions and limits of purchase grace periods, including the need to pay the required balance by its due date. A one-month teaching lag does not calculate an actual grace period. Existing revolving debt, cash advances, cash-like transactions, fees or missed due dates need a separate calculation using the agreement. Match the measure to the question before adding transactions Across twelve months, direct purchases total CAD 36,000 and card purchases total CAD 9,600. Consumption recorded once is therefore CAD 45,600. The bank has paid CAD 36,000 directly and CAD 8,800 to settle eleven earlier card-purchase batches, for purchase-related cash outflow of CAD 44,800. Both totals answer useful questions. CAD 45,600 measures consumption assigned to the window; CAD 44,800 measures the relevant bank outflows inside it. Their CAD 800 difference is exactly the remaining purchase liability. A bank-only report has a timing difference from a consumption report, rather than necessarily containing a transaction error. Adding the CAD 8,800 repayments to the CAD 45,600 purchases produces CAD 54,400. That calculation counts purchases once when incurred and again when the associated liability is settled. The third chart makes this recording mistake visible beside the two correctly named measures. A system that records only bank outflows can still be useful for cash planning. It needs the opening and closing liabilities to explain the boundary between reporting periods. A system that categorizes card purchases when they occur should classify subsequent repayments consistently so that the same consumption is not counted again. A savings transfer changes the location of money The household transfers CAD 7,200 into savings over the year. That is an account-level saving action, but it is not an additional CAD 7,200 cost to the consolidated household. Each transfer lowers chequing and raises savings by the same amount. At month twelve, chequing holds CAD 18,000 and savings hold CAD 12,200. Subtracting the CAD 800 card purchase liability gives CAD 29,400 of listed net financial assets. Relative to the opening CAD 15,000, the increase is CAD 14,400. The waterfall independently reconciles that increase: CAD 60,000 take-home receipts minus CAD 45,600 consumed purchases equals CAD 14,400. Card repayments and internal savings transfers each have zero immediate net effect on this consolidated measure. That does not make their dates irrelevant to the accounts that must fund them. FCAC defines net worth as assets less liabilities. This example includes only two bank accounts and one card purchase liability, so its result is deliberately called listed net financial assets. It is not a complete household balance sheet. An unpaid purchase liability still belongs in the model even when its assumed payment deadline has not yet passed. Settle the final bill without inventing another expense Position thirteen pays the last CAD 800 card bill. It supplies no new income, purchase or savings transfer. Chequing falls to CAD 17,200, savings stay at CAD 12,200 and the card purchase liability becomes zero. The combined net amount remains CAD 29,400. The final position is a settlement event, not a forecast that ordinary life pauses for a thirteenth month. It closes the twelve-month purchase cohort so that total bank outflow eventually equals that cohort’s consumption. A real following month would add its own income, purchases and other obligations. When applying the idea to statements, retain transaction dates, statement dates and actual processing dates. Match card payments to the corresponding liabilities and distinguish refunds, interest, fees and asset purchases from this guide’s simple consumed purchases. Check that opening balances reconcile before interpreting a later difference. The monthly model receives income before its payments. It cannot establish that the actual bank account stays above zero between paydays or that a payment will reach the issuer on time. Use the related dated cash tools for that task. The purpose here is to make each transaction’s role visible, so that consumption, payments, transfers and balances can all reconcile without counting the same purchase twice.
08dc3a53bbaebc9efbe57ea0698dca9bb7a677ed.zh: 将一次购买记录为消费，跟踪卡负债直至还款，并将您自己账户之间的转账视为账户变动。银行存款余额只是家庭状况的一部分。针对每笔交易询问三个问题预算应用程序可以显示卡上的杂货购买、从支票到卡的后续付款以及储蓄转账。这三者都改变了账户，但它们并不都衡量新的消费。将每一笔借记都视为另一项家庭开支，会使平衡计划看起来好像钱消失了两次。对于每个条目，询问消耗了什么、移动了哪个帐户以及负债是否发生变化。消费卡购买会产生负债，但不会立即减少银行账户的余额。随后的偿还会减少现金和负债。转账到您自己的储蓄账户可以在两个地点之间转移资产。 FCAC 的预算指南支持根据实际报表审查收入、储蓄和支出。本指南添加了一个原始的综合分类账来解释这些报表如何组合在一起。它是一种教学模式，而不是规定的会计准则或税收计算。定义 12 个月的窗口和嵌套支出份额 原始示例在每个模型月开始时收到 5,000 加元的实得收入。 60% 的费用直接来自支票，即 3,000 加元。然后，卡购买输入将应用于剩余的 2,000 加元。因此，40% 的卡份额意味着卡购买金额为 800 加元，而不是原始 5,000 加元的另外 40%。每月总消费为 3,800 加元，扣除两个购买类别后还剩 1,200 加元。储蓄转移投入将盈余的 50%（即 600 加元）从支票转移到单独的储蓄账户。另外 600 加元在每月正常流量结算后仍处于支票状态。在这个有限的示例中，这些嵌套份额使消费不会大于当前收入。他们没有制定适当的支出目标，也没有证明一个真正的家庭能够履行其所有义务。该工具忽略了额外的贷款、超出输入实得金额的税收、紧急情况和其他账户。开户支票为 10,000 加元，单独储蓄为 5,000 加元，该卡开始时没有购买责任。两个银行账户都不会赚取利息。每次建模购买都会被消耗，没有持续的车辆、库存或其他资产价值。购买保留资产需要不同的分类账。将购买月份与还款月份分开 卡的新购买金额将在下一个标准月份支付。因此，第一个月消耗 3,800 加元，而只有 3,000 加元留给商户或发卡机构。差价是已消费的商品需支付 800 加元。该金额并不是通过选择该卡而产生的额外节省。第 2 个月到第 12 个月每月支付之前 800 加元的卡账单，并进行另外 800 加元的卡购物。尽管支付的具体购买金额不同，但在每个普通月份中，消费和与购买相关的银行流出均为 3,800 加元。第一个图表将这三种不同的情况分组：第一个月、每个循环月份和仅最终结算事件。中间行是每月金额，而不是十一个月的总额。然后，累积图表显示完整的十二个月金额和剩余的时间间隙。该模型假设没有卡利息或费用。 FCAC 解释了购买宽限期的条件和限制，包括需要在到期日之前支付所需余额。一个月的教学滞后并不计算实际的宽限期。现有的循环债务、现金垫款、类似现金的交易、费用或错过的到期日需要使用协议进行单独计算。在添加交易之前将衡量标准与问题进行匹配 在 12 个月内，直接购买总额为 36,000 加元，卡购买总额为 9,600 加元。因此记录一次的消费为 45,600 加元。该银行已直接支付 36,000 加元，并支付 8,800 加元来结算之前的 11 批卡购买，与购买相关的现金流出为 44,800 加元。两个总数都回答了有用的问题。 45,600 加元测量分配给窗口的消耗； 44,800 加元衡量其内部相关银行资金流出。他们的 800 加元差额正是剩余的购买责任。仅银行报告与消费报告存在时间差异，但不一定包含交易错误。将 8,800 加元的还款额与 45,600 加元的采购额相加，得出 54,400 加元。该计算在发生时对购买进行一次计数，并在相关负债结算时再次进行计算。第三张图表使这个记录错误在两个正确命名的度量旁边可见。仅记录银行流出的系统对于现金规划仍然有用。它需要期初负债和期末负债来解释报告期间之间的界限。对卡购买进行分类的系统应该对后续还款进行一致的分类，以便不会再次计算相同的消费。储蓄转账改变了资金的去向 该家庭一年内将 7,200 加元转入储蓄。这是一项账户级别的储蓄行动，但并不会给合并家庭带来 7,200 加元的额外成本。每次转账都会减少支票并增加相同金额的储蓄。第 12 个月，支票持有 18,000 加元，储蓄持有 12,200 加元。减去 800 加元的卡购买负债，得出列出的净金融资产为 29,400 加元。相对开盘15,000加元，上涨14,400加元。瀑布独立调节了这一增量：60,000 加元带回家的收据减去 45,600 加元消费的购买量等于 14,400 加元。卡还款和内部储蓄转账对这一综合指标的直接净影响为零。但这并不意味着他们的日期与必须为他们提供资金的账户无关。 FCAC 将净资产定义为资产减去负债。本例仅包含两个银行账户和一张卡购买负债，因此其结果特意称为列出的金融资产净值。它不是完整的家庭资产负债表。即使假定的付款期限尚未过去，未付的购买负债仍属于该模型。结清最终账单，无需再产生其他费用。位置 13 支付最后一张 800 加元的卡账单。它不提供新的收入、购买或储蓄转移。支票费用降至 17,200 加元，储蓄金额保持在 12,200 加元，购卡负债为零。合并净额仍为 29,400 加元。最终的立场是一个解决事件，而不是对普通生活暂停第十三个月的预测。它关闭了十二个月的购买队列，以便银行总流出最终等于该队列的消费。真正的下个月会增加自己的收入、购买和其他义务。将这一想法应用于报表时，保留交易日期、报表日期和实际处理日期。将卡支付与相应的负债相匹配，并将退款、利息、费用和资产购买与本指南的简单消费购买区分开来。在解释后续差异之前检查期初余额是否一致。月度模式在付款之前收到收入。它无法确定发薪日期间实际银行账户的余额是否保持在零以上，或者付款能否按时到达发卡机构。使用相关的过时现金工具来完成该任务。这里的目的是让每笔交易的作用可见，以便消费、支付、转账和余额都可以对账，而无需对同一笔交易进行两次计数。

d07c24812f25ad5d5bf22b58bf32ed304371f1d2.src: A reserve statistic needs a population, asset definition, threshold and reference year. A household cash target also needs its own spending calendar; the same number of months can describe very different amounts. Ask what the reserve is supposed to replace “Three months of savings” sounds like a single target. It can instead mean three months of a low-income threshold, three months of usual household income, or three months of bills that still need paying during an interruption. The time unit matches while the dollar amounts differ. Statistics Canada’s protection-from-income-shocks indicator uses liquid assets relative to the after-tax low-income measure. It is a population measure of financial resilience. It does not establish that a particular household can fund three months of its actual lifestyle or contractual payments. The first two charts preserve the published statistical definitions. The last two let readers inspect independent invented budgets. Keeping those questions distinct makes both more useful: the survey describes an aggregate pattern, while a household plan identifies cash amounts and dates that its own resources must cover. Read six survey waves without inventing the years between them The three-month LIM-based estimate rises from 63.6% in 1999 to 71.4% in 2023, a difference of 7.8 percentage points. The chart shows all six published reference years in the selected series. It does not fill missing years with modeled observations or imply uninterrupted annual improvement. The denominator is persons of all ages in all family types across the ten provinces. The three territories are excluded. A percentage of persons is not interchangeable with a percentage of households: households of different sizes can contribute different numbers of people to a person-based measure. Whiskers show the supplied 95% confidence bounds. They describe uncertainty around estimated population shares, rather than the range of savings balances held by individuals. The chart does not calculate a formal difference test, establish why the estimates changed, or show that the same people became more resilient. Its latest observation is 2023, even though this guide was reviewed in October 2026. Change one definition before comparing a headline The 2023 chart varies both the required duration and the published income basis. Longer coverage requires more assets when the other definition stays fixed. Changing the income basis changes the benchmark against which those assets are assessed. For three months, the published share is 71.4% on the national after-tax low-income-measure basis and 63.6% on the household-income basis. That difference is not a count of households missing a recommended target. These are overlapping survey classifications, and their percentages cannot be added into separate population groups. The LIM benchmark reflects household-size adjustment and a national income distribution. The household-income measure uses after-tax income and excludes capital gains. Neither is identical to an itemized essential-expense budget. Before comparing an article, dashboard or social-media headline, record its denominator, benchmark, duration and year rather than relying on the word “savings” alone. Translate three independent benchmarks into dollars The interactive example starts with CAD 10,000 of cash assumed available after withdrawal costs and tax. Its invented annual benchmark is CAD 30,000, its entered annual household income after tax is CAD 72,000, and its entered monthly essential expenses are CAD 4,500. These inputs are not estimates taken from the survey. For three months, the resulting targets are CAD 7,500, CAD 18,000 and CAD 13,500 respectively. The same CAD 10,000 balance exceeds the first target, falls CAD 8,000 below the income-based target and falls CAD 3,500 below the essential-expense target. Passing one comparison therefore does not settle the others. The invented benchmark is deliberately labelled. It is not a current official LIM amount, and the tool does not implement household-size equivalization or classify the reader under Statistics Canada’s methodology. The cash bar is also repeated for visual comparison, rather than allocated three times. A plan still has only the original CAD 10,000 available. A payment calendar can also reveal costs hidden by a monthly average. Suppose the CAD 4,500 monthly figure excludes a separate CAD 1,200 obligation due in the second month. Three months then require CAD 14,700, leaving CAD 4,700 to fund. Entering CAD 400 more per month reproduces that three-month total, but spreads the obligation across dates. That shortcut cannot establish whether enough cash is available on its actual due date. Separate counted assets from money available for the next bill The source indicator’s liquid-asset definition includes deposits, securities and registered savings. For a household payment calendar, an asset’s quoted value and its usable cash proceeds can differ. A security may change in price before sale; an account can involve withdrawal tax, settlement time or access conditions. The cash input assumes those practical questions have already been resolved. It accepts an amount available when needed after relevant costs and tax, rather than applying an automatic haircut to every type of asset. It also assumes the amount has not already been reserved for an unrelated bill. The earmarking guide illustrates that separate allocation problem. At the default essential-spending input, CAD 10,000 funds about 2.22 months. This is a continuous expense ratio, not a guaranteed date at which money runs out. Actual rent, loan payments and annual bills arrive on particular dates. Replacement income or benefits would require a dated cash-flow schedule; none is silently assumed here. Stress the cash target without treating the grid as a forecast The matrix compares fixed essential-expense rows with one, three, six and nine months of coverage. Every cell subtracts the same entered cash from that scenario’s expense requirement and floors the additional amount at zero. A zero does not report zero risk; it says only that the entered cash covers the selected arithmetic target. For example, CAD 4,500 of monthly essentials requires CAD 27,000 for six months. With CAD 10,000 already available, the additional amount is CAD 17,000. At CAD 6,000 per month, the same six-month duration needs CAD 26,000 more. The darker cells indicate larger cash shortfalls, not more likely events. A future saving plan is another separate question. Adding CAD 500 at each month-end would close a CAD 3,500 shortfall after seven deposits if the target stays fixed and no cash is withdrawn. Those promised deposits do not enlarge the amount available for an emergency today. Use the official charts to understand what a reserve statistic measures and the hypothetical charts to ask a narrower budget question. A workable next calculation starts with essential payments, realistic incoming cash, access dates and existing earmarks. A national share can inform that discussion, but it does not choose a household’s reserve target or replace its own cash calendar.
d07c24812f25ad5d5bf22b58bf32ed304371f1d2.zh: 储备统计需要人口、资产定义、阈值和参考年份。家庭现金目标还需要有自己的支出日历；相同的月份数可以描述截然不同的金额。询问储备金应该取代什么“三个月的储蓄”听起来像是一个单一的目标。相反，它可能意味着三个月的低收入门槛、三个月的正常家庭收入或三个月在中断期间仍需要支付的账单。时间单位一致，但美元金额不同。加拿大统计局的收入冲击保护指标使用相对于税后低收入指标的流动资产。它是衡量财务弹性的人口指标。它没有规定特定家庭可以为其三个月的实际生活方式或合同付款提供资金。前两张图表保留了已发布的统计定义。最后两个让读者检查独立发明的预算。保持这些问题的明确性使得两者都更有用：调查描述了总体模式，而家庭计划则确定了其自身资源必须覆盖的现金金额和日期。阅读六次调查浪潮，无需发明它们之间的年份 基于 LIM 的三个月估计值从 1999 年的 63.6% 上升到 2023 年的 71.4%，相差 7.8 个百分点。该图表显示了所选系列中所有六个已发布的参考年。它并不用模型观察来填补缺失的年份，也不意味着不间断的年度改进。分母是十个省份所有家庭类型的所有年龄段的人口。这三个地区被排除在外。人口百分比与家庭百分比不可互换：不同规模的家庭可以为基于人的衡量标准贡献不同数量的人口。晶须显示提供的 95% 置信界限。他们描述了估计人口份额的不确定性，而不是个人持有的储蓄余额的范围。该图表没有计算正式的差异测试，没有确定估计值变化的原因，也没有表明同一个人变得更有弹性。尽管本指南是在 2026 年 10 月审查的，但其最新观察是 2023 年。在比较标题之前更改定义 2023 年图表的所需期限和公布的收入基础均有所不同。当其他定义保持不变时，更长的覆盖范围需要更多的资产。改变收入基础会改变评估这些资产的基准。三个月来，公布的全国税后低收入比例为 71.4%，家庭收入为 63.6%。这种差异并不是未达到建议目标的家庭数量。这些是重叠的调查分类，它们的百分比不能添加到单独的人口组中。 LIM 基准反映了家庭规模调整和国民收入分配。家庭收入衡量标准使用税后收入，不包括资本收益。两者都与逐项必要支出预算不同。在比较文章、仪表板或社交媒体标题之前，记录其分母、基准、持续时间和年份，而不是仅仅依赖“节省”一词。将三个独立的基准转换为美元 交互式示例以 10,000 加元的现金开始，假定扣除提款费用和税费后可用。其设定的年度基准为30,000加元，其输入的税后家庭年收入为72,000加元，其输入的每月基本开支为4,500加元。这些输入并不是根据调查得出的估计值。三个月的目标分别为 7,500 加元、18,000 加元和 13,500 加元。同样的 10,000 加元余额超出第一个目标，比收入目标低 8,000 加元，比基本支出目标低 3,500 加元。因此，通过一项比较并不能解决其他问题。发明的基准是故意标记的。这不是当前的官方 LIM 金额，并且该工具不会实施家庭规模等效或根据加拿大统计局的方法对读者进行分类。现金栏也重复进行视觉比较，而不是分配三次。计划仍然只有原来的 10,000 加元可用。付款日历还可以显示每月平均隐藏的成本。假设每月 4,500 加元的数字不包括第二个月到期的 1,200 加元的单独债务。三个月需要 14,700 加元，剩下 4,700 加元可供资助。每月再输入 400 加元即可重现三个月的总额，但将义务分摊到各个日期。该捷径无法确定在实际到期日是否有足够的现金可用。将计数资产与可用于下一张账单的资金分开源指标的流动资产定义包括存款、证券和注册储蓄。对于家庭付款日历，资产的报价价值及其可用现金收益可能有所不同。证券在出售前可能会发生价格变化；账户可能涉及提款税、结算时间或访问条件。现金投入假设这些实际问题已经得到解决。它接受在相关成本和税收后需要时可用的金额，而不是对每种类型的资产进行自动削减。它还假设该金额尚未为不相关的账单预留。指定用途指南说明了单独分配问题。在默认的基本支出投入下，10,000 加元大约可以使用 2.22 个月。这是一个持续的费用比率，而不是保证资金用完的日期。实际租金、贷款付款和年度账单会在特定日期到达。替代收入或福利需要一份注明日期的现金流量表；这里没有默认任何内容。强调现金目标，而不将网格视为预测 该矩阵将固定基本支出行与一、三、六和九个月的覆盖范围进行比较。每个单元格都会从该场景的费用要求中减去输入的相同现金，并将额外金额限制为零。零并不代表零风险；它只是说输入的现金覆盖了选定的算术目标。例如，每月 4,500 加元的必需品需要六个月 27,000 加元。已有 10,000 加元可用，额外金额为 17,000 加元。按每月 6,000 加元计算，同样的六个月期限需要多花 26,000 加元。较暗的单元格表示更大的现金短缺，而不是更可能发生的事件。未来的储蓄计划是另一个单独的问题。如果目标保持固定且不提取现金，则每个月末增加 500 加元即可弥补 7 次存款后 3,500 加元的缺口。这些承诺的存款并没有增加今天可用于紧急情况的金额。使用官方图表来了解储备统计数据的衡量标准，并使用假设图表来提出更狭窄的预算问题。可行的下一个计算从基本付款、实际现金收入、访问日期和现有专项资金开始。全国份额可以为这种讨论提供信息，但它不会选择家庭的储备目标或取代自己的现金日历。

12db340606782717e7bfb785aa2f5e937a5326ef.src: Original cash invested is not always the current adjusted cost base.
