。以 60 岁购买力计算的 9,000 加元的报价意味着在相同价格假设下 67 岁的名义金额不同：大约 10,338.17 加元。引用基础条比较同一数字的两种解释。他们不会计算两项可用福利或建议索赔年龄。如果报价已经意味着未来第一年实际支付 9,000 加元，则再次按七年的通货膨胀率计算将导致年度金额高估约 1,338.17 加元。因此，该模型以输入的第一付款年度金额开始后续流，并仅在付款开始后应用其单独的收入增长假设。相反，生命周期和临时输入从第一个建模年份开始。这些不同的起始基地在控件旁边注明。年度缺口总额不是必需的投资余额 该矩阵更改了首次付款年后期收入金额及其开始年龄，同时保留其他选定的假设。稍后开始的重复名义金额不是起始年度购买力的重复金额。每个单元格汇总了 90 岁之前的正年度支出缺口。整个计划的默认总额约为 172,308.05 加元。该数字未经折现，并且不会逐年出现盈余。它既不是开仓资本要求，也不是建议的投资组合撤资。将一系列缺口转换为融资资产计划需要启动资产、回报、成本、提款时间、税收和处理任何盈余的规则。该工具假设该人仍然活着，并且所描述的付款在选定的年龄范围内仍然可用。它不附加生存概率、衡量终生价值或比较养老金选择。其范围较小的任务是揭示收入日历以及需要另一个支持资金来源的年份。将年度说明替换为实际计划证据 分别请求生命周期和临时金额，以及每个组成部分开始或结束的确切月份。记录每个报价金额是否已在其未来付款年度或规定的当前价格年度中表达。这里使用的年度年龄标签省略了部分年份的付款。它们不是每月实施计划的生日规则、处理滞后或残疾条款。联邦消息来源说明了为什么这种精确性很重要：它描述了在 65 岁生日后一个月结束的桥梁，并解释了提前或推迟 CPP/QPP 退休时间与临时付款的相互作用。该计算器不应用这些个人资格或调整计算。其后来的收入必须根据输入的年龄独立支持。然后将金额与家庭支出和退休计划的其余部分进行核对。让幸存者的变化、税收估算、健康成本和指数条件可见，而不是将它们隐藏在单一的年增长率中。当前养老金存款总额是当前现金状况的有用证据；需要逐个组件的时间表来了解可能发生的变化。

ac71ccb75dbb4ce1fdf032d786860030300472d5.src: Only hours that actually remove paid work create the modeled earnings loss. Non-work time can still matter to the decision, but its subjective value belongs in a separate comparison from cash outlays. Compare the same completed task before comparing prices A decision to complete a task yourself can change both money and personal time. A lower materials bill alone does not describe the full cash effect, and assigning a wage to every free hour can misstate it in the other direction. Begin with a comparable scope. The federal Office of Consumer Affairs renovation guide emphasizes detailed work and contract information. Here, the hired quote and the DIY alternative are assumed to deliver the same defined task. The model does not assess quality, qualifications or whether a particular job is appropriate for DIY. Restore the example to use a CAD 3,000 all-in hired price, CAD 1,200 of DIY materials and CAD 300 of new tools and other upfront costs. All known taxes and fees are already included. The tools receive no resale or future-use credit in this example, so the entire initial outlay remains in the cash comparison. Identify paid work that would actually be lost The DIY task takes fifty personal hours. The selected 40% share means twenty of those hours genuinely displace paid work that would otherwise be available. At independently entered after-tax earnings of CAD 30 per displaced hour, the household forgoes CAD 600 of take-home income. The other thirty hours come from non-work time. They may be valuable, but the model does not assume those hours could automatically have been sold at the person’s wage. A fixed-salary employee doing a task on a free weekend might enter a zero displaced-work share even if their usual hourly-equivalent salary is high. The distinction depends on the actual alternative, not simply an employment contract’s headline pay. A reduction in overtime, a cancelled paid shift or foregone billable work can create a cash effect. Free time that would not have produced earnings does not create the same missing cash inflow. Tax and work-related costs should already be reflected in the independently entered net earnings amount. Reconcile the cash saving without pricing leisure twice The DIY cash-resource cost is CAD 1,200 of materials plus CAD 300 of new tools plus CAD 600 of earnings actually forgone, for CAD 2,100. Compared with the CAD 3,000 hired price, this produces a CAD 900 cash-resource saving. The waterfall retains the distinction between cash spent and cash not earned. The CAD 600 is not another invoice from a supplier; it is a reduction in household inflow. Both effects matter to how much money remains available after the task. No charge for the remaining thirty DIY hours appears in this cash bridge. Adding a subjective leisure value here and then adding it again in a broader comparison would count it twice. Likewise, a work hour already valued through lost after-tax earnings should not receive a second charge as a non-work hour. Add a subjective time value as a separate layer The example independently values each non-work hour at CAD 40. Thirty DIY non-work hours then have a subjective value of CAD 1,200. Hiring the task uses five non-work coordination hours, valued at CAD 200. Adding those separate time values to cash-resource costs gives CAD 3,300 for DIY and CAD 3,200 for hiring. The broader comparison therefore favors hiring by CAD 100 under that preference, even though DIY saves CAD 900 in cash resources. The stacked bars show which part of each total is cash and which part is a non-cash valuation. Those combined amounts are decision aids, not bank balances, invoices or investment returns. The CAD 40 input can reflect how strongly a person values time for rest, family or other activities. Another household can reasonably enter a different amount, including zero. The tool does not claim to discover an objective price for personal time. Read the relevant time difference before dividing the cash saving DIY uses forty-five more personal hours overall than the five-hour coordination alternative. However, twenty DIY hours have already been charged through the CAD 600 of lost earnings. The remaining non-work-time difference is thirty DIY hours minus five coordination hours, or twenty-five hours. At the default cash saving, a subjective value of CAD 900 ÷ 25 = CAD 36 per additional non-work hour makes the broader totals equal. That threshold is a preference comparison after accounting for actual lost pay. It is not an hourly wage offer or a statement that the person can earn CAD 36 for every free hour. The matrix instead stays cash-only. It changes task hours and the share that actually displaces paid work, holding the quote, materials, tools and after-tax earnings selected. Subjective time value does not affect those cells. This keeps an affordability question separate from how a household chooses to value its time. Record what could change the comparison Confirm comparable scope, materials, completion standard and included costs before using the result. A quote with cleanup or warranty provisions cannot be compared fairly with a DIY budget that silently omits the relevant work or cost. The model does not assign a warranty value or estimate the cost of redoing a failed task. Check the time estimate against the household calendar. Hired-task coordination is assumed to use non-work time only; if it also displaces paid work, another earnings-loss entry is needed. New tool resale, later reuse, borrowing costs and differences in completion dates can also change the analysis. They should be added explicitly rather than treated as invisible benefits or expenses. The four views support a transparent decision: the hours split, the cash bridge, the separate time valuation and the displaced-work sensitivity. A household can then see whether DIY is affordable, how much cash it would preserve, and what personal time it requires. The calculation does not decide how much that time should matter to the person making the choice.
ac71ccb75dbb4ce1fdf032d786860030300472d5.zh: 只有实际消除有偿工作的时间才会造成建模的收入损失。非工作时间仍然对决策很重要，但其主观价值应与现金支出分开比较。在比较价格之前先比较已完成的相同任务 自己完成任务的决定可能会改变金钱和个人时间。仅较低的材料费用并不能描述全部的现金效应，并且将工资分配给每个空闲时间可能会在另一个方向上错误地表述它。从可比较的范围开始。联邦消费者事务办公室的装修指南强调详细的工作和合同信息。这里，假设雇佣报价和 DIY 替代方案能够交付相同的定义任务。该模型不评估质量、资格或特定工作是否适合 DIY。恢复示例使用 3,000 加元的总租用价格、1,200 加元的 DIY 材料和 300 加元的新工具以及其他前期成本。所有已知的税费均已包含在内。在此示例中，这些工具不会获得转售或未来使用信用，因此整个初始支出仍保留在现金比较中。确定实际上会损失的有偿工作 DIY 任务需要 50 个人时间。选定的 40% 份额意味着其中 20 个小时真正取代了本来可以进行的有偿工作。按独立输入的每流离失所小时 30 加元的税后收入计算，该家庭放弃了 600 加元的实得收入。另外三十个小时来自非工作时间。它们可能很有价值，但该模型并不假设这些时间可以自动按照该人的工资出售。在空闲周末执行任务的固定工资员工可能会进入零替代工作份额，即使他们通常的小时等价工资很高。这种区别取决于实际的选择，而不仅仅是雇佣合同的总体工资。减少加班、取消带薪轮班或放弃计费工作可以产生现金效应。不会产生收入的空闲时间不会产生同样缺失的现金流入。税收和工作相关成本应已反映在独立输入的净利润金额中。协调现金节省，无需两次定价休闲 DIY 现金资源成本为 1,200 加元的材料，加上 300 加元的新工具，再加上实际放弃的 600 加元的收入，即 2,100 加元。与 3,000 加元的租用价格相比，这可节省 900 加元的现金资源。瀑布保留了支出的现金和未赚取的现金之间的区别。 CAD 600 不是供应商开具的另一张发票；这是家庭流入的减少。这两种影响都与任务完成后剩余的可用金钱有关。剩余三十个小时的 DIY 小时不收取任何费用。在这里添加一个主观休闲价值，然后在更广泛的比较中再次添加它会算两次。同样，已经通过税后收入损失评估的工作时间不应作为非工作时间再次收取费用。添加主观时间值作为单独的图层 该示例将每个非工作时间独立评估为 40 加元。然后，三十个 DIY 非工作时间的主观值为 1,200 加元。雇用该任务需要使用 5 个非工作协调时间，价值为 200 加元。将这些单独的时间价值添加到现金资源成本中，DIY 费用为 3,300 加元，雇用费用为 3,200 加元。因此，更广泛的比较倾向于在这种偏好下以 100 加元的价格雇用员工，尽管 DIY 可以节省 900 加元的现金资源。堆叠条显示每个总额中哪一部分是现金，哪一部分是非现金估值。这些合计金额是决策辅助工具，而不是银行余额、发票或投资回报。 CAD 40 输入可以反映一个人对休息、家庭或其他活动时间的重视程度。另一个家庭可以合理地输入不同的金额，包括零。该工具并不声称能够发现个人时间的客观价格。在划分之前先阅读相关的时差，与 5 小时的协调替代方案相比，节省现金的 DIY 总体上多使用 45 个小时的个人时间。然而，20 个小时的 DIY 时间已经被计入 600 加元的收入损失。剩余的非工作时间差是三十 DIY 小时减去五个协调小时，即二十五小时。在默认现金节省下，每额外非工作时间主观价值为 900 加元 ÷ 25 = 加元 36，使得更广泛的总金额相等。该阈值是在考虑实际工资损失后的偏好比较。它不是按小时工资的报价，也不是该人每个免费小时可赚取 36 加元的声明。相反，该矩阵仅保留现金。它改变了任务时间和实际取代有偿工作的份额，保留了选定的报价、材料、工具和税后收入。主观时间值不会影响这些单元格。这使得负担能力问题与家庭如何选择珍惜时间分开。记录可能改变比较的内容，然后在使用结果之前确认可比范围、材料、完成标准和包含的成本。带有清理或保修条款的报价无法与默默忽略相关工作或成本的 DIY 预算进行公平比较。该模型不会分配保修值或估计重做失败任务的成本。根据家庭日历检查预计时间。假设雇佣任务协调仅使用非工作时间；如果它也取代了有偿工作，则需要另一个收入损失分录。新工具的转售、以后的重用、借用成本和完成日期的差异也会改变分析。它们应该被明确地添加，而不是被视为无形的收益或支出。四种观点支持透明的决策：时间分割、现金桥梁、单独的时间评估和转移工作敏感性。然后，家庭可以了解 DIY 是否负担得起，可以节省多少现金，以及需要多少个人时间。计算并不能决定这段时间对做出选择的人有多重要。

dcc0909d23220d6b91c96ca8322b740ce5290025.src: An early return of principal changes the income calendar. Test what happens to later coupons and what return the received money can earn afterward. The maturity date is not the only date to read A bond’s coupon and original maturity can suggest a long stream of income. A call provision can change that stream. The issuer may have the right to redeem the bond before its stated maturity under the contract’s terms. Investor.gov’s callable-bond explanation describes the issuer paying the call price and stopping future interest payments. It also highlights the risk of reinvesting the returned money at a less attractive rate. The issuer’s call right is different from an investor’s right to demand an early cash-out. This tool uses original hypothetical cash flows rather than an actual bond quote. It assumes a purchase at face value, annual coupons and a call at face value immediately after a selected coupon. Actual contracts may have different call prices, premiums, protection periods and payment details. Separate principal returned from coupons no longer paid The default face amount is CAD 10,000 with a 6% annual coupon, so each full coupon is CAD 600. The original maturity is ten years. The no-call case pays ten coupons totalling CAD 6,000 and returns CAD 10,000 at the end of year 10. The selected early-call case pays coupons in years 1, 2 and 3, then returns CAD 10,000 immediately after the third coupon. Its issuer coupons total CAD 1,800. It pays no coupons in years 4–10. The difference in issuer coupons is CAD 4,200, but that is not a CAD 4,200 principal loss. Principal has arrived seven years earlier and can be used or reinvested. A complete cash comparison needs to account for that earlier receipt rather than comparing coupon totals alone. Use one common endpoint and state what happens to every receipt The example retains all coupons and principal receipts in a separate reinvestment pool. At each year-end, money already in the pool earns the selected annual return, then the new coupon or redemption arrives. The default return is 2% as an independent assumption. The line chart begins at zero because the opening CAD 10,000 has bought the bond. The large jump at a redemption date represents principal entering the pool. Before original maturity, the chart omits any bond still outstanding, so it is not a comparison of complete interim portfolios. At year 10, both cases have redeemed. The no-call pool is about CAD 16,569.83 and the early-call pool about CAD 13,596.12 under the default assumptions. The common-date difference is approximately negative CAD 2,973.71. These endpoints assume the receipts were retained, rather than spent on household bills. Reconcile missing coupons with the benefit of earlier principal The waterfall begins with the negative CAD 4,200 difference in coupons received from the issuer. It then adds the extra growth on principal that arrived at year 3 rather than year 10. Finally, it includes the difference in growth on the two coupon streams. These components reconcile the gap between the terminal pools. The common principal amount cancels, because both scenarios ultimately return the same face value. The gap is not a quoted bond price, a mark-to-market loss or a guarantee of what a replacement investment will earn. Set reinvestment to zero to isolate nominal receipts. With no growth after receipt, the gap is exactly the CAD 4,200 of issuer coupons no longer paid. Increasing the reinvestment assumption changes the contribution made by the earlier principal. Test the replacement return without predicting the issuer’s decision The matrix changes the call year and reinvestment return while preserving the same face amount, coupon and original maturity. Each cell compares the two cases at the original maturity date. A later call preserves more issuer coupons but leaves less time for early principal to compound. At a 6% reinvestment assumption matching the default 6% coupon, the two terminal pools coincide in this par-purchase example. Both payment schedules can then compound to the same endpoint. With a reinvestment return above the coupon rate, an early principal receipt can even produce a larger modeled terminal pool. That arithmetic does not forecast a favourable call or show when an issuer would rationally exercise its option. The call date and reinvestment return are independent scenario inputs. No option value, probability, credit risk or market pricing is estimated. Build the income plan around the payment terms and the use of cash If coupons are intended to pay ongoing expenses, the relevant question includes how that spending will be replaced after an early call. The reinvested-pool example deliberately retains every receipt, so it does not calculate a household withdrawal plan. Review the actual call schedule and redemption terms before relying on a coupon calendar. Distinguish the annual coupon amount, cash paid at redemption and any replacement-income assumption. For a premium-price purchase or different call amount, the par-value illustration would need a different initial and redemption cash-flow comparison. The related bond-goal guide examines a different timing issue: needing cash before a bond matures. Here the timing changes because the issuer returns principal earlier than the plan expected. Both situations show why an income plan needs dates and cash-flow terms alongside a headline percentage.
dcc0909d23220d6b91c96ca8322b740ce5290025.zh: 提前返还本金会改变收入日历。测试一下以后的优惠券会发生什么以及收到的钱之后可以赚取什么回报。到期日并不是解读债券票息的唯一日期，原始到期日可以表明有长期的收入来源。呼叫规定可以改变该流。发行人有权在合同条款规定的到期日之前赎回债券。 Investor.gov 对可赎回债券的解释描述了发行人支付赎回价格并停止未来支付利息。它还凸显了以不太有吸引力的利率对返还资金进行再投资的风险。发行人的赎回权与投资者要求提前套现的权利不同。该工具使用原始假设现金流量而不是实际债券报价。它假设按面值购买、年度优惠券以及在选择优惠券后立即按面值调用。实际合约可能有不同的看涨期权价格、权利金、保护期和付款细节。不再支付的优惠券单独返还本金 默认票面金额为 10,000 加元，年利率为 6%，因此每张全额优惠券为 600 加元。原始期限为 10 年。未通知案例支付十张优惠券，总计 6,000 加元，并在第 10 年年底返还 10,000 加元。选定的提前通知案例支付第 1 年、第 2 年和第 3 年的优惠券，然后在第三个优惠券后立即返还 10,000 加元。其发行优惠券总额为 1,800 加元。第 4-10 年不支付息票。发行人息票差异为 4,200 加元，但这并不是 4,200 加元的本金损失。本金提前七年到达，可以使用或再投资。完整的现金比较需要考虑到之前的收据，而不是仅比较优惠券总额。使用一个通用端点并说明每张收据会发生什么情况该示例将所有优惠券和本金收据保留在单独的再投资池中。每年年底，池中已有的资金将获得选定的年度回报，然后新的优惠券或赎回到达。作为独立假设，默认回报率为 2%。折线图从零开始，因为开盘价 10,000 加元已购买债券。赎回日的大幅跃升代表本金进入资金池。在原始到期之前，该图表忽略了任何尚未偿还的债券，因此它不是完整中期投资组合的比较。第 10 年，两个案例都得到了救赎。在默认假设下，无呼叫池约为 16,569.83 加元，提前呼叫池约为 13,596.12 加元。共同日期差异约为负 2,973.71 加元。这些端点假设收据被保留，而不是用于家庭账单。将缺失的优惠券与早期本金的利益进行核对 瀑布始于从发行人处收到的优惠券存在 4,200 加元的负差额。然后，它添加了第 3 年而不是第 10 年的本金额外增长。最后，它包括两个息票流的增长差异。这些组件弥补了终端池之间的差距。共同本金金额取消，因为两种情况最终返回相同的面值。这种差距不是债券报价、按市价计价的损失，也不是替代投资收益的保证。将再投资设置为零以隔离名义收入。由于收到后没有增长，缺口正好是不再支付的发行人优惠券的 4,200 加元。增加再投资假设会改变早期本金的贡献。在不预测发行人决定的情况下测试替代回报 该矩阵改变了赎回年和再投资回报，同时保留相同的票面金额、息票和原始期限。每个单元格都会比较原始到期日的两个案例。稍后的赎回可以保留更多的发行人优惠券，但留给早期本金复利的时间更少。在 6% 的再投资假设与默认的 6% 息票相匹配的情况下，两个终端池在这个平价购买示例中是一致的。然后，两个付款计划可以复合到同一端点。由于再投资回报高于票面利率，提前收到本金甚至可以产生更大的模型终端池。该算术并不能预测有利的看涨期权，也不能显示发行人何时会理性地行使其选择权。赎回日期和再投资回报是独立的场景输入。不估计期权价值、概率、信用风险或市场定价。围绕付款条件和现金使用制定收入计划如果优惠券旨在支付持续支出，相关问题包括在提前致电后如何替换该支出。再投资池示例故意保留每张收据，因此它不计算家庭提款计划。在依赖优惠券日历之前，请先查看实际的通话时间表和兑换条款。区分年度息票金额、赎回时支付的现金以及任何重置收入假设。对于溢价购买或不同的赎回金额，面值说明将需要不同的初始现金流量和赎回现金流量比较。相关的债券目标指南研究了一个不同的时间问题：债券到期前需要现金。这里时间发生了变化，因为发行人比计划预期更早返还本金。这两种情况都说明了为什么收入计划需要日期和现金流条款以及标题百分比。

d8ca010bc557f6239f3cdb5c157b319cbd3d4932.src: A low annual usage charge can hide a substantial upfront payment and continuing fees. Divide the complete cost by nights actually used, and keep the model’s finish date separate from the contract’s obligations. Identify the commitment before comparing the nightly price A vacation ownership, right-to-use arrangement or points membership can combine an upfront purchase with recurring charges. Its value to a household depends on the rights obtained, the dates available, how often those rights are used and the costs that continue even in a year without travel. The Government of Canada’s consumer guide to timeshares distinguishes different arrangements and recommends examining availability, additional fees, ongoing costs and resale conditions. The examples here do not reproduce any provider’s contract. They assume a cash purchase and enough availability for the entered usage. Begin with comparable accommodation: similar dates, location, room type, taxes and included services. A membership entitlement is not evidence that a desired booking can be made. A rental price observed for a quiet week is also not a reliable comparison for a peak holiday stay. The model keeps those qualitative questions outside its arithmetic rather than pretending the costs settle them. The first annual bill does not include the purchase already paid The default case pays CAD 30,000 at the start, then CAD 1,300 of first-year dues and a CAD 100 booking charge in each year with use. It uses seven nights per year for a fifteen-year reporting window. Dues rise by an assumed 4% annually, and a hypothetical CAD 5,000 assessment arrives in year eight. First-year recurring costs are CAD 1,400, compared with CAD 1,750 for seven rental nights at CAD 250 each. The annual-cost bars could therefore make the ownership case look cheaper if the upfront purchase were ignored. The cumulative cash chart begins at CAD 30,000 precisely to prevent that omission. Across the full window, dues total about CAD 26,030.66. Adding the purchase, CAD 1,500 of booking charges and the CAD 5,000 assessment brings ownership cash paid to about CAD 62,530.66. The rental alternative, with a separate 3% annual price-growth assumption, totals about CAD 32,548.10. Those are original scenario results, not market prices or a forecast for a particular resort. Divide by nights used, not nights advertised Seven nights per year across fifteen years produce 105 nights actually used. Dividing the complete nominal ownership cost by that usage gives about CAD 595.53 per night. This is an allocation of the reporting-window cost, not an additional charge paid when checking in. Unused entitlement does not become free accommodation in the model. If no nights are used, booking fees disappear under the stated assumption, but the purchase, dues and any included assessment remain. The cost-per-used-night metric then says that no nights were used instead of dividing by zero or reporting a misleading zero cost. The sensitivity matrix shows why actual use matters. More nights spread the same assumed purchase and fixed annual charges across more consumption. That does not prove more nights are available or desirable, and travelling more can create costs excluded here. Also avoid comparing the ownership average directly with today’s rental quote: rental prices change across the window too. Compare the same period and cost basis on both sides. Recurring increases and occasional assessments have different effects Dues grow on an increasing base. At the default 4% assumption, year-eight dues are about CAD 1,710.71, before the booking charge and the entered assessment. That assessment lifts the ownership cash cost in year eight to about CAD 6,810.71. A smooth average annual amount would conceal the year when the larger payment is due. The annual bars include the first year, the finish, each fifth year within the window and any included assessment year. The waterfall then reconciles all purchase, dues, booking and assessment dollars. Together they show both the accumulation of recurring costs and the concentration of a selected extra bill. The assessment is a stress input. It is not a reserve study, an estimate of a property’s condition or a probability-weighted forecast. A bill assigned after the reporting finish is excluded from the current total; it has not been forgiven. Real contracts can contain other charges or different collection dates, which need to be added to an actual cash plan. Discounting future charges does not make the invoice smaller The final comparison places undiscounted cash costs beside present values. The purchase is at time zero. Annual costs are placed at year-end and divided by (1 + discount rate) year . At the default 3% discount assumption, ownership costs have a present value of about CAD 55,415.26 and rental costs about CAD 25,485.44. These present values express the timing difference on a common comparison date. They are not balances in an investment account, additional costs to add to the nominal totals or an estimate of the membership’s resale price. The selected discount rate is a valuation assumption, not an offered investment return. A future CAD 5,000 assessment still requires CAD 5,000 when it falls due even though its present value is smaller today. Actual annual dues can also be collected earlier than the model’s year-end convention. For liquidity planning, replace the annual aggregate with actual payment dates; a discounted cost comparison does not establish how much cash must be available before each invoice. The reporting finish is not a promised exit The fifteen-year default is a measurement window. It does not establish that a deed, lease-like arrangement or membership ends then, that a buyer will appear, or that a provider will release the household from further charges. No resale receipt, exit payment or rental income from unused rights is included. If a real arrangement continues beyond the window, the omitted costs remain relevant to the decision. Extending the model includes more years of the assumed dues and usage, but it still cannot determine legal obligations or saleability. An expected resale amount needs its own evidence about the net receipt, timing and costs rather than being inserted simply to make a comparison look favourable. Read the actual contract and the applicable local requirements independently of the charts. For a foreign-currency obligation, convert dues and other payments on a consistent basis and stress the exchange rate separately. The Government of Canada guide was last modified in June 2024; it is useful consumer context, while current contract terms and jurisdiction-specific questions require fresh checking. Build the comparison from use, costs and commitments you can verify Record the rights, booking limits and dates the household can realistically use. List the cash purchase, all recurring fees and possible additional charges. Choose the same accommodation and usage basis for the rental comparison. Test lower use and higher dues without assuming either is a forecast. Keep cash due dates, reporting-window costs and actual exit conditions separate. The result is a structured cost comparison, not a recommendation for or against a product. Enjoyment, flexibility, booking risk, travel costs and the household’s willingness to accept a long commitment remain part of the decision alongside the numbers.
d8ca010bc557f6239f3cdb5c157b319cbd3d4932.zh: 较低的年使用费可能隐藏大量的预付款和持续费用。将总成本除以实际使用的天数，并将模型的完成日期与合同义务分开。在比较每晚价格之前确定承诺 度假所有权、使用权安排或积分会员资格可以将预付费用与经常性费用结合起来。它对一个家庭的价值取决于所获得的权利、可用日期、这些权利的使用频率以及即使在一年没有旅行的情况下仍会持续的成本。加拿大政府的分时度假消费者指南区分了不同的安排，并建议检查可用性、额外费用、持续成本和转售条件。此处的示例不复制任何提供商的合同。他们假设现金购买并且有足够的可用性来满足输入的用途。从可比较的住宿开始：类似的日期、地点、房间类型、税费和包含的服务。会员资格并不能证明可以进行所需的预订。安静的一周观察到的租金价格也不能与高峰假期住宿进行可靠的比较。该模型将这些定性问题排除在计算之外，而不是假装成本可以解决这些问题。第一份年度账单不包括已支付的购买费用 默认情况下，首先支付 30,000 加元，然后支付 1,300 加元的第一年会费，并在使用时每年支付 100 加元的预订费。它每年使用七个晚上作为十五年的报告窗口。假定会费每年增加 4%，假设第八年将缴纳 5,000 加元的费用。第一年的经常性费用为 1,400 加元，而七晚租赁费用为 1,750 加元，每晚 250 加元。因此，如果忽略前期购买，年度成本条可能会使所有权案例看起来更便宜。累积现金图表从 30,000 加元开始，正是为了防止这种遗漏。整个窗口的会费总额约为 26,030.66 加元。加上此次购买、1,500 加元的预订费和 5,000 加元的评估费，支付的所有权现金约为 62,530.66 加元。租金替代方案（单独假设年价格增长率为 3%）总计约为 32,548.10 加元。这些是原始情景结果，而不是市场价格或特定度假村的预测。除以已使用的天数，而不是广告上宣传的天数 15 年中每年 7 个夜晚可得出实际使用的 105 个夜晚。将全部名义拥有成本除以使用量得出每晚约 595.53 加元。这是报告窗口费用的分配，而不是入住时支付的额外费用。未使用的权利不会成为模型中的免费住宿。如果没有使用住宿天数，则预订费用在上述假设下消失，但购买费用、会费和任何包含的评估仍然存在。然后，每晚成本指标表示没有使用任何晚数，而不是除以零或报告误导性的零成本。敏感性矩阵显示了实际使用的重要性。更多的住宿天数将相同的假设购买和固定年费分散到更多的消费中。这并不能证明有更多的夜晚可供选择或值得拥有，更多的旅行可能会产生此处不包括的成本。还要避免将平均拥有量与今天的租金报价直接进行比较：租金价格也会随着时间的推移而变化。比较双方相同的周期和成本基础。经常性增加和偶尔评估会产生不同的影响会费在不断增加的基础上增长。按照默认 4% 的假设，在预订费用和输入的评估之前，第八年的会费约为 1,710.71 加元。该评估将第八年的所有权现金成本提升至约 6,810.71 加元。平滑的平均年金额将掩盖较大付款到期的年份。年度栏包括第一年、结束年、窗口内的每个第五年以及任何包含的评估年。然后，瀑布会核对所有购买、会费、预订和评估费用。它们一起显示了经常性成本的积累和选定的额外账单的集中度。评估是一种压力输入。它不是一项储量研究、对财产状况的估计或概率加权预测。报告结束后分配的账单不计入当前总数；它没有被原谅。实际合同可能包含其他费用或不同的收款日期，需要将其添加到实际现金计划中。贴现未来费用不会使发票变小最终的比较将未贴现的现金成本放在现值旁边。购买时间为零。年度成本放在年底并除以 (1 + 折扣率) 年 。按照默认 3% 折扣假设，所有权成本的现值约为 55,415.26 加元，租赁成本约为 25,485.44 加元。这些当前值表示共同比较日期的时间差异。它们不是投资账户中的余额、添加到名义总额中的额外成本或会员转售价格的估计。所选贴现率是估值假设，而非提供的投资回报。未来 5,000 加元的评估在到期时仍需要 5,000 加元，即使其现值较小。实际年费也可以在模型年终大会之前收取。对于流动性规划，用实际支付日期替换年度总计；折扣成本比较并不能确定每张发票之前必须有多少现金。报告的完成并不是承诺的退出。十五年的默认期限是一个衡量窗口。它并没有规定契约、类似租赁的安排或会员资格随后就结束，买方将会出现，或者提供者将免除该家庭的进一步费用。不包括转售收据、退出付款或未使用权利的租金收入。如果实际安排在窗口期后继续进行，则忽略的成本仍然与决策相关。扩展模型包括更多年的假定费用和使用，但它仍然无法确定法律义务或可销售性。预期转售金额需要有关于净收入、时间和成本的证据，而不是仅仅为了使比较看起来有利而插入。独立于图表阅读实际合同和适用的当地要求。对于外币债务，按一致的基础折算应付款和其他付款，并分别强调汇率。加拿大政府指南最后一次修改是在 2024 年 6 月；这是有用的消费者背景，而当前的合同条款和特定于司法管辖区的问题需要重新检查。根据您可以验证的使用、成本和承诺进行比较，记录家庭可以实际使用的权利、预订限制和日期。列出现金购买、所有经常性费用和可能的额外费用。选择相同的住宿和使用基础进行租金比较。测试较低的使用量和较高的会费，而不假设其中任何一个都是预测。将现金到期日、报告窗口成本和实际退出条件分开。结果是结构化的成本比较，而不是对产品的推荐或反对。除了数字之外，享受、灵活性、预订风险、旅行费用以及家庭接受长期承诺的意愿仍然是决定的一部分。

2a9c7ac4c34eaa5ccf30ed121bb0144e8babdfaf.src: A market index describes its defined construction population and period. A workable household project still needs a current scope, a complete quote and cash for commitments outside that quote. Read what the index measures before using its percentage Statistics Canada’s 24 July 2026 release reported a 0.5% quarterly rise in the residential Building Construction Price Index for its 15-CMA composite. The first chart also displays six selected local changes, including positive and negative values. It is not a complete ranking. The index measures contractor prices for new buildings. It excludes land and specified development, design, tax and real-estate costs. It is not seasonally adjusted, and prior-quarter values may be revised. It is neither a renovation quote nor a rebuilding appraisal. The composite is not the simple average of the six local observations shown. Those scope distinctions explain why a household cannot turn the headline into a complete project budget. A statistic can supply useful background while leaving the particular work, quantities, condition and contractual inclusions unresolved. The model therefore keeps the official chart fixed and asks for a separate quote. Give the earlier estimate and the current quote a clear scope The example starts with an earlier contract budget of CAD 80,000: CAD 40,000 for materials, CAD 30,000 for labour and CAD 10,000 for other contract costs. The current quote allocates CAD 44,000, CAD 34,500 and CAD 10,000 to the same three headings, totaling CAD 88,500. The category chart makes the changes visible. Materials are CAD 4,000 higher, labour CAD 4,500 higher and other costs unchanged. Together these add CAD 8,500 to the earlier estimate, a 10.625% difference. That calculation does not establish a market inflation rate. The original estimate may have been incomplete, and the specification or quantity of work may have changed. The Canadian Home Builders’ Association’s contract guide recommends comparing quotes against the same plans and specifications. It distinguishes an early rough estimate from a detailed quote and discusses scope, payment terms, taxes and written changes. Use that checklist to establish what is actually being compared before attributing a difference to prices. Allocate the quoted taxes and costs once The calculator’s categories are bookkeeping allocations of the current contract total. They need not match every invoice line. Each amount belongs in one category only, and the three amounts together should reconcile to the quote being reviewed. Include the applicable quoted taxes consistently in those entries. If a contractor’s tax line applies across the job, allocate it across the categories or include it once within the other-cost entry. Do not add it again outside the quote. The tool does not calculate a tax rate or decide whether a supply is taxable. Known outside costs have a separate input. They might include independently obtained design services, temporary accommodation or another item that the particular contract leaves to the household. Enter only costs that are actually outside the entered quote. A service already included by the contractor must not be budgeted a second time. A CAD 88,500 quote can exceed a CAD 100,000 cash plan At first glance, a CAD 88,500 quote appears to fit within CAD 100,000 of assigned cash. The example also has CAD 5,000 of known costs outside the quote and a separately selected contingency equal to 10% of the quote. The contingency earmark is CAD 8,850, so the full selected commitment is CAD 88,500 + CAD 5,000 + CAD 8,850 = CAD 102,350 . The waterfall ends at −CAD 2,350 . The household needs that much additional funding, or a change in the work or other commitments, to support this particular plan. The starting cash must already be available for this project after other household commitments. Money required for the next mortgage payment cannot also fund the renovation. The tool creates no credit line, grant, insurance payment or investment-sale proceeds to fill a negative result. A contingency is reserved money, not a certain extra invoice A contingency holds capacity for an uncertain requirement. It is not automatically paid to a contractor, an investment loss or a prediction that costs will rise by the entered percentage. If unused, it remains household cash. The chart subtracts the earmark when calculating unassigned project cash because that amount has a job in the plan. This treatment does not reduce net worth at the time of budgeting. It prevents the same cash being presented both as a contingency and as money available for another purpose. The percentage applies to the current contract quote alone. It does not apply to the original budget or to known outside costs. At the default quote, a 5% reserve is CAD 4,425; at 10% it is CAD 8,850. Neither setting is presented as a universal professional standard or a probability-based estimate of the project’s risks. Let a quote change affect its reserve as well as its price The matrix scales the current quote by −10%, 0%, +10% and +20%, and separately tests contingency rates of 0%, 5%, 10% and 20%. Known outside costs and available cash remain selected. Every cell reports additional cash needed beyond the amount already assigned. A 10% quote increase raises the example’s contract total to CAD 97,350. With a 10% contingency, the new reserve is CAD 9,735. Adding CAD 5,000 outside costs produces CAD 112,085 of commitments and a CAD 12,085 funding need. The extra need is CAD 9,735 larger than the original CAD 2,350 gap: CAD 8,850 of quote change plus CAD 885 of additional contingency. Holding the reserve fixed while calling it 10% of a larger quote would fail to preserve the stated rule. The matrix recalculates both parts. Finish the scope review, then build the payment calendar A funded total still does not prove that every deposit or progress payment can be made on its date. This calculator assumes all entered cash is already available and does not model dates. Use the separate renovation-payment article to map actual milestones against saving receipts and other obligations. The index also cannot establish an insurer’s replacement-cost estimate, an accepted claim or a coverage limit. Those questions belong in a separate property and policy review. A lower quarterly construction-price change does not by itself justify lowering a particular policy amount. Define the work and compare consistent specifications. Reconcile the current quote, inclusions and taxes. Add verified costs that sit outside that quote. Assign a separate contingency and test changes in both amounts. Match the resulting commitments to actual cash and payment dates. Keep the source period beside the statistic and the quotation date beside the project amount. The two pieces of evidence can inform the same review while answering different questions.
2a9c7ac4c34eaa5ccf30ed121bb0144e8babdfaf.zh: 市场指数描述了其定义的建筑人口和时期。一个可行的家庭项目仍然需要当前的范围、完整的报价以及报价之外承诺的现金。在使用其百分比之前，请先阅读该指数衡量的内容加拿大统计局 2026 年 7 月 24 日发布的报告显示，其 15-CMA 综合住宅建筑价格指数季度上涨 0.5%。第一个图表还显示了六个选定的局部变化，包括正值和负值。这不是一个完整的排名。该指数衡量新建筑的承包商价格。它不包括土地和特定的开发、设计、税收和房地产成本。它没有经过季节性调整，上一季度的值可能会被修改。这既不是装修报价，也不是重建评估。该综合结果并不是所显示的六个局部观测值的简单平均值。这些范围差异解释了为什么家庭无法将标题转化为完整的项目预算。统计数据可以提供有用的背景，同时让特定的工作、数量、条件和合同内容悬而未决。因此，该模型保持官方图表固定，并要求单独报价。为先前的估算和当前报价提供明确的范围 该示例以 80,000 加元的早期合同预算开始：材料 40,000 加元，人工 30,000 加元，其他合同成本 10,000 加元。目前的报价将44,000加元、34,500加元和10,000加元分配给相同的三个标题，总计88,500加元。类别图表使更改可见。材料上涨 4,000 加元，人工上涨 4,500 加元，其他成本不变。这些合计比之前的估计增加了 8,500 加元，相差 10.625%。该计算并未确定市场通胀率。最初的估算可能不完整，工作规格或数量可能发生变化。加拿大住宅建筑商协会的合同指南建议将报价与相同的计划和规格进行比较。它区分了早期的粗略估算和详细的报价，并讨论了范围、付款条件、税收和书面变更。在将差异归因于价格之前，使用该清单来确定实际比较的内容。分配一次报价的税费和成本计算器的类别是当前合同总额的簿记分配。它们不需要匹配每个发票行。每个金额仅属于一个类别，并且三个金额合计应与正在审核的报价相符。在这些条目中一致地包含适用的报价税。如果承包商的税线适用于整个工作，请将其分配到各个类别或将其包含在其他成本条目中。不要在报价之外再次添加它。该工具不会计算税率或决定供应是否应税。已知的外部成本有单独的输入。它们可能包括独立获得的设计服务、临时住宿或特定合同留给家庭的其他项目。仅输入实际超出输入报价的成本。承包商已包含的服务不得再次列入预算。 88,500 加元的报价可能超过 100,000 加元的现金计划 乍一看，88,500 加元的报价似乎适合 100,000 加元的指定现金。该示例还包含报价之外 5,000 加元的已知成本以及单独选择的相当于报价 10% 的意外费用。应急专项资金为 8,850 加元，因此选定的全额承诺为 88,500 加元 + 5,000 加元 + 8,850 加元 = 102,350 加元。瀑布的终点价格为 -CAD 2,350 。该家庭需要大量额外资金，或者改变工作或其他承诺，以支持这一特定计划。在做出其他家庭承诺之后，该项目的启动资金必须已经可用。下一次抵押贷款所需的资金也无法为翻修提供资金。该工具不会创建信用额度、赠款、保险付款或投资销售收益来填补负面结果。应急资金是预留资金，而不是某种额外发票。应急资金具有满足不确定需求的能力。它不会自动支付给承包商、投资损失或预测成本将按输入的百分比上涨。如果未使用，它仍然是家庭现金。该图表在计算未分配的项目现金时减去了专项拨款，因为该金额在计划中占有一席之地。这种处理方法不会减少预算时的净资产。它可以防止相同的现金既作为应急资金又作为可用于其他目的的资金。该百分比仅适用于当前合同报价。它不适用于原始预算或已知的外部成本。按照默认报价，5% 准备金为 4,425 加元；按 10% 计算，价格为 8,850 加元。这两种设置都不是通用的专业标准，也不是基于概率的项目风险估计。让报价变化影响其准备金和价格 该矩阵将当前报价按-10%、0%、+10%和+20%缩放，并分别测试0%、5%、10%和20%的意外率。已知的外部成本和可用现金仍处于选择状态。每个单元都报告超出已分配金额的额外现金需求。报价上涨 10% 会使该示例的合同总额达到 97,350 加元。加上 10% 的意外开支，新储备金为 9,735 加元。加上 5,000 加元的外部成本，产生 112,085 加元的承诺和 12,085 加元的资金需求。与原来 2,350 加元的差距相比，额外需要 9,735 加元：报价变更 8,850 加元加上额外应急费用 885 加元。保持储备金固定，同时称其为较大报价的 10%，将无法保留规定的规则。矩阵重新计算这两个部分。完成范围审查，然后建立付款日历 资助总额仍然不能证明每笔定金或进度付款都可以在其日期支付。该计算器假设所有输入的现金均已可用，并且不对日期进行建模。使用单独的装修付款文章根据节省收据和其他义务来映射实际里程碑。该指数也无法确定保险公司的重置成本估算、接受的索赔或承保限额。这些问题属于单独的财产和政策审查。较低的季度建筑价格变化本身并不能证明降低特定的保单金额是合理的。定义工作并比较一致的规格。核对当前报价、所含内容和税费。添加该报价之外的经过验证的成本。分配单独的意外事件并测试这两个金额的更改。将由此产生的承诺与实际现金和付款日期相匹配。将来源期间保留在统计数据旁边，将报价日期保留在项目金额旁边。这两个证据可以在回答不同问题的同时为同一评论提供信息。

10b991037aa5c9c6e4e27913ce0c777efe30b8bf.src: Compare the exact benchmark with fund NAV total return first. Then account for the price, spread and conversion costs of your own transaction. Keep three return records separate An index return describes a calculation maintained by an index provider. A fund’s NAV total return describes the performance of its net assets with the stated distribution-reinvestment convention. Your account return additionally reflects the prices and dates of your trades, your cash flows, and any investor-level costs. Write all three on separate lines. Comparing your brokerage account gain with a headline price index can mix distributions, purchase timing, and fund implementation in one unexplained difference. A reliable comparison starts with matching dates, currency, benchmark version, and return definition. The CFA Institute’s ETF overview discusses tracking, trading costs, and premiums or discounts. Those are related dimensions, but they require different measurements. Tracking difference measures the return gap On this page, tracking difference means fund NAV total return minus benchmark total return over the same interval. Some publishers reverse the sign, so check the stated convention. If the benchmark returns 8.00% and the fund returns 7.72%, the difference is −0.28 percentage points, or −28 basis points. Tracking difference = fund NAV total return − matching benchmark total return Do not subtract the fund’s expense ratio again from a published return that is already net of those expenses. Doing so would charge the same cost twice. Similarly, if the benchmark has a net-dividend convention, do not assume the resulting gap is entirely caused by withholding tax. For a multi-year comparison, state whether you subtract annualized returns or compare cumulative wealth. These produce different-looking numbers. An eight-year cumulative shortfall cannot be labelled an annual cost without a suitable annualization. Vanguard Canada’s index-tracking explanation uses this fund-minus-index convention and distinguishes the gap from its standard-deviation measure. The OSC Investor Office’s ETF Facts sample describes displayed performance as net of expenses, supporting the check against deducting an embedded expense twice. Read the actual return definition before applying that check to a real statement. A small annual gap compounds into a different cumulative comparison The controls start both references at CAD 10,000. The benchmark’s hypothetical annual total return is 8.00%, and the fund’s annual NAV total return is 7.72%. The annual fund-minus-benchmark tracking difference is therefore −0.28 percentage points. These are assumed net NAV results; no separate expense-ratio subtraction follows. After ten identical annual factors, benchmark reference wealth is about CAD 21,589.25 and fund NAV wealth is about CAD 21,036.01. The signed fund-minus-benchmark wealth difference is approximately negative CAD 553.24. Relative to the same initial CAD 10,000, that is a −5.5324 percentage-point difference between the two cumulative returns . That cumulative return gap is neither the annual −0.28 percentage-point gap nor the percentage by which ending fund wealth is below ending benchmark wealth. Each comparison uses a different denominator or horizon. Dividing −5.5324 by ten would not recover the annual rate difference. The signed bars state each horizon explicitly. Changing the annual gap to a positive value lets the hypothetical fund exceed the benchmark; this is a sensitivity, not evidence that a real fund can repeatedly achieve that result. The benchmark wealth reference is also a calculation, rather than a directly investable account with no implementation costs. Tracking error measures how variable the gap is Tracking error is commonly the annualized standard deviation of periodic fund-minus-benchmark returns. It asks how much the gap fluctuates. It does not directly measure how much return the investor lost over the whole period. Both series have an arithmetic mean gap of −0.02 percentage points per month. Fund A has zero variability in this deliberately artificial sample; Fund B does not. This is a demonstration of the distinction, not enough history for a useful tracking-error estimate. Equal arithmetic mean gaps also do not guarantee equal compounded wealth. In a real study, record daily or monthly frequency, the sample period, the standard-deviation convention, and the annualization factor. Compare like with like rather than ranking incompatible published statistics. The monthly chart uses the exact four observations in this table, independent of the annual controls. The two artificial series have the same simple mean and different dispersion, but the page does not present their annualized standard deviations as useful estimates. A four-observation pattern illustrates a definition; it does not establish a fund’s likely future tracking error. Do not compound the active-return differences by themselves to reconstruct fund wealth. You would also need the benchmark’s return for each matching month, then compound the fund and benchmark series separately. The monthly pattern and the annual wealth path are deliberately separate examples. Build an explanation instead of guessing from the fee Suppose a hypothetical one-year gap is −0.28 percentage points. An analyst’s illustrative reconciliation might assign −0.15 to operating expenses, −0.06 to portfolio trading, −0.08 to unrecovered taxes, +0.03 to net lending revenue, and −0.02 to other implementation effects. The sum is −0.28. This is an invented attribution, not a claim that public reports reveal each component exactly. In actual research, label observed expenses separately from inferred residuals. Sampling, cash balances, valuation timing, index changes, and the treatment of corporate actions can also require investigation. A one-year favorable residual is not automatically a repeatable skill. Read the fund’s reports, benchmark methodology, replication policy, and lending disclosures before extrapolating it. Avoid choosing a fund because of a tiny return advantage that cannot be explained or survives only over one chosen interval. Your entry and exit add another layer The SEC ETF bulletin explains that exchange prices can differ from NAV and that the bid–ask spread affects investor costs. These trading effects sit outside a clean NAV-to-index comparison. Imagine an unchanged order book with a bid of 49.95 and ask of 50.05. Buying 200 units at the ask costs 10,010. An immediate sale at the bid returns 9,990, a loss of 20 before commissions. Relative to the 50 midpoint, the initial purchase costs 10 and the sale another 10. This full round-trip spread is 0.20% of the 10,000 midpoint value. A limit order controls the worst price you accept, but it can remain unfilled. Compare the quote with current underlying-market conditions; yesterday’s closing NAV may be a poor intraday fair-value reference when the underlying market is closed or moving quickly. The separate ETF bid–ask spread and order-cost guide diagrams investor execution cash. Those costs belong to your trade record. They must not be inserted into fund NAV tracking difference as though every investor incurred the same execution price or commission. Read the four figures as two controlled and two fixed examples The first two figures share the controls: they compare annual NAV and benchmark growth factors, then show their cumulative return differences at stated horizons. The final two figures retain the original article’s independent examples: four monthly active returns and a one-year attribution that sums to −0.28 percentage points. A change to the annual-gap input does not rewrite the fixed monthly pattern or scale the invented attribution components. That would imply a relationship which the example has not established. Their purpose is to show the difference between a measured gap, its variation and a proposed explanation. The attribution waterfall uses percentage points throughout. A positive lending-revenue entry offsets part of the negative entries; it is not a separate return to add again to the ending wealth line. Real disclosures may support some components better than others. Leave an unexplained residual visible instead of presenting an exact-looking invented explanation as measured evidence. A comparison sheet that can be checked Identify the legal fund, exact share class, benchmark, and hedging policy. Compare fund NAV and matching benchmark total returns over identical periods. Record operating expenses and realized tracking differences without subtracting costs twice. Inspect spread, premium or discount history, brokerage charges, and currency-conversion costs. Check holdings, replication, lending, and the explanation for persistent residuals. For a long holding period, a persistent annual gap can outweigh a modest one-time trading cost. For frequent transactions, spreads and commissions can matter much more. Estimate both using the intended behavior, and keep that estimate separate from the fund’s published performance record.
10b991037aa5c9c6e4e27913ce0c777efe30b8bf.zh: 首先将确切的基准与基金资产净值总回报进行比较。然后考虑您自己交易的价格、点差和转换成本。将三个返回记录分开 索引返回描述由索引提供者维护的计算。基金的资产净值总回报率描述了其净资产在规定的分配-再投资惯例下的表现。您的账户回报还反映了您交易的价格和日期、您的现金流以及任何投资者层面的成本。将所有三个写在不同的行上。将您的经纪账户收益与整体价格指数进行比较，可能会将分布、购买时机和基金实施混合在一起，产生一种无法解释的差异。可靠的比较从匹配日期、货币、基准版本和返回定义开始。 CFA 协会的 ETF 概述讨论了跟踪、交易成本以及溢价或折扣。这些是相关的尺寸，但它们需要不同的测量。追踪差异衡量回报差距 在本页中，追踪差异是指同一区间内基金资产净值总回报减去基准总回报。有些出版商颠倒了符号，因此请检查规定的约定。如果基准回报率为 8.00%，基金回报率为 7.72%，则差异为 -0.28 个百分点，即 -28 个基点。跟踪差值 = 基金资产净值总回报 - 匹配基准总回报 不要从已经扣除这些费用的公布回报中再次减去基金的费用比率。这样做会收取相同费用两次。同样，如果基准有净股息约定，则不要假设由此产生的缺口完全是由预扣税引起的。对于多年比较，请说明您是减去年化回报还是比较累积财富。这些会产生看起来不同的数字。如果没有适当的年度化，八年的累积缺口就不能被标记为年度成本。加拿大先锋集团的指数跟踪解释采用了基金减去指数的惯例，并将差距与其标准差衡量标准区分开来。 OSC 投资者办公室的 ETF 事实样本将显示的业绩描述为扣除费用，支持两次扣除嵌入费用的检查。在将该检查应用于实际语句之前，请阅读实际的返回定义。较小的年度差距会导致不同的累积比较。对照的起始价格为 10,000 加元。该基准的假设年度总回报率为8.00%，基金的年度资产净值总回报率为7.72%。因此，年度基金减去基准跟踪差异为-0.28 个百分点。这些是假设的净资产净值结果；随后不进行单独的费用比率扣除。经过十个相同的年度因素后，基准参考财富约为21,589.25加元，基金资产净值财富约为21,036.01加元。签署的基金减去基准财富差约为负 553.24 加元。相对于同样的初始 10,000 加元，两次累积回报之间存在 -5.5324 个百分点的差异。该累积回报差距既不是年度-0.28个百分点的差距，也不是期末基金财富低于期末基准财富的百分比。每次比较都使用不同的分母或范围。将 -5.5324 除以 10 无法恢复年利率差异。带符号的条明确地说明了每个范围。将年度差距更改为正值可以让假设的基金超过基准；这是一种敏感性，而不是真正的基金可以反复实现这一结果的证据。基准财富参考也是一种计算，而不是一个没有执行成本的直接投资账户。跟踪误差衡量差距的变化程度跟踪误差通常是定期基金收益减去基准收益的年化标准差。它询问差距波动有多大。它并不直接衡量投资者在整个期间损失了多少回报。这两个系列的算术平均差距为每月-0.02 个百分点。基金 A 在这个故意人造的样本中具有零变异性；基金B则没有。这是区别的演示，没有足够的历史来进行有用的跟踪误差估计。算术平均差距相等也不能保证复合财富相等。在实际研究中，记录每日或每月的频率、样本期、标准差约定和年化因子。比较同类数据，而不是对不兼容的已发布统计数据进行排名。月度图表使用该表中的四个观测值，与年度控制无关。这两个人工序列具有相同的简单均值和不同的离差，但该页面并未将其年化标准差作为有用的估计值。四观察模式说明了一个定义；它没有确定基金未来可能出现的跟踪误差。请勿通过复合主动回报差异来重建基金财富。您还需要每个匹配月份的基准回报，然后分别对基金和基准系列进行复合。每月的财富路径和每年的财富路径是故意分开的例子。建立一个解释，而不是根据费用进行猜测 假设假设的一年差距为 -0.28 个百分点。分析师的说明性调节可能会将-0.15分配给运营费用，-0.06分配给投资组合交易，-0.08分配给未收回的税收，+0.03分配给净贷款收入，而-0.02分配给其他实施效果。总和是-0.28。这是一种虚构的归因，而不是声称公开报告准确地揭示了每个组成部分。在实际研究中，将观察到的费用与推断的残差分开标记。抽样、现金余额、估值时机、指数变化以及公司行为的处理也可能需要调查。一年的有利剩余并不自动成为可重复的技能。在进行推断之前，请阅读该基金的报告、基准方法、复制政策和贷款披露信息。避免因为无法解释或仅在选定的时间间隔内存在的微小回报优势而选择基金。您的进场和出场增加了另一层 SEC ETF 公告解释说，交易所价格可能与资产净值不同，而且买卖价差会影响投资者成本。这些交易影响不属于干净的资产净值与指数比较的范围。想象一下订单簿未更改，出价为 49.95，要价为 50.05。按要价购买 200 件的价格为 10,010 美元。按出价立即出售可返回 9,990 美元，扣除佣金前损失 20 美元。相对于 50 中点，初始购买成本为 10，销售成本为 10。此完整往返价差为 10,000 中点值的 0.20%。限价单控制您接受的最差价格，但它可以保持未成交状态。将报价与当前的基础市场状况进行比较；当基础市场休市或快速波动时，昨天的收盘资产净值可能是一个较差的盘中公允价值参考。单独的 ETF 买卖差价和订单成本指导图显示了投资者的执行现金。这些费用属于您的交易记录。它们不得插入基金资产净值跟踪差异中，就好像每个投资者都承担相同的执行价格或佣金一样。将四个数字视为两个受控示例和两个固定示例。前两个数字共享控制：它们比较年度资产净值和基准增长因子，然后显示它们在规定范围内的累积回报差异。最后两个数字保留了原始文章的独立示例：四个月的主动回报和一年的归因，总计为-0.28个百分点。对年度差距输入的更改不会重写固定的每月模式或扩展发明的归因组件。这将意味着示例尚未建立的关系。它们的目的是显示测量的差距、其变化和建议的解释之间的差异。归因瀑布始终使用百分比。正的贷款收入条目抵消了部分负条目；它不是再次添加到最终财富线的单独回报。真实的披露可能比其他部分更好地支持某些组成部分。留下无法解释的残留可见内容，而不是提供看起来精确的发明解释作为衡量证据。可检查的比较表 确定合法基金、确切的股票类别、基准和对冲政策。比较同一时期的基金资产净值和匹配基准总回报。记录运营费用并实现跟踪差异，无需两次减去成本。检查点差、溢价或折价历史记录、经纪费用和货币兑换成本。检查持有、复制、借贷以及持久残差的解释。对于长期持有期而言，持续的年度缺口可能超过适度的一次性交易成本。对于频繁的交易，点差和佣金可能更重要。使用预期行为进行估计，并将该估计与基金公布的业绩记录分开。

84fd1f5ea252fe3abaf2b6b20792126294f47364.src: A beneficiary payment and a government assistance repayment are different outflows. Read each destination separately before interpreting the reduction in the RDSP balance. Identify where each dollar leaving the plan goes A withdrawal-related reduction in a Registered Disability Savings Plan (RDSP) balance need not equal the money directed to the beneficiary. A permitted payment can be accompanied by a separate repayment of government grants and bonds. Those two destinations should remain visible in the household’s cash plan. Employment and Social Development Canada’s withdrawal guidance explains that certain withdrawals can trigger assistance repayment. The illustration here isolates an ordinary proportional-repayment case for a beneficiary who remains eligible for the Disability Tax Credit (DTC), before the calendar year in which they turn sixty. It assumes that the issuer has separately confirmed the proposed payment is permitted. It does not decide whether someone can withdraw, establish an annual payment limit or cover specified disability savings plans, loss of DTC eligibility, closure or death. Those conditions can change the applicable treatment and need their own review. Use the applicable assistance holdback amount rather than lifetime grants The assistance holdback amount, or AHA, is a defined measure of recent government assistance, reduced by relevant amounts already repaid. It is not simply every grant and bond ever received, and it is not automatically the entire RDSP balance. The default example enters an assumed issuer-confirmed AHA of CAD 10,000 and a plan fair market value of CAD 100,000. These are invented records for teaching. The calculator does not derive the holdback from account age, contribution history or a presumed final grant date. Payment dates and prior repayments matter when an issuer determines the applicable amount. The ordinary definition refers to the preceding ten-year period, while special circumstances require separate treatment. A single balance field cannot establish that a particular assistance payment has aged out. The controls’ limits are illustration boundaries, rather than RDSP program limits. They keep sufficient plan assets in every displayed case so that the selected gross payment and assistance repayment can be reconciled without a negative plan value. Apply the ordinary repayment calculation to the hypothetical payment For the scoped ordinary case, section 5.3 of the Canada Disability Savings Regulations sets repayment as the least of three amounts: three dollars per dollar of the disability assistance payment, pre-payment plan fair market value and the applicable AHA. The gross beneficiary payment is CAD 2,500. Three times that amount is CAD 7,500, below both the CAD 10,000 entered AHA and CAD 100,000 opening value. The modeled assistance repayment is consequently CAD 7,500 . The beneficiary payment and assistance repayment together remove CAD 10,000 from the plan. Subtracting those two outflows leaves CAD 90,000 in the RDSP. The waterfall traces each destination rather than presenting the whole CAD 10,000 reduction as cash paid to the beneficiary. This calculation assumes the ordinary rule applies. It does not convert an entered request into an authorized payment or replace the issuer’s application of other payment conditions. Read the cap without treating several scenarios as repeated payments The line chart varies a single gross beneficiary payment against the same hypothetical starting record. Assistance repayment initially rises at three times the gross payment, until the entered AHA caps it. The combined plan outflow includes both the payment and repayment. With the default CAD 10,000 AHA, the cap is reached at a gross payment of CAD 10,000 divided by three. The plot includes that exact turning point, rather than drawing a smoothed curve that obscures the change in slope. Each point is an alternative single transaction. It is not a sequence of withdrawals that each starts again with CAD 10,000 of holdback. In the selected CAD 2,500 example, repaying CAD 7,500 reduces the entered AHA to CAD 2,500 immediately after the modeled repayment, assuming no intervening changes. The grouped bars compare different hypothetical starting AHAs while holding the selected payment constant. Actual subsequent payments require an updated issuer record, including any new assistance, aging or other relevant event. Distinguish plan outflow from household wealth lost For a small payment while the three-for-one rule is uncapped, CAD 1 directed to the beneficiary can be accompanied by CAD 3 repaid to government. The matrix describes this as CAD 4 leaving the RDSP for each CAD 1 of gross beneficiary payment. That is a measure of plan outflow, rather than CAD 4 of household wealth automatically disappearing. If the beneficiary retains the CAD 1 outside the RDSP, it remains a household asset. In the default example, CAD 90,000 remains in the plan and CAD 2,500 is directed outside it, totaling CAD 92,500 before any tax or other cost. The separate CAD 7,500 government repayment explains the reduction from the original CAD 100,000 combined resources under that retained-cash assumption. Spending the beneficiary payment would create a further change outside this plan-only ledger. A lower outflow ratio after the cap binds is not a reason to request more money. A larger payment can lower that ratio while still removing more dollars from the plan. The actual cash need and the permitted payment are separate decisions. Confirm the permitted payment and spendable cash separately A gross beneficiary payment does not establish after-tax spending cash. The payment’s composition and applicable tax treatment require separate calculation. This tool does not divide it into taxable and non-taxable portions, estimate withholding or assess effects on benefits. The CRA’s RDSP guide discusses payment conditions and exceptions beyond the simplified ordinary case. Confirm the applicable AHA, permitted payment, repayment amount and net cash treatment with the issuer before using real amounts in a plan. The legal consolidation consulted was current to 30 September 2026 and last amended on 29 June 2021; the sources were reviewed on 25 October 2026. Recheck the current rules and the account record for an actual transaction. The four charts explain a narrow reconciliation while keeping those unresolved eligibility and payment details outside the arithmetic.
84fd1f5ea252fe3abaf2b6b20792126294f47364.zh: 受益人付款和政府援助偿还是不同的流出。在解释 RDSP 余额减少之前，请分别阅读每个目的地。确定离开计划的每一美元的去向 注册残障储蓄计划 (RDSP) 余额中与提款相关的减少不一定等于直接流向受益人的资金。允许的付款可以伴随着政府补助和债券的单独偿还。这两个目的地应该在家庭的现金计划中保持可见。加拿大就业和社会发展部的提款指南解释说，某些提款可能会触发援助偿还。这里的插图隔离了受益人在年满 60 岁之前仍然有资格获得残疾税收抵免 (DTC) 的普通比例还款案例。它假设发行人已单独确认允许提议的付款。它不决定某人是否可以提款、设立年度付款限额或承保指定的残疾储蓄计划、丧失 DTC 资格、关闭或死亡。这些情况可能会改变适用的治疗方法，需要自行审查。使用适用的援助保留金额而不是终生补助金 援助保留金额 (AHA) 是近期政府援助的明确衡量标准，减去已偿还的相关金额。它不仅仅是收到的每笔赠款和债券，也不会自动成为整个 RDSP 余额。默认示例输入假设发行人确认的 AHA 为 10,000 加元，计划公平市场价值为 100,000 加元。这些是为教学而发明的记录。该计算器不会根据帐户年龄、缴款历史或假定的最终授予日期得出保留金额。当发行人确定适用金额时，付款日期和提前还款很重要。一般定义是指前十年，特殊情况需另行处理。单个余额字段无法确定特定援助付款已过期。控件的限制是插图边界，而不是 RDSP 程序限制。他们在每个展示的案例中都保留了足够的计划资产，以便可以对所选的总付款和援助还款进行核对，而不会出现负计划价值。将普通还款计算应用于假设付款 对于范围内的普通情况，《加拿大残疾人储蓄条例》第 5.3 节将还款设置为三个金额中的至少一个：残疾援助金每 1 美元 3 美元、预付款计划公平市场价值和适用的 AHA。受益人付款总额为 2,500 加元。该金额的三倍为 7,500 加元，低于输入 AHA 的 10,000 加元和开仓值 100,000 加元。因此，模拟的援助偿还金额为 7,500 加元。受益人付款和援助偿还一起从计划中扣除 10,000 加元。减去这两笔资金流出后，RDSP 中剩下 90,000 加元。瀑布会追踪每个目的地，而不是将 10,000 加元的减免额全部作为现金支付给受益人。此计算假设适用普通规则。它不会将输入的请求转换为授权付款或取代发行人对其他付款条件的应用。阅读上限，而不将多种情况视为重复付款。折线图根据相同的假设起始记录来改变单个总受益人付款。援助还款最初会增加至总付款的三倍，直到 AHA 设定上限。合并计划流出包括付款和还款。默认 AHA 为 10,000 CAD，付款总额为 10,000 CAD 除以三即可达到上限。该图包含了确切的转折点，而不是绘制一条模糊斜率变化的平滑曲线。每个点都是一个替代的单笔交易。这并不是一系列提款，每次提款都以 10,000 加元的扣留重新开始。在所选的 2,500 加元示例中，假设没有任何中间更改，则在建模还款后，偿还 7,500 加元会立即将输入的 AHA 减少到 2,500 加元。分组条比较不同假设的起始 AHA，同时保持所选付款不变。实际的后续付款需要更新的发行人记录，包括任何新的援助、账龄或其他相关事件。区分计划流出和家庭财富损失 对于小额付款，在三买一规则没有上限的情况下，可以将 1 加元直接交给受益人，同时向政府偿还 3 加元。该矩阵将其描述为每 1 加元的受益人总支付额需要 4 加元的 RDSP。这是衡量计划流出的指标，而不是家庭财富自动消失的 4 加元。如果受益人在 RDSP 之外保留 1 加元，它仍然是家庭资产。在默认示例中，90,000 加元保留在计划中，2,500 加元直接用于计划之外，总计 92,500 加元（不含任何税费或其他成本）。政府单独偿还 7,500 加元解释了在保留现金假设下原始 100,000 加元合并资源的减少。支出受益人付款将在该仅限计划的分类账之外产生进一步的变化。上限约束后较低的流出率并不是要求更多资金的理由。较大的付款可以降低该比率，同时仍从计划中扣除更多资金。实际的现金需求和允许的付款是单独的决定。分别确认允许的付款和可支出现金 受益人付款总额不构成税后支出现金。付款的构成和适用的税收处理需要单独计算。该工具不会将其分为应税部分和非应税部分、估计预扣税或评估对福利的影响。 CRA 的 RDSP 指南讨论了简化普通情况之外的付款条件和例外情况。在计划中使用实际金额之前，请与发行人确认适用的 AHA、允许的付款、还款金额和净现金处理。咨询的法律合并有效期截至2026年9月30日，最后一次修订于2021年6月29日；来源已于 2026 年 10 月 25 日审核。重新检查当前规则和实际交易的账户记录。这四张图表解释了狭隘的对账，同时将那些未解决的资格和付款细节保留在算术之外。

5004705047c5eadd467edd520aabe5b3dc26cd66.src: Track sales-tax money separately from the customer payment total. A bank balance can include tax still owed, while a potential refund may not yet be cash. Separate the sale from the tax within the same deposit A customer payment can contain both the price of a sale and GST/HST charged on it. Both amounts may reach the same bank account, but the full deposit is not automatically business income available for an owner’s household spending. CRA’s collection guidance states that collected GST/HST is held in trust until remitted. The first chart therefore splits the hypothetical monthly customer receipt into CAD 10,000 excluding tax and CAD 1,300 of separately entered GST/HST. The example assumes a registrant and uses independently supported tax amounts as inputs. It does not choose a place-of-supply rate, decide whether a sale is taxable or test whether registration is required. These are management-ledger illustrations, not completed GST/HST returns. Keep the input-tax assumption explicit CRA’s net-tax guidance describes the regular method using tax collected or collectible and eligible input tax credits, with applicable adjustments. A business cannot assume every tax-looking payment qualifies for the same credit. The default operating cash payment is CAD 6,000 excluding tax. Another CAD 400 is paid as GST/HST and assumed fully eligible, documented and claimed as an input tax credit in the relevant model period. The simplified monthly net-tax amount is CAD 1,300 − CAD 400 = CAD 900. No adjustment or special method is modeled. If the entered tax paid would be only partly recoverable, or if the business uses a different calculation method, this simplified ledger does not establish the correct filing amount. Use the applicable records and method before treating the illustrated reserve as a real liability estimate. Follow the bank movement before treating the balance as free cash Each default month brings CAD 11,300 of customer cash and pays CAD 6,400 of operating costs including the separately entered input tax. The bank position increases by CAD 4,900. Of that increase, CAD 900 represents positive unsettled net tax in the illustration. The other CAD 4,000 is the difference between receipts and operating cash payments excluding GST/HST. It is a narrow operating cash subtotal, not a calculation of taxable income or an owner’s after-tax pay. Income tax, payroll, capital purchases, debt payments and other commitments are outside this tool. After three months, opening cash of CAD 5,000 has become CAD 19,700. The positive tax reserve is CAD 2,700, leaving a cash position of CAD 17,000 after that reserve. The two lines show these different readings of the same bank resources. Paying an amount already reserved is not a second operating cost The model groups months 1–3 into a first period and months 4–6 into a second. At the start of month 4, it pays the first period’s positive CAD 2,700 net-tax amount. This is an explicitly selected planning event, not a statutory deadline calculated from a reporting frequency. The later bank position includes that payment once. By the end of month 6, the bank funding position is CAD 31,700. A new CAD 2,700 reserve has accumulated for the second period, so the position after that reserve is CAD 29,000. The waterfall reconciles opening cash, receipts and payments. The closing reserve remains inside the bank amount; deducting it as a bank payment and then subtracting it again from closing cash would double-count the same obligation. The after-reserve metric performs the planning subtraction separately. A potential refund needs a separate receipt assumption Change the eligible input-tax assumption above the tax charged and received. The simplified net-tax result then becomes negative. The illustration tracks that amount as a potential receivable and reserves no negative amount from the bank. At the first period boundary, a negative amount remains a separate potential receivable awaiting cash. The tool does not deposit it automatically in month 4. The second period’s negative amount also remains outside the bank total. This makes the cash needed to wait for a possible refund visible without promising an approval or payment date. The eligibility assumption is still essential. A mathematical negative result does not establish that CRA owes the amount or when it will arrive. The cash ledger contains only the receipts actually assumed to have occurred, while the chart preserves the potential amount awaiting cash. Connect the tax record to the business and household plan CRA’s collection guidance notes that tax charged belongs in the reporting period covering the invoice date even if the customer has not yet paid. This model deliberately assumes invoices and related cash are received in the same month. It therefore does not solve the additional funding need created by unpaid invoices. For an actual plan, keep the invoice record, collection date, eligible purchase-tax record and remittance calendar distinct. A tax reserve is also separate from the provision for personal or corporate income tax. The related self-employment guide addresses how business cash connects to an owner’s household draw. The position after the GST/HST reserve is a useful intermediate number. Apply the other business obligations and household commitments before deciding what can leave the account. If the modeled position is negative, it identifies missing funding; it does not assume a bank will supply credit.
5004705047c5eadd467edd520aabe5b3dc26cd66.zh: 与客户付款总额分开跟踪销售税金额。银行余额可能包括仍欠的税款，而潜在的退款可能还不是现金。在同一笔存款中将销售与税收分开客户付款可以包含销售价格和对其收取的 GST/HST。这两笔金额可能会存入同一个银行账户，但全额存款不会自动成为可用于业主家庭支出的商业收入。 CRA 的征收指南规定，征收的 GST/HST 将由信托机构保管，直至汇出。因此，第一个图表将假设的每月客户收入分为 10,000 加元（不含税）和 1,300 加元（单独输入的 GST/HST）。该示例假设注册人并使用独立支持的税额作为输入。它不选择供应地税率、决定销售是否应税或测试是否需要注册。这些是管理分类账插图，不是完整的 GST/HST 申报表。保持进项税假设明确 CRA 的净税指引描述了使用已征收或可征收税款以及符合条件的进项税抵免的常规方法，并进行了适用的调整。企业不能假设每笔看似纳税的付款都符合相同的抵免资格。默认运营现金支付为 6,000 加元（不含税）。另外 400 加元作为 GST/HST 支付，并假设完全符合相关模型期间的进项税抵免资格、记录并申请。简化后的每月净税额为 1,300 加元 − 400 加元 = 900 加元。未对调整或特殊方法进行建模。如果输入的已付税款只能部分收回，或者如果企业使用不同的计算方法，则此简化分类账不会建立正确的申报金额。在将说明准备金视为实际负债估计之前，请使用适用的记录和方法。在将余额视为自由现金之前，请跟踪银行动态 每个违约月份都会带来 11,300 加元的客户现金，并支付 6,400 加元的运营成本（包括单独输入的进项税）。银行头寸增加 4,900 加元。其中，900 加元代表图中未结算的正净税额。另外 4,000 加元是收入与运营现金付款之间的差额，不包括 GST/HST。它是狭义的经营现金小计，而不是应税收入或所有者的税后工资的计算。所得税、工资、资本购买、债务支付和其他承诺不在此工具范围内。三个月后，开仓现金5000加元变成了19700加元。正税收储备金为 2,700 加元，扣除该储备金后，现金头寸为 17,000 加元。这两行显示了相同银行资源的不同读数。支付已预留的金额不是第二个运营成本 该模型将第 1-3 个月分组为第一个期间，将第 4-6 个月分组为第二个期间。在第 4 个月开始时，它支付第一期的正净税额 2,700 加元。这是明确选择的规划事件，而不是根据报告频率计算的法定截止日期。稍后的银行头寸包括一次该付款。截至第 6 月底，银行资金头寸为 31,700 加元。第二期已累积 2,700 加元的新储备金，因此该储备金之后的头寸为 29,000 加元。瀑布调节期初现金、收入和付款。期末准备金保留在银行金额内；将其作为银行付款扣除，然后再次从结清现金中扣除，会重复计算相同的义务。预留后指标单独执行计划减法。潜在退款需要单独的收款假设 将符合条件的进项税假设更改为高于收取和收到的税款。简化后的净税结果将变为负值。该插图将该金额跟踪为潜在应收款，并且没有从银行保留负金额。在第一期边界，负金额仍然是等待现金的单独潜在应收款。该工具不会在第 4 个月自动存入。第二个期间的负金额也保留在银行总额之外。这使得等待可能的退款所需的现金可见，而无需承诺批准或付款日期。资格假设仍然至关重要。数学上的负结果并不能证明 CRA 欠下该金额或该金额何时到达。现金分类账仅包含实际假设已发生的收款，而图表则保留等待现金的潜在金额。将税务记录与企业和家庭计划联系起来 CRA 的征收指南指出，即使客户尚未付款，所收取的税款也属于发票日期的报告期内。该模型故意假设发票和相关现金在同一个月收到。因此，它并不能解决因未付发票而产生的额外资金需求。对于实际计划，请保持发票记录、收款日期、合格的购置税记录和汇款日历不同。税收储备金也与个人或企业所得税的拨备分开。相关的自营职业指南阐述了企业现金如何与业主的家庭收入联系起来。 GST/HST 储备金后面的位置是一个有用的中间数字。在决定哪些内容可以离开帐户之前，请先应用其他业务义务和家庭承诺。如果建模头寸为负，则表明资金缺失；它不假设银行将提供信贷。

0edc3355991c146aa7ec98872ffbabff7782a6b2.src: A maturity amount cannot fund an earlier bill by itself. Compare the cash available after the bill and all loan settlement, using the actual withdrawal and credit terms. Confirm access before comparing a quoted rate The FCAC’s GIC and term-deposit disclosure guide identifies principal and interest payment terms, charges, and whether early cashing is possible. It also describes disclosure of net proceeds and charges before an allowed early redemption. That information requirement does not establish that a locked product can be broken. The two contracts in this model are independently authored assumptions. No bank’s withdrawal permission, minimum balance, interest treatment or product rate is imported. Both routes begin with CAD 20,000 and must fund the same CAD 5,000 bill after ninety completed days. They finish at day 365. The comparison includes only these defined cash flows. It cannot replace checking the actual contract or deciding how much accessible cash the household needs for other purposes. Apply the cashable rate to the principal that remains The hypothetical cashable contract pays 3% simple annual interest on daily principal. It permits a principal-only partial withdrawal after thirty completed days. The model assumes all accrued interest is paid at day 365, with no withdrawal fee or change in the selected rate. The first ninety days earn interest on CAD 20,000. The CAD 5,000 withdrawal then pays the bill, leaving CAD 15,000 to earn interest for the remaining 275 days. Interest across those two intervals totals approximately CAD 486.99. Ending cash is therefore approximately CAD 15,486.99: remaining principal plus the modeled interest. The interest had not been received when the earlier bill was due, so it is not counted as part of that bill’s funding. Actual cashable products can have different withdrawal and interest rules; these particular assumptions need independent confirmation before use. Treat the bridge as a separate prerequisite and liability The locked contract pays 4.5% simple interest for the full year and releases nothing earlier. It returns CAD 20,900 at day 365. That larger maturity amount alone cannot pay the day-ninety bill. The second route assumes a separately available CAD 5,000 bridge advance funds that bill. At an assumed 8% simple annual rate over 275 days, bridge interest is approximately CAD 301.37. Both loan principal and interest become payable at day 365. After repaying CAD 5,301.37 from maturity proceeds, approximately CAD 15,598.63 remains. The waterfall deducts the loan settlement once. It does not deduct the earlier bill again because the bridge advance already funded it. If the assumed credit is unavailable, this locked-deposit route cannot fund the earlier bill as modeled. Compare the actual interest paths, not two untouched deposits The locked-plus-bridge route finishes approximately CAD 111.64 ahead in the default, before fees and taxes. The shared initial principal and shared bill cancel when the two ending balances are compared. The interest bridge explains the remainder: CAD 900 of locked interest less approximately CAD 486.99 of cashable interest gives about CAD 413.01. Subtract approximately CAD 301.37 of bridge interest, leaving the CAD 111.64 difference. Using CAD 600 as cashable interest would be inconsistent with this scenario. That would assume the entire CAD 20,000 stayed invested for the full year, even though CAD 5,000 funded the earlier bill. Likewise, comparing only the two deposit rates would omit the separate borrowing cost. Keep the amount invested, withdrawal date and funding route consistent throughout the comparison. Test timing and borrowing cost while holding the bill constant The matrix varies the completed days before the bill and the simple bridge rate. Initial principal, the bill percentage and both deposit rates stay selected. Each signed cell is locked-plus-bridge ending cash minus cashable ending cash at the common day-365 endpoint. A later bill shortens the borrowing interval but also leaves more principal earning the cashable rate before withdrawal. The calculation includes both effects. Changing the bill’s percentage changes how much principal leaves the cashable deposit and how much the bridge must advance. A positive cell is an arithmetic advantage under the chosen assumptions, not proof of an available or suitable strategy. Fees, taxes, changing rates or repayment conditions can change the result. A negative locked-route endpoint means additional outside cash is required at settlement; the model does not create further borrowing to fill it. Build the payment plan from confirmed net amounts and dates For an actual decision, confirm whether partial withdrawal is permitted, how it changes interest, when interest is paid, and what charges or minimum balances apply. Obtain the expected net amount rather than assuming the headline deposit rate determines the withdrawal proceeds. Confirm any separate funding source before relying on it. Its amount, fees, interest convention, payment dates and maturity need to match the bill and deposit dates. Paying interest regularly or repaying principal earlier would require different cash flows from the single settlement modeled here. The example uses a fixed 365-day year, simple interest, no fees and no tax. It does not model rollovers, emergency access rights or lending approval. Its purpose is to compare equal starting resources, the same expense and a common finish date while making the cost and availability of the earlier funding explicit.
0edc3355991c146aa7ec98872ffbabff7782a6b2.zh: 到期金额本身无法为较早的账单提供资金。使用实际的提款和信用条款，比较账单和所有贷款结算后的可用现金。在比较报价之前确认访问 FCAC 的 GIC 和定期存款披露指南确定了本金和利息支付条款、费用以及是否可以提前兑现。它还描述了在允许提前赎回之前披露净收益和费用。该信息要求并不表明锁定的产品可以被破坏。该模型中的两个合约是独立编写的假设。不导入银行的取款权限、最低余额、利息处理或产品利率。两条路线的起始费用都是 20,000 加元，并且在完成 90 天后必须支付同样的 5,000 加元账单。它们在第 365 天结束。比较仅包括这些定义的现金流量。它不能取代检查实际合同或决定家庭需要多少可用现金用于其他目的。将可兑现利率应用于剩余本金 假设的可兑现合约按每日本金还款 3% 的简单年利率。它允许在三十个完整天后仅提取本金的部分资金。该模型假设所有应计利息均在第 365 天支付，没有提款费用或所选利率的变化。前 90 天可赚取 20,000 加元的利息。然后提取 5,000 加元支付账单，剩下 15,000 加元可赚取剩余 275 天的利息。这两个时间段的利息总计约为 486.99 加元。因此，期末现金约为 15,486.99 加元：剩余本金加上模拟利息。较早的账单到期时尚未收到利息，因此不计入该账单资金的一部分。实际变现产品可能有不同的提现和利息规则；这些特定假设在使用前需要独立确认。将桥梁视为单独的先决条件和责任 锁定合同全年支付 4.5% 的单利，并且不会提前释放任何内容。第 365 天返回 20,900 加元。仅靠这一较大的到期金额无法支付第 90 天的账单。第二条路线假设有单独可用的 5,000 加元过桥预付款。假定 275 天的简单年利率为 8%，过桥利息约为 301.37 加元。贷款本金和利息均于第 365 天支付。从到期收益中偿还 5,301.37 加元后，大约还剩 15,598.63 加元。瀑布一次扣除贷款结算。它不会再次扣除之前的账单，因为过桥预付款已经为其提供了资金。如果假定的信用不可用，则该锁定存款途径无法为模型中的早期账单提供资金。比较实际的利息路径，而不是两笔未触及的存款。锁定加桥梁路线在默认情况下提前完成约 111.64 加元（未扣除费用和税费）。当比较两个期末余额时，共享初始本金和共享账单取消。利息桥梁解释了其余部分：锁定利息 900 加元减去可兑现利息约 486.99 加元，得到约 413.01 加元。减去大约 301.37 加元的过桥利息，留下 111.64 加元的差额。使用 600 加元作为可兑现利息与这种情况不一致。这假设全年的投资额为 20,000 加元，尽管之前的账单有 5,000 加元的资金。同样，仅比较两种存款利率会忽略单独的借贷成本。在整个比较过程中保持投资金额、提款日期和资金途径一致。在保持帐单不变的情况下测试时间和借贷成本 该矩阵会改变帐单前的完成天数和简单过桥利率。初始本金、账单百分比和存款利率均保持选定状态。每个签名的单元格都是锁定加桥期结束现金减去公共 365 天端点处的可兑现结束现金。较晚的法案缩短了借款间隔，但也留下了更多本金在提款前赚取可兑现利率。计算包括这两种效应。改变账单的百分比会改变可兑现存款的本金金额以及桥梁必须预付的金额。正细胞是在所选假设下的算术优势，而不是可用或合适策略的证明。费用、税收、变化的利率或还款条件可能会改变结果。负的锁定路线端点意味着结算时需要额外的外部现金；该模型不会创造进一步的借贷来填补它。根据已确认的净额和日期制定还款计划 对于实际决策，请确认是否允许部分提款、利息如何变化、何时支付利息以及适用哪些费用或最低余额。获取预期净额，而不是假设总体存款利率决定取款收益。在依赖任何单独的资金来源之前先确认它。其金额、费用、利息约定、付款日期和到期日需要与账单和存款日期相匹配。定期支付利息或提前偿还本金将需要与此处建模的单一结算不同的现金流量。该示例使用固定的一年 365 天、单利、无费用、无税款。它不会对展期、紧急访问权或贷款审批进行建模。其目的是比较同等的起始资源、相同的费用和共同的完成日期，同时明确早期资金的成本和可用性。

88581bd7b578b0af810ea3cd7d534ab694e74a58.src: A low current premium creates a future resource only if the household keeps the unused budget. That cash belongs to the household reserve, not to the term policy. Separate the current payment from the renewal conditions The Financial Consumer Agency of Canada’s life-insurance guide explains that certain term policies may be renewed and premiums may increase at renewal. It also distinguishes term insurance from policies with cash value. Those general points do not establish the terms of a particular contract. The illustration takes two monthly premium amounts as independent inputs. It does not estimate premiums from age, health, occupation or an insurer’s pricing. Nor does it establish that renewal or conversion is available, that a new application will be accepted, or that both periods provide the same benefits. Begin a real review with the policy’s actual premium schedule, renewal conditions and coverage details. Confirm whether a future amount is specified by the contract or depends on a new quote. A comparison of cash payments is not a recommendation to cancel or replace existing coverage. Give the two periods an explicit length and boundary The default has two ten-year periods. A selected CAD 50 monthly premium applies in months one through 120. An independently selected CAD 250 monthly premium applies in months 121 through 240. The equal lengths and fixed premium within each block are simplifying assumptions. An actual renewal schedule with annual changes or different term lengths needs its own dates and amounts. This calculator does not extend either selected premium indefinitely beyond its stated block. The household assigns CAD 150 each month to the dedicated premium budget. That assignment arrives before the modeled premium payment. It is a transfer from other household resources, not additional household income. The remaining regular budget must be able to support the full assignment throughout the twenty-year example. Keep the early difference if it is meant to fund the later bill During the first period, each CAD 150 assignment pays a CAD 50 premium and retains CAD 100. With no interest and no withdrawals, 120 monthly differences build a CAD 12,000 cash reserve. During the second period, the CAD 250 premium exceeds the ongoing CAD 150 assignment by CAD 100 per month. The reserve supplies that difference for 120 months and finishes at zero. The path chart shows the accumulation and later use of the same separately held cash. If the first-period CAD 100 difference is spent elsewhere, it is not available for the later premiums. The household would need a different funding plan, such as more cash assigned during the second period or a separately funded reserve. The illustration does not assume an emergency fund can be used twice or automatically restore cash spent on another goal. Premium totals and a reserve balance are different quantities First-period premiums total CAD 6,000. Second-period premiums total CAD 30,000. The combined CAD 36,000 equals 240 household assignments of CAD 150, so the dedicated budget reconciles to zero in the default. The waterfall records those assignments and premium outflows. It does not turn CAD 36,000 of payments into an investment balance. The CAD 12,000 peak reserve is cash the household retained before paying later premiums; it is not cash accumulated inside the term policy. Likewise, cumulative premiums do not measure the value of protection received or a refund payable on cancellation. The model calculates no death benefit, claim probability, surrender value, tax outcome or return on premiums. Use the related coverage-needs guide to examine the household funding gap that insurance is intended to address. Test the future premium beside the ongoing assignment The matrix varies the second-period premium and monthly household assignment while keeping the first premium, period lengths and selected opening reserve fixed. Each cell reports extra cash needed at the beginning to prevent any modeled negative balance. A zero cell means the selected cash assignments and reserve cover that particular payment schedule. It does not confirm that the assignment is affordable, the premium is available or the coverage is sufficient. A positive cell is an unfunded requirement, rather than an automatic loan. A larger opening reserve shifts the whole path upward. A larger monthly assignment changes the path over time. They are different commitments to household cash, so check both the amount tied up initially and the recurring amount no longer available for other priorities. The lowest balance matters alongside the final reconciliation. Review coverage and funding when the actual schedule changes Review the plan before a confirmed renewal or other premium change. Compare the payment dates with actual income receipts and other commitments. The monthly assignment-before-premium convention must match the real cash calendar; a later transfer cannot fund an earlier debit. Keep the dedicated reserve visible in the household balance sheet and avoid counting it simultaneously toward another goal. If the reserve earns interest, incurs tax or is used for another purpose, record those cash flows explicitly rather than assuming the zero-return path still applies. This example assumes every selected premium is paid and models no death, claim, cancellation or lapse. It also assumes no further renewal after the second block. Its purpose is to make the funding schedule reviewable while leaving policy rights, underwriting, coverage suitability and actual premium commitments to separately verified information.
88581bd7b578b0af810ea3cd7d534ab694e74a58.zh: 仅当家庭保留未使用的预算时，当前较低的保费才能创造未来资源。这些现金属于家庭储备，而不是保单。将当前付款与续保条件分开加拿大金融消费者局的人寿保险指南解释说，某些定期保单可能会续保，并且续保时保费可能会增加。它还将定期保险与具有现金价值的保单区分开来。这些一般要点并不构成特定合同的条款。该图以两个每月保费金额作为独立输入。它不会根据年龄、健康状况、职业或保险公司的定价来估算保费。它也没有规定可以续订或转换，新的申请将被接受，或者两个时期提供相同的福利。开始对保单的实际保费表、续保条件和承保详细信息进行真正的审查。确认未来金额是由合同指定还是取决于新报价。现金支付的比较并不建议取消或更换现有的保险。为两个时期指定明确的长度和边界 默认有两个十年期。选定的 50 加元每月保费适用于第 1 至 120 个月。独立选择的 250 加元每月保费适用于第 121 至 240 个月。每个区块内的相同长度和固定保费简化了假设。具有年度变化或不同期限长度的实际续订时间表需要有自己的日期和金额。该计算器不会将任何选定的保费无限期地延长到超出其规定的范围。该家庭每月分配 150 加元作为专用保费预算。该任务在模型溢价支付之前到达。这是来自其他家庭资源的转移，而不是额外的家庭收入。剩余的常规预算必须能够支持整个二十年的全部任务。如果要为以后的账单提供资金，请保留早期差额。在第一个期间，每项 150 加元的任务需支付 50 加元的溢价，并保留 100 加元。在没有利息和提款的情况下，120 个月的差额可建立 12,000 加元的现金储备。在第二个期间，每月 250 加元的保费比正在进行的 150 加元的分配多出 100 加元。储备供应的差异持续 120 个月，最终为零。路径图显示了相同的单独持有现金的积累和以后的使用。如果第一期的100加元差额用于其他地方，则不能用于以后的保费。该家庭需要不同的资金计划，例如在第二阶段分配更多现金或单独资助的储备金。该插图并未假设应急基金可以使用两次或自动恢复用于另一个目标的现金。保费总额和准备金余额的数量不同 第一期保费总额为 6,000 加元。第二期保费总计 30,000 加元。合计 36,000 加元等于 240 个家庭分配的 150 加元，因此默认情况下专用预算将调整为零。瀑布记录了这些任务和溢价流出。它不会将 36,000 加元的付款转化为投资余额。 12,000加元的峰值储备金是家庭在支付后续保费之前保留的现金；它不是在期限保单内积累的现金。同样，累积保费也不能衡量所获得的保障的价值或取消时应付的退款。该模型不计算死亡抚恤金、索赔概率、退保价值、税务结果或保费回报。使用相关的承保需求指南来检查保险旨在解决的家庭资金缺口。除了正在进行的分配之外，还测试未来的保费 该矩阵会改变第二期保费和每月家庭分配，同时保持第一期保费、期间长度和选定的期初准备金固定。每个单元在开始时都会报告所需的额外现金，以防止出现任何建模负余额。零单元格意味着所选现金分配和储备金涵盖该特定付款计划。它并不确认转让是否负担得起、保费是否可用或承保范围是否足够。阳性细胞是无资金支持的要求，而不是自动贷款。较大的开放储备会使整个路径向上移动。随着时间的推移，更大的每月任务会改变路径。它们是对家庭现金的不同承诺，因此请检查最初占用的金额和不再可用于其他优先事项的经常性金额。最低余额与最终对账同样重要。当实际计划发生变化时，审查承保范围和资金情况 在确认续保或其他保费变更之前审查计划。将付款日期与实际收入收入和其他承诺进行比较。每月分配先于保费的惯例必须与实际现金日历相匹配；较晚的转账无法为较早的借记提供资金。在家庭资产负债表中保持专用储备的可见性，并避免同时将其计入另一个目标。如果准备金赚取利息、产生税收或用于其他目的，请明确记录这些现金流量，而不是假设零回报路径仍然适用。此示例假设每笔选定的保费均已支付，并且没有死亡、索赔、取消或失效的模型。它还假设在第二个区块之后不再进一步更新。其目的是使资金计划可审查，同时将保单权利、承保、承保适用性和实际保费承诺留给单独验证的信息。

1941a44f88906be4d27e7af851fa21b78594385d.src: A closing price level does not reveal when the price increases arrived. Earlier increases can affect more withdrawals, even when the investment return and final price level match. Hold the inflation factors constant and change only their order The first chart draws two price paths. In the original example, one has three years of 8% inflation followed by seven years of 2%. The other reverses exactly those ten annual factors. Both finish with the same price level: approximately 144.7 when the starting index is 100. The rates are invented. They are not a replay of Canadian CPI, an estimate of future prices or probabilities assigned to a retirement scenario. Their purpose is to hold the total compounded increase constant while changing when it occurs. The two blocks remain labelled A and B when inputs change. If block A is entered below block B, the first path no longer represents higher inflation arriving early. If both rates are equal, the paths coincide. The labels describe order rather than promising which sequence is more difficult. Every spending request needs a price observation and a payment date The first annual withdrawal request is made immediately at the start of year one, before any modeled inflation or investment return. The next year’s request follows the price level after year one. Each later request uses the preceding year-end price index to maintain the same selected spending basket. The second chart shows these requested nominal amounts. A price increase early in the horizon affects several later requests. A price increase at the very end cannot change an earlier bill that has already been requested. This convention also explains the tenth inflation update. It determines the closing year-ten price level and purchasing power, but an eleventh withdrawal is outside the ten-year horizon. The year-ten request uses the first nine price increases. Matching closing indices therefore does not require the ten withdrawal amounts or their sum to match.
