Keep returns identical to isolate the inflation-spending channel The third chart gives both withdrawal paths the same initial capital and the same constant nominal investment return. The original example starts with CAD 500,000, requests CAD 25,000 immediately, and uses an assumed 5% effective nominal return every year. Each request first uses the capital available at the start of that year. The remaining capital then earns the selected return. The tool records any amount that cannot be funded; it does not borrow automatically or show a negative investment account. Under the original assumptions, the A-first path requests about CAD 315,286 across the decade and ends with about CAD 403,919. The reversed path requests about CAD 279,084 and ends with about CAD 450,086. Both original examples fund all ten requests. The difference combines extra spending with the growth forgone on earlier withdrawals; it is not an investment-performance difference. The no-spending line is a control. It removes all withdrawal requests and therefore produces one common investment path. It is not a retirement lifestyle that a household can adopt without a separate source of income. Discount every requested withdrawal from its actual timing The fourth chart calculates the opening capital required to fund the ten requests under the selected constant return, ending with no capital requirement beyond the horizon. The first request is immediate and is not discounted. The request at the start of year two is discounted one year, and so on. The equation is required opening capital = Σ requested spending in year t ÷ (1 + nominal return) t − 1 for years one through ten. These cash-flow dates must agree with the portfolio recurrence; using year-end discounting would answer a different question. In the original example, the requirements are approximately CAD 252,029 with block A first and CAD 223,686 with block B first. The difference is approximately CAD 28,342. A third bar holds the initial spending request and nominal return constant while removing all price increases, providing a separate inflation control. This is an arithmetic funding identity for ten known requests and one certain return assumption. It is not a recommended reserve, a safe withdrawal rate or a statement that retirement ends after ten years. Read unmet spending beside the remaining portfolio The final chart separates requested spending into amounts funded and left unfunded. A lower funded total can mean that the household could not meet its needs. It should not be praised as a more efficient spending strategy without reading the unfunded segment. Try reducing initial capital. The opening-capital requirement bars do not change because they depend on the requested spending path and return. The actual portfolio path and unmet requests do change. Later returns cannot retroactively finance an earlier request that lacked capital. A real retirement plan would also include pensions, tax, fees, changing spending quantities, benefit indexation, cash timing and uncertain returns. Price increases may differ by category, and households may adjust discretionary spending. This example isolates one channel to make its effect visible. Keep a record of whether values are nominal or in today’s purchasing power. Specify when each withdrawal happens. Test earlier as well as later inflation pressure. Show any spending cuts or unmet requests beside capital balances. Extend the horizon and add other resources before treating the exercise as a retirement plan. The useful question is how price changes reach the budget through time, rather than only which index value appears at the finish.
1941a44f88906be4d27e7af851fa21b78594385d.zh: 收盘价水平并不能揭示价格上涨何时到来。即使投资回报与最终价格水平相匹配，较早的上涨也可能会影响更多的提款。保持通胀因素不变，仅改变其顺序 第一张图表绘制了两条价格路径。在最初的例子中，三年的通货膨胀率为 8%，随后七年的通货膨胀率为 2%。另一个正好相反这十个年度因素。两者最终的价格水平相同：当起始指数为 100 时，价格水平约为 144.7。利率是发明的。它们不是加拿大消费物价指数的重演，也不是对未来价格或退休情景概率的估计。它们的目的是保持总复合增长恒定，同时在复合增长发生时发生变化。当输入更改时，这两个块仍标记为 A 和 B。如果区块 A 进入区块 B 下方，则第一条路径不再代表提前到来的更高通胀。如果两个速率相等，则路径重合。标签描述了顺序，而不是承诺哪个顺序更困难。每个支出请求都需要价格观察和付款日期第一个年度提款请求是在第一年开始时立即提出的，在任何建模的通货膨胀或投资回报之前。下一年的要求遵循第一年之后的价格水平。后面的每个请求都使用前一个年终价格指数来维持相同的选定支出篮子。第二个图表显示了这些请求的名义金额。早期的价格上涨会影响后来的几个请求。最后的价格上涨不能改变已经要求的较早的账单。本次会议还解释了第十次通胀更新。它决定了最后十年的价格水平和购买力，但第十一次撤资超出了十年的范围。第十年请求使用前九次价格上涨。因此，匹配收盘指数不需要十个提款金额或其总和匹配。保持回报相同以隔离通胀支出渠道 第三张图给出了两种提取路径相同的初始资本和相同的恒定名义投资回报。原始示例从 500,000 加元开始，立即请求 25,000 加元，并使用假设的每年 5% 的有效名义回报。每个请求首先使用当年年初的可用资金。剩余的资本然后赚取选定的回报。该工具记录任何无法资助的金额；它不会自动借款或显示负投资账户。根据最初的假设，A-first 路径在十年内需要大约 315,286 加元，最终需要大约 403,919 加元。反向路径请求约 279,084 加元，结束时约需 450,086 加元。两个原始示例都为所有十个请求提供资金。这种差异结合了额外支出和早期提款所放弃的增长；这不是投资绩效差异。无支出线是一个控制线。它消除了所有提款请求，因此产生了一种共同的投资路径。这不是一个没有独立收入来源的家庭可以采取的退休生活方式。将每个请求的提款与其实际时间进行折扣 第四个图表计算了在选定的恒定回报下为十个请求提供资金所需的期初资本，最终没有超出范围的资本要求。第一个请求是立即的，并且不打折扣。第二年开始时的请求可享受一年折扣，依此类推。该等式为所需的期初资本 = Σ t 年要求的支出 ÷ (1 + 名义回报) t − 1（第一年到第十年）。这些现金流日期必须与投资组合的重复周期一致；使用年终折扣可以回答不同的问题。在原始示例中，首先使用块 A 的要求约为 252,029 加元，首先使用块 B 的要求约为 223,686 加元。差额约为 28,342 加元。第三根柱子保持初始支出请求和名义回报不变，同时消除所有价格上涨，提供单独的通胀控制。这是十个已知请求和一个特定回报假设的算术资金恒等式。它不是建议的储备金、安全提款率或十年后退休结束的声明。阅读剩余投资组合旁边的未满足支出最终图表将请求的支出分为已资助的金额和未资助的金额。资金总额较低可能意味着家庭无法满足其需求。如果不了解无资金部分，就不应该将其称赞为更有效的支出策略。尝试减少初始资本。开业资本要求栏不会改变，因为它们取决于所请求的支出路径和回报。实际的投资组合路径和未满足的请求确实会发生变化。后来的回报无法追溯性地为先前缺乏资金的请求提供资金。真正的退休计划还包括养老金、税收、费用、变化的支出数量、福利指数、现金发放时间和不确定的回报。价格上涨可能因类别而异，家庭可能会调整可自由支配的支出。此示例隔离一个通道以使其效果可见。记录价值是名义价值还是当今的购买力。指定每次提款发生的时间。提前和后期测试通胀压力。除资本余额外，还应显示任何支出削减或未满足的要求。在将这项活动视为退休计划之前，请扩大视野并添加其他资源。有用的问题是价格变化如何随着时间的推移达到预算，而不仅仅是最终出现哪个指数值。

69ea9dbcc39616075287b04776074bf1e5b398f1.src: Portfolio return is a weighted arithmetic mean in this one-year model. Portfolio standard deviation also depends on how the two returns move together. Neither number establishes the right investment plan. Define the returns before drawing the portfolio Two portfolios with identical capital weights can have different risk when their investments behave differently together. This article isolates that relationship using two hypothetical assets, A and B. Neither name represents a fund, a security, a country or an asset-class forecast. The example assigns 60% to A and 40% to B at the start of one year. A has an assumed arithmetic mean return of 4% and a return standard deviation of 6%. B has corresponding assumptions of 8% and 18%. Their assumed correlation is 0.2. These are chosen inputs for an explanation, rather than estimates extracted from market data. The public CFA Institute portfolio-risk overview identifies individual risk, return and correlation as determinants of portfolio risk. The calculations below apply those general relationships to this independent example. They do not reproduce a historical portfolio or select an allocation for the reader. Read the arithmetic mean separately from a growth forecast The one-year portfolio return is 0.6 times A’s realized return plus 0.4 times B’s realized return. Taking its arithmetic mean gives 0.6 × 4% + 0.4 × 8% = 5.6% . Changing correlation leaves this mean unchanged when the weights and both asset means stay fixed. An arithmetic mean describes a distribution’s average one-period return. It is not a promised return, a compound annual growth rate or a complete retirement projection. A multiyear calculation would need further assumptions about the sequence of returns, changing weights, contributions, withdrawals and costs. This calculator supplies none of those assumptions. The capital input translates standard deviation into Canadian dollars. It does not change either asset’s return characteristics. Doubling the portfolio from CAD 100,000 to CAD 200,000 doubles the dollar translation while leaving the percentage mean and standard deviation unchanged. Use the allocation curves to see the missing relationship The first chart varies A’s weight from 0% to 100%, assigning the remainder to B. It compares the selected correlation with −0.5 and +1. At each endpoint only one asset remains, so all curves meet at that asset’s standalone standard deviation. For nonnegative weights and correlation +1, portfolio standard deviation equals the weighted sum of the two standalone standard deviations. At the default weights, that sum is 0.6 × 6% + 0.4 × 18% = 10.8% . At correlation 0.2, the calculated standard deviation is about 8.67% . The difference comes from covariance, with the standalone risks held fixed. Reducing correlation cannot increase variance in this particular two-asset, long-only comparison. It need not reduce risk below the risk of the safer individual asset at every weight. Nor does the result mean that adding any second holding improves every plan. The quantities and their relationship both matter. A point on the scatter plot is an allocation The horizontal coordinate of each point is calculated annual standard deviation. Its vertical coordinate is the assumed arithmetic mean return. Hollow points represent allocations at ten-percentage-point intervals; the larger filled point identifies the exact selected weight, including an intermediate weight if entered. The default selected point is therefore approximately (8.67%, 5.60%). It is not an observed year, a simulated future outcome or an investor’s survey response. The chart plots alternative portfolios derived from the same inputs. The table identifies every allocation and both coordinates. A point with a lower mean and at least as much standard deviation as another point has an unattractive comparison on those two selected measures. That observation does not establish a universally optimal investment. This small opportunity set omits taxes, liquidity, inflation exposure, downside asymmetry, restrictions and the household’s required payment dates. Add variance terms before taking the square root Write the weights as fractions wA and wB, standalone standard deviations as σA and σB, and correlation as ρ. Portfolio variance is wA²σA² + wB²σB² + 2wAwBρσAσB . Portfolio standard deviation is the square root of that total. The waterfall uses squared percentage points to make the arithmetic readable. Its default first term is (0.6 × 6)² = 12.96. The second is (0.4 × 18)² = 51.84. The covariance cross term is 2 × 0.6 × 0.4 × 0.2 × 6 × 18 = 10.368. Together they produce variance of 75.168 squared percentage points . Its square root is approximately 8.66995 percentage points. The chart labels round displayed values, while the calculation retains precision. These three variance components cannot be added as if they were three percentage returns. A negative covariance term reduces the variance total; it does not represent a payment, investment profit or negative standalone variance. State a convention before calling something a risk contribution The signed bars assign half of the weighted covariance cross term to A and half to B. On that stated convention, A receives 12.96 + 5.184 = 18.144 squared percentage points. B receives 51.84 + 5.184 = 57.024. Their sum reconciles to 75.168. These figures describe contributions to variance. They are neither capital weights nor additive contributions to standard deviation. Reporting 18.144 as A’s percentage allocation would confuse the measurement unit and the question being answered. A contribution can become negative. For example, keep the default weights and standalone risks but change correlation to −0.5. A’s attributed variance becomes 12.96 − 12.96 = 0; at correlation −1 it becomes −12.96. The other contribution offsets it so total variance stays nonnegative. This describes the model’s covariance relationship and does not establish a reliable real-world hedge. Test the relationship instead of treating one estimate as permanent The matrix varies both correlation and allocation. It holds the two standalone standard deviations fixed. At correlation −1, A’s 75% weight and B’s 25% weight give equal weighted standard deviations of 4.5 percentage points with perfectly opposite movements. Their modeled portfolio standard deviation is zero. That cancellation requires an exact relationship in this idealized model. It is not evidence that an available pair of investments is risk-free. Estimated correlations depend on the observations, frequency, currency and measurement period; future relationships can differ. Zero correlation also does not generally establish statistical independence. Standard deviation alone cannot specify the probability of losing money or the worst loss. Without a distributional assumption, “one standard deviation” is not a stated confidence interval. The default CAD 8,669.95 dollar translation is a dispersion measure for CAD 100,000, rather than a maximum loss, a reserve target or a guaranteed band around the mean. Bring the chart back to the goal and payment calendar Investor.gov’s asset-allocation overview connects allocation choices with investing horizon and risk tolerance. It also explains diversification across and within investment categories. Counting account names or fund wrappers does not by itself establish different underlying exposures. For a real planning exercise, record the goal’s amount and date, identify money needed before a market recovery could be tolerated, and inspect the underlying investments. Then document how actual risk estimates were obtained and test plausible changes in the relationships. This article’s adjustable inputs illustrate those questions without answering them for a particular household. The model has no leverage, short positions, taxes, fees, exchange-rate conversion, cash flows or trading constraints. Its calculations are a transparent starting point for understanding diversification. A complete plan must still fund the actual obligations and fit the investor’s capacity and willingness to bear losses.
69ea9dbcc39616075287b04776074bf1e5b398f1.zh: 在这个一年期模型中，投资组合回报是加权算术平均值。投资组合标准差还取决于两个回报如何共同变化。这两个数字都无法制定正确的投资计划。在绘制投资组合之前定义回报 当两个具有相同资本权重的投资组合的投资表现不同时，它们可能具有不同的风险。本文使用两种假设资产 A 和 B 来隔离这种关系。这两个名称都不代表基金、证券、国家或资产类别预测。该示例在一年开始时将 60% 分配给 A，将 40% 分配给 B。 A 的假设算术平均回报率为 4%，回报标准差为 6%。 B有相应的假设8%和18%。他们假设的相关性是 0.2。这些是为了解释而选择的输入，而不是从市场数据中提取的估计。 CFA 协会公开的投资组合风险概述将个人风险、回报和相关性确定为投资组合风险的决定因素。下面的计算将这些一般关系应用于这个独立的示例。他们不会复制历史投资组合或为读者选择分配。将算术平均值与增长预测分开读取 一年投资组合回报率为 A 已实现回报的 0.6 倍加上 B 已实现回报的 0.4 倍。取算术平均值得出 0.6 × 4% + 0.4 × 8% = 5.6% 。当权重和两种资产均值保持固定时，相关性的变化会使该均值保持不变。算术平均值描述了分布的平均一期回报。它不是承诺的回报、复合年增长率或完整的退休预测。多年计算需要对回报顺序、权重变化、贡献、提取和成本进行进一步假设。该计算器不提供这些假设。资本投入将标准差换算成加元。它不会改变任何资产的回报特征。将投资组合从 100,000 加元翻倍至 200,000 加元，美元换算也翻倍，同时百分比均值和标准差保持不变。使用分配曲线查看缺失的关系 第一个图表将 A 的权重从 0% 更改为 100%，将剩余部分分配给 B。它将所选相关性与 -0.5 和 +1 进行比较。在每个端点仅保留一项资产，因此所有曲线均满足该资产的独立标准差。对于非负权重和相关性 +1，投资组合标准差等于两个独立标准差的加权和。在默认权重下，该总和为 0.6 × 6% + 0.4 × 8.67%。差异来自协方差，独立风险保持固定。在这个特定的两种资产的多头比较中，降低相关性不会增加方差。它不需要将风险降低到低于每个权重的更安全的个人资产的风险。结果也不意味着添加任何第二个控股可以改善每个计划。数量及其关系都很重要。散点图上的一个点是一个分配值，每个点的横坐标就是计算的年标准差。其纵坐标是假设的算术平均回报。空心点代表以十个百分点为间隔的分配；较大的填充点标识精确选择的重量，包括中间重量（如果输入）。因此，默认选定点约为 wA 和 wB，将独立标准差写为 σA 和 σB，并将相关性写为 ρ。投资组合方差为 wA²σA² + wB²σB² + 2wAwBρσAσB 。投资组合标准差是该总数的平方根。瀑布使用平方百分比来使算术可读。其默认第一项为 (0.6 × 6)² = 12.96。第二个是 (0.4 × 18)² = 51.84。协方差交叉项为 2 × 0.6 × 0.4 × 0.2 × 6 × 18 = 10.368。它们总共产生 75.168 个平方百分点的方差。其平方根约为 8.66995 个百分点。图表标记显示的值，而计算保留精度。这三个方差分量不能像三个百分比回报一样相加。负协方差项会减少方差总计；它不代表付款、投资利润或负独立差异。在将某项称为风险贡献之前先声明一个约定。带符号的条将加权协方差交叉项的一半分配给 A，另一半分配给 B。根据该约定，A 获得 12.96 + 5.184 = 18.144 平方百分点。 B 收到 51.84 + 5.184 = 57.024。他们的总和一致为 75.168。这些数字描述了对方差的贡献。它们既不是资本权重，也不是标准差的附加贡献。将 18.144 报告为 A 的分配百分比会混淆测量单位和所回答的问题。贡献可能会变成负数。例如，保留默认权重和独立风险，但将相关性更改为 -0.5。 A 的归因方差变为 12.96 − 12.96 = 0；相关性为-1 时，它变为-12.96。其他贡献抵消了它，因此总方差保持非负值。这描述了模型的协方差关系，并没有建立可靠的现实世界对冲。测试关系，而不是将一个估计视为永久矩阵。矩阵会改变相关性和分配。它保持两个独立标准差固定。在相关性为 -1 时，A 的 75% 权重和 B 的 25% 权重给出了 4.5 个百分点的等权标准差，且走势完全相反。他们建模的投资组合标准差为零。这种取消需要在这个理想化模型中存在精确的关系。这并不能证明现有的投资组合是无风险的。估计的相关性取决于观察、频率、货币和测量周期；未来的关系可能会有所不同。零相关性通常也不能建立统计独立性。标准差本身并不能说明亏损或最严重损失的概率。如果没有分布假设，“一个标准差”就不是规定的置信区间。默认的 8,669.95 加元换算是 100,000 加元的分散衡量标准，而不是最大损失、储备目标或均值周围的保证区间。将图表带回目标和付款日历 Investor.gov 的资产配置概述将配置选择与投资期限和风险承受能力联系起来。它还解释了投资类别之间和内部的多元化。计算账户名称或基金包装本身并不会建立不同的基础风险敞口。对于真正的规划练习，记录目标的金额和日期，确定可以容忍市场复苏之前所需的资金，并检查基础投资。然后记录如何获得实际风险估计并测试关系中的合理变化。本文的可调整输入说明了这些问题，但没有回答特定家庭的问题。该模型没有杠杆、空头头寸、税收、费用、汇率转换、现金流或交易限制。它的计算是理解多元化的透明起点。一个完整的计划仍然必须为实际义务提供资金，并适合投资者承担损失的能力和意愿。

5ea0a9f9e725580f9e77009aa0336cc0cd466ca7.src: The number and the convention belong together. Convert them to a common annual growth factor and a matching payment-period rate before comparing the payment. Read the convention before dividing the rate by twelve An annual percentage printed beside the word interest does not tell you every detail needed for a payment calculation. The quotation needs a compounding convention, and the payment schedule needs a rate for its own period. FCAC’s sample fixed-mortgage information box illustrates interest compounded twice a year but charged monthly. It also presents annual percentage rate separately, including applicable fees. The example is useful for understanding the labels; its figures are not a current mortgage offer. This tool places three interpretations of one entered number side by side: a nominal quote with the selected compounding count, a nominal quote compounded monthly, and a number treated as already effective for one year. They share a principal and complete repayment horizon, with no fees. None is asserted to be the convention used by every lender or product. Build the annual growth factor, then translate to a payment month For a nominal annual rate j compounded m times a year, the annual growth factor is (1 + j ÷ m) m . Subtract one to obtain the effective annual interest rate. Rates in this equation are decimals, so 5% is entered as 0.05. The equivalent monthly rate is (1 + j ÷ m) m ÷ 12 − 1 . This preserves the same annual growth factor across twelve equal model months. A nominal rate compounded twice yearly is therefore converted with an exponent of one-sixth after dividing the quote by two. If the entered number is already an effective annual rate, the monthly conversion is (1 + j) 1/12 − 1 . Dividing by twelve instead would make a different assumption. The tool retains unrounded rates for calculations; rounding an intermediate rate can change a long amortization schedule. Compare the same rate number without assuming the same interest With the original 5% input, nominal twice-yearly compounding implies an effective annual rate of 5.0625%. Nominal monthly compounding implies approximately 5.11619%. The already-effective annual interpretation is exactly 5%. The first chart displays the conversions on the same effective annual basis. For an original CAD 300,000 principal repaid through three hundred monthly payments, the corresponding payments are approximately CAD 1,744.81, CAD 1,753.77 and CAD 1,734.41. These are original mathematical results, not three borrowing offers. The same-number comparison deliberately changes economic rates. It should not be read as a claim that compounding creates extra cost when effective annual rates are held equal. If two quotes are first converted to the same annual growth factor, they also produce the same equivalent monthly rate and payment under the remaining common assumptions. Carry the converted rate through the actual interest and principal split The second chart shows additional cumulative interest relative to treating the entered number as an already-effective annual rate. Subtracting the same baseline makes a small convention difference easier to see. A zero line means equal cost to that baseline, not that the loan charges no interest. Each case solves its own payment to repay the same principal over the same number of months, with no rate renewal. The third chart examines payment one. Interest is opening principal times the converted monthly rate. The remainder of the payment reduces principal. The final payment is capped at the amount still owed so that a small rounding residual is not treated as a new debt. The fourth chart translates selected nominal annual quotes across annual, twice-yearly, monthly and 365-period compounding. It shows effective annual percentages to two decimal places, with more precision retained inside the calculation. The 365-period row is a mathematical count, not a dated daily-accrual contract; it does not address leap years or an actual day-count rule. An effective interest conversion still does not include every borrowing cost Converting interest conventions is one part of comparing borrowing. A real offer can also have fees, required conditions, optional products, repayment restrictions, early-exit costs or a rate that changes before the debt is fully repaid. Those are outside this exercise. The complete repayment horizon in the tool is not a promise that a mortgage rate remains fixed for its whole amortization. Actual contractual terms and renewals must be checked separately. The calculated effective annual interest rate is also not an all-in APR disclosure: no fee has been included in its cash flows. Record the quoted number and whether it is nominal or effective. Record the compounding and payment frequencies separately. Translate to a common annual growth factor. Use the matching payment-period rate for the repayment calculation. Add actual fees and contractual terms before assessing a live offer. These steps explain why two calculators can disagree while displaying the same annual number. Before changing the principal or repayment budget to force agreement, check whether they used the same rate convention.
5ea0a9f9e725580f9e77009aa0336cc0cd466ca7.zh: 数字和约定是一体的。在比较付款之前，将它们转换为共同的年增长率和匹配的付款期比率。在将利率除以十二之前先阅读惯例 利息一词旁边印有的年百分比并不能告诉您付款计算所需的所有细节。报价需要复利约定，付款计划需要其自身期间的汇率。 FCAC 的固定抵押贷款信息框样本显示，利息每年复利两次，但每月收取一次。它还单独显示年度百分比率，包括适用的费用。该示例对于理解标签很有用；其数据并非当前的抵押贷款报价。该工具并排放置一个输入数字的三种解释：具有所选复利计数的名义报价、每月复利的名义报价以及被视为已有效一年的数字。他们共享本金和完整的还款期限，且不收取任何费用。没有一个被声称是每个贷款机构或产品都使用的惯例。建立年增长因子，然后转换为付款月份 对于名义年利率 j 每年复利 m 次，年增长因子为 (1 + j ÷ m) m 。减一即可得到实际年利率。此等式中的比率为小数，因此 5% 输入为 0.05。等值月利率为 (1 + j ÷ m) m ÷ 12 − 1 。这在十二个相同的模型月份中保留了相同的年增长率。因此，每年复利两次的名义利率在报价除以二后以六分之一的指数进行转换。如果输入的数字已经是有效年利率，则每月转换为 (1 + j) 1/12 − 1 。除以十二会做出不同的假设。该工具保留未四舍五入的比率进行计算；四舍五入中间利率可以改变较长的摊销时间表。在不假设相同利率的情况下比较相同的利率数字 对于最初的 5% 输入，名义每年两次复利意味着有效年利率为 5.0625%。名义月复利约为 5.11619%。已经生效的年度解释恰好是5%。第一个图表显示了相同有效年度基础上的转换。对于原30万加元的本金，每月300元还款，相应的还款金额约为1,744.81加元、1,753.77加元和1,734.41加元。这些是原始的数学结果，而不是三个借用报价。相同数字的比较故意改变经济利率。不应将其理解为当有效年利率相同时复利会产生额外成本的主张。如果两个报价首先转换为相同的年增长系数，则在其余共同假设下，它们也会产生相同的等值月费率和付款。通过实际利息和本金分割来计算转换后的利率 第二个图表显示了相对于将输入的数字视为已经有效的年利率的额外累积利息。减去相同的基线可以更容易地看到小的约定差异。零线意味着成本与该基线相同，而不是贷款不收取利息。每个案例都自行解决付款问题，在相同的月份内偿还相同的本金，无需更新利率。第三张图表检查付款一。利息是期初本金乘以转换后的月利率。剩余的付款减少了本金。最终付款的上限为仍欠金额，因此小额四舍五入余额不会被视为新债务。第四张图表将选定的名义年度报价转换为年度、每年两次、每月和 365 个周期的复利。它显示了有效的年度百分比，精确到小数点后两位，并在计算中保留了更高的精度。 365 个周期的行是一个数学计数，而不是一个注明日期的每日应计合约；它不涉及闰年或实际的天数规则。有效利率转换仍然不包括所有借款成本 转换利息惯例是比较借款的一部分。真实报价还可以包含费用、所需条件、可选产品、还款限制、提前退出成本或在债务完全偿还之前发生变化的利率。这些不属于本练习的范围。该工具中的完整还款期限并不承诺抵押贷款利率在整个摊销中保持固定。实际的合同条款和续签必须单独检查。计算出的有效年利率也不是全部年利率披露：其现金流量中未包含任何费用。记录引用的数字以及它是名义上的还是有效的。分别记录复利和付款频率。转换为共同的年增长率。使用匹配的还款期利率进行还款计算。在评估实时报价之前添加实际费用和合同条款。这些步骤解释了为什么两个计算器在显示相同的年度数字时可能会出现不一致。在更改本金或还款预算以强制达成协议之前，请检查他们是否使用相同的利率约定。

14d5a9937e37ab713c8d18bbd5cf515d2cdff55c.src: The date a temporary benefit ends and the date another income source begins are separate inputs. Put both on the calendar before relying on the first pension payment. Identify which part of the pension is temporary A quoted pension payment can contain components with different durations. A household that spends the first total indefinitely may miss a scheduled reduction even when the plan pays exactly what it promised. The federal public service pension explanation distinguishes a lifetime pension from a temporary bridge benefit. Under the described plan, the bridge normally ends after the member reaches 65, with an earlier end possible on entitlement to CPP/QPP disability benefits. The page also explains why starting a reduced CPP/QPP pension early can leave a lower combined income after the bridge ends. Those are features of the named plan, rather than rules for every employer pension. The amounts and annual bands in this tool are independent hypothetical inputs. Obtain the actual statement, net-payment estimate and end date from the relevant administrator before applying them to a household. Map three income components in the same price basis The worked example begins with the whole-year period at age 60. Ongoing pension income is CAD 32,000 a year after tax, and a temporary bridge supplies another CAD 8,000. Spending begins at CAD 45,000, leaving a CAD 5,000 annual gap before savings. The first whole-year band without the bridge is age 65. A separate CAD 14,000 annual income source starts at age 67. Each amount is entered in year-1 dollars, then increased by the same 2% assumption. At the original price level, income therefore moves from CAD 40,000 to CAD 32,000 and later to CAD 46,000. The composition chart selects the first and last bands plus the bands around the two changes. The income-and-spending chart retains every annual observation. Neither treats the later source as an automatic continuation of the bridge. Changing the later start age changes the calendar only. It does not increase that source’s annual amount as a real CPP deferral calculation might. A different start-age quotation must be assessed separately. Budget the years after the bridge stops The initial CAD 5,000 gap is manageable only if resources are assigned to it. When the bridge ends before later income starts, the first-year-price gap becomes CAD 13,000 a year. The chart then applies the common annual increase to the actual nominal amounts in each band. The selected opening cash reserve is CAD 30,000. Across the whole fifteen-year schedule, the minimum required opening cash is about CAD 55,013.36. The additional requirement above the selected reserve is therefore about CAD 25,013.36. This calculation looks for the deepest cumulative annual deficit. It does not simply sum every shortfall while ignoring a surplus elsewhere. The model saves any annual surplus in the same zero-interest cash ledger, and allows it to fund subsequent obligations. A later surplus still cannot pay an earlier bill on its original due date. That is why the largest earlier deficit determines the required opening amount even when the ending position improves. Read negative cash as an unfunded position The cash chart begins immediately before the first modeled age band. Each following point adds that year’s income and subtracts spending. At the defaults, the position ends the fifteenth year at about negative CAD 15,154.23. That is a funding need, not an approved overdraft or an actual negative savings account. The tool calculates no borrowing interest, asset sale or government support to fill it. A real plan would need to change resources, spending or timing before the payment became due. The extra-starting-cash result is conditional on the modeled ordering: annual receipts are available before the annual spending settlement. Monthly rent, bill dates and a birthday-month pension change can require a different buffer. The federal plan’s actual monthly bridge-end rule is not reproduced by these whole-year bands. A larger reserve can fund the illustrated calendar, but this horizon omits later care needs, survivor changes and spending after the final year. It is an annual transition exercise, not a lifetime adequacy assessment. Separate a timing sensitivity from an available pension choice The matrix varies the first year without the bridge and the later-income start age. Each cell reports additional opening cash after the selected reserve, holding all entered amounts fixed. A lower cell does not mean an administrator offers that end age or that a government pension can be moved without changing its amount. Some cells may move a transition outside the selected horizon, in which case that transition has not been tested. Read the horizon with the result. OSFI’s Pension Members’ Guide emphasizes checking the details of the particular plan with its administrator. For a practical review, request a breakdown of ongoing and temporary components, identify each end date, obtain independent estimates of other income, and compare the resulting net receipts with essential and flexible spending. Use exact monthly dates for an implemented budget. Keep any decision about CPP/QPP start age, pension options, tax, disability benefits or survivor protection separate from this deliberately simplified cash comparison.
14d5a9937e37ab713c8d18bbd5cf515d2cdff55c.zh: 临时福利结束的日期和另一个收入来源开始的日期是单独的输入。在依赖第一笔养老金支付之前，将两者都放在日历上。确定养老金的哪一部分是临时的 报价的养老金付款可以包含不同期限的组成部分。无限期支出第一笔支出的家庭可能会错过计划的削减，即使该计划完全支付了其承诺的金额。联邦公共服务养老金的解释将终身养老金与临时过渡福利区分开来。根据所述计划，过渡期通常在会员年满 65 岁后结束，如果有权享受 CPP/QPP 残疾福利，则可以提前结束。该页面还解释了为什么尽早开始减少 CPP/QPP 养老金可能会在过渡期结束后留下较低的综合收入。这些是指定计划的特点，而不是每个雇主养老金的规则。该工具中的金额和年度范围是独立的假设输入。在将实际报表、净付款估算和结束日期应用于家庭之前，请先从相关管理人员处获取。以相同的价格基础绘制三个收入组成部分 工作示例从 60 岁的全年开始。持续的养老金收入每年税后为 32,000 加元，一座临时桥梁另外提供 8,000 加元。支出从 45,000 加元起，每年在节省之前还有 5,000 加元的缺口。第一个没有桥梁的全年范围是 65 岁。从 67 岁开始，单独的 14,000 加元年收入来源。每个金额均以第一年美元输入，然后按相同的 2% 假设增加。因此，在原来的价格水平上，收入从 40,000 加元变为 32,000 加元，然后变为 46,000 加元。成分图选择第一个和最后一个波段以及两个变化周围的波段。收入和支出图表保留了每年的观察结果。两者都没有将后来的来源视为桥梁的自动延续。更改较晚的开始年龄只会更改日历。它不会像真正的 CPP 延期计算那样增加该来源的年度金额。不同的起始年龄报价必须单独评估。桥梁停止后的几年进行预算 只有分配了资源，最初的 5,000 加元缺口才可以管理。当桥梁在以后的收入开始之前结束时，第一年的价格差距将变为每年 13,000 加元。然后，该图表将共同的年度增长应用于每个区间的实际名义金额。选定的期初现金储备为 30,000 加元。在整个十五年计划中，所需的最低开业现金约为 55,013.36 加元。因此，选定储备金之上的额外要求约为 25,013.36 加元。该计算寻找最深的累计年度赤字。它并不是简单地将所有短缺相加而忽略其他地方的盈余。该模型将任何年度盈余保存在同一零息现金分类账中，并允许其为后续债务提供资金。较晚的盈余仍无法在原定到期日支付较早的账单。这就是为什么即使期末头寸有所改善，早期最大赤字也决定了所需的开仓金额。将负现金视为无资金头寸 现金图表从第一个建模年龄范围之前开始。以下每一点都会加上当年的收入并减去支出。在默认情况下，该头寸在第 15 年结束时价格约为负 15,154.23 加元。这是资金需求，而不是批准的透支或实际的负储蓄账户。该工具不计算借款利息、资产出售或政府支持来填补这一空缺。真正的计划需要在付款到期之前改变资源、支出或时间安排。额外起始现金结果取决于建模订单：年度收据在年度支出结算之前可用。每月租金、账单日期和生日月份养老金变化可能需要不同的缓冲。这些全年范围并未重现联邦计划的实际每月桥端规则。更大的储备金可以为插图日历提供资金，但这个范围忽略了后来的护理需求、幸存者的变化和最后一年之后的支出。这是年度过渡演习，而不是终生充分性评估。将时间敏感性与可用养老金选择分开 该矩阵在没有桥梁的第一年和后来的收入开始年龄有所不同。每个单元格报告选定储备后的额外期初现金，并保持所有输入的金额固定。较低的单元格并不意味着管理人员提出终止年龄或可以在不改变金额的情况下转移政府养老金。一些小区可能会将转换移到所选范围之外，在这种情况下，该转换尚未经过测试。阅读结果的地平线。 OSFI 的《养老金会员指南》强调与其管理人员检查特定计划的详细信息。对于实际审查，要求对持续和临时组成部分进行细分，确定每个结束日期，获得其他收入的独立估计，并将最终的净收入与基本和灵活的支出进行比较。使用准确的每月日期来执行预算。将有关 CPP/QPP 起始年龄、养老金选择、税收、残疾福利或幸存者保护的任何决定与这种故意简化的现金比较分开。

3e065a3fcad05dbcbb3ce2d8b6bf313b52c2337e.src: A gross payment to the beneficiary can trigger a separate government repayment. Check both outflows and the issuer’s payment capacity before treating an account balance as available cash. Start with a confirmed payment type and holdback snapshot An RDSP supports long-term saving for a person with a disability. A spending decision needs more than an account value: the issuer must establish the payment rules, the assistance holdback amount and any annual payment capacity that applies. The CRA’s payment guide distinguishes disability assistance payments from lifetime disability assistance payments, and explains that payment limits depend on the plan’s situation. An entered capacity in this tool means a remaining amount already confirmed by the issuer. The calculator does not establish that capacity itself. This example isolates an ordinary proportional-repayment case: a beneficiary under 60 with continuing Disability Tax Credit eligibility. It excludes specified disability savings plans, specified-year exceptions, DTC-loss cases, closure and death. Those situations can require different treatment. A result here cannot substitute for the issuer’s assessment of a real request. Trace a CAD 5,000 request through both outflows The hypothetical plan starts at CAD 100,000. Its confirmed assistance holdback amount is CAD 21,000, and independently confirmed remaining annual payment capacity is CAD 10,000. The beneficiary requests a gross payment of CAD 5,000. For the ordinary case, the CRA’s RDSP guide describes a proportional repayment of CAD 3 of grants and bonds for each CAD 1 withdrawn, capped at the assistance holdback amount. The example therefore repays min(3 × 5,000, 21,000) = CAD 15,000 . Two outflows reduce the account: CAD 5,000 for the beneficiary and CAD 15,000 for the government. Remaining plan value is 100,000 − 5,000 − 15,000 = CAD 80,000 . The government repayment is additional to the gross beneficiary payment. It is not taken a second time from that CAD 5,000. The payment may contain taxable amounts. This illustration does not calculate that composition, tax payable, benefit interactions or the beneficiary’s after-tax spending money. “Gross beneficiary payment” is deliberately the label used in the charts. Read the bend where the holdback cap is reached The curve compares independent payment alternatives from the same opening snapshot. With a CAD 21,000 holdback, the three-to-one repayment reaches its cap at a CAD 7,000 gross payment. Below that point, an extra CAD 1 of payment increases total plan depletion by CAD 4 in this narrow example: CAD 1 to the beneficiary and CAD 3 repaid. Above the cap, the repayment remains CAD 21,000. A CAD 10,000 permitted payment would therefore remove CAD 31,000 in total. This is arithmetic for one event under the stated conditions. It does not describe investment performance, an annual expense ratio or a tax rate. Nor is the curve a series of withdrawals: every point starts with the same original assets and holdback. The formula matrix keeps this distinction visible. Each cell shows only the capped repayment formula. A displayed number does not confirm that its hypothetical withdrawal satisfies annual limits or leaves adequate assets. Keep the remaining restriction separate from remaining assets After the default event, repaying CAD 15,000 also reduces the entered holdback from CAD 21,000 to CAD 6,000. The second comparison chart shows that amount alongside CAD 80,000 of remaining assets. The two quantities must not be added. Holdback identifies a repayment-related amount within the plan’s circumstances; it is not another investment account. ESDC’s technical guidance explains that the applicable period and repayment obligation depend on the event, age and DTC status, and that earlier repayments must be considered. The calculator conservatively caps the beneficiary payment at both the entered annual capacity and plan value above the confirmed opening holdback. It then applies the separate repayment. If the entered holdback already exceeds plan value, the tool illustrates no payment and leaves the discrepancy for issuer review. For example, with CAD 25,000 of assets and CAD 21,000 of holdback, only CAD 4,000 lies above that opening restriction. Even an entered annual capacity of CAD 10,000 does not make the full request fundable in this illustration. Use the actual assistance history before making a date decision A recent contribution date, a recent grant date and an account-opening date are different facts. The assistance calculation needs the issuer’s grant, bond and repayment history and the applicable event rules. A blanket instruction to wait ten years from the latest personal deposit can answer the wrong question. This tool accepts a confirmed holdback snapshot. It does not age individual grants, reconstruct past repayments, predict new grants or roll a future date forward. Lowering the holdback control means testing another assumed snapshot; it does not establish that the lower number will apply on a chosen date. Confirm the payment type and gross amount with the issuer. Obtain the assistance holdback and remaining annual capacity for the actual request. Separate beneficiary cash, government repayment and remaining assets. Check the payment’s tax composition and any benefit interactions separately. Place the confirmed spendable amount in the household’s spending calendar. The purpose is to understand the two outflows before committing the money. It does not recommend a withdrawal, determine program eligibility or calculate a personalized disability-savings strategy.
3e065a3fcad05dbcbb3ce2d8b6bf313b52c2337e.zh: 向受益人支付的总金额可以触发政府单独还款。在将账户余额视为可用现金之前，请检查流出量和发行人的支付能力。从确认的付款类型和保留快照开始 RDSP 支持残疾人的长期储蓄。支出决策需要的不仅仅是账户价值：发行人必须制定支付规则、援助保留金额以及任何适用的年度支付能力。 CRA 的付款指南将残疾援助付款与终身残疾援助付款区分开来，并解释说付款限额取决于计划的情况。在此工具中输入的容量是指发行人已确认的剩余金额。计算器本身并不确定该容量。此示例隔离了一个普通的按比例还款案例：60 岁以下且具有持续残疾税收抵免资格的受益人。它不包括指定的残疾储蓄计划、指定年份的例外情况、DTC 损失案例、关闭和死亡。这些情况可能需要不同的处理。这里的结果不能代替发行人对真实请求的评估。通过两个流出跟踪 5,000 加元的请求 假设计划从 100,000 加元开始。其确认的援助保留金额为21,000加元，独立确认的剩余年度支付能力为10,000加元。受益人要求支付总额 5,000 加元。对于普通情况，CRA 的 RDSP 指南描述了每提取 1 加元，按比例偿还 3 加元的补助金和债券，上限为援助扣留金额。因此，该示例偿还 min(3 × 5,000, 21,000) = CAD 15,000 。两次资金外流减少了账户：受益人 5,000 加元，政府 15,000 加元。剩余计划价值为 100,000 − 5,000 − 15,000 = 80,000 加元。政府还款额是受益人总付款额之外的。这 5,000 加元不会被第二次提取。付款可能包含应税金额。本图并未计算该构成、应缴税款、福利互动或受益人的税后支出。 “受益人付款总额”是图表中特意使用的标签。阅读达到保留上限的曲线 该曲线比较了同一开盘快照中的独立支付方案。由于有 21,000 加元的保留，三对一还款额达到了总还款额 7,000 加元的上限。低于该点，额外支付 1 加元，计划总消耗会增加 4 加元，在此狭义示例中：向受益人支付 1 加元，偿还 3 加元。超过上限后，还款金额仍为 21,000 加元。因此，允许支付 10,000 加元，总共会减少 31,000 加元。这是在规定条件下的一个事件的算术结果。它不描述投资业绩、年费用比率或税率。该曲线也不是一系列的提款：每个点都以相同的原始资产和保留开始。公式矩阵使这种区别显而易见。每个单元格仅显示上限还款公式。显示的数字并不能确认其假设的提款满足年度限额或留下足够的资产。将剩余限制与剩余资产分开。 违约事件发生后，偿还 15,000 加元也会将输入的保留金额从 21,000 加元减少到 6,000 加元。第二个比较图显示了该金额以及 80,000 加元的剩余资产。两个数量不得相加。保留确定计划情况下与还款相关的金额；它不是另一个投资账户。 ESDC 的技术指南解释说，适用的期限和还款义务取决于事件、年龄和 DTC 状态，并且必须考虑提前还款。计算器保守地将受益人付款上限限制为输入的年容量和高于确认的期初保留的计划价值。然后它会应用单独的还款。如果输入的保留金额已经超过计划价值，该工具将显示没有付款，并将差异留给发行人审核。例如，资产为 25,000 加元，保留金额为 21,000 加元，只有 4,000 加元超出开放限制。在此图中，即使输入的年产能为 10,000 加元，也无法满足全部请求的资助要求。在做出日期决定之前，请使用实际的援助历史记录 最近的捐款日期、最近的授予日期和开户日期是不同的事实。援助计算需要发行人的赠款、债券和还款历史记录以及适用的事件规则。从最近一次个人存款起等待十年的一揽子指示可能会回答错误的问题。该工具接受已确认的保留快照。它不会对个人补助金进行老化、重建过去的还款、预测新的补助金或向前滚动未来的日期。降低保留控制意味着测试另一个假设的快照；它并没有规定较低的数字将适用于选定的日期。与发卡机构确认付款类型和总金额。获取实际请求的援助保留和剩余年容量。单独的受益人现金、政府还款和剩余资产。单独检查付款的税收构成和任何福利相互作用。将确认的可支出金额放入家庭的支出日历中。目的是在投入资金之前了解两次流出情况。它不建议提款、确定计划资格或计算个性​​化的残疾储蓄策略。

e69aa85fcdb43a1022a1da5802ca5758eea55625.src: A property’s sale value does not measure the rebuilding bill. Review the rebuilding estimate, policy terms and available cash together. Give each property figure the right job A home’s market value, estimated rebuilding cost and policy coverage limit can be three different amounts. The first describes a possible sale; the second estimates a construction task; the third is part of an insurance contract. Intact’s Canadian replacement-cost explanation , published on 2 July 2026, distinguishes rebuilding from market value and describes the role of construction characteristics and current costs. It also notes that some policies have replacement provisions subject to their own conditions. The Insurance Bureau of Canada likewise advises insuring the cost to rebuild with like-quality materials and omitting the market price of the underlying land. Its wildfire guidance states that a home policy does not insure the land, and that an owner who takes a cash settlement still owns the land. These are separate valuation concepts, so the difference between a market price and a rebuilding estimate is not itself a measurement of land value. This calculator uses the market figure only as context and does not subtract it from, or add it to, the rebuilding comparison. The hypothetical comparison starts with CAD 1.2 million of market value, CAD 650,000 of covered rebuilding cost and a CAD 600,000 dwelling limit. Market value supplies context but does not enter the calculator’s claim arithmetic. Changing only that number leaves the modeled payout and cash need unchanged. This is not an appraisal or a quote for a particular insurer. The selected figures are teaching assumptions, and a broker or insurer must confirm what the actual contract covers. Write the payout assumption before using the number The model assumes a total covered dwelling loss. Its teaching contract first caps the covered rebuilding cost at the dwelling limit, then subtracts a fixed deductible, with the payout floored at zero: Assumed payout = max[0, min(covered rebuilding cost, dwelling limit) − deductible] . With the starting figures and a CAD 2,500 deductible, the modeled payout is CAD 597,500. The owner’s share is CAD 52,500. Against CAD 50,000 of assigned cash, that leaves CAD 2,500 to fund. The order in the formula matters. An actual contract may apply limits, deductibles, replacement provisions or other adjustments differently. This illustration applies no coinsurance percentage and does not generalize a foreign jurisdiction’s underinsurance rule. It provides a transparent assumed cash calculation rather than determining an actual claim. An endorsement described as guaranteed replacement cost may pay above the stated dwelling amount, but only when its own conditions are satisfied; the Insurance Bureau of Canada’s wildfire guidance describes a common same-site rebuilding requirement. A fixed annual growth input in this model is not an inflation-protection clause or evidence that such an endorsement applies. A positive comparison gap can coexist with a qualifying endorsement, and a zero gap can coexist with exclusions, deductibles or unmet conditions, so neither sign determines the actual settlement. Watch rebuilding costs and the stated limit separately The default cost increase is 5% annually, while the coverage limit grows by 2%. After five years, the rebuilding estimate is about CAD 829,583.02 and the assumed limit is about CAD 662,448.48. Applying the same fixed deductible gives a modeled insurer payment of about CAD 659,948.48. The owner’s share reaches about CAD 169,634.53, of which about CAD 119,634.53 exceeds the selected cash reserve. These are compounded sensitivities. They are not a construction-price forecast, a probability of a loss or a statement that an insurer will increase a particular limit by 2%. The lines make visible what happens when two independently entered quantities grow at different rates. A policy review can change the relevant inputs. Updated measurements, renovations, materials, local labour conditions and the contract’s actual replacement provisions need to be reflected in a fresh assessment rather than assumed away by a smooth curve. Reconcile the owner’s share without counting the deductible twice The funding waterfall begins with the covered rebuilding bill. It subtracts the assumed insurer payment and then the cash assigned to the owner’s share. A positive endpoint identifies additional funding; a negative endpoint identifies assigned cash left over. The deductible is already incorporated in the payout formula. Adding it again to the waterfall would overstate the funding need. Similarly, an insurance payment cannot be counted both as a reduction in the rebuilding bill and as a separate cash receipt a second time. The illustration assumes the modeled payout and cash are available when the bill is due. Actual claim advances, contractor deposits and reimbursement dates can produce an additional timing need. The separate reimbursement guide explains that kind of calendar without assuming an eventual payment can finance an earlier bill. No home sale, borrowing or investment liquidation is created automatically. The reported additional amount is a problem to plan for, rather than evidence that a loan is available. Read the parts of protection this dwelling example leaves out FCAC’s home-insurance guide describes protection that may include belongings, liability and additional living expenses when a home cannot be occupied. Those categories have their own terms and are not added to this dwelling-only estimate. The model also excludes land, contents, exclusions, bylaw and demolition provisions, extended or guaranteed replacement coverage, premium changes and claim-handling delays. A positive cash result for one assumed rebuilding bill says nothing about these other needs. The matrix changes the construction-cost increase and the hypothetical loss date while keeping the limit-growth assumption, deductible and cash fixed. A cell is a conditional funding calculation. None is a risk rating or an estimate of which year a loss will occur. Confirm the current rebuilding estimate and the property details behind it. Read the applicable dwelling limit, deductible and replacement conditions. List related living and other costs separately. Check when funds would be available against likely payment stages. Review the policy after material changes to the home or its use. The calculation helps organize that review. Actual coverage and claim outcomes depend on the insurer’s assessment and policy wording.
e69aa85fcdb43a1022a1da5802ca5758eea55625.zh: 房产的销售价值并不能衡量重建费用。一起审查重建估算、政策条款和可用现金。为每个房产提供合适的工作 房屋的市场价值、估计重建成本和保单承保限额可以是三个不同的金额。第一个描述了可能的出售；第二个估算施工任务；第三是保险合同的一部分。 Intact 于 2026 年 7 月 2 日发布的加拿大重置成本解释将重建与市场价值区分开来，并描述了建筑特征和当前成本的作用。它还指出，一些保单根据自身情况设有替换条款。加拿大保险局同样建议使用同等质量的材料确保重建成本，并忽略底层土地的市场价格。其野火指南指出，房屋保单并不为土地提供保险，接受现金结算的业主仍然拥有土地。这些是单独的估值概念，因此市场价格和重建估算之间的差异本身并不是土地价值的衡量标准。该计算器仅使用市场数据作为背景，不会将其从重建比较中减去或添加到重建比较中。假设的比较从 120 万加元的市场价值、65 万加元的承保重建成本和 60 万加元的住房限额开始。市场价值提供背景信息，但不进入计算器的索赔算术。仅更改该数字会使模型支付和现金需求保持不变。这不是对特定保险公司的评估或报价。所选数据是教学假设，经纪人或保险公司必须确认实际合同涵盖的内容。在使用数字之前写下支出假设 该模型假设承保住房损失总额。其教学合同首先将承保的重建成本限制在住房限额，然后减去固定的免赔额，支付底价为零：假设支付 = max[0, min(承保的重建成本, 住房限额) − 免赔额] 。考虑到起始数字和 2,500 加元的免赔额，模型支出为 597,500 加元。业主的份额为 52,500 加元。相对于 50,000 加元的指定现金，还剩下 2,500 加元可供资助。公式中的顺序很重要。实际合同可能会以不同的方式应用限制、免赔额、更换条款或其他调整。该说明不适用共同保险百分比，也没有概括外国管辖区的保险不足规则。它提供透明的假设现金计算，而不是确定实际索赔。被描述为保证重置成本的背书可以支付高于规定的住房金额的费用，但前提是满足其自身条件；加拿大保险局的野火指南描述了常见的同一地点重建要求。该模型中的固定年增长投入并不是通货膨胀保护条款，也不是此类认可适用的证据。正比较差距可以与合格认可共存，零差距可以与排除、免赔额或未满足条件共存，因此这两个标志都不能确定实际的结算。分别关注重建成本和规定的限额 默认成本每年增加 5%，而承保限额每年增加 2%。五年后，重建费用约为 829,583.02 加元，假设限制约为 662,448.48 加元。应用相同的固定免赔额，模型保险公司支付的金额约为 659,948.48 加元。所有者份额达到约169,634.53加元，其中约119,634.53加元超出选定的现金储备。这些都是复合敏感性。它们不是建筑价格预测、损失概率或保险公司将特定限额提高 2% 的声明。这些线条显示了当两个独立输入的数量以不同的速率增长时会发生什么。政策审查可以改变相关输入。更新的测量、翻新、材料、当地劳动条件和合同的实际更换条款需要反映在新的评估中，而不是通过平滑曲线来假设。核对业主的份额，无需两次计算免赔额 资金瀑布从承保的重建账单开始。它减去假定的保险公司付款，然后减去分配给所有者份额的现金。积极的终点确定了额外的资金；负端点标识分配的剩余现金。免赔额已纳入支付公式中。再次将其添加到瀑布中会夸大资金需求。同样，保险付款不能既算作重建费用的减少，又不能算作第二次单独的现金收入。该图假设账单到期时模型支付和现金可用。实际索赔预付款、承包商押金和报销日期可能会产生额外的时间需求。单独的报销指南解释了这种日历，但没有假设最终付款可以支付较早的账单。不会自动创建房屋销售、借款或投资清算。报告的额外金额是一个需要计划的问题，而不是贷款可用的证据。阅读此住宅示例中遗漏的保护部分 FCAC 的家庭保险指南描述了可能包括财产、责任和房屋无法入住时的额外生活费用的保护。这些类别有自己的术语，不会添加到仅住宅的估算中。该模型还排除了土地、内容、排除、附例和拆除条款、延长或保证的更换保险、保费变化和索赔处理延迟。一项假定的重建法案的积极现金结果并没有说明这些其他需求。该矩阵改变了建筑成本增加和假设损失日期，同时保持限制增长假设、免赔额和现金固定。单元格是有条件的资金计算。没有一个是风险评级或对哪一年会发生损失的估计。确认当前的重建估算及其背后的财产详细信息。阅读适用的住房限制、免赔额和更换条件。单独列出相关的生活费用和其他费用。根据可能的付款阶段检查资金何时可用。在房屋或其用途发生重大变化后审查该政策。计算有助于组织审查。实际承保范围和索赔结果取决于保险公司的评估和保单措辞。

e1caa48f637ce00859fd78bf21e191f942e22de8.src: A withdrawal can move an allocation toward a target, but the target applies to the smaller portfolio left behind. Taking cash out does not always complete the rebalance. Ask where the same withdrawal will come from Two portfolios can begin with the same holdings, provide the same spending cash and finish with different asset weights. The difference can come entirely from the choice of assets sold, even before any market movement. Investor.gov defines rebalancing as bringing a portfolio back toward its original allocation. This article considers a related cash-flow question: when money already needs to leave, how much of that allocation adjustment can the required sale accomplish? The example has only equity and bond buckets. It does not select securities or judge the entered target’s suitability. The SEC’s allocation guide places asset mix in the context of investment horizon and risk tolerance. A mechanically achievable percentage is not automatically the right percentage for a household. Reconcile the starting holdings and the cash leaving The default portfolio is CAD 300,000 with 70% in equity and 30% in bonds. That means CAD 210,000 of equity and CAD 90,000 of bonds. The requested withdrawal is CAD 30,000 before tax and transaction costs. Both illustrated rules supply exactly that CAD 30,000. Both leave a CAD 270,000 investment portfolio. The first stacked comparison therefore has the same ending total under either rule, making it possible to inspect composition without confusing it with a difference in wealth. The cash withdrawn is outside the remaining portfolio. It is not shown as another investment asset, and no return is applied to it. The tool also does not claim that a gross withdrawal is the same as a household’s after-tax spending amount. A proportional sale preserves the existing weight The proportional rule uses the starting 70/30 mix to fund the withdrawal. It sells CAD 21,000 of equity and CAD 9,000 of bonds, leaving CAD 189,000 and CAD 81,000 respectively. CAD 189,000 divided by CAD 270,000 is still 70%. Selling both buckets in proportion does not by itself correct the original allocation drift. It simply scales the portfolio down under the model’s no-price-change assumptions. This is a useful control case. If a proposed withdrawal strategy claims to change risk exposure, check the weights of what remains rather than the percentage of the withdrawal that came from each asset. Those are different denominators. Apply the target to the portfolio remaining after the withdrawal The entered target is 60% equity. After CAD 30,000 leaves, that target would mean CAD 162,000 of equity in the CAD 270,000 remaining portfolio. Starting from CAD 210,000, reaching it would require CAD 48,000 of equity sales. The spending withdrawal is only CAD 30,000. The directed rule is not allowed to sell CAD 48,000 and silently reinvest CAD 18,000 in bonds. It can sell only enough assets to provide the requested spending cash. It therefore takes all CAD 30,000 from equity in the default example. The remaining holdings are CAD 180,000 of equity and CAD 90,000 of bonds. Equity falls to about 66.67%: closer to 60%, but not at the target. Make the extra exchange visible rather than hiding it inside the withdrawal The default directed portfolio still has CAD 18,000 more equity than the 60% target permits. Reaching the target would require a separate exchange: sell another CAD 18,000 of equity and buy CAD 18,000 of bonds. That exchange is not executed in the model. The matrix reports this residual in dollars. Positive means equity still above target; negative means equity below target. A negative cell would require an equity purchase, funded by an equal bond reduction, if the target were to be reached with a separate trade. Rows replace the target equity percentage. Columns replace the withdrawal with a percentage of starting assets. The original equity weight remains selected. This lets the reader see when a cash withdrawal can finish the adjustment and when it cannot. Respect the assets available and the amount actually needed The directed rule cannot sell a negative amount or more than the holding available. Within those limits, it chooses the source split closest to the entered equity target after funding the withdrawal. It does not use leverage or buy an asset during the spending transaction. With a CAD 75,000 withdrawal under the default starting mix, taking all of it from equity leaves CAD 135,000 of equity and CAD 90,000 of bonds, exactly a 60/40 mix. A larger withdrawal can require sales from both buckets. If the entire portfolio is spent, there is no remaining allocation to measure. Requests above available assets are capped, with the unfunded amount displayed separately. Tax, dealing charges, spreads, settlement dates, registered-account rules and future market changes need another layer of planning. The charts compare sale sources for a single hypothetical transaction; they do not establish a withdrawal order that is best for every account.
e1caa48f637ce00859fd78bf21e191f942e22de8.zh: 撤回可以将配置转向目标，但该目标适用于留下的较小投资组合。取出现金并不总能完成再平衡。询问相同的提款将来自哪里 两个投资组合可以以相同的持股开始，提供相同的支出现金，并以不同的资产权重结束。差异可能完全来自于出售资产的选择，甚至在任何市场变动之前也是如此。 Investor.gov 将再平衡定义为将投资组合恢复到原来的配置。本文考虑一个相关的现金流问题：当资金已经需要离开时，所需的销售可以完成多少分配调整？该示例仅包含股票和债券桶。它不选择证券或判断输入目标的适用性。美国证券交易委员会的配置指南将资产组合置于投资期限和风险承受能力的背景下。机械上可实现的百分比并不一定是适合家庭的百分比。调节初始持有量和剩余现金 默认投资组合为 300,000 加元，其中 70% 为股票，30% 为债券。这意味着 210,000 加元的股权和 90,000 加元的债券。请求的提款金额为 30,000 加元（不含税和交易费用）。两条图示规则均提供 30,000 加元。两人都留下了 27 万加元的投资组合。因此，第一个堆叠比较在任一规则下都具有相同的最终总数，从而可以检查构成而不会将其与财富差异混淆。提取的现金不属于剩余投资组合。它不显示为其他投资资产，并且不应用任何回报。该工具也没有声称总提款额与家庭的税后支出金额相同。按比例出售保留现有权重 比例规则使用起始的 70/30 混合来为提款提供资金。它出售了 21,000 加元的股票和 9,000 加元的债券，分别剩下 189,000 加元和 81,000 加元。 189,000 加元除以 270,000 加元仍然是 70%。按比例出售两个桶本身并不能纠正原始分配偏差。它只是在模型的无价格变化假设下缩小投资组合的规模。这是一个有用的控制案例。如果提议的提款策略声称要改变风险敞口，请检查剩余资产的权重，而不是来自每项资产的提款百分比。这些是不同的分母。将目标应用于提款后剩余的投资组合 输入的目标是 60% 的股权。在 30,000 加元离开后，该目标将意味着 270,000 加元的剩余投资组合中的权益为 162,000 加元。起始价为 210,000 加元，要达到这一目标，需要出售 48,000 加元的股权。支出提款仅为30,000加元。指令性规则不允许出售 48,000 加元并默默地将 18,000 加元再投资于债券。它只能出售足够的资产来提供所需的支出现金。因此，在默认示例中，它从权益中取出全部 30,000 加元。剩余资产为 180,000 加元的股权和 90,000 加元的债券。股权下降至约 66.67%：接近 60%，但未达到目标。让额外的交易可见，而不是将其隐藏在提款中 默认定向投资组合的权益仍比 60% 目标允许的多 18,000 加元。达到目标需要进行单独的交换：再出售 18,000 加元的股权并购买 18,000 加元的债券。该交换不在模型中执行。矩阵以美元报告该残差。积极意味着股本仍高于目标；负数意味着净值低于目标。如果要通过单独的交易达到目标，则负值单元将需要购买股权，并通过同等的债券削减来提供资金。行取代目标股权百分比。列用起始资产的百分比代替提款。仍选择原来的股权权重。这可以让读者看到现金提取何时可以完成调整，何时不能完成调整。尊重可用资产和实际需要的数量 定向规则不能出售负数量或超过可用持有量的资产。在这些限制内，它会选择在资助提款后最接近输入的股权目标的来源分割。它在支出交易期间不使用杠杆或购买资产。在默认起始组合下提取 75,000 加元，将其全部从股权中取出，剩下 135,000 加元的股权和 90,000 加元的债券，恰好是 60/40 的组合。更大的提款可能需要两个桶的销售。如果整个投资组合都用完，则没有剩余分配可供衡量。超过可用资产的请求受到限制，未提供资金的金额单独显示。税收、交易费用、点差、结算日期、注册账户规则和未来市场变化需要另一层规划。这些图表比较了单个假设交易的销售来源；他们没有建立最适合每个账户的提款指令。

235538eaddb838759f5b202279e27e78e7024a9a.src: A later income increase cannot fund an earlier shortfall. Put the temporary benefit’s last payment and the replacement income’s first payment on the same calendar. Separate the lifetime pension from the temporary payment The annual pension-bridge guide explores whole-year bands and a common increase in income and spending. This page adds a monthly cash ledger tied to a stated December-birthday convention, with independently entered CPP cash and spending growth separated from flat income. A pension statement can contain more than one income component. A total received this month should not automatically become the amount entered for every future year. The first graphic separates ongoing income, a temporary bridge and independently entered CPP cash. For the federal public service plan, Treasury Board’s age-65 guide distinguishes a lifetime pension from a bridge ending on the first of the month after the sixty-fifth birthday. Entitlement to CPP or QPP disability benefits can end the bridge earlier. This illustration excludes that disability case and does not establish eligibility. The example uses independently entered net cash amounts rather than a service-and-salary pension formula. No tax withholding rule is applied. A real statement’s gross components must be reconciled with actual spendable receipts before using them in a household cash plan. Make the birthday and payment convention explicit The model begins in January after an assumed December sixtieth birthday. Its first five calendar years cover January ages sixty through sixty-four. The bridge pays through the December turning sixty-five, then stops the following January. This selected convention places the first month without bridge cash at month 61, five years after the start. The tool is not asking for a birth date and cannot produce a personal final-payment date. Use the administrator’s actual statement to map a real birthday and processing calendar. CPP starts in January at the selected whole age. Choosing sixty-seven therefore starts its first modeled payment in month 85. Income arrives before that month’s spending. Application delays, arrears, retroactive payments and spending before the monthly deposit are outside this simplified schedule. Do not assume the bridge amount equals the later CPP amount The federal guide explains that taking CPP retirement benefits earlier or later does not move the ordinary age-65 end of its bridge. The two plans’ amounts should not be treated as interchangeable. A household may lose one amount and later receive a different one. The current CPP start-age guide also makes clear that timing affects actual monthly benefits. Here the CPP amount is independently entered for the chosen start. The tool does not apply start-age percentages or convert a quotation at one age into a quotation at another. The matrix intentionally holds the entered CPP cash unchanged while varying its start date. It isolates a timing question. It is not a complete comparison of claiming ages, a lifetime-income ranking or a recommendation to claim at the earliest displayed date. Follow the default budget before and after the bridge stops The default ongoing lifetime pension is CAD 2,200 per month, with CAD 500 of other net income. Before the bridge ends, another CAD 700 brings monthly resources to CAD 3,400. Spending is CAD 3,500, leaving a CAD 100 monthly gap. After sixty months, CAD 6,000 has been drawn from the initial CAD 20,000 reserve, leaving CAD 14,000. In the next twenty-four months, the bridge has ended and CPP has not begun. Income is only CAD 2,700, so the gap grows to CAD 800 per month. Immediately before CPP starts, the cumulative funding need reaches CAD 25,200. The entered reserve is CAD 5,200 short. Negative cash on the chart represents that unmet need; the tool does not open an overdraft, sell an investment or supply the missing money. A recovered ending balance does not repair a missed payment At the selected CPP start, CAD 1,000 of new monthly cash raises resources to CAD 3,700. With unchanged spending, the monthly difference becomes positive CAD 200. The reserve path then rises. At the end of the fifteen-year schedule, modeled cash is again positive CAD 14,000. That endpoint does not remove the earlier CAD 5,200 shortage. The required starting reserve comes from the deepest cumulative deficit across the whole ledger, not from the final balance. For this particular calendar, CAD 25,200 of starting cash would keep all modeled month-end balances nonnegative. It is a scenario result, not a universal emergency-fund recommendation. Payments within a month could still require a separate daily calendar. Test spending growth separately from pension indexing All income inputs remain fixed nominal cash amounts. The spending-growth control raises costs each January. It does not apply statutory indexation to the pension or CPP. This deliberately separates a spending stress from a benefit calculation. Try increasing spending growth or moving the assumed CPP receipt to age seventy. Read the reserve trough and the full starting reserve requirement as well as the endpoint. The matrix replaces temporary bridge cash and start age while retaining the other inputs. For an actual retirement plan, add the verified payment dates, indexing provisions, tax effects and other benefits or assets that apply. This tool includes no OAS, GIS, investment growth, mortality or account withdrawal rules. Its purpose is narrower: make the temporary-income expiry visible before committing the same cash to future spending.
235538eaddb838759f5b202279e27e78e7024a9a.zh: 后来的收入增加无法弥补早期的收入短缺。将临时福利的最后付款和替代收入的第一笔付款放在同一日历上。将终身养老金与临时付款分开年度养老金桥梁指南探讨了全年范围以及收入和支出的共同增长。此页面添加了与规定的 12 月生日惯例相关的每月现金分类账，其中独立输入的 CPP 现金和支出增长与固定收入分开。养老金报表可以包含多个收入部分。本月收到的总额不应自动成为未来每年输入的金额。第一张图将持续收入、临时桥梁和独立输入的 CPP 现金分开。对于联邦公共服务计划，财政部的 65 岁指南将终身养老金与在 65 岁生日后下个月的第一天结束的过渡养老金区分开来。获得 CPP 或 QPP 残疾福利的权利可以提前结束过渡。此说明排除了该残疾情况，并且不确定资格。该示例使用独立输入的净现金金额，而不是服务和工资养老金公式。不适用任何预扣税规则。在将真实报表的总金额用于家庭现金计划之前，必须将其与实际可支出收入进行核对。明确生日和付款约定 该模型从假定的 12 月六十岁生日后的 1 月开始。它的前五个日历年涵盖六十岁至六十四岁的一月。这座桥在十二月六十五岁之前一直支付费用，然后在第二年一月停止运行。该选定的惯例将没有过渡现金的第一个月定为第 61 个月，即开始五年后。该工具不询问出生日期，也无法生成个人最终付款日期。使用管理员的实际报表来映射真实的生日和处理日历。 CPP 于一月份在选定的整个年龄开始。因此，选择 67 号将在第 85 个月开始其第一次模拟付款。收入先于该月的支出到达。申请延迟、拖欠、追溯付款和每月存款之前的支出不在此简化时间表之内。不要假设过渡金额等于后来的 CPP 金额 联邦指南解释说，提前或推迟领取 CPP 退休福利并不会改变普通 65 岁过渡过渡金额。这两个计划的金额不应被视为可以互换。一个家庭可能会损失一笔金额，然后又收到另一笔金额。目前的 CPP 起始年龄指南还明确指出，时间会影响实际的每月福利。此处为所选开始单独输入 CPP 金额。该工具不会应用起始年龄百分比或将一个年龄的报价转换为另一个年龄的报价。该矩阵有意保持输入的 CPP 现金不变，同时改变其开始日期。它隔离了一个时间问题。它并不是对申报年龄、终生收入排名或最早显示日期申报的建议的完整比较。桥梁停止前后遵循默认预算 默认持续终身养老金为每月 2,200 加元，其他净收入为 500 加元。在桥梁结束之前，另外 700 加元每月的资源将达到 3,400 加元。支出为 3,500 加元，每月还有 100 加元的缺口。六十个月后，从最初的 20,000 加元储备中提取了 6,000 加元，剩下 14,000 加元。在接下来的二十四个月里，大桥已经结束，CPP 还没有开始。收入只有2700加元，所以差距扩大到每月800加元。在 CPP 启动前，累计资金需求达到 25,200 加元。输入的储备金不足 5,200 加元。图表上的负现金代表未满足的需求；该工具不会进行透支、出售投资或补足缺失的资金。收回的期末余额并不能修复错过的付款 在选定的 CPP 开始时，每月 1,000 加元的新现金将资源增加到 3,700 加元。在支出不变的情况下，每月差额变为正 200 加元。然后准备金路径上升。十五年计划结束时，模拟现金再次为正 14,000 加元。该端点并不能消除之前 5,200 加元的短缺。所需的起始准备金来自整个账本中最深的累积赤字，而不是来自最终余额。对于这个特定的日历，25,200 加元的起始现金将使所有建模的月末余额保持非负数。这是一个情景结果，而不是普遍的紧急基金建议。一个月内的付款可能仍然需要单独的日历。与养老金指数分开测试支出增长 所有收入投入均保持固定的名义现金金额。支出增长控制每年一月都会增加成本。它不适用于养老金或 CPP 的法定指数化。这故意将支出压力与收益计算分开。尝试增加支出增长或将假定的 CPP 收入推迟到 70 岁。阅读储备槽和完整的起始储备要求以及终点。该矩阵取代了临时过渡现金和开始年龄，同时保留其他输入。对于实际的退休计划，请添加经过验证的付款日期、指数规定、税收影响以及其他适用的福利或资产。该工具不包括 OAS、GIS、投资增长、死亡率或账户提款规则。其目的范围更窄：在将相同的现金用于未来支出之前，让临时收入到期变得可见。

15b40b0294a10d33e471afbe3d737f32ca46a685.src: Compare what the contract covers and who receives an accepted claim, alongside its premium. A declining debt benefit and a level personal benefit are not the same promise. Begin with the type of insurance, not just the word “mortgage” FCAC’s mortgage-life rights guide distinguishes optional mortgage life insurance from mortgage default insurance. They address different events and should not be treated as interchangeable products. This article compares two hypothetical death-benefit contracts: a mortgage-life limit tied to the remaining debt and an individual policy with an entered level benefit. It does not model default, disability, critical illness or unemployment coverage. All insurance amounts and premiums are assumptions. The tool cannot determine whether a person qualifies, whether a claim will be accepted or which contract is suitable. The graphics assume both contracts remain in force and any illustrated death claim is fully eligible and accepted. A debt-linked benefit can shrink as the mortgage is repaid FCAC’s comparison of optional mortgage products describes mortgage-life benefits paid to the lender and decreasing with the mortgage balance. Its comparison with individual life insurance also identifies the different beneficiary and coverage structure. The first chart uses those two structures as selected contract assumptions. The mortgage-life limit follows the scheduled debt after each payment. The individual policy’s entered benefit remains fixed throughout the chosen comparison period. Neither curve is a probability-weighted payout. A level benefit above the debt does not mean that extra money will necessarily be received; an insured event and a valid claim are still required. A benefit below the debt leaves a funding gap in this deliberately limited comparison. Use the same loan schedule under both insurance alternatives The default begins with CAD 400,000 of mortgage principal, a 25-year amortization and a nominal 5% rate compounded semiannually. The model converts that quote to an equivalent monthly rate and calculates a level month-end payment. The mortgage assumptions are identical under both insurance alternatives. Selecting a different premium does not change the loan’s interest rate or accelerate its repayment. Insurance premiums are separate cash expenses and are not treated as additional principal payments. The comparison keeps the mortgage rate unchanged for the full displayed horizon. It therefore does not reproduce a real sequence of mortgage renewals. Fees, refinancing, extra payments, arrears and changes in the debt contract are excluded. A personal review should use the actual projected balance at the date being considered. Follow the premium cash separately from the conditional benefit The default mortgage-life premium is CAD 60 per month and the individual-policy premium is CAD 40. Over ten years, with the default mortgage still outstanding, those assumed cash commitments total CAD 7,200 and CAD 4,800. The second chart accumulates the premiums as payments. They are not contributions to an investment account and do not create an accessible reserve. The illustration includes no savings component, surrender value or investment return. Both premiums are assumed flat within the selected horizon. The mortgage-life premium stops after the month the debt reaches zero; the individual policy continues for the full comparison period. Those are model conventions. Actual renewal prices, expiry dates and termination conditions must come from the written policies. Trace who receives an accepted claim and how cash is used The third graphic assumes death immediately after the final scheduled mortgage payment shown in the selected horizon. For the mortgage-life example, the accepted benefit equals the remaining debt and is paid to the lender. For the individual-policy example, the named beneficiary receives the fixed benefit and is assumed to choose mortgage repayment first. The chart separates the amount applied to debt from any residual. This use of the individual benefit is an illustration, not an automatic instruction imposed on the beneficiary. If the entered individual benefit is too small, residual family cash is zero and the remaining debt is reported in the figure note. The waterfall shows benefit less outstanding mortgage. A negative endpoint means a debt-funding shortfall, not a negative insurance payout or a new loan. Compare the actual promises before making a protection change Price is one part of the comparison. Confirm the insured person, policy term, beneficiary, coverage limit, exclusions, evidence requirements and whether the contract continues when a mortgage is refinanced or moved. The calculator does not verify any of those terms. FCAC’s rights guide calls for charges, express consent and cancellation information for applicable optional products, with a separate disclosure from a bank. Use that disclosure and the policy wording to ask questions about the actual contract, rather than treating this generic curve as a quote. A family’s protection need may also include other debts, replacement income and near-term expenses. Conversely, other verified coverage or resources may already fund part of the need. This narrow two-contract illustration is not a complete insurance-needs analysis and does not recommend replacing or cancelling an existing policy.
15b40b0294a10d33e471afbe3d737f32ca46a685.zh: 比较合同涵盖的内容、谁收到已接受的索赔以及保费。债务福利下降和个人福利水平提高并不是同一个承诺。从保险类型开始，而不仅仅是“抵押贷款”一词 FCAC 的抵押贷款人寿权利指南将可选抵押人寿保险与抵押贷款违约保险区分开来。它们处理不同的事件，不应被视为可互换的产品。本文比较了两种假设的死亡抚恤金合同：与剩余债务相关的抵押贷款寿命限制和具有输入水平福利的个人保单。它不模拟违约、残疾、重大疾病或失业保险。所有保险金额和保费均为假设。该工具无法确定一个人是否符合资格、索赔是否会被接受或者哪个合同合适。该图表假设两份合同仍然有效，并且任何插图死亡索赔均完全符合条件并被接受。随着抵押贷款的偿还，与债务挂钩的福利可能会减少 FCAC 对可选抵押贷款产品的比较描述了支付给贷款机构的抵押贷款终身福利，并随着抵押贷款余额的增加而减少。其与个人人寿保险的比较还确定了不同的受益人和承保结构。第一个图表使用这两种结构作为选定的合同假设。抵押贷款期限限制遵循每次付款后预定的债务。在整个选定的比较期内，个人保单输入的福利保持固定。两条曲线都不是概率加权的支出。高于债务的福利水平并不意味着一定会收到额外的钱；仍需要保险事件和有效索赔。在这种刻意限制的比较中，低于债务的收益会留下资金缺口。两种保险方案均使用相同的贷款计划 违约起始金额为 400,000 加元的抵押本金、25 年摊销期和每半年复利一次的名义利率 5%。该模型将该报价转换为等值的月费率，并计算月末付款水平。两种保险方案的抵押贷款假设是相同的。选择不同的保费不会改变贷款利率或加速还款。保险费是单独的现金支出，不被视为额外的本金还款。该比较使抵押贷款利率在整个显示范围内保持不变。因此，它不会重现抵押贷款续签的真实顺序。费用、再融资、额外付款、欠款和债务合同的变更不包括在内。个人审查应使用考虑日期的实际预计余额。将保费现金与有条件福利分开跟踪。默认抵押贷款终身保费为每月 60 加元，个人保单保费为 40 加元。十年来，由于默认抵押贷款仍未偿还，这些假设的现金承诺总计为 7,200 加元和 4,800 加元。第二个图表将保费累积为付款。它们不是对投资账户的捐款，也不会创建可动用的储备金。该插图不包括储蓄成分、退保价值或投资回报。假定两种保费在选定的范围内持平。抵押贷款寿险保费在债务达到零的月份后停止；个人政策在整个比较期内持续有效。这些是模型约定。实际续订价格、有效期和终止条件必须来自书面保单。跟踪谁收到了已接受的索赔以及如何使用现金 第三张图假设在所选范围内显示的最终预定抵押贷款付款后立即死亡。对于抵押贷款的例子，接受的利益等于剩余债务并支付给贷款机构。对于个人保单示例，指定受益人收到固定福利，并假定首先选择抵押贷款还款。该图表将应用于债务的金额与任何剩余金额分开。个人福利的这种使用只是一种说明，而不是强加给受益人的自动指示。如果输入的个人福利太小，则剩余家庭现金为零，剩余债务将在数字注释中报告。瀑布显示收益减去未偿抵押贷款。负终点意味着债务资金短缺，而不是负保险支出或新贷款。在进行保护更改之前比较实际承诺 价格是比较的一部分。确认受保人、保单期限、受益人、承保限额、除外责任、证据要求以及抵押贷款再融资或转移时合同是否继续。计算器不会验证任何这些术语。 FCAC 的权利指南要求适用可选产品的收费、明确同意和取消信息，并由银行单独披露。使用该披露和保单措辞来询问有关实际合同的问题，而不是将此通用曲线视为报价。家庭的保护需求还可能包括其他债务、重置收入和近期支出。相反，其他经过验证的覆盖范围或资源可能已经满足了部分需求。这种狭隘的两份合同说明并不是完整的保险需求分析，并且不建议更换或取消现有保单。

a8df1a790b351d2ad1509cc558dbf9144da65782.src: Ask which units are included before comparing a debt balance. A median among borrowers excludes nonborrowers, and multiplying it by a holding share does not generally produce the population mean. Ask whether the statistic describes everyone or only debt holders A headline about how much debt families owe can conceal an important filtering step. Some statistics include all family units, while others describe only units that hold a particular debt. A dollar balance without its population definition can therefore be easy to misread. The first two charts use Statistics Canada’s Survey of Financial Security table 11-10-0016-01 . One measures the share holding each selected debt type. The other gives the median balance among holders of that debt, excluding units with no holding of it. The reference population combines economic families with persons outside an economic family. It is not simply a count of individual adults or occupied dwellings. The 2023 survey covers the ten provinces and excludes Indigenous communities and collective dwellings. Its observations are context for understanding a population, rather than amounts a particular household ought to borrow. Keep the holding share beside the holder-only balance In 2023, the estimated holding shares were 39.0% for mortgage debt, 18.7% for lines of credit, 36.0% for credit-card and instalment debt, 12.0% for student loans and 27.1% for vehicle loans. Mortgage debt includes principal-residence mortgages and mortgages on other real estate. The corresponding holder-only median balances were CAD 205,000, CAD 20,000, CAD 4,500, CAD 14,000 and CAD 20,000. These amounts use 2023 constant dollars. The survey reference year is 2023 and the release date is 29 October 2024; they are not current borrowing offers or a snapshot of today’s accounts. A relatively common debt can have a comparatively small median balance among its holders. Conversely, a less common category can still matter greatly to the units that owe it. Neither the percentage alone nor the median alone supplies the full distribution of balances, interest rates or required payments. The categories overlap. One family unit can have a mortgage, a vehicle loan and a credit-card balance. The holding shares are therefore not slices of one mutually exclusive pie and should not be added to find the share with any debt. Read confidence intervals as uncertainty about an estimate The official table supplies lower and upper 95% confidence bounds. The charts show them as whiskers and repeat both endpoints in the data tables. These are published survey intervals, rather than uncertainty ranges invented by this website. For example, mortgage holding has an estimate of 39.0% with bounds of 38.0% and 39.9%. The holder-only mortgage median is CAD 205,000 with bounds of CAD 200,000 and CAD 215,000. The first interval concerns an estimated share; the second concerns an estimated median. Neither means individual mortgage balances mostly fall between CAD 200,000 and CAD 215,000. A confidence interval around a summary statistic is different from the spread of people’s actual balances. The selected charts do not show percentiles or individual-level data. Sampling, coverage and published rounding limit what can be concluded. The bars are descriptive; the page does not perform a significance test, infer a causal relationship between debt categories or place a reader at a national debt percentile. Build a separate population where every value is known The interactive illustration is independent of the survey. It creates exactly 100 unweighted family units. At the default, forty hold an invented debt balance of CAD 10,000 each and sixty owe zero of that debt. Neither control starts from an official observation. The median among the forty positive-debt units is CAD 10,000 because every one owes that amount. The median across all 100 units is zero: after sorting all balances, both the fiftieth and fifty-first observations are zero. The population mean is different again. Total debt is forty times CAD 10,000, or CAD 400,000. Dividing by 100 gives CAD 4,000 per invented family unit . This is an average over everyone, including the sixty zero balances. All three results are internally consistent. They answer different questions about an explicitly specified dataset. The example does not imply that real borrowers have equal debts or that the actual survey can be reconstructed from one percentage and one median. Watch the median respond differently when more units hold debt The final chart changes the whole number of holders from zero to one hundred while retaining the selected positive balance. Every point represents a different invented population, not the same families moving through time. With fewer than fifty holders, both middle observations in this particular population remain zero. At exactly fifty holders, the ordinary even-sample median averages a zero balance and a CAD 10,000 balance, producing CAD 5,000. At fifty-one holders, both middle observations are CAD 10,000. The mean rises gradually with the holder count because total debt rises by the same amount for each added identical borrower. The holder-only median stays CAD 10,000 whenever at least one holder exists. With no holders, that conditional median is unavailable; assigning it zero would hide the empty subset. This unweighted teaching rule is not a reproduction of the survey’s weighting or estimation procedure. It isolates the effect of including zero balances before interpreting a summary statistic. Use population context without turning a median into a personal limit In the invented population, multiplying the holder share by the identical holder balance gives the all-unit mean because every positive balance is known and equal. That shortcut does not generally work with a real conditional median. The population mean requires the conditional mean, alongside the holding share, rather than the middle holder’s balance. Likewise, adding several holder-only medians does not create the debt of one typical family. Each category can describe a different subset, and medians do not generally add even when measurements come from the same population. For a household plan, list its actual balances, contractual rates, payment amounts and due dates. Consider available cash and repayment capacity separately from national comparisons. The official charts clarify who and what was measured; the independent illustration makes the arithmetic consequences of changing that denominator visible.
a8df1a790b351d2ad1509cc558dbf9144da65782.zh: 在比较债务余额之前询问包括哪些单位。借款人的中位数不包括非借款人，将其乘以控股份额通常不会得出总体平均值。询问统计数据是描述了所有人还是仅描述了债务持有者 有关家庭欠债多少的标题可能会掩盖一个重要的过滤步骤。一些统计数据包括所有家庭单位，而另一些统计数据仅描述持有特定债务的单位。因此，没有人口定义的美元余额很容易被误读。前两张图表使用加拿大统计局的金融安全调查表 11-10-0016-01。其中一个衡量的是每种选定债务类型的持有份额。另一个给出了该债务持有者的余额中位数，不包括没有持有该债务的单位。参考人口包括经济家庭和经济家庭以外的人。它不仅仅是单个成年人或有人居住的住宅的计数。 2023 年的调查覆盖十个省份，不包括原住民社区和集体住宅。它的观察是了解人口的背景，而不是特定家庭应该借贷的金额。在仅持有者余额之外保留控股份额 2023 年，预计抵押债务持股比例为 39.0%，信贷额度持股比例为 18.7%，信用卡和分期债务持股比例为 36.0%，学生贷款持股比例为 12.0%，车辆贷款持股比例为 27.1%。抵押贷款债务包括主要住宅抵押贷款和其他房地产抵押贷款。相应的仅持有人余额中位数分别为 205,000 加元、20,000 加元、4,500 加元、14,000 加元和 20,000 加元。这些金额使用 2023 年不变美元。调查参考年为2023年，发布日期为2024年10月29日；它们不是当前的借款报价或当前账户的快照。相对常见的债务在其持有人之间的余额中位数可能相对较小。相反，不太常见的类别对于欠它的单位来说仍然很重要。单独的百分比或中位数都不能提供余额、利率或所需付款的完整分布。类别重叠。一个家庭单位可以拥有抵押贷款、车辆贷款和信用卡余额。因此，持有的股份并不是一个互斥的蛋糕的各个部分，也不应该相加来找到带有任何债务的份额。将置信区间解读为估计的不确定性 官方表格提供了 95% 置信区间的下限和上限。图表将它们显示为胡须，并在数据表中重复两个端点。这些是已发布的调查间隔，而不是本网站发明的不确定性范围。例如，抵押贷款持有量的估计值为 39.0%，界限为 38.0% 和 39.9%。仅限持有人的抵押贷款中位数为 205,000 加元，上限为 200,000 加元和 215,000 加元。第一个区间涉及估计份额；第二个涉及估计中位数。这两种情况都意味着个人抵押贷款余额大多落在 200,000 加元至 215,000 加元之间。摘要统计数据的置信区间与人们实际余额的分布不同。所选图表不显示百分位数或个人级别数据。抽样、覆盖范围和公布的舍入限制了可以得出的结论。条形图是描述性的；该页面不进行显着性检验、推断债务类别之间的因果关系或将读者置于国家债务百分位数处。建立一个单独的群体，其中每个值都是已知的。交互式插图独立于调查。它恰好创建了 100 个未加权的家庭单位。在违约情况下，40 人持有每人 10,000 加元的虚构债务余额，而 60 人所欠债务为零。这两种控制都是从官方观察开始的。四十个正债单位的中位数是 10,000 加元，因为每个人都欠这个数额。所有 100 个单位的中位数为零：对所有余额进行排序后，第 50 个和第 51 个观测值均为零。总体平均值又不同了。债务总额为 10,000 加元的四十倍，即 400,000 加元。除以 100 得出每个发明的家庭单位为 4,000 加元。这是每个人的平均值，包括六十个零余额。所有三个结果在内部都是一致的。他们回答有关明确指定的数据集的不同问题。该示例并不意味着真正的借款人拥有相同的债务，也不意味着实际调查可以根据一个百分比和一个中位数来重建。当更多单位持有债务时，观察中位数的不同反应。最终图表将持有者总数从零更改为一百，同时保留选定的正余额。每个点都代表不同的虚构人口，而不是随着时间推移而移动的相同家庭。由于持有者少于 50 个，该特定群体中的两个中间观测值仍然为零。正好有 50 个持有者，普通偶数样本中位数平均余额为零，余额为 10,000 加元，结果为 5,000 加元。在 51 个持有者中，两个中间观察值均为 10,000 加元。平均值随着持有人数量的增加而逐渐上升，因为每增加一个相同的借款人，总债务就会增加相同的数额。只要存在至少一名持有者，仅持有者的中位数将保持在 10,000 加元。如果没有持有者，则该条件中位数不可用；将其分配为零将隐藏空子集。这种未加权的教学规则并不是调查加权或估计程序的复制。它在解释汇总统计数据之前隔离了包含零余额的影响。使用人口背景，而不将中位数转变为个人限制 在发明的人口中，将持有人份额乘以相同的持有人余额即可得出所有单位平均值，因为每个正余额都是已知的且相等。该捷径通常不适用于真实的条件中位数。总体平均值需要条件平均值以及控股份额，而不是中间持有人的余额。同样，增加几个仅持有者的中位数并不会产生一个典型家庭的债务。每个类别可以描述不同的子集，即使测量来自同一总体，中位数通常也不会相加。对于家庭计划，列出其实际余额​​、合同费率、付款金额和到期日。将可用现金和还款能力与国家比较分开考虑。官方图表阐明了测量对象和测量内容；独立的插图使改变分母的算术结果变得可见。

dc1d3a6b26892aae4649cb41a39c31d1f7816ba0.src: The currency on the trading screen tells you how you pay. The assets and hedge policy determine the currency exposure you carry. Separate the different currency labels A Canadian investor can purchase a CAD-listed fund that owns foreign assets. Paying in Canadian dollars does not by itself eliminate the effect of exchange rates. A USD trading line likewise does not tell you the full economic currency exposure of the companies inside it. Record four fields: the currency in which you trade, the currency used to report fund values, the currencies of the underlying assets, and the fund’s hedge target. For multinational businesses, revenues, costs, and financing can introduce additional economic exposures beyond the currency of a share listing. Investor.gov’s international-investing overview identifies exchange-rate changes as one source of international investment risk. The CAD calculations below apply that general mechanism to an invented Canadian-dollar example; they do not forecast an exchange rate. The State Street issuer explanation distinguishes an ETF’s trading currency from its underlying currency exposure. Its publication is international context; no product, domicile or tax comparison from that article is modeled here. A fund return measured in USD may already reflect several underlying currency moves. Translating that USD performance into CAD is a measurement conversion, not proof that all holdings have one economic USD exposure. Use an exchange-rate quote with explicit units Define S as Canadian dollars per one US dollar. An increase in S means one US dollar buys more Canadian dollars. If R USD is the investment’s USD total return and all wealth is measured at the beginning and end, the unhedged CAD return is: 1 + R CAD = (1 + R USD ) × (S end ÷ S start ) This convention assumes any distributions remain within the USD investment and are reflected in its total return. If dividends are converted into CAD on their payment dates, translate those cash flows separately. A single ending exchange rate would otherwise misstate their timing. If your data source instead quotes US dollars per Canadian dollar, invert the relevant ratio. Writing the units beside both exchange rates is an inexpensive way to prevent a sign error. The controls use FCU for one selected foreign-currency unit. The worked USD example is one instance of that convention. A foreign-unit ledger begins with CAD wealth divided by the starting CAD-per-FCU quote. Apply the foreign-currency total return to those units, then multiply by the ending CAD-per-FCU quote to obtain ending CAD wealth. Never add CAD and FCU amounts or translate a performance number already reported in CAD a second time. Work through a gain, a headwind and a break-even point Begin with CAD 10,000 at CAD 1.25 per USD. Ignoring conversion costs, you acquire USD 8,000 of assets. Assume the USD investment earns 8% with distributions reinvested, leaving USD 8,640. Translate the ending wealth under three hypothetical exchange rates. In the first row, the foreign asset rises while the USD buys fewer Canadian dollars. The currency move is −8%, but 8% + (−8%) is not the final return. Multiplication produces −0.64% because the translation also affects the investment gain. The break-even ending rate is 1.25 ÷ 1.08 = approximately 1.1574 CAD per USD. This threshold is conditional on the assumed 8% investment return and zero costs. It is a sensitivity result, not an estimate of where the currency should trade. An 8% move does not become the opposite 8% when you invert it The default quote falls from 1.25 to 1.15 CAD per FCU, a decline of 8%. The reciprocal rises from 0.80 to approximately 0.869565 FCU per CAD, an increase of about 8.70%. The two percentage denominators differ.
