They describe the same conversion in different units, not independent gains and losses. Reciprocal quote change = 1 ÷ (1 + original quote change) − 1 When Q is quoted in FCU per CAD, the correct CAD growth factor is (1 + foreign asset return) × (Q start ÷ Q end ). Using Q end ÷ Q start would reverse the economic direction. Put units beside every input before comparing performance statements. The reciprocal bars isolate this quote-reading issue. The separate foreign-investment return guide shows the asset–currency interaction in a waterfall and compares repeated annual scenarios. This page’s ending-quote curve holds the foreign wealth fixed instead of extending a repeated annual forecast. A break-even quote is conditional on the asset result The final curve solves for the quote change that makes ending nominal CAD wealth equal starting CAD wealth. Its formula is 1 ÷ (1 + foreign asset return) − 1. At an 8% asset gain, a 7.4074% quote decline reaches break-even; an 8% decline goes further and produces the default 0.64% CAD loss. After a 20% foreign asset loss, a 20% quote increase is insufficient: 0.80 × 1.20 − 1 equals −4%. A 25% increase is required to restore the starting nominal CAD amount. The resulting curve is asymmetric because the percentage base changes, not because an assumed market relationship has been discovered. The curve spans foreign asset returns from −50% to +50%. A −50% asset result requires a 100% quote increase, which exceeds the quote-change control’s maximum; it remains visible on the curve rather than being clipped to the control range. A complete 100% unlevered asset loss cannot be repaired by any finite positive exchange rate. That boundary is excluded from the controls and curve. All thresholds exclude costs, taxes and inflation. They also assume no contributions, withdrawals or interim CAD conversion of distributions. None is a forecast, a likelihood, a trading signal or a hedge recommendation. What a hedge attempts to change A currency hedge takes an offsetting position intended to reduce specified exchange-rate movements. Funds commonly use foreign-exchange forwards and reset positions periodically. The actual coverage can differ from the target as asset values and cash flows change. Read the current prospectus for the hedge target, reset frequency, instruments, and residual exposure. Hedging one reporting currency is not automatically the same as hedging all of the currencies associated with the underlying holdings. A hedged return is not simply the local-market return less a fixed fee. CME’s FX pricing explanation connects forward and futures pricing with interest-rate differences. Implementation, trading, collateral, and imperfect coverage can also affect results. A hedge can remove a favorable currency contribution as well as an unfavorable one. It does not remove the market risk of the assets. Vanguard Canada’s FAQ describes extra expenses, an imperfect offset and the loss of favorable currency benefits as possible implications of hedging. An unchanged exchange-rate reference in an illustration is therefore not the performance of a real hedge. The charts here calculate unhedged translation only; they do not evaluate a forward contract, a hedge ratio or a hedged fund’s return. Connect currency exposure with the spending liability Start with what the portfolio must eventually pay. A CAD expense due soon and a flexible foreign-currency expense decades away create different problems. Evaluate the asset’s role, the size of its currency sensitivity, and how much uncertainty the spending plan can absorb. For a hypothetical 20,000 allocation, an isolated 10% translation move is about 2,000 before interactions with the asset return. Write that amount beside the relevant spending goal. Then test a joint scenario in which the asset falls and the currency moves against the investor. Partial hedging can leave part of the translation exposure in place, but its implementation still needs a stated policy. There is no universal hedge ratio on this page. Select and review a policy against the portfolio’s actual obligations instead of treating a recent currency trend as a complete investment thesis. Checks before comparing hedged and unhedged funds Confirm that the funds hold comparable assets and follow comparable benchmarks. Identify the target currency, hedge policy, fees, and distribution conventions. Compare returns in the same investor currency over the same dates. Separate fund hedge implementation from your brokerage conversion cost. Model both favorable and adverse currency outcomes with the spending goal in view. The index workbench on TickerLantern uses normalized currency-neutral scenarios. Its result is not automatically a CAD forecast. To build one, translate the modeled wealth or each dated cash flow under explicit exchange-rate assumptions and include the chosen hedge implementation consistently.
dc1d3a6b26892aae4649cb41a39c31d1f7816ba0.zh: 交易屏幕上的货币会告诉您如何付款。资产和对冲政策决定了您所承担的货币风险。区分不同的货币标签加拿大投资者可以购买拥有外国资产的加元上市基金。以加元支付本身并不能消除汇率的影响。同样，美元交易线并不能告诉您其中公司的全部经济货币风险。记录四个字段：您交易的货币、用于报告基金价值的货币、标的资产的货币以及基金的对冲目标。对于跨国企业来说，收入、成本和融资可能会带来股票上市货币以外的额外经济风险。 Investor.gov 的国际投资概览将汇率变化视为国际投资风险的来源之一。下面的 CAD 计算将该通用机制应用于一个发明的加元示例；他们不预测汇率。道富银行发行人的解释将 ETF 的交易货币与其基础货币敞口区分开来。其出版具有国际背景；此处没有对该文章中的产品、住所或税收比较进行建模。以美元衡量的基金回报可能已经反映了几种基础货币的变动。将美元表现转化为加元是一种衡量转换，并不能证明所有持有的资产都具有单一的美元经济风险。使用具有明确单位的汇率报价 将 S 定义为每 1 美元加元。 S 的增加意味着一美元可以购买更多的加元。如果 R USD 是投资的美元总回报，并且所有财富均在开始和结束时计量，则未对冲的 CAD 回报为： 1 + R CAD = (1 + R USD ) × (S end ÷ S start ) 此约定假设任何分配都保留在美元投资内，并反映在其总回报中。如果股息在支付日转换为加元，请单独换算这些现金流量。否则，单一的最终汇率会错误地表述其时机。如果您的数据源报价为美元兑加元，请反转相关比率。将单位写在两种汇率旁边是防止符号错误的一种廉价方法。控件使用 FCU 来表示一种选定的外币单位。美元的实际例子就是该惯例的一个例子。外国单位分类账以加元财富除以每个 FCU 的起始加元报价开始。将外币总回报应用于这些单位，然后乘以每 FCU 的期末加元报价即可获得期末加元财富。切勿添加 CAD 和 FCU 数量或再次转换 CAD 中已报告的性能数据。克服盈利、逆风和盈亏平衡点 从 10,000 加元开始，价格为每美元 1.25 加元。忽略转换成本，您获得了 8,000 美元的资产。假设美元投资收益 8%，分配再投资，剩下 8,640 美元。将期末财富换算为三种假设汇率。第一行中，外国资产上涨，而美元购买的加元减少。货币变动为-8%，但8%+(-8%)并不是最终回报。乘法产生-0.64%，因为平移也会影响投资收益。盈亏平衡最终汇率为 1.25 ÷ 1.08 = 大约 1.1574 加元兑换 1 美元。该阈值以假设的 8% 投资回报率和零成本为条件。这是一个敏感性结果，而不是对货币应该交易的位置的估计。当您反转它时，8% 的变动不会变成相反的 8% 默认报价从每 FCU 1.25 加元降至 1.15 加元，下降 8%。倒数从 0.80 升至每 CAD 约 0.869565 FCU，增幅约为 8.70%。两个百分比分母不同。它们描述的是不同单位的相同转换，而不是独立的收益和损失。相互报价变化 = 1 ÷ (1 + 原始报价变化) − 1 当 Q 以每加元的 FCU 报价时，正确的加元增长系数为 (1 + 外国资产回报) × (Q 开始 ÷ Q 结束 )。使用 Q 结束 ÷ Q 开始将会逆转经济方向。在比较性能陈述之前，将单位放在每个输入旁边。倒数条隔离了这个报价读取问题。单独的外国投资回报指南显示了瀑布式的资产与货币相互作用，并比较了重复的年度情景。本页的结尾报价曲线保持外国财富固定，而不是延长重复的年度预测。盈亏平衡报价以资产结果为条件。最终曲线求解使最终名义加元财富等于起始加元财富的报价变化。其公式为1 ÷ (1 + 外国资产回报) − 1。在资产收益为8%的情况下，报价跌幅为7.4074%，达到盈亏平衡；进一步下跌 8% 会产生默认的 0.64% 加元损失。外国资产损失 20% 后，报价上涨 20% 是不够的：0.80 × 1.20 − 1 等于 −4%。需要增加 25% 才能恢复起始的加元名义金额。由此产生的曲线是不对称的，因为百分比基数发生了变化，而不是因为假设的市场关系已经被发现。该曲线涵盖了外国资产回报率从-50%到+50%的范围。 -50% 的资产结果需要 100% 的报价增加，这超出了报价更改控制的最大值；它在曲线上保持可见，而不是被剪切到控制范围内。任何有限的正汇率都无法修复完全 100% 无杠杆资产损失。该边界被排除在控件和曲线之外。所有门槛均不包括成本、税收和通货膨胀。他们还假设没有捐款、取款或分配的临时加元转换。没有一个是预测、可能性、交易信号或对冲建议。对冲试图改变什么 货币对冲采取抵消头寸，旨在减少特定的汇率变动。基金通常使用外汇远期并定期重置头寸。随着资产价值和现金流量的变化，实际覆盖范围可能与目标有所不同。阅读当前招股说明书，了解对冲目标、重置频率、工具和剩余风险敞口。对冲一种报告货币并不自动与对冲与基础资产相关的所有货币相同。对冲回报不仅仅是当地市场回报减去固定费用。芝商所的外汇定价解释将远期和期货定价与利率差异联系起来。实施、交易、抵押品和不完善的覆盖范围也会影响结果。对冲可以消除有利的货币贡献，也可以消除不利的货币贡献。它并不能消除资产的市场风险。先锋加拿大公司的常见问题解答描述了对冲可能产生的额外费用、不完美的抵消以及有利货币利益的损失。因此，插图中不变的汇率参考并不是真正对冲的表现。这里的图表仅计算未对冲的换算；他们不评估远期合约、对冲比率或对冲基金的回报。将货币风险与支出负债联系起来 从投资组合最终必须支付的金额开始。即将到期的加元费用和数十年后的灵活外币费用会产生不同的问题。评估资产的作用、其货币敏感性的大小以及支出计划可以吸收多少不确定性。对于假设的 20,000 分配，在与资产回报交互之前，孤立的 10% 转换移动约为 2,000。在相关支出目标旁边写下该金额。然后测试资产下跌和货币对投资者不利的联合场景。部分对冲可以保留部分折算风险，但其实施仍需要明确的政策。本页没有通用的对冲比率。根据投资组合的实际义务选择和审查政策，而不是将最近的货币趋势视为完整的投资论点。比较对冲基金和非对冲基金之前的检查 确认基金持有可比资产并遵循可比基准。确定目标货币、对冲政策、费用和分配惯例。比较同一投资者货币在同一日期的回报。将基金对冲实施与经纪转换成本分开。考虑到支出目标，对有利和不利的货币结果进行建模。 TickerLantern 上的指数工作台使用标准化的货币中性情景。其结果不会自动生成 CAD 预测。要构建一个，请在明确的汇率假设下转换建模的财富或每个日期的现金流量，并一致地包括所选的对冲实施。

8a29950b8296b2ec9ea56ee38963212a78c68a23.src: Financing a premium can reduce the cash needed at the start while increasing the debt and total payments. Compare that cost schedule separately from what a policy actually covers. Separate the protection decision from the payment decision Choosing whether a policy meets a household need and choosing how to pay for it are related decisions, but they answer different questions. A premium can look small when folded into a monthly loan payment, even though it creates a larger borrowing obligation. The example begins with CAD 25,000 needed for a purchase or another loan purpose. An optional policy has a hypothetical one-time premium of CAD 1,800. If that premium is financed, the starting debt is CAD 26,800, while usable cash for the purchase remains CAD 25,000. The additional CAD 1,800 goes to the insurer rather than becoming extra spending money. The Financial Consumer Agency of Canada describes credit or loan insurance as optional and discusses recurring and one-time premiums. The charts here are original cost illustrations, not quotes from a lender or insurer. They do not determine whether a particular policy, applicant or claim qualifies. The payment increase includes principal and interest With a five-year term and an 8% nominal annual rate compounded monthly, the base CAD 25,000 loan requires about CAD 506.91 each month. Adding the CAD 1,800 premium raises the modeled payment to about CAD 543.41. The difference is about CAD 36.50 per month. Over sixty payments, the financed premium generates about CAD 2,189.85 of additional repayments. That consists of the CAD 1,800 premium and about CAD 389.85 of financing interest. The waterfall makes the two parts visible. Treating the monthly increase as though it were merely CAD 1,800 divided by sixty would leave out the interest. The loan uses a fixed monthly interest rate equal to the nominal annual rate divided by twelve. Payments occur at month-end and the final payment clears the remaining balance. The model does not round each month’s interest to cents, so an actual lender schedule can differ slightly. Fees, taxes, changing rates and early repayment would require further adjustments. A lower first payment does not settle the full cost comparison Paying CAD 1,800 from separate cash uses the entire premium before the first loan payment. Financing it spreads premium-related repayments over the loan term. A separate hypothetical recurring-premium quote of CAD 35 per month uses CAD 35 at the end of each covered month. The calendar chart isolates those insurance-related outlays. Through month twelve, the cash-premium case has used CAD 1,800, the financed-premium case about CAD 437.97, and the recurring case CAD 420. The ordinary base-loan repayment is excluded from this chart because it is common to all three cases. That earlier cash retention can matter to a household with a tight reserve. It also comes with a continuing payment obligation and, for the financed case, interest. This tool does not assign a return to retained cash or decide how much liquidity is appropriate. Read the early cash need and the full-term cost together rather than treating either number alone as the answer. The cheapest premium schedule may describe different protection The recurring-premium example totals CAD 2,100 across sixty months. The cash one-time premium totals CAD 1,800, and the financed premium totals about CAD 2,189.85. Those are cost figures under entered assumptions. They do not establish an ordering of insurance value. Actual policies can differ in eligibility, insured events, maximum benefits, definitions, exclusions and claim timing. A recurring premium may also depend on a balance or another contractual measure instead of remaining flat. The entered monthly quote therefore needs independent confirmation; the tool does not derive it from the one-time premium or assume the policies are equivalent. FCAC recommends reviewing the insurance certificate and comparing the protection with other coverage already held. A cost analysis can help identify the payment commitment, but it cannot replace that coverage review. No claim probability or claim payment is included here, and the loan-only baseline contains no insurance benefit. Count the premium once when reconciling total payments The stacked bars contain three parts: repayment of the cash advanced for the loan purpose, loan interest, and insurance premiums. In the financed case, the interest segment includes interest attributable to the premium. The premium itself is included in the premium segment even though it is repaid through the loan. Adding both the full insured-loan principal and another CAD 1,800 premium to the same bar would count the premium twice. Omitting the premium because it was financed would understate the amount being repaid. The chart instead keeps usable loan-purpose cash fixed and reconciles the complete payment total. The balance chart shows the other side of that ledger. Both loans decline to zero over the same term, but the financed-premium loan starts higher and requires a higher payment. A payment history can therefore look similar in shape while representing a different starting debt and a different monthly commitment. A longer term and a policy change need separate treatment The matrix keeps the one-time premium fixed and changes only the rate and financing term. Its cells show total premium-related repayments, including interest. A longer term can reduce the payment per month while increasing the sum paid. At zero interest, every cell equals the entered premium. The illustration keeps the loan and premium schedule in place for the full selected term. It does not estimate a refund when coverage is cancelled, calculate a lender’s payout statement or assume that cancelling a policy automatically removes the premium from an outstanding loan. A changed contract or early payoff needs a revised cash ledger using the actual terms. FCAC directs readers to the certificate and insurer for cancellation steps. Keep any actual refund, its date and its destination separate from the remaining loan balance. A refund expected later is not cash already available for today’s bill, and a balance shown on a policy illustration is not a confirmed loan payout amount. Collect the figures that make a comparison usable Confirm the net cash needed for the purchase and the total amount borrowed. Identify whether the premium is paid from cash, added to debt or charged separately. Get the rate, term, monthly payment and total scheduled repayments on a consistent basis. Read the policy’s eligibility, benefit and limitation terms independently of its price. Check actual cancellation, refund and loan-payoff terms before changing either agreement. The five charts are designed to keep each part of that conversation visible. They explain the cost mechanics without choosing a policy, valuing a potential claim, or replacing the household’s wider protection and cash-flow plan.
8a29950b8296b2ec9ea56ee38963212a78c68a23.zh: 融资保费可以减少一开始所需的现金，同时增加债务和总付款。将成本表与保单实际承保范围分开进行比较。将保障决策与支付决策分开 选择保单是否满足家庭需求和选择如何支付是相关的决策，但它们回答不同的问题。当将保费折入每月贷款付款时，保费可能看起来很小，尽管它会产生更大的借贷义务。该示例首先需要 25,000 加元用于购买或其他贷​​款目的。可选保单的假设一次性保费为 1,800 加元。如果支付该溢价，起始债务为 26,800 加元，而用于购买的可用现金仍为 25,000 加元。额外的 1,800 加元将归保险公司所有，而不是成为额外的支出。加拿大金融消费者机构将信用或贷款保险描述为可选保险，并讨论了经常性和一次性保费。这里的图表是原始成本说明，而不是来自贷款机构或保险公司的报价。他们无法确定特定保单、申请人或索赔是否合格。还款额增加包括本金和利息。 期限为 5 年，名义年利率为 8%，每月复利 25,000 加元的基本贷款每月需要约 506.91 加元。添加 1,800 加元保费后，模型付款额将达到约 543.41 加元。每月差价约为 36.50 加元。超过 60 次付款后，融资保费产生约 2,189.85 加元的额外还款。其中包括 1,800 加元的保费和约 389.85 加元的融资利息。瀑布使这两个部分清晰可见。如果将每月增加的金额视为 1,800 加元除以 60，则可以忽略利息。贷款采用固定月利率，等于名义年利率除以十二。付款在月底进行，最后付款将清除剩余余额。该模型不会将每个月的利息四舍五入到美分，因此实际的贷款机构时间表可能略有不同。费用、税收、利率变化和提前还款都需要进一步调整。较低的首付款并不能解决全部成本比较 用单独现金支付 1,800 加元会使用首笔贷款付款之前的全部保费。融资将与保费相关的还款分摊到贷款期限内。每月 35 加元的单独假设经常性保费报价在每个涵盖月末使用 35 加元。日历图表隔离了那些与保险相关的支出。截至第 12 个月，现金保费案例已使用 1,800 加元，融资保费案例约为 437.97 加元，经常性案例已使用 420 加元。普通基本贷款还款未包含在该图表中，因为这三种情况都很常见。对于储备紧张的家庭来说，提前保留现金可能很重要。它还附带持续付款义务，对于融资案例，还附带利息。该工具不会分配保留现金的回报或决定适当的流动性。将早期现金需求和长期成本放在一起，而不是单独将任一数字视为答案。最便宜的保费表可能会描述不同的保护 经常性保费示例在 60 个月内总计 2,100 加元。现金一次性保费总计1,800加元，融资保费总计约2,189.85加元。这些是输入假设下的成本数字。他们没有建立保险价值的排序。实际保单在资格、保险事件、最大利益、定义、排除和索赔时间方面可能有所不同。经常性保费也可能取决于余额或其他合同措施，而不是保持不变。因此，输入的每月报价需要独立确认；该工具并不是从一次性保费中得出这一结论，也不是假设保单是等效的。 FCAC 建议审查保险凭证并将该保障与已持有的其他保险进行比较。成本分析可以帮助确定付款承诺，但不能取代承保范围审查。这里不包括索赔概率或索赔付款，仅贷款基准不包含保险福利。核对总付款时计算一次保费 堆叠条包含三部分：偿还贷款预支现金、贷款利息和保险费。在融资情况下，利息部分包括保费利息。保费本身包含在保费部分中，即使它是通过贷款偿还的。将全额保险贷款本金和另外 1,800 加元的保费加到同一个条中，保费将被计算两次。由于保费是融资而忽略保费会低估偿还的金额。相反，该图表将可用的贷款用途现金保持固定，并核对了全部付款总额。余额图显示了该分类账的另一面。两笔贷款在同一期限内均降至零，但融资溢价贷款的起始金额较高，且需要支付更高的金额。因此，付款历史记录在形状上可能相似，但代表不同的起始债务和不同的每月承诺。较长期限和政策变化需要单独处理 该矩阵保持一次性保费固定，仅更改利率和融资期限。其单元格显示与保费相关的还款总额，包括利息。较长的期限可以减少每月的付款额，同时增加支付的金额。在零利息的情况下，每个单元格都等于输入的溢价。该插图将贷款和保费表保留在整个选定期限内。它不会在保险取消时估计退款，计算贷款机构的付款单或假设取消保单会自动从未偿贷款中扣除保费。合同变更或提前付款需要使用实际条款修改现金分类账。 FCAC 引导读者联系证书和保险公司以执行取消步骤。将任何实际退款、退款日期和目的地与剩余贷款余额分开。稍后预计的退款并不是今天账单上已经可用的现金，保单说明上显示的余额也不是已确认的贷款支付金额。收集可供比较的数据，确认购买所需的净现金和借入的总金额。确定保费是用现金支付、添加到债务中还是单独收取。一致地获取利率、期限、每月还款额和计划还款总额。无论其价格如何，请阅读保单的资格、福利和限制条款。在更改任一协议之前，请检查实际的取消、退款和贷款偿还条款。这五个图表旨在使对话的每个部分保持可见。他们解释了成本机制，但没有选择保单、评估潜在索赔或更换家庭更广泛的保障和现金流计划。

6543ea523b1aa83154a20c467237529927077c80.src: The CAD growth factor combines the asset’s local growth factor with the change in CAD per foreign unit. Adding the two percentage changes omits their interaction. State the currency in which you measure the result An investment can rise in its own currency while declining in the currency used for the household budget. Its local value and the amount of CAD represented by each foreign unit are separate factors. Both affect the CAD value of an unhedged position. The SEC’s international-investing bulletin explains this general currency risk using a U.S.-dollar perspective. This article applies the same translation principle to original hypothetical CAD examples. It does not reproduce a market return series or assess a particular investment. The model holds one foreign-currency exposure without additions or withdrawals. Its asset-return assumption includes any distributions reinvested in the foreign currency. It assumes that the exposure is unhedged and excludes taxes, trading charges and conversion fees. Read the exchange-rate quote in the stated direction The currency control always means the percentage change in CAD per one foreign currency unit . If it is positive, each foreign unit translates into more CAD. If it is negative, each foreign unit translates into fewer CAD. The Bank of Canada’s daily exchange-rate page expresses one foreign unit converted into CAD and identifies its published rates as indicative. No rate from that page is used in this tool. The controls and examples are independent assumptions, not executable conversion quotes. For a fictional quote moving from 1.35 CAD per foreign unit to 1.215, the CAD value of each foreign unit falls by 10%. The reciprocal quote rises by about 11.11%, rather than exactly 10%. Reversing the quote changes the denominator as well as the direction, so simply reversing a percentage sign can give the wrong input. Multiply the two growth factors The one-year CAD return is (1 + local asset return) × (1 + currency change) − 1 . In the default case, the asset gains 10% in its foreign currency while CAD per foreign unit falls 10%. The CAD factor is 1.10 × 0.90 = 0.99, producing a 1% decline. A CAD 10,000 opening position therefore becomes CAD 9,900 after one year, before the excluded costs and taxes. The two percentages do not cancel because the currency translation applies to the ending foreign-currency value, which already includes the asset’s gain. The one-year waterfall expands the calculation into the opening CAD 10,000, a CAD 1,000 asset effect, a negative CAD 1,000 currency effect on the opening amount and a negative CAD 100 interaction. These four entries reconcile CAD 9,900 without mixing units. Distinguish an unchanged result from opposite percentage signs For a 10% local asset gain to translate into exactly zero CAD return, the currency factor would need to be 1 ÷ 1.10. That is a decline in CAD per foreign unit of about 9.09%. A 10% decline is slightly larger and produces the default loss. The fixed matrix shows other one-year combinations. A negative asset return and a positive currency change can partly offset each other, while a negative currency change can deepen an asset loss. The result depends on the pair of factors, not on the asset direction alone. The matrix assigns no probability to its scenarios. It also does not say that asset and currency returns are independent in observed markets. It isolates the translation arithmetic without estimating their joint behaviour. Use a repeated scenario without mistaking it for an observed path The default path repeats the same two annual assumptions for five years. The combined CAD factor of 0.99 repeats five times, so CAD 10,000 becomes about CAD 9,509.90. If the currency quote instead remained unchanged, the same hypothetical local asset return would produce about CAD 16,105.10. The grouped bars keep the entered asset return and starting amount fixed while replacing only the annual currency assumption. Each row has its own stated horizon. This makes the currency sensitivity visible without crediting one scenario with extra deposits or a different local asset performance. Real annual returns and exchange rates do not need to repeat. These lines connect modeled annual endpoints and contain no historical observations. The unchanged-quote comparison is a counterfactual with a constant exchange rate, not a simulated currency hedge with its own costs and mechanics. Connect the measurement currency to the household goal A household that will spend CAD needs to understand the position’s CAD value. A household with a future bill in the same foreign currency has a different currency-matching question. The foreign-goal guide separates the bill’s own price from the CAD amount required to fund it. For an actual account, identify the relevant exposure and the currency in which performance is reported before using a return number in a plan. This tool does not infer the underlying exposures of a fund, measure a company’s operating currencies or choose a hedge. Finally, allow for the costs and dates of making funds spendable. The illustrated investment values are translated reference amounts. Actual sale proceeds and conversion cash require the applicable prices, charges, taxes and settlement arrangements.
6543ea523b1aa83154a20c467237529927077c80.zh: 加元增长因子将资产的本地增长因子与每外国单位加元的变化相结合。添加两个百分比变化会忽略它们的相互作用。说明衡量结果所用的货币 投资可能以本国货币计算上升，而以家庭预算所用货币计算则下降。它的本地价值和每个外国单位代表的加元金额是单独的因素。两者都会影响未对冲头寸的加元价值。美国证券交易委员会的国际投资公告从美元的角度解释了这种一般货币风险。本文将相同的转换原则应用于原始假设的 CAD 示例。它不会重现市场回报系列或评估特定投资。该模型持有一种外币敞口，无需增加或提取。其资产回报假设包括以外币再投资的任何分配。它假设风险敞口未经对冲，且不包括税费、交易费和转换费。按规定方向阅读汇率报价 货币管制始终意味着每一个外币单位加元的百分比变化。如果为正，则每个外国单位都会转化为更多的加元。如果为负数，则每个外国单位转换为较少的加元。加拿大央行的每日汇率页面显示一外币单位兑换为加元，并将其公布的汇率标识为指示性汇率。此工具不使用该页面的汇率。控件和示例是独立的假设，不是可执行的转换报价。对于从每外国单位 1.35 加元到 1.215 的虚构报价，每个外国单位的加元价值下降 10%。倒数报价上涨约11.11%，而不是恰好10%。反转引号会改变分母和方向，因此简单地反转百分号可能会给出错误的输入。将两个增长因子相乘 加元一年回报率为 (1 + 本地资产回报) × (1 + 货币变动) − 1 。在违约情况下，资产以外币计值上涨 10%，而每外币单位加元则下跌 10%。加元系数为 1.10 × 0.90 = 0.99，下降 1%。因此，10,000 加元的未平仓头寸在一年后将变为 9,900 加元（未扣除成本和税费）。这两个百分比不会取消，因为货币换算适用于期末外币价值，其中已包括资产收益。一年瀑布将计算扩展到开仓 10,000 加元、1,000 加元资产效应、开仓金额负 1,000 加元货币效应以及负 100 加元交互作用。这四个条目在没有混合单元的情况下调节了 9,900 加元。区分不变的结果和相反的百分号 要将 10% 的本地资产收益转化为恰好为零的加元回报，货币系数需要为 1 ÷ 1.10。每外国单位加元下降约 9.09%。 10% 的跌幅稍大一些，会产生违约损失。固定矩阵显示其他一年组合。负资产回报和正汇率变动可以部分抵消，而负汇率变动可能会加剧资产损失。结果取决于这对因素，而不仅仅取决于资产方向。该矩阵没有为其场景分配概率。它也没有说资产和货币回报在观察到的市场中是独立的。它隔离翻译算法而不估计它们的联合行为。使用重复的场景，不要将其误认为是观察到的路径 默认路径在五年内重复相同的两个年度假设。合并 CAD 系数 0.99 重复五次，因此 10,000 加元大约变为 9,509.90 加元。如果货币报价保持不变，相同的假设本地资产回报将产生约 16,105.10 加元。分组的条形图保持输入的资产回报和起始金额固定，同时仅替换年度货币假设。每行都有自己规定的地平线。这使得货币敏感性变得可见，而无需将额外存款或不同的本地资产表现计入某一场景。实际年回报率和汇率无需重复。这些线连接建模的年度端点，并且不包含历史观测值。不变报价比较是恒定汇率的反事实，而不是具有自身成本和机制的模拟货币对冲。将衡量货币与家庭目标联系起来 将花费加元的家庭需要了解该职位的加元价值。未来账单采用相同外币的家庭会面临不同的货币匹配问题。外国目标指南将账单本身的价格与为其提供资金所需的加元金额分开。对于实际账户，在计划中使用退货编号之前，请先确定相关风险敞口以及报告绩效所用的货币。该工具不会推断基金的潜在风险、衡量公司的运营货币或选择对冲。最后，考虑到资金可支出的成本和日期。所示的投资价值是换算后的参考金额。实际销售收益和转换现金需要适用的价格、费用、税费和结算安排。

c203a3ef400b53ee16e46c919395a1317b06b490.src: A larger saving balance does not by itself establish progress toward an affordable goal. Compare the account and the goal price at the same future date, using separately stated assumptions. A target amount needs a date as well as a number A saving plan can pass an old target while still falling short of the purchase it was meant to fund. The account may have grown, but the cost of the same goal may have changed too. A comparison with the original price answers a different question from a comparison with the bill due at the planned purchase date. The FCAC’s goal-setting guidance pairs an amount with a timeframe and recommends reviewing the plan. This guide extends that planning structure by giving the goal price and the saving account separate growth assumptions. The goal is a fixed quantity: the same underlying purchase throughout the illustration. Its price increases at a constant assumed rate. An actual family may instead reduce the scope, choose another supplier or change the purchase. Those are useful decisions, but they should be recorded as changes to the goal rather than silently hidden inside an assumed investment return. Read the price and saving paths together Restore the example to start with a CAD 50,000 goal, CAD 10,000 already assigned to it and CAD 500 added at every month-end for eight years. The goal price is assumed to increase by 5% annually. The saving account earns a separate assumed 3% effective annual return. At the deadline, the account holds about CAD 66,751.42. That is more than the original CAD 50,000 target, but the modeled goal now costs about CAD 73,872.77. The shortfall is about CAD 7,121.35. Using today’s price as the future target would incorrectly describe this particular plan as fully funded. The line chart places both amounts on one nominal-CAD scale and the same calendar. The account receives monthly contributions after that month’s growth. The goal price uses proportional monthly compounding of its annual assumption. Neither line is a forecast or a quotation. Their purpose is to make the consequences of the chosen assumptions visible. Solve the contribution without treating it as an investment return The required-transfer calculation first grows the starting balance to the deadline. It then asks how much of the future goal remains to be funded by new monthly contributions. Each earlier contribution has more months to grow than a later one. With monthly account rate r and n contributions, the accumulated value of one dollar contributed at each month-end is ((1 + r) n − 1) ÷ r . The required monthly transfer is the remaining future funding need divided by that factor. When the account return is zero, the factor is simply n. If starting funds alone already cover the modeled goal, the required new contribution is zero. At the default settings, the solved monthly amount is about CAD 565.84, rather than CAD 500. The calculation uses unrounded values internally; displayed cents can leave a small rounding difference if used as an actual standing instruction. A transfer also needs to fit the household budget and the rules of the chosen account. The solver does not establish either affordability or available registered-account contribution room. A longer wait changes both sides of the plan The deadline bars solve separate two-, five-, eight- and twelve-year plans. Every case starts with the same assigned savings and the same current goal price. Each future date receives its own accumulated account value and its own repriced goal. Extra time creates more contribution dates and more opportunity for account growth. It also exposes the goal to more assumed price increases. The resulting required monthly amount reflects both effects. It should not be interpreted as a comparison that keeps the future purchase price fixed while only adding saving years. Under some combinations of a fast-growing price and a lower account return, extending a sufficiently distant deadline may stop reducing the required monthly amount. This is a property of those assumptions, not a prediction that waiting is always harmful. The appropriate response is to review the goal, saving capacity and timing together. Raising the return assumption solely to make an unaffordable plan appear funded leaves the underlying uncertainty unresolved. Reconcile the gap before deciding how to close it The waterfall starts with today’s CAD 50,000 goal and adds about CAD 23,872.77 of modeled price increase. It subtracts the CAD 10,000 starting balance, CAD 48,000 of new contributions and about CAD 8,751.42 of account growth. The endpoint is the same CAD 7,121.35 shortfall shown above. This separates the household’s contribution effort from the account’s return. The CAD 48,000 is not a gain earned by the investment; it is new money the household supplied. Similarly, the increase in the target is not a loss inside the account. It is a change in the price of the separate goal. If accumulated funds exceed the target, the waterfall retains a negative endpoint to show the surplus. The headline instead reports zero unfunded amount. Those displays use different sign conventions for different purposes, so the surplus should not be added back to the account a second time. Keep the plan tied to supported prices and usable cash The matrix changes goal-price growth and the account return independently. It holds the starting price, starting balance and deadline selected in the tool. Every cell solves the full monthly transfer under that combination. The cells are scenarios, not confidence intervals, success rates or recommendations for particular investments. For an actual plan, replace the starting cost with a dated, relevant estimate and record what it includes. Check whether deposits are due before the final purchase date; a single deadline cannot represent an earlier payment schedule. Confirm which savings are exclusively assigned to this goal rather than also required for an emergency reserve or another bill. Review the price and the account at consistent intervals. A real target can change abruptly, while account returns can be uneven or negative. This simple tool excludes those paths, taxes and fees. Its practical contribution is a repeatable funding question: at the date the money is needed, how much does the goal cost, how much is actually assigned to it, and what saving commitment closes the supported gap?
c203a3ef400b53ee16e46c919395a1317b06b490.zh: 更大的储蓄余额本身并不能推动实现可负担目标的进展。使用单独陈述的假设，比较未来同一日期的账户价格和目标价格。目标金额需要一个日期和一个数字。储蓄计划可以通过旧的目标，但仍达不到其原本要资助的购买金额。账户可能增加了，但同一目标的成本也可能发生了变化。与原始价格的比较与与计划购买日期到期的账单的比较所回答的问题不同。 FCAC 的目标设定指南将金额与时间框架配对，并建议审查该计划。本指南通过给出目标价格和储蓄账户单独的增长假设来扩展该计划结构。目标是固定数量：整个插图中的基本购买量相同。它的价格以恒定的假定速度上涨。实际的家庭可能会缩小范围、选择其他供应商或改变购买方式。这些都是有用的决定，但它们应该记录为目标的变化，而不是默默地隐藏在假设的投资回报中。一起阅读价格和节省路径 恢复该示例，以 50,000 加元的目标开始，已为其分配 10,000 加元，并在八年内每个月末添加 500 加元。假设目标价格每年上涨5%。储蓄账户可赚取单独的假定有效年回报率 3%。截至截止日期，该账户持有约 66,751.42 加元。这超出了最初的 50,000 加元目标，但现在的模型目标成本约为 73,872.77 加元。缺口约为 7,121.35 加元。使用今天的价格作为未来目标会错误地将这个特定计划描述为资金充足。折线图将这两个金额显示在一个名义 CAD 比例和相同的日历上。该账户在该月增长后收到每月供款。目标价格使用其年度假设的按比例月复利。这两行都不是预测或报价。他们的目的是使所选假设的后果可见。解决贡献，而不将其视为投资回报 所需转移计算首先将起始余额增加到截止日期。然后，它会询问未来目标的多少仍需通过新的每月捐款来资助。每个早期的贡献都比后来的贡献有更多的时间来增长。根据每月账户利率 r 和 n 供款，每个月末供款 1 美元的累计价值为 ((1 + r) n − 1) ÷ r 。所需的每月转账是剩余的未来资金需求除以该系数。当账户收益为零时，该因子就是n。如果仅启动资金就已经涵盖了模型目标，则所需的新捐款为零。在默认设置下，每月解决的金额约为 565.84 加元，而不是 500 加元。计算内部使用未舍入的值；如果用作实际的常规指令，显示的分可能会留下小的舍入差异。转账还需要符合家庭预算和所选账户的规则。解决者不会建立负担能力或可用的注册账户供款空间。更长的等待会改变计划的双方。最后期限解决了单独的两年、五年、八年和十二年计划。每个案例都以相同的指定节省和相同的当前目标价格开始。每个未来日期都会收到自己的累积帐户价值和自己的重新定价目标。额外的时间可以创造更多的贡献日期和更多的帐户增长机会。它还使目标面临更多假设的价格上涨。由此产生的每月所需金额反映了这两种影响。它不应被解释为保持未来购买价格固定而仅增加储蓄年限的比较。在价格快速增长和账户回报较低的某些组合下，延长足够远的期限可能会停止减少所需的每月金额。这是这些假设的一个特性，而不是预测等待总是有害的。适当的应对措施是审查目标，同时节省容量和时间。仅仅为了使一项无法负担的计划看起来有资金而提高回报假设，就会导致潜在的不确定性得不到解决。在决定如何缩小差距之前先调和差距瀑布从今天的 50,000 加元目标开始，并增加了约 23,872.77 加元的模拟价格上涨。它减去 10,000 加元的起始余额、48,000 加元的新捐款以及约 8,751.42 加元的账户增长。终点与上图所示的缺口相同，为 7,121.35 加元。这将家庭的缴款努力与账户的回报分开。 48,000加元不是投资赚取的收益；这是家庭提供的新钱。同样，目标的增加并不是账户内部的损失。这是单独目标的价格变化。如果累积资金超过目标，瀑布会保留负端点以显示盈余。相反，标题报告无资金数额为零。这些显示出于不同目的使用不同的符号约定，因此不应将盈余再次添加回帐户。将计划与支持的价格和可用现金联系起来。矩阵独立地改变目标价格增长和账户回报。它保存工具中选择的起始价格、起始余额和截止日期。每个单元格都解决了该组合下的完整每月转移。这些单元格是场景，而不是置信区间、成功率或特定投资的建议。对于实际计划，将起始成本替换为注明日期的相关估算，并记录其包含的内容。检查定金是否在最终购买日期之前到期；单一截止日期不能代表较早的付款时间表。确认哪些节省专门用于此目标，而不是紧急储备金或其他账单所需的。定期审查价格和账户。真实的目标可能会突然改变，而账户回报可能会参差不齐或为负。这个简单的工具排除了这些路径、税费。它的实际贡献是一个可重复的资金问题：在需要资金的日期，目标成本是多少，实际分配给它的金额是多少，以及什么储蓄承诺可以弥补支持的缺口？

653707bd028694acce477e6317b92de43e7d1ece.src: Naming a bank balance an emergency fund, a tax reserve and a purchase fund does not create three balances. Reconcile all claims to the same cash and then check the payment dates. Separate a purpose label from an additional asset Suppose a household sees CAD 30,000 in a bank account and mentally describes it as enough for a CAD 12,000 emergency reserve. Later, the same statement seems sufficient for a CAD 9,000 bill. A planned CAD 14,000 purchase also looks smaller than the displayed balance. Each statement can appear reasonable in isolation while the three claims together exceed the cash. The combined requirement is CAD 35,000. Only CAD 30,000 exists at the start, so the full claims are overcommitted by CAD 5,000. Repeating the balance beside each goal does not make the difference available. The FCAC’s budgeting guidance treats saving goals as part of the same plan as income and expenses. This article applies that idea to money already accumulated. It does not prescribe a reserve size or decide which personal goal should receive priority. Allocate existing money once, in an explicit order The opening-allocation bars use a stated illustrative order: assign cash to the protected floor, then the required bill, then the planned purchase. This is an accounting convention for the example, not a legal priority rule or an optimized recommendation. The first CAD 12,000 is assigned to the floor, leaving CAD 18,000. The required bill receives CAD 9,000, leaving CAD 9,000. The purchase requests CAD 14,000 but can be assigned only the remaining CAD 9,000. Its opening funding gap is therefore CAD 5,000. The three assigned amounts add to CAD 30,000, exactly the actual balance. Another order could move the unfunded amount to a different purpose; it would not eliminate the total shortage. A dedicated bank subaccount can make an assignment easier to track, but a transfer between a household’s own accounts does not create new resources. Reconcile the combined balances and assignments once. Understand what the opening waterfall subtracts The opening waterfall begins with the real bank balance and subtracts all requested claims. Its negative CAD 5,000 endpoint describes unassigned capacity after those full requests. It is not the bank’s actual closing balance, because no bill has been paid merely by writing down the earmarks. This distinction matters when reviewing a household balance sheet. Earmarked cash remains an asset. A planned expense is a future use of that asset. Subtracting the cash from net worth when it is labelled, and then subtracting the later bill again, would count the same use twice. The allocation test deliberately ignores future income. It answers whether all the purposes can be funded immediately from current cash. The next chart adds a separate calendar to answer whether new money can close the gap before each bill. Passing that second test does not mean the opening claims were fully funded at the start. Future saving helps only before the relevant payment The default calendar adds CAD 500 of new money before each month’s bills. It pays the required CAD 9,000 bill in month four and the CAD 14,000 purchase in month eight. The CAD 12,000 protected floor is a reference amount retained as cash throughout, not a third bill paid away. After the required bill, the account holds CAD 23,000. By month eight, new saving and the purchase payment leave CAD 11,000. That is still a positive bank balance, but it is CAD 1,000 below the selected protected floor. At year-end, the account has recovered to CAD 13,000. A year-end review would therefore miss the earlier use of the protected money. The calendar needs CAD 1,000 of extra starting cash to stay at or above the floor at every modeled date. That is different from the CAD 5,000 opening allocation shortage: four thousand dollars of new saving has arrived by the purchase date, reducing the funding problem before the bill is paid. Test the floor, purchase size and new-money assumption The matrix changes the planned-purchase amount and monthly new money. Starting cash, the selected floor, the required bill and both payment months stay fixed. Each cell measures additional starting cash needed to preserve the floor at every date, including time zero. If both bills fall in the same month, the ledger adds them before testing the remaining cash. If a bill actually arrives before that month’s income, a more detailed daily calendar may require additional accessible cash. The modeled order of receipts before bills should therefore be checked against real dates. The tool pays entered bills in full even if the balance becomes negative. That negative amount identifies an unfunded need; it is not an assumed overdraft approval, credit line or permission to miss another payment. No borrowing interest is hidden in the chart. Changing or postponing a purchase would require an explicit new scenario. Keep one source of truth for cash assigned to goals Start with a dated statement balance for money that is actually accessible. List every purpose already claiming part of it. Confirm bill amounts and dates independently; the field labelled required bill can represent a tax payment, but this tool neither determines tax owed nor establishes its due date. Record an amount as assigned, still unfunded or paid. When a bill is paid, reduce both bank cash and its outstanding claim so that a completed expense does not remain in the future budget. When new saving arrives, assign it once. Interest, refunds or transfers should be added only when the plan has supported amounts and receipt dates. Use the four views together: requested versus assigned money, total opening capacity, the real cash calendar and alternative funding assumptions. A reserve is useful only to the extent that the cash remains available when needed. A good set of labels helps reveal that availability; the labels themselves cannot supply it.
653707bd028694acce477e6317b92de43e7d1ece.zh: 将银行余额命名为应急基金、税收储备金和购​​买基金并不会产生三种余额。将所有索赔与相同现金进行核对，然后检查付款日期。将用途标签与附加资产分开假设一个家庭在银行账户中看到 30,000 加元，并在心里将其描述为足以用于 12,000 加元的紧急储备。后来，对于一张 9,000 加元的钞票来说，同样的语句似乎就足够了。计划购买 14,000 加元，看起来也比显示的余额要少。每项声明单独看来都是合理的，而三项索赔加起来就超过了现金。合计要求为 35,000 加元。开始时只有 30,000 加元，因此全部索赔多出了 5,000 加元。重复每个目标旁边的平衡并不能产生差异。 FCAC 的预算指南将储蓄目标视为与收入和支出相同的计划的一部分。本文将这个想法应用到已经积累的金钱上。它没有规定储备规模或决定哪个个人目标应优先考虑。以明确的顺序一次性分配现有资金 开放分配条使用规定的说明性顺序：将现金分配到受保护的楼层，然后是所需的账单，然后是计划的购买。这是示例的会计惯例，而不是法律优先规则或优化建议。第一个 12,000 加元分配给楼层，剩下 18,000 加元。所需账单收到 9,000 加元，剩下 9,000 加元。采购请求 14,000 加元，但只能分配剩余的 9,000 加元。因此，其期初资金缺口为 5,000 加元。分配的三笔金额加起来为 30,000 加元，正是实际余额。另一项订单可能会将未提供资金的金额转移到其他目的；它不会消除总体短缺。专用的银行子账户可以使分配更容易跟踪，但家庭自己的账户之间的转账不会创造新的资源。核对合并余额和分配一次。了解期初瀑布减去什么 期初瀑布从实际银行余额开始，减去所有请求的索赔。其负 5,000 加元端点描述了在这些完整请求之后未分配的容量。这不是银行的实际期末余额，因为没有任何账单仅通过减记专项拨款来支付。在审查家庭资产负债表时，这种区别很重要。指定用途的现金仍然是一种资产。计划费用是该资产的未来使用。从贴有标签的净值中减去现金，然后再减去后来的账单，就会将相同的用途计算两次。分配测试故意忽略未来收入。它回答了所有用途是否可以立即从当前现金中获得资金。下一张图表添加了一个单独的日历来回答新资金是否可以缩小每张账单之前的差距。通过第二次测试并不意味着最初的索赔一开始就得到了全额资助。未来的储蓄仅在相关付款之前有帮助默认日历在每个月的账单之前添加 500 加元的新资金。它在第四个月支付了所需的 9,000 加元账单，并在第八个月支付了 14,000 加元的购买费用。 12,000 加元的受保护下限是始终以现金形式保留的参考金额，而不是已付清的第三张账单。支付所需账单后，账户内有 23,000 加元。到第八个月，新增储蓄和购买付款还剩 11,000 加元。这仍然是正银行余额，但比选定的受保护下限低 1,000 加元。截至年底，账户已恢复至13,000加元。因此，年终审查将错过受保护资金的早期使用。该日历需要 1,000 加元的额外起始现金才能在每个建模日期保持在底价或高于底价。这与 5,000 加元的期初分配短缺不同：在购买日期之前，已有 4,000 加元的新储蓄到达，减少了账单支付前的资金问题。测试下限、购买规模和新资金假设 该矩阵会更改计划购买金额和每月新资金。起始现金、所选楼层、所需账单和两个付款月份均保持不变。每个单元都会测量每个日期（包括零时间）保留地板所需的额外起始现金。如果两张账单都在同一个月内发生，分类账会在测试剩余现金之前将它们添加起来。如果账单实际上在当月收入之前到达，则更详细的每日日历可能需要额外的可用现金。因此，应根据实际日期检查建模的账单前收据顺序。即使余额变为负数，该工具也会全额支付输入的账单。该负数表明存在资金不足的需求；它不是假定的透支批准、信用额度或错过另一笔付款的许可。图表中没有隐藏借款利息。更改或推迟购买需要明确的新场景。保留分配给目标的现金的一个真实来源 从一份注明日期的实际可用资金的报表余额开始。列出已经声明其一部分的每一个目的。独立确认账单金额和日期；标记为必填账单的字段可以代表纳税，但该工具既不能确定所欠税款，也不能确定其到期日期。记录分配的金额，但尚未提供资金或已付款。支付账单后，减少银行现金及其未偿索赔，以便已完成的费用不会保留在未来的预算中。当新的保存到达时，分配一次。仅当计划支持金额和收款日期时，才应添加利息、退款或转账。同时使用四个视图：请求资金与分配资金、总开放能力、实际现金日历和替代资金假设。储备金只有在需要时仍能使用的情况下才有用。一组好的标签有助于揭示可用性；标签本身无法提供它。

e8d145e481d81e04606f0b4f91c94195adb53d11.src: A lender’s principal remains owed when an investment falls. Measure the remaining own capital and the interest cash already paid, rather than interpreting the asset’s percentage change as the household’s full result. Write down the asset and the liability separately Borrowing can make an investment account larger without adding the same amount to household net worth. A CAD 30,000 loan adds CAD 30,000 of purchasing power and a CAD 30,000 liability. The account statement shows the investment; a complete plan also needs the debt. The Autorité des marchés financiers explains the risks of borrowing to invest , including that the loan and interest remain payable when investments lose value. The charts isolate that arithmetic with original inputs. They do not determine whether a lender will approve a loan or whether borrowing is appropriate for a particular household. The example invests CAD 20,000 of own capital with CAD 30,000 of borrowed principal, creating a CAD 50,000 investment. Interest is paid from new outside household money. The investment is sold at the selected final date and the original loan principal is repaid then. There is no assumption that the investment pays distributions to cover the monthly bill. A 20% asset loss can remove half the original own capital The default asset-change input is a cumulative negative 20% over the entire three-year horizon. It is not negative 20% in each year. The CAD 50,000 investment therefore falls by CAD 10,000 and is sold for CAD 40,000. Repaying the unchanged CAD 30,000 loan leaves CAD 10,000. Relative to the original CAD 20,000 of own capital, half remains before considering outside interest payments. The asset’s 20% decline and the own-capital reduction use different denominators. The sale waterfall makes the distinction explicit: own money plus the borrowed principal, plus the investment-value change, less the loan repaid. If sale proceeds are below the loan, the arithmetic endpoint becomes negative. The chart retains that gap rather than flooring it at zero. It does not determine the borrower’s legal liability, the availability of other collateral or contractual guarantees. Paying the interest elsewhere does not remove its cost At the assumed nominal annual loan rate of 8%, the unchanged CAD 30,000 principal requires CAD 200 of interest each month. Across three years, the household supplies CAD 7,200 of outside cash. The model pays it as it arises, so it is not added to the loan balance. The account’s sale residual is CAD 10,000, but the complete investment result also subtracts the CAD 20,000 initially supplied and the CAD 7,200 interest paid along the way. That leaves a negative CAD 17,200 result. It is an amount of money lost across the modeled cash flows, not an annualized return or a statement that the whole loss occurred at the final sale. The annual-interest bars show alternative assumed loan rates on the same principal. These cash commitments exist even when the asset supplies no cash income. A principal repayment schedule, loan fees, changing interest rates or capitalized interest would require another ledger. None is silently included here. Compare equal household resources, not a free interest budget A no-loan alternative invests only the same CAD 20,000 of own capital. To keep the household-resource comparison consistent, it also receives the same CAD 200 of outside money each month. It retains that money in zero-return cash because it has no loan-interest bill to pay. After the same cumulative 20% investment decline, the unborrowed investment is CAD 16,000. Adding CAD 7,200 of retained cash gives CAD 23,200 of ending resources. The borrowed alternative has CAD 10,000 after repaying principal. The difference is negative CAD 13,200. That difference consists of the CAD 6,000 loss on the borrowed investment portion and CAD 7,200 of interest paid instead of retained. The extra monthly money is not treated as an investment gain in the no-loan case. Both households received it; one kept it and the other used it to service debt. This is why the ending-resource lines and the net-investment-result headline answer related but different questions. A positive result does not establish that borrowing helped Change the cumulative investment move to positive 20% while leaving the three-year horizon and 8% nominal loan rate unchanged. The CAD 50,000 investment becomes CAD 60,000, leaving CAD 30,000 after loan repayment. Subtracting own starting capital and outside interest produces a positive CAD 2,800 investment result. The no-loan alternative has a CAD 24,000 investment plus CAD 7,200 of retained outside cash, or CAD 31,200. The borrowed choice is still CAD 1,200 behind on the same household-resource basis. Making money overall and benefiting from the borrowing are therefore separate tests. In this simple zero-fee, zero-tax, zero-cash-return setup, the incremental borrowed portion needs a cumulative asset gain greater than the loan rate multiplied by the number of years to finish ahead. At the defaults that threshold is 24% over three years. It is not a guaranteed return, a quoted loan hurdle, or a sufficient assessment of risk. The asset path may also create cash or contractual problems before the endpoint. Use the stress views to identify obligations outside the investment The signed matrix changes cumulative asset moves and loan sizes. It deducts the original own capital and every outside interest payment from sale proceeds after repaying principal. More borrowing increases both market exposure and required interest cash. Negative cells remain visible; the matrix does not attach a probability to them. Real borrowing can add collateral requirements, early demands for repayment, trading restrictions, fees and tax questions. The illustration intentionally calculates none of those. Its fixed principal, fixed interest rate and ability to wait until the endpoint are assumptions that would need to be supported by an actual agreement. In particular, these charts must not be used to estimate a margin call or a permitted brokerage borrowing limit. Begin a household review with the money required for bills, reserves and debt service independently of investment performance. Then record the actual liability beside the asset and trace interest payments from their real cash source. The useful lesson is the reconciliation: asset value, loan principal, remaining own capital and cash already paid are different quantities, and a plan needs all of them.
e8d145e481d81e04606f0b4f91c94195adb53d11.zh: 当投资下降时，贷款机构仍需偿还本金。衡量剩余自有资本和已支付的利息现金，而不是将资产的百分比变化解释为家庭的全部结果。分别记下资产和负债 借款可以扩大投资账户，而无需将相同金额的资金添加到家庭净资产中。 30,000 加元的贷款增加 30,000 加元的购买力和 30,000 加元的负债。账户报表显示投资情况；一个完整的计划也需要债务。金融市场管理局解释了借贷投资的风险，包括当投资贬值时仍需支付贷款和利息。这些图表将该算术与原始输入隔离开来。他们无法确定贷款人是否会批准贷款或借款是否适合特定家庭。该示例用 30,000 加元的借入本金投资 20,000 加元的自有资本，创建 50,000 加元的投资。利息是用新的外部家庭资金支付的。投资将在选定的最终日期出售，然后偿还原始贷款本金。没有假设投资会支付分配来支付每月的账单。 20% 的资产损失可以消除一半的原始自有资本。 默认资产变动输入在整个三年范围内累计为负 20%。每年不负20%。因此，50,000 加元的投资减少了 10,000 加元，并以 40,000 加元的价格出售。偿还不变的 30,000 加元贷款后还剩 10,000 加元。相对于原来的 20,000 加元自有资本，在考虑外部利息支付之前还剩下一半。资产下降 20% 和自有资本减少使用不同的分母。销售瀑布使区别变得明确：自有资金加上借入的本金，加上投资价值的变化，减去偿还的贷款。如果出售收益低于贷款，算术端点变为负数。该图表保留了这一差距，而不是将其定为零。它不决定借款人的法律责任、其他抵押品或合同担保的可用性。在其他地方支付利息并不能消除其成本。假设名义年贷款利率为 8%，不变的 30,000 加元本金每月需要 200 加元的利息。三年来，该家庭提供了 7,200 加元的外部现金。该模型在出现时支付，因此不会添加到贷款余额中。该账户的出售剩余为10,000加元，但完整的投资结果还减去最初提供的20,000加元和一路支付的7,200加元利息。这样就留下了 17,200 加元的负结果。它是建模现金流中损失的金额，而不是年化回报或最终销售时发生全部损失的声明。年利率条显示相同本金的替代假设贷款利率。即使资产不提供现金收入，这些现金承诺仍然存在。本金偿还计划、贷款费用、利率或资本化利息的变化都需要另一个分类账。没有一个被默默地包含在这里。比较同等的家庭资源，而不是自由利息预算 无贷款替代方案仅投资相同的 20,000 加元自有资本。为了保持家庭资源比较的一致性，它每月还收到同样的 200 加元的外部资金。它以零回报现金形式保留这笔钱，因为它没有贷款利息账单需要支付。同样累计投资下降 20% 后，未借投资为 16,000 加元。添加 7,200 加元的保留现金即可得到 23,200 加元的期末资源。借来的替代品在偿还本金后还有 10,000 加元。差额为负 13,200 加元。该差额包括借入投资部分的 6,000 加元损失和支付而非保留的利息 7,200 加元。在无贷款情况下，每月额外的钱不被视为投资收益。两户人家都收到了；一个人保留它，另一个人用它来偿还债务。这就是为什么最终资源线和净投资结果标题回答了相关但不同的问题。积极的结果并不能证明借款有助于将累计投资转向正 20%，同时保持三年期限和 8% 的名义贷款利率不变。 5万加元的投资变成6万加元，还清贷款后还剩下3万加元。减去自有启动资金和外部利息，投资结果为 2,800 加元。无贷款替代方案的投资额为 24,000 加元，加上 7,200 加元保留的外部现金，即 31,200 加元。在相同的家庭资源基础上，借用的选择仍落后 1,200 加元。因此，总体赚钱和从借款中受益是不同的测试。在这种简单的零费用、零税收、零现金回报的设置中，增量借款部分需要累积资产收益大于贷款利率乘以提前完成的年数。默认情况下，三年内该阈值为 24%。它不是保证回报、报价贷款门槛或充分的风险评估。资产路径还可能在端点之前产生现金或合同问题。使用压力视图来识别投资之外的义务 签署的矩阵会改变累积资产变动和贷款规模。偿还本金后，从销售收入中扣除原始自有资本和各项对外支付的利息。更多的借款增加了市场风险和所需的利息现金。阴性细胞仍然可见；矩阵没有给它们附加概率。真实借款可能会增加抵押品要求、提前还款要求、交易限制、费用和税务问题。该插图故意没有计算这些。其固定本金、固定利率和等待终点的能力是需要得到实际协议支持的假设。特别是，这些图表不得用于估计追加保证金或允许的经纪借款限额。开始对账单、准备金和偿债所需的资金进行家庭审查，与投资绩效无关。然后在资产旁边记录实际负债，并从其真实现金来源追踪利息支付。有用的教训是对账：资产价值、贷款本金、剩余自有资本和已支付的现金是不同的数量，而计划需要所有这些。

0b56ed51a004289507fbd43963f8c2b4186af10e.src: A building reserve and a personal reserve do different jobs. Once an owner assessment is independently confirmed, test every payment date against cash that is actually yours to use. Keep the building’s money separate from your personal cash A condominium or strata corporation may hold funds for common expenses while an owner separately keeps a household reserve. The two balances are not interchangeable. A contribution already made through strata fees does not become personal cash available to pay a new bill. British Columbia’s official guidance distinguishes special levies from ordinary monthly strata fees and describes the corporation’s contingency reserve fund. Those sources provide context for the separation in these graphics. This article does not calculate legal approval, unit entitlement, who owes an assessment on a sale or whether the building’s reserve is adequate. The starting point for the tool is an independently confirmed assessment amount allocated to one owner, with a payment calendar. Enter that owner-level amount once. Do not subtract an assumed share of the building reserve again unless the actual assessment calculation has already been formally changed. A building balance is not a personal account you can simply withdraw. An assessment sits beside the monthly fee The first chart compares an ordinary month with the selected assessment months. The ordinary strata fee continues in both. The extra segment is the assessment instalment. This makes a cash commitment visible without suggesting that the regular fee automatically stops while an assessment is being paid. The original example assumes an owner-level assessment of CAD 18,000, paid in three equal CAD 6,000 instalments at the starts of months six, nine and twelve. The ordinary monthly strata fee is CAD 500 and is already funded outside the personal assessment reserve. The displayed month types are not an annual total. There can be many ordinary months between instalments. Before using the reserve contribution field, confirm that mortgage or rent, strata fees, taxes, insurance and ordinary living costs are already in the main household budget. The tool assumes the remaining monthly saving is available after those commitments. Check the reserve before the bill, rather than after the next deposit The second chart follows the personal assessment reserve. Each instalment comes at the start of its month. That month’s new saving arrives at month-end. A transfer received after a bill cannot make the earlier payment timely. With CAD 5,000 already earmarked and CAD 400 saved monthly, the original example funds the first CAD 6,000 instalment. It does not fund all of the next two. The separate deadline bars retain total unfunded assessment bills of CAD 8,600, even though continued deposits leave CAD 5,200 in the reserve at month twenty-four. This is a useful distinction between a balance and a successful funding calendar. The positive ending account is not proof that the payments were affordable when due. Unpaid bills are neither forgiven nor paid from automatic credit. Later deposits remain available for later uses; they do not silently cure the earlier shortfalls. The last deadline is not always the binding one The fourth chart calculates the monthly contribution needed to fund every deadline. For an instalment due in month m, only m − 1 month-end deposits have arrived. The test compares cumulative bills due by that month with opening reserve plus those earlier deposits. For each deadline after month one, the required monthly saving is (cumulative assessment due − opening reserve) ÷ deposits received before the deadline , floored at zero. The tool takes the greatest requirement across all instalments. With the original schedule, that is approximately CAD 1,181.82 monthly. Rounding a real standing transfer down could leave a small shortfall. A month-one instalment needs opening cash. If it exceeds the opening reserve, no amount saved later each month can fund it on time. The matrix marks that case unavailable instead of dividing by zero or pretending the first transfer arrived early. Different approved instalment dates would require a new calendar, not a more optimistic label. Use the cash result alongside the actual assessment documents The tool assumes equal instalments at a regular spacing. An actual resolution may have unequal amounts, different dates, conditions or interest consequences. Use its confirmed schedule when preparing an implemented plan, and verify the applicable provincial rules and responsibility before a purchase or sale. If the model shows a gap, distinguish possible sources of funding: personal cash already accessible, new affordable saving before the bill, a separately confirmed funding arrangement, or a formally changed payment schedule. None is supplied automatically here. Selling an investment or borrowing also creates its own timing, cost and tax questions. Confirm the amount allocated to the owner and every due date. Keep corporate reserves and personal reserves on separate ledgers. Fund ordinary strata fees in the main budget. Check cash before each assessment instalment. Retain every unfunded bill until a workable solution is identified. The objective is a realistic personal funding calendar. It is not a prediction of a future levy or a recommendation that a particular building should collect or spend its reserves.
0b56ed51a004289507fbd43963f8c2b4186af10e.zh: 建筑保护区和个人保护区的作用不同。一旦业主评估得到独立确认，请根据您实际使用的现金测试每个付款日期。将建筑物的资金与您的个人现金分开。公寓或分层公司可能持有用于共同开支的资金，而业主则单独保留家庭储备金。两种天平不可互换。已经通过分层费用做出的贡献不会成为可用于支付新账单的个人现金。不列颠哥伦比亚省的官方指南将特别税与普通的每月分层费用区分开来，并描述了公司的应急储备基金。这些来源为这些图形中的分离提供了背景。本文不计算法律批准、单位权利、谁应对销售进行评估或建筑物的储备是否充足。该工具的起点是分配给一位业主的独立确认的评估金额以及付款日历。输入所有者级别金额一次。除非实际评估计算已正式更改，否则不要再次减去建筑储备的假定份额。大厦余额不是您可以简单提取的个人账户。评估位于月费旁边。第一个图表将普通月份与选定的评估月份进行了比较。两者均继续收取普通分层费用。额外部分是评估分期付款。这使得现金承诺变得可见，而不表明在支付评估时定期费用自动停止。原始示例假设所有者评估为 18,000 加元，在第 6、9 和 12 个月开始时分三期等额支付 6,000 加元。普通的每月分层费用为 500 加元，已在个人入息税储备金之外提供资金。显示的月份类型不是年度总计。分期付款之间可能有许多普通月份。在使用准备金缴款字段之前，请确认抵押贷款或租金、分层费用、税收、保险和普通生活费用已包含在主要家庭预算中。该工具假设在这些承诺之后剩余的每月节省是可用的。在账单之前检查准备金，而不是在下一次存款之后检查准备金 第二个图表遵循个人评估准备金。每期付款均在月初进行。该月的新储蓄将于月底到达。账单后收到的转账无法及时支付较早的款项。由于已指定 5,000 加元，每月节省 400 加元，原始示例为第一笔 6,000 加元提供资金。它不会为接下来的两个项目提供资金。单独的截止日期保留了总计 8,600 加元的无资金评估账单，尽管持续存款在第 24 个月留下了 5,200 加元的储备金。这是余额和成功融资日历之间的有用区别。正数的期末账目并不能证明到期付款是可以负担的。未付账单既不会被免除，也不会通过自动信用支付。后来的存款仍可供以后使用；他们并没有默默地解决早期的缺陷。最后的截止日期并不总是具有约束力的第四个图表计算每个截止日期所需的每月捐款。对于 m 月到期的分期付款，仅收到 m − 1 笔月末存款。该测试将该月到期的累积账单与期初准备金加上较早的存款进行比较。对于第一个月后的每个截止日期，所需的每月储蓄为（累计应付摊款 - 期初准备金）÷截止日期之前收到的存款，下限为零。该工具满足所有分期付款中的最高要求。按照原计划，每月约为 1,181.82 加元。将实际的常设转会向下舍入可能会留下一个小缺口。一个月一期的分期付款需要开户现金。如果超过了期初准备金，那么每个月以后节省的金额都无法按时提供资金。该矩阵标记该情况不可用，而不是除以零或假装第一次传输提前到达。不同的批准分期付款日期需要新的日历，而不是更乐观的标签。将现金结果与实际评估文件一起使用该工具假定定期等额分期付款。实际决议可能具有不同的金额、不同的日期、条件或利益后果。在准备实施计划时使用其确认的时间表，并在购买或销售前核实适用的省级规则和责任。如果模型显示存在缺口，请区分可能的资金来源：已经可用的个人现金、账单前新的负担得起的储蓄、单独确认的资金安排或正式更改的付款时间表。这里不会自动提供任何内容。出售投资或借款也会产生其自身的时间安排、成本和税务问题。确认分配给所有者的金额和每个到期日。将公司准备金和个人准备金保存在不同的分类账上。在主要预算中资助普通分层费用。每次评估分期付款前检查现金。保留所有无资金支持的账单，直到找到可行的解决方案。目标是一个现实的个人融资日历。它不是对未来征税的预测，也不是对特定建筑物应收集或花费其储备金的建议。

1a76f2cd4eb45fd314be18244c2e308136724c47.src: A smaller inflation-adjusted debt is not cash received from the lender. Affordability still depends on the income and living costs that surround each unchanged payment. A contract amount and its purchasing power are different measurements A fixed nominal loan payment is an amount of currency due under the assumed contract. Its real value expresses that same amount in the purchasing power of a chosen starting date. Inflation can change the second measurement without changing the first. The Bank of Canada explains inflation as a persistent rise in the average price level and the resulting loss of purchasing power. The tool uses that concept to translate amounts into starting-date dollars. It does not use current CPI observations or forecast future inflation. The first chart puts the nominal payment beside its real equivalent. If the nominal payment is P and prices rise at an assumed annual rate i, the real amount after t years is P ÷ (1 + i) t . The lender still receives P dollars. The difference between the lines is not a rebate, a principal repayment or money deposited in the borrower’s account. Principal falls because payments repay it The second chart follows the remaining loan balance after each payment, in nominal and starting-date dollars. The nominal schedule charges opening balance times the nominal annual interest rate divided by twelve, then applies the monthly payment. The final payment is capped to clear the remaining amount. The original example is a CAD 25,000 loan over five years at an assumed fixed 6% nominal annual rate. Its monthly payment is approximately CAD 483.32. Both debt-balance lines reach zero at repayment. One does not reach zero sooner merely because its vertical axis uses purchasing power. At an assumed 4% annual price increase, the reference value of the final contractual payment is about CAD 397.25 in starting-date dollars. This conversion cannot be counted as a second source of debt reduction on top of the actual amortization. Keep the principal ledger in nominal dollars, with the real presentation as a separate view. Prices do not automatically raise the paycheque The third chart adds the household around the loan. Take-home income and non-debt living costs begin at independently entered amounts, then grow at their separate assumed rates. The loan payment remains fixed. The resulting monthly surplus is income less living costs less that payment. In the original example, take-home income starts at CAD 5,000 monthly and non-debt living costs at CAD 3,500. Income increases at an assumed 1% annually while living costs increase at 4%. The starting monthly surplus after the loan payment is about CAD 1,016.68. At the final payment date it is about CAD 513.45. The real value of the payment has fallen, yet less nominal monthly cash remains after the assumed commitments. This is not a contradiction: the price-level denominator and the household cash budget answer different questions. Rising essential costs can use up the income that must also fund the unchanged payment. Stress pay and prices independently The matrix changes annual price growth and annual take-home growth while retaining the same loan and starting budget. Each cell reports the monthly surplus at the selected loan’s final payment date, with that last payment still included. The loan-free month afterwards is outside the chart. Read down one income-growth column to see the effect of higher living costs. Read across a price row to see how a different income path changes the available cash. Negative cells are funding gaps in the monthly budget. They do not come with an automatic overdraft, a reduction in spending or extra employment. These are deterministic cases. The grid does not estimate how wages will respond to inflation, whether an employer will grant a raise, or the likelihood that any particular household will maintain its income. A household’s cost basket can also move differently from an aggregate price index. Use real values for comparison and nominal dollars for bill planning Real values help compare purchasing power across time. Actual bill planning needs the currency amounts and payment dates that will apply. A plan can use both views while keeping their units explicit. This is a monthly run-rate budget, not a bank-account ledger. It does not test whether income arrives before a payment within the month. Nor does it include new borrowing, loan fees, tax changes, refinancing, unemployment or a change in the selected fixed rate. Those require separate assumptions and, for a real loan, the actual agreement. Record the nominal payment and the period for which it is fixed. Keep the principal repayment schedule separate from price-level conversions. Estimate income and major living costs independently. Test lower income growth as well as higher prices. Map the actual receipt and payment dates before relying on the monthly surplus. A claim that inflation reduces the real burden of debt is incomplete until the income and spending budget is examined. These charts show why a mathematical reduction in purchasing-power value does not settle the next payment’s affordability.
1a76f2cd4eb45fd314be18244c2e308136724c47.zh: 经通胀调整后的较小债务不是从贷款机构收到的现金。负担能力仍然取决于每笔不变付款的收入和生活成本。合同金额及其购买力是不同的衡量标准。固定名义贷款付款是根据假定合同应付的货币金额。它的实际价值表示所选起始日期的相同购买力金额。通货膨胀可以改变第二个测量值而不改变第一个测量值。加拿大央行将通货膨胀解释为平均价格水平持续上涨以及由此导致的购买力损失。该工具使用该概念将金额转换为起始日期美元。它不使用当前消费者物价指数观察结果或预测未来通胀。第一张图表将名义付款与其实际等额付款放在一起。如果名义付款为 P 并且价格以假设的年增长率 i 上涨，则 t 年后的实际金额为 P ÷ (1 + i) t 。贷款机构仍然收到 P 美元。额度之间的差额不是回扣、本金偿还或存入借款人账户的资金。本金下降是因为付款偿还了本金。第二张图表显示了每次付款后的剩余贷款余额（以名义美元和起始日期美元表示）。名义时间表收取期初余额乘以名义年利率除以十二，然后应用每月付款。最终付款有上限以清除剩余金额。最初的示例是五年期 25,000 加元的贷款，假定固定名义年利率为 6%。其每月付款约为 483.32 加元。偿还时两条债务余额线均为零。一个数不会仅仅因为它的纵轴使用购买力而更快地达到零。假设每年价格上涨 4%，最终合同付款的参考价值约为 397.25 加元（以起始日期美元计算）。这种转换不能算作实际摊销之外的第二个债务减少来源。将主分类账保留为名义美元，并将真实的呈现形式作为单独的视图。价格不会自动提高工资 第三张图表添加了贷款周围的家庭。实得收入和非债务生活成本以独立输入的金额开始，然后以各自假定的比率增长。贷款付款保持固定。由此产生的每月盈余是收入减去生活费用减去付款。在最初的示例中，实得收入每月 5,000 加元起，无债务生活费用为 3,500 加元。假设收入每年增长 1%，而生活成本则增长 4%。还款后每月起始盈余约为1,016.68加元。在最终付款日，金额约为 513.45 加元。付款的实际价值已经下降，但在承担假设的承诺后，每月名义现金仍然减少。这并不矛盾：价格水平分母和家庭现金预算回答了不同的问题。不断上涨的基本成本可能会耗尽收入，而这些收入还必须为不变的付款提供资金。独立地强调薪酬和价格 该矩阵改变了年度价格增长和年度实得增长，同时保留相同的贷款和起始预算。每个单元格报告所选贷款最终付款日期的每月盈余，其中仍包括最后一次付款。之后的无贷款月份不在图表之内。阅读一篇收入增长专栏，看看生活成本上升的影响。阅读价格行，了解不同的收入路径如何改变可用现金。负单元格是每月预算中的资金缺口。它们不会自动透支、减少支出或增加就业。这些是确定性情况。该网格不会估计工资将如何应对通货膨胀、雇主是否会加薪，或者任何特定家庭维持收入的可能性。家庭的成本篮子的变动也可能与总价格指数不同。使用实际价值进行比较，使用名义美元进行账单计划 实际价值有助于比较不同时间段的购买力。实际的账单计划需要适用的货币金额和付款日期。计划可以使用这两种视图，同时保持其单位明确。这是每月的运行预算，而不是银行账户分类账。它不会测试收入是否在当月付款之前到达。也不包括新借款、贷款费用、税收变化、再融资、失业或所选固定利率的变化。这些需要单独的假设，对于真正的贷款，需要实际的协议。记录名义付款及其固定期限。将本金偿还计划与价格水平转换分开。独立估计收入和主要生活费用。测试较低的收入增长和较高的价格。在依赖每月盈余之前映射实际收款和付款日期。在收入和支出预算得到审查之前，通货膨胀减少实际债务负担的说法是不完整的。这些图表显示了为什么购买力价值的数学下降并不能解决下一次付款的负担能力。

e1d66e679a77ba527bb62122c12ea3b942381eea.src: A purchase schedule changes transaction costs and time in the market. Compare equal deposits and keep waiting cash in the result before choosing a frequency. These are future contributions, not a lump sum already in hand The comparison starts with the same initial cash and adds the same contribution at the beginning of every modeled week. Neither strategy borrows contributions from later paycheques. This is a different decision from choosing when to invest a lump sum that already exists. One strategy purchases every week. The other accumulates cash and purchases at the selected interval. On a scheduled purchase date it pays one fixed fee from the available cash and invests the rest. If cash does not exceed the fee, the purchase is skipped and no fee is charged. Every model year contains fifty-two weeks. Buying every four weeks therefore creates thirteen scheduled opportunities a year. It does not mean twelve calendar-month purchases. That distinction matters when translating a frequency into a fee total or comparing it with a real payroll and brokerage schedule. A fixed charge can be a large share of a small purchase Investor.gov distinguishes transaction fees from ongoing investment expenses. This tool focuses on one fixed charge per completed purchase. It excludes annual fund expenses, spreads, exchange charges and other account costs, which would need to be added for a real implementation decision. The original example contributes CAD 100 weekly for ten fifty-two-week years, with a hypothetical CAD 5 fee per purchase. Buying every week completes 520 trades and pays CAD 2,600 in nominal fees. Buying every four weeks completes 130 trades and pays CAD 650, assuming each scheduled purchase can be funded. The difference in nominal charges is CAD 1,950. That is not automatically the ending wealth difference: paying a fee also changes the capital left to earn returns, while batching changes how long contributions stay in cash. The first chart therefore compares total resources as well as the fee chart. Waiting money still belongs in the comparison The third chart shows the first model year’s waiting cash. Contributions arrive, earn the selected cash return when retained, and are transferred on completed purchase dates. The repeated rise and fall can be a planned batching process, rather than evidence of a failed contribution. At the finish, total resources equal invested asset value plus cash still waiting. This matters when the chosen interval does not divide the number of modeled weeks exactly. A final contribution is not lost merely because the next scheduled purchase is after the horizon. Initial cash also follows the selected schedule. If a reader enters a large opening amount, it waits until the first scheduled purchase in that strategy. That is an explicit assumption, not a recommendation to delay deploying an existing lump sum. Use zero opening cash to isolate the implementation of future weekly saving. Fee savings and market exposure can pull in different directions The original example assumes an effective annual asset return of 5% and cash return of 2%, converted to weekly factors. At ten model years, weekly buying ends at approximately CAD 63,705 and four-week buying at approximately CAD 66,165. Both have received the same CAD 52,000 of contributions. Those are original calculations for a smooth invented return path, not historical strategy results. The asset and cash returns do not fluctuate. A higher asset return can increase the opportunity cost of waiting, while a negative asset return can make delayed exposure beneficial in this particular model. Real markets provide changing prices and uncertain paths. The fourth chart changes the fee and purchase interval. Every cell subtracts a weekly-purchase strategy with the same row fee and all other selected assumptions. Positive values favour that interval within the cell; negative values favour weekly buying. The matrix does not assign probabilities or identify a universally best trading frequency. Check the full implementation before changing the schedule A real platform may have commission-free purchases, minimum ticket sizes, fractional-unit restrictions, automatic plans or different charges for different products. The model does not assess the availability, quality or terms of any broker. A zero entered trade fee also does not mean an investment has no ongoing expenses. Confirm the actual deposit timing, purchase timing, fee schedule, settlement arrangements and treatment of small residual cash. Consider whether the chosen schedule is easy to follow when income changes. An implementation that is hard to maintain can produce a different cash path from the one drawn here. Hold the saving budget and deposit dates constant. Count completed purchases rather than only scheduled dates. Deduct fees from the same resources used to invest. Include uninvested cash at the comparison date. Test more than one relationship between asset and cash returns. The question is how to implement an already appropriate saving plan. A lower transaction bill does not establish that the underlying investment, account or risk level is suitable for the goal.
e1d66e679a77ba527bb62122c12ea3b942381eea.zh: 购买计划会改变交易成本和市场时间。在选择频率之前，比较等额存款并等待结果兑现。这些是未来的捐款，而不是已经在手的一次性付款。比较从相同的初始现金开始，并在每个建模周开始时添加相同的捐款。这两种策略都没有从后来的薪水中借用捐款。这与选择何时投资已经存在的一次性投资是不同的决定。每周购买一种策略。另一个则按照选定的时间间隔积累现金和购买。在预定的购买日期，它从可用现金中支付一笔固定费用，并将其余部分用于投资。如果现金未超过费用，则跳过购买且不收取任何费用。每个模型年包含五十二周。因此，每四个星期购买一次，每年创造十三个预定机会。这并不意味着十二个日历月的购买。当将频率转换为费用总额或将其与实际工资和经纪计划进行比较时，这种区别很重要。固定费用可能占小额购买的很大一部分。 Investor.gov 将交易费用与持续投资费用区分开来。该工具针对每次完成的购买收取一笔固定费用。它不包括年度基金费用、点差、兑换费用和其他账户成本，这些费用需要添加才能做出真正的实施决策。最初的示例每周贡献 100 加元，持续 10 年 52 周，假设每次购买费用为 5 加元。每周购买完成 520 笔交易并支付 2,600 加元的象征性费用。假设每次预定的购买都能获得资助，每四个星期购买一次即可完成 130 笔交易并支付 650 加元。名义费用差额为 1,950 加元。这并不会自动结束财富差异：支付费用也会改变赚取回报的剩余资本，而批量改变捐款保留现金的时间。因此，第一个图表比较了总资源和费用图表。等待资金仍然属于比较第三个图表显示了第一个车型年的等待资金。捐款到达，保留时赚取选定的现金回报，并在完成的购买日期转移。重复的上升和下降可能是有计划的批处理过程，而不是贡献失败的证据。最终，总资源等于投资资产价值加上仍在等待的现金。当选择的间隔不能准确地除以建模周数时，这一点很重要。最终的贡献不会仅仅因为下一次计划购买是在期限之后而丢失。初始现金也遵循选定的时间表。如果读者输入较大的开仓金额，它将等到该策略中的第一次预定购买。这是一个明确的假设，而不是延迟部署现有一次性付款的建议。使用零期现金来隔离未来每周储蓄的实施。费用节省和市场敞口可能会向不同方向拉动。最初的示例假设有效的年度资产回报率为 5%，现金回报率为 2%（转换为每周因素）。在十个车型年中，每周购买量约为 63,705 加元，四周购买量约为 66,165 加元。两人均收到了同样的 52,000 加元捐款。这些是对发明的平滑返回路径的原始计算，而不是历史策略结果。资产和现金回报不波动。较高的资产回报可能会增加等待的机会成本，而负资产回报可能会使延迟暴露在该特定模型中受益。真实市场提供了不断变化的价格和不确定的路径。第四张图表更改了费用和购买间隔。每个单元格都减去具有相同行费用和所有其他选定假设的每周购买策略。正值有利于单元内的该间隔；负值有利于每周购买。该矩阵不会分配概率或确定普遍最佳的交易频率。在更改时间表之前检查完整的实施情况真实的平台可能有免佣金购买、最小门票尺寸、分数单位限制、自动计划或不同产品的不同收费。该模型不评估任何经纪商的可用性、质量或条款。零输入交易费用也不意味着投资没有持续费用。确认实际存款时间、购买时间、费用表、结算安排及小额剩余现金处理。考虑当收入发生变化时，所选择的时间表是否易于遵循。难以维护的实现可能会产生与此处绘制的不同的现金路径。保持储蓄预算和存款日期不变。计算已完成的购买，而不仅仅是计划的日期。从用于投资的相同资源中扣除费用。包括比较日未投资的现金。测试资产和现金回报之间的多种关系。问题是如何实施已经合适的储蓄计划。较低的交易费用并不能证明基础投资、账户或风险水平适合目标。

f4c4bd2227bf367ef81f020ba579a89aeb2aabba.src: A household may own enough money and still face an earlier payment gap. Record access, authority and timing alongside every balance assigned to essential bills. Begin with the person who must make the payment A balance sheet records ownership and debt. A payment plan also needs to identify who can give an instruction, which account they can use and when the funds become accessible. These questions can matter during an illness, an absence or an interruption in normal account access. The Government of Canada’s financial power-of-attorney overview distinguishes authority to manage someone’s property from ownership of that property. It also explains that document names and requirements vary across provinces and territories. A financial model cannot establish that a document or proposed instruction is valid. The calculator starts after that separate authority check. Its opening amount means money already usable by the authorized bill payer. Its delayed balance means existing household cash that becomes usable on an independently assumed date. That date is a stress input, rather than a bank processing standard or a legal deadline. Give the opening and delayed balances different roles The example has CAD 2,000 accessible at the start and a separate CAD 12,000 balance awaiting access until day 21. The household owns CAD 14,000 across these two balances. Only CAD 2,000 can fund a payment before the second amount becomes usable. The first chart shows those two balances and their labelled total. Do not add the total bar to its components. Releasing CAD 12,000 later changes where the money can be used; it does not create CAD 12,000 of earnings, a gift or an investment gain. An actual access record should avoid storing login credentials, passwords or verification codes. Record the institution, the account’s purpose, the person’s confirmed role and the institution’s process for giving authorized instructions. Keep sensitive account details in a private location appropriate for the people who need them. Find the shortage before the delayed money arrives Living costs are CAD 4,500 per thirty-day period, allocated at CAD 150 a day. Before the start of day 21, twenty daily amounts have left: 20 × CAD 150 = CAD 3,000 . Against CAD 2,000 initially available, that creates a CAD 1,000 funding gap. The separate CAD 12,000 arrives before day 21’s spending. Net income of CAD 2,500 arrives after spending on days 30 and 60. Those later receipts improve the account balance, but cannot make the earlier payments without another resource. The graph retains within-day payment points rather than showing only a reassuring month-end amount. The comparison grants access to the same separate balance at the start of day 1. Both paths use identical assets, income and expenses. Their difference is timing. Neither path assumes an overdraft, a bill extension or an automatic transfer from some unlisted account. Reconcile the end without losing the access problem After sixty days, the example has received all CAD 12,000 of delayed cash and two CAD 2,500 income payments, and has paid CAD 9,000 of living costs. The ending balance is CAD 2,000 + CAD 12,000 + CAD 5,000 − CAD 9,000 = CAD 10,000 . That positive endpoint coexists with the earlier CAD 1,000 shortage. All allowed access dates occur within sixty days, so changing the date preserves the endpoint while potentially changing the minimum balance. The waterfall reconciles the total resources; the daily line answers whether those resources arrive in time. The matrix varies access dates and spending. Its values show additional opening cash beyond the amount already entered. A zero cell covers the selected simplified calendar. It does not establish a complete emergency reserve or a probability that an institution will process an instruction by that date. Review the access plan when circumstances change Identify the essential bills and their actual payment dates. Confirm who is authorized to give instructions for each intended resource. Ask the institution what documents and procedures apply to that role. Test a delay without assuming that another account or credit facility is available. Keep a current, private record that an authorized person can locate. A joint account and an authority to act for another person have different ownership and responsibility implications. The government’s overview discusses both. Use the arrangement that has been properly established for the circumstances; this calculator neither selects an arrangement nor grants access. This is a living-household cash exercise. Death, estate administration, beneficiary payments and estate authority require a separate plan. The estate-liquidity article covers the related timing question without treating the two situations as interchangeable.
f4c4bd2227bf367ef81f020ba579a89aeb2aabba.zh: 一个家庭可能拥有足够的钱，但仍然面临较早的付款缺口。记录访问权限、权限和时间以及分配给基本账单的每笔余额。从必须付款的人开始资产负债表记录所有权和债务。付款计划还需要确定谁可以发出指示、他们可以使用哪个帐户以及何时可以使用资金。在生病、缺席或正常帐户访问中断期间，这些问题可能很重要。加拿大政府的财务授权书概述将管理某人财产的权力与该财产的所有权区分开来。它还解释了文件名称和要求因省份和地区而异。财务模型无法确定文件或拟议指示的有效性。计算器在单独的权限检查后启动。其开放金额是指授权账单付款人已经可以使用的资金。其延迟余额意味着现有的家庭现金可以在独立假定的日期变得可用。该日期是一个压力输入，而不是银行处理标准或法定期限。赋予期初余额和延迟余额不同的角色 该示例在开始时可访问 2,000 加元，并在第 21 天之前有一个单独的 12,000 加元余额等待访问。该家庭在这两个余额中拥有 14,000 加元。在第二笔金额可用之前，只需 2,000 加元即可完成付款。第一个图表显示了这两个余额及其标记的总计。不要将总栏添加到其组件中。释放 12,000 加元，之后更改资金的用途；它不会创造 12,000 加元的收入、礼物或投资收益。实际的访问记录应避免存储登录凭据、密码或验证码。记录机构、账户用途、人员确认的角色以及机构发出授权指令的流程。将敏感的帐户详细信息保存在适合需要这些信息的人员的私人位置。在迟到的钱到达之前找到短缺情况 生活费用为每 30 天 4,500 加元，每天分配 150 加元。在第 21 天开始之前，还剩下 20 个每日金额：20 × CAD 150 = CAD 3,000 。与最初可用的 2,000 加元相比，这就造成了 1,000 加元的资金缺口。额外的 12,000 加元在第 21 天的消费之前到达。在第 30 天和第 60 天消费后，将获得 2,500 加元的净收入。这些较晚的收据改善了帐户余额，但如果没有其他资源，则无法进行较早的付款。该图表保留了当天的付款点，而不是仅显示令人放心的月末金额。通过比较，可以在第一天开始时访问相同的单独余额。两条路径都使用相同的资产、收入和支出。他们的区别在于时机。这两种路径均不假定透支、账单延期或从某些未列出的帐户自动转账。调和结束不丢失访问问题 六十天后，该示例已收到全部 12,000 加元的延迟现金和两笔 2,500 加元的收入付款，并已支付 9,000 加元的生活费用。期末余额为 2,000 加元 + 12,000 加元 + 5,000 加元 - 9,000 加元 = 10,000 加元。这一积极的终点与之前 1,000 加元的短缺同时存在。所有允许的访问日期都发生在六十天内，因此更改日期可以保留端点，同时可能会更改最低余额。瀑布调和总资源；每日线路回答这些资源是否及时到达。该矩阵会改变访问日期和支出。其值显示超出已输入金额的额外期初现金。零单元格覆盖选定的简化日历。它没有建立完整的应急储备或机构在该日期之前处理指令的可能性。当情况发生变化时审查访问计划 确定基本账单及其实际付款日期。确认谁有权为每个预期资源提供说明。询问该机构哪些文件和程序适用于该职位。在不假设其他帐户或信用额度可用的情况下测试延迟。保留授权人员可以找到的最新私人记录。联名账户和代表他人行事的授权具有不同的所有权和责任含义。政府的概述讨论了两者。使用针对具体情况适当制定的安排；该计算器既不选择排列也不授予访问权限。这是一项家庭现金活动。死亡、遗产管理、受益人付款和遗产管理机构需要单独的计划。遗产-流动性文章涵盖了相关的时间安排问题，但没有将这两种情况视为可以互换。

55cf65ac99cf88bf901fb44e0f4e9dc03a91098f.src: Owned cash can pay a bill without creating debt. A borrowing limit helps only if it is usable, and drawing it creates a second cash-flow task: repayment. Put cash and borrowing capacity in separate columns A CAD 10,000 unused credit limit is not CAD 10,000 already saved. It describes potential borrowing capacity under an agreement. Drawing money increases cash and debt together. The unused amount itself is neither a deposit balance nor an addition to household net worth. The FCAC’s line-of-credit guide describes borrowing up to a limit and paying interest on the amount borrowed. Actual access methods, fees, interest and minimum payments depend on the product and agreement. This article uses an independently selected availability percentage. A zero, partial or full amount is a hypothetical stress, rather than a forecast about a lender’s actions or an interpretation of its contractual rights. Confirm actual terms and usable funds separately before relying on borrowing for a payment. Reconcile the immediate expense before looking at repayments The default has CAD 5,000 of uncommitted cash and an unexpected CAD 8,000 bill. Cash pays the first CAD 5,000. With all of the entered unused borrowing capacity assumed usable, a CAD 3,000 draw funds the remainder. No part of the bill is then left without funding. The waterfall begins with the amount needing payment and deducts the cash actually applied and the debt actually drawn. It does not subtract the full unused limit when less money is needed. If only CAD 2,000 of credit were usable, the model would draw CAD 2,000 and report the remaining CAD 1,000 bill as unfunded. An unfunded bill is kept separate from the borrowing balance. The tool does not assume that it can be ignored, paid late or automatically financed elsewhere. Likewise, cash already assigned to rent, tax or another imminent payment should not be entered as uncommitted emergency cash. Give the new debt an affordable repayment source After drawing CAD 3,000, the example pays all monthly interest and an additional CAD 300 of principal at each month-end. Its hypothetical nominal annual rate is 10%, divided by twelve for the monthly calculation. The first interest charge is CAD 25, so the first modeled payment is CAD 325. The next month begins with CAD 2,700 of principal. Interest falls to CAD 22.50 and the modeled payment becomes CAD 322.50. Ten principal repayments clear the CAD 3,000 draw. Their interest charges total CAD 137.50. The chart continues to month 24 with a zero balance after repayment. Those payments require money from outside the starting reserve. They have not been proven affordable by funding the initial bill. At zero principal repayment, paying interest alone leaves the original debt outstanding. The model does not copy a lender’s actual minimum-payment rule. Read a fully funded bill beside the debt it creates The grouped bars change owned cash while keeping the bill and assumed usable borrowing capacity fixed. They show two distinct consequences: new debt drawn and the immediate amount still without funding. Both should be read before deciding that a reserve is adequate. The matrix changes the bill and the accessible share of the selected unused limit. A zero cell means that cash plus an actual draw can cover that particular bill. It does not mean the bill was paid entirely from savings or that later debt payments will fit the budget. A larger existing reserve requires earlier saving effort and may earn a different return from other assets. This calculator does not compare investment opportunities or prescribe a universal reserve size. It isolates how a bill is funded and what borrowing remains afterward. Rebuilding the reserve is a separate instruction In the default, all CAD 5,000 of opening cash has been spent. Repaying the CAD 3,000 debt does not put that CAD 5,000 back into savings.
