A complete recovery plan therefore needs both a feasible debt-payment schedule and a separate saving schedule. Subtract known commitments before counting cash as available. Confirm the amount and date of the unexpected payment. Check actual borrowing terms and access without counting a limit as an asset. Fund all required interest and principal from the ongoing budget. Write a reserve-rebuilding plan and test another interruption. Rates, fees, timing and income can change. This fixed-rate, no-new-draw illustration gives a clear baseline. Review it against actual statements and the household budget before using it for a real borrowing decision.
55cf65ac99cf88bf901fb44e0f4e9dc03a91098f.zh: 拥有的现金可以支付账单而不会产生债务。借款限额只有在可用时才有帮助，提取借款限额会产生第二项现金流任务：还款。将现金和借贷能力分在不同的栏内 未使用的 10,000 加元信用额度并不是已保存的 10,000 加元。它描述了协议下的潜在借贷能力。提取资金会同时增加现金和债务。未使用的金额本身既不是存款余额，也不是家庭净资产的补充。 FCAC 的信用额度指南描述了借款金额不得超过限额并按借款金额支付利息。实际的访问方式、费用、利息和最低付款取决于产品和协议。本文使用独立选择的可用性百分比。零、部分或全额金额是一种假设压力，而不是对贷款机构行为的预测或其合同权利的解释。在依靠借款付款之前，请分别确认实际条款和可用资金。在考虑还款之前核对即时费用 违约者有 5,000 加元未承诺现金和意外的 8,000 加元账单。现金支付首笔 5,000 加元。假设输入的所有未使用借款能力均可用，则提取 3,000 加元即可为剩余资金提供资金。该法案的任何部分都将得到资金支持。瀑布从需要支付的金额开始，扣除实际使用的现金和实际提取的债务。当需要较少的钱时，它不会减去全部未使用的限额。如果只有 2,000 加元的信用可用，该模型将提取 2,000 加元，并将剩余的 1,000 加元账单报告为无资金支持。无资金支持的账单与借款余额分开保存。该工具并不假设它可以被忽略、延迟支付或自动在其他地方融资。同样，已经分配给租金、税款或其他即将付款的现金不应作为未承诺的紧急现金输入。为新债务提供负担得起的还款来源 在提取 3,000 加元后，该示例将支付所有每月利息，并在每个月底额外支付 300 加元的本金。其假设名义年利率为10%，除以十二进行月度计算。第一笔利息费用为 25 加元，因此第一笔模拟付款为 325 加元。下个月开始的本金为 2,700 加元。利息降至 22.50 加元，模拟付款变为 322.50 加元。偿还 10 笔本金后，即可提取 3,000 加元。他们的利息费用总计 137.50 加元。该图表持续到第 24 个月，还款后余额为零。这些付款需要来自起始储备金之外的资金。事实证明，通过资助最初的账单，它们还没有被证明是负担得起的。在零本金偿还的情况下，仅支付利息就使原始债务未偿还。该模型并未复制贷款机构的实际最低还款额规则。在其产生的债务旁边阅读全额资助的账单。分组的金条会改变拥有的现金，同时保持账单和假设的可用借贷能力固定。它们表现出两种不同的后果：新的债务被提取以及仍然没有资金的直接金额。在决定储备是否充足之前，应阅读这两篇文章。该矩阵更改账单和所选未使用限制的可访问份额。零单元格意味着现金加上实际提款可以支付该特定账单。这并不意味着账单完全由储蓄支付，也不意味着以后的债务偿还将符合预算。较大的现有储备需要更早的储蓄努力，并且可能会获得与其他资产不同的回报。该计算器不会比较投资机会或规定通用储备规模。它隔离了账单的融资方式以及之后剩下的借款。重建准备金是一项单独的指令。默认情况下，开仓现金 5,000 加元已全部用完。偿还 3,000 加元的债务并不会将这 5,000 加元重新存入储蓄。因此，一个完整的恢复计划需要一个可行的债务偿还时间表和一个单独的储蓄时间表。在计算可用现金之前减去已知的承诺。确认意外付款的金额和日期。检查实际借款条款和访问权限，而不将限制计为资产。从正在进行的预算中提供所有所需的利息和本金。编写储备重建计划并测试另一次中断。费率、费用、时间和收入可能会发生变化。这个固定费率、无新抽奖的插图给出了清晰的基线。在将其用于真正的借贷决策之前，请根据实际报表和家庭预算对其进行审查。

9e69231ed8f394e3b8a11a83bd535f1f084ba6a5.src: An average asking rent, an existing tenant’s payment and your own quote answer different questions. Use the statistics for context and the actual option for the cash plan. Identify the quarter, unit type and rental population The first chart uses Statistics Canada’s Q2 2026 rent comparison , released on 9 September 2026. It shows two-bedroom apartments in five selected census metropolitan areas. Amounts are monthly current Canadian dollars. Asking rent comes from advertised rental listings. Paid rent describes amounts paid by existing renter households. These are different populations, with potentially different apartment characteristics and inclusions. The experimental estimates are subject to revision. The five locations were selected to show several relationships between the measures. They are not a complete ranking of Canadian rental markets, a sample of equivalent apartments or evidence that a particular household should relocate. A CMA also covers a broader area than a single neighbourhood. A difference between averages is not a tenant’s rent increase For Vancouver, the displayed asking and paid averages are CAD 3,030 and CAD 2,470. Subtracting gives CAD 560. Toronto’s corresponding difference is CAD 490, from CAD 2,650 less CAD 2,160. The relationship is not positive everywhere. Calgary’s asking average of CAD 1,890 is CAD 40 below its paid average of CAD 1,930. Edmonton’s two figures are both CAD 1,570. Regina’s asking average is CAD 100 lower than its paid average. The signed bars make those directions explicit. These subtractions compare groups in the same quarter. They do not follow one tenant from an old apartment into a matched new apartment. They therefore cannot establish what a particular move, renewal or rent increase will cost. Statistics Canada’s release also distinguishes these rent levels from the CPI rent index’s price-change concept. Replace the average with the option you can actually rent The budget tool has its own rent-quote input. It does not choose a city average for you. The default uses CAD 2,400 rent, CAD 150 utilities outside that rent, CAD 40 tenant insurance and CAD 200 transport for the location. Rent, utilities and tenant insurance total CAD 2,590 a month. Adding transport brings the location-related cash requirement to CAD 2,790. Whether the amount is workable then depends on income and every other commitment, rather than on the rent number alone. Check what the quote includes. If heating, parking or another service is already included, do not add the same amount again outside rent. Conversely, a lower advertised rent can come with separate costs. Compare actual inclusions and travel requirements before interpreting an apparent price difference. Keep saving and other living costs in the reconciliation With CAD 5,500 monthly take-home income, CAD 2,790 of location-related costs, CAD 2,000 of other living expenses and a CAD 500 saving allocation, the default leaves CAD 210 unassigned each month. The waterfall makes every subtraction visible. The saving allocation remains a household asset, but it is committed cash in this plan. Omitting it would change the question from whether the option supports the selected goals to whether it covers current consumption alone. A negative residual requires a funding source or a change in commitments. This is a take-home cash budget. It is not a formal landlord, mortgage, benefit or statistical affordability test, and it does not apply a universal percentage threshold. Moving deposits and overlapping rents belong in a separate dated transition plan, rather than being hidden inside a recurring monthly average. Use the income-and-quote matrix to test the margin The matrix replaces net household income and the actual rent quote. Utilities, insurance, transport, other living expenses and saving remain selected. Every cell reports the monthly amount left after those commitments. Negative cells show a shortfall. A small positive amount should also prompt a review of omitted or irregular expenses. The matrix has no probability model, and the official city averages are not used inside it. It is a deterministic check of the amounts entered. Use the statistics to understand their defined market and period. Obtain a real quote and a clear list of inclusions. Build a complete recurring budget from net income. Fund deposits, moving costs and overlap on their actual dates. Recheck the plan when the quote, income or household changes. Keep the original observation date beside any cited statistic. A newly retrieved historical table is still a historical observation, not a current offer available to the household.
9e69231ed8f394e3b8a11a83bd535f1f084ba6a5.zh: 平均租金要价、现有租户的付款和您自己的报价可以回答不同的问题。使用统计数据了解现金计划的背景和实际选项。确定季度、单位类型和出租人口 第一张图表使用加拿大统计局 2026 年 9 月 9 日发布的 2026 年第二季度租金比较。它显示了五个选定的人口普查大都市区的两居室公寓。金额为每月现值加元。询问租金来自广告出租列表。已付租金是指现有租户家庭支付的金额。这些是不同的人群，具有潜在不同的公寓特征和内含物。实验估计可能会被修改。选择这五个地点是为了显示措施之间的几种关系。它们不是加拿大租赁市场的完整排名、同等公寓的样本或特定家庭应该搬迁的证据。 CMA 还覆盖比单个社区更广泛的区域。平均租金之间的差异并非租户的租金上涨 对于温哥华，显示的平均要价和已付租金分别为 3,030 加元和 2,470 加元。减去后得到 560 加元。多伦多相应的差价是 490 加元，从 2,650 加元减去 2,160 加元。这种关系并非到处都是积极的。卡尔加里的平均要价为 1,890 加元，比其平均付费 1,930 加元低 40 加元。埃德蒙顿的两个数字都是1,570加元。里贾纳的平均要价比其平均付费低 100 加元。带符号的条使这些指示变得明确。这些减法比较同一季度的各组。他们不会跟随一个租户从旧公寓搬到配套的新公寓。因此，他们无法确定特定的搬迁、续租或租金上涨的成本。加拿大统计局的发布还将这些租金水平与 CPI 租金指数的价格变化概念区分开来。用您实际可以租赁的选项替换平均值。预算工具有自己的租金报价输入。它不会为您选择城市平均值。默认使用 2,400 加元的租金、150 加元的租金之外的水电费、40 加元的租户保险和 200 加元的交通费。每月租金、水电费和租户保险总计 2,590 加元。添加交通后，与地点相关的现金需求将达到 2,790 加元。这笔金额是否可行取决于收入和其他所有承诺，而不仅仅是租金数额。检查报价包含哪些内容。如果已包含供暖、停车或其他服务，请勿在租金之外再次添加相同金额。相反，较低的广告租金可能会带来单独的费用。在解释明显的价格差异之前，先比较实际包含的内容和旅行要求。在对账中保留储蓄和其他生活成本 由于每月实得收入 5,500 加元、地点相关成本 2,790 加元、其他生活费用 2,000 加元以及 500 加元的储蓄分配，默认情况下每月留下 210 加元未分配。瀑布让每一个减法都可见。储蓄分配仍然是家庭资产，但在该计划中是承诺现金。省略它会将问题从该选项是否支持所选目标转变为是否仅涵盖当前消费。负残差需要资金来源或承诺的改变。这是带回家的现金预算。它不是正式的房东、抵押贷款、福利或统计负担能力测试，也不适用通用的百分比阈值。转移押金和重叠租金属于单独的、注明日期的过渡计划，而不是隐藏在经常性的月平均值中。使用收入和报价矩阵来测试利润 该矩阵取代了家庭净收入和实际租金报价。公用事业、保险、交通、其他生活费用和储蓄仍然被选中。每个单元格都会报告这些承诺后每月剩余的金额。阴性细胞显示不足。少量的正金额也应该促使对遗漏或不正常的费用进行审查。该矩阵没有概率模型，并且内部不使用官方城市平均值。这是对输入金额的确定性检查。使用统计数据来了解其定义的市场和时期。获得真实的报价和清晰的内含物清单。根据净收入制定完整的经常性预算。资金存款、搬家费用和实际日期重叠。当报价、收入或家庭发生变化时，重新检查计划。将原始观察日期保留在任何引用的统计数据旁边。新检索的历史表仍然是历史观察，而不是家庭可用的当前报价。

6449605f70048cdf38209f1ba4d41cd1942d0f42.src: Several holdings can carry the same underlying risk. A useful diversification review follows the assets and economic drivers through every wrapper. A long holdings list can hide a short risk list Imagine a portfolio with a global equity ETF, a US large-company ETF, a technology fund, and direct shares in a familiar platform company. It has four line items, but the same company may appear in all four. Different fund names do not establish independent exposures. FINRA’s concentration-risk overview describes concentration through correlated assets, employer stock, performance drift, and overlapping funds. Use that as a prompt to inspect what you own underneath each wrapper. The purpose of a look-through analysis is to identify the risk being taken deliberately. Concentration is not automatically a mistake, and broad diversification cannot prevent every loss. The useful question is whether one adverse event could damage several holdings and the spending plan at the same time. Use a complete fictional matrix before changing the balances The interactive case starts with CAD 40,000 in Fund A, CAD 30,000 in Fund B, CAD 20,000 in Fund C and CAD 10,000 directly in Company A. Every name is invented. The four balances total CAD 100,000 at one hypothetical valuation instant. The worked amounts in this section describe the restored example; the charts follow your edited balances. The matrix publishes every position in each fund, with no undisclosed remainder. Each column totals 100%. Company A is the same issuer wherever it appears, including the direct holding. Bond issuers D and E are distinct invented issuers. Changing a balance creates an independent snapshot. It does not demonstrate how a purchase was funded or account for tax, fees or a sale elsewhere. The chosen mix is a calculation fixture, not a recommended allocation. Combine Company A without adding extra portfolio wealth Company A contributes CAD 16,000 through Fund A, CAD 9,000 through Fund B and nothing through Fund C. The direct position adds CAD 10,000. The waterfall therefore reconciles CAD 35,000 of Company A, or 35% of the selected CAD 100,000 portfolio. The direct holding alone is 10% of the total. Its label therefore omits another 25 percentage points of the same issuer allocation held through funds. Those fund portions are already inside the portfolio total; they are not another CAD 25,000 of wealth to add on top. The combined issuer shares are A 35%, B 18%, C 19%, bond issuer D 12% and bond issuer E 16%. They total 100%. Doubling every input balance doubles the dollar allocations while preserving these percentages. With no balances entered, percentage allocations are unavailable; an empty portfolio is not evidence of diversification. Keep asset class, geography and account labels in separate views The underlying asset-class split is CAD 72,000 of equities and CAD 28,000 of bonds. Separately, the invented issuer geography tags produce CAD 69,000 classified as US and CAD 31,000 as non-US. Each is a complete alternative partition of the same CAD 100,000. Do not add the 69% US figure to the 72% equity figure. Some of the same dollars appear in both. A mutually exclusive joint view would contain 53% US equity, 19% non-US equity, 16% US bonds and 12% non-US bonds. These tags do not establish trading currency, revenue geography, hedging or independent economic risks. An account name is another layer. The OSC Investor Office explains that a TFSA can hold different types of investment. Its registration label therefore does not supply an asset allocation. Splitting unchanged holdings between account labels does not change their combined underlying composition. No account transfer, tax result or contribution-room calculation is modeled. A separate worked example: Company X In a separate example using different fictional funds, suppose a portfolio holds 50% in Fund P, 30% in Fund Q, and 20% in direct shares of Company X. Fund P has 6% in X and Fund Q has 12%. Assume cash-free, unlevered funds and aligned holdings dates. Look-through issuer weight = direct weight + Σ (fund portfolio weight × issuer weight inside fund) The direct position understates total issuer exposure by 6.6 percentage points. On a 100,000 portfolio, the combined economic allocation is 26,600. Adding the full value of the funds to this look-through position would double-count the wrappers; each portfolio dollar should be allocated only once at the selected analysis level. Translate exposure into a conditional loss If Company X falls 40% while every other underlying holding is unchanged, the first-order portfolio effect is 26.6% × −40% = −10.64%. For the 100,000 example, that is a loss of 10,640. This isolates issuer exposure and assumes no rebalancing, derivatives, distributions, or spillovers. A more demanding scenario allows other companies with shared customers, financing needs, or valuation sensitivities to fall too. Assign shocks to mutually exclusive groups of underlying assets. Do not apply a sector loss and then add the same issuer loss again if that issuer was already included in the sector. Scenarios reveal sensitivity; they do not supply probabilities. A precise-looking loss estimate remains conditional on the shocks selected. Record the assumptions and test several narratives rather than presenting one stress as the expected outcome. Map common drivers beyond the largest stock Issuer weights are only one view. Add separate maps for sector, geography, currency, credit quality, interest-rate exposure, and liquidity. These maps answer different questions, so their totals should not be added together into one exposure percentage. For example, holdings in several industries might all depend on inexpensive refinancing. A rise in borrowing costs can affect their earnings or valuations together. Equally, a domestic listing does not prove that revenue and costs are domestic. Label listing-based classifications separately from economic estimates. Employer shares deserve a household view: employment income, future bonuses, and invested wealth may all depend on the same company. A real-estate-heavy household may also carry local economic exposure outside its brokerage account. These observations broaden the analysis without pretending that every household asset has a continuously observable market price. Preserve the limits of the holdings data Use a dated holdings file for each fund and record whether it is complete. A top-ten list can establish some overlap but cannot establish the absence of other overlap. A fund-of-funds structure requires another look-through layer; align identifiers and avoid counting the intermediate wrapper as an additional asset. For derivatives, short positions, or leveraged products, simple market-value weights may be misleading. Exposure may require notional, delta, or another measure suited to the contract. Keep those measures labelled and separate from ordinary unlevered cash-equity weights. If one fund reports month-end holdings and another is daily, disclose the mismatch. Missing coverage should remain “unknown.” Filling it with an assumed zero can make a portfolio appear more diversified precisely where the evidence is weakest. Turn a snapshot into a repeatable policy Define the portfolio and household assets included in the review. Record dated values and look through funds using the best available holdings. Calculate issuer and sector exposures, retaining unknown coverage. Stress common drivers and compare losses with the capacity to meet planned spending. Set review dates and explicit triggers for reassessing concentration. A trigger can lead to a review rather than an automatic sale. Taxes, transaction costs, liquidity, restrictions, and the purpose of the investment all affect the implementation. New contributions or staged changes may alter the exposure differently from a single trade. The finished review should state the largest known exposures, the missing data, the tested scenarios, and the reason for any concentration retained. That record makes a later decision easier to evaluate when prices and portfolio weights change.
6449605f70048cdf38209f1ba4d41cd1942d0f42.zh: 多种持股可能会带来相同的潜在风险。有用的多元化审查通过每个包装来跟踪资产和经济驱动因素。长的持股清单可以隐藏短的风险清单想象一下，一个包含全球股票ETF、美国大公司ETF、科技基金以及熟悉的平台公司的直接股票的投资组合。它有四个行项目，但同一家公司可能会出现在所有四个行项目中。不同的基金名称不建立独立的风险敞口。 FINRA 的集中度风险概述通过相关资产、雇主股票、业绩偏差和重叠基金来描述集中度。使用它作为提示来检查每个包装下面拥有的内容。透视分析的目的是识别故意承担的风险。集中化并不是必然的错误，广泛的多元化也不能避免每一次损失。有用的问题是，一项不利事件是否会同时损害多项资产和支出计划。更改余额之前使用完整的虚构矩阵 交互式案例从 A 基金 40,000 加元、B 基金 30,000 加元、C 基金 20,000 加元以及 A 公司直接 10,000 加元开始。每个名字都是虚构的。在一个假设估值时刻，四笔余额总计为 100,000 加元。本节中的工作量描述了恢复的示例；图表遵循您编辑的余额。该矩阵公布了每个基金的每个仓位，没有未披露的剩余部分。每列总计 100%。 A公司无论在哪里出现，都是同一发行人，包括直接控股。债券发行人 D 和 E 是不同的发明发行人。更改余额会创建独立快照。它没有说明购买资金是如何提供的，也没有说明税收、费用或在其他地方的销售情况。所选择的组合是计算固定装置，而不是推荐的分配。合并公司 A，而不增加额外的投资组合财富 公司 A 通过基金 A 出资 16,000 加元，通过基金 B 出资 9,000 加元，不通过基金 C 出资。直接头寸增加 10,000 加元。因此，瀑布调节了 A 公司的 35,000 加元，即所选 100,000 加元投资组合的 35%。仅直接持有就占总数的10%。因此，其标签省略了通过基金持有的同一发行人分配的另外 25 个百分点。这些基金部分已经包含在投资组合总额内；他们并不是另外 25,000 加元的财富。发行人合并后的股份为A 35%、B 18%、C 19%、债券发行人D 12%、债券发行人E 16%。他们合计100%。将每个投入余额加倍会使美元分配加倍，同时保留这些百分比。如果没有输入余额，则无法进行百分比分配；空的投资组合并不是多元化的证据。将资产类别、地理位置和账户标签保留在单独的视图中 基础资产类别划分为 72,000 加元的股票和 28,000 加元的债券。另外，所发明的发行者地理标签产生分类为美国的 69,000 加元和分类为非美国的 31,000 加元。每个都是同样10万加元的完整替代分区。不要将 69% 的美国数据添加到 72% 的股权数据中。两者中都出现了一些相同的美元。相互排斥的联合视图将包含 53% 的美国股权、19% 的非美国股权、16% 的美国债券和 12% 的非美国债券。这些标签不建立交易货币、收入地理、对冲或独立经济风险。帐户名是另一层。 OSC 投资者办公室解释说，TFSA 可以持有不同类型的投资。因此，其注册标签不提供资产配置。在账户标签之间分割未改变的持股不会改变它们的组合基础成分。没有对账户转账、税务结果或供款室计算进行建模。一个单独的工作示例：X 公司 在使用不同虚构基金的单独示例中，假设投资组合持有基金 P 的 50%、基金 Q 的 30% 和 X 公司的直接股份 20%。基金 P 持有 X 的 6%，基金 Q 持有 12%。假设无现金、无杠杆资金和一致的持有日期。透视发行人权重 = 直接权重 + Σ（基金投资组合权重 × 基金内部发行人权重） 直接头寸低估了发行人总风险敞口 6.6 个百分点。对于 100,000 的投资组合，综合经济分配为 26,600。将资金的全部价值添加到这个透视头寸中将会重复计算包装器；每个投资组合美元只能在选定的分析级别分配一次。将风险敞口转化为有条件损失 如果 X 公司股价下跌 40%，而其他所有基础持股均保持不变，则一阶投资组合效应为 26.6% × −40% = −10.64%。以 100,000 为例，即损失 10,640。这隔离了发行人的风险，并假设没有再平衡、衍生品、分配或溢出。如果情况更加严峻，其他具有共同客户、融资需求或估值敏感性的公司也会下跌。将冲击分配给相互排斥的基础资产组。如果发行人已包含在该部门中，请勿应用部门损失，然后再次添加相同的发行人损失。情景揭示敏感性；他们不提供概率。精确的损失估计仍然取决于所选的冲击。记录假设并测试几种叙述，而不是将一种压力呈现为预期结果。绘制最大股票发行人权重之外的常见驱动因素只是一种观点。添加针对部门、地理位置、货币、信用质量、利率风险和流动性的单独地图。这些地图回答不同的问题，因此不应将它们的总数加在一起形成一个曝光百分比。例如，多个行业的持股可能都依赖于廉价的再融资。借贷成本的上升可能会共同影响他们的收益或估值。同样，在国内上市并不能证明收入和成本都在国内。将基于列表的分类与经济估计分开标记。雇主股票值得家庭看待：就业收入、未来奖金和投资财富可能都取决于同一家公司。房地产密集型家庭还可能在其经纪账户之外承担当地经济风险。这些观察扩大了分析范围，但没有假装每项家庭资产都有一个持续可观察的市场价格。保留持有数据的限制 对每只基金使用注明日期的持有文件并记录其是否完整。前十名列表可以确定一些重叠，但不能确定不存在其他重叠。基金的基金结构需要另一个透视层；对齐标识符并避免将中间包装器视为额外资产。对于衍生品、空头头寸或杠杆产品，简单的市值权重可能会产生误导。风险敞口可能需要名义、德尔塔或其他适合合约的衡量标准。将这些指标贴上标签，并与普通的无杠杆现金权益权重分开。如果一只基金报告月末持有量，而另一只基金报告每日持有量，请披露不匹配情况。缺失的覆盖范围应该保持“未知”。用假设的零填充它可以使投资组合在证据最弱的地方显得更加多元化。将快照转变为可重复的政策 定义审查中包含的投资组合和家庭资产。记录过时的价值并使用最佳的可用资产来浏览基金。计算发行人和行业的风险敞口，保留未知的覆盖范围。强调共同驱动因素，并将损失与满足计划支出的能力进行比较。设置审查日期和明确的触发器来重新评估集中度。触发器可以导致审核而不是自动销售。税收、交易成本、流动性、限制和投资目的都会影响实施。新的贡献或分阶段的变化可能会改变与单一交易不同的风险敞口。完成的审查应说明最大的已知暴露、缺失的数据、测试的场景以及保留任何浓度的原因。当价格和投资组合权重发生变化时，该记录使得以后的决策更容易评估。

2e07f0c006176f3581c4bc078c4ddbadca79e9cc.src: An average return can produce an attractive average ending balance while leaving a substantial lower tail. The distribution and its assumptions matter as much as the central number. A smooth projection answers a narrower question than a household goal A calculator can turn CAD 50,000 into CAD 132,664.89 after twenty years at a constant 5% annual return. That arithmetic is correct. It does not establish that an investor will receive a smooth 5% each year or have that particular amount when a bill is due. The charts add an explicit distribution around a single starting amount. They assume a 5% mean simple annual return and a 15% standard deviation of annual log returns. Under those assumptions, the model’s mean ending balance is still CAD 132,664.89, but its median is about CAD 105,935.06. The difference comes from the distribution’s shape, rather than different deposits or a hidden fee. This is an original mathematical example. No historical market series is used, the parameters are not estimated for any investment, and the tool does not select securities. The purpose is to show what a probability statement depends on before treating it as evidence that a real goal is adequately funded. Read one vertical slice of the fan at a time The first chart shades two ranges. The outer band connects the 5th and 95th percentiles at each year. The inner band connects the 25th and 75th percentiles. The dark line follows the median. All begin at the same starting capital because no investment uncertainty has accumulated at time zero. At the default twenty-year finish, the 5th percentile is about CAD 35,142.98 and the 95th percentile about CAD 319,330.83. Under the assumed continuous distribution, 5% of final balances lie below the first value and 5% above the second. Neither endpoint is a guaranteed minimum or maximum. A positive mean return does not rule out ending with less than the initial amount. The lines are pointwise summaries, not examples of actual market paths. The investor occupying the median rank in year five need not occupy that rank in year twenty. A central 90% range at each date also does not establish that 90% of entire investment paths remain inside the shaded band for every year. The mean and median are different summaries, not competing forecasts The median splits a continuous probability distribution into two equal parts. The mean is the probability-weighted average of all its values. A right-skewed distribution can contain relatively infrequent large balances that pull the mean above the median. With the default inputs, the mean is about 25.23% above the median. That does not mean the model has discovered a free investment premium. The upper tail is part of the same assumed distribution that also contains disappointing outcomes. Removing that tail from the explanation while retaining its effect on the mean would give a misleading picture. The summary bars place the 5th percentile, median, mean and 95th percentile beside each other. The mean is not another percentile and need not sit halfway between the endpoints. When the volatility assumption is set to zero, uncertainty disappears from this model: all four values collapse to the same deterministic balance. That is a mathematical control, not evidence that any actual product can deliver the selected return without risk. A model probability is conditional on the model you chose The default nominal comparison amount is CAD 100,000. The model places about 46.58% of ending balances below it. This result is conditional on every stated input and distributional assumption; it is not a measured failure frequency for Canadian investors or an assessment of anyone’s personal chance of success. The outcome-range bars divide all possible non-negative ending balances into disjoint intervals. Each range includes its lower boundary and excludes its upper boundary. The final range includes everything at or above its lower boundary. Their unrounded probabilities add to 100%, and the ranges do not discard the far upper tail. Read these as categorical probability bars. The dollar intervals have different widths, so their bar areas should not be interpreted as a continuous histogram density. Changing the goal changes the interval boundaries and the comparison probability; it does not change the underlying wealth distribution. The data tables preserve the range labels and values so that the visible statement can be checked. Know which return the formula treats as the mean Let r be the assumed mean simple annual return and s the standard deviation of annual log gross return, both expressed as fractions. The model sets the mean log gross return to m = ln(1 + r) − s² ÷ 2 . It then assumes independent, identically distributed normal log gross returns in every year. After T years, the log of the wealth multiple has mean Tm and standard deviation s√T. A percentile is starting capital × exp(Tm + s√T × z) , where z is the corresponding standard-normal quantile. Expected ending wealth is starting capital × (1 + r) T . These relations explain why changing dispersion while preserving the expected simple return can change the median without changing the mean. The NIST lognormal-distribution reference describes the underlying distribution, its quantiles and its distinct mean and median. TickerLantern applies those mathematical relationships to an original financial illustration. The volatility input is explicitly a log-return standard deviation; treating it as an interchangeable simple-return standard deviation would define a different model. Use the sensitivity matrix to question the assumptions The matrix changes log-return dispersion and the nominal balance being tested. Expected simple return, starting capital and horizon remain fixed. A different cell is a different conditional calculation, not stronger evidence that a target is safe. At zero dispersion, the result is either 0% or 100%, with equality counted as meeting the comparison amount. Real returns need not be independent or normally distributed in log space. Market regimes, changing volatility, severe tail events, investment costs, taxes and inflation can materially change outcomes. Contributions and withdrawals would also change the wealth distribution and are deliberately absent here. A long horizon does not remove those modeling limitations. FINRA’s discussion of investment-analysis tools illustrates why assumptions, methodology and the hypothetical nature of projected outcomes need clear explanation. It is cited as U.S. educational context, not as an endorsement of this tool or a determination of Canadian requirements. Before using an uncertain return to support an important payment, revisit the cash contribution, the date, the goal’s flexibility and what would happen if the balance were inadequate.
2e07f0c006176f3581c4bc078c4ddbadca79e9cc.zh: 平均回报可以产生有吸引力的平均期末余额，同时留下大幅较低的尾部。分布及其假设与中心数一样重要。平滑的预测回答了比家庭目标更狭窄的问题。计算器可以在 20 年后以 5% 的恒定年回报率将 50,000 加元转换为 132,664.89 加元。这个算术是正确的。它并没有规定投资者每年都会获得 5% 的平稳收益，或者在账单到期时获得该特定金额。这些图表添加了围绕单个起始金额的显式分布。他们假设平均简单年回报率为 5%，年对数回报标准差为 15%。根据这些假设，该模型的平均期末余额仍为 132,664.89 加元，但中位数约为 105,935.06 加元。差异来自于分布的形状，而不是不同的存款或隐藏费用。这是一个原始的数学例子。不使用历史市场序列，不估计任何投资的参数，并且该工具不选择证券。目的是在将概率陈述视为真正目标获得足够资金的证据之前，先展示概率陈述所依赖的内容。一次读取风扇的一个垂直切片 第一个图表阴影了两个范围。外部带连接每年的第 5 个和第 95 个百分位数。内带连接第 25 个百分位数和第 75 个百分位数。暗线沿着中线。所有这些都以相同的起始资本开始，因为在零时间没有积累投资不确定性。在默认的二十年结束时，第 5 个百分位数约为 35,142.98 加元，第 95 个百分位数约为 319,330.83 加元。在假设的连续分布下，最终余额的 5% 低于第一个值，5% 高于第二个值。这两个端点都不是保证的最小值或最大值。正的平均回报并不排除最终金额低于初始金额的可能性。这些线条是逐点总结，而不是实际市场路径的示例。在第五年占据中位排名的投资者不必在第二年占据该排名。每个日期的中心 90% 范围也并不能证明每年整个投资路径的 90% 都保持在阴影范围内。均值和中位数是不同的总结，而不是相互竞争的预测。中位数将连续概率分布分成两个相等的部分。平均值是其所有值的概率加权平均值。右偏分布可能包含相对罕见的大额余额，将平均值拉至中位数以上。使用默认输入时，平均值比中位数高出约 25.23%。这并不意味着该模型已经发现了免费的投资溢价。上尾部是相同假设分布的一部分，也包含令人失望的结果。从解释中删除尾巴，同时保留其对均值的影响，会产生误导性的图像。摘要条将第 5 个百分位数、中位数、平均值和第 95 个百分位数放在一起。平均值不是另一个百分位数，也不需要位于端点之间的中间。当波动性假设设置为零时，不确定性从该模型中消失：所有四个值都崩溃到相同的确定性平衡。这是一种数学控制，并不能证明任何实际产品都可以在没有风险的情况下提供选定的回报。模型概率取决于您选择的模型。默认名义比较金额为 100,000 加元。该模型将约 46.58% 的期末余额置于其下方。该结果取决于每个规定的输入和分布假设；它不是对加拿大投资者的失败频率进行衡量，也不是对任何人个人成功机会的评估。结果范围条将所有可能的非负期末余额划分为不相交的区间。每个范围包括其下限并排除其上限。最终范围包括处于或高于其下限的所有内容。它们的未舍入概率加起来为 100%，并且范围不会丢弃最上端的尾部。将它们视为分类概率条。美元区间具有不同的宽度，因此它们的条形区域不应被解释为连续的直方图密度。改变目标会改变区间边界和比较概率；它不会改变潜在的财富分配。数据表保留范围标签和值，以便可以检查可见的语句。了解公式将哪个回报视为平均值 令 r 为假设的平均简单年回报，s 为年对数总回报的标准差，两者均以分数表示。该模型将平均对数总回报设置为 m = ln(1 + r) − s² ÷ 2 。然后假设每年的独立、同分布的正态对数总回报。 T年后，财富倍数的对数为平均值Tm和标准差s√T。百分位数是起始资本 × exp(Tm + s√T × z) ，其中 z 是相应的标准正态分位数。预期期末财富为起始资本 × (1 + r) T 。这些关系解释了为什么在保持预期简单回报的同时改变离差可以改变中位数而不改变均值。 NIST 对数正态分布参考描述了基本分布、其分位数及其独特的平均值和中位数。 TickerLantern 将这些数学关系应用到原始的财务插图中。波动率输入明确是对数返回标准差；将其视为可互换的简单返回标准差将定义不同的模型。使用敏感性矩阵质疑假设 该矩阵会改变对数返回离散度和正在测试的名义平衡。预期简单回报、启动资金和期限保持固定。不同的单元格是不同的条件计算，而不是表明目标安全的更有力的证据。零色散时，结果为 0% 或 100%，相等则视为满足比较量。实际回报不必是独立的或在对数空间中呈正态分布。市场体制、不断变化的波动性、严重的尾部事件、投资成本、税收和通货膨胀都可以极大地改变结果。缴款和提款也会改变财富分配，这里故意不予考虑。长远的眼光并不能消除这些建模限制。 FINRA 对投资分析工具的讨论说明了为什么假设、方法和预测结果的假设性质需要明确的解释。它被引用为美国的教育背景，而不是对该工具的认可或对加拿大要求的确定。在使用不确定的回报来支持重要付款之前，请重新审视现金捐助、日期、目标的灵活性以及如果余额不足会发生什么。

84f063d8bc876e62f828d27fb08cb1ed36f572a6.src: The post-statement grace period and the entire interval from purchase to payment are different lengths. Use the actual statement due date and keep its full-payment cash assigned. Keep posting, statement closing and payment due dates separate A credit-card transaction has more than one relevant date. The purchase may be made on one day and posted to the account on another. The statement then closes on its own schedule, and the payment is due on the date shown for that statement. Treating those dates as interchangeable can lead to a cash plan built around the wrong deadline. The Financial Consumer Agency of Canada explains that the grace period begins at the end of the billing period. Federally regulated financial institutions must provide at least twenty-one days. Avoiding purchase interest also depends on paying the applicable balance in full as required. This article assumes one eligible purchase, no prior balance and no other transactions. Cash advances, cash-like transactions and balance transfers are outside the illustration; FCAC explains that their treatment differs from purchases qualifying for the interest-free grace period. Use a numbered cycle to see why the whole interval varies The model invents a thirty-day billing cycle. Its statement closes on day 30, and the selected post-statement gap is twenty-one days. The resulting hypothetical due date is day 51. These are numbered teaching days, not the dates on a real account. The default purchase posts on day 5. It therefore has twenty-five days before the cycle closes and another twenty-one days after closing, for forty-six days from posting to the common due date . Calling all forty-six days the post-statement grace period would combine two different intervals. The dashed line in the first chart isolates the selected twenty-one-day gap; the other line includes time before statement closing. Each point represents a separate posting-day scenario within the same invented cycle. The due date does not reset by another twenty-one days whenever a purchase posts. Actual posting, billing and payment dates must come from the account record rather than this simplified thirty-day template. Match the full statement target with cash available by the due day The only purchase is CAD 1,500, which is also the full statement-payment target. CAD 1,000 is already assigned when the purchase posts. The household then allocates another CAD 10 on each following day through the due day, before the assumed payment. Forty-six allocations add CAD 460, bringing available assigned cash to CAD 1,460. The full-payment target therefore exceeds the available cash by CAD 40. The model identifies this funding gap without assuming that the bank supplies the missing amount. With the same CAD 1,000 opening reserve and forty-six-day interval, the required daily allocation is CAD 500 divided by forty-six. Rounding up to the nearest cent gives CAD 10.87 a day. Those allocations produce CAD 500.02, enough for the target under the stated timing convention. The daily allocation is a budget assumption, not a recommended saving amount. It needs a supported household source. The tool earns no interest on assigned cash and assumes each allocation is actually available before the planned payment. Change the posting day while keeping the statement due date fixed Move the hypothetical posting to day 30. Only the selected twenty-one days remain before day 51. With the same opening reserve and CAD 10 daily allocation, the available cash becomes CAD 1,210, leaving a CAD 290 shortfall. Move posting to day 1 instead. Fifty days of allocations provide CAD 500, taking assigned cash to CAD 1,500 and covering the full target. The purchase price has not changed; only the time available under this invented saving convention has changed. This comparison does not recommend buying earlier to obtain more time. A purchase still needs to fit the financial plan, and moving a posting date is not necessarily within the cardholder’s control. The arithmetic shows why a single advertised grace-period length cannot tell you every transaction’s full purchase-to-payment interval. For an actual plan, do not assume that a transaction near statement closing will fall into a preferred cycle. Confirm which statement includes it and which due date applies before treating extra time as available. Cash remaining in a bank account can already be committed Using a card delays a cash outflow, but it also creates an obligation. Money still visible in a bank account is not automatically available for another goal when it has been assigned to the card bill. The reserve chart compares those assigned resources with the full statement target. The waterfall subtracts the target from opening assigned cash plus new allocations. A negative endpoint is a provisional shortfall, rather than a payment that has successfully occurred or an authorized account overdraft. The model does not execute a payment or calculate the issuer’s interest if the target is missed. Minimum-payment requirements and eligibility for interest-free purchase treatment are separate questions. The calculator deliberately supplies no minimum-payment amount and does not treat an affordable partial payment as satisfying the full-payment target. The matrix varies opening assigned cash and daily allocations while retaining the selected purchase and dates. A zero cell means those resources fund this one hypothetical bill. It does not establish that other household obligations have also been covered. Replace the template with the statement and payment-processing facts For a real account, identify the applicable statement balance, closing date and due date. Confirm how the issuer treats existing balances and transaction types, and inspect the agreement when interest-free eligibility is uncertain. The example’s clean starting account cannot resolve those questions for another account. Allow for the chosen payment method and the time required for the issuer to receive or credit it. The model places the final allocation before the due-day payment by assumption. It does not account for processing cutoffs, non-business days, failed transfers or delays. Reconcile actual payment confirmation separately from internal cash earmarking. A reserve can make a bill affordable without sending anything to the issuer. These charts connect the timing and funding questions, while leaving the real account’s dates, conditions and completed payment to be verified from its records.
84f063d8bc876e62f828d27fb08cb1ed36f572a6.zh: 结单后宽限期和从购买到付款的整个间隔时间长短不同。使用实际的报表到期日并保留其全额付款现金。将过帐日期、对账单关闭日期和付款到期日期分开 一笔信用卡交易有多个相关日期。购买可能在某一天进行，并在另一天过帐到帐户。然后，该对帐单将按其自己的时间表关闭，付款到期日为该对帐单显示的日期。将这些日期视为可互换的可能会导致围绕错误的最后期限制定现金计划。加拿大金融消费者机构解释说，宽限期从计费期结束时开始。联邦监管的金融机构必须提供至少二十一天的时间。避免购买利息还取决于按要求全额支付适用余额。本文假设有一次符合条件的购买，没有先前余额且没有其他交易。现金预支、类现金交易和余额转移不在说明范围内； FCAC 解释说，他们的待遇与符合免息宽限期资格的购买不同。使用编号周期来了解整个间隔变化的原因 该模型发明了 30 天的计费周期。其报表在第 30 天结束，选定的报表后间隙为 21 天。由此产生的假设到期日是第 51 天。这些是编号的教学日，而不是真实账户上的日期。默认采购在第 5 天过帐。因此，在周期结束前还有 25 天，结束后还有 21 天，从过帐到共同到期日有 46 天。将所有四十六天称为声明后宽限期将结合两个不同的间隔。第一个图表中的虚线隔离了选定的二十一天缺口；另一行包括报表结束之前的时间。每个点代表同一发明周期内的一个单独的发布日场景。每当发布购买时，到期日不会再重置二十一天。实际过帐、计费和付款日期必须来自帐户记录，而不是这个简化的三十天模板。将完整报表目标与到期日可用现金相匹配唯一的购买金额为 1,500 加元，这也是完整报表付款目标。采购过帐时已分配 CAD 1,000。然后，该家庭会在接下来的每一天（直至到期日）在假定付款之前再分配 10 加元。 46 项分配增加了 460 加元，使可用分配现金达到 1,460 加元。因此，全额付款目标超出可用现金 40 加元。该模型在不假设银行补足缺失金额的情况下识别了这一资金缺口。在同样的 1,000 加元开仓准备金和四十六天间隔的情况下，每日所需分配额为 500 加元除以四十六。四舍五入到最接近的美分后，每天为 10.87 加元。这些分配产生 500.02 加元，足以实现规定的时间约定下的目标。每日分配是预算假设，而不是建议的储蓄金额。它需要有支持的家庭资源。该工具不会从分配的现金中赚取利息，并假设每次分配在计划付款之前实际上可用。更改过帐日期，同时保持对帐单到期日固定。将假设的过帐移至第 30 天。第 51 天之前仅保留选定的 21 天。在相同的期初准备金和每日 10 加元分配的情况下，可用现金变为 1,210 加元，缺口为 290 加元。将发布移至第一天。五十天的拨款提供 500 加元，将分配的现金达到 1,500 加元并实现全部目标。购买价格没有变化；只是本发明的储蓄约定下的可用时间发生了变化。这个比较不建议提前购买以获得更多时间。购买仍然需要符合财务计划，并且移动过帐日期不一定在持卡人的控制范围内。该算术说明了为什么单个广告宽限期长度无法告诉您每笔交易的完整购买到付款间隔。对于实际计划，不要假设接近报表关闭的交易将落入首选周期。在将加时视为可用之前，请先确认哪个报表包含此内容以及适用哪个截止日期。银行账户中剩余的现金已经可以使用，使用银行卡会延迟现金流出，但也会产生义务。当银行账户中仍然可见的资金被分配到卡账单后，不会自动用于其他目标。储备图表将分配的资源与完整报表目标进行比较。瀑布从期初分配的现金加上新的分配中减去目标。负端点是临时短缺，而不是已成功发生的付款或授权帐户透支。如果未达到目标，该模型不会执行付款或计算发行人的利息。最低付款要求和免息购买待遇的资格是不同的问题。计算器故意不提供最低付款金额，并且不会将负担得起的部分付款视为满足全额付款目标。该矩阵会改变期初分配的现金和每日分配，同时保留选定的购买和日期。零细胞意味着这些资源为这一假设的账单提供资金。它没有规定其他家庭义务也被涵盖在内。将模板替换为对账单和付款处理事实 对于真实账户，请确定适用的对账单余额、截止日期和到期日。确认发行人如何处理现有余额和交易类型，并在免息资格不确定时检查协议。该示例的干净起始帐户无法解决其他帐户的这些问题。考虑到所选的付款方式以及发行人接收或贷记付款所需的时间。该模型根据假设将最终分配放在到期日付款之前。它不考虑处理截止、非工作日、传输失败或延迟。将实际付款确认与内部现金指定分开进行核对。储备金可以使账单变得负担得起，而无需向发行人发送任何内容。这些图表将时间和资金问题联系起来，同时让真实账户的日期、条件和已完成的付款从其记录中进行验证。

f5af145b95e69b3c86237080aec1c66c9df54145.src: Read the planned percentage beside the portfolio amount. A lower equity share can reduce a snapshot’s percentage loss while a larger account produces a greater dollar loss. An allocation path describes a mix, not an income guarantee A target-date strategy can change its investment mix as a goal approaches. The SEC’s March 2025 target-date-fund bulletin explains glide paths and notes that funds with the same target date can differ. Its discussion concerns U.S.-registered mutual funds and ETFs; it is general context here, not a description of a Canadian plan or a particular product. The charts use an independently authored allocation path. No actual fund, expected return or recommended equity weight is selected. The purpose is to separate a percentage allocation from the dollars to which that percentage applies. That distinction matters when saving continues. An account can become more conservatively allocated by one percentage measure while its equity amount remains larger than it was earlier. Neither the mix nor the amount alone tells us whether a retirement income plan is adequate. Specify the endpoint, contributions and reset convention The default begins with CAD 100,000 and adds CAD 20,000 at each year-end for thirty years. All assets earn zero return before the separate shock exercise. The total therefore reaches CAD 700,000 entirely through new saving, without any assumption about market performance. The planned equity share falls in a straight line from 80% at the start to 35% at the target. The other-asset share is the remainder. At year fifteen, halfway through this authored path, the planned equity share is 57.5%. Each year-end portfolio is reset to that mix after the contribution, without tax or transaction costs. This is a simplifying allocation convention, not a simulation of actual trades or a promise that new deposits alone can achieve every target weight. The related rebalancing guide addresses the constraints of changing a mix using contributions without sales. Multiply the percentage by the portfolio it describes At the start, 80% of CAD 100,000 is CAD 80,000 in equities. At the target, 35% of CAD 700,000 is CAD 245,000. The percentage has fallen by 45 percentage points, yet the equity amount is a little over three times its starting level. The path also shows why endpoints are not the whole story. In this default, the largest whole-year equity amount occurs at year twenty-four. The portfolio then contains CAD 580,000, and its planned equity share is 44%, giving CAD 255,200 in equities. Equity dollars subsequently fall to CAD 245,000 by the target as the allocation reduction outweighs the additional saving. This peak follows from the chosen contribution and allocation formulas. It is not a forecast that a real account will peak at that time or that a fund follows this straight-line schedule. A smaller percentage loss can accompany a larger dollar loss Apply a hypothetical 30% decline to equity values while leaving other assets unchanged. At the starting snapshot, the modeled change is negative CAD 24,000: 30% of CAD 80,000. That equals 24% of the initial total portfolio. At the target snapshot, the modeled change is negative CAD 73,500: 30% of CAD 245,000. It equals 10.5% of the larger portfolio. The portfolio-level percentage effect is smaller, but the dollar effect is greater. The peak-equity snapshot produces a CAD 76,560 decline under the same isolated assumption. These are independent snapshot comparisons. The model does not apply all three losses in succession or reduce the contribution path by them. Other assets staying unchanged is an explicit stress assumption, not a claim that bonds, cash substitutes or other holdings cannot lose value. Keep the exposure question separate from the funding question The matrix varies the target equity share and annual saving while retaining the selected capital, horizon and equity-decline assumption. Every cell shows the magnitude of the hypothetical target-snapshot loss in Canadian dollars. Saving more can increase that dollar amount because more capital is present. This does not make saving less a stronger plan. A smaller portfolio may show a smaller modeled loss while providing fewer resources for the goal. Likewise, reducing the equity share changes exposure but does not itself determine an achievable return or sufficient retirement income. The starting equity share changes the interim path and its possible peak. It does not change the endpoint matrix, which uses the selected ending share and contribution-only ending balance. Read the percentage, balance and cash-flow purpose together rather than interpreting a single smaller cell as an improvement. Review the actual path and the money that will be needed For a real plan, identify the expected use dates, planned contributions, accessible reserves and other income sources. A dollar loss can have different consequences depending on whether withdrawals begin next month or the goal has flexibility. This contribution-only example calculates neither withdrawal capacity nor recovery time. Read a fund’s actual allocation policy, fees and full glide path. Some paths continue changing after the named date; this model stops at its selected target. The SEC bulletin also states that target-date mutual funds and ETFs do not guarantee sufficient retirement income. A calendar label cannot replace a review of the whole plan. The charts exclude investment growth, inflation, withdrawals, fees, tax and trading restrictions. Their value is a transparent check of the relationship among saving, percentages and dollars. Use them to frame an exposure question before making a goal-specific decision, without treating an authored path or shock as a forecast or a suitable allocation.
f5af145b95e69b3c86237080aec1c66c9df54145.zh: 阅读投资组合金额旁边的计划百分比。较低的股本份额可以减少快照的百分比损失，而较大的账户会产生更大的美元损失。分配路径描述的是组合，而不是收入保证 目标日期策略可以随着目标的临近而改变其投资组合。美国证券交易委员会 2025 年 3 月目标日期基金公告解释了下滑路径，并指出具有相同目标日期的基金可能会有所不同。其讨论涉及在美国注册的共同基金和 ETF；这里是一般上下文，而不是对加拿大计划或特定产品的描述。这些图表使用独立创作的分配路径。未选择实际基金、预期收益或推荐股权权重。目的是将百分比分配与该百分比适用的美元分开。当储蓄继续存在时，这种区别很重要。一个账户的分配可以更加保守，增加一个百分比，而其净值金额仍然比以前大。无论是组合还是金额本身都不能告诉我们退休收入计划是否足够。指定端点、贡献和重置约定 默认从 100,000 加元开始，并在三十年内每年年底添加 20,000 加元。在单独的冲击行动之前，所有资产的回报为零。因此，在不考虑市场表现的情况下，通过新的储蓄，总额达到 700,000 加元。计划股权比例从开始时的80%直线下降至目标的35%。其他资产份额为剩余部分。到第 15 年，也就是本文所写路径的一半时，计划的股权份额为 57.5%。每个年终投资组合在缴款后都会重置为该组合，无需缴税或交易成本。这是一个简化的分配惯例，而不是对实际交易的模拟，也不是仅靠新存款就可以实现每个目标权重的承诺。相关的重新平衡指南解决了使用贡献而不销售来改变组合的限制。将百分比乘以它所描述的投资组合 一开始，100,000 加元的 80% 是 80,000 加元的股票。按照目标，700,000 加元的 35% 为 245,000 加元。这一比例下降了 45 个百分点，但股本金额却是初始水平的三倍多一点。该路径还说明了为什么端点并不是故事的全部。在本次违约中，最大的全年股本金额出现在第二十四年。该投资组合包含 580,000 加元，其计划股权份额为 44%，即 255,200 加元的股票。由于分配减少超过了额外节省，权益美元随后按目标跌至 245,000 加元。这个峰值是根据所选择的贡献和分配公式得出的。这并不是预测真实账户将在那时达到顶峰，也不是基金遵循这条直线时间表。较小的百分比损失可能会伴随较大的美元损失。假设股票价值下跌 30%，同时保持其他资产不变。在起始快照中，建模变化为负 24,000 加元：80,000 加元的 30%。这相当于初始投资组合总额的 24%。在目标快照中，建模变化为负 73,500 加元：245,000 加元的 30%。它相当于较大投资组合的 10.5%。投资组合层面的百分比效应较小，但美元效应较大。在同样的孤立假设下，峰值股本快照会下跌 76,560 加元。这些是独立的快照比较。该模型不会连续应用所有三种损失或减少它们的贡献路径。其他资产保持不变是一种明确的压力假设，而不是声称债券、现金替代品或其他持有的资产不会损失价值。将风险暴露问题与融资问题分开。矩阵会改变目标股权份额和年度节省，同时保留选定的资本、期限和股权下降假设。每个单元格都显示假设的目标快照损失的大小（以加元为单位）。储蓄更多可以增加美元金额，因为存在更多资本。这并不意味着减少储蓄成为一个更强有力的计划。较小的投资组合可能会显示较小的模型损失，同时为目标提供的资源较少。同样，减少股权份额会改变风险敞口，但其本身并不决定可实现的回报或足够的退休收入。起始股权份额改变了临时路径及其可能的峰值。它不会更改端点矩阵，该矩阵使用选定的期末份额和仅贡献期末余额。将百分比、余额和现金流目的放在一起解读，而不是将单个较小的单元解释为改进。检查实际路径和所需资金对于真正的计划，确定预期使用日期、计划捐款、可用储备和其他收入来源。美元损失可能会产生不同的后果，具体取决于提款是下个月开始还是目标具有灵活性。这个仅贡献的示例既不计算提款能力，也不计算恢复时间。阅读基金的实际分配政策、费用和完整的下滑路径。有些路径在指定日期之后继续变化；该模型停在其选定的目标处。 SEC 公告还指出，目标日期共同基金和 ETF 不能保证足够的退休收入。日历标签不能代替对整个计划的回顾。这些图表不包括投资增长、通货膨胀、提款、费用、税收和交易限制。它们的价值是对储蓄、百分比和美元之间关系的透明检查。在做出针对特定目标的决策之前，使用它们来构建暴露问题，而不将编写的路径或冲击视为预测或适当的分配。

9d2f431bbddc3705e2be35c95457513a191b46c5.src: The sticker price, price per kilogram and cash paid at checkout measure different things. Compare the same quantity, then carry leftover stock into the next purchase. Put both packages on the same measurement basis A package can keep the same shelf price while containing less product. The total price alone would show no increase, but the price of the quantity you actually use has changed. For a household budget, that difference matters when you keep buying the same amount of the product over time. The Office of Consumer Affairs’ unit-pricing guide explains how a standard weight, volume or item measure helps compare similar products. It also describes shrinkflation as a reduction in quantity without a matching reduction in the retail price. This tool uses invented package examples rather than naming a brand or quoting a current offer. Compare contents that serve the same purpose and use the same unit. A kilogram of one product is not automatically equivalent to a kilogram of another if concentration, quality or usable yield differs. The model assumes comparable usable contents so it can isolate the quantity and cash arithmetic. A percentage weight reduction and a percentage unit-price increase differ The default reference package costs CAD 6 for 750 grams. Its unit price is CAD 8 per kilogram. The comparison package costs the same CAD 6 for 650 grams, or about CAD 9.23 per kilogram. The package contains 100 grams less, a reduction of about 13.33% from the original 750 grams. The unit price rises by about 15.38%, calculated as (6 ÷ 650) ÷ (6 ÷ 750) − 1 . The two percentages differ because their denominators differ. The bar chart uses price per kilogram for both packages. Change the comparison price independently of its size to see whether a lower sticker price compensates for the smaller contents. The tool can show a saving as well as an increase; its labels do not assume the comparison package is always more expensive. Budget for the whole packages you can actually buy The default household consumes 6,000 grams each month and starts with no stock. In month 1, eight reference packages supply exactly that amount and cost CAD 48. The comparison needs ten whole packages, costing CAD 60 and supplying 6,500 grams. Only 6,000 of those grams are consumed in the month. The remaining 500 grams are carried forward. In month 2, that stock reduces the quantity that must be bought, so the model does not round the full 6,000 grams upward again as though the cupboard were empty. Buying fractional packages would produce a smooth consumption-cost estimate, but it would not describe the checkout payment. Conversely, rounding every month independently and discarding the leftover stock would overstate future purchases under this model’s no-waste assumption. Keep unused stock separate from money available to spend Across twelve default months, the reference alternative buys 96 packages for CAD 576. The comparison buys 111 packages for CAD 666 and ends with 150 grams unused. The cumulative checkout difference is CAD 90. At the comparison unit cost, the 72,000 grams consumed have a purchase cost of about CAD 664.62. The remaining stock has an allocated purchase cost of about CAD 1.38. Together they reconcile the CAD 666 already paid. The stock allocation is not another charge and is not money that remains in the bank. The stacked bars make that distinction visible for both alternatives. Their totals compare actual modeled checkout cash, while the segments explain how much of the purchased quantity was consumed or still held. Different ending inventories mean the cash difference is not exactly the same as the cost difference for equal quantities consumed. Test package size and price without assuming a bulk bargain The matrix replaces the comparison package size and price while holding monthly use, the reference package and the selected horizon constant. Every cell applies the same whole-package rule and carries stock forward. A larger package need not have a lower unit price, and even a low unit price can require a larger payment on the first shopping trip. Read a positive cell as more total checkout cash than the reference and a negative cell as less. These are selected price-and-size scenarios, not observed supermarket prices or forecasts. They also assume that every gram remains usable. For a real comparison, separately consider storage space, spoilage, the risk of buying more than the household will use and any extra shopping or delivery cost. This model holds those items at zero; it does not turn a favourable unit price into a recommendation to buy more. Connect the unit calculation to the recurring cash budget Record the price, net quantity and common unit when comparing two offers. Estimate the quantity the household actually uses, then check how many whole packs are required for the next purchase after counting usable stock already at home. The cash chart follows cumulative payments, so it can reveal a larger early shopping payment even when the long-run unit cost looks attractive. It does not calculate a bank balance or assume that borrowing fills a shortfall. Fit the payment into the broader food and household budget. Finally, revise the assumptions when the price, package size or usage changes. A unit-price calculation explains the cost of quantity, while a purchase calendar explains how that cost reaches the household’s cash account.
9d2f431bbddc3705e2be35c95457513a191b46c5.zh: 标价、每公斤价格和结账时支付的现金衡量的是不同的东西。比较相同的数量，然后将剩余的库存带入下一次采购。将两个包装置于相同的测量基础上 一个包装可以保持相同的货架价格，同时包含更少的产品。仅总价格不会增加，但您实际使用的数量的价格发生了变化。对于家庭预算来说，当您随着时间的推移继续购买相同数量的产品时，这种差异很重要。消费者事务办公室的单位定价指南解释了标准重量、体积或物品尺寸如何帮助比较类似产品。它还将收缩通货膨胀描述为数量减少而零售价格却没有相应下降。该工具使用发明的包装示例，而不是命名品牌或引用当前报价。比较具有相同目的并使用相同单位的内容。如果浓度、质量或可用产量不同，一公斤一种产品并不自动等同于一公斤另一种产品。该模型假设可用内容具有可比性，因此可以隔离数量和现金算术。重量减少百分比和单价增加百分比不同。默认参考包的价格为 750 克 6 加元。其单价为每公斤8加元。对比包装的价格相同，均为 650 克 6 加元，即每公斤约 9.23 加元。包装内重量减少了100克，比原来的750克减少了约13.33%。单价上涨约15.38%，计算公式为(6 ÷ 650) ÷ (6 ÷ 750) − 1 。这两个百分比不同是因为它们的分母不同。条形图使用两种包装的每公斤价格。独立于其大小更改比较价格，看看较低的标价是否可以补偿较小的内容。该工具可以显示节省和增加；它的标签并不认为比较包总是更贵。您实际可以购买的整个套餐的预算 默认家庭每月消耗 6,000 克，并且开始时没有库存。在第 1 个月，八个参考包正好提供了这个数量，成本为 48 加元。比较需要十个完整包，成本为 60 加元，供应 6,500 克。该月仅消耗了其中 6,000 克。剩余的 500 克结转。在第 2 个月，该库存减少了必须购买的数量，因此该模型不会再次向上舍入全部 6,000 克，就好像橱柜是空的一样。购买部分套餐将产生平滑的消费成本估算，但它不会描述结帐付款。相反，在该模型的无浪费假设下，每月独立舍入并丢弃剩余库存会夸大未来的采购量。将未使用的库存与可用于支出的资金分开。在 12 个默认月份中，参考替代方案以 576 加元的价格购买了 96 包。比较以 666 加元的价格购买了 111 包，最终有 150 克未使用。累计结帐差额为 90 加元。按比较单位成本计算，消耗的 72,000 克的购买成本约为 664.62 加元。剩余库存的分配采购成本约为 1.38 加元。他们一起核对已支付的 666 加元。股票分配不是另一笔费用，也不是留在银行的钱。堆叠的条形使这两种选择都可以看到这种区别。他们的总数比较了实际建模的结账现金，而细分则解释了有多少购买数量被消耗或仍然持有。不同的期末库存意味着现金差异与消耗相同数量的成本差异并不完全相同。测试包装尺寸和价格，无需假设批量讨价还价 该矩阵取代了比较包装尺寸和价格，同时保持每月使用量、参考包装和所选范围不变。每个单元都应用相同的整包规则并结转库存。较大的套餐不一定具有较低的单价，即使单价较低也可能需要在第一次购物时支付较多的费用。将正值单元格视为结帐现金总额比参考值多，将负值单元格视为结帐现金总额比参考值少。这些是选定的价格和尺寸情景，而不是观察到的超市价格或预测。他们还假设每一克仍然可用。为了进行真正的比较，请分别考虑存储空间、损坏、购买超过家庭使用量的风险以及任何额外的购物或送货成本。该模型将这些项目保持为零；它不会将有利的单价转变为购买更多的建议。将单位计算连接到经常性现金预算 比较两个报价时记录价格、净数量和常用单位。估计家庭实际使用的数量，然后在计算家里已有的可用库存后检查下次购买需要多少整包。现金图表遵循累积付款，因此即使长期单位成本看起来很有吸引力，它也可以显示更大的早期购物付款。它不计算银行余额或假设借款填补缺口。将这笔付款纳入更广泛的食品和家庭预算。最后，当价格、包装尺寸或用途发生变化时修改假设。单价计算解释了数量成本，而购买日历则解释了该成本如何到达家庭现金账户。

bf940ee9fea4f364705fe2e5c24e75946f01ad19.src: A larger investment balance funded by a loan is accompanied by debt. Compare net positions using the same household cash commitment, and keep repayment risk separate from an assumed return. Match the household contribution before comparing account balances Borrowing can place a large amount in an investment account immediately. A comparison with a smaller account funded from monthly saving can then look persuasive simply because the opening gross balances are different. The debt and the ongoing cash commitment need to be included before interpreting that comparison. This illustration compares two invented cases starting with zero own-money investment equity. The first borrows CAD 50,000 and invests it immediately. Its investment asset and loan liability initially offset each other. The second has neither that investment asset nor a loan. Both cases then use the same monthly household cash. This is the central control on the comparison: money spent servicing debt in one case is available for investing in the other. Giving the borrower an extra monthly payment source while withholding it from the comparison would change the resources supplied by the household. Split the common cash budget between interest and new investing The assumed loan rate is 7% simple annual interest, paid in twelve equal monthly amounts on unchanged principal. CAD 50,000 therefore incurs approximately CAD 291.67 of monthly interest. The selected extra investing cash after that payment is CAD 100. The derived household cash commitment is CAD 291.67 + CAD 100 = approximately CAD 391.67 per month , with full precision retained in the calculation. The borrowing case pays its interest and invests the remaining CAD 100. The no-loan case invests the entire common amount. Across ten years, each case uses CAD 47,000 of new household cash. The borrower allocates CAD 35,000 to interest and CAD 12,000 to new investment. The no-loan case invests all CAD 47,000. The stacked bars show these equal totals with different allocations. The budget is derived from the selected loan and extra investing amount. The tool assumes the household can provide it; it does not assess affordability. Raising the loan rate raises the common cash requirement rather than discovering a new source of household income. Subtract the loan before reading the ending investment position Both investments receive a hypothetical 5% effective annual total return, converted to equal monthly compound factors. Every monthly contribution arrives after that month’s growth, and all investment distributions remain reinvested. There are no investment fees or taxes. After ten years, the borrowing case holds investment assets of approximately CAD 96,881.05. The original CAD 50,000 principal is still owed. Repaying it leaves a net investment position of approximately CAD 46,881.05. The no-loan case accumulates about CAD 60,458.90 and has no investment loan to repay. Under these assumptions, borrowing finishes approximately CAD 13,577.86 behind the matched-cash comparison. The line chart shows investment value less loan for the borrowing case, rather than presenting its larger gross account as additional owned wealth. Its final net amount also is not investment profit relative to household cash supplied. Contributions, investment growth and debt repayment answer different parts of the reconciliation. Reconcile the final repayment without deducting interest twice The waterfall begins with CAD 50,000 invested from the loan, adds CAD 12,000 of later household money actually invested and approximately CAD 34,881.05 of investment growth, then subtracts the CAD 50,000 principal repaid at the end. The resulting CAD 46,881.05 matches the net-position line. Interest does not appear as another deduction from this bridge because it was already paid from the household cash budget and reduced the amount contributed to the investment. Deducting CAD 35,000 again here would count the same interest outflow twice. Interest still matters economically. Its cost is visible in the budget allocation and in the no-loan case’s ability to invest more each month. A separate lifetime profit ledger could subtract household cash from final resources, but it must use a clearly stated definition and consistent timing. No loan interest is added to principal in this illustration. Capitalizing unpaid interest, making principal instalments or using investment withdrawals to service debt would create different paths and require different cash-flow assumptions. Read the rate matrix as a conditional comparison The matrix changes annual loan interest and the effective annual investment return. Every cell supplies the same household cash to its paired cases, using that row’s monthly interest plus the selected extra investing amount. The common budget changes between rows. A useful arithmetic check is the case where the monthly investment growth factor equals the loan’s monthly interest rate. With no fees or taxes, the paired endpoints then coincide. A 7% simple annual interest charge paid monthly corresponds to about 7.23% effective annual growth when expressed on a monthly compound basis. This equivalence is a mathematical threshold under fixed assumptions, not a forecast, available investment yield or suitability test. The comparison uses a constant return rather than an uncertain sequence of market movements. Negative investment-minus-debt values remain negative. If a sale does not cover principal, another repayment source would be required. Extending the horizon does not guarantee recovery or remove the obligation to pay the loan. Bring the contract and uncertain household capacity back into the decision The AMF’s borrowing-to-invest guidance emphasizes that losses can occur while loan repayment and interest remain due. It also describes the possibility of repayment demands and the need to consider changes in personal circumstances. This model assumes interest can be paid from outside household cash throughout and principal is not demanded until the selected final date. It supplies no collateral-call protection, interest deduction, borrowing approval or guarantee that a lender will preserve the arrangement after a market decline. For an actual decision, assess repayment capacity independently of hoped-for investment gains, and inspect the terms governing interest, collateral, repayment and fees. Evaluate investment risk and suitability separately. The charts make the accounting comparison inspectable; a favorable cell cannot establish that borrowing is appropriate for the household or that the assumed return will occur.
bf940ee9fea4f364705fe2e5c24e75946f01ad19.zh: 由贷款资助的较大投资余额伴随着债务。使用相同的家庭现金承诺来比较净头寸，并将还款风险与假设回报分开。在比较账户余额之前先匹配家庭贡献 借款可以立即将大量资金存入投资账户。与每月储蓄资助的较小账户进行比较看起来很有说服力，因为期初总余额不同。在解释这种比较之前，需要包括债务和持续的现金承诺。该图比较了两个自有资金投资权益为零的发明案例。第一个人借了 50,000 加元并立即进行投资。其投资资产与贷款负债初始相互抵消。第二个既没有投资资产也没有贷款。两种情况都使用相同的每月家庭现金。这是比较的核心控制：一种情况下用于偿还债务的资金可用于投资另一种情况。为借款人提供额外的每月还款来源，同时不进行比较，将会改变家庭提供的资源。将共同现金预算分为利息和新投资 假定贷款利率为 7% 的简单年利率，按十二个月等额支付，本金不变。因此，50,000 加元每月产生约 291.67 加元的利息。付款后选定的额外投资现金为 100 加元。得出的家庭现金承诺为每月 291.67 加元 + 100 加元 = 约 391.67 加元，计算时保留完整精度。借款案例支付利息并投资剩余的 100 加元。无贷款案例投资全部普通金额。十年间，每个案件都使用了 47,000 加元的新家庭现金。借款人分配 35,000 加元用于利息，12,000 加元用于新投资。无贷款案例投资全部47,000加元。堆积条显示了具有不同分配的这些相等的总数。预算来自所选贷款和额外投资金额。该工具假设家庭可以提供；它不评估负担能力。提高贷款利率会提高共同现金需求，而不是发现新的家庭收入来源。在读取期末投资头寸之前减去贷款 两项投资均获得假设的 5% 有效年度总回报（转换为相等的月复合因子）。每个月的供款都会在该月的增长之后到达，并且所有投资分配仍会进行再投资。没有投资费用或税收。十年后，借款案件持有投资资产约96,881.05加元。原来的5万加元本金仍欠。偿还后，净投资头寸约为 46,881.05 加元。无贷款案件累计金额约60,458.90加元，无投资贷款需要偿还。根据这些假设，与匹配现金比较相比，借款完成额约为 13,577.86 加元。该折线图显示了借款案例的投资价值减去贷款，而不是将其较大的总账户显示为额外拥有的财富。其最终净额也不是相对于家庭现金供应的投资利润。捐款、投资增长和债务偿还回答了调节表的不同部分。核对最终还款，不扣除两次利息 瀑布从贷款投资的 50,000 加元开始，加上后来实际投资的 12,000 加元的家庭资金和大约 34,881.05 加元的投资增长，然后减去最后偿还的本金 50,000 加元。所得 46,881.05 加元与净头寸线相符​​。利息不会作为此桥梁的另一项扣除出现，因为它已经从家庭现金预算中支付，并减少了投资金额。此处再次扣除 35,000 加元，将同样的利息流出计算两次。利息在经济上仍然很重要。其成本在预算分配和无贷款情况下每月增加投资的能力中可见一斑。单独的终生利润分类账可以从最终资源中扣除家庭现金，但它必须使用明确的定义和一致的时间安排。在此示例中，本金中没有添加贷款利息。将未付利息资本化、进行本金分期付款或使用投资提款来偿还债务将创造不同的路径并需要不同的现金流量假设。阅读利率矩阵作为条件比较 该矩阵会改变年贷款利息和有效年投资回报。每个单元都使用该行的每月利息加上选定的额外投资金额，为其配对的案例提供相同的家庭现金。行之间的共同预算会发生变化。一个有用的算术检查是每月投资增长因子等于贷款每月利率的情况。无需任何费用或税费，配对端点即可重合。按月复利计算，每月支付 7% 的简单年利率相当于约 7.23% 的有效年增长率。这种等价性是固定假设下的数学阈值，而不是预测、可用投资收益率或适用性测试。该比较使用恒定回报而不是不确定的市场变动序列。投资减去债务的负值仍然为负。如果出售不能覆盖本金，则需要其他还款来源。延长期限并不保证收回贷款或免除偿还贷款的义务。将合同和不确定的家庭能力重新纳入决策之中 AMF 的借贷投资指南强调，在贷款偿还和利息到期的情况下，可能会发生损失。它还描述了还款要求的可能性以及考虑个人情况变化的需要。该模型假设利息可以自始至终用外部家庭现金支付，并且在选定的最终日期之前不需要本金。它不提供抵押品赎回保护、利息扣除、借款批准或保证贷款人在市场下跌后保留该安排。对于实际决策，应独立于期望的投资收益来评估还款能力，并检查有关利息、抵押品、还款和费用的条款。分别评估投资风险和适宜性。图表使会计比较易于检查；有利的单元无法确定借款适合该家庭或会发生假定的回报。

7980a7104f0d347727d73db1fe65b97c0b2e215b.src: A smaller positive inflation rate means prices are rising more slowly. It does not erase the increases already embedded in the price level. Ask whether the headline describes a level or a change A price index and an inflation rate answer different questions. The index records a price level relative to its reference period. A percentage change compares two index levels. When that change becomes smaller but remains positive, the newer level is still higher. The first two charts use Canada’s all-items annual-average Consumer Price Index from Statistics Canada Table 18-10-0005-01 . The dated observations cover 2020–2025 and use the reference 2002=100. The line shows levels; the bars calculate changes from one annual average to the next. The index rises from 137.0 in 2020 to 164.2 in 2025. The increase from 2024 to 2025 is smaller than the increase from 2021 to 2022, yet 164.2 remains above every earlier annual value shown. A slower pace and a higher endpoint can occur together. Keep the comparison period consistent Statistics Canada’s 2025 annual review , released 19 January 2026, reports a 2.1% annual-average CPI increase for 2025. It explains that annual-average comparisons differ from the monthly twelve-month change: an annual average combines the twelve monthly index readings, while a monthly comparison uses the same month one year earlier. These charts therefore do not describe December 2025 prices or the latest monthly inflation rate in 2026. They retain a complete annual period so the levels and changes share a consistent time basis. Six annual points also cannot show every rise and fall that occurred between them. The change bars are calculated from published index values rounded to one decimal. That rounding can affect a percentage calculated afterward. Use the displayed data tables to inspect the exact source levels and the derived values instead of treating extra decimal places as greater source precision. Calculate the accumulated change from the endpoints The cumulative index change is 164.2 ÷ 137.0 − 1 , or about 19.85%. This compares the 2025 annual-average level with the 2020 annual-average level across five intervals. It does not say that prices increased by that amount in any single year. Adding the five percentage changes is not the same calculation. Each year’s percentage applies to that year’s starting level. Chaining the growth factors reproduces the ratio of the final index to the initial index because the intermediate index terms cancel. A zero inflation assumption after 2025 would hold the newer level constant in this simplified example. Returning to the earlier level would require a decline, not merely a smaller positive increase. The size of a decline is measured against the higher starting level, so it is not numerically equal to the earlier cumulative rise. Translate an index ratio into a clearly labelled budget illustration Enter a hypothetical monthly expense expressed in 2020 dollars. The default CAD 3,000 is scaled by each annual index divided by 137.0. At the 2025 index, the result is about CAD 3,595.62. This assumes the expense moves exactly with the all-items CPI and that the underlying quantity or standard of consumption stays comparable. The waterfall starts with CAD 3,000 and adds the changes in that monthly expense equivalent. Its endpoint is a new monthly level. The intervening steps are not a total of the bills paid during the five years; calculating actual historical spending would require the amounts and frequency of those bills. An individual budget can change differently because of its spending mix, contracts, location or choices. The entered amount is not an observed Canadian household average, and the index ratio does not calculate your personal inflation rate. Use the separate spending-basket guide when comparing how categories affect your own expense mix. Separate future assumptions from the historical evidence The future line starts at the CPI-scaled 2025 expense and applies two user-selected annual changes. The default 2% followed by 1% produces 1.02 × 1.01 − 1 = 3.02% cumulative growth. The monthly expense equivalent becomes about CAD 3,704.21 after the two hypothetical years. The flat comparator applies zero change in both years and stays at CAD 3,595.62. It does not fall back to CAD 3,000. That comparison shows why a return to low inflation would not, by itself, restore an older household budget. Try a negative future change to illustrate a declining price level. The fixed matrix gives other two-year combinations independently of the controls. A 2% increase followed by a 2% decrease gives 1.02 × 0.98 − 1, or minus 0.04%, rather than exactly zero. These scenarios illustrate arithmetic; they assign no probability to future inflation. Update the dollar budget using the level you actually face For a household decision, start with current bill amounts and the dates they become payable. A dated CPI comparison can explain accumulated price pressure, but it does not replace a quote for rent, an insurance renewal or a grocery budget based on what the household buys. Keep the amount, comparison period and unit beside every number. An index value of 164.2 is neither CAD 164.20 nor a 164.2% annual inflation rate. A 2.1% annual-average change is not automatically the rate on every category or every family’s bill. When testing the next budget, label the future changes as assumptions and revise them when bills become known. The planning question is how many dollars the household will need and when, even when the headline percentage looks smaller than before.
7980a7104f0d347727d73db1fe65b97c0b2e215b.zh: 较小的正通胀率意味着物价上涨速度较慢。它不会消除已经嵌入价格水平的上涨。询问标题是否描述了水平或变化 价格指数和通货膨胀率回答了不同的问题。该指数记录相对于其参考期的价格水平。百分比变化比较两个指数水平。当这种变化变得较小但仍保持正值时，新的水平仍然较高。前两张图表使用加拿大统计局表 18-10-0005-01 中的加拿大所有项目年平均消费者价格指数。带日期的观察涵盖 2020-2025 年，并使用参考 2002=100。线条显示水平；这些条形图计算从一个年度平均值到下一个年度平均值的变化。该指数从 2020 年的 137.0 升至 2025 年的 164.2。2024 年至 2025 年的增幅小于 2021 年至 2022 年的增幅，但 164.2 仍高于之前显示的每个年度值。较慢的速度和较高的终点可以同时发生。保持比较期一致 加拿大统计局于 2026 年 1 月 19 日发布的 2025 年年度审查报告称，2025 年 CPI 年均增幅为 2.1%。它解释说，年均比较与 12 个月的月度变化不同：年均值结合了 12 个月的指数读数，而月度比较则使用一年前的同一个月。因此，这些图表并未描述 2025 年 12 月的价格或 2026 年最新的月度通胀率。它们保留了完整的年度周期，因此水平和变化具有一致的时间基础。六个年点也无法展现他们之间发生的每一次兴衰。变化条是根据已发布的指数值计算的，四舍五入到小数点后一位。该四舍五入可能会影响随后计算的百分比。使用显示的数据表检查确切的源级别和派生值，而不是将额外的小数位视为更高的源精度。计算端点的累积变化 累积指数变化为 164.2 ÷ 137.0 − 1 ，即约 19.85%。这将 2025 年年平均水平与 2020 年五个区间的年平均水平进行了比较。它并没有说任何一年的价格上涨幅度都是如此。添加五个百分比变化并不是相同的计算。每年的百分比适用于当年的起始水平。由于中间指数项取消，链接增长因子会重现最终指数与初始指数的比率。在此简化示例中，2025 年之后的零通胀假设将使新水平保持不变。回到之前的水平需要下降，而不仅仅是较小的正增长。下降的幅度是根据较高的起始水平来衡量的，因此它在数字上并不等于早期的累计上升。将指数比率转换为明确标记的预算说明 输入以 2020 年美元表示的假设每月费用。默认 3,000 加元按每个年度指数除以 137.0 进行缩放。以 2025 年指数计算，结果约为 3,595.62 加元。这假设费用完全随着所有项目的 CPI 变化，并且基本消费数量或标准保持可比。瀑布从 3,000 加元开始，并添加每月费用等值的变化。其终点是新的月度水平。中间步骤并非五年内所支付账单的总和；计算实际历史支出需要这些账单的金额和频率。个人预算可能会因其支出组合、合同、地点或选择而发生不同的变化。输入的金额不是观察到的加拿大家庭平均值，并且指数比率不会计算您的个人通货膨胀率。在比较类别如何影响您自己的支出组合时，请使用单独的支出篮指南。将未来假设与历史证据分开 未来线从 2025 年 CPI 费用开始，并应用两个用户选择的年度变化。默认 2%，随后 1% 产生 1.02 × 1.01 − 1 = 3.02% 累积增长。假设的两年后，每月费用约为 3,704.21 加元。持平比较器在这两年中均采用零变化，并保持在 3,595.62 加元。它不会回落至 3,000 加元。这一比较表明，为什么回归低通胀本身并不能恢复较旧的家庭预算。尝试用未来的负变化来说明价格水平的下降。固定矩阵给出了独立于控件的其他两年组合。增加 2%，然后减少 2%，得到 1.02 × 0.98 − 1，即负 0.04%，而不是恰好为零。这些场景说明了算术；他们没有为未来的通货膨胀分配任何概率。使用您实际面临的水平更新美元预算 对于家庭决策，请从当前账单金额及其应付日期开始。过时的消费物价指数比较可以解释累积的价格压力，但它不能取代租金报价、保险续保或基于家庭购买的杂货预算。在每个数字旁边注明金额、比较期间和单位。指数值 164.2 既不是 164.20 加元，也不是 164.2% 的年通货膨胀率。 2.1% 的年平均变化并不自动成为每个类别或每个家庭账单的变化率。在测试下一个预算时，将未来的变化标记为假设，并在法案公布时对其进行修改。规划问题是家庭将需要多少美元以及何时需要，即使总体百分比看起来比以前要小。

8055b0974884d2c91e345837755e951da292532c.src: An expected deposit refund is different from cash already available. Find the lowest balance on the calendar before using a positive final balance to judge the move’s funding. Start with accessible cash and a separate refund assumption The fictional household allocates CAD 4,000 before the first model day. That amount excludes the old deposit still held elsewhere and money already reserved for other bills. Four CAD 2,000 net pay deposits arrive on days ten, twenty-five, forty and fifty-five. The household separately expects CAD 900 back from its old-home deposit, with actual cash availability assumed on day thirty-five. The refund is entered as an amount expected to arrive, rather than inferred from the original deposit, interest rules or a claim against a landlord. The first chart follows daily cash. A second line begins with the minimum opening amount that funds every listed day. It changes the starting reserve, while keeping every receipt, cost and date the same. It does not automatically borrow the difference or move a required rent payment. List the old rent, new rent, deposit and moving payment separately The assumed cash obligations are CAD 1,800 of final old-home rent and CAD 1,000 of new deposit cash on day one, CAD 600 of moving costs on day fourteen, and CAD 2,000 of new-home rent on days fifteen and forty-five. Four CAD 900 living-cost payments occur on days seven, twenty-two, thirty-seven and fifty-two. These are entered cash dates, not a determination of when a lease ends or how rent must be prorated. Some rent paid within the sixty-day window can cover occupancy beyond it. The calendar therefore measures payments, rather than accrued housing expense for an exactly matched occupancy period. At the starting inputs, cash falls to negative CAD 300 after the first new-rent payment on day fifteen. It reaches negative CAD 1,200 after the living-cost payment on day twenty-two. The day-thirty-five refund cannot pay either earlier obligation without another identified source. Distinguish the required reserve from the final cash balance Funding all listed events requires CAD 5,200 before day one. With CAD 4,000 already allocated, the additional opening requirement is CAD 1,200. The fully funded line reaches zero at its lowest point; it does not represent income earned or a loan approved by the model. The originally allocated path nevertheless ends day sixty with positive CAD 1,900. That endpoint can coexist with the earlier shortfall because later receipts restore the cash balance. A positive final total alone does not establish that every payment was fundable when due. The second figure provides thirty-day receipt and payment summaries. In the first thirty days, cash received is CAD 4,000 and cash paid is CAD 7,200. Opening cash leaves a day-thirty balance of CAD 800, even though the daily balance previously fell below zero. The summary cannot replace the dated check. Reconcile money paid without treating every deposit as consumption The waterfall begins with CAD 4,000, adds CAD 8,000 of pay and the CAD 900 refund received, then subtracts CAD 5,800 of rent, CAD 1,000 of new deposit cash, CAD 600 of moving costs and CAD 3,600 of living payments. The endpoint is CAD 1,900. The new deposit uses cash but is not automatically a permanently lost expense. The old refund returns money previously held elsewhere; it is not a second paycheque in this ledger. Any eventual deduction, deposit interest or dispute needs its own evidence and treatment. Do not include the old deposit in starting bank cash and add its refund again later. Conversely, a deposit still held can represent a separate expected claim without being available to pay the next bill. The model does not value or adjudicate that claim. Test arrival dates and amounts without predicting a legal result The grid changes opening cash and the assumed arrival of the same CAD 900 refund. With the starting costs, a receipt on day ten or twenty reduces the required opening fund to CAD 4,300. The CAD 4,000 allocation would then need another CAD 300. A receipt on day thirty-five requires CAD 5,200 because the worst funding point has already occurred. Moving the receipt to day sixty-one leaves that same peak requirement in this example, while reducing day-sixty cash to CAD 1,000. Every delay does not mechanically increase the worst shortfall; its position relative to other events matters. An earlier cell assumes an actual earlier payment. It does not create a right to demand that timing. A day after sixty means no refund has arrived within the plotted window, not that the claim has vanished. For a disputed or uncertain receipt, reducing the assumed amount or setting it to zero tests funding without deciding what is legally owed. Keep BC deposit rules separate from the cash-arrival control For ordinary tenancies covered by BC’s Residential Tenancy Act, RTB guidance describes a security deposit capped at half the first month’s rent and a separate pet damage deposit capped at half a month’s rent. The calculator accepts assumed cash amounts and does not determine whether a specific requested charge is lawful. Section 38 of the Act generally requires repayment with applicable interest or an application claiming against a deposit within fifteen days after the later of tenancy end and the landlord’s receipt of the tenant’s written forwarding address. Inspection rights, written retention consent, orders and statutory exceptions can affect the result. That process is different from a promise that spendable bank funds arrive fifteen days after moving. The RTB return calculator addresses process dates and initiation. This guide does not calculate service, legal deadlines, interest, permitted deductions, penalties or entitlement, and the BC context should not be applied automatically to another jurisdiction. Replace the fictional calendar with confirmed obligations and evidence Confirm the old tenancy’s actual end and rent obligation, the new agreement’s payment dates and deposit amounts, and the moving quote. Keep any overlap or proration agreement separate from the day on which keys physically change hands. For the old deposit, retain receipts, condition reports, inspection communications and the written forwarding-address record. Identify any agreed deduction, application or order and the amount actually returned. The RTB moving-out guidance provides context; these graphs do not resolve a disputed settlement. Finally, use the date money becomes available, including the payment method’s processing time, rather than only a cheque or transfer instruction date. Same-day receipts are assumed available before outflows in this example. If that cannot be verified, separate the events and retain enough cash for the earlier obligation. The reserve is a timing requirement alongside the move’s eventual costs.
8055b0974884d2c91e345837755e951da292532c.zh: 预期押金退款与现有现金不同。在使用正的最终余额来判断此举的资金之前，找到日历上的最低余额。从可用现金和单独退款假设开始 虚构家庭在第一个模型日之前分配了 4,000 加元。该金额不包括仍在其他地方持有的旧存款以及已为其他票据预留的资金。第十、二十五、四十和五十五天将收到四笔 2,000 加元的净付费存款。该家庭预计从旧房押金中收回 900 加元，假设实际可用现金在第三十五天。退款是按照预期到达的金额输入的，而不是根据原始押金、利息规则或对房东的索赔推断的。第一张图表遵循每日现金。第二行以每个上市日资助的最低开仓金额开始。它改变了起始储备，同时保持每张收据、成本和日期相同。它不会自动借用差额或转移所需的租金。分别列出旧房租金、新房租金、押金和搬家费 承担的现金义务为第一天旧房最终租金 1,800 加元和新房押金现金 1,000 加元，第十四天搬迁费用 600 加元，第十五天和四十五天新房租金 2,000 加元。第 7 天、第 22 天、第 37 天和第 52 天分别支付四笔 900 加元的生活费。这些是输入的现金日期，而不是确定租赁何时结束或如何按比例分配租金。在六十天的期限内支付的部分租金可以支付超过该期限的入住费用。因此，该日历衡量的是付款，而不是完全匹配的入住期间的应计住房费用。在开始输入时，在第 15 天支付第一笔新租金后，现金跌至负 300 加元。第 22 天支付生活费后，金额达到负 1,200 加元。如果没有其他确定的来源，第三十五天的退款无法支付之前的任何一项义务。将所需准备金与最终现金余额区分开来 资助所有列出的活动在第一天之前需要 5,200 加元。已分配 4,000 加元，额外开放要求为 1,200 加元。资金充足的线在最低点达到零；它不代表赚取的收入或模型批准的贷款。然而，最初分配的路径在第 60 天结束时仍获得 1,900 加元的正值。该端点可以与早期的短缺共存，因为后来的收据恢复了现金余额。仅凭正数的最终总额并不能证明每笔付款在到期时均可获得资助。第二个数字提供了三十天的收款和付款摘要。前三十天内，收到的现金为 4,000 加元，支付的现金为 7,200 加元。期初现金剩余第 30 天余额为 800 加元，尽管每日余额之前已降至零以下。摘要不能代替注明日期的支票。核对支付的款项，而不将每笔押金都视为消费瀑布从 4,000 加元开始，加上 8,000 加元的工资和收到的 900 加元的退款，然后减去 5,800 加元的租金、1,000 加元的新押金现金、600 加元的搬家费用和 3,600 加元的生活付款。终点为 1,900 加元。新存款使用现金，但不会自动成为永久损失的费用。旧退款退回之前在其他地方持有的资金；它不是这个分类账中的第二张工资支票。任何最终的扣除、存款利息或争议都需要有自己的证据和处理。请勿将旧存款包含在起始银行现金中，并在稍后再次添加其退款。相反，仍然持有的存款可以代表单独的预期索赔，而无法支付下一张账单。该模型不评估或裁决该主张。测试到达日期和金额，而不预测法律结果 网格会更改初始现金和假定到达的相同 900 加元退款。加上起始成本，第十天或二十天的收据将所需的开业资金减少到 4,300 加元。 4,000 加元的分配将需要另外 300 加元。第三十五天的收据需要 5,200 加元，因为最糟糕的资金点已经发生。在本示例中，将收据移至第 61 天会保留相同的峰值需求，同时将第 60 天的现金减少到 1,000 加元。每次延误都不会机械地增加最严重的短缺；它相对于其他事件的位置很重要。较早的单元假定实际较早付款。它并不创造要求该时间安排的权利。六十后的一天意味着在指定的时间内没有收到退款，但这并不是说索赔已经消失。对于有争议或不确定的收据，减少假定金额或将其设置为零测试资金，而不决定合法欠款。将不列颠哥伦比亚省押金规则与现金到达控制分开 对于不列颠哥伦比亚省住宅租赁法涵盖的普通租赁，RTB 指南描述了押金上限为第一个月租金的一半，以及单独的宠物损坏押金上限为半个月租金。计算器接受假设的现金金额，但不会确定特定请求的费用是否合法。该法第 38 条一般要求在租赁结束和房东收到租户的书面转发地址后 15 天内偿还并支付相应的利息或提出押金索赔申请，以较晚者为准。检查权、书面保留同意书、命令和法定例外情况都会影响结果。这个过程与可使用的银行资金在搬家后十五天到达的承诺不同。 RTB 回报计算器可计算流程日期和启动时间。本指南不计算服务、法定期限、利息、允许的扣除、处罚或权利，并且 BC 背景不应自动应用于其他司法管辖区。用已确认的义务和证据替换虚构的日历确认旧租赁的实际结束和租金义务、新协议的付款日期和押金金额以及移动报价。将任何重叠或按比例分配协议与钥匙实际易手之日分开保存。对于旧存款，请保留收据、状况报告、检查通讯和书面转发地址记录。确定任何商定的扣除额、申请或订单以及实际退还的金额。 RTB 搬出指南提供了背景信息；这些图表并不能解决有争议的解决方案。最后，使用资金可用的日期，包括付款方式的处理时间，而不仅仅是支票或转账指令日期。在此示例中，假定当日收货在流出之前可用。如果无法验证这一点，请将事件分开并保留足够的现金来履行先前的义务。储备金是与此举的最终成本一起的时间要求。

6a4bd79da3f8aeffd3133a7a8cfbed63a6e7af77.zh: 家庭福利现金发放时间

60befbc22273103f57cc30c09d66d0c849266726.src: Confirm the benefit amount and payment pattern independently. A benefit assigned to a later date can support the annual budget while leaving an earlier bill unfunded. Keep the benefit period separate from the calendar year The CRA’s CCB payment page , updated 22 October 2026 and reviewed here on 25 October, provides twelve scheduled 2026 dates. Its mapping uses the 2024 tax year for January–June payments and the 2025 tax year for July–December payments. A calendar-year budget can therefore contain portions of two benefit periods. The CRA amount guide explains the annual July recalculation using prior-year adjusted family net income. This is a reference-year relationship, not a calculation of the amount an individual family will receive. The model takes two independently entered monthly receipt amounts. It does not calculate eligibility, adjusted family net income, child-age effects, custody arrangements or combined provincial benefits. An actual family’s notice and expected payment details must establish the receipt amounts and pattern before they belong in a working cash plan. Enter known receipts rather than inferring an entitlement The authored default assigns CAD 450 to each scheduled January–June receipt and CAD 600 to each scheduled July–December receipt. Those six-month amounts total CAD 6,300 across the 2026 schedule. They are hypothetical inputs, not published maximum CCB amounts. Each half-year remains constant solely to make the calendar readable. A reassessment, changed family circumstances, stopped payment or other adjustment may require a more detailed schedule. Entering zero does not decide whether a benefit is payable; it simply removes that assumed receipt from the arithmetic. Use the monthly model only where a recurring monthly pattern has been independently established. CRA also describes a lump-sum arrangement for low annual entitlements. The calculator does not create that arrangement or transform a small entered amount into a monthly entitlement. No future-year payment schedule is inferred from the 2026 dates. Place the bill before the benefit when that matches the budget The dedicated budget begins with no opening cash. On every month’s first day, the household assigns CAD 150 from its other resources and then pays a selected CAD 600 child-related bill. The month initially reaches negative CAD 450. Under the default timing, the first CAD 450 benefit receipt later returns January’s balance to zero. The same pattern repeats through June. A later receipt does not retroactively provide the cash needed on the first day, so the required extra opening reserve is CAD 450.
