From July, the selected CAD 600 receipt exceeds that month’s CAD 450 gap by CAD 150. The dedicated balance gradually improves. Other household funding is an allocation from resources outside this sub-budget; it is not a newly created source of total household wealth. Confirm that the allocation is affordable alongside the rest of the family’s commitments. Reconcile the annual surplus separately from the interim reserve Twelve assignments of CAD 150 provide CAD 1,800. Add CAD 6,300 of benefit receipts and subtract twelve CAD 600 bills, or CAD 7,200. The calendar-year reconciliation leaves CAD 900. That positive ending amount coexists with the earlier CAD 450 funding requirement. The opening reserve shifts the cash path upward; it does not change the benefit entitlement or make the selected expense cheaper. Looking only at the annual surplus would miss the need to fund the first bill before its later receipt. The waterfall stops on 31 December. It includes only receipts that the selected timing places inside 2026. A delayed receipt arriving after that date belongs in the later collection segment, not in the year-end cash balance. The chart data retains the full dates of each funding assignment, bill and receipt. Test a receipt delay without presenting it as a forecast The lag control adds a hypothetical number of calendar days after every scheduled date. It does not alter CRA’s published schedule, predict a processing delay or guarantee that a bank balance will be available at a particular time. With a 14-day lag in the default, all selected receipts still arrive during 2026, and the final balance remains CAD 900. The required opening cash increases to CAD 900 because another first-of-month bill can arrive before the delayed receipt. At 35 days, the selected December receipt moves to 15 January 2027. The 2026 balance becomes CAD 300; the later CAD 600 receipt brings the collection-only endpoint to CAD 900. No 2027 bill or additional household funding is modeled during that runoff segment, so it is not a complete forecast of the following year. Keep the dedicated reserve connected to actual family cash flow The matrix changes the opening reserve and other monthly household funding while retaining the benefit inputs, selected bill and lag. Each cell reports extra starting cash required to keep every modeled bill funded. It does not report extra benefits, a tax saving or a probability of a shortfall. For implementation, confirm the actual expected receipts, list the relevant bills and place both on a calendar with other income. Keep costs entered here separate from costs already included elsewhere, and count each reserved dollar once. A bill already paid from another budget should not be deducted again without transferring its funding too. Review the plan after a confirmed payment or cost change. This is a fixed-year cash illustration, not an application tool or an entitlement calculator. Its purpose is to show when supported resources arrive, how much cash is needed beforehand and why the timing question remains important even when the annual total looks comfortable.
60befbc22273103f57cc30c09d66d0c849266726.zh: 独立确认福利金额和支付方式。分配给较晚日期的福利可以支持年度预算，同时使较早的账单没有资金支持。将福利期与日历年分开 CRA 的 CCB 付款页面于 2026 年 10 月 22 日更新，并于 10 月 25 日在此处进行审核，提供了 12 个预定的 2026 年日期。其映射对 1 月至 6 月的付款使用 2024 年纳税年度，对 7 月至 12 月的付款使用 2025 年纳税年度。因此，日历年预算可以包含两个福利期的部分内容。 CRA 金额指南解释了使用上一年调整后的家庭净收入对每年 7 月进行的重新计算。这是参考年关系，而不是单个家庭将收到的金额的计算。该模型采用两个独立输入的每月收款金额。它不计算资格、调整后的家庭净收入、儿童年龄影响、监护权安排或综合省级福利。实际家庭的通知和预期付款详细信息必须先确定收款金额和模式，然后才能纳入工作现金计划。输入已知收据而不是推断权利 创建的默认值将 450 加元分配给每个计划的 1 月至 6 月收据，将 600 加元分配给每个计划的 7 月至 12 月收据。 2026 年计划中这六个月的金额总计 6,300 加元。它们是假设的输入，而不是公布的最大 CCB 金额。每半年保持不变只是为了使日历可读。重新评估、家庭情况改变、停止付款或其他调整可能需要更详细的时间表。输入零并不能决定是否支付福利；它只是从算术中删除假设的收据。仅当已独立建立每月循环模式时才使用每月模型。 CRA 还描述了针对低年度福利的一次性安排。计算器不会创建该安排或将少量输入的金额转换为每月的权利。从 2026 年的日期无法推断出未来一年的付款时间表。当与预算相匹配时，将账单放在福利之前。专用预算开始时没有期初现金。每个月的第一天，家庭从其他资源中分配 150 加元，然后支付选定的 600 加元与儿童相关的账单。该月最初达到负 450 加元。在默认时间下，第一笔 450 加元的福利收据随后会将 1 月份的余额归零。同样的模式在整个六月都会重复。较晚的收据并不能追溯​​提供第一天所需的现金，因此所需的额外开仓准备金为450加元。从7月份开始，所选的600加元收据超出当月450加元的缺口150加元。专用余额逐渐改善。其他家庭资金是从本子预算之外的资源分配的；它不是家庭总财富的新创造来源。确认分配的资金以及家庭的其他承诺是可以负担的。将年度盈余与临时储备金分开进行调节 12 次 150 加元的分配提供 1,800 加元。添加 6,300 加元的福利收据并减去十二张 600 加元的账单，即 7,200 加元。日历年对账后剩下 900 加元。这一正数的最终金额与之前的 450 加元资金要求并存。期初准备金使现金路径向上移动；它不会改变福利权利或使所选费用更便宜。只看年度盈余会忽略在随后收到第一份账单之前为其提供资金的需要。瀑布于 12 月 31 日停止。它仅包括所选时间在 2026 年之内放置的收据。在该日期之后到达的延迟收据属于较晚收款部分，而不属于年末现金余额。图表数据保留每项资金分配、账单和收据的完整日期。测试接收延迟而不将其作为预测呈现 滞后控件在每个计划日期后添加假设的日历天数。它不会改变 CRA 公布的时间表、预测处理延迟或保证银行余额将在特定时间可用。默认情况下有 14 天的延迟，所有选定的收据仍会在 2026 年期间到达，最终余额仍为 900 加元。所需的期初现金增加到 900 加元，因为另一张第一个月的账单可能会在延迟收据之前到达。 35 天后，所选 12 月收据将移至 2027 年 1 月 15 日。2026 年余额变为 300 加元；后来的 600 加元收据将仅收款端点带到了 900 加元。在该径流阶段没有对 2027 年账单或额外家庭资金进行建模，因此这不是对下一年的完整预测。保持专用准备金与实际家庭现金流相关联 该矩阵改变了期初准备金和其他每月家庭资金，同时保留福利投入、选定的账单和滞后。每个单元都会报告为每个模拟账单提供资金所需的额外起始现金。它不报告额外福利、节税或短缺的可能性。为了实施，确认实际的预期收入，列出相关账单并将其与其他收入放在日历上。将此处输入的成本与其他地方已包含的成本分开，并将每笔保留的美元计算一次。已从其他预算支付的账单不应在未转移其资金的情况下再次扣除。确认付款或费用变更后查看计划。这是固定年期现金说明，不是申请工具或权利计算器。其目的是显示受支持的资源何时到达、事先需要多少现金以及为什么即使年度总额看起来不错，时机问题仍然很重要。

44058a95748b43d5ef4ea7b3ed4a60338b70d047.src: Compare the cash actually received with every repayment. A quoted interest rate and a payment amount do not, by themselves, explain the effect of an upfront fee. Separate contract principal from net cash advanced The hypothetical loan has CAD 10,000 of contract principal and a 5% upfront fee withheld from its proceeds. The fee is CAD 500, so the borrower receives CAD 9,500. The repayment schedule still amortizes CAD 10,000. The first waterfall makes that difference visible. This is one particular fee arrangement. A charge paid separately from other cash or added to financed principal would require a different opening ledger. Do not combine those treatments by withholding the fee and also adding it to the loan balance. The Financial Consumer Agency of Canada’s personal-loan guide identifies interest, fees and term as elements of borrowing cost. The amounts and rate conventions here are independently authored examples. They are not a lender quote, an eligibility assessment or a recommendation to borrow. State the rate and payment conventions before comparing schedules The default uses an 8% nominal annual interest rate divided by twelve, with 36 payments at month-end. The full term is also the full amortization period. There is no unpaid balloon at the end and no rate renewal during the schedule. The unrounded monthly payment is approximately CAD 313.36. Interest for each month applies to the principal outstanding before that payment. The remainder of the payment reduces principal. As principal falls, monthly interest falls and more of the same payment reduces the balance. The path chart separates outstanding principal, cumulative principal repaid and cumulative interest paid. Changing only the withheld fee leaves these contractual paths unchanged. It changes the initial cash received. Actual agreements may use different dates, interest conventions, rounding or charges, all of which need to be reconciled before using an illustration as a payment plan. Subtract net proceeds from payments without charging the fee twice The modeled 36 payments total approximately CAD 11,281.09. Of that amount, CAD 10,000 repays contract principal and approximately CAD 1,281.09 is interest. The initial proceeds, however, were only CAD 9,500. Payments less net proceeds therefore equal approximately CAD 1,781.09. That difference reconciles to CAD 1,281.09 of interest plus the CAD 500 withheld fee. The stacked chart shows these two cost components, rather than describing every repayment dollar as a borrowing expense. Once the fee has reduced initial proceeds, do not add it again to the payment-minus-proceeds difference. Conversely, subtracting the full CAD 10,000 contract principal from payments and stopping there would omit the withheld fee’s cost. Keep the opening cash event and the repayment ledger beside one another. Define the annualized cash-flow measure precisely The calculator finds the monthly discount rate at which the scheduled equal payments have a present value equal to the CAD 9,500 actually received. It then compounds that monthly rate over twelve periods. In the default, this effective annual cash-flow rate is approximately 12.15%. With no withheld fee, the same calculation gives approximately 8.30% effectively per year. That differs from the stated 8% nominal annual rate because the example converts a monthly rate into an annually compounded measure. The fee then creates an additional difference by reducing the proceeds supporting the same payment stream. This explicitly defined measure is not a calculation of statutory disclosed APR. FCAC’s disclosure guide lists annual interest, APR when different, payment details and other charges for federally regulated fixed-rate loans. Use the actual disclosure and applicable calculation rules for a regulated comparison. A longer term can lower one rate measure while increasing total interest The matrix varies the fee percentage and the number of monthly repayments while retaining the contract principal and nominal annual interest rate. Every cell recalculates both the payment and the net-advance discount rate. Spreading an upfront fee over more months can reduce its annualized impact. That does not mean the longer loan necessarily costs fewer dollars. A longer repayment schedule usually leaves principal outstanding for more time, creating additional interest under this fixed-rate model. Read the monthly commitment, full payment total, fee and effective cash-flow measure together. A lower payment can help a monthly budget while extending indebtedness. A lower annualized measure can coexist with a larger full-term dollar cost. None of those measures alone decides whether the loan meets a household’s needs. Reconcile the offer with the household’s payment calendar Begin with the amount that will actually arrive, the amount owed, every required charge and the date of each repayment. Confirm whether optional services are included, how interest accrues and what changes if the loan is repaid early. This calculator assumes the full schedule is completed. Then place the payments beside actual take-home receipts and existing commitments. A mathematical payment does not establish that cash will be available on the withdrawal date. Avoid treating a fee-financed or fee-withheld offer as interchangeable with an offer that delivers a different usable amount. The illustration excludes loan insurance, other fees, missed payments, extra payments, refinancing and tax. Calculations retain full precision and reconcile a tiny numerical residual in the last payment. They explain the relationship among principal, proceeds and cost without determining legal compliance, qualifying terms or a personal borrowing decision.
44058a95748b43d5ef4ea7b3ed4a60338b70d047.zh: 将实际收到的现金与每次还款进行比较。报价利率和付款金额本身并不能解释预付费用的影响。将合同本金与预付现金净额分开 该假设贷款的合同本金为 10,000 加元，并从其收益中预扣 5% 的预付费用。费用为 500 加元，因此借款人收到 9,500 加元。还款计划仍需摊销 10,000 加元。第一个瀑布使这种差异显而易见。这是一种特殊的费用安排。与其他现金分开支付或添加到融资本金中的费用将需要不同的期初分类账。不要通过预扣费用并将其添加到贷款余额中来结合这些处理方法。加拿大金融消费者机构的个人贷款指南将利息、费用和期限确定为借贷成本的要素。此处的金额和费率惯例是独立撰写的示例。它们不是贷款机构报价、资格评估或借款建议。比较时间表之前先说明利率和付款约定 默认使用 8% 的名义年利率除以 12，月底付款 36 次。完整期限也是完整摊销期限。最后没有未付的气球，并且在计划期间没有费率续订。每月未四舍五入的付款额约为 313.36 加元。每月的利息适用于付款前未偿还的本金。剩余的付款减少了本金。随着本金下降，每月利息也会下降，而更多的相同付款会减少余额。路径图将未偿还本金、累计偿还本金和累计支付利息分开。仅更改预扣费用会使这些合同路径保持不变。它改变了最初收到的现金。实际协议可能使用不同的日期、利息约定、四舍五入或费用，所有这些都需要在使用插图作为付款计划之前进行协调。减去付款的净收益，无需收取两次费用 建模的 36 笔付款总计约为 11,281.09 加元。其中，10,000 加元用于偿还合同本金，约 1,281.09 加元为利息。然而，最初的收益仅为 9,500 加元。因此，付款减去净收益大约等于 1,781.09 加元。该差额相当于 1,281.09 加元的利息加上 500 加元的预扣费用。堆积图显示了这两个成本组成部分，而不是将每一美元还款描述为借款费用。一旦费用减少了初始收益，请勿将其再次添加到付款减去收益差额中。相反，从付款中减去 10,000 加元的全部合同本金并停止，就可以忽略预扣费用的成本。将期初现金事件和还款分类账放在一起。精确定义年化现金流量指标 计算器可计算出计划等额付款的现值等于实际收到的 9,500 加元的每月贴现率。然后，它会在十二个时期内对每月利率进行复合。在违约情况下，有效年现金流量约为 12.15%。如果没有预扣费用，同样的计算得出每年的有效收益率约为 8.30%。这与规定的 8% 名义年利率不同，因为该示例将月利率转换为年复利指标。然后，该费用通过减少支持相同支付流的收益而产生额外的差异。这一明确定义的衡量标准并非法定披露年利率的计算。 FCAC 的披露指南列出了联邦监管的固定利率贷款的年利息、年利率（不同情况下的年利率）、付款细节和其他费用。使用实际披露和适用的计算规则进行规范比较。较长期限可以降低一项利率指标，同时增加总利息。该矩阵改变费用百分比和每月还款次数，同时保留合同本金和名义年利率。每个单元格都会重新计算付款和净预付款折扣率。将预付费用分摊到更多月份可以减少其年化影响。这并不意味着贷款期限越长，花费的美元就越少。较长的还款计划通常会使本金未偿还的时间更长，从而在这种固定利率模式下产生额外的利息。一起阅读每月承诺、全额付款总额、费用和有效现金流量指标。较低的付款可以帮助每月预算，同时扩大债务。较低的年化指标可以与较高的长期美元成本共存。这些措施都不能单独决定贷款是否满足家庭的需求。使报价与家庭的付款日历保持一致从实际到达的金额、欠款金额、每项所需费用以及每次还款日期开始。确认是否包含可选服务、利息如何累积以及提前偿还贷款会发生什么变化。该计算器假设完整的时间表已完成。然后将付款放在实际带回家的收据和现有承诺旁边。数学付款并不能确定在提款日可以获得现金。避免将收费融资或扣费优惠视为可与提供不同可用金额的优惠互换。该图不包括贷款保险、其他费用、逾期付款、额外付款、再融资和税收。计算保持完全精确，并协调最后一次付款中的微小数值残差。它们解释了本金、收益和成本之间的关系，但没有确定法律合规性、合格条款或个人借贷决定。

c93c02c42bd6c4057656460948fef4fd8e9ae2f4.src: Interest reporting, access to investment cash and the date tax must be funded are separate questions. A growing locked balance cannot automatically pay a bill due before maturity. Separate interest income from accessible cash A compound investment can earn interest without delivering that interest to a chequing account. The balance grows inside the product, while the household’s available cash may remain unchanged. That difference matters if an income-related payment must be funded before the investment matures. The CRA’s line 12100 guidance explains that interest on term deposits, GICs and similar investments may need to be reported for each complete investment year even when cash is paid later and no T5 slip has been received. Waiting for maturity does not automatically postpone reporting all the interest. This article illustrates the resulting cash-planning question for a non-registered compound investment. It does not calculate a return or deadline for a particular taxpayer. Registered accounts, ownership attribution, other income, credits and benefit effects require their own rules and records. Keep the investment and the outside reserve in separate ledgers The example invests CAD 100,000 for five years at a hypothetical 4% effective annual rate, compounded annually. It assumes that neither principal nor interest can be withdrawn before maturity. The first completed investment year adds CAD 4,000 of interest, leaving CAD 104,000 inside the locked investment. An independently assumed tax rate of 30% produces CAD 1,200 of modeled tax funding for that year. The tax money comes from outside the investment. Deducting it from the GIC would contradict the selected no-access assumption and would also change subsequent compound interest. The outside ledger starts with CAD 2,000 and receives CAD 50 at every month-end. Those transfers are new household saving, rather than investment profit. Outside cash earns zero interest in this simplified exercise. The graph labels any negative outside balance as a provisional funding gap. It does not create an overdraft, loan or hidden injection of money. A plan with such a gap needs an additional supported funding source before it can be implemented. State the funding dates without mistaking them for tax law For transparency, the model funds the assumed tax at the end of each completed investment year, after that month’s reserve transfer. At the end of the final investment year, it first receives the maturity proceeds and then funds the last modeled tax amount. Those are deliberately chosen arithmetic dates. A completed investment year, a calendar tax year, a filing deadline and a tax-payment deadline are not interchangeable. Actual reporting and payment requirements must be checked separately, including any instalment obligation. The CRA page reviewed on 25 October 2026 is dated 20 January 2026 and includes 2025-return examples. It supports the distinction between accrued interest and cash received; it does not supply the calculator’s funding calendar or its 30% input. For a real account, identify the investment’s issue and maturity dates, actual interest records and applicable tax requirements before mapping cash transfers to payment dates. The tool’s investment-year labels intentionally avoid claiming to be a calendar-year filing schedule. Find the shortage before looking at the final payout The first four years add interest of CAD 4,000, CAD 4,160, CAD 4,326.40 and CAD 4,499.46, with calculations retaining unrounded precision. Their modeled tax funding totals approximately CAD 5,095.76 . By the fourth year-end, the outside ledger has received the CAD 2,000 opening reserve plus forty-eight CAD 50 transfers, or CAD 4,400. After the accumulated modeled tax payments, its provisional balance is negative CAD 695.76. This is the largest pre-maturity shortage in the default scenario. The household would need approximately CAD 695.76 of additional opening cash, rounded up to cents, to cover those simplified dates without a negative balance. The exact underlying requirement is calculated before display rounding. It is additional to the CAD 2,000 already assigned. The investment itself is still growing at that point. Its larger balance does not solve the cash shortage when access is unavailable. The first chart focuses on outside cash before maturity, keeping the earlier shortage visible instead of compressing it beside the much larger future payout. Annual interest is shown separately. Reconcile the maturity endpoint without ignoring external saving After five years, gross interest totals CAD 21,665.29 and the maturity proceeds are CAD 121,665.29. The modeled final-year tax funding is about CAD 1,403.83, bringing all five years’ modeled tax to CAD 6,499.59. The final waterfall begins with the CAD 100,000 investment, adds the CAD 2,000 opening outside reserve, CAD 3,000 of new monthly saving and CAD 21,665.29 of gross interest, then subtracts all modeled tax. The arithmetic cash endpoint is approximately CAD 120,165.70. That endpoint includes the new household resources and cannot be read as the investment alone earning CAD 20,165.70 after tax. The return contribution is the gross interest less modeled tax; the opening reserve and monthly transfers have different origins. A positive endpoint also does not prove that the earlier plan worked. The calculation carries a provisional funding deficit through time to reveal it. Maturity proceeds arriving later cannot retroactively settle a payment that lacked cash before maturity. Use the reserve matrix to test a funding plan The matrix varies the assumed tax rate and the monthly outside allocation, holding the selected principal, interest rate, horizon and opening reserve fixed. Every cell recalculates the greatest pre-maturity shortage. A zero cell means the entered resources cover this simplified schedule, rather than proving no tax is payable. A larger monthly allocation requires room in the household budget. An increased opening reserve also needs a supported source and should not be counted as simultaneously available for another goal. Neither change modifies the locked investment’s gross compound return in this example. Use actual statements and issuer information to reconcile reportable interest, and check current tax guidance before filing or paying. Then build a dated outside-cash plan. The practical lesson is a reconciliation: what has been earned, what is accessible, what must be paid, and which resources can reach the payment date.
c93c02c42bd6c4057656460948fef4fd8e9ae2f4.zh: 利息报告、获得投资现金以及必须缴纳税款的日期是不同的问题。不断增长的锁定余额无法自动支付到期前到期的账单。将利息收入与可动用现金分开复合投资可以赚取利息，而无需将利息存入支票账户。余额在产品内部增长，而家庭的可用现金可能保持不变。如果必须在投资到期之前为与收入相关的付款提供资金，那么这种差异就很重要。 CRA 的第 12100 行指南解释说，即使稍后支付现金且未收到 T5 票据，也可能需要报告每个完整投资年度的定期存款、担保投资证和类似投资的利息。等待到期并不会自动推迟报告所有利息。本文说明了非注册复合投资所产生的现金规划问题。它不计算特定纳税人的纳税申报表或截止日期。注册账户、所有权归属、其他收入、积分和福利效果需要有自己的规则和记录。将投资和外部储备保存在单独的分类账中 该示例投资 100,000 加元，为期五年，假设有效年利率为 4%，每年复利。它假设本金和利息都不能在到期前提取。第一个完成的投资年度增加了 4,000 加元的利息，在锁定投资中留下 104,000 加元。独立假设的 30% 税率会产生当年 1,200 加元的模型税收资金。税金来自投资之外。从 GIC 中扣除它会与所选的禁止进入假设相矛盾，并且还会改变随后的复利。外部分类账从 2,000 加元开始，每个月末收到 50 加元。这些转移是新的家庭储蓄，而不是投资利润。在这种简化的操作中，外部现金赚取零利息。该图将任何负外部余额标记为临时资金缺口。它不会产生透支、贷款或隐性注入资金。存在如此差距的计划需要额外的资金来源支持才能实施。说明融资日期，不要将其误认为是税法。为了提高透明度，该模型在每个完成的投资年度结束时，即当月的准备金转移之后，为假定的税收提供资金。在最终投资年度结束时，它首先收到到期收益，然后为最后建模的税额提供资金。这些日期是经过精心选择的算术日期。已完成的投资年度、日历纳税年度、申报截止日期和纳税截止日期不可互换。实际报告和付款要求必须单独检查，包括任何分期付款义务。 2026 年 10 月 25 日审核的 CRA 页面日期为 2026 年 1 月 20 日，包含 2025 年申报表示例。它支持区分应计利息和收到的现金；它不提供计算器的资金日历或其 30% 输入。对于真实账户，在将现金转移映射到付款日期之前，请确定投资的发行和到期日期、实际利息记录和适用的税收要求。该工具的投资年度标签有意避免声称是日历年的归档时间表。在查看最终支出之前找出短缺情况 前四年增加利息 4,000 加元、4,160 加元、4,326.40 加元和 4,499.46 加元，计算保留四舍五入的精度。他们的模型税收资金总额约为 5,095.76 加元。到第四年年底，外部分类账已收到 2,000 加元的期初准备金加上 48 笔 50 加元的转账，即 4,400 加元。累计模拟纳税后，其临时余额为负 695.76 加元。这是默认情况下最大的提前到期短缺。该家庭需要大约 695.76 加元的额外期初现金（四舍五入为美分）才能满足这些简化的日期而不出现负余额。确切的基本要求是在显示舍入之前计算的。这是对已分配的 2,000 加元的补充。那时投资本身仍在增长。其较大的余额并不能解决无法访问时的现金短缺问题。第一个图表重点关注到期前的外部现金，使早期的短缺保持可见，而不是将其压缩到更大的未来支出旁边。年利息单独显示。在不忽略外部储蓄的情况下调节到期终点 五年后，总利息总额为 21,665.29 加元，到期收益为 121,665.29 加元。模拟的最后一年税收资金约为 1,403.83 加元，使所有五年的模拟税收达到 6,499.59 加元。最后的瀑布从 100,000 加元的投资开始，加上 2,000 加元的外部准备金、3,000 加元的新每月储蓄和 21,665.29 加元的总利息，然后减去所有模型税。算术现金端点约为 120,165.70 加元。该端点包括新的家庭资源，不能被解读为税后仅赚取 20,165.70 加元的投资。回报贡献是总利息减去模型税；期初准备金和每月转账的来源不同。积极的终点也并不能证明早期的计划有效。该计算通过时间来揭示临时资金赤字。稍后到达的到期收益不能追溯结算到期前缺乏现金的付款。使用准备金矩阵测试融资计划 该矩阵会改变假设税率和每月外部分配，保持选定的本金、利率、期限和期初准备金固定。每个细胞都会重新计算最大的提前期短缺。零单元格意味着输入的资源涵盖了这个简化的时间表，而不是证明无需缴纳税款。更大的每月拨款需要家庭预算中有空间。增加的开放储备也需要有支持的来源，并且不应被视为同时可用于另一个目标。在本例中，这两种变化都不会改变锁定投资的总复合回报率。使用实际报表和发行人信息来调节应报告利息，并在提交或付款之前检查当前的税务指导。然后制定一个过时的外部现金计划。实践的教训是对账：已经赚到了什么，可以获取什么，必须支付什么，以及哪些资源可以到达支付日期。

3cc43101f72ba22267aa7c8c1f96819a76453f91.src: A higher later tax-saving rate is only part of the comparison. Earlier cash has a use during the wait, so value both alternatives at the same date. Separate making a contribution from claiming its deduction An RRSP contribution and an RRSP deduction are related records with different roles. A contribution places money into the plan. A deduction is claimed on a tax return within the applicable limit. An amount reported as contributed does not have to be fully deducted on the same return. CRA’s contribution questions and answers explains that unused contributions can be deducted in a future return up to the deduction limit. Its unused-contribution guidance describes reporting the contributions and locating the recorded unused amount. This article examines a narrow timing choice: the same eligible, already-funded contribution and the same deduction amount in both alternatives. It does not compare contributing now with contributing later, or RRSPs with another account. The common RRSP assets are held identical so the charts can isolate the tax-saving cash. Estimate the tax reduction over the whole deduction The default amount is CAD 10,000. A current assumed tax reduction of CAD 25 per CAD 100 deducted produces CAD 2,500. The later assumption of CAD 35 per CAD 100 produces CAD 3,500. These are independently chosen teaching inputs rather than federal or provincial tax brackets. A deduction may cross several tax brackets. Its total income-tax reduction divided by the deduction amount can therefore differ from the marginal rate on the next dollar of income. A real comparison should estimate the return with and without the deduction and review any other affected items separately. No benefit or credit interaction is calculated here. Nor does a tax saving necessarily mean a cheque of that amount: it may reduce an outstanding tax balance. The cash comparison requires an amount that is actually available for the modeled use. Place both amounts at the later cash-availability date Time 0 is the date when the current alternative’s tax-saving cash becomes available. The later amount becomes available four full model years afterward in the default example. These dates are abstractions for cash timing, not a claim that filing a return releases money immediately or that the waiting period equals a particular number of tax returns. If the CAD 2,500 current saving is retained outside the RRSP and earns a constant 5% annually after assumed tax and costs, its value after four years is CAD 2,500 × 1.05⁴ = CAD 3,038.77 . The later CAD 3,500 receipt is therefore CAD 461.23 larger at that same date under the selected assumptions. Comparing CAD 2,500 today directly with CAD 3,500 later omits the use of the earlier cash. Conversely, applying four years of growth to both amounts would give the deferred alternative growth before its cash exists. The line chart compounds only the earlier receipt and shows the later receipt as a final jump. Calculate the later rate needed to cover the wait With a positive deduction amount, equal cash values occur when the later saving rate equals the current saving rate × (1 + opportunity return) raised to the waiting years . The common deduction amount cancels from that comparison. At the defaults, 25% × 1.05⁴ is about 30.39%. A later assumed rate of 30% is higher than 25%, yet its CAD 3,000 saving would be slightly below CAD 3,038.77 at the comparison date. A higher rate by itself does not establish that waiting wins. Change the return to zero to remove this particular opportunity cost. Try a negative return to see the effect of a loss on the retained saving. The constant return is a scenario, not a promise that an investment will provide it. If the earlier saving would be used differently, choose an appropriate comparison rather than assuming this cash account describes the household. Stress the rate and the delay as separate uncertainties The matrix replaces the later assumed tax-saving rate and the waiting period while retaining the other inputs. Each cell compares the two alternatives at that row’s later receipt date. A negative amount favours the current saving’s opportunity value; a positive amount favours the later receipt in this limited calculation. The rows end in different years, so they are not four wealth amounts measured on one common calendar date. They show how each proposed wait changes its own comparison. The matrix assigns no probability to an income rise or a future tax-saving rate. The waterfall explains the selected case: later saving, less the current saving forgone, less the growth on that current saving. This reconciliation helps identify whether an apparent advantage comes from the assumed tax reduction or the treatment of time. Check the deduction record and the household use of the cash CRA identifies unused contributions on the RRSP Deduction Limit Statement and related records. Keep contribution receipts, reported unused amounts and the amount actually deducted distinct. A decision to claim less this year does not create additional contribution room or make an otherwise excessive contribution permissible. Confirm that the chosen deduction is available in the relevant year before applying a timing comparison. The calculator assumes eligibility in both alternatives and does not test room, excess-contribution tax, transfers or repayment designations. It also does not value different future withdrawals because the contribution and RRSP path are common to both cases. Finally, connect the cash choice to the household plan. If the earlier saving is spent, used to repay debt or needed for an upcoming bill, its use differs from the retained account drawn here. Compare that actual use and its dates with the later saving before treating an illustrative dollar difference as a decision.
3cc43101f72ba22267aa7c8c1f96819a76453f91.zh: 较高的后期节税率只是比较的一部分。较早的现金在等待期间会有用处，因此请在同一日期评估这两种选择。将供款与申报扣除分开 RRSP 供款和 RRSP 扣除是具有不同作用的相关记录。捐款将资金投入该计划。在适用限额内的纳税申报表上申请扣除。报告为贡献的金额不必在同一份申报表中完全扣除。 CRA 的供款问题和解答解释说，未使用的供款可以在未来的申报表中扣除，最高可达扣除限额。其未使用捐款指南描述了报告捐款并查找记录的未使用金额。本文研究了一个狭窄的时间选择：两种选择中相同的合格、已资助的捐款和相同的扣除金额。它不会将现在的供款与以后的供款进行比较，或者将 RRSP 与其他帐户进行比较。常见的 RRSP 资产持有相同，因此图表可以隔离节税现金。估计整个扣除额的减税额 默认金额为 10,000 加元。目前假设每扣除 100 加元减税 25 加元，则可得到 2,500 加元。后来假设每 100 加元为 35 加元，结果为 3,500 加元。这些是独立选择的教学投入，而不是联邦或省的税级。扣除额可能跨越多个税级。因此，其所得税减免总额除以扣除金额可能与下一美元收入的边际税率不同。真正的比较应该估计扣除和不扣除扣除的回报，并单独审查任何其他受影响的项目。这里不计算任何利益或信用互动。节税也不一定意味着检查该金额：它可能会减少未缴税款余额。现金比较需要实际可用于建模用途的金额。将这两个金额放在较晚的现金可用日期时间 0 是当前替代方案的节税现金可用的日期。在默认示例中，较晚的金额在四个完整模型年后可用。这些日期是现金时间的抽象，而不是声称提交申报表会立即释放资金或等待期等于特定数量的纳税申报表。如果 2,500 加元的当前储蓄保留在 RRSP 之外，并在扣除假定的税收和成本后每年赚取 5% 的固定利率，则四年后其价值为 2,500 加元 × 1.05⁴ = 3,038.77 加元。因此，根据选定的假设，后来收到的 3,500 加元的收据在同一日期增加了 461.23 加元。将今天的 2,500 加元与后来的 3,500 加元直接进行比较，忽略了之前现金的使用。相反，将四年的增长应用于这两个金额将在其现金存在之前提供递延的替代增长。折线图仅复合较早的收据，并将较晚的收据显示为最终跳转。计算弥补等待所需的后期利率 如果扣除金额为正，则当后期储蓄率等于当前储蓄率 × (1 + 机会回报) 提高到等待年数时，现金价值相等。共同扣除金额从该比较中取消。默认情况下，25% × 1.05⁴ 约为 30.39%。后来假定的 30% 利率高于 25%，但在比较日节省的 3,000 加元将略低于 3,038.77 加元。较高的比率本身并不能证明等待会获胜。将回报更改为零以消除这个特定的机会成本。尝试使用负回报来查看损失对保留储蓄的影响。持续回报只是一种情景，而不是投资能够提供这种回报的承诺。如果早期的储蓄会有不同的用途，请选择适当的比较，而不是假设该现金账户描述了该家庭。强调税率和延迟作为单独的不确定性 该矩阵取代了后来假设的节税率和等待期，同时保留其他输入。每个单元格都会比较该行较晚接收日期的两个备选方案。负金额有利于当前储蓄的机会价值；在这个有限的计算中，正数有利于稍后收到。这些行以不同的年份结束，因此它们不是在一个共同日历日期测量的四个财富金额。它们展示了每个建议的等待如何改变其自身的比较。该矩阵没有分配收入增加或未来节税率的概率。瀑布解释了所选的情况：以后的储蓄，放弃的当前储蓄较少，当前储蓄的增长较少。这种调节有助于确定明显的优势是否来自假设的减税或时间处理。检查现金的扣除记录和家庭使用情况 CRA 在 RRSP 扣除限额声明和相关记录上确定未使用的供款。保留捐款收据、报告的未使用金额和实际扣除的金额。今年减少申报的决定不会创造额外的缴款空间或允许额外的缴款。在应用时间比较之前，请确认所选扣除额在相关年份可用。该计算器假定两种选择均符合资格，并且不测试空间、超额缴款税、转移或还款指定。它也不重视未来不同的提款，因为两种情况的供款和 RRSP 路径是相同的。最后，将现金选择与家庭计划联系起来。如果之前的储蓄被花费、用于偿还债务或需要用于即将到来的账单，则其用途与此处提取的保留帐户不同。在将说明性的美元差异视为决定之前，将实际使用及其日期与后来的节省进行比较。

c5fc478b4fe230e79f6eb253f393c6c8ce559d35.src: A financed insurance premium becomes mortgage principal and carries interest. The down payment, applicable premium tax and other closing costs still require their own cash funding. Identify what is insured and who receives the protection Mortgage default insurance and insurance that pays a household after a death or disability address different risks. The Financial Consumer Agency of Canada explains that mortgage loan insurance protects the lender if the borrower cannot make the mortgage payments. Paying its premium does not create equivalent income protection for the borrower. This distinction matters when building a home-purchase budget. The premium can be part of the borrowing transaction while the household still needs a plan for payments, emergency cash and other risks. Combining all of those protections under one insurance label can obscure what has actually been purchased. The illustration assumes an approved owner-occupied purchase with a traditional down payment. It does not assess a property, borrower, credit record, income qualification or required minimum cash. Its purpose is to reconcile a selected premium with debt and cash, after eligibility has been considered separately. Read the premium percentage against the base loan The fixed reference chart uses three selected rows from CMHC’s published premium table , reviewed on 25 October 2026. Its premium-on-total-loan rates are 2.80% for the published 80.01%–85% loan-to-value band, 3.10% for 85.01%–90%, and 4.00% for 90.01%–95%. These are pricing bands, not average premiums paid by a population or a personalized quote. The chart uses the premium-on-total-loan column; CMHC’s separate portability column is not interchangeable with it. The non-traditional-down-payment row is also outside this illustration. The numerical controls keep the price between CAD 100,000 and CAD 500,000, the down payment between 5% and 19.99%, and amortization at no more than twenty-five years. Those boundaries define the example’s scope rather than a full lending rule. Refunds, surcharges, credits and product-specific adjustments are not modeled. Add the premium once to the opening mortgage The default purchase price is CAD 500,000 and the down payment is 10%, or CAD 50,000. The base loan is consequently CAD 450,000. Its pre-premium loan-to-value ratio is 90%, which selects the 3.10% rate in this simplified schedule. The premium is CAD 450,000 × 3.10% = CAD 13,950 . With the full premium financed, the opening mortgage is CAD 463,950. Applying the rate to the CAD 500,000 property price would use the wrong denominator. Repeatedly applying insurance to the premium-inclusive loan would also misstate this calculation. The stacked bars repeat the calculation at several down-payment percentages while holding the selected price fixed. Each total consists of the base loan plus financed premium. The down payment remains cash supplied by the purchaser and is not added as a third component of mortgage debt. These bars do not establish which down payment creates the best whole-household outcome. Different down payments use different amounts of cash, and real financing offers can also carry different rates or conditions. Isolate the payment and interest attributable to financing the premium The rate assumption is a nominal 5% annually, compounded semi-annually, converted to an equivalent monthly rate. The illustration holds that rate unchanged for a twenty-five-year, 300-payment amortization. There are no prepayments, later charges or renewal-rate changes. At that convention, the mathematical payment on CAD 450,000 of principal is approximately CAD 2,617.22 monthly. Adding the financed premium raises the modeled payment to about CAD 2,698.36, an increment of CAD 81.13 before display rounding. The base-only amount is a calculation reference, not an offer of an otherwise identical uninsured loan. At a common rate and amortization, the payment formula is linear in principal. That lets the tool isolate how much of the full payment corresponds to the additional CAD 13,950. Across 300 unchanged payments, approximately CAD 24,340.17 is attributable to that financed component: CAD 13,950 of premium principal and CAD 10,390.17 of interest. The line chart tracks the remaining premium principal and cumulative interest separately. Neither line should be added again to the original premium as a new opening charge. Build the closing-cash ledger alongside the loan ledger The example begins with CAD 65,000 of available closing cash. It uses CAD 50,000 for the down payment and CAD 5,000 for independently entered other closing costs. The premium-tax input initially equals zero, leaving CAD 10,000 after those modeled payments. Zero is a placeholder rather than a conclusion that no tax applies. Where an independently verified tax on the premium is payable outside the loan, enter its applicable percentage. The calculator multiplies that assumption by the CAD 13,950 premium and deducts the resulting cash payment. Financing the premium means it is already included in mortgage debt. Deducting CAD 13,950 again from this closing-cash ledger would describe paying it twice. By contrast, a tax paid outside the loan or other closing expense needs separate cash funding. A negative waterfall endpoint remains a funding gap; the tool does not repair it with an overdraft or another loan. Other closing costs must exclude the down payment, financed premium and separately entered premium tax to prevent overlap. Check the approved premium and future payment conditions The official premium chart stays fixed while hypothetical price, down payment and financing inputs change. This preserves the difference between a checked public schedule and a scenario built from it. The lender’s actual approved premium and financing details remain the relevant amounts for a live purchase. Confirm which costs are paid at closing, which are financed, and whether any credit, refund or adjustment applies. Verify applicable tax independently; this page supplies no province-specific tax determination. Keep a supported cash reserve separate from funds already committed to completion. Finally, distinguish amortization from the term over which an actual rate is fixed. The twenty-five-year interest total assumes no rate changes merely to make the arithmetic inspectable. Use a separate renewal and household-payment plan for real future obligations. A clear purchase ledger should show the cash used now, the principal borrowed now and the assumptions behind payments made later.
c5fc478b4fe230e79f6eb253f393c6c8ce559d35.zh: 融资的保险费成为抵押贷款本金并附带利息。首付、适用的保费税和其他成交费用仍然需要他们自己的现金融资。确定投保对象以及谁获得保护 抵押贷款违约保险和在死亡或残疾后向家庭付款的保险可解决不同的风险。加拿大金融消费者机构解释说，如果借款人无法支付抵押贷款，抵押贷款保险可以保护贷款机构。支付保费并不能为借款人创造同等的收入保护。在制定购房预算时，这种区别很重要。保费可以作为借贷交易的一部分，而家庭仍然需要一个付款、紧急现金和其他风险的计划。将所有这些保护结合在一个保险标签下可能会掩盖实际购买的内容。该图假设业主自用购买已获批准并支付传统首付。它不评估财产、借款人、信用记录、收入资格或所需的最低现金。其目的是在单独考虑资格后，将选定的保费与债务和现金进行调节。阅读基本贷款的保费百分比固定参考图表使用了 CMHC 发布的保费表中选定的三行，并于 2026 年 10 月 25 日进行了审核。其总贷款溢价率在已发布的 80.01%–85% 贷款价值范围内为 2.80%，在 85.01%–90% 范围内为 3.10%，在 90.01%–95% 范围内为 4.00%。这些是定价范围，而不是人群支付的平均保费或个性化报价。该图表使用总贷款溢价栏； CMHC 的独立便携柱不可与其互换。非传统首付行也在该图之外。数控控制价格在10万至50万加元之间，首付在5%至19.99%之间，摊销期限不超过25年。这些边界定义了示例的范围，而不是完整的贷款规则。退款、附加费、积分和特定于产品的调整未建模。首付按揭加一次溢价默认购房价格为50万加元，首付为10%，即5万加元。因此，基本贷款为 450,000 加元。其预保费贷款价值比率为90%，在此简化表中选择3.10%的利率。保费为 450,000 加元 × 3.10% = 13,950 加元。全额保费融资后，开业抵押贷款金额为 463,950 加元。将此汇率应用于 500,000 加元的房产价格会使用错误的分母。重复为含保费贷款申请保险也会错误地表述这一计算。堆积的条形图以几个首付百分比重复计算，同时保持选定的价格固定。每笔总额包括基本贷款加上融资溢价。首付仍然是买方提供的现金，不会作为抵押贷款债务的第三部分添加。这些标准并不能确定哪种首付可以带来最佳的全家结果。不同的首付使用不同数量的现金，实际融资报价也可能具有不同的利率或条件。分离支付保费的付款和利息 利率假设为名义年利率 5%，每半年复利一次，转换为等值的月利率。该图表明，对于 25 年、300 次付款的摊销，该利率保持不变。没有预付款、后期费用或续订费率变更。在那次大会上，450,000 加元本金的计算支付金额约为每月 2,617.22 加元。添加融资保费后，模型付款额将增加至约 2,698.36 加元，比显示舍入前增加了 81.13 加元。仅基本金额仅供计算参考，而不是提供其他相同的无保险贷款。按照共同利率和摊销法，支付公式原则上是线性的。这使得该工具可以隔离全额付款中有多少对应于额外的 13,950 加元。在 300 笔不变的付款中，大约 24,340.17 加元属于该融资部分：13,950 加元的溢价本金和 10,390.17 加元的利息。折线图分别跟踪剩余溢价本金和累计利息。这两条线均不应作为新的开仓费用再次添加到原始保费中。与贷款分类账一起构建期末现金分类账 该示例以 65,000 加元的可用期末现金开始。它使用 50,000 加元作为首付款，并使用 5,000 加元作为独立输入的其他结账成本。保费税投入最初为零，在这些建模付款后剩下 10,000 加元。零只是一个占位符，而不是不征税的结论。如果独立核实的保费税是在贷款之外支付的，请输入其适用的百分比。计算器将该假设乘以 13,950 加元的保费，并扣除由此产生的现金支付。为溢价融资意味着它已经包含在抵押贷款债务中。从这个期末现金账簿中再次扣除 13,950 加元相当于支付了两次。相比之下，贷款或其他结账费用之外支付的税款需要单独的现金融资。负瀑布终点仍然是资金缺口；该工具不会通过透支或其他贷款来修复它。其他成交成本必须排除首付、融资保费和单独输入的保费税，以防止重叠。检查批准的保费和未来付款条件 官方保费图表保持不变，而假设价格、首付和融资投入发生变化。这保留了检查的公共时间表和根据其构建的场景之间的差异。贷款机构实际批准的保费和融资详细信息仍然是实时购买的相关金额。确认哪些费用在成交时支付、哪些费用已融资，以及是否适用任何抵免、退款或调整。独立核实适用的税费；本页不提供特定于省份的税收确定。将受支持的现金储备与已承诺完成的资金分开。最后，将摊销与实际利率固定的期限区分开来。二十五年的利息总额假设利率没有变化，只是为了使算术易于检查。使用单独的续订和家庭付款计划来履行未来的实际义务。清晰的采购分类账应该显示现在使用的现金、现在借入的本金以及以后付款背后的假设。

2d2d8dd6821bd5fc9f61c1a284eff40ad940b9ed.src: A refundable deposit can still create a cash shortage. Match payments and expected receipts to dates, then fund the lowest point rather than relying on the final total. A move has both a cost budget and a cash calendar A move can look affordable when you subtract an expected deposit refund from the total bill. The payment calendar may tell a different story. Your next landlord may need a deposit while your previous landlord still holds the old one. Movers and extra rent may also be payable before the next amount you can save from income. The Financial Consumer Agency of Canada’s renting guide includes account setup charges, moving services and supplies among the costs to consider. Those categories help build a complete budget. This article adds a second step: assign the cash movements to dates. All amounts in the tool are hypothetical CAD inputs. They are not estimates of local rent, typical moving charges or legally permitted deposits. The six-month window begins when the new deposit is paid; it is not a legal notice or refund period. Keep the regular household budget outside the move ledger The default scenario starts with CAD 2,500 already available for the move. It adds CAD 400 at each month-end. That monthly amount is what remains after regular rent, groceries, utilities, debt payments and other continuing commitments. It is not gross salary or the whole bank deposit from a paycheque. Extra overlap rent is the additional rent caused by carrying both places beyond the regular rent already allowed for in your household budget. Entering both full rental payments here after also deducting regular rent elsewhere would count part of the cost twice. If the new ongoing rent is higher, update your regular budget before choosing the monthly surplus. The assumed old-deposit refund is also separate from the opening cash. Money still held by someone else is not part of the amount available today. If it has already arrived and is included in your opening cash, set the future refund input to zero. Find the low point before counting later receipts The model pays a CAD 1,200 new deposit at the start of month 1. The move pool falls from CAD 2,500 to CAD 1,300, then the month-end surplus raises it to CAD 1,700. At the start of month 2, CAD 2,000 of extra rent and CAD 1,500 of moving/setup costs create a funding position of minus CAD 1,800. That negative number is an unmet need using the selected resources. The model has not arranged a loan or assumed a bank will honour an overdraft. A CAD 1,000 refund at the end of month 3 improves the later arithmetic but cannot pay a bill due at the start of month 2. The line chart shows both the position after bills and the position after receipts. Its default low point is minus CAD 1,800, even though the six-month endpoint is positive CAD 1,200. Looking only at the final balance would miss the earlier financing problem. Calculate the initial amount needed to preserve your selected buffer Choose the cash amount you want to keep available throughout the move. The default is CAD 500 as an illustration, not a prescribed reserve. The required additional initial cash equals the greater of zero and the selected buffer minus the lowest before-receipt funding position . At the defaults, CAD 500 minus negative CAD 1,800 is CAD 2,300. Adding that amount before month 1 would shift every point upward by CAD 2,300 and leave CAD 500 at the modeled low point. The chart continues to show the entered resources so that the original shortfall remains visible; it does not quietly assume you have found the extra money. Possible changes include saving more before committing, reducing quoted moving costs or changing the assumed overlap. Test changes separately to see which payment date they affect. If borrowing is considered, its availability, fees and repayments need a separate household cash plan. Stress the refund without treating a scenario as a legal deadline Move the refund from month 3 to month 5, then choose 7 to put it outside the six-month window. Try a smaller refund as a separate test. These assumptions show how much the plan depends on a receipt whose timing or amount still needs confirmation. A refund outside the chart is not assumed to be permanently lost. Deposit rules and processes depend on the jurisdiction and tenancy. As one local example, British Columbia’s deposit guidance describes condition inspections, a written forwarding address and procedures for returning or retaining deposits. Check the applicable process and actual records before treating a refund as available cash. This calculator determines no entitlement, lawful deposit cap or statutory deadline. The sensitivity matrix counts months when the position before receipts is below your chosen buffer. It does not measure the size of the shortage: two scenarios can have the same count and very different dollar gaps. Read it alongside the low-point metric and the payment chart. Use the endpoint as a reconciliation after checking the dates The waterfall adds opening cash, six monthly transfers and the refund actually scheduled within the window. It subtracts the new deposit, extra rent and moving/setup costs. At the defaults, CAD 2,500 + CAD 2,400 + CAD 1,000 − CAD 1,200 − CAD 2,000 − CAD 1,500 equals CAD 1,200. The new deposit remains tied up throughout these six months. The tool does not assume that it returns on a convenient date, earns interest or can be substituted for a rent payment. Its eventual treatment belongs in the applicable agreement and local rules. Keep a simple dated record of quotations, deposit payments, receipts and expected refunds. Update the plan as amounts become confirmed, while preserving enough cash for payments that arrive first. The useful result is a move schedule you can fund at each step.
2d2d8dd6821bd5fc9f61c1a284eff40ad940b9ed.zh: 可退还的押金仍然可能造成现金短缺。将付款和预期收入与日期相匹配，然后为最低点提供资金，而不是依赖最终总额。搬家同时具有成本预算和现金日历 当您从总账单中减去预期押金退款时，搬家看起来会很实惠。付款日历可能会讲述不同的故事。您的下一位房东可能需要一笔押金，而您的前任房东仍持有旧押金。搬运工和额外租金也可能在您可以从收入中节省下一笔金额之前支付。加拿大金融消费者机构的租赁指南包括账户设置费、搬家服务和用品等需要考虑的成本。这些类别有助于制定完整的预算。本文添加了第二步：将现金变动分配给日期。该工具中的所有金额均为假设的 CAD 输入。它们不是对当地租金、典型搬家费用或法律允许的押金的估计。六个月的窗口从支付新的押金时开始；这不是法律通知或退款期限。将常规家庭预算保留在搬迁分类账之外 默认情况下，从已可用于搬迁的 2,500 加元开始。每个月底增加 400 加元。每月的金额是扣除正常租金、杂货、水电费、债务支付和其他持续承诺后剩下的金额。它不是工资总额或工资支票中的全部银行存款。额外重叠租金是指因将两个地方的租金超出家庭预算中已允许的正常租金而产生的额外租金。在扣除其他地方的正常租金后，在此处输入全额租金，会将部分成本计算两次。如果新的持续租金较高，请在选择每月盈余之前更新您的常规预算。假定的旧存款退款也与开仓现金分开。仍然由其他人持有的钱不属于今天可用的金额的一部分。如果它已经到达并包含在您的期初现金中，请将未来退款输入设置为零。在计算后续收款之前找到最低点 该模型在第 1 月初支付 1,200 加元的新押金。移动池从 2,500 加元下降到 1,300 加元，然后月末盈余将其提高到 1,700 加元。在第 2 个月开始时，2,000 加元的额外租金和 1,500 加元的搬迁/安装费用导致资金头寸为负 1,800 加元。该负数表示使用所选资源未满足需求。该模型没有安排贷款，也没有假设银行会兑现透支。第 3 个月末的 1,000 加元退款改善了后面的算术，但无法支付第 2 月初到期的账单。折线图显示了账单后的头寸和收款后的头寸。尽管六个月的终点为正 1,200 加元，但其默认低点为负 1,800 加元。只看最终余额会忽略早期的融资问题。计算保留所选缓冲所需的初始金额 选择您希望在整个搬迁过程中保持可用的现金金额。默认值为 500 加元（仅供参考），并非规定储备金。所需的额外初始现金等于零和所选缓冲减去最低收款前资金头寸中的较大者。默认情况下，500 加元减去负 1,800 加元等于 2,300 加元。在第 1 个月之前添加该金额将使每个点向上移动 2,300 加元，并将 500 加元留在建模的低点。图表继续显示输入的资源，以便原始短缺仍然可见；它不会悄悄地假设你已经找到了额外的钱。可能的改变包括在承诺之前节省更多，减少报价的搬家成本或改变假设的重叠。单独测试更改以查看它们影响哪个付款日期。如果考虑借贷，其可用性、费用和还款需要单独的家庭现金计划。强调退款，而不将具体情况视为法定期限 将退款从第 3 个月移至第 5 个月，然后选择 7 将其置于六个月窗口之外。尝试较小的退款作为单独的测试。这些假设表明该计划在多大程度上取决于其时间或金额仍需要确认的收据。图表之外的退款不视为永久丢失。押金规则和流程取决于司法管辖区和租赁。作为当地的一个例子，不列颠哥伦比亚省的押金指南描述了状况检查、书面转发地址以及退还或保留押金的程序。在将退款视为可用现金之前，请检查适用的流程和实际记录。该计算器无法确定任何权利、合法存款上限或法定期限。当收据前的头寸低于您选择的缓冲区时，敏感度矩阵会计算月份。它没有衡量短缺的规模：两种情况可能具有相同的数量和截然不同的美元缺口。请与最低点指标和付款图表一起阅读。检查日期后，使用端点作为对账。瀑布添加了期初现金、六个月的转账以及窗口内实际安排的退款。它减去新的押金、额外租金和搬家/安装费用。默认情况下，2,500 加元 + 2,400 加元 + 1,000 加元 - 1,200 加元 - 2,000 加元 - 1,500 加元等于 1,200 加元。新存款在这六个月内一直处于冻结状态。该工具并不假设它会在方便的日期返回、赚取利息或可以替代租金。其最终处理属于适用的协议和当地规则。保留一份简单的、注明日期的报价、押金支付、收据和预期退款记录。金额确认后更新计划，同时保留足够的现金以支付先到的款项。有用的结果是您可以为每一步提供资金的搬家时间表。

7ae7c2cd58b2d703dd955def453e5ca36eea8a48.src: The ask and bid already incorporate the assumed spread. Reconcile the actual cash paid and received before adding costs, and keep trading costs separate from fund expenses and market returns. Define the quote and its denominator An ETF’s displayed price is not a complete trading budget. A buyer may face an ask quote, a seller a bid quote, and either may incur a broker commission. Understanding how those pieces fit together helps distinguish a transaction’s cash cost from the investment’s later performance. This illustration starts with a hypothetical CAD 25 quote midpoint and a full bid–ask spread of 20 basis points of that midpoint. One basis point is 0.01 percentage point, so the full spread is 0.20%. The assumed quotes are symmetric: the ask is CAD 25.025 and the bid is CAD 24.975. Each side is 10 basis points from the midpoint, rather than 20. The full CAD 0.05 spread separates the ask from the bid. The midpoint is just the average of those two quotes; the calculator does not identify it as NAV, an executable price or independently verified fair value. Reconcile the dollars paid and received The example buys 400 whole units at the assumed ask and pays a CAD 5 commission. The units cost CAD 10,010 and the total purchase cash is CAD 10,015 . At this point, the CAD 10 concession relative to midpoint is already embedded in the executed price. Suppose the midpoint remains CAD 25 until a later sale, and the full spread remains 20 basis points. Selling 400 units at the assumed bid produces CAD 9,990 before commission. Deducting the CAD 5 exit commission leaves CAD 9,985 of sale cash. The completed round trip therefore loses CAD 30: CAD 9,985 received less CAD 10,015 paid. The waterfall explains the same result as zero midpoint movement, less CAD 10 of entry spread concession, CAD 10 of exit spread concession and CAD 10 of combined commissions. Do not deduct another full spread from those cash figures. Buying at the ask and selling at the bid has already included it under these assumptions. A commission is an additional charge; a spread concession is a difference between execution price and the chosen reference quote. Separate proportional costs from fixed ticket charges The grouped bars compare independent trades of different unit quantities. Spreads remain the same percentage of the respective quote midpoints. At unchanged midpoint, doubling units doubles the dollar spread concession while keeping its share of entry midpoint notional unchanged. The selected flat commissions behave differently. With one executed order on each side, their combined CAD 10 cost is spread across more units in a larger transaction. The chart expresses both cost components relative to units multiplied by entry midpoint, before commissions, so the denominator is consistent across the bars. This comparison does not recommend increasing a purchase beyond the financial plan. It isolates a fee schedule’s arithmetic. A smaller suitable purchase and a larger unsuitable purchase cannot be ranked by transaction-cost percentage alone. The model permits at least 24 whole units and at most 24 executed orders per side. The same total units can therefore be divided into whole-unit orders without requiring fractional-share trading. It assumes each order receives the same respective quote and incurs the selected flat charge. Read more orders as the same capital divided differently The matrix holds the selected total units fixed while changing the number of executed orders and the spread. Four orders per side do not mean four times as many units or four times the invested capital. They divide the same total quantity into smaller pieces. At the default 400 units, unchanged midpoint and 20-basis-point spreads, four CAD 5 commissions on entry and four on exit total CAD 40. Spread concessions still total CAD 20, producing a CAD 60 net loss. With a zero commission input, splitting the same quantity adds no modeled commission cost. Each matrix row replaces both the entry and exit full spreads with its labelled value. Outside the matrix, the controls allow those two spreads to differ. Real prices and depth may change between orders, so neither view predicts what splitting a live order will cost. Solve the movement needed to recover the modeled costs A small increase in midpoint does not automatically make the completed trade profitable. Under the default assumptions, net sale proceeds equal purchase cash only after the midpoint rises by approximately 0.3003%. The calculation includes both commissions and the exit bid discount from its new midpoint. That threshold is slightly different from dividing CAD 30 by CAD 10,000, because the exit spread concession also grows with the exit midpoint. The tool solves the cash equality directly rather than treating every cost as a fixed opening-dollar amount. The final chart varies midpoint movement and displays net gain or loss after the assumed execution costs. It omits fund distributions, management expenses, taxes, foreign exchange and other account charges. It is therefore a narrow trading reconciliation rather than an ETF’s complete holding-period total return. Treat price protection and execution certainty as separate questions Vanguard Canada’s trading guidance explains that a limit order sets an acceptable execution price but can remain partly or entirely unfilled. It also notes that market conditions and the tradability of underlying holdings can affect ETF spreads. This calculator assumes a complete fill at the selected ask and bid, with enough quoted depth and no market impact. It does not model a limit order’s fill probability, guarantee that a displayed quote remains available, or assume that a limit order eliminates spread costs. For an actual transaction, check the current quote, quantity, broker charges and order terms alongside the investment plan. Keep the quote time and denominator visible when comparing spreads. A clear reconciliation of paid and received cash is useful precisely because it leaves the uncertain execution outcome and the separate investment decision open to proper review.
7ae7c2cd58b2d703dd955def453e5ca36eea8a48.zh: 卖价和买价已经包含了假设的价差。在增加成本之前对实际支付和收到的现金进行核对，并将交易成本与基金费用和市场回报分开。定义报价及其分母 ETF 显示的价格并不是完整的交易预算。买方可能面临要价，卖方可能面临出价，两者都可能产生经纪人佣金。了解这些部分如何组合在一起有助于区分交易的现金成本和投资的后期表现。该图以假设的 25 加元报价中点和该中点 20 个基点的完整买卖价差开始。 1 个基点为 0.01 个百分点，因此全部利差为 0.20%。假设报价是对称的：卖价为 25.025 加元，买价为 24.975 加元。每边距中点 10 个基点，而不是 20 个基点。0.05 加元的完整价差将卖价与买价分开。中点就是这两个报价的平均值；计算器不会将其识别为资产净值、可执行价格或独立验证的公允价值。核对支付和收到的美元 该示例按照假定的要价购买 400 个完整单位，并支付 5 加元的佣金。这些单位的售价为 10,010 加元，购买现金总额为 10,015 加元。此时，相对于中点的 10 加元优惠已经嵌入到执行价格中。假设中点仍为 25 加元，直至稍后出售，而全部利差仍为 20 个基点。按假定出价出售 400 套，佣金前可赚取 9,990 加元。扣除 5 加元的退出佣金，剩下 9,985 加元的销售现金。因此，完成的往返行程损失 30 加元：收到的 9,985 加元减去已付的 10,015 加元。瀑布将相同的结果解释为零中点变动，减去 10 加元的入场价差优惠、10 加元的退出价差优惠和 10 加元的合并佣金。不要从这些现金数字中再扣除全部利差。按要价买入和按出价卖出已经包含在这些假设下。佣金是额外收费；点差优惠是执行价格与所选参考报价之间的差异。将比例成本与固定门票费用分开 分组条比较不同单位数量的独立交易。点差保持各自报价中点的相同百分比。在中点不变的情况下，单位加倍使美元价差优惠加倍，同时保持其名义入场中点份额不变。选定的固定佣金表现不同。双方执行一个订单后，其总成本为 10 加元，分摊到较大交易中的更多单位。该图表表示相对于单位的成本组成部分乘以佣金前的入场中点，因此各条形的分母是一致的。这种比较并不建议增加超出财务计划的购买量。它隔离了费用表的算术。较小的合适购买和较大的不合适购买不能仅根据交易成本百分比来排序。该模型允许每侧至少 24 个完整单位和最多 24 个执行订单。因此，相同的总单位可以分为整单位订单，而无需进行零碎股份交易。它假设每个订单收到相同的报价并产生选定的固定费用。读取更多订单，因为相同的资金划分不同。矩阵保持选定的总单位固定，同时更改执行订单的数量和点差。每方四份订单并不意味着四倍的单位数量或四倍的投资资本。他们将相同的总量分成更小的部分。在默认 400 个单位、中点和 20 个基点点差不变的情况下，入场时收取 4 个 5 加元佣金，退出时收取 4 个佣金，总计 40 加元。利差优惠总计仍为 20 加元，产生 60 加元的净损失。在零佣金输入的情况下，分割相同的数量不会增加建模佣金成本。每个矩阵行都用其标签值替换进入和退出的全部价差。在矩阵之外，控件允许这两个点差不同。订单之间的实际价格和深度可能会发生变化，因此两种视图都无法预测拆分实时订单的成本。解决收回建模成本所需的运动中点的小幅增加不会自动使已完成的交易有利可图。在默认假设下，只有在中点上涨约 0.3003% 后，净出售收益才等于购买现金。该计算包括佣金和新中点的退出报价折扣。该阈值与 30 加元除以 10,000 加元略有不同，因为退出利差优惠也随着退出中点而增长。该工具直接解决现金平等问题，而不是将每项成本视为固定的开盘金额。最终图表会改变中点变动，并显示假定执行成本后的净收益或损失。它省略了基金分配、管理费用、税收、外汇和其他账户费用。因此，这是一个狭义的交易调节，而不是 ETF 的完整持有期总回报。将价格保护和执行确定性视为单独的问题 Vanguard Canada 的交易指南解释说，限价订单设定了可接受的执行价格，但可以部分或完全未执行。它还指出，市场状况和标的资产的可交易性可能会影响 ETF 价差。该计算器假设所选卖价和买价完全成交，具有足够的报价深度并且没有市场影响。它不会对限价订单的成交概率进行建模，不会保证显示的报价仍然可用，也不会假设限价订单消除了点差成本。对于实际交易，请检查当前报价、数量、经纪人费用和订单条款以及投资计划。比较点差时，保持报价时间和分母可见。清楚地核对支付和收到的现金是有用的，因为它使不确定的执行结果和单独的投资决策可以接受适当的审查。

a2b7c282aebb888d43c661fad4acc2c51d1d6401.src: Read the usable cash, growing loan balance and property scenario together. A future arithmetic gap is not a calculation of the liability payable under an actual reverse-mortgage contract. Start with the cash that remains after the initial deductions A reverse mortgage is a loan secured against home equity. The FCAC’s consumer guide describes it for homeowners usually aged fifty-five or older, with eligibility and borrowing amounts depending on the property, owners and lender. These charts do not calculate that eligibility. The first figure starts with a fictional CAD 200,000 gross advance. It deducts CAD 4,000 of upfront costs and CAD 40,000 required to settle an existing secured loan. The result is CAD 156,000 of cash available from this particular funding arrangement. The new debt starts at CAD 200,000. It does not start at CAD 156,000, and the model does not add the fees or old payout to the gross advance again. The deductions explain how the borrowed money is used. If they exceed the advance, the chart shows an initial cash requirement that needs another source; it does not increase approved borrowing automatically. Follow interest added to the balance For this illustration, the nominal annual rate stays at 7%, divided by twelve, and no regular payment or further advance occurs. Each month, interest is added to the modeled balance. The formula after m months is 200,000 × (1 + 0.07/12) m . After fifteen years, the calculated balance is about CAD 569,789.35. Of that amount, CAD 200,000 is the original gross advance and CAD 369,789.35 is accumulated interest. The stacked chart keeps those two components visible over independent elapsed-time scenarios. The interest grows with the balance on which it is charged. It is therefore different from multiplying the original amount by 7% and fifteen years. Monthly capitalization is an explicit teaching convention here, rather than a claim about every lender’s contract. A real rate can change, compounding can differ and additional advances or repayments would alter the path. Give the property its own assumption The home starts at a hypothetical CAD 750,000. With the selected 2% annual value increase, its modeled value after fifteen years is CAD 1,009,401.25. That calculation is independent of the loan’s interest rate. The second chart places home value beside the loan balance. The property is an asset; its assumed appreciation does not itself make a cash payment to the lender. A different value path can leave more or less equity even when the advance and interest terms are unchanged. The smooth line is not a property appraisal, an observed house-price series or a forecast for a neighbourhood. The model also excludes upkeep, insurance, property taxes and the way the household uses its advance. It cannot establish the complete cost of staying in the home or the change in total household wealth. Reconcile a sale before interpreting the remainder At the selected fifteen-year date, assumed selling costs of 4% reduce the CAD 1,009,401.25 modeled sale value by about CAD 40,376.05. That leaves CAD 969,025.20 before settling the loan in this partial reconciliation. Subtracting the uncapped calculated balance of CAD 569,789.35 gives a raw property remainder of about CAD 399,235.86. The fourth figure displays those steps. It excludes other claims, actual closing adjustments, taxes and any contractual repayment charge. This property-only remainder does not add back the initial CAD 156,000 of net proceeds. That money may have been spent, retained or used for another purpose, none of which is tracked here. Counting it as an asset at the future date would require a separate cash and investment ledger. Treat a negative cell as arithmetic before contract protections The final grid changes the constant loan rate and annual home-value assumption independently while preserving the selected gross advance, horizon and selling-cost percentage. Negative cells mean that modeled net sale value is below the uncapped mathematical balance. That difference does not establish that a borrower or estate must pay the shortfall from other assets. For a specifically attributed example, HomeEquity Bank describes a conditional No Negative Equity Guarantee for CHIP . Its stated conditions include maintaining the property, paying property taxes and insurance, and meeting mortgage obligations. It excludes administrative expenses and interest accumulated after the due date. The chart does not reproduce that guarantee or extend it to every product. Simply replacing debt with the smaller of the calculated balance and the modeled sale value would also fail to represent all of those conditions. Actual protections, valuation terms, sale costs, obligations and repayment dates need the signed contract and a lender statement. Put the repayment event and household obligations on a calendar The FCAC’s home-equity borrowing overview identifies sale, moving out, the last borrower’s death and default as repayment events for a reverse mortgage. The actual timing and consequences depend on the agreement. The selected sale year is only a scenario; it is not permission to leave the balance outstanding until that date. Retaining ownership comes with ongoing costs and contractual responsibilities. The absence of a regular mortgage payment in these charts does not fund property taxes, repairs, insurance or a later move. Those obligations belong in the household cash budget alongside any use of the advance. An estate may also face a repayment deadline before every other administrative step is complete. The graphs calculate neither estate administration nor a bridge facility. Record the relevant repayment trigger, required evidence, settlement window and other housing commitments separately from the interest calculation. Bring the complete quote back to the planning question A reviewable quote needs the approved gross advance, any existing secured-debt payout, itemized fees, net proceeds, rate and compounding method, future-advance terms, repayment conditions and available protections. Confirm how any guarantee treats property obligations, due dates and excluded amounts. The personal planning question then needs its own dates and dollars. How much usable cash is required, when is it needed, what recurring housing costs continue, and what cash would be available if the household moves earlier? The model’s one-advance structure cannot answer a plan that needs later borrowing without adding those future cash flows. Keep the fictional sensitivities as a way to inspect the mechanics. Compare actual alternatives with matched cash needs, expenses and ending assets and debts. Neither a large initial advance nor a positive modeled property remainder alone determines whether a reverse mortgage suits a particular retirement plan.
a2b7c282aebb888d43c661fad4acc2c51d1d6401.zh: 一起阅读可用现金、不断增长的贷款余额和房地产情况。未来算术缺口不是根据实际反向抵押合同应付负债的计算。从初始扣除后剩余的现金开始 反向抵押贷款是以房屋净值为担保的贷款。 FCAC 的消费者指南将其描述为通常年龄为 55 岁或以上的房主，资格和借款金额取决于房产、业主和贷款机构。这些图表不计算该资格。第一个数字以虚构的 200,000 加元预付款开始。它扣除 4,000 加元的前期成本和结清现有担保贷款所需的 40,000 加元。该特定融资安排的结果是 156,000 加元的可用现金。新债务起价为 200,000 加元。它的起价不是 156,000 加元，并且该模型不会再次将费用或旧付款添加到预付款总额中。扣除额解释了借来的钱是如何使用的。如果超出预付款，图表会显示初始现金需求，需要其他来源；它不会自动增加批准的借款。跟踪添加到余额中的利息 在此示例中，名义年利率保持在 7% 除以 12，并且不会发生定期付款或进一步预付款。每个月，利息都会添加到模型余额中。 m 个月后的公式为 200,000 × (1 + 0.07/12) m 。十五年后，计算出的余额约为 569,789.35 加元。其中，200,000 加元为原始预付款总额，369,789.35 加元为累计利息。堆叠图表使这两个组件在独立的经过时间场景中可见。利息随着收取的余额而增长。因此，它与原始金额乘以 7% 再乘以 15 年是不同的。每月资本化是这里的明确教学惯例，而不是对每个贷款机构合同的主张。实际利率可能会发生变化，复利可能会有所不同，额外的预付款或还款也会改变路径。给房产一个自己的假设 假设房屋起价为 750,000 加元。按照选定的每年 2% 的价值增长，十五年后其模型价值为 1,009,401.25 加元。该计算与贷款利率无关。第二张图表将房屋价值放在贷款余额旁边。财产是资产；其假定的升值本身并不向贷款机构支付现金。即使预付款和利息条款不变，不同的价值路径也会留下或多或少的净值。平滑线不是财产评估、观察到的房价序列或对社区的预测。该模型还排除了维护费、保险费、财产税以及家庭使用预付款的方式。它无法确定居住在家里的全部成本或家庭总财富的变化。在解释剩余部分之前对销售进行调节 在选定的十五年日期，假设销售成本为 4%，则模型销售价值 1,009,401.25 加元会减少约 40,376.05 加元。在此部分调节中，在结清贷款之前还剩下 969,025.20 加元。减去未上限的计算余额 569,789.35 加元，原始财产余额约为 399,235.86 加元。第四张图显示了这些步骤。它不包括其他索赔、实际结算调整、税费和任何合同还款费用。这笔仅用于财产的剩余部分不会加回最初的 156,000 加元的净收益。这笔钱可能已被花费、保留或用于其他目的，此处均未进行追踪。在未来将其计为资产将需要单独的现金和投资分类账。在合同保护之前将负单元格视为算术最终网格会独立更改恒定贷款利率和年度房屋价值假设，同时保留选定的总预付款、期限和销售成本百分比。负单元格意味着建模的净销售额低于无上限的数学余额。这种差异并不意味着借款人或遗产必须用其他资产来支付缺口。举一个具体的例子，HomeEquity Bank 为 CHIP 描述了有条件的无负资产担保。其规定的条件包括维护财产、缴纳财产税和保险以及履行抵押贷款义务。它不包括管理费用和到期日后累积的利息。该图表并未复制该保证或将其扩展到每种产品。简单地用计算余额和建模销售价值中的较小者替换债务也无法代表所有这些条件。实际的保护、估价条款、销售成本、义务和还款日期需要签署的合同和贷款机构声明。将还款事件和家庭义务列入日历 FCAC 的房屋净值借贷概述将出售、搬出、最后一位借款人的死亡和违约视为反向抵押贷款的还款事件。实际时间和后果取决于协议。所选择的销售年份只是一个场景；在此日期之前不允许保留未清余额。保留所有权需要持续的成本和合同责任。这些图表中没有定期抵押贷款付款，因此无法为财产税、维修、保险或以后的搬家提供资金。这些债务与预付款的任何使用一起属于家庭现金预算。在所有其他行政步骤完成之前，遗产还可能面临还款期限。这些图表既不计算遗产管理，也不计算桥梁设施。将相关还款触发点、所需证据、结算窗口和其他住房承诺与利息计算分开记录。将完整的报价带回规划问题可审查的报价需要批准的预付款总额、任何现有的担保债务支付、逐项费用、净收益、利率和复利方法、未来预付款条款、还款条件和可用的保护。确认任何担保如何处理财产义务、到期日和排除金额。个人规划问题需要有自己的日期和资金。需要多少可用现金、何时需要、持续的经常性住房费用以及如果家庭提早搬家，可以获得哪些现金？该模型的一次性预付款结构无法满足需要稍后借款而不增加未来现金流的计划。保持虚构的敏感性作为检查机制的一种方式。将实际替代方案与匹配的现金需求、支出以及期末资产和债务进行比较。无论是大额初始预付款还是正模型财产剩余，都无法单独决定反向抵押贷款是否适合特定的退休计划。

2f971863c2f6946adc650c8f1ba3a04fd0aad56b.src: Calendar dates help identify which contribution records need review. Determining who reports a withdrawal also requires the applicable tax process and the full relevant history. Identify the contributor and the annuitant before drawing the calendar A spousal or common-law partner RRSP involves two roles. The contributor makes deposits for the other person’s plan, while the annuitant is the person entitled to receive the plan amounts. A useful withdrawal review keeps those roles and the relevant records clear before discussing a tax result. The annual inputs in this tool represent one contributor’s deposits to the same annuitant’s RRSPs across calendar years. They are hypothetical totals, not contribution-room estimates or instructions to make deposits. The annuitant’s own contributions are a separate history and are not silently added to this contributor’s ledger. CRA’s spousal-RRSP withdrawal guidance describes circumstances in which a contributor may report some or all of a withdrawal. The article explains the calendar component of that review without calculating anyone’s income allocation. Build the window from calendar-year labels The reviewed CRA framework considers the withdrawal year and the two preceding calendar years. If the hypothetical withdrawal is in 2029, the displayed review covers 2027, 2028 and 2029. For a 2028 withdrawal, the three labels become 2026, 2027 and 2028. The stacked bars apply that arithmetic to the same entered annual record. Each colour shows one relative year in the review. The bar total is a sum of contribution records to examine. It is not a calculation of attributed income, because no withdrawal amount or full attribution history is supplied to this tool. The controls cover 2025–2031 so every displayed three-year window is complete within the illustration. For an actual review, gather the relevant records across plans rather than looking only at the account from which money will be withdrawn. Verify the applicable rules and tax-year process before acting on a future-date example. Read the month gap without replacing the calendar rule A deposit in December 2026 and an example withdrawal in January 2029 are 25 month labels apart. Yet the 2029 review labels are 2027, 2028 and 2029, which exclude 2026. Moving the example deposit to January 2026 makes the elapsed gap 36 months while leaving the same calendar-year membership. The reverse comparison also matters. A December 2026 deposit and a December 2028 withdrawal are 24 month labels apart, and 2026 remains inside the 2026–2028 review. The amount of time between two dates and the three calendar years selected by the rule should therefore be recorded as separate facts. The calculation is 12 × (withdrawal year − contribution year) + withdrawal month − contribution month . It uses month labels rather than exact days. The fixed matrix compares several 2026 deposit months with several 2029 withdrawal months, while the bar chart uses the months selected in the controls. A later contribution can change the relevant record set The default ledger has CAD 5,000 in 2026 and zero in the other years. The 2027 and 2028 windows include that recorded amount. The 2029 window does not. This is an example of selecting records by year; a zero bar should not be interpreted as a complete tax conclusion. Now enter CAD 2,000 for 2028. The 2029 window includes that later amount even though it still excludes 2026. Focusing on the date of the earliest deposit would miss the newer record. The graph keeps each year separate so that the later contribution is visible. These future annual amounts are planning assumptions. A real review uses deposits actually made and the complete relevant history. The calendar-year ledger is also separate from the year for which a contribution deduction may be claimed. Keep the deposit receipt date rather than inferring it from a deduction on a return. Use the calendar as the start of the income-reporting review CRA provides Form T2205 for determining the income amounts the contributor and annuitant must report in the applicable circumstances. Its published worked example considers a withdrawal and contribution history together. A window total on its own is therefore insufficient to allocate a withdrawal between people. This tool does not model earlier withdrawals or attribution, relationship or residency exceptions, RRIF minimums, specified pension plans or FHSA transfers. It also calculates no withholding or final tax. Those matters should be checked in the applicable current process rather than inferred from the date graphics. For the household cash plan, separately record the gross withdrawal, immediate proceeds, any tax allowance and when the money is required. Read the withholding guide for that distinction. The calendar can improve the record review while the withdrawal’s legal, reporting and cash consequences remain distinct planning questions.
2f971863c2f6946adc650c8f1ba3a04fd0aad56b.zh: 日历日期有助于确定哪些捐款记录需要审查。确定谁报告提款还需要适用的税务流程和完整的相关历史记录。在制定日历之前确定供款人和年金领取人 配偶或同居伴侣 RRSP 涉及两个角色。供款人为他人的计划存入存款，而年金受益人是有权获得计划金额的人。在讨论税务结果之前，有用的提款审查可以使这些角色和相关记录保持清晰。该工具中的年度输入代表一个供款人跨日历年向同一年金受益人的 RRSP 存入的存款。它们是假设的总数，而不是供款室估计或存款指示。年金受益人自己的贡献是一个单独的历史记录，不会默默地添加到该贡献者的分类账中。 CRA 的配偶 RRSP 提款指南描述了供款人可以报告部分或全部提款的情况。这篇文章解释了该审查的日历部分，但没有计算任何人的收入分配。从日历年标签构建窗口 审查后的 CRA 框架考虑了提取年份和之前的两个日历年。如果假设提款是在 2029 年，则显示的回顾涵盖 2027 年、2028 年和 2029 年。对于 2028 年提款，三个标签将变为 2026 年、2027 年和 2028 年。堆叠条形将该算术应用于相同的输入年度记录。每种颜色显示评论中的一个相对年份。栏总数是要检查的贡献记录的总和。它不是归属收入的计算，因为没有向该工具提供提款金额或完整的归属历史记录。控件涵盖 2025-2031 年，因此插图中显示的每个三年窗口都是完整的。对于实际审查，请收集跨计划的相关记录，而不是仅查看将从中提取资金的帐户。在对未来日期的示例采取行动之前，请验证适用的规则和纳税年度流程。读取月份间隙而不替换日历规则 2026 年 12 月的存款和 2029 年 1 月的取款示例相距 25 个月标签。然而，2029 年的审核标签为 2027 年、2028 年和 2029 年，其中不包括 2026 年。将示例存款移至 2026 年 1 月，会使经过的时间间隔为 36 个月，同时保留相同的日历年会员资格。反向比较也很重要。 2026 年 12 月的存款和 2028 年 12 月的取款相隔 24 个月标签，2026 年仍处于 2026-2028 年审查范围内。因此，两个日期之间的时间长度和规则选择的三个日历年应记录为单独的事实。计算公式为：12×（提款年份-缴款年份）+提款月份-缴款月份。它使用月份标签而不是确切的日期。固定矩阵比较了 2026 年的几个存款月份和 2029 年的几个取款月份，而条形图则使用控件中选择的月份。稍后的贡献可以更改相关记录集。默认分类账在 2026 年有 5,000 加元，其他年份为零。 2027 年和 2028 年的窗口期包括该记录的金额。 2029 年窗口则不然。这是按年份选择记录的示例；零标准不应被解释为完整的税收结论。现在输入 2028 年的 2,000 加元。2029 年的窗口包括后来的金额，尽管它仍然排除 2026 年。关注最早存款的日期会错过较新的记录。该图表将每年分开，以便可以看到后来的贡献。这些未来年度金额是计划假设。真正的审查使用实际存款和完整的相关历史记录。日历年分类账也与可以申请缴款扣除的年份分开。保留存款收据日期，而不是从申报表的扣除中推断出来。使用日历作为收入报告审核的开始 CRA 提供表格 T2205，用于确定供款人和年金受益人在适用情况下必须报告的收入金额。其发布的工作示例一起考虑了取款和贡献历史。因此，窗口总额本身不足以在人们之间分配提款。该工具不会对早期提款或归属、关系或居住例外、RRIF 最低限额、指定养老金计划或 FHSA 转移进行建模。它还不计算预扣税或最终税。这些事项应在适用的当前流程中进行检查，而不是从日期图形中推断。对于家庭现金计划，单独记录提款总额、即时收益、任何税收减免以及何时需要这笔钱。请阅读预扣税指南了解这一区别。日历可以改进记录审查，而提款的法律、报告和现金后果仍然是不同的规划问题。

4dd7379e7a8da826e355aaa09cdf4fb74f5b08ab.src: Compare the interest retained after tax with price growth. Keep tax-payment timing and inflation adjustments separate before interpreting an account’s growth. Start with the interest that stays in the account A hypothetical CAD 50,000 accessible savings balance earns 4% gross interest during its first year. That is CAD 2,000 before tax. With an independently assumed 40% combined tax rate on each dollar of interest, the model pays CAD 800 of tax from the same account and retains CAD 1,200. The ending balance is CAD 51,200. Its nominal increase is 2.4%, rather than the 4% gross rate. The tax assumption is deliberately simple: it does not calculate federal or provincial brackets, credits, deductions or benefit reductions for a particular household. The CRA’s interest-income guidance explains reporting interest paid or credited on bank accounts, including income for which no information slip is received. The source supplies reporting context; the calculator’s rate and payment timing remain original assumptions. Divide by price growth to measure purchasing power Under a constant 3% inflation assumption, an amount that bought CAD 50,000 of goods at the start would require CAD 51,500 after one year. The modeled CAD 51,200 balance is higher in dollars but falls short of that purchasing-power benchmark. The exact annual real rate is one plus the after-tax nominal rate, divided by one plus inflation, minus one. Here that is 1.024 divided by 1.03, minus one: approximately negative 0.58%. Simply subtracting 3% from 2.4% gives a nearby approximation, rather than the exact compound relationship. The Bank of Canada’s investment calculator also distinguishes interest and inflation effects when illustrating savings values. This article uses its own model and inputs. Neither the 4% interest assumption nor 3% inflation is a current market observation, a product quote or a forecast. State where the tax money comes from and when it leaves Every modeled year credits interest to the opening balance, then pays tax immediately from that balance. The next year earns interest only on what remains. This convention makes the compounding effect of retained net interest inspectable. Real tax payments follow the applicable reporting and payment requirements. A bank does not necessarily withhold the assumed amount merely because this example subtracts tax at year-end. A household paying tax from employment income would also need to record that outside cash contribution before comparing total household resources. Keep this accessible-savings example separate from a locked investment whose interest is taxable before cash can be withdrawn. The CRA page discusses term deposits and similar investments separately. Use confirmed account terms and actual tax dates when building a funding calendar; the related instalment guide explains why reserving money and paying tax are different events. Compare nominal growth with the same amount of starting-date buying power The line chart shows three labelled paths: a before-tax reference balance, the balance after the modeled annual tax payments, and that after-tax balance expressed in starting-date purchasing power. No path receives new deposits or spending withdrawals. The before-tax reference leaves every gross interest dollar invested. It is a mathematical reference, not an assertion that a registered account is available, appropriate or able to provide the assumed rate. Its extra ending value includes the compounding effect of interest that the taxed account could no longer retain. The real path divides the after-tax balance by the cumulative price-growth factor. Inflation is not a separate invoice deducted from the account. A gap between nominal and real values is a difference in valuation units. Compare the real path with the original principal when asking whether buying power has increased. Reconcile the actual interest ledger before attributing the gap The waterfall begins with initial cash, adds the gross interest actually earned by the taxed account and subtracts the modeled tax actually paid from it. Those steps reconcile exactly to its ending nominal balance. Use that account’s own annual interest amounts. Subtracting its tax from the untouched reference account’s much larger interest total would combine two different balance paths. The tax also changes later interest, so the ending-value difference between paths is not generally equal to the simple sum of tax payments. The chart excludes fees and all personal tax interactions. Its interest and tax totals are cash-model components, not a completed tax return or an amount to copy onto a reporting slip. Reconcile real income to the actual statements and applicable tax guidance before filing. A required break-even rate is a threshold, not an available offer With the model’s assumptions, preserving buying power requires gross interest times one minus the assumed tax rate to equal inflation. At 40% tax and 3% inflation, that implies a 5% gross annual rate. The threshold covers no fee, withdrawal or other cost. The matrix varies the tax and inflation assumptions while retaining the selected gross interest rate. Its cells are annual real rates; principal and the number of years do not change that annual relationship. Those controls do change how many dollars the balance path gains or loses over time. Do not turn the required rate into a reason to accept a product’s risk or restrictions. The household may need accessible cash for near-term payments even when its modeled real return is negative. This example clarifies the trade-off and the cash assumptions without selecting an account, recommending an investment or promising a return.
4dd7379e7a8da826e355aaa09cdf4fb74f5b08ab.zh: 将税后保留利息与价格增长进行比较。在解释账户增长之前，将纳税时间和通货膨胀调整分开。从账户中保留的利息开始 假设可使用的储蓄余额为 50,000 加元，第一年可赚取 4% 的总利息。即税前 2,000 加元。根据独立假设的每美元利息 40% 的综合税率，该模型从同一账户支付 800 加元的税款并保留 1,200 加元。期末余额为 51,200 加元。其名义增长率为2.4%，而不是4%的毛利率。税收假设故意简单：它不计算特定家庭的联邦或省级、抵免、扣除或福利减少。 CRA 的利息收入指南解释了报告银行账户支付或记入的利息，包括未收到信息单的收入。来源提供报告背景；计算器的费率和付款时间仍然是最初的假设。除以价格增长来衡量购买力 在通货膨胀率恒定为 3% 的假设下，一开始购买 50,000 加元的商品，一年后将需要 51,500 加元。模型中的 51,200 加元余额以美元计算较高，但低于购买力基准。确切的年度实际利率是一加税后名义利率除以一加通货膨胀再减一。这里是 1.024 除以 1.03，减一：大约为负 0.58%。只需从 2.4% 中减去 3% 即可得出近似值，而不是精确的复合关系。加拿大央行的投资计算器在说明储蓄价值时还区分了利息和通货膨胀的影响。本文使用自己的模型和输入。 4% 的利率假设和 3% 的通货膨胀都不是当前的市场观察、产品报价或预测。说明税款从何而来以及何时离开 每个模型年度都会将利息计入期初余额，然后立即从该余额中纳税。下一年只赚取剩余部分的利息。这一惯例使得留存净利息的复利效应变得可检验。实际纳税遵循适用的报告和付款要求。银行不一定会仅仅因为该示例在年底扣除税款而扣留假定金额。在比较家庭总资源之前，通过就业收入纳税的家庭还需要记录外部现金贡献。将这种易于储蓄的示例与锁定投资分开，锁定投资的利息在提取现金之前需要纳税。 CRA 页面分别讨论定期存款和类似投资。建立资金日历时使用确认的账户条款和实际纳税日期；相关分期指南解释了为什么存钱和缴税是不同的事件。将名义增长与相同数量的起始日期购买力进行比较 该折线图显示了三个标记路径：税前参考余额、建模年度纳税后的余额以及以起始日期购买力表示的税后余额。没有路径接收新的存款或支出提款。税前参考保留了投资的每一美元总利息。它是一个数学参考，而不是断言注册帐户可用、适当或能够提供假定的汇率。其额外的最终价值包括纳税账户无法再保留的利息的复利效应。实际路径将税后余额除以累计价格增长因子。通货膨胀不单独从发票账户中扣除。名义价值和实际价值之间的差距是估价单位的差异。当询问购买力是否增加时，将真实路径与原始本金进行比较。在归因缺口之前调节实际利息分类账瀑布从初始现金开始，添加纳税账户实际赚取的总利息，并从中减去实际支付的模型税款。这些步骤与其期末名义余额完全一致。使用该账户自己的年利息金额。从未受影响的参考账户的大得多的利息总额中减去税收将结合两种不同的平衡路径。税收也会改变后来的利息，因此路径之间的最终价值差异通常不等于税收支付的简单总和。该图表不包括费用和所有个人税务互动。其利息和税收总额是现金模式的组成部分，而不是完整的纳税申报表或复制到报告单上的金额。在提交之前将实际收入与实际报表和适用的税务指导进行核对。所需的盈亏平衡率是一个门槛，而不是一个可用的报价根据模型的假设，保持购买力需要总利息乘以一减去假定的税率来等于通货膨胀。如果税率为 40%，通货膨胀率为 3%，则意味着年毛利率为 5%。该门槛不包括任何费用、提款或其他费用。该矩阵改变税收和通货膨胀假设，同时保留选定的毛利率。其单元格为年度实际利率；本金和年数不会改变年度关系。这些控制确实会改变平衡路径随着时间的推移获得或损失的美元数量。请勿将要求的利率作为接受产品风险或限制的理由。即使模拟的实际回报为负，该家庭也可能需要可用现金来支付短期支出。该示例阐明了权衡和现金假设，而无需选择账户、推荐投资或承诺回报。

a4f60f2782f747c956e6003e7aeb9be8cf93dc4c.src: Borrowed cash can support today’s spending while the repayment balance grows. Keep the amount received, the debt owed and the uncertain home-sale value in separate parts of the plan. Put the loan proceeds and the liability in different columns A home can be valuable while supplying little cash for monthly bills. Borrowing against it can convert some financing capacity into spendable money, but the cash arrives with a liability. A useful plan therefore tracks both the money delivered and the amount that will eventually need to be addressed. The Financial Consumer Agency of Canada’s reverse-mortgage guide explains that interest is added to the loan and that fees may be financed or paid separately. It also describes different ways of receiving funds. Actual availability and terms depend on the agreement. This calculator isolates those mechanics. It begins with an opening advance, adds specified fees to the loan, then assumes additional month-end advances without regular repayments. These entries are independent assumptions. The tool does not establish that a borrower qualifies or that a lender would authorize the selected cash schedule. Reconcile the opening advance with financed fees The default home value is CAD 750,000. The borrower receives CAD 150,000 at the start, while CAD 5,000 of costs are added to the opening loan. The initial liability is consequently CAD 155,000 , even though the borrower receives only CAD 150,000 of cash. Those financed fees are not an additional cash advance available for household spending. They nevertheless become part of the balance on which the hypothetical loan interest accumulates. Paying them separately would require a different opening cash plan and a smaller financed balance. The illustration then adds CAD 500 of borrowed cash at each month-end for fifteen years. Those 180 advances total CAD 90,000. Combined with the initial cash, the borrower receives CAD 240,000 over the full period. The amounts are nominal CAD and have not been adjusted for purchasing power. A fixed CAD 500 advance may buy less in later years. The calculator also does not assume those advances are savings: their later spending, retention or investment is outside this loan ledger. Follow the compounding debt separately from cumulative cash The selected interest assumption is a constant 7% effective annual rate. It is converted to an equivalent monthly rate using 1.07 to the power of one-twelfth, less one. Each month, interest first accrues on the opening balance; the new CAD 500 advance is then added. After fifteen years, the modeled loan reaches approximately CAD 583,202.27. Its components are CAD 150,000 of opening cash borrowed, CAD 5,000 of financed fees, CAD 90,000 of later advances and CAD 338,202.27 of accrued interest. The first chart compares that debt balance with cumulative cash received. The widening gap is financed fees plus interest, rather than additional spending money. A month without a regular repayment can still add to the amount owed. The effective-rate convention is explicit so the arithmetic can be checked. A quoted product might use a different compounding convention, change rates, charge further fees or restrict advances. This model does not convert an advertisement into a contractual repayment schedule.
