Read the future sale bridge before calling an amount equity The independent home-value assumption is 2% growth each year. It takes CAD 750,000 to approximately CAD 1,009,401.25 after fifteen years. Hypothetical sale costs of 5% use about CAD 50,470.06, leaving CAD 958,931.19 before addressing the loan. Subtracting the modeled CAD 583,202.27 balance leaves an arithmetic sale-value residual of approximately CAD 375,728.92. The waterfall shows the same subtraction using each component of the debt, so financed fees and later cash advances do not disappear inside a single endpoint. This residual is not cash automatically available while the owner continues living in the home. It assumes a sale at the illustrated value and cost percentage. Other secured debts, tax, penalties, legal costs and estate obligations could require further adjustments. Nor is it a complete household-net-worth comparison. Previously advanced money may have been spent or may still exist elsewhere. Without tracking those uses and assets, comparing only the home residual with an unborrowed home would leave out part of the household’s financial history. Vary the loan rate and home-value path independently The matrix keeps the opening home, advances, fees, horizon and sale-cost assumption fixed. Rows change annual home-value growth and columns change the effective annual loan rate. Each cell is a separate possible arithmetic path, with no probability assigned to it. A home-value assumption does not change the loan’s compounding rate. Likewise, slower home appreciation does not automatically reduce the amount owed in the model. Keeping these assumptions independent makes the effect of each visible. Negative residuals remain negative rather than being hidden at zero. They identify a gap between hypothetical sale proceeds and the modeled balance. They do not determine a borrower’s legal shortfall obligation or apply any contractual no-negative-equity protection. Those questions require the actual agreement and applicable rules. Try a zero loan rate as an accounting check: the closing balance equals total cash advanced plus financed fees. That scenario isolates principal accumulation; it is not presented as an available loan offer. Connect the debt projection with a dated housing and cash plan FCAC describes repayment events including selling, moving out, the last borrower’s death and default, with timing and conditions governed by the agreement. A chosen fifteen-year chart horizon therefore cannot be treated as a guaranteed period before repayment is required. For an actual plan, identify what could change the living arrangement, what continuing home costs remain, and how a repayment event would be funded. Confirm draw availability, interest conventions, fees and relevant conditions rather than assuming that today’s terms extend unchanged for decades. Compare the resulting cash plan with supported alternatives, including different housing arrangements or other suitable financing. The graphs do not select an option. They make today’s borrowing and its later balance visible together, so the decision can be assessed alongside future housing needs and the resources that remain available.
a4f60f2782f747c956e6003e7aeb9be8cf93dc4c.zh: 借来的现金可以支持今天的支出，同时还款余额也会增加。将收到的金额、所欠的债务和不确定的房屋销售价值分别放在计划的不同部分中。将贷款收益和负债放在不同的栏目中 房屋可能很有价值，但每月提供的现金很少。以它为抵押借款可以将一些融资能力转化为可支配资金，但现金到来时会带来负债。因此，一个有用的计划应该跟踪已交付的资金和最终需要解决的金额。加拿大金融消费者机构的反向抵押贷款指南解释说，利息会添加到贷款中，并且费用可以单独融资或支付。它还描述了接收资金的不同方式。实际可用性和条款取决于协议。这个计算器隔离了这些机制。它从期初预付款开始，在贷款中添加指定的费用，然后在没有定期还款的情况下承担额外的月末预付款。这些条目是独立的假设。该工具并不能确定借款人是否符合资格或贷款人是否会授权选定的现金计划。将预付款与融资费用进行核对 默认房屋价值为 750,000 加元。借款人在开始时收到 150,000 加元，同时在期初贷款中添加 5,000 加元的费用。因此，即使借款人仅收到 150,000 加元的现金，初始负债仍为 155,000 加元。这些融资费用并不是可用于家庭支出的额外现金预支。然而，它们成为假设贷款利息累积的余额的一部分。单独支付将需要不同的期初现金计划和较小的融资余额。然后，该插图在十五年的每个月末添加了 500 加元的借入现金。这 180 笔预付款总计 90,000 加元。加上初始现金，借款人在整个期限内可获得 240,000 加元。这些金额为名义加元，未根据购买力进行调整。固定的 500 加元预付款可能会在以后的几年中购买更少的东西。计算器也不假设这些预付款是储蓄：它们后来的支出、保留或投资不在此贷款分类账之外。将复利债务与累积现金分开跟踪。选定的利率假设为 7% 的恒定有效年利率。使用 1.07 的十二分之一次方（减一）将其转换为等效的月费率。每个月，利息首先根据期初余额产生；然后添加新的 500 加元预付款。十五年后，模型贷款达到约 583,202.27 加元。其组成部分包括 150,000 加元的期初借入现金、5,000 加元的融资费用、90,000 加元的后期预付款和 338,202.27 加元的应计利息。第一张图表将债务余额与累计收到的现金进行了比较。不断扩大的差距是由费用加利息提供的，而不是额外的支出。一个月不定期还款仍然会增加欠款。有效率约定是明确的，因此可以检查算术。报价产品可能会使用不同的复利惯例、更改利率、收取更多费用或限制预付款。该模型不会将广告转换为合同还款计划。在调用金额权益之前，请先阅读未来的销售桥梁。独立房屋价值的假设是每年增长 2%。十五年后，需要 750,000 加元，大约为 1,009,401.25 加元。假设 5% 的销售成本大约需要 50,470.06 加元，在解决贷款之前还剩下 958,931.19 加元。减去模型中的 583,202.27 加元余额，算术销售价值剩余约为 375,728.92 加元。瀑布显示使用债务的每个组成部分进行相同的减法，因此融资费用和后来的现金预付款不会在单个端点内消失。当业主继续住在家里时，这笔剩余费用不会自动成为现金。它假设按所示的价值和成本百分比进行销售。其他担保债务、税收、罚款、法律费用和遗产义务可能需要进一步调整。它也不是完整的家庭净资产比较。先前预付的资金可能已被花掉或可能仍存在于其他地方。如果不跟踪这些用途和资产，仅将房屋剩余与未借用的房屋进行比较就会遗漏家庭的部分财务历史。独立改变贷款利率和房屋价值路径 该矩阵保持期初房屋、预付款、费用、期限和销售成本假设固定。行改变年度房屋价值增长，列改变有效年度贷款利率。每个单元格都是一个单独的可能算术路径，没有为其分配概率。房屋价值假设不会改变贷款的复利率。同样，房屋升值速度放缓并不会自动减少模型中的欠款金额。保持这些假设的独立性可以使每个假设的效果可见。负残差仍然为负，而不是隐藏为零。他们确定了假设的销售收入与模型余额之间的差距。他们不确定借款人的法定短缺义务或应用任何合同无负资产保护。这些问题需要实际协议和适用规则。尝试使用零贷款利率作为会计检查：期末余额等于预支现金总额加上融资费用。这种情况隔离了本金积累；它不作为可用贷款报价提供。将债务预测与有日期的住房和现金计划联系起来 FCAC 描述了还款事件，包括出售、搬出、最后一位借款人的死亡和违约，以及协议规定的时间和条件。因此，所选择的十五年图表期限不能被视为需要还款之前的保证期。对于实际计划，请确定哪些因素可能会改变生活安排、剩余的持续住房费用以及如何为还款活动提供资金。确认提款可用性、利息约定、费用和相关条件，而不是假设今天的条款几十年不变。将最终的现金计划与支持的替代方案进行比较，包括不同的住房安排或其他合适的融资。图表未选择任何选项。它们使今天的借款和后来的余额一起可见，因此可以根据未来的住房需求和剩余可用资源来评估决策。

433429c3a464971b4c73e453cec304b1c7d53055.src: Read the denominator before judging a spending share. A ratio can change because the bill changes, because other spending changes, or because income changes. Keep the year, household population and statistic visible Statistics Canada’s 2023 Survey of Household Spending release , dated 21 May 2025, compares households grouped into income quintiles. This article retains that dated release’s figures. It does not describe current prices or claim to reproduce the latest revised statistical table. Canada-level estimates cover the provinces, with territorial capitals reported separately. The release uses current nominal dollars, includes sales taxes and generally averages a category across households with and without spending on it. The displayed annual amounts are means, not medians. A quintile comparison describes different groups. It is not an experiment in which the same household receives a pay rise while everything else stays fixed. Household size, age, housing circumstances and location can differ. No causal effect or confidence interval is estimated here. A share of consumption is not a share of income The grouped chart reproduces selected shelter, food and transportation shares for the lowest and highest income quintiles. Their denominator is total current consumption. The three displayed categories are part of a larger spending basket; they do not constitute a complete income budget. Suppose a separate hypothetical household spends CAD 2,200 on housing and CAD 2,800 on the other categories it has selected. Housing represents 44% of that CAD 5,000 spending total. If take-home cash is CAD 6,000, the same bill represents approximately 36.67% of take-home cash. Both calculations can be correct because they answer different questions. The first describes the composition of selected spending. The second compares one payment with a cash receipt. Neither percentage can be compared directly with a published ratio until its denominator and cost coverage have been matched. Put a percentage beside the size of its spending basket The second official chart shows the annual average consumption totals for the two income groups. A lower category share can belong to a substantially larger total. Reading the percentage alone cannot tell us which group spends fewer dollars on that category. For an independent arithmetic example, 35% of CAD 3,000 is CAD 1,050. By contrast, 30% of CAD 8,000 is CAD 2,400. The second share is five percentage points lower, yet the resulting dollar amount is CAD 1,350 higher. These are authored monthly numbers, not reconstructed survey households. Do not multiply rounded published shares by unrelated income estimates to create an official dollar bill. Even multiplying a reported rounded share by its matching spending total produces an approximation, rather than a separately observed household amount. The charts retain the source’s reported shares and reported totals as distinct measures. A rising housing share can accompany an improving cash balance The editable default has CAD 6,000 of take-home cash and CAD 5,000 of selected monthly spending: CAD 2,200 housing, CAD 900 food, CAD 700 transportation and CAD 1,200 other spending. The waterfall leaves CAD 1,000 before any unentered uses. Now reduce other selected spending by CAD 500 while keeping housing and income unchanged. Selected spending becomes CAD 4,500 and the cash remainder rises to CAD 1,500. Housing’s share of selected spending increases to approximately 48.89%, even though the housing bill has not increased and more cash remains. This is a denominator effect. A ratio that looks less favourable in isolation may coexist with an improved cash position. Keep the actual bill, the comparison total and the cash remainder beside the percentage. A spending-share target alone cannot explain affordability or distinguish a rising cost from a falling denominator. Treat the remainder as money still needing a complete allocation The monthly exercise is independent of the survey. It uses selected cash amounts without asserting an exact mapping to statistical consumption definitions. Keep the inputs non-overlapping: a transport cost included in the transport field should not appear again in other spending. The remainder is not automatically saving. It must still cover every omitted use, such as debt principal payments, goal contributions, irregular bills or tax not already reflected in take-home cash. If an item is already inside an entered amount, do not subtract it again merely because it appears in that checklist. The matrix varies housing spending and take-home cash, retaining food, transport and other selected spending. Negative cells show a funding gap. Positive cells show cash before unentered uses. It does not assign an income quintile, recommend a housing percentage or establish that every payment is funded on its actual due date. Use group statistics to ask a better household question When a comparison attracts attention, write down the group, year, unit and denominator. Ask whether it is a mean or median, whether the spending category includes nonspenders and whether the figure measures annual consumption, monthly cash flow or income. Resolve those differences before treating a gap as a problem to fix. Then work from actual receipts and bills. A household may deliberately spend more in one category while having lower obligations elsewhere. Another may have a modest percentage but little cash available after required payments. Group membership cannot settle either case. Use the source charts for context and the cash model for an inspectable arithmetic example. For implementation, extend the budget to all commitments and put their dates beside income receipts. Review both dollars and ratios when circumstances change, rather than assuming a lower percentage necessarily means a smaller bill or a stronger financial position.
433429c3a464971b4c73e453cec304b1c7d53055.zh: 在判断支出份额之前先阅读分母。比率可能会因为账单变化、其他支出变化或收入变化而变化。保持年份、家庭人口和统计数据可见加拿大统计局于 2025 年 5 月 21 日发布的 2023 年家庭支出调查对按收入五分位数分组的家庭进行了比较。本文保留了该日期发布的数据。它没有描述当前价格或声称复制最新修订的统计表。加拿大层面的估计涵盖各省，并单独报告地区首府。该报告使用当前的名义美元，包括销售税，并且通常对有和没有支出的家庭进行平均。显示的年度金额是平均值，而不是中位数。五分位比较描述了不同的群体。这并不是一个让同一家庭加薪而其他一切保持不变的实验。家庭人数、年龄、住房环境和地点可能有所不同。这里没有估计因果效应或置信区间。消费的份额不是收入的份额 分组图表再现了最低和最高收入五分位数的选定住房、食品和交通份额。它们的分母是总电流消耗。显示的三个类别是更大支出篮的一部分；它们并不构成完整的收入预算。假设一个单独的假设家庭在住房上花费 2,200 加元，在其选择的其他类别上花费 2,800 加元。住房支出占 5,000 加元总支出的 44%。如果带回家的现金为 6,000 加元，则同一张钞票约占带回家现金的 36.67%。两种计算都可能是正确的，因为它们回答了不同的问题。第一个描述了选定支出的构成。第二个将一笔付款与现金收据进行比较。在其分母和成本覆盖范围匹配之前，这两个百分比都不能直接与公布的比率进行比较。在支出篮子规模旁边写上百分比 第二个官方图表显示了两个收入群体的年平均消费总额。较低类别的份额可能属于更大的总数。仅仅阅读百分比并不能告诉我们哪个群体在该类别上花费的钱更少。对于一个独立的算术示例，3,000 加元的 35% 是 1,050 加元。相比之下，8,000 加元的 30% 就是 2,400 加元。第二个份额低 5 个百分点，但最终金额却高出 1,350 加元。这些是每月编写的数字，而不是重建的调查家庭。不要将四舍五入的公布股票乘以不相关的收入估计来创建官方美元钞票。即使将报告的四舍五入份额乘以其匹配的支出总额也会产生近似值，而不是单独观察的家庭金额。这些图表保留了来源报告的份额和报告的总数作为不同的衡量标准。住房份额的增加可以伴随着现金余额的改善可编辑的默认值有 6,000 加元的带回家现金和 5,000 加元的选定每月支出：2,200 加元的住房、900 加元的食品、700 加元的交通和 1,200 加元的其他支出。瀑布在任何未输入的使用之前留下 1,000 加元。现在将其他选定支出减少 500 加元，同时保持住房和收入不变。指定消费金额变为 4,500 加元，现金余额增加至 1,500 加元。尽管住房费用没有增加并且还有更多现金，但住房在特定支出中所占的份额增加到约 48.89%。这是分母效应。单独来看不太有利的比率可能与现金状况的改善并存。将实际账单、比较总额和现金余额保留在百分比旁边。仅凭支出份额目标无法解释承受能力或区分成本上升与分母下降。将剩余部分视为仍需要完整分配的资金 每月的操作与调查无关。它使用选定的现金金额，而不断言与统计消费定义的精确映射。保持投入不重叠：运输字段中包含的运输成本不应再次出现在其他支出中。剩余部分不会自动保存。它仍然必须涵盖所有遗漏的用途，例如债务本金还款、目标捐款、不规则账单或尚未反映在实得现金中的税收。如果某个项目已经在输入的金额内，请勿仅仅因为它出现在该清单中而再次减去它。该矩阵改变了住房支出和带回家的现金，保留食品、交通和其他选定的支出。阴性细胞显示资金缺口。阳性细胞显示未输入的使用前的现金。它没有分配收入五分位，建议住房百分比或确定每笔付款均在实际到期日提供资金。使用群体统计数据提出更好的家庭问题 当比较引起注意时，写下群体、年份、单位和分母。询问它是平均值还是中位数，支出类别是否包括非支出者，以及该数字是否衡量年度消费、每月现金流或收入。在将差距视为需要解决的问题之前先解决这些差异。然后根据实际收据和账单进行工作。一个家庭可能会故意在某一类别上花费更多，而在其他类别上承担较少的义务。另一种可能比例不大，但在要求付款后可用的现金很少。团体成员资格不能解决这两种情况。使用源图表作为上下文，使用现金模型作为可检查的算术示例。为了实施，将预算扩展到所有承诺，并将其日期放在收入收据旁边。当情况发生变化时，审查美元和比率，而不是假设较低的百分比必然意味着较小的账单或更强的财务状况。

7b8c4f790a2957faed246d82a4968dae95713860.src: A steady monthly payment changes cash timing. It does not cap the cost of energy or turn a provider credit into cash already available in your bank account. Check what the actual payment plan reviews An equal-payment arrangement can make utility payments easier to budget, but the instalment is not necessarily the final cost of the service. A household needs to track both the payment schedule and the cost accumulating behind it. BC Hydro’s public customer-service summary , reviewed on 25 October 2026, describes instalments informed by past usage, reviews every four months and an anniversary reconciliation that may produce an additional charge or a credit. Its Electric Tariff controls if the summary conflicts with the tariff. The calculator is an original generic illustration with twelve fixed instalments and a settlement afterward. It does not simulate BC Hydro’s review process, anniversary invoice, tariffs or account rules. Use the actual provider’s current bill and terms when building a real payment calendar. Show monthly cost separately from the amount paid The reference annual all-in cost is CAD 2,400. The selected 15% increase brings the modeled annual cost to CAD 2,760. That total includes whatever taxes and charges the user has already allowed for; the calculator adds no tariff or tax amount of its own. An authored seasonal pattern allocates the cost across twelve abstract months. Its weights add to twelve. The first month has a weight of 1.5, so its allocated cost is CAD 345: CAD 2,760 divided by twelve and multiplied by 1.5. This is a mathematical allocation, not a weather forecast, meter reading or issued bill. The instalment remains CAD 200 per month. After the first allocated cost and payment, the provider ledger is positive CAD 145. This interim difference is not treated as an overdue bill under the hypothetical arrangement. It simply records cost accumulated beyond the instalments paid so far. Keep the household reserve outside the provider account The second path chart separates that provider balance from cash reserved by the household. The default reserve begins at zero and receives CAD 30 at every month-end. It reaches CAD 360 before the assumed settlement, with no interest. The provider balance equals cumulative allocated cost less cumulative instalments. Positive means cost exceeds payments; negative means payments exceed cost. The household reserve is money still held separately, ready to help pay a positive settlement charge. These are different ledgers. Do not add an overpayment credit to household cash as if it were a refund already received. Likewise, setting aside CAD 30 does not itself pay CAD 30 to the utility. The household must fund both the CAD 200 instalment and the CAD 30 reserve transfer during the month. Reconcile the full year before deciding what extra cash is needed Twelve CAD 200 instalments total CAD 2,400. Against the CAD 2,760 modeled cost, the provider balance is an extra CAD 360 charge. The waterfall shows this reconciliation without deducting the household reserve, because that cash has not yet been paid. The separate CAD 360 reserve can fund the charge in the default, leaving no additional funding gap. The model assumes all twelve reserve transfers arrive before the extra settlement is due. If the real charge arrives earlier, a future transfer cannot fund it retroactively; the dates need to be changed in the household plan. For a credit example, change annual cost growth to negative 10%. Modeled cost becomes CAD 2,160, leaving a CAD 240 provider credit after CAD 2,400 of instalments. The calculator retains that credit on the provider ledger and leaves the household reserve untouched. It assumes no cash refund or automatic withdrawal right. A larger instalment can reduce settlement without reducing consumption cost The matrix varies the annual cost change down the rows and the monthly instalment across columns. It retains the selected reference cost, opening cash reserve and monthly reserve saving. Every cell reports extra cash needed after the available reserve has funded any positive settlement charge. A zero cell can arise because instalments already cover the annual cost or because the separate reserve covers the difference. It does not mean that energy became cheaper. Raising the instalment can exchange a smaller later charge for larger earlier cash payments. Check that earlier commitment against the rest of the budget. A plan that avoids a year-end shortage by making monthly payments unaffordable has shifted the problem. An actual provider may adjust instalments during its review process; the fixed schedule here deliberately holds that mechanism constant so its arithmetic remains visible. Use the actual tracker and a dated settlement plan Review the bill’s current usage, instalments billed, payments received, balance and review date. An opening credit, missed payment or change in occupancy can affect a real account. None is silently inserted into this clean-start illustration. Update the annual cost estimate when supported information changes, then reconcile the remaining payment schedule and reserve transfers. Separate known bills from uncertain usage changes. Keep enough detail to explain why the projected settlement moved rather than treating every difference as a rate increase. The model excludes interest, late fees, rebates and borrowing. Its seasonal allocation does not estimate physical electricity consumption or the savings from an upgrade. The planning task is to fund the payments when they arrive, preserve the distinction between provider credit and household cash, and check whether the reserve is available before the actual annual adjustment becomes due.
7b8c4f790a2957faed246d82a4968dae95713860.zh: 稳定的每月付款会改变现金时间。它不会限制能源成本，也不会将提供商信用转化为您银行帐户中已有的现金。检查实际付款计划的审查内容 等额付款安排可以使公用事业付款更容易预算，但分期付款不一定是服务的最终成本。家庭需要跟踪付款时间表及其背后累积的成本。 BC Hydro 的公共客户服务摘要于 2026 年 10 月 25 日审核，描述了根据过去使用情况通知的分期付款、每四个月审核一次以及可能产生额外费用或积分的周年对账。如果摘要与关税相冲突，其电力关税将进行控制。该计算器是一个原始的通用插图，有十二笔固定分期付款和随后的结算。它不模拟 BC Hydro 的审查流程、周年发票、关税或账户规则。构建真实的付款日历时，请使用实际提供商的当前账单和条款。将每月费用与支付金额分开显示 参考年度总费用为 2,400 加元。选定的 15% 增幅使模型年度成本达到 2,760 加元。该总额包括用户已经允许支付的任何税费；该计算器不添加自己的关税或税额。编写的季节性模式将成本分配到十二个抽象月份。它的重量加起来是十二。第一个月的权重为 1.5，因此其分配成本为 345 加元：2,760 加元除以 12 再乘以 1.5。这是一种数学分配，而不是天气预报、抄表或开具的账单。分期付款仍为每月 200 加元。在第一次分配成本和付款后，提供商分类帐为正 145 加元。根据假设安排，此中期差异不会被视为逾期账单。它只是记录迄今为止已支付的分期付款之外的累计成本。将家庭储备金保留在提供者账户之外 第二个路径图将提供者余额与家庭保留的现金分开。默认储备金从零开始，并在每个月末收到 30 加元。在假定结算前达到 360 加元，无利息。提供者余额等于累计分配成本减去累计分期付款。积极意味着成本超过支付；负数意味着付款超过成本。家庭准备金仍然是单独持有的资金，准备帮助支付正数的结算费用。这些是不同的分类账。不要将多付信用额添加到家庭现金中，就像已收到退款一样。同样，预留 30 加元本身并不向公用事业公司支付 30 加元。该家庭必须在当月支付 200 加元的分期付款和 30 加元的储备金转账。在决定需要多少额外现金之前核对全年情况 十二笔 200 加元的分期付款总计 2,400 加元。相对于 2,760 加元的模拟成本，提供商余额是额外的 360 加元费用。瀑布显示了这种调节，但没有扣除家庭准备金，因为现金尚未支付。单独的 360 加元储备金可以为违约时的费用提供资金，不会留下额外的资金缺口。该模型假设所有十二笔储备金转账均在额外结算到期之前到达。如果实际费用提前到达，则未来的转账无法追溯提供资金；家庭计划中的日期需要更改。以信贷为例，将年度成本增长率更改为负 10%。模型成本变为 2,160 加元，在分期付款 2,400 加元后留下 240 加元的提供商信用额。计算器将该信用保留在提供者分类账上，并且家庭储备不变。它不承担现金退款或自动提款权。较大的分期付款可以在不降低消费成本的情况下减少结算。该矩阵沿行改变年度成本变化，沿列改变每月分期付款。保留选定的参考成本、期初现金储备和每月储备储蓄。在可用储备金支付任何正结算费用后，每个单元都会报告所需的额外现金。可能会出现零单元，因为分期付款已经涵盖了年度成本，或者因为单独的储备金涵盖了差额。这并不意味着能源变得更便宜。提高分期付款额可以用较小的后期费用换取较大的早期现金付款。检查先前的承诺与预算的其余部分。一项通过让每月付款变得难以负担来避免年底短缺的计划已经转移了这个问题。实际提供商可能会在审核过程中调整分期付款；这里的固定时间表故意保持该机制不变，因此其算术仍然可见。使用实际跟踪器和注明日期的结算计划查看账单的当前使用情况、分期付款、收到的付款、余额和审核日期。开仓信用、错过付款或入住情况发生变化都会影响真实账户。没有一个被默默地插入到这个干净启动的插图中。当支持的信息发生变化时更新年度成本估算，然后协调剩余的付款计划和储备金转移。将已知账单与不确定的使用变化分开。保留足够的细节来解释为什么预计的和解发生变化，而不是将每个差异都视为费率上涨。该模型不包括利息、滞纳金、回扣和借款。其季节性分配不会估计实际用电量或升级节省的费用。规划任务是在付款到达时为其提供资金，保留提供者信贷和家庭现金之间的区别，并在实际年度调整到期之前检查准备金是否可用。

3d393908064ae1d94b67cee64d66c925450f0a26.src: A distribution moves value out of the fund. Read the remaining investment together with the cash received, and distinguish the payment schedule from the return earned. Keep three different measurements in view A fund can send cash to its investors while its unit value declines. That combination raises a useful question: how much value remains in the investment, how much has moved outside it, and how have the two together changed? Looking at only the payout or only the unit price leaves part of the answer out. A distribution is a payment from a fund to its holders. Net asset value, or NAV, describes the value remaining per unit. Total return measures investment performance with distributions included under the stated calculation convention. These measurements have different denominators and should not be substituted for one another. The SEC’s fund-distributions bulletin explains the general mechanics: payments transfer value to holders, reinvestment buys additional shares, and a high distribution rate does not establish strong performance. This article uses those mechanics in an independent CAD illustration; it does not apply U.S. reporting or tax rules to Canadian accounts. Define the cash schedule before comparing percentages The illustration begins with CAD 100,000 invested at a hypothetical NAV of CAD 10, giving the holder 10,000 units. The selected scheduled annual distribution is 8% of the initial NAV. That produces CAD 0.80 per original unit annually, paid as twelve equal monthly amounts of about CAD 0.066667. The holder of the original 10,000 units therefore receives about CAD 666.67 each month, CAD 8,000 each year and CAD 40,000 over five years. Calculations retain full precision and use fractional units; displayed dollars are rounded. Neither the monthly amount nor the annual schedule is a promise from an actual fund. The schedule uses the initial CAD 10 NAV throughout. It is not 8% of each later month’s changing fund value. This distinction matters when reading a yield-like label: identify the payment numerator, the price or NAV denominator, and the period before comparing percentages. The calculator’s distribution percentage is a cash-setting input, separate from its performance assumption. Reconcile the fund value with cash retained outside The independent performance assumption is a constant 5% effective annual fund total return before investor costs. The model converts it to an equivalent monthly growth factor. Each month, the unit NAV first grows by that factor and then the scheduled per-unit distribution is deducted. For a holder who keeps the original units and retains every payment in outside cash earning zero interest, the five-year fund value is about CAD 82,419.00. The outside cash totals CAD 40,000. Together, the holder has approximately CAD 122,419.00 , before taxes and costs. The waterfall reconciles the fund-only endpoint: CAD 100,000 initially invested, plus about CAD 22,419.00 of cumulative investment growth on the changing fund balance, less CAD 40,000 transferred outside. The distribution is already included in the outside asset. Adding it again as extra investment profit would count the same cash twice. The unit NAV finishes around CAD 8.24. That price alone omits the cash transferred to the holder. Conversely, calling the entire CAD 40,000 of payments profit would omit the reduction in resources remaining in the original units. Compare retaining cash with reinvesting each payment The second holder starts with the same CAD 100,000 and receives the same per-unit distribution policy. Every payment is immediately reinvested at the post-distribution NAV, so the holder acquires additional fractional units instead of accumulating outside cash. In this frictionless illustration, reinvestment preserves full exposure to the assumed fund return. The ending value is CAD 100,000 × 1.05 to the fifth power, or approximately CAD 127,628.16. The difference from the collect-and-retain outcome is about CAD 5,209.16. That difference comes from the different subsequent investment exposure of the distributed money. It is not an additional return created by the payment itself. Both holders receive the same assumed fund growth factors, but the first moves part of the resources into zero-interest cash. A fair comparison must state what happens to payments. Spending them, earning interest elsewhere, paying tax or incurring reinvestment charges would change the household outcome. None occurs in this example. Both charts retain all resources, and neither holder supplies new money after the opening investment. Change the payout and return assumptions independently The comparison chart varies the scheduled distribution from 0% to 10% of initial NAV while holding the selected return and horizon fixed. Under the default positive return, larger cash distributions move more resources away from later fund growth. The fully reinvested endpoint remains the same across those hypothetical schedules. Set the annual total return to zero. With the default distribution and horizon, the original-unit fund value becomes CAD 60,000 and outside cash becomes CAD 40,000. Total resources remain CAD 100,000. The payment has rearranged the resources without producing investment growth. With a negative return assumption, cash moved outside at zero interest can cushion losses relative to leaving everything exposed to that invented declining path. That result does not identify a preferred payout policy for an uncertain future. Real returns vary, distributions can change, and money needed for spending may require a different plan. Use the charts to ask better questions about an actual fund The model does not classify any payment as interest, dividends, capital gains or return of capital for tax purposes. A falling NAV, or a scheduled payout above an assumed return, cannot by itself establish the tax character of a real distribution. Fund records and applicable account and tax rules are needed for that separate question. For an actual investment, inspect the distribution policy, whether amounts can change, the treatment of reinvestment and the performance calculation being presented. Check whether quoted returns already deduct fund expenses and which investor-level costs remain outside them. Finally, connect the investment to the spending plan. Cash delivered on a schedule can help fund bills, but its convenience does not determine whether total resources are growing or shrinking. Track what remains invested, what has been received, what has been spent, and what is still available. These four charts keep that reconciliation visible before attaching a performance label to a payout.
3d393908064ae1d94b67cee64d66c925450f0a26.zh: 分配将价值移出基金。将剩余投资与收到的现金一起阅读，并将付款时间表与赚取的回报区分开来。考虑三种不同的衡量标准 基金可以在其单位价值下降时向投资者发送现金。这种组合提出了一个有用的问题：投资中剩余了多少价值，有多少价值转移到了投资之外，以及两者一起发生了怎样的变化？只看支出或只看单价就无法得到部分答案。分配是基金向其持有人支付的款项。资产净值（NAV）描述了每单位的剩余价值。总回报衡量投资绩效，并按照规定的计算惯例进行分配。这些测量值具有不同的分母，不应相互替代。美国证券交易委员会的基金分配公告解释了一般机制：付款将价值转移给持有人，再投资购买额外的股票，高分配率并不代表强劲的业绩。本文在独立的 CAD 插图中使用了这些机制；它不适用于加拿大账户的美国报告或税务规则。在比较百分比之前定义现金计划 下图以假设资产净值为 10 加元投资 100,000 加元开始，为持有人提供 10,000 个单位。选定的预定年度分配是初始资产净值的8%。每原始单位每年产生 0.80 加元，每月支付十二等额，约为 0.066667 加元。因此，最初 10,000 单位的持有者每月收到约 666.67 加元，每年收到 8,000 加元，五年内收到 40,000 加元。计算保留完全精度并使用小数单位；显示的美元是四舍五入的。每月金额和年度计划都不是实际基金的承诺。该时间表始终使用最初的 10 加元资产净值。它不是每个月变化的基金价值的 8%。在阅读类似收益的标签时，这种区别很重要：确定付款分子、价格或资产净值分母以及比较百分比之前的时期。计算器的分配百分比是现金设定输入，与其业绩假设分开。将基金价值与保留在外部的现金进行核对 独立业绩假设是在投资者成本之前，有效年度基金总回报率恒定为 5%。该模型将其转换为等效的月增长因子。每个月，单位资产净值首先按该系数增长，然后扣除预定的单位分配。对于保留原始单位并保留每笔付款的外部现金赚取零利息的持有人来说，五年期基金价值约为 82,419.00 加元。外部现金总计 40,000 加元。持有人总共拥有约 122,419.00 加元（扣除税费和费用）。瀑布调节仅基金端点：初始投资 100,000 加元，加上基金余额变化导致的累计投资增长约 22,419.00 加元，减去转移到外部的 40,000 加元。该分配已包含在外部资产中。再次添加作为额外的投资利润，同样的现金会被计算两次。该单位资产净值约为 8.24 加元。仅该价格就忽略了转移给持有人的现金。相反，如果将全部付款利润称为 40,000 加元，则会忽略原始单位中剩余资源的减少。比较保留现金与每笔付款的再投资 第二个持有者以相同的 100,000 加元开始，并获得相同的每单位分配政策。每笔付款都会立即按照分配后的资产净值进行再投资，因此持有者可以获得额外的小数单位，而不是积累外部现金。在这个无摩擦的例子中，再投资保留了假定基金回报的全部风险。最终值为 CAD 100,000 × 1.05 的五次方，即大约 CAD 127,628.16。与收集并保留结果的差异约为 5,209.16 加元。这种差异来自于所分配资金的后续投资风险不同。它不是付款本身产生的额外回报。两个持有者都获得相同的假定基金增长因素，但第一个持有者将部分资源转为零息现金。公平的比较必须说明付款情况。花掉它们、在其他地方赚取利息、纳税或产生再投资费用都会改变家庭的结果。本例中没有出现任何情况。两种图表都保留了所有资源，并且在开仓投资后，任何持有者都不会提供新资金。独立更改支付和回报假设 比较图将预定分配从初始资产净值的 0% 更改为 10%，同时保持选定的回报和期限固定。在默认正回报的情况下，更大的现金分配会将更多资源从后期基金增长中转移出来。在这些假设的时间表中，完全再投资的终点保持不变。将年度总回报设置为零。根据默认分配和期限，原始单位基金价值变为 60,000 加元，外部现金变为 40,000 加元。总资源仍为 100,000 加元。这笔付款重新配置了资源，但没有产生投资增长。在负回报假设下，以零利率转移出去的现金可以缓冲损失，而不是让一切都暴露在所发明的下降路径中。该结果并未确定针对不确定的未来的首选支付政策。实际回报各不相同，分配可能会发生变化，支出所需的资金可能需要不同的计划。使用图表提出有关实际基金的更好问题 该模型不会出于税收目的将任何付款分类为利息、股息、资本利得或资本回报。资产净值下降或计划支付高于假定回报，本身无法确定实际分配的税收特征。该单独的问题需要基金记录以及适用的账户和税务规则。对于实际投资，检查分配政策、金额是否可以改变、再投资的处理以及所列的业绩计算。检查报价回报是否已扣除基金费用，以及哪些投资者层面的成本仍在其中。最后，将投资与支出计划联系起来。按计划交付的现金可以帮助支付账单，但其便利性并不能决定总资源是增长还是萎缩。跟踪剩余投资、已收到的投资、已花费的投资以及仍然可用的投资。在将绩效标签附加到支出之前，这四个图表可以使对账保持可见。

1f091925312c4ffc9f0bb4ab926639859aa89408.src: Time-weighted return follows the investment path independently of external cash flows. Money-weighted return also reflects how much money was exposed to each part of that path. Start by separating account balance from investment performance A larger year-end investment account can reflect gains, new contributions or both. The opening and closing balances alone cannot tell you which. Before interpreting a return percentage, reconcile the external cash that entered or left the account during the measurement period. This invented example starts with CAD 10,000. The investment loses 20% over the first six months and gains 25% over the next six. Another CAD 10,000 arrives immediately after month six’s return, and there are no withdrawals, distributions, taxes or fees. The account finishes at CAD 22,500. Of the CAD 12,500 increase from its opening balance, CAD 10,000 is new money. The remaining CAD 2,500 is investment gain. The waterfall makes those components explicit. Dividing the entire balance increase by the opening investment would label an external deposit as profit and produce a misleading percentage. Link the investment’s return factors The first CAD 10,000 falls to CAD 8,000 by the end of the first half. A 25% gain then brings that original exposure back to CAD 10,000. The linked annual return is (1 − 0.20) × (1 + 0.25) − 1 = 0% . Adding negative 20% and positive 25% would instead give positive 5%, which is not the compounded result. The second percentage applies to the smaller value after the first loss. A percentage recovery must be read against its own starting base. The normalized chart applies the same factors to an unchanged CAD 1,000 investment. It reaches CAD 800 at month six and CAD 1,000 at year-end. No external money enters that line, so its ending-to-opening ratio isolates the linked investment return. In the interactive example, each six-month total return is spread evenly across its six months using equivalent compound factors. The smooth-looking path is a modeling choice, not observed daily prices or evidence that markets move evenly. See which money experienced each part of the year The new CAD 10,000 enters after the first-half loss. It therefore does not experience that loss in the selected scenario. It is exposed to the second-half 25% gain and becomes CAD 12,500. Combined with CAD 10,000 from the recovered original investment, this explains the CAD 22,500 ending account. The account chart shows a vertical step from CAD 8,000 to CAD 18,000 at month six. Two observations at that date represent values immediately before and after the contribution. The jump is external cash arriving; it is not a sudden market return. Consequently, the investment’s zero linked return and the account’s positive dollar gain can both be correct. More money was present during the favorable half of this particular invented year. The result does not mean an account holder or manager generated an additional 25% return on all the money for the entire year. Solve a rate that respects the contribution date A money-weighted return fits a compound rate to the dated account cash flows and ending value. Here the annual rate r satisfies 10,000 × (1 + r) + 10,000 × (1 + r) 0.5 = 22,500 . The first amount is present for one year and the second for half a year. The solution is approximately 16.89%. It is an annual money-weighted rate for this one-year horizon, rather than a claim that every dollar earned 16.89% during its actual holding time. Using the common annual factor over each amount’s exposure period reconciles the final value. Dividing the CAD 2,500 gain by CAD 20,000 of total deposits gives 12.5%. That simple ratio ignores how long the second deposit was invested. It is therefore a different calculation from the money-weighted rate and from the linked time-weighted return. The calculator uses twelve equal month fractions and solves one unique positive growth factor. It is not a daily XIRR tool, and real statement date conventions, charges and additional cash flows can produce different reported figures. Compare alternative dates without treating hindsight as a plan The final chart moves the same contribution across twelve possible month-end dates while retaining the selected return path. Every point is a separate complete-year scenario. It is not the year-to-date return earned by the corresponding month. The time-weighted line stays fixed because the underlying investment path is unchanged. The money-weighted line can move because the new money experiences different portions of that path. If the contribution is zero, the two methods coincide in this simplified account. A contribution after month twelve also leaves the two rates equal: it arrives at the terminal date and has no time to earn a return inside the measured year. Its cash still raises the final balance, but the money-weighted equation assigns it zero exposure time. The displayed path is already known because it was invented for teaching. A favorable date in this comparison cannot identify the future best date to invest. Planning decisions need to account for available cash, goals, risk and uncertainty rather than selecting a past turning point after seeing the outcome. Read the method and period beside an actual return Fidelity Canada’s investor education distinguishes time-weighted investment performance from dollar-weighted personal performance, which reflects the amount and timing of account cash flows. Those descriptions explain why two percentages can answer different questions. Before comparing actual statements or a fund fact sheet, align the period, currency, fee treatment and return method. Confirm which transfers count as external flows and whether an account number includes cash or several investments. A method label does not make mismatched periods or different portfolios directly comparable. Use the cash reconciliation to understand the dollars and the return methodology to understand the percentage. Neither replaces the other. This article supplies transparent arithmetic for one contribution, while an actual multi-transaction account needs its complete dated flow history and the provider’s stated conventions.
1f091925312c4ffc9f0bb4ab926639859aa89408.zh: 时间加权回报遵循独立于外部现金流的投资路径。货币加权回报还反映了该路径各部分的投资金额。首先将账户余额与投资业绩分开较大的年终投资账户可以反映收益、新贡献或两者兼而有之。仅凭期初余额和期末余额无法告诉您具体情况。在解释回报率之前，先对计量期间进入或离开账户的外部现金进行核对。这个发明的例子起价为 10,000 加元。该投资在前 6 个月内损失 20%，在接下来的 6 个月内收益 25%。另外 10,000 加元在第 6 个月的回报后立即到账，并且没有提款、分配、税款或费用。该账户最终金额为 22,500 加元。较期初余额增加 12,500 加元，其中 10,000 加元为新资金。剩下的 2,500 加元是投资收益。瀑布使这些组件变得明确。将全部余额增量除以期初投资会将外部存款标记为利润，并产生误导性的百分比。挂钩投资回报因素 上半年末，最初的 10,000 加元跌至 8,000 加元。 25% 的收益将使原始敞口回到 10,000 加元。挂钩年回报率为 (1 − 0.20) × (1 + 0.25) − 1 = 0% 。添加负 20% 和正 25% 将得到正 5%，这不是复合结果。第二个百分比适用于第一次损失后的较小值。回收百分比必须根据其自身的起始基础来读取。标准化图表将相同的因素应用于不变的 1,000 加元投资。第六个月达到 800 加元，年底达到 1,000 加元。没有外部资金进入该线，因此其期末与期初比率隔离了挂钩的投资回报。在交互式示例中，每个六个月的总回报使用等效的复合因子均匀分布在其六个月内。看起来平滑的路径是一种建模选择，而不是观察到的每日价格或市场均匀波动的证据。看看一年中的每个部分经历了哪些资金 上半年亏损后进入新的 10,000 加元。因此，它在选定的场景中不会经历这种损失。下半年将上涨 25%，达到 12,500 加元。加上收回的原始投资中的 10,000 加元，这就解释了期末账户的 22,500 加元。账户图表显示第六个月从 8,000 加元垂直上升到 18,000 加元。该日期的两个观察值代表贡献之前和之后的值。跳跃是外部现金到达；这并不是市场的突然回归。因此，投资的零关联回报和账户的正美元收益都可能是正确的。在这个特定的发明年份的有利的一半期间出现了更多的资金。结果并不意味着账户持有人或经理全年的所有资金都获得了额外 25% 的回报。求解符合缴款日期的利率 货币加权回报率适合指定日期的账户现金流量和期末价值的复合利率。这里年利率 r 满足 10,000 × (1 + r) + 10,000 × (1 + r) 0.5 = 22,500 。第一个金额存在一年，第二个金额存在半年。解约为16.89%。它是这一年范围内的年度货币加权利率，而不是声称每美元在实际持有期间赚取 16.89%。在每个金额的暴露期内使用共同的年度因子来协调最终值。将 2,500 加元的收益除以总存款的 20,000 加元，得出 12.5%。这个简单的比率忽略了第二笔存款的投资时间。因此，它的计算方式不同于货币加权利率和链接的时间加权回报率。该计算器使用十二个等月分数并求解一个独特的正增长因子。它不是每日 XIRR 工具，实际报表日期惯例、费用和额外现金流可能会产生不同的报告数字。比较替代日期，而不将事后诸葛亮视为计划 最终图表在十二个可能的月末日期之间移动相同的贡献，同时保留选定的返回路径。每个点都是一个单独的全年情景。它不是相应月份赚取的年初至今的回报。时间加权线保持固定，因为基础投资路径未改变。货币加权线可以移动，因为新货币经历了该路径的不同部分。如果贡献为零，则两种方法在此简化说明中一致。第十二个月之后的捐款也使两个利率相等：它到达最终日期，并且没有时间在测量的年份内获得回报。它的现金仍然会提高最终余额，但货币加权方程将其分配的暴露时间为零。显示的路径是已知的，因为它是为教学而发明的。此比较中的有利日期无法确定未来的最佳投资日期。规划决策需要考虑可用现金、目标、风险和不确定性，而不是在看到结果后选择过去的转折点。请阅读实际回报旁边的方法和期限富达加拿大的投资者教育将时间加权投资业绩与美元加权个人业绩区分开来，后者反映了账户现金流量的金额和时间。这些描述解释了为什么两个百分比可以回答不同的问题。在比较实际报表或基金概况（Fund Facts）之前，请调整期间、货币、费用处理和回报方法。确认哪些转账算作外部流量，以及账号是否包含现金或多项投资。方法标签不会使不匹配的期间或不同的投资组合直接具有可比性。使用现金调节表了解美元，使用回报方法了解百分比。两者都不能取代另一个。本文为一笔贡献提供了透明的算术，而实际的多交易帐户需要其完整的日期流历史记录和提供商规定的约定。

aa2594f1660ee508f5e1d690f1158c9b21209b11.src: Settling the old lender and eliminating the old shortfall are different things. Read the trade proceeds, payout, cash applied and new principal together before comparing monthly payments. Compare the old payout with gross trade proceeds Suppose the old lender needs CAD 28,000 to settle the current vehicle loan, while the dealer offers CAD 22,000 for the car before that debt is paid. The trade proceeds fall CAD 6,000 short of the payout. The FCAC describes negative equity as owing more on a vehicle than it is worth and explains the risk of carrying the shortfall into replacement financing. For this closing model, signed trade equity is gross trade proceeds − old lender payout . The starting result is negative CAD 6,000. The amount quoted for the trade is therefore different from the cash left after settling the old loan. A promise to pay the old lender does not establish that the shortfall has been waived. Read how the replacement agreement funds that payout. The BC Vehicle Sales Authority also identifies rolling trade-in negative equity into a new loan as a cause of negative equity. Approval to finance it still depends on the actual lender and transaction. Reconcile the new principal once, without double-counting the trade The first chart adds a fictional CAD 40,000 replacement price, CAD 2,000 of other purchase charges and the CAD 28,000 old-loan payout. It subtracts CAD 22,000 of gross trade proceeds and CAD 5,000 of cash applied. The result is CAD 43,000 of new loan principal. The equivalent calculation is CAD 40,000 + CAD 2,000 + CAD 6,000 old shortfall − CAD 5,000 cash. These are alternative reconciliations. Adding both the full old payout and the shortfall, or subtracting both the full trade allowance and net trade equity, would count part of the transaction twice. All tax is excluded. The charges field does not quietly supply a GST/HST/PST estimate, and the loan shortfall does not determine the tax treatment. This is a defined financing illustration, not the full amount required under a dealer’s itemized purchase agreement. Keep unused cash and positive equity visible The same controls can show a trade worth more than the old payout. Positive trade equity reduces the amount to fund. Available cash is applied only up to the remaining transaction need; any unused offered cash stays with the household in this model. If net trade proceeds exceed the replacement price and charges, the waterfall ends below zero. That endpoint represents modeled cash released after the listed settlement, while new borrowing is zero. The calculator does not create a negative loan or count an unnecessary down payment as spent. For the interest attribution, cash first funds the replacement price and charges, then any remaining old shortfall. If cash pays the entire transaction need, there is no financed shortfall and no new-loan interest attributed to it. This allocation is a declared way to explain the numbers, rather than a lender’s separate account for each dollar borrowed. Read the monthly payment beside the complete repayment total At the fictional 7% nominal annual rate over seventy-two months, the CAD 43,000 loan requires an unrounded monthly payment of about CAD 733.11 when displayed to cents. The model divides the annual rate by twelve and assumes equal month-end payments, with no balloon or payment holiday. The next two charts use the same principal and rate across independent terms. One shows monthly payments; the other stacks principal and full-term interest. A longer term lowers the payment in this positive-rate example but increases total interest. The selected seventy-two-month loan incurs about CAD 9,783.72 of interest over its entire term. The model retains unrounded payments for calculations, so it is not a lender’s cents-rounded schedule or APR disclosure. The payment also excludes insurance, fuel or charging, parking, maintenance and every tax amount. A smaller loan payment alone does not establish a smaller complete household transport budget. Isolate interest on the old shortfall without inventing a free alternative In the starting transaction, the CAD 6,000 old shortfall is included in the CAD 43,000 new loan. At the same new rate and seventy-two-month term, this portion accounts for about CAD 102.29 of each unrounded monthly payment and CAD 1,365.17 of total interest. Those amounts are a mathematical attribution under one common rate and term. They are not remaining interest under the old contract. An otherwise identical loan with CAD 6,000 less principal would have a smaller payment, but that shortfall would need funding elsewhere; it has not disappeared. The final grid shows interest alone on separately financed shortfalls of zero, CAD 3,000, CAD 6,000 and CAD 12,000 over alternative terms. Repayment of the shortfall principal is additional. At a zero rate, interest becomes zero while the borrowed principal still needs to be repaid. A cash-versus-finance decision would also need to track the extra upfront cash used or retained. Follow the replacement value separately from its financing The fourth chart starts vehicle value at CAD 40,000, while loan principal starts at CAD 43,000. Financing fees and old debt do not automatically add to the replacement vehicle’s market value. The starting modeled negative equity is therefore CAD 3,000, which differs from the old CAD 6,000 shortfall because charges and cash also affect the closing bridge. The selected 15% annual value-decline assumption gives CAD 28,900 after twenty-four months. The modeled loan balance then is about CAD 30,614.71, leaving a CAD 1,714.71 gap before any sale costs. The value line is an invented smooth path, not an appraisal, a statistical forecast or a guaranteed trade offer. A crossing of the two lines would indicate nonnegative equity under these assumptions. It cannot guarantee a real date when selling requires no extra cash. Obtain actual net sale proceeds and a dated lender payout when the decision arises. Carry the model back to the actual written quotes Obtain the old lender’s payout for the intended settlement date, the dealer’s gross trade offer and conditions, the replacement cash price, itemized charges and taxes, and the new lender’s approved amount, rate, payment schedule and total borrowing cost. Confirm whether a balloon or other obligation exists outside the ordinary payments. Keep the old-loan settlement and lien release explicit. The FCAC’s car-lien guidance describes the lender’s registered claim and the importance of verifying repayment and removal. The calculator assumes full settlement; it cannot verify that the transaction actually clears the old security. Tax treatment needs a separate check under the applicable federal and provincial rules. CRA’s trade-in guidance distinguishes different customer and transaction situations. Keep the tax exclusion attached to these charts, then reconcile the actual taxable amounts from the written agreement. Use the closing bridge to understand the financing; a decision to keep or replace the car requires the wider ownership costs and household cash plan.
aa2594f1660ee508f5e1d690f1158c9b21209b11.zh: 解决旧贷款机构和消除旧缺口是不同的事情。在比较每月付款之前，请先阅读交易收益、支出、所用现金和新本金。将旧付款与总贸易收益进行比较 假设旧贷款机构需要 28,000 加元来结清当前车辆贷款，而经销商在偿还债务之前为汽车提供 22,000 加元。贸易收益比付款少 6,000 加元。 FCAC 将负资产描述为车辆所欠的金额超过其价值，并解释了将不足额转入替代融资的风险。对于此成交模型，已签署的贸易权益是总贸易收益 – 旧贷款机构付款。起始结果为负 6,000 加元。因此，交易报价与偿还旧贷款后剩余的现金不同。承诺向旧贷款机构付款并不表明缺口已被免除。了解更换协议如何为该付款提供资金。不列颠哥伦比亚省汽车销售管理局还将以旧换新负资产转入新贷款作为负资产的一个原因。是否批准融资仍取决于实际的贷款机构和交易。核对一次新本金，无需重复计算交易 第一张图表添加了虚构的 40,000 加元重置价格、2,000 加元其他购买费用以及 28,000 加元旧贷款支付。它减去 22,000 加元的贸易总收入和 5,000 加元的现金使用。结果是 43,000 加元的新贷款本金。等价计算为 40,000 加元 + 2,000 加元 + 6,000 加元旧缺口 – 5,000 加元现金。这些是替代协调。添加全部旧支出和差额，或者减去全部贸易补贴和净贸易权益，会将部分交易计算两次。所有税费均不包括在内。费用字段不会悄悄提供 GST/HST/PST 估算，贷款缺口也不会决定税收处理。这是一个明确的融资说明，而不是经销商逐项购买协议中要求的全额金额。保持未使用的现金和正股本可见相同的控制可以显示交易的价值高于旧的支出。正的贸易净值减少了融资金额。可用现金仅用于满足剩余交易需求；在这种模式下，任何未使用的现金都会留在家庭中。如果净交易收益超过重置价格和费用，瀑布将结束于零以下。该端点代表上市结算后释放的模拟现金，而新借款为零。该计算器不会产生负贷款或将不必要的首付计入支出。对于利息归属，现金首先为重置价格和费用提供资金，然后再为任何剩余的旧缺口提供资金。如果现金支付全部交易需求，则不存在融资缺口，也不会产生新贷款利息。这种分配是解释这些数字的一种公开方式，而不是贷款人为借入的每一美元设立一个单独的账户。请阅读完整还款总额旁边的每月还款额。按照 72 个月的虚构 7% 名义年利率，43,000 加元的贷款需要按美分显示的每月未四舍五入金额约为 733.11 加元。该模型将年利率除以十二，并假设月末付款相等，没有气球或付款假期。接下来的两张图表在独立条款中使用相同的本金和利率。一个显示每月付款；另一个是本金和全额利息。在这个正利率例子中，较长的期限会降低还款额，但会增加总利息。选定的 72 个月贷款在整个期限内产生约 9,783.72 加元的利息。该模型保留了未四舍五入的付款计算，因此它不是贷款机构的四舍五入时间表或年利率披露。该付款还不包括保险、燃油或充电、停车、维护和每项税费。仅较小的贷款支付并不能建立较小的完整家庭交通预算。隔离旧缺口的利息，无需发明免费替代方案 在起始交易中，6,000 加元的旧缺口包含在 43,000 加元的新贷款中。按照相同的新利率和 72 个月期限，这部分约占每笔未四舍五入每月付款的 102.29 加元，总利息为 1,365.17 加元。这些金额是在一个共同利率和期限下的数学归属。他们没有旧合同下的剩余利息。如果本金少 6,000 加元，则其他方面相同的贷款的付款额会较少，但这一缺口需要其他地方融资；它并没有消失。最终表格仅显示了替代条款中单独融资缺口为零、3,000 加元、6,000 加元和 12,000 加元的利息。短缺本金的偿还是额外的。在零利率下，利息为零，而借入的本金仍需要偿还。现金与融资的决策还需要跟踪使用或保留的额外预付现金。将重置价值与其融资分开第四张图表的车辆价值起价为 40,000 加元，而贷款本金起价为 43,000 加元。融资费用和旧债务不会自动增加替换车辆的市场价值。因此，起始模型负资产为 3,000 加元，这与旧的 6,000 加元缺口不同，因为费用和现金也会影响结束桥。选定的年度价值下降 15% 的假设得出 24 个月后为 28,900 加元。模型得出的贷款余额约为 30,614.71 加元，扣除任何销售成本后还存在 1,714.71 加元的缺口。价值线是一条发明的平滑路径，而不是评估、统计预测或有保证的交易报价。两条线的交叉表明这些假设下的非负资产。当出售不需要额外现金时，它不能保证真实的日期。在做出决定时获得实际的净销售收益和注明日期的贷款机构付款。将模型带回实际书面报价 获取旧贷款机构在预定结算日的付款、交易商的总交易报价和条件、重置现金价格、逐项费用和税金，以及新贷款机构批准的金额、利率、付款时间表和总借贷成本。确认普通付款之外是否存在巨额债务或其他义务。保持旧贷款结算和留置权释放的明确性。 FCAC 的汽车留置权指南描述了贷款机构的登记索赔以及验证还款和清除的重要性。计算器假设全额结算；它无法验证交易是否确实清算了旧证券。税务处理需要根据适用的联邦和省规则进行单独检查。 CRA的以旧换新指南区分了不同的客户和交易情况。将免税额附在这些图表上，然后根据书面协议核对实际应税金额。使用收桥了解融资情况；保留或更换汽车的决定需要更广泛的拥有成本和家庭现金计划。

a649144d4a3dba5b7f3f96575f5ac6e8883ff7f7.src: A national percentage is useful context. Your next bill needs cash that is accessible and has not already been assigned to another payment. Identify the population, observation date and currency The Federal Reserve’s 2025 SHED savings chapter , published in May 2026, reports emergency-expense responses from U.S. adults. The first chart reproduces table 26’s six savings-only capacity bands. All survey amounts are U.S. dollars. The methodology describes an October 17–28, 2025 online survey, a final sample of 12,934 and weighting to the U.S. civilian, noninstitutionalized adult population. These are estimates with survey limitations, not a census of bank balances. No confidence intervals are constructed here. The editable household exercise below uses independently chosen Canadian-dollar amounts. It does not convert the survey thresholds or assume the U.S. distribution describes Canadian households. Keep that currency and population distinction visible before comparing a headline with your own budget. A choice of payment method is different from available capacity One survey measure asks whether a USD 400 expense would be paid with cash or its equivalent, which includes a card paid at the next statement. Another asks the largest expense that could be covered with savings alone. The second chart keeps these questions separate. “Would” describes a selected payment approach. “Could” describes a claimed ability under the question’s conditions. A person might preserve savings and choose another payment method, or intend to pay a statement using income that has not arrived yet. Neither answer alone tells us which dollars are free of other commitments on a specific bill date. Do not add the two percentages, subtract one to identify a known group of people, or read the difference as an improvement over time. Separate aggregate answers do not reveal their person-level overlap. Likewise, the open-ended highest savings band cannot supply an average balance: amounts inside that band are not reported by the chart. Subtract commitments before calling the account an emergency reserve The independent example starts with CAD 9,000 of accessible cash. CAD 6,000 is already assigned to known payments due before another inflow. That leaves CAD 3,000 available for an additional bill, even though the account statement still displays CAD 9,000. An unexpected CAD 4,000 payment would bring the combined ledger to negative CAD 1,000. The calculator reports that funding gap rather than treating the existing account balance as wholly available. Its available-cash metric is floored at zero. If known commitments alone exceed cash, the combined funding requirement still includes that pre-existing shortage. Enter non-overlapping commitments. If an annual insurance premium is already counted in known bills, do not include the same premium again as an unexpected shock. A payment that will be cancelled or funded from a genuinely separate resource belongs in a revised ledger, with the change recorded explicitly. Use the waterfall to check the full payment set The waterfall begins with cash once, deducts known commitments once and deducts the additional payment once. Its final balance can be positive, zero or negative. A negative result identifies money still needed; the model does not create a line of credit or assume permission to miss a bill. Both payment groups are assumed due before the next receipt. If wages arrive between them, replace this short check with an actual dated calendar. An expected reimbursement after the bill is paid does not fund the earlier payment unless an interim resource is available. Separating a reserve into a labelled savings account can help tracking, but moving money between your own accounts does not itself add household cash. Count the same dollars once across accounts. Check transfer access, withdrawal restrictions and amounts already pledged elsewhere before treating a displayed balance as immediately spendable. Stress the new bill beside the obligations already due The matrix varies known commitments down the rows and the additional payment across columns. Accessible cash remains at the selected input. Each cell shows extra funding needed to pay both groups without another inflow. A zero cell means that particular combination is covered by the selected cash. It does not establish a complete emergency-fund target, a probability of avoiding hardship, or the affordability of all later months. A larger bill, delayed income, several shocks or an inaccessible account could change the result. Use the matrix to locate a boundary worth planning around. For example, when a cell shows a funding gap, identify a real resource, a possible timing change or an expense adjustment. The color cannot decide which response is feasible. It simply makes the arithmetic of the chosen payment set easier to inspect. Build a reserve policy from the household calendar Start with cash that can actually be accessed. List bills already promised to it, then identify plausible additional expenses and income interruptions separately. Give each item an amount, a date and an identified funding source. Keep accessible emergency cash distinct from longer-term investments whose sale value or availability may change. After using a reserve, the next question is how and when it can be rebuilt while regular payments continue. A funding gap that can be solved once may recur if the household has no saving capacity afterward. Use the related budget and sinking-fund guides to connect this immediate check with a repeatable monthly plan. The survey helps readers question a simplified headline. The household ledger helps them question an account balance. Neither substitutes a national rank for a workable payment calendar, and the model makes no borrowing, tax, investment or product recommendation.
a649144d4a3dba5b7f3f96575f5ac6e8883ff7f7.zh: 全国百分比是有用的背景。您的下一张账单需要可用且尚未分配给其他付款的现金。确定人口、观察日期和货币 美联储于 2026 年 5 月发布的 2025 SHED 储蓄章节报告了美国成年人的紧急支出应对措施。第一个图表再现了表 26 的六个仅节省容量的容量范围。所有调查金额均为美元。该方法描述了 2025 年 10 月 17 日至 28 日的在线调查，最终样本为 12,934 人，并以美国平民、非机构化成年人口为权重。这些是具有调查局限性的估计，而不是银行余额普查。这里没有构建置信区间。下面的可编辑家庭练习使用独立选择的加元金额。它不会转换调查阈值或假设美国分布描述了加拿大家庭。在将标题与您自己的预算进行比较之前，请注意货币和人口的区别。支付方式的选择与可用容量不同 一项调查措施询问是否用现金或等价物支付 400 美元的费用，其中包括在下一张账单上支付的卡。另一个问题是仅靠储蓄就能支付的最大开支。第二张图表将这些问题分开。 “愿意”描述了选定的付款方式。 “可以”描述了在问题条件下声称的能力。一个人可能会保留储蓄并选择其他付款方式，或者打算使用尚未到达的收入来支付账单。这两个答案都无法单独告诉我们哪些美元在特定账单日期不受其他承诺。不要将两个百分比相加，减去一个百分比来识别已知的一组人，或将差异视为随着时间的推移而取得的进步。单独的汇总答案不会揭示其个人层面的重叠。同样，开放式最高储蓄区间无法提供平均余额：图表不会报告该区间内的金额。在将该帐户称为紧急储备金之前减去承诺额 独立示例以 9,000 加元的可用现金开始。 6,000 加元已分配给另一笔资金流入之前到期的已知付款。这样一来，即使账户对账单上仍显示 9,000 加元，仍可支付 3,000 加元的额外账单。意外支付 4,000 加元将使总账变为负 1,000 加元。计算器报告资金缺口，而不是将现有账户余额视为完全可用。其可用现金指标为零。如果仅已知的承诺就超过了现金，则合并后的资金需求仍包括先前存在的短缺。输入不重叠的承诺。如果年度保险费已计入已知账单中，请勿再次将相同的保险费计入意外冲击。将被取消或由真正独立的资源资助的付款属于修订后的分类账，并明确记录了更改。使用瀑布检查完整的付款集瀑布从现金开始一次，扣除已知承诺一次，并扣除一次额外付款。其最终余额可以为正、零或负。负面结果表明仍需要资金；该模型不会创建信用额度或假设允许错过账单。假定两个付款组均在下一次收据之前到期。如果工资在他们之间到达，请用实际注明日期的日历替换这张简短的支票。除非有临时资源，否则账单支付后的预期报销不会为之前的付款提供资金。将储备金分成有标签的储蓄账户可以帮助跟踪，但在自己的账户之间转移资金本身并不会增加家庭现金。跨账户计算一次相同的美元。在将显示的余额视为可立即支出之前，请检查转账权限、提款限制以及已在其他地方承诺的金额。在已经到期的义务旁边强调新账单。矩阵改变了行中的已知承诺和跨列的额外付款。可用现金保留在所选输入处。每个单元格都显示了在没有其他资金流入的情况下支付两组费用所需的额外资金。零单元格表示所选现金涵盖特定组合。它没有建立完整的紧急资金目标、避免困难的可能性或所有后续几个月的承受能力。更大的账单、延迟的收入、几次冲击或无法访问的账户都可能改变结果。使用矩阵来定位值得规划的边界。例如，当某个单元显示资金缺口时，确定实际资源、可能的时间变化或费用调整。颜色无法决定哪种响应是可行的。它只是使所选付款集的算术更易于检查。从家庭日历中制定储备政策，从实际可用的现金开始。列出已经承诺的账单，然后分别确定可能的额外费用和收入中断。为每个项目指定金额、日期和确定的资金来源。保留可获取的应急现金，与销售价值或可用性可能发生变化的长期投资区分开来。使用储备金后，下一个问题是如何以及何时在继续定期付款的情况下重建储备金。曾经可以解决的资金缺口，如果以后家庭没有储蓄能力，可能会再次出现。使用相关的预算和专项储备金指南将这项即时检查与可重复的月度计划联系起来。该调查帮助读者质疑简化的标题。家庭分类账可以帮助他们查询账户余额。两者都不能用国家排名来替代可行的付款日历，并且该模型不提供借款、税收、投资或产品推荐。

7ab1bd64ba0a09befb11c7d019f53d0012dd1bdf.src: A gain applies to the capital that remains. Inflation can move the target, while new saving can restore an account balance without being investment performance. Measure the required gain from the capital that remains A loss and a later gain use different starting amounts. In this hypothetical example, a CAD 100,000 portfolio loses 30% immediately and falls to CAD 70,000. Regaining CAD 30,000 requires a gain of approximately 42.86% on the remaining CAD 70,000. Applying a 30% gain instead produces CAD 91,000. The same percentage with the opposite sign does not undo the loss because its denominator is smaller. In general, a fractional loss L requires a subsequent gain of L divided by (1 minus L) to regain the original nominal amount, assuming no deposits or withdrawals. The loss control stops below 100%. At a total loss, there is no remaining capital on which a percentage recovery can operate. This arithmetic does not identify an investment that will produce the required gain. Investor.gov’s risk explanation emphasizes that invested principal can be lost. A fixed dollar target can lose purchasing power while you wait The second target preserves what the original capital could buy, using the selected constant price-growth assumption. At 2% annual inflation for ten years, CAD 100,000 of original purchasing power becomes a nominal target of approximately CAD 121,899.44. Reaching that amount from CAD 70,000 requires a cumulative gain of approximately 74.14% without new deposits. This is larger than the 42.86% required merely to regain the old dollar amount. The first chart displays both cumulative requirements over the selected horizon. The inflation input is an authored assumption, not a current CPI observation or a forecast of the household’s spending basket. Investor.gov discusses inflation risk as a loss of buying power when money fails to keep pace with prices. The personal-inflation guide can help distinguish a broad price index from a particular household goal. Convert the horizon into an annual requirement carefully The headline annual requirement is the constant compound rate that would take post-loss capital to the purchasing-power target over the selected whole years, without any new deposits. It equals the target-to-remaining-capital ratio raised to one divided by the number of years, minus one. In the default, that rate is approximately 5.70% annually. It is not the 74.14% cumulative requirement divided by ten, and it is not an available yield. A required return describes the mathematics of a goal; it does not establish that the risk needed to pursue it is affordable. Changing the horizon changes both the compounding time and the inflation-adjusted target. A longer interval gives capital more time to grow but also gives prices more time to rise. The calculation keeps those two effects inside the same equation rather than subtracting a rough inflation allowance from a cumulative percentage. Compare the paths using the same year-end checkpoints The path chart begins immediately after the loss. Both portfolios then receive the selected constant nominal annual total return. One receives no further money. The other receives the selected deposit after each year’s return, so a new contribution first earns a return in the following year. At 5% for ten years, the no-deposit portfolio ends near CAD 114,022.62. It first regains the old CAD 100,000 amount at the eighth annual checkpoint, but it never reaches the moving purchasing-power target within the modeled ten years. The chart tests only those whole-year checkpoints. It does not estimate an actual recovery date, a typical market waiting time or the likelihood of another loss. Its smooth return assumption deliberately removes volatility so that the denominator, inflation and deposit effects can be inspected separately. Reconcile new saving before describing performance With CAD 3,000 deposited at every year-end, the default ending portfolio is approximately CAD 151,756.30. The household added CAD 30,000 after the loss. Subtracting that cash and the CAD 70,000 post-loss starting amount leaves approximately CAD 51,756.30 of subsequent modeled investment growth. The waterfall uses those three components. It does not subtract the original CAD 30,000 loss again, because that loss is already reflected in the CAD 70,000 opening capital. Nor does it call every dollar above the old statement balance an investment profit. A deposit can bring an account back above its previous high even when investment performance has not recovered. Keep contribution records beside the statement. This dollar reconciliation is not an annual performance measure, a money-weighted return, a realized capital gain or a determination of tax cost basis. Read the target gap without turning it into a return promise The matrix varies the immediate loss and subsequent annual return. It keeps the selected capital, horizon, inflation and year-end contributions unchanged. Every cell subtracts the same inflation-adjusted original-capital target from that scenario’s ending portfolio. A positive amount is a modeled surplus; a negative amount is a modeled shortfall. Neither color reports a probability or says that a portfolio is safe. A household may also need a different target because of withdrawals, changed expenses or an earlier use date. Those changes require their own cash flows rather than an unexplained adjustment to expected returns. For planning, record three separate facts: capital remaining after the loss, future money that can realistically be added, and the amount and timing of the goal. The model excludes fees and taxes and retains all distributions within total return. Its purpose is to make the recovery arithmetic inspectable before a required percentage is mistaken for a forecast.
7ab1bd64ba0a09befb11c7d019f53d0012dd1bdf.zh: 收益适用于剩余资本。通货膨胀可以改变目标，而新储蓄可以恢复账户余额，但不会影响投资绩效。使用不同的起始金额来衡量仍为亏损的资本所需的收益和后来的收益。在这个假设的例子中，100,000 加元的投资组合立即损失 30%，跌至 70,000 加元。要重新获得 30,000 加元，需要在剩余 70,000 加元的基础上获得约 42.86% 的收益。如果应用 30% 的增益，则会产生 91,000 加元。具有相反符号的相同百分比并不能消除损失，因为它的分母更小。一般来说，假设没有存款或取款，部分损失 L 需要随后的收益 L 除以（1 减 L）才能恢复原始名义金额。损失控制在 100% 以下停止。在完全亏损的情况下，没有剩余资本可以进行百分比回收。该算术无法识别将产生所需收益的投资。 Investor.gov 的风险解释强调投资本金可能会损失。固定的美元目标可能会在您等待时失去购买力第二个目标使用选定的恒定价格增长假设保留原始资本可以购买的东西。按十年 2% 的年通货膨胀率计算，100,000 加元的原始购买力成为约 121,899.44 加元的名义目标。从 70,000 加元达到这一金额需要在不增加新存款的情况下累积收益约 74.14%。这比仅仅恢复原来的美元金额所需的 42.86% 还要高。第一个图表显示选定范围内的两个累积需求。通胀输入是一个假设，而不是当前的消费者物价指数观察或家庭支出篮子的预测。 Investor.gov 将通货膨胀风险视为货币跟不上价格步伐时购买力的损失。个人通胀指南可以帮助区分广泛的价格指数和特定的家庭目标。小心地将期限转换为年度要求 总体年度要求是恒定的复合利率，在选定的整个年份中，亏损后的资本将达到购买力目标，而无需任何新存款。它等于目标与剩余资本比率提高到一除以年数减一。在默认情况下，该利率约为每年 5.70%。它不是 74.14% 的累积要求除以 10，也不是可用收益率。所需回报描述了目标的数学；它并没有证明追求这一目标所需的风险是可以承受的。改变期限会改变复利时间和通货膨胀调整后的目标。较长的时间间隔让资本有更多的时间增长，但也让价格有更多的时间上涨。该计算将这两种效应保持在同一等式内，而不是从累积百分比中减去粗略的通货膨胀津贴。使用相同的年终检查点比较路径 路径图在损失后立即开始。然后，两个投资组合都会获得选定的恒定名义年总回报。一个人不会收到更多的钱。另一方在每年的回报后收到选定的存款，因此新的贡献首先在下一年获得回报。十年期利率为 5%，无存款投资组合最终接近 114,022.62 加元。它首先在第八个年度检查点恢复了原来的 100,000 加元，但在模拟的十年内从未达到移动购买力目标。该图表仅测试那些全年检查点。它不会估计实际恢复日期、典型的市场等待时间或再次损失的可能性。其平滑回报假设故意消除了波动性，以便可以分别检查分母、通货膨胀和存款效应。在描述业绩之前调节新的储蓄 由于每年年底存入 3,000 加元，默认的期末投资组合约为 151,756.30 加元。损失后该家庭又增加了3万加元。减去现金和 70,000 加元的亏损后起始金额，后续模型投资增长额约为 51,756.30 加元。瀑布使用这三个组件。它不会再次减去原来的 30,000 加元损失，因为该损失已经反映在 70,000 加元的期初资本中。它也不把旧报表余额上的每一美元都称为投资利润。即使投资表现尚未恢复，存款也可以使账户恢复到之前的高点之上。将捐款记录保留在声明旁边。这种美元调节表不是年度业绩衡量标准、货币加权回报、已实现的资本收益或税收成本基础的确定。阅读目标差距，而不将其转化为回报承诺 该矩阵会改变即时损失和随后的年度回报。它保持选定的资本、期限、通货膨胀和年终缴款不变。每个单元格都会从该情景的最终投资组合中减去相同的经通胀调整的原始资本目标。正数是模拟盈余；负数是模拟的缺口。两种颜色都没有报告概率或表明投资组合是安全的。由于提款、费用变化或使用日期提前，家庭也可能需要不同的目标。这些变化需要它们自己的现金流，而不是对预期回报进行不明原因的调整。为了进行规划，记录三个单独的事实：损失后剩余的资本、未来可以实际添加的资金以及目标的金额和时间。该模型不包括费用和税金，并将所有分配保留在总回报内。其目的是在所需百分比被误认为预测之前使恢复算法可检查。

590238c3e5cd3150ba879196d1b78767557e4d94.src: The amount repaid, the remaining term and the contractual comparison-rate method all matter. Use a simplified chart to understand sensitivity, then obtain a dated lender payout statement. Identify the contract and the event before calculating a charge A mortgage term is the period during which the current contract applies; amortization is the longer repayment schedule. The remaining-term control in this guide is about months left in the current contract. Entering the full remaining amortization would answer a different question. The FCAC explains that an open mortgage can be broken without a prepayment penalty, while breaking a closed mortgage normally creates one. Other exit costs can still apply. Open or closed describes repayment flexibility; fixed or variable describes rate behaviour. A variable-rate loan is not automatically open. The charts assume a hypothetical full repayment of a closed mortgage during an unexpired term, with the entire entered balance subject to the illustrative charge. They do not calculate a permitted partial prepayment, an open-mortgage charge or the penalty-free payment available at term maturity. Those are different contractual situations. Calculate the two teaching amounts, then apply the stated rule Start with CAD 350,000 repaid in full, an annual contract rate of 5.5%, a hypothetical comparison rate of 4% and twenty-four months remaining. The first calculation is 350,000 × 5.5% × 3/12 = CAD 4,812.50 . This uses a simple quarter-year convention for three months. The positive rate gap is 1.5 percentage points. Holding the balance constant gives a simple interest-rate-difference amount of 350,000 × 1.5% × 24/12 = CAD 10,500 . The model floors the gap at zero and selects the greater of this amount and three months of interest. The first chart therefore selects CAD 10,500. It does not add the first two bars together. Adding the separately entered CAD 400 of other exit costs produces CAD 10,900 in this illustration. The balance, annual rates, time convention, zero floor and higher-of rule are declared teaching assumptions; they are not a lender’s quotation algorithm. Read a method crossover without treating it as an optimal break date The second chart changes the remaining term from one to sixty months while keeping the selected balance and rates fixed. The three-month amount stays level, and the simple interest-difference amount increases in proportion to time. With the starting 5.5% contract rate and 1.5-point gap, the two calculations are equal at eleven months: 1.5% × 11 equals 5.5% × 3. Beyond that point, the simple interest difference is larger. With no positive rate gap, the simple IRD is zero and this model’s three-month amount remains the selected charge. Each point is an independent scenario. Waiting a month in real life can change the balance, available comparable term, comparison rate and contractual exceptions. This line is not a forecast of future quotes. Its crossover also says nothing about whether refinancing recovers its costs; that requires a separate comparison of benefits, costs and remaining debt. Check what the lender means by its comparison rate The FCAC’s prepayment guide explains that lender methods and rate pairs can differ. A posted rate, the borrower’s contract rate, the original discount and a rate associated with a comparable remaining term may enter the calculation. A newly advertised rate for another product is not automatically the correct comparison. For a specific public lender example, RBC describes three months of interest for its closed variable-rate mortgages and the greater of three months and IRD for its closed fixed-rate mortgages. Its explanation also discusses the original rate reduction, present value and a balance declining with scheduled payments. The simple constant-balance formula here does not reproduce that process. The matrix shows how the selected higher-of amount responds to alternative comparison rates and remaining terms. Its cells exclude the entered other costs. It illustrates the specified arithmetic rather than establishing one rule for all Canadian variable or fixed contracts. Separate outstanding principal from the additional exit costs The fourth chart reconciles modeled payout cash: CAD 350,000 of outstanding principal, CAD 10,500 of selected illustrative charge and CAD 400 of other costs. The sum is CAD 360,900. Principal repayment extinguishes a liability. It is a cash requirement, but it is not another break fee. The charge and other entered costs are additional cash uses. Comparing fee totals without separating principal can make the cost of exiting appear much larger than the actual additional expense. A real payout can also include accrued interest, adjustments and other secured amounts that this model omits. The FCAC’s discharge guide describes the separate process of removing the lender’s registered security. Professional or discharge costs may apply; the CAD 400 input is only an assumption, not an estimate for a particular property or province. Use the balance comparison without assuming a prepayment privilege The fifth chart applies the same simplified rules to independent balances equal to 50%, 75% and 100% of the entered amount. At the starting rates and term, the higher charges are CAD 5,250, CAD 7,875 and CAD 10,500. Including the same CAD 400 of other costs gives CAD 5,650, CAD 8,275 and CAD 10,900. This isolates balance sensitivity. It does not say that a borrower may first reduce a real balance to one of those amounts without a charge. A contract’s lump-sum allowance, reset date and restrictions need separate verification. The lender may also have specific conditions for using a privilege near a full payout. FCAC notes that prepayment privileges vary and may refer to a percentage of original principal. Do not automatically subtract a percentage of today’s balance from the amount subject to a charge. Porting to another property also depends on eligibility and conditions; it is not an unconditional waiver of every cost. Obtain the inputs and validity date that the charts cannot supply Before using a number in a transaction budget, identify the full or partial repayment amount, intended payout date, applicable privilege, original rate and discount, comparable remaining term and the lender’s calculation method. Confirm the exact charge, other payable costs and any cash-back repayment. The FCAC’s mortgage-prepayment rights page explains required calculation information and the written-statement commitments of banks following the mortgage-prepayment code. Keep that scope: the same code does not necessarily apply to every Canadian lender. A statement’s validity period and the factors that can change the amount matter. Use these charts to understand why a quoted amount changes when its inputs change. For a decision about replacing the mortgage, carry the verified charge into a comparison over the same horizon, alongside payments, interest, other costs and ending debt. A lower new payment alone does not establish that breaking the old contract is financially beneficial.
590238c3e5cd3150ba879196d1b78767557e4d94.zh: 偿还金额、剩余期限和合同比较利率法都很重要。使用简化的图表来了解敏感性，然后获取注明日期的贷款机构付款声明。在计算费用之前确定合同和事件 抵押期限是指当前合同适用的期间；摊销是指较长的还款期限。本指南中的剩余期限控制约为当前合同剩余的几个月。输入全部剩余摊销将回答不同的问题。 FCAC 解释说，解除开放式抵押贷款无需支付提前还款罚金，而解除封闭式抵押贷款通常会产生提前还款罚金。其他退出费用仍然适用。开放式或封闭式描述了还款灵活性；固定或可变描述速率行为。浮动利率贷款不会自动开放。这些图表假设在未到期期限内全额偿还已关闭的抵押贷款，并按照说明性费用计算全部输入的余额。他们不计算允许的部分预付款、开放式抵押贷款费用或到期时的免罚金。这些是不同的合同情况。计算两个教学金额，然后应用规定的规则：从全额偿还 350,000 加元开始，年合同利率为 5.5%，假设比较利率为 4%，剩余时间为 24 个月。第一个计算结果为 350,000 × 5.5% × 3/12 = CAD 4,812.50 。这使用了三个月的简单季度惯例。正利率差距为1.5个百分点。保持余额不变，简单利率差额为 350,000 × 1.5% × 24/12 = 10,500 加元。该模型将差距定为零，并选择该金额和三个月利息中的较大者。因此，第一个图表选择 10,500 加元。它不会将前两个条加在一起。在此图中，加上单独输入的 400 加元的其他退出成本，得出 10,900 加元。余额、年利率、时间约定、零下限和更高的规则是宣布的教学假设；它们不是贷款机构的报价算法。阅读方法交叉，而不将其视为最佳中断日期 第二个图表将剩余期限从 1 个月更改为 60 个月，同时保持选定的余额和利率固定。三个月金额保持不变，单利差额金额随时间成比例增加。起始合约利率为 5.5%，差距为 1.5 点，两个计算结果在 11 个月时相等：1.5% × 11 等于 5.5% × 3。超过该点，单利差异更大。由于没有正利率差距，简单的 IRD 为零，并且该模型的三个月金额仍然是选定的费用。每个点都是一个独立的场景。在现实生活中等待一个月可能会改变余额、可用可比条款、比较率和合同例外情况。这条线不是对未来报价的预测。它的交叉也没有说明再融资是否可以收回成本。这需要单独比较收益、成本和剩余债务。检查贷款人的比较利率的含义 FCAC 的预付款指南解释说，贷款人的方法和利率对可能有所不同。公布的利率、借款人的合同利率、原始折扣以及与可比剩余期限相关的利率都可以进入计算。另一种产品的新广告价格并不自动是正确的比较。对于特定的公共贷款机构示例，加拿大皇家银行 (RBC) 描述了其封闭式浮动利率抵押贷款的三个月利息以及封闭式固定利率抵押贷款的三个月利息和 IRD 中的较大者。其解释还讨论了最初的利率降低、现值以及按计划付款而减少的余额。这里的简单恒平衡公式并不能重现该过程。该矩阵显示了所选的较高金额如何响应替代比较率和剩余条款。其单元格不包括输入的其他成本。它说明了指定的算术，而不是为所有加拿大可变或固定合同建立一项规则。将未偿本金与额外退出成本分开 第四个图表对模拟支付现金进行了调节：未偿本金 350,000 加元、选定说明性费用 10,500 加元以及其他费用 400 加元。总金额为 360,900 加元。本金偿还消除了负债。这是现金要求，但不是另一笔违约金。费用和其他输入的成本是额外的现金用途。在不分离本金的情况下比较费用总额可能会使退出成本看起来比实际的额外费用大得多。实际支出还可以包括应计利息、调整和该模型省略的其他担保金额。 FCAC 的解除指南描述了解除贷款机构注册担保的单独流程。可能需要支付专业费用或出院费用； CAD 400 输入只是一个假设，而不是对特定财产或省份的估计。使用余额比较而不假定预付款特权第五个图表将相同的简化规则应用于等于输入金额的 50%、75% 和 100% 的独立余额。按照起始费率和期限，较高费用为 5,250 加元、7,875 加元和 10,500 加元。包括同样 400 加元的其他费用，分别为 5,650 加元、8,275 加元和 10,900 加元。这隔离了平衡敏感性。它并没有说借款人可以首先将实际余额减少到这些金额之一，而无需支付任何费用。合同的一次性津贴、重置日期和限制需要单独核实。贷款机构还可能有使用接近全额付款的特权的特定条件。 FCAC 指出，提前还款特权各不相同，可能涉及原始本金的一定百分比。不要自动从收费金额中减去今天余额的百分比。移植到另一处房产也取决于资格和条件；这并不是无条件放弃所有费用。获取图表无法提供的输入信息和有效日期 在交易预算中使用数字之前，确定全部或部分还款金额、预期还款日期、适用的特权、原始利率和折扣、可比较的剩余期限以及贷款机构的计算方法。确认确切的费用、其他应付费用和任何现金返还。 FCAC 的抵押贷款提前还款权利页面解释了所需的计算信息以及银行遵循抵押贷款预付款代码的书面声明承诺。保持范围：相同的代码不一定适用于每个加拿大贷款机构。报表的有效期和可能改变金额的因素很重要。使用这些图表可以了解为什么报价金额会随着输入的变化而变化。对于更换抵押贷款的决定，请将经过验证的费用与付款、利息、其他成本和结束债务一起在同一时间范围内进行比较。仅较低的新付款并不能证明打破旧合同在经济上是有利的。

7f6ceaf5f346e605f78377bf2697428e530d82d9.src: An economic family’s income, an unattached person’s income and a monthly cash budget are different measurements. Keep the population, year and cash definition visible before comparing dollar amounts. Ask whose income the number describes A national income headline can look like a convenient benchmark for a household budget. Before using it, identify the unit behind the observation. A family’s pooled income and one person’s income answer different questions, even when both are expressed in dollars. The 2024 Canadian Income Survey release distinguishes economic families from people outside an economic family. Related people living together can form one economic family; unrelated roommates can be separate unattached-person units. A dwelling is therefore not automatically the same as the income unit in these charts. That distinction matters before comparing a number with a salary. A family can contain more than one income recipient, while its resources support more than one person. Dividing a family median by two does not produce an observed individual median, and dividing it by twelve does not establish what any particular employee receives on a payday. Read the official medians with their population and dollar year The release reports a 2024 combined median after-tax income of CAD 75,500, a family median of CAD 108,900 and an unattached-person median of CAD 41,000. The first chart presents these as separate comparisons. The combined observation includes the two subgroup populations, so the bars are not additive. The second chart retains the family-versus-person distinction while showing senior and non-senior groups. Family senior status follows the highest income earner’s age, rather than requiring every family member to be a senior. Neither graphic adjusts the displayed amounts for family size or different spending needs. The estimates use 2024 constant dollars and were released on 29 April 2026. The original table extract was checked on 25 October 2026. These observations describe their reference population and year; they are not current salary offers, required budgets or a forecast of what a reader will earn. Keep uncertainty and the income definition beside the bars A median locates the middle of a distribution; it does not show its full spread. These selected medians cannot place a reader at a precise percentile or establish that two units with the same income have the same financial circumstances. The selected table observations carry Statistics Canada’s quality code A. The extract supplies no exact coefficient of variation or numeric confidence interval, so the charts do not invent error bars or a significance test. Survey coverage restrictions also apply, including the exclusion of people living on reserves and other Indigenous settlements in the provinces. After-tax income combines market income and government transfers, less income tax. It should not be substituted for a single employee’s regular bank deposit. The practical budgeting question is narrower: which cash resources will actually be available to this defined budget, and which payments must those resources cover? Build a cash ledger from independently supported amounts The editable example begins with CAD 6,000 of monthly after-tax cash resources, or CAD 72,000 for twelve months. It does not begin with one of the source medians. Other annual cash is initially zero and must exclude any amount already included in the monthly entry. Monthly fixed spending is CAD 3,500 and variable spending is CAD 1,400. Together, those use CAD 58,800 over the year. Another CAD 3,000 of annual bills brings spending to CAD 61,800. The independently chosen saving goal is CAD 6,000. The resulting unassigned cash is CAD 72,000 − CAD 61,800 − CAD 6,000 = CAD 4,200 . Saving is shown as a separate allocation rather than consumption. If it is actually transferred to a savings account, it remains a household asset; the calculation simply stops treating it as unassigned cash available for another purpose. Use the matrix to test your plan rather than rank your income The matrix changes monthly cash resources and variable spending. Fixed spending, annual bills, other resources and the saving goal stay selected. A negative cell identifies an annual plan that is not funded by the entered resources. No cell estimates a national income percentile, a poverty threshold or a recommended saving rate. The scenarios are independently entered nominal CAD budgets, while the observed charts use a defined 2024 statistical dollar basis. The tool does not adjust a current budget into that historical purchasing-power basis. At CAD 6,000 of monthly resources, increasing variable spending by CAD 400 a month uses another CAD 4,800 over a year. Under the other defaults, that moves unassigned cash from positive CAD 4,200 to negative CAD 600. This is an arithmetic change in the invented budget, not a measured relationship between income groups in the survey. Turn a benchmark into useful context without making it a target Use the source charts to understand which unit and period an income comparison describes. Then define the people and obligations included in the actual plan. A budget shared by two unrelated people may combine cash for particular bills without becoming one economic family in the statistical definition. Reconcile the cash inputs with supported receipts and avoid overlap between monthly and annual amounts. A tax refund, transfer or irregular payment needs its own amount and date if it is not already included. This annual ledger does not determine tax, benefit eligibility or the opening cash required before a particular receipt arrives. A useful financial plan connects available resources with the household’s own costs and goals. The graphs keep the published context inspectable while leaving that plan independent. A number can be informative about a population without becoming the amount a particular household should earn, spend or save.
