36e65f1e8ef58dd992702842e821179762fac6e3.zh: 通过乘以生长因子来合成序列。其算术平均值并不自动等于最终财富再生产的年率。在计划中使用之前定义平均值算术平均值将个人年回报率相加并除以年数。复合年利率提出了一个不同的问题：什么恒定的年增长率可以重现整个时期从期初资本到期末资本的变化？默认组合是第一年回报率为 25%，第二年回报率为 15%。算术平均值为 (25% − 15%) ÷ 2，即 5%。单独的平滑参考每年赚取 5%。这些路径的算术平均值相同，但增长因子不同。 FINRA 回报计算解释提供了年化业绩和复利的一般背景。这里的所有回报路径和金额都是独立假设的，没有历史市场系列、投资报价或预测。每次回报乘一加元 从 10,000 加元开始，以后不得存款或取款。 25% 的收益乘以 1.25，即达到 12,500 加元。接下来的 15% 损失将较大余额乘以 0.85，剩下 10,625 加元。两年总涨幅为6.25%。相反，平滑的 5% 参考将相同的起始量乘以 1.05 两次。最终收于 11,025 加元，总涨幅为 10.25%。因此，将算术平均值应用为恒定复合假设会在一对后夸大该特定交替路径的结束金额 400 加元。带符号的条形显示所选收益和损失在零附近。他们的百分比是年度总回报，并保留分配。它们并不是每次都以原始美元金额为回报。第二年的损失取决于第一年收益后的余额。计算完整货币对的复合利率 如果算术平均值为 m 并且每次收益与其相差 s，则两个因子为 1 + m + s 和 1 + m − s。它们的乘积为 (1 + m) 2 − s 2 。该表达式中的费率是小数。因此，该完整两年对的年复合利率是 [(1 + m) 2 − s 2 ] 的平方根减去 1 。当 m = 0.05 和 s = 0.20 时，结果约为每年 3.08%。两年后，它从 10,000 加元复制到 10,625 加元。当利差为零时，两者的回报都等于平均值​​，并且复合利率与之匹配。在固定该算术平均值的同时增加价差会减少该构造比较中的乘积。这是该示例的数学条件，而不是声称真正的投资者可以在自由选择波动性的同时保持预期收益不变。将回报价差与回报顺序分开 资本图表也反转了该货币对，首先应用负 15%，然后应用正 25%。它的第一年余额不同，但其两年终点是相同的：两个因子相乘以任一顺序给出相同的乘积。该模型仅重复完整的对，因此两条交替路径每隔一年在选定的最终日期相遇。后来的捐款或取款不会改变任何回报所面临的资金。对于需要提前出售的人来说，不同的中期余额仍然很重要，但这种出售不属于这种模式。这种区别有助于区分两个教训。相同算术平均值下，不同的收益利差可以产生不同的复合增长。当相同的因素适用于未受影响的初始投资时，仅不同的订单不会改变全期产品。请阅读相关的退休指南，了解路径中提款的单独影响。将更长的视野和敏感性矩阵视为假设 分组的条形图比较两年、十年、二十年和三十年，同时保留选定的资本、平均值和利差。在默认的 20 年情况下，平滑参考价格高于重复交替对约 8,197.62 加元。该差额不是从账户中扣除的费用；而是从账户中扣除的费用。它是两个建模最终值之间的差异。该矩阵改变算术平均值和百分点利差，然后显示完整货币对的年复合率。即使算术平均值可能为零或正数，阴性细胞也会识别复合损失。阴影不会为这些返回模式分配可能性。这两种工具都故意使用确定性路径。他们不会估计资产的预期回报、统计波动性、多元化收益或实现目标的概率。真正的投资组合通常不会在两个固定年度回报之间交替，其费用、税收、现金流和持股变动可能很重要。使增长惯例与现金流模型保持一致在将回报假设输入财务计划之前，记录它是名义回报还是实际回报、算术回报还是几何回报、成本之前还是成本之后以及基于什么期间或来源。没有这些定义的数字可以以改变其含义的方式应用。固定利率储蓄计算器使用输入的回报作为复利规则。它不会仅仅因为标签上写着“平均”就模拟分布。添加捐款或取款需要对其日期进行建模；未触及的初始投资的几何比率并不自动成为家庭的货币加权结果。使用该示例作为对解释的检查，而不是假设保证平稳回报或选择特定投资的理由。对于真正的目标，还要检查资金可以继续投资的时间、早期损失的影响、成本、税收和灵活的融资选择。图表的目的是在允许单个平均值代替整个计划之前使比率定义和乘法可见。

f1ef3aa4bec78b15a66fa94013a441f39514b6a9.src: A stable payment is a cash-flow fact, not proof that debt is falling. Compare the payment with interest charged on the current balance and check the contract’s response to a shortfall. Separate a fixed payment from a fixed interest rate A variable-rate mortgage can have a payment amount that stays unchanged for a time. That does not hold the borrowing rate or the interest portion of the payment constant. If interest rises while the cash payment stays the same, less of that payment is available to reduce principal. The Financial Consumer Agency of Canada explains trigger rates and negative amortization for variable-rate loans with fixed payments. Its guidance also directs borrowers to the agreement and their financial institution for the actual trigger and available options. This tool is an invented loan ledger. It applies a selected capitalization rule to show the arithmetic of unpaid interest; it does not establish that a lender permits that behavior, how long it may continue, or what action an actual agreement requires. Read the first twelve payments before the rate changes The default starts with CAD 400,000 of debt, a 5% nominal annual rate compounded monthly and CAD 2,400 paid at each month-end. Interest is the opening monthly balance multiplied by the annual quoted rate divided by twelve. The first month’s interest is about CAD 1,666.67. The rest of the CAD 2,400 payment reduces principal. After twelve payments, debt is about CAD 390,995.51, a reduction of about CAD 9,004.49 from the opening balance. Both comparison paths use this same first year. The alternative payment is introduced only after the selected rate change. This keeps their debt balances identical at the moment the new rate begins, making the next month’s payment allocation directly comparable. At the new rate, compare the interest charge with the cash paid The selected nominal annual rate becomes 8% after twelve completed months, so month thirteen uses the new rate. Interest on the shared opening balance is about CAD 2,606.64. The fixed-payment path still pays CAD 2,400. Its principal allocation is CAD 2,400 − CAD 2,606.64 = negative CAD 206.64 . Under this model’s capitalization assumption, that shortfall is added to debt, which ends the month at about CAD 391,202.14. The alternative pays CAD 3,200 after the change. Against the same first changed-month interest, it reduces principal by about CAD 593.36. This path needs CAD 800 more cash that month. The difference is a budget commitment as well as a debt result; the additional payment is not generated automatically by the calculation. Understand the algebraic trigger without treating it as a lender quote In this monthly-compounding model, the interest-only boundary occurs when opening debt × nominal annual rate ÷ 12 = monthly payment . Solving for the annual rate gives payment multiplied by twelve, divided by opening debt. At the default balance immediately before the change, that illustrative boundary is about 7.3658% nominal annually. The selected 8% rate is above it, so the unchanged payment does not cover the modeled monthly interest. Exactly at the boundary, payment covers interest and contributes zero principal. This result uses the entered balance and a specific compounding convention. A contract may use other timing, payment components or trigger provisions. Confirm its exact rate and response with the lender. The grid is an explanation of the relationship between rate, debt and payment, rather than a substitute for the agreement’s calculation. Reconcile debt, cash payments and interest over the full window Over sixty model months, the unchanged-payment path pays CAD 144,000 in cash and incurs about CAD 146,639.47 of interest charges. Its ending debt is therefore CAD 400,000 + CAD 146,639.47 − CAD 144,000 = CAD 402,639.47 . About CAD 11,643.96 of interest is added to debt during months when payment is below the charge. That amount is larger than the net increase from the original debt because the first year had already reduced principal. “Interest added” and “ending debt minus original debt” measure different things. The alternative pays CAD 182,400 in cash, incurs about CAD 139,959.53 of interest and ends owing about CAD 357,559.53. Its larger cash commitment is CAD 38,400 over the window. The balance comparison does not invest cash retained by the fixed-payment path or value that liquidity; it is a loan-ledger comparison. Use the matrix to identify the question that needs action The matrix starts every cell with the same debt immediately before the change. Its rows replace the nominal annual rate, and its columns replace the monthly payment. A positive cell shows principal reduction in the first changed month. A negative cell shows interest that would be added under the illustrative rule. The cumulative-interest chart reports charges, including amounts not paid in cash. Once added to the balance, those amounts can generate further interest in later periods. Calling the entire charge “interest paid” would hide that distinction. The model has no fees, property-tax component, renewal, missed-payment penalty or lender intervention. Review those items separately, together with the cash needed for a changed payment or additional principal. The useful output is an explicit comparison: what cash is paid, what interest is charged, whether debt is reducing, and what the agreement requires if the current payment becomes insufficient.
f1ef3aa4bec78b15a66fa94013a441f39514b6a9.zh: 稳定的支付是现金流的事实，而不是债务下降的证据。将付款与当前余额收取的利息进行比较，并检查合同对短缺的反应。将固定付款与固定利率分开 浮动利率抵押贷款的付款金额可以在一段时间内保持不变。这并不能使借款利率或付款的利息部分保持不变。如果利息上升而现金支付保持不变，则可用于减少本金的支付会减少。加拿大金融消费者机构解释了固定还款浮动利率贷款的触发利率和负摊销。其指南还指导借款人了解协议及其金融机构，了解实际触发因素和可用选项。这个工具是一个发明的贷款分类账。它应用选定的资本化规则来显示未付利息的算术；它没有规定贷款人是否允许这种行为，这种行为可以持续多久，或者实际协议需要采取什么行动。在利率变化之前阅读前十二笔付款 违约起始金额为 400,000 加元的债务，每月复利 5% 的名义年利率，并在每个月底支付 2,400 加元。利息是期初每月余额乘以年报价除以十二。第一个月的利息约为1,666.67加元。剩余的 2,400 加元付款减少了本金。支付十二次后，债务约为 390,995.51 加元，比期初余额减少约 9,004.49 加元。两种比较路径都使用相同的第一年。仅在选定的费率发生变化后才会引入替代付款方式。这使得他们的债务余额在新利率开始时保持相同，从而使下个月的付款分配直接具有可比性。按照新利率，将利息费用与支付的现金进行比较。选定的名义年利率在十二个月后变为 8%，因此第 13 个月使用新利率。共享期初余额的利息约为 2,606.64 加元。固定付款方式仍需支付 2,400 加元。其主要分配为 2,400 加元 – 2,606.64 加元 = 负 206.64 加元。根据该模型的资本化假设，该缺口将被添加到债务中，月底债务约为 391,202.14 加元。变更后替代方案需支付 3,200 加元。与相同的第一个更改月份利息相比，本金减少了约 593.36 加元。这条路当月还需要 800 加元的现金。区别在于预算承诺和债务结果；额外付款不是通过计算自动生成的。理解代数触发器，而不将其视为贷款机构报价 在这个按月复利模型中，仅利息边界出现在开立债务 × 名义年利率 ÷ 12 = 每月付款 时。求解年利率就是付款额乘以 12，再除以期初债务。按照变化前的默认余额，该说明性边界约为每年名义利率的 7.3658%。所选的 8% 利率高于该利率，因此不变的付款不涵盖模拟的月利息。恰好在边界处，付款涵盖利息并贡献零本金。此结果使用输入的余额和特定的复利约定。合同可以使用其他时间安排、支付组件或触发条款。与贷款机构确认其确切利率和回应。网格是对利率、债务和付款之间关系的解释，而不是协议计算的替代品。在整个窗口内调节债务、现金支付和利息 在 60 个模型月内，不变的支付路径支付 144,000 加元现金，并产生约 146,639.47 加元的利息费用。因此，其期末债务为 CAD 400,000 + CAD 146,639.47 – CAD 144,000 = CAD 402,639.47 。当付款低于费用时，大约 11,643.96 加元的利息会添加到债务中。该金额大于原始债务的净增加额，因为第一年已经减少了本金。 “增加的利息”和“结束债务减去原始债务”衡量的是不同的东西。另一种选择是支付 182,400 加元现金，产生约 139,959.53 加元利息，最终欠款约 357,559.53 加元。其较大的现金承诺为 38,400 加元。余额比较不投资固定支付路径保留的现金或价值流动性；这是贷款分类账的比较。使用矩阵来确定需要采取行动的问题 矩阵在更改之前立即以相同的债务开始每个单元格。它的行取代了名义年利率，它的列取代了每月付款。阳性细胞显示在第一个变化的月份中主要减少。负值单元格表示将根据说明性规则添加的兴趣。累积利息图表报告费用，包括未以现金支付的金额。一旦添加到余额中，这些金额可以在以后的时期产生更多的利息。将全部费用称为“已付利息”会掩盖这种区别。该模式不收取任何费用、财产税、续约、逾期付款罚款或贷款机构干预。单独审查这些项目，以及更改付款或额外本金所需的现金。有用的输出是一个明确的比较：支付了多少现金，收取了多少利息，债务是否减少，以及如果当前支付不足，协议需要什么。

36af76bc8ad7169d2e42bd90f97a844138b817ac.src: An operating subtotal is different from cash available to the owner. Principal repayments, capital payments and tax cash can create a funding need even when a narrower income measure is positive. Begin with money collected and a defined period A rental budget can show several different measures: scheduled rent, rent collected, operating income, debt payments and cash retained. Giving each number a separate name prevents one from being used as a substitute for another. The default example covers one year and all of the modeled property’s receipts and payments. Rent is CAD 3,200 for each occupied month, with one whole month producing no rent. Collected rent is therefore 11 × CAD 3,200 = CAD 35,200 . There is no assumed later recovery of the missing month’s rent. The no-rent-month input is a cash stress, not a local vacancy statistic or an assessment of a tenancy. It can represent a deliberately simplified collection gap, but it does not decide contractual rent owed, legal remedies or the treatment of a bad debt. A real ledger needs the actual receipts and the period to which they relate. Calculate the operating comparator without calling it taxable income Operating cash costs are assumed to continue at CAD 600 for every month, including the month without collected rent. Their annual total is CAD 7,200. The model also includes CAD 10,000 of independently entered annual loan interest. Collected rent less those operating costs and interest is CAD 18,000. This is the article’s explicitly limited operating-less-interest comparator. It is not a tax assessment or a complete accounting profit, and it includes no depreciation, capital cost allowance, accrual adjustment or review of deduction eligibility. The CRA’s rental-expense guidance distinguishes current and capital expenses and sets out conditions for deductions. A cash payment’s label alone does not establish its tax treatment. These charts accept independently supported cash inputs and preserve the distinction between a teaching subtotal and an actual rental-income calculation. Subtract principal from cash while keeping its economic meaning visible The owner pays another CAD 8,000 toward loan principal during the year. That payment uses cash and reduces a liability. It is separate from the CAD 10,000 interest cost, even if both appear inside the same regular mortgage debit. The CRA states that rental-property mortgage or loan principal repayments are not deductible . This is one reason a tax-oriented income number and an owner’s cash flow can differ. The model does not assume that a principal payment becomes a freely available asset that can pay the next bill. Annual principal and interest are entered separately. The tool does not infer them from the total mortgage payment, calculate an amortization schedule or project a future renewal rate. Use a supported statement breakdown when replacing the example. Counting the whole mortgage debit as interest would misdescribe both this cash ledger and the underlying repayment. Include the capital payment and tax cash once each The example pays CAD 5,000 for a separate capital project and allocates CAD 3,000 to tax cash. Both amounts sit outside the CAD 600 monthly operating-cost entry. The default reconciliation is CAD 18,000 − CAD 8,000 − CAD 5,000 − CAD 3,000 = CAD 2,000 retained cash. The capital input is a payment, rather than an estimate of how much market value the project creates. A CAD 5,000 outlay does not automatically increase the property’s sale price by CAD 5,000. The calculator also makes no deduction or depreciation claim for it. The tax allowance is independently entered. It is not a percentage automatically applied to the operating subtotal, a final tax bill or a refund calculation. A tax payment or earmark can reflect other facts and dates. Keep the amount outside operating costs if it is entered here, and avoid including the same cash use in two fields. Test the rent-collection months and larger cash outlays The line chart changes the number of months with collected rent while retaining all annual payments. Its two lines differ by principal repayments, capital cash and the tax allowance. Their vertical separation explains how the same receipt pattern can produce a positive operating comparator and a much smaller owner cash result. With the default payments, annual cash uses total CAD 33,200. At CAD 3,200 per collected month, the arithmetic threshold is 10.375 months. Because the control uses whole months, eleven collected months produce positive annual cash and ten produce a CAD 1,200 annual funding gap. The matrix combines no-rent months with alternative capital cash payments. It assigns no likelihood to either stress. A negative cell records money the owner would need to supply over the year; it does not authorize borrowing, identify an available credit line or show the maximum balance that could be needed between actual receipt and payment dates. Add the calendar before relying on a positive annual total A one-year surplus does not establish that an early bill is funded. A large repair payment can arrive before later rent, while property taxes or insurance may be payable on particular dates. Put those dates beside accessible opening cash to measure the actual short-term buffer. This model excludes the initial purchase, down payment, land-transfer costs, selling costs, changes in property value and return on the owner’s invested capital. It therefore does not calculate a property investment return or establish whether purchasing a rental is attractive. It also excludes shared ownership, personal-use portions and short-term-rental-specific rules. Use the ledger to reconcile supported receipts with distinct cash uses, then obtain the accounting and tax calculations appropriate to the actual property. The planning output is the amount retained or supplied under the entered year’s assumptions, with the economic role of each payment visible. It is a starting point for a dated cash plan rather than a substitute for one.
36af76bc8ad7169d2e42bd90f97a844138b817ac.zh: 营业小计不同于所有者可用的现金。即使较小的收入指标为正值，本金偿还、资本支付和税收现金也可能产生融资需求。从收取的资金和规定的期限开始租金预算可以显示几种不同的衡量标准：预定租金、收取的租金、营业收入、债务支付和保留现金。给每个数字一个单独的名称可以防止一个数字被用作另一个数字的替代品。默认示例涵盖一年以及建模财产的所有收入和付款。每个入住月的租金为 3,200 加元，整月不产生租金。因此，收取的租金为 11 × 3,200 加元 = 35,200 加元。没有假设以后可以收回所欠一个月的租金。无租金月份的输入是现金压力，而不是当地的空置统计数据或租赁评估。它可以代表故意简化的收款缺口，但它不能决定所欠的合同租金、法律补救措施或坏账的处理。真正的分类账需要实际收据及其相关的期间。计算运营比较器，而不将其称为应税收入，假设运营现金成本每月继续为 600 加元，包括未收取租金的月份。他们的年度总收入为 7,200 加元。该模型还包括独立输入的 10,000 加元的年度贷款利息。收取的租金减去运营成本和利息为 18,000 加元。这是本文明确限制的无利息比较。它不是税务评估或完整的会计利润，也不包括折旧、资本成本补贴、应计调整或扣除资格审查。 CRA 的租金支出指南区分了经常支出和资本支出，并规定了扣除条件。现金支付的标签本身并不能确定其税收待遇。这些图表接受独立支持的现金投入，并保留教学小计和实际租金收入计算之间的区别。从现金中减去本金，同时保持其经济意义可见 业主在这一年中另外支付 8,000 加元的贷款本金。该付款使用现金并减少负债。它与 10,000 加元的利息成本是分开的，即使两者都出现在同一个常规抵押贷款借记中。 CRA 规定，出租房产抵押贷款或贷款本金的还款不可扣除。这是税收收入数据和所有者现金流量可能不同的原因之一。该模型并不假设本金还款成为可以支付下一笔账单的可自由使用的资产。年度本金和利息分别输入。该工具不会从抵押贷款总额中推断出它们，也不会计算摊销时间表或预测未来的续订率。替换示例时使用受支持的语句细分。将整个抵押借方计为利息会错误地描述该现金分类账和基础还款。包括资本付款和税款现金各一次 该示例为单独的资本项目支付 5,000 加元，并将 3,000 加元分配给税款现金。这两项金额均不属于每月 600 加元的运营成本条目。默认调节为 CAD 18,000 – CAD 8,000 – CAD 5,000 – CAD 3,000 = CAD 2,000 保留现金。资本投入是一种支付，而不是对项目创造多少市场价值的估计。 5,000 加元的支出不会自动使房产的售价增加 5,000 加元。该计算器也不对其进行任何扣除或折旧索赔。免税额是独立输入的。它不是自动应用于营业小计、最终税单或退款计算的百分比。纳税或专项拨款可以反映其他事实和日期。如果在此处输入，请将金额保留在运营成本之外，并避免在两个字段中包含相同的现金使用。测试收取租金的月份和较大的现金支出 折线图更改收取租金的月份数，同时保留所有年度付款。这两条线在本金偿还、资本现金和税收减免方面有所不同。它们的垂直分离解释了相同的收据模式如何产生积极的运营比较和小得多的所有者现金结果。如果拖欠付款，每年的现金使用总额为 33,200 加元。如果每月收集 3,200 加元，算术阈值为 10.375 个月。由于该控制使用整个月份，因此收集的 11 个月会产生正的年度现金，而 10 个月会产生 1,200 加元的年度资金缺口。该矩阵将无租金月份与替代资本现金支付结合起来。它没有给任何一个压力分配任何可能性。负数单元格记录业主一年内需要提供的资金；它不授权借款、确定可用信用额度或显示实际收款日期和付款日期之间可能需要的最大余额。在依赖正的年度总额之前添加日历 一年盈余并不能证明早期账单得到资助。大笔维修费用可以在后续租金之前支付，而财产税或保险可能会在特定日期支付。将这些日期与可用的期初现金放在一起，以衡量实际的短期缓冲。该模型不包括初始购买、首付、土地转让成本、销售成本、房产价值变化和所有者投资资本回报。因此，它不会计算房地产投资回报或确定购买租金是否有吸引力。它还排除共享所有权、个人使用部分和短期租赁特定规则。使用分类账将支持的收据与不同的现金用途进行核对，然后获得适合实际财产的会计和税收计算。计划产出是在输入年份的假设下保留或提供的金额，每笔付款的经济作用可见。它是过时现金计划的起点，而不是替代方案。

50668e685ee4149e0b47a0df496d7484d36fbec7.src: A payment schedule and a retained-wealth comparison answer different questions. Interest spent on a bill is no longer an asset, and paid interest earns compound growth only when it is retained and reinvested. Keep the principal, rate and maturity the same A fixed-rate certificate can supply periodic interest or accumulate interest until maturity. The timing affects the cash a household receives before the term ends. It can also affect the resources retained when paid interest is spent or saved elsewhere. The example starts both choices with CAD 50,000, a hypothetical 4% annual rate and a five-year maturity. One pays CAD 2,000 at the end of every year. The other adds annual interest to the certificate and pays its accumulated amount only at maturity. These are invented terms, not available rates or issuer quotations. The Autorité des marchés financiers’ debt-securities overview describes periodic and compound interest structures for GICs. Actual contracts need their own interest calculation, payment schedule and access conditions. The examples here assume annual calculation and make no claim about deposit-insurance eligibility or an issuer’s particular certificate. Read the payment bars before interpreting a yield The annual-payout choice supplies CAD 2,000 at each of the first four year-ends. In year five, it pays CAD 2,000 of interest and returns CAD 50,000 of principal, producing a CAD 52,000 cash receipt on that date. The compounding choice supplies no earlier cash under this assumed contract. At maturity, it pays CAD 50,000 × 1.04 5 = CAD 60,832.65 , allowing for displayed rounding. The maturity bars include capital being returned; they are not measures of that year’s interest yield. A household that needs cash in year two cannot automatically spend the accrued amount shown on the compounding line. The graph records an accumulated contract value, not an early-redemption price or a promise of access. Match a real spending deadline to confirmed payment dates and redemption provisions. Give each annual interest payment an explicit destination The default annual-payout choice spends half of each CAD 2,000 interest payment and saves the other half outside the certificate. That means CAD 1,000 of consumption and CAD 1,000 of outside saving at each year-end. The outside account earns an assumed 2% annually before the next year-end deposit. Its first CAD 1,000 deposit receives no additional growth at the instant it arrives. Earlier deposits receive more years of outside interest than later ones, and the final deposit arrives at maturity with no subsequent year of growth inside the selected horizon. After five years, the outside account holds about CAD 5,204.04. It consists of CAD 5,000 of saved certificate interest plus CAD 204.04 earned outside. Another CAD 5,000 of certificate interest has already been spent. The retained-resource line includes principal and outside savings, while keeping that past consumption separate. Reconcile the resources without counting principal twice The payout choice retains CAD 50,000 of principal plus CAD 5,204.04 outside savings, or CAD 55,204.04 at maturity. Its waterfall checks that result using original principal, all certificate interest paid, outside interest earned and consumption. The reconciliation is CAD 50,000 + CAD 10,000 + CAD 204.04 − CAD 5,000 = CAD 55,204.04 . Returning the original CAD 50,000 at maturity converts the certificate asset into cash; it does not create another CAD 50,000 of wealth alongside a continuing certificate asset. The compounding choice retains CAD 60,832.65 and has funded no consumption in this example. Comparing that ending amount directly with CAD 55,204.04 includes a difference in spending as well as reinvestment. It would be misleading to describe the whole CAD 5,628.60 retained-resource gap as inferior investment performance. Use the matrix to separate reinvestment from consumption The matrix varies the outside account return and the share of paid interest spent. Each cell shows payout-choice resources minus compounding-choice resources at the common maturity. A negative cell can therefore arise because interest was consumed, because the outside rate was lower, or from both effects. When no certificate interest is spent and the outside account earns the same 4% annual rate, the two choices finish with the same retained resources under these annual conventions. The certificate pays CAD 2,000 each year, and the separate account compounds those payments at the matching rate. That equality is a mathematical control, not a promise that a matching reinvestment rate will be available. Outside rates can change and may involve different access conditions, taxes or risk. A higher assumed outside rate can increase the payout path’s endpoint, but the matrix assigns neither a likelihood nor a provider recommendation to any rate. Add taxes, contract conditions and the household calendar separately All amounts are before taxes and fees. The model does not determine tax recognition or payment dates for either structure, and it does not assume that receiving no cash automatically means having no tax obligation. The account wrapper and applicable rules need their own review. Confirm whether a real certificate’s quoted rate, compounding convention and payment frequency match the example. Check the term, maturity instructions, early-redemption conditions and any renewal process. An outside account is a separate arrangement; its rate and availability should not be attributed to the certificate issuer without evidence. Use the payment chart to plan cash receipts and the retained-resource ledger to explain what happened to interest after receipt. Then compare alternatives with the household’s actual spending needs stated consistently. Money already used to meet a bill has provided consumption, while money still held can fund a later need; the charts keep those roles distinct.
50668e685ee4149e0b47a0df496d7484d36fbec7.zh: 付款时间表和保留财富比较回答了不同的问题。花在票据上的利息不再是资产，支付的利息只有保留并再投资时才能实现复合增长。保持本金、利率和期限相同固定利率凭证可以提供定期利息或累积利息直至到期。时间安排会影响家庭在期限结束前收到的现金。当支付的利息被花费或保存在其他地方时，它还会影响保留的资源。该示例以 50,000 加元开始两种选择，假设年利率为 4%，期限为五年。每年年底支付 2,000 加元。另一种是在证书上增加年利息，并仅在到期时支付其累积金额。这些是发明的术语，不是可用的利率或发行人报价。金融市场管理局的债务证券概述描述了担保投资证的定期和复利结构。实际合约需要自己的利息计算、付款时间表和访问条件。此处的示例假设按年度计算，并且不对存款保险资格或发行人的特定证书提出任何要求。在解释收益之前，请先阅读付款栏。年度付款选项在前四个年末每年提供 2,000 加元。第五年，它支付 2,000 加元的利息并返还 50,000 加元的本金，并在该日产生 52,000 加元的现金收据。根据该假定合同，复利选择不提供早期现金。到期时，它支付 CAD 50,000 × 1.04 5 = CAD 60,832.65 ，允许显示舍入。到期条包括返还的资本；它们不是当年利息收益率的衡量标准。第二年需要现金的家庭不能自动花费复利线上显示的应计金额。该图表记录了累计合同价值，而不是提前赎回价格或访问承诺。将实际支出截止日期与已确认的付款日期和兑换条款相匹配。为每笔年利息支付提供明确的目的地 默认的年支付选择是花费每笔 2,000 加元利息支付的一半，并将另一半保存在证书之外。这意味着每年年底有 1,000 加元的消费和 1,000 加元的外部储蓄。假设外部账户在下一年年底存款之前每年赚取 2% 的利息。它的第一笔 1,000 加元存款在到达的那一刻就不会再增加。较早的存款比较晚的存款获得更多年的外部利息，并且最终存款到期时，在选定的期限内没有随后的年份增长。五年后，外部账户持有约 5,204.04 加元。其中包括 5,000 加元的储蓄凭证利息加上在外部赚取的 204.04 加元。另外 5,000 加元的凭证利息已被花掉。保留资源线包括本金和外部储蓄，同时将过去的消费分开。调节资源，无需两次计算本金 支付选择保留 50,000 加元的本金加上 5,204.04 加元的外部储蓄，或到期时保留 55,204.04 加元。它的瀑布使用原始本金、所有已支付的证书利息、赚取的外部利息和消费来检查结果。调节结果为 50,000 加元 + 10,000 加元 + 204.04 加元 - 5,000 加元 = 55,204.04 加元。到期返还原5万加元，将凭证资产转换为现金；它不会与持续的凭证资产一起创造另外 50,000 加元的财富。在此示例中，复利选择保留 60,832.65 加元，并且没有为任何消耗提供资金。直接将该期末金额与 55,204.04 加元进行比较，包括支出和再投资方面的差异。将整个 5,628.60 加元的保留资源缺口描述为较差的投资绩效可能会产生误导。使用矩阵将再投资与消费分开 该矩阵会改变外部账户回报和支付利息支出的份额。每个单元格显示共同到期日的支付选择资源减去复利选择资源。因此，由于利息被消耗、外部利率较低或两者兼而有之，就会出现负单元格。当没有花费证书利息并且外部账户赚取相同的 4% 年利率时，这两种选择在这些年度惯例下将获得相同的保留资源。该证书每年支付 2,000 加元，单独的账户按匹配利率复合这些付款。这种平等是一种数学控制，而不是提供相匹配的再投资率的承诺。外部费率可能会发生变化，并且可能涉及不同的准入条件、税收或风险。较高的假设外部利率可以增加支付路径的端点，但矩阵既不会为任何利率分配可能性，也不会分配提供商建议。分别添加税费、合同条件和家庭日历 所有金额均为税费前的金额。该模型并未确定这两种结构的税务确认或付款日期，并且并不假设没有收到现金自动意味着没有纳税义务。帐户包装和适用的规则需要自己审查。确认真实证书的报价利率、复利约定和支付频率是否与示例相符。检查期限、到期说明、提前赎回条件和任何续订流程。外部账户是一项单独的安排；其速率和可用性不应在没有证据的情况下归因于证书颁发者。使用付款图表来计划现金收入，并使用保留资源分类账来解释收到后利息的情况。然后将替代方案与一致表述的家庭实际支出需求进行比较。已经用来支付账单的钱已经提供了消费，而仍然持有的钱可以满足以后的需求；图表将这些角色区分开来。

d379e105cd439962eca00a5806c4697a3ae64e72.src: The same total payment can reduce different parts of a card balance. Interest cost depends on which balances remain, so the allocation rule belongs beside the payment amount and the rates. Keep transaction balances and their rates separate A credit card can contain amounts charged at different interest rates. A single total balance then hides information needed to understand the next interest charge and how a payment changes the account. The FCAC explains that different transaction types can carry different rates and describes highest-rate-first or proportional treatment of amounts paid above the minimum. It also directs borrowers to the agreement for the issuer’s allocation rules. This calculator does not identify an actual card’s rules or calculate its legal minimum. The example starts with CAD 5,000 in bucket A at an assumed 18% nominal annual rate and CAD 2,000 in bucket B at 30%. There are no new transactions, promotional expiries, fees, grace periods or rate changes. Interest is simplified to the opening monthly balance multiplied by its annual rate divided by twelve. Use the same explicit minimum assumption in both paths The illustrative minimum is the smaller of the interest-inclusive statement total and the greater of CAD 25 or the selected percentage of that total. The default percentage is 3%. It is a model parameter, not a statement about the minimum that applies to a particular borrower or province. First-cycle interest is CAD 75 in bucket A and CAD 50 in bucket B. The total statement becomes CAD 7,125. Three percent gives an illustrative minimum of CAD 213.75. The selected fixed payment budget is CAD 300, leaving CAD 86.25 above that minimum. For this comparison, the minimum portion is allocated proportionally to the two statement balances in both paths. That is an explicit shared assumption. It must not be read as the issuer’s actual treatment of the minimum. Keeping it identical isolates what changes when the excess CAD 86.25 is allocated by a different rule. Follow the first payment into each bucket The proportional minimum allocation sends CAD 152.25 to bucket A and CAD 61.50 to bucket B. Under highest-rate-first excess allocation, the remaining CAD 86.25 goes to bucket B because its entered rate is higher. After that first payment, bucket A is CAD 4,922.75 and bucket B is CAD 1,902.25. Their total is CAD 6,825. Under proportional excess allocation, the whole CAD 300 payment follows the statement-balance weights. Bucket A ends at about CAD 4,861.32 and bucket B at about CAD 1,963.68. Both totals are CAD 6,825 because the same CAD 125 interest was added and the same CAD 300 was paid. The difference appears in the mix remaining for the next cycle. The higher-rate balance is smaller under the first rule, so its next interest charge is smaller, even though the combined first-cycle debt is identical. Compare complete repayment costs only when both schedules finish Under the defaults, highest-rate-first excess allocation repays the combined debt in thirty cycles. Total interest is about CAD 1,929.91. Proportional excess allocation takes thirty-one cycles and incurs about CAD 2,169.54. The modeled full-payoff interest difference is about CAD 239.64. The component bars show why each bucket need not have lower interest separately. Highest-first incurs about CAD 1,494.11 in bucket A and CAD 435.79 in bucket B. Proportional allocation incurs about CAD 1,248.02 and CAD 921.52 respectively. The increase in A’s interest is smaller than the reduction in B’s interest. The result keeps the same total payment budget while debt remains, with the last payment capped at what is owed. It does not invest money released by an earlier payoff or compare the household’s wealth after later saving. Those would be additional cash flows with their own assumptions. Keep a blocked or unfinished path visibly incomplete If the entered payment is below the illustrative minimum for a cycle, the model stops before projecting that cycle. A CAD 100 payment cannot start the default schedule because it is below CAD 213.75. The tool does not invent an approved reduced payment or simulate an actual late-payment regime. A one-point debt line therefore means no payment cycle could be projected under those assumptions. Interest and payments shown for an unfinished path cover completed modeled cycles only. They exclude the unprojected future and must not be called a lifetime cost. The schedule also stops after 120 cycles if debt remains. A low payment can leave an unpaid balance or fail to offset interest under some entered terms. The payoff metric then reports no completed payoff, and the comparison with a full repayment cost is unavailable. No default fee, penalty rate or credit-reporting outcome is calculated. Read the rate-and-payment matrix beside the actual agreement The matrix changes bucket B’s rate and the fixed monthly payment budget. It reports an interest saving only when both hypothetical paths fully repay within the limit and meet their assumed minimums. Unavailable cells preserve that condition rather than treating an incomplete result as zero cost. Bucket B is not always the higher-rate balance after edits. The highest-first method sorts the two actual entered rates. At equal rates, the allocation mix does not change the combined interest result under this simplified ledger. The chart labels retain A and B so that a rate edit does not silently change which balance is being followed. For a real card, confirm each transaction balance, rate, minimum formula, payment allocation and processing date. Actual daily interest, grace periods and fees can materially change the statement. The graphs teach how an allocation rule changes a defined repayment ledger; they do not replace the agreement or supply instructions for a live payment.
d379e105cd439962eca00a5806c4697a3ae64e72.zh: 相同的支付总额可以减少卡余额的不同部分。利息成本取决于剩余余额，因此分配规则属于付款金额和利率。将交易余额及其利率分开 信用卡可以包含按不同利率收取的金额。然后，单个总余额隐藏了了解下一次利息费用以及付款如何改变帐户所需的信息。 FCAC 解释说，不同的交易类型可能具有不同的费率，并描述了对高于最低支付金额的最高费率优先或按比例处理。它还指导借款人遵守发行人分配规则的协议。该计算器无法识别实际卡的规则或计算其法定最低限额。该示例首先在 A 桶中存入 5,000 加元，假定名义年利率为 18%，在 B 桶中存入 2,000 加元，假定名义年利率为 30%。没有新交易、促销到期、费用、宽限期或费率变化。利息简化为期初每月余额乘以年利率除以十二。在两条路径中使用相同的明确最小假设 说明性最小值是含利息报表总额中的较小者和 25 加元或该总额的选定百分比中的较大者。默认百分比为 3%。它是一个模型参数，而不是关于适用于特定借款人或省份的最小值的声明。第一周期利息为 A 组中的 75 加元，B 组中的 50 加元。总报表变为 7,125 加元。百分之三给出的说明性最小值为 213.75 加元。选定的固定付款预算为 300 加元，比最低限额高出 86.25 加元。对于此比较，最小部分按比例分配给两个路径中的两个报表余额。这是一个明确的共同假设。不得将其解读为发行人对最低限度的实际待遇。保持相同可以隔离当通过不同规则分配多余的 CAD 86.25 时发生的变化。按照第一笔付款进入每个存储桶 按比例最低分配将 152.25 加元发送到存储桶 A，将 61.50 加元发送到存储桶 B。在最高利率优先的超额分配下，剩余的 86.25 加元进入存储桶 B，因为其输入的利率较高。第一次付款后，A 桶的金额为 4,922.75 加元，B 桶的金额为 1,902.25 加元。他们的总金额为 6,825 加元。在比例超额分配下，整个 300 加元付款遵循报表余额权重。 A 组的价格约为 4,861.32 加元，B 组的价格约为 1,963.68 加元。两者总计均为 6,825 加元，因为添加了相同的 125 加元利息并支付了相同的 300 加元。差异出现在下一个周期剩余的混合物中。在第一个规则下，利率较高的余额较小，因此其下一个利息费用较小，即使第一周期债务总额相同。仅当两个计划都完成时才比较完整的还款成本。在违约情况下，利率最高的超额分配将在三十个周期内偿还合并债务。总利息约为 1,929.91 加元。按比例超额分配需要三十一个周期，产生约 2,169.54 加元。模型中的全额还款利息差约为 239.64 加元。组成条显示了为什么每个桶不需要单独具有较低的利息。最高优先分配在 A 组中产生约 1,494.11 加元，在 B 组中产生约 435.79 加元。按比例分配分别产生约 1,248.02 加元和 921.52 加元。 A的利息增加量小于B的利息减少量。结果保持相同的总付款预算，而债务仍然存在，最后一次付款的上限为所欠金额。它不会投资早期支付释放的资金，也不会比较后来储蓄后的家庭财富。根据他们自己的假设，这些将是额外的现金流。保持阻塞或未完成的路径明显不完整如果输入的付款低于一个周期的说明性最低金额，则模型会在预测该周期之前停止。 100 加元付款无法启动默认计划，因为它低于 213.75 加元。该工具不会发明经批准的减少付款或模拟实际的逾期付款制度。因此，一分债务额度意味着在这些假设下无法预测付款周期。未完成路径显示的利息和付款仅涵盖已完成的建模周期。它们排除了未预测的未来，并且不能被称为终身成本。如果债务仍然存在，则该计划也会在 120 个周期后停止。低额付款可能会留下未付余额或无法抵消某些输入条款下的利息。然后，支付指标报告没有完成支付，并且无法与全额还款成本进行比较。不计算违约金、罚款率或信用报告结果。阅读实际协议旁边的费率和付款矩阵 该矩阵更改了存储桶 B 的费率和固定的每月付款预算。仅当两条假设路径在限额内完全偿还并达到假定的最低限额时，它才会报告利息节省。不可用的单元格会保留该条件，而不是将不完整的结果视为零成本。存储桶 B 并不总是编辑后利率较高的余额。从高到低的方法对两个实际输入的费率进行排序。在同等利率下，分配组合不会改变该简化分类账下的综合利息结果。图表标签保留 A 和 B，以便汇率编辑不会默默地更改所遵循的余额。对于真实卡，请确认每笔交易余额、费率、最低公式、付款分配和处理日期。实际每日利息、宽限期和费用可能会对报表产生重大影响。这些图表说明了分配规则如何更改定义的还款分类账；他们不会取代协议或提供实时付款的说明。

b936b7156763e2b6a654f47173b00fb6e178df33.src: Keep the lender’s assessed payments and gross-income ratios beside an independent household cash budget. Each view reveals a different constraint. Write down which question each calculation answers Mortgage planning involves more than finding a payment a calculator will accept. An underwriting ratio compares specified obligations with income under a lender’s assessment. A household budget asks whether the actual cash arriving can cover the home, everyday life, debt repayments and saving. A decision can look comfortable in one view and tight in the other. The tool keeps those views side by side. Gross annual income is used only in the ratio calculation. Monthly take-home income is entered separately for the cash budget. It does not convert one into the other or estimate an income-tax return. FCAC’s mortgage-preparation guidance discusses income, housing costs, debt and the household budget. The charts develop an original example from independently entered values. They do not check a credit file, verify income or make an application decision. Use assessed obligations consistently in the ratios Gross debt service, or GDS, compares the assessed housing amount with gross income. Total debt service, or TDS, adds assessed other-debt obligations. The tool expresses annual income monthly so numerator and denominator cover the same period. For the cited comparison, CMHC publishes 39% GDS and 44% TDS references . Its housing treatment includes qualifying principal and interest, property taxes, heating and half of applicable condominium fees. Those references are held fixed in the chart and were reviewed on 25 October 2026. The default assessed housing total is CAD 3,850 monthly: CAD 3,200 qualifying principal and interest, CAD 300 property tax, CAD 150 heat and CAD 200 from half of the full CAD 400 condo fee. Against CAD 10,000 gross monthly income, GDS is 38.5%. Adding CAD 500 of assessed other debt makes TDS 43.5%. These are original example calculations. Actual income acceptance, debt assessment and other conditions need confirmation with the applicable lender and insurer. The tool takes the assessed other-debt obligation as an input rather than assuming that every contractual minimum is the amount used in underwriting. Keep the assessed payment separate from the payment you expect to make A qualifying payment can be calculated at a rate above the mortgage contract rate. The tool therefore asks for actual principal and interest and qualifying principal and interest separately. Neither amount is derived from the other here; both should be independently checked when a real mortgage is being considered. As reviewed on 25 October 2026, OSFI describes the minimum qualifying rate for uninsured mortgages as the greater of the contract rate plus two percentage points or 5.25%. It describes application to most newly underwritten residential mortgages at federally regulated lenders. OSFI also identifies an exception for qualifying uninsured straight switches between federally regulated lenders at renewal, without an increase to the loan or amortization. This article does not determine whether a case meets that exception or another rule. Do not use a new-borrowing illustration to infer the requirements of every renewal or transfer. Pay the full bill in the household cash ledger The ratio’s treatment of part of a cost does not reduce the actual bill. The cash waterfall therefore includes the full condo fee, actual mortgage payment and entered property tax and heat. It also includes other non-overlapping home costs, such as insurance or maintenance, that the household needs to fund. In the default budget, CAD 7,500 of take-home income funds CAD 3,700 of housing costs, CAD 500 of other repayments, CAD 2,500 of non-housing living costs and CAD 750 of planned saving. Only CAD 50 remains. Both displayed ratios are below the cited reference percentages, yet this example has very little unused monthly cash. Each cost should appear once. Put other home costs outside the tax, heat and condo amounts already entered. Put non-housing living expenses outside debt repayments and saving. If an assessed debt amount differs from the actual repayment, retain the distinction instead of forcing one number into both calculations. Inspect payment room and budget flexibility together The income curve asks how much qualifying mortgage principal and interest fits within both reference ratios after the selected assessed obligations. It is payment room, not a mortgage principal amount, a house price or a pre-approval. Turning it into a loan amount would require an independently checked rate, amortization and other financing inputs. The budget matrix asks a separate question. It changes take-home income and everyday living costs while preserving gross income and the assessed obligations. The GDS/TDS ratios therefore stay unchanged, even though the amount of actual cash remaining can move from a surplus to a shortfall. Use the two views to frame the next review: verify the assessed inputs, fund closing costs separately, check irregular home expenses, and test whether saving and an accessible reserve remain feasible. A negative budget needs an explicit response. A positive one still needs review against real payment dates and costs that may be missing from the first draft.
b936b7156763e2b6a654f47173b00fb6e178df33.zh: 将贷款人的评估付款和总收入比率与独立的家庭现金预算放在一起。每个视图都揭示了不同的约束。写下每个计算回答的问题 抵押贷款规划不仅仅涉及找到计算器可接受的付款。承保比率将特定义务与贷款机构评估的收入进行比较。家庭预算询问实际收到的现金是否能够满足家庭、日常生活、债务偿还和储蓄的需要。一项决定可能在一种观点看来很舒服，但在另一种观点看来却很严格。该工具将这些视图并排保存。年总收入仅用于比率计算。每月实得收入单独输入现金预算。它不会将其中一种转换为另一种，也不会估计所得税申报表。 FCAC 的抵押贷款准备指南讨论了收入、住房成本、债务和家庭预算。这些图表根据独立输入的值开发了一个原始示例。他们不检查信用档案、核实收入或做出申请决定。在比率中一致地使用评估债务 总偿债额 (GDS) 将评估的住房金额与总收入进行比较。总偿债额（TDS）增加了评估的其他债务义务。该工具表示每月的年收入，因此分子和分母涵盖同一时期。对于引用的比较，CMHC 发布了 39% GDS 和 44% TDS 参考文献。其住房待遇包括合格的本金和利息、财产税、供暖费和一半的适用公寓费。这些参考信息已固定在图表中，并于 2026 年 10 月 25 日进行了审核。默认评估的住房总额为每月 3,850 加元：3,200 加元的合格本金和利息、300 加元的财产税、150 加元的取暖费以及 400 加元公寓全额费用一半中的 200 加元。相对于每月总收入 10,000 加元，GDS 为 38.5%。加上 500 加元的评估其他债务，TDS 为 43.5%。这些是原始示例计算。实际收入接受、债务评估和其他条件需要与适用的贷款人和保险公司确认。该工具将评估的其他债务义务作为输入，而不是假设每个合同最低金额都是承保中使用的金额。将评估的付款与您预期支付的付款分开。合格的付款可以按高于抵押贷款合同利率的利率计算。因此，该工具要求分别提供实际本金和利息以及合格本金和利息。这里的两个金额都不是从另一个金额派生出来的；当考虑真正的抵押贷款时，两者都应该独立检查。根据 2026 年 10 月 25 日的审查，OSFI 将无保险抵押贷款的最低合格利率描述为合同利率加两个百分点或 5.25% 的较高者。它描述了联邦监管贷款机构大多数新承保的住宅抵押贷款的应用。 OSFI 还确定了一个例外情况，即在续约时，符合条件的无保险的贷款机构可以在联邦监管的贷款机构之间直接转换，而无需增加贷款或摊销。本文并不确定某个案例是否符合该例外情况或其他规则。不要使用新借用的插图来推断每次续借或转让的要求。支付家庭现金分类账中的全部账单 该比率对部分成本的处理不会减少实际账单。因此，现金瀑布包括全额公寓费、实际抵押贷款付款以及输入的财产税和供暖费。它还包括家庭需要资助的其他非重叠的家庭成本，例如保险或维护费用。在默认预算中，7,500加元的实得收入用于支付3,700加元的住房费用、500加元的其他还款、2,500加元的非住房生活费用和750加元的计划储蓄。只剩下50加元了。两个显示的比率均低于引用的参考百分比，但此示例几乎没有未使用的每月现金。每个成本应该出现一次。将其他住房成本计入已输入的税费、供暖费和公寓金额之外。将非住房生活支出放在偿还债务和储蓄之外。如果评估的债务金额与实际还款额不同，请保留这种区别，而不是在两个计算中强制使用同一个数字。一起检查还款空间和预算灵活性收入曲线询问在选定的评估义务后，合格的抵押贷款本金和利息在两个参考比率中的符合程度。这是还款房，不是抵押本金，不是房价，也不是预批。将其转化为贷款金额需要独立检查的利率、摊销和其他融资投入。预算矩阵提出了一个单独的问题。它改变了实得收入和日常生活成本，同时保留了总收入和分摊义务。因此，即使实际剩余现金量可能从盈余变为短缺，GDS/TDS 比率仍保持不变。使用这两个视图来构建下一次审查：验证评估的投入，分别资助结算成本，检查不规则的家庭开支，并测试储蓄和可用储备是否仍然可行。负预算需要明确的回应。积极的仍需要根据第一稿中可能遗漏的实际付款日期和费用进行审查。

6c7b6cfa13c1f7168db0fa66b8a001a90cb632c1.src: An aggregate saving ratio describes a sector with an accounting definition. Set a personal saving commitment from actual cash flow, goals and deadlines rather than copying that percentage. Read the date, population and denominator before the percentage The latest observation in the reviewed Statistics Canada table is a 3.7% household saving rate for the second quarter of 2026. The table was released on 28 August 2026 and retrieved for this article on 25 October 2026. It is not an October monthly reading. The first chart shows twelve consecutive quarters, from 2023 Q3 through 2026 Q2, from one release vintage. Each observation is the published ratio of household net saving to household disposable income. It is not a return on a savings account, a percentage of people who save, or an average bank-transfer instruction. The chart’s largest value within this displayed window is 5.9% in 2024 Q3. The latest 3.7% is 2.2 percentage points below that observation. It is 0.4 percentage points above revised 2026 Q1. Those are comparisons of published percentages, not explanations of why the rate changed or evidence of how any particular household fared. Reproduce the accounting bridge before interpreting the result The second chart reconstructs 2026 Q2 household net saving from the same source rows. In annualized CAD billions, disposable income is 1,860.216, final consumption expenditure is 1,844.124 and the change in pension entitlements is 51.828. The identity is disposable income − final consumption expenditure + change in pension entitlements = household net saving . In the displayed units, 1,860.216 − 1,844.124 + 51.828 equals 67.920. Omitting the pension adjustment would not reproduce the published saving amount. Dividing 67.920 by 1,860.216 and multiplying by one hundred gives about 3.6512%, which rounds to the published 3.7%. The chart data table retains three decimal places of billions, preserving the source’s million-dollar precision. The amounts are sector accounting flows; the pension adjustment does not mean an equivalent cash transfer entered every household’s bank account during that quarter. Keep annualized flows separate from quarterly cash The selected source dimension is seasonally adjusted at annual rates. Seasonal adjustment addresses estimated seasonal and calendar patterns, and annualization expresses the dollar flows at an annual pace. The displayed amounts should not be read as literal cash received or spent over the three calendar months alone. The annualization applied to both dollar flows cancels in the saving-to-income ratio. Do not multiply the saving-rate percentage by four. The rate is also not an investment yield and cannot be inserted into a compound-interest model as a return assumption. Statistics Canada’s household-sector scope includes unincorporated businesses and excludes non-profit institutions serving households. Its disposable-income concept has a broader accounting construction than one person’s take-home-pay deposit. These definitions are why this article calls the measure Canada’s household saving rate , rather than treating it as an economy-wide national saving measure or an individual budget ratio. Define a different, explicitly personal cash budget The third chart starts again with a hypothetical household. It does not scale down the statistical sector totals. Monthly net cash income is CAD 6,000, ordinary living costs are CAD 4,200, required debt-principal payments are CAD 300 and predictable irregular bills total CAD 3,600 per year. Reserving one-twelfth of those irregular bills allocates CAD 300 a month. After living costs, required principal and that reserve, CAD 1,200 remains before the saving-goal transfer. A requested CAD 500 transfer leaves CAD 700 unallocated in this selected plan. The CAD 500 transfer is about 8.33% of entered net cash income. That arithmetic uses a different numerator and denominator from the official 3.7% statistic. It is not evidence that this household is saving more adequately than another, and the model does not calculate national-accounts pension accrual or classify every cash item as statistical consumption. Separate planned transfers from spending and principal payments The annual-bill reserve is money assigned to known future obligations. It can remain in a savings account temporarily without becoming free money for a second goal. The example excludes those bills from the ordinary living-cost input so the same annual expense is not counted twice. Debt principal is listed separately from living costs. Repaying principal reduces a liability, while using cash that cannot simultaneously fund the requested goal transfer. Loan interest can be included in the living-cost amount; adding the entire loan payment there and principal again in its own field would double-count part of the commitment. The requested goal transfer is a planning instruction, not a guarantee that cash is available. If obligations and the requested transfer exceed income, the waterfall ends below zero. That negative endpoint represents an unfunded plan; it does not create an overdraft or automatically move the requested amount. Use the matrix to test a goal-based commitment The matrix changes monthly net income and the requested goal transfer while preserving the selected living costs, principal payments and irregular-bill reserve. Every cell reports cash left after those allocations. It is a monthly budget sensitivity, rather than a distribution of Canadian households or a prediction of income. A positive cell shows headroom within this partial budget. A negative one identifies a funding gap that needs a change in resources, spending, commitments or timing. Unlisted expenses and an emergency reserve still require their own review. The FCAC’s budgeting guide provides a framework for tracking receipts, spending and goals. Set a goal in dollars with a date, estimate its required contribution and reconcile that amount with actual cash flow. Review the statistical chart as economic context while retaining its source date and revisions. This keeps a useful public indicator in its proper role: evidence about the household sector, alongside a separately defined plan for the money one household needs to manage.
6c7b6cfa13c1f7168db0fa66b8a001a90cb632c1.zh: 总储蓄率描述了具有会计定义的部门。根据实际现金流、目标和期限设定个人储蓄承诺，而不是照搬该百分比。阅读百分比前的日期、人口和分母 经审查的加拿大统计局表格中的最新观察结果是 2026 年第二季度的家庭储蓄率为 3.7%。该表格于 2026 年 8 月 28 日发布，并于 2026 年 10 月 25 日检索本文。这不是 10 月份的月度读数。第一张图表显示了一个发布年份的连续十二个季度，从 2023 年第三季度到 2026 年第二季度。每个观察值都是公布的家庭净储蓄与家庭可支配收入的比率。它不是储蓄账户的回报、储蓄者的百分比或平均银行转账指令。该图表在此显示窗口内的最大值为 2024 年第三季度的 5.9%。最新的 3.7% 比该观察值低 2.2 个百分点。比修订后的 2026 年第一季度高出 0.4 个百分点。这些是对公布的百分比的比较，而不是对比率变化原因的解释或任何特定家庭表现如何的证据。在解释结果之前重现会计桥梁第二张图表根据相同的源行重建了 2026 年第二季度的家庭净储蓄。按年化十亿加元计算，可支配收入为 1,860.216，最终消费支出为 1,844.124，养老金权益变化为 51.828。恒等式为可支配收入−最终消费支出+养老金权益变化=家庭净储蓄。在显示单位中，1,860.216 − 1,844.124 + 51.828 等于 67.920。忽略养老金调整将不会重现公布的储蓄金额。将 67.920 除以 1,860.216 再乘以 100，所得结果约为 3.6512%，四舍五入为公布的 3.7%。图表数据表保留了十亿的小数点后三位，保留了源的百万美元精度。这些金额是部门会计流量；养老金调整并不意味着该季度有等额现金转移进入每个家庭的银行账户。将年化流量与季度现金分开选定的源维度按年率进行季节性调整。季节性调整涉及估计的季节和日历模式，年化表示美元每年的流动速度。显示的金额不应被理解为仅在三个日历月内收到或支出的字面现金。适用于美元流动的年化抵消了储蓄与收入的比率。不要将储蓄率百分比乘以四。该利率也不是投资收益率，不能作为回报假设插入复利模型中。加拿大统计局的家庭部门范围包括非法人企业，不包括为家庭服务的非营利机构。它的可支配收入概念比一个人的实得工资存款具有更广泛的会计结构。这些定义就是为什么本文将该指标称为加拿大家庭储蓄率，而不是将其视为整个经济范围的国民储蓄指标或个人预算比率。定义不同的、明确的个人现金预算 第三张图表再次从假设的家庭开始。它不会缩小统计部门的总数。每月净现金收入为 6,000 加元，普通生活费用为 4,200 加元，所需的债务本金付款为 300 加元，每年可预测的不定期账单总计 3,600 加元。保留这些不规则账单的十二分之一每月可分配 300 加元。扣除生活费用、所需本金和准备金后，在储蓄目标转移之前还剩 1,200 加元。所请求的 500 加元转账在该选定计划中留下 700 加元未分配。 500 加元转账约占输入净现金收入的 8.33%。该算术使用与官方 3.7% 统计数据不同的分子和分母。没有证据表明这个家庭的储蓄比另一个家庭更充足，并且该模型不计算国民账户养老金应计额或将每个现金项目分类为统计消费。从支出和本金还款中单独计划转移 年度票据准备金是分配给已知的未来义务的资金。它可以暂时保留在储蓄账户中，而不会成为第二个目标的免费资金。该示例将这些账单排除在普通生活成本投入之外，因此相同的年度支出不会计算两次。债务本金与生活费用分开列出。偿还本金减少了负债，但使用的现金无法同时为所请求的目标转移提供资金。贷款利息可以包含在生活费用金额中；在那里添加全部贷款付款并在其自己的领域再次添加本金将重复计算部分承诺。所请求的目标转移是一项计划指示，而不是现金可用的保证。如果义务和请求的转移超过收入，瀑布就会低于零。该负终点代表一个没有资金支持的计划；它不会创建透支或自动转移请求的金额。使用矩阵测试基于目标的承诺 该矩阵会更改每月净收入和所要求的目标转移，同时保留选定的生活成本、本金还款和不规则账单准备金。每个单元都会报告分配后剩余的现金。它是每月预算敏感性，而不是加拿大家庭的分布或收入预测。正值单元格显示此部分预算内的空间。负数表示存在资金缺口，需要改变资源、支出、承诺或时间安排。未列出的费用和紧急储备金仍需要自行审查。 FCAC 的预算指南提供了跟踪收入、支出和目标的框架。设定一个带有日期的美元目标，估计其所需的贡献，并将该金额与实际现金流量进行核对。将统计图表作为经济背景进行审查，同时保留其来源日期和修订。这使有用的公共指标发挥了应有的作用：有关家庭部门的证据，以及一个家庭需要管理的资金的单独定义的计划。

9bad185fa848d61e26cc499827ea167e5c7d7351.src: A month can finish with money in the account after borrowing was needed earlier. Count the qualifying debits and negative-balance days, then separate fees, interest and principal owed. A positive monthly total does not fund every earlier bill The default account starts with CAD 500 and receives two CAD 2,200 net pay deposits, on days five and twenty. Outflows are a CAD 1,800 housing bill on day one, four CAD 400 spending debits on days seven, fourteen, twenty-one and twenty-eight, and a CAD 500 bill on day twelve. Before borrowing charges, receipts and spending leave CAD 1,000 at month-end: CAD 500 + CAD 4,400 − CAD 3,900. But the first housing bill arrives before either pay deposit. Paying it turns the account balance negative CAD 1,300. The positive final total cannot make that earlier funding requirement disappear. The model assumes the listed transactions are authorized and funded within an available overdraft arrangement. It does not establish an approved limit or guarantee that a bank will process a payment. The FCAC overdraft guide explains the product’s general mechanics and the need to check the agreement. State exactly which transaction triggers a charge The first hypothetical arrangement charges a flat CAD 5 on day thirty, even if borrowing was not used. The second charges CAD 5 after every positive debit that leaves the account negative. That includes a debit that increases an overdraft already outstanding. A zero-dollar debit is ignored. In the default per-debit case, the housing payment triggers the first fee. After the first salary arrives and the next spending debit is paid, the day-twelve bill takes the account below zero again and triggers another fee. The day-fourteen debit increases that negative balance and triggers a third fee. This is a defined teaching structure, not a universal meaning of “pay per use.” Agreements may charge differently, waive fees, use thresholds or group transactions by day. Counting only transitions from positive to negative would undercount this example’s fees because it would overlook the debit that adds to an existing overdraft. Calculate the interest on the balance that is actually negative Both examples assume a 21% nominal annual borrowing rate. At the end of each day, after deposits, spending and applicable fees, interest accrues as the negative balance multiplied by 21% divided by 365. A positive or zero balance incurs no overdraft interest. The daily interest accrues separately until it is debited after day thirty. The model does not charge daily interest on previously accrued but unposted interest during this month. Fees, however, reduce cash immediately when they are charged, so they can increase the interest-bearing balance. Under the defaults, the flat arrangement incurs approximately CAD 4.37 of interest and CAD 5 of fees. The per-debit arrangement incurs approximately CAD 4.45 of interest and CAD 15 of fees. Total charges are therefore about CAD 9.37 and CAD 19.45. These are independently calculated illustrations; they are not current institution quotations or an estimate of the account’s annual borrowing cost. Keep the cash bridge separate from the price of borrowing The peak-borrowing bars answer how far below zero the account goes. In the default, the largest negative balance is CAD 1,300 under the flat arrangement and CAD 1,305 under per-debit fees. That amount measures a cash bridge, while the fee-and-interest bars measure its modeled cost. A deposit first reduces the negative account balance before leaving positive cash. The model does not treat the overdraft as free savings, count its limit as income or assume that interest payments reduce the principal. A plan can have a modest charge and still need a substantial amount of money before payday. The default flat arrangement has ten days with a negative end-of-day transaction balance before the final interest debit. The per-debit arrangement has twelve. Fees can make a nearly balanced day negative and keep it negative until another receipt. The two paths therefore need separate ledgers rather than a common debt balance with two fee totals attached afterward. Test the buffer and the pay date without changing monthly pay The matrix replaces opening cash and the first pay date. The second pay deposit always follows fifteen days later. All pay amounts and spending dates remain selected, so the comparison changes timing and the initial buffer rather than quietly increasing earnings. Each cell reports the per-debit arrangement’s fees plus interest for this one modeled month. It is not the opening cash required to avoid all borrowing and is not a prediction of future bank fees. A smaller charge can coexist with an outstanding overdraft at the end, which must be read from the actual cash path. Deposits precede debits when they share a day in this example. Real processing order, holds and cut-off times may differ. If a payment and salary are close together, verify when money becomes available instead of assuming their shared calendar date guarantees sufficient funds. Use actual transaction history before changing the arrangement List deposits and required payments by their actual availability dates. Separate fee-triggering transactions from days with debt outstanding. Check the agreement’s fee definitions, waivers, limits and repayment conditions. Reconstruct daily balances and interest using the institution’s convention. Test a realistic opening buffer or an agreed change to a bill date. Review whether the shortfall repeats in later months. The model excludes declined payments, NSF charges, linked-account transfers and subsequent-month repayment. It does not compare an authorized overdraft with an unauthorized missed payment or assess eligibility for credit. Its purpose is to show why monthly averages, transaction counts and borrowing days belong together. Reducing charges can help, but a recurring gap also needs a household cash-flow plan and a feasible reserve-building schedule.
9bad185fa848d61e26cc499827ea167e5c7d7351.zh: 之前需要借钱后，一个月就可以用完账户里的钱了。计算合格借方和负余额天数，然后将所欠费用、利息和本金分开。每月总额为正数并不能为之前的每笔账单提供资金 默认账户从 500 加元开始，并在第五天和第 20 天收到两笔 2,200 加元的净工资存款。流出是第一天 1,800 加元的住房账单，第七、十四、二十一和二十八天的四笔 400 加元的支出借方，以及第十二天的 500 加元的账单。在借贷费用、收据和支出之前，月底还剩 1,000 加元：500 加元 + 4,400 加元 – 3,900 加元。但第一笔住房账单是在支付押金之前到达的。支付后，账户余额将变为负 1,300 加元。最终的正数总额不能使之前的资金需求消失。该模型假设列出的交易在可用的透支安排内获得授权和资助。它不建立银行处理付款的批准限额或保证。 FCAC 透支指南解释了产品的一般机制以及检查协议的必要性。准确说明哪笔交易触发收费 第一个假设安排在第 30 天收取 5 加元的固定费用，即使没有使用借贷。第二个账户在每次借记正数（导致账户出现负数）后收取 5 加元。这包括增加已经未清的透支的借方。零美元借记将被忽略。在默认按借记的情况下，住房付款会触发第一笔费用。第一份工资到达并支付下一笔支出借方后，第十二天的账单再次使帐户低于零并触发另一笔费用。第十四天的借方会增加负余额并触发第三笔费用。这是一个明确的教学结构，而不是“按使用付费”的普遍含义。协议可能会收取不同的费用、免除费用、使用门槛或按天进行团体交易。仅计算从正值到负值的转换会低估此示例的费用，因为它会忽略增加现有透支的借方。计算实际负余额的利息 这两个示例都假设名义年借款利率为 21%。每天结束时，扣除存款、支出和适用费用后，利息按照负余额乘以 21% 再除以 365 计算。正余额或零余额不会产生透支利息。每日利息单独累积，直至三十天后记入借方。该模型不会对本月之前应计但未过帐的利息收取每日利息。然而，收取费用后，现金会立即减少，因此可以增加计息余额。在违约情况下，统一安排将产生约 4.37 加元的利息和 5 加元的费用。每次借记安排大约产生 4.45 加元的利息和 15 加元的费用。因此，总费用约为 9.37 加元和 19.45 加元。这些是独立计算的插图；它们不是当前的机构报价或账户年度借贷成本的估计。将现金桥梁与借款价格分开 借款峰值栏反映了账户低于零的程度。默认情况下，统一安排下的最大负余额为 1,300 加元，每借记费用下的最大负余额为 1,305 加元。该金额衡量现金桥梁，而费用和利息栏则衡量其建模成本。存款首先会减少负账户余额，然后留下正现金。该模型不将透支视为自由储蓄，也不将其限额计为收入或假设利息支付会减少本金。计划的收费可能不高，但在发薪日前仍需要大量资金。默认固定安排在最终利息借记之前有十天的日终交易余额为负数。每借方安排有十二个。费用可能会使几乎平衡的一天变成负数，并在收到另一笔收据之前一直保持负数。因此，这两条路径需要单独的分类账，而不是共同的债务余额，然后附加两个费用总额。在不改变月薪的情况下测试缓冲和支付日期 该矩阵取代了期初现金和第一个支付日期。第二次支付押金总是在十五天后发生。所有支付金额和支出日期均保持选定状态，因此比较会改变时间和初始缓冲，而不是悄悄增加收入。每个单元格报告每个借记安排的费用以及该模型月份的利息。它不是避免所有借款所需的期初现金，也不是对未来银行费用的预测。较小的费用可以与最后的未偿透支共存，这必须从实际的现金路径中读取。在此示例中，当存款共用一天时，存款先于借记。实际处理顺序、保留时间和截止时间可能有所不同。如果付款和薪水接近，请验证资金何时可用，而不是假设他们的共享日历日期保证有足够的资金。在更改安排之前使用实际交易历史记录 按实际可用日期列出存款和所需付款。将费用触发交易与未偿债务天数分开。检查协议的费用定义、豁免、限制和还款条件。使用机构惯例重建每日余额和利息。测试实际的期初缓冲或商定的帐单日期更改。检查短缺是否会在接下来的几个月中再次出现。该模型不包括拒绝付款、NSF 费用、关联账户转账和后续月份还款。它不会将授权透支与未经授权的逾期付款进行比较，也不会评估信贷资格。其目的是展示为什么月平均数、交易数和借贷天数属于同一组。降低费用可以有所帮助，但经常出现的缺口还需要家庭现金流计划和可行的储备建设时间表。

60a7225cdea2473792c10e24ec06052506b33c6c.src: A population threshold and an individual cash budget are different measurements. Keep the survey period and group denominator visible, then reconcile your own shelter payment with net income and the rest of the household plan. Identify exactly what the official percentage counts Statistics Canada’s release of 21 September 2026 reports Canadian Housing Survey results for reference year 2024. Its housing-affordability measure uses shelter costs relative to total before-tax household income. The first chart shows the share of households spending at least 30% of that income on shelter. For all households, the reported shares are 21.5% in 2018, 19.5% in 2021, 22.0% in 2022 and 23.2% in 2024. These are separate survey-cycle observations. The 2020 cycle was delayed to 2021. The chart does not fill in unobserved annual values or imply that the latest observation describes a household’s situation today. A value of 23.2% here is the proportion of households above the published threshold. It is not an average shelter share of income. Confusing those denominators would turn a population count into an entirely different budget measure. Read each tenure rate within its own group The 2024 comparison reports 5.7% for owners without a mortgage, 26.1% for owners with a mortgage and 33.7% for renters. Each rate uses households within that named tenure group as its denominator. The bars do not represent three slices of the entire population and should not be added together. The release covers the provinces, with 2024 collection running from 28 October 2024 to 31 March 2025. It is a dated national survey comparison, rather than a local rental quote or a current mortgage-offer comparison. The displayed release table supplies no confidence intervals, so the graphics make no significance claim. These descriptive differences also do not isolate what would happen if a specific family changed tenure. Households can differ in income, age, location, debt and other characteristics. The comparison is useful context for identifying questions, not a causal estimate of the savings from buying or renting. Do not substitute a before-tax ratio for spendable cash The editable budget begins with CAD 80,000 of annual before-tax income, CAD 5,000 of monthly net income received and CAD 2,000 of monthly shelter cash cost. Annualizing that shelter amount gives CAD 24,000. Dividing by CAD 80,000 produces a 30% gross-income ratio. The same CAD 2,000 is 40% of the CAD 5,000 received each month. Neither percentage changes the bill; only the denominator changes. The two income fields are independently entered assumptions, without a tax or payroll calculation linking them. Reconcile the actual gross and net figures before using a personal comparison. The simple ratio is an educational calculation. It does not reproduce every survey measurement rule, establish a lender’s underwriting result or determine whether a household qualifies for assistance. A published classification can provide context without becoming a recommended maximum payment. Subtract the rest of the household commitments The default net cash budget subtracts CAD 2,000 of shelter, CAD 2,000 of other living costs, CAD 300 of other required debt payments and CAD 500 assigned to saving. That leaves CAD 200 per month not yet assigned. The waterfall makes each subtraction visible instead of treating everything beyond shelter as discretionary money. The CAD 500 saving transfer is an allocation of cash, rather than a consumption expense or a tax. If that money is assigned to another goal, it is not also available to pay a housing bill without changing the goal’s funding plan. Likewise, keep other debt payments outside shelter only when they have not already been counted there. For a homeowner, a mortgage payment’s principal component still leaves the bank account even though it may build equity. The cash budget must fund it on time. A rise in net worth does not automatically provide liquid money for groceries, insurance or an upcoming property-tax instalment. Stress the residual rather than relying on one ratio The matrix changes shelter costs and other living costs while retaining selected net income, other debt payments and assigned saving. Cells show the monthly cash not yet allocated. Negative amounts identify a shortfall in the entered budget; positive amounts are not automatically safe to spend if irregular expenses are missing. Changing the before-tax income field alters the gross ratio but does not change this net cash ledger. That separation is deliberate. A larger gross salary figure cannot pay a bill unless it also translates into cash available to the household on the relevant dates. Try a higher shelter payment with the same saving commitment, then increase other living costs. The test helps locate how little room remains when several costs move together. These are hypothetical dollar stresses without probabilities, forecasts of local rents or a statistical distribution derived from the surveyed households. Rebuild the personal housing decision from current evidence Record the current, fully inclusive shelter cash costs and payment dates. Reconcile before-tax household income with actual net receipts. Include required debt payments, regular living costs and dated irregular bills. Identify saving already promised to other goals. Test higher costs or a temporary income interruption. Review the immediate cash buffer as well as the monthly residual. The official comparison remains fixed when you edit these inputs. Your budget does not change the survey observations, and national survey rates do not reconstruct your family’s finances. For a real purchase or lease, use current quotations, actual account receipts and the relevant agreement. Read the related home-purchase guide for upfront costs and the rent-versus-buy guide for a common-horizon comparison. This article connects statistical context with household arithmetic while keeping their populations, dates and purposes separate.
60a7225cdea2473792c10e24ec06052506b33c6c.zh: 人口阈值和个人现金预算是不同的衡量标准。保持调查期间和组分母可见，然后将您自己的住房付款与净收入和家庭计划的其余部分进行核对。准确确定官方百分比的计算依据 加拿大统计局 2026 年 9 月 21 日发布的报告显示了 2024 年参考年的加拿大住房调查结果。其住房负担能力指标使用相对于税前家庭总收入的住房成本。第一个图表显示了将至少 30% 收入用于住房的家庭比例。对于所有家庭，2018 年报告的比例为 21.5%，2021 年为 19.5%，2022 年为 22.0%，2024 年为 23.2%。这些是单独的调查周期观察结果。 2020 年周期推迟到 2021 年。该图表没有填写未观察到的年度值，也没有暗示最新观察结果描述了家庭当前的情况。这里的 23.2% 是高于公布阈值的家庭比例。这不是庇护所收入的平均份额。混淆这些分母将使人口统计变成完全不同的预算指标。阅读各自组内的每个保有权率 2024 年的比较报告显示，无抵押贷款的业主为 5.7%，有抵押贷款的业主为 26.1%，租房者为 33.7%。每个比率都使用该指定保有权组内的家庭作为分母。这些条形并不代表整个总体的三部分，因此不应加在一起。该发布覆盖各省，2024年的收集时间为2024年10月28日至2025年3月31日。这是一份过时的全国调查比较，而不是当地的租金报价或当前的抵押贷款报价比较。显示的发布表不提供置信区间，因此图形没有任何意义。这些描述性差异也并不能孤立特定家庭改变保有权时会发生什么。家庭的收入、年龄、地点、债务和其他特征可能有所不同。这种比较是识别问题的有用背景，而不是对购买或租赁节省的因果估计。请勿用税前比率代替可支出现金 可编辑预算从每年税前收入 80,000 加元、收到的每月净收入 5,000 加元以及每月住房现金费用 2,000 加元开始。按年计算该庇护所金额为 24,000 加元。除以 80,000 加元即可得出 30% 的总收入比率。同样的2,000加元是每月收到的5,000加元的40%。这两个百分比都不会改变账单；只有分母改变。这两个收入字段是独立输入的假设，没有将它们链接起来的税收或工资计算。在进行个人比较之前，先核对实际的毛额和净额。简单比率是一种教育计算。它不会重现每项调查测量规则，确定贷款人的承保结果或确定家庭是否有资格获得援助。已发布的分类可以提供背景信息，但不会成为建议的最高付款额。减去其余的家庭承诺 默认净现金预算减去 2,000 加元的住房费用、2,000 加元的其他生活费用、300 加元的其他所需债务支付以及分配给储蓄的 500 加元。每月还有 200 加元尚未分配。瀑布使每一次减法都可见，而不是把庇护所之外的一切都视为可自由支配的钱。 500加元储蓄转账是现金分配，而不是消费支出或税收。如果这笔钱被分配给另一个目标，则在不改变目标融资计划的情况下也无法支付住房账单。同样，仅当其他债务尚未计入避难所时，才将其保留在避难所之外。对于房主来说，抵押贷款的主要部分仍然留在银行账户中，尽管它可能会增加资产净值。现金预算必须按时提供资金。净资产的增加并不会自动为食品杂货、保险或即将到来的财产税分期付款提供流动资金。强调剩余而不是依赖一个比率 该矩阵改变了住房成本和其他生活成本，同时保留选定的净收入、其他债务支付和分配的储蓄。单元格显示尚未分配的每月现金。负数表明输入的预算存在短缺；如果不存在非常规开支，正数的支出并不一定是安全的。更改税前收入字段会更改总比率，但不会更改此净现金分类帐。这种分离是故意的。较大的工资总额无法支付账单，除非它也转化为家庭在相关日期可用的现金。在相同的储蓄承诺下尝试更高的住房付款，然后增加其他生活成本。该测试有助于确定当多种成本一起移动时剩余的空间所剩无几。这些是假设的美元压力，没有概率、对当地租金的预测或来自调查家庭的统计分布。根据当前证据重建个人住房决定 记录当前的、完全包容的住房现金成本和付款日期。将税前家庭收入与实际净收入进行核对。包括所需的债务偿还、正常生活费用和注明日期的不规则账单。确定已承诺用于其他目标的节省。测试更高的成本或暂时的收入中断。检查即时现金缓冲以及每月剩余金额。当您编辑这些输入时，官方比较保持不变。您的预算不会改变调查观察结果，全国调查率也不会重建您家庭的财务状况。对于实际购买或租赁，请使用当前报价、实际账户收据和相关协议。请阅读相关的购房指南了解前期成本，并阅读租赁与购买指南进行共同比较。本文将统计背景与家庭算术联系起来，同时将其人口、日期和目的分开。

fdbed8f6139846c8e1faa28df03464ce6a3ee5aa.src: A fixed coupon does not fix the amount you can receive from an early sale. Match the investment’s cash dates to the date of the spending goal. Separate face amount, purchase price and coupon A bond can carry a fixed coupon and still have a changing market price. The face amount is the principal the issuer is scheduled to repay at maturity. The purchase price is what the buyer pays today. The coupon is a contractual cash payment, often expressed as a percentage of face. These quantities are related but are not interchangeable. In the default illustration, CAD 10,000 of face pays a CAD 400 annual coupon for ten years. At a 4% effective annual discount yield, its price immediately after a coupon date is CAD 10,000. Changing the market yield does not rewrite that CAD 400 coupon in this fixed-coupon example; it changes what a buyer would pay for the remaining payments. The SEC’s investor bulletin on interest-rate risk explains the general relationship between fixed-rate bond prices and market rates. Our chart supplies a separate annual-payment calculation. It is not a current bond offer or an estimate of a particular issuer’s creditworthiness. A scheduled principal repayment may arrive after your bill If the cash goal is three years away and the bond matures in ten, funding the goal from the bond can require a sale with seven years still outstanding. The scheduled maturity principal does not automatically become available at year three. The sale price depends on the remaining cash flows and the yield a buyer requires at that time. The tool applies the selected yield reset immediately after purchase and keeps that yield constant afterward. At a reset to 6%, the default bond is worth about CAD 8,528 immediately after the change. Its later market value moves toward maturity value as the remaining term shortens, assuming all payments occur as modeled. This is a controlled pricing scenario, not a forecast of an interest-rate path. Actual market prices also respond to changing credit spreads, trading conditions, optionality and other factors omitted here. An issuer failing to pay would invalidate the assumed coupon and principal receipts. Include the coupon cash exactly once The path chart adds three possible components: the current market value of a still-outstanding bond, coupons already received and retained, and principal received at maturity. Before maturity, retained principal is zero. After maturity, the outstanding bond value is zero. This prevents counting the principal twice. Coupons and maturity proceeds earn no interest in this illustration. At a goal date after maturity, the wealth line is therefore flat once the final coupon and principal have arrived. A personal plan could reinvest that cash, but then it would need a reinvestment rate, payment schedule and another risk assessment. The chart’s points fall immediately after each annual coupon or maturity payment. The purchase occurs immediately after a coupon boundary with no accrued interest. Real bonds often pay on a different schedule, and an actual settlement can include accrued interest and dealing costs. Read the present-value formula behind the price For face amount F, annual coupon C, effective annual yield y and N remaining annual payments, the price is the sum of C ÷ (1 + y) t for t = 1 to N, plus F ÷ (1 + y) N . A higher discount yield reduces the present value of those same promised amounts. At zero yield, price becomes F + NC. At the coupon rate, an ordinary annual-coupon bond at a coupon boundary prices at face in this simplified model. These are useful mathematical checks, not evidence that a particular instrument is offered at those levels. The matrix changes term and yield while preserving face and coupon. A cell is a price at one date. It does not include coupons already received or a future return calculation. Compare the same column across terms to see how a longer stream of fixed payments changes the sensitivity. A holding-period dollar gain is different from the quoted yield The waterfall adds retained coupons to exit value or maturity principal, then subtracts the original purchase price. The total is a nominal holding-period gain or loss in dollars. A positive coupon step can be offset by selling below the purchase price; coupon income alone does not describe the whole result. The purchase yield is used to discount the initial cash flows. It is not automatically the realized compound return when coupons sit idle and the bond is sold before maturity. This article deliberately does not label the dollar gain as an annualized yield or calculate an investor’s after-tax result. For a dated goal, record each usable cash receipt and the amount that depends on an early sale. Compare that calendar with the bill date. A suitable plan also considers the issuer, currency, liquidity, fees, tax treatment and whether other resources can cover a price shortfall. Maturity matching addresses one timing issue; it does not remove every investment risk.
fdbed8f6139846c8e1faa28df03464ce6a3ee5aa.zh: 固定优惠券并不能确定您可以从早期销售中获得的金额。将投资的现金日期与支出目标的日期相匹配。单独的票面金额、购买价格和息票债券可以带有固定息票，但市场价格仍然会变化。票面金额是发行人计划到期偿还的本金。购买价格是买家今天支付的价格。优惠券是一种合同现金支付，通常以面值的百分比表示。这些数量相关但不可互换。在默认插图中，10,000 CAD 的面值可支付 400 CAD 的年优惠券，为期十年。按 4% 的有效年折扣收益率计算，息票日后其价格为 10,000 加元。更改市场收益率不会重写此固定息票示例中的 400 加元息票；它改变了买家支付剩余款项的金额。美国证券交易委员会关于利率风险的投资者公告解释了固定利率债券价格与市场利率之间的一般关系。我们的图表提供了单独的年度付款计算。它不是当前的债券要约或对特定发行人信誉度的估计。预定的本金偿还可能会在您的账单之后到达。如果现金目标是三年后，而债券在十年内到期，那么用债券为目标提供资金可能需要在尚未偿还的七年内出售。预定到期本金不会在第三年自动可用。销售价格取决于剩余现金流和买家当时所需的收益率。该工具在购买后立即应用所选收益率重置，并在之后保持该收益率恒定。重置为 6% 后，默认债券的价值约为 8,528 加元。假设所有付款均按照模型进行，随着剩余期限的缩短，其后期市场价值将趋向到期价值。这是受控定价情景，而不是利率路径的预测。实际市场价格也会对不断变化的信用利差、交易条件、选择性和此处省略的其他因素做出反应。发行人未能付款将使假定的息票和本金收入无效。只包含一次息票现金 路径图添加了三个可能的组成部分：尚未偿还的债券的当前市场价值、已收到并保留的息票以及到期时收到的本金。到期前，保留本金为零。到期后，未偿还债券价值为零。这可以防止对本金进行两次计数。在此示例中，息票和到期收益不会产生任何利息。因此，在到期后的目标日期，一旦最终息票和本金到达，财富线就会保持平坦。个人计划可以将这些现金再投资，但随后需要再投资率、付款时间表和另一项风险评估。图表的点在每次年度息票或到期付款后立即下降。购买发生在优惠券边界之后，没有应计利息。真正的债券通常按不同的时间表支付，实际的结算可能包括应计利息和交易成本。阅读价格背后的现值公式 对于票面金额 F、年息 C、有效年收益率 y 和 N 剩余年付款，价格为 C ÷ (1 + y) t（t = 1 到 N）之和，加上 F ÷ (1 + y) N 。较高的折扣收益率会降低相同承诺金额的现值。收益率为零时，价格变为 F + NC。在票面利率上，普通年息债券在票面边界上的价格是在这个简化模型中的。这些是有用的数学检查，而不是证明在这些级别提供特定工具的证据。该矩阵改变了期限和收益率，同时保留了面子和息票。一个单元格是一个日期的价格。它不包括已收到的优惠券或未来的回报计算。比较不同期限的同一列，看看较长的固定付款流如何改变敏感性。持有期美元收益与报价收益率不同。瀑布将保留息票添加到退出价值或到期本金中，然后减去原始购买价格。总额是以美元计算的名义持有期损益。正优惠券步骤可以通过低于购买价格出售来抵消；仅凭票息收入并不能描述全部结果。购买收益率用于对初始现金流进行贴现。当息票闲置并且债券在到期前出售时，它不会自动实现复合回报。本文故意没有将美元收益标记为年化收益率或计算投资者的税后结果。对于有日期的目标，记录每笔可用的现金收入以及取决于早期销售的金额。将该日历与帐单日期进行比较。合适的计划还考虑发行人、货币、流动性、费用、税收待遇以及其他资源是否可以弥补价格缺口。成熟度匹配解决了一个时间问题；它并不能消除所有投资风险。

784dceee1e3440cd19266991621c40c0cc86b275.src: A higher advertised reward rate applies only to eligible purchases on the stated terms. Compare the cash actually earned with the fee and interest, using spending the household already intended to make. Keep the purchase budget fixed before comparing rewards A rewards comparison starts with purchases the household already plans to make. Increasing spending to reach a reward threshold creates a new expense as well as a reward. These charts therefore hold an existing annual budget fixed when comparing the two hypothetical cards. The example uses CAD 24,000 of eligible annual purchases. Forty percent, or CAD 9,600, belongs to a bonus category. The premium card pays an assumed 3% on qualifying purchases up to an annual purchase-dollar cap, and 1% on the remainder. It charges a CAD 120 annual fee. The comparison card charges no annual fee and pays 1% on all those purchases. The FCAC’s credit-card guide identifies rates, fees and rewards as important comparison features and notes that interest can reduce reward value. No actual card, approval criterion, merchant classification or offered reward rate is used here. The terms are original teaching assumptions. Apply the category cap before multiplying by the reward rate The premium card’s annual cap is CAD 10,000 of purchases eligible for its bonus rate. Under the default mix, bonus purchases are CAD 9,600, so the cap does not yet bind. Those purchases earn CAD 288. The remaining CAD 14,400 earns CAD 144 at the 1% base rate. Total gross cash back is therefore CAD 432. The no-fee card earns CAD 240 on the same CAD 24,000 of purchases. The gross difference is CAD 192, but that is before the premium card’s CAD 120 annual fee. Its advantage after the fee is CAD 72 in this invented example. If the bonus-category share rises to 50%, the household has CAD 12,000 of purchases in that category. Only CAD 10,000 earns 3%; the remaining CAD 2,000 earns the base rate along with other purchases. The category-mix line therefore stops gaining an additional bonus once the cap is reached. An annual purchase cap is different from a limit on the cash reward itself. Separate gross cash back from the net result The waterfall begins with the two cash-back components and subtracts the annual fee. At zero entered interest, its endpoint is CAD 312. That amount is gross cash back of CAD 432 less the CAD 120 fee; it is not the same as the CAD 72 advantage over another card that also earns rewards. The annual interest input is an independently entered cash cost. It is applied equally to both cards, so the comparison does not silently give one card a different repayment pattern. If CAD 400 is entered, the premium card’s net reward becomes negative CAD 88 and the no-fee card’s becomes negative CAD 160. The premium card still has a CAD 72 relative advantage because a common CAD 400 cost cancels in the subtraction. Both absolute results are negative, however. A favourable comparison with one alternative does not mean that rewards cover all costs. The model does not calculate actual interest from statement dates, grace periods, rates or daily balances. Read the spending curve as alternatives, not a target Each point on the spending chart represents a different existing annual purchase budget with the same category share and reward terms. The line is useful for identifying where a fee is covered by incremental cash back. It does not suggest increasing spending until a preferred card wins. With the default terms, the premium card earns two extra percentage points only on bonus-eligible purchases. Before the cap binds, a 40% bonus-category share creates an extra reward of 0.8% of total eligible purchases. Covering a CAD 120 fee therefore requires CAD 15,000 of those purchases: CAD 120 divided by 0.008. That threshold relies on the selected mix, rates and cap. If the mix changes, or a merchant is ineligible, the calculation changes. After the CAD 10,000 bonus-purchase cap is reached, the maximum extra reward at the default rates is CAD 200 before the fee. More base-rate spending then adds the same reward to both cards. Use the matrix to isolate the fee and the category mix The matrix keeps annual eligible purchases at the selected total and varies two assumptions: the premium fee and the bonus-category share. Positive cells show a premium-card advantage under these terms; negative cells show a no-fee-card advantage. Neither colour is an assessment of a real product’s suitability. The common interest amount does not change the matrix because it is deducted from both choices. The waterfall and line charts still show its effect on absolute net cash back. This separation helps answer two distinct questions: which entered card has the better relative result, and whether either card’s rewards exceed the entered costs. Benefits such as travel cover, lounge access, purchase protection or introductory bonuses are excluded. Add a benefit only after confirming that it is available, useful and not already supplied elsewhere. A headline advertised value is not automatically equivalent to cash the household would otherwise spend. Reconcile the model with the actual card agreement For a real comparison, classify a supported purchase history using each issuer’s eligibility rules. Confirm whether caps apply by month, year, category or account, and whether spending above a cap receives a base rate. Review exclusions, redemption conditions, additional-card fees and any applicable merchant charges. This model assumes every earned dollar is redeemed at its entered cash value. It does not value points, account for expiry, calculate a minimum redemption threshold or assume that a welcome offer repeats annually. These features can change the result and need their own supported amounts and dates. Keep repayment planning separate from reward optimization. The charts compare the same purchases and an explicit cost allowance; they do not calculate a borrowing limit, a credit score or an affordable repayment. A practical comparison preserves the purchase budget, verifies the terms and checks the resulting costs in dollars before treating a reward rate as a saving.
784dceee1e3440cd19266991621c40c0cc86b275.zh: 更高的广告奖励率仅适用于符合规定条款的合格购买。使用家庭已经打算赚取的支出，将实际赚取的现金与费用和利息进行比较。在比较奖励之前保持购买预算固定 奖励比较从家庭已经计划进行的购买开始。增加支出以达到奖励阈值会产生新的支出和奖励。因此，在比较两张假设的卡片时，这些图表保持现有的年度预算固定。该示例使用符合条件的年度采购金额 24,000 加元。百分之四十，即 9,600 加元，属于奖金类别。对于符合年度购买金额上限的合格购买，高级卡假定支付 3%，其余部分支付 1%。收取 120 加元的年费。比较卡不收取年费，并为所有购买支付 1%。 FCAC 的信用卡指南将利率、费用和奖励视为重要的比较特征，并指出利息会降低奖励价值。这里没有使用实际的卡、批准标准、商户分类或提供的奖励率。这些术语是原始教学假设。在乘以奖励率之前应用类别上限高级卡的年度上限为符合奖励率的 10,000 加元的购买。在默认组合下，奖金购买金额为 9,600 加元，因此尚未绑定上限。这些购买可赚取 288 加元。其余 14,400 加元按 1% 的基本利率赚取 144 加元。因此，现金返还总额为 432 加元。免费卡在同样 24,000 加元的购买中可赚取 240 加元。总差额为 192 加元，但未包含高级卡 120 加元年费。在本发明的示例中，扣除费用后的优势是72加元。如果奖金类别份额上升至 50%，则家庭在该类别中的购买金额为 12,000 加元。仅需10,000加元即可赚取3%；剩余的 2,000 加元可与其他购买一起赚取基本费率。因此，一旦达到上限，类别混合线将停止获得额外奖励。年度购买上限与现金奖励本身的限制不同。将总现金返还与净结果分开瀑布从两个现金返还部分开始，然后减去年费。输入利息为零时，其终点为 312 加元。该金额为 432 加元的总现金返还减去 120 加元的费用；它与另一张同样可以获得奖励的卡相比 72 加元的优势不同。年利息输入是独立输入的现金成本。它同样适用于两张卡，因此比较不会默默地赋予一张卡不同的还款模式。如果输入 400 加元，高级卡的净奖励将变为负 88 加元，免费卡的净奖励将变为负 160 加元。高级卡仍然具有 72 加元的相对优势，因为普通 400 加元的成本在减法中被抵消。然而，这两个绝对结果都是负面的。与一种替代方案进行有利的比较并不意味着奖励涵盖了所有成本。该模型不会根据报表日期、宽限期、利率或每日余额计算实际利息。将支出曲线视为替代方案，而不是目标 支出图表上的每个点代表不同的现有年度购买预算，具有相同的类别份额和奖励条件。该行可用于确定增量现金返还涵盖哪些费用。在首选卡获胜之前，它并不建议增加支出。根据默认条款，高级卡仅在符合奖励资格的购买中赚取两个额外百分点。在上限生效之前，40% 的奖金类别份额可产生符合资格购买总额 0.8% 的额外奖励。因此，支付 120 加元的费用需要购买 15,000 加元：120 加元除以 0.008。该阈值取决于所选的组合、费率和上限。如果组合发生变化，或者商家不符合资格，计算方式就会发生变化。达到 10,000 加元购买奖励上限后，默认费率下的最高额外奖励为 200 加元（不含费用）。更多的基本费率支出将为两张卡带来相同的奖励。使用矩阵来分离费用和类别组合 该矩阵将年度合格购买保持在选定的总额，并改变两个假设：溢价费用和奖金类别份额。在这些条款下，阳性细胞显示出高级卡的优势；阴性细胞显示出免费卡的优势。这两种颜色都不是对真实产品适用性的评估。共同利息金额不会改变矩阵，因为它是从两种选择中扣除的。瀑布图和折线图仍然显示了其对绝对净现金返还的影响。这种分离有助于回答两个不同的问题：哪张输入的卡具有更好的相对结果，以及任一卡的奖励是否超过输入的成本。旅行保险、休息室使用权、购买保护或介绍奖金等福利不包括在内。仅在确认福利可用、有用且其他地方尚未提供后才添加福利。标题广告的价值并不自动等同于家庭原本会花费的现金。使模型与实际卡协议一致 为了进行真正的比较，请使用每个发卡机构的资格规则对支持的购买历史记录进行分类。确认上限是否按月、年、类别或账户适用，以及超出上限的支出是否会获得基本费率。查看例外情况、兑换条件、附属卡费用和任何适用的商户费用。该模型假设赚取的每一美元都以其输入的现金价值进行兑换。它不重视积分、考虑到期时间、计算最低兑换阈值或假设欢迎优惠每年都会重复。这些功能可能会改变结果，并且需要它们自己支持的金额和日期。将还款计划与奖励优化分开。这些图表比较了相同的采购和明确的成本补贴；他们不计算借款限额、信用评分或负担得起的还款额。实际比较可以保留购买预算，验证条款并检查由此产生的美元成本，然后再将奖励率视为节省。

b0850768e817e7a009c9ca7fce8711346c0b749b.src: Accelerated biweekly payments change the annual cash commitment as well as the payment dates. Compare both before attributing the interest difference to frequency alone. Start with three clearly defined payment rules A mortgage payment can become smaller each time it leaves the account while the total paid during a year becomes larger. The labels matter because “biweekly” and “accelerated biweekly” describe different cash commitments. The FCAC’s mortgage-selection guide defines regular biweekly as the monthly payment multiplied by twelve and divided by twenty-six. Accelerated biweekly uses half the monthly payment on each of twenty-six payment occasions. That second rule produces thirteen monthly-payment equivalents in a full scheduled year.
