The charts apply those payment definitions to one hypothetical opening mortgage. They keep the selected rate unchanged through payoff to isolate the mechanics. An actual mortgage has a term, renewal conditions and contractual payment provisions that can change the path. No future renewal rate is inferred from the example. Convert the rate before calculating each period’s interest The example starts with CAD 400,000, a twenty-five-year amortization and a hypothetical 5% nominal annual rate compounded semi-annually. The equivalent monthly rate is (1 + 0.05 ÷ 2) 2/12 − 1 , rather than 5% divided by twelve. At a payment frequency f, the equivalent rate per payment period is (1 + nominal annual rate ÷ 2) 2/f − 1 . Compounding that rate for f equal model periods recovers the same effective annual rate. For the monthly payment, the model uses three hundred scheduled periods and the ordinary amortizing-payment equation. A model year contains exactly twelve monthly periods or twenty-six biweekly periods. This is an equal-period comparison, rather than a calendar with exact fourteen-day intervals and occasional twenty-seventh payment dates. Payment amounts are retained at full precision; a lender’s cents rounding and dated interest calculations can produce different final figures. Reconcile each payment with a full year’s budget The calculated monthly payment is about CAD 2,326.42, or CAD 27,917.04 over twelve scheduled payments. Regular biweekly is about CAD 1,073.73 on each occasion, giving the same CAD 27,917.04 annual scheduled total before final-payment adjustments. Accelerated biweekly is about CAD 1,163.21 each time. Twenty-six such payments schedule about CAD 30,243.46 a year. The difference is about CAD 2,326.42, equal to one extra monthly-payment equivalent. The first-year stacked bars divide actual cash paid between principal and interest. A principal payment reduces the liability; interest is the cost of borrowing. The accelerated path has more principal reduction in part because it receives more cash. Its lower individual payment than the monthly amount should not be read as a smaller annual commitment. Follow each balance to its own payoff date Under the unchanged default rate, the monthly path finishes at twenty-five model years. Regular biweekly finishes after six hundred and forty-nine equal periods, or about 24.96 model years. It pays about CAD 296,401.90 of interest, compared with about CAD 297,925.98 for monthly payments. The accelerated path finishes after five hundred and fifty-nine periods, or 21.50 model years. Its modeled interest is about CAD 249,577.30. The difference from monthly payments is about CAD 48,348.69 under these assumptions. That larger difference combines timing with higher annual payments; it is not the isolated value of moving the same cash to different dates. Each curve stops at its own payoff, and the last payment is reduced to the balance plus accrued period interest. No additional full payment is collected after the mortgage reaches zero. Use the matrix to compare rates without hiding payment changes The matrix replaces the nominal annual rate and calculates all three payment methods again. Principal and original amortization remain fixed, but the base monthly payment is recalculated for each rate row. Cells show interest to the relevant payoff date. Read across a row to compare methods at one rate. Reading down a column changes both interest and the payment required by the same original amortization. It is not a test that holds the current payment fixed after a rate increase. At a zero rate, interest is zero for every method. Accelerated repayment can still finish sooner because it schedules more principal during a model year. This boundary helps separate a payment-speed result from an interest-cost result. Choose a schedule that fits cash arriving in the household Compare the proposed dates with actual net-pay receipts and existing bill dates. A biweekly salary does not guarantee that a mortgage debit falls after it. Keep enough accessible cash for the period before the first receipt, rather than relying only on the annual surplus. Confirm whether the lender permits the payment-frequency change, how it calculates the new amount and whether any payment increase counts against a contractual privilege. The model does not assess penalties, product eligibility or the effect of an upcoming renewal. A useful planning record contains the payment amount, scheduled yearly total, principal path and the cash buffer needed between dates. Those four measures show the practical trade-off: more cash directed to the mortgage can reduce debt sooner, but that cash also needs to fit the wider household plan.
b0850768e817e7a009c9ca7fce8711346c0b749b.zh: 每两周加速付款会改变年度现金承诺以及付款日期。在将利息差异仅归因于频率之前，先对两者进行比较。从三个明确定义的付款规则开始 每次离开帐户时，抵押贷款付款可能会减少，而一年内支付的总额会增加。这些标签很重要，因为“每两周一次”和“每两周加速一次”描述了不同的现金承诺。 FCAC 的抵押贷款选择指南将定期每两周定义为每月付款乘以十二除以二十六。加速双周付款在二十六个付款场合中每次使用每月付款的一半。第二条规则在整个计划年份中产生了十三个月的付款额。这些图表将这些付款定义应用于一项假设的期初抵押贷款。他们通过支付来保持选定的利率不变，以隔离机制。实际的抵押贷款具有可以改变路径的期限、续签条件和合同付款条款。从该示例中没有推断出未来的续订率。在计算每个期间的利息之前转换利率 该示例以 400,000 加元开始，为期 25 年摊销，假设名义年利率为 5%，每半年复利一次。等效的月利率为 (1 + 0.05 ÷ 2) 2/12 − 1 ，而不是 5% 除以 12。在支付频率 f 下，每个支付周期的等价利率为 (1 + 名义年利率 ÷ 2) 2/f − 1 。对 f 个相等模型周期的该利率进行复利可恢复相同的有效年利率。对于每月付款，该模型使用三百个预定周期和普通摊销付款方程。一个模型年恰好包含十二个每月周期或二十六个双周周期。这是等周期比较，而不是具有精确的十四天间隔和偶尔的二十七个付款日期的日历。付款金额完全精确保留；贷款机构的美分四舍五入和注明日期的利息计算可能会产生不同的最终数字。将每笔付款与全年预算进行核对 计算得出的每月付款约为 2,326.42 加元，或 12 次预定付款为 27,917.04 加元。定期每两周一次的费用约为 1,073.73 加元，最终付款调整前的年度计划总额为 27,917.04 加元。加速每两周一次大约1,163.21加元。此类付款计划有 26 项，每年金额约为 30,243.46 加元。差额约为 2,326.42 加元，相当于每月额外支付一笔等值金额。第一年的堆积条将实际支付的现金分为本金和利息。本金还款减少了负债；利息是借贷成本。加速路径有更多的本金减少，部分原因是它收到了更多的现金。其个人付款低于每月金额不应被视为较小的年度承诺。按照每个余额到其自己的还款日期 在违约率不变的情况下，每月路径在二十五个模型年结束。定期每两周结束一次，经过 649 个相等的周期，即大约 24.96 个模型年。它支付的利息约为 296,401.90 加元，而每月付款约为 297,925.98 加元。加速路径在 559 个周期或 21.50 个模型年后结束。其模拟利息约为 249,577.30 加元。在这些假设下，与每月付款的差异约为 48,348.69 加元。这种更大的差异结合了时间安排和更高的年付款；它不是将相同的现金转移到不同日期的孤立价值。每条曲线都在其自己的支付处停止，最后一次支付减少到余额加上应计期间利息。抵押贷款为零后，不再收取额外的全额付款。使用矩阵比较费率而不隐藏付款更改 该矩阵替换名义年利率并再次计算所有三种付款方式。本金和原始摊销保持固定，但每个费率行的基本每月还款额会重新计算。细胞对相关的还款日期表现出兴趣。跨行读取以一种速率比较方法。向下阅读一列会更改相同原始摊销所需的利息和付款。这并不是一项在加息后保持当前付款不变的测试。在零利率下，每种方法的利息都是零。加速还款仍然可以更快完成，因为它在一个模型年安排了更多本金。该边界有助于将支付速度结果与利息成本结果分开。选择适合现金到达家庭的时间表 将建议日期与实际净付款收据和现有账单日期进行比较。双周工资并不能保证抵押贷款债务随之减少。在首次收款之前的一段时间内保留足够的可用现金，而不是仅仅依靠年度盈余。确认贷款机构是否允许更改付款频率、如何计算新金额以及任何付款增加是否违反合同特权。该模型不评估处罚、产品资格或即将到来的续订的影响。有用的计划记录包含付款金额、计划的年度总额、主要路径以及日期之间所需的现金缓冲。这四项措施显示了实际的权衡：更多的现金用于抵押贷款可以更快地减少债务，但这些现金也需要适应更广泛的家庭计划。

52ce4e0e6edfd96d532677c52926cba1dadd6667.src: A zero interest rate does not remove a forgone cash discount or an upfront fee. Compare the same starting resources and monthly budget, then subtract debt before interpreting retained cash. Record both all-in prices before comparing the payment size A merchant may offer a discount for immediate full payment alongside an instalment plan advertised with no interest. The choice includes the purchase price and the calendar of payments. A small instalment alone does not describe the total amount committed. The default purchase has an all-in price of CAD 10,000. Paying in full now receives a hypothetical 5% discount, producing a CAD 9,500 cash price. The alternative finances the full CAD 10,000 over twenty-four equal month-end payments and charges a separate CAD 100 upfront fee. The item is identical in both cases. Quebec’s Office de la protection du consommateur discusses financing promotions , including possible immediate-payment discounts and charges when promotional conditions are not met. This example does not apply a province’s legal rules. Its simplified contract always receives every payment on time and charges no interest on the instalment principal. Separate zero interest from zero additional cost Dividing CAD 10,000 by twenty-four gives an unrounded monthly payment of CAD 416.666…. The calculator keeps fractional cents internally so the principal is fully repaid at the selected final date. An actual lender may round payments and adjust the last instalment. The nominal total paid under financing is CAD 10,100: CAD 10,000 of principal plus the CAD 100 upfront fee. The immediate-payment price is CAD 9,500. The CAD 600 difference consists of the CAD 500 forgone discount and the CAD 100 fee. That CAD 600 is a comparison of purchase payments before any return on money retained. It is not a statutory annual percentage rate, an annualized borrowing charge or an investment loss. Describing the financed principal as interest-free can coexist with a higher total purchase payment when the alternative price is discounted. Give both choices the same starting cash and monthly resources A comparison can accidentally favour financing if it invests the cash retained but ignores the payments coming from future income. The model therefore gives both choices identical resources: opening cash equal to the undiscounted price plus the financing fee, and an available monthly amount equal to one instalment. Under the defaults, both start with CAD 10,100. The cash buyer pays CAD 9,500, leaving CAD 600 in the account. The financed buyer pays the CAD 100 fee, leaving CAD 10,000 in the account and owing CAD 10,000 on the purchase. At each month-end, the financed buyer uses the available CAD 416.666… to make the payment. The cash buyer saves the same amount. Both accounts receive the same assumed return before that month-end flow. Neither path receives an extra contribution that is unavailable to the other, and no instalment is silently paid from an unmodeled source. Read the cash balance and the debt together The account-balance chart shows how much money is retained or saved. At the beginning, financing appears to retain much more cash: CAD 10,000 compared with CAD 600. It also carries the purchase debt. That liability needs to remain visible when comparing financial positions. The next chart subtracts remaining purchase debt from the financed account. At index zero, that net position is zero, while the cash buyer has CAD 600 and no purchase debt. The identical item is excluded from both sides, so its value is not counted twice or assigned a different resale price to favour one choice. Purchase debt declines by an equal amount after each instalment and reaches zero after month twenty-four. At that common endpoint, the account comparison and the account-minus-debt comparison coincide. An earlier cash balance is a liquidity observation; the final net position answers a different question about the resources remaining after this purchase debt has been repaid. Test the account return without treating it as an available offer The default account return is a hypothetical 3% effective annual rate after taxes and costs. It is converted to a monthly compound rate using (1 + annual rate) 1/12 − 1 . The calculator does not simply divide the effective annual rate by twelve. At a zero account return, the cash buyer finishes with CAD 10,600: its initial CAD 600 plus CAD 10,000 of later savings. The financed buyer finishes with CAD 10,000. Financing’s endpoint advantage is therefore negative CAD 600, matching the nominal purchase-payment difference. This is a useful reconciliation of the two ledgers. At the default 3% annual return, the financed account ends at CAD 10,609 and the cash buyer’s account at about CAD 10,925.36. Financing’s endpoint advantage is therefore negative CAD 316.36. A positive return gives the financed buyer more time earning on retained cash, while the cash buyer earns on a smaller opening balance and later deposits. The matrix compares that timing effect with different cash discounts. Higher-return rows are conditional arithmetic, not forecasts, deposit quotations or evidence that an uncertain investment can safely fund a fixed payment commitment. Bring the comparison back to the actual cash commitment Confirm the total payable, discount eligibility, any deposit, mandatory fee, tax timing and each due date. A plan requiring an immediate tax payment or a final balloon payment is different from the equal month-end principal schedule shown here. Replace the schedule rather than hiding a different payment pattern inside the return input. The model assumes the monthly resource is available throughout the term. It does not test job loss, a missed payment, a promotional-rate expiry, accelerated collection or charges arising from a broken condition. A real payment plan needs enough accessible cash to meet its actual dates, even if an endpoint comparison looks favourable. Use both the total-payment chart and the account-minus-debt chart. The first identifies the immediate discount and fee trade-off; the second applies equal resources over time. The result is a transparent comparison of an invented contract, rather than a recommendation to borrow, invest the proceeds or choose a particular financing provider.
52ce4e0e6edfd96d532677c52926cba1dadd6667.zh: 零利率并不能消除放弃的现金折扣或预付费用。比较相同的起始资源和每月预算，然后在解释保留现金之前减去债务。在比较付款金额之前记录两个总价 商家可能会提供立即全额付款的折扣以及广告中的无息分期付款计划。选择包括购买价格和付款日历。仅小额分期付款并不能描述承诺的总金额。默认购买总价为 10,000 加元。现在全额付款可享受 5% 的假设折扣，现金价格为 9,500 加元。另一种选择是通过 24 次月末等额付款来全额支付 10,000 加元，并单独收取 100 加元的预付费用。两种情况下的项目都是相同的。魁北克省消费者保护办公室讨论融资促销活动，包括在不满足促销条件时可能的立即付款折扣和收费。本示例不适用各省的法律规则。其简化的合同总是按时收到每笔付款，并且对分期本金不收取任何利息。将零利息与零附加成本分开 将 10,000 加元除以二十四，得出每月未四舍五入的还款额 416.666 加元……。计算器在内部保留小数美分，以便在选定的最终日期全额偿还本金。实际的贷款机构可能会四舍五入付款并调整最后的分期付款。融资名义支付总额为 10,100 加元：10,000 加元本金加上 100 加元预付费用。立即付款价格为 9,500 加元。 600 加元的差额包括 500 加元放弃的折扣和 100 加元的费用。 600 加元是在保留任何资金回报之前购买付款的比较。它不是法定年利率、年化借款费用或投资损失。当替代价格打折时，将融资本金描述为无息可以与更高的总购买付款共存。为两种选择提供相同的起始现金和每月资源 如果比较保留的现金用于投资但忽略了来自未来收入的付款，则比较可能会意外地偏向融资。因此，该模型为两种选择提供了相同的资源：开仓现金等于未折现价格加上融资费用，每月可用金额等于一笔分期付款。默认情况下，两者均以 10,100 加元起。现金买家支付 9,500 加元，账户中留下 600 加元。融资买家支付 100 加元的费用，在账户中留下 10,000 加元，并在购买时欠 10,000 加元。在每个月末，融资买家使用可用的 416.666 加元……进行付款。现金购买者节省了相同的金额。两个账户在该月末流量之前收到相同的假设回报。任何一条路径都会收到另一条路径无法获得的额外贡献，并且不会从未建模的来源默默支付任何分期付款。一起阅读现金余额和债务 账户余额图表显示保留或节省了多少钱。一开始，融资似乎保留了更多的现金：10,000 加元，而 600 加元。它还带有购买债务。在比较财务状况时，这种责任需要保持可见。下一张图表从融资账户中减去剩余的购买债务。在指数为零时，净头寸为零，而现金买家有 600 加元且没有购买债务。相同的物品被排除在双方之外，因此其价值不会被计算两次或分配不同的转售价格以支持一种选择。每次分期付款后，购买债务都会减少等量，并在第 24 个月后达到零。在该共同端点处，账户比较和账户减去债务比较重合。较早的现金余额是流动性观察；最终净头寸回答了有关偿还购买债务后剩余资源的另一个问题。测试账户回报，而不将其视为可用报价 默认账户回报是假设的税费后 3% 的有效年利率。使用 (1 + 年利率) 1/12 − 1 将其转换为月复利利率。该计算器并不是简单地将有效年利率除以十二。如果账户回报为零，现金买家将获得 10,600 加元：最初的 600 加元加上后来的储蓄 10,000 加元。融资买家最终获得 10,000 加元。因此，融资的终点优势为负 600 加元，与名义购买付款差额相符。这是两个分类账的有用调节。按照默认的 3% 年回报率，融资账户最终为 10,609 加元，现金买家账户约为 10,925.36 加元。因此，融资的终点优势为负 316.36 加元。正回报使融资买家有更多时间通过保留现金赚取收入，而现金买家则通过较小的期初余额和后续存款赚取收入。该矩阵将时间效应与不同的现金折扣进行了比较。高回报行是条件算术，而不是预测、存款报价或不确定投资可以安全地为固定付款承诺提供资金的证据。将比较返回到实际现金承诺确认应付总额、折扣资格、任何押金、强制性费用、纳税时间和每个到期日。要求立即纳税或最终一次性付款的计划与此处显示的等额月末本金时间表不同。替换计划而不是在退货输入中隐藏不同的付款模式。该模型假设每月资源在整个期限内可用。它不会测试失业、拖欠付款、促销利率到期、加速收款或因破损状况而产生的费用。真正的付款计划需要足够的可用现金来满足其实际日期，即使终点比较看起来有利。使用总付款图表和账户减去债务图表。第一个确定了直接折扣和费用的权衡；第二个随着时间的推移应用相同的资源。结果是对发明的合同进行透明比较，而不是建议借款、投资收益或选择特定的融资提供商。

6442c8dc8039cf7e87deb4957cffb41a99545150.src: Compare the amount the recipient actually receives with the complete CAD payment. A zero sender fee can still accompany a less favourable conversion rate. Give the recipient the same net amount in both comparisons An international transfer has two sides: what leaves the sender’s account and what becomes available to the recipient. Comparing sender fees alone can miss a difference in the exchange rate or a charge deducted at the other end. The FCAC’s money-transfer guidance recommends considering transfer charges, exchange-rate costs and possible recipient charges. It also identifies delivery timing as part of a service comparison. This article’s editable model isolates the amount calculation and does not evaluate a provider’s reliability, speed or protections. The model fixes the recipient’s net need, expressed in generic foreign-currency units, or FCU. Both hypothetical services must deliver that same amount after a common recipient charge. The sender supplies enough additional foreign currency to cover that charge. This creates a comparison with the same final benefit instead of comparing two transfers that leave different amounts available abroad. Read the official case as dated evidence with a limited scope The fixed chart reproduces the fee and conversion-markup components from FCAC’s published worked example . Its three anonymized services deliver USD 1,000 using quotes recorded on 23 June 2026. The page is dated 23 October 2026. Those are selected case quotes, not a representative distribution or present-day provider ranking. The chart remains fixed when model controls change. Its role is to show two separate cost components; the editable comparison below uses different, explicitly invented terms. For the model, retain that habit of separating components, then obtain supported quotes for the actual transaction. A quote needs a date, a currency pair, the amount sent, the net receipt and the funding method. Comparing figures from different times or payment methods can introduce another difference that the fee label does not explain. State which currency is on each side of the exchange rate The selected reference rate is 1.40 CAD per FCU. At that rate, delivering 1,000 FCU without any charges has a reference principal of CAD 1,400. The reference is hypothetical; it is not a live market rate, a guaranteed executable rate or the historical rate used in the official case. A markup is added to this CAD-per-FCU rate. Service A’s assumed 3% markup produces 1.40 × 1.03 = 1.442 CAD per FCU . Service B’s 0.5% markup produces 1.407 CAD per FCU. A larger number in this quotation direction means more Canadian dollars are required for each foreign-currency unit. Reversing the quotation to FCU per CAD would reverse that visual direction. Taking the reciprocal changes the rate’s units, and an apparently identical percentage adjustment would not necessarily describe the same conversion. The calculator keeps one explicit CAD-per-FCU convention throughout rather than mixing quotation directions across the charts. Reconcile the complete payment and repeated budget At the default 1,000 FCU net receipt and zero recipient fee, Service A requires CAD 1,442 and charges no separate sender fee. The extra cost above the CAD 1,400 reference principal is CAD 42 per transfer. Service B requires CAD 1,407 for the conversion plus a CAD 10 sender fee, for a total of CAD 1,417. Its extra cost is CAD 17 per transfer. Its nonzero visible fee is compatible with a CAD 25 lower total payment under these invented terms. Twelve identical transfers require CAD 17,304 through A and CAD 17,004 through B, a CAD 300 difference. These are full CAD funding budgets, including money delivered for the recipient’s use. They are not entirely fees. The group bars place reference principal beside total payment so that the principal and the extra costs are not confused. Test transfer size and recipient charges separately The extra-cost curve varies only the net foreign-currency receipt per transfer. A flat sender fee has more weight relative to a small transfer, while a rate markup grows with the converted amount. Their combination can make the preferred cost result depend on transfer size. With the default terms and no recipient charge, the difference between the two modeled rate markups is 2.5% of the CAD 1.40 reference rate, or CAD 0.035 per FCU. Offsetting B’s extra CAD 10 sender fee therefore requires about 285.71 FCU per transfer. This is a threshold for the invented quotes, rather than a general minimum remittance amount. A recipient charge changes the foreign-currency amount that must be purchased. For example, a 20 FCU deduction means funding 1,020 FCU to leave 1,000 FCU net. The model applies the service’s rate to the full 1,020 FCU. At a zero net target, it assumes no transfer at all and charges nothing, so the flat-fee curve has a separate zero-transfer boundary. Use the matrix to prepare a quote comparison The matrix varies the net receipt and Service B’s rate markup. Other selected terms stay fixed, including sender fees, the recipient charge, reference rate and transfer count. Positive cells mean B costs less over the budget period; negative cells mean A costs less. All repeated transfers use identical inputs. The model does not predict exchange rates over a year or assume that today’s quote will remain available. If future receipts are needed on several dates, record those deadlines and stress the reference rate separately. A lower fee does not remove the risk of an adverse currency movement before a later transfer. For an actual payment, confirm how the transfer will be funded, when the rate is fixed, what the recipient can collect and how completion is confirmed. Include any additional funding or intermediary charges that apply. Keep the receipt and reference number. The graphs explain the amount comparison, while the actual payment plan also needs supported terms and enough time for the money to arrive.
6442c8dc8039cf7e87deb4957cffb41a99545150.zh: 将收款人实际收到的金额与全额加元付款进行比较。零发送者费用仍然可能伴随着不太有利的转换率。在两次比较中为收件人提供相同的净额国际转账有两个方面：离开发件人帐户的内容以及收件人可以使用的内容。仅比较发件人费用可能会遗漏汇率差异或另一端扣除的费用。 FCAC 的汇款指南建议考虑转账费用、汇率成本和可能的收款人费用。它还将交付时间确定为服务比较的一部分。本文的可编辑模型隔离了金额计算，并且不评估提供商的可靠性、速度或保护。该模型确定了接收者的净需求，以通用外币单位（FCU）表示。两种假设的服务必须在收取共同的收件人费用后提供相同的金额。发件人提供足够的额外外币来支付该费用。这样可以对相同的最终福利进行比较，而不是比较在国外留下不同金额的两次转移。将官方案例视为范围有限的日期证据。固定图表复制了 FCAC 已发布的工作示例中的费用和转换加成部分。其三项匿名服务使用 2026 年 6 月 23 日记录的报价提供 1,000 美元。该页面的日期为 2026 年 10 月 23 日。这些是选定的案例报价，而不是代表性分布或当前提供商排名。当模型控件发生变化时，图表保持固定。它的作用是显示两个独立的成本组成部分；下面的可编辑比较使用了不同的、明确发明的术语。对于模型，保留分离组件的习惯，然后获取实际交易的支持报价。报价需要日期、货币对、发送金额、净收款和资金方式。比较不同时间或付款方式的数字可能会带来费用标签未解释的另一个差异。说明汇率两侧的货币 选定的参考汇率为每 FCU 1.40 加元。按照这个速度，免费交付 1,000 个 FCU 的参考本金为 1,400 加元。参考文献是假设的；它不是实时市场汇率、有保证的可执行汇率或官方案例中使用的历史汇率。此每 FCU 的 CAD 费率中添加了加价。服务 A 假设 3% 的加价为每个 FCU 带来 1.40 × 1.03 = 1.442 加元。服务 B 0.5% 的加价为每个 FCU 带来 1.407 加元。该报价方向的数字越大，意味着每个外币单位需要更多的加元。将每 CAD 的报价反转为 FCU 将反转该视觉方向。采用倒数会改变汇率的单位，并且表面上相同的百分比调整不一定会描述相同的转换。该计算器始终保持一种明确的 CAD-per-FCU 惯例，而不是在图表中混合报价方向。协调完整付款和重复预算 在默认的 1,000 FCU 净收款和零收件人费用的情况下，服务 A 需要 1,442 加元，并且不收取单独的发件人费用。高于 1,400 加元参考本金的额外费用为每次转账 42 加元。服务 B 需要 1,407 加元进行转换，加上 10 加元的发送者费用，总计 1,417 加元。每次接送的额外费用为 17 加元。根据这些发明条款，其非零可见费用与 25 加元的较低总付款兼容。 12 次相同的转账需要通过 A 支付 17,304 加元，通过 B 需要 17,004 加元，相差 300 加元。这些是加元的全部资金预算，包括交付给接收者使用的资金。它们并不完全是费用。集团金条将参考本金放在总付款旁边，以便本金和额外费用不会混淆。分别测试转账规模和收款人费用 额外成本曲线仅改变每次转账的净外币收入。相对于小额转账，固定的发送者费用具有更大的权重，而费率加价则随着转换金额的增加而增加。它们的组合可以使首选成本结果取决于传输大小。在默认条款且不收取收件人费用的情况下，两个模型费率加价之间的差异为 1.40 加元参考费率的 2.5%，即每个 FCU 0.035 加元。因此，抵消 B 的额外 10 加元发送者费用，每次转账大约需要 285.71 FCU。这是发明报价的门槛，而不是一般的最低汇款金额。收款人费用会改变必须购买的外币金额。例如，扣除 20 FCU 意味着资助 1,020 FCU，留下 1,000 FCU 净额。该模型将服务费率应用于全部 1,020 个 FCU。在零净目标下，它假设根本没有转移并且不收取任何费用，因此固定费用曲线具有单独的零转移边界。使用矩阵准备报价比较 该矩阵会改变净收入和服务 B 的费率加成。其他选定的条款保持不变，包括发件人费用、收件人费用、参考费率和转账计数。阳性细胞意味着 B 在预算期内的成本较低；负细胞意味着 A 的成本较低。所有重复传输都使用相同的输入。该模型不会预测一年内的汇率，也不会假设今天的报价仍然可用。如果未来需要在多个日期收到收据，请记录这些截止日期并单独强调参考利率。较低的费用并不能消除稍后转账之前货币不利变动的风险。对于实际付款，请确认转账的资金方式、费率何时确定、收款人可以收取什么以及如何确认完成。包括任何适用的额外资金或中介费用。保留收据和参考号。图表解释了金额比较，而实际的付款计划还需要支持的条款和足够的时间让资金到达。

8a301d248d7c54e0d5fe841ae8354706e855d3d3.src: An annualized headline rate describes a rate, not a guaranteed one-year interest amount. The rate window, eligible balance and later rate determine the cash earned. Put the rate and its end date on the same page A savings advertisement can quote an annual percentage while making that rate available for only a few months. The planning comparison needs both pieces: how the rate is expressed and how long it applies to money that is actually eligible. The FCAC’s savings-account guide discusses introductory rates and comparing account terms. A promotion should therefore be read alongside the ongoing rate and any conditions, rather than treated as an indefinitely available return. The two accounts here are invented. They receive the same opening CAD 20,000 and the same CAD 500 at each month-end. One pays a hypothetical 5% annual quoted rate for four opening model months on up to CAD 50,000, then 2%. The comparison pays a constant 3%. These figures are selected assumptions, not current offers or a ranking of savings products. Translate an annual quote into the modeled interest dollars The model divides the quoted annual rate by twelve, credits interest on the opening monthly balance and then adds the month-end deposit. This represents nominal annual rates with monthly crediting over equal model months. It does not reproduce an account’s daily-balance calculation or its actual month lengths. With no additional deposits, CAD 20,000 at a 5% nominal annual rate for four monthly credits earns about CAD 335.42. It does not earn CAD 1,000 simply because the quoted annual rate is 5%. That larger amount would be a simple full-year calculation before considering the actual crediting convention. If the same balance subsequently earns 2% for eight model months, its full twelve-month interest is about CAD 608.15. The example illustrates why a promotional rate cannot be applied to the entire horizon after the promotion has expired. The interactive default also includes deposits, so its interest dollars differ from this no-deposit teaching example. Separate money saved from interest credited After twenty-four CAD 500 deposits, both default accounts have received CAD 32,000 of capital: the initial CAD 20,000 plus CAD 12,000 of later contributions. The contribution line stays identical across the two choices. The promotion account ends at about CAD 33,264.73, including CAD 1,264.73 in interest. The steady account ends at about CAD 33,586.55, including CAD 1,586.55 in interest. The difference is about CAD 321.82 in favour of the steady account within this selected window. A larger ending balance caused by depositing more would be a different comparison. Holding contributions equal makes this difference attributable to the modeled interest rules. The charts do not add an assumed transfer to a new promotion after the first one ends, and they do not assume the ongoing rate changes later. Check which dollars receive the promotional rate During the entered promotional months, this model applies the promotion rate to the smaller of the opening balance and the selected cap. Any excess earns the base rate. Afterward, the entire opening balance earns the base rate. That is one explicitly chosen tier formula. Actual promotions may define new money, eligible customers, deposit dates or qualifying transactions differently. A balance in the account is not by itself evidence that the whole amount qualifies. Read the applicable offer before replacing the hypothetical cap with a real one. Interest credited earlier becomes part of the next month’s opening balance in the calculation. It can therefore use some of the eligible cap. Setting the cap to zero removes the promotional tier entirely. If a selected promotional rate is below the base rate, the model applies that lower rate to the eligible tier rather than silently substituting a better rate. Read the later interest blocks and the sensitivity matrix The default promotion account earns about CAD 671.09 during months one through twelve, compared with CAD 691.51 in the steady account. During months thirteen through twenty-four, the figures are about CAD 593.65 and CAD 895.04. The early headline advantage does not persist through this full comparison. The bar pairs keep each period’s interest separate. If the selected horizon leaves a final period shorter than twelve months, its exact month range is labelled and the amount is not annualized. Comparing unequal blocks as if both covered a full year would distort the result. The matrix changes only promotional length and the base rate. Each cell reports the promotion account’s ending balance minus the same steady-account endpoint. Negative values indicate a lower ending balance, not a loss of contributed capital. A matrix cell is a conditional calculation, not the probability of obtaining a future offer. Make the comparison practical before moving cash Confirm the promotion’s start and end dates, the eligible amount and the normal rate. Include account and transfer charges when relevant. This example excludes both charges and tax, so its interest is a gross amount available before those adjustments. Also check when transferred funds become accessible. A savings account chosen for near-term bills needs more than an attractive annual quote: the money must be usable when payment is due. The model credits every monthly deposit without a hold or transfer delay. Keep a reminder before the promotional window ends and compare the next available choices using the same cash-flow assumptions. The central task is to reconcile the rate, time, balance and actual interest dollars. That produces a more useful comparison than choosing the largest number in an advertisement.
8a301d248d7c54e0d5fe841ae8354706e855d3d3.zh: 年化标题利率描述的是利率，而不是保证的一年利息金额。利率窗口、合格余额和后期利率决定了赚取的现金。将费率及其结束日期放在同一页上 储蓄广告可以引用年度百分比，但该费率仅可使用几个月。计划比较需要两部分：如何表达利率以及它适用于实际合格资金的期限。 FCAC 的储蓄账户指南讨论了介绍利率和比较账户条款。因此，促销应与现行利率和任何条件一起考虑，而不是被视为无限期的回报。这里的两个帐户是发明的。他们收到相同的期初 20,000 加元，并在每个月末收到相同的 500 加元。假设四个开放模型月份的年报价为 5%，最高为 50,000 加元，然后为 2%。比较固定支付 3%。这些数字是选定的假设，而不是当前的报价或储蓄产品的排名。将年度报价转换为模型利息美元 该模型将报价年利率除以 12，在期初每月余额中记入利息，然后添加月末存款。这代表名义年利率，每月计入相同的模型月份。它不会重现帐户的每日余额计算或其实际月份长度。在没有额外存款的情况下，20,000 加元，按 5% 的名义年利率，四个月的信用额，可赚取约 335.42 加元。它不会仅仅因为报价的年利率是 5% 就赚取 1,000 加元。在考虑实际的计入惯例之前，这一较大数额将是一个简单的全年计算。如果相同的余额随后在 8 个模型月内赚取 2%，则其 12 个月的全部利息约为 608.15 加元。该示例说明了为什么在促销期满后促销率不能应用于整个范围。交互式默认还包括存款，因此其利息金额与此无存款教学示例不同。从记入利息中节省的资金 在进行了 24 笔 500 加元存款后，两个违约账户均收到了 32,000 加元的资本：最初的 20,000 加元加上后来的捐款 12,000 加元。两种选择的贡献线保持相同。促销账户最终金额约为 33,264.73 加元，其中包括利息 1,264.73 加元。稳定账户最终约为 33,586.55 加元，其中包括 1,586.55 加元利息。差异约为 321.82 加元，有利于该选定窗口内的稳定账户。由于存入更多资金而导致的期末余额更大将是不同的比较。保持缴款相等使得这种差异归因于建模的利息规则。这些图表不会在第一个促销活动结束后将假定的转移添加到新的促销活动中，并且不会假定随后的汇率会发生变化。检查哪些美元获得促销率 在输入的促销月份期间，此模型将促销率应用于期初余额和所选上限中的较小者。任何超额部分均可赚取基本费率。之后，全部期初余额将赚取基本利率。这是一个明确选择的层级公式。实际的促销活动可能会以不同的方式定义新资金、合格客户、存款日期或合格交易。账户余额本身并不能证明全部金额合格。在用真实的上限替换假设的上限之前，请先阅读适用的报价。提前记入的利息将成为下个月期初余额的一部分进行计算。因此，它可以使用一些符合条件的上限。将上限设置为零会完全删除促销级别。如果选定的促销费率低于基本费率，该模型会将较低的费率应用于符合条件的级别，而不是默默地替换为更好的费率。阅读后面的利息块和敏感性矩阵 默认促销帐户在第 1 个月到第 12 个月的收入约为 671.09 加元，而稳定帐户的收入为 691.51 加元。第 13 个月至第 24 个月的数字约为 593.65 加元和 895.04 加元。通过这种全面的比较，早期的标题优势并没有持续存在。条对将每个期间的利息分开。如果所选期限的最终期间短于十二个月，则将标记其确切的月份范围，并且金额不会按年计算。比较不相等的区块，就好像两者都涵盖了一整年一样，会扭曲结果。该矩阵仅更改促销长度和基本费率。每个单元格报告促销帐户的期末余额减去相同的稳定帐户端点。负值表示期末余额较低，而​​不是实缴资本损失。矩阵单元是条件计算，而不是获得未来报价的概率。在转移现金之前进行实际比较确认促销的开始和结束日期、合格金额和正常费率。包括相关的账户和转账费用。此示例不包括费用和税收，因此其利息是这些调整之前的可用总额。还要检查转移的资金何时可以使用。选择用于短期账单的储蓄账户需要的不仅仅是有吸引力的年度报价：资金必须在付款到期时可用。该模型记入每月的存款，没有保留或转移延迟。在促销窗口结束之前保留提醒，并使用相同的现金流假设来比较下一个可用的选择。中心任务是协调利率、时间、余额和实际利息美元。这比在广告中选择最大的数字产生更有用的比较。

bb2e2e4ad119dc7c92f1460b97df1919f2629da1.src: Refunding the same foreign amount does not necessarily reverse the original CAD cash flow. The later conversion and the treatment of fees both matter. Start with the direction of the exchange-rate quote The original price is expressed in foreign currency units, abbreviated FCU. The reference quote is Canadian dollars per one FCU. To translate the foreign amount into reference CAD, multiply the amount by that quote. A higher CAD-per-FCU quote makes the same foreign purchase cost more Canadian dollars. The default foreign purchase is 1,000 FCU at an assumed reference of CAD 1.35 per FCU. The reference amount is therefore CAD 1,350. A hypothetical purchase conversion cost of 2.5% adds CAD 33.75, taking the modeled charge to CAD 1,383.75. These are chosen conversion references and separately entered costs. They are not live rates, card-network quotes or an issuer’s actual settlement formula. A price displayed on a shopping day may differ from the rate and date ultimately used under a card agreement. Translate the refund independently from the purchase The example then refunds the full 1,000 FCU at a later hypothetical reference of CAD 1.30 per FCU. That produces a CAD 1,300 reference credit. With no additional refund deduction and no original-fee rebate selected, the modeled credited amount is CAD 1,300. Net cash paid is CAD 1,383.75 − CAD 1,300 = CAD 83.75 . The difference consists of CAD 50 from the changed conversion reference and CAD 33.75 of retained purchase conversion cost. The waterfall shows each part separately. The FCAC’s credit-card explanation describes how foreign-currency transactions and refunds can produce different Canadian-dollar amounts. The charts make that general mechanism visible with independent, editable assumptions rather than predicting the result of a particular return. Treat the refund fee and an original-fee rebate as different entries A refund can involve more than a new exchange rate. The tool has one control for a deduction from the reference refund and another for the share of the original purchase fee returned on the refunded portion. They represent different cash entries and are not automatically linked. For example, adding a 2.5% refund deduction to the default would reduce the CAD 1,300 reference credit by CAD 32.50. Returning the full original CAD 33.75 fee would instead increase the credit by that amount. Each change should appear once in the cash-flow bridge. Actual treatment depends on the agreement. Tangerine’s cardholder agreement provides an example with conversion charges on foreign debits and credits and a retained original conversion charge. It is a specific agreement, not a universal rule for every card. Use the current terms governing the card and transaction being reviewed. Do not call the whole remaining debit a loss after a partial return The refund-share control changes how much of the original foreign purchase is returned. At 50%, the default refund is 500 FCU. The reference credit is CAD 650, and the remaining net CAD debit is CAD 733.75 under the selected zero-refund-fee, zero-original-fee-rebate assumptions. That net debit includes payment for the half of the purchase that was not returned. It should not be described as a CAD 733.75 exchange loss. With a full refund, the endpoint isolates the conversion and fee differences in this model; with a partial refund, retained goods or services are also part of the economic result. An original-fee rebate is proportional to the refunded share before the selected rebate percentage is applied. If no part of the purchase is refunded, the tool generates no refund credit or fee rebate. This keeps the fee calculation aligned with the amount actually returned. Compare the CAD checkout quote with the full foreign-charge cost A merchant may offer to convert a foreign price into Canadian dollars before the charge reaches the card. Visa’s dynamic-currency-conversion guidance explains the choice and the need to inspect conversion details. The purchase-only bar chart compares the selected foreign-charge cost with three invented CAD checkout quotes. Using the same CAD 1,350 reference, markups of 2%, 4% and 6% produce CAD 1,377, CAD 1,404 and CAD 1,431. The foreign-charge example, including its entered purchase conversion cost, is CAD 1,383.75. The hypothetical CAD quotes assume no additional issuer charge. Actual cross-border transactions settled in CAD can have other fees, so the chart does not establish which option is cheaper on a real checkout screen. Compare all disclosed amounts and the card agreement. The chart excludes refunds, credit-card borrowing interest and any reward value. Use the matrix to separate a rate change from a fee decision The matrix sets refund references at 90%, 95%, 100% and 105% of the selected purchase reference. Its columns vary how much of the original purchase fee is returned. Purchase terms, refund share and the separately entered refund deduction stay fixed. Read across a row to isolate the original-fee rebate. Read down a column to see the effect of the conversion reference. A negative net-cash endpoint means the modeled credit exceeds the original debit, which can happen under the entered rates. It is neither a guaranteed refund outcome nor an arbitrage strategy. For a practical budget, keep the original statement amount, the confirmed foreign refund and the actual CAD credit. Allow for the time before the credit is usable and check the card’s payment requirements while the refund is pending. A merchant’s confirmation in foreign currency is useful evidence, but it is not the final Canadian-dollar amount in the account.
bb2e2e4ad119dc7c92f1460b97df1919f2629da1.zh: 退还相同金额的外汇并不一定会扭转原来的加元现金流。后期的转换和费用的处理都很重要。从汇率报价的方向开始 原始价格以外币单位表示，缩写为FCU。参考报价为每一个 FCU 加元。要将外国金额转换为参考加元，请将金额乘以该报价。每 FCU 的加元报价越高，相同的外国采购成本就越高。默认国外采购量为 1,000 个 FCU，假设参考价格为每个 FCU 1.35 加元。因此，参考金额为 1,350 加元。假设购买转换成本为 2.5%，则增加 33.75 加元，使模型费用达到 1,383.75 加元。这些是选择的转换参考和单独输入的成本。它们不是实时汇率、卡网络报价或发卡机构的实际结算公式。购物日显示的价格可能与卡协议中最终使用的费率和日期不同。独立于购买转换退款 该示例随后以每个 FCU 1.30 加元的后续假设参考价格全额退款 1,000 个 FCU。这会产生 1,300 加元的参考积分。在未进行额外退款扣除且未选择原始费用回扣的情况下，模拟的贷记金额为 1,300 加元。支付的现金净额为 1,383.75 加元 – 1,300 加元 = 83.75 加元。差异包括更改后的转换参考的 50 加元和保留采购转换成本的 33.75 加元。瀑布分别展示了每个部分。 FCAC 的信用卡解释描述了外币交易和退款如何产生不同的加元金额。这些图表通过独立的、可编辑的假设使一般机制可见，而不是预测特定回报的结果。将退款费用和原始费用回扣视为不同的条目 退款可能不仅仅涉及新的汇率。该工具有一个控件用于从参考退款中扣除，另一个控件用于控制退款部分退回的原始购买费用的份额。它们代表不同的现金条目并且不会自动链接。例如，在默认情况下添加 2.5% 的退款扣除额将使 1,300 加元的参考积分减少 32.50 加元。退还全部 33.75 加元的原始费用会增加该金额的积分。每个变化都应该在现金流桥中出现一次。实际待遇以协议为准。 Tangerine 的持卡人协议提供了一个示例，其中包含外国借记卡和贷记卡的转换费用以及保留的原始转换费用。这是一个特定的协议，而不是每张卡的通用规则。使用管理正在审核的卡和交易的现行条款。部分退货后，不要将全部剩余借方称为损失 退款份额控制改变了原始外国购买的退回金额。 50% 时，默认退款为 500 FCU。在选定的零退款费用、零原始费用回扣假设下，参考贷款机构为 650 加元，剩余的净加元借方为 733.75 加元。该净借方包括未退回的一半购买款项。不应将其描述为 733.75 加元的汇兑损失。通过全额退款，端点隔离了该模型中的转换和费用差异；通过部分退款，保留的商品或服务也是经济成果的一部分。原始费用返利与应用所选返利百分比之前的退还份额成正比。如果购买的任何部分均未退款，则该工具不会产生退款信用或费用回扣。这使得费用计算与实际返还的金额保持一致。将加元结帐报价与国外全额费用进行比较 商家可能会在费用到达卡之前将国外价格转换为加元。 Visa 的动态货币兑换指南解释了选择以及检查兑换详细信息的必要性。仅用于购买的条形图将选定的国外费用与三个发明的 CAD 结帐报价进行比较。使用相同的 1,350 加元参考，加价 2%、4% 和 6% 分别产生 1,377 加元、1,404 加元和 1,431 加元。国外费用示例（包括输入的购买转换成本）为 1,383.75 加元。假设的加元报价不承担发行人额外费用。以加元结算的实际跨境交易可能会产生其他费用，因此该图表并未确定在真实结账屏幕上哪种选项更便宜。比较所有披露的金额和卡协议。该图表不包括退款、信用卡借款利息和任何奖励价值。使用矩阵将费率更改与费用决策分开 该矩阵将退款参考设置为所选购买参考的 90%、95%、100% 和 105%。它的栏目不同，原始购买费用的返还金额也不同。购买条款、退款份额和单独输入的退款扣除额保持不变。阅读一行以隔离原始费用回扣。向下阅读一列以查看转换参考的效果。负净现金端点意味着建模的贷款机构超过原始借方，这可能在输入的利率下发生。它既不是保证退款结果，也不是套利策略。对于实际预算，请保留原始报表金额、已确认的外汇退款和实际的加元贷记。等待信用额度可用之前的一段时间，并在退款待处理期间检查卡的付款要求。商家的外币确认是有用的证据，但这并不是账户中最终的加元金额。

21e415a58d0b6c7ce17e4684b86ce8e63dab8dcd.src: An employer can affect both the assets you own and the income you use for bills. Test those channels together before counting company shares as a cash reserve. One company can appear on both sides of the plan An employee holding company shares has two different exposures to the same organisation: the market value of an investment and the cash income from employment. A weak company outcome can put both under pressure. Looking only at the investment account can miss the dependence of the household budget on the same business. The SEC’s investor bulletin on ten investing principles identifies employer stock as a particular concentration concern because investment losses can coincide with losing employment. That is the reason for testing a joint stress. It does not establish how likely the combination is for a specific company or employee. This tool deliberately combines an immediate share-price fall with an interruption in take-home earnings. It does not model a named issuer, estimate a default probability or infer a relationship from historical data. The values and dates are editable assumptions chosen to expose the mechanics of a cash plan. Separate the asset loss from the loss of recurring income The first chart isolates the employer-share loss. In the original example, CAD 60,000 of shares falls by 40%, leaving CAD 36,000 and a CAD 24,000 asset-value loss. The initial CAD 12,000 of accessible cash and CAD 140,000 of other financial investments remain unchanged in this controlled comparison. Holding other assets unchanged is a modelling control, not a claim that they would be protected in a downturn. A more extensive stress could also reduce their prices, examine fund overlap and change the time required to access them. They are intentionally not sold to rescue the cash ledger here. Only existing vested, saleable shares belong in the share-value field. An unvested award, an option exercise opportunity and a share already owned are different rights. Future awards should not be counted as money already available. This model does not establish vesting, continued employment conditions, sale permission or the value of employee options. A monthly income figure still needs a receipt date The cash ledger lasts twelve months. Each month’s essential bill comes first; income arrives at month-end. During the selected interruption, the household receives the separately entered net replacement cash. Afterwards it receives the normal take-home amount. The same schedule applies to both share-holding alternatives. With CAD 4,000 of monthly essentials, CAD 1,000 of replacement cash and a six-month interruption, the original hold-shares example accumulates CAD 10,000 of unfunded bills. Some of that gap occurs in month seven: the first resumed CAD 6,000 pay receipt still arrives after that month’s bill. Annual totals alone would conceal this timing problem. The second chart shows cash after the bill and before income. A zero point can indicate exhausted cash, with part of the bill still unpaid. The third chart retains those unpaid amounts separately. Later salary does not retrospectively make an earlier payment timely, and the model does not automatically add a loan or assume that a creditor will wait. A possible share sale is a separate access and tax question The alternative assumes all entered company shares are sold immediately after the initial price shock. The selected usable percentage converts gross market value into independently assumed net spending cash. It can allow for money held back for tax or costs, but it does not calculate either. At the original 40% share-price fall and 90% usable percentage, CAD 32,400 enters accessible cash. That makes the initial spending pool CAD 44,400. It funds every requested bill in the original twelve-month example. The remaining share value is excluded from spending and is not treated as a calculated tax liability or refund. This assumption can fail if shares are restricted, the market is illiquid, settlement is delayed, or a sale is not permitted. Before using sale proceeds in a real cash calendar, verify the actual terms and the separately estimated tax obligation. The chart is not an instruction to sell and does not value the longer-term opportunity of holding the shares. Use the matrix to test dependence rather than predict an event The fourth chart varies the share-price loss and the length of the income interruption. Every cell uses the assumed immediate-sale path, with the selected usable-cash percentage, opening reserve, income amounts and essential bills. A larger share loss reduces what a sale can contribute to the reserve. The rows are stresses, not probabilities. The columns are durations, not forecasts of time needed to find work. Even the zero-interruption column needs enough opening cash for the first bill because ordinary pay arrives afterwards. If the replacement amount exceeds normal income, a longer interruption can improve cash in this model; the tool preserves that input rather than assuming a direction. List the employer-linked assets and distinguish vested holdings from contingent awards. Identify cash accessible independently of the employer. Draw the dates of bills and independently confirmed net income receipts. Test a share loss and an earnings interruption in the same calendar. Resolve every unfunded payment and verify sale restrictions and tax before implementation. Those steps connect portfolio concentration with household resilience. The result is a funding test, not an allocation recommendation or an estimate of job-loss risk.
21e415a58d0b6c7ce17e4684b86ce8e63dab8dcd.zh: 雇主可以影响您拥有的资产和您用于账单的收入。在将公司股票计算为现金储备之前，先对这些渠道进行测试。一家公司可以出现在计划的两侧 持有公司股票的员工对同一组织有两种不同的风险：投资的市场价值和就业现金收入。公司业绩不佳可能会给双方带来压力。只看投资账户可能会忽略家庭预算对同一企业的依赖。美国证券交易委员会关于十项投资原则的投资者公告将雇主股票确定为特别值得关注的集中问题，因为投资损失可能与失业同时发生。这就是测试关节压力的原因。它没有确定这种组合对于特定公司或员工的可能性有多大。该工具故意将股价立即下跌与实得收益中断结合起来。它不会对指定发行人进行建模、估计违约概率或从历史数据推断关系。这些值和日期是可编辑的假设，旨在揭示现金计划的机制。将资产损失与经常性收入损失分开 第一个图表将雇主份额损失分开。在最初的示例中，60,000 加元的股票下跌了 40%，留下 36,000 加元和 24,000 加元的资产价值损失。在此受控比较中，初始 12,000 加元的可用现金和 140,000 加元的其他金融投资保持不变。保持其他资产不变是一种建模控制，而不是声称它们在经济低迷时期会受到保护。更广泛的压力还可能降低其价格、检查资金重叠并改变获取它们所需的时间。故意不出售它们是为了拯救这里的现金分类账。只有现有的既得、可出售股票才属于股票价值范围。未归属奖励、期权行使机会和已拥有的股份是不同的权利。未来的奖励不应算作已经可用的资金。该模型不规定归属、持续雇佣条件、销售许可或员工期权的价值。每月收入数字仍需要收据日期 现金分类账持续十二个月。每个月的基本账单是第一位的；收入月底到账。在选定的中断期间，家庭收到单独输入的净替代现金。之后它会收到正常的带回家金额。相同的时间表适用于两种股权选择。由于每月 4,000 加元的必需品、1,000 加元的替代现金和六个月的中断，最初的持有股票示例累积了 10,000 加元的无资金账单。其中一些差距出现在第七个月：第一张恢复的 6,000 加元工资收据仍然在该月的账单之后到达。仅年度总数就可以掩盖这个时间问题。第二张图表显示了账单之后、收入之前的现金。零点可能表明现金已用完，部分账单仍未支付。第三张图表单独保留了那些未支付的金额。较晚的工资不会及时追溯较早的付款，并且该模型不会自动添加贷款或假设债权人会等待。可能的股票出售是一个单独的准入和税收问题另一种假设是，所有输入的公司股票在初始价格冲击后立即出售。选定的可用百分比将总市场价值转换为独立假定的净支出现金。它可以允许保留用于税收或成本的资金，但它也不计算。在最初的股价下跌 40% 和可用百分比为 90% 的情况下，32,400 加元进入可用现金。这使得初始支出池为 44,400 加元。它为最初的十二个月示例中的每个请求的账单提供资金。剩余股份价值不计入支出，也不被视为计算的纳税义务或退款。如果股票受到限制、市场流动性不足、结算延迟或不允许出售，则该假设可能会失败。在实际现金日历中使用销售收益之前，请验证实际条款和单独估计的纳税义务。该图表并非出售指令，也不重视持有股票的长期机会。使用矩阵来测试依赖性而不是预测事件第四张图表改变了股价损失和收入中断的长度。每个单元都使用假定的立即销售路径，以及选定的可用现金百分比、期初准备金、收入金额和基本账单。较大的股份损失会减少出售对储备金的贡献。这些行是压力，而不是概率。这些列是持续时间，而不是对找到工作所需时间的预测。即使是零中断专栏也需要足够的现金来支付第一张账单，因为普通工资是随后到达的。如果更换金额超过正常收入，则较长时间的中断可以改善该模型中的现金；该工具会保留该输入，而不是假设一个方向。列出与雇主相关的资产，并将既得资产与或有奖励区分开来。确定独立于雇主的可用现金。绘制账单日期和独立确认的净收入收入。在同一日历中测试股票损失和收益中断。解决每笔无资金支持的付款，并在实施前核实销售限制和税收。这些步骤将投资组合集中度与家庭弹性联系起来。结果是资金测试，而不是分配建议或失业风险估计。

fe7fd315872b428b08202eb18f937339beec9cea.src: A payment method has a price and a cash calendar. Check both before treating a low quoted rate or a large retained bank balance as the deciding fact. Compare the same item with the same resources A cash discount and a financing offer can make the same purchase look like two very different decisions. To compare them, begin with an identical item, an identical starting cash balance and an identical monthly amount available after ordinary expenses. The item’s ownership value is then common to both paths. Paying now uses the full price after the selected discount. Financing borrows the undiscounted full price and pays the setup fee immediately from cash. The loan is repaid through equal monthly instalments, with a capped final payment. The model assumes no balloon amount and no optional early repayment. Both paths receive the same monthly budget at month-end. In the pay-now path it rebuilds cash. In the financed path cash first meets the loan payment; the later budget then replenishes the account. This arrangement prevents the comparison from quietly giving one payment method more household income than the other. A reserve can fall short before a monthly budget balances The first chart shows each cash position after the loan payment but before the month-end budget arrives. Month zero includes the discounted purchase payment or financing fee. The selected reserve floor provides a reference, not a universal recommendation. In the original example the item costs CAD 10,000 before a 3% cash discount. Paying now from CAD 15,000 leaves CAD 5,300. That is only CAD 300 above the selected CAD 5,000 floor, even though the household continues to have a CAD 500 monthly budget afterwards. A separate bill due immediately would still need a place in the plan. Financing preserves more initial cash but also creates required payments. A negative chart position means the entered resources cannot fund the assumed payment at that time. It is not an automatically approved overdraft. The model does not price a rescue loan or penalties; it suppresses the ending economic comparison whenever either path needs additional funding. Add the discount you give up to fees and loan interest The second chart follows the outstanding purchase loan. The original example uses a hypothetical 5% nominal annual loan rate and twenty-four monthly payments. The payment is approximately CAD 438.71, and total loan interest is about CAD 529.13. Actual lender quotes can use different conventions and additional charges. The third chart adds the CAD 300 cash discount forgone, CAD 150 setup fee and CAD 529.13 interest. The resulting extra purchase outlay from financing is approximately CAD 979.13 over the full term. This is a nominal cash-cost premium; it has not yet included what retained cash earns or when the payments occur. At a zero-interest loan rate, interest disappears from that bridge, but the fee and forgone discount can remain. Calling an offer zero interest therefore does not establish that both payment methods have the same economic cost. The entered rate also excludes the cash-paid fee and discount effect, so it is not an all-in statutory APR disclosure. Keep cash interest separate from the cost of the purchase Positive cash balances earn the selected effective annual return, converted to a monthly equivalent. In the original example that assumption is 3%. After the final payment, the pay-now path holds about CAD 17,969 and the financed path about CAD 17,268. Both have no purchase debt remaining and own the same item. The roughly CAD 702 difference is smaller than the nominal purchase-cost premium because the financed path held more interest-earning cash earlier. It is an illustration before tax on that interest, with no guarantee that a cash rate stays available. A risky investment return is not an interchangeable substitute for a cash yield in a payment plan. The fourth chart tests financing across loan rates and monthly budgets. Each cell measures the greatest gap below the selected reserve floor at any payment date. It is a conservative estimate of additional starting cash needed, not a probability of missed payment. If that cash is actually added, rerun the full ledger because its interest will also affect the path. Read the agreement before turning the illustration into a commitment FCAC’s personal-loan guidance identifies the interest, fees, term and repayment obligation as parts of borrowing cost. For a real purchase, collect the cash price and the financing price in writing, confirm the total payments, and check whether there are conditions attached to the discount. Look for deferred-interest clauses, compulsory add-ons, late charges, rate changes, security over the item and early-payment terms. None is included in this ordinary fixed-rate example. Enter a sales-tax-inclusive purchase price on a consistent basis; the tool does not determine how tax law applies to an actual rebate. A cheaper payment method can still leave too little accessible cash. A method that retains cash can still be unaffordable when income arrives late or declines. The final decision needs a workable calendar and a clear account of the extra cost. Use both views together and resolve any negative positions before interpreting a modelled advantage.
fe7fd315872b428b08202eb18f937339beec9cea.zh: 付款方式有价格和现金日历。在将低报价或大量留存银行余额视为决定性事实之前，请检查两者。将相同的商品与相同的资源进行比较现金折扣和融资优惠可以使相同的购买看起来像是两个截然不同的决定。要对它们进行比较，请从相同的项目、相同的起始现金余额以及扣除普通费用后相同的每月可用金额开始。该物品的所有权价值对于两条路径都是相同的。现在付款使用所选折扣后的全价。融资借入未贴现的全价并立即用现金支付设立费。贷款按月等额分期偿还，最终还款额有上限。该模型假设没有大额金额，也没有可选的提前还款。两条路径在月底收到相同的每月预算。在立即付费的道路上，它重建了现金。在融资路径中，现金首先满足贷款支付；随后的预算将补充该帐户。这种安排可以防止比较悄悄地给予一种支付方式比另一种支付方式更多的家庭收入。在每月预算余额之前储备金可能会不足 第一个图表显示了贷款支付后但月末预算到达之前的每个现金头寸。零月份包括折扣购买付款或融资费用。所选预留楼层仅供参考，并非普遍推荐。在最初的示例中，该商品在享受 3% 现金折扣之前的售价为 10,000 加元。现在支付 15,000 加元还剩下 5,300 加元。尽管该家庭之后每月的预算仍然是 500 加元，但这只比选定的 5,000 加元底价高出 300 加元。立即到期的单独账单仍需要在计划中占有一席之地。融资可以保留更多的初始现金，但也会产生所需的付款。负图表位置意味着输入的资源无法为当时假定的付款提供资金。这不是自动批准的透支。该模型不对救援贷款或罚款进行定价；每当任何一条路径需要额外资金时，它都会抑制最终的经济比较。添加您给予的费用和贷款利息的折扣 第二个图表显示了未偿还的购买贷款。最初的示例使用假设的 5% 名义年贷款利率和二十四个月的还款额。付款金额约为438.71加元，贷款利息总额约为529.13加元。实际贷款机构报价可以使用不同的惯例和额外费用。第三张图表添加了放弃的 300 加元现金折扣、150 加元安装费和 529.13 加元利息。整个期限内，融资产生的额外购买支出约为 979.13 加元。这是名义上的现金成本溢价；它尚未包括留存现金收入或付款发生时间。在零利率贷款利率下，利息从这座桥上消失，但费用和放弃的折扣可以保留。因此，将报价称为零利率并不能证明两种支付方式具有相同的经济成本。输入的利率还排除了现金支付费用和折扣影响，因此它不是全部法定年利率披露。将现金利息与购买成本分开 正现金余额可赚取选定的有效年度回报，并转换为每月等值回报。在最初的例子中，假设是 3%。最终付款后，立即付款路径约为 17,969 加元，融资路径约为 17,268 加元。两人都没有剩余的购买债务，并且拥有相同的物品。大约 702 加元的差异小于名义购买成本溢价，因为融资路径较早持有更多生息现金。这是该利息税前的说明，不能保证现金利率保持可用。有风险的投资回报不能替代付款计划中的现金收益。第四张图表测试了贷款利率和每月预算的融资情况。每个单元格都会测量任何付款日期低于所选保留底线的最大差距。这是对所需额外起始现金的保守估计，而不是错过付款的可能性。如果实际添加了该现金，请重新运行完整的分类账，因为其利息也会影响路径。在将说明变成承诺之前，请先阅读协议 FCAC 的个人贷款指南将利息、费用、期限和还款义务确定为借款成本的一部分。实际购买的，应书面收取现金价款和融资价款，确认付款总额，并检查折扣是否附加条件。寻找延期利息条款、强制性附加条款、滞纳金、费率变化、项目担保和提前付款条款。这个普通的固定利率示例中不包含任何内容。输入一致的含销售税的购买价格；该工具无法确定税法如何适用于实际退税。更便宜的支付方式仍然会留下太少的可用现金。当收入迟到或下降时，保留现金的方法仍然难以承担。最终的决定需要一个可行的日历和对额外成本的明确说明。在解释建模优势之前，结合使用两种观点并解决任何负面立场。

05a286bfe2bfcb7e6c020cecffdf0bdd526f5497.src: A wealth median describes a particular group at a particular date. It does not tell you how much cash a family can spend or what your own plan needs. Read the population, date and unit first Statistics Canada’s 2023 Survey of Financial Security release , published on 29 October 2024, reports family wealth in 2023 constant Canadian dollars. “Families” includes economic families and unattached individuals. Age refers to the major income earner. Coverage is the ten provinces, excluding Indigenous communities and collective dwellings. These observations describe 2023, even when you read the article in 2026. They are not current account balances. The sample has sampling variability and does not adequately represent the very wealthy; the release supplies no confidence intervals for the selected comparisons. The age and provincial wealth guide provides broader context. Here the focus is how housing and pension status change comparisons within selected age groups. Before using any benchmark, write down four items: who was measured, when they were measured, which balance-sheet definition was used, and whether the statistic is a median or mean. A number with the wrong denominator can be precise and still answer the wrong question. Keep housing and pension status visible Among families with a major income earner under 35, median net worth was CAD 457,100 with a principal residence and CAD 44,000 without one. For ages 55–64, the four displayed medians range from CAD 11,900 with neither a principal home nor an employer pension to a rounded CAD 1.4 million with both. The bars show group differences. They do not measure what would happen if the same family bought a home tomorrow, nor isolate housing from earnings, age within the band, borrowing or other circumstances. Treat them as context for a question, rather than the answer to a purchase decision. A median is the middle observation after ordering the measured values. It is neither an average account balance nor a recommended target. A family above a median may have an unaffordable monthly budget; another below it may have reliable income and modest future spending needs. Build your own balance sheet without double counting The independent worked example has CAD 600,000 of net home equity, CAD 250,000 of pension and restricted assets, CAD 100,000 of other investments and CAD 20,000 of uncommitted cash. These non-overlapping amounts add to CAD 970,000. The example is not a reconstruction of a median family. It deliberately combines a large balance-sheet total with a much smaller immediate cash amount so the two planning jobs remain visible. Net home equity is already after the mortgage. Entering equity and then deducting the same mortgage again would understate net worth. Conversely, entering the home’s gross value as equity would overstate it. A fuller balance sheet would list each asset and liability separately, with a valuation date and consistent ownership share. Use care with pension values. A benefit valuation may belong on a balance sheet without being a bank account you can withdraw. If pension income already funds retirement spending in another projection, do not also spend its entire balance-sheet value as available cash in that same projection. Give immediately available cash its own test The last graphic assumes income stops for six months. Essential bills are CAD 4,000 per month and an additional CAD 8,000 bill arrives immediately. Required cash is therefore 8,000 + 6 × 4,000 = CAD 32,000 . Against CAD 20,000 of uncommitted cash, the unfunded need is CAD 12,000. The CAD 970,000 net-worth total does not settle that difference automatically. This model does not sell investments, borrow against a property or draw pension benefits. That is a deliberately narrow stress, not a recommendation that every family hold six months of the same expenses. Actual needs depend on job income, available support, payment dates, insurance and the consequences of selling assets. FCAC’s goal-setting guidance identifies access to short-term savings as a separate consideration. Change one component and ask what actually improved Increase home equity by CAD 100,000 while leaving cash unchanged. The hypothetical net-worth waterfall increases by CAD 100,000, but the six-month funding gap stays CAD 12,000. That is the distinction between balance-sheet value and resources assigned to a payment. Next increase cash by CAD 12,000 while keeping all other fields unchanged. The stress becomes fully funded and net worth also rises. This edit assumes new resources: it does not represent moving money from investments to cash. To model a transfer, reduce investments by the same amount so total wealth remains constant. For a practical review, keep three separate records: a dated balance sheet, a calendar of spending and receipts, and a list of assets that could become cash with their costs and restrictions. Review progress against your own obligations and goals alongside any population comparison.
05a286bfe2bfcb7e6c020cecffdf0bdd526f5497.zh: 财富中位数描述了特定日期的特定群体。它不会告诉您一个家庭可以花多少钱或您自己的计划需要什么。首先阅读人口、日期和单位加拿大统计局于 2024 年 10 月 29 日发布的 2023 年金融安全调查报告，报告了按 2023 年不变加元计算的家庭财富。 “家庭”包括经济家庭和单身个人。年龄是指主要收入来源。覆盖范围为十个省份，不包括原住民社区和集体住宅。这些观察描述的是 2023 年，即使您在 2026 年阅读这篇文章。它们不是经常账户余额。样本存在抽样变异性，并不能充分代表非常富有的人；该版本没有为所选比较提供置信区间。年龄和省份财富指南提供了更广泛的背景。这里的重点是住房和养老金状况如何改变选定年龄组内的比较。在使用任何基准之前，写下四个项目：测量对象、测量时间、使用哪种资产负债表定义以及统计数据是中位数还是均值。分母错误的数字可能很精确，但仍然会回答错误的问题。保持住房和养老金状况可见 在主要收入来源年龄在 35 岁以下的家庭中，有主要居所的家庭净资产中位数为 457,100 加元，没有主要居所的家庭净资产中位数为 44,000 加元。对于 55 至 64 岁的人群，显示的四位中位数范围为既没有主要住房也没有雇主养老金的 11,900 加元，到两者都有的 140 万加元。条形图显示了组间差异。他们没有衡量如果同一个家庭明天买房会发生什么，也没有将住房与收入、年龄范围、借贷或其他情况分开。将它们视为问题的背景，而不是购买决策的答案。中位数是对测量值进行排序后的中间观察值。它既不是平均账户余额，也不是推荐目标。中位数以上的家庭可能每月的预算难以承担；低于它的另一个可能有可靠的收入和适度的未来支出需求。建立您自己的资产负债表，无需重复计算 独立工作示例有 600,000 加元的净房屋净值、250,000 加元的养老金和限制资产、100,000 加元的其他投资以及 20,000 加元的未承诺现金。这些不重叠的金额加起来为 970,000 加元。这个例子并不是对中产家庭的重建。它故意将庞大的资产负债表总额与小得多的即时现金金额结合起来，以便两项规划工作仍然可见。净房屋净值已经是抵押贷款之后的值。输入股本，然后再次扣除相同的抵押贷款会低估净资产。相反，将房屋的总价值作为权益输入则会夸大其价值。更完整的资产负债表将分别列出每项资产和负债，并附有估值日期和一致的所有权份额。使用具有养老金价值的护理。福利评估可能属于资产负债表，而不是您可以提取的银行账户。如果养老金收入已经为另一个预测中的退休支出提供资金，则不要在同一预测中将其全部资产负债表价值作为可用现金支出。对立即可用的现金进行自己的测试最后一张图表假设收入停止六个月。基本账单为每月 4,000 加元，额外的 8,000 加元账单将立即到达。因此，所需现金为 8,000 + 6 × 4,000 = 32,000 加元。相对于 20,000 加元未承诺现金，未提供资金的需求为 12,000 加元。 970,000 加元的净资产总额不会自动结算该差额。这种模式不出售投资、以财产为抵押借款或提取养老金福利。这是刻意缩小的压力，而不是建议每个家庭承担六个月的相同费用。实际需求取决于工作收入、可用支持、付款日期、保险和出售资产的后果。 FCAC 的目标设定指南将获得短期储蓄作为单独的考虑因素。更改一个组件并询问实际改善了什么 将房屋净值增加 100,000 加元，同时保持现金不变。假设的净资产瀑布增加 100,000 加元，但六个月的资金缺口仍为 12,000 加元。这就是资产负债表价值和分配给付款的资源之间的区别。接下来增加现金 12,000 加元，同时保持所有其他字段不变。压力变得充足，净资产也上升。此编辑假设有新资源：它并不代表将资金从投资转移到现金。要模拟转移，请减少相同数量的投资，以使总财富保持不变。为了进行实际审查，请保留三份单独的记录：一份注明日期的资产负债表、一份支出和收入的日历，以及一份可以变现的资产清单及其成本和限制。根据您自己的义务和目标以及任何人口比较来审查进展情况。

5008627f08ffe25ac8e8b4195e3d5e25da5f40a5.src: A transfer can be fully paid today while leaving later household needs unfunded. Test the gift date, the spending plan and less favourable returns together. Define the promise and the resources that fund it A family may want to help an adult child with housing, education or another major expense. The planning question is how that commitment fits alongside the donor’s future withdrawals, rather than whether the current statement balance exceeds the gift. This independent example begins with CAD 500,000 available for both purposes. It requests household withdrawals of CAD 20,000 in the first year, increasing by 2% annually for twenty-five years, and compares a CAD 100,000 gift now with the same nominal gift in year six. The household withdrawal input means the amount this portfolio must supply. Other reliable income should be accounted for separately when estimating it. Do not enter the household’s whole budget if pensions already pay part of that budget, or count those pensions again as portfolio assets. The model is a cash-capacity illustration. It does not decide whether a transfer should be a gift, loan, advance on an estate or ownership interest, and does not calculate tax or legal consequences. Keep payment dates and priorities explicit In every year, the modeled gift is paid first if it is due. The household withdrawal comes next, and the remaining portfolio then earns the selected effective return after costs. Year-end balances therefore reflect payments made before that year’s growth. With an immediate gift, the first-year calculation is (500,000 − 100,000 − 20,000) × 1.03 = CAD 391,400 . With no gift in that year it is (500,000 − 20,000) × 1.03 = CAD 494,400 . Gift priority is an explicit teaching convention that exposes the consequences of making the commitment. It is not a recommendation to put a transfer ahead of essentials. An implementation could reserve household needs first, reduce the gift or make it conditional; each would require a different instruction. Actual gifts and withdrawals are capped at the money available. The model never silently borrows to make the transfer, and unmet gift requests are shown separately from unmet household withdrawals. A paid gift can coexist with a later spending gap At the default constant 3% return, the no-gift path funds all requested household withdrawals and ends after twenty-five years with about CAD 113,354.78. That remaining amount is not a required reserve; the calculator imposes no terminal target. The immediate CAD 100,000 gift is fully paid, but the same household requests later exceed available assets by a cumulative CAD 90,639.86. The ending portfolio is zero. The year-six gift is also fully paid. Delaying it leaves money in the portfolio longer under the positive-return assumption, reducing the cumulative household shortfall to about CAD 64,314.28. It does not remove the shortfall. These sums are nominal requests in their respective years. They receive no interest and are not a debt balance or a present value. A later surplus cannot retroactively deliver a missed household payment. Check the endpoint without losing the missing payments The waterfall reconciles the selected delayed-gift path: starting assets, less the gift actually delivered, less household withdrawals actually paid, plus cumulative modeled gains or losses, equals remaining assets. Requested amounts that were never paid do not belong in that balance-sheet reconciliation. They remain a separate planning obligation. This is why a portfolio path that simply ends at zero can hide a substantial gap unless the unmet requests are reported too. If a gift date is later than the selected horizon, the chart labels it outside the horizon and records no in-period gift. That case is not an affordable delayed gift; the comparison ends before testing the promise. Extend the horizon or bring the date inside it before drawing a conclusion. If the later gift date is year one, its path must coincide with the immediate-gift path. If the gift amount is zero, all three portfolio paths must coincide. These simple checks help interpret more complex settings. Test a smaller promise before selecting a larger assumed return The matrix compares four gift amounts with four constant-return assumptions while holding the selected date, spending schedule and horizon fixed. It reports only household requests that could not be funded. The separate transfer chart is needed to see whether the gift itself was delivered. A zero household shortfall is limited to that cell’s invented path and horizon. Smooth returns omit sequence risk, and an endpoint above zero says nothing about care needs, spending after the horizon or an intended inheritance. The same nominal gift later also buys a different amount if prices rise. Try a smaller gift, a different date and a longer horizon. Record which household expenses would be affected if returns were lower or additional support was needed. FCAC’s goal-setting framework provides the general discipline of assigning amounts, dates and priorities; the family must supply its own constraints. The government’s aging-in-place checklist also prompts planning for unexpected health-related support and home repairs. Those needs would have to be budgeted explicitly here, rather than assumed covered by the unallocated endpoint. Before making a real commitment, establish what is accessible after withdrawal tax and transaction costs, retain resources for the donor’s own needs, and clarify the transfer’s terms with appropriate professional help. The charts do not confirm tax treatment, legal ownership or an entitlement to repayment.
5008627f08ffe25ac8e8b4195e3d5e25da5f40a5.zh: 今天就可以全额支付转账，而以后的家庭需求则得不到资助。一起测试礼物日期、消费计划和不太有利的回报。定义承诺和为其提供资金的资源 家庭可能希望帮助成年子女支付住房、教育或其他主要费用。规划问题是该承诺如何与捐赠者未来的提款相适应，而不是当前的报表余额是否超过捐赠。这个独立示例的起始金额为 500,000 加元，可用于这两个目的。它要求家庭在第一年提取 20,000 加元，二十五年内每年增加 2%，并将现在 100,000 加元的礼物与第六年相同名义的礼物进行比较。家庭提款投入是指该投资组合必须提供的金额。其他可靠收入在预计时应当单独核算。如果养老金已经支付了家庭预算的一部分，则不要输入家庭的全部预算，或者将这些养老金再次计入投资组合资产。该模型是现金能力的说明。它不决定转让是否属于赠与、贷款、遗产预付款或所有权权益，也不计算税收或法律后果。明确付款日期和优先顺序 每年，如果到期，则首先支付模仿的礼物。接下来是家庭提款，然后剩余的投资组合在扣除成本后获得选定的有效回报。因此，年终余额反映了当年增长之前支付的款项。如果立即赠送，第一年的计算结果为 (500,000 − 100,000 − 20,000) × 1.03 = 391,400 加元。如果当年没有礼物，则为 (500,000 − 20,000) × 1.03 = 494,400 加元。礼物优先是一种明确的教学惯例，暴露了做出承诺的后果。不建议将转会置于必需品之上。实施时可以首先保留家庭需求，减少礼物或设定有条件；每个都需要不同的指令。实际礼物和提款的上限为可用金额。该模型从不默默借钱进行转账，未满足的礼物请求与未满足的家庭提款分开显示。付费礼物可以与以后的支出缺口共存。在默认的恒定 3% 回报率下，无礼物路径为所有要求的家庭提款提供资金，并在 25 年后结束，金额约为 113,354.78 加元。剩余金额不是法定准备金；计算器没有强加最终目标。立即支付的 100,000 加元礼物已全额支付，但同一家庭随后的请求超出了可用资产，累计金额达 90,639.86 加元。期末投资组合为零。六年级的礼物也已全额支付。在正回报假设下，推迟投资会使投资组合中的资金更长，从而将累计家庭缺口减少至约 64,314.28 加元。它并不能消除短缺。这些金额是各自年份的象征性请求。它们不收取任何利息，也不是债务余额或现值。后来的盈余不能追溯支付错过的家庭付款。检查端点而不丢失缺失的付款瀑布会协调所选的延迟礼物路径：起始资产减去实际交付的礼物，减去实际支付的家庭提款，加上累积模型收益或损失，等于剩余资产。从未支付的请求金额不属于该资产负债表调节范围。它们仍然是一项单独的规划义务。这就是为什么简单地以零结束的投资组合路径可能会隐藏巨大的差距，除非也报告了未满足的请求。如果礼物日期晚于所选范围，图表会将其标记在范围之外，并且不会记录期间礼物。那个箱子不是一个负担得起的延迟礼物；比较在测试承诺之前结束。在得出结论之前，扩大视野或将日期纳入其中。如果较晚的礼物日期是第一年，则其路径必须与直接礼物路径一致。如果礼物金额为零，则所有三个投资组合路径必须重合。这些简单的检查有助于解释更复杂的设置。在选择较大的假设回报之前测试较小的承诺 该矩阵将四个礼物金额与四个恒定回报假设进行比较，同时保持选定的日期、支出计划和范围固定。它仅报告无法获得资助的家庭请求。需要单独的转运表来查看礼物本身是否已交付。零家庭短缺仅限于该细胞发明的路径和视野。平滑回报忽略了顺序风险，高于零的终点没有说明护理需求、期后支出或预期继承。如果价格上涨，同样的象征性礼物后来也会购买不同数量的礼物。尝试较小的礼物、不同的日期和更长的视野。记录如果回报较低或需要额外支持，哪些家庭支出会受到影响。 FCAC 的目标设定框架提供了分配金额、日期和优先事项的一般规则；家庭必须提供自己的约束。政府的就地老龄化清单还促使人们规划意外的健康相关支持和房屋维修。这些需求必须在这里明确预算，而不是假设由未分配的端点覆盖。在做出真正的承诺之前，先确定扣除提款税和交易成本后可以获得的资源，保留资源以满足捐赠者自身的需求，并在适当的专业帮助下澄清转移条款。这些图表并未确认税收待遇、合法所有权或还款权利。

76296ba578d2ed33a50b9386e83f53fbe146cd24.src: An adjustment rule may preserve more capital by asking you to spend less. The chart must show the reduction in consumption as clearly as the remaining portfolio. Define a rule the household could actually follow “Be flexible” is too vague to put into a retirement budget. A useful illustration states when the review happens, which withdrawal measure is tested, what cut occurs, and which essential expenses cannot voluntarily be cut. This example starts with CAD 600,000 and requests CAD 30,000 at the start of the first year. The initial withdrawal rate is 5%. The uncut target then rises by 2% each year. These are invented assumptions, not a safe-withdrawal recommendation. From year two, the alternative rule first increases the previous request for inflation. It divides that request by the opening portfolio. If the ratio exceeds the initial rate by more than 25% in relative terms, it applies one 10% cut. The threshold is 5% × 1.25 = 6.25% , not 30% and not a 25-percentage-point addition. The example allows 25% of the initial request to be flexible. Its first-year essential floor is therefore CAD 22,500, increasing with inflation. Every later cut is bounded by that floor. Follow the second-year decision in dollars The first invented return is −18%. After withdrawing CAD 30,000, the remaining CAD 570,000 falls to CAD 467,400. Both policies have the same first-year payment and ending capital. The uncut second-year request is CAD 30,600. Dividing by the opening CAD 467,400 gives about 6.55%, which crosses the 6.25% threshold. Applying the 10% cut reduces the request to CAD 27,540, above the second-year essential floor of CAD 22,950. The second invented return is −8%. The alternative portfolio ends that year at CAD 404,671.20, compared with CAD 401,856 under full indexation. The difference comes from a smaller withdrawal and the return on the money left behind; it is not a higher investment return. Only one cut is applied per annual review. The model does not repeatedly cut within the same year until the withdrawal ratio falls under the threshold. Read capital and consumption together The fixed twenty-return sequence is disclosed above the figures and includes another −10% year later in the illustration. It is not a historical backtest or a forecast. The same returns apply to both policies, and there are no government or employer pensions in this isolated portfolio comparison. With the defaults, the rule makes three actual cuts. Across twenty years it requests about CAD 168,267.55 less than full indexation and ends with about CAD 231,762.88. All its reduced requests are funded in this particular path. The fully indexed policy runs out of assets and leaves about CAD 22,323.60 of its requests unfunded. Its funded payments still total more than the alternative’s, because it asks for more consumption earlier. Reading only the endpoint would hide this material difference. Nominal totals across different years are bookkeeping sums, not present values. The model does not assign a utility value to an earlier holiday or a later contingency reserve. An essential floor limits cuts; it cannot create income The floor is a constraint on the requested spending rule. It is not an insurance benefit or an external income guarantee. If the portfolio cannot pay the request, the calculator caps the actual payment and records the remainder as unfunded. The stacked bars keep these two concepts apart. Voluntarily forgone requests are reported as the reduction from full indexation. Unfunded requests are spending the policy still asked for but assets could not deliver. Adding them without labels would blur two different experiences for the household. Set the flexible share to zero. Both policies then request the fully indexed amount, whatever trigger or cut is entered. This is a useful reality check for a budget dominated by essentials: a theoretical adjustment strategy cannot assume discretionary spending that does not exist. Use the matrix to inspect the cost of the rule The final figure changes the trigger and cut size. Every cell reports total requested spending forgone over the same twenty years. A zero cut produces zero voluntary reduction. A larger result means more consumption has been removed, not that the strategy has a higher probability of success. The rule has no automatic restoration to the original target after recovery. Each following year starts from the previously reduced request, increased for inflation, and tests the threshold again. A strategy with catch-up increases or upper and lower guardrails would be a different policy. For a real spending review, separate essential bills from flexible purchases, identify non-portfolio income, and decide which adjustments are tolerable before a difficult year. Investor.gov’s older-investor guidance supports reviewing changing circumstances and account information; it does not endorse this invented rule. The illustration excludes taxes, mandatory registered-account withdrawals, mortality, asset allocation changes and needs after year twenty. A positive endpoint in one chosen sequence cannot establish lifetime adequacy.
76296ba578d2ed33a50b9386e83f53fbe146cd24.zh: 调整规则可以通过要求您减少支出来保留更多资本。该图表必须像剩余投资组合一样清楚地显示消费的减少。定义家庭实际上可以遵循的规则“保持灵活性”太模糊，无法纳入退休预算。一个有用的例子说明了审查何时进行、测试了哪些退出措施、发生了什么削减以及哪些基本费用不能自愿削减。此示例从 600,000 加元开始，并在第一年年初请求 30,000 加元。初始提款率为5%。未削减的目标每年增加 2%。这些都是虚构的假设，而不是安全提款建议。从第二年开始，替代规则首先增加之前的通货膨胀要求。它将该请求除以开放投资组合。如果相对而言该比率超出初始税率25%以上，则削减10%。阈值是 5% × 1.25 = 6.25% ，而不是 30% ，也不是增加 25 个百分点。该示例允许 25% 的初始请求具有灵活性。因此，第一年的基本底线为 22,500 加元，并随着通货膨胀而增加。以后的每次切割都以该楼层为界。按照以美元计算的第二年决策第一个发明的回报率为-18%。提取30,000加元后，剩余的570,000加元降至467,400加元。两种保单的首年付款和期末资本相同。未削减的第二年请求为 30,600 加元。除以开盘价 467,400 加元，得出的结果约为 6.55%，突破了 6.25% 的门槛。削减 10% 后，需求将减少至 27,540 加元，高于第二年基本底线 22,950 加元。第二个发明的回报率为-8%。另类投资组合当年结束时的价格为 404,671.20 加元，而完全指数化下的价格为 401,856 加元。差异来自较小的提款和剩余资金的回报；这并不是更高的投资回报。每次年度审核仅适用一次削减。该模型不会在同一年内重复削减，直至退出比例低于阈值。一起阅读资本和消费 固定的 20 回报序列在图上方公开，并在插图中包括一年后的另一个 -10%。这不是历史回测或预测。两种保单的回报率相同，并且在这个孤立的投资组合比较中没有政府或雇主养老金。使用默认值时，该规则会进行三次实际削减。二十年来，它要求比完全指数化少约 168,267.55 加元，最终要求约 231,762.88 加元。所有减少的请求都通过这一特定途径提供资金。完全索引的保单耗尽了资产，并导致约 22,323.60 加元的请求得不到资助。它的资助支付总额仍然高于替代方案，因为它要求更早的消费。只读取端点会隐藏这种实质性差异。不同年份的名义总额是簿记金额，而不是现值。该模型不会为较早的假期或较晚的应急储备分配效用值。基本限制削减；它不能创造收入 下限是对所要求的支出规则的限制。它不是保险福利或外部收入保证。如果投资组合无法支付请求，计算器将限制实际付款并将剩余部分记录为无资金。堆叠的条形将这两个概念分开。自愿放弃的请求被报告为完全指数化的减少。未提供资金的请求正在支出仍要求的保单，但资产无法交付。在没有标签的情况下添加它们会模糊家庭的两种不同体验。将灵活份额设置为零。然后，无论输入什么触发器或削减，这两个策略都请求完全索引的金额。对于以基本要素为主的预算来说，这是一个有用的现实检验：理论上的调整策略不能假设不存在的可自由支配支出。使用矩阵检查规则的成本最终数字会更改触发和切割尺寸。每个单元都报告在同一二十年中所放弃的总支出。零削减产生零自愿削减。结果越大意味着消除了更多的消耗，但并不意味着该策略成功的可能性更高。该规则恢复后不会自动恢复到原始目标。接下来的每一年，从之前减少的要求开始，因通货膨胀而增加，并再次测试阈值。追赶式增长或上下护栏的策略将是不同的政策。对于真正的支出审查，将基本账单与灵活购买分开，确定非投资组合收入，并在困难的一年之前决定哪些调整是可以容忍的。 Investor.gov 的老年投资者指南支持审查不断变化的情况和账户信息；它不认可这个发明的规则。该图不包括税收、强制性注册账户提款、死亡率、资产配置变化和二十年后的需求。一个选定序列中的正终点不能确定终生充足性。

52045fc0dc11ec34b9bc6359f9997fda14d116db.src: A higher take-home salary can leave only a small cash improvement after work costs. Show the time commitment separately before judging the offer. Start with comparable take-home amounts A job offer may advertise a higher salary while changing commuting, meals, parking, clothing, care arrangements and the time available at home. The useful starting comparison is the cash the household can actually receive, followed by the costs required to earn it. The tool asks for monthly take-home pay in the current and proposed jobs. Enter independently estimated amounts after payroll deductions on the same basis. It does not convert gross salaries into net pay, estimate income tax or treat a discretionary bonus as certain. If the offer is quoted biweekly, use the actual annual payroll expectation before converting it to a comparable monthly amount. The default moves from CAD 4,500 to CAD 5,000 of monthly take-home pay, a CAD 6,000 annual increase. That is a starting point rather than the final household improvement. Both amounts cover all twelve months; commuting occurs only during the selected working weeks. A partial first year or an unpaid gap between jobs needs its own dated cash plan. The cash bridge subtracts the cost difference The current job requires three commuting days per week for 46 weeks, at CAD 12 per return trip. Annual commuting cost is CAD 1,656. Other work costs are CAD 50 per month, adding CAD 600. The proposed job requires five commuting days per week at CAD 28 per return trip, producing CAD 6,440 of travel costs plus CAD 1,200 of other work costs. Specified annual work costs therefore rise from CAD 2,256 to CAD 7,640, a CAD 5,384 increase. Subtracting that increase from the CAD 6,000 take-home improvement leaves CAD 616 per year , or about CAD 51.33 per month, before omitted household effects. The waterfall subtracts the incremental costs. Subtracting all of the new commuting cost while ignoring the old cost would understate the gain; subtracting neither would overstate it. A cost that falls adds to the bridge. If the final step is negative, the offer leaves less cash under the entered assumptions despite any higher pay. Include costs that actually change, and avoid charging them twice Use the return-trip daily input for costs that vary with office attendance. Fuel and parking may fit this structure when the rate is reasonably stable. A monthly transit pass does not necessarily cost less because one office day is removed, so place a fixed pass cost in the monthly field instead of pretending it is entirely variable. Other monthly costs can include a separately estimated change in work meals or clothing. Count only the relevant additional amount if an expense would also occur at home. Do not enter the same parking or travel bill in both fields. A new vehicle, relocation, child care or a substantial change in insurance needs more detail than this compact comparison provides. The annual bars show take-home receipts and specified costs separately. Their difference is cash remaining before ordinary living expenses and saving, not a complete disposable-income statistic. The FCAC budgeting guide provides general context for tracking actual income and expenses. The salary amounts, cost schedule and calculations here are original hypothetical examples. Read the time chart without inventing an hourly wage The current return trip takes 45 minutes; the proposed trip takes 90 minutes. Across the default working weeks, annual commuting rises from 103.5 hours to 345 hours. That is an additional 241.5 hours travelling for the CAD 616 partial annual cash improvement. The model leaves those hours visible rather than automatically assigning them a dollar value. A shorter trip may support caregiving, rest, study or another activity that the household values differently. Conversely, a role can offer development, stability or satisfaction that a cash-only comparison does not capture. These are commuting hours, not total hours worked. Dividing annual take-home pay by this travel time would not produce a meaningful hourly wage. Differences in contracted hours, overtime, remote availability and unpaid responsibilities require separate inputs and judgment. The chart gives one time commitment a clear scale without pretending to evaluate the entire employment decision. Use the break-even pay as a cash comparison, not a salary recommendation The break-even metric asks what monthly take-home pay the new job would need to leave the same cash after the specified work costs. It equals (current annual remaining cash + proposed annual work costs) ÷ 12 . With the defaults, the result is about CAD 4,948.67 per month. That is a net-pay figure. It is not the gross salary to request from an employer, and converting it requires an independently appropriate payroll estimate. It also leaves out pension accrual, employer matching, insurance benefits, stock compensation and other non-cash terms. A higher break-even amount can result when new cash costs are substantial even though the advertised salary increase looks large. The sensitivity matrix tests alternative office attendance and return-trip costs for the new job. Holding pay and other inputs fixed, three commuting days at CAD 28 per day would leave CAD 3,192 of additional annual cash in this example. That possibility is useful only if the arrangement is actually available and durable. Build a decision record with money, time and unresolved terms Verify comparable annual take-home expectations and the first payment date. List work costs that change, separating per-day costs, fixed costs and one-time costs. Document the office schedule, return-trip travel time and whether either can change. Compare retirement and insurance benefits separately from current cash. Check how the transition affects reserves, care arrangements and existing commitments. The illustration assumes a full year in each role, constant pay, a stable schedule and known costs. It does not model a probation period, future pay rises, job loss, changing travel prices or a late reimbursement. Use the result to locate the assumptions that matter, then test them against the actual offer and household budget before making a commitment.
