b775da132d6e325f945cf3122923ff2be7ceb697.zh: 较低的付款要求可以减轻本月的预算，同时延长债务。一起跟踪余额、还款日期和总利息。为什么减少的付款值得重新审视想象一下，打开一张卡对账单，发现所需的付款已经减少。这可能是值得欢迎的现金流缓解。它不会告诉您剩余债务将多快消失。当还款额占余额下降的一定比例时，每月用于还款的资金可能会减少，从而形成小额付款的长尾。第一个图表遵循该机制。它从现有余额开始，收取一个月的利息，然后应用假设的最低余额。只要付款金额超过最低金额，比较就会保留所选付款金额。两种路径都假设没有新的购买和按时付款。 FCAC 解释说，最低公式各不相同，支付更多费用可以减少还款时间和利息。将协议用于实际帐户。这里选择的百分比和美元下限是教学输入，而不是适用于每张加拿大卡的规则的声明。将这两条线理解为不同的家庭承诺所维持的策略不仅仅是在相同的现金流上获得更快的投资回报。提早离开家庭通常需要更多的钱。收益来自减少未来利息的余额；成本是可用于其他需求的现金减少，而更多的付款仍在继续。付款图表使这种权衡显而易见。选择的 300 加元金额被视为下限，更高的模型最低金额仍优先。最终付款减少至实际欠款金额。这可以避免向帐户支付过多费用或将所选金额视为低于可接受的最低金额。检查承诺是否符合住房、食品、所需的债务支付和其他基本账单。如果没有，从数学上看，较短的还款计划并不能解决现金流问题。在选择无法资助的路径之前，请考虑预算和可用的援助。准确了解模型中的利息和本金 对于期初余额 B 和名义年利率 a，简化的每月利息费用为 B × a ÷ 12 ，其中 a 表示为小数。应付金额变为 B 加上该费用。然后，该模型采用输入的美元下限和所选金额百分比中的较大者，上限为应付金额。对于维护策略，实际付款是该模型最低金额和所选维护金额中的较大者，同样以应付金额为上限。新余额是应付金额减去实际付款。下个月从该余额开始，因此提前支付本金会减少以后的利息。真实卡可以使用日常计算和多种余额类别。费用、宽限期、预付现金、促销条款和付款日期可能会改变结果。此示例特意使用一个速率桶。它不会复制声明、确定法律要求的最低限额或模拟错过付款的后果。未完成的余额仍然是一项义务堆叠的条形显示已支付的款项以及在每条路径停止日期仍欠的余额。它们合计等于原始本金加上截至该日期收取的利息。如果路径已完成，则剩余余额段为零。如果没有，将已支付的款项视为全额还款成本将隐藏债务。 600 个月后停止计算。 NR 单元表示余额尚未在该窗口内偿还。这并不意味着债务已经消失或剩余利息为零。以足够高的利率支付低比例的付款甚至可以使余额增长。这些条可以覆盖不同的时间长度，因为每条路径在完成时都会停止。他们通过这些端点来衡量名义现金和债务，而不是对支付后释放的款项进行再投资。它们不是对共同未来日期的投资财富的比较。将矩阵转化为付款决策 阅读一个费率行以测试几个维护的金额。然后向下阅读付款栏，看看不同的利息假设会产生什么作用。起始余额和最低规则保持不变。在每个单元格中，建模的最小值都会覆盖较小的维护量；栏标题并不承诺付款永远不会超过它。从可以持续的付款开始，并记下其模拟的完成日期。接下来测试适度的增长，然后测试更高的速度。如果该计划依赖于保持较低的促销率，请使用单独的余额转账指南将其到期后的期限包括在内。边做边回顾实际的陈述。新的支出、改变的费率和费用可以改变终点。偿还债务后，对可用现金做出新的决定：重建储备或为另一个目标提供资金需要新的指令，而不是隐藏在该计算器内的假设。

9a7ee8873ad75873bf7ca38a02c06cb023042329.src: A repeatable saving rule can make a series of small pay increases meaningful. The larger balance requires real contributions and less spending along the way. Begin with the increase that actually reaches the budget A raise expressed as a percentage of gross salary does not directly tell you how much more can be spent or saved. Deductions, benefit costs and payroll contributions can change the amount reaching the bank account. Start with an independently checked increase in take-home pay, then decide which new expenses that money must cover. This example uses a fixed dollar increase in monthly take-home pay at each annual anniversary. Year one has no increase. The first step arrives at the start of year two and continues thereafter. Another equal step begins in year three. This is a hypothetical income path, not a forecast of wages or a promise of annual raises. FCAC’s budgeting guidance brings income, spending, saving and changing circumstances into the same review. The tool starts after that review: its original monthly saving must already be affordable, and the entered increases must be available after any separately planned rise in essential costs. A small recurring increase accumulates into a larger pool Suppose the assumed monthly take-home increase is CAD 150 each year. Monthly income in year two is CAD 150 higher than at the start; in year three it is CAD 300 higher. By year ten, nine increases make the monthly difference CAD 1,350. These are accumulated additions to recurring income, not a single annual bonus. The selected saving share applies to that accumulated pool. With a 50% rule, half of each increase adds to monthly saving and half adds to spending. Earlier saving increases continue when the next increase arrives. The first chart annualizes both parts, so each bar equals twelve times that year’s monthly pool. The chart excludes original spending and original saving to keep the new-money decision visible. A larger bar later in the period comes from the assumed sequence of increases. It is not evidence that investments generated additional salary or that spending has automatically remained affordable. Compare saving rules with the income path held constant The three curves share starting savings, original monthly contributions, the pay-rise schedule, the assumed return and the finish date. They differ only in how much of each raise is saved. Saving none of the raises preserves only the original saving habit. Saving all assigns the entire increase to the account. The selected rule sits between those endpoints. These are different consumption choices. A household on the all-saving path has less additional spending during the period. Calling its larger endpoint better investment performance would confuse effort with return. The same assumed investment return applies to every path. Try a zero return first. The difference between endpoints then equals the additional cash contributed. Next test a lower or negative return to see how the investment assumption changes the outcome without changing the pay-rise commitment. Separate the saving effort from the investment effect The waterfall subtracts the zero-capture path from the selected path. Common starting savings and original deposits cancel. The first step is the total extra contributions funded by the rule. The second is the difference between the resulting extra wealth and those contributions: growth when positive, an investment loss when negative. The monthly return is (1 + annual return) 1/12 − 1 . Each month, the existing account grows at that rate before the month-end deposit arrives. Every deposit therefore gets only the remaining months of growth; the calculation does not give a late deposit the return earned by the initial balance. For N whole years and a fixed monthly pay-rise step S, the cumulative extra contributions are 12 × S × saving share × N(N − 1) ÷ 2 . This formula checks the saving effort independently of any investment return. All amounts are nominal CAD before account taxes and fees. Choose a rule that survives changing circumstances The matrix varies the saved percentage and planning horizon. It shows additional ending savings relative to saving none of the raises over the same number of years. A thirty-year case contains more assumed pay increases than a ten-year case, so the gap combines more contributions with more time for investment growth. A household might first assign part of an observed increase to essentials, then divide what remains between saving and optional spending. That real-world sequence is separate from this simplified tool. Inflation, caregiving, changing hours and a missed raise can all reduce the amount available. Write the rule in monthly dollars and review it when actual pay changes. An automatic transfer can implement a feasible decision, but it should follow the cash-flow check. Use the multiple-goal guide to decide where the extra saving goes; this article does not choose an account, set contribution room or rank goals for you.
9a7ee8873ad75873bf7ca38a02c06cb023042329.zh: 可重复的储蓄规则可以使一系列小额加薪变得有意义。更大的余额需要真正的贡献和一路上更少的支出。从实际达到预算的加薪开始 以占工资总额的百分比表示的加薪并不能直接告诉您还可以花费或节省多少。扣除额、福利成本和工资缴款可能会改变银行账户的金额。首先独立检查实得工资的增长，然后决定这笔钱必须支付哪些新费用。此示例使用每个周年纪念日每月实得工资的固定美元增长。第一年没有增加。第一步在第二年年初到达，并在此后继续。另一个同样的步骤从第三年开始。这是假设的收入路径，而不是工资预测或每年加薪的承诺。 FCAC 的预算指南将收入、支出、储蓄和不断变化的环境纳入同一审查范围。该工具在审查后启动：其最初的每月节省必须已经是可以承受的，并且输入的增长必须在任何单独计划的基本成本上涨之后可用。小额经常性增加会累积成一个更大的资金池 假设假设每月实得增加每年为 150 加元。第二年的月收入比开始时增加150加元；第三年则上涨 300 加元。到第十年，九次增加使每月差额达到 1,350 加元。这些是经常性收入的累积增加，而不是单一的年度奖金。所选储蓄份额适用于该累积池。按照 50% 的规则，每次增加的一半会增加每月储蓄，一半会增加支出。当下一次增加到来时，先前的储蓄增加将继续。第一个图表对这两个部分进行了年度化，因此每个条形等于当年月度池的十二倍。该图表不包括原始支出和原始储蓄，以保持新资金决策的可见性。该时期后期的较大条形图来自假设的增加序列。没有证据表明投资产生了额外的工资或支出自动保持在负担得起的水平。将储蓄规则与保持不变的收入路径进行比较 这三条曲线共享起始储蓄、原始每月供款、加薪时间表、假设回报和完成日期。它们的区别仅在于每次加薪节省了多少。不储蓄任何加薪只会保留原来的储蓄习惯。全部保存会将增加的全部金额分配给该帐户。所选规则位于这些端点之间。这些都是不同的消费选择。处于全储蓄路径的家庭在此期间的额外支出较少。称其较大的端点为更好的投资绩效会混淆努力与回报。相同的假设投资回报适用于每条路径。首先尝试归零。端点之间的差异就等于贡献的额外现金。接下来测试较低或负的回报，看看投资假设如何在不改变加薪承诺的情况下改变结果。将节约努力与投资效果分开瀑布从所选路径中减去零捕获路径。普通起始存款和原始存款取消。第一步是规则资助的额外捐款总额。第二个是由此产生的额外财富与这些贡献之间的差异：正数时增长，负数时投资损失。月回报率为 (1 + 年回报) 1/12 − 1 。每个月，在月底存款到达之前，现有账户都会以该速度增长。因此，每笔存款只能获得剩余几个月的增长；该计算不会给出延迟存款初始余额所赚取的回报。对于 N 年，每月固定加薪步长 S，累计额外缴款为 12 × S × 储蓄份额 × N(N − 1) ÷ 2 。该公式检查独立于任何投资回报的储蓄努力。所有金额均为扣除账户税费前的名义加元。选择适应不断变化的环境的规则 该矩阵会改变节省的百分比和计划期限。它显示了相对于相同年份没有节省任何加薪的额外期末节省。三十年的案例比十年的案例包含更多的假设加薪，因此这种差距结合了更多的贡献和更多的投资增长时间。家庭可能首先将观察到的增长的一部分分配给必需品，然后将剩余的部分分配给储蓄和可选支出。现实世界的序列与这个简化的工具是分开的。通货膨胀、护理、改变工作时间和错过加薪都会减少可用金额。以每月美元为单位编写规则，并在实际工资发生变化时进行审查。自动转移可以实现可行的决策，但应遵循现金流量检查。使用多目标指南来决定额外节省的资金去向；本文不会为您选择账户、设置贡献空间或排名目标。

db2dbbb57ef132e20806259820c149ccf698bfc6.src: An annual surplus does not tell you whether the next bill is funded. A dated cash calendar reveals the gap between average income and money already available. A monthly average is not a deposit date Dividing annual take-home pay by twelve is useful for comparing a year’s resources with a year’s costs. It does not tell you which day the money reaches an account. If bills arrive before salary, the household needs accessible opening cash even when the annual budget has a surplus. The FCAC’s budgeting guide emphasizes recording money received and spent. This article adds an explicit date to every modeled flow. Its purpose is to make payment timing visible alongside the annual total. The calendar is an invented 2027 example. It starts salary receipts on the selected January day and repeats them every fourteen days. It does not reproduce an employer’s payroll calendar, calculate wages earned or determine net pay from a salary. The same-day order is conservative: fixed bills and daily spending leave before that day’s salary arrives. Read two-payday and three-payday months on the actual calendar The default pays CAD 2,000 net on 8 January 2027, then every fourteen days. There are twenty-six receipts in this selected year, totaling CAD 52,000. April and October each contain three receipts, while the other ten months contain two. Annual receipts divided by twelve are about CAD 4,333.33 per month. Actual monthly receipts are CAD 4,000 or CAD 6,000 in this example. A monthly commitment based on the average therefore uses cash from the larger-receipt months to support the smaller ones. The first chart also shows outgoings: CAD 1,800 of fixed bills once each month plus CAD 60 on every calendar day. January costs CAD 3,660; February costs CAD 3,480. The daily allowance is intentionally calendar-based, including weekends. Do not multiply a workday-only allowance by every day of the year when adapting the example. Follow the account before the first payday The opening accessible reserve is CAD 500. Fixed bills of CAD 1,800 are due on 1 January, before any receipt. The same day also uses CAD 60 of other spending. By the moment immediately before the 8 January salary receipt, eight daily amounts have been paid. The total cost before that receipt is CAD 1,800 + 8 × CAD 60 = CAD 2,280 . Against CAD 500 already available, the unfunded amount is CAD 1,780. The CAD 2,000 receipt then takes the modeled account to positive CAD 220 at the end of that day. Looking only at the payday’s closing balance would miss the earlier shortage. The second chart therefore retains both points for every date: cash after costs but before salary, and cash after any salary. Negative values mark a funding requirement; the tool does not assume an authorized overdraft, delayed bill or available loan. Keep the annual surplus and the opening reserve in the same view Annual fixed bills total CAD 21,600 and other spending totals CAD 21,900. Combined outgoings are CAD 43,500. Against CAD 52,000 of salary receipts, the selected year generates CAD 8,500 of net cash before counting the opening reserve. The waterfall reconciles the endpoint: CAD 500 + CAD 52,000 − CAD 21,600 − CAD 21,900 = CAD 9,000 . That positive year-end amount coexists with the CAD 1,780 initial shortage. A later surplus cannot make an earlier payment on its own. The required-opening-cash metric is CAD 2,280, the amount which would keep this entire default schedule funded if it were accessible at the start. It includes cash already selected, so the additional amount is CAD 1,780. Increasing opening cash changes the funding gap and ending account amount dollar for dollar; it does not change salary, bills or the cash generated during the year. Use the date matrix without assuming equal annual receipts The matrix moves the first January receipt and the recurring monthly bill day. Each cell runs the full daily ledger again and finds the minimum opening reserve needed before any same-day salary receipt. Pay per receipt and all cost amounts stay fixed. A fourteen-day sequence can place twenty-six or twenty-seven paydays inside a calendar year, depending on the first date. Starting on 1 January 2027 produces twenty-seven in this mathematical schedule. The cells therefore do not all represent equal annual salary. They answer a cash-calendar question using the actual in-year receipts created by each selected date. Use the employer’s confirmed dates in practice, including holiday shifts. For example, the federal public-service calendar shows a specific employer schedule and explains its holiday adjustments and payment in arrears. Those employer-specific dates and rules are not applied to this invented calendar. Assign the next receipt before treating it as spendable List the bills due before the following payday, including automatic transfers and irregular commitments. Compare that dated list with cash that is already accessible. A three-payday month may provide room to build the opening buffer or fund another goal, but the next month’s obligations still need to be reserved. Keep genuinely unexpected costs separate from this known timing requirement. The opening amount here covers only the modeled bills and daily allowance. It is not a complete emergency reserve, and it includes no annual insurance payment, tax instalment, interest, service charge or unlisted purchase. The model fixes bills to a day from one through twenty-eight, so every selected day exists in every month. It has no business-day adjustments, leap-year logic beyond its fixed 2027 calendar or automatic rollover into another year. Before adopting the schedule, replace grouped bills with actual due dates and verify that receipts are settled and usable when needed.
db2dbbb57ef132e20806259820c149ccf698bfc6.zh: 年度盈余并不能告诉您下一个账单是否有资金支持。一份过时的现金日历揭示了平均收入与现有资金之间的差距。月平均数不是存款日期 将年实得工资除以 12 对于比较一年的资源和一年的成本很有用。它不会告诉您钱哪一天到达帐户。如果账单先于工资到达，即使年度预算有盈余，家庭也需要可用的期初现金。 FCAC 的预算指南强调记录收到和支出的资金。本文为每个建模流程添加了明确的日期。其目的是使付款时间与年度总额一起可见。该日历是一个发明的 2027 年示例。它从选定的一月份的某一天开始收到工资收据，并每十四天重复一次。它不会复制雇主的工资日历、计算赚取的工资或确定工资的净工资。当日订单是保守的：固定账单和日常支出在当天的工资到达之前就离开。阅读实际日历上的两个发薪日月份和三个发薪日月份 默认在 2027 年 1 月 8 日支付 2,000 加元净额，然后每十四天支付一次。本年度有 26 张收据，总计 52,000 加元。四月和十月各包含三张收据，而其他十个月则包含两张。年收入除以 12 约为每月 4,333.33 加元。在本示例中，实际每月收入为 4,000 加元或 6,000 加元。因此，基于平均值的每月承诺使用较大收入月份的现金来支持较小收入月份。第一个图表还显示了支出：每月一次 1,800 加元的固定账单，加上每个日历日的 60 加元。一月费用为 3,660 加元； 2 月份的费用为 3,480 加元。每日津贴有意基于日历，包括周末。在调整示例时，请勿将仅限工作日的津贴乘以一年中的每一天。在第一个发薪日之前关注账户 开放储备金为 500 加元。固定账单 1,800 加元应于 1 月 1 日（在任何收据之前）到期。当天还用了60加元的其他消费。截至 1 月 8 日收到工资之前，已支付每日八笔款项。收据前的总费用为 1,800 加元 + 8 × 60 加元 = 2,280 加元。与现有的 500 加元相比，未提供资金的金额为 1,780 加元。当天结束时，2,000 加元的收据会将模拟账户的金额转为 220 加元。只看发薪日的期末余额会忽略之前的短缺情况。因此，第二个图表保留了每个日期的两个点：成本之后但工资之前的现金，以及任何工资之后的现金。负值标志着资金需求；该工具不假设授权透支、延迟账单或可用贷款。将年度盈余和期初准备金保持在同一视图中 年度固定账单总计 21,600 加元，其他支出总计 21,900 加元。合计支出为 43,500 加元。相对于 52,000 加元的工资收入，选定年份在计算期初准备金之前会产生 8,500 加元的净现金。瀑布调和端点： CAD 500 + CAD 52,000 – CAD 21,600 – CAD 21,900 = CAD 9,000 。年底的正数与最初 1,780 加元的短缺同时存在。较晚的盈余不能自行提前支付。所需的期初现金指标为 2,280 加元，如果一开始就可以使用的话，这笔金额将为整个默认计划提供资金。其中包括已选择的现金，因此额外金额为 1,780 加元。增加期初现金会改变资金缺口和期末账户金额；它不会改变当年的工资、账单或现金。使用日期矩阵而不假设年度收入相等 该矩阵会移动第一个一月收入和定期每月账单日。每个单元再次运行完整的每日分类账，并找到在收到任何当天工资之前所需的最低期初准备金。按收据付款，所有费用金额保持不变。十四天的序列可以在一个日历年内放置二十六个或二十七个发薪日，具体取决于第一个日期。从 2027 年 1 月 1 日开始，这个数学时间表将产生 27 个。因此，这些单元格并不都代表相同的年薪。他们使用每个选定日期创建的实际年内收据来回答现金日历问题。在实践中使用雇主确认的日期，包括假期轮班。例如，联邦公共服务日历显示了特定的雇主时间表，并解释了其假期调整和拖欠工资。这些雇主特定的日期和规则不适用于本发明的日历。在将下一张收据视为可支出之前对其进行分配列出下一个发薪日之前到期的账单，包括自动转账和不定期承诺。将已注明日期的清单与已经可用的现金进行比较。三个发薪日的月份可能会提供空间来建立期初缓冲或为另一个目标提供资金，但仍需要保留下个月的义务。将真正意外的成本与已知的时间要求分开。这里的开仓金额仅包括模拟账单和每日津贴。它不是完整的紧急储备金，不包括年度保险费、税款分期付款、利息、服务费或非上市购买。该模型将账单固定为从一到二十八的一天，因此每个月都存在每个选定的日期。除了固定的 2027 年日历之外，它没有工作日调整、闰年逻辑或自动转入另一年。在采用时间表之前，将分组的账单替换为实际到期日，并验证收据是否已结算并在需要时可用。

05230565656be78d45cc2467b94e069bfd602e57.src: An emergency reserve is a repeating cash-flow process. A later contribution can rebuild the balance, but it cannot fund a bill that was already due. Using the reserve changes the next planning decision A reserve can do its job successfully and still leave a household exposed afterward. Paying an urgent bill reduces the cash available for the next one. The useful follow-up is not just whether the original target was sensible; it is how much remains, how quickly it can be rebuilt and what happens if another need arrives sooner. FCAC distinguishes unexpected expenses from occasional expenses that can be planned in the ordinary budget. This article concentrates on rebuilding after an unexpected use. Recurring annual bills belong in a separate calendar so they do not repeatedly consume money intended for surprises. The two bills in the tool are deliberately hypothetical. Their amounts and dates do not describe observed Canadian household losses, an insurance forecast or the chance of a second event. The scenario makes a timing problem visible before a more detailed plan is built. Check the money available when the bill arrives The ledger begins with the selected reserve and runs for 24 months. At the start of a bill month, the unexpected expense arrives before the next contribution. The bill can use only the reserve cash already present. At month-end, the affordable contribution rebuilds the reserve toward the selected target. For example, if CAD 500 remains when a CAD 1,000 bill arrives, the ledger funds CAD 500 and records CAD 500 as unmet. A CAD 400 deposit later that month improves the ending reserve. It does not make the earlier CAD 500 gap disappear. This is why the chart shows both cash after bills and cash after the contribution. The account is never allowed to become negative. A shortfall is recorded outside it, without assuming an overdraft, credit-card balance, delayed payment or help from another person. Each of those would require its own terms and cash-flow consequences. Rebuilding is limited by both the budget and the target The entered monthly contribution is money available after ordinary commitments. The model transfers only what is needed to reach the target, up to that contribution. Once the target is reached, further transfers pause until another bill reduces the reserve. Money not transferred stays outside this ledger. This distinction matters when comparing the contribution setting with actual deposits. A CAD 400 setting over 24 months does not necessarily create CAD 9,600 of deposits. Some months may need less, and some may need none. The waterfall uses the actual transferred amounts to reconcile starting cash, funded bills and ending cash. If starting cash is already above the target, the model retains it. It does not force a withdrawal merely to match the chosen line. The target is an assumption for rebuilding, not a maximum balance, an assessed personal reserve requirement or an account contribution limit. The second bill tests the recovery period Read the matrix across one monthly-saving row. Moving the second bill later may allow more rebuilding before it arrives. If the reserve reaches its target first, waiting longer adds no further reserve under this rule. A target smaller than a later bill can therefore leave a gap even after a long recovery period. Read down one date column to compare affordable contribution amounts. Faster rebuilding can reduce exposure, but only if the household can actually make those transfers. Raising a number in the tool does not create surplus in the ordinary budget. If both bills share a month, they are combined before that month’s deposit. Changing dates can also place the second labelled bill before the first. The model follows chronological cash movements rather than assuming the labels establish an order. Every matrix cell reports total unmet bills at their actual modeled due dates. Track the balance and the unresolved need separately The recovery metric counts months from the last positive bill until the reserve is at or above target at a month-end. Zero means it reaches the target in that same month, or is already there when there are no positive bills. NR means the target is not reached within the 24-month window; it is not a forecast of permanent failure. A restored reserve does not prove every bill was funded. The headline shortfall remains visible even after later contributions rebuild the account. Before treating the scenario as workable, identify how an earlier gap would be paid and whether that would create repayments that reduce future saving. A practical review records the remaining reserve, the next affordable transfer, known upcoming bills and any unresolved expense. Add separately confirmed reimbursements only when their timing is known. Use the insurance-reimbursement guide for that extension, and revisit the target when essential spending or household responsibilities change.
05230565656be78d45cc2467b94e069bfd602e57.zh: 紧急储备是一个重复的现金流过程。稍后的捐款可以重建余额，但无法为已到期的账单提供资金。使用保护区会改变下一个规划决策 保护区可以成功地完成其工作，但之后仍然会让家庭暴露在风险之中。支付紧急账单会减少下一笔账单的可用现金。有用的后续行动不仅在于最初的目标是否合理，还在于最初的目标是否合理。问题在于还剩下多少，重建的速度有多快，以及如果另一个需求更早到来会发生什么。 FCAC 将意外费用与可在普通预算中计划的偶发费用区分开来。本文重点讨论意外使用后的重建。经常性的年度账单属于单独的日历，因此它们不会重复消耗用于意外的资金。该工具中的两个法案是故意假设的。它们的金额和日期并不描述观察到的加拿大家庭损失、保险预测或发生第二次事件的可能性。在制定更详细的计划之前，该场景使时间问题变得显而易见。帐单到达时检查可用资金 分类账从选定的储备金开始，运行 24 个月。在帐单月份开始时，意外费用会在下一次供款之前到达。该账单只能使用现有的储备现金。月底，负担得起的捐款将按照选定的目标重建储备。例如，如果在收到 1,000 加元的账单时剩余 500 加元，则分类账会为 500 加元提供资金，并将 500 加元记录为未满足。当月晚些时候存入 400 加元可以提高期末准备金。它并没有让之前 500 加元的差距消失。这就是为什么图表显示账单后的现金和捐款后的现金。账户永远不允许变成负数。短缺记录在其外部，不假设透支、信用卡余额、延迟付款或他人的帮助。每一项都需要其自己的条款和现金流后果。重建受到预算和目标的限制 输入的每月捐款是普通承诺后可用的资金。该模型仅传输达到目标所需的内容，直至该贡献。一旦达到目标，进一步的转账就会暂停，直到另一项法案减少准备金。未转移的资金保留在该分类账之外。在将供款设置与实际存款进行比较时，这种区别很重要。 24 个月内 400 加元的存款不一定能产生 9,600 加元的存款。有些月份可能需要更少，有些月份可能不需要。瀑布使用实际转移金额来调节起始现金、融资账单和期末现金。如果起始现金已经高于目标，该模型将保留它。它不会仅仅为了匹配所选线路而强制提款。该目标是重建的假设，而不是最高余额、评估的个人准备金要求或账户缴款限额。第二个账单测试恢复期 读取每月储蓄行中的矩阵。推迟第二项法案可能会在它到来之前进行更多的重建。如果储备首先达到目标，则根据此规则等待更长的时间不会增加更多储备。因此，即使在经过很长的恢复期之后，比后来的法案更小的目标也可能会留下差距。阅读日期栏以比较负担得起的捐款金额。更快的重建可以减少风险，但前提是家庭能够真正进行这些转移。提高工具中的数字不会在普通预算中产生盈余。如果两个账单共用一个月，则在该月的存款之前合并。更改日期还可以将第二个贴有标签的账单放在第一个账单之前。该模型遵循时间顺序的现金流动，而不是假设标签建立了顺序。每个矩阵单元都会报告实际建模到期日的未满足账单总额。分别跟踪余额和未解决的需求 恢复指标计算从最后一次正账单到储备金达到或高于月末目标的月份。零意味着当月达到目标，或者在没有正账单时已经达到目标。 NR表示24个月窗口内未达到目标；这并不是永久性失败的预测。恢复储备金并不能证明每项账单都得到了资助。即使在后来的捐款重建账户之后，总体缺口仍然显而易见。在将该方案视为可行之前，请确定如何支付早期的缺口以及这是否会产生减少未来储蓄的还款。实际审查记录剩余准备金、下一次负担得起的转移、已知的即将发生的账单以及任何未解决的费用。仅在已知时间时添加单独确认的报销。使用延期的保险报销指南，并在基本支出或家庭责任发生变化时重新审视目标。

3a139f13bbab7e3fbae410c00ed3bab462e6861b.src: A maturity can release both capital and interest. The planning question is whether each cash need arrives after enough money becomes accessible. Read the payment and access terms before building a ladder The FCAC’s GIC disclosure guide identifies contract details that matter: principal repayment, interest payment, early access and automatic reinvestment. A quoted rate alone does not specify when money reaches a spending account. This illustration buys five equal non-cashable amounts at the start, with original terms of one, two, three, four and five years. Every term uses the same hypothetical 4% effective annual rate, compounded annually. Principal and accumulated interest are paid together at maturity. Those are selected contract assumptions, not current product offers. An actual ladder can have different rates, interest-payment frequencies, redemption provisions and account restrictions. Confirm the issuer’s agreement and maturity instructions before relying on a release date. Separate interest earned from the capital coming back CAD 50,000 is split into five CAD 10,000 rungs. The first releases CAD 10,400 after one year: CAD 10,000 of principal and CAD 400 of interest. The second releases CAD 10,816 after two years, including CAD 816 of interest. The fifth rung releases about CAD 12,166.53 after five years. Across all five original maturities, proceeds total about CAD 56,329.75. Only about CAD 6,329.75 is interest. The remaining CAD 50,000 is the original capital becoming accessible again. Calling the full maturity stream “income” would overstate the economic gain. The stacked bars keep the two parts visible. Each rung compounds for its own term; the first rung is not assumed to continue earning after it matures. Put each bill after the maturity that is meant to fund it The default also holds CAD 5,000 in a separate liquid reserve. It earns zero in this example. The household needs CAD 12,000 at each of five year-ends, after that year’s maturity proceeds arrive. After the first release and bill, liquid cash is CAD 3,400. After year two it is CAD 2,216. It reaches its lowest year-end point at about CAD 1,163.23 in year four, then ends year five at about CAD 1,329.75. The waterfall checks the endpoint: starting reserve plus returned principal plus interest, less CAD 60,000 of bills. The default reserve covers this particular annual calendar. It does not establish that a monthly living-expense schedule would remain funded between the shown dates. Compare access timing even when the final proceeds are larger The comparison puts the same CAD 50,000 into one five-year non-cashable term at the same rate. The starting reserve and five annual bills remain identical. This term releases no principal or interest before year five. After the fourth annual bill, its unfunded cash position is negative CAD 43,000. The large fifth-year maturity cannot travel backward to meet those earlier commitments. The displayed additional starting cash measures that timing gap. Because all capital compounds for five years in the single term, its final interest is larger under these assumptions. The chart therefore makes both facts visible: more late interest and less early access can occur together. No new borrowing, early redemption or additional cash injection is hidden in either path. Treat renewal as a new cash-allocation decision This is a run-off ladder: matured money remains cash or pays bills. Nothing automatically rolls into a new five-year term. A renewing ladder would need a different ledger, including the amount retained for spending and the amount locked away again. The matrix changes annual needs and starting reserves while keeping the invested capital and rate selected. Its cells show extra starting cash needed at the deepest modeled shortfall, not simply the final deficit. Larger reserves belong outside the initial GIC purchases. For a real plan, list the exact maturity dates, expected proceeds, account access conditions and spending deadlines. Review renewal instructions before each maturity. Taxes, deposit-insurance capacity and registered-account withdrawal rules are separate checks; none is inferred from this hypothetical cash schedule.
3a139f13bbab7e3fbae410c00ed3bab462e6861b.zh: 到期可以释放本金和利息。规划问题是每次现金需求是否在足够的资金到位后才到达。在构建阶梯之前阅读付款和访问条款 FCAC 的 GIC 披露指南确定了重要的合同细节：本金偿还、利息支付、早期访问和自动再投资。单独的报价并不能说明资金何时到达支出账户。该插图一开始就购买了五笔等额的不可兑现金额，原始期限为一年、两年、三年、四年和五年。每个期限都使用相同的假设有效年利率 4%，每年复利。本金和累计利息到期时一起支付。这些是选定的合同假设，而不是当前的产品报价。实际的阶梯可以有不同的利率、利息支付频率、赎回条款和账户限制。在依赖发行日期之前，请确认发行人的协议和到期指示。从返还的 50,000 加元资本中赚取的单独利息分为五个 10,000 加元的梯级。第一个在一年后释放 10,400 加元：本金 10,000 加元，利息 400 加元。第二次在两年后释放 10,816 加元，其中包括利息 816 加元。五年后，第五级释放约 12,166.53 加元。所有五个原始到期日的收益总额约为 56,329.75 加元。利息大约只有 6,329.75 加元。剩下的5万加元是可以再次使用的原始资金。将完整的到期流称为“收入”会夸大经济收益。堆叠的条形使两个部分保持可见。每个梯级都有其自己的术语；第一级在成熟后不会继续盈利。每张票据到期后都将为其提供资金。违约金还以单独的流动储备金形式持有 5,000 加元。在这个例子中它的收益为零。在当年的到期收益到达后，该家庭每年需要 12,000 加元。首次发放和账单后，流动现金为 3,400 加元。第二年后为 2,216 加元。第四年达到最低年终点，约为 1,163.23 加元，第五年结束时约为 1,329.75 加元。瀑布检查端点：起始准备金加上返还的本金和利息，减去 60,000 加元的票据。默认储备金涵盖该特定年度日历。它并没有规定每月生活费用表在所示日期之间仍将得到资助。即使最终收益更大，也可以比较访问时间 该比较将相同的 50,000 加元以相同的利率纳入一个五年期不可兑现期限。起始准备金和五份年度账单保持不变。该期限在第五年之前不释放本金或利息。第四次年度账单后，其无资金的现金头寸为负 43,000 加元。第五年的大额到期日无法倒退以兑现先前的承诺。显示的额外起始现金衡量了时间差距。由于所有资本在单一期限内复合五年，因此在这些假设下其最终利息更大。因此，该图表使这两个事实变得可见：更多的后期兴趣和更少的早期访问可以同时发生。这两条途径都没有隐藏新的借款、提前赎回或额外的现金注入。将续约视为新的现金分配决策 这是一个径流阶梯：到期的资金仍然是现金或支付账单。没有什么会自动进入新的五年任期。更新的阶梯需要不同的分类账，包括保留用于支出的金额和再次锁定的金额。该矩阵改变年度需求和起始储备，同时保持选定的投资资本和利率。它的单元格显示了在最严重的模型短缺情况下所需的额外起始现金，而不仅仅是最终的赤字。较大的储备不属于初始 GIC 购买的范围。对于真正的计划，请列出确切的到期日、预期收益、帐户访问条件和支出期限。在每次到期前查看续订说明。税收、存款保险能力和注册账户取款规则是单独检查的；从这个假设的现金计划中没有推断出任何内容。

01f6567c57ef3f8c96e7a7170a5ea2046cad0766.src: Unused grant room is only one constraint. Contributions, annual grant capacity, earlier contribution history and the calendar-year deadline must work together. Distinguish a contribution from a basic grant The Government of Canada’s CESG guide explains the basic 20% grant, ordinary annual capacity of CAD 500 and catch-up capacity of up to CAD 1,000 when unused room exists. The lifetime CESG limit is CAD 7,200 per beneficiary, including any additional CESG. The fixed reference chart compares grant dollars on CAD 1,000, CAD 2,500 and CAD 5,000 of contributions. With sufficient unused room and all other conditions met, CAD 5,000 can attract CAD 1,000 of basic CESG. Without earlier unused room, that larger contribution does not double the ordinary CAD 500 grant. The grant is separate from the family’s contribution and is not an investment return. This model excludes additional CESG, the Canada Learning Bond and provincial benefits. It assumes basic eligibility and Canadian residence throughout the relevant calendar years. Make the simplified earlier history explicit The default begins in the calendar year the beneficiary turns thirteen. Four earlier calendar years each received CAD 2,500 of contributions. The scenario places those funded years at the beginning of the child’s calendar-year history, with no withdrawals or other RESP transactions. That creates CAD 10,000 of prior family contributions and CAD 2,000 of prior basic CESG. Thirteen prior eligible calendar years accumulated CAD 6,500 of basic room, so CAD 4,500 remains unused before the first new year. The earlier-years control is capped at the number of prior calendar years. This is a deliberately constructed history, not an account reconstruction. Real records may include different amounts, residency periods, other subscribers, additional grants or grant repayments, requiring a promoter’s reconciliation. Apply the annual and lifetime limits in sequence The default requests CAD 5,000 each year from the year turning thirteen through the year turning seventeen. Each year first adds CAD 500 of new basic room, then applies that year’s contribution and the grant constraints. The five new grants are CAD 1,000 each, producing CAD 5,000 of new basic CESG. Prior plus new grants total CAD 7,000, leaving CAD 200 of lifetime grant headroom. Family contributions total CAD 35,000, including the earlier CAD 10,000. The CRA’s contribution-limit page sets a separate CAD 50,000 lifetime contribution ceiling across all RESPs for the beneficiary. Grants do not consume that contribution ceiling. This tool leaves requests above remaining contribution capacity unplaced and does not create an excess contribution. Check the special history condition before ages sixteen and seventeen The government’s grant guide requires an earlier contribution history for CESG at ages sixteen and seventeen: by the end of the calendar year turning fifteen, either CAD 2,000 must have been contributed and not withdrawn, or at least CAD 100 in each of four years. The model tracks both tests. Its earlier CAD 2,500 years satisfy the first condition whenever at least one exists. Without earlier funded years, new contributions through the year turning fifteen can establish a qualifying history. For example, change the start age to sixteen and earlier funded years to zero. A new contribution is still placed within the model’s RESP capacity, but no basic CESG is credited: a current contribution cannot repair a missed pre-sixteen condition. The tool assumes no withdrawals that would undo that history. Read unused room alongside the remaining calendar Unused basic room in the default remains CAD 2,000 at the end, even though lifetime grant headroom is only CAD 200. These numbers describe different constraints. Neither permits a new CESG after the end of the calendar year turning seventeen. The matrix waits zero to three years before starting the annual requests. A two-year delay leaves only the years turning fifteen, sixteen and seventeen in the default history. Even a larger annual request cannot bypass the annual grant ceiling. Compare the contribution budget with verified records and remaining eligible years. No return, tax deduction, education withdrawal or payment-processing lag is included. The charts explain timing and limits; they do not confirm an actual grant award or recommend using education savings ahead of other household needs.
01f6567c57ef3f8c96e7a7170a5ea2046cad0766.zh: 未使用的拨款空间只是限制之一。捐款、年度拨款能力、早期捐款历史和日历年截止日期必须一起发挥作用。区分捐款与基本补助金 加拿大政府的 CESG 指南解释了 20% 的基本补助金、通常每年 500 加元的容量以及在存在未使用房间时最多 1,000 加元的追赶能力。每个受益人的终身 CESG 限额为 7,200 加元，包括任何额外的 CESG。固定参考图表比较了 1,000 加元、2,500 加元和 5,000 加元捐款的赠款金额。如果有足够的未使用空间并满足所有其他条件，5,000加元可以吸引1,000加元的基本CESG。如果没有之前未使用的房间，这笔更大的捐款不会是普通 500 加元补助金的两倍。该补助金与家庭捐款分开，不是投资回报。该模型不包括额外的 CESG、加拿大学习债券和省级福利。它假定在​​相关日历年中具有基本资格和加拿大居住权。使简化的早期历史变得明确 默认从受益人年满十三岁的日历年开始。前四个日历年每年收到 2,500 加元的捐款。该方案将这些资助年份置于孩子日历年历史的开始，没有提款或其他 RESP 交易。这将产生 10,000 加元的先前家庭捐款和 2,000 加元的先前基本 CESG。之前的 13 个符合资格的日历年累计了 6,500 加元的基本客房，因此在第一个新年之前还有 4,500 加元未使用。较早年份的控制上限为之前日历年的数量。这是刻意构建的历史，而不是重建的账目。真实记录可能包括不同的金额、居住期限、其他订阅者、额外赠款或赠款偿还，需要发起人进行核对。按顺序应用年度和终生限额 默认要求从 13 岁到 17 岁每年 5,000 加元。每年首先增加 500 加元的新基本房，然后应用当年的捐款和补助金限制。五项新赠款每项金额为 1,000 加元，产生 5,000 加元的新基本 CESG。先前的拨款加上新的拨款总计 7,000 加元，终身拨款余量为 200 加元。家庭捐款总额为 35,000 加元，其中包括之前的 10,000 加元。 CRA 的缴款限额页面为受益人的所有 RESP 单独设置了 50,000 加元的终生缴款上限。赠款不消耗该捐款上限。该工具将超出剩余贡献能力的请求保留为未放置状态，并且不会产生超额贡献。检查 16 岁和 17 岁之前的特殊历史条件 政府的补助金指南要求提供 16 岁和 17 岁的早期 CESG 缴款历史：到 15 岁的日历年年底，必须已缴款 2,000 加元且不得提取，或者每四年至少缴款 100 加元。该模型跟踪这两个测试。只要至少有一个存在，其早先的 2,500 加元就满足第一个条件。如果没有早期的资助年份，十五岁那年的新捐款可以建立合格的历史。例如，将开始年龄更改为十六岁，将更早的资助年份更改为零。新的贡献仍然放在模型的 RESP 容量内，但没有记入基本的 CESG：当前的贡献无法修复错过的 16 岁之前的情况。该工具假设没有任何提款会撤销该历史记录。将未使用的空间与剩余日历一起读取。默认情况下，未使用的基本空间最终仍为 2,000 加元，尽管终身拨款净空仅为 200 加元。这些数字描述了不同的限制。两者都不允许在年满十七岁的日历年结束后建立新的 CESG。该矩阵在开始年度请求之前会等待零到三年。延迟两年后，默认历史记录中只剩下十五岁、十六岁和十七岁的年份。即使是更大的年度申请也不能绕过年度拨款上限。将缴款预算与经过验证的记录和剩余的合格年份进行比较。不包括退货、减税、教育退学或付款处理延迟。图表解释了时间和限制；他们没有确认实际的补助金，也没有建议在其他家庭需求之前使用教育储蓄。

009961559a458ea935f57e0e0470580c8764573c.src: Compare all payment dates together. A small first instalment changes when cash leaves; it does not reduce the purchase price or remove the later commitments. Start with the actual payment agreement The FCAC’s buy-now-pay-later guide explains that these arrangements finance a purchase with credit and can use different payment models. A promotional zero rate does not establish that every possible charge is zero. This example deliberately uses a narrow contract assumption: four equal payments, the first at purchase and the next three every two weeks. There is no interest, administration charge or late fee in the calculation. Those are hypothetical terms, not a description of every provider. Confirm the amount, frequency, number of payments and fees in a real agreement. The model does not approve credit or decide how a provider handles missed payments, returns, refunds or a disputed purchase. A negative cash point means the planned payment needs another source. Combine the plans before judging affordability Plan A purchases CAD 800 at week zero. Plan B purchases CAD 600 at week two, and plan C purchases CAD 400 at week four. The two-week gap is editable; all three purchases are assumed to go ahead. Each plan divides its amount into quarters. A requires CAD 200 per payment, B CAD 150 and C CAD 100. Total purchases are CAD 1,800. The obligation bars show the first quarter and the remaining three quarters for each purchase. The calendar then adds payments due in the same week. Weeks four and six each require CAD 450 across the three plans. Looking at A’s CAD 200 or C’s CAD 100 alone would miss that combined demand. No full purchase amount is also deducted beside the instalments. Put the cash resource after the payment that precedes it The default allocates CAD 300 of starting cash and CAD 100 of weekly surplus after all other commitments. Surplus arrives at the end of weeks one through twelve; no additional resource is inserted at time zero. After A’s immediate first payment, cash is CAD 100. In week two, CAD 350 of payments leave before the week-end surplus, putting cash at negative CAD 150. The same week ends at negative CAD 50 after the CAD 100 resource arrives. The two lines distinguish those observation points. The schedule does not assume an automatic overdraft, a new loan or a late-payment arrangement. It records the amount that must be funded if each stated payment is to occur on time. Measure the deepest need rather than the final balance alone The lowest point is negative CAD 700 after week-eight payments, before that week’s surplus. The schedule therefore needs CAD 1,000 at the start, or CAD 700 more than the entered cash. By the end of week twelve, all CAD 1,800 of purchases have been paid and twelve CAD 100 surplus amounts have arrived. Starting cash plus resources less payments is CAD 300 + CAD 1,200 − CAD 1,800, or negative CAD 300. That final deficit is smaller than the earlier funding need. Later resources do not remove a past shortfall. If cash is added to bridge it, record that source and any repayment obligation separately. No borrowing cost or missed-payment fee is hidden in these totals. Test the purchase spacing without treating delay as a discount The matrix changes the gap between starting plans and the weekly surplus. Starting balances and purchase amounts stay selected. Every case runs through week twelve and receives exactly twelve weekly surplus amounts. Spacing can change the peak and the starting buffer needed even though total purchases remain CAD 1,800. It does not change the price, guarantee approval or make another commitment affordable automatically. Equal quarters also use unrounded arithmetic; a real issuer may allocate the final cents differently. Before another purchase, add its instalments to the existing dated list. Include other bills in the underlying budget before deciding what surplus remains for this calendar. If the combined schedule is unfunded, changing payment labels alone does not close the cash gap.
009961559a458ea935f57e0e0470580c8764573c.zh: 将所有付款日期放在一起比较。当现金离开时，第一笔分期付款的一小部分会发生变化；它不会降低购买价格或取消后续承诺。从实际付款协议开始 FCAC 的“先买后付款”指南解释说，这些安排通过信贷为购买提供资金，并且可以使用不同的付款模式。促销零费率并不意味着所有可能的费用都是零。这个例子故意使用了一个狭隘的合同假设：四次等额付款，第一次是在购买时付款，接下来的每两周付款三次。计算中不包含利息、管理费或滞纳金。这些是假设术语，并非对每个提供商的描述。在真实协议中确认金额、频率、付款次数和费用。该模型不批准信用或决定提供商如何处理错过的付款、退货、退款或有争议的购买。现金点为负数意味着计划的付款需要其他来源。在判断负担能力之前合并计划 A 计划在第 0 周购买 800 加元。计划 B 在第二周购买 600 加元，计划 C 在第四周购买 400 加元。两周的间隔是可以编辑的；假设所有三项购买都会继续进行。每个计划将其金额分为几个季度。 A 要求每次付款 200 加元，B 要求每次付款 150 加元，C 要求每次付款 100 加元。总购买量为 1,800 加元。义务栏显示每次购买的第一季度和剩余三个季度。然后，日历会添加同一周到期的付款。第四周和第六周的三个计划各需要 450 加元。仅考虑 A 的 200 加元或 C 的 100 加元会忽略这一综合需求。除分期付款外，也不会扣除全额购买金额。将现金资源放在之前的付款之后。默认情况下会在所有其他承诺之后分配 300 加元的起始现金和 100 加元的每周盈余。盈余在第一至十二周结束时到达；在时间零处没有插入额外的资源。 A 立即完成第一笔付款后，现金为 100 加元。第二周，在周末盈余之前还剩下 350 加元的付款，使现金为负 150 加元。在 100 加元资源到达后，同一周结束时为负 50 加元。两条线区分了这些观察点。该时间表不假设自动透支、新贷款或逾期付款安排。它记录了每笔规定的付款按时发生时必须提供的金额。衡量最深层次的需求，而不仅仅是最终余额 第八周付款后、该周盈余之前的最低点为负 700 加元。因此，该计划在开始时需要 1,000 加元，或者比输入的现金多 700 加元。到第 12 周结束时，所有 1,800 加元的采购均已支付，并且 12 个 100 加元的剩余金额已到达。起始现金加上资源减去付款为 300 加元 + 1,200 加元 - 1,800 加元，或负 300 加元。最终赤字小于之前的资金需求。后来的资源并不能消除过去的短缺。如果添加现金来弥补，请单独记录该来源和任何还款义务。这些总额中没有隐藏借贷成本或逾期付款费用。测试购买间隔，而不将延迟视为折扣 该矩阵改变了起始计划和每周盈余之间的差距。起始余额和购买金额保持选定状态。每个案件都会持续第十二周，并收到恰好十二周的盈余金额。即使总购买量仍为 1,800 加元，间隔也可以改变所需的峰值和起始缓冲区。它不会自动改变价格、保证批准或做出另一项负担得起的承诺。等分也使用不四舍五入的算术；真正的发行人可能会以不同的方式分配最终的美分。在进行另一次购买之前，将其分期付款添加到现有的日期列表中。在决定本日历剩余的盈余之前，将其他账单纳入基础预算中。如果合并后的计划没有资金支持，仅更改付款标签并不能弥补现金缺口。

03e94f477b3d21be25681448f19a2703b83744c9.src: New contributions can move weights toward a chosen target without selling. Whether they reach it depends on the existing holdings, the target and the cash available. Separate maintaining a chosen mix from selecting the right mix Rebalancing asks how to bring holdings toward an existing allocation. It does not, by itself, decide which allocation fits a person’s goals, risk tolerance, liquidity needs or time horizon. The SEC’s Investor.gov rebalancing explanation describes selling overweight holdings, buying underweight holdings and redirecting ongoing contributions as different approaches. It also notes that transaction fees and tax consequences can matter. This guide isolates the new-contribution arithmetic with two abstract asset buckets. A and B are not named securities or recommended investments. The target is a user assumption, prices remain fixed, and no sale, tax, trading cost or return is calculated. Compare current dollars with a target at the same new total The starting values are CAD 65,000 in A and CAD 35,000 in B, totaling CAD 100,000. A therefore represents 65%. The chosen hypothetical target is 60% A and 40% B. Adding CAD 5,000 raises the total to CAD 105,000. At that new total, an exact target reference would hold CAD 63,000 in A and CAD 42,000 in B. Existing A is already above CAD 63,000, so buying more A cannot close the gap. The buy-only allocation puts all CAD 5,000 into B. Holdings become CAD 65,000 and CAD 40,000, and A’s share falls to about 61.90%. That improves alignment without fully restoring the 60% target. The target reference bar is not an executed trade. Use the contribution once and avoid an implicit sale The desired new purchase of A is target A share × total after contributing − current A value . The model caps that amount between zero and the available contribution. Any remaining new money buys B. A negative desired amount does not turn into an automatic sale. Instead, A receives zero new money. If the desired amount exceeds all available cash, the entire contribution goes to A and B receives none. Those limits keep existing holdings intact and ensure purchases sum to the contribution. When enough cash is available, the model can split it between both buckets to reach the target under its fixed-price, fractional-value assumptions. Calculate the contribution threshold from the overweight holding When A is overweight, adding only B reaches the target when current A ÷ (current total + new cash) = target A share . Solving gives new cash of current A divided by target share, less current total. In the example, CAD 65,000 ÷ 60% − CAD 100,000 is CAD 8,333.333… . The displayed cash threshold rounds upward to CAD 8,333.34. This is total new cash from the starting snapshot: the entered CAD 5,000 is part of it, leaving CAD 3,333.34 beyond that contribution. Practical order sizes, spreads and minimum purchases can still prevent an exact real trade. If B is overweight, the corresponding calculation uses current B and B’s target share. If the portfolio already matches, no corrective cash is needed. An empty portfolio has no defined starting weight; the tool says so, although positive new money can be allocated in the chosen proportions. Read remaining drift without interpreting it as performance The contribution curve changes only new cash while holding current values and target fixed. Its displayed range ends no higher than CAD 200,000, so a large required threshold may lie beyond the plotted range. The matrix varies targets and contribution amounts. It reports absolute allocation gaps in percentage points, not investment returns. For example, 65% versus 60% is a five-percentage-point gap; that is a different calculation from a relative percentage change. Actual markets move while contributions accumulate. Account restrictions, transaction costs, taxes and the suitability of the target require separate review. This illustration does not establish that buy-only rebalancing is preferable to selling, or that either bucket has a better future return. Use it to understand the cash constraint around an independently chosen plan.
03e94f477b3d21be25681448f19a2703b83744c9.zh: 新的贡献可以在不出售的情况下将权重移向选定的目标。他们能否实现这一目标取决于现有持股、目标和可用现金。将维持选定的组合与选择正确的组合分开重新平衡询问如何将持有的资产纳入现有的分配。它本身并不能决定哪种分配适合个人的目标、风险承受能力、流动性需求或时间范围。美国证券交易委员会的 Investor.gov 再平衡解释描述了出售超重持股、买入减持持股以及重新调整持续贡献的不同方法。它还指出，交易费用和税收后果可能很重要。本指南将新贡献算法与两个抽象资产桶隔离开来。 A 和 B 不是指定证券或推荐投资。目标是用户假设，价格保持固定，不计算销售、税收、交易成本或回报。将当前美元与相同新总额的目标进行比较 A 的起始值为 65,000 加元，B 的起始值为 35,000 加元，总计 100,000 加元。因此A代表65%。所选的假设目标是 60% A 和 40% B。加上 5,000 加元，总数将达到 105,000 加元。按照新的总额，准确的目标参考值是 A 为 63,000 加元，B 为 42,000 加元。现有 A 已经高于 63,000 加元，因此购买更多 A 无法缩小差距。只买分配将所有 5,000 加元投入 B. Holdings，变成 65,000 加元和 40,000 加元，A 的份额降至约 61.90%。这改善了一致性，但没有完全恢复 60% 的目标。目标参考柱不是已执行的交易。使用一次出资，避免隐性出售 A 所需的新购买量为目标 A 股 × 出资后总额 − 当前 A 值。该模型将该金额限制在零和可用贡献之间。任何剩余的新资金都会购买 B。负的期望金额不会变成自动销售。相反，A 收到的新资金为零。如果所需金额超过所有可用现金，则全部捐款将归 A 而 B 则一无所获。这些限制使现有持股保持完整，并确保购买金额符合贡献。当有足够的现金可用时，该模型可以将其分配到两个桶中，以达到固定价格、分值假设下的目标。计算增持贡献门槛 当 A 增持时，仅添加 B 即可达到目标，此时 A ÷（当前总额 + 新增现金）= 目标 A 股。求解得出当前 A 的新现金除以目标份额，减去当前总额。在示例中，CAD 65,000 ÷ 60% − CAD 100,000 为 CAD 8,333.333…。显示的现金阈值向上舍入为 8,333.34 加元。这是起始快照中的新现金总额：输入的 5,000 加元是其中的一部分，除此之外还剩下 3,333.34 加元。实际的订单规模、点差和最低购买量仍然可能妨碍准确的真实交易。如果B超重，则相应计算使用当前B和B的目标份额。如果投资组合已经匹配，则不需要纠正现金。空投资组合没有明确的起始权重；该工具是这样说的，尽管可以按选定的比例分配积极的新资金。读取剩余漂移，而不将其解释为绩效贡献曲线仅改变新现金，同时保持当前值和目标固定。其显示范围最终不高于 CAD 200,000，因此所需的较大阈值可能超出绘制的范围。该矩阵的目标和贡献金额各不相同。它以百分点报告绝对分配差距，而不是投资回报。例如，65% 与 60% 相差五个百分点；这是与相对百分比变化不同的计算。实际市场随着贡献的积累而变化。账户限制、交易成本、税收和目标公司的适合性需要单独审查。这个例子并没有证明只买再平衡比卖出更可取，或者任一桶都有更好的未来回报。用它来了解独立选择的计划的现金限制。

e12bfaec9caa4138abd693dbed857a014f305fc8.src: An HBP balance can fall through designated repayments or income inclusions. Only the repayment is money put back into the plan. Begin with a confirmed balance and required repayment year The CRA’s HBP repayment guide explains the annual statement, required repayments and treatment of shortfalls. This illustration starts within a required repayment period, using an already confirmed opening balance and years remaining. The default is CAD 30,000 with fifteen required years left. Its first calendar label is 2031. The tool does not establish a withdrawal’s eligibility, identify a first due year from a withdrawal date or apply special repayment exceptions. The current CRA overview reports extended temporary repayment relief for first withdrawals in 2026–2028. Timing guidance can change, and the detailed repayment page still describes the earlier relief window. Confirm the applicable first due year and statement before entering a real schedule. Divide the opening balance by required years remaining For the first modeled year, CAD 30,000 divided by fifteen produces a CAD 2,000 minimum. In a later year, the calculation uses that year’s opening balance and the years still left in the original repayment period. The selected regular designated contribution is CAD 1,500. An extra CAD 3,000 is designated in the first modeled required year, bringing that year’s repayment to CAD 4,500. The remaining HBP balance becomes CAD 25,500. The next minimum is therefore CAD 25,500 divided by fourteen, or about CAD 1,821.43. Paying extra changes subsequent minima; it does not automatically turn the following required year into a payment holiday. The model uses unrounded arithmetic, while an actual filing should follow the statement amounts. Keep an income inclusion separate from a contribution From the second year onward, the default CAD 1,500 repayment is about CAD 321.43 below the required minimum. That difference becomes an RRSP income inclusion in this simplified schedule and also reduces the recorded HBP balance. It does not put CAD 321.43 into an RRSP. The two cumulative lines therefore track different reductions: money actually contributed and designated, and amounts included in income because they were not repaid. Across all fifteen years, designated repayments total CAD 25,500 and income inclusions total CAD 4,500. Together they discharge the CAD 30,000 opening balance. A final HBP balance of zero therefore does not establish that the original CAD 30,000 was fully restored as retirement savings. Budget tax separately from the amount included in income The tax-budget control applies a hypothetical flat 30% allowance to income inclusions. On the default CAD 4,500 total inclusion, that creates CAD 1,350 of allowance. Repayment cash plus this allowance totals CAD 26,850. The CAD 4,500 inclusion itself is not an additional CAD 4,500 payment to CRA. Actual tax depends on the whole return, rates, deductions, credits and other consequences. This allowance calculates none of those, and is neither withholding nor an actual tax estimate. Designated HBP repayments are not deducted again on the return. They need the appropriate contribution and designation process. An ordinary contribution left undesignated is not assumed to satisfy the HBP minimum here; the input means an amount successfully designated for that year. Compare repayment patterns without equating them to investment outcomes The matrix changes the regular annual repayment and the extra contribution in the first modeled required year. It totals only the assumed tax allowance on resulting inclusions. The opening balance, remaining years and allowance percentage stay selected. A sufficiently large first-year payment can clear the balance early; the tool caps that repayment at the amount outstanding and leaves future modeled repayments at zero. It does not move the unused budget into another investment or treat it as a deductible contribution. Use a separate household budget to decide how much cash can be committed. This schedule excludes investment growth, borrowing costs, transactions before the modeled period, changes in residency and age-related or death-related exceptions. Reconcile the CRA statement, contribution receipts and designation before relying on a real annual amount.
e12bfaec9caa4138abd693dbed857a014f305fc8.zh: HBP 余额可能会因指定还款或收入包含而减少。只有还款才是将资金重新投入到计划中。从确认余额和要求还款年份开始 CRA 的 HBP 还款指南解释了年度报表、要求还款和缺口处理。此示例在规定的还款期内开始，使用已确认的期初余额和剩余年数。默认值为 30,000 加元，还剩 15 年。它的第一个日历标签是 2031 年。该工具不会建立提款资格，也不会识别提款日期的第一个到期年份或应用特殊还款例外情况。目前的 CRA 概览报告延长了 2026 年至 2028 年首次提款的临时还款减免。时间指导可能会发生变化，详细的还款页面仍然描述了早期的救济窗口。在输入实际时间表之前确认适用的第一个到期年份和报表。将期初余额除以所需的剩余年数 对于第一个建模年份，30,000 加元除以 15 加元得出最小值 2,000 加元。在以后的一年中，计算使用当年的期初余额和原还款期限剩余的年份。选定的定期指定捐款为 1,500 加元。在第一个模型要求年份额外指定 3,000 加元，使该年的还款额达到 4,500 加元。剩余的 HBP 余额变为 25,500 加元。因此，下一个最小值是 25,500 加元除以 14，即大约 1,821.43 加元。支付后续最低金额的额外变更；它不会自动将下一个所需年份变成付款假期。该模型使用不四舍五入的算术，而实际归档应遵循报表金额。将收入包含与供款分开 从第二年起，默认还款 1,500 加元比最低要求低约 321.43 加元。该差异将成为此简化表中包含的 RRSP 收入，并且还会减少记录的 HBP 余额。它不会将 321.43 加元纳入 RRSP。因此，这两条累计线跟踪不同的减少额：实际贡献和指定的资金，以及因未偿还而计入收入的金额。在所有 15 年中，指定还款总额为 25,500 加元，收入包含总额为 4,500 加元。他们共同清偿了 30,000 加元的期初余额。因此，最终 HBP 余额为零并不能证明原来的 30,000 加元已完全恢复为退休储蓄。将税收预算与收入中包含的金额分开 税收预算控制对收入包含的内容适用假设的 30% 固定免税额。默认总包含金额为 4,500 加元，这将创建 1,350 加元的津贴。还款现金加上这笔津贴总计 26,850 加元。 4,500 加元的包含本身并不是向 CRA 额外支付 4,500 加元。实际税额取决于整个申报表、税率、扣除额、抵免额和其他后果。该津贴不计算这些，也不是预扣税，也不是实际的税收估算。指定的 HBP 还款不会在申报表中再次扣除。他们需要适当的贡献和指定流程。未指定的普通贡献不被假定满足此处的 HBP 最小值；输入指的是当年成功指定的金额。比较还款模式，而不将其等同于投资成果 该矩阵改变了定期年度还款和第一个建模所需年份的额外缴款。它仅合计所产生的内含物的假设税收减免。期初余额、剩余年限和津贴百分比保持选定状态。足够大的首年付款可以提前结清余额；该工具将还款上限限制为未偿还金额，并将未来模型还款额保持为零。它不会将未使用的预算转移到另一项投资中或将其视为可扣除的捐款。使用单独的家庭预算来决定可以投入多少现金。该表不包括投资增长、借贷成本、建模期间之前的交易、居住地的变化以及与年龄相关或与死亡相关的例外情况。在依赖实际年度金额之前，请核对 CRA 报表、缴款收据和指定。

40ac34366b62590fdba799ecc92cdb0aaf1a150e.src: Define the baseline and fund the upfront cost first. Then test the savings, maintenance and useful operating horizon rather than treating one payback number as a guarantee. Define the additional project before calculating its payback A financial comparison needs a clear alternative. If equipment already needs replacing, distinguish the cost of the baseline replacement from the additional cost of the more efficient option. Otherwise, an upgrade can be charged for work that would happen anyway. Measure bill savings against that same baseline, rather than crediting the upgrade with savings the baseline replacement would also deliver. The City of Kingston’s home-energy retrofit information describes using an energy evaluation, tailored recommendations and contractor quotes to plan the work. That is assessment context; it does not establish the costs or savings used in this article. The default is CAD 10,000 of additional cash paid now. It assumes no financing and no future rebate receipt. An incentive that might arrive later needs its own eligibility and payment-date review; it should not automatically be treated as cash available before the contractor is paid. Subtract additional maintenance from the estimated bill saving The first-year gross energy-bill saving is hypothetically CAD 1,200. Additional maintenance is CAD 100, producing CAD 1,100 of first-year net cash benefit. These amounts are assumptions rather than a measured result for a particular home or technology. The estimate should describe money avoided, not simply a percentage change in energy use without a price basis. Weather, occupancy, operating settings, the existing equipment and future prices can affect the actual bill difference. In the model, avoided energy spending grows 2% annually because of the selected nominal price-growth assumption. Maintenance stays constant at CAD 100 each year. This isolates the two lines explicitly; it is not a forecast that every project cost or energy tariff follows the same rate. Read cash recovery at the assumed payment dates Both project cost and timing matter. The cumulative cash curve begins at negative CAD 10,000, then adds each year’s net benefit at year-end. No monthly receipt is inserted between those annual points. If the first-year CAD 1,100 benefit stayed constant, cost divided by that benefit would give about 9.09 years of simple payback. Under the selected growth assumption, the modeled annual cash endpoints first recover the cost in year nine. At the end of fifteen years, cumulative undiscounted cash benefit after the initial cost is CAD 9,252.10. That is a scenario total, not a bank balance guaranteed by the upgrade. The model assumes the benefits continue for all selected years, with no new equipment replacement during the horizon. Use discounted value for a different time-value question A dollar saved much later is not the same cash resource as a dollar available now. The discounted curve divides each nominal annual cash flow by (1 + nominal discount rate) year before adding it to the upfront cost. At the hypothetical 4% discount rate, the discounted cumulative curve first reaches zero in year eleven, and the fifteen-year net present value is CAD 4,049.39. The present-value waterfall separately shows avoided bills and maintenance rather than hiding both in one net line. Positive NPV means the modeled benefits exceed costs after discounting at that selected rate. It does not mean the project pays a guaranteed 4% investment return, and NPV is not an internal rate of return. Cash payback and discounted value answer related but different questions. Stress the savings estimate and costs before relying on the result The matrix changes upfront cost and the proportion of the estimated gross bill saving that materializes. Maintenance, price growth, discount rate and operating years remain selected. A lower saving can materially change the result even if the installation price is unchanged. Reduce the horizon if the expected operating period is shorter. This tool grants no property resale premium, calculates no carbon benefit and places no dollar value on comfort or health. It also excludes borrowing costs, tax effects and equipment failure. Use assessment evidence and actual quotes to replace the assumptions. Keep the project’s physical suitability and any incentive conditions separate from the financial arithmetic, and fund the upfront payment without relying on savings that only arrive in later years.
40ac34366b62590fdba799ecc92cdb0aaf1a150e.zh: 定义基线并首先为前期成本提供资金。然后测试节省、维护和有用的运营期限，而不是将一个投资回收期数字视为保证。在计算投资回报之前定义额外的项目 财务比较需要一个明确的替代方案。如果设备已经需要更换，请将基准更换的成本与更高效选项的额外成本区分开来。否则，升级可能会因无论如何都会发生的工作而收费。根据相同的基准来衡量节省的账单，而不是将升级与基准替换也能带来的节省归功于升级。金斯顿市的家庭能源改造信息描述了如何使用能源评估、量身定制的建议和承包商报价来规划工作。那就是评估背景；它没有确定本文中使用的成本或节省。默认是现在支付 10,000 加元的额外现金。它假设没有融资，也没有未来的回扣收据。稍后可能出现的激励措施需要对其自身的资格和付款日期进行审查；在向承包商付款之前，不应将其自动视为可用现金。从预计节省的电费中减去额外维护费用 第一年节省的能源费用总额假设为 1,200 加元。额外维护费为 100 加元，第一年净现金收益为 1,100 加元。这些金额是假设，而不是特定家庭或技术的测量结果。估算应该描述避免的资金，而不仅仅是没有价格基础的能源使用百分比变化。天气、入住情况、操作设置、现有设备和未来价格都会影响实际账单差异。在该模型中，由于选定的名义价格增长假设，避免的能源支出每年增长 2%。每年维护费用保持在 100 加元不变。这明确地隔离了两条线；这并不是每个项目成本或能源关税都遵循相同比率的预测。阅读假定付款日期的现金回收情况 项目成本和时间安排都很重要。累积现金曲线从负 10,000 加元开始，然后在年底添加每年的净收益。这些年度点之间不会插入月度收据。如果第一年 1,100 加元的收益保持不变，则成本除以该收益即可得到约 9.09 年的简单投资回收期。在选定的增长假设下，建模的年度现金端点首先在第九年收回成本。十五年后，扣除初始成本后的累计未贴现现金福利为 9,252.10 加元。这是一个情景总计，而不是升级所保证的银行余额。该模型假设收益在所有选定的年份中持续存在，并且在此期间没有新设备更换。使用折扣值解决不同的时间价值问题 很久以后节省的一美元与现在可用的一美元不是同一个现金资源。贴现曲线将每个名义年现金流量除以（1 + 名义贴现率）年，然后将其添加到前期成本中。在假设的 4% 贴现率下，贴现累积曲线在第十一年首先达到零，十五年净现值为 4,049.39 加元。现值瀑布分别显示避免的账单和维护费用，而不是将两者隐藏在一根网线中。正 NPV 意味着按所选利率贴现后，建模收益超过成本。这并不意味着该项目保证支付 4% 的投资回报，NPV 也不是内部回报率。现金回收和折扣价值回答了相关但不同的问题。在依赖结果之前强调节省的估计和成本 该矩阵会改变前期成本以及实现的估计总账单节省的比例。维护、价格增长、折扣率和运营年限仍处于选择状态。即使安装价格不变，较低的节省也会显着改变结果。如果预期运营期较短，则缩短期限。该工具不授予房产转售溢价，不计算碳效益，也不以舒适或健康为美元价值。它还排除了借贷成本、税收影响和设备故障。使用评估证据和实际报价来代替假设。将项目的物理适宜性和任何激励条件与财务算术分开，并为预付款提供资金，而不依赖于仅在以后几年才能实现的节省。

9c18cfda19ce9b8b7e99df40337e1ad9cf5f86a3.src: Compare the same period of household life. Benefit receipts alone omit work income, different spending phases and the money needed before later pay arrives. Keep published EI rules separate from net budget inputs The Government of Canada’s parental-benefit overview lists basic replacement rates of 55% for standard and 33% for extended benefits, subject to weekly caps and eligibility. One parent can receive up to thirty-five standard or sixty-one extended parental-benefit weeks; shared-family maxima differ. The first graphic presents those gross percentages. It does not apply them to the work-pay control. The benefit-amount page explains that insurable earnings and other details determine the actual amount, and that some employers offer top-ups. This is a single-parent cash illustration outside Quebec, excluding maternity weeks and benefit sharing. Confirm option rules before payments begin: the government restricts switching once a parental-benefit payment has been made. The tool neither chooses an option nor tests entitlement. Compare equal time, including the work period after leave Both alternatives run for seventy-eight weeks from the first modeled parental week. That is a comparison window, not a statutory claim deadline or the date of birth. The parent returns to modeled work income immediately after the selected leave weeks. The standard example has CAD 600 of level net weekly leave income for thirty-five weeks, followed by CAD 1,000 of net work income. Extended leave uses CAD 360 for sixty-one weeks, then the same CAD 1,000 work income. Other household net income is CAD 400 every week. These are independent assumptions, potentially including separately checked top-ups in the parent’s leave amount. No gross-to-net conversion, changing top-up, delayed first receipt, Working While on Claim or job guarantee is calculated. Allow spending to change when work resumes The household spends CAD 900 a week during leave and CAD 1,100 after work resumes. The higher working budget can represent an independently estimated combination of care, commuting and other changes; it is not a child-care subsidy calculation. During standard leave, weekly income is CAD 1,000 including other household income, giving a CAD 100 surplus. During extended leave, the corresponding total is CAD 760, leaving a CAD 140 weekly shortfall. After work resumes, both cases have a CAD 300 weekly surplus under the selected budget. Setup cash outflow is CAD 2,000 at time zero, and both cases begin with CAD 5,000. Bills leave at the start of each week; income arrives at week-end. A real partial week or different pay calendar needs a more detailed schedule. Reconcile leave income, work income and spending After all seventy-eight weeks and the final income receipts, standard-plan cash is CAD 19,400 and extended-plan cash is negative CAD 440. The CAD 19,840 difference is not explained by comparing weekly benefits alone. Extended leave produces CAD 960 more net leave-period income in this example, but CAD 26,000 less net work income inside the common window. It also spends CAD 5,200 less because more weeks use the lower leave budget. The waterfall reconciles those three differences. Starting cash, setup and other household income are identical, so they cancel from that comparison. The model does not assign a financial value to family time, wellbeing, career effects or preferences. Those remain part of the broader decision. Measure the cash bridge before the first returning-work pay Extended-plan cash reaches negative CAD 6,640 after week-sixty-two bills, before the first modeled work income. The schedule needs CAD 11,640 of starting cash, or CAD 6,640 beyond the selected reserve. Later work receipts do not erase that earlier need. The cash lines show pre-income points, while headline ending cash includes the last week-end receipt. Negative balances are unfunded needs, not approved borrowing. If actual top-ups stop partway through leave or costs arrive on different dates, replace the level phases with a dated plan. The matrix varies leave spending and other household income for the extended scenario. Work spending, the parent’s net-income assumptions and selected weeks remain fixed. Use it to test cash capacity alongside confirmed program and employer information, rather than treating a modeled result as an EI award or a recommendation about family leave.
9c18cfda19ce9b8b7e99df40337e1ad9cf5f86a3.zh: 比较同一时期的家庭生活。仅福利收据就忽略了工作收入、不同的支出阶段以及后续工资到达之前所需的资金。将已发布的 EI 规则与净预算投入分开加拿大政府的父母福利概述列出了标准福利的基本替代率为 55%，扩展福利的基本替代率为 33%，但须遵守每周上限和资格。一位家长最多可获得三十五周的标准或六十一周的延长育儿福利周；共享家庭的最大值不同。第一张图显示了这些总百分比。它不适用于工作工资控制。福利金额页面解释了可参保收入和其他详细信息决定了实际金额，并且一些雇主提供充值服务。这是魁北克省以外的单亲现金说明，不包括产假周和福利分享。在付款开始之前确认选项规则：一旦支付了父母福利，政府就会限制转换。该工具既不选择选项也不测试权利。比较相同的时间，包括休假后的工作时间，这两种选择都从第一个模拟育儿周开始运行七十八周。这是一个比较窗口，而不是法定的索赔截止日期或出生日期。在选定的休假周后，家长立即返回模型工作收入。标准示例的三十五周每周净休假收入为 600 加元，其次是 1,000 加元的净工作收入。延长休假使用 360 加元 61 周，然后使用同样的 1,000 加元工作收入。其他家庭每周净收入为 400 加元。这些是独立的假设，可能包括单独检查的父母休假金额的补充。不计算总净额转换、更改充值、延迟首次收款、领取工资或工作保证。允许复工后支出发生变化 该家庭在休假期间每周支出 900 加元，复工后每周支出 1,100 加元。较高的工作预算可以代表护理、通勤和其他变化的独立估计组合；这不是儿童保育补贴的计算。标准休假期间，每周收入为 1,000 加元，包括其他家庭收入，有 100 加元的盈余。延长休假期间，相应总额为 760 加元，每周缺口 140 加元。复工后，两个案例在所选预算下每周都有 300 加元的盈余。零时刻的设定现金流出为 2,000 加元，两种情况均以 5,000 加元开始。账单在每周开始时发出；收入在周末到达。真正的部分周或不同的工资日历需要更详细的时间表。核对休假收入、工作收入和支出 在所有 78 周和最终收入收据之后，标准计划现金为 19,400 加元，扩展计划现金为负 440 加元。仅通过比较每周福利无法解释 19,840 加元的差异。在本例中，延长休假会导致休假期间净收入增加 960 加元，但公共窗口内的净工作收入减少 26,000 加元。它还减少了 5,200 加元的支出，因为使用的休假预算减少了更多周数。瀑布调和了这三个差异。起始现金、设置和其他家庭收入是相同的，因此它们从比较中取消。该模型没有为家庭时间、幸福感、职业影响或偏好分配经济价值。这些仍然是更广泛决定的一部分。在第 62 周的账单之后，在第一个模型工作收入之前，测量第一个返回工作工资之前的现金桥梁，扩展计划现金达到负 6,640 加元。该时间表需要 11,640 加元的起始现金，或超出选定储备的 6,640 加元。后来的工作收据并不能消除早期的需求。现金行显示预收入点，而标题结束现金包括上周末的收据。负余额是没有资金支持的需求，而不是批准的借款。如果实际充值在休假期间停止或费用在不同日期到达，请用已注明日期的计划替换级别阶段。该矩阵在扩展情景下改变了休假支出和其他家庭收入。工作支出、父母的净收入假设和选定的周数保持不变。使用它来测试现金能力以及已确认的计划和雇主信息，而不是将建模结果视为 EI 奖励或有关家庭休假的建议。

a32b9e512730f9de22e4f284450c10d6322c638a.src: A fair terminal comparison needs the same ending position. Here the leased car is returned and the purchased car is sold with its remaining loan repaid. Compare a full-term return with a purchase followed by sale A lower monthly lease payment does not settle the total-cost question. The purchase option can leave both an asset and a loan, while the lease contract can require a different ending transaction. The Vehicle Sales Authority of British Columbia’s financing and leasing guide emphasizes understanding the total obligation, taxes, fees and ending conditions. The FCAC’s car-financing overview also separates financing choices from their risks. This model assumes comparable vehicles and a forty-eight-month lease. At that date, the leased car is returned, while the purchased car is sold and its remaining principal repaid. Both choices then leave no vehicle and no purchase-loan balance. Keeping the owned car or buying out the lease would require a different comparison. Trace the purchase price, down payment and loan The hypothetical all-in purchase price is CAD 42,000. A CAD 5,000 down payment leaves CAD 37,000 financed over sixty months at a constant 6% nominal annual rate divided by twelve. The calculated loan payment is approximately CAD 715.31. Additional buyer costs are CAD 50 monthly, making the first recurring commitment about CAD 765.31. Identical operating costs common to both choices are omitted; differences must be entered separately. After forty-eight payments, about CAD 8,311.18 of principal remains. The model’s net sale proceeds before debt repayment are CAD 22,000, leaving roughly CAD 13,689 of terminal equity after that principal is paid. Sale proceeds should already reflect selling and loan-closure charges, without subtracting the principal twice. Reconcile the buy-and-sell cost without adding the price twice The purchase waterfall adds the applied down payment, loan payments within the window, additional running costs and remaining principal paid at sale. It then subtracts the net sale proceeds before debt. The resulting cost is CAD 28,046.24. Down payment plus loan payments plus final principal equals purchase price plus interest, so adding the purchase price again would double-count the financed portion. The down payment is capped at price; a larger requested amount is not treated as spent. Loan payments stop at payoff if the selected loan period is shorter than the lease term. Intermediate amounts are unrounded until display, so an actual quoted payment schedule can differ slightly. Include the full lease obligation and its return charges The lease example pays CAD 2,000 at signing, CAD 550 a month for forty-eight months and CAD 500 of entered return charges. No additional lessee running costs are selected. The full cash cost is CAD 28,900. Signing cash excludes monthly instalments and refundable deposits in this model. If a real quote includes the first instalment at signing, separate it so it is not counted again in the monthly stream. No tax rate or lease financing rate is inferred from the quote. The car is assumed returned with no buyout and no residual-value obligation beyond the entered charges. That is a specific contract assumption. Confirm distance, wear, administration and other obligations; early termination and refundable deposits are outside this comparison. Read the terminal saving alongside the earlier cash commitment Under the defaults, lease cost minus buy-and-sell cost is positive CAD 853.76, so buying and selling has the lower modeled net cost. That result depends on the entered sale proceeds, payment quotes and extra costs. The cumulative cash chart shows why this does not automatically make buying easier to fund. Purchase payments are higher before the final sale credit arrives. If the sale proceeds fall below remaining principal, the shortfall needs other cash at closing; it is not forgiven by selling the car. The matrix varies net resale proceeds and the monthly lease quote. Positive cells mean the lease costs more; negative cells favor it on this arithmetic. The model assigns no resale probability and discounts no cash flow. Review affordability and contract flexibility as well as the full-term total before committing.
a32b9e512730f9de22e4f284450c10d6322c638a.zh: 公平的最终比较需要相同的结束位置。在这里，租赁的汽车被归还，购买的汽车被出售并偿还剩余的贷款。将全额回报与先购买后出售进行比较 较低的每月租赁付款并不能解决总成本问题。购买选项可以同时保留资产和贷款，而租赁合同可能需要不同的结束交易。不列颠哥伦比亚省车辆销售管理局的融资和租赁指南强调了解总义务、税收、费用和结束条件。 FCAC 的汽车融资概述还将融资选择与其风险分开。该模型假设具有可比车辆和四十八个月的租赁期。届时，租赁的汽车将被归还，所购买的汽车将被出售并偿还剩余的本金。这两种选择都不会留下任何车辆，也没有购买贷款余额。保留自有汽车或买断租赁需要进行不同的比较。追踪购买价格、首付和贷款 假设的总购买价格为 42,000 加元。首付 5,000 加元，可在 60 个月内以 6% 的名义年利率除以 12 获得 37,000 加元的融资。计算得出的贷款付款额约为 715.31 加元。额外的买家费用为每月 50 加元，首次定期承诺费用约为 765.31 加元。两种选择共有的相同运营成本被省略；差异必须单独输入。支付四十八次后，本金剩余约 8,311.18 加元。该模型在债务偿还前的净出售收益为 22,000 加元，在支付本金后留下约 13,689 加元的终端权益。销售收入应该已经反映了销售和贷款结清费用，而不需要两次减去本金。协调买卖成本，无需两次增加价格 购买瀑布增加了所申请的首付、窗口内的贷款支付、额外的运行成本和出售时支付的剩余本金。然后减去债务前的净销售收益。由此产生的成本为 28,046.24 加元。首付加上贷款付款加上最终本金等于购买价格加利息，因此再次添加购买价格将重复计算融资部分。首付款以价格为上限；较大的请求金额不会被视为已花费。如果所选的贷款期限短于租赁期限，则贷款付款将在还清时停止。中间金额在显示之前不会四舍五入，因此实际报价的付款计划可能会略有不同。包括全部租赁义务及其返还费用 该租赁示例在签署时支付 2,000 加元，在 48 个月内每月支付 550 加元，并输入 500 加元的返还费用。没有选择额外的承租人运行成本。全部现金费用为 28,900 加元。在此模式中，签署现金不包括每月分期付款和可退还押金。如果实际报价包含签署时的第一期付款，请将其分开，这样就不会再次计入每月流中。从报价中并未推断出税率或租赁融资利率。假定车辆归还时没有买断，也没有超出输入费用的残值义务。这是一个特定的合同假设。确认距离、佩戴、管理和其他义务；提前终止和可退还押金不在此比较范围内。结合之前的现金承诺，阅读码头节省费用 在默认情况下，租赁成本减去买卖成本为正 853.76 加元，因此买卖的模型净成本较低。该结果取决于输入的销售收入、付款报价和额外费用。累积现金图表显示了为什么这不会自动使购买更容易融资。在最终销售信用到达之前，购买付款会更高。如果出售收益低于剩余本金，则在成交时缺口需要其他现金；卖车是不能原谅的。该矩阵会改变净转售收益和每月租赁报价。正电池意味着租赁成本更高；阴性细胞在这个算术上青睐它。该模型不指定转售概率，也不对现金流进行折扣。在做出承诺之前，请先审查负担能力、合同灵活性以及整个期限的总额。

3d54e18ecc23cfb79ce09abdfee1b1aaaec4ceba.src: Identify the eligible deposits, category and actual member institution first. Then include accrued interest when comparing the combined amount with the applicable cap. Use the member and category as the coverage unit CDIC’s coverage overview states that eligible deposits are insured up to CAD 100,000, including principal and interest, in each covered category at a member institution. Eligibility matters: a balance is not insured simply because it appears on a financial account statement. This guide restricts the illustration to deposits held in one name by the same individual across both members. CDIC explains that eligible savings, chequing and term deposits in that category are combined . Opening a second account within the same member and category does not provide a second CAD 100,000 cap. Member A and member B are hypothetical and assumed genuinely distinct. Use the official member list to check the relevant institution and trade name. A branch or brand label alone is not enough evidence for the model’s separate-member assumption. Aggregate the starting balances before testing the limit The example has CAD 60,000 of eligible savings and CAD 30,000 of other eligible one-name deposits at member A. Together they make CAD 90,000, leaving CAD 10,000 of headroom under the illustrated cap. Member B has CAD 50,000 in the same one-name category. Because B is assumed to be a separate CDIC member, its balance is tested against its own cap. The example therefore starts with CAD 140,000 within the two assumed coverage limits. Include all eligible amounts in the same member/category, not just the deposit currently being considered. Starting figures should already reflect interest accrued up to that date. The model grows only subsequent interest; it does not reconstruct missing account records or verify eligibility. Retained interest can take a balance above the cap The default assumes a constant 4% effective annual rate for five years, with all interest retained and compounded. This is a hypothetical rate, not an available offer. There are no new deposits, withdrawals, tax payments or fees. Member A’s CAD 90,000 grows to CAD 109,498.76. Applying the same assumed CAD 100,000 cap leaves CAD 9,498.76 above it. Member B’s CAD 50,000 grows to CAD 60,832.65 and remains below its own cap. Combined projected balances are about CAD 170,331.41, of which CAD 160,832.65 is within the modeled caps. The interest chart shows A starting below the cap and exceeding it by year three under these assumptions. That does not forecast an actual deposit yield or a future change in insurance rules. Treat interest headroom as a sensitivity calculation Under a fixed cap and constant compounded rate, a starting amount that grows exactly to the cap is cap ÷ (1 + annual rate) years . At 4% for five years, that is about CAD 82,192.71 for a CAD 100,000 cap. This is arithmetic for the stated assumptions, not a universal deposit allocation. Actual interest-crediting terms, other eligible deposits, ownership records, accrued amounts and future rules can change the comparison. Money withdrawn to pay tax would also change the balance path, but no such withdrawal is assumed here. The matrix varies the interest assumption and horizon while keeping starting balances and member classification selected. Unused headroom at B is not subtracted from an excess at A. Each member/category is tested separately before the excesses are added. Keep coverage, liquidity and investment risk as separate questions An amount above the modeled cap is not a predicted loss. It is an amount this illustration does not count as insured under its assumptions. CDIC protection concerns eligible deposits if a member fails; it does not make a locked-in deposit accessible whenever a bill arrives. The coverage overview also distinguishes eligible deposits from products such as mutual funds, shares and ETFs. A product’s account wrapper does not replace the need to identify what is held. For a review, record the actual member, ownership category, all eligible balances and accrued interest, then check the payment or maturity dates separately. Other categories and provincial insurance schemes require their own rules; this single-category example does not calculate them.

b9715efea226d26893aa6f3b5c1828ddba5c00db.src: Confirm the income that would actually continue or begin, then put its receipt dates beside the bills. A sustainable ongoing budget can still need an immediate cash bridge. Build an independent survivor income estimate A retirement household’s income after a partner’s death cannot be reconstructed safely by halving the old total or assuming every payment continues. Identify each pension, annuity and other income source, then confirm its treatment and likely net cash amount. The Government of Canada’s CPP survivor-pension page provides a specific example of this caution: a CPP survivor pension combined with a CPP retirement or disability pension is not necessarily the sum of the two separate benefits. This tool calculates no CPP entitlement, employer-plan percentage or tax result. Its ongoing after-death income is an independent input. Use benefit estimates, plan terms and an appropriate tax allowance to establish that amount rather than applying a percentage to the old household’s net income. Estimate survivor expenses separately from income The two-person example has CAD 6,000 of monthly net income and CAD 5,000 of running costs, leaving CAD 1,000. The independently entered survivor figures are CAD 4,300 of ongoing net income and CAD 3,800 of monthly costs, leaving CAD 500. Those expenses are not assumed to halve when the household changes. Housing and other commitments may continue, while some spending changes. Replace the hypothetical budget with a specific list rather than scaling every category by the same percentage. The before-and-after bars describe ongoing monthly amounts only. They exclude transition payments and the temporary receipt gap. A positive CAD 500 ongoing surplus therefore does not establish how much cash is needed at the beginning. Use cash that is confirmed accessible at the start The example has CAD 10,000 of liquid cash available to the survivor and an assumed CAD 8,000 transition outflow at time zero. That leaves CAD 2,000 before the first month’s running bills. This is a cash-availability illustration, not an estate valuation. It determines neither who owns an account nor when an estate distribution, insurance claim or other asset becomes accessible. A later expected receipt should not automatically be entered as cash available now. The full monthly running budget is paid at the start of each month. Income arrives at month-end. Even if there is no additional benefit-processing gap, cash is still needed for the first bills before that income arrives. Put the initially unreceived portion on a dated cash calendar Of the expected CAD 4,300 monthly income, CAD 1,500 is assumed not received in each of the first three full months. The remaining CAD 2,800 arrives each month during that interval. Full ongoing income begins at the end of month four. This is a stress assumption, not a processing standard or a pension calculation. No catch-up arrears payment is inserted automatically. Any confirmed arrears would be a separate dated receipt in a detailed cash plan; their omission here does not determine benefit entitlement. After the month-four bills but before that month’s income, cash reaches negative CAD 4,800. Starting cash required for the selected schedule is CAD 14,800, which is CAD 4,800 more than the entered reserve. The first full receipt arrives after that lowest point. Read the deepest shortage as well as the eventual balance After twenty-four months of the assumed cash flows, the ledger ends at CAD 9,500. That later amount does not pay an earlier unfunded bill. Negative points indicate another source is needed; the chart does not authorize borrowing or assume access to somebody else’s funds. The receipt-gap bars hold ongoing income and costs selected while changing only the initial gap. The matrix varies the survivor’s ongoing net income and monthly budget. The unreceived portion cannot exceed total income, a cash-budget convention rather than a legal benefit rule. Review accessible cash, transition payments, each continuing income source and its expected first receipt. Update the plan when an administrator confirms the amount or timing. The model holds later income and costs constant and stops at the selected horizon; inflation, tax changes, later arrears and investment returns require separate work.
b9715efea226d26893aa6f3b5c1828ddba5c00db.zh: 确认实际将继续或开始的收入，然后将其收据日期放在账单旁边。可持续的持续预算仍然需要立即建立现金桥梁。建立独立的遗属收入估算 退休家庭在伴侣去世后的收入无法通过将旧总收入减半或假设每笔付款继续进行来安全地重建。确定每项养老金、年金和其他收入来源，然后确认其待遇和可能的净现金金额。加拿大政府的 CPP 遗属养老金页面提供了这一警告的具体示例：CPP 遗属养老金与 CPP 退休金或伤残养老金相结合，不一定是两项单独福利的总和。该工具不计算 CPP 权利、雇主计划百分比或纳税结果。其死后持续的收入是一项独立投入。使用福利估计、计划条款和适当的税收减免来确定该金额，而不是对老家庭的净收入应用一个百分比。将遗属费用与收入分开估算 两人示例的每月净收入为 6,000 加元，运营成本为 5,000 加元，剩下 1,000 加元。独立输入的幸存者数字是 4,300 加元的持续净收入和 3,800 加元的每月费用，剩下 500 加元。当家庭发生变化时，这些费用不会减半。住房和其他承诺可能会继续，但一些支出会发生变化。用具体的列表替换假设的预算，而不是按相同的百分比缩放每个类别。前后条形图仅描述持续的每月金额。它们不包括过渡付款和临时收入缺口。因此，500 加元的持续盈余并不能确定一开始需要多少现金。使用一开始就确认可用的现金 该示例为幸存者提供了 10,000 加元的流动现金，并假定在零时间有 8,000 加元的过渡流出。这样一来，第一个月的账单还剩 2,000 加元。这是现金可用性的说明，而不是房地产估值。它既不决定谁拥有账户，也不决定何时可以获取遗产分配、保险索赔或其他资产。稍后的预期收据不应自动输入为现在可用的现金。每月的全部运行预算在每个月初支付。月底到账。即使没有额外的福利处理缺口，在收入到来之前仍然需要现金来支付第一笔账单。将最初未收到的部分记入已注明日期的现金日历中。在预期的 4,300 加元月收入中，假设前三个月每月未收到 1,500 加元。在此期间，每个月都会收到剩余的 2,800 加元。全部持续收入从第四个月末开始。这是一个压力假设，而不是处理标准或养老金计算。不会自动插入追加欠款。任何已确认的欠款将在详细的现金计划中单独注明日期的收据；他们在这里的遗漏并不决定福利权利。在第四个月的账单之后、该月的收入之前，现金达到负 4,800 加元。所选时间表所需的起始现金为 14,800 加元，比输入的准备金多 4,800 加元。第一份完整收据在最低点之后到达。了解最严重的短缺情况以及最终余额 经过 24 个月的假设现金流量，账簿最终为 9,500 加元。稍后的金额不会支付之前未提供资金的账单。负分表明需要另一个来源；该图表并不授权借款或假设可以使用他人的资金。收据缺口条保留所选的持续收入和成本，同时仅更改初始缺口。该矩阵改变了幸存者的持续净收入和每月预算。未收到的部分不能超过总收入，这是现金预算惯例，而不是法定福利规则。审查可用现金、过渡付款、每个持续收入来源及其预期的第一笔收入。当管理员确认金额或时间后更新计划。该模型保持后期收入和成本不变，并在选定的范围内停止；通货膨胀、税收变化、后期欠款和投资回报需要单独处理。

d70e12f755edaa777c006d9817557194bc463a8f.src: Compare the same principal, amortization and time window. A payment reduction includes principal-repayment differences, so it is not automatically the financing-cost saving. Get the switching costs before comparing the new rate The FCAC’s guide to breaking a mortgage contract explains why a lower offered rate must be considered alongside fees and any prepayment charge. It also points out that qualification and other options can affect the decision. The break-charge control is an external quote assumption. This tool does not estimate an interest-rate differential, select a lender or decide whether the borrower qualifies. Confirm the charge, other closing costs, quote expiry and applicable conditions directly. All upfront costs are paid from cash in this comparison. They are not added to the new loan, and no additional borrowing is taken. If the actual proposal finances costs or changes the remaining amortization, it needs a different cash and debt schedule. Put both mortgages on the same comparison basis The default balance is CAD 400,000 with twenty years remaining. The current hypothetical quoted rate is 6%; the proposed rate is 4.5%. Both use nominal annual rates compounded semi-annually and converted to monthly rates for this illustration. Both loans retain the same remaining amortization, but each has its own calculated monthly payment.
