The current payment is approximately CAD 2,848.75 and the proposed payment CAD 2,521.62, a reduction of about CAD 327.13. The comparison lasts thirty-six months, with both rates held constant only within that window. It does not forecast the next renewal. Choose a window for which the rate assumptions are meaningful; a twenty-year amortization does not mean a twenty-year rate commitment. Separate principal repayment from the cost of borrowing The example enters CAD 8,000 of break charge and CAD 2,000 of other closing costs, totaling CAD 10,000 paid at time zero. That initial cash must be available even though future payments are lower. Over thirty-six months, modeled interest is about CAD 68,241 on the current loan and CAD 50,972 on the proposed loan. The model’s unrounded interest difference is about CAD 17,269. After upfront costs, the financing-cost advantage is approximately CAD 7,269. The cost bars exclude principal repayment because it reduces a liability rather than representing interest or a fee. Intermediate amounts remain unrounded until display, so adding independently rounded figures can differ by cents. These are scenario calculations, not a lender’s repayment statement. Check remaining principal alongside the cash released Cumulative payment relief after the CAD 10,000 upfront cost is only about CAD 1,777 by month thirty-six. The proposed loan also has a lower remaining balance: approximately CAD 360,193 versus CAD 365,685. The current-minus-proposed debt difference is about CAD 5,492. Adding that liability reduction to cash payment relief gives the approximately CAD 7,269 financing-cost advantage. The two measures reconcile because both choices started with the same debt. This identity helps explain why payment reduction alone is incomplete. Part of a payment is principal, and the two repayment paths do not retire identical principal amounts during the window. The debt bars are liabilities at the comparison date, not additional charges to add again to the interest-cost bars. Use the two recovery curves and then stress the assumptions The cash-relief curve and interest-saving curve both begin at negative CAD 10,000. Under the default assumptions, cumulative interest saving covers the cost in month twenty-one, while cumulative payment relief covers it in month thirty-one. Those crossings answer different questions. The first is an undiscounted financing-cost comparison; the second asks when payment reductions have replenished the cash paid upfront. Neither assumes the released cash earns a return or that later rates remain unchanged beyond the window. The matrix changes the proposed rate and total cash-paid costs while holding the other terms selected. A positive result means lower modeled interest plus fees in this window. Review liquidity, loan terms, qualification and the possibility of moving or refinancing again before relying on that result. A favorable arithmetic comparison is one part of the decision.
d70e12f755edaa777c006d9817557194bc463a8f.zh: 比较相同的本金、摊销和时间窗口。还款减少包括本金偿还差额，因此它不会自动节省融资成本。在比较新利率之前先了解转换成本 FCAC 违反抵押贷款合同的指南解释了为什么必须考虑较低的利率以及费用和任何预付款费用。它还指出，资格和其他选项可能会影响决策。中断费用控制是外部报价假设。该工具不会估计利率差异、选择贷款人或决定借款人是否符合资格。直接确认费用、其他成交费用、报价到期日和适用条件。在此比较中，所有前期成本均以现金支付。它们不会添加到新贷款中，也不会进行额外借款。如果实际提案为成本提供资金或改变剩余摊销，则需要不同的现金和债务时间表。将两种抵押贷款置于相同的比较基础上。默认余额为 40 万加元，剩余期限为 20 年。当前假设报价率为6%；建议利率为4.5%。在此说明中，两者均使用半年复利的名义年利率并转换为月利率。两项贷款保留相同的剩余摊销，但每项贷款都有自己计算的每月还款额。当前付款约为 2,848.75 加元，拟付款为 2,521.62 加元，减少约 327.13 加元。比较持续三十六个月，两个比率仅在该窗口内保持不变。它不会预测下一次更新。选择利率假设有意义的窗口；二十年摊销并不意味着二十年利率承诺。将本金偿还与借款成本分开 该示例输入 8,000 加元的违约金和 2,000 加元的其他结账费用，总计在时间零支付的 10,000 加元。即使未来付款较低，初始现金也必须可用。在 36 个月内，当前贷款的模拟利息约为 68,241 加元，拟议贷款的模拟利息约为 50,972 加元。该模型的未舍入利差约为 17,269 加元。扣除前期成本后，融资成本优势约为 7,269 加元。成本栏不包括本金偿还，因为它减少了负债而不是代表利息或费用。中间金额在显示之前保持不四舍五入，因此添加独立四舍五入的数字可能会存在美分差异。这些是情景计算，而不是贷款机构的还款声明。检查剩余本金以及释放的现金 10,000 加元的预付费用后，到第 36 个月，累计付款减免仅为约 1,777 加元。拟议贷款的剩余余额也较低：约为 360,193 加元，而 365,685 加元。当前债务减去拟议债务差额约为 5,492 加元。将责任减少与现金支付减免相结合，可带来约 7,269 加元的融资成本优势。这两种措施是一致的，因为两种选择都是从相同的债务开始的。这一特性有助于解释为什么仅减少付款是不完整的。付款的一部分是本金，并且两个还款路径在窗口期间不会收回相同的本金金额。债务条是比较日的负债，而不是再次添加到利息成本条中的额外费用。使用两条回收曲线，然后强调假设 现金救济曲线和利息节省曲线均以负 10,000 加元开始。在默认假设下，累积利息节省涵盖了第 21 个月的成本，而累积付款减免涵盖了第 31 个月的成本。这些交叉点回答了不同的问题。第一个是未贴现的融资成本比较；第二个问题询问付款减少何时补充了预付现金。两者都没有假设释放的现金能够获得回报，或者之后的利率在窗口之后保持不变。该矩阵改变了提议的费率和总现金支付成本，同时保留所选的其他条款。积极的结果意味着此窗口中的模型利息加费用较低。在依赖该结果之前，请审查流动性、贷款条款、资格以及再次搬迁或再融资的可能性。有利的算术比较是决策的一部分。

78a38bcf76e9e4cf9657877c96496628b71b7b8b.src: Check each household’s access to cash and payment dates separately. A combined surplus or an expected transfer does not prove that every earlier obligation is funded. Keep the cash illustration separate from legal entitlements Justice Canada’s separation and divorce overview emphasizes decisions about housing and finances and the need to understand applicable federal, provincial or territorial law. This article addresses a cash-budget question without deciding those legal issues. Enter income, available cash and any net transfer from independently confirmed arrangements. The model does not divide property, calculate child or spousal support, determine tax treatment or release anyone from an existing debt. The transfer control is simply a signed cash assumption: positive means household A pays household B; negative reverses the direction. It is not a suggested amount, an entitlement calculation or a substitute for documenting obligations and access to funds. Rebuild the running costs of each household The previous single household spends CAD 6,000 a month in the example. New running costs are CAD 3,500 for A and CAD 3,000 for B, totaling CAD 6,500. The entered increase is CAD 500; it is not a universal estimate of what separation costs. Net income before the transfer is CAD 5,000 for A and CAD 3,000 for B. With an assumed CAD 500 monthly transfer from A to B, A’s recurring surplus is CAD 1,000 and B’s is CAD 500. The combined monthly surplus is CAD 1,500. The transfer cancels across that total: moving money between these two ledgers cannot create additional combined income. The resources chart keeps each recipient’s inflow and payer’s commitment visible rather than assuming funds remain pooled. Identify the one-time cash outflows and accessible starting balances The example assigns CAD 4,000 of transition cash outflow to A and CAD 3,000 to B at time zero. Cash confirmed available is CAD 5,000 for A and CAD 2,000 for B. Immediately after those outflows, A has CAD 1,000 and B has an unfunded CAD 1,000 need. A transition outflow may include a deposit that remains an asset as well as expenses. The chart follows cash availability; it is not a profit-and-loss statement or a determination of who owns the asset. Do not also count the same cash as available in another reserve. The previous household’s running cost is shown only for comparison. If an old-home obligation continues while new costs begin, include the actual obligation in the relevant new budget or transition lines. The tool does not automatically fund an overlap. Check the point before the next income receipt Each month, the assumed transfer occurs at the start, running costs are paid, and income arrives at month-end. In month one, A’s cash falls from CAD 1,000 to negative CAD 3,000 after the transfer and costs. B falls to negative CAD 3,500 after the transfer received and running costs. The additional starting cash needs are therefore CAD 3,000 for A and CAD 3,500 for B under these assumptions. After month-one income, A is positive CAD 2,000 and B is negative CAD 500. B reaches zero after month-two income. By the end of twelve months, the ledgers show CAD 13,000 for A and CAD 5,000 for B if all assumed cash flows occur. Those later amounts do not erase an earlier shortage. The lines show pre-income points, so their final plotted values deliberately exclude the last month-end pay. Test individual affordability without assuming a transfer can always arrive The transfer is assumed paid on time even when the sender’s modeled ledger is negative. That negative point flags a funding issue to resolve; in reality it could also affect the recipient’s expected cash. No overdraft, new loan or access to the other household’s funds is approved or assumed. The matrix changes A’s and B’s running costs. Each cell adds their separately calculated additional starting-cash requirements. It does not treat an excess in one existing account as automatically available to cover another person’s shortage. The FCAC’s budgeting guide supports reviewing actual income and expenses as circumstances change. For this transition, keep separate dated records of agreed transfers, accessible cash, ongoing commitments and initial payments. Revisit the cash plan when confirmed legal, tax or benefit information changes.
78a38bcf76e9e4cf9657877c96496628b71b7b8b.zh: 分别检查每个家庭获得现金的情况和付款日期。合并盈余或预期转移并不能证明每一项早期债务都得到了资助。将现金说明与法律权利分开加拿大司法部的分居和离婚概述强调有关住房和财务的决定以及了解适用的联邦、省或地区法律的必要性。本文讨论了现金预算问题，但没有解决这些法律问题。输入收入、可用现金以及来自独立确认的安排的任何净转移。该模型不会分割财产、计算子女或配偶赡养费、确定税收待遇或免除任何人的现有债务。转移控制只是一个签署的现金假设：正数意味着家庭 A 向家庭 B 付款；正数意味着家庭 A 向家庭 B 付款；负值则反转方向。它不是建议金额、权利计算或记录义务和资金获取的替代品。重建每个家庭的运营成本 示例中之前的单个家庭每月花费 6,000 加元。新的运行成本为 A 3,500 加元，B 3,000 加元，总计 6,500 加元。输入的增量为 CAD 500；它并不是对分离成本的普遍估计。 A 转移前的净收入为 5,000 加元，B 为 3,000 加元。假设每月从 A 转移到 B 500 加元，则 A 的经常性盈余为 1,000 加元，B 为 500 加元。合计每月盈余为 1,500 加元。转账在总额中被取消：在这两个分类账之间转移资金不能创造额外的合并收入。资源图表使每个接收者的流入和付款人的承诺可见，而不是假设资金保持汇集。确定一次性现金流出和可访问的起始余额 该示例在时间零时将 4,000 加元的过渡现金流出分配给 A，将 3,000 加元分配给 B。确认可用的现金为 A 5,000 加元，B 2,000 加元。在这些资金流出后，A 立即有 1,000 加元，B 则有 1,000 加元的无资金需求。过渡流出可能包括仍为资产的存款以及费用。该图表遵循现金可用性；它不是损益表，也不是资产所有者的确定。不要同时计算其他储备中可用的相同现金。显示以前家庭的运行成本仅供比较。如果在新成本开始时旧房义务仍然存在，请将实际义务包括在相关的新预算或过渡线中。该工具不会自动为重叠提供资金。检查下一次收入收据之前的点 每个月，假设的转移发生在月初，支付运行成本，收入在月底到达。第一个月，扣除转账和费用后，A 的现金从 1,000 加元降至负 3,000 加元。在收到转账和运行成本后，B 跌至负 3,500 加元。因此，在这些假设下，A 的额外起始现金需求为 3,000 加元，B 的额外起始现金需求为 3,500 加元。第一个月收入后，A 为正 2,000 加元，B 为负 500 加元。第二个月收入后，B 为零。到 12 个月结束时，如果所有假设的现金流都发生，分类账显示 A 为 13,000 加元，B 为 5,000 加元。后来的数量并不能消除之前的短缺。这些线显示预收入点，因此它们的最终绘制值故意排除上个月末的工资。测试个人的承受能力，而不假设转账总能到达即使发送者的建模账本为负，转账也会按时支付。这个负面因素标志着需要解决的资金问题；事实上，它也可能影响收款人的预期现金。不会批准或假设透支、新贷款或使用其他家庭的资金。该矩阵改变了 A 和 B 的运行成本。每个单元添加其单独计算的额外起始现金需求。它不会将一个现有帐户的多余部分视为自动可用于弥补另一个人的短缺。 FCAC 的预算指南支持根据情况变化审查实际收入和支出。对于这种过渡，请单独保存商定转让、可用现金、持续承诺和初始付款的注明日期的记录。当确认的法律、税务或福利信息发生变化时，重新审查现金计划。

1b1bf20b6b18fc6abfdca8da81feea81c433c987.src: Withholding is tax prepaid at withdrawal. Budget the cash received now and any later difference from the full tax cost without subtracting the prepaid amount twice. Start with the type of withdrawal and the applicable withholding The CRA’s RRSP withdrawal page lists withholding rates that depend on the withdrawal amount and residency. For the ordinary Canadian-resident case modeled outside Quebec, the rate is 10% up to CAD 5,000, 20% above CAD 5,000 through CAD 15,000, and 30% above CAD 15,000. This guide models one lump-sum request. It excludes Quebec withholding, non-residents, spousal attribution, registered-plan withdrawal programs and series of payments. Confirm the actual treatment and any fee with the institution before using a cash figure for a real transaction. The first chart applies the amount-based rate to the whole request. These rates are different from marginal income-tax brackets, where a higher rate generally applies only to a slice of taxable income. The chart is an explanation of withholding mechanics, not a recommendation for choosing a withdrawal amount. Read the withholding thresholds without mistaking them for tax brackets A single CAD 5,000 example has CAD 500 withheld and CAD 4,500 of proceeds before a separate fee. At CAD 5,000.01, the modeled 20% withholding rounds to CAD 1,000, leaving CAD 4,000.01 before the fee. The immediate cash can fall when the gross request crosses a threshold. That change describes the timing of tax prepaid; it does not show that the final tax liability has the same jump. The examples are independent requests for comparison, rather than a proposed sequence or withdrawal-splitting strategy. For transparency, withholding is rounded to cents in this illustration. Institutional processing can involve additional facts. The exact settlement and any special treatment require confirmation, and a series of requests is outside the tool’s scope. Reconcile the default request to the cash available now The default requests CAD 10,000, giving CAD 2,000 of modeled withholding and CAD 8,000 paid before a separately funded CAD 50 transaction fee. The household’s net cash from the transaction is CAD 7,950. The fee control represents an expense paid from other cash. It is not an assumed reduction in the amount subject to withholding, and the model grants it no tax deduction. The fee is zero when no withdrawal occurs. If a small withdrawal and a large separate fee produce a negative net transaction result, that is a need for other cash to pay the fee. It is not a negative payment from the institution. Keep the gross request, prepaid tax, institution’s payment and separate charges visible in the ledger. Compare withholding with the full incremental tax assumption The final-tax control is an independently entered effective incremental rate on the entire withdrawal. It does not calculate actual federal or provincial brackets, credits or benefit reductions. The default assumes 30%, producing CAD 3,000 of incremental tax. Because CAD 2,000 has already been withheld, the modeled additional settlement is CAD 1,000. Net cash after the full assumed tax and fee is CAD 6,950: CAD 10,000 less CAD 3,000 less CAD 50. Equivalently, start with immediate net cash of CAD 7,950 and subtract the additional CAD 1,000. Subtracting both CAD 2,000 withheld and the full CAD 3,000 again would overstate tax by counting the prepaid amount twice. A lower final-tax assumption can instead produce excess withholding, but the tool does not approve or date a refund. Check the intended spending against final cash as well as today’s proceeds The default spending need is CAD 7,000. Immediate net transaction cash exceeds that by CAD 950, while modeled final cash is CAD 50 short. Spending all the apparent early surplus would leave the later tax difference unfunded under these assumptions. The tax-comparison bars hold the request and withholding fixed while changing the independent final-tax assumption. The matrix varies the gross request and assumed effective tax rate, then compares final cash with the selected spending need. Use an actual incremental tax estimate when available and reserve any expected settlement before treating the proceeds as fully spendable. This one transaction comparison does not determine how much retirement capital to withdraw or the effect on the rest of a long-term plan.
1b1bf20b6b18fc6abfdca8da81feea81c433c987.zh: 预扣税是提款时预缴的税款。预算现在收到的现金和以后与全部税收成本的差额，而不减去预付金额两次。从提款类型和适用的预扣税开始 CRA 的 RRSP 提款页面列出了取决于提款金额和居住地的预扣税率。对于魁北克省以外的普通加拿大居民案件，5,000加元以下的税率为10%，5,000加元以上至15,000加元以上的税率为20%，15,000加元以上的税率为30%。本指南模拟了一次总付请求。它不包括魁北克预扣税、非居民、配偶归属、注册计划提款计划和一系列付款。在使用现金进行实际交易之前，请先与机构确认实际治疗和任何费用。第一个图表将基于金额的费率应用于整个请求。这些税率与边际所得税税率不同，后者较高的税率通常仅适用于一部分应税收入。该图表是对预扣机制的解释，而不是选择提款金额的建议。阅读预扣税起征点，不要将其误认为税级。单个 5,000 加元的示例已预扣 500 加元，并在单独收费之前扣除了 4,500 加元的收益。在 5,000.01 加元的情况下，模型中的 20% 预扣税变为 1,000 加元，在费用前留下 4,000.01 加元。当总请求超过阈值时，即时现金可能会下降。这一变化描述了预缴税款的时间；它并没有表明最终的纳税义务有同样的跳跃。这些例子是独立的比较请求，而不是建议的顺序或提款分割策略。出于透明度考虑，本图中预扣税额四舍五入为美分。机构处理可能涉及其他事实。确切的结算和任何特殊处理都需要确认，而一系列请求超出了该工具的范围。将默认请求与当前可用现金进行核对 默认请求 10,000 加元，提供 2,000 加元的模拟预扣税，并在单独资助 50 加元的交易费之前支付 8,000 加元。该家庭从交易中获得的净现金为 7,950 加元。费用控制代表用其他现金支付的费用。这不是预扣金额的假设减少，并且该模型不给予任何税收减免。当没有发生提现时，费用为零。如果小额提款和大额单独费用产生负的净交易结果，则需要其他现金来支付费用。这不是机构的负付款。在分类账中保留总请求、预付税款、机构付款和单独费用。将预扣税与全额增量税收假设进行比较 最终税收控制是针对整个提款独立输入的有效增量税率。它不计算实际的联邦或省级等级、抵免或福利减少。默认假设为 30%，产生 3,000 加元的增量税。由于已预扣 2,000 加元，因此模拟的额外结算为 1,000 加元。全额假设税费后的净现金为 6,950 加元：10,000 加元减 3,000 加元减 50 加元。同样，从立即净现金 7,950 加元开始，减去额外的 1,000 加元。如果同时减去预扣的 2,000 加元和全额的 3,000 加元，则会将预付金额计算两次，从而多报税款。较低的最终税假设反而会产生超额预扣税，但该工具不会批准退款或确定退款日期。根据最终现金以及今天的收益检查预期支出 默认支出需求为 7,000 加元。即时净交易现金超出 950 加元，而模拟最终现金则少 50 加元。在这些假设下，花掉所有明显的早期盈余将使后期的税收差异得不到资金支持。税收比较条保持请求和预扣税固定，同时改变独立的最终税收假设。该矩阵改变总请求和假设的有效税率，然后将最终现金与选定的支出需求进行比较。使用实际增量税收估算（如果有），并在将收益视为完全可支出之前保留任何预期结算。这一交易比较并不能确定提取多少退休资本或对长期计划的其余部分的影响。

7f0d75fd0c27e72a96c74b6be8db3fa2d4135cdf.src: Label the income year, the benefits received and the later deduction period. An annual recovery estimate and future withholding credits belong to different parts of the tax and cash calendar. Use a threshold for a named income year Service Canada’s resident OAS repayment explanation uses a CAD 93,454 threshold for 2025 income and a 15% calculation on the excess. This guide fixes that income year instead of silently reusing its threshold for a later year. The input is the relevant adjusted income for the recovery calculation. The CRA’s line 23500 guidance identifies adjustments to the starting income amount and directs taxpayers to the Federal Worksheet. The tool does not reconstruct those adjustments from account balances or deposits. Enter the appropriate income including OAS where applicable; do not add the entered pension again. This is an OAS-only Canadian-resident illustration, excluding net federal supplements, EI repayment and non-resident tax. Use the worksheet and actual slips for a return. Calculate the excess, then limit the simplified recovery to the pension The default relevant 2025 income is CAD 100,000. Subtracting CAD 93,454 leaves CAD 6,546; 15% is CAD 981.90. The example enters CAD 9,000 of gross 2025 OAS. The model caps recovery at that entered annual pension. The remaining amount is CAD 8,018.10 before ordinary income tax. The cap is for this simplified OAS-only case and is not a substitute for the complete social-benefits repayment calculation. The income curve holds the selected pension cap fixed and shows the threshold and capped section explicitly. The matrix varies relevant income and pension received. Its hypothetical pension amounts are not official annual maxima or a determination of eligibility, age treatment or residence history. Place the later monthly deduction in its own payment period The monthly cash chart runs from January 2026 through June 2027. Its first six months use a separately entered prior recovery deduction, which starts at zero in the example. The later illustration begins in July 2026 and runs for twelve months. To make the cash arithmetic explicit, the tool divides CAD 981.90 by twelve and rounds the monthly planning deduction to cents, giving CAD 81.83. Gross monthly OAS is independently assumed constant at CAD 750. The result after this deduction alone is CAD 668.17. Twelve deductions at CAD 81.83 total CAD 981.96, six cents more than the annual illustration. Actual deductions follow the Advisory Letter, so the tool does not present its rounding convention as an official payment quote. It also caps a modeled deduction at monthly gross OAS; that display cap does not cancel an actual obligation. Avoid counting later withholding as a second annual recovery charge The annual bridge concerns benefits received in 2025. The cash chart concerns payments in 2026 and 2027. Its gross monthly amount can differ from the earlier annual pension, so multiplying future monthly cash by twelve will not generally reproduce the annual bridge. Recovery tax withheld from a pension payment is reported as tax deducted for that payment year. The CRA explains how the amount shown on the slip is claimed with income tax deducted, while the repayment calculation is completed separately. In this fixed example, the new deduction appears for six months in calendar 2026 and six in 2027, or CAD 490.98 in each calendar year. Do not add all twelve future deductions to CAD 981.90 and label the result the tax on the same 2025 pension. Keep the liability calculation and payment-year credits distinct. Refresh the pension amount and the income estimate separately The cash chart deliberately holds gross monthly OAS constant to isolate deduction timing. It does not model quarterly pension changes, ordinary income-tax withholding, an age-related increase or a future-year recovery threshold. If the relevant income changes substantially, the expected deduction based on an earlier year may not match the current situation. The CRA’s line 23500 page describes a request to reduce recovery tax at source when the stated conditions apply. The tool neither submits that request nor assumes approval. For a working retirement budget, record the Advisory Letter’s effective date and deduction, the gross pension payment and the expected tax-return treatment. Compare those dated amounts with the spending calendar. Use this illustration to understand the moving parts, then replace its assumptions with the confirmed figures.
7f0d75fd0c27e72a96c74b6be8db3fa2d4135cdf.zh: 标记收入年度、收到的福利和后期扣除期间。年度回收估计和未来预扣税额属于税收和现金日历的不同部分。使用指定收入年份的阈值加拿大服务局的居民 OAS 还款解释使用 2025 年收入 93,454 加元的阈值，并对超额部分按 15% 计算。本指南修复了该收入年度，而不是默默地在以后的一年中重新使用其阈值。输入是用于回收率计算的相关调整收入。 CRA 的第 23500 行指南确定了对起始收入金额的调整，并指导纳税人查阅联邦工作表。该工具不会根据账户余额或存款重建这些调整。输入适当的收入，包括适用的 OAS；请勿再次添加已输入的养老金。这是仅限 OAS 加拿大居民的说明，不包括净联邦补助金、EI 还款和非居民税。使用工作表和实际单据进行退货。计算超额部分，然后将简化的回收限制为养老金。默认的2025年相关收入为10万加元。减去 93,454 加元，剩下 6,546 加元； 15% 为 981.90 加元。该示例输入 2025 年 OAS 总额 9,000 加元。该模型将恢复上限限制在进入年度养老金的水平。普通所得税前剩余金额为 8,018.10 加元。该上限仅适用于这种简化的 OAS 情况，不能替代完整的社会福利还款计算。收入曲线保持选定的养老金上限固定，并明确显示阈值和上限部分。该矩阵随相关收入和养老金的变化而变化。其假设的养老金金额不是官方的年度最高限额，也不是资格、年龄待遇或居住历史的确定。将稍后的每月扣除额放入其自己的付款期中 每月现金图表从 2026 年 1 月到 2027 年 6 月。其前六个月使用单独输入的先前恢复扣除额，在示例中从零开始。后面的插图从 2026 年 7 月开始，持续十二个月。为了使现金算术更加明确，该工具将 981.90 加元除以 12，并将每月计划扣除额四舍五入为美分，得到 81.83 加元。独立假设每月 OAS 总额恒定为 750 加元。仅扣除此费用后的结果为 668.17 加元。扣除 12 项，扣除 81.83 加元，总计 981.96 加元，比年度插图多了 6 美分。实际扣除额遵循咨询函，因此该工具不会将其舍入约定作为官方付款报价。它还限制了每月总 OAS 的模拟扣除额；该显示上限并不取消实际义务。避免将后来的预扣税计算为第二个年度追缴费用 年度过桥涉及 2025 年收到的福利。现金表涉及 2026 年和 2027 年的付款。其每月总金额可能与之前的年度养老金不同，因此将未来每月现金乘以 12 一般不会重现年度过桥。从养老金支付中预扣的恢复税将作为该支付年度的扣除税款报告。 CRA 解释了如何申报单据上显示的金额并扣除所得税，而还款计算则单独完成。在此固定示例中，新扣除额在 2026 年出现 6 个月，在 2027 年出现 6 个月，即每个日历年 490.98 加元。不要将所有 12 项未来扣除额加到 981.90 加元，并将结果标记为同一 2025 年养老金的税款。保持负债计算和付款年度信用不同。分别刷新养老金金额和收入估算 现金图表特意保持每月 OAS 总额不变，以隔离扣除时间。它没有对季度养老金变化、普通所得税预扣、与年龄相关的增长或未来年份恢复阈值进行建模。如果相关收入发生较大变化，以前年度的预期扣除额可能与当前情况不符。 CRA 的第 23500 行页面描述了在规定条件适用时从源头减少回收税的请求。该工具既不提交该请求也不假定获得批准。对于工作退休预算，记录咨询函的生效日期和扣除额、养老金支付总额和预期的纳税申报表处理。将这些日期金额与支出日历进行比较。使用此图来了解移动部件，然后用已确认的数字替换其假设。

d5263cc03eb32dd1b6bc8655942e31b88db62c24.zh: 美洲国家组织兑现时间

2d76ed64bac185fed706397881cadc09b4cf92a2.src: Compare additional take-home pay with all additional costs and any net income that stops. Use a confirmed care quote for the household, with published averages as context. Read the child-care observations with their scope Statistics Canada’s Child care arrangements, 2025 release reports national monthly mean expenses of CAD 663 in 2022, CAD 508 in 2023 and CAD 435 in 2025 for children aged zero to five using full-time centre-based care. These are parent-reported current-dollar means for care of at least thirty hours per week. They are not medians, individual provider quotes or a promise that a space is available. The survey includes arrangements beyond those participating in the federal child-care system. The release was published on 21 October 2025 and retrieved here on 25 October 2026. Its 2022 comparison excludes territories, while 2023 and 2025 include them and draw on differing survey sources. The bars describe the published observations; they are not a constant-coverage price index or a causal estimate of one policy. Replace the regional average with the actual household quote The regional chart shows thirteen published 2025 means, taken from the release’s chart CSV. Only the 2025 column is used. Its 2022 territory cells contain a missing-data footnote marker, which must not be treated as a dollar fee. A regional average cannot establish a particular family’s bill or care quality. Confirm the provider, number of children, hours, extra charges and the net amount the household will pay. A subsidy already reflected in that net quote must not be deducted again. The two official-data graphics stay fixed when the budget controls change. The editable care input starts at a hypothetical CAD 800 for additional household care, rather than automatically treating the national per-child observation as the household’s actual cost. Compare the incremental monthly cash changes The default adds CAD 3,500 of monthly take-home pay, already net of payroll deductions. It subtracts CAD 800 of additional care, CAD 200 of commuting and CAD 150 of other work costs. It also subtracts CAD 500 of other net household income that stops or falls when work resumes. That is an independent assumption, not a calculation of parental benefits, tax credits or income-tested assistance. Do not include the same reduction in both the take-home pay estimate and this line. The resulting monthly cash change is positive CAD 1,850. Existing household income and expenses that are identical in both situations cancel out of this incremental comparison. This is not a full household budget or a statement that gross employment income is entirely spendable. Fund setup costs before relying on later monthly gains One-time setup costs are CAD 1,500 in the example. The cumulative chart begins at negative CAD 1,500 at time zero, then adds CAD 1,850 for each full month. It reaches positive CAD 350 after month one and CAD 20,700 after twelve months. The monthly periods assume the full first month’s pay is received inside that month. Real payroll dates, a partial first month or deposits required before care begins can create an earlier cash requirement. A positive month-end cumulative result does not provide that earlier funding automatically. If recurring monthly cash change is zero or negative and setup is positive, setup is not recovered. If recovery lies beyond the selected horizon, the tool says so. Zero setup gives month zero for that metric even when later cash changes are negative; read the monthly result as well. Stress the care quote and take-home pay without reducing the decision to one number The matrix varies monthly household care costs and additional take-home pay. Commuting, other work costs and other net income lost stay selected. It reports a monthly cash difference, with setup considered separately in the cumulative chart. Check a lower pay estimate and a higher care quote before committing fixed expenses. A part-time arrangement may change several lines at once, so update the full set of assumptions rather than scaling one cost and holding everything else without review. The cash comparison leaves out career progression, retirement benefits, time, care preferences and job security. Those can matter even when two scenarios have similar cash results. Use the charts to clarify the budget question while keeping those other goals visible in the broader decision.
2d76ed64bac185fed706397881cadc09b4cf92a2.zh: 将额外的实得工资与所有额外成本和任何停止的净收入进行比较。使用经确认的家庭护理报价，并以公布的平均值作为背景。阅读儿童保育观察及其范围 加拿大统计局 2025 年儿童保育安排报告称，使用全日制中心保育的 0 至 5 岁儿童的全国月平均费用在 2022 年为 663 加元，2023 年为 508 加元，2025 年为 435 加元。这些是家长报告的按现价计算的每周至少三十个小时的照顾费用。它们不是中间值、个别提供商的报价或可用空间的承诺。该调查包括参与联邦儿童保育系统之外的安排。该新闻稿于 2025 年 10 月 21 日发布，并于 2026 年 10 月 25 日在此处检索。其 2022 年的比较不包括地区，而 2023 年和 2025 年则包括这些地区，并利用不同的调查来源。条形描述了已发表的观察结果；它们不是恒定覆盖范围的价格指数或对一项保单的因果估计。将地区平均值替换为实际家庭报价 地区图表显示了 13 个已发布的 2025 年平均值，取自发布的图表 CSV。仅使用 2025 列。其 2022 年领土单元格包含缺失数据脚注标记，不得将其视为美元费用。地区平均数无法确定特定家庭的账单或护理质量。确认提供者、儿童人数、工作时间、额外费用以及家庭将支付的净金额。已反映在该净报价中的补贴不得再次扣除。当预算控制发生变化时，这两个官方数据图表保持不变。可编辑的护理投入从假设的 800 加元开始，用于额外的家庭护理，而不是自动将全国每个儿童的观察结果视为家庭的实际成本。比较每月现金增量变化 默认情况下，每月实得工资增加 3,500 加元，已扣除工资扣除额。扣除 800 加元的额外护理费用、200 加元的通勤费用和 150 加元的其他工作费用。它还减去恢复工作后停止或下降的其他家庭净收入 500 加元。这是一个独立的假设，而不是对父母福利、税收抵免或收入测试援助的计算。不要在实得工资估算和这条线中包括同样的减少。由此产生的每月现金变化为正 1,850 加元。在这两种情况下，现有家庭收入和支出相同，从而抵消了这种增量比较。这不是完整的家庭预算，也不是总就业收入完全可以支出的声明。在依赖以后每月收益之前的基金设立成本 在示例中，一次性设立成本为 1,500 加元。累积图表从零时间的负 1,500 加元开始，然后每个整月增加 1,850 加元。第一个月后，其价格达到 350 加元，十二个月后，价格达到 20,700 加元。每月期间假设在该月内收到第一个月的全额工资。实际工资发放日期、第一个月的部分时间或护理开始前所需的存款可能会产生更早的现金需求。正的月末累计结果不会自动提供较早的资金。如果经常性每月现金变化为零或负数且设置为正，则设置不会恢复。如果恢复超出了选定的范围，该工具就会如此说明。即使后来的现金变化为负，零设置也会为该指标提供零月份；还要阅读每月的结果。强调护理报价和实得工资，而不将决策减少到一个数字 该矩阵会改变每月的家庭护理费用和额外的实得工资。通勤、其他工作成本和其他净收入损失保持选择。它报告每月现金差异，并在累积图表中单独考虑设置。在支付固定费用之前，请检查较低的工资估算和较高的护理报价。兼职安排可能会同时更改几条生产线，因此更新全套假设，而不是缩放一项成本并保留其他所有内容而不进行审查。现金比较忽略了职业发展、退休福利、时间、护理偏好和工作保障。即使两种情况的现金结果相似，这些也可能很重要。使用图表来阐明预算问题，同时在更广泛的决策中保持其他目标的可见性。

f9e0c6d14677958032fc617c076f3c3a20a8c1c7.src: Build the household draw from cash that remains after business obligations and a tax provision. Profit, collected cash and uncommitted cash answer different questions. Keep invoices, operating profit, cash and owner draws distinct A customer invoice can record work completed without putting money into the bank. Operating profit can be positive while cash is tied up in receivables. An owner’s withdrawal then moves cash into the household budget without changing the modeled operating profit. The CRA’s sole-proprietorship overview explains that personal income tax applies to business net income and that instalment payments may be required. It does not make a fixed percentage of every invoice a universal tax rate. This tool is a simplified management ledger for an unincorporated owner, rather than a tax return. All invoices exclude sales taxes. Costs are assumed to be operating cash payments; the model does not determine whether an expense is deductible or account for inventory, capital allowances or GST/HST. Follow the same twelve-month example through the ledger The default issues CAD 12,000 of invoices each month, or CAD 144,000 over twelve months. Operating cash costs are 30% of invoiced revenue: CAD 3,600 a month and CAD 43,200 for the year. Invoice-based operating profit is CAD 100,800 before owner draws and the tax provision. The owner withdraws CAD 4,000 at each month’s start, totaling CAD 48,000. Those withdrawals reduce the business cash available even though they do not reduce this operating-profit figure. A hypothetical 25% allowance on positive operating profit creates a CAD 2,100 monthly tax earmark, reaching CAD 25,200. This is a target reserved for future obligations, not an assessment of income tax, CPP or QPP. A loss creates no new earmark in the illustration and no assumed tax refund. Allow for the collection delay and opening cash needs With one full month of collection delay, month one’s invoice is received at the end of month two. The schedule starts without older invoices waiting to be collected. Consequently, only eleven monthly invoices arrive inside the twelve-month horizon. Cash receipts are CAD 132,000 and CAD 12,000 remains receivable at year-end. The final invoice is not written off; its later receipt simply lies outside this chart. Operating costs and household withdrawals are still paid in month twelve. Starting cash is CAD 10,000. At the start of month two, the second CAD 7,600 of operating costs and owner draws falls due before any customer receipt. With the first month’s CAD 2,100 earmark also reserved, uncommitted cash is negative CAD 7,300. The model therefore needs CAD 17,300 at the start, or CAD 7,300 beyond the selected amount. Do not treat earmarked money as spare household income The year-end cash ledger before the earmark is CAD 50,800: opening cash plus receipts, less operating costs and withdrawals. Subtracting the CAD 25,200 target leaves CAD 25,600 uncommitted. The waterfall reconciles that amount from invoices by also removing the uncollected balance. The earmark remains cash if it has been funded and held. Subtract it once when measuring spendable resources. If cash is below the target, the target is partly unfunded; recording a reserve label does not create the missing money. No remittance is made inside this model. If a fully funded earmark is later used for an equal tax payment, both cash and the outstanding earmark fall by that amount, leaving uncommitted cash unchanged at that instant. Actual payment dates and revised amounts still need a separate calendar. Test customer timing and owner withdrawals together The collection-delay bars keep the invoice and expense assumptions fixed while changing when customers pay. Even zero full-month delay requires opening cash here because costs and draws precede month-end receipts. The matrix changes owner withdrawals and the hypothetical earmark percentage. It measures additional opening cash, rather than recommending a draw or claiming that a selected percentage settles the tax bill. More available opening cash can bridge timing; it does not make an ongoing loss sustainable. Replace the equal invoices with a detailed forecast before using a real plan. Review collection risk, expense due dates, tax estimates and remittances, then pass the household only the net amount it can use. The existing variable-income guide begins at that household stage; this guide explains the business cash steps that come first.
f9e0c6d14677958032fc617c076f3c3a20a8c1c7.zh: 利用扣除商业义务和税收准备金后剩余的现金来建立家庭支出。利润、收取的现金和未承诺的现金回答了不同的问题。保持发票、营业利润、现金和业主提款的区别客户发票可以记录已完成的工作，而无需将钱存入银行。当现金被应收账款占用时，营业利润可能为正。然后，业主的提款将现金转移到家庭预算中，而不会改变建模的营业利润。 CRA 的独资企业概述解释说，个人所得税适用于企业净收入，并且可能需要分期付款。它并未将每张发票的固定百分比设为通用税率。该工具是非法人所有者的简化管理分类账，而不是纳税申报表。所有发票均不含销售税。成本假设为运营现金支付；该模型无法确定某项费用是否可扣除或计入库存、资本补贴或 GST/HST。通过分类帐遵循相同的 12 个月示例默认每月开具 12,000 加元的发票，或者在 12 个月内开具 144,000 加元。运营现金成本占发票收入的 30%：每月 3,600 加元，全年 43,200 加元。基于发票的营业利润为 100,800 加元（扣除业主提款和税款准备金）。业主在每个月开始时提取 4,000 加元，总计 48,000 加元。这些提款减少了可用的商业现金，尽管它们并没有减少营业利润数字。假设正营业利润的 25% 免税额会产生 2,100 加元的每月税收专项资金，达到 25,200 加元。这是为未来义务保留的目标，而不是所得税、CPP 或 QPP 的评估。图中的损失不会产生新的专项拨款，也不会假定退税。考虑到收款延迟和开立现金需求 如果收款延迟一整月，则在第二个月末收到第一个月的发票。该计划开始时没有等待收集的旧发票。因此，在 12 个月内只有 11 张每月发票到达。现金收入为 132,000 加元，年末应收现金为 12,000 加元。最终发票未核销；它后来的收据根本不在这张图表之外。运营成本和家庭提款仍需在第十二个月支付。起始现金为 10,000 加元。第二个月开始时，第二笔 7,600 加元的运营成本和业主提款在客户收到任何款项之前到期。加上第一个月的 2,100 加元预留款，未承诺的现金为负 7,300 加元。因此，该模型一开始需要 17,300 加元，或者超出所选金额 7,300 加元。不要将专项资金视为家庭闲置收入 专项资金之前的年末现金分类为 50,800 加元：期初现金加收据，减去运营成本和提款。减去 25,200 加元的目标，剩下 25,600 加元未承诺。瀑布还通过删除未收余额来调节发票金额。如果已提供资金并持有，该专项资金仍为现金。在衡量可消耗资源时减去一次。如果现金低于目标，则目标部分资金不足；记录保留标签不会造成丢失的钱。该模型内不进行汇款。如果后来将全额资助的专项资金用于同等纳税，则现金和未偿专项资金都会减少该金额，从而使未承诺的现金立即保持不变。实际付款日期和修改后的金额仍然需要单独的日历。一起测试客户时间和所有者提款 收款延迟条使发票和费用假设保持固定，同时在客户付款时发生变化。即使零整月延迟也需要在这里开设现金，因为成本和提款先于月末收据。该矩阵改变了所有者提款和假设的指定用途百分比。它衡量额外的期初现金，而不是建议提取或声称选定的百分比来结算税单。更多可用的开业现金可以弥补时机；它不会使持续的损失变得可持续。在使用真正的计划之前，用详细的预测代替同等的发票。审查收款风险、费用到期日、税收估算和汇款，然后仅向家庭传递其可以使用的净额。现有的可变收入指南从家庭阶段开始；本指南解释了首要的商业现金步骤。

71b33ebb18c772d2877c7a738c8f7750465fbe55.src: A replacement reserve needs enough money when each bill arrives. Dividing the final total by the full horizon can miss an earlier funding gap. Build a component list beside the routine upkeep budget A home’s mortgage payment does not describe its full cash needs. Routine upkeep may fit into monthly spending, while a roof or heating replacement requires a larger amount at a particular time. CMHC’s capital-replacement planning overview describes listing major components, their remaining useful lives and replacement costs, and distinguishes that process from annual maintenance. That page addresses housing providers; the household example here uses the planning distinction without reproducing a formal reserve study. The tool selects only a roof, heating equipment and an appliance bundle. A real inventory may need additional components and professional condition information. The intervals are hypothetical assumptions, not a published lifespan table, an inspection result or advice to defer a necessary repair. Count repeated events and grow each cost to its payment year The default costs in today’s dollars are CAD 15,000 for the roof, CAD 7,000 for heating and CAD 3,000 for appliances. The assumed intervals are eight, six and four years respectively. First replacements occur at those intervals and subsequent replacements repeat at the same spacing. Inside twelve years, the roof appears once, heating twice and appliances three times. Their repeated costs at today’s prices total CAD 38,000. That is different from buying each component only once for CAD 25,000. A constant 3% annual replacement-cost growth assumption applies from today to every event date. It produces CAD 48,794.36 of replacement bills within the horizon. The component chart separates repeated base costs from assumed growth and also shows routine upkeep as a separate cash category. Neither the costs nor the growth rate are market quotes or statistical forecasts. Watch for components that fall due together The annual bars show appliance replacement in year four, heating in year six, roof and appliances together in year eight, and heating and appliances together in year twelve. The year-eight bill is CAD 22,801.86, even though no replacement is modeled in several other years. Starting reserve is CAD 5,000 and monthly reserve saving is CAD 300. Contributions arrive at month-end before any year-end replacement bill. No investment return is earned. After the year-eight bill, the selected reserve is negative CAD 736.75. The final year ends negative CAD 594.36. That smaller ending deficit does not repair the larger earlier shortage. Negative values represent unfunded needs; the chart assumes neither an overdraft nor borrowing to complete the work. Size the monthly contribution to every event date For each replacement date, subtract the starting reserve from cumulative bills and divide by the number of monthly contributions available by that date. The largest positive result is the monthly contribution needed under this zero-return schedule. Simply spreading the final net requirement across 144 months suggests about CAD 304.13 a month. Year eight instead requires about CAD 307.6745. Rounding the largest requirement up to cents gives CAD 307.68, which keeps all modeled points funded. The second line uses that calculated contribution with the same costs and starting reserve. It illustrates the timing constraint; it is not a guarantee about actual repair costs. A changed scope, earlier failure or omitted component can still make the reserve insufficient. Separate routine spending and test earlier replacements The default also enters CAD 100 a month for routine upkeep. It stays outside the replacement reserve and remains constant in this illustration. The selected monthly maintenance commitment is therefore CAD 400: CAD 300 reserved and CAD 100 spent separately. Do not subtract the routine allowance from the reserve again. The matrix moves each first replacement earlier by up to three years, no earlier than year one, while leaving its repeat interval unchanged. This can change the number of bills inside twelve years as well as the time available to save. Cost growth runs only to each revised payment date. Update the inventory from condition assessments, quotes and completed work. Keep an emergency cushion for events outside the selected schedule, and avoid counting the same starting cash in both reserves. Condominium or strata obligations require the relevant building documents and rules; this household illustration does not calculate them.
71b33ebb18c772d2877c7a738c8f7750465fbe55.zh: 每张账单到达时，更换准备金都需要足够的钱。将最终总额除以整个范围可能会错过早期的资金缺口。在日常维护预算旁边建立一个组成部分清单房屋的抵押贷款付款并不能描述其全部现金需求。日常维护可能适合每月支出，而屋顶或暖气更换在特定时间需要更大的金额。 CMHC 的资本更换计划概述列出了主要部件、其剩余使用寿命和更换成本，并将该过程与年度维护区分开来。该页面涉及住房提供者；这里的家庭示例使用了规划区别，而没有复制正式的储备研究。该工具仅选择屋顶、加热设备和电器包。真实的库存可能需要额外的组件和专业状况信息。这些间隔是假设性的假设，而不是已发布的寿命表、检查结果或推迟必要维修的建议。计算重复事件并将每项成本增加到其付款年份 按今天的美元计算，默认成本为屋顶 15,000 加元、供暖费用 7,000 加元和电器费用 3,000 加元。假设的时间间隔分别为八年、六年和四年。第一次更换以这些间隔进行，后续更换以相同的间隔重复。十二年之内，屋顶出现一次，暖气出现两次，电器出现三次。按今天的价格计算，它们的重复成本总计为 38,000 加元。这与花费 25,000 加元只购买一次每个组件不同。从今天开始，每年重置成本增长 3% 的恒定假设适用于每个活动日期。预计将产生 48,794.36 加元的替代票据。组成部分图表将重复的基本成本与假设的增长分开，并将日常维护作为单独的现金类别显示。成本和增长率都不是市场报价或统计预测。留意一起到期的组件 年度条形图显示第四年的设备更换、第六年的供暖、第八年的屋顶和设备以及第十二年的供暖和设备。第八年的钞票金额为 22,801.86 加元，尽管其他几年都没有替代钞票。起始准备金为 5,000 加元，每月节省的准备金为 300 加元。捐款在月底到达，比任何年终更换账单早。没有获得投资回报。八年账单后，选定的准备金为负 736.75 加元。最后一年结束时为负 594.36 加元。较小的期末赤字并不能修复早期较大的短缺。负值代表没有资金支持的需求；该图表假设既不透支也不借款来完成工作。确定每个活动日期的每月供款规模 对于每个更换日期，从累积账单中减去起始准备金，然后除以该日期之前可用的每月供款数量。最大的积极成果是零回报计划下所需的每月供款。如果将最终净需求简单地分摊到 144 个月内，则表明每月约为 304.13 加元。第八年则需要大约 307.6745 加元。将最大要求四舍五入至美分，得到 307.68 加元，这使得所有建模点都得到资助。第二行使用具有相同成本和起始准备金的计算出的贡献。它说明了时间限制；它不能保证实际的维修费用。范围的改变、早期的故障或遗漏的组件仍然可能导致储备不足。单独的日常支出并测试早期更换默认情况下还会输入每月 100 加元的日常维护费用。它位于替代储备之外，并在此图中保持不变。因此，选定的每月维护承诺为 400 加元：预留 300 加元，单独支出 100 加元。不要再从储备金中扣除日常津贴。该矩阵将每个第一次替换提前最多三年，不早于第一年，同时保持其重复间隔不变。这可以改变十二年内的账单数量以及可保存的时间。成本增长仅持续到每个修改后的付款日期。根据状况评估、报价和已完成的工作更新库存。为选定时间表之外的事件保留应急缓冲，并避免在两个储备中计算相同的起始现金。公寓或分契物业的义务需要相关的建筑文件和规则；这个家庭插图没有计算它们。

13e3580b956255b75bebe87c6ce10e14e06e574d.src: Fund the gross gift when it is paid. Count a tax saving only when it can actually free cash for the budget, and keep it separate from the gift itself. Start with the cash commitment to the recipient A donation pledge belongs in the household budget at its gross amount. A later tax saving can affect household cash, but it does not reduce the amount the recipient needs to receive on the gift date. The CRA’s donor guidance explains the role of registered charities, other qualified donees and official donation receipts. A payment to an organization does not automatically establish an individual’s usable credit. The CRA’s Gifts and Income Tax guide for 2025 describes donation credits as non-refundable and based on eligible gifts. This article uses that general context without applying 2025 rates to a later year. It calculates no federal or provincial credit, eligibility limit or actual tax refund. Compare three schedules with the same annual gift total The default monthly gift is CAD 200. Over one year that is CAD 2,400, and over the full twenty-four months the recipient receives CAD 4,800. Three schedules preserve those annual totals. The monthly schedule pays CAD 200 at each month’s start. The year-start alternative pays CAD 2,400 at the start of months one and thirteen. The year-end alternative pays CAD 2,400 at the start of months twelve and twenty-four, the final month of each modeled year. Other household budget surplus contributes CAD 150 at each month-end. That amount is available after the household’s other commitments. It must not already include the tax saving entered in the separate control, or the same resource would be counted twice. Enter a usable saving and its arrival date independently The default assumes CAD 600 attributable to first-year gifts becomes usable at the end of month sixteen. This amount is an independent scenario input, rather than a tax calculation or a promise that a refund arrives then. A non-refundable credit may reduce tax otherwise payable. Depending on the broader return and payments already made, the household effect can be a smaller payment rather than a cash refund. Include only the amount that can actually become available to this giving budget, at the appropriate time. The illustration caps the entered saving at first-year gifts and sets it to zero when there are no gifts. That is a modeling convention, not a statutory credit limit. No tax benefit from second-year gifts is received within the horizon, and no carryforward or gift of appreciated property is modeled. Measure the lowest cash point before later resources arrive With monthly gifts, the plan needs CAD 950 of starting cash under the default assumptions. Starting cash is CAD 1,000, leaving a lowest modeled balance of CAD 50. Gifts are paid before that month’s budget surplus and any assumed tax saving. The year-start schedule needs CAD 3,000 at the start because its second annual gift falls before the assumed saving arrives. The year-end schedule needs CAD 750 because more monthly budget contributions accumulate before each gift. These are timing comparisons, not rankings of generosity or impact. The cash lines show the point just after month-start gifts. Month-end resources have not yet arrived at each plotted point. After all month-twenty-four resources, every schedule ends at CAD 400: CAD 1,000 starting cash plus CAD 3,600 of budget contributions and CAD 600 of usable saving, less CAD 4,800 of gifts. Keep the two-year cash measure separate from lifetime cost The waterfall shows CAD 4,800 of gifts less the one CAD 600 saving realized inside the horizon, giving CAD 4,200 of net gift cash outflow. It is not the lifetime after-tax cost of both years’ donations, because any later second-year benefit is outside the schedule. The matrix varies the usable saving and when it arrives in year two. It shows total starting cash required for monthly gifts. An earlier or larger usable saving can ease later cash needs, but it cannot pay an earlier gift retroactively. Before committing, confirm the recipient, the intended amount, gift dates, receipt treatment and a conservative usable tax assumption. Retain the gross commitment in the budget even if the saving is uncertain. The charts organize those cash decisions while leaving actual tax calculations and the choice of recipient outside the model.
13e3580b956255b75bebe87c6ce10e14e06e574d.zh: 支付总礼物后，为其提供资金。只有当它实际上可以为预算节省现金时才算节税，并将其与礼物本身分开。从对接受者的现金承诺开始 捐赠承诺的总额属于家庭预算。稍后的节税可能会影响家庭现金，但不会减少接受者在礼物日期需要收到的金额。 CRA 的捐赠指南解释了注册慈善机构、其他合格受赠者和官方捐赠收据的作用。向组织付款并不会自动建立个人的可用信用。 CRA 的 2025 年礼品和所得税指南将捐赠抵免描述为不可退还，且基于符合条件的礼品。本文使用了一般背景，但没有将 2025 年的费率应用于以后的一年。它不计算联邦或省信用、资格限额或实际退税。比较具有相同年度礼物总额的三个计划 默认每月礼物为 200 加元。一年以上为 2,400 加元，在完整的 24 个月内，接收者收到 4,800 加元。三个时间表保留了这些年度总数。每月计划在每个月开始时支付 200 加元。年初替代方案在第一个月和第十三个月开始时支付 2,400 加元。年终替代方案在第 12 个月和第 24 个月（每个模拟年份的最后一个月）开始时支付 2,400 加元。其他家庭预算盈余在每个月底贡献 150 加元。该金额在家庭做出其他承诺后即可使用。它不得已包括在单独控件中输入的节税，否则同一资源将被计算两次。单独输入可用储蓄及其到达日期 默认情况下，第一年礼物的 600 加元在第 16 个月末可用。该金额是一个独立的场景输入，而不是税收计算或退款到达的承诺。不可退还的抵免额可以减少其他应缴税款。根据更广泛的回报和已支付的付款，家庭效应可能是较小的付款而不是现金退款。仅包括在适当的时间实际可以用于此捐赠预算的金额。该插图限制了第一年礼物中输入的储蓄上限，并在没有礼物时将其设置为零。这是一个建模惯例，而不是法定信用限额。短期内不会收到第二年赠与的税收优惠，也不会模拟升值财产的结转或赠与。在后续资源到达之前衡量最低现金点 对于每月赠品，该计划在默认假设下需要 950 加元的起始现金。起始现金为 1,000 加元，最低模型余额为 50 加元。礼品在当月预算盈余和任何假设的节税之前支付。年初计划一开始就需要 3,000 加元，因为第二份年度礼物在假定的节省到达之前就已发放。年终计划需要 750 加元，因为每次捐赠之前都会积累更多的每月预算捐款。这些是时间比较，而不是慷慨程度或影响力的排名。现金行显示了月初礼物之后的要点。月末资源尚未到达每个标绘点。扣除所有 24 个月的资源后，每个计划的最终金额为 400 加元：1,000 加元的起始现金加上 3,600 加元的预算捐款和 600 加元的可用储蓄，减去 4,800 加元的礼物。将两年现金指标与终生成本分开 瀑布显示 4,800 加元的礼物减去在地平线上实现的 600 加元的节省，从而产生 4,200 加元的净礼物现金流出。这不是两年捐赠的终生税后成本，因为任何后来的第二年福利都不在计划范围内。该矩阵改变了可用储蓄以及第二年到达的时间。它显示每月礼物所需的起始现金总额。较早或较大的可用储蓄可以缓解以后的现金需求，但不能追溯支付较早的礼物。在做出承诺之前，请确认收件人、预期金额、礼物日期、收据处理和保守的可用税收假设。即使节约不确定，也要保留预算中的总承诺。这些图表组织了这些现金决策，同时将实际的税收计算和接收者的选择保留在模型之外。

e61b6ca1a27c7cef31b3d9d8a81c9252eaa0383b.src: Agree on the shared budget first. Then compare how each assignment rule fits both people’s resources and separate commitments. Define what belongs in the shared commitment A household can agree on a percentage split and still disagree about what that percentage covers. Start with a common list of bills, then decide which savings transfers are also shared commitments. Keep separate personal obligations visible alongside that list. The FCAC’s guide to managing money as a couple describes different arrangements for sharing expenses and suggests discussing transfer timing, contribution percentages and a potential loss of income. The right arrangement depends on the people and their circumstances. This example focuses on monthly allocation arithmetic. Shared bills are CAD 4,000 and the agreed shared savings transfer is CAD 800. Together they require CAD 4,800 each month. The transfer remains an asset, but it is committed cash for this budget rather than money available for another bill. Compare equal amounts with shares of take-home income Person A has CAD 5,000 of monthly take-home income; Person B has CAD 3,000. Under equal shares, each is assigned CAD 2,400 of the shared total. Under the income rule, A earns 62.5% of the combined CAD 8,000 and B earns 37.5%. Applying those weights to CAD 4,800 assigns A CAD 3,000 and B CAD 1,800. The formula uses take-home income before separate personal commitments. Both rules assign exactly CAD 4,800. The grouped bars show who is assigned the money, not a saving produced by the rule. Neither rule is automatically fair in every household: unpaid work, income stability, personal obligations and the agreed purpose of savings can all matter to the discussion. Check each person after their separate commitments The default separate commitments are CAD 500 for A and CAD 300 for B. After those amounts and equal shared assignments, A has CAD 2,100 left and B has CAD 300. Under income shares, A has CAD 1,500 and B has CAD 900. Those individual remainders explain why the same shared total can feel different under two rules. Equal amounts consume 48% of A’s take-home income and 80% of B’s; income shares consume 60% of each income in this particular example, before separate obligations. The income-check chart deliberately compares amounts rather than percentages. If an income becomes zero, a percentage burden would be undefined. An assignment above the income bar is clearly unfunded even before separate commitments. A smaller assignment can still be unaffordable once those other commitments are deducted. Keep the household balance separate from the allocation Combined take-home income is CAD 8,000. Subtracting CAD 800 of separate commitments leaves CAD 7,200. After CAD 4,000 of shared bills and the CAD 800 savings transfer, CAD 2,400 remains unassigned. The waterfall gives the same endpoint under both rules. Reassigning a bill between people cannot create household income or reduce the amount paid to a landlord, utility or savings account. If the endpoint is negative, the entered plan has an unmet household need. A positive household endpoint can coexist with one person’s shortage. Resolving that situation requires an explicit agreement about contributions, transfers or commitments. The model does not assume that one person automatically covers the other’s obligations or that money in an account is legally shared. Use the matrix to discuss changes before they happen The matrix replaces A’s income and scales the shared total while holding B’s income selected. Each cell shows A’s income-based assignment minus an equal half. A positive number assigns A more than half; a negative number assigns less. Neither sign measures whether a household is better off. If both entered incomes are zero, the current income-weighted comparison is omitted because there is no income share to calculate. Equal assignment remains visible, with the household cash shortage shown separately. The matrix still describes its explicitly hypothetical positive A-income cases. Agree when to revisit the arrangement: a job change, leave, irregular pay or a changed savings goal may alter what is workable. Match transfers to actual bill dates as well as monthly totals. This tool does not determine taxes, benefits, joint borrowing liability, property ownership or account access; those questions need their own facts and applicable rules.
e61b6ca1a27c7cef31b3d9d8a81c9252eaa0383b.zh: 首先就共享预算达成一致。然后比较每个分配规则如何适合人们的资源和单独的承诺。定义共同承诺的内容 家庭可以就百分比分配达成一致，但仍然对该百分比所涵盖的内容存在分歧。从共同的账单清单开始，然后决定哪些储蓄转移也是共同承诺。在该列表旁边保留单独的个人义务。 FCAC 的夫妻资金管理指南描述了分摊费用的不同安排，并建议讨论转账时间、缴款百分比和潜在的收入损失。正确的安排取决于人和他们的情况。此示例重点介绍每月分配算法。共享账单为 4,000 加元，商定的共享储蓄转账为 800 加元。每月总共需要 4,800 加元。这笔转移仍然是一项资产，但它是用于该预算的现金，而不是可用于另一项法案的资金。将等额金额与实得收入份额进行比较 A 的月实得​​收入为 5,000 加元； B 拥有 3,000 加元。在均等分配的情况下，每人分配到共享总额中的 2,400 加元。根据收入规则，A 赚取 8,000 加元总额的 62.5%，B 赚取 37.5%。将这些权重应用到 4,800 加元，分配 A 为 3,000 加元，B 分配为 1,800 加元。该公式使用在单独的个人承诺之前的实得收入。两条规则都分配了 4,800 加元。分组的条形图显示分配给谁的钱，而不是规则产生的节省。这两条规则都不一定对每个家庭都是公平的：无偿工作、收入稳定性、个人义务和商定的储蓄目的都对讨论很重要。检查每个人各自的承诺。默认的单独承诺是 A 500 加元，B 300 加元。在这些金额和平等共享分配之后，A 剩下 2,100 加元，B 剩下 300 加元。在收入分成下，A 剩下 1,500 加元，B 剩下 900 加元。这些单独的剩余部分解释了为什么相同的共享总额在两种规则下会感觉不同。等量消耗了 A 的实得收入的 48%，B 的 80%；在这个特定的例子中，在单独的义务之前，收入份额消耗了每项收入的 60%。收入检查图表有意比较金额而不是百分比。如果收入为零，则负担百分比将不确定。即使在单独的承诺之前，收入水平以上的任务显然也没有资金支持。一旦扣除其他承诺，较小的任务仍然无法承担。将家庭余额与分配分开 合并实得收入为 8,000 加元。减去单独承诺的 800 加元，剩下 7,200 加元。在 4,000 加元的共享账单和 800 加元的储蓄转账之后，还有 2,400 加元仍未分配。瀑布在两种规则下给出相同的端点。在人们之间重新分配账单不能创造家庭收入或减少支付给房东、公用事业或储蓄账户的金额。如果终点为负，则输入的计划有未满足的家庭需求。积极的家庭终点可以与一个人的短缺共存。解决这种情况需要就捐款、转移或承诺达成明确的协议。该模型并不假设一个人自动承担另一个人的义务，也不假设账户中的资金是合法共享的。使用矩阵在变化发生之前对其进行讨论 该矩阵替换 A 的收入并调整共享总额，同时保持选择 B 的收入。每个单元格显示 A 的基于收入的分配减去一半。正数表示 A 超过一半；负数分配较少。这两个指标都无法衡量一个家庭的境况是否变得更好。如果输入的收入均为零，则忽略当前收入加权比较，因为没有可计算的收入份额。平等分配仍然显而易见，家庭现金短缺情况单独显示。该矩阵仍然描述了其明确假设的正 A 收入案例。商定何时重新考虑安排：工作变动、休假、工资不规律或储蓄目标的改变可能会改变可行的方案。将转账与实际账单日期以及每月总额相匹配。该工具无法确定税收、福利、联合借款责任、财产所有权或账户访问权限；这些问题需要有自己的事实和适用的规则。

5e10b066032cb84523d041fdef45023d7f3eefce.src: Start with the full purchase cash requirement, subtract the credited deposit once, then compare the remaining amount with cash actually available now. Use the price-based minimum as a starting point The Financial Consumer Agency of Canada’s down-payment table sets out a basic price-based minimum: 5% for a home costing CAD 500,000 or less. Above that price and below CAD 1.5 million, the calculation is CAD 25,000 plus 10% of the portion over CAD 500,000. At CAD 1.5 million or more, the basic minimum becomes 20% of the entire purchase price. The first chart uses separate price examples to show that threshold. Immediately below CAD 1.5 million the basic amount is about CAD 125,000; at CAD 1.5 million it is CAD 300,000. This is a narrow rule illustration. A lender can require more, and the cash calculation does not assess income, credit, the property, or mortgage qualification. The selected down payment cannot fall below the basic minimum in this model. Treat the deposit as part of the price already funded The hypothetical home costs CAD 700,000. A requested 10% down payment is CAD 70,000, above the basic CAD 45,000 minimum. A CAD 20,000 deposit has already been paid and is assumed credited toward that same purchase price. The down payment still due is therefore CAD 50,000. Adding the deposit to CAD 70,000 again would count the same purchase funding twice. The waterfall first shows the complete cash requirement and then subtracts the credited deposit once. The tool assumes the whole deposit is credited without a refund. If it exceeds the requested down payment, the modeled down payment increases to include it; a deposit above the price is capped at the price. Real contract terms and adjustments need confirmation. A deposit’s due date also matters: money needed before closing must already be accessible then. Give closing costs their own budget lines The default uses a 3% closing-cost allowance, or CAD 21,000, plus CAD 2,000 of additional fixed closing costs and CAD 5,000 for moving and setup. These are hypothetical placeholders. The percentage does not calculate a provincial transfer tax or establish the actual legal bill. Replace allowances with quotes and a closing statement as those become available. Ensure the fixed-cost line excludes items already covered by the percentage allowance. A practical ledger records the description, amount, due date and source of each charge. CMHC explains mortgage loan insurance and the possibility of paying a premium upfront or financing it. This tool calculates neither premiums nor taxes on them. Add confirmed cash charges once to the appropriate allowance; a financed amount needs a separate mortgage analysis. Retained cash is still part of the funding requirement The example deliberately retains CAD 10,000 after closing. That money remains an asset, but it must be funded if the purchase is to leave the intended reserve intact. Calling it a closing fee would misdescribe it; leaving it out would hide the desired cash cushion. The total requirement is CAD 108,000: CAD 70,000 down, CAD 21,000 closing allowance, CAD 2,000 fixed costs, CAD 5,000 setup and CAD 10,000 reserve. Subtracting the CAD 20,000 credited deposit leaves CAD 88,000 to cover. Cash available now is CAD 80,000 after the deposit has been paid. The additional amount to arrange is CAD 8,000. Entering the pre-deposit bank balance would wrongly make the paid deposit appear available a second time. Test the price and down payment before committing the cash The remaining-requirement bars show where the CAD 88,000 goes. The matrix then varies price and the requested down-payment percentage. The basic rule and deposit floor continue to apply, so requesting a smaller percentage does not bypass them. A higher down payment increases cash committed to the property, while a price increase can also raise the percentage-based closing allowance. The matrix keeps fixed costs and current available cash unchanged. It does not estimate local taxes, future selling costs or investment returns. Review the payment calendar alongside this total. Funds tied up in another property, a pending withdrawal or an investment sale may arrive after a deposit or closing obligation. A zero modeled shortfall means the entered cash lines balance; it does not establish borrowing capacity or the affordability of ongoing ownership.
5e10b066032cb84523d041fdef45023d7f3eefce.zh: 从全额购买现金要求开始，减去一次存入的押金，然后将剩余金额与现在实际可用的现金进行比较。使用基于价格的最低限额作为起点加拿大金融消费者管理局的首付表规定了基于价格的基本最低限额：对于价格为 500,000 加元或以下的房屋，首付比例为 5%。高于该价格且低于 150 万加元的，计算为 25,000 加元加上 50 万加元以上部分的 10%。如果金额为 150 万加元或以上，则基本最低金额为总购买价格的 20%。第一个图表使用单独的价格示例来显示该阈值。紧接着150万加元以下，基本金额约为125,000加元； 150万加元是30万加元。这是一个狭义的规则说明。贷款机构可以要求更多，并且现金计算不评估收入、信用、财产或抵押贷款资格。所选首付不能低于该模型中的基本最低金额。将押金视为已提供资金的价格的一部分 假设的房屋成本为 700,000 加元。要求支付 10% 的首付为 70,000 加元，高于基本最低 45,000 加元。 20,000 加元的押金已支付，并假定计入相同的购买价格。因此，尚需支付的首付款为 50,000 加元。再次将押金添加到 70,000 加元，则相同的购买资金将被计算两次。瀑布首先显示完整的现金需求，然后减去一次记入的存款。该工具假设全部押金已存入且不予退款。如果超过了要求的首付款，则模型中的首付款会增加以包含该首付款；高于价格的押金以该价格为上限。真正的合同条款和调整需要确认。押金的到期日也很重要：成交前所需的资金必须已经可以使用。为结算成本提供自己的预算线 默认情况下使用 3% 的结算成本津贴，即 21,000 加元，加上 2,000 加元的额外固定结算成本以及 5,000 加元的移动和设置费用。这些是假设的占位符。该百分比不计算省转让税或确定实际的法律账单。当报价和结束语可用时，用报价和结束语替换津贴。确保固定成本行不包括百分比补贴已涵盖的项目。实用的分类账记录了每项费用的描述、金额、到期日和来源。 CMHC 解释了抵押贷款保险以及预付保费或融资的可能性。该工具既不计算保费也不计算税收。将确认的现金费用添加到适当的津贴中一次；融资金额需要单独的抵押贷款分析。保留现金仍然是资金需求的一部分 该示例在成交后故意保留 10,000 加元。这笔钱仍然是一种资产，但如果购买要保持预期储备完好无损，就必须为其提供资金。称其为成交费是错误的描述。忽略它会隐藏所需的现金缓冲。总需求为 108,000 加元：70,000 加元首付、21,000 加元结账津贴、2,000 加元固定成本、5,000 加元设置和 10,000 加元储备金。减去存入的 20,000 加元押金，还剩下 88,000 加元。支付押金后，现在可用现金为 80,000 加元。额外安排金额为 8,000 加元。输入预存款银行余额会错误地使已支付的存款再次显示为可用。在投入现金之前测试价格和首付 剩余需求栏显示 88,000 加元的去向。然后，该矩阵会改变价格和要求的首付百分比。基本规则和存款下限继续适用，因此请求较小的百分比并不能绕过它们。较高的首付会增加投入该房产的现金，而价格上涨也可以提高基于百分比的结算津贴。该矩阵保持固定成本和当前可用现金不变。它不估计地方税、未来销售成本或投资回报。与此总额一起查看付款日历。占用其他财产、待提款或投资出售的资金可能会在存款或交割义务之后到达。零模型缺口意味着输入的现金额度余额；它不建立借贷能力或持续所有权的承受能力。

d224089a869f34d318a2c819ec2b433d6fb7fe99.src: Separate each balance, rate and payment obligation. A zero future-interest rate reduces borrowing costs but does not make the opening amount disappear. Separate the federal rule from other education borrowing The National Student Loans Service Centre’s current-interest-rate explanation states that accumulation of interest on Canada Student Loans was permanently eliminated effective 1 April 2023. That rule concerns federal student loans, not every debt used to pay for education. Provincial or territorial loans and private borrowing can have different terms. The model therefore keeps the Canada Student Loan amount at zero new interest and gives a second education-debt balance its own hypothetical rate. The default 6% for that second balance is an assumption, not a quoted provincial or bank rate. Enter current amounts owed. Any earlier accrued amount still payable must remain in the opening ledger. This illustration calculates future interest and payments; it does not decide how a servicer applies payments between historical interest, principal or portions of an integrated loan. Put the first payment date into the post-study budget Canada’s repayment-start guide describes a six-month non-repayment period after leaving school and directs borrowers to their loan terms and the relevant servicer. That interval is different from a permanent absence of payment obligations. The charts begin when repayment starts. They do not simulate the study period, a waiting-period interest convention or the date a specific person’s payment is due. Confirm the opening balance, required payment, first due date and payment channel from the actual account. A new graduate’s monthly plan may also need housing deposits, work transport and irregular setup costs. Enter the amount available for loan payments after those other commitments, rather than treating the full first paycheque as disposable cash. Turn each opening balance into an illustrative payment The default has CAD 20,000 of Canada Student Loan debt and CAD 10,000 of other education debt. Both use 120 illustrative monthly repayment periods. That selected term is a modeling choice, not a statement of the official default schedule or an approved repayment option. At zero new interest, CAD 20,000 divided by 120 is CAD 166.666… per month. Rounding the scheduled payment up to cents gives CAD 166.67, with a smaller final payment. The other balance at a hypothetical 6% nominal annual rate requires CAD 111.03 under the model’s monthly-interest convention. The combined scheduled amount is CAD 277.70. Against the default CAD 300 monthly budget, the model shows no shortfall and CAD 22.30 remains outside these scheduled payments. Changing the budget control does not change an obligation or authorize a lower payment; it only changes the comparison. Read principal repayment and borrowing cost separately The stacked bars show opening amounts and new modeled interest. The federal bar has no new-interest segment, but the CAD 20,000 still needs to be repaid. Removing interest reduces the cost above that opening amount rather than removing the balance itself. The balance paths use the same selected horizon. The zero-rate component declines in equal scheduled amounts until the capped final payment. On the interest-bearing component, part of each early payment covers interest, so the principal reduction grows as the outstanding balance falls. The calculation charges the selected nominal annual rate divided by 12 before each month-end payment. Actual loan statements may use daily interest, different payment dates, changing rates or integrated payment-allocation rules. The paths are transparent comparisons, not a reproduction of a servicer’s statement. Compare a lower monthly payment with a longer commitment The matrix varies the other-debt rate and the illustrative term for both balances. Federal new interest stays zero. A longer term spreads its opening amount over more payments without adding new federal interest under the selected rule. For interest-bearing debt, a longer term can reduce the scheduled monthly amount while increasing total interest. A smaller payment is therefore only one part of the choice. Compare total cost, the length of the commitment and the budget’s ability to absorb changes. The tool excludes repayment assistance, forgiveness, tax credits, missed payments and future policy changes. If the actual payment does not fit the budget, review the servicer’s available options and eligibility before changing payments. Keep this modeled schedule separate from an approved arrangement and refresh it when actual balances or terms change.
d224089a869f34d318a2c819ec2b433d6fb7fe99.zh: 将每个余额、费率和付款义务分开。未来利率为零会降低借贷成本，但不会使期初金额消失。将联邦规则与其他教育借款分开国家学生贷款服务中心的现行利率解释指出，自 2023 年 4 月 1 日起，加拿大学生贷款的利息累积将被永久取消。该规则涉及联邦学生贷款，而不是用于支付教育费用的所有债务。省或地区贷款和私人借款可以有不同的条款。因此，该模型将加拿大学生贷款金额保持在零新利息，并为第二个教育债务余额提供了自己的假设利率。第二个余额的默认 6% 是一个假设，而不是省级或银行报价。输入当前欠款金额。任何仍应付的早期应计金额必须保留在期初分类账中。该图计算了未来的利息和付款；它不决定服务机构如何在历史利息、本金或综合贷款的部分之间进行支付。将首次还款日期纳入毕业后预算加拿大的还款开始指南描述了离开学校后六个月的免还款期，并指导借款人了解其贷款条款和相关服务机构。该间隔不同于永久不履行付款义务。当还款开始时，图表开始。它们不会模拟研究期、等待期利息约定或特定人付款到期的日期。从实际账户确认期初余额、所需付款、首次到期日和付款渠道。应届毕业生的每月计划可能还需要住房押金、工作交通和不定期的安装费用。在其他承诺之后输入可用于贷款支付的金额，而不是将第一张工资支票视为可支配现金。将每笔期初余额转为说明性付款 违约的加拿大学生贷款债务为 20,000 加元，其他教育债务为 10,000 加元。两者都使用 120 个示例性每月还款期。该选定的条款是一种建模选择，而不是官方默认时间表或批准的还款选项的声明。如果新利息为零，20,000 加元除以 120 就是每月 166.666 加元。将预定付款四舍五入为美分，得出 166.67 加元，最终付款金额较小。根据该模型的月利息惯例，假定名义年利率为 6% 的其他余额需要 111.03 加元。预计总金额为 277.70 加元。与默认的 300 加元每月预算相比，该模型显示没有缺口，并且 22.30 加元仍超出这些计划付款。改变预算控制并不改变义务或授权较低的付款；它只会改变比较。分别读取本金偿还和借贷成本堆叠条显示期初金额和新模型的利息。联邦律师协会没有新增利息部分，但2万加元仍需偿还。去除利息会降低高于开仓金额的成本，而不是去除余额本身。平衡路径使用相同的选定范围。零利率部分以相同的预定金额下降，直到达到上限的最终付款为止。在计息部分，每笔提前付款的一部分都包含利息，因此本金减少随着未偿余额的下降而增加。计算方法是在每个月末付款前将选定的名义年利率除以 12。实际贷款报表可能使用每日利息、不同的付款日期、变化的利率或综合付款分配规则。这些路径是透明的比较，而不是服务人员声明的复制。将较低的每月还款额与较长的承诺进行比较 该矩阵改变了其他债务率和两种余额的说明性期限。联邦新利息保持为零。较长期限将其期初金额分摊到更多付款中，而不会根据所选规则增加新的联邦利息。对于有息债务，期限较长可以减少每月预定金额，同时增加总利息。因此，较小的付款只是选择的一部分。比较总成本、承诺期限和预算吸收变化的能力。该工具不包括还款援助、宽恕、税收抵免、逾期付款和未来的政策变化。如果实际付款不符合预算，请在更改付款之前检查服务机构的可用选项和资格。将此建模时间表与已批准的安排分开，并在实际余额或条款发生变化时刷新它。

cb786dc5abc35d3acd251d3080ac5656f380d545.src: Use an average to frame the question, then replace it with the actual tuition quote and add the other costs. A tuition figure alone cannot establish how much cash a student needs. Read the official numbers with their population and period Statistics Canada’s Table 37-10-0045-01 reports preliminary 2026/2027 national undergraduate tuition averages of CAD 8,021 for Canadian students and CAD 42,062 for international students. The first graphic presents those published observations, rather than values calculated from the budget controls. These are weighted averages for full-time students at public degree-granting institutions, expressed in current dollars. They are tuition amounts, not complete living budgets or individual program quotations. The difference between the groups can reflect different program and institution mixes. The ten-province graphic shows the Canadian undergraduate observations from the same release. It includes no territory. A province’s bar is not the price every student pays there, and a lower average does not rank the quality or overall affordability of a particular program. Keep a weighted average separate from a personal quote The survey methodology explains how institutions report fees and how enrolment weights are used to combine them. The current table uses 2023/2024 enrolment weights. The national estimate is not a simple average of the provincial bars. A weighted mean is also different from a median. These bars do not say that half of students pay less than the displayed amount, and they provide no price range for a particular program. Program mix and residency treatment also affect comparisons. Some provincial averages incorporate different fees for in-province and out-of-province Canadian students. The source marks the current academic year preliminary, even though the selected CSV status cells are blank. The data were released on 16 September 2026 and retrieved for this article on 25 October 2026. The two observation charts remain fixed when the controls change. For a personal plan, replace the editable tuition value with the institution’s quote and confirm which fees that quote includes. Add the costs that tuition does not cover The default budget starts at the published CAD 8,021 Canadian undergraduate national average. The remaining amounts are hypothetical: CAD 1,000 of additional compulsory fees, CAD 1,000 of books and equipment, and CAD 1,000 of travel and setup. Living and local transport are budgeted at CAD 1,400 a month for eight months, adding CAD 11,200. The resulting modeled total is CAD 22,221. Tuition is about 36.10% of this particular example; that share is not a population estimate of what students generally spend. The waterfall expresses all the cost lines and confirmed funding in CAD. Check for overlap when entering real amounts: a residence package might already include food, or a quoted fee might already include a compulsory charge. Each actual cost belongs in the ledger once. Subtract confirmed resources without treating borrowing as a price reduction The example enters CAD 12,000 of confirmed funding, leaving CAD 10,221 to arrange under the selected budget. The funding input does not calculate grants, scholarships, tax benefits, family support or loan approval. A loan can supply cash for a bill while creating a separate repayment obligation. If borrowing is included in confirmed funding, the budget gap may close without the underlying education cost becoming smaller. Record that repayment plan separately. A negative waterfall endpoint means entered funding exceeds this budget; the additional-funding metric is then floored at zero. The tool assigns no destination to the surplus. A zero-cost example reports that no modeled cost share is available rather than dividing by zero. Test the living-cost calendar and revise the plan The matrix varies monthly living costs and the number of months to cover. Tuition, fees, books, setup and confirmed funding remain selected. A twelve-month living plan therefore adds summer costs without automatically changing the tuition entry. The model does not prorate tuition when the living-cost duration changes. Tuition schedules can depend on programs, credits, terms and status, so the quote needs its own review. The matrix contains hypothetical allowances and is not an accommodation-price survey. Use the observed averages as context, then build a dated personal cost and funding list. The charts distinguish an official statistical benchmark from the cash a particular plan needs, while leaving enrolment choices, funding approval and account-withdrawal rules to their own evidence.
cb786dc5abc35d3acd251d3080ac5656f380d545.zh: 使用平均值来构建问题，然后将其替换为实际的学费报价并添加其他费用。仅凭学费数字并不能确定学生需要多少现金。请阅读包含人口和时期的官方数据加拿大统计局的表 37-10-0045-01 报告了 2026/2027 年全国本科生平均学费初步数据，加拿大学生为 8,021 加元，国际学生为 42,062 加元。第一张图显示了那些已发表的观察结果，而不是根据预算控制计算出的值。这些是公立学位授予机构全日制学生的加权平均值，以现价美元表示。它们是学费金额，而不是完整的生活预算或个别课程报价。各组之间的差异可以反映不同的项目和机构组合。十个省的图表显示了同一版本中加拿大本科生的观察结果。它不包括任何领土。一个省的标准并不是每个学生在那里支付的价格，较低的平均价格并不能对特定项目的质量或整体负担能力进行排名。将加权平均值与个人报价分开调查方法解释了机构如何报告费用以及如何使用入学权重将它们结合起来。当前表格使用 2023/2024 年入学权重。全国的估算并不是各省酒吧的简单平均。加权平均值也不同于中位数。这些酒吧并没有说一半的学生支付的费用低于显示的金额，并且他们没有提供特定课程的价格范围。项目组合和住院医师待遇也会影响比较。一些省份的平均费用包含了加拿大省内和省外学生的不同费用。尽管所选的 CSV 状态单元格为空白，但源将当前学年标记为初步。数据于 2026 年 9 月 16 日发布，并于 2026 年 10 月 25 日为本文检索。当控件发生变化时，两个观测图保持固定。对于个人计划，请将可编辑的学费值替换为机构的报价，并确认报价包含哪些费用。添加学费未涵盖的费用 默认预算起始于公布的加拿大本科生全国平均水平 8,021 加元。其余金额为假设金额：1,000 加元的额外强制费用、1,000 加元的书籍和设备费用以及 1,000 加元的差旅和安装费用。生活和当地交通预算为每月 1,400 加元，持续 8 个月，增加 11,200 加元。模型得出的总金额为 22,221 加元。学费约为该特定示例的 36.10%；这个比例并不是对学生总体支出的总体估计。瀑布以加元表示所有成本线和已确认的资金。输入实际金额时检查是否重叠：居住套餐可能已经包含食物，或者报价的费用可能已经包含强制收费。每个实际成本只属于分类账一次。减去已确认的资源，而不将借款视为降价 该示例输入 12,000 加元的已确认资金，留下 10,221 加元可根据选定的预算进行安排。资金投入不计算助学金、奖学金、税收优惠、家庭支持或贷款批准。贷款可以为账单提供现金，同时产生单独的还款义务。如果借款包含在已确认的资金中，预算缺口可能会缩小，而基础教育成本不会变小。单独记录该还款计划。负瀑布终点意味着输入的资金超出了该预算；然后，额外资金指标将降至零。该工具没有为盈余指定目的地。零成本示例报告没有可用的建模成本份额，而不是除以零。测试生活费用日历并修改计划 该矩阵会改变每月的生活费用和需要支付的月数。学费、杂费、书籍、设置和确认的资金仍处于选择状态。因此，十二个月的生活计划会增加夏季费用，但不会自动更改学费条目。当生活费用持续时间发生变化时，该模型不会按比例分配学费。学费表可能取决于课程、学分、条款和状态，因此报价需要单独审核。该矩阵包含假设的津贴，并不是住宿价格调查。使用观察到的平均值作为背景，然后建立一个注明日期的个人成本和资金清单。这些图表将官方统计基准与特定计划所需的现金区分开来，同时将注册选择、资金批准和账户取款规则留给自己的证据。

4757a911df5230431bf9da693980abe0a07aa83c.src: A low starting rate is one input. Include the transfer fee, the amount left when the promotion ends and the payment schedule before comparing borrowing costs. Read what the offer applies to and when it ends The FCAC’s credit-card guide explains balance-transfer fees and promotions that apply for a specified period. It also distinguishes purchase grace periods from balance transfers, which do not receive that purchase grace period. This model isolates one transferred debt. There are no new purchases, cash advances or competing rate buckets. The transfer fee is added to the opening balance and receives the same modeled rate. An actual agreement can treat fees and payments differently. The promotional rate applies for a selected number of monthly cycles. The follow-on rate then applies to remaining debt prospectively. The model includes neither retroactive interest nor the consequences of losing a promotion through a missed payment. All rates and terms are hypothetical. Include the fee in the amount that needs repayment The default current balance is CAD 10,000 at a 20% nominal annual rate. A transfer fee of 3% adds CAD 300, so the alternative starts with CAD 10,300 of debt. A zero promotional rate does not remove that fee. The selected payment is CAD 400 at each month-end. With twelve promotional cycles at 0%, those payments reduce the transferred balance by CAD 4,800. CAD 5,500 therefore remains when the promotion ends. From the next cycle, the example charges a 22% nominal annual rate divided by twelve on remaining debt before the payment. Actual cards can calculate daily interest and use different payment allocation rules. The illustration uses one explicit monthly convention so the schedule can be inspected. Solve the payment needed to clear during the promotion The second metric calculates a constant monthly amount that would repay the fee-inclusive balance within the promotional cycles. At 0%, CAD 10,300 divided by twelve is CAD 858.333… per month. The tool rounds up to CAD 858.34, with the final payment capped at the remaining amount. Rounding down to CAD 858.33 would leave four cents after twelve payments. That amount is more than the selected CAD 400 payment. The difference explains why the default schedule continues beyond the promotion. At a positive promotional rate, the tool uses the fixed-payment amortization formula rather than simply dividing principal by months. If zero promotional cycles are selected, the new balance begins at the follow-on rate and no within-promotion payment is reported. A zero original debt creates no transfer fee in the model. The metric does not determine affordability or replace actual minimum-payment requirements. Compare the complete schedule when it is available Under the defaults, the current balance clears in month thirty-three and incurs approximately CAD 3,044.21 of interest. The transferred balance clears in month twenty-eight, with approximately CAD 895.35 of interest and the CAD 300 fee. The transfer’s modeled borrowing cost is therefore CAD 1,195.35, about CAD 1,848.86 below the current-card cost under these assumptions. Original principal is excluded from both cost bars because it must be repaid either way. Interest on the financed fee is already included in the interest component. The charts stop at payoff or 120 months. A “Not repaid” metric means the model did not clear that balance within the limit. Charges for an incomplete schedule are partial and cannot be called a full repayment cost. The matrix uses NR instead of reporting a full-life cost for such cases. Test the payment and the time available The matrix changes monthly payments and promotional cycles while holding the original balance, fee and rates fixed. Each completed cell shows total interest plus the fee. A larger promotional window helps only within the entered repayment schedule and assumptions. The comparison keeps the same fixed payment while each balance remains outstanding. It does not invest money released after earlier payoff, add an annual card fee or simulate new spending. Those effects belong in a wider household comparison if they apply. The FCAC notes that missed payments can cause the loss of promotional terms. Check the agreement, transaction types, fee treatment, minimum payments and expiry dates before relying on an actual offer. The four graphics explain a cost schedule without treating a headline rate as a complete borrowing decision.
4757a911df5230431bf9da693980abe0a07aa83c.zh: 低起始率是一种输入。在比较借贷成本之前，请包括转让费、促销结束时剩余的金额以及付款时间表。了解优惠适用范围及结束时间 FCAC 信用卡指南解释了特定期间适用的余额转账费用和促销活动。它还将购买宽限期与余额转账区分开来，后者不享受购买宽限期。该模型隔离了一笔转移债务。没有新的购买、预支现金或竞争利率。转账费将添加到期初余额中，并获得相同的模型费率。实际协议可以以不同的方式对待费用和付款。促销费率适用于选定的每月周期数。然后后续利率适用于未来的剩余债务。该模型既不包括追溯利息，也不包括因错过付款而失去促销的后果。所有费率和条款均为假设。将费用包含在需要还款的金额中 默认当前余额为 10,000 加元，名义年利率为 20%。 3% 的转让费会增加 300 加元，因此替代方案以 10,300 加元的债务开始。零促销率并不能消除该费用。选择的付款方式为每月月底 400 加元。由于 12 个促销周期的利率为 0%，这些付款使转移余额减少了 4,800 加元。因此，促销结束后还剩 5,500 加元。从下一个周期开始，该示例对付款前的剩余债务收取 22% 的名义年利率除以 12。实际的卡可以计算每日利息并使用不同的付款分配规则。该插图使用了一种明确的每月惯例，因此可以检查时间表。解决促销期间需要清算的付款第二个指标计算每月固定金额，该金额将在促销周期内偿还含费用余额。如果利率为 0%，则 10,300 加元除以 12 等于每月 858.333 加元。该工具四舍五入为 858.34 加元，最终付款上限为剩余金额。向下舍入到 858.33 加元，十二次付款后剩下 4 美分。该金额超过所选的 400 加元付款。这种差异解释了为什么默认计划在促销活动结束后仍继续存在。在正促销率下，该工具使用固定付款摊销公式，而不是简单地将本金除以月份。如果选择零促销周期，新余额将从后续费率开始，并且不会报告促销内付款。零原始债务在模型中不会产生转让费。该指标并不决定负担能力或取代实际的最低付款要求。比较可用时的完整计划 在默认情况下，当前余额将在第 33 个月清算并产生大约 3,044.21 加元的利息。转移的余额将在第 28 个月清算，其中包括大约 895.35 加元的利息和 300 加元的费用。因此，转移的模型借款成本为 1,195.35 加元，比这些假设下的活期卡成本低约 1,848.86 加元。原始本金不包括在两个成本条中，因为无论哪种方式都必须偿还。融资费用的利息已包含在利息部分中。图表停止于收益或 120 个月。 “未偿还”指标意味着模型没有清除限额内的余额。不完整的时间表的费用是部分的，不能称为全额还款成本。该矩阵使用 NR，而不是报告此类情况的全寿命成本。测试付款和可用时间 该矩阵会更改每月付款和促销周期，同时保持原始余额、费用和费率固定。每个完整的单元格显示总利息加上费用。较大的促销窗口仅在输入的还款时间表和假设范围内有帮助。比较保持相同的固定付款，而每个余额仍保持未清状态。它不会投资提前支付后释放的资金、增加卡年费或模拟新的支出。如果这些影响适用的话，则属于更广泛的家庭比较。 FCAC 指出，逾期付款可能会导致促销条款失效。在依赖实际报价之前，请检查协议、交易类型、费用处理、最低付款额和到期日。这四张图表解释了成本表，但没有将总体利率视为完整的借款决策。

7276e5b78ffbbbfa5f3ef0166c3c3c8b8900c846.src: The eventual amount reimbursed and the cash needed to pay invoices answer different questions. Track both the benefit calculation and the timing of bills and receipts. Separate the invoice, recognized amount and insurer payment The FCAC’s health-insurance guide highlights that a policy may pay only a percentage of a claim or impose a maximum annual amount. The actual contract determines what is covered and how a claim is assessed. This illustration assumes approved private-benefit claims and uses an explicit calculation order: cap the recognized amount at the invoice, apply the remaining deductible, apply the insurer’s percentage, then apply the remaining insurer-payment maximum. Those are hypothetical contract conventions, not rules for every plan. The tool calculates neither eligibility nor a public dental or health-program benefit. The number and size of invoices are financial assumptions, rather than a recommendation about treatment or clinical need. Follow the remaining deductible and maximum through the claims The default schedule has a CAD 600 invoice at the start of each of six consecutive months in one benefit year. CAD 500 per invoice is recognized. The remaining deductible starts at CAD 100, the insurer percentage is 80%, and the remaining insurer-payment maximum is CAD 1,500. For the first claim, CAD 500 less CAD 100 leaves CAD 400 to which the 80% share applies. The modeled reimbursement is CAD 320. The next two claims reimburse CAD 400 each. Only CAD 380 remains under the payment maximum for the fourth claim. The fifth and sixth invoices still cost CAD 600 each, but the maximum has been exhausted and their modeled reimbursements are zero. Total invoices are CAD 3,600, total reimbursement is CAD 1,500, and the unreimbursed cost is CAD 2,100. The bars show why a headline 80% share does not mean 80% of every invoice is paid. Place cash receipts after the invoices that generate them Every invoice is paid at the start of its month. A two-month receipt delay means the first claim, from month one, is reimbursed at the end of month three. Even zero full-month delay means month-end payment in this model, rather than payment at the provider’s counter. The household also contributes CAD 150 of other budget surplus at each month-end. That amount is assumed available after regular household costs and premiums, before the invoices shown here. It must not include a reimbursement that is already entered elsewhere in the schedule. The default starts with CAD 1,500 allocated cash. After the month-three invoice, cash reaches zero before the later month-end resources arrive. After the month-four invoice it reaches negative CAD 130, although that month ends positive at CAD 420. A positive month-end observation can therefore hide an earlier funding need. Use the deepest shortage to measure starting cash needs The lowest default position after an invoice is negative CAD 230 in month six. The starting amount needed for the entire schedule is CAD 1,730, or CAD 230 beyond the selected reserve. A negative chart point represents an unfunded need, not an approved overdraft. The model continues through invoice months plus receipt delay, so all assumed claims have a receipt date within the horizon. With the selected monthly surplus, the default ledger ends month eight at positive CAD 600. That eventual balance does not remove the earlier shortage. The receipt-delay bars keep invoices and eventual reimbursement unchanged. Under the defaults, zero full-month delay requires CAD 1,350 at the start, while four months requires CAD 2,530.
