Timing can change liquidity needs without changing the eventual benefit amount. Check the timing assumption as well as the coverage percentage The matrix varies the insurer share and receipt delay. Recognized costs, deductible, payment maximum, invoice count, budget surplus and starting cash stay selected. Different percentages can produce the same eventual payment when the maximum binds. All invoices are assigned to one benefit year, with no maximum reset. The model excludes direct billing, a second plan, claim disputes, premiums, tax credits and borrowing costs. Actual reimbursement dates and contract ordering need confirmation before using a schedule for real payments. The four graphics keep ultimate cost and temporary cash needs visible together. A practical review records the invoice amount and due date, the confirmed benefit calculation, the expected receipt date and the source that funds the interval.
7276e5b78ffbbbfa5f3ef0166c3c3c8b8900c846.zh: 最终报销的金额和支付发票所需的现金回答了不同的问题。跟踪福利计算以及账单和收据的时间。将发票、认可金额和保险公司付款分开 FCAC 的健康保险指南强调，保单可能仅支付索赔的一定比例或规定最高年度金额。实际合同决定了承保范围以及如何评估索赔。此图假设已批准的私人福利索赔并使用明确的计算顺序：限制发票上已确认的金额，应用剩余的免赔额，应用保险公司的百分比，然后应用剩余的保险公司付款最高限额。这些是假设的合同约定，而不是每个计划的规则。该工具既不计算资格，也不计算公共牙科或健康计划福利。发票的数量和大小是财务假设，而不是有关治疗或临床需求的建议。按照剩余的免赔额和最高限额进行索赔 默认计划在一个福利年度的连续六个月的每个月初都有一张 600 加元的发票。每张发票 500 加元均被认可。剩余免赔额起价为 100 加元，保险公司百分比为 80%，剩余保险公司付款最高限额为 1,500 加元。对于第一项索赔，500 加元减去 100 加元，剩下 400 加元，适用 80% 的份额。模型报销金额为 320 加元。接下来的两项索赔各报销 400 加元。第四次索赔的最高付款额仅剩 380 加元。第五张和第六张发票的价格仍为每张 600 加元，但最高限额已用完，其模型报销金额为零。发票总额为 3,600 加元，报销总额为 1,500 加元，未报销费用为 2,100 加元。这些条形图说明了为什么标题 80% 份额并不意味着每张发票的 80% 都已支付。将现金收据放在生成现金收据的发票之后 每张发票均在月初支付。两个月的收据延迟意味着从第一个月开始的第一次索赔将在第三个月末得到报销。即使是零全月延迟也意味着在这种模式下需要月底付款，而不是在提供商柜台付款。该家庭还在每个月末贡献 150 加元的其他预算盈余。该金额假定是在常规家庭费用和保费之后、此处显示的发票之前可用的。它不得包括已在时间表其他地方输入的报销。默认情况下，分配的现金为 1,500 加元。在第三个月的发票之后，在稍后的月末资源到达之前，现金达到零。在第四个月的发票之后，它达到负 130 加元，尽管该月最终为正值 420 加元。因此，正值的月末观察可以隐藏早期的资金需求。使用最严重的短缺来衡量起始现金需求 第六个月，发票后的最低默认头寸为负 230 加元。整个计划所需的起始金额为 1,730 加元，或超出选定储备的 230 加元。负图表点代表资金不足的需求，而不是批准的透支。该模型持续到发票月份加上收货延迟，因此所有假设的索赔都有一个收货日期。根据选定的每月盈余，默认分类账在第八个月结束时为正 600 加元。最终的余额并不能消除之前的短缺。收据延迟栏使发票和最终报销保持不变。在默认情况下，零整月延迟开始时需要 1,350 加元，而四个月则需要 2,530 加元。时机可以改变流动性需求，但不会改变最终的福利金额。检查时间假设以及承保百分比 该矩阵会改变保险公司的份额和接收延迟。确认的成本、免赔额、最高付款额、发票数量、预算盈余和起始现金保持选定。当最高限额绑定时，不同的百分比可以产生相同的最终付款。所有发票都分配给一个福利年度，没有最高限额重置。该模型不包括直接计费、第二个计划、索赔纠纷、保费、税收抵免和借贷成本。在使用实际付款时间表之前，需要确认实际报销日期和合同订购。这四个图形将最终成本和临时现金需求放在一起可见。实际审查会记录发票金额和到期日、已确认的福利计算、预计收到日期以及该期间的资金来源。

8cc0c48b735114ee690acb74bbb39e9c41dd9336.src: An ordinary withdrawal reduces account value now and restores contribution room next calendar year. A same-year deposit still needs room that is already available. Keep account value separate from contribution room The CRA’s withdrawal guidance states that an ordinary TFSA withdrawal does not immediately create new available contribution room. The amount returns as room on January 1 of the next calendar year. Replacing money earlier requires unused room that is already available. This calendar models a holder eligible and resident in Canada throughout both illustrated years. Starting room is assumed already reconciled across all of the holder’s TFSAs. It is entered separately from combined account value because one amount cannot be inferred from the other. The model includes only the selected ordinary contributions and withdrawal, with no investment returns or other transactions. It excludes transfers, specified distributions, excess histories and non-resident periods. It is an explanation of one transaction sequence, rather than a statement of anyone’s actual room. Follow what changes during the withdrawal year The default starts with CAD 40,000 of combined account value and CAD 7,000 of unused room. The first requested CAD 5,000 contribution fits, raising value to CAD 45,000 and reducing available room to CAD 2,000. The next event is a CAD 10,000 ordinary withdrawal. Account value falls to CAD 35,000, while available room remains CAD 2,000. The value and room bars therefore move differently at exactly the same event. A later request to contribute CAD 10,000 is capped at the remaining CAD 2,000 in this model. That deposit raises value to CAD 37,000 and leaves no current-year room. The other CAD 8,000 of the request is marked unplaced; it never enters an account and is not modeled as an actual excess contribution. Build the next-year room calculation from its components When the new calendar year begins, the model adds unused room from the prior year, the ordinary withdrawal actually made, and a separate new-dollar-room assumption. Under the defaults, those components are zero, CAD 10,000 and CAD 7,000 respectively, producing CAD 17,000 before the next contribution. The requested CAD 15,000 year-two deposit fits. Combined account value then reaches CAD 52,000, and unused room is CAD 2,000. The account-value check is opening value plus the three deposits actually placed, less the withdrawal actually made. The new-year addition is an editable assumption, not an official future-year limit or a forecast. The CRA’s published table lists CAD 7,000 for 2026, but the applicable year, eligibility and transaction history must be checked for an actual calculation. Read requests and accepted transactions separately The contribution bars show the requested amount as a total, split between the deposit placed and the amount left out. This deliberately prevents the illustration from placing money beyond its simplified room calculation. The withdrawal is also capped at the account value available at that event. A request above that amount does not create extra cash or additional restored room. The new-year waterfall uses the withdrawal actually modeled, rather than the original request. The unplaced contribution amount is not a tax penalty, an investment loss or a balance in another account. The calendar assigns it no destination. A household budget needs its own record of where withdrawn or unplaced cash goes and whether a later contribution can be funded. Use the matrix to isolate the same-year constraint The matrix varies starting unused room and the later year-one contribution request. The first selected contribution still uses room before that later request. Each cell shows the amount of the later request that cannot be placed. Changing the ordinary withdrawal cannot change this same-year result. It changes account value and the following year’s restoration instead. That distinction is the reason a withdrawal confirmation alone is insufficient evidence that the same amount can be contributed again immediately. The CRA also explains that room applies collectively across a holder’s TFSAs and recommends reconciling records rather than relying only on a displayed account figure. Verify current room and transactions before making an actual deposit. These graphics make the ordinary timing visible without determining eligibility, calculating tax on excesses or replacing the holder’s full transaction ledger.
8cc0c48b735114ee690acb74bbb39e9c41dd9336.zh: 普通提款现在会减少账户价值，并在明年恢复供款空间。同年存款仍需要已有的空间。将账户价值与供款空间分开 CRA 的提款指南指出，普通 TFSA 提款不会立即创建新的可用供款空间。该金额将于下一个日历年 1 月 1 日作为房间返还。提前更换资金需要已可用的未使用房间。该日历模拟了在所示的两个年份中符合资格且居住在加拿大的持有人。假设所有持有人的 TFSA 的起始空间已得到协调。它与合并账户价值分开输入，因为无法从一个金额推断出另一个金额。该模型仅包括选定的普通供款和提款，没有投资收益或其他交易。它不包括转移、指定分配、超额历史和非居民时期。它是对一个交易顺序的解释，而不是对任何人实际房间的陈述。遵循提款年度内的变化 默认情况下，账户总价值为 40,000 加元，未使用房间为 7,000 加元。第一个请求的 5,000 加元捐款适合，将价值提高到 45,000 加元，并将可用空间减少到 2,000 加元。下一个活动是 10,000 CAD 普通提款。账户价值降至 35,000 加元，而可用空间仍为 2,000 加元。因此，在完全相同的事件中，价值条和房间条的移动方式不同。在此模型中，后来请求贡献 10,000 加元的上限为剩余 2,000 加元。这笔押金使价值增加到 37,000 加元，并且没有留下当年的空间。请求中的另外 8,000 加元被标记为未支付；它永远不会进入账户，也不会被建模为实际的超额捐款。从其组成部分构建下一年的房间计算当新的日历年开始时，模型添加上一年未使用的房间、实际提取的普通提款以及单独的新美元房间假设。在默认情况下，这些组件为零，分别为 10,000 加元和 7,000 加元，在下一次贡献之前产生 17,000 加元。所要求的第二年押金为 15,000 加元。账户总价值达到 52,000 加元，未使用的房间为 2,000 加元。账户价值检查是期初价值加上实际存入的三笔存款，减去实际提款。新年的增加是一个可编辑的假设，而不是官方的未来一年限制或预测。 CRA 公布的表格列出了 2026 年的 7,000 加元，但实际计算时必须检查适用年份、资格和交易历史。分别读取请求和接受的交易 贡献栏显示请求的总金额，分为存入的存款和未支付的金额。这故意阻止插图将金钱放置在其简化的房间计算之外。提款也以该活动时可用的账户价值为上限。高于该金额的请求不会产生额外的现金或额外的恢复房间。新年瀑布使用实际建模的提款，而不是原始请求。未到位的捐款金额不是税收罚款、投资损失或其他账户的余额。日历没有为其指定目的地。家庭预算需要有自己的记录，记录提取或未放置的现金的去向以及是否可以为以后的捐款提供资金。使用矩阵来隔离同年约束 该矩阵从未使用的房间和后来的第一年捐款请求开始变化。第一个选定的贡献仍然在后面的请求之前使用空间。每个单元格显示后来无法发出的请求的金额。改变普通提款额并不能改变同年的结果。它会改变账户价值和下一年的恢复。这种区别是单凭提款确认并不足以证明可以立即再次存入相同金额的证据。 CRA 还解释说，空间适用于持有人的 TFSA，并建议核对记录，而不是仅依赖显示的账户数据。在进行实际存款之前验证当前房间和交易。这些图形使普通时间可见，无需确定资格、计算超额税或更换持有人的完整交易分类账。

c6eabe4f00e1afe781a56fa42d639e312d1bb9c2.src: The gross RESP withdrawal and the money available for education can differ. Keep contribution refunds, educational assistance payments and the student’s wider tax calculation separate. Identify the payment type before calling it income The CRA distinguishes contribution refunds from educational assistance payments , or EAPs. Contribution refunds are paid tax-free under the applicable plan conditions. EAPs include grants, bonds and earnings, and are included in the beneficiary student’s income. This example assumes a Canadian-resident beneficiary remains eligible in a qualifying full-time program beyond the first thirteen consecutive weeks. The promoter is assumed to have confirmed both the contribution amount and gross EAP amount available for the modeled budget after the applicable checks. The entered EAP capacity is not a calculation from an account’s headline value. It does not independently allocate grants and earnings, verify a beneficiary’s grant history or approve an expense. The source-use chart deliberately shows only the amounts assumed available for this scenario. Confirm capacity before choosing a withdrawal mix For a qualifying program, the ordinary EAP limit is CAD 8,000 during the first thirteen consecutive weeks. Different period limits apply to specified part-time programs. The model does not calculate those periods or approve an exception; its assumed eligible full-time case is beyond the initial period. The CRA’s EAP bulletin also describes an administrative review threshold of CAD 29,459 for 2026. That threshold is a promoter guideline, not an unconditional annual withdrawal entitlement. Reasonableness and other eligibility requirements still matter. The illustration calculates neither grant repayments nor the consequences of a beneficiary becoming ineligible. Those cases require their own review. Confirming payment types and available amounts with the promoter comes before relying on this budget arithmetic. Connect gross EAP, an allowance and contribution cash The default education budget is CAD 24,000, with CAD 4,000 of confirmed outside funding. The remaining net amount to fund is CAD 20,000. The example has CAD 20,000 of available contributions and CAD 15,000 of confirmed gross EAP capacity. The selected gross EAP request is CAD 10,000. With a hypothetical 10% tax budget allowance, CAD 1,000 is set aside and CAD 9,000 remains for the education budget. A contribution withdrawal of CAD 11,000 then fills the remaining net need, leaving no funding gap under these assumptions. Afterward, the model shows CAD 9,000 of contribution capacity and CAD 5,000 of EAP capacity unused. Those are scenario remainders, rather than a guarantee that the same amount will qualify for a later withdrawal. No return or future enrolment schedule is modeled. Keep the budget allowance separate from actual student tax The allowance percentage is a planning assumption applied only to the modeled EAP. It does not calculate withholding, tuition credits, final tax, benefit changes or the effect of other income. A zero allowance would be an assumption in the tool, not a determination that a student owes no tax. The model caps the gross EAP at the request, confirmed capacity and the remaining education budget after outside funding, before that allowance. The last cap is a voluntary cash-budget convention. It is not an additional legal EAP limit or a method for determining a promoter’s approval. Contribution cash fills any remaining need only up to its entered availability. If those two sources and outside funding are insufficient, the waterfall ends negative and the funding-gap metric is positive. Outside funding above the full budget can instead leave unassigned cash. Compare the sources left after funding the same budget The request curves hold the budget and available sources fixed while varying the gross EAP request. They show how the remaining contribution amount and unused EAP capacity change. The curves do not optimize tax across several study years or recommend one mix. The matrix changes education costs and confirmed outside funding. Each cell calculates the extra amount needed after the selected withdrawal assumptions. Its cost levels are hypothetical, rather than tuition statistics or a statement of expenses an RESP promoter will accept. A practical review needs actual eligible costs, proof of enrolment, confirmed payment capacity and a separate tax estimate. The four graphics connect those inputs to a net funding ledger while keeping the RESP’s payment rules and the household’s spending decision distinct.
c6eabe4f00e1afe781a56fa42d639e312d1bb9c2.zh: RESP 提款总额和可用于教育的资金可能有所不同。将缴款退款、教育援助付款和学生更广泛的税收计算分开。在称之为收入之前先确定付款类型 CRA 将缴款退款与教育援助付款 (EAP) 区分开来。根据适用的计划条件，供款退款是免税的。 EAP 包括助学金、债券和收入，并包含在受益学生的收入中。此示例假设加拿大居民受益人在连续前十三周后仍然有资格参加合格的全日制计划。假定发起人在进行适当的检查后已确认可用于模型预算的捐款金额和 EAP 总额。输入的 EAP 容量不是根据账户的标题值计算得出的。它不独立分配赠款和收入、核实受益人的赠款历史或批准费用。来源-使用图表特意仅显示了假定可用于该场景的数量。选择提款组合之前确认容量 对于符合资格的计划，前连续十三周内的普通 EAP 限额为 8,000 加元。不同的期限限制适用于特定的兼读制课程。该模型不会计算这些期间或批准例外情况；其假设的符合资格的全日制案例超出了初始期限。 CRA 的 EAP 公告还描述了 2026 年行政审查门槛为 29,459 加元。该门槛是发起人指南，而不是无条件的年度提款权利。合理性和其他资格要求仍然很重要。该插图既没有计算赠款偿还额，也没有计算受益人不符合资格的后果。这些案件需要他们自己审查。在依赖此预算算法之前，需要与发起人确认付款类型和可用金额。连接总 EAP、津贴和缴款现金 默认教育预算为 24,000 加元，其中确认的外部资金为 4,000 加元。剩余的资金净额为 20,000 加元。该示例有 20,000 加元的可用贡献和 15,000 加元的已确认总 EAP 容量。所选 EAP 请求总额为 10,000 加元。根据假设的 10% 税收预算津贴，预留 1,000 加元，剩余 9,000 加元用于教育预算。然后提取 11,000 加元的捐款即可满足剩余的净需求，在这些假设下不会留下资金缺口。之后，模型显示 9,000 加元的贡献容量和 5,000 加元的 EAP 容量未使用。这些是情景剩余，而不是保证相同的金额有资格在以后提款。没有对返回或未来的注册时间表进行建模。将预算津贴与实际学生税分开。津贴百分比是仅适用于建模 EAP 的计划假设。它不计算预扣税、学费抵免、最终税、福利变化或其他收入的影响。零津贴是该工具中的一个假设，而不是确定学生不欠税。该模型根据请求、确认的容量以及外部资助后、津贴之前的剩余教育预算对总 EAP 进行限制。最后一个上限是自愿现金预算公约。它不是额外的法定 EAP 限制，也不是确定发起人是否批准的方法。捐款现金只能满足其输入的可用情况的任何剩余需求。如果这两个来源和外部资金不足，瀑布将以负值结束，资金缺口指标为正值。超过全部预算的外部资金可能会留下未分配的现金。比较资助相同预算后剩余的来源 请求曲线保持预算和可用来源固定，同时改变总 EAP 请求。它们显示了剩余捐款金额和未使用的 EAP 容量如何变化。这些曲线并没有优化几个研究年的税收，也没有推荐一种组合。该矩阵改变了教育成本并确认了外部资金。每个单元格都会计算选定的提款假设后所需的额外金额。其成本水平是假设的，而不是 RESP 发起人会接受的学费统计数据或费用报表。实际审查需要实际的合格费用、注册证明、确认的支付能力和单独的税收估算。这四个图形将这些输入连接到净资金分类账，同时保持 RESP 的支付规则和家庭的支出决定不同。

1323efcc4f76c27b54b13dddc01c90bb4b07e557.src: Interest avoided is only one part of the comparison. Track accessible savings and debt separately, and keep the monthly payment allocation identical in both choices. Confirm the prepayment terms before comparing the arithmetic The FCAC’s prepayment guide explains that a mortgage may permit extra payments or lump sums, with limits set by the contract. Paying more than the permitted amount can create a charge. The related rights page describes prepayment disclosures for federally regulated lenders. This comparison assumes the selected lump sum is permitted without a penalty. It does not calculate a privilege or verify a particular mortgage. A real prepayment charge, access restriction or change in contract terms would need to be added to the decision. Both choices start with the same mortgage and cash. One applies a lump sum immediately; the other retains that cash in savings. The original monthly mortgage payment is preserved in both, rather than automatically lowered after the prepayment. Match the starting resources and the monthly allocation The default mortgage is CAD 300,000, with twenty-five years of remaining amortization and a 4.5% quoted nominal annual rate. The example chooses semi-annual compounding converted to an equivalent monthly rate. It produces a scheduled payment of approximately CAD 1,660.42 a month. A CAD 20,000 prepayment reduces the initial mortgage to CAD 280,000 and leaves none of that selected cash liquid. Keeping the cash leaves the initial debt at CAD 300,000 and the CAD 20,000 available in savings. Home value is identical in both choices and is excluded from the comparison. Rates remain constant throughout the selected five-year horizon. The model does not predict renewal terms or assume every mortgage follows its chosen compounding convention. Use the actual disclosed calculation and payment schedule for a real contract. Read the cash path beside the mortgage path With the same scheduled payment applied to less opening debt, the prepayment path has a smaller mortgage throughout the default period. After five years, debt is approximately CAD 238,405.09 with prepayment and CAD 263,389.16 while keeping the cash. Under the selected 2% effective annual savings return after tax and costs, the retained CAD 20,000 grows to CAD 22,081.62. The prepayment choice has no liquid savings from that sum during the default horizon. The cash chart makes this difference visible instead of counting lower debt as cash on demand. If a modeled mortgage is cleared before the horizon, the unused part of its original monthly payment allocation moves into savings at month-end. The other choice receives the same treatment. This prevents the comparison from silently spending freed payments in one case while saving them in the other. Reconcile interest avoided with the savings-growth difference Net financial position in this limited comparison is liquid savings minus mortgage debt. The common home value cancels. Both options begin with the same net position and receive identical monthly payment allocations, so the difference can be reconciled through financing costs and savings growth. The default prepayment avoids approximately CAD 4,984.07 of mortgage interest over five years. It also gives up CAD 2,081.62 of modeled savings growth. The difference is approximately CAD 2,902.45 in favour of prepayment under these constant assumptions. The waterfall shows that reconciliation. It is an end-of-horizon nominal comparison, not an annual return, a present-value calculation or a valuation of liquidity. Positive arithmetic does not establish that allocating the selected cash to a mortgage fits the household’s other commitments. Test savings returns and cash amounts without losing the funding match The matrix supplies alternative initial cash amounts and after-tax savings returns. Each pair keeps the same mortgage, scheduled payment and horizon. Its signed cells show the prepayment choice’s cash-minus-debt position relative to keeping that cell’s cash liquid. Prepayment cannot exceed the debt in the model. If more cash is entered, the excess remains in savings, and any payment allocation no longer needed for debt also goes there. A zero mortgage or zero selected cash produces no advantage from a prepayment that does not occur. The savings return is a hypothetical constant net rate, with no investment-risk distribution. The model excludes charges, mortgage-interest deductions, actual account rules and future rate changes. Review the cash reserve needed for other purposes alongside the arithmetic, using confirmed contract terms and a budget that leaves each dollar assigned once.
1323efcc4f76c27b54b13dddc01c90bb4b07e557.zh: 避免利息只是比较的一部分。分别跟踪可用储蓄和债务，并在两种选择中保持每月付款分配相同。在比较算术之前确认预付款条款 FCAC 的预付款指南解释说，抵押贷款可能允许额外付款或一次性付款，但限额由合同规定。支付超过允许的金额可能会产生费用。相关权利页面描述了联邦监管的贷款机构的预付款披露。此比较假设允许选择的一次性付款而不会受到处罚。它不计算特权或验证特定抵押贷款。实际的预付款费用、访问限制或合同条款的变更需要添加到决策中。两种选择都以相同的抵押贷款和现金开始。立即一次性付清；另一个则将现金保留在储蓄中。原来的每月抵押贷款付款在两者中都保留，而不是在预付款后自动降低。匹配起始资源和每月分配 默认抵押贷款为 300,000 加元，剩余摊销年限为 25 年，名义年利率为 4.5%。该示例选择将半年复利转换为等值的月利率。它每月产生约 1,660.42 加元的预定付款。预付款 20,000 加元可将初始抵押贷款减少至 280,000 加元，并且不会留下任何选定的现金流动性。保留现金后，初始债务为 300,000 加元，还有 20,000 加元可用于储蓄。两种选择的房屋价值相同，因此被排除在比较之外。在选定的五年范围内，利率保持不变。该模型不会预测续约条款，也不会假设每项抵押贷款都遵循其选择的复利惯例。使用真实合同中实际披露的计算和付款时间表。阅读抵押贷款路径旁边的现金路径 由于相同的预定付款适用于较少的期初债务，因此预付款路径在整个违约期内的抵押贷款金额较小。五年后，提前还款的债务约为 238,405.09 加元，保留现金的债务约为 263,389.16 加元。根据选定的税后和成本后 2% 的有效年度储蓄回报，保留的 20,000 加元将增长至 22,081.62 加元。在违约期限内，预付款选择不会从该金额中获得流动资金。现金图表使这种差异显而易见，而不是将较低的债务视为按需现金。如果模型抵押贷款在期限之前结清，则其原始每月付款分配中未使用的部分将在月底转为储蓄。另一个选择也受到同样的待遇。这可以防止比较在一种情况下默默地花费释放的付款，而在另一种情况下保存它们。调和避免的利息与储蓄增长差异 在这个有限的比较中，净财务状况是流动储蓄减去抵押贷款债务。普通房屋价值取消。两种选择均以相同的净头寸开始，并获得相同的每月付款分配，因此可以通过融资成本和储蓄增长来调节差异。违约预付款可避免五年内约 4,984.07 加元的抵押贷款利息。它还放弃了 2,081.62 加元的模拟储蓄增长。在这些不变的假设下，预付款的差异约为 2,902.45 加元。瀑布表明了这种和解。它是期末名义比较，而不是年度回报、现值计算或流动性估值。正算术并不能证明将选定的现金分配给抵押贷款符合家庭的其他承诺。在不失去资金匹配的情况下测试储蓄回报和现金金额 该矩阵提供替代的初始现金金额和税后储蓄回报。每对都保留相同的抵押贷款、定期付款和期限。其签名单元显示了预付款选择相对于保持该单元现金流动性的现金减去债务状况。预付款不能超过模型中的债务。如果输入更多现金，多余的部分仍保留在储蓄中，并且债务不再需要的任何支付分配也将存入其中。零抵押贷款或零选择现金不会因未发生的预付款而产生任何优势。储蓄回报是假设的恒定净利率，没有投资风险分布。该模型不包括费用、抵押贷款利息扣除、实际账户规则和未来利率变化。使用已确认的合同条款和预算，在计算的同时审查其他目的所需的现金储备，使每一美元分配一次。

2f197ad5c29d855b87500d4be0f0c8a09e283e0d.src: A repayment comparison needs the same starting debts and total budget. Keep base payments in place, then show where released payments and extra cash go. Separate the priority rule from the amount you can pay The FCAC’s debt-repayment guide describes prioritizing either higher interest rates or smaller balances, while continuing required minimum payments on every debt. It also notes the importance of past-due accounts and the motivation a repayment approach may provide. This comparison isolates the order of extra payments. Both strategies use identical debts, rates, illustrative base payments and a fixed total monthly budget. It does not compare an aggressive budget for one strategy with a smaller budget for the other. The base-payment fields are modeling inputs, rather than calculations of contractual minimums. Actual obligations can follow different formulas or change over time. Reconcile those requirements before using an illustration to plan a payment. Build one budget and keep released payments working The default debts are CAD 5,000 at a 20% nominal annual rate, CAD 1,000 at 10%, and CAD 8,000 at 8%. Their base payments are CAD 125, CAD 50 and CAD 160 a month. Adding CAD 300 of extra monthly money produces one CAD 635 budget. Each month, the model charges interest at the nominal annual rate divided by twelve. It then pays each active debt’s base amount, capped at the amount owed. The remaining budget goes to the selected priority debt. If that debt is cleared, unused money reaches the next debt in the same month. When an account is repaid, its released base payment stays inside the CAD 635 total rather than disappearing from the plan. The final payment is capped at the total amount owed. The model does not assume any subsequent unused debt budget is invested elsewhere. Read the difference inside the repayment paths The highest-rate-first approach, often called an avalanche, directs remaining cash to debt A in the default example. The smallest-balance-first approach, often called a snowball, initially directs it to debt B. Both still make the other entered base payments. After the first payment cycle, total debt is CAD 13,510 in both cases. The allocation differs: highest-rate-first leaves approximately CAD 4,658.33 on A and CAD 958.33 on B, while smallest-balance-first leaves CAD 4,958.33 on A and CAD 658.33 on B. Debt C has the same balance in both. Later interest charges reflect where those balances remain. Under the defaults, both schedules clear during month twenty-five. The shared payoff month therefore hides a cost difference: interest totals about CAD 1,630.86 for highest-rate-first and CAD 1,712.87 for smallest-balance-first, a difference of approximately CAD 82.01. Distinguish a completed schedule from a partial one The charts stop after all debts are cleared or after 120 months. A “Not repaid” metric means the model did not clear the debt inside that limit. It does not mean repayment is mathematically impossible under every later schedule. Interest for an incomplete path is only the amount charged within those 120 months. It must not be read as a full-life repayment cost. The matrix reports NR instead of a full-cost figure for such a case. A rising balance indicates that the entered payments do not cover modeled interest. Balances are hypothetical and no credit limit, late fee, new purchase, rate change, promotional offer or lender intervention is modeled. The exercise cannot determine the effect of missed payments or predict a credit score. Compare payment capacity alongside the ordering choice The matrix changes debt A’s rate and the extra monthly amount while retaining the other selected inputs. Every cell uses the highest-rate-first rule and the same base-payment convention. It shows how the cost changes when the funding available to that rule changes. The smallest-balance rule is based on current balances after the month’s base payments. Rate and debt letter resolve ties. The highest-rate rule resolves ties by balance and then letter. These conventions keep an otherwise ambiguous comparison reproducible. A practical plan also needs a payment amount the household can maintain, funds for essential expenses and a review of actual account terms. Use the graphics to understand the cost of an ordering choice while keeping the budget, minimum obligations and ability to follow the schedule explicit.
2f197ad5c29d855b87500d4be0f0c8a09e283e0d.zh: 还款比较需要相同的起始债务和总预算。保持基本付款到位，然后显示释放的付款和额外现金的去向。将优先规则与您可以支付的金额分开 FCAC 的债务偿还指南描述了优先考虑较高的利率或较小的余额，同时继续要求每笔债务的最低还款额。它还指出了逾期账户的重要性以及还款方式可能提供的动力。这种比较隔离了额外付款的顺序。两种策略都使用相同的债务、利率、说明性基本付款和固定的每月预算总额。它不会将一种策略的激进预算与另一种策略的较小预算进行比较。基本支付字段是建模输入，而不是合同最低金额的计算。实际义务可以遵循不同的公式或随着时间的推移而变化。在使用插图来计划付款之前，请先协调这些要求。制定一份预算并保持已发放的付款正常运行 违约债务为 5,000 加元（按名义年利率 20%）、1,000 加元（按 10% 计算）和 8,000 加元（按 8% 计算）。他们的基本付款为每月 125 加元、50 加元和 160 加元。每月增加 300 加元的额外资金即可产生 635 加元的预算。该模型每月按名义年利率除以 12 收取利息。然后，它支付每笔活跃债务的基本金额，上限为所欠金额。剩余预算用于选定的优先债务。如果该债务被清偿，未使用的资金将用于当月的下一笔债务。当账户还款时，其释放的基本付款将保留在 635 加元总额内，而不是从计划中消失。最终付款的上限为所欠总额。该模型不假设任何后续未使用的债务预算投资于其他地方。了解还款路径中的差异 在默认示例中，最高利率优先方法（通常称为雪崩）将剩余现金引导至债务 A。最小余额优先的方法（通常称为滚雪球）最初将其定向到债务 B。双方仍然支付对方输入的基本付款。第一个付款周期后，两种情况下的总债务均为 13,510 加元。分配有所不同：最高利率优先在 A 上留下约 4,658.33 加元，在 B 上留下 958.33 加元，而最小余额优先在 A 上留下 4,958.33 加元，在 B 上留下 658.33 加元。债务 C 的余额相同。稍后的利息费用反映了这些余额的剩余位置。在默认情况下，两个计划都会在第 25 个月期间清除。因此，共享还款月隐藏了成本差异：最高利率优先的利息总额约为 1,630.86 加元，余额最小优先的利息总额约为 1,712.87 加元，差异约为 82.01 加元。区分已完成的时间表和部分时间表。图表在所有债务清偿完毕后或 120 个月后停止。 “未偿还”指标意味着模型没有清除该限额内的债务。这并不意味着在每一个较晚的时间表下，从数学上讲，还款都是不可能的。不完整路径的利息仅为这 120 个月内收取的金额。不得将其解读为终身还款成本。对于这种情况，矩阵报告的是 NR，而不是全部成本数字。余额增加表明输入的付款不包括模型利息。余额是假设的，没有对信用限额、滞纳金、新购买、利率变化、促销优惠或贷款机构干预进行建模。该练习无法确定错过付款的影响或预测信用评分。比较支付能力和订购选择 该矩阵改变了债务 A 的利率和额外的每月金额，同时保留其他选定的输入。每个单元都使用最高费率优先规则和相同的基本付款约定。它显示了当该规则可用的资金发生变化时成本如何变化。最小余额规则基于当月基本付款后的当前余额。利率和债务信解决了联系。最高率规则通过平衡然后字母来解决关系。这些约定使原本模糊的比较具有可重复性。实用的计划还需要家庭可以维持的付款金额、基本开支的资金以及对实际账户条款的审查。使用图形了解订购选择的成本，同时明确预算、最低义务和遵循时间表的能力。

f4c6a5a2700a805b2cd3b364227d1e33675b84c9.src: Calculate the required gross withdrawal separately from the spending budget. Money leaving a RRIF is not automatically money spent, and a tax allowance is not a tax assessment. Establish which minimum calculation applies The CRA’s minimum-amount guidance calculates the ordinary minimum from the RRIF’s fair market value at the start of the year and an applicable prescribed factor. The annual minimum begins in the year after the RRIF is established. This tool assumes the account already exists before the illustrated year, uses the annuitant’s whole age at the beginning of that year, and applies the “All other RRIFs” factor column . It does not calculate an establishment-year minimum, a spouse-age election, legacy qualifying or pre-1986 treatment, or the special calculation for locked-in annuity contracts held inside a RRIF. Confirm the applicable account category, age basis and opening value with the carrier before using an actual withdrawal figure. The source table and Income Tax Regulations section 7308 were reviewed for this article on 25 October 2026. Apply the factor to opening assets For the stated ordinary case, the factor below age seventy-one is one divided by ninety minus the beginning-of-year age. The table supplies the later factors, including 5.28% at age seventy-one, 5.40% at seventy-two and 20% at ninety-five or older. The default opening value is CAD 500,000 and the year-start age is seventy-two. Multiplying by 5.40% produces a CAD 27,000 minimum for the illustrated year. The factor is a withdrawal rule; it does not describe an investment return or a personally sustainable spending rate. The factor graphic presents the rule table across ages, rather than projecting an account over those ages. The opening value is not assumed to remain CAD 500,000 for the rest of a person’s life. This is a single-year illustration with no future balance path. Compare the request with the modeled gross withdrawal The entered gross withdrawal request is CAD 30,000. Because it exceeds the CAD 27,000 minimum, the modeled gross withdrawal is CAD 30,000. A request below the minimum is lifted to that minimum in this ordinary example. The tool also caps the modeled withdrawal at the entered asset balance. That cap reflects its simplified assumption of no in-year change in asset value. It is not a calculation of account liquidity, a sale order or confirmation of how much an actual portfolio can produce on a particular date. The bars display all three amounts so the request is not silently confused with the modeled withdrawal. If opening assets are zero, both the minimum and available gross withdrawal are zero. The separate spending input can still show an unfunded requirement. Bridge gross cash to a separate spending assignment The default budget allowance is 25% of the modeled gross withdrawal, or CAD 7,500. Subtracting it from CAD 30,000 leaves CAD 22,500 for comparison with CAD 18,000 of assigned net spending. The ledger therefore shows CAD 4,500 of cash remaining unassigned. The 25% allowance is a hypothetical budgeting choice. It is not a prescribed withholding rate, an estimate of final income tax, a tax-credit calculation or a prediction of a refund. An actual tax calculation needs the wider household facts and applicable rules. The spending entry is the part of the household budget assigned to this RRIF cash, rather than necessarily the entire household’s expenses. A positive remainder is not automatically consumed or invested elsewhere. A negative remainder means the assigned spending needs another source under the selected allowance. Keep withdrawals, assets and spending distinct in the wider plan The matrix varies year-start ages and assigned spending while retaining opening assets, the requested gross amount and the assumed allowance percentage. Each cell is cash left or extra funding needed for one year. Gold negative cells and teal positive cells are signed cash positions. Where the minimum exceeds the gross request, the model increases the withdrawal. That may create cash beyond the assigned spending amount. A transfer out of a registered account and a household purchase are different events; the remainder needs its own destination rather than being counted twice. The tool does not calculate benefit interactions, pension splitting, restrictions on locked-in plans, actual withholding, final tax or lifetime sustainability. Review those separately using current rules and account information. The four graphics clarify the relationship between one year’s minimum and its budget without turning the minimum factor into a retirement withdrawal recommendation.
f4c6a5a2700a805b2cd3b364227d1e33675b84c9.zh: 与支出预算分开计算所需的提款总额。离开 RRIF 的钱不会自动花掉，税收减免也不是税收评估。确定适用的最低金额计算 CRA 的最低金额指导根据 RRIF 年初的公平市场价值和适用的规定因素计算普通最低金额。年度最低限额从 RRIF 设立后的当年开始。该工具假设该账户在所示年份之前就已存在，使用该年年初年金受益人的整个年龄，并应用“所有其他 RRIF”因子列。它不计算最低成立年限、配偶年龄选择、遗产资格或 1986 年之前的待遇，也不计算 RRIF 内持有的锁定年金合同的特殊计算。在使用实际提款金额之前，请与运营商确认适用的账户类别、年龄基础和开户金额。本文于 2026 年 10 月 25 日审查了源表和所得税条例第 7308 条。 将因子应用于期初资产 对于上述普通情况，71 岁以下的因子是 1 除以 90 减去年初年龄。该表提供了后面的因素，包括71岁为5.28%，72岁为5.40%，95岁及以上为20%。默认开仓金额为 500,000 加元，起始年龄为 72 岁。乘以 5.40% 得出所示年份的最低 27,000 加元。该因素是提款规则；它不描述投资回报或个人可持续的支出率。因子图显示了跨年龄段的规则表，而不是预测这些年龄段的帐户。假设人的余生期初价值不会保持在 500,000 加元。这是一个单年插图，没有未来的平衡路径。将请求与建模的总提款额进行比较 输入的总提款请求为 CAD 30,000。由于超过了 27,000 加元的最低限额，因此模拟的提款总额为 30,000 加元。在这个普通示例中，低于最小值的请求将被提升到该最小值。该工具还将模拟提款上限限制在输入的资产余额内。该上限反映了资产价值年内没有变化的简化假设。它不是对账户流动性的计算、销售订单或对实际投资组合在特定日期可以产生多少收益的确认。条形图显示所有三个金额，因此请求不会默默地与建模的提款混淆。如果期初资产为零，则最低提款额和可用总提款额均为零。单独的支出输入仍然可以显示无资金支持的需求。将现金总额桥接至单独的支出任务 默认预算津贴为模拟总提款额的 25%，即 7,500 加元。从 30,000 加元中减去它，剩下 22,500 加元，以便与分配的净支出 18,000 加元进行比较。因此，账本显示还有 4,500 加元现金未分配。 25% 的津贴是一个假设的预算选择。它不是规定的预扣税率、最终所得税的估计、税收抵免计算或退款预测。实际的税收计算需要更广泛的家庭事实和适用的规则。支出条目是分配给该 RRIF 现金的家庭预算的一部分，而不一定是整个家庭的支出。正余数不会自动消耗或投资到其他地方。负余数意味着分配的支出需要选定津贴下的另一个来源。在更广泛的计划中保持提款、资产和支出不同 该矩阵改变了年初年龄和分配的支出，同时保留期初资产、要求的总金额和假设的津贴百分比。每个单元都剩余现金或一年所需的额外资金。金色阴性细胞和青色阳性细胞是签署的现金头寸。当最小值超过总请求时，模型会增加提款。这可能会创造超出指定支出金额的现金。注册账户转出和家庭购买是不同的事件；其余的需要有自己的目的地，而不是被计算两次。该工具不计算福利互动、养老金分割、锁定计划限制、实际预扣税、最终税收或终生可持续性。使用当前规则和帐户信息分别查看这些内容。这四个图表阐明了一年的最低限额与其预算之间的关系，而没有将最低限额转变为退休提款建议。

1f2f482c26a98812b9815532ab1a4346f9176804.src: A dollar earmarked for one goal cannot also fund another. Compare each deadline with cumulative saving capacity, and make the allocation rule visible. Write each remaining amount beside its own deadline The FCAC’s goal-setting guidance starts with priorities, amounts and timeframes. This illustration puts three remaining funding amounts on one calendar so their claims on the same monthly budget can be seen together. Enter only the money still to be raised for each goal. Existing earmarked savings have already been accounted for before these inputs. Amounts are fixed nominal CAD targets for their payment dates; the model applies no additional inflation or investment return. The default goals require CAD 6,000 by month twelve, CAD 12,000 by month twenty-four and CAD 18,000 by month thirty-six. Their labels remain A, C and B respectively because each input keeps its own identity when dates change. The shared month-end saving budget is CAD 900. Check cumulative obligations at every deadline At month twelve, cumulative funding due is CAD 6,000. At month twenty-four it is CAD 18,000, including the earlier goal. At month thirty-six it reaches CAD 36,000. The obligation chart steps up at those dates and compares the totals with the shared budget accumulated over time. A CAD 900 monthly budget supplies CAD 32,400 over thirty-six months. It cannot fully fund CAD 36,000 under this zero-return model. A positive final saving total is therefore not evidence that all goals fit the plan. The minimum constant budget for the deadline-first rule is the largest cumulative amount due divided by its deadline month. The default checks are CAD 500, CAD 750 and CAD 1,000 per month. The binding figure is CAD 1,000, assuming saving can begin now and funds can be earmarked early without restrictions. Compare two explicit allocation rules Deadline-first funding fills the earliest unfinished goal, then sends remaining cash to the next one. Under the default CAD 900 budget, A and C reach their full targets by their own deadlines. B receives CAD 14,400 by month thirty-six, leaving CAD 3,600 unfunded. The equal-share rule divides each month’s contribution among all active unfinished goals. If a share would exceed a goal’s remaining need, the excess is redistributed within the same month. A goal stops receiving money after its deadline, even when it was not fully funded. In the default equal-share case, A has CAD 3,600 at month twelve and C has CAD 9,000 at month twenty-four. B eventually reaches CAD 18,000. The shortfalls at A and C’s deadlines total CAD 5,400. Equal monthly amounts are not the same as equal progress toward different deadlines. Later unused cash cannot repair an earlier missed date The equal-share example leaves CAD 1,800 of the thirty-six-month contribution capacity unallocated after the remaining active goal has been funded. That later money is recorded separately. The model does not move it backward in time to make the missed deadlines appear successful. The cumulative-funding chart shows the amount earmarked in time under each rule. It is not a cash-account balance after purchases, and the model does not simulate the purchases themselves. Recorded goal funding remains committed once and is not reused for another goal. Deadline ties are resolved by goal letter in the deadline-first case. Both rules cap funding at a goal’s remaining target. A zero target needs no contributions, and a zero budget leaves every positive target unfunded. These conventions make the comparison reproducible. Test amounts, timing and priorities together The matrix supplies alternative monthly budgets and scales all selected deadlines, rounding to whole months with a one-month minimum. Goal amounts remain unchanged. Each cell totals shortfalls at the individual deadlines under the deadline-first rule. The minimum-budget metric is an arithmetic feasibility threshold for this model. It assumes no restricted accounts, no return, no opening funding and divisible month-end contributions. It does not establish affordability in the household budget or decide which goal should have priority. A real review may change an amount, postpone a flexible date or give a personally important goal precedence over another. The charts expose the consequence of a chosen rule; they do not rank the value of the goals. Record that judgment separately from the calculation so timing and personal priorities remain understandable.
1f2f482c26a98812b9815532ab1a4346f9176804.zh: 专门用于一个目标的一美元不能同时为另一个目标提供资金。将每个期限与累计储蓄能力进行比较，使分配规则可见。将每个剩余金额写在其截止日期旁边 FCAC 的目标设定指南从优先级、金额和时间表开始。此图将三个剩余资金金额放在一个日历上，以便可以同时查看他们对同一月度预算的索赔。仅输入每个目标仍需筹集的资金。现有的专项储蓄已在这些投入之前计算在内。金额是其付款日期的固定名义加元目标；该模型不适用额外的通货膨胀或投资回报。默认目标要求在第十二个月之前达到 6,000 加元，在第二十四个月之前达到 12,000 加元，在第三十六个月之前达到 18,000 加元。它们的标签分别保持为 A、C 和 B，因为当日期更改时每个输入都保持自己的标识。共享的月末储蓄预算为 900 加元。在每个截止日期检查累积义务 在第 12 个月，累积应付资金为 6,000 加元。第 24 个月的收入为 18,000 加元，包括之前的目标。第三十六个月达到 36,000 加元。义务图表在这些日期逐步增加，并将总额与随着时间推移累积的共享预算进行比较。每月 900 加元的预算可在 36 个月内提供 32,400 加元。在这种零回报模式下，它无法全额资助 36,000 加元。因此，最终储蓄总额为正并不能证明所有目标都符合计划。截止日期优先规则的最小恒定预算是最大累计应付金额除以截止日期月份。默认支票为每月 500 加元、750 加元和 1,000 加元。约束金额为 1,000 加元，假设现在就可以开始储蓄，并且资金可以不受限制地提前指定用途。比较两个明确的分配规则：截止日期优先的资金满足最早未完成的目标，然后将剩余的现金发送到下一个目标。在默认的 900 加元预算下，A 和 C 在各自的截止日期前完成了全部目标。 B 在第三十六个月收到 14,400 加元，剩下 3,600 加元没有资金。平等分享规则将每个月的贡献分配给所有活跃的未完成目标。如果份额超出目标的剩余需求，超出部分将在当月内重新分配。目标在截止日期后将停止收到资金，即使资金尚未充足。在默认均等情况下，A 在第 12 个月拥有 3,600 加元，C 在第 24 个月拥有 9,000 加元。 B 最终达到 18,000 加元。 A 和 C 的截止日期时的缺口总计 5,400 加元。每月相同的金额并不等同于在不同截止日期上取得的相同进展。后来未使用的现金无法修复之前错过的日期。平等份额示例在剩余的活动目标获得资助后，36 个月的缴款能力中还有 1,800 加元未分配。后来的钱是单独记录的。该模型不会及时向后移动，以使错过的最后期限看起来很成功。累积资金图表显示了每条规则下指定时间的金额。它不是购买后的现金账户余额，并且该模型并不模拟购买本身。记录的目标资金仍然承诺一次，不会重复用于另一个目标。在截止日期优先的情况下，截止日期关系通过目标信解决。这两条规则都将资金上限限制在目标的剩余目标上。零目标不需要捐款，零预算使每个积极目标都没有资金支持。这些约定使比较具有可重复性。一起测试数量、时间安排和优先级 该矩阵提供了替代的每月预算，并调整了所有选定的最后期限，四舍五入到整月，最少一个月。目标金额保持不变。根据截止日期优先规则，每个单元格在各个截止日期时总计不足。最小预算指标是该模型的算术可行性阈值。它假设没有限制账户、没有回报、没有开户资金和可分割的月末捐款。它不会确定家庭预算的承受能力，也不会决定哪个目标应该优先。真正的审查可能会改变金额、推迟灵活的日期或将个人重要的目标优先于另一个目标。图表揭示了所选规则的后果；他们没有对目标的价值进行排名。将判断与计算分开记录，以便时间安排和个人优先事项保持易于理解。

402d59a04713d4bef6592a724bc27bc9bdb946bb.src: A monthly benefit amount tells only part of the story. Put the first receipt, overlapping income and the final modeled payment on a calendar before assessing the cash reserve. Read the contract, then build the cash calendar The Financial Consumer Agency of Canada’s disability-insurance guide highlights waiting times, benefit amounts, tax treatment, definitions of disability and coordination with other benefits. Those details affect both eligibility and the cash a household can use. A policy’s headline payment should not automatically be treated as additional net income. This illustration assumes a selected benefit is approved and available after all taxes and offsets. It does not assess a claim or determine an entitlement. Continuing household income, temporary salary or sick pay, and the entered net insurance benefit are separate receipts in a monthly ledger. The waiting input counts full months with no insurance receipt. A three-month wait means the first modeled payment arrives at the end of month four. The payment-count input then specifies how many monthly receipts occur within the selected horizon. These are hypothetical timing assumptions, rather than a policy quotation or a prediction of recovery. The income gap can change more than once The default household spends CAD 4,500 each month and retains CAD 1,500 of continuing net income. Temporary salary or sick pay adds CAD 2,500 in each of the first two months. The remaining monthly gap is CAD 500 while that temporary payment is present. In month three, the temporary receipt has ended but insurance has not yet begun. The gap rises to CAD 3,000. In months four through nine, the entered CAD 2,200 insurance payment brings total net receipts to CAD 3,700, leaving CAD 800 a month to fund from cash. The six modeled insurance payments then finish. Months ten through twelve again have a CAD 3,000 monthly gap. The first graphic makes these phases visible. It does not assume that a policy necessarily stops after six payments; that count is an editable stress scenario for the example. Fund the deepest cash need, including the starting cost The example also includes CAD 1,000 of one-time costs before the first month. From CAD 10,000 allocated cash, the starting position after that payment is CAD 9,000. The reserve then pays each monthly difference between receipts and spending. Across the twelve-month schedule, the monthly gaps total CAD 17,800. Adding the initial CAD 1,000 gives a required starting amount of CAD 18,800. After the CAD 10,000 reserve already entered, another CAD 8,800 is needed under these assumptions. The path first goes negative in month ten. A negative point is an unfunded requirement, not a bank balance the household is allowed to maintain. The second cash curve removes insurance receipts while keeping everything else the same, providing a no-receipt stress comparison without assigning it a probability. Check overlaps and avoid counting the same support twice The income-source bars sum only receipts inside the selected horizon. The default totals are CAD 18,000 of continuing income, CAD 5,000 of temporary pay and CAD 13,200 of entered insurance benefits. Amounts scheduled after the horizon do not appear in those totals. The calculator adds inputs as entered. If temporary pay overlaps the insurance phase, the model does not reduce either amount automatically. Actual coordination needs to be resolved before using the figures: a payment already included in continuing income must not also be entered as a separate benefit. Use amounts available for household bills after the relevant deductions and offsets. A gross insurance amount or an expected reimbursement can differ from spendable cash on the date a bill arrives. This model calculates neither tax nor the contractual treatment of another source of support. Review waiting time, payment duration and the wider interruption The matrix varies full waiting months and the number of insurance payments. Each cell is additional starting cash after the selected reserve, calculated across the same household schedule. Temporary pay, ongoing income, spending and the initial cost remain unchanged. A longer wait and a shorter payment period affect different parts of the calendar. If payments begin after the illustrated horizon, none is counted. If income exceeds spending in a month, the surplus remains in the modeled cash reserve; the starting-cost requirement still exists before those receipts arrive. The schedule excludes inflation, interest, claim administration, premiums and changes in spending or work capacity. Replace the assumptions with supported dates and net amounts when reviewing an actual arrangement. The useful output is a dated cash requirement alongside the coverage terms, rather than a conclusion that a headline replacement percentage makes every month affordable.
402d59a04713d4bef6592a724bc27bc9bdb946bb.zh: 每月的福利金额只能说明部分情况。在评估现金储备之前，将第一张收据、重叠收入和最终模拟付款放在日历上。阅读合同，然后制定现金日历加拿大金融消费者机构的残疾保险指南重点介绍了等待时间、福利金额、税务处理、残疾定义以及与其他福利的协调。这些细节会影响资格和家庭可以使用的现金。保单的总体付款不应自动被视为额外净收入。此图假设选定的福利在所有税费和抵销后已获得批准并可用。它不评估索赔或确定权利。持续家庭收入、临时工资或病假工资以及输入的净保险福利是每月分类账中的单独收据。等待输入计算完整月份，没有保险收据。三个月的等待意味着第一笔模拟付款将在第四个月月底到达。然后，付款计数输入指定在选定范围内发生的每月收款数量。这些是假设性的时间假设，而不是政策报价或复苏预测。收入差距可能会多次变化 默认家庭每月支出 4,500 加元，并保留 1,500 加元的持续净收入。临时工资或病假工资前两个月每月增加 2,500 加元。当临时付款存在时，每月剩余的缺口为 500 加元。第三个月，临时收据已经结束，但保险尚未开始。差距扩大至3,000加元。第四个月到第九个月，输入的 2,200 加元保险付款使总净收入达到 3,700 加元，每月剩下 800 加元可以用现金支付。六种模式的保险金支付完毕。第 10 个月到第 12 个月再次出现 3,000 加元的每月缺口。第一张图使这些阶段变得可见。它并不假设保单一定会在六次付款后停止；该计数是该示例的可编辑压力场景。为最深的现金需求提供资金，包括起始成本 该示例还包括第一个月之前 1,000 加元的一次性成本。从分配的 10,000 加元现金开始，付款后的起始头寸为 9,000 加元。然后，储备金每月支付收入和支出之间的差额。在 12 个月的计划中，每月缺口总计 17,800 加元。添加初始 1,000 加元，所需起始金额为 18,800 加元。在输入 10,000 加元储备金后，根据这些假设，还需要另外 8,800 加元。该路径在第十个月首次变为负值。缺点是没有资金支持的要求，而不是允许家庭维持的银行余额。第二条现金曲线删除了保险收据，同时保持其他所有内容相同，提供了无收据压力比较，而不分配概率。检查重叠并避免将相同的支持计算两次 收入来源栏仅对所选范围内的收入进行求和。默认总额为 18,000 加元的持续收入、5,000 加元的临时工资和 13,200 加元的保险福利。期限之后安排的金额不会出现在这些总数中。计算器会添加输入的内容。如果临时工资与保险阶段重叠，该模型不会自动减少任何金额。在使用这些数字之前需要解决实际协调问题：已经包含在持续收入中的付款不得也作为单独的福利输入。使用相关扣除和抵消后的家庭账单可用金额。总保险金额或预期报销可能与账单到达之日的可支出现金有所不同。该模型既不计算税收，也不计算其他支持来源的合同待遇。审查等待时间、付款持续时间和更广泛的中断 该矩阵会改变完整的等待月数和保险付款次数。每个单元格是选定储备之后的额外起始现金，根据同一家庭时间表计算。临时工资、持续收入、支出和初始成本保持不变。更长的等待时间和更短的付款期限会影响日历的不同部分。如果付款在所示期限之后开始，则不计算在内。如果一个月的收入超过支出，则盈余仍保留在模拟现金储备中；在这些收据到达之前，起始成本要求仍然存在。该表不包括通货膨胀、利息、索赔管理、保费以及支出或工作能力的变化。在审查实际安排时，用支持的日期和净额替换假设。有用的输出是一个过时的现金需求以及承保条款，而不是一个标题替换百分比使每个月都可以承受的结论。

7767704dd120ed965b105e22ee300710ef1bc919.src: An income contract can replace part of a liquid portfolio with scheduled payments. Compare the payment, liquidity, inflation exposure and contract terms without treating cumulative receipts as an annual yield. Distinguish income from an accessible account balance The FCAC’s annuity guide distinguishes life income from fixed-term payments and describes options for survivors or beneficiaries. It also explains that payments can combine interest, returned capital and risk pooling. A payout amount therefore cannot be read as investment interest alone. This illustration assumes an immediate level-payment life-only contract. Every displayed receipt is conditional on the annuitant remaining alive. No guarantee period, survivor continuation, death benefit, tax calculation or contract surrender value is included. The entered payment per CAD 100,000 of premium is hypothetical, not an available insurer quote. The model scales it linearly with the selected premium allocation. Actual products, pricing and terms require separate verification. The graph does not estimate an expected lifetime payout or assign a probability to the selected payment horizon. See what remains liquid after the allocation The default illustration begins with CAD 500,000 of liquid capital and allocates 40%, or CAD 200,000, to the income contract. The waterfall leaves CAD 300,000 of liquid capital at the purchase date. The premium has been exchanged for contractual income. It is not labelled an immediate investment loss or a fee. Equally, it is not still available as cash for a separate purchase. The tool does not value the contract, so the waterfall endpoint is liquid capital rather than total wealth. The remaining liquid amount has no modeled return or withdrawal schedule here. A complete retirement budget would assign that money to reserves, future spending or other purposes, and compare those uses with the income supplied by the contract. A payout percentage does not isolate investment return The default hypothetical payment is CAD 550 a month for each CAD 100,000 of premium. On CAD 200,000, that produces CAD 1,100 a month, or CAD 13,200 over twelve payments. Annual cash paid divided by premium is 6.6%. That 6.6% is a cash-payout ratio. It does not separate interest from returned capital or pooling, and it assumes neither a redeemable principal balance nor a residual estate value. It is not directly comparable with a savings-account interest rate or a portfolio’s total return. The cumulative-receipts chart compares the original premium with payments actually assumed to occur. At CAD 1,100 per month, 181 receipts total CAD 199,100 and 182 total CAD 200,200. The nominal cash-receipt crossover is therefore 182 months, or fifteen years and two months, conditional on receiving every payment. Keep the receipt crossover separate from inflation and opportunity cost After thirty years of the selected payments, cumulative gross receipts total CAD 396,000. Comparing that sum with the CAD 200,000 premium does not account for when each receipt arrived, tax, inflation or returns that an alternative arrangement might have produced. The purchasing-power chart isolates one of those issues. The nominal monthly amount remains CAD 1,100. With 2% annual inflation, its purchasing power after thirty years is approximately CAD 607.28 in purchase-date dollars. The year-zero point is a comparison of payment amounts, not a payment received at purchase. An indexed payment would require its own terms and quote. This tool does not assume that an increasing payment can be purchased for the same premium and initial amount. The constant-payment illustration simply makes the price exposure visible. Compare contracts and household needs on the same basis The matrix shows cumulative gross payments as a percentage of a fixed CAD 100,000 premium at several hypothetical monthly amounts and durations. A cell above 100% means nominal cash received exceeds that premium, conditional on all the displayed payments occurring. It is not a gain after opportunity cost, an annual rate, an insurer offer or a survival probability. The fixed grid remains independent of the selected allocation. Choosing zero allocation leaves the selected payment at zero and reports no premium-receipt crossover. The FCAC guide also notes that contract options, tax treatment and the ability to change or cancel vary. Review those terms alongside other household income, the need for accessible cash and the treatment of a survivor or estate. The four graphics support that cash-flow discussion without deciding whether an annuity is suitable or ranking it against an investment portfolio.
7767704dd120ed965b105e22ee300710ef1bc919.zh: 收入合同可以用定期付款取代部分流动投资组合。比较付款、流动性、通货膨胀风险和合同条款，而不将累积收入视为年收益率。区分收入和可访问账户余额 FCAC 的年金指南区分了终身收入和定期付款，并描述了幸存者或受益人的选择。它还解释说，付款可以结合利息、返还资本和风险分担。因此，支付金额不能单独解读为投资利息。本图假设签订的是立即水平付款终身合同。每张显示的收据都以年金受益人是否还活着为条件。不包括保证期、幸存者延续、死亡抚恤金、税收计算或合同退保价值。输入的每 100,000 加元保费付款额是假设的，并非保险公司的可用报价。该模型根据所选的保费分配对其进行线性缩放。实际产品、定价和条款需要单独验证。该图不会估计预期的终生支付或为选定的支付期限分配概率。查看分配后剩余的流动资金 默认示例从 500,000 加元的流动资本开始，并将 40%（即 200,000 加元）分配给收入合同。瀑布在购买之日留下了 300,000 加元的流动资金。保费已兑换为合同收入。它没有被标记为立即投资损失或费用。同样，它仍然不能以现金形式单独购买。该工具不对合约进行估值，因此瀑布端点是流动资本而不是总财富。此处剩余的液体量没有模型化的回报或提款时间表。完整的退休预算会将这笔钱分配给储备金、未来支出或其他用途，并将这些用途与合同提供的收入进行比较。支付百分比并不孤立投资回报 默认假设支付额为每月每 100,000 加元保费 550 加元。如果金额为 200,000 加元，每月可赚取 1,100 加元，或分 12 次付款可赚取 13,200 加元。每年支付的现金除以保费为 6.6%。 6.6% 是现金支付比率。它不将利息与返还资本或资金池分开，也不假定可赎回的本金余额或剩余遗产价值。它不能与储蓄账户利率或投资组合的总回报直接比较。累积收入图表将原始保费与实际假设发生的付款进行比较。按每月 1,100 加元计算，181 张收据总计 199,100 加元，182 张收据总计 200,200 加元。因此，名义现金收据交叉期为 182 个月，即十五年零两个月，以收到每笔付款为条件。将收入交叉与通货膨胀和机会成本分开 所选付款三十年后，累计总收入总计 396,000 加元。将该金额与 200,000 加元的保费进行比较，并未考虑每张收据到达的时间、税收、通货膨胀或替代安排可能产生的回报。购买力图表隔离了其中一个问题。每月名义金额仍为 1,100 加元。按年通货膨胀率 2% 计算，三十年后的购买力按购买日美元计算约为 607.28 加元。年零点是付款金额的比较，而不是购买时收到的付款。指数支付需要有自己的条款和报价。该工具并不假设可以以相同的保费和初始金额购买增加的付款。持续支付的说明只是让价格风险变得可见。在相同的基础上比较合同和家庭需求 该矩阵显示了在几个假设的每月金额和持续时间下，累计支付总额占 100,000 加元固定保费的百分比。高于 100% 的单元格表示收到的名义现金超过该溢价，条件是所有显示的付款均发生。它不是机会成本、年费率、保险公司报价或生存概率之后的收益。固定网格保持独立于所选分配。选择零分配会使所选付款为零，并且不会报告保费收据交叉。 FCAC 指南还指出，合同选项、税务处理以及更改或取消的能力各不相同。将这些条款与其他家庭收入、可用现金的需求以及幸存者或遗产的待遇一起审查。这四个图表支持现金流量讨论，而不决定年金是否合适或将其与投资组合进行排名。

9da1b1184cfb013537ab6542a4b4f3f57cba221f.src: A foreign-currency goal has a price and a currency exposure. Keep both units explicit, then translate the future bill and its conversion costs into the currency being saved. Write the currency unit on both sides of the plan A tuition payment, family expense or planned purchase abroad may be priced in one currency while savings accumulate in Canadian dollars. The goal is the number of foreign units owed on the payment date, rather than a CAD amount that can remain unchanged regardless of exchange rates. This example uses the generic label foreign currency unit, or FCU . Define that unit consistently for the bill and the exchange-rate input. The rate is CAD paid per one FCU, so a higher number makes the same foreign bill more expensive in Canadian dollars. The Bank of Canada’s daily-rate page uses foreign units converted into CAD and explains that its published rates are indicative averages. They are not executable provider quotes. The default rate here is an independent hypothetical assumption; the calculator does not fetch or predict an exchange rate. Project the bill in its own currency first The default bill is 20,000 FCU at today’s price, payable in thirty-six months. At an assumed 3% annual price increase in that currency, the amount becomes 21,854.54 FCU after three years. That change is a foreign-price assumption, separate from the currency translation. Multiplying by the selected 1.40 CAD per FCU produces a CAD 30,596.36 reference cost, before rounding the intermediate calculation. The example then adds a 2% conversion charge, approximately CAD 611.93, and one CAD 25 fee. The full unrounded calculation gives a terminal funding target of CAD 31,233.28. The waterfall expresses every step in CAD, including the effect of the foreign-price increase. It does not add foreign units directly to Canadian dollars. The conversion percentage is an explicit markup on the reference CAD amount; actual providers may express their charges or offered rate differently. Match the saving schedule to the translated deadline amount The example starts with CAD 5,000 and adds CAD 500 at each month-end. A constant 2% effective annual CAD return is converted to its equivalent monthly rate. After thirty-six deposits, the modeled savings are CAD 23,836.16, leaving approximately CAD 7,397.12 below the translated bill. The required-contribution metric solves for the constant month-end CAD deposit that would reach the selected target from the selected starting amount. In the default case it is approximately CAD 699.60 a month. This result is an arithmetic funding amount, not evidence that the household budget can support it. The target line is flat because it shows the bill already projected to the deadline, translated at the selected terminal rate. It is not a claim that the bill costs that amount at every earlier date. All savings remain in CAD until one conversion at the end. Change the rate without changing the foreign bill The rate bars hold the foreign bill, payment date and charges constant while varying only CAD per FCU. If each foreign unit requires more CAD, the reference cost and percentage conversion charge both rise. A fixed fee remains the same. These alternatives are scenarios with no probabilities attached. They do not describe historical volatility or establish a likely future range. Reversing a quote also reverses the arithmetic: FCU per CAD would require division, whereas the convention used throughout this tool requires multiplication. If the real plan includes staged payments or savings already held in the foreign currency, one terminal conversion is an incomplete representation. Such a plan needs separate dated amounts and currency balances. This example isolates a single CAD-funded payment so the units remain easy to follow. Compare the deadline and the contribution together The matrix changes the terminal rate and the number of months available. Each cell reprojects the foreign price for that duration, translates it and solves for the necessary month-end CAD saving. Starting CAD assets, the selected savings return and charges remain fixed. More time gives contributions longer to accumulate, but it also allows the assumed foreign price to rise for longer. The result reflects both effects. If existing savings already fund the modeled bill, the required contribution is floored at zero. A zero foreign bill creates no conversion order and no flat fee in this illustration. A planning review can adjust the purchase amount, contribution, timing or currency arrangement. The graphs do not choose among those options or calculate a hedge. Their purpose is to show the foreign obligation, the CAD funding path and the exchange-rate assumption as three explicit parts of the same goal.
9da1b1184cfb013537ab6542a4b4f3f57cba221f.zh: 外币目标有价格和货币风险。保持两个单位明确，然后将未来的账单及其转换成本转换为要保存的货币。在计划的两面写上货币单位 学费、家庭开支或计划的国外购物可能会以一种货币定价，而储蓄会以加元累积。目标是付款日所欠的外国单位数量，而不是无论汇率如何都可以保持不变的加元金额。此示例使用通用标签外币单位或 FCU 。为账单和汇率输入一致地定义该单位。该费率按每个 FCU 支付加元，因此数字越高，相同的外国钞票以加元计算的价格就越贵。加拿大央行的每日利率页面使用转换为加元的外国单位，并解释其公布的利率是指示性平均值。它们不是可执行的提供商报价。这里的违约率是一个独立的假设；计算器不会获取或预测汇率。首先以本国货币计算账单 默认账单按今天的价格计算为 20,000 FCU，需在三十六个月内支付。假设该货币每年价格上涨 3%，三年后该金额将变为 21,854.54 FCU。这种变化是一种外国价格假设，与货币换算无关。在对中间计算进行四舍五入之前，乘以所选的每个 FCU 1.40 加元可得出 30,596.36 加元的参考成本。然后，该示例添加了 2% 的兑换费，约为 611.93 加元，以及一笔 25 加元的费用。完整的四舍五入计算得出的最终资金目标为 31,233.28 加元。瀑布表示 CAD 中的每一步，包括国外价格上涨的影响。它不会直接将外国单位添加到加元中。兑换百分比是参考加元金额的明确标记；实际的提供商可能会以不同的方式表达他们的收费或报价。将储蓄计划与换算后的截止日期金额相匹配 该示例从 5,000 加元开始，并在每个月末添加 500 加元。恒定的 2% 有效年度加元回报率将转换为等值的月利率。进行 36 次存款后，模型节省金额为 23,836.16 加元，比换算后的账单低大约 7,397.12 加元。所需缴款指标求解将从所选起始金额达到所选目标的恒定月末加元存款。默认情况下，每月约为 699.60 加元。这个结果是一个算术资金数额，并不是家庭预算能够支持的证据。目标线是平坦的，因为它显示账单已预计到截止日期，并按选定的最终汇率换算。这并不是说账单在每个较早日期的费用都是如此。所有节省的金额均保留为 CAD，直到最后进行一次转换。更改费率而不更改外国账单 费率栏保持外国账单、付款日期和费用不变，而每个 FCU 仅改变加元。如果每个外国单位需要更多加元，则参考成本和百分比转换费用都会上升。固定费用保持不变。这些替代方案是没有附加概率的场景。它们没有描述历史波动性或确定未来可能的范围。反转引用也会反转算术：每个 CAD 的 FCU 需要除法，而整个工具中使用的约定需要乘法。如果实际计划包括分期付款或已经以外币持有的储蓄，则一次终端转换是不完整的表示。此类计划需要单独注明日期的金额和货币余额。此示例隔离了单笔 CAD 资助的付款，因此这些单位仍然易于理解。将截止日期和缴款一起比较 矩阵会更改最终费率和可用月数。每个单元格都会重新预测该期间的国外价格，对其进行转换并解决必要的月末 CAD 节省问题。启动 CAD 资产后，所选储蓄回报和费用保持固定。时间越长，捐款积累的时间就越长，但也使得假定的外国价格上涨的时间更长。结果反映了这两种效应。如果现有储蓄已经为模拟账单提供资金，则所需缴款额将为零。在此图中，零外国账单不会创建转换订单，也不会产生固定费用。计划审查可以调整采购金额、贡献、时间或货币安排。这些图表不会在这些选项中进行选择或计算对冲。它们的目的是表明对外义务、加元融资路径和汇率假设是同一目标的三个明确部分。

6a45517de2b4831790a0bb7ba8e080394e1ba4d9.src: List amounts and access dates separately. Assets expected to become cash later may leave immediate costs unfunded, even when the ledger ends with a positive balance. Distinguish an asset from money available to pay an invoice An estate can have valuable property while lacking cash for a bill due now. Access, sale timing, secured debt and administrative requirements affect when an amount becomes usable. British Columbia’s estate guide describes duties including listing assets and debts, paying valid obligations, filing returns and preparing accounts. Its guidance is specific to B.C.; other jurisdictions have their own requirements. This illustration tracks estate cash only. Starting cash is assumed accessible to the authorized representative, and a later asset sale supplies a separate receipt. No personal money from an executor or beneficiary is automatically included. The sale input means cash after selling costs and secured loans, before the separate tax and debt payment entered in the controls. It is not the gross property value. Entering a liability in both the net-sale figure and the separate payment would count the same obligation twice. Put immediate and recurring obligations on a calendar The example starts with CAD 25,000 of accessible cash and CAD 20,000 of immediate obligations, leaving CAD 5,000 at time zero. It then pays CAD 1,500 of carrying and administration costs each month for twenty-four months. A separate CAD 60,000 payment is scheduled at the end of month six. This input is a placeholder for a separately estimated tax or debt obligation. The model does not calculate an actual liability, determine claim priority or assign a statutory deadline. The later net sale receipt is CAD 250,000 in month nine. Under the model’s explicit convention, receipts arrive at the beginning of their selected month and bills settle at month-end. Actual settlement dates within a month can matter, so a monthly ledger should not replace a dated payment list when the margin is tight. Read the deepest shortage as well as the endpoint The selected cash path falls below zero before the sale. At the end of month six, after the separate payment, the position is negative CAD 64,000. Continuing carrying costs take it to negative CAD 67,000 after month eight, just before the modeled month-nine receipt. The maximum-additional-cash metric is therefore CAD 67,000. It is the amount which, if available at the start without interest or repayment, would keep this selected ledger from falling below zero. The tool does not establish that borrowing, an advance or any other funding source is available. The comparison curve moves the same receipt up to three months earlier while keeping every amount unchanged. A different receipt date can reduce the peak funding need even though the final balance remains identical. The curves connect month-end observations; they do not show every intra-month movement. Reconcile the totals without calling the remainder distributable The totals waterfall adds CAD 25,000 of starting cash and CAD 250,000 of later proceeds, then subtracts CAD 20,000 of immediate obligations, CAD 36,000 of recurring costs and the separate CAD 60,000 payment. It ends at CAD 159,000. That positive endpoint coexists with the earlier CAD 67,000 funding gap. Neither figure measures the full estate’s legal solvency or the amount beneficiaries may receive. Assets and obligations outside this ledger, later assessments, unresolved claims and professional costs could change the result. The CRA’s clearance-certificate guidance explains the representative’s tax exposure when assets are distributed without clearance and tax remains owing. A positive cash forecast does not replace clearance, legal advice or the other requirements applicable to a distribution. Stress the dates and document the assumptions The matrix changes the sale-receipt month and the separate payment month. Each cell finds the deepest cash shortage over the full twenty-four-month ledger after counting starting cash. Immediate obligations and monthly costs remain fixed. Same-month receipts precede bills by convention. Use the grid to identify a dependency that needs verification: a planned receipt may need confirmed authority, a completed sale and accessible settlement funds. The selected dates are neither predicted processing times nor permission to postpone an obligation. The ledger includes no interest on borrowing and no investment return on temporary cash. It assumes the monthly costs continue for the whole horizon and includes no beneficiary distribution. A practical review replaces placeholders with supported amounts and dates, records what remains uncertain, and checks who has authority to act before treating an apparent funding solution as available.
6a45517de2b4831790a0bb7ba8e080394e1ba4d9.zh: 分别列出金额和访问日期。即使账本最终结余为正，预计稍后将变成现金的资产也可能导致直接成本无法得到资助。区分资产和可用于支付发票的资金 遗产可以拥有有价值的财产，但缺乏现金支付现在到期的账单。获取、销售时间、担保债务和管理要求会影响金额何时可用。不列颠哥伦比亚省的遗产指南描述了职责，包括列出资产和债务、支付有效义务、提交申报表和准备账目。其指南专门针对 BC 省；其他司法管辖区有自己的要求。此插图仅追踪遗产现金。假设授权代表可以使用起始现金，并且稍后的资产出售会提供单独的收据。执行人或受益人的个人资金不会自动包含在内。销售投入是指扣除销售成本和担保贷款后、在单独的税收和债务支付进入控制之前的现金。它不是财产总价值。在净销售额和单独付款中输入负债会将同一义务计算两次。将即时债务和经常性债务列入日历 该示例从 25,000 加元的可用现金和 20,000 加元的即时债务开始，在时间为零时留下 5,000 加元。然后，它在二十四个月内每月支付 1,500 加元的持有和管理费用。计划于第六个月月底单独支付 60,000 加元。此输入是单独估计的税收或债务义务的占位符。该模型不计算实际责任、确定索赔优先权或指定法定期限。第九个月的后期净销售收入为 250,000 加元。根据该模型的明确惯例，收据在所选月份的月初到达，账单在月底结算。一个月内的实际结算日期可能很重要，因此当保证金紧张时，每月分类账不应取代有日期的付款清单。阅读最严重的短缺以及终点 选定的现金路径在销售前降至零以下。第六个月末，单独付款后，头寸为负 64,000 加元。持续的持有成本在第八个月之后（就在模拟的第九个月收据之前）将其降至负 67,000 加元。因此，最大额外现金指标为 67,000 加元。如果一开始就可以使用，无需利息或偿还，该金额将防止所选分类账跌至零以下。该工具并未确定是否可以使用借款、预付款或任何其他资金来源。比较曲线将同一张收据提前三个月，同时保持每笔金额不变。即使最终余额保持不变，不同的收款日期也可以减少高峰资金需求。曲线连接月末观察结果；它们并不显示每个月内的变动。核对总计，而不称剩余部分可分配 总计瀑布添加 25,000 加元的起始现金和 250,000 加元的后续收益，然后减去 20,000 加元的直接债务、36,000 加元的经常性成本和单独的 60,000 加元付款。最终价格为 159,000 加元。这一积极的终点与之前 67,000 加元的资金缺口并存。这两个数字都没有衡量全部遗产的法定偿债能力或受益人可能收到的金额。该分类账之外的资产和义务、后期评估、未解决的索赔和专业成本可能会改变结果。 CRA 的清关证书指南解释了在未经清关的情况下分配资产且仍欠税款时代表的税务风险。积极的现金预测并不能取代许可、法律建议或适用于分配的其他要求。强调日期并记录假设 矩阵更改销售收据月份和单独付款月份。在计算起始现金后，每个单元都发现整个二十四个月的账本中最严重的现金短缺。直接义务和每月费用保持不变。按照惯例，同月收据先于账单。使用网格来识别需要验证的依赖项：计划的收据可能需要确认的授权、完成的销售和可用的结算资金。所选日期既不是预计的处理时间，也不是推迟义务的许可。该分类账不包括借款利息，也不包括临时现金的投资回报。它假设每月成本在整个范围内持续存在，并且不包括受益人分配。实际审查用支持的金额和日期替换占位符，记录仍然不确定的内容，并在将明显的资助解决方案视为可用之前检查谁有权采取行动。

0fe644ed038648c69490c0c1ac421f5c3b7e90be.src: A retirement plan needs a calendar as well as a total. Temporary earnings may end before another income source starts, leaving a larger withdrawal request in the intervening years. Draw the income calendar before choosing a withdrawal amount Retirement rarely replaces one paycheque with a single identical payment. An ongoing pension, temporary work, a later pension and personal savings can each follow a different schedule. The Government of Canada’s retirement-income overview describes public pensions, workplace plans and personal savings as separate sources. Actual benefits depend on their own rules and the individual’s history. This illustration starts with net amounts available to the household. It does not estimate pension entitlements or calculate tax. Enter a spending target, income already available, temporary work and an additional income source with its own starting year. All amounts use year-one purchasing power and then rise at the selected common annual rate. The first chart compares the resulting annual spending and income paths. It makes changes in the funding mix visible before a portfolio withdrawal rule is applied. The additional-income amount stays the same in year-one dollars when its start date changes; no delayed-pension enhancement is assumed. Notice the years between temporary work and later income The default target is CAD 60,000 a year, with CAD 18,000 of ongoing income and CAD 12,000 of temporary work for three years. Year one therefore asks savings to supply CAD 30,000. With the selected 2% annual cash-flow increase, the next two requests are CAD 30,600 and CAD 31,212. Temporary work then ends, while the additional income does not start until year six. The year-four withdrawal request rises to CAD 44,570.74 and year five to CAD 45,462.15. Those amounts reflect both the income interruption and the common annual increase. A flat average across the full horizon would hide the timing of the larger requests. In year six, the additional CAD 24,000 of annual income, stated in year-one dollars, becomes available. The nominal gap falls to CAD 19,873.45. It does not disappear because the combined ongoing sources still cover only CAD 42,000 of the CAD 60,000 base spending target. Separate the bridge subtotal from the full illustration The first metric adds withdrawal requests in the years before the additional source begins. In the default case, that is approximately CAD 181,844.89 over the first five years. It is an undiscounted nominal subtotal, rather than the capital needed on the starting date. The capital metric instead discounts every requested withdrawal across the selected twelve-year horizon. The formula is starting capital = sum of each year’s requested withdrawal divided by (1 + return) raised to that year . At the default constant 4% annual return, the result is approximately CAD 264,151.23. This amount funds only the displayed withdrawals under the selected timing. It requires no terminal reserve and includes no expenses after year twelve. Calling it a complete retirement target would overlook the rest of the person’s life, as well as uncertain returns, taxes and changing needs. Keep unfunded spending separate from portfolio assets The portfolio chart starts with CAD 200,000 in the default example. Each year, the balance earns the assumed return before the requested year-end withdrawal. The actual withdrawal cannot exceed available assets. Any difference is added to a separate cumulative unfunded-spending series. After depletion, the portfolio remains at zero; this model adds no new deposits. The unfunded curve is neither an investment account nor an available credit line. It records spending the assumed portfolio could not supply, without assuming that spending was financed elsewhere. If income exceeds spending, the withdrawal request is zero. That surplus is left unallocated rather than automatically saved. A real plan can assign it a destination, but doing so would introduce an additional decision about contributions, access and future use. Test the bridge without turning it into a pension recommendation The matrix changes the spending target and the later-income start year, keeping the selected return, horizon, temporary-work schedule and income amount. Its cells use the full-horizon present-value calculation. Changing a date can alter capital needs even when the annual income amount is unchanged. Actual CPP, OAS or workplace-pension timing may also change benefit amounts, tax, eligibility and household outcomes. Those effects are outside this generic calendar. Use current personal estimates and the relevant program rules before comparing an actual start-age choice. Review the bridge alongside the sequence-risk and longevity guides. This article explains the schedule of a transition; those additional questions concern uncertain return order and how long a wider plan must last. A useful review records both the dates that create the largest requests and the assumptions that could make those requests harder to fund.
0fe644ed038648c69490c0c1ac421f5c3b7e90be.zh: 退休计划需要日历和总计。临时收入可能会在另一个收入来源开始之前结束，从而在接下来的几年中留下更大的提款请求。在选择提款金额之前绘制收入日历退休很少用单笔相同的付款取代一张薪水支票。持续养老金、临时工作、后期养老金和个人储蓄可以遵循不同的时间表。加拿大政府的退休收入概述将公共养老金、工作场所计划和个人储蓄描述为不同的来源。实际的好处取决于他们自己的规则和个人的历史。此图从家庭可用净金额开始。它不估计养老金权利或计算税收。输入支出目标、现有收入、临时工作和具有自己起始年份的额外收入来源。所有金额均使用第一年购买力，然后按选定的共同年利率上涨。第一个图表比较了由此产生的年度支出和收入路径。在应用投资组合撤回规则之前，它使资金组合的变化可见。当开始日期发生变化时，额外收入金额以第一年美元计算保持不变；假设没有延迟养老金增加。注意临时工作和以后收入之间的年数 默认目标是每年 60,000 加元，其中持续收入 18,000 加元，三年临时工作收入 12,000 加元。因此，第一年要求节省 30,000 加元。根据选定的年度现金流增长 2%，接下来的两个请求分别是 30,600 加元和 31,212 加元。然后临时工作结束，而额外收入直到第六年才开始。第四年的提款请求升至 44,570.74 加元，第五年则升至 45,462.15 加元。这些金额反映了收入中断和普遍的年度增长。整个范围内的平坦平均值将隐藏较大请求的时间。第六年，额外的年收入 24,000 加元（以第一年美元计算）变为可用。名义缺口降至 19,873.45 加元。它并没有消失，因为合并后的持续来源仍仅覆盖 60,000 加元基本支出目标中的 42,000 加元。将桥梁小计与完整说明分开 第一个指标添加了附加来源开始之前几年的提款请求。在默认情况下，前五年约为 181,844.89 加元。这是未贴现的名义小计，而不是开始日期所需的资本。相反，资本指标对选定的十二年范围内每笔请求的提款进行折扣。公式为起始资本 = 每年要求提款的总和除以当年筹集的（1 + 回报）。按默认固定年回报率 4% 计算，结果约为 264,151.23 加元。该金额仅资助所选时间下显示的提款。它不需要终端储备，并且十二年后不包含任何费用。将其称为完整的退休目标会忽视人的余生，以及不确定的回报、税收和不断变化的需求。将无资金支持的支出与投资组合资产分开 在默认示例中，投资组合图表以 200,000 加元开始。每年，余额都会在要求的年终提款之前赚取假定的回报。实际提现不能超过可用资产。任何差额都会添加到单独的累积无资金支出系列中。耗尽后，投资组合仍为零；该模型不增加新的存款。无资金曲线既不是投资账户，也不是可用的信用额度。它记录了假设的投资组合无法提供的支出，而不假设支出是由其他地方融资的。如果收入超过支出，则提款请求为零。该盈余未分配而不是自动保存。真正的计划可以为其分配一个目的地，但这样做会引入有关贡献、访问和未来使用的额外决策。测试桥梁，而不将其转变为养老金建议 该矩阵更改支出目标和较晚的收入开始年份，保持选定的回报、期限、临时工作时间表和收入金额。其单元格使用全范围现值计算。即使年收入金额不变，更改日期也会改变资本需求。实际的 CPP、OAS 或工作场所养老金时间也可能会改变福利金额、税收、资格和家庭结果。这些影响不属于这个通用日历。在比较实际的起始年龄选择之前，请使用当前的个人估计和相关计划规则。与序列风险和寿命指南一起回顾桥梁。本文解释了过渡的时间表；这些额外问题涉及不确定的退货令以及更广泛的计划必须持续多久。有用的审查会记录创建最大请求的日期以及可能使这些请求更难获得资助的假设。

a48dbfb47503d3adf70d24cf802aa23f2987cdb3.src: An unpaid care role can affect a budget through both extra bills and reduced earnings. Build one incremental cash ledger, then compare its timing with the money actually available. Use survey context without treating it as a personal forecast Statistics Canada’s 2022 survey , published in April 2024, reports mutually exclusive shares of 58.1% with no unpaid care, 14.4% providing adult care only, 21.9% child care only and 5.6% both. The target population was non-institutionalized people aged 15 or older living off-reserve in the ten provinces; the reference was care in the previous twelve months. The first graphic displays those rounded survey estimates. It remains fixed when scenario inputs change. The source provides confidence intervals; the chart does not estimate an individual’s future care needs or the price of paid help. The other three graphics are hypothetical cash calculations for a selected arrangement. Their hours, hourly cost, earnings reduction and support amounts are editable assumptions. They are not estimates derived from the survey. Add both sides of the household cash impact Start with the budget before the new arrangement. The model takes the monthly surplus already left after that budget, then calculates what the care arrangement changes. Paid support and additional transport or supplies add outflows. A reduction in net earnings removes receipts even though it is not a bill from a provider. The default eight hours of paid support each week at CAD 35 per hour becomes CAD 1,213.33 per average month, using 52 weeks divided by twelve. Add CAD 150 of transport and supplies and CAD 800 of lower monthly net earnings. The combined incremental burden is CAD 2,163.33. Confirmed net support of CAD 300 and the existing CAD 500 monthly budget surplus reduce the amount drawn from cash to CAD 1,363.33 per month. The waterfall makes these offsets visible so a source of help is not accidentally deducted twice or counted before it is available. Place one-time expenses at the start The default arrangement also requires CAD 2,000 at setup. That amount is paid before the recurring monthly flows begin. The reserve path therefore starts at CAD 10,000 after setup from the selected CAD 12,000 starting reserve. At the selected monthly draw, the illustrative cash position is still positive after month seven and negative after month eight. The negative section represents unfunded cash needs. It does not assume a bank permits an overdraft, a family member lends money, or a provider allows payment to be postponed. Across twenty-four months, setup plus recurring net draws requires CAD 34,720 of starting cash under the model. After counting the CAD 12,000 already allocated, the additional amount is CAD 22,720. These figures use the unrounded monthly arithmetic; displayed values may be rounded to cents. Use support amounts that can actually fund the schedule The support input is a net receipt that is assumed available every month. It does not calculate a tax credit, employer benefit, public program payment or reimbursement. A benefit paid later cannot fund an earlier invoice unless another source covers the interval. Keep the earnings reduction consistent with the starting budget. If the base budget already uses the lower earnings, adding the same reduction again would overstate the burden. Similarly, enter only additional travel and supplies, rather than costs already included in regular household spending. A negative monthly draw means entered resources exceed the incremental recurring burden. Even then, setup still needs funding at time zero. The required-starting-cash measure therefore cannot fall below the setup amount merely because later monthly receipts replenish cash. Vary the arrangement and revisit the wider plan The matrix compares paid support hours and durations while holding other selected inputs fixed. Each cell reports the additional starting cash after the chosen reserve. It is a funding comparison, rather than a determination of how many care hours are suitable. Different arrangements may also change the caregiver’s earnings, travel or support eligibility. The fixed-grid comparison isolates hours and duration, so those related effects must be considered separately. A new quote or confirmed work schedule provides a reason to update the inputs. The model does not put a monetary value on all unpaid work, calculate lost pension contributions, assess health needs or evaluate care quality. Those questions require their own information. The ledger’s purpose is narrower and practical: identify which receipts change, which bills arrive, when setup must be paid and whether available cash covers the selected schedule.
a48dbfb47503d3adf70d24cf802aa23f2987cdb3.zh: 无酬护理角色可能会通过额外的账单和收入减少来影响预算。建立一个增量现金分类账，然后将其时间与实际可用资金进行比较。使用调查背景，而不是将其视为个人预测加拿大统计局于 2024 年 4 月发布的 2022 年调查显示，58.1% 的人不提供无偿护理，14.4% 的人只提供成人护理，21.9% 的人只提供儿童护理，5.6% 的人两者都提供。目标人群是居住在十个省份的非保留地的 15 岁或以上的非收容人口；参考内容是过去十二个月的护理。第一张图显示了这些四舍五入的调查估计值。当场景输入发生变化时，它保持固定。来源提供了置信区间；该图表不会估计个人未来的护理需求或有偿帮助的价格。其他三个图表是针对选定安排的假设现金计算。他们的工作时间、每小时成本、收入减少和支持金额都是可编辑的假设。它们不是根据调查得出的估计值。添加家庭现金影响的双方 从新安排之前的预算开始。该模型采用预算后剩余的每月盈余，然后计算护理安排的变化。有偿支持和额外的运输或物资增加了资金外流。净收入的减少会消除收据，即使它不是来自提供商的账单。默认每周 8 小时的付费支持（每小时 35 加元）变为每月 1,213.33 加元（按 52 周除以 12 计算）。添加 150 加元的运输和用品以及 800 加元的较低月净利润。合计增量负担为 2,163.33 加元。已确认的 300 加元净支持和现有的 500 加元每月预算盈余使每月提取的现金金额减少至 1,363.33 加元。瀑布使这些偏移量变得可见，因此帮助来源不会意外地被扣除两次或在可用之前被计数。一开始就记下一次性费用 默认安排在设置时也需要 2,000 加元。该金额是在每月定期流量开始之前支付的。因此，在从选定的 12,000 加元起始储备设置后，储备路径的起始价格为 10,000 加元。在选定的每月提款中，说明性现金头寸在第七个月后仍为正值，在第八个月后仍为负值。负数部分代表没有资金支持的现金需求。它不假设银行允许透支、家庭成员借钱或提供商允许推迟付款。在该模型下，在 24 个月内，设置加上经常性净提款需要 34,720 加元的起始现金。算上已分配的 12,000 加元后，额外金额为 22,720 加元。这些数字使用不四舍五入的月度算术；显示的值可能四舍五入为分。使用能够实际为计划提供资金的支持金额 支持输入是假设每月可用的净收据。它不计算税收抵免、雇主福利、公共计划付款或报销。稍后支付的福利不能为较早的发票提供资金，除非有其他来源涵盖该时间间隔。使收入减少与起始预算保持一致。如果基本预算已经使用了较低的收入，那么再次增加相同的减少就会夸大负担。同样，仅输入额外的旅行和用品，而不是已包含在常规家庭支出中的费用。每月负数提取意味着输入的资源超过了增量经常性负担。即便如此，设置在零时间仍然需要资金。因此，所需的起始现金指标不能仅仅因为后来的每月收入补充现金而低于设定金额。改变安排并重新审视更广泛的计划 该矩阵比较付费支持时间和持续时间，同时保持其他选定输入固定。每个单元格报告选定储备后的额外起始现金。这是资金比较，而不是确定多少护理时间合适。不同的安排也可能会改变看护者的收入、旅行或赡养资格。固定网格比较隔离了时间和持续时间，因此必须单独考虑这些相关影响。新的报价或确认的工作计划提供了更新输入的理由。该模型没有对所有无酬工作进行货币价值计算，也没有计算养老金缴款损失、评估健康需求或评估护理质量。这些问题需要自己的信息。分类账的目的更窄且更实用：确定哪些收据发生变化、哪些账单到达、何时必须支付设置以及可用现金是否满足所选时间表。

9802438f82ab7b72cce93f0f9630fcebf3c2a7d5.src: A cheaper replacement home does not automatically release the difference in prices. Mortgage balances, transaction costs and the funding of the replacement determine the cash result. Start with the proceeds available after selling The sale price is a gross amount. Before assigning it to another goal, account for the current mortgage repayment and the applicable selling costs. The Financial Consumer Agency of Canada’s selling guide lists costs such as legal and discharge fees and possible commissions, moving expenses and mortgage prepayment charges. This model separates a percentage-based selling allowance from other sale-side costs and a tax provision. The percentages and fixed amounts are hypothetical inputs, not commission quotations, statutory tax rates or a calculation of a mortgage penalty. The default CAD 900,000 sale less CAD 36,000 of percentage-based costs, CAD 5,000 of other provisions and a CAD 250,000 mortgage repayment leaves CAD 609,000. The model does not determine whether a tax exemption applies or calculate tax due on the sale. Fund the replacement and the move The next step is the replacement purchase price, its purchase costs, and moving or setup costs, less the assumed new mortgage. The FCAC’s homebuying guide emphasizes upfront costs beyond the mortgage and lists examples of closing expenses. For a CAD 650,000 replacement, a 3% purchase-cost allowance adds CAD 19,500 and moving costs add CAD 5,000. The default 30% assumed mortgage finances CAD 195,000. The cash needed for those settlements is therefore CAD 479,500. The assumed mortgage percentage is a scenario input. It does not establish qualification, available proceeds, insurance treatment, interest rates or monthly affordability. A real plan needs confirmed financing and actual closing figures. The tool’s percentage-based cost allowances also cannot replace calculations of charges that follow different rules. Read the full reconciliation The waterfall adds sale proceeds, subtracts sale costs, repays the old loan, pays for the replacement and its costs, and adds the new financing. Its endpoint is cash released or additional cash needed under the selected assumptions. The default net cash release is CAD 129,500. The home-price difference alone is CAD 250,000, but mortgage debt falls by CAD 55,000 and entered transaction and moving costs total CAD 65,500. Those uses of funds explain why the price difference overstates the cash available for another goal. The step order is an accounting reconciliation, not a closing calendar. In particular, adding mortgage funding as a later step does not assert that the borrower must first pay the purchase price entirely in cash. The model assumes the settlements occur together; a different sequence requires a separate timing and bridging review.
