d21844710d96e58b31b9819875dda05b48d2c4a4.zh: 比较相同净节省成本的可支出结果。账户总余额本身并不能显示税后可用资金。从不同的纳税时间开始加拿大税务局的RRSP概述解释说，可扣除的供款可以减少税收，计划内的收入通常在保留期间受到保护，并且付款通常是应纳税的。 CRA 的 TFSA 概述解释说，捐款不可扣除，合格账户收入和取款通常免税。这些图表将这些机制隔离开来。他们假设两个账户持有的投资获得完全相同的回报，并且两个账户都有足够的可用空间用于建模贡献。他们不选择投资、计算资格或估计个人的实际税单。税收减免和提款税以适用于全部相关金额的固定百分比输入。实际扣除和提款可以跨越不同的范围，并与其他收入、福利和信贷相互作用。这里的百分比是假设的假设，而不是公布的联邦或省税率。保持个人储蓄成本不变 假设可用的税后储蓄预算为 B，完全可扣除的 RRSP 供款的税收减免为 t。模型化的 RRSP 总贡献为 B ÷ (1 − t) 。税收减免弥补了该捐款与 B 之间的差额。TFSA 直接收到 B。对于 10,000 加元的个人预算和 40% 的税收减免，RRSP 供款为 16,666.67 加元。假设税收减免为 6,666.67 加元，净成本为 10,000 加元。 TFSA 捐款为 10,000 加元。在没有税收处理的情况下比较这些总存款将无法理解它们之间的差异。这假设救济金可以立即使用，并为较大的存款提供资金，例如通过适当安排的现金流流程。稍后收到的退款会产生时间或财务问题。如果退款是花掉而不是包含在储蓄中，那与今天不同的消费是不同的比较。该工具不会对退款延迟或借贷成本进行建模。阅读税后条形图和增长路径 期末余额图表显示账户价值和建模的可支出价值。对于RRSP，第二条从整个余额中扣除假定的提款税。对于 TFSA，这两个条在此处假设的合格免税待遇下是一致的。 20 年利率为 5%，默认 TFSA 达到 26,532.98 加元。假定全额提款需缴纳 30% 的税后，RRSP 总计还剩 30,955.14 加元。差异来自于选定的税率关系，具有相同的增长假设和净初始储蓄成本。折线图显示了早期日期的相同比较。每个 RRSP 积分均假定在该日期使用相同的选定税率完全提款。它不是一系列年度提款、收入提款策略或强制性注册账户付款的计算。所选择的回报在实践中是平滑的且具有不确定性。使用矩阵查看等利率结果 如果 RRSP 扣除减免和提款率相等，则该模型会产生与 TFSA 相同的可支出结果。从代数上来说，RRSP 净值 ÷ TFSA = (1 − 提款率) ÷ (1 − 扣除减免率) 。共同增长因子与起始预算取消。该矩阵将比率减一显示为百分比差异。正值代表模拟的RRSP金额较大；负细胞意味着它更小。这些金额是相对于 TFSA 结果的金额，而不是年化投资回报。改变期限或共同投资回报不会改变这种孤立的比率。瀑布式调节 RRSP 总余额、提款税费和 TFSA 比较金额。税收减免一开始就已经为总贡献提供了资金。再次将退款添加到期末余额中会将同一资源计数两次。在决定之前添加规则和现金流限制实际账户选择还取决于可用的供款和扣除空间、使用日期、访问需求、取款规则、雇主安排和家庭更广泛的税收情况。检查当前 CRA 对这些问题的指导，而不是将这个简化的说明扩展到其假设之外。该工具假设任一合格账户内均为单笔存款且没有额外的税收拖累。它省略了费用、预扣机制、收入测试福利、未来账户转换规则、遗产处理和税法变化。现在无法完全使用的扣除也打破了立即救济的假设。记录净节省成本、如何资助和使用税收减免，以及未来提款税的合理范围。然后将结果与目标的时间安排和流动性要求进行比较。透明的比较有助于识别需要审查的变量；最大的总余额本身并不能解决账户决策。

57c9707bec2d3f7f1fa5e896f16107d55ea868b6.src: A later start trades early cash flow for a larger payment later. Compare that trade-off with the cost of funding the waiting period and the household’s other needs. Separate the age adjustment from the entitlement estimate The Government of Canada’s CPP start-age guidance states that the standard start age is 65, with starts available from 60 to 70. Before 65, the monthly amount is reduced by 0.6% for each month early. After 65, it increases by 0.7% for each month delayed, through age 70. The first chart applies those factors to one common assumed age-65 entitlement. At the default CAD 1,000 per month, the illustrative payments are CAD 640 at 60, CAD 1,000 at 65 and CAD 1,420 at 70. The CAD 1,000 input is neither an official maximum nor an average payment. A personal CPP estimate also depends on the contribution record and applicable calculation rules. Working longer or changing future contributions can change that underlying entitlement. This tool freezes the entitlement to isolate the age adjustment. It does not retrieve a contribution history or calculate the pension that a particular person will receive. Read the cash-flow head start The cumulative chart counts the payments received by each birthday. At the chosen starting birthday, cumulative receipts are zero; the following birthday includes twelve month-end payments. The age axis begins at 60 so the years relevant to the comparison remain visible. Starting at 65 provides five years of payments before a start at 70 begins. Under the default assumption, that head start is CAD 60,000 in constant purchasing-power dollars. After 70, the later-start case receives CAD 420 more each month. It gradually makes up the difference if the person continues receiving payments. Ignoring discounting, tax and all other effects, the continuous arithmetic crossover is about age 81.9 for 65 versus 70. With month-end payments, the first crossover is at the 143rd payment after age 70. This is a conditional receipt calculation. It does not establish the age a person will live to or recommend waiting until 70. Account for when the money arrives A dollar available sooner and a dollar received decades later have different timing. The present-value bars discount each monthly payment back to age 60 using the selected real annual rate, converted to an equivalent monthly rate. All payments in the illustration are expressed in constant purchasing-power dollars. The discount rate must therefore also be real. Using a nominal investment return against these real cash flows would mix measurement bases. The tool does not separately forecast CPI or reproduce actual annual CPP indexation. A positive discount rate gives more weight to earlier payments. The matrix compares start-at-70 receipts with start-at-65 receipts over several final ages and discount rates. Each signed cell is a present-value difference at age 60. A negative cell favors the earlier receipts under that calculation; a positive cell favors the later receipts. There is no probability attached to a cell. Plan the years before the pension starts The charts count CPP receipts only. They do not deduct the resources needed to pay household expenses while waiting. If employment, other pensions or savings must cover that period, write down the annual shortfalls and identify their funding sources. A person who uses an investment portfolio for the bridge may make larger withdrawals before CPP starts. The portfolio’s return sequence, tax cost and remaining flexibility then matter. The sequence-risk guide explains why the same average investment return can produce different results when withdrawals occur. Conversely, a household with sufficient income from elsewhere may value the larger later monthly payment differently from one with immediate cash needs. A simple cumulative-payment crossover cannot represent all those circumstances. Compare a full household cash-flow plan alongside the receipt chart. Treat longevity and benefit interactions separately Every plotted receipt assumes the person is alive to receive it. The model applies no survival probabilities and computes no expected present value. A comparison through age 95 is an assumption about the payment horizon, rather than a prediction or a statement about population life expectancy. Taxes, income-tested benefits, survivor benefits, disability-related provisions, future contributions and QPP rules are outside the tool. These can affect an actual decision. A household review should also consider health, a spouse or partner’s cash flows, debt costs, flexibility and the consequence of living longer than initially planned. Use an up-to-date personal estimate and verify the applicable rules before implementing a start date. Keep the entitlement estimate, age adjustment, payment timing and bridge funding as distinct inputs. The four charts make one part of that decision visible while leaving room for the circumstances that a receipt-only model cannot resolve.
57c9707bec2d3f7f1fa5e896f16107d55ea868b6.zh: 较晚的开始可以用较早的现金流来换取稍后更大的付款。将这种权衡与等待期的资金成本和家庭的其他需求进行比较。将年龄调整与权利估算分开加拿大政府的CPP起始年龄指南规定，标准起始年龄为65岁，起始年龄为60岁至70岁。在65岁之前，每月金额提前每月减少0.6%。 65 岁之后，每延迟一个月，该福利就会增加 0.7%，一直到 70 岁。第一个图表将这些因素应用于一个常见的假定 65 岁的权利。在默认每月 1,000 加元的情况下，说明性付款额为 60 岁时为 640 加元、65 岁时为 1,000 加元、70 岁时为 1,420 加元。输入的 1,000 加元既不是官方最高付款额，也不是平均付款额。个人 CPP 估算还取决于缴款记录和适用的计算规则。工作时间更长或改变未来的缴款可能会改变基本权利。该工具冻结了隔离年龄调整的权利。它不会检索缴款历史或计算特定人将收到的养老金。阅读现金流头开始 累积图表计算每个生日收到的付款。在选定的起始生日，累计收据为零；接下来的生日包括十二个月末付款。年龄轴从 60 岁开始，因此与比较相关的年份仍然可见。从 65 岁开始提供五年付款，然后从 70 岁开始付款。在默认假设下，以不变购买力美元计算，领先优势为 60,000 加元。 70 岁以后，较晚开始的案件每月会多收到 420 加元。如果该人继续收到付款，它会逐渐弥补差额。忽略折扣、税收和所有其他影响，65 岁与 70 岁的连续算术交叉点约为 81.9 岁。对于月末付款，第一次交叉点是 70 岁后的第 143 次付款。这是有条件收据计算。它没有规定一个人的寿命，也没有建议等到 70 岁。 考虑钱何时到账 较早收到的一美元和几十年后收到的一美元有不同的时间。现值条使用选定的实际年利率（转换为等值月利率）对 60 岁之前的每月付款进行折扣。图中的所有付款均以恒定购买力美元表示。因此，贴现率也必须是真实的。使用名义投资回报与这些实际现金流量会混合衡量基础。该工具不会单独预测 CPI 或重现实际的年度 CPP 指数。正的贴现率给予提前付款更多的权重。该矩阵比较了 70 岁起的收据和 65 岁起的收据在几个最终年龄和折扣率下的情况。每个带符号的单元格都是 60 岁时的现值差异。负的单元格有利于该计算下较早的收据；阳性细胞有利于后来的收据。细胞不存在任何概率。规划养老金开始前的年份 该图表仅计算 CPP 收入。他们不会在等待期间扣除支付家庭开支所需的资源。如果就业、其他养老金或储蓄必须覆盖该时期，请记下年度缺口并确定其资金来源。使用投资组合作为桥梁的人可能会在 CPP 开始之前提取更多资金。投资组合的回报顺序、税收成本和剩余的灵活性都很重要。顺序风险指南解释了为什么相同的平均投资回报在发生提款时会产生不同的结果。相反，一个从其他地方获得足够收入的家庭可能会与有即时现金需求的家庭不同地评估稍后每月支付的较大金额。简单的累积付款交叉不能代表所有这些情况。将完整的家庭现金流计划与收据图表进行比较。分别对待长寿和利益相互作用每张绘制的收据都假设该人还活着以接收它。该模型不应用生存概率，也不计算预期现值。 95 岁之前的比较是对还款期限的假设，而不是对人口预期寿命的预测或陈述。税收、收入测试福利、遗属福利、残疾相关条款、未来缴款和 QPP 规则均不在该工具范围内。这些都会影响实际的决定。家庭审查还应考虑健康状况、配偶或伴侣的现金流、债务成本、灵活性以及寿命超过最初计划的后果。在实施开始日期之前，使用最新的个人估算并验证适用的规则。将权利估算、年龄调整、付款时间和过桥资金保留为不同的输入。这四个图表使该决策的一部分变得可见，同时为仅收据模型无法解决的情况留出了空间。

81449ff239cda7b88906d25a75ee7fc2185468e1.src: The comparison depends on the full cash flows and the holding period. Include the down payment’s alternative use, ownership costs and the costs of leaving. Give both households the same starting resources A useful comparison begins with homes that provide comparable housing services and households that start with the same money. A larger property with a different location or quality changes the living arrangement as well as the financing decision. The buyer uses starting capital for the down payment and purchase costs. The renter invests that same capital. In the default example, a CAD 600,000 home, 20% down payment and 2% purchase costs require CAD 132,000. The mortgage begins at CAD 480,000; the renter’s investment portfolio begins at CAD 132,000. The Financial Consumer Agency of Canada’s homebuying guide emphasizes costs beyond the mortgage and lists examples of closing expenses. The percentages in these charts are hypothetical placeholders. They are not quotations for transfer tax, legal fees, commissions or a particular transaction. Invest the cost advantage in either direction Every month, the tool calculates each household’s housing cash outflow. It gives both households a common budget equal to the higher amount. Whichever option is cheaper invests the difference at month-end. This can be the renter or the owner, and the direction can change as rent and owner costs evolve. The owner pays mortgage principal and interest plus combined carrying costs. The carrying-cost assumption is a yearly percentage of the current modeled home value, allocated monthly. It can stand for a budget allowance for property tax, insurance, maintenance and similar expenses, but those actual bills need their own estimates. The renter pays the selected rent, increasing once a year at the assumed rate. The FCAC renting guide notes that additional rental expenses depend on the arrangement. Shared utilities and lifestyle costs are omitted here as equal in both cases. Add a difference to the budget before applying the comparison to unlike living arrangements. Distinguish the cash required from the cost consumed The first-year bars compare average monthly housing outflows before investing any cost difference. Mortgage principal is included because it must be paid, but it also reduces debt. Therefore, the outflow bars are not a pure economic-expense comparison between rent and interest. The mortgage uses a 25-year amortization and the same explicit semi-annual quoted-rate convention as the renewal guide. Its rate remains unchanged for the entire selected comparison. That simplifies the calculation but leaves renewal uncertainty out. Actual future payments may differ. Both portfolios earn the same effective annual investment return, converted to a monthly rate. Home value also changes smoothly each month at the selected annual assumption. Repairs can be uneven, investments fluctuate and neither growth rate is assured. A smooth path is a calculation convention, not a forecast of the experience of either household. Compare the resources available after an exit The owner’s line equals home value less assumed sale costs and outstanding mortgage debt, plus any investment portfolio accumulated from a monthly cost advantage. The renter’s line is the investment portfolio. Every point on the owner’s line assumes a sale at that date, including the starting point. That sale convention means the buyer starts below the renter after transaction costs. Purchase costs have been consumed, and the chart also allows for a hypothetical immediate sale cost. Longer holding periods give other cash flows and value changes more time to matter; they do not guarantee that either option wins. With the default assumptions, modeled year-ten resources are CAD 360,031.78 for the owner and CAD 287,564.12 for the renter. The waterfall reconciles the home value, sale costs, debt and both portfolios to show the difference. The endpoint measures relative modeled wealth, not the home’s investment profit or an annual return. Test assumptions that could reverse the comparison The matrix reruns the monthly comparison for different home-value changes and investment returns. Each signed cell is owner ending wealth minus renter ending wealth. It also recalculates the carrying costs tied to modeled home value. A positive result favors the owner within the model; a negative result favors the renter. Test a shorter stay, higher carrying costs, a weaker home-value path and different rent growth. Consider whether the assumed investments and regular saving would actually be maintained. A renter who spends the cost difference or an owner who faces an unbudgeted major repair follows a different path. The model excludes taxes and housing benefits, default insurance, moving expenses, detailed condominium assessments, rent-law constraints and the costs of mortgage changes. Its minimum down-payment input of 20% avoids modeling insured-mortgage premiums but does not establish eligibility or approval. Flexibility, location, stability and the household’s other goals also deserve weight. Use actual comparable-home costs and current contract terms before making the commitment.
81449ff239cda7b88906d25a75ee7fc2185468e1.zh: 比较取决于全部现金流量和持有期限。包括首付的替代用途、拥有成本和离开成本。为两个家庭提供相同的起始资源 有用的比较始于提供可比住房服务的家庭和以相同资金开始的家庭。位置或质量不同的较大房产会改变居住安排以及融资决策。买方使用启动资金支付首付款和购买费用。承租人投资同样的资本。在默认示例中，一套 600,000 加元的房屋，20% 的首付和 2% 的购买成本需要 132,000 加元。抵押贷款起价为48万加元；承租人的投资组合起价为 132,000 加元。加拿大金融消费者局的购房指南强调了抵押贷款之外的成本，并列出了成交费用的例子。这些图表中的百分比是假设的占位符。它们不是转让税、法律费用、佣金或特定交易的报价。向任一方向投资成本优势该工具每个月都会计算每个家庭的住房现金流出。它为两个家庭提供了等于较高金额的共同预算。无论哪种选择更便宜，都可以在月底投资差额。这可以是承租人，也可以是业主，而且方向可能会随着租金和业主成本的变化而改变。业主支付抵押贷款本金和利息以及综合持有成本。持有成本假设是当前模型房屋价值的每年百分比，每月分配。它可以代表财产税、保险、维护和类似费用的预算补贴，但这些实际账单需要自己的估计。承租人支付选定的租金，每年按假定费率增加一次。 FCAC 租赁指南指出，额外的租金费用取决于安排。此处省略了共享公用事业和生活成本，因为在这两种情况下都是相同的。在将比较应用于不同的生活安排之前，先添加预算差异。区分所需的现金和消耗的成本第一年的条形图比较了投资任何成本差异之前的平均每月住房流出量。抵押贷款本金被包括在内，因为它必须支付，但它也减少了债务。因此，流出栏并不是租金和利息之间纯粹的经济支出比较。该抵押贷款采用 25 年摊销期，并采用与续约指南相同的明确的半年度报价利率惯例。在整个选定的比较中，其比率保持不变。这简化了计算，但排除了更新的不确定性。未来的实际付款可能会有所不同。两种投资组合都获得相同的有效年度投资回报（转换为月利率）。在选定的年度假设下，房屋价值每个月也会平稳变化。修复工作可能参差不齐，投资波动，而且增长率也无法保证。平滑路径是一种计算惯例，而不是对任一家庭的经历的预测。比较退出后可用的资源业主的额度等于房屋价值减去假设的销售成本和未偿还的抵押贷款债务，加上每月成本优势积累的任何投资组合。承租人的线是投资组合。业主线上的每个点都假定在该日期出售，包括起始点。这种销售惯例意味着买方在扣除交易成本后的起价低于承租人。购买成本已消耗，图表还考虑了假设的立即销售成本。持有期越长，其他现金流和价值变化就有更多的时间发挥作用；他们不保证任何一个选项都会获胜。根据默认假设，建模的十年资源为所有者提供 360,031.78 加元，为承租人提供 287,564.12 加元。瀑布调整了房屋价值、销售成本、债务和两个投资组合以显示差异。端点衡量的是相对模型财富，而不是房屋的投资利润或年回报。测试可能逆转比较的假设 该矩阵针对不同的房屋价值变化和投资回报重新运行每月比较。每个带符号的单元格都是所有者期末财富减去租客期末财富。它还重新计算与模型房屋价值相关的持有成本。积极的结果有利于模型中的所有者；负面结果对承租人有利。测试较短的停留时间、较高的持有成本、较弱的房屋价值路径和不同的租金增长。考虑是否能够真正维持假设的投资和定期储蓄。花费成本差额的租户或面临预算外重大维修的业主则走不同的道路。该模型不包括税收和住房福利、违约保险、搬家费用、详细的公寓评估、租金法限制和抵押贷款变更成本。其 20% 的最低首付输入避免了对保险抵押贷款保费进行建模，但没有建立资格或批准。灵活性、位置、稳定性和家庭的其他目标也值得重视。在做出承诺之前，请使用实际的可比房屋成本和当前合同条款。

e1ac40adadefa10d3bb2ce481c3b40906e612ddf.src: A renewal changes the cost of financing the balance that remains. Test the payment against your budget while keeping the payoff date visible. Separate the next contract from the payoff horizon A mortgage term and its amortization answer different questions. The term describes the period covered by a particular contract. Amortization describes the repayment horizon used to calculate the scheduled payment. The Financial Consumer Agency of Canada’s renewal guide explains these distinctions and the choices involved at renewal. This illustration starts with a balance today, a current quoted rate and a remaining amortization. The assumed first term lasts five years. After 60 month-end payments, the renewal scenario applies a new rate to the balance still owed and recalculates the payment for the remaining years. The comparison keeps the original payoff date. With the default CAD 400,000 balance, 20-year amortization and 4% quoted rate, the modeled monthly payment is CAD 2,416.99. A 6% renewal rate after five years changes it to CAD 2,750.51, an increase of CAD 333.53. These are original hypothetical calculations, not current lender offers or a forecast of rates. Why two balance paths can reach zero together The first chart compares continuing at the original rate with changing the rate after five years. Both balances reach the same scheduled end date because the renewal payment adjusts. A higher rate does not have to mean a longer loan when the payment increases enough to preserve amortization. Do not read the balance line as the amount paid. A payment contains both interest and principal. Interest is a financing cost; principal reduces the debt. The stacked chart separates those components for years one through five and years six through ten in the renewal scenario. Those two five-year periods start with different balances. Their interest amounts therefore reflect both the rate and the amount still owed. They are successive stages of one financing path, rather than two otherwise identical loans. For a rate-only comparison, use the matrix, which holds the initial balance constant across its cells. Turn the payment change into a cash-flow test The payment bars show the recurring budget effect more directly than the outstanding-balance lines. Compare the increase with the amount left after ordinary spending, other required debt payments and planned saving. A budget that balances only by suspending every other goal has little flexibility. Try a higher renewal rate and record the monthly difference. Multiply that difference by twelve to estimate the annual cash-flow adjustment, while keeping it separate from a change in total interest over the full loan. The annual budget effect and lifetime borrowing cost answer different questions. Property taxes, home insurance, condominium charges, repairs and utilities remain outside the payment calculation. A reserve for these costs can be necessary even when the mortgage payment itself fits. The emergency-fund guide provides a separate way to model an income interruption; mortgage affordability alone does not measure that resilience. Read across the amortization matrix Each cell shows the monthly payment for today’s selected starting balance, using the displayed rate and amortization. Reading across a row isolates the horizon change. Reading down a column isolates the rate change. The grid uses the starting balance, so its cells are not renewal quotes based on the smaller year-five balance. At a positive rate, a longer amortization lowers the scheduled payment but keeps money borrowed for longer. Under an unchanged rate and a fully repaid loan, total scheduled interest is payment × number of payments − original principal. A lower monthly payment can therefore accompany a larger cumulative interest bill. Actual renewal options may involve lender requirements, fees, insurance considerations, contractual restrictions or a reassessment of the application. The chart does not establish that a particular amortization is available. Obtain the actual terms before treating a modeled payment as an executable option. Keep the compounding convention explicit This example assumes a quoted nominal annual rate compounded semi-annually. If j is that annual rate as a decimal, the equivalent monthly rate is m = (1 + j ÷ 2) 1/6 − 1 . For balance B and N remaining monthly payments, the payment is Bm ÷ [1 − (1 + m) −N ] . At zero interest, it is B ÷ N. Each month’s interest is opening balance × m. The payment first covers that interest and the remainder reduces principal. At renewal, the formula uses the remaining balance and remaining number of payments. The selected renewal rate then stays constant until payoff in this model. The tool excludes fees, prepayments, default-insurance premiums and later rate changes. Contracts can use different conventions. Read the lender’s disclosed interest calculation and payment schedule, then compare the resulting cash flows with this illustration. A useful review records the actual renewal date, balance, payment options and planned source of any increase.
e1ac40adadefa10d3bb2ce481c3b40906e612ddf.zh: 续约会改变剩余余额的融资成本。根据您的预算测试付款，同时保持付款日期可见。将下一份合同与还款期限分开 抵押贷款期限及其摊销回答了不同的问题。该术语描述了特定合同所涵盖的期间。摊销描述了用于计算预定还款额的还款期限。加拿大金融消费者管理局的续订指南解释了这些区别以及续订时涉及的选择。此图从今天的余额、当前报价和剩余摊销开始。假定的第一任期为期五年。 60 个月末付款后，续订方案将对仍欠余额应用新的利率，并重新计算剩余年份的付款。比较保留原始付款日期。如果默认余额为 400,000 加元、20 年摊销和 4% 报价率，则模型每月付款额为 2,416.99 加元。五年后按 6% 的续订率变为 2,750.51 加元，增加了 333.53 加元。这些是最初的假设计算，而不是当前贷款人的报价或利率预测。为什么两条平衡路径可以一起达到零 第一张图表比较了继续保持原始利率与五年后改变利率的情况。由于续订付款调整，两个余额都达到相同的预定结束日期。当还款额增加到足以保留摊销时，较高的利率并不一定意味着更长的贷款。不要将余额线视为支付的金额。付款包含利息和本金。利息是融资成本；本金减少了债务。堆叠图表将续订场景中第一年到第五年以及第六年到第十年的这些组件分开。这两个五年期以不同的余额开始。因此，他们的利息金额反映了利率和仍欠金额。它们是一条融资路径的连续阶段，而不是两笔完全相同的贷款。对于仅速率比较，请使用矩阵，该矩阵在其单元格中保持初始平衡恒定。将付款变化转变为现金流量测试 付款栏比未偿余额线更直接地显示经常性预算的影响。将增加的金额与扣除普通支出、其他所需债务支付和计划储蓄后剩余的金额进行比较。仅通过暂停其他所有目标来平衡的预算几乎没有灵活性。尝试更高的续订率并记录每月的差异。将该差值乘以 12 来估算年度现金流量调整，同时将其与全额贷款总利息的变化分开。年度预算效应和终生借贷成本回答了不同的问题。财产税、家庭保险、公寓费、维修费和水电费不在付款计算范围内。即使抵押贷款还款本身合适，也可能需要为这些费用预留准备金。应急基金指南提供了一种单独的方法来模拟收入中断；抵押贷款负担能力本身并不能衡量这种弹性。仔细阅读摊销矩阵 每个单元格都会使用显示的利率和摊销显示当前所选起始余额的每月付款。跨行读取会隔离地平线变化。向下读取一列可以隔离速率变化。网格使用起始余额，因此其单元格不是基于较小的第五年余额的续订报价。在正利率下，较长的摊销会降低预定的还款额，但可以使借入的资金保持更长时间。在利率不变且全额偿还贷款的情况下，计划利息总额为还款额×还款次数-原始本金。因此，较低的每月还款额可能会伴随着较高的累积利息费用。实际的续约选项可能涉及贷款机构要求、费用、保险考虑、合同限制或对申请的重新评估。该图表并未表明特定的摊销可用。在将建模付款视为可执行选项之前获取实际条款。保持复利约定明确 本示例假设引用的名义年利率每半年复利一次。如果 j 是小数形式的年利率，则等效月利率为 m = (1 + j ÷ 2) 1/6 − 1 。对于余额 B 和 N 剩余每月付款，付款为 Bm ÷ [1 − (1 + m) −N ] 。零利息时为 B ÷ N。每个月的利息为期初余额 × m。付款首先支付利息，其余部分减少本金。续订时，该公式使用剩余余额和剩余付款次数。然后，所选的续订率将保持不变，直到在此模型中获得回报。该工具不包括费用、预付款、违约保险费和后期费率变化。合同可以使用不同的约定。阅读贷款机构披露的利息计算和付款时间表，然后将所得现金流量与此图进行比较。有用的审查记录了实际续订日期、余额、付款选项和任何增加的计划来源。

1d1b15e7ec2ddda455d7ac13970697b7a1aaf041.src: Start with the household’s obligations and surviving resources. A salary multiple alone cannot explain the amount or duration of the funding need. Begin with the household shortfall A protection plan asks what the household would need to fund if an income earner died. The Financial Consumer Agency of Canada’s life-insurance overview describes uses such as replacing income, supporting dependants and paying debts. It also distinguishes coverage types and emphasizes understanding the policy. The relevant income gap is the difference between future spending and the surviving household’s available income. It is not automatically the deceased person’s gross salary. Employment-related expenses might end, care costs might rise, and the surviving household may have its own earnings or benefits. Estimate those cash flows before entering a shortfall. The line chart starts with an annual after-tax gap and increases it each year at the selected escalation rate. The default CAD 40,000 first-year shortfall grows at 2% for 20 years. The first payment arrives at the end of year one. A need that begins immediately, varies by life stage or ends earlier requires a different cash-flow schedule. Translate future support into an amount today Adding future nominal shortfalls gives the total dollars expected to be paid across different dates. Present value asks what amount today could fund those payments if it earned the selected net return. This model discounts the cash flows at an assumed nominal rate after costs and tax. For first annual gap G, escalation g, discount rate d and n support years, the income amount today is Σ G(1 + g) t−1 ÷ (1 + d) t , summed from t = 1 to n. Immediate costs are then added without discounting. Escalation and discounting are different operations; using a real rate while also inflating the cash flows would mix conventions. The default 3% net discount rate produces a combined need of CAD 759,067.82, including CAD 50,000 of immediate costs. A discount rate is an assumption about funding the future payments. It is not a guaranteed return available from an investment or an insurance policy. A lower assumed rate increases the amount needed today for the same positive future shortfalls. Read the waterfall without counting resources twice The waterfall first adds immediate costs and the present value of income support. It then subtracts assets allocated to this need and existing death benefits. Teal steps add needs; gold steps subtract resources. The navy endpoint shows the modeled net gap or surplus. With CAD 100,000 of allocated assets and CAD 300,000 of existing benefits, the default additional funding gap is CAD 359,067.82. The figure is a planning estimate under the selected assumptions. It does not identify a suitable policy, establish insurability or determine a premium. Use a consistent treatment for debts. If immediate costs include paying off the mortgage, remove the corresponding mortgage payments from the future spending gap. If assets are assigned here, do not also promise the same dollars to education and retirement. A home or restricted account may not supply cash when the household needs it; this simplified model assumes the entered resources are fully available today. Test the support period and the discount rate together The grouped bars compare several support periods against the same available resources. A longer period includes more annual shortfalls. The matrix then varies both duration and discount rate, showing the additional gap after resources in each case. The shading represents amounts, not probabilities. A darker cell is not more likely. A zero cell means the specified resources cover the modeled need in that scenario; it does not establish that the existing coverage has suitable conditions, duration, ownership or beneficiaries. Different obligations can have different end dates. Childcare may end before education begins; a partner may retire later; an outstanding debt may be repaid along the way. A detailed plan can replace the single smooth income-gap curve with dated cash flows. Keeping those dates visible is more informative than hiding every obligation in one rounded salary multiple. Review the resources as carefully as the need Check whether employer coverage continues after a job change and whether the benefit amount, policy term and conditions match the period being modeled. Verify settlement timing, access to assets, beneficiary arrangements and tax treatment for the actual contract and household. These are separate from the present-value calculation. The charts assume a death occurs today and then fund the resulting household shortfalls. They do not apply mortality probabilities, compare expected insurance claims with premiums or value an insurance policy. They also omit underwriting, exclusions, premium affordability and changes in future coverage. Review the plan when dependants, debts, income, care needs or existing benefits change. Record which expenses are included, which resources are committed, and which assumptions would change the gap most. The result is a documented funding question to resolve with the relevant licensed professionals, rather than a coverage recommendation generated by a chart.
1d1b15e7ec2ddda455d7ac13970697b7a1aaf041.zh: 从家庭的义务和幸存资源开始。仅靠工资倍数无法解释资金需求的金额或持续时间。从家庭短缺开始 保护计划询问如果收入者死亡，家庭需要提供什么资金。加拿大金融消费者管理局的人寿保险概述描述了替代收入、赡养家属和偿还债务等用途。它还区分了承保类型并强调对保单的理解。相关收入差距是未来支出与幸存家庭可用收入之间的差额。它不会自动成为死者的总工资。与就业相关的费用可能会结束，护理费用可能会上升，幸存家庭可能会有自己的收入或福利。在出现短缺之前估计这些现金流。该折线图以年度税后缺口开始​​，并以选定的递增率每年增加。第一年默认的 40,000 加元缺口在 20 年内以 2% 的速度增长。第一笔付款在第一年年底到达。立即开始、随生命阶段变化或提前结束的需求需要不同的现金流量表。将未来的支持转化为今天的金额加上未来的名义缺口就得出了不同日期预计支付的美元总额。现值询问如果获得选定的净回报，今天可以为这些付款提供多少资金。该模型以扣除成本和税项后的假定名义利率对现金流量进行贴现。对于第一个年度差距 G、升级 g、贴现率 d 和 n 个支持年，今天的收入金额为 Σ G(1 + g) t−1 ÷ (1 + d) t ，从 t = 1 到 n 求和。然后立即添加成本而不打折扣。升级和折扣是不同的操作；使用实际利率同时夸大现金流量会混淆惯例。默认 3% 净折扣率产生的总需求为 759,067.82 加元，其中包括 50,000 加元的直接成本。贴现率是为未来付款提供资金的假设。它不是投资或保险单的保证回报。较低的假设利率会增加当前所需的金额，以应对未来同样的正缺口。阅读瀑布，无需两次计算资源 瀑布首先添加直接成本和收入支持的现值。然后减去分配给该需求的资产和现有的死亡抚恤金。青色台阶增加了需求；黄金台阶会减少资源。海军端点显示建模的净缺口或盈余。分配资产为 100,000 加元，现有福利为 300,000 加元，默认额外资金缺口为 359,067.82 加元。该图是所选假设下的规划估计。它不确定合适的保单、建立可保性或确定保费。对债务采取一致的处理方式。如果直接成本包括偿还抵押贷款，则从未来支出缺口中扣除相应的抵押贷款付款。如果资产分配在这里，请不要承诺将同样的资金用于教育和退休。当家庭需要现金时，家庭或受限账户可能无法提供现金；此简化模型假设输入的资源今天完全可用。一起测试支持期和折扣率 分组条将多个支持期与相同的可用资源进行比较。较长的时期包括更多的年度缺口。然后，矩阵会改变持续时间和折扣率，显示每种情况下资源之后的额外差距。阴影代表数量，而不是概率。较暗的细胞的可能性并不大。零单元意味着指定的资源满足该场景中的建模需求；它没有规定现有保险具有适当的条件、期限、所有权或受益人。不同的义务可以有不同的结束日期。儿童保育可能会在教育开始之前结束；合伙人可以稍后退休；未偿还的债务可以一路偿还。详细的计划可以用过时的现金流量取代单一的平滑收入差距曲线。保持这些日期可见比将每项义务隐藏在一个四舍五入的工资倍数中更能提供信息。根据需要仔细审查资源 检查雇主承保范围在工作变动后是否继续，以及福利金额、保单条款和条件是否与建模期间相符。核实实际合同和家庭的结算时间、资产获取、受益人安排和税务处理。这些与现值计算是分开的。这些图表假设今天发生了死亡，然后为由此产生的家庭短缺提供资金。他们不应用死亡率概率、将预期保险索赔与保费进行比较或评估保险单。他们还忽略了承保、排除、保费承受能力和未来承保范围的变化。当家属、债务、收入、护理需求或现有福利发生变化时，请审查该计划。记录包括哪些费用、承诺哪些资源以及哪些假设最能改变差距。结果是一个记录在案的资金问题，需要与相关持牌专业人士一起解决，而不是由图表生成的承保范围建议。

d98e4b0ecf2ea94b1126fca5072c7098611a1365.src: An education goal has several payment dates. Estimate the whole cost calendar, then solve the saving requirement with explicit return and inflation assumptions. Define what one study year needs to cover Begin with an annual budget at today’s prices. Depending on the plan, that may include tuition, compulsory fees, books, supplies, housing, food, travel and equipment. A published tuition figure alone would not describe the entire cost of studying away from home. The default CAD 20,000 is a hypothetical all-in budget, not a Canadian tuition average or an institution’s quotation. Choose an amount for a specific study plan and document what it includes. Domestic or international status, program, location, living arrangements and the number of years can all change that starting budget. Every study year has its own price date. The cost bars inflate the starting annual budget separately to each study year. With study beginning in twelve years and 3% annual cost growth, year one costs more than today’s budget, while later study years are more expensive again. The 3% assumption is a sensitivity input, not an official education-price forecast. Know what the reserve target means This model reserves the full sum of the future nominal study costs when study begins. The reserve earns zero during study. That convention makes the cost calendar easy to inspect: each year’s nominal budget is funded at the start, without assuming investment earnings during the withdrawal period. For annual budget C today, cost-growth rate g, y years until study and s study years, the target is Σ C(1 + g) y+k , with k running from zero to s − 1. The default four-year reserve is CAD 119,297.03. This is the total modeled funding requirement before any scholarships, grants, work income or borrowing. A model that keeps unused funds invested during study could produce a different starting requirement and introduce additional investment risk. A monthly payment calendar could also differ from this annual illustration. Compare models only after aligning their cost dates, return assumptions and cash-flow timing. Compare the selected contribution with the solved contribution The savings chart shows two paths from the same starting balance. One uses the monthly amount selected in the controls. The other solves for the month-end contribution required to reach the reserve target by the study start date, using the same assumed effective annual return. The default CAD 10,000 already saved plus CAD 200 per month grows to CAD 52,728.71 after twelve years at an assumed 4% annual return. The solved monthly contribution is CAD 562.59. These paths use smooth returns; they do not describe the changing value of an actual investment portfolio. If existing savings alone already fund the target under the assumptions, the required new contribution is zero. The model does not invent a negative contribution or recommend withdrawing the excess. Future account rules, other education goals and uncertainty still need consideration. Use the waterfall and matrix to locate the pressure The waterfall adds each study year’s cost and subtracts the savings projected at the start. A positive endpoint is an unfunded reserve; a negative endpoint is a modeled surplus. Investment growth is already included in projected savings, so it must not be added again as a separate resource. The matrix changes the years until study and the return assumption. It recalculates the future cost target for every column. A longer waiting period provides more time to save and potentially compound, but it also allows more years of cost growth. The cells show the monthly saving required after both effects. Read several return rows rather than choosing the most convenient result. If a plan works only at a high assumed return, identify what else can change: contributions, the study budget, timing or outside funding. A higher target return brings uncertainty; it does not make the required outcome dependable. Add account benefits only after checking eligibility The Government of Canada’s education-savings overview explains RESPs and education-savings benefits. Eligibility and applicable rules require their own review. This calculator includes no grants, tax benefits, contribution limits or account withdrawal rules, and the solved contribution is not an RESP contribution recommendation. Keep a separate dated list of confirmed outside resources. Distinguish money already available from a possible scholarship, future student employment or a loan that must be repaid. Subtracting unconfirmed resources from the goal can make the displayed gap appear smaller without improving the underlying plan. Refresh the budget as a program and location become clearer. As the first payment approaches, review when cash must be available and how much value fluctuation the remaining horizon can tolerate. The plan should connect each cost date to an available source of money, then update as costs, family contributions and confirmed benefits change.
d98e4b0ecf2ea94b1126fca5072c7098611a1365.zh: 一个教育目标有多个付款日期。估计整个成本日历，然后通过明确的回报和通货膨胀假设来解决储蓄要求。定义一个研究年需要涵盖的内容 首先以当前价格制定年度预算。根据计划，这可能包括学费、强制性费用、书籍、用品、住房、食物、旅行和设备。仅公布的学费数字并不能描述离家学习的全部费用。默认的 20,000 加元是假设的全部预算，而不是加拿大的平均学费或机构的报价。为特定的学习计划选择一个金额并记录其包含的内容。国内或国际地位、项目、地点、生活安排和年数都可能改变起始预算。每个学习年都有自己的价格日期。成本条会分别增加每个研究年的起始年度预算。由于学习从 12 年开始，每年费用增长 3%，第一年的费用超过了今天的预算，而后来的学习年份又更加昂贵。 3% 的假设是一个敏感性输入，而不是官方的教育价格预测。了解储备目标的含义 该模型在研究开始时储备未来名义学习成本的全额。学习期间储备金收入为零。这一惯例使得成本日历易于检查：每年的名义预算在开始时就得到资助，而不假设提款期间的投资收益。对于今天的年度预算 C、成本增长率 g、研究前 y 年和 s 个研究年，目标为 Σ C(1 + g) y+k ，其中 k 从 0 到 s − 1。默认的四年储备金为 119,297.03 加元。这是扣除任何奖学金、助学金、工作收入或借款之前的总模拟资金需求。在研究期间保留未使用的资金进行投资的模型可能会产生不同的起始要求并引入额外的投资风险。每月付款日历也可能与此年度插图有所不同。仅在调整成本日期、回报假设和现金流时间安排后才能比较模型。将选定的缴款与已解决的缴款进行比较 储蓄图表显示了来自相同起始余额的两条路径。人们使用在控件中选择的每月金额。另一种方法使用相同的假设有效年回报率来解决在研究开始日期之前达到准备金目标所需的月末缴款。默认已存 10,000 加元加上每月 200 加元，十二年后将增至 52,728.71 加元，假定年回报率为 4%。解决的每月供款为 562.59 加元。这些路径使用平滑返回；它们没有描述实际投资组合的价值变化。如果仅现有储蓄就已经为假设下的目标提供了资金，则所需的新捐款为零。该模型不会发明负贡献或建议提取多余的部分。未来的账户规则、其他教育目标和不确定性仍然需要考虑。使用瀑布和矩阵来定位压力 瀑布增加了每个研究年的成本并减去了开始时预计的节省。积极的终点是没有资金储备；负端点是模拟的盈余。投资增长已包含在预计储蓄中，因此不得将其作为单独的资源再次添加。该矩阵改变了研究之前的年份和回报假设。它重新计算每个列的未来成本目标。较长的等待期提供了更多的时间来节省和潜在的复合，但它也允许更多年的成本增长。单元格显示两种效果后所需的每月节省。读取多个返回行而不是选择最方便的结果。如果一项计划仅在高假设回报下有效，请确定还有什么可以改变：捐款、研究预算、时间安排或外部资金。较高的目标回报带来不确定性；它不会使所需的结果变得可靠。仅在检查资格后添加账户福利 加拿大政府的教育储蓄概述解释了 RESP 和教育储蓄福利。资格和适用规则需要他们自己审查。该计算器不包含补助金、税收优惠、缴款限额或账户提款规则，并且解决的缴款不是 RESP 缴款建议。保留一份已确认的外部资源的单独的、注明日期的列表。将已经可用的资金与可能的奖学金、未来的学生就业或必须偿还的贷款区分开来。从目标中减去未确认的资源可以使显示的差距显得更小，而无需改进底层计划。随着计划和地点变得更加清晰，更新预算。随着第一次付款的临近，检查何时必须有现金以及剩余期限可以承受多少价值波动。该计划应将每个费用日期与可用资金来源联系起来，然后随着费用、家庭缴款和确认福利的变化而更新。

ff74fa6140f060105defbe9d6f780a22baf5ee1e.src: Net worth measures assets less liabilities on a date. Cash flow and accessible reserves answer different questions about the household’s ability to meet payments. Put every balance on the same date A household balance sheet records what you own and what you owe. Net worth is assets − liabilities . The Financial Consumer Agency of Canada’s financial-planning lesson explains this calculation using current values and distinguishes the balance sheet from the household budget. Use a common observation date. Mixing an old home estimate, today’s investment statement and a debt balance from last year can create a misleading total. Record valuation uncertainty alongside assets that have no readily observable market price. The default example lists a CAD 600,000 home, CAD 150,000 in market investments and CAD 30,000 in cash. Assets total CAD 780,000. Subtracting a CAD 350,000 mortgage and CAD 20,000 of other debts gives CAD 410,000 net worth. All figures are hypothetical and describe a simplified balance sheet. Follow the bridge from gross assets to net worth The waterfall adds each asset and subtracts each debt. The final navy bar is the net amount. Its endpoint can be negative: that means the listed liabilities exceed the listed asset values. A signed result is more informative than clipping the chart at zero. Keep the home and mortgage treatment consistent. This chart lists gross home value as an asset and the mortgage as a liability. Alternatively, a presentation could show home equity alone. Adding home equity and then subtracting the mortgage again would count the debt twice. Debt repayment and saving can affect the balance sheet in different ways. Paying principal with existing cash reduces cash and debt by the same amount, leaving net worth unchanged at that instant. Paying interest reduces cash without reducing principal. Future interest savings, fees, taxes and changes in asset values are separate effects rather than an immediate increase created by moving cash between rows. Read composition alongside accessibility The donut divides listed gross assets among the home, investments and cash. Its denominator is total listed assets before debt. It does not show an investment allocation, household spending shares or the fraction of net worth available to spend. A home can dominate gross assets while supplying little immediate liquidity. Accessing its value may require selling, borrowing, paying costs or changing living arrangements. An investment account may be easier to sell but exposed to price movements, settlement timing, account restrictions or tax consequences. Cash and deposits also need context: some may be committed to upcoming bills or a separate goal. Add a liquidity review alongside the net-worth total, listing which resources can meet which payments and when. The emergency-reserve tool starts from spending needs, rather than assuming that a positive balance sheet guarantees a sufficient cash buffer. Watch the equity cushion change under stress The grouped bars compare asset values with debts under separate home and investment declines, then both together. Cash and debt balances remain fixed in these instantaneous scenarios. A fall in a financed asset’s market value does not automatically reduce the amount owed. In the default combined stress, home value falls 20% and investments fall 25%. Assets become CAD 622,500 while debts remain CAD 370,000. Net worth becomes CAD 252,500, a CAD 157,500 reduction, or about 38.4% of starting net worth. The percentage change in net worth can exceed the percentage change in gross assets because the liabilities remain. The matrix expands this into combinations of home and market declines. Each signed cell reports resulting net worth in CAD. Gold negative cells mean debts exceed stressed assets. The selected stress percentages and matrix are alternative assumptions, with no probability attached and no forecast of property or investment prices. Connect the snapshot to the rest of the plan This simplified example omits pensions, businesses, other property, taxes triggered by sale, transaction costs and additional obligations. A more complete inventory can include those items with clear definitions. Be careful when combining amounts before and after tax or treating a future income entitlement as an immediately spendable lump sum. A rise in net worth can come from saving, debt reduction, asset-price changes or new information about values. Track those drivers separately when comparing dates. An increase caused by a property revaluation does not necessarily improve the monthly budget; a change in interest costs can tighten cash flow without immediately changing principal balances. Use the balance sheet with a cash-flow plan, emergency reserve and dated goals. Record the valuation date, sources and included obligations, then repeat on a consistent basis. The useful question is how the household’s resources support its commitments over time, rather than whether one headline number is above someone else’s.
ff74fa6140f060105defbe9d6f780a22baf5ee1e.zh: 净值衡量的是某一日期的资产减去负债。现金流和可用储备回答了有关家庭支付能力的不同问题。将所有余额放在同一日期家庭资产负债表记录您拥有的资产和您所欠的资产。净值是资产-负债。加拿大金融消费者机构的财务规划课程使用当前值解释了这种计算，并将资产负债表与家庭预算区分开来。使用共同的观察日期。将旧房估算、今天的投资报表和去年的债务余额混合起来可能会产生误导性的总额。记录估值不确定性以及没有易于观察的市场价格的资产。默认示例列出了 600,000 加元的房屋、150,000 加元的市场投资和 30,000 加元的现金。资产总额78万加元。减去 350,000 加元的抵押贷款和 20,000 加元的其他债务，得到 410,000 加元的净资产。所有数字均为假设，描述的是简化的资产负债表。沿着从总资产到净值的桥梁瀑布添加每项资产并减去每项债务。最后的海军条是净额。它的终点可以是负数：这意味着列出的负债超过列出的资产价值。带符号的结果比将图表剪裁为零更能提供更多信息。保持住房和抵押贷款待遇一致。该图表将房屋总价值列为资产，将抵押贷款列为负债。或者，演示文稿可以仅显示房屋净值。添加房屋净值，然后再次减去抵押贷款，就会对债务进行两次计算。债务偿还和储蓄可以以不同的方式影响资产负债表。用现有现金支付本金可以减少相同数量的现金和债务，从而使净资产保持不变。支付利息会减少现金，但不会减少本金。未来的利息节省、费用、税收和资产价值的变化是单独的影响，而不是通过在行之间转移现金而立即增加。阅读成分和可访问性 甜甜圈将列出的总资产分为房屋、投资和现金。其分母是债务前的总上市资产。它没有显示投资分配、家庭支出份额或可用于支出的净资产比例。房屋可以在总资产中占据主导地位，但几乎无法提供即时流动性。要获得其价值可能需要出售、借贷、支付费用或改变生活安排。投资账户可能更容易出售，但面临价格变动、结算时间、账户限制或税务后果的影响。现金和存款也需要背景：有些可能致力于即将到来的账单或单独的目标。在净资产总额旁边添加流动性审查，列出哪些资源可以满足哪些付款以及何时付款。紧急储备工具从支出需求出发，而不是假设积极的资产负债表可以保证足够的现金缓冲。观察压力下股票缓冲的变化 分组的条形图将资产价值与单独的住房和投资下降下的债务进行比较，然后将两者放在一起。在这些瞬时情况下，现金和债务余额保持不变。融资资产市场价值的下降不会自动减少所欠金额。在违约综合压力下，房屋价值下降 20%，投资下降 25%。资产变为 622,500 加元，债务仍为 370,000 加元。净资产变为 252,500 加元，减少 157,500 加元，约占起始净资产的 38.4%。由于负债仍然存在，净值的百分比变化可能超过总资产的百分比变化。该矩阵将其扩展到国内和市场下降的组合。每个签名的单元格都会报告最终的加元净值。黄金负值细胞意味着债务超过压力资产。所选的压力百分比和矩阵是替代假设，没有附加概率，也没有对财产或投资价格的预测。将快照与计划的其余部分连接起来 这个简化的示例省略了养老金、企业、其他财产、销售引发的税收、交易成本和额外义务。更完整的清单可以包括那些具有明确定义的项目。在合并税前和税后金额或将未来收入权利视为可立即支出的一次性款项时要小心。净资产的增加可以来自储蓄、债务减少、资产价格变化或有关价值的新信息。比较日期时单独跟踪这些驱动程序。财产重估造成的增加并不一定会改善每月预算；利息成本的变化可以收紧现金流，但不会立即改变本金余额。将资产负债表与现金流量计划、紧急储备金和指定日期的目标结合使用。记录评估日期、来源和包含的义务，然后在一致的基础上重复。有用的问题是，随着时间的推移，家庭的资源如何支持其承诺，而不是一个总体数字是否高于其他人的数字。

eda20d01e6477c79959cd88f7875931e867975ba.src: A future dollar amount needs a price-level assumption. Compare what the money can buy as well as the number printed on the account statement. Start with the cost of a familiar budget The first chart grows today’s monthly cost at the selected annual inflation rate. It holds the quantity and quality of the spending basket constant. If your family, housing or lifestyle changes, that is a separate planning adjustment rather than an inflation effect. A monthly budget of CAD 3,000 at a constant 3% inflation assumption becomes about CAD 6,281 after 25 years. This is an original calculation, not a forecast of Canadian prices. The increase compounds: applying 3% to the original budget every year without increasing the base would understate it. The Bank of Canada’s inflation overview describes CPI and its inflation-target framework. A policy target is not a promise that prices or your personal expenses will grow at that rate every year. Use more than one assumption for a long horizon. See the difference between stable dollars and stable purchasing power The second chart holds a cash amount at CAD 10,000 with no nominal interest. Its purchasing power is shown in today’s dollars after fixed comparison periods. The nominal balance remains unchanged, while positive inflation reduces the goods and services it can purchase. This is not an argument that every dollar should be invested in risky assets. Money needed for an imminent bill has a different role from long-term retirement capital. Liquidity and the ability to make a payment on time can justify holding cash even when its real return is low. Compare the emergency-fund guide for that distinction. An emergency reserve is designed to absorb a cash-flow shock. A growth portfolio is exposed to market risk and may be down precisely when the money is needed. Translate nominal return into a real return The matrix compares assumed nominal returns with inflation rates. A positive account return can still mean a loss of purchasing power. The exact relationship is real return = (1 + nominal return) ÷ (1 + inflation) − 1 . For example, a 5% nominal return with 3% inflation gives a real return of about 1.94%, before tax and fees. Subtracting 3% from 5% is a useful approximation at modest rates, but it is not the exact compounding relationship. These cells are sensitivity calculations, not estimates of investment success. The matrix does not assign probabilities, and it does not allow you to choose a return simply because it is needed to meet a goal. Your spending basket can differ from the average A household that rents, a household with a fixed mortgage payment, and a household facing large care expenses may experience different pressures. An aggregate price index is useful context but cannot reconstruct every household’s cost changes. Build your own starting basket from actual recurring spending. Separate price changes from changes in quantity, such as moving to a larger home or adding a family member. For a detailed plan, examine major categories separately rather than hiding every uncertainty in one average rate. Do not combine a real return with a second inflation deduction. If both future cash flows and portfolio returns are expressed in today’s dollars, maintain that basis throughout the model. If the model is nominal, inflate the expenses and use nominal returns consistently. Put an inflation review into the plan Write the goal in today’s dollars and retain that baseline. Test at least a lower and higher inflation assumption. Identify expenses whose prices or quantities could change differently. Check whether income sources adjust with prices, and under what terms. Update the budget from observed spending rather than only changing the forecast rate. A spending plan becomes easier to review when nominal amounts, real amounts, dates and assumptions are clearly labelled. The charts are designed to make those relationships visible before a more detailed tax, benefit or investment model is added.
eda20d01e6477c79959cd88f7875931e867975ba.zh: 未来的美元金额需要价格水平假设。比较这些钱可以买什么以及账户对账单上打印的数字。从熟悉的预算成本开始 第一个图表以选定的年通货膨胀率计算今天的每月成本。它使支出篮子的数量和质量保持不变。如果您的家庭、住房或生活方式发生变化，那是单独的规划调整，而不是通货膨胀效应。如果假设通货膨胀率恒定为 3%，则每月预算为 3,000 加元，25 年后将变为约 6,281 加元。这是原始计算，而不是对加拿大价格的预测。增加的金额会增加：每年在原始预算的基础上增加 3%，而不增加基数，这会低估预算。加拿大央行的通胀概览描述了 CPI 及其通胀目标框架。政策目标并不是承诺物价或您的个人开支每年都会以同样的速度增长。长期使用多个假设。查看稳定美元和稳定购买力之间的差异 第二张图表持有 10,000 加元的现金，没有名义利息。经过固定的比较期后，其购买力以今天的美元计算。名义余额保持不变，而正通胀减少了可以购买的商品和服务。这并不是说每一美元都应该投资于风险资产。即将发生的账单所需的资金与长期退休资本具有不同的作用。即使实际回报较低，流动性和按时付款的能力也可以证明持有现金是合理的。请比较应急基金指南以了解这一区别。紧急储备金旨在吸收现金流冲击。增长型投资组合面临市场风险，并且可能在需要资金时恰好下跌。将名义回报转化为实际回报 该矩阵将假设的名义回报与通货膨胀率进行比较。正的账户回报仍然可能意味着购买力的损失。确切的关系是实际回报 = (1 + 名义回报) ÷ (1 + 通货膨胀) − 1 。例如，名义回报率为 5%，通货膨胀率为 3%，税费前的实际回报率为 1.94% 左右。在适当的比率下，从 5% 减去 3% 是一个有用的近似值，但这并不是精确的复利关系。这些单元格是敏感性计算，而不是投资成功的估计。该矩阵不分配概率，并且不允许您仅仅因为需要实现目标而选择回报。您的支出篮子可能与普通家庭有所不同。租房的家庭、有固定抵押贷款还款的家庭以及面临巨额护理费用的家庭可能会面临不同的压力。总价格指数是有用的背景，但无法重建每个家庭的成本变化。根据实际经常性支出构建您自己的起始篮子。将价格变化与数量变化分开，例如搬到更大的房子或增加家庭成员。对于详细的计划，请分别检查主要类别，而不是将所有不确定性隐藏在一个平均比率中。不要将实际回报与第二次通货膨胀扣除结合起来。如果未来现金流和投资组合回报都以今天的美元表示，则在整个模型中保持该基础。如果模型是名义模型，则增加费用并一致使用名义回报。将通货膨胀审查纳入计划中 以今天的美元计算目标并保留该基准。至少测试较低和较高的通胀假设。确定价格或数量可能发生不同变化的费用。检查收入来源是否随价格变化以及在何种条件下变化。根据观察到的支出更新预算，而不仅仅是改变预测率。当名义金额、实际金额、日期和假设都被明确标记时，支出计划就更容易审查。这些图表旨在在添加更详细的税收、福利或投资模型之前使这些关系可见。

ba0cf023e150ac05ea802daec04c149a768a6e03.src: Use household statistics for context. Build the emergency reserve from the expenses and risks your own household needs to cover. Read the official spending comparison carefully The first chart uses Statistics Canada’s Survey of Household Spending for 2021 and 2023, published on 21 May 2025. It shows average annual spending on goods and services among households in the provinces. It is a dated survey comparison, not a current monthly cost-of-living reading. The seven displayed categories sum to CAD 67,125 in 2021 and CAD 76,750 in 2023. Shelter is the largest displayed category. These are nominal dollar amounts. Changes can reflect prices, quantities, household circumstances and spending choices; they are not category inflation rates. The chart’s denominator is household consumption, not after-tax income. Savings, income taxes and other items outside this consumption definition are not an “unspent” residual. These averages are not a recommended allocation, a median budget, or an assessment of what a particular family should spend. Build your own essential-expense baseline List the spending you would need to maintain during an interruption in earnings: housing, basic food, utilities, transport, insurance and required payments. Identify which amounts could fall and which would remain due. Add a provision for predictable irregular costs in a separate budget. The Financial Consumer Agency of Canada distinguishes unexpected expenses from occasional expenses that can be planned. Its emergency-fund guidance describes three to six months of regular expenses or income as possible starting points. The tool uses expenses rather than income so the coverage calculation stays explicit. Its six-month default is an example, not an assessment of your needs. Job stability, insurance, dependants, access to other resources and the ability to reduce spending can all affect an appropriate reserve. Read the reserve-building curve The second chart starts with your current cash reserve and adds the selected monthly saving. It stops new deposits once the target is reached. If the current reserve already exceeds the target, it retains the existing amount instead of pretending money has been withdrawn. At CAD 3,000 of monthly essential expenses and six months of coverage, the target is CAD 18,000. Starting with CAD 3,000 and adding CAD 500 per month takes 30 months to close the CAD 15,000 gap, assuming no interest, withdrawals or expense changes. Try a smaller first milestone if the full target feels distant. For example, the initial objective might be one month of essential expenses, followed by successive additions. The important point is to make the funding schedule fit the cash available after required bills. Test the cost of an expense shock The third chart raises essential expenses by 10% and 20% while keeping the selected number of coverage months fixed. This shows how a reserve can become inadequate even when its dollar balance does not fall. These increases are hypothetical stresses, not statistical confidence bounds. You could instead test a specific event such as a rent change, a car replacement or additional care needs. Keep the cost of a known upcoming purchase separate from the reserve for genuinely uncertain events. Also examine accessibility. A reserve intended for urgent payments needs to be available on the relevant timeline. Check withdrawal terms, settlement timing and possible penalties rather than treating every account balance as equally usable cash. Create a reserve routine Reconcile the essential-expense figure with recent bills. Choose an initial coverage target and a realistic monthly transfer. Keep predictable annual expenses in the regular budget. Review coverage after a housing, family or employment change. After using the reserve, write a replenishment schedule. The reserve is part of the overall plan. Balance its funding with required debt payments and other commitments. The debt guide shows the interest effect of repayment choices; it does not assume that eliminating every cash buffer is the right way to accelerate repayment.
ba0cf023e150ac05ea802daec04c149a768a6e03.zh: 使用家庭统计数据作为背景。从您自己的家庭需要承担的费用和风险中建立应急储备。仔细阅读官方支出比较 第一张图表使用加拿大统计局 2025 年 5 月 21 日发布的 2021 年和 2023 年家庭支出调查。它显示了各省家庭在商品和服务上的平均年度支出。这是一个过时的调查比较，而不是当前的每月生活成本数据。 2021 年展示的七个类别总计为 67,125 加元，2023 年为 76,750 加元。住房是展示的最大类别。这些是名义金额。变化可以反映价格、数量、家庭情况和支出选择；它们不是类别通货膨胀率。该图表的分母是家庭消费，而不是税后收入。储蓄、所得税和消费定义之外的其他项目不是“未花费”的剩余部分。这些平均值不是建议的分配、预算中位数或对特定家庭应该支出的评估。建立您自己的基本支出基准 列出您在收入中断期间需要维持的支出：住房、基本食品、公用事业、交通、保险和所需付款。确定哪些金额可能会减少，哪些金额仍应到期。在单独的预算中添加可预测的非常规费用的准备金。加拿大金融消费者管理局将意外开支与可计划的偶然开支区分开来。其紧急基金指南将三到六个月的常规支出或收入描述为可能的起点。该工具使用支出而不是收入，因此覆盖范围计算保持明确。其六个月的默认设置只是一个示例，而不是对您的需求的评估。工作稳定性、保险、家属、获得其他资源的机会以及减少支出的能力都会影响适当的准备金。阅读储备金建设曲线 第二张图表从您当前的现金储备开始，并添加所选的每月储蓄。一旦达到目标，它就会停止新的存款。如果当前准备金已超过目标，则保留现有金额，而不是假装已提取资金。如果每月基本费用为 3,000 加元，保险期限为 6 个月，目标是 18,000 加元。假设没有利息、提款或费用变化，从 3,000 加元开始，每月增加 500 加元，需要 30 个月才能缩小 15,000 加元的缺口。如果感觉完整的目标很遥远，请尝试较小的第一个里程碑。例如，最初的目标可能是一个月的基本开支，然后是连续增加。重要的一点是使融资计划符合所需账单后可用的现金。测试费用冲击的成本 第三个图表将基本费用提高了 10% 和 20%，同时保持选定的承保月份数固定。这表明，即使美元余额没有下降，储备也可能会变得不足。这些增加是假设的压力，而不是统计置信界限。您可以改为测试特定事件，例如租金变化、汽车更换或额外护理需求。将已知即将购买的成本与真正不确定事件的储备分开。还要检查可访问性。需要在相关时间表上提供用于紧急付款的储备金。检查提款条款、结算时间和可能的处罚，而不是将每个账户余额视为同等可用的现金。创建储备例程 将基本费用数字与最近的账单进行核对。选择初始覆盖目标和现实的每月转移。将可预测的年度支出纳入常规预算。在住房、家庭或工作发生变化后查看承保范围。使用完储备后，编写补充计划。该储备是总体规划的一部分。平衡其资金与所需的债务支付和其他承诺。债务指南显示还款选择的利息效应；它并不认为消除所有现金缓冲是加速还款的正确方法。

1c31df48d6cf809d8e018b44f9a183e68854a1e1.src: A savings plan has several adjustable parts. Begin with the contribution and time horizon you can sustain, then test a range of returns. Read the gap between saving and growth The first chart separates money contributed from the portfolio’s modeled value. The contribution line includes your initial savings and each monthly deposit. The difference between the lines is growth under the selected return assumption. With a negative return, that difference can be a loss. The curve is a mathematical illustration. It does not show the path of a real investment. Markets do not supply a smooth annual return, and an account can lose value even while you continue contributing. The Investor.gov compound-interest calculator also treats initial capital, contributions, time and the estimated rate as distinct inputs. Try setting the return to zero. The two lines should coincide. This is a useful baseline: the plan’s progress then comes entirely from your own deposits, making the required saving effort visible. Compare the same finish date The second chart compares starting monthly contributions now with delaying them by five or ten years. All cases share the selected finish date, contribution amount and return. Existing starting savings remain invested in every case. The delayed cases skip deposits rather than making larger catch-up payments later. This comparison changes both the amount contributed and the time each deposit has to grow. It should not be interpreted as a pure investment-performance comparison. Starting sooner can improve the modeled endpoint at a positive return, but it also requires setting money aside sooner. A practical follow-up is to ask what would make an earlier start feasible: a smaller initial transfer, redirecting an expense, or a gradual increase as income changes. A larger assumed return can make a spreadsheet balance without making the required outcome reliable. Use the matrix as a stress test The matrix varies the horizon and return while preserving your selected initial savings and monthly contribution. Each cell is an alternative scenario. Darker shading means a larger ending amount; it does not mean the outcome is more likely. For a goal with a firm deadline, read down one time column and compare several rates. For a flexible goal, compare what additional time might accomplish. Keep the return convention consistent: these are nominal returns before tax, fees and inflation. If only the most optimistic cell meets the goal, identify the funding gap. Possible changes include increasing contributions, changing the goal, delaying the deadline or finding other resources. Taking more risk creates a wider range of possible results; it does not guarantee the higher cell. Know exactly how the example compounds The annual return is an effective rate. The equivalent monthly rate is (1 + annual return) 1/12 − 1 . Each month, the existing balance grows by that rate and a deposit arrives at month-end. Using annual return divided by 12 would represent a different rate convention. For an initial amount B, monthly deposit C, monthly rate m and N months, the ending value is B(1 + m) N + C[(1 + m) N − 1] ÷ m . When m is zero, use B + CN. The tool uses a month-by-month recurrence, which also handles delayed deposits explicitly. Real account results depend on actual deposit dates, changing returns, costs and tax treatment. This calculator does not impose contribution limits or determine account eligibility. Use the relevant current account rules when turning an illustration into an implemented plan. Translate the chart into a monthly decision Describe the goal in today’s dollars and give it a date. Separate near-term cash needs from money that can remain invested. Choose a contribution that fits actual cash flow. Test a lower-return scenario and an interruption in deposits. Review progress as income, prices and the goal change. The ending balance is only one planning measure. Also record how much money you must contribute, whether the schedule leaves a cash reserve, and how flexible the goal is. Read the inflation guide next to translate a future balance into purchasing power.
1c31df48d6cf809d8e018b44f9a183e68854a1e1.zh: 储蓄计划有几个可调整的部分。从您可以维持的贡献和时间范围开始，然后测试一系列回报。了解储蓄与增长之间的差距 第一个图表将贡献的资金与投资组合的建模价值分开。供款额度包括您的初始储蓄和每月存款。两条线之间的差异是所选回报假设下的增长。如果回报为负，这种差异可能会造成损失。该曲线是一个数学图解。它没有显示真正的投资路径。市场不会提供平稳的年度回报，即使您继续捐款，账户也可能会损失价值。 Investor.gov 复利计算器还将初始资本、出资、时间和估计利率视为不同的输入。尝试将返回设置为零。两条线应该重合。这是一个有用的基线：计划的进度完全来自您自己的存款，从而使所需的储蓄努力可见。比较相同的完成日期第二个图表比较了现在开始的每月缴款与延迟五年或十年的缴款。所有案例共享选定的完成日期、捐款金额和回报。在任何情况下，现有的起始储蓄仍可用于投资。延迟的案件会跳过存款，而不是稍后进行更大的补足付款。这种比较会改变贡献的金额和每笔存款增长的时间。它不应被解释为纯粹的投资业绩比较。尽早开始可以改善建模终点并获得正回报，但也需要尽早拨出资金。一个实际的后续行动是询问什么可以使较早的开始变得可行：较小的初始转移，重新调整支出，或随着收入变化而逐渐增加。较大的假设回报可以使电子表格保持平衡，但所需的结果并不可靠。使用矩阵作为压力测试 该矩阵会改变期限和回报，同时保留您选择的初始储蓄和每月供款。每个单元格都是一个替代场景。阴影越深意味着结束金额越大；这并不意味着结果更有可能发生。对于有明确期限的目标，请阅读一个时间栏并比较几个比率。对于灵活的目标，请比较额外的时间可能实现的目标。保持回报惯例一致：这些是税、费用和通货膨胀前的名义回报。如果只有最乐观的单元达到目标，则确定资金缺口。可能的改变包括增加贡献、改变目标、推迟截止日期或寻找其他资源。承担更多的风险会产生更广泛的可能结果；它不保证更高的小区。确切地知道示例是如何复合的 年回报率是有效利率。等值月利率为 (1 + 年回报率) 1/12 − 1 。每个月，现有余额都会按该比率增长，存款会在月底到达。使用年回报率除以 12 将代表不同的利率惯例。对于初始金额 B、每月存款 C、月利率 m 和 N 个月，最终值为 B(1 + m) N + C[(1 + m) N − 1] ÷ m 。当m为零时，使用B+CN。该工具采用逐月重复的方式，也明确处理延迟存款。真实账户结果取决于实际存款日期、变化的回报、成本和税务处理。该计算器不施加捐款限制或确定帐户资格。将说明转变为实施计划时，请使用相关的经常账户规则。将图表转化为每月决策 用今天的美元描述目标并给出日期。将近期现金需求与可以继续投资的资金分开。选择适合实际现金流的捐款。测试低回报场景和存款中断。随着收入、价格和目标的变化审查进展情况。期末余额只是一项计划措施。还要记录您必须贡献多少钱、时间表是否留有现金储备以及目标的灵活性。接下来阅读通货膨胀指南，将未来的余额转化为购买力。

bc3adcf93c36d92018e55b801796f229483693b5.src: A payment decision changes both the time in debt and the interest paid. Check that the payment reduces principal before relying on a payoff date. Follow the remaining balance The first chart compares your selected monthly payment with the same payment plus an extra amount. The interest rate and starting balance stay fixed. The final payment is reduced to the amount owed rather than collecting a full payment after the debt is cleared. At the start of the default example, CAD 10,000 at an assumed nominal annual rate of 18% incurs CAD 150 of interest over one simplified month. A CAD 300 payment therefore reduces principal by CAD 150 in that first month. Later interest falls as the balance declines. The chart is not a reconstruction of a credit-card statement. Actual products may use daily accrual, different transaction rates, grace periods, fees and changing minimum payments. Read the agreement and statement before treating any modeled date as a contractual payoff quote. Separate the amount borrowed from the financing cost The stacked bars divide a completed repayment schedule into original principal and cumulative interest. Both paths repay the same starting principal. Any reduction in total paid comes from a change in financing cost under the selected assumptions. Do not compare only the monthly payment. A lower payment can make the current budget easier while extending the repayment period and increasing interest. Conversely, a larger payment needs to be affordable; a plan that repeatedly forces new borrowing may fail to deliver the modeled saving. If the selected payment is no larger than the first month’s interest, it does not reduce principal in this simplified model. The tool reports “Not repaid” instead of inventing a payoff date. It also withholds a lifetime-interest total when the schedule is not completed within the model limit. Read the rate-and-payment matrix The matrix uses your starting balance with a fixed set of rates and payments. Each cell shows months to repay, including a partial final payment. NR means the debt is not repaid within the 600-month limit, including cases where the payment fails to reduce the balance. This is a sensitivity map. A lower rate is not assumed to be available, and a larger payment is not assumed to fit your budget. If a refinancing offer exists, compare fees, term, variable-rate risk and any collateral implications separately. A rate cut and an extra payment affect the model through different channels. The former reduces the charge on the outstanding balance; the latter reduces the balance more quickly. A genuine comparison needs both the repayment schedule and the total cost. Place the debt inside the whole budget Make a list of all obligations, interest rates, due dates and minimum payments. The Government of Canada’s Six Steps to Get Out of Debt discusses directing extra repayment toward high-rate debt and, alternatively, small balances for motivation, while maintaining required payments. The chart models one balance and cannot decide the entire order of repayment. Arrears, essential living costs, secured obligations, promotional terms and restrictions may change priorities. It also does not value employer matching contributions, tax effects or access to emergency cash. Keep the avoided borrowing cost distinct from a risky investment’s expected return. Repaying a fixed-rate balance changes an interest obligation under its terms; an investment forecast does not guarantee that it will outperform that cost. Check the recurrence and the implementation The monthly recurrence is new balance = old balance × (1 + annual nominal rate ÷ 12) − actual payment , with payment capped at the amount owed. No new purchases or fees are added. A completed schedule satisfies total payments approximately equal to principal plus modeled interest, subject to rounding. Use the statement’s actual rate and identify any separate balances. Keep required payments current. Choose an extra payment that leaves a workable cash-flow margin. Confirm any prepayment restrictions or charges. Reconcile the next statement with the planned progress. If the plan cannot cover essential costs and required payments, that is a cash-flow problem to address directly. A longer chart does not create the capacity to pay.
bc3adcf93c36d92018e55b801796f229483693b5.zh: 付款决定会改变债务期限和支付的利息。在确定还款日期之前，请检查付款是否会减少本金。跟踪剩余余额 第一个图表将您选择的每月付款与相同付款加上额外金额进行比较。利率和起始余额保持固定。最终付款将减少至所欠金额，而不是在债务清偿后收取全额付款。在默认示例开始时，假设名义年利率为 18%，10,000 加元在一个简化的一个月内会产生 150 加元的利息。因此，支付 300 加元会在第一个月减少本金 150 加元。随后，随着余额的减少，利息也会下降。该图表不是信用卡对账单的重建。实际产品可能会使用每日累积、不同的交易费率、宽限期、费用和更改最低付款额。在将任何建模日期视为合同支付报价之前，请阅读协议和声明。将借款金额与融资成本分开 堆积条将已完成的还款计划划分为原始本金和累计利息。两条路径都偿还相同的起始本金。支付总额的任何减少都来自于所选假设下融资成本的变化。不要只比较每月付款。较低的还款额可以使当前的预算更加容易，同时延长还款期限并增加利息。相反，较大的付款需要是负担得起的；反复强制新借款的计划可能无法实现模拟的储蓄。如果所选付款不大于第一个月的利息，则在此简化模型中不会减少本金。该工具报告“未偿还”，而不是发明还款日期。当计划未在模型限制内完成时，它还会扣留终生利息总额。阅读费率和付款矩阵 该矩阵使用您的起始余额以及一组固定的费率和付款。每个单元格都显示还款月数，包括部分最终付款。 NR是指债务在600个月的期限内没有偿还，包括付款未能减少余额的情况。这是一张敏感度图。不假定可以提供较低的费率，也不假定较大的付款额适合您的预算。如果存在再融资要约，请分别比较费用、期限、可变利率风险和任何抵押品影响。降息和额外付款通过不同渠道影响模型。前者减少了未清余额的费用；后者会更快地减少余额。真正的比较需要还款时间表和总成本。将债务纳入整个预算 列出所有债务、利率、到期日和最低还款额。加拿大政府摆脱债务的六个步骤讨论了将额外的还款用于高利率债务，或者小额余额以激励，同时维持所需的付款。该图表模拟了一种余额，并不能决定整个还款顺序。欠款、基本生活费用、担保义务、促销条款和限制可能会改变优先事项。它还不重视雇主匹配的缴款、税收影响或获得紧急现金的机会。将避免的借贷成本与风险投资的预期回报区分开来。偿还固定利率余额会改变其条款下的利息义务；投资预测并不能保证其表现会优于成本。检查循环周期及执行情况 每月循环周期为新增余额=旧余额×（1+年名义利率÷12）−实际还款额，最高还款额为所欠金额。不添加新的购买或费用。完成的时间表满足总付款约等于本金加模拟利息（四舍五入）。使用报表的实际汇率并确定任何单独的余额。保持所需付款的最新状态。选择一笔额外付款，留下可行的现金流余量。确认任何预付款限制或费用。使下一个陈述与计划进度保持一致。如果该计划无法支付基本成本和所需付款，那就是需要直接解决的现金流问题。较长的图表并不能创造支付能力。

c96ae665406b319518ea1bb5a9c17a7b2289468b.zh: 独立股票研究/加拿大银行 五个特许经营权。五次不同的估值辩论。阅读业务、测试收益、挑战价格。深入的加拿大银行研究，包括运营预测、信贷和资本分析、情景估值和交互式回报模型。 2026 年 10 月 25 日发布了四项新分析。价格截至 10 月 23 日；截至 7 月 31 日的财务状况。现有的 RBC 票据保留其单独注明日期的快照。 RY·皇家银行 强大的特许经营权，有限的估值缓冲 阅读原始的高级分析、预测模型、信用和资本审查、估值情景和历史回报研究。分析 10 月 18 日·价格 2026 年 10 月 16 日 阅读加拿大皇家银行研究 ↗ BMO · BMO BMO：美国回报必须赢得估值溢价 信贷​​正常化和资本效率正在重建盈利。股价是 7 月普通帐面值的两倍多，还需要美国特许经营权的资本回报率持续提高。参考收盘价为 236.87 加元 我们的 2027 财年每股收益为 17.15 加元 分析 10 月 25 日·价格 2026 年 10 月 23 日 阅读 BMO 研究 ↗ BNS·丰业银行 丰业银行：更好的银行仍需要合理的入场价格 经济好转正在产生更强劲的盈利，但接近 7 月普通账簿两倍的价格已经预期更多。加拿大的资金、国际信贷和资本纪律决定了复苏能否持续。参考收盘价 130.00 加元 我们 2027 财年每股收益 9.56 加元 分析 10 月 25 日·价格 2026 年 10 月 23 日 阅读丰业银行研究 ↗ CM·CIBC CIBC：回报更强劲，轻松重新评级的空间更小 加拿大盈利能力的提高和美国业务的稳定增强了特许经营权。现在的估值要求在税收优惠、交易费用和拨备发放正常化后这些回报仍能持续。参考收盘价 159.59 加元 我们 2027 财年每股收益 11.56 加元 分析 10 月 25 日 · 价格 2026 年 10 月 23 日 阅读 CIBC 研究 ↗ TD · TD TD：复苏有代价；控制仍然很重要 资本回报和更强劲的盈利基础为特许经营提供了支持。要求较高的初始估值仍需要持久的美国执行力、良好的加拿大信用和持久的控制改进。参考收盘价 174.47 加元 我们 2027 财年每股收益 11.19 加元 分析 10 月 25 日·价格 2026 年 10 月 23 日 阅读道明研究 ↗ 比较 通用框架；2026 年 10 月 23 日价格明显的业务风险 ↑ 比率源自日期价格和银行定义的调整后收益。这些是研究锚点，而不是统一的回报排名。每篇文章都解释了自己的盈利基础、预测驱动因素、所选倍数、风险和证据差距。您可以测试的每篇新文章都包括 2026 财年至 2028 财年的运营桥梁、熊市/基准/牛市估值、每股收益和市盈率敏感性、净资产收益率/帐面交叉检查、信用成本压力计算器和五年现金流回报。分析附带源链接和可下载模型输入。未来业绩和股息仍不确定。

5a382bdc336c4fd1fdf0ad96ab42f35415107444.src: Once a portfolio funds spending, the order of returns matters. A long-run average alone cannot describe the path of available retirement capital. Compare two paths with the same ingredients The first chart uses ten invented annual returns. One sequence begins with losses of 20% and 10%; the other reverses the entire sequence. Starting capital and the withdrawal rule are identical. Both sequences contain exactly the same returns. Withdrawals occur at the start of each year, before that year’s return applies. This convention is deliberately explicit because moving the payment date changes the result. The selected annual increase raises requested spending each year; it does not change the return series. Schwab’s sequence-risk explanation describes how early losses can be particularly damaging when a portfolio is funding withdrawals. Our chart uses its own invented return series and assumptions, rather than copying Schwab’s example or estimating a historical retirement outcome. Read the return bars before interpreting the balance The grouped bars show the annual return in each sequence. Negative values fall below zero. Their order differs, but their arithmetic average and no-withdrawal compounded return are the same. With no deposits or withdrawals, the ending balance is the starting amount multiplied by all ten return factors. Reordering multiplication does not change that product. Intermediate balances still differ, which can matter for liquidity and behaviour even in the no-withdrawal case. Set the withdrawal to zero and inspect the final balances. They should match up to rounding. That comparison acts as a control: it helps isolate the role of cash flows instead of attributing every difference to a change in average investment performance. Why the withdrawal changes the arithmetic When money is withdrawn, it no longer participates in subsequent gains or losses. A poor early return can leave a smaller balance supporting later withdrawals. The same dollar spending can then consume a greater fraction of the remaining portfolio. The recurrence used here is ending balance = (opening balance − funded withdrawal) × (1 + annual return) . Funded withdrawal cannot exceed available assets. If requested spending is larger, the remaining balance is zero and the unmet amount is recorded separately. The tool reports unfunded withdrawals because a zero balance must not look like a successfully financed spending plan. In a depleted path, actual funded spending can differ between the two sequences even though the requested rule is identical. Keep a teaching comparison separate from a retirement forecast Ten hand-picked returns cannot establish a sustainable withdrawal rate or a probability of success. There is no statistical confidence interval here, no simulation distribution and no claim that either sequence is likely to occur. A full plan also needs a longer horizon, longevity assumptions, pension and benefit cash flows, taxes, investment costs, asset allocation, inflation and spending flexibility. Currency and household obligations can add further constraints. Those items are outside this demonstration. Do not treat the first withdrawal as a recommended percentage of savings. It is an input that exposes the relationship. A plan that works under one invented sequence may fail under a different drawdown, a longer life or a larger spending need. Use the charts to ask better planning questions Which essential expenses are covered by reliable income outside the portfolio? How much spending could be delayed or reduced after a market decline? What liquid resources are available without selling volatile assets? How would a longer retirement or a higher cost level change the funding gap? When will the withdrawal plan be reviewed and adjusted? Flexibility can change the required cash flows, while asset allocation changes the range of investment paths. Neither can be assessed from a single average return. Use this visual explanation as a starting point for a plan with explicit obligations, documented assumptions and a review process.
5a382bdc336c4fd1fdf0ad96ab42f35415107444.zh: 一旦投资组合为支出提供资金，回报的顺序就很重要。仅凭长期平均值无法描述可用退休资本的路径。比较具有相同成分的两条路径第一个图表使用十个发明的年回报率。一个序列以 20% 和 10% 的损失开始；另一个则颠倒整个顺序。起始资金和提款规则相同。两个序列包含完全相同的返回值。提款发生在每年年初，当年的申报表适用之前。这个约定是故意明确的，因为移动付款日期会改变结果。选定的年度增长会增加每年所需的支出；它不会改变返回序列。施瓦布的顺序风险解释描述了当投资组合为提款提供资金时，早期损失可能特别具有破坏性。我们的图表使用自己发明的回报系列和假设，而不是复制施瓦布的例子或估计历史退休结果。在解释余额之前先阅读回报率条形图 分组的条形图显示每个序列中的年回报率。负值低于零。它们的顺序不同，但算术平均和无提款复合收益是相同的。在没有存款或取款的情况下，期末余额是起始金额乘以所有十个回报系数。重新排序乘法不会改变该乘积。中间余额仍然不同，即使在不提款的情况下，这也可能对流动性和行为产生影响。将提款设置为零并检查最终余额。它们应该与四舍五入相匹配。这种比较起到了控制作用：它有助于隔离现金流量的作用，而不是将每一个差异都归因于平均投资业绩的变化。为什么提款会改变算术 当钱被提款时，它不再参与后续的收益或损失。早期回报不佳可能会留下较小的余额来支持以后的提款。同样的美元支出可以消耗剩余投资组合的更大比例。这里使用的递推式是期末余额 = (期初余额 − 提款) × (1 + 年回报率) 。资金提款不能超过可用资产。如果请求的支出较大，则余额为零，未满足的金额单独记录。该工具报告无资金的提款，因为零余额看起来不像一个成功融资的支出计划。在耗尽路径中，即使请求的规则相同，两个序列之间的实际资助支出也可能不同。将教学比较与退休预测分开 十个精心挑选的回报无法确定可持续的提款率或成功概率。这里没有统计置信区间，没有模拟分布，也没有声称任何一个序列都可能发生。完整的计划还需要更长的期限、长寿假设、养老金和福利现金流、税收、投资成本、资产配置、通货膨胀和支出灵活性。货币和家庭义务可能会增加进一步的限制。这些项目不在本演示范围内。不要将首次提款视为建议的储蓄百分比。它是公开关系的输入。在一种发明的序列下有效的计划可能会在不同的回撤、更长的寿命或更大的支出需求下失败。使用图表提出更好的规划问题 哪些基本开支由投资组合之外的可靠收入支付？市场下跌后可以推迟或减少多少支出？在不出售波动性资产的情况下可以获得哪些流动资源？更长的退休时间或更高的成本水平将如何改变资金缺口？提款计划何时进行审核和调整？灵活性可以改变所需的现金流，而资产配置则改变投资路径的范围。两者都不能通过单一平均回报进行评估。使用此视觉解释作为具有明确义务、记录的假设和审查过程的计划的起点。

At more than twice July common book, the share price also requires lasting improvement in the return on capital committed to the U.S. franchise. TickerLantern Research 25 October 2026 Financials: quarter ended 31 July 2026 Watchlist · return recovery already matters Can the U.S. franchise lift returns on total equity after the credit comparison becomes harder? Our FY2027 modeled EPS of C$17.15 and 13.5× exit P/E imply C$231.53 in October 2027 and a +0.6% cash-dividend-inclusive return. This is a conditional valuation case. The case at a glance CAD Reference close C$236.87 12-month model value C$231.53 FY2027 EPS · our model C$17.15 Base total return +0.6% Price: 23 October 2026 Financials: 31 July 2026 Analysis: 25 October 2026 Evidence confidence: high for cited actuals; forecasts are judgment. Forecasts, exit multiples, return hurdles and review flags are TickerLantern assumptions. No licensed consensus feed or point-in-time valuation backtest is represented. Investment case A return recovery with a demanding entry price ↑ BMO offers exposure to a recovery in the earnings power of a large North American banking franchise. The investment question is how much further the return on shareholder capital can improve once easier credit comparisons fade. At the October 23 close of C$236.87 , the shares trade at an analyst-calculated 16.47× trailing adjusted EPS and 2.10× July book value . The former uses FY2025 adjusted EPS of C$12.16 plus nine-month FY2026 EPS of C$11.11, less the comparable C$8.89: a C$14.38 trailing measure. Neither the price nor the multiple describes an undiscovered turnaround. Our valuation test separates business progress from the return available to a new shareholder. Faster profit growth can coexist with a disappointing share return if the starting multiple already capitalizes the improvement. A book-value cross-check makes that burden visible: with 4% perpetual growth and a 9.5% equity cost, the observed book multiple implies a sustainable ROE of approximately 15.5%. Raising the equity cost to 10% increases the required ROE to approximately 16.6%. These are stylized steady-state inferences, not price targets. The favorable case requires deposits and fee relationships to deepen while lending produces acceptable returns after losses. A lower share count can help per-share earnings, but it cannot repair weak economics on the capital that remains deployed. We would become more constructive if recurring returns advance without greater credit risk or a higher valuation multiple. We would become less constructive if the recovery needs persistent reserve relief, unusually strong markets, or repeated disposals to meet the earnings path. Bank of Montreal — TSX historical price · Daily historical data BMO Fourth Quarter and Fiscal 2025 Results · Table 2, adjusted results and EPS BMO Q3 2026 Report to Shareholders · Tables 1–5, 8–9 and 12; printed pp. 7–12, 15–19 Earnings quality Read the operating recovery beside the accounting charges ↑ Q3 FY2026 reported EPS was C$2.38 , against C$3.96 adjusted ; reported and adjusted ROE were 8.4% and 14.0%. Divestiture-related goodwill reductions explain much of that divergence. Our nine-month bridge attributes the C$1.409 billion increase in adjusted income to C$1.210 billion higher pre-provision profit, C$655 million lower credit provisions and C$456 million higher tax. Performing allowances account for C$439 million of the credit improvement. The calculation supports an operating recovery, while also identifying a benefit that should not automatically recur. Adjusted earnings are useful for forecasting the continuing business because they remove specified accounting and transaction items. They also require economic judgment. Excluding an acquisition-related goodwill charge does not reimburse shareholders for the original purchase price. An analysis that accepts the recurring earnings benefit but ignores the capital loss gives an incomplete account of value creation. We therefore use adjusted common income for the earnings model, and retain reported book value and capital allocation as independent tests. The forecast should start with actual nine-month results and an explicit fourth-quarter estimate. Annualizing the best quarter can quietly embed favorable trading activity, seasonal effects and lower preference-share distributions into every future period. Each forecast change should have a named driver: revenue, expense, impaired losses, performing allowances, taxes or shares. Earnings quality improves when ordinary customer activity carries more of the growth and the need for adjustments narrows. A widening reported-to-adjusted gap would warrant a lower confidence rating even if headline adjusted EPS meets our estimate. BMO Q3 2026 Report to Shareholders · Tables 1–5, 8–9 and 12; printed pp. 7–12, 15–19 Franchise and returns The U.S. franchise must earn back its capital burden ↑ The Bank of the West transaction was announced at US$16.3 billion and completed in February 2023. Its strategic promise was scale and a broader customer base; its economic test is the return earned on all capital committed. U.S. Banking's Q3 adjusted ROE was 9.8% . A return measured after excluding acquisition goodwill can be materially different from the return on total common equity. The distinction matters: attractive returns after removing goodwill do not establish that the total acquisition investment has earned its cost. We underwrite the U.S. opportunity through customer economics. Commercial borrowers can support payments, treasury and wealth relationships, making the total relationship more valuable than a standalone loan spread. The bank must convert that potential into durable operating deposits and fees. Growing loans faster than relationship funding can weaken the funding mix, increase marginal costs and expose the franchise to a less forgiving credit cycle. Headline balance growth is therefore insufficient evidence of success. Canada, wealth and capital markets can generate capital and soften a weak U.S. period, but their strength also creates a temptation to overlook the largest remaining return gap. Capital-market activity and wealth fees share exposure to market conditions; they are not independent cushions in every downturn. Our base case should normalize strong market earnings rather than compound them indefinitely. The franchise earns a stronger premium when U.S. returns rise through deeper relationships and better productivity while the established businesses sustain their economics. If U.S. returns stall after credit costs normalize, the case for a higher group multiple weakens.
